title: Post-1.0 compatibility and external-verifier roadmap
description:
## What & scope
Group the four explicitly registered post-1.0 roadmap deliverables without pulling any of them into G0-G4: the APFS Local durability profile after an asupersync non-io_uring backend exists, the harder Windows profile after APFS, BoltCompatProfileV2 write support with its own conformance gate, and the dependency-free external verifier SDK. This is a discoverability/closure epic, not a 1.0 release prerequisite.

## Why
Standalone roadmap tasks were semantically correct but easy to miss in epic-oriented planning. One post-1.0 aggregate makes deferral explicit, preserves prerequisite order, and prevents future documentation from silently implying these capabilities shipped in 1.0.

## Design and boundary
Each child retains its exact platform/protocol/proof ownership and independent gate. Every child depends on its declared foundation/1.0 prerequisite; this epic depends on the children. No G0-G4 gate, 1.0 workstream epic, or capability manifest may depend on this epic. Reserved schemas/profiles remain frozen where the plan requires, while activation stays absent until each child passes.

## Success Criteria
- All four children close with their own unit/property/fault/conformance/E2E and detailed diagnostic evidence.
- APFS remains blocked on the named asupersync backend; Windows remains ordered after APFS; Bolt V2 passes its write/TCK/differential corpus; the verifier SDK proves dependency-free independent verification.
- A graph test proves this epic is downstream of G4 and never in any G0-G4 prerequisite closure.
- Capability/docs tests prove each unfinished roadmap item is advertised as absent/post-1.0, never partial.
- The roadmap rollup emits versioned JSONL with child id, prerequisite/gate state, platform/profile/version, evidence references, verdict, and replay commands; no child may inherit another child or G4 green bar.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: attaching post-1.0 tasks to W10/W11/G4 epics in the blocking direction, silently dropping them, or representing them as vague prose. Risk is roadmap drift; explicit graph and capability tests keep status honest.

## Provenance
Plan registered platform/compatibility roadmap after §19 workstreams and §15 external verification/publication goals.

title: Every check.sh run is voided by routine br writes: 1 tracked-file write per 1.9 min against a 35-min run
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-27 by pane3 while closing the diagnostic half (fgdb-g996).

THE RATE. .beads/.br_history keeps one snapshot per JSONL write, so it is a
complete write log for a TRACKED file. Over 20:00-23:59 UTC: 126 writes, a mean
of ONE TRACKED-FILE WRITE EVERY 1.9 MINUTES. Against a ~35-minute check.sh that
is ~18 expected voiding writes per run. At this rate a full run essentially
cannot complete un-voided.

OBSERVED, NOT ONLY PREDICTED. Two of two runs inspected were voided:
 * 18:29:23-18:40:02 -- three JSONL content changes inside the run (18:29:24,
   18:36:07, 18:37:51); each of the three UNRUN verdicts had exactly one inside
   its window. Full attribution in fgdb-g996.
 * 19:36:13-19:46:44 (exit 1) -- ONE movement in the whole run, caught live by a
   20s shadow sampler: .beads/issues.jsonl between 19:45:01 and 19:45:21.
   .br_history confirms a write at 19:45:20. check.sh reported `UNRUN check.sh:
   tree changed under the run` with HEAD unmoved, and named nothing.

ROUTINE USAGE, NOT MISUSE. `--no-auto-flush` is the OPT-OUT, so every br
create/update/close in ANY pane rewrites the tracked export with no commit.

THE LANDING LEASE CANNOT CLOSE THIS. A lease binds COMMITS; this is a WRITE.
fgdb-eesn works exactly as designed and is orthogonal to this defect.

WHAT IT COSTS, precisely -- worse than a wasted 35 minutes. On the 19:36 run
`w1_cross_crate_determinism_e2e` went RED exit 1, and its own log shows that red
IS `tree changed under the run` (window 19:43:22-19:46:44, containing the
19:45:20 write) -- an ARTIFACT. In the SAME run `RED core: UBS over every tracked
Rust source` fired over a domain of 119 tracked RUST sources, and the only file
that moved was .beads/issues.jsonl, which is NOT in that domain -- so that red is
REAL. Today the whole verdict is void, so both are discarded and the 35 minutes
are spent again. The cost is not delay; it is a real UBS baseline drift that a
re-run buries.

OPTIONS (none chosen -- needs a ruling):
 (i)  SWARM DISCIPLINE: no br writes while a check.sh is in flight. Doctrine
      unless enforced, and doctrine is what already failed here.
 (ii) MAKE A br WRITE TAKE THE LANDING LEASE. RECOMMENDED. br writes are
      sub-second, so the blocked window is negligible -- the inverse of the eesn
      tradeoff where the holder ran 35 minutes. Needs a wrapper or hook, since br
      is a third-party binary we do not modify.
      IF IT IS BUILT, GUARD BY THE LEASE, NOT BY pgrep: pane3 wrote an ad-hoc
      `pgrep -af 'bash scripts/check.sh'` guard for this very bead and it matched
      ITS OWN COMMAND LINE and aborted a safe write. eesn had already designed
      that defect out by pattern-matching nothing; the holder file (name, epoch,
      ttl, pid, proc start time) plus `kill -0` is the instrument.
 (iii) EXCLUDE .beads FROM THE FINGERPRINT -- REJECTED, recorded so it is not
      re-proposed: g0_identity_e2e genuinely READS that corpus, so a mid-run
      change is a REAL void. The tripwire is right to fire; suppressing it trades
      an honest UNRUN for a false PASS.

CONTROL THE FIX (it must be able to fail): run check.sh while a pane deliberately
issues br writes; confirm they are serialised and the run completes un-voided;
then NEUTER the guard and confirm the void returns. A guard whose absence changes
nothing was never producing the result.

DEPENDS ON fgdb-g996 for the naming: without the path in the UNRUN you cannot
tell an artifact red from a real one, which is the salvage this bead is about.
notes:
RE-DERIVED 2026-07-27 by pane4 at HEAD 1a6fdc2. (The re-derivation is in NOTES; the
filed text is the DESCRIPTION above and is untouched.)

VERDICT: THE PREMISE HOLDS AND IS STRONGER THAN FILED. THE RECOMMENDED FIX IS
FORBIDDEN BY THE RULING IT INVOKES. Both halves moved, in opposite directions:
the defect is worse than the bead argued and the bead's own instrument understated
it, while option (ii) — the one marked RECOMMENDED — is ruled out by policy ruling
FOUR of scripts/lib/landing_lease.sh, the exact file it proposes to extend.

--- THE INSTRUMENT IS WRONG IN TWO WAYS, BOTH UNDER-COUNTING ---------------------
The premise sentence is: ".beads/.br_history keeps one snapshot per JSONL write, so
it is a complete write log for a TRACKED file." Both clauses are false.

  (1) IT IS A CAPPED, ROTATING RING. Measured: a default `br update` that moved the
      export ADDED snapshot 20260728_022206 while the total stayed pinned at 105 —
      so one was evicted. The consequence is visible in the corpus: the retained
      history spans 2026-07-26 16:06:39 .. 2026-07-28 02:2x UTC (34.2 h) with a
      29-HOUR HOLE, 2026-07-26 16:55 -> 2026-07-27 21:55 UTC, holding ZERO
      snapshots. CONTROL: `git log --since/--until -- .beads/issues.jsonl` finds
      **259 commits** inside that hole, and a commit implies at least one write. So
      >=259 writes left no trace. The bead's own 20:00-23:59 UTC window is inside
      the hole and CANNOT BE RE-DERIVED AT ALL.
  (2) IT IS NOT ONE SNAPSHOT PER WRITE even inside the window. Two default writes
      run back to back: both moved the export (sha 6ebcc8b5 -> 743b8af6 ->
      0409fb23); only the FIRST produced a snapshot. One counterexample falsifies a
      universal. (Mechanism not determined — intervals run 5s..104s median, so it
      is not a simple one-per-minute throttle. Reported as a result, not a theory.)

BOTH ERRORS UNDER-COUNT, so the filed 126-writes/4h is a LOWER BOUND and the
conclusion survives its instrument. But nobody re-deriving it will reconcile, and
the memory note "only .br_history is a complete beads write log" needs the caveat.

--- THE RATE, RE-DERIVED ON THE RETAINED WINDOW ----------------------------------
2026-07-27 21:55:57 -> 2026-07-28 02:17:27 UTC, 4.36 h, 100 snapshots:
    22.9 writes/hour, mean interval 2.64 min      (filed: 1.9 min — 27% SLOWER)
    expected writes inside a 35-min run: 13.4     (filed: ~18)
So the headline number does NOT reproduce, and in the bead's disfavour.

--- BUT THE MEAN WAS THE WRONG INSTRUMENT, AND THE RIGHT ONE IS FAR STRONGER -----
A 1.9-min mean is perfectly compatible with a 40-minute quiet gap; a mean cannot
support "a full run essentially cannot complete un-voided". The gap distribution
can, and does:
    max gap in the live window:            16.8 min
    gaps >= 35 min:                        0
    35-min windows with ZERO writes:       0 of 229   (0.0%)
    20-min windows with ZERO writes:       0 of 244   (0.0%)
CONTROL — the sweep must be able to return non-zero, and it decays monotonically:
    2 min 54.2% free | 5 min 20.1% | 8 min 8.2% | 10 min 4.3% | 15 min 0.8% |
    20 min 0.0% | 35 min 0.0%
So the zero is licensed by accounting, not by a broken reader. The bead's claim is
not merely true on average — a 35-minute un-voided run was IMPOSSIBLE across the
entire retained window, and so was a 20-minute one.

--- THE REST OF THE PREMISE: HELD ------------------------------------------------
 * `--no-auto-flush` is the opt-out: `br create --help` line 35, "Skip auto JSONL
   export". HELD.
 * The lease binds COMMITS, not writes: scripts/git_hooks/pre-commit.sh:62-63
   allows every branch but `main`, and the hook's own text says "build, test, run
   gates, git add, and commit in your own scratch worktree -- all unaffected".
   The hook is INSTALLED and live at .git/hooks/pre-commit (core.hooksPath unset).
   HELD.
 * The cost claim is structurally sound at HEAD: UBS's domain is the tracked Rust
   set = **119 tracked .rs**, reproducing the filed figure exactly.
   .beads/issues.jsonl is 1 of 199 tracked files, is inside the fingerprint (which
   hashes EVERY tracked file) and outside UBS's domain. HELD.
 * Option (iii)'s rejection stands: g0_identity_e2e reads .beads at run time, as
   AGENTS.md documents and as was mutation-proven 2026-07-27. HELD.
 * NOT RE-DERIVABLE, reported as a result: the two observed voided runs (18:29 and
   19:36) — their logs are gone and their window is inside the .br_history hole.
   The phenomenon does not depend on them; the gap sweep above establishes it.
 * STALE: "DEPENDS ON fgdb-g996". g996 is CLOSED; its fix landed at 5e2d682, and
   `gate_tree_diff` is now called from `gate_check_tree_stable`. The naming this
   bead waits on EXISTS. That unblocks option (v) below.

--- THE PRESCRIPTION: OPTION (ii) IS RULED OUT -----------------------------------
P1 IT IS FORBIDDEN BY THE RULING IT INVOKES. scripts/lib/landing_lease.sh records
   four operator policy rulings; FOUR reads: "HOLD LANDINGS, NEVER PANES. A
   leased-out pane must still derive, stage and run read-only checks. Only
   `git commit` on branch `main` is bound ... Holding panes rather than landings is
   what cost pane4 forty minutes." A br write is not a landing. Binding it to the
   lease is exactly holding a pane, and the file already records that this was
   tried and what it cost.
P2 THE JUSTIFICATION MEASURES THE WRONG DIRECTION. "br writes are sub-second, so
   the blocked window is negligible" describes how long a br write would block a
   check.sh from STARTING. That is not the cost. check.sh holds the lease for its
   WHOLE run by explicit design (check.sh:1508 and the comment "WHY THE WHOLE RUN
   AND NOT JUST THE CARGO PHASES"), so every br write in every pane would wait up
   to ~35 minutes. Turn the bead's own headline number around: 13.4 br writes
   refused per run, and since 0 of 229 35-min windows are write-free, EVERY run
   refuses some. The bead calls this "the inverse of the eesn tradeoff"; it is the
   SAME tradeoff, pointed at the panes instead of the landings.
P3 THE BEAD NAMES THE FLAG THAT MAKES A NON-BLOCKING FIX POSSIBLE AND THEN DOES
   NOT PROPOSE IT. See fgdb-wv3v — option (iv), PROVEN, not argued.
P4 THE BEAD'S OWN COST ANALYSIS SUPPORTS A FIFTH OPTION IT DOES NOT DRAW.
   See fgdb-41p3 — option (v).

STATUS: STAYS OPEN. The defect is real, unrepaired, and the bead's own framing —
"OPTIONS (none chosen -- needs a ruling)" — is still the right one. What changed is
that the option marked RECOMMENDED is eliminated, and two better-supported ones are
on the table. The ruling now chooses among (i) discipline, (iv) defer the export,
and (v) scope the void.
close_reason: Owner ruling recorded: native project-wide auto-flush disable plus lease-aware explicit export is the primary fix; gate-domain scoping remains independent defense in depth.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: RULING at HEAD f0d72db. Reject option (i): unenforced discipline already failed. Reject option (ii): binding every br mutation to the 35-minute landing lease violates the explicit hold-landings-never-panes policy and stalls the whole swarm. Reject option (iii): excluding .beads from the fingerprint would certify a corpus that g0_identity_e2e actually reads. Select option (iv) as the primary prevention, refined to use br native project configuration rather than a per-mutation wrapper: commit sync.auto_flush=false in .beads/config.yaml so all routine DB mutations are mechanically non-exporting, then own the tracked export through one lease-aware explicit-flush helper used at session completion. That helper must defer only while a live BINDING lease exists; FREE flushes; BREAKABLE, UNREADABLE, and unknown state fail open loudly and flush, preserving landing_lease ruling THREE. It must use landing_lease_state as a plain call, never command substitution. The shared DB remains authoritative during deferral; an explicit flush exports its current total state, and the existing completion workflow owns eventual convergence. Behavioral proof on deployed br 0.2.16 in isolated /data/tmp/fgdb-09iz-config-probe.3oUTkk: after sync.auto_flush=false, a second DB issue left issues.jsonl byte-identical at sha256 889f2bd8c23e2d849d98f47c30af746d2940d682f1d2cc24272ec89a8655657a and one line; br sync --flush-only changed it to 0a2ce315e38be932753da99cdfaad9a9abfbd3564c2fca5d9b398473c2b03360 and two lines. Keep option (v), fgdb-41p3, open as independent defense in depth for unavoidable non-Beads movement and real-red salvage; it requires complete gate-domain declarations and must not delay the narrower prevention. Execute fgdb-wv3v first, then reassess fgdb-41p3.

title: Production Cx construction path: fgdb::Database is unopenable outside tests (only constructor is test-gated Cx::for_testing)
description: Found by GentleCat during p95p premise re-derivation (mail 22225, HEAD 12de7a0). fgdb::Database requires &CommitCx -> PurposeContexts::narrow_runtime_root(&Cx<cap::All>), but the only Cx<cap::All> constructor is asupersync's Cx::for_testing(), gated #[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-internals"))] — its own doc says production consumers cannot construct one out of band. Consequences: (1) the spine's 'a human can actually run it' claim is doctest-only — no binary can open a database; (2) the SS17 benchmark gates cannot be honestly measured (p95p blocker); (3) the embedded-library posture (README posture 1) is not actually consumable. Fix direction: a production runtime-root constructor in the fgdb composition crate (or an asupersync-sanctioned production entry), preserving the capability-narrowing doctrine — NOT a test-feature leak into production builds. Blocks honest p95p measurement; feeds W10 CLI posture.
close_reason: Closed by orchestrator PeachTiger. Fix landed 77e512d: production runtime-root constructor + crates/fgdb/examples/open_a_database.rs — a real binary that opens, writes, drops, reopens, and agrees (exit 0, re-run confirmed by assignee at close time; mail 22339). Capability narrowing preserved per bead constraint; §17 measurement unblocked (d104645 already measuring through the production path). Database is no longer unopenable outside tests; embedded posture is consumable.

comments.author: GentleCat
comments.text:
PARTIALLY DISCHARGED by 77e512d, and the premise is now SHARPER than I filed it.

WHAT LANDED: crates/fgdb/examples/open_a_database.rs -- a real main() that
creates a database, writes through the real two-fsync path, reads, drops every
handle, reopens from only the path and keys, asserts agreement, exits 0.
'cargo run --example open_a_database' is now a thing a person can run. That
discharges consequence (1) in the bead body ('the spine's a-human-can-run-it claim
is doctest-only -- no binary can open a database'). An example rather than a
[[bin]] because workspace_topology gives the embedded posture binary_name = '' and
assigns the 'fgdb' binary name to the cli posture (entry crate fgdb-cli); a [[bin]]
would claim a name the registry hands elsewhere. cargo test compiles examples, so
it cannot rot silently.

THE SHARPENING, measured at pinned rev 3e8d08e. I filed this bead saying the only
constructor is the test-gated Cx::for_testing. That understates it:
  - Cx::for_testing() AND Cx::for_request() are both
    #[cfg(any(test, feature = 'test-internals'))], and asupersync's [features]
    table (Cargo.toml:77) does NOT define 'test-internals'. The documented opt-in
    does not exist at this revision.
  - asupersync's own doc names the production path explicitly: 'Production callers
    that need a request-scoped Cx must go through
    crate::runtime::Runtime::request_cx_with_budget ... The only ambient-free way
    to mint a Cx in production is through the runtime boundary.'
  - That method is declared pub(crate) at src/runtime/builder.rs:3453. Every call
    site is inside #[cfg(test)] mod tests in observability/pressure_governor.rs.
  - No public method on Runtime returns a Cx at all (enumerated its pub fn set).
So the sanctioned production path is CONTRADICTED BY ITS OWN VISIBILITY MODIFIER.
This is not 'fgdb has not written the constructor yet' -- no external crate can
write one. run_async_under_lab is the only public, ungated Cx source, and it is
the lab runtime.

WHAT REMAINS, and it is NOT fixable inside fgdb: consequences (2) and (3) stand.
The §17 gates still cannot be honestly measured (p95p), and the embedded posture
is still not consumable on a production runtime. The fix has to be upstream --
make Runtime::request_cx_with_budget pub (which merely matches what asupersync's
doc already tells production callers to do), or declare the 'test-internals'
feature the cfg-gates reference. Filed as an UPSTREAM bead; this one should stay
open until that lands, then fgdb swaps the lab entry for the runtime entry in one
small change and the example becomes a production witness.

NOT CLAIMED: no performance numbers. The example's module doc says outright that
lab timings cannot speak to §17's across-cores throughput or p99 gates, because
the lab scheduler is deterministic and serialized.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: POST-CLOSE REALITY CORRECTION 2026-08-09 (GoldBarn, fgdb-ii5j). The close reason overstates what 77e512d proved. It landed a real executable example, but that example runs under the lab runtime; it did not land a sanctioned production Runtime -> Cx path. crates/fgdb/examples/open_a_database.rs and crates/fgdb/tests/cx_probe.rs both explicitly say production Cx acquisition remains unavailable at pinned asupersync 3e8d08e. The live residue is fgdb-r8fa (in_progress). This comment corrects the record without reopening or conflating the successfully landed runnable example with the unresolved upstream authority boundary.

title: §15 remaining: statement publication/delivery and terminal attempt semantics in the oracle
notes:
SCOPED FROM THE PLAN TEXT 2026-07-30 (JadeSnow) — and the scoping found a LIVE DEFECT in the
transaction layer that landed in 4f860e9, not merely a missing feature.

THE DEFECT. plan:672: "Read-close is legal only from cumulative ProvenReadOnly; otherwise the write
terminal path applies EVEN IF ALL EFFECTS NORMALIZE TO NO-OP." Transaction::commit currently returns
TxnOutcome::NothingToCommit whenever the effect set is empty, with no notion of what the statements
were CAPABLE of. So a transaction whose statements were mutation-capable but whose effects all
normalized away is reported identically to a genuinely read-only one. The plan says those are
different terminal paths, and it says so in the one sentence that anticipates exactly this case.

That distinction is not cosmetic. plan:992 has commit() returning WriteCommitted | ReadClosed |
Aborted | Unknown, so the terminal outcome is part of the public contract; and plan:672 adds that a
class exceeding the attempt ceiling rejects BEFORE storage observation, which only means anything if
mutation potential is carried rather than inferred from the effects that happened to survive.

THE MODEL THE PLAN GIVES, small enough to land whole:
1. STATEMENT LIFECYCLE (plan:403): "Every statement is durably Open before execution and terminally
   Published, Failed, or Abandoned." A closed union with three terminals — and Abandoned is the one
   with no analogue in the current code, which only has published-or-failed.
2. WORKSPACE GENERATIONS (plan:403, 672): "successful statements advance one predecessor-linked
   workspace generation"; generation zero starts cumulative_mutation_potential = ProvenReadOnly and
   "successful statement publication takes the MONOTONE JOIN, so a mutation-capable statement can
   never be reclassified away". Predecessor-linked and monotone are both testable directly.
3. TERMINAL ATTEMPT SEMANTICS (plan:672, 992): read-close legal only from cumulative ProvenReadOnly;
   otherwise the write terminal path, no-op effects notwithstanding.

WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT SHAPE FOR THE ORACLE. The join is monotone, so the interesting laws are the ones
where it must NOT go backwards: a mutation-capable statement that FAILS, a mutation-capable statement
whose effects normalize to nothing, and a read-only statement following a mutation-capable one must all
leave the cumulative potential mutation-capable. Each is a plausible implementation slip and each has a
one-line law.

LAWS THE CLOSURE OWES:
- generation zero is ProvenReadOnly, and a read-only transaction read-closes;
- a mutation-capable statement whose effects all normalize to no-op takes the WRITE terminal path — the
  sentence above, made executable, and the discriminator against today's behaviour;
- the join never goes backwards across any of the three cases named above;
- each successful publication advances exactly ONE generation, and generations are predecessor-linked
  (so a gap or a re-used generation is refused);
- a FAILED statement publishes nothing and advances no generation, while earlier publications keep
  theirs — the multi-statement error policy already landed, now visible in the generation counter;
- Abandoned is distinguishable from Failed: a caller deciding whether to retry needs to tell "this
  statement was rejected" from "this statement never reached a terminal".
Mutation-prove each; in particular, deriving mutation potential from the surviving effects instead of
carrying it must redden the no-op law, since that is precisely the current implementation.

SCOPE BOUNDARY, so this does not sprawl: the durable BEGIN/attempt-registration machinery around it
(LocalBeginReservationSpec, TxnOutcomeRecord lineage, ownership leases, capability replay) is W12/§13
protocol surface and belongs to other beads. What §15 asks fgdb-reference for is the SEMANTICS —
which terminal a given statement history reaches, and what the generation counter says — over canonical
maps. Model those and nothing else; the same subset-not-substitute rule that governed
EnsureEdgeByTriple applies, and a fabricated attempt-registration record would be exactly the
counterfeit shape this crate keeps finding.

STATEMENT PUBLICATION/DELIVERY: the DELIVERY half (result streams, ACK/resume, RESULT_BEGIN/CHUNK/END)
is FGP wire surface and is NOT this crate's business. The publication half — that a statement's results
become visible exactly when it reaches Published, and never for Failed or Abandoned — is, and it is the
part that pairs with the generation counter.
close_reason: Fixed in d45188f; exact-commit repository gate and four discriminating mutants settled.

title: Strata adjacency format cannot represent the plan's multigraph: parallel edges (same src+relation+dst, distinct EIds) corrupt or silently mis-answer
description:
VERIFIED BY CONSTRUCTION at HEAD (fresh-eyes scout StrataSim F1; reviewed by VioletBasin). Plan line 191: 'Edges ... may be parallel ... EId is the unconditional parallel-edge discriminator.' The oracle honors it (CreateEdge checks only eid uniqueness, fgdb-reference/src/lib.rs:946-985; neighbours() dedups dsts via BTreeSet). Strata's AdjacencyEntry (crates/fgdb-strata/src/lib.rs:56-72) has NO EId — identity is (src, relation, dst), so the parallel-edge discriminator is dropped at the format boundary.

TRIGGER A (false corruption): commit 2 CreateEdge e10 (1->2); commit 3 CreateEdge e20 (1->2). Both legal. Writer forced-seals; merge_neighbours at as_of >= 3 sees (dst=2, created 2) and (dst=2, created 3) both live -> RootError::OverlappingVersions: a legal history reported as 'not a sequence of states'.

TRIGGER B (silent wrong answer): ONE commit with CreateEdge e10 (1->2) and CreateEdge e20 (1->2); commit 4 DeleteEdge e10. The two creates collapse into ONE pending entry (same-version replace, writer.rs:269-272); the delete of e10 tombstones the KEY -> the lone entry becomes a tombstone. Merge at >= 4 -> []. Oracle: e20 live -> neighbours(1) = [2]. No error anywhere.

BLIND SPOT: strata_oracle_differential.rs's Step enum never creates two live edges with the same (src,dst); no strata/sim test covers parallel edges.

FIX SKETCH (lane-owner decision — format change): add eid: EId to AdjacencyEntry (ENTRY_LEN 56->72, BLOCK_FORMAT_V1->V2). Canonical block key becomes (src, relation, dst, eid); since identities never recycle (6.2), each key has exactly one interval — forced-seal then fires only on genuine re-creation. Merge groups per eid, supersedes per eid, collects dsts into a BTreeSet (preserves the oracle's set semantics); keep OverlappingVersions as 'two live intervals for ONE eid' (impossible-by-construction corruption). scan_neighbours dedups dsts likewise. STOPGAP (NOT plan-compliant): writer refuses a second live eid per key — narrows to simple graph, contradicts plan:191. Related: fgdb-3usp (EdgeAlreadyLive, landed) guards the same-live-eid overwrite; this bead is the KEY-level multigraph gap that guard cannot close.
close_reason: Fixed both parallel-edge corruption paths with EId-aware Strata block V2 and permanent identity spending.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
PREMISE RE-DERIVED AND HOLDS, 2026-07-31 (JadeSnow). Both structural claims verified independently at HEAD: plan:191 reads verbatim 'EId is the unconditional parallel-edge discriminator', and AdjacencyEntry (crates/fgdb-strata/src/lib.rs:56-72) carries exactly src, relation, dst, created_at, retired_at -- no EId. ENTRY_LEN is 16+8+16+8+8, confirming there is no room for one. The bead is correct and Trigger B (silent wrong answer) is the worst defect class we have open.

BUT THE FIX SKETCH HAS A FALSE PREMISE, filed as fgdb-s50d and now a blocker on this bead. The sketch says 'since identities never recycle (6.2), each key has exactly one interval'. The PLAN says that (plan:221, 225, 553). OUR ORACLE DOES NOT ENFORCE IT: uniqueness is checked against the live map only (lib.rs:934, 959) while deletion removes the entry (lib.rs:1019, 1049), so create-after-delete of the same EId is accepted today. grep for 'spent' over fgdb-reference/src/lib.rs returns zero hits -- there is no spent set at all.

CONSEQUENCE FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS BEAD: if you key blocks on (src, relation, dst, eid) and then treat OverlappingVersions as impossible-by-construction corruption, you reintroduce Trigger A one level down -- a legal-per-the-oracle history (create e10, delete e10, create e10) becomes a hard error. Resolve fgdb-s50d first so 'can one eid have two intervals' has an answer, then key against that answer.

NOT CLAIMING THE LANE. fgdb-strata has three recent commits from other panes (fgdb-j0ae, fgdb-rbyv) and this is a V1->V2 format change across 11 files; whoever holds that lane should take it.

title: BlockWriter refuses a cascade that is not the live incident set
description:
The oracle refuses DeleteVertex when `sorted_retired_incident_edges` is not exactly the live incident set (`CascadeImageMismatch`). The fold retires whatever list the row carries. An undercount leaves dangling edges after the vertex is gone.

## Background
`Database::write` derives the exact cascade. A lawful write is fine. Recovery folds the stream through `BlockWriter`, which currently trusts the declared list (preflight only checks each named eid is live and ordered). A hostile or corrupt capsule with an empty/short cascade deletes the vertex and leaves incident edges live — the same dangling-graph class as r196/7g91.

This does **not** recompute a different retirement list. It verifies declared == live incident, then retires the declared list. Related to 7g91. Not parent-child to open `819`.

## Technical Approach
- After the vertex-is-live check, compare declared cascade to `live_incident_edges(vid)`.
- Inequality is `WriteError::CascadeImageMismatch { vid, declared, actual }`.
- Then the existing preflight/retire loop runs on a list now known equal.
- Update cascade tests that expected UnknownEdge/CascadeOrderViolation for a non-equal list to expect CascadeImageMismatch (oracle's reason).
- New test: undercount (empty cascade, one live incident) refuses and leaves the edge live.

## Success Criteria
- Undercount and overcount refuse before any retirement.
- Exact cascade still retires both directions and folds same-commit members.
- `cargo test -p fgdb-strata --test block_writer` exit 0.
- spine + spine_differential stay green.
- `819` stays open.

## Test Plan
block_writer cascade tests; spine; spine_differential.
close_reason: BlockWriter verifies DeleteVertex cascade == live incident set (CascadeImageMismatch). Write-path cascade now keeps same-batch deleted incident eids so NENF vertex-first apply matches. spine 41/41, spine_differential 16/16, block_writer 25/25. 819 stays open.

title: PROPOSAL for the owner: re-key the AGENTS.md memorialization clause from 'is a revert' to 'is memorialized' — agent-authored, NOT to be landed by any agent
description:
OWNER DECISION REQUIRED. This bead exists ONLY to carry a proposed one-line edit to
AGENTS.md to the owner. AGENTS.md is the project constitution and RULE 0 makes it the
owner's document. NO AGENT MAY LAND THIS. Filed by pane4 at the orchestrator's
instruction after the same proposal was twice queued for landing and twice stopped;
the tree has never carried the change (verified: AGENTS.md line 86 is unmodified,
`git log --all -- AGENTS.md` shows four commits, none of them this edit).

=====================================================================
THE EXACT DIFF (AGENTS.md, line 86, one line, nothing else)
=====================================================================
-These are the constitutional, non-negotiable rules from §1 of the plan. Violating any of them is a revert, memorialized in `docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md`.
+These are the constitutional, non-negotiable rules from §1 of the plan. Violating any of them is memorialized in `docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md` — whether the repair is a revert or, as the Backwards Compatibility rule requires, a fix in place.

=====================================================================
THE REASON (measured, not argued)
=====================================================================
The clause makes memorialization conditional on an event this project has never
performed and is forbidden by AGENTS.md itself from performing.

Measured over all 705 commits reachable at e0bddd3:
  commits produced by `git revert` .................. 1
  commits with any revert semantics in the subject .. 3
  of those, reverting a DOCTRINE VIOLATION .......... 0

All three are beads bookkeeping (46e654e, 3a7248f, 1994b8e), and 1994b8e is a
catalog write withdrawn because a construction-order law forbade it — the system
working, not a violation of it.

The reason there are zero is in the same document. Under Backwards Compatibility
AGENTS.md mandates: "Never create compatibility shims or wrappers for deprecated
APIs. Just fix the code directly." This project therefore repairs doctrine
violations IN PLACE and always has. The 44 entries now in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md
are all in-place repairs; not one is a revert.

=====================================================================
WHAT BREAKS IF THIS IS NOT DONE
=====================================================================
1. The clause's literal reading can only ever produce an EMPTY ledger. A future
   reader who takes it literally is correct to conclude that all 44 entries are
   out of scope, and the correct action under that reading is to delete them. The
   entry floor (currently 44, in scripts/g0_negative_evidence_e2e.sh) would then go
   red — but the argument would be "the constitution says reverts", with the
   constitution on the side of emptying the memorial.

2. It leaves the doctrine self-contradictory in a way that is now load-bearing
   rather than cosmetic: one clause requires a revert, another forbids the
   mechanism. Before m172 nothing read either clause, so the contradiction was
   inert. A registered live gate now reads both.

3. It is the vacuity class the project has spent the night closing, one level up.
   A universally-quantified obligation whose domain is empty reports green forever
   (cf. fgdb-fginv-spine-zero-live-checkers-v05b, where 20 clauses were stub and
   "CI cross-checks that every ID has a live checker" was true and empty; and
   fgdb-regcheck-closure-vacuous-no-control-hp0f). Leaving it as-is preserves
   exactly that shape inside the doctrine's own enforcement sentence.

=====================================================================
WHAT DOES NOT BREAK, AND WHY THIS IS NOT URGENT
=====================================================================
Nothing is red today and nothing goes red if this is declined. The gate enforces
BOTH readings already: law 4 requires every revert-semantics commit to carry a
structural disposition (3 of 3 dispositioned, so the literal clause is guarded and
would fire the moment a revert lands), while the ledger is populated from the event
that actually occurs. Declining costs only the contradiction in item 2.

If the owner prefers the opposite resolution — keep "is a revert" and narrow the
ledger to reverts only — that is coherent too, but it requires deleting 44 entries
and lowering the floor, and it should be an explicit owner decision rather than a
side effect. NAME WHICH RESOLUTION YOU WANT; do not let an agent infer it.

=====================================================================
PROVENANCE
=====================================================================
Findings: fgdb-negative-evidence-ledger-does-not-exist-m172 (closed; 37c28c0,
a3a5f8c). Ledger entries NE-0042/0043/0044 record the surrounding defects.
Related: fgdb-g0-doc-sync-usq is the natural home for the general law "every repo
path AGENTS.md names must exist", which m172's gate now implements as its law 1.

title: Strata compaction can emit blocks larger than MAX_BLOCK_ENTRIES
description: Fresh-eyes finding at HEAD 5410ffe. compact() packs retained versions by per-key depth but never enforces the durable block format ceiling MAX_BLOCK_ENTRIES. A valid partition with more than that many retained distinct keys compacts to one oversized Vec, after which encode_block rejects the compactor's own output as ImplausibleEntryCount. This violates the module claim that compaction returns lawful encodable blocks and breaks the seal/compact integration at scale. Fix must cap every output block while preserving one-version-per-key, deterministic ordering, nondecreasing root publication frontiers, answer equivalence for every sequence at or above the floor, and idempotence. Add a small-limit test seam rather than allocating 16 million entries; include a red control showing the current packer exceeds the limit, capacity-boundary cases, repeated-key depth cases, and a proof that every produced block encodes under the production ceiling.

Finished blocks retain canonical key order and are sorted by truthful upper sequence frontier before root publication.

title: private_subject.sh leaks ~82MB per gate run with no lifetime or owner: 18.5GB across 113 dirs, and the tmp pool is 98.5% ours not foreign
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-27 02:1x by pane3, at HEAD eda507f, while disk was at 8.8G free
(100%). This is a TOOLING LEAK, not housekeeping.

## The number

  /data/tmp/tmp.* pool                165 dirs   22.2 GB

  by producer:
    private_subject.sh                113 dirs   18.5 GB   <-- one library
    appendix-baseline harness          19 dirs    3.7 GB
    other registry-check gate          27 dirs    0.3 GB
    unclassified / possibly foreign     6 dirs    0.1 GB

**159 of 165 dirs, and 22.6 of 22.7 GB, are OURS.** The pool has been
characterised to the owner as foreign and off-limits. It is 98.5% our own gate
output. Age: 104 of the private_subject dirs are dated 2026-07-26, 9 are
2026-07-27 -- i.e. one and two days of swarm gate runs, never reaped.

For scale: 22.2 GB is more than TWICE the 8.8 GB free at the time of measurement.
Reclaiming this pool alone ends the disk emergency without touching the 52G
foreign target dir or the 79G of finished-session scratchpads.

## The mechanism, and it is documented in the leaking file itself

`scripts/lib/private_subject.sh` is sourced by three gates:
    scripts/g0_claims_e2e.sh
    scripts/g0_spine_e2e.sh
    scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh
Each `mktemp -d`s a fresh work dir and calls `subject_build`, which writes
`libregistry_check.rlib` (64 MB) + `registry-check` (18 MB) = ~82 MB per run,
per script. The library's own header states the cost and the policy:

    #   73MB  per script per run, so 219MB for one full scripts/check.sh
    # On 2026-07-26 that landed on a volume at 95% carrying 9594 stale
    # `/data/tmp/tmp.*` directories from every gate that mktemps. Reaping those is
    # swarm hygiene and is deliberately NOT done here: nothing in this library, or
    # in any script that sources it, deletes a file.

So the leak is KNOWN, MEASURED, and consciously deferred to "swarm hygiene" --
except no swarm hygiene process existed, so the deferral was to nobody. A
81-82 MB allocation per gate run with no owner and no reaper is how a 906 GB
volume reached 100%.

## Why the current design is right about deletion and wrong about lifetime

Nothing in the library deleting a file is CORRECT under RULE 1 and must stay: a
gate script must never be the thing that removes data. The defect is that the
artifact has no declared LIFETIME and no declared OWNER, so "do not delete here"
became "never deleted anywhere".

## Fix options, cheapest first (not implemented -- this bead is the measurement)

1. CONTENT-ADDRESS AND SHARE THE SUBJECT. The three gates build a byte-identical
   subject from the same tree. Build once into a path keyed by the source hash
   (`/data/tmp/fgdb-subject-<sha>/`) and have all three reuse it. Turns 219 MB per
   check.sh into 82 MB per distinct tree state, and makes reaping trivial because
   the key says which trees are stale. `subject_is_fresh` already computes the
   freshness predicate this needs.
2. DECLARE A LIFETIME. Have the library write a `REAPABLE-AFTER` stamp into each
   work dir and add one accountable reaper (the orchestrator's
   scripts/disk_hygiene.sh) that honours it. Keeps the no-delete rule inside the
   gates while giving the artifact an owner.
3. AT MINIMUM, REPORT IT. The library prints nothing about the space it takes.
   Emitting the path and byte count per run would have surfaced 18.5 GB long
   before 100%.

## Cross-check on the claim that this pool is foreign

I classify a dir as ours by a positive marker, not by absence: `bin/registry-check`
present => private_subject.sh; a file named `appendix-baseline.*` => the appendix
harness. The 6 dirs I could not attribute are left as "possibly foreign" and are
134 MB total, so no reclamation decision turns on them.

## Provenance of this bead

Filed at the orchestrator's request after the pane3 cfg6 inventory (fgdb-cfg6)
showed that five `/data/tmp/tmp.*` dirs attributed to other projects were in fact
this repo's own g0-e2e evidence. That correction is what prompted measuring the
whole pool rather than the five. Sweeping the pool is the orchestrator's call and
goes through their hygiene path; pane3 has deleted nothing.

DO NOT REAP /data/tmp/tmp.G5czm7QFIs until fgdb-ia2b is fixed -- its
spine-baseline.jsonl is the recorded evidence for that bead's script_undeclared
finding.
notes:
LANDED 3caaeb0 -- library and all three call sites, verified end to end. This
supersedes the "designed, not landed" note above; everything it recorded as the
plan is now the shipped code, and the numbers below are from the shipped runs
rather than from a prototype.

THE DEMONSTRATION, three gates against one shared cache:
  subject cache before g0_claims     (empty)
  after g0_claims_e2e.sh             75M, 1 dir   cold build, 12.4s total
  after g0_spine_e2e.sh              75M, 1 dir   4.6s, ZERO new bytes
  after g0_identity_e2e.sh           75M, 1 dir   90s,  ZERO new bytes
Before this commit that sequence cost 3 x 75MB = 225MB, none ever reclaimed.
All three printed "PASS: control: the subject runner reuses one directory and
leaves no residue".

MUTATION-PROVED AGAINST THE SHIPPED CODE, both halves fire:
  runner keyed per run          "subject runner does not reuse: ...-117111336
                                then ...-36398924"
  runner that never publishes   "subject runner left per-run residue:
                                ...partial.588887"
  unmodified runner             PASS in 0.165s, 388KB
Cost 0.5% of the 75MB it protects.

THE CONTROL IS HERMETIC ON PURPOSE, and this is the one design decision worth
carrying forward: my first draft asserted subject-path stability against the LIVE
repository and failed on its first run, because a neighbouring pane committed a
checker source in the 8 seconds between the two acquisitions. Shipped that way it
would have redded all three gates at random -- a worse defect than the leak it
guards. It now runs against a throwaway fixture crate, so it tests the RUNNER's
logic and nothing about the tree's stillness.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, stated in the header so the next reader does not have to
re-derive it: it is a 3x cut, not a bound. 111 commits touched
tools/registry-check/src over the window in which 113 of these directories
appeared -- 1.02 per commit -- so sharing across runs recovers almost nothing;
what is guaranteed is sharing within one check.sh. Reuse and self-cleanup are

title: concurrent_bead_creation_cannot_red_another_panes_tree: a failed CONTROL is indistinguishable from a failed GUARD
description:
REACHABILITY COUPLING. Second instance of the owner-adopted principle: a
mechanism whose verdict OR REACHABILITY is a function of the condition it
validates is not a validator. (Instance 1 = fgdb-checker-mirrors-subject-prose-23u1,
verdict coupling by containment. Instance 3 = hdyv, colour coupling by
irrelevant magnitude.)

=== THE SHAPE ===
tools/registry-check/tests/architecture_decisions.rs:950
concurrent_bead_creation_cannot_red_another_panes_tree

Its control, at :985:

    assert!(
        write_and_validate(&corpus).is_empty(),
        "the unmodified fixture must be as green as the repo it mirrors"
    );

`corpus` is the LIVE .beads/issues.jsonl, read at :954. So when the repo is red
from a bead-provenance cause -- PRECISELY THE CLASS THIS GUARD EXISTS TO CATCH --
the control fires first and:
  - the k=1..5 concurrent-creation growth loop (:992-1004) NEVER EXECUTES
  - the vacuity control that proves a lost record is still caught (:1006+)
    NEVER EXECUTES
The guard is disabled by the condition it detects. fgdb-ft79 recorded exactly
this happening: five architecture tests red, and this one "fails at 'the
unmodified fixture must be as green as the repo it mirrors' -- it is reporting
the same red one layer up."

=== THE CONTROL IS NOT THE DEFECT AND MUST NOT BE REMOVED ===
Owner-confirmed. Without it, an empty violation set could mean the fixture is
not being read at all -- the same law as license-the-zero-by-accounting. Deleting
the control would convert a loud-red guard into a silent-green one, which by
standing policy is strictly worse.

=== THE DEFECT: UNRUN IS REPORTED AS FAILED ===
The panic reads "the unmodified fixture must be as green as the repo it mirrors".
An operator triaging a red suite parses that as "concurrent bead creation reds
the tree" -- i.e. as THIS GUARD'S SUBJECT FAILING. What actually happened is
"this guard never ran". Three distinct states are collapsed into one report:
  PASS    guard ran, subject is sound
  FAIL    guard ran, subject is broken      <- what the message implies
  UNRUN   guard did not run, precondition unmet  <- what actually occurred
UNRUN MUST NOT READ AS FAILED, AND MUST NOT READ AS PASSED. Same law as
no-cargo-flag-recovers-a-compile-failure: an artifact whose binary never ran
must read UNRUN.

=== SUGGESTED FIX SHAPE (not yet authorised) ===
Keep the control; change what it REPORTS. The baseline check should emit a
distinct, self-describing outcome naming the precondition and the codes that
broke it -- e.g. panic text of the form
"UNRUN: baseline corpus is already red (codes: [...]); this guard cannot
distinguish concurrent-creation damage from pre-existing damage and did not
run" -- so the operator reads a skipped precondition, not a failed subject.
The k-loop and vacuity control stay exactly as they are.

DO NOT convert it to a silent skip. A guard that quietly does not run is
instance 1 of this same principle. The requirement is that UNRUN be VISIBLE and
DISTINCT, not that it be quiet.

=== PRIORITISATION NOTE (standing policy) ===
This one fails LOUDLY RED and was cleared in one night. 23u1 fails SILENTLY
GREEN and shipped three false RESOLVES. Rank silent-green defects above
loud-red ones. This bead is P2 for that reason, not P1 -- its failure mode is
visible, and the cost is operator misdiagnosis rather than shipped phantoms.

=== ATTRIBUTION ===
Not introduced by any change tonight; the coupling is inherent to the control
as written. Verified independently at HEAD 57610e9 by building
architecture-check with two plain rustc calls in a .git-free quiet root (no
cargo, no build slot): exit 0, 891 events, 0 non-pass, 463 records indexed,
resolution classes bet_label 307 / direct_owner 98 / family_rule 39 /
exact_override 19. The suite is green RIGHT NOW, which is exactly why this
defect is invisible right now.
close_reason: SUBSUMED by fgdb-guard-disabled-by-its-own-trigger-70q9 (pane3), commits 7e6d692 / 6d66187 / 39ccdb8. Verified at HEAD, not assumed: architecture_decisions.rs:993-1004 now computes repo_verdict from the live repo and asserts mirror_verdict == repo_verdict, replacing the is_empty() control this bead was filed against. Their fix is BETTER than the one proposed here: I proposed distinguishing UNRUN from FAILED in the report, which keeps the unrun state and makes it legible; they made the control DIFFERENTIAL, which removes the unrun state altogether -- the guard now runs even when the tree is red from the cause it detects, and a fixture that is not being read still fails because it produces a DIFFERENT verdict rather than an empty one. Full protection kept, ambient red tolerated. Nothing left to do; not re-done.

title: Root-slot generation overflow can commit D2 before an unpublishable root
description: The integrated spine increments slot_generation with unchecked +1 in ordinary write, compaction, and stale-slot healing. At u64::MAX, a write may make Chronicle durable at D2 before overflow is discovered, leaving a commit whose derived root can never advance the highest-generation slot; debug builds panic and wrapping builds propose a nonmonotonic generation. The master plan requires next_generation=checked_add(...), exhaustion to fail-close writes, and a fenced clone/migration rather than wrap or saturation. Repair all three call sites through one checked authority. Ordinary write must refuse with a typed pre-D2 error and preserve chain/frontier/root; compaction must refuse before derived publication; stale-slot healing must return a typed open error without mutating the max slot. Add end-to-end max-generation controls and a lawful max-1 -> max publication control.
notes: Implemented one checked next_slot_generation authority across ordinary writes, compaction, and stale-slot healing. Typed SlotGenerationExhausted errors refuse before Chronicle D2 or replacement publication. Added two real spine integration tests: max-1 publishes max, then write/compaction refuse with frontier/manifest/root unchanged and cold reopen proves no refused row; a stale max-generation slot makes open refuse without mutating manifest.root. Evidence at source HEAD e6b52954624c43a94619bbf8c3b3604960edf033 with only the two scoped paths dirty: both exact tests rc0, full fgdb spine 69/69 rc0, strict fgdb all-target clippy rc0, fmt/diff-check rc0, scoped UBS rc0, and bash scripts/check.sh rc0 with core 9/9 plus registered live 33/33, zero red/unrun. RCH did not schedule because hz2 reported disk_critical_without_fresh_telemetry; verification therefore ran locally. No-claim: this adds the required fail-closed signal, not a product clone/migration workflow.
close_reason: Checked generation exhaustion now fails closed before D2/publication across write, compaction, and open-time healing; focused, full spine, strict clippy/UBS, and governed full gate are green.

title: Genesis-vs-fork race: certification is blind to fork-created coordinates — a forked child accepts a genesis-claimed commit
description:
Verified by construction (fresh-eyes scout RefDelta IMPORTANT-2; code regions confirmed by VioletBasin). certification_since (fgdb-reference/src/lib.rs:2236-2246) inserts ConflictKey::CoordinateExistence only from the coordinate's OWN history first record. fork_branch_at (lib.rs:2721-2797) creates coordinates/origins with NO stream append and NO history record. So a forked child has empty own history, and the fork that falsifies a pending genesis claim is invisible to certification.

TRIGGER: commit T1 (seq 1, lcs 10) creating v1 on (G,P). txn = Transaction::begin_genesis(db, G, C) — C absent, claims_genesis. txn executes CreateVertex(v2) (fresh). db.fork_branch(G, P, C) (no commit). txn.commit(db, rel, sem, CommitSeq(2), LogicalCommandSeq(20)): provenance passes; certification_since(G,C,0) yields no CoordinateExistence (own history empty); lineage walk yields only Element(Vertex(v1)) — disjoint — no conflict — apply succeeds. Branch C now has TWO creators: origin says Fork{P,@10}, yet its first own commit is a genesis-claimed template evaluated against the empty graph.

Severity: disjoint writes leave materialized state self-consistent (before-images verify) and overlapping writes ARE caught by ordinary element keys; rated IMPORTANT because the oracle certifies a history containing a false claim — the dfk3/re6w class. Fix sketch: certification_since fires CoordinateExistence whenever the coordinate exists in origins AND has no own record with commit_seq <= since (harmless to non-genesis transactions — only genesis claimants carry the key in mine); and/or Transaction::commit: if self.claims_genesis && db.branch_origin(graph, branch).is_some() -> Conflicted{[CoordinateExistence]}.
close_reason: Fixed and verified green at 89c969e. certification_since now also fires CoordinateExistence when the coordinate is in origins with no own record at or before the basis, so the second way a coordinate comes into existence -- a fork, which appends nothing to the stream -- is no longer invisible to certification. Three laws landed: the bead's trigger verbatim (MUTATION-PROVEN: forcing the clause off fails exactly that test and nothing else), plus two controls that both still pass with the fix off, so neither rides on it -- an unrelated fork must not defeat a genesis claim, and a freshly forked branch must accept its first ordinary write. The non-obvious precondition (origins holds Genesis too, but only from first write inside the candidate, strictly after certification) is verified and recorded at the fix site, because the fix is correct for a reason that lives in a different function. 43/43 in transaction_anomalies, full crate and fgdb-sim green, ubs Critical 0. NOTE ON ATTRIBUTION: I authored this in the shared worktree and another pane committed it before I could; the commit message is theirs and accurate. Content verified intact at HEAD.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
PREMISE RE-DERIVED AND HOLDS EXACTLY, 2026-08-01 (JadeSnow). Both structural claims verified independently at HEAD (line numbers had shifted by +97 after b6a399c, so I located them by name):

 - certification_since inserts CoordinateExistence solely from self.history.get(&(graph, branch)).first(), i.e. the coordinate's OWN history;
 - fork_branch_at inserts into coordinates/applied_through/origins and writes NO history record. Its own comment says so: 'The child's state is materialized; its HISTORY is not copied. The child owns an empty record vector.'

So the blindness is structural, exactly as filed.

ONE DETAIL IN THE FIX SKETCH NEEDED CHECKING BEFORE EITHER VARIANT WAS SAFE, and it is not obvious from the sketch. Both variants key on 'exists in origins', and origins holds GENESIS TOO -- lib.rs apply_template does origins.entry(key).or_insert(BranchOrigin::Genesis) on first write. If that ran before certification, either variant would refuse EVERY genesis transaction rather than only the raced one. It does not: the genesis entry is written inside the all-or-nothing candidate, strictly after certification_since is called from Transaction::commit. The sketch is therefore correct, but it is correct for a reason that lives in a different function, so I have recorded that coupling at the fix site.

(Also noted: BranchOrigin::Genesis is reachable only through that or_insert; there is exactly one origins.insert in the crate and it is fork_branch_at's.)

IMPLEMENTED the first variant -- certification_since fires the key when the coordinate is in origins and has no own record at or before the basis -- because that puts the correction in the conflict-key machinery where any future consumer of certification_since inherits it, rather than in one call site.

THREE LAWS LANDED, and the two controls are the point:
 - a_fork_defeats_a_pending_genesis_claim_on_the_same_coordinate: the trigger from this bead, verbatim. MUTATION-PROVEN: forcing the new clause off makes exactly this test fail and nothing else, so it is a real law rather than a tautology.
 - a_fork_of_another_branch_leaves_a_genesis_claim_alone: forking is not rare, and a fix that refused every genesis on any database containing a fork would satisfy the law above while breaking branching outright.
 - a_freshly_forked_branch_accepts_its_first_ordinary_write: the fix marks a forked coordinate as existence-created for EVERYONE, not only genesis claimants. That is deliberate and inert -- the key bites only when it is in both sets and only a genesis claimant carries it in its own -- but inertness was a claim, and this is what makes it an assertion. Both controls still pass with the fix forced off, so neither is riding on it.

title: The lab VFS does not exist and the first fsync already shipped (§15 ordering violation)
notes:
MEASURED 2026-07-29 at 0949f0b; premise re-derived twice. Read the SIZING section at the
bottom before scoping — the second re-derivation changed the size of this job by a lot.

THE PLAN'S CLAIM (§15, verification ladder, first bullet): "The entire database runs under
asupersync's lab runtime: virtual time, seeded deterministic scheduling, virtual TCP, a lab
VFS (injectable latency, torn writes, bit flips, ENOSPC, fsync lies), chaos at every
obligation boundary. ... THE LAB VFS EXISTS BEFORE THE FIRST FSYNC (W1)."

THE FACT: it does not, and the first fsync shipped some time ago.
- crates/fgdb-chronicle/src/store.rs (9e725b4) fsyncs through a named barrier(cx, file).
- crates/fgdb-chronicle/src/commit.rs (20a30f2) fsyncs twice per commit, D1 and D2.

WHAT THE SEAM IS. asupersync ALREADY SHIPS the abstraction: src/fs/vfs.rs defines
`pub trait Vfs` and `pub trait VfsFile` plus a `UnixVfs` real implementation. It does NOT
ship a fault-injecting one — searching src/lab/ for torn_write / fsync_lie / ENOSPC returns
nothing, and while src/lab/ has chaos.rs, injection.rs and ldfi.rs, none is a VFS. So the
plan's "lab VFS" is OURS to write as an implementation of THEIR trait. Consume-as-is
applies to the trait, not to the fault model.

AND THE REASON NOTHING CAN BE INJECTED TODAY: fgdb-chronicle does not use that trait at
all. store.rs and commit.rs both `use std::fs` and hold std::fs::File directly; measured
across crates/, NOTHING in the workspace references asupersync::fs or Vfs (fgdb-unsafe-vfs
is the mmap island, unrelated). There is no seam to inject at.

MY FIRST DRAFT OF THIS BEAD SAID to build it "behind the Cx restriction boundary that
already exists". That is wrong and I am recording it rather than quietly replacing it:
`cx.with_restriction` is where a lab runtime attaches SCHEDULING effects; it is not a file
handle and cannot make read, write or sync lie.

WHY IT MATTERS. The crash-point matrix (crash_point_matrix.rs) and the durability/semantics
differential (durability_semantics_e2e.rs) inject crashes with a test-only enum arm,
CrashPoint, threaded through the PRODUCTION commit path. That models "the process stopped
at instant X" and nothing else. It structurally CANNOT model:
- an fsync that returns success without persisting (the fsync lie) — the single most
  important failure a two-fsync protocol must survive, and the one its correctness
  argument assumes away;
- a torn write INSIDE one file. tear_log_tail_for_test truncates a whole suffix; real
  tearing can lose an interior sector, and the torn-tail rule's whole "missing bytes versus
  wrong bytes" discrimination has never been tested against that;
- bit flips. NOTE this got materially more valuable on 2026-07-29: capsules are now
  erasure-coded (03e7d7e, e940592) and capsule::recover drops symbols that fail their MAC,
  so injected bit rot now has something real to heal. Before that, injecting bit flips into
  raw capsule bytes could only ever have proved they do not heal.
- ENOSPC mid-write. Measured this session: the host filesystem hit 100% and it surfaced as
  opaque cargo and rustc errors, with the database never exercised at all;
- injectable latency, which the publication sequencer will need.

So those suites are GREEN and their coverage is narrower than it reads.

ALSO: CrashPoint is a test-only enum arm in a production signature (commit_with_crash). A
faulting Vfs would let the production path have exactly one shape — the doctrine-7 argument
for building it rather than widening CrashPoint.

=== SIZING, and this is the part that changes the plan ===

asupersync's VfsFile is ASYNC: `VfsFile: AsyncRead + AsyncWrite + AsyncSeek + Send + Unpin`
and every method returns `impl Future`. fgdb-chronicle's I/O is entirely SYNCHRONOUS today
(std::fs::File, blocking read/write/sync_all).

So step 1 is not "swap a type". It is MAKING CHRONICLE'S DURABLE PATH ASYNC — store.rs and
commit.rs at minimum, and every caller including fgdb-sim's harness. That is a real
architectural change, not a refactor that can be slipped into another increment.

It is also the direction the plan already points: §15 says the ENTIRE database runs under
the lab runtime, and doctrine 3 has every I/O function taking `&Cx` precisely so the
runtime can be swapped. Chronicle taking `&CommitCx` and then calling blocking std::fs
underneath is honouring the letter of doctrine 3 while the capability context governs
nothing about the I/O itself. Worth stating plainly: that is the actual defect here, and
the missing lab VFS is its symptom.

SCOPE, in order, and DO NOT try to do these in one increment:
1. Decide the async boundary for chronicle's durable path, and land it against UnixVfs so
   behaviour is unchanged and the existing suites stay green. This is the load-bearing
   step and probably the largest single change in the crate's life so far.
2. Implement a faulting Vfs (torn writes, fsync lies, bit flips, ENOSPC, latency) seeded
   from the lab runtime so every failure is replayable.
3. Re-express the crash matrix against it. REMOVE NOTHING until the VFS-based tests are
   proven at least as strong as CrashPoint's — mutation-prove the new ones first.

BLOCKS honest crash coverage for w2-commit-protocol, w2-root-bootstrap, w2-recovery.
RELATED: fgdb-w2-filesystem-profiles-46y decides how large a write may be before it can
tear; the faulting Vfs is what would let that profile be TESTED rather than declared.
close_reason: Orchestrator close (PeachTiger) with cited evidence: the lab VFS exists and the commit path runs through it. bac511b (FaultVfs + write_with_crash spine), 9b80da3 (Vfs-generic CommitCoordinator, async durable path), 8876ea4 (crash matrix re-expressed over FaultVfs; seam-split child fgdb-w14j). All three SHAs verified in git log. --force rationale: the open blocker edge from fgdb-verif-sim-q97e is a coarse inherited edge, stale in fact for THIS bead's scope — 1xtp's own complaint (lab VFS missing, fsync ordering violated) is discharged by direct artifact evidence; q97e's remaining items do not owe 1xtp anything (its 1xtp-owned LDFI rows were re-derived and re-homed at c8efe8a). Closing unblocks fgdb-milt.

comments.text:
ONE OF THE FOUR FAULT CLASSES NEVER NEEDED THE MIGRATION 2026-07-30 (JadeSnow). Bit rot is landed;
the async VFS work is unchanged and still needed for the other three.

THE FINDING. This bead sizes the fault-injection work as an async migration of chronicle's durable
path, and that is correct for the faults a process CANNOT OBSERVE: an fsync that returns success
without persisting, a tear inside a single write, ENOSPC mid-write, injectable latency. Each needs a
filesystem that lies underneath an async VfsFile. Bit rot is not one of those. It is damage that
appears in a file BETWEEN a successful write and a later read, so a test can simply write the damage
itself -- no seam required, no trait, no migration. Conflating the four classes left this campaign
waiting on work it never required, and the bead's own text is what made that visible by listing them
together.

LANDED as a ten-law campaign in crates/fgdb-chronicle/tests/capsule_bit_rot.rs, over REAL capsule
files that a real commit wrote, read back through CommitCoordinator::read_capsule: heal within the
repair budget, fail closed one symbol past it, the budget as the EXACT boundary asserted in a single
test, identity recomputation on healed bytes (FG-INV-09), header and magic refusals, and that reading
heals the ANSWER rather than the FILE.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT DISCHARGE. It discharges §15's bit-rot half against the durable path, and
it is the first test anywhere in the workspace to prove doctrine 5's "RaptorQ heals corrupt symbols"
end to end rather than at the codec layer: mutating the per-symbol MAC filter in capsule::recover
reddens five of the ten laws. It discharges NOTHING about fsync lies, interior torn writes, ENOSPC or
latency, and the crash matrix's CrashPoint remains exactly as narrow as this bead describes.

FOR WHOEVER TAKES STEP 1: the campaign is deliberately written against the SYNCHRONOUS read path, so
it will need the same migration as everything else when that lands. It is not an obstacle to it -- the
laws are about what read_capsule returns, not about how it reads -- but do not treat these ten green
tests as evidence that the durable path is fault-tested. They cover one class of four.

METHOD NOTE worth reusing: mutation found a law I was missing. Silencing the repair-budget check in
recover left the entire campaign green, because every other law damages either a symbol or a header
field the decoder cannot cross-check. The declared repair count CAN be cross-checked, against the
closed profile registry the authenticated fec_profile selects, and the check exists precisely because
surviving symbols do not reveal how many repair symbols originally existed. A frame allowed to restate
its own durability class would read as healthy while sitting one flip from unrecoverable. The added
law rots that field structurally -- located from the first symbol's offset rather than a hardcoded
header width, and asserting it decoded the expected value before touching it.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
STEP 2 OF 3 LANDED at bac511b (2026-08-04, MaroonCanyon). crates/fgdb-sim/src/vfs.rs (907
lines) + tests/lab_vfs.rs (488 lines) + the pub mod line in src/lib.rs.

PROVENANCE NOTE, because the commit message does not say any of this: my scoped commit
lost a race with another pane, which committed the shared index while my landing was
queued behind a check.sh lease. My files went in under that pane's subject line
("feat(sim,fgdb): land lab FaultVfs and public write_with_crash spine path") and my own
commit returned RC=1, nothing to commit. Worktree matched HEAD exactly afterwards, so the
landed bytes are the reviewed ones -- but the rationale below was in the lost message and
is recorded here instead.

WHAT LANDED. Only step 2 of this bead's own three-step scope: a faulting Vfs. Step 1
(Chronicle's async migration) and step 3 (re-expressing the crash matrix) are untouched
and nothing in fgdb-chronicle was modified, so neither is harder than before.

THE MEASURED CONSTRAINT THAT DECIDED THE DESIGN, and the thing worth not rediscovering:
asupersync::fs::Metadata::from_std is pub(crate), and ReadDir is only constructible from a
real std::fs::ReadDir inside asupersync. Vfs::metadata / symlink_metadata / read_dir all
return those types, so A PURE IN-MEMORY VFS CANNOT BE WRITTEN FROM OUTSIDE THAT CRATE. Any
lab VFS must decorate a real backing Vfs and delegate those three.

From that follows the write-back model: a FaultFile holds the file image in memory and
touches the backing store only on an honest sync. This is also the only way the fsync lie
is observable at all -- a decorator that forwards writes leaves the bytes in the host page
cache, where they survive any simulated crash, so the lie would be undetectable by
construction.

FOUR FAULT CLASSES, all seeded from one in-house SplitMix64 stream:
  - fsync lie: returns Ok having written nothing, and leaves the bytes DIRTY, so a later
    honest sync still writes them -- what a real write-back cache does. Witnessed twice:
    once that the lie loses the data across a crash, once that the next honest sync
    recovers it.
  - torn write: drops one INTERIOR sector and keeps the sectors on both sides. This is the
    case tear_log_tail_for_test cannot produce (it truncates a whole suffix), so the
    torn-tail rule's "missing bytes versus wrong bytes" discrimination had never faced a
    hole with valid bytes after it. The test asserts the hole reads as zeros AND that the
    sector after it is intact.
  - bit flip: one bit of what the flush just wrote; the test asserts exactly one byte
    differs and exactly the reported bit.
  - ENOSPC: refuses the flush at a byte budget, returns raw_os_error 28, and leaves every
    sector dirty.
crash() invalidates every pre-crash handle, so unsynced bytes cannot leak across a crash
through a caller that kept its file open.

CONTROLS, because a fault harness only ever run with faults on cannot tell "the fault
fired" from "the harness is broken":
  - a faultless plan must be byte-transparent and inject nothing;
  - an INELIGIBLE tear (fewer than 3 dirty sectors, so no interior sector exists) must
    inject nothing under Trigger::Always -- so "fired zero times" is a checked outcome;
  - two different seeds must diverge. Without this the determinism test would pass just as
    well against a generator that always returned the same answer.

GATE: cargo test -p fgdb-sim --test lab_vfs -> 10 passed, 0 failed, exit 0.

NOT MODELLED, stated rather than faked:
  - injectable latency, the fifth §15 class -> filed as fgdb-milt with the three candidate
    clock designs and the acceptance bar (a test that FAILS if the delay is not awaited;
    asserting "an event was recorded" would pass against a placebo, which is fgdb-4bxh's
    exact defect).
  - OpenOptions::append (the cursor starts at 0 on every open).
  - cross-handle visibility of unsynced bytes: dirty bytes are visible only through the
    handle that wrote them. Deliberately stricter than a real shared page cache, so the
    model can only fail a test reality would also fail, never the reverse.
All three are documented at the module head, not just here.

STILL OPEN ON THIS BEAD: steps 1 and 3. Step 3 in particular must be mutation-proven at
least as strong as CrashPoint BEFORE anything is removed -- the bead's own instruction, and
the lab VFS existing does not by itself discharge it.

TRACKER NOTE: this bead is graph-blocked by fgdb-verif-sim-q97e, which refused the claim
(br update --status=in_progress -> "cannot claim blocked issue"). That edge is coarse for
this slice: fgdb-sim is already an active crate with 8 test files, and what q97e still owes
(LDFI campaign registry, shrinker, dual-run driver) would CONSUME a faulting VFS rather than
produce one. Raised with PeachTiger on thread fgdb-1xtp.

title: Deployed br tag 0.2.19 still lacks the post-tag partial-batch exit-code fix
description:

title: A14 blocker: adjudicate 14 HA/GC families and two impossible orders
description:
A14 has zero source-forced catalog rows remaining at the bfc9385 archive boundary. Of 18 top-level candidates, 4 are landed and 14 are unminted.

Two reservation-backed logical kinds are UNSATISFIABLE under the settled both-directions construction-order law: ConfigPayloadFloor (reserved 0x0277) and GcProposal (reserved 0x029f). Their StrongRef edges from MandatoryInventory require order >= 25, while GcDecisionRecord.config_payload_floor_ref and GcDecisionRecord.proposal_ref require order <= 15. No integer satisfies 25 <= order <= 15. An authorized reference-strength or construction-order correction is required; do not mint either kind by guessing.

The remaining 12 families are: five confirmed but unreserved class-gated candidates (GcCancellationAuthorityFor<Local>, GcCancellationAuthorityFor<Meta>, GcCancellationAuthorityFor<Shard>, MandatoryInventoryEntry, RemotePreparedIdentity); two ambiguous command-spec candidates needing class adjudication (LocalGcApplyQuarantineSpec, LocalGcCancellationAuthorizeSpec); and five name-only/bodyless candidates needing exact source schema before classification (CurrentCheckpointObservation, GcIrreversibleDispatchGuard, MandatoryInventoryClassRegistry, RegisteredStrongRef, RetiredLocal).

Dependent structural residue: one union and two arms remain on unminted MandatoryInventoryEntry. Source spelling is RetainedStrong | CurrentCheckpointObservation, so source tags must be RetainedStrong 0x0001 and CurrentCheckpointObservation 0x0002. The census displays them alphabetically in the opposite order; source order wins.

Field boundary: 122 of 127 fields remain. 90 have unminted owners and 32 have landed logical owners. Across all 122, 67 have NO exact_type in source and 55 have one. Within the 32 landed-owner rows, 23 have no exact_type; the remaining 9 split into 2 blocked by the impossible orders above and 7 blocked by unresolved vocabulary (GcCancellationAuthorityFor<Role>, PortableGcPhysicalTerminalEvidence, CanonicalPublicationEvidence<Role>, AwaitingPhysicalDisposition, MandatoryInventoryEntry). READY = 0. Ownership is not the dominant blocker.

The pinned source census also omits PayloadReceipt and the physical-plane schemas named by prior a14 analysis; repair or expand the source census before freezing those formats. Acceptance: resolve the two impossible order windows, settle or source-complete all 12 other families, register referenced vocabulary, and preserve source arm order.

comments.text:
THE ONLY PART OF fgdb-oicl THAT IS NOT AN ASSIGNMENT DEFECT. Split out of oicl at
5b484ec, which discharged the whole mechanical class (22 symbols / 53 rows) and left
exactly this. Measured with the balanced-scan min-cut solver rebuilt from the tree it
measures; every edge below is the source spelling, not a paraphrase.

=== WHY NO INTEGER FIXES THESE ===
`projection_dag_future_result` is NON-STRICT — it fires on `target.order > containing.order`,
witnessed by 80 landed equal-order retaining edges. A non-strict relation over an ACYCLIC
graph is satisfiable by construction (give every symbol the same integer), so the ONLY
genuinely unsatisfiable cases are where the source graph CYCLES. That is this bead.

All three cycles sit at CO-EQUAL orders today, which is exactly why the tree is green:
co-equality satisfies dag_future_result. It does NOT satisfy `dag_cycle`, which walks the
EDGE SET alone. They go red the moment their field rows land, and no order will save them.
This is the dangerous shape — green now, frozen later.

=== THE THREE CYCLES, BY CLOSING EDGE ===

C1  a10 global txn, 3 symbols, all at order 60
      GlobalPrepareAdmissionSpec.global_outcome_preparation_ref
          : StrongRef<GlobalTxnOutcomePreparationRecord>

      back edge `KeyEnvelopeNode.inherited_roots[].source_root_ref` points at a DIFFERENT,
      parent-branch envelope root (the members alongside it are source_graph, source_branch,
      source_envelope_epoch). It is lineage provenance, not ownership.
  C1  `expected_registered_outcome_ref` names a PRE-ACTION state to compare against. The
      `expected_` prefix is a real pattern here, not a reading: GlobalPrepareAdmissionSpec
      carries four more of them (expected_topology_state_ref, expected_workspace_generation_ref,
      expected_cumulative_read_witness_root_ref, expected_cumulative_logical_effect_root_ref),
      all currently StrongRef.
  C2  the freeze/proof pair is a terminal-evidence back-reference, the same shape.

A comparison basis does not need to keep its subject alive — that is the a01
identity-is-not-reachability law — and fgdb-u3gr has ALREADY RULED the repair form for
exactly this semantics: `digest256` + `digest_class`, `reference_semantics = "none"`,
`identity_class = "inline"` (the weak-identity variant being WeakDigest + weak_identity,
comparison-only, excluded from reachability / GC / checkpoint / backup traversal). So this
is that existing ruling applied at three named links, not three new designs.

=== FORKS, COSTED ===

FORK A (recommended) — amend the three provenance links to the ruled non-retaining form.
  Scope per link: the plan source member, the Appendix catalog + projections, the source
  census/assignment pins for the owning slice, and any regression test that names the
  member. The five-link d8b51ed precedent touched 12 files / 456 insertions / 68 deletions;
  three single-link amendments across three slices are smaller each but cross the same
  surfaces. C3 is the cheapest (0 landed field rows on both ends) and is the natural pilot.
  After each cycle is broken, its component becomes an ordinary min-cut batch that the
  existing solver already emits — C2's is solved and sitting on fgdb-oicl at 3 symbols /
  6 rows.

FORK B (not recommended) — admit retaining cycles via a checker exception or a typed
  mutual-reference relation. A name allowlist is textually small but leaves an unbounded
  retaining cycle in the reachability/GC and checkpoint-vector walkers, which are keyed on
  construction_order. A sound typed relation needs registered schema vocabulary plus
  explicit GC/checkpoint/backup cut semantics and negative tests, so its complete-system
  cost is at least Fork A's while weakening the invariant.

FORK C (do nothing) — free today and stays green, because co-equal orders satisfy
  dag_future_result. It fails the moment any of the 13 landed field rows across C1/C2 grow
  a sibling, and the order is frozen by then. This is the option the oicl bead's own root
  cause warns about: mint first, land the body later, discover the contradiction after it
  is expensive.

DECISION REQUESTED: approve Fork A and confirm the u3gr non-retaining form applies at
these three links, or require the larger typed design. If Fork A, C3 (KeyEnvelope, zero
landed field rows) is the pilot and C2 should be sequenced with the a08 self-edge repair
on fgdb-suhb so the audit component is fixed once rather than twice.

title: Candidate 3: make law citations RESOLVE against laws.toml, not merely fail to be copied
description:
SUCCESSOR TO fgdb-n061 (landed 81280f6), which removed the 450 mirrored
rationale literals. That took the four circular classes to zero — no existence
query about Appendix A resolves against a copy of Appendix A any more.

WHAT IT DID NOT DO. A law citation inside a catalog rationale now has NO
representation in the checker at all. Before: it resolved against a copy (wrong
answer, confidently). After: it resolves against nothing (no answer). Neither is
"the citation names a law that exists and is registered".

THE ARTIFACT, from the n061 scope's candidate 3: add `cited_laws:
&'static [&'static str]` to AmbiguityAdjudicationContractPin (~77 non-empty
rows, ~1,200 chars) plus a resolver requiring every law name occurring in
row.rationale to appear in pin.cited_laws AND resolve to a `registered` row in
registries/laws.toml, failing CLOSED with its own violation code. laws.rs says
this itself: the registry exists "so that a later guard can require citations to
resolve to IDs rather than to prose."

THE LANDMINE, and it is why this was NOT bolted onto n061. "No source law
requires authenticated membership proofs" is ordinary English that both the uzzh
extractor and a fresh independent one match as a law citation. A naive resolver
lands RED on day one. Extraction must require the name be backticked or
anchor-adjacent, and THAT DISCRIMINATION MUST BE RED-PROVED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS
— a real citation is extracted, that sentence is not — rather than handled by
allowlisting the sentence. That is a sub-project with its own control, not a
rider on a removal.

PREREQUISITE WORTH CHECKING FIRST: registries/laws.toml cannot currently express
"enforced but undocumented". `registered` requires BOTH a non-empty enforcement
AND an aNN:LINE anchor (tools/registry-check/tests/laws.rs,
law_source_anchor_missing), so a law that is genuinely enforced but has no plan
line to point at must be filed `unadjudicated` or `fabrication-candidate`, both
of which understate it. 5 of 9 rows carry an empty enforcement. The owner ruled
on 2026-07-27 that the schema must express it and that an anchor is required
only for plan-anchored rows; that ruling is NOT landed. A resolver that requires
`registered` will therefore reject citations of laws that are real and enforced.
Needs the catalog token.

RE-DERIVE BEFORE STARTING: laws.toml is 9 rows at HEAD, not 10 — created in one
commit (57610e9) and never modified since.

Filed by pane2, 2026-07-27. Nothing deleted.
