title: Census drops the FIRST name of every '`A` and `B` are ...' definition: 13 of 13 sites, 13 top-level candidates invisible
description:
The structural source census drops the FIRST name of every "`A` and `B` are ..." definition sentence
in Appendix A. Measured 13 of 13 sites, zero exceptions, mechanism mutation-proven by a swap control.
Thirteen real top-level schema candidates are therefore invisible to the entire Appendix A closure,
and at least two catalog rows cannot be landed because of it.

## The population, with its denominator
Appendix A (plan lines 1388-2728) contains 13 sentences of the form
    `A` and `B` are <definition>
For every one of the 13, the census emits B as a top-level schema candidate and does NOT emit A:

  A (DROPPED)                                        B (kept)
  LocalReadWitnessRef                                LocalWriteSummaryRef
  ResultLeaseRef                                     ResultSemanticOwnerRef
  MetaCertificateLedger                              ShardCertificateLedger
  MetaAuthorizationEvidence<Tag>                     ProtocolAuthorizationEvidence<Tag>
  AuthorizedDeltaPublicProvenance                    PublicDeliveryDigest
  RestoreSourceLeaseAcquireReceipt                   RestoreSourceLeaseRenewReceipt
  CanonicalBootstrapOpenersRef<Role>                 CanonicalVerifiedObjectInventoryRef<Role>
  PreBootstrapDispatchPublicationEvidence<Action>    PreBootstrapNeverSentProof<Action>
  OperationalRestoreTerminalPinBasisRef<Role>        AbandonedRestoreTerminalPinBasisRef<Role>
  LocalRestoreStateRef                               MetaRestoreStateRef
  ReservedReservationUseRef<Role>                    ClaimedReservationUseRef<Role>
  RestoreReconciliationEvidenceRef<Role>             RestoreExplicitRetentionOwnerRef<Role>
  ExternalCasRestoreServicePromotionManifestRef      ExternalCasRestoreServicePromotionReceiptRef

  A-dropped-and-B-kept: 13 / both-censused: 0 / both-absent: 0   (denominator 13)

Census total is 1237 schema candidates, so this is a 13-row undercount (about 1.05%) concentrated
entirely in generated-reference and paired-evidence families.

## The mechanism, named at the line
appendix_source.rs:1407  prose_definition_head()
    let display_name = simple_type_display(&fragment.text)?;
    has_definition_cue(&fragment.after).then_some(display_name)
A fragment becomes a definition head only if the text IMMEDIATELY AFTER it carries a definition cue.
In "`A` and `B` are ...", fragment A's trailing text is " and " -- no cue -- so A never becomes a
head and prose_schema_links() (appendix_source.rs:1415) never builds a link for it. Only B, whose
trailing text is " are ...", is linked. The conjunction is never treated as distributing the copula.

## Control (positional, not name-specific) -- FIRED
Swapping the two names in the a20 sentence, with nothing else changed:
  baseline:  ManifestRef ABSENT, ReceiptRef CENSUSED, 1237 total candidates
  swapped:   ManifestRef CENSUSED, ReceiptRef ABSENT, 1237 total candidates
The censused identity follows the POSITION, not the name, and the total is unchanged -- so it is a
strict one-of-two selection, not an omission of an extra. Reproduce with probe_swap.rs in
/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane4_ivsp (set MUT="<from>|<to>").

## Why this is load-bearing right now, not cosmetic
A top-level [[target]] claims its candidate with source_key "top|<Name>". A census-absent name has no
candidate to claim, so no row can be landed for it. In a20 alone this blocks two of the eleven
actionable exact-typed field candidates:
  GlobalRestoreServiceFinalizeSpec.manifest_ref          :: ExternalCasRestoreServicePromotionManifestRef
  RestoreShardOperationalAck.operational_terminal_pin_basis_ref :: OperationalRestoreTerminalPinBasisRef<Shard>
Both exact types are among the 13 dropped. Note the asymmetry this produces: the SIBLING
ExternalCasRestoreServicePromotionReceiptRef is landed as wire_type 0x054f with three field rows
already citing it, while its co-defined twin -- same sentence, same shape, same slice -- has no row of
any kind. The catalog currently records half of a construct the source defines as a pair.

## Fix shape (not implemented here)
prose_schema_links must distribute the copula across a conjunction: when a fragment's trailing text is
a pure conjunction connector (" and ", ", ", " and its ") and a LATER fragment on the same line carries
the definition cue, every conjunct in that chain becomes a definition head sharing the one RHS.
Guard it CLOSED: only chain across fragments that are themselves simple_type_display names, and stop
at sentence_ends() exactly as the existing scan does.

## Expected blast radius when fixed -- MUST be re-measured before landing
Adding 13 top-level candidates moves per-slice top_level_candidate_count and the
top_level_candidate_ids_sha256 transcript for every affected slice, plus the global census counts.
Those are DECLARED pins in registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml and are recomputed live (mutating one
fires [source_structural_census_mismatch]), so this needs the base-derived pin cycle
(/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/refreeze_identity_pins.sh), never a hard-coded value. Derive the affected slice
set by re-running the census, do not infer it from the table above -- the 13 sites span many slices.

## Reproduce
Build the checker with rustc from the repo dir (no build slot needed; recipe in
/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane4_ivsp/APPLY.md), then run probe_conj.rs (13-site sweep) and probe_swap.rs
(swap control) from that directory.

title: amendment-sitting: define the five named-but-never-defined §6.2 Tier-D fields (visibility_intervals, descriptor_key, property_patch_refs, stripe_range, + DeltaPartitionRoot residues)

Prepared 2026-08-04 by JadeSnow under PeachTiger allocation (msg 22321). Labels: b2, strata, w3, formats.
PeachTiger conducts the sitting; rulings recorded per amendment convention, explicitly subject to the
human owner override.

THE DEFECT CLASS. Plan L534 declares DeltaBlockVersion {format,partition_id,descriptor_key,
stripe_range,sorted_entries[],visibility_intervals[],property_patch_refs[],predecessor,
canonical_logical_digest}. FOUR of those names occur in the plan EXACTLY ONCE -- in that list -- with
no element type, no cardinality vs sorted_entries[], no semantics. A field named once in a struct
literal is a name, not a contract: it cannot be implemented and it cannot be registered.

CENSUS WITH A CONTROL (whole-plan occurrences):
  visibility_intervals 1 | stripe_range 1 | property_patch_refs 1 | descriptor_key 1
  DeltaPartitionRoot   2  <- CONTROL, a real used name in the same section
Two occurrences is NORMAL for this thin section, so a low count is not the finding; "named, never
defined" is. CORRECTION worth carrying: descriptor_key was earlier counted at 2 -- the second hit
(L890) is a DIFFERENT concept, descriptor MASKING in fgdb-secure-view. Block-sense descriptor_key is
in the same once-only class.

STANDING EVIDENCE, the byte chain (real codec, 256-entry block, 41fb41b + 5500358; independently
confirmed by ChartreuseSalmon msg 22327):
  current V2 layout                          72 B/entry (56 fit 4 KiB)
  identity codec on the CURRENT six-field entry  43 B/entry (2.6x over ceiling)
  §6.2 own entry shape, two identity columns     13 B/entry
§6.2 ceiling is <=16, so 13 leaves exactly 3 B for user_key_ref?/prop_row_ref/flags. Every ruling
below spends against that 3 B, which is why fields 1 and 3 must be ruled TOGETHER.

DECISIVE FIELD: visibility_intervals cardinality. PeachTiger by2l ruling hoists created_at/retired_at
INTO it, and whether that hoist achieves anything depends entirely on this:
  1A one interval PER ENTRY -> 13+16 = 29 B/entry; 256x29 = 7424 B, nearly 2x the stated block size;
     only ~141 entries fit 4 KiB. DOMINATED -- it makes §6.2 OWN 4KiB/256/<=16 numbers mutually
     contradictory and makes the by2l hoist a byte-economy no-op. Picking 1A means also amending
     those three numbers.
  1B run-length/coalesced. 1B-i (explicit [start_row,end_row) span) is never worse than 1A and
     typically ~0 B/entry, preserving the stable-identity sort law and degrading gracefully under
     interleaving. RECOMMENDED.
  1C one interval per block -> 0 B/entry but forces a block split whenever any edge retires, which
     conflicts with landed compaction behaviour (compaction_preserves_parallel_edge_identities). A
     genuine trade; its block-churn cost is UNMEASURED.
Whatever wins, keep the half-open [created,retired) window and zero-encodes-live, or the landed
retirement_is_half_open law changes meaning.

OTHER FIELDS (full reasoning in the artifact):
  descriptor_key   -> 4C (src, relation, DIRECTION). 4A (src,relation) is the obvious answer and
                      looks INCOMPLETE: the same paragraph names reverse-family destination-grouped
                      blocks, so without a direction discriminant forward and reverse blocks for one
                      descriptor collide on identity. ChartreuseSalmon is BLOCKED ON THIS NOW.
  property_patch_refs -> 3B (block-level ref set + per-entry prop_row_ref indexing into it). Only
                      reading under which §6.2 listing prop_row_ref as a separate per-entry member
                      is not redundant. Consumes most of the 3 B headroom.
  stripe_range     -> 2A+2C (explicit half-open [dst_lo,dst_hi) pair, Option for non-hubs). This one
                      HAS a second semantic site: L536 "Giant hubs stripe the neighbor-ID space into
                      independently locked/versioned candidate ranges, and WITNESS GRANULARITY
                      FOLLOWS THE DURABLE STRIPE IDENTITY." So the axis is CORRECTNESS (SSI witness
                      granularity), not bytes -- w4-ssi-witnesses wants to be in the room. Rejecting
                      2B (index into descriptor_map_ref) because it makes a block uninterpretable
                      without its partition root, for ~0.1 B/entry.

SURFACED BY THE DERIVATION: DeltaPartitionRoot descriptor_map_ref and canonical_partition_digest are
the same once-only class (overflow_state IS spelled inline and is fine). Measured against
crates/fgdb-strata/src/root.rs: implemented root is {graph,branch,partition,published_at,blocks}, so
THREE of six normative fields are absent and two implemented fields are not normative at all. ge6a
cannot register the object either way. Recommend they ride this sitting.

SITTING ORDER: (1) visibility_intervals -- rule first, everything spends its headroom; (3)
property_patch_refs -- competes for the same 3 B; (4) descriptor_key -- ChartreuseSalmon blocked now;
(2) stripe_range -- wants the SSI consumer; (5) the DeltaPartitionRoot residues -- unblocks ge6a.

OPEN / NOT YET MEASURED: ChartreuseSalmon is producing candidate-visibility-layout measurements
(interval cardinality, reference width, actual 4 KiB fit) that land directly on field 1 and should be
folded in before the sitting. The 1C block-churn cost is unmeasured and needs a workload run to
quantify honestly. Those two are the only gaps between this pack and a decision.

title: Engine WriteBatch CompareAndSet on edges is witnessed
description:
Witness `WriteBatch::compare_and_set_edge_property`. The vertex CAS path is tested; the edge method exists in production and has no caller.

## Background

The spine, independent differential, and generated mixer all drive `compare_and_set_vertex_property`. `compare_and_set_edge_property` is a live method on the same type and shares the `PendingRow::CompareAndSet` arm, but nothing calls it. A broken edge-CAS match, AbortWrite miss, or NoOp miss stays green.

This is a related subset of the write-path line. It does **not** close `819`, `94z`, `og6n`, or `iyc`. Do not parent-child this to those open umbrellas.

- Spine unit: edge CAS match writes; AbortWrite miss refuses; NoOp miss leaves the edge and a sibling write intact.
- Independent differential: same three outcomes against `fgdb-reference` `CompareAndSet` on `ElementId::Edge`.
- Generated mixer: a lawful edge-CAS arm (match with AbortWrite, or explicit NoOp-miss). Do not propose AbortWrite mismatch.

## Success Criteria

- Match, AbortWrite miss, and NoOp miss are each asserted (not only match).
- Generated mixer can emit an edge CAS; a write refusal remains a generator defect.
- `cargo test -p fgdb --test spine -- cas` and `cargo test -p fgdb-sim --test spine_differential` exit 0.
- `819` stays open.

## Test Plan
- Spine: seed an edge with PropertyKeyId(11), CAS match, AbortWrite miss, NoOp miss + sibling.
- Differential: engine vs independent reference Intents on the same three outcomes.
- Generated histories stay green with the extra arm.

title: The landing lease guards commits, but check.sh's domain fingerprint is over WORKTREE content — an uncommitted edit voids another pane's run just as surely
notes:
FOUND 2026-08-01 BY COMMITTING THE OFFENCE, not by reading code. I read the lease refusal, believed
its advice, kept working in the main worktree, and voided a 21-minute run belonging to another pane.
Filed against myself.

THE TWO MECHANISMS DISAGREE ABOUT WHAT "MOVING THE TREE" MEANS.

The landing lease is a PRE-COMMIT guard. Its refusal message is explicit about scope, and it is the
message that misled me:

    YOU ARE NOT BLOCKED FROM WORKING. This holds LANDINGS, not panes. Edit, build,
    test, run gates, git add, and commit in your own scratch worktree -- all
    unaffected. Only a commit on main is refused [...]

Read naturally, "Edit, build, test [...] all unaffected" says editing in the main worktree is safe
and only the commit matters.

check.sh disagrees, because its domain fingerprint is taken over WORKING-TREE CONTENT:

    scripts/lib/gate_verdict.sh:178
      git ls-files -z 2>/dev/null | xargs -0 sha256sum

`sha256sum` reads the file on disk, not the index and not HEAD. So a tracked file edited and left
UNCOMMITTED changes the fingerprint exactly as much as one that is committed. When the run ends,
gate_scope_void_result reclassifies every verdict whose domain moved:

    UNRUN core: cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast -- tracked input domain
                all-tracked moved during check.sh

`all-tracked` covers nearly everything, and `tracked-rust` / `rust-format` cover every .rs file, so
editing ONE .rs file in the main worktree voids the cargo steps, the UBS step, and every registered
binary and cargo-test verdict of an in-flight run. ~35 minutes and a build slot, lost, with no signal
to the editor that anything happened.

WHY THE GUARD CANNOT SIMPLY BE EXTENDED. A pre-commit hook fires on an event; editing has no event to
hook. So this is not "add a check to the lease" -- the lease is the wrong instrument for the hazard,
and pretending otherwise would produce a guard that still fails open.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY HELP, roughly in order of cost:

 1. FIX THE MESSAGE FIRST -- it is the cheapest and it is currently ACTIVELY WRONG. It should say
    that any edit to a tracked file in the main worktree voids the in-flight run, and that the
    scratch-worktree advice is the remedy rather than a footnote. I followed the message and it cost
    someone a run; the next agent will do the same.
 2. HAVE check.sh RUN AGAINST A QUIET COPY. The corpus-copy machinery already exists (gate work-dirs,
    and the `git ls-files | tar` quiet-root idiom is used elsewhere in this repo). A run whose subject
    is a snapshot cannot be moved by anyone, which converts this from a coordination problem into a
    non-problem and also removes the need for panes to serialise at all.
 3. FAIL FASTER. Detecting the move only at the END is what makes it expensive. A mid-run re-check
    (say between phases) could abort in 2 minutes instead of 35.

DO NOT "FIX" THIS BY WEAKENING THE DETECTION. The UNRUN reclassification is correct and it is one of
the better things in this gate: a verdict over a tree that changed mid-run describes no single tree,
and reporting it as PASS would be a lie. The defect is that the hazard is easy to trigger and the
guidance points the wrong way -- not that the gate notices.

MEASURED CONTEXT, so nobody has to re-derive the blast radius: the domain vocabulary is
all-tracked / tracked-rust / tracked-shell / rust-format (scripts/lib/gate_verdict.sh:250-263), and
scripts/check.sh plus scripts/lib/gate_verdict.sh are inputs to EVERY narrowed verdict by explicit
rule, so editing either one voids everything regardless of domain.

title: check.sh's run-level tree-stability void discards REAL reds; scope it by the moved path's domain now that g996 landed the naming
notes:
OPTION (v) for fgdb-09iz, filed 2026-07-27 by pane4 at HEAD 1a6fdc2 while
re-deriving that bead. It is NOT fgdb-09iz's rejected option (iii): that one
SUPPRESSES the tripwire; this one ATTRIBUTES it.

THE OBSERVATION IS ALREADY IN fgdb-09iz, WHICH DOES NOT DRAW IT. On the 19:36 run:
  * `w1_cross_crate_determinism_e2e` went RED, and its own log shows that red IS
    "tree changed under the run" — an ARTIFACT of the mid-run .beads write.
  * In the SAME run, "RED core: UBS over every tracked Rust source" fired. Its
    domain is the tracked Rust set, and the only path that moved was
    .beads/issues.jsonl, which is not in it — so that red is REAL.
  * "Today the whole verdict is void, so both are discarded and the 35 minutes are
    spent again. The cost is not delay; it is a real UBS baseline drift that a
    re-run buries."
That is an argument for scoping the void, and the bead stops one sentence short.

WHY IT IS BUILDABLE NOW AND WAS NOT WHEN 09iz WAS FILED. fgdb-09iz is blocked on
fgdb-g996 "for the naming: without the path in the UNRUN you cannot tell an
artifact red from a real one". g996 is CLOSED. Its fix landed at 5e2d682 and
`gate_check_tree_stable` now calls `gate_tree_diff "$GATE_TREE_LIST_START"
"$list_end"` under a "WHAT MOVED:" heading. The missing input EXISTS.

THE STRUCTURE, measured at HEAD:
  * The tripwire is ALREADY per-gate: `gate_check_tree_stable` compares that
    gate's own start/end fingerprint and names $GATE_NAME.
  * check.sh ALSO calls `gate_init "check.sh"` at line ~1509, giving the whole run
    ONE ~35-minute window. That run-level window is the one that essentially
    always fires: 0 of 229 sampled 35-min windows in the retained .br_history are
    write-free, and 0 of 244 20-minute ones.
  * Gate domains are already explicit and derived from git, not from a directory:
    `run_ubs` uses `gate_tracked_sources '*.rs'` = 119 tracked .rs at HEAD, and
    refuses to fall back (the hdyv defect). The fingerprint, by contrast, hashes
    ALL 199 tracked files by design, so that it catches deletions and staged edits.
  So the two facts needed to attribute a void — WHAT MOVED and WHAT EACH GATE
  READS — are both already computed. They are simply never compared.

THE PROPOSAL. When the run-level window fires, intersect the moved-path set with
each gate's declared domain. A gate whose domain contains a moved path is UNRUN,
as today. A gate whose domain contains none of them keeps its verdict. The
run-level verdict reports both sets explicitly.

WHAT MUST NOT BE LOST — the third-state doctrine (AGENTS.md):
  * FAIL CLOSED ON AN UNDECLARED DOMAIN. A gate that does not declare what it
    reads must be treated as reading EVERYTHING and stay UNRUN. Anything else
    converts an honest UNRUN into a false PASS, which is precisely why option
    (iii) was rejected — see g0_identity_e2e, which reads .beads at run time and
    reports "ok. 1 passed" when the corpus is absent.
  * THE TOKEN VOCABULARY IS CLOSED: PASS, FAIL, RED, UNRUN. A scoped void must
    express itself inside it, and every FAIL still needs its anchored line, or the
    verdict-contract closure gate (fgdb-udco) turns this gate red itself.
  * A gate's DOMAIN IS ITS OWN CLAIM and needs the same treatment as any other
    declared closure: an under-declared domain silently rescues a red that should
    have been voided. Whatever declares it needs a completeness guard, or it fails
    open.

CONTROL THE FIX. Run check.sh; move ONLY .beads/issues.jsonl mid-run; confirm the
Rust-domain gates keep their verdicts and the .beads-reading gates go UNRUN. Then
move a tracked .rs mid-run and confirm the Rust gates DO go UNRUN. A scoping rule
that never voids anything is the false-PASS failure wearing a new name.

description: The last normative DeltaBlockVersion field short of the deferred stripe_range: predecessor: ConditionalCoordinateRef<DeltaBlockVersion>? — the per-block MVCC chain (§6.2). UNLIKE V5's fields this changes the ROOT MODEL: today a root lists every block and readers merge the whole publication list; with predecessor chains a published block head reaches an immutable predecessor chain and readers walk until the first version satisfying all visibility predicates, with newer sibling-branch versions SKIPPED not terminal. Design carefully against: FG-INV-03 (finite acyclic newer-first chains, links within one owning generation), the current tombstone-supersede whole-list merge (the two precedence models must not coexist ambiguously), compaction (chain-aware), ge6a manifest fast-open (the consumer that wants this), and edge property UPDATES (which need a version discriminator this chain provides). Recommend a design pass against §6.2 + frankensqlite's page-chain donor before code; the seam that made da6b cheap (format-first, laws both directions) applies but the merge-model decision must come first.
close_reason: Per-block predecessor chains are durable and law-enforced at every admission seam; publication order IS the chain (FG-INV-03 by construction). Read-side chain walk remains ge6a's increment (f7de164).

comments.text: DESIGN ANALYSIS (OrangeDeer, 2026-08-08, from plan L534-537 re-read). The target model is DeltaPartitionRoot{...sorted_block_head_refs[]...}: the root names one HEAD per descriptor family and each head reaches an immutable predecessor chain; readers walk newest-first until the first version satisfying ALL visibility predicates (newer sibling-branch versions SKIPPED not terminal). The current FGSR lists EVERY block in publication order and merges whole-list under tombstone-supersede — a DIFFERENT precedence model. Three options: (A) full jump — FGSR V3 heads-only roots + chain-walk reads + chain-aware compaction in one increment: correct end state, huge blast radius, and the branch-ancestry predicate has no consumer yet (single-branch spine). (B) format-only reservation — predecessor framed+validated but always-None, 2t7q-style fail-closed: cheap but the field is inert (counterfeit-parameter hazard; 2t7q's reservation precedent was blessed only with a validated refusal arm, which always-None does not exercise). (C) RECOMMENDED — load-bearing chain at SEAL, list reads unchanged: writer links each sealed block's predecessor to the prior head of the SAME descriptor family; admission validates FG-INV-03 (finite, acyclic, strictly newer-first, links within one root's closure) as a REAL law with mutation controls; reads stay whole-list (answers provably identical — the chain is publication order restricted to one descriptor); compaction rebuilds chains per repacked family. ge6a then flips reads to chain-walk as ITS increment, with the chain already durable and law-covered. Note V5 interaction: predecessor joins the header AFTER the digest? NO — chain link is physical lineage, NOT logical content; keep it OUT of the canonical_logical_digest transcript (two re-encodings of one logical state under different chain histories must digest identically, same argument as partition exclusion... actually partition IS excluded from digest too — digest covers statements only, pinned by the_partition_id_is_durable_and_distinct). Suggested layout: optional 32B predecessor id + 1 presence byte after the digest, header 81->114, breaking-major V6. Open question for the implementer: does a descriptor family's FIRST block in a compacted repack point at nothing (chain restart, root carries the generation) or at the retired pre-compaction head (history chain vs state chain)? Plan L536 'publication never stamps or mutates an old object' + generational roots suggests chain restart per generation with the OLD root still reachable — recommend chain-restart, state-chain semantics.

title: check.sh has no isolation from concurrent landings: a mid-run commit turns four identity pins red on a green tree
notes:
STATUS: fix LANDED at 38cca3f. All three red-proofs DONE (results below). NOT yet closed; two follow-ups outstanding. Written for a successor who knows the standing laws and nothing about this bead.

=== WHAT WAS WRONG ===
scripts/check.sh runs ~35 min while other panes land commits, and it had no isolation from that. A commit landing mid-run turned four identity pins red on a tree where every pin was correct. Cost: a full diagnostic cycle for pane2, a 40-min landing hold for pane4, two false attributions to the orchestrator.

=== THE DIAGNOSIS: TWO CLOCKS (the part you cannot re-derive cheaply) ===
This is NOT really about check.sh being slow. The checker reads its own subject at two different times:
  * COMPILE time -- tools/registry-check/src/*.rs pulls source in with include_str!, so the pinned constants are frozen into the test binary when cargo builds it.
  * RUN time -- tools/registry-check/tests/identity.rs reads the corpus with std::fs::read_to_string(repo_root().join(...)) when the test executes.
A commit landing between those two moments desynchronises them: the pin is from tree T0, the data is from tree T1. The pin then "drifts" against a corpus it was never computed from, and the failure names whichever file happens to be resident. Nothing is actually wrong with the pins or the code they blame.

Corollary that matters: THE BUILD TOKENS CANNOT FIX THIS. They serialise BUILDS. The event that voids a run is a `git commit` from a pane that holds no build slot at all. Do not reach for a token here and think it is handled.

=== THE FIX (38cca3f), in scripts/lib/gate_verdict.sh ===
Chose the THIRD STATE over making the red go away. A gate whose subject changed underneath it DID NOT RUN in the sense the udco contract already names: its assertions executed, but not against any single tree, so neither passes nor failures are claims about anything. PASS would certify a tree never wholly tested. FAIL would blame whichever pane's code was resident when the assertion fired -- the false attributions. So: UNRUN, carrying both shas, non-zero either way. Lives in the shared library, so all 11 gates that source the contract inherit it from one definition.

New: gate_tree_fingerprint(), gate_tree_head(), gate_check_tree_stable(). gate_init captures the fingerprint; gate_verdict and the EXIT trap compare it.

=== FINGERPRINT DESIGN, and why each choice ===
fingerprint = sha256( `git rev-parse HEAD` + `git ls-files -z | xargs -0 sha256sum` , stderr folded in ).
  * HEAD catches the landing.
  * Tracked-file CONTENT catches what HEAD misses: a staged edit, an uncommitted worktree change, a file deleted mid-run.
  * stderr is folded into the digest deliberately -- if a tracked file vanishes mid-run, sha256sum's error IS the evidence the tree moved, and a digest that ignored it would report a void run as clean.
  * Outside a git worktree both calls return the same sentinel, so the comparison is a no-op. Correct: a tree nothing can commit to cannot be raced.

UNTRACKED PATHS ARE EXCLUDED, AND THIS IS LOAD-BEARING. The gates create their own scratch dirs, logs and quiet roots while they run. If untracked state were hashed, every gate would fingerprint its own work and report UNRUN on every run -- a guard disabled by its own trigger, the exact shape we hunt. Verified BEFORE choosing this: check.sh writes only inside its temp work roots and never mutates a tracked file, so a tracked-content fingerprint cannot self-trigger. If you ever widen this to untracked paths, you will brick every gate.

A HEAD-ONLY COMPARISON IS INSUFFICIENT -- measured, not argued. Proof case D below edits a tracked file without committing: HEAD is identical at both ends, so a HEAD-only check reports PASS on a run whose subject moved. The diagnostic distinguishes the two, saying "working-tree or index edit, not a landing" when HEAD held still.

COST, measured on this repo: 195 tracked files / 24.7 MB, 101 ms per call, twice per gate = 0.005% of a 35-min run. The alternative (run each gate against a detached snapshot so commits cannot reach it) copies in 47 ms but forces a COLD REBUILD in the snapshot path, costing far more than the whole tripwire, and still cannot say WHY a run was void. Cost did not decide this; the third state did.

=== THE THREE PROOFS: DONE, ALL GREEN ===
Harness kept at /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane3_49ng_proof.sh, clone at /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane3_49ng. Gate used: scripts/g0_negative_evidence_e2e.sh (a g0 script -- builds with standalone rustc, costs NO build slot).
  A  static tree, gate green            -> PASS  rc=0   (9 passed / 0 failed / 0 unrun)
  C  real commit lands mid-run          -> UNRUN rc=1   both shas present and different: 38cca3f02e81 -> f06d07acdf5b
  B  static tree, genuinely red         -> FAIL  rc=1   3 law-1 FAILs, 0 unrun -- the third state did NOT swallow a real failure
Case B was made red by CONTENT only (perl edit so the AGENTS.md lines naming plannerV2.rs / strata_improved.rs / exec_enhanced.rs stop saying NEVER, tripping law 1's prohibition-classification guard), committed BEFORE the run so the tree was static throughout. Nothing was deleted.
Additionally mutation-proven: neuter gate_check_tree_stable and cases C and D report PASS rc=0 -- a green verdict over a moving tree. Cases A and B unchanged, so the mutation is surgical and the tripwire is what produces the UNRUNs.
  D  uncommitted tracked edit mid-run   -> UNRUN rc=1   (synthetic harness; this is the case that kills a HEAD-only design)

=== THE TRAP, if you re-run or extend the proofs ===
Proving this REQUIRES a commit to land during a gate run. Doing that in /data/projects/frankengraphdb voids whatever real run is in flight and costs the swarm ~35 minutes -- the exact harm this bead is about. ALWAYS use an isolated clone under /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane3_49ng (git clone --local, read-only on the live repo). Check `pgrep -af check.sh` first regardless.
Second trap, found the hard way: in gate_on_exit you must use `exit`, NOT `rc=1`. By the time an EXIT trap runs the status is already fixed and `return` cannot override it. The first cut used `rc=1` and a real gate raced by a real commit emitted UNRUN on stdout while exiting 0 -- saying "did not run" and "success" in the same breath, the very contradiction this bead removes. A synthetic probe CANNOT catch this if it moves the tree before gate_verdict; only a real-gate run that moves the tree after gate_verdict reaches that window.

=== HONEST LIMIT OF THIS FIX ===
The tripwire makes the loss LEGIBLE, not FREE. It converts a 35-min false-red into a 35-min honest UNRUN. It diagnoses; it does not prevent. Preventing it needs either a `landing` token in /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/token.sh (check.sh holds it for its duration; any pane acquires it before `git commit`) -- cheap, uses the existing substrate, and actually saves the 35 minutes -- or running check.sh against a detached snapshot. The landing token is the recommendation. Demonstrated live: commit 38cca3f itself landed ~11 minutes into pane2's check.sh and voided it. The fix caught its own author.

=== STILL OUTSTANDING ===
 1. Close this bead (naming 38cca3f and the three proofs).
 2. NO DURABLE REGRESSION TEST. The proofs live in /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/, not in the repo. Landing them as a registered gate needs a new .sh ENUMERATED in registries/checker_index.toml -- a glob will not claim it, only enumeration fires -- and registries/** is under the CATALOG token. Until that lands, this fix is protected only by a transcript.
 3. File the `landing` token follow-up described above.

=== FLAGGED, NAMED NOT TOUCHED ===
/data/projects/frankengraphdb/rc/ -- untracked, created 2026-07-27 17:02-17:03, ~67 MB of standalone-rustc output dropped at the repo root instead of a temp dir: rc/registry-check (8.2 MB), rc/identity_test (12 MB), rc/lib_test (14 MB), rc/libregistry_check.rlib (33 MB). Not mine. NOT deleted -- deletion authority is the orchestrator's. Note it is UNTRACKED, so the fingerprint above deliberately ignores it; that exclusion is exactly what stops the guard firing on gate artifacts.
=== CLOSED 2026-07-27 by pane3. Re-proof at a later HEAD + durable gate landed. ===

Everything above stands and was re-verified, not taken on trust. The three proofs
above were taken at 38cca3f; HEAD had since moved, so they were RE-RUN at HEAD
72aec3f in a fresh isolated clone (/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane3_49ng_r2, harness
/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane3_49ng_r2_proof.sh, output preserved separately at
pane3_49ng_r2_out so the original transcript was not overwritten).

RE-PROOF RESULTS — verdict token and exit code as OBSERVED, not summarised.
The token is the one contract line that appeared at column 0 of the gate's
stdout; rc is the gate's exit status, which is the actual verdict.

  A  static tree, gate green
       token = PASS    rc = 0     tally: 9 PASS / 0 FAIL / 0 UNRUN
  C  real commit lands mid-run
       token = UNRUN   rc = 1     tally: 9 PASS / 0 FAIL / 1 UNRUN
       stderr diagnostic carried BOTH shas and they differ:
         HEAD at start: 72aec3fbd6f408572cb0f674c2e4397c7e2c1be6
         HEAD at end:   0bd4fb76404d93b95ae58840b2fab005564e9b8c
  B  static tree, gate genuinely red
       token = FAIL    rc = 1     tally: 9 PASS / 3 FAIL / 0 UNRUN
       ZERO UNRUN lines: the third state did NOT swallow the real failure.
       The 3 FAILs are law 1 prohibition-classification, one each for
       plannerV2.rs / strata_improved.rs / exec_enhanced.rs.

CASE C IS THE SHARPEST ARTIFACT IN THIS BEAD. All nine of its own assertions
emitted PASS, and the gate still exited 1 under UNRUN. Nine passes that are not
claims about any single tree. That is the whole thesis in one transcript, and it
is why PASS would have been the wrong answer: the assertions did pass, and it
did not matter.

=== OUTSTANDING ITEM 2 IS NOW CLOSED: THE PROOF IS DURABLE ===
Landed ce0d0ca: scripts/g0_tree_stability_e2e.sh, ENUMERATED in
registries/checker_index.toml. Tracked as fgdb-mt2b (closed with this).

It is NOT the /data/tmp harness moved into the repo. That harness clones the
whole repo (61 MB per run, ~25 MB new blocks) and races a `sleep 0.35`, so it
would both litter like rc/ and flake. The landed gate builds a synthetic few-KB
git repo whose subject gate sources the REAL scripts/lib/gate_verdict.sh and
moves its own tree at a point it CHOOSES. No build slot, no race, and it never
commits in the live worktree. Six directions, observed:

  A_still_green            token=PASS   rc=0
  B_still_red              token=FAIL   rc=1   and zero UNRUN
  C_landing_midrun         token=UNRUN  rc=1   two differing shas
  D_worktree_edit          token=UNRUN  rc=1   HEAD EQUAL both ends
  E_trap_window_no_verdict token=UNRUN  rc=1   via the EXIT trap
  F_mutation_control       token=PASS   rc=0   (tripwire neutered => UNRUN stops)
  gate total: 11 passed, 0 failed, 0 unrun, rc=0

A CORRECTION TO THE HANDOFF NOTE ABOVE, measured. The note says the exit-vs-rc
window is reached by "a real-gate run that moves the tree AFTER gate_verdict".
It is not. gate_verdict sets GATE_TREE_CHECKED=1, so gate_check_tree_stable is
ONE-SHOT and the EXIT trap's later call returns immediately. A move strictly
after gate_verdict is therefore NOT detected -- verified by building exactly
that case first and watching it report token=PASS rc=0. That is CORRECT
behaviour, not a gap: the verdict is a true claim about the tree that was stable
from gate_init through gate_verdict, and a commit landing after the run ended
does not falsify it. The trap's branch is live only for a gate that exits
WITHOUT reaching gate_verdict (gate_die, an unguarded `set -e` abort, an explicit
early exit) -- the fail-fast path, which is exactly where a moving tree would
otherwise be blamed on whichever code was resident. Case E is built that way.

THE GATE IS LOAD-BEARING IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, mutation-proven on a path-correct
mirror (/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane3_49ng_mirror) rather than on the live library,
so no other pane ever saw a neutered contract:
  pristine library                     -> 11 passed,  0 failed,  rc=0
  gate_check_tree_stable neutered      ->  4 passed,  7 failed,  rc=1
  trap `exit 1` regressed to `rc=1`    ->  9 passed,  2 failed,  rc=1
The last one reproduces the ORIGINAL defect verbatim in the subject:
token=UNRUN, rc=0 -- "did not run" and "success" in the same breath -- and
case E is the ONLY case that catches it. Without E the regression would be
invisible to this gate.

REGISTRATION PROVEN BOTH WAYS on a quiet root, because a closure check that
passes proves nothing until it can fail:
  registered      -> registry-check validate rc=0, zero script_undeclared
  registration removed -> rc=1, violation[script_undeclared] naming
                          scripts/g0_tree_stability_e2e.sh exactly
This confirms the standing law: only the ENUMERATION-based check fires. The
glob-based mechanisms answer "covered" and can never fail.

CONFORMANCE: check.sh's own verdict-contract readers report 11 of 11 gates
conformant, with a positive control (a deliberately non-conformant gate) firing
both L2 and L3/L4 so the reader is known to be able to fail. NOTE FOR THE NEXT
READER: those readers pipe grep into sed, and the first run of that control was
done by sourcing check.sh's bash functions into zsh, where `sed` did not resolve
inside the pipelines -- so every violation was silently swallowed and the result
read "0 nonconformant". A broken reader producing a green, in the middle of a
bead about exactly that. Drive check.sh's functions with bash, and never accept
a conformance zero without a control that fires.

=== WHAT REMAINS, and it is NOT this bead ===
fgdb-eesn -- the PREVENTION half (a `landing` token). This bead only ever
promised to make the loss LEGIBLE, and it does: a mid-run landing now costs an
honest UNRUN instead of a false red plus a diagnostic cycle. It does not save
the 35 minutes. fgdb-eesn is where that is bought.

=== NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY ===
scripts/check.sh was NOT run end-to-end for this change (~35 min + a build slot).
The change is one new .sh plus one TOML row, and every gate that bears on it was
run directly and is recorded above: bash -n, shellcheck --severity=warning,
registry-check validate (rc=0), the script-closure control in both directions,
the verdict-contract readers with a positive control, and the gate itself with
two mutations. A full check.sh run would additionally execute the new gate inside
the chain; that is worth doing on the next scheduled run rather than starting a
35-minute run whose own subject is the tree every other pane is committing to.

=== FLAGGED, STILL NOT TOUCHED ===
/data/projects/frankengraphdb/rc/ -- ~67 MB of standalone-rustc output at the
repo root, untracked, not this pane's. Owner has since identified it as
accumulated g0 e2e output (those scripts compile with rustc and never clean up,
~70 MB per run) and ruled it swarm litter rather than anyone's work product.
Deletion authority is the owner's; it was left exactly where it is. It is
UNTRACKED, so the fingerprint deliberately ignores it -- that exclusion is what
stops the tripwire firing on gate artifacts.
close_reason: Fix landed 38cca3f (tree-stability tripwire in scripts/lib/gate_verdict.sh); durable gate landed ce0d0ca. Three proofs re-run at HEAD 72aec3f in an isolated clone, observed tokens and exit codes: A static+green token=PASS rc=0; C commit lands mid-run token=UNRUN rc=1 with both shas present and differing (72aec3fbd6f4 -> 0bd4fb76404d); B static+genuinely-red token=FAIL rc=1 with zero UNRUN, so the third state did not swallow a real failure. C is the sharpest: all nine of its own assertions emitted PASS and it still exited 1 under UNRUN. Prevention half is fgdb-eesn; it is not this bead.

title: WriteBatch must stamp BirthOrdinal from visit order, not durable-create cardinality
description: spa1 ruled graph-cardinality BirthOrdinal illegal: the same request must emit the same ordinals regardless of unrelated population, and a folded-away or no-op visit must not renumber what follows by restamping survivors. WriteBatch still stamps from snapshot.next_birth_ordinal (count of durable creates) and vaz4 restamps the folded net densely from that count — both are the cardinality derivation. Count every PendingRow visit (including ensure/CAS/delete no-ops) like evaluate(), stamp creates with that 1-based ordinal, and do not restamp after fold.
close_reason: WriteBatch now stamps Create birth_ordinals from the 1-based visit index over every PendingRow, including ensure/CAS/delete no-ops. Fold does not restamp. Same request against empty vs populated graphs keeps ordinal 1; a folded-away earlier create leaves the survivor at visit 2; a no-op ensure keeps slot 1 so the following create is 2.

title: The unsafe ledger's Miri-specific exclusions are being read as ASAN/TSAN exclusions, which those reasons do not justify — then build the three lanes
description:
Successor to fgdb-czlt, closed on re-derivation. czlt's counts and feasibility
HELD; its exclusion classification did not, and that must be fixed BEFORE any
lane manifest exists, or the manifest encodes the error as the contract.

## THE DEFECT — measured at HEAD 9e55c5e, per site, by reading all six rows

czlt states: "excluded BY CONSTRUCTION and must stay excluded — fgdb-unsafe-simd
(2 sites): x86 intrinsics are outside Miri's supported set; fgdb-unsafe-vfs
(3 sites): Miri does not execute inline asm."

BOTH REASONS ARE MIRI-SPECIFIC AND NEITHER TRANSFERS. ASAN and TSAN are compiled
instrumentation running native code: they handle x86 intrinsics and inline asm
without difficulty. So five sites are described as excluded by construction from
three tools on the strength of a reason that excludes them from exactly one.
Encoding that into a per-tool lane manifest would ship a FALSE exclusion, and the
bidirectional 1:1 check would then certify it — a checker agreeing with a wrong
input is the failure mode this project keeps closing.

## WHAT THE LEDGER ACTUALLY SAYS TODAY (all six no_claim_boundary texts read)

  simd-control-group-sse2   "NOT Miri-checked — the x86 intrinsics are outside
                             the lane's supported set ... the Miri/ASAN/TSAN
                             lanes remain open work on fgdb-w1-unsafe-islands-eqrq"
  arena-region-blocks-mut   "NOT Miri-checked yet ... unlike the SIMD island this
                             crate uses no intrinsics, so it is a candidate for
                             that lane rather than excluded from it"
  simd-control-prefetch     "NOT Miri-checked."            <- no ASAN/TSAN word
  vfs-mmap-readonly         "NOT Miri-checked — Miri does not execute inline asm" <- ditto
  vfs-mapping-view-bytes    "NOT Miri-checked — ... inline asm, which Miri does
                             not execute"                   <- ditto
  vfs-mapping-munmap        "NOT Miri-checked, for the same reason as its sibling
                             rows"                          <- ditto

So: 4 of 6 sites are SILENT on ASAN and TSAN — 8 of the 18 site x tool cells
leave the absence to be inferred. AND the 2 that do name all three do NOT state
an ASAN/TSAN boundary either; they DEFER all three to fgdb-w1-unsafe-islands-eqrq.
czlt's claim that "every row says so in its no_claim_boundary rather than leaving
the absence to be inferred" is therefore false in both directions: 4 rows say
nothing, and the other 2 point elsewhere instead of stating a boundary.

## THE CORRECTED SEQUENCE (czlt had 0 and 1 in the wrong order)

0. STATE THE BOUNDARY PER TOOL, PER SITE — 18 cells, none inferred. For the five
   asm/intrinsic sites the honest text is NOT "excluded by construction" but "no
   ASAN/TSAN lane is claimed today; the Miri exclusion does not extend to them."
   That is a different sentence with a different consequence: it makes them
   CANDIDATES, which is a larger eventual scope than czlt assumed.
1. THEN the per-tool lane manifest and the bidirectional 1:1 checker. Writing the
   manifest first means writing it to match the ledger's current silence.
2. THEN install miri and amend rust-toolchain.toml, and run the arena site green
   under Miri with edit_path_differential as its workload.

## WHAT czlt PROVED AND NEED NOT BE REDONE

 * 6 [[site]] + 3 [[island]] tables; split simd 2 / arena 1 / vfs 3 — exact.
 * MIRI IS PUBLISHED for the pinned nightly-2026-07-05, together with rust-src
   and llvm-tools. Miri is not shipped for every nightly, so this was a real
   dead-on-arrival risk and it is RETIRED. It is only uninstalled;
   rust-toolchain.toml declares components = ["rustfmt","clippy"], so enabling it
   amends the pin, which that file says to do deliberately.
 * arena-region-blocks-mut is genuinely the right first Miri candidate: its whole
   unsafe surface is one ledgered block, no asm!, no core::arch.

## UNVERIFIED, carried forward rather than dropped

czlt's "192 batches" figure. edit_path_differential.rs drives THREE fixed seeds
(1, 0x1234_5678_9abc_def0, 0xdead_beef_cafe_f00d) and contains no literal 192.
Confirm by running the harness (needs a build slot) before quoting it.

## CONTROL THE FIX (it must be able to fail)

After step 0, the 1:1 checker must FAIL when a cell is removed from either side —
prove it by deleting one ASAN cell from the manifest and one from a row, in two
separate runs, and confirm each direction reddens independently. A bidirectional
check proven in only one direction is a one-directional check.
close_reason: Acceptance contract implemented and pinned full gate green.

title: registry_epoch bump doctrine is unenforced and discharged 2 of 11 times; the reminder or the tree is wrong
description:
`refreeze_identity_pins.sh` closes every pin cycle with this reminder:

    REMINDER: an added/retired row also owes a registry_epoch bump in BOTH the catalog
    [[projection_epoch]] row and the expected_epoch const (identity.rs doctrine; precedent e7b6f09).
    Nothing detects a missing bump, so it is on you.

It states a doctrine, admits nothing enforces it, and hands the obligation to the operator. Measured
over the last 16 commits touching registries/durable_fields.toml, the obligation is discharged 2
times out of 11.

## The measurement

For each commit touching the file, comparing it to its parent — the projection's `[registry]
registry_epoch` value against its `[[field]]` row count:

    3cce2b2  epoch 77->77  rows 975->981   feat(a20): 6 exact-StrongRef field rows   <== rows moved, epoch did not
    d4b0aa2  epoch 77->77  rows 976->975   fix(census): slash tokens                 <== rows moved, epoch did not
    3c1c936  epoch 77->77  rows 964->976   feat(a10): ConfigurationTransitionSpec    <== rows moved, epoch did not
    2aa796a  epoch 77->77  rows 953->964   feat(a08): 11 W12 lifecycle rows          <== rows moved, epoch did not
    955c1ef  epoch 76->77  rows 943->953   chore(beads): a14 re-derived              (both moved)
    c8438a2  epoch 76->76  rows 936->943   feat(k3sa): record the 7 collections      <== rows moved, epoch did not
    65a21da  epoch 76->76  rows 923->936   fix(appendix): cut fourteen self-edges    <== rows moved, epoch did not
    f68ad32  epoch 76->76  rows 881->923   feat(a05): 42-row plain-StrongRef tranche <== rows moved, epoch did not
    6b1b6c9  epoch 76->76  rows 880->881   feat(a20): one checker-accepted field     <== rows moved, epoch did not
    6c379ed  epoch 75->76  rows 800->880   feat(a12): checkpoint/resource field order(both moved)

Row count moved in 11 of the 16; the epoch moved with it in 2. Four commits changed the file without
moving the row count at all (8b38752, 0ee737f, 305af7e, 336688a, 47a8c00, eda507f) and correctly did
not bump.

d4b0aa2 is the sharpest case: it RETIRED a row (976 -> 975). If the doctrine covers retirement — the
reminder says "added/retired" — then a released projection lost a row inside an unchanged epoch.

## Why this is not just sloppiness

The doctrine is unfalsifiable as currently written. `registry_epoch` is a released-format version on
a projection whose row set is append-only-by-pin; nothing in registry-check reads the epoch against
the row count, `appendix-regenerate` does not derive it, and the g0 identity e2e has an assertion
for `neg-registry-epoch` (rejecting a *malformed* epoch) but none binding the epoch to content. So a
missing bump is invisible to all ten gates, and 9 of 11 have gone missing.

Either:
  (a) the doctrine is right and the tree carries 9 missed bumps that should be reconciled once, with
      a checker added so the tenth cannot happen; or
  (b) the doctrine is wrong for additive row landings — the epoch versions the SCHEMA, not the row
      set, and only a breaking change owes a bump — in which case the reminder is the defect and
      should be narrowed to say so, because as written it makes every honest operator either add a
      spurious bump or knowingly skip a stated obligation.

This needs the owner's ruling before anyone acts, which is why it is filed rather than fixed. The
shape is the "doctrine clause keyed to an event nobody measured" class: the rule was written from a
single precedent (e7b6f09) and never checked against the population it governs.

## Do not resolve it by bumping

A pane that reads the reminder and bumps unilaterally makes it worse: the epoch then advances on
some landings and not others with no rule distinguishing them, which is strictly less legible than
the current uniform non-bump. This increment (fgdb-a20-restore-promotion-ivsp, +2 durable_fields
rows) deliberately followed 3cce2b2 and did not bump.
close_reason: Owner ruled reading (b): epoch versions the schema vocabulary; reminder narrowed in the swarm helper (untracked); measurement re-derived at f1573b8 showing unanimous practice both directions

title: Repair the token substrate: liveness not age, a documented or removed release-force, a status that can see staleness, and token.sh under version control
notes:
SUCCESSOR TO fgdb-wzyl, filed by pane2 at HEAD a3a49e5 (2026-07-28) after re-deriving wzyl's
premise per fgdb-rhvi. wzyl's DEFECT HOLDS — this bead is the repair, plus three things the
re-derivation corrected or added.

CARRIED FORWARD FROM wzyl, all re-verified line by line against
/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/token.sh (unmodified since 2026-07-25 03:26, which PREDATES the bead):
  * acquire is `mkdir "$lock"` (line 56); if the directory exists it exits 1 UNCONDITIONALLY,
    regardless of the hold's age. There is no path from the age check to acquiring.
  * No reaper exists anywhere. The only two `rmdir` sites are line 82 (release) and line 102
    (steal), both human-initiated. Nothing is time-based.
  * No queue. acquire is non-blocking, so the lock is won by whoever calls mkdir in the instant
    after a release, and FIFO-by-wait-time is not expressible in the substrate at all.
  * Therefore a TTL is a LABEL, not a timeout, and what actually prevented starvation is the
    release discipline, not the number.

CORRECTION 1 — FALSIFIED SUB-CLAIM, mutation-proven with paired controls. wzyl says "steal is the
only path that clears another holder". IT IS NOT. `release` bypasses its own holder check when the
agent name is the literal string `force`:
    line 79:  if [ "$h" != "$who" ] && [ "$who" != "force" ]; then REFUSED ... fi
Proven on a private probe token (wzylprobe), acquired as pane9-fakeholder, then:
    release wzylprobe pane2-imposter  -> "REFUSED: ... held by pane9-fakeholder"      rc=1
    release wzylprobe force           -> "RELEASED wzylprobe (was pane9-fakeholder)"  rc=0
Both directions fired; the probe token was cleaned up and `status` reports all tokens free.
CONSEQUENCE: there is no 32-minute floor for clearing a stranded lease. `release <tok> force`
needs no age threshold and no steal ceremony. wzyl's headline ("clearing it needs a human steal
after TTL+20m") overstates the cost. The underlying defect — no liveness signal, so a human must
decide — still stands, but the swarm's mental model of what it costs is wrong.
AND `force` IS UNDOCUMENTED: the usage header lists acquire/renew/release/status/steal, and the
`*)` fallback usage line lists the same five. `force` appears only in the code and in the REFUSED
message. So the escape hatch exists, is cheap, and nobody is told about it.

CORRECTION 2 — wzyl UNDERSTATES the defect, in a way worth fixing. It attributes the age check to
what "`status` PRINTS" (citing line 65). That check is in the ACQUIRE branch. The `status` branch
(lines 106-118) has NO age comparison at all — it prints
    "$n: HELD by ${h:-?} for Nm (ttl ${l:-?}m)"
unconditionally, with no EXCEEDS message and no grace logic. So a pane or an orchestrator surveying
the lanes with `status` CANNOT SEE that a lease is stale. The staleness signal is visible only to
someone who tries to acquire and fails. That is worse than filed, and it is the cheapest thing here
to fix.

CORRECTION 3 — EVIDENCE DECAY (fgdb-rhvi axis D). wzyl's "MEASURED TONIGHT, not hypothetical"
citation is /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane3_i1rx_apply3/autoland.sh sitting in a sleep-3 retry loop for
~25 minutes. THAT PATH NO LONGER EXISTS — not the script, not the directory. The observation was
presumably true when made, but its artifact is gone and the claim is no longer verifiable from it.
Same class as the gb9g lesson: a driver survives while its input directory is swept from /data/tmp.

ADDED BY THE RE-DERIVATION — the structural problem under all of the above:
TOKEN.SH IS NOT UNDER VERSION CONTROL. `git ls-files | grep -c token.sh` = 0. It lives only at
/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/token.sh. Consequences: a repair cannot be reviewed, gated, or attributed;
`git log` cannot answer "did this change?" (I had to fall back on mtime); and the file sits in
exactly the directory tree that has already been swept out from under pane3's artifact above. The
whole coordination substrate for the swarm is one unversioned 5.6 KB file in /data/tmp.

THE REPAIR, in the order I would do it, cheapest and safest first:
  1. Move token.sh into the repo and claim it in the file-coverage closure. Everything else becomes
     reviewable once this is done, and it is the only item with no design risk.
  2. Make `status` report staleness — reuse the acquire branch's own age+grace comparison so there
     is ONE reader of that rule, not two. Cheap, and it makes the current failure visible.
  3. Decide `force`: document it in both usage strings, or remove it. Do not leave a cheap
     undocumented override under a ceremony that the docs present as mandatory.
  4. Have the holder write its PID, so "proven dead" is checkable rather than human-judged.
  5. ONLY THEN let expiry ACT, gated on the PID being gone — a LIVENESS answer, never an age one.
     wzyl already names the risk correctly: an age threshold breaks a live-but-slow holder, which
     is exactly what the current design refuses to do. Compare the stale-bead sweep lesson, where
     an age threshold deleted 37 pin-clean staged rows because BLOCKED work is untouched precisely
     for being blocked.
  6. A real queue (ticket file per waiter) only if 1-5 prove insufficient; it is the largest change
     and the polling-loop starvation it targets may be adequately addressed by 4+5.

Evidence in bead comments.

title: Register the existing collections oracle matrix and close the two-seed dispatch-parity gap
notes:
SPLIT OUT OF fgdb-og31 by pane2 at HEAD 59a1d81 (2026-07-28), after re-deriving og31's premise
with the fgdb-rhvi procedure. og31's title says "run the collections_e2e matrix" and its body says
"run the ORIGINAL collections_e2e matrix" — both assert an existing artifact. IT DOES NOT EXIST.

MEASURED. `git grep -l collections_e2e` over the tracked tree returns exactly ONE file:
.beads/issues.jsonl, i.e. og31's own description. CONTROL, because a zero from a search is worth
nothing without one: the same query for a known-present gate, g0_spine_e2e, returns 6 tracked files.
The 14 e2e scripts that exist are 9 g0_* (architecture_decisions, claims, identity,
negative_evidence, proof_lanes, spine, threat, topology, tree_stability) and 5 w1_* (bigint,
codec_pipeline_scalar, codec_scalar, cross_crate_determinism, foundation_types). None is collections.

So this is not a re-run. It is a BUILD, and it is plausibly larger than the integration it was
filed behind. THE FIVE ORACLES, exactly as og31 enumerates them:
  1. ART plus the edit-distance oracle. crates/fgdb-collections/src/art.rs against levenshtein.rs.
  2. Target-vector hash join plus an INDEPENDENT map oracle. hash_table.rs. "Independent" is
     load-bearing — an oracle built from the same code proves nothing.
  3. Succinct rank/select. succinct.rs.
  4. Scalar/target dispatch parity across TWO seeds. AllocationTarget in succinct.rs is the
     dispatch; parity must hold per seed, not in aggregate.
  5. Region cancellation/reclamation logs, i.e. the evidence for og31's
     bytes_reclaimed == bytes_allocated assertion on the CANCELLATION path.

PLUS THE OBLIGATIONS ANY NEW scripts/*_e2e.sh INHERITS, which are not free and are easy to miss:
  * the shared verdict contract in scripts/lib/gate_verdict.sh — stdout is the verdict transcript,
    one anchored `FAIL ` token at column 0, and the three states PASS/FAIL/UNRUN with green only
    for "ran and passed". A gate whose body is skipped whole must emit UNRUN, not fall through.
  * registration in registries/checker_index.toml, which check.sh enumerates AT RUN TIME, so the
    new gate is in scope the moment it is registered and it fails closed.
  * the file-coverage closure — every tracked file must be claimed by a gate or declared exempt
    with a stated reason, and check.sh takes the tracked set from `git ls-files` at run time.
  * a control that FIRES. Per the standing law, a conformance zero without a control that can fail
    is not evidence.

CONSTRAINT INHERITED FROM og31, do not lose it in the split: the named probe-latency and ART
point/range benchmark rows stay CONSUMER benchmark-class claims. An island microbenchmark must not
be presented as proving them, and the arena's ledger row (crates/fgdb-unsafe-arena/src/region.rs)
attaches no benchmark at all — verified, both `benchmark` and `benchmark_ids` are absent.

DEPENDS ON og31: oracles 1-4 exercise the three fgdb-collections modules, and oracle 5 needs the
RegionAlloc integration to exist before there is a cancellation path to log.

title: Apply gpms state-value ruling: one direct precondition row; 21 R1 rows already covered or owner-blocked
notes:
SUCCESSOR TO fgdb-gpms. The RULING is made and enforced (see gpms's note and the identity.rs law
`idr_refinement_claims_resolve_to_a_registered_arm`). This bead is the APPLICATION, and it is not
one job — the 190 candidates partition by whether their referent exists.

RE-DERIVED AT HEAD dbaab71, not inherited. All numbers below reproduce with the two probes in
/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane2_ivsp (dump_all_fields.rs over lines 1388..2728 and the catalog's own 21
[[slice]] rows, which still match /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane4_ivsp/slices.txt byte-for-byte):
11740 field candidates over 1020 owners; the class is 190 over 18 slices with exactly 1 landed
(a01 RemoteRetentionGrantRecord.state), reproducing gpms's per-slice tally digit for digit.

THE CLASSIFIER IS NOT THE PROSE. gpms's text says 'exact type is X::Y, OR a bare CamelCase name that
appears as a source_arm_name and is not itself a registered identity'. Read faithfully — splitting a
multi-type cell on '|' and testing each part — that yields 346 candidates and 15 landed, not 190/1.
The 190 requires matching the WHOLE exact_types cell: 94 contain '::', 96 are whole-cell bare arm
names. Whoever applies this must use the whole-cell rule or the population moves by 82%.

PARTITION BY REFERENT (this is the actual work breakdown):
  R1  22  type is U::V, U is a registered union, V is a registered arm of it   -> AUTHORABLE NOW
  R5  31  type is a bare arm name owned by exactly one union                   -> needs per-candidate
          source resolution before use; see the unsoundness proof below
  R2  41  U is a registered union, V is not one of its arms                    -> BLOCKED
  R3   3  U resolves to an ARM name, V unregistered (the seal_state family)    -> BLOCKED, fgdb-6v86
  R4  28  U registered nowhere                                                 -> BLOCKED
  R6  65  bare arm name owned by 2..47 unions                                  -> BLOCKED on a
          disambiguation rule; the worst is a name owned by 47 unions
  Sum 190.

R5 IS UNSOUND AS A GLOBAL LOOKUP — PROVEN, NOT SUSPECTED. `PromotedAwaitingReopen` occurs exactly
once as a source_arm_name (a18 LocalRestorePhase 0x0003), so global uniqueness resolves it
unambiguously; but a20:2601's Meta-path field would then bind to the LOCAL union, because
`MetaRestorePhase` is declared at a18:2381 and registered with zero arm rows (fgdb-2a50). A
role-token disagreement scan finds only 2 of the 31, and one of those two is a false positive
(a05 required_floor_arm:MetaSuccessor -> ShardingMigrationRetentionFloor, where the ARM is
Meta-named and the union needn't be), so the heuristic is not the law. The law is: resolve the
referent from the candidate's own source location, never by global name lookup.

A SECOND POPULATION THE gpms CLASSIFIER DOES NOT COVER. 196 candidates over 18 slices, 127 distinct
type names, whose whole exact type is a bare CamelCase name registered NOWHERE — not as name /
union_name / symbol, and not as a source_arm_name either. Two of a20's nine residue rows are in it:
    ServiceCatalogPromotionReservationReceipt.state :: ReservedHiddenNonexpiring        (a20:2581)
    CatalogActivatedHidden.admission :: CompositePromotionReceiptRequired               (a20:2587)
These are NOT all state values — the bucket also holds ordinary unlanded type references — so it
needs its own classifier before it needs a ruling. Two sub-shapes are already visible in a20:
  * SINGLETON STATE. a20:2581 binds `state:ReservedHiddenNonexpiring` with no union anywhere. Source
    silence claims less, never more: this is a closed ONE-arm discriminant, and landing it as such is
    faithful and minimal. Do not invent sibling arms.
  * PROSE STATE LITERAL. a20:2587 is `CatalogActivatedHidden{admission=CompositePromotionReceiptRequired}`
    inside a numbered prose sequence, using '=' not ':'; the census accepts '=' as a type separator
    deliberately (appendix_source.rs:2636). The owner is an EXTERNAL catalog row state, not a durable
    schema of ours, and the next clause in the same sentence writes the positional form
    `Operational{PromotionReceiptRequired}` with no member name at all. Adjudicate whether this is a
    field row at all before ruling its type.

THE ONE a20 ROW THAT IS AUTHORABLE TODAY, fully specified so it can be landed without re-derivation:
    containing_schema = "LocalRestoreServiceCompletionSpec"
    stable_name       = "expected_restore_registry_state"        source: a20:2605
    referent          = LocalRestorePhase arm 0x0003 PromotedAwaitingReopen (a18:2381), union
                        tag_wire_type = u8, so the refined tag is ONE byte
    exact_wire_type   = a NEW kind="discriminant" wire type, encoding_context in the enforced
                        grammar: "... admits only the PromotedAwaitingReopen arm (arm_tag 0x0003) of
                        the LocalRestorePhase union ..."
    identity_class    = "inline"   (FORCED — non_reference_wire_identity_class_mismatch)
    reference_semantics = "none"   cardinality = "one"   max_size_bytes = 1
    field_tag         = derive from the host's own source ordinal AND its landed sparse gap, and
                        require the two readings to agree (the method that got a20's last two tags
                        right, 4/4 and 6/6)
    wire_type_id      = next free above 0x0551; check for an EXISTING reservation at that family
                        first and mint at its code if one exists
  Landing it also requires adding (LocalRestoreServiceCompletionSpec, expected_restore_registry_state)

description:
MEASURED 2026-07-27 at HEAD 7905c27 by pane3 while re-deriving fgdb-d2ax.

`ls registries/` returns 20 registries. Both registries that plan section 5.1
names as normative are ABSENT:

    registries/command_contracts.toml            -- absent
    registries/command_type_classification.toml  -- absent

This is not a gap in the plan. Section 5.1 specifies both completely.

COMMAND_CONTRACTS.TOML. One row per role-valid command arm, with the exact schema
given verbatim in 5.1 (command_contract_id, role:Local|Meta|Shard,
outer_command_union, outer_wire_tag, input_schema_id, input_wire_tag,
inner_wire_tag?, body_schema_id, result_schema_id, applied_record_schema_id,
handler_symbol, transition_class:Semantic|Maintenance|Scaffolding, sequence_effects,
expected_state_schema_id, authority_arm, authority_evidence_target_schema_id?,
terminal_audit_freeze_arm, terminal_audit_gate_arm, payload_availability_rule,
publication_mode, construction_dag_recipe_id, consumed_state_slots[],
written_state_slots[], checkpoint_floor_classes[], backup_restore_gc_classes[],
posture_feature_predicate, format_epoch_range, status). Rows are per concrete
inner tag; 5.1 states outright that an outer family 'never hides an open
subcommand'.

COMMAND_TYPE_CLASSIFICATION.TOML. Assigns every independently addressable
normative input-looking type -- 5.1 says explicitly 'including every type whose
stable name ends in Spec' -- exactly one of SIX classes:
    RegisteredCommandInput{command_contract_id} | PreOrderArtifact |
    CertificateInput | ResultOnly | ProjectionInput | RuntimeOnly

WHY THIS IS P0 RATHER THAN A06 HOUSEKEEPING. Section 5.1 makes these two a
G0-enforced two-way total bijection: 'Every inhabitable Local, Meta, or Shard
command-union arm resolves to exactly one live command-contract row; every live
row resolves to exactly one union arm, one registered canonical input, one exact
body/result/applied-record triple, and one exhaustive Rust apply handler. Every
independently addressable input-like type has one classification row ... Duplicate
tags, aliases that encode a second command, wildcard bodies, unresolved associated
types, prose-only phases, unhandled rows, handlers without rows, or a command
input classified as its own future result are G0 failures.' None of that can be
enforced while the registries do not exist, so the enforcement reads as satisfied
by absence -- the same fail-open-by-vacuity shape this swarm has closed repeatedly
tonight (a7c8's unpinned split, 5qcg's inert exclusions, d9pd's unenforced
SC2015).

THE ANTI-INFERENCE RULE IT CARRIES, which is load-bearing and currently unenforced:

    'A suffix conveys no semantics. In particular an ordinary schema/index
     definition is a SchemaOp carried by a transaction; it cannot silently acquire
     a catalog/schema/index control command merely because prose calls it a
     specification.'

fgdb-d2ax describes seven a06 candidates as 'command-looking Spec families'. That
phrasing is exactly the inference 5.1 forbids, and there is no registry to check
it against. Until this lands, every slice with Spec-suffixed candidates has the
same hole.

IMMEDIATE CONSUMER: fgdb-d2ax, whose seven Spec families are blocked on this and
were recorded as blocked on 'an owner ruling'. They are not -- the classification
is specified; the file is missing. Re-scoping that blocker is why this bead
exists.

'independently addressable input-looking', i.e. how large the classification table
has to be. Someone should count that before estimating.

SIXTY-ONE ARE ALREADY CLASSIFIED. That is not noise, it is a seed and a
constraint at the same time:

    classification must be consistent with;
  * a constraint — any proposed classification that contradicts one of those 61
    is wrong by construction, and that gives the table a CHECKABLE first draft
    rather than 197 free choices.

is a real non-vacuous control before a single new row is authored.

One row per role-valid command arm. Upper bound from the projection: 541
wire_types rows (531 logical_object_kinds rows for reference). Its schema has 27

(consumed_state_slots, written_state_slots, checkpoint_floor_classes,
backup_restore_gc_classes), and §5.1 also requires durable_state_slots.toml to
resolve them — which is likewise absent. So this half has its own missing

197 rows across 20 slices, plus a 541-arm-bound second registry that depends on a
THIRD absent registry (durable_state_slots.toml), with a G0 two-way total
bijection and generated exhaustive-match tests over the result. That is a
workstream, not a bead. Building a partial version is actively worse than none:

the exact fail-open-by-vacuity shape closed three times tonight (a7c8's unpinned
split, 5qcg's inert exclusions, d9pd's unenforced SC2015).

title: W5 Stage 1: implement and prove binary FreeJoin
description:
## What & scope
Implement and independently close the first Loom risk-reduction stage: the final GLA-compatible binary FreeJoin kernel over authorized Strata tries/cursors. Own binary relation binding, key-order negotiation, exact intersection/probe semantics, duplicate/multiplicity handling, cancellation/resource accounting, and a deliberately nonadaptive pinned plan profile. This is a final subset of the unified operator family, not a hash-join substitute or throwaway executor.

## Why
§20 identifies FreeJoin/factorization/adaptivity as the crown-jewel risk and mandates the evidence order binary FreeJoin -> run-trie WCOJ -> factorized columns -> adaptivity. A separately closable binary stage gives later work an oracle-grounded semantic and complexity baseline while preserving the one-family design.

## Design and phase contract
Use the canonical GLA rows, answer/security contracts, `QueryCx`, `ResourceLedger`, and Secure View cursors. The kernel accepts two trie-shaped inputs and emits canonical vector batches with exact Z/multiplicity semantics, deterministic CGSE tie breaks, positive/negative/gap witness traces, and complexity-witness counters. A pinned deterministic plan selects build/probe or ordered intersection from declared features; no learned/adaptive choice, factorized output, or multiway leapfrog activation is permitted in this stage. Spill and cancellation use the final executor obligations and never expose unauthorized cardinality.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Unit tests cover every binary key/order shape, empty/duplicate/skewed inputs, NULL/value semantics, multiplicities, witness emission, canonical ordering, arithmetic/resource boundaries, cancellation points, and fail-closed authorization.
- Property/model and differential tests compare arbitrary small binary joins against `fgdb-reference`, flatten vector batches, vary physical representations and compaction, and assert identical rows, witnesses, logical digests, and declared complexity counters.
- Mutation/fuzz suites attack GLA rows, trie cursors, codecs, key comparisons, corrupt batches, resource exhaustion, and cancellation at every obligation boundary.
- E2E runs authenticated GQL through binder -> pinned binary FreeJoin -> authorized Strata cursors -> SSI/constraint validation -> canonical result/replay across spill, restart, and representation changes; an unauthorized edge type fails before observation.
- The stage evidence report publishes semantic corpus results and operation/bytes/memory distributions separately from later WCOJ/factorization/adaptivity claims.
- Detailed JSONL diagnostics record `{run_id,stage:"binary-freejoin",query_and_plan_digest,input_relation_and_cursor_commitments,key_order,policy_epoch,pinned_action,rows_and_multiplicities,witness_digest,op_count,bytes,memory_spill,cancel_or_fault,oracle,verdict,evidence_refs,seed,replay_command}` with protected facts redacted.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: a separate hash-join engine, parser-interpreted execution, post-filter authorization, unbounded materialization, or borrowing later-stage evidence. Risk is a baseline optimized to one representation; representation differential and explicit counters prevent it.

## Provenance
Plan §§8.1-8.4, §15, §17, §20 FreeJoin risk mitigation, B3/B5, FG-INV-05/06/09/19/20.

title: Bound manifest.root recovery reads against post-metadata growth
description: RootStore::read_file checks metadata length against the fixed manifest.root size, then calls unbounded read_to_end. If the inode grows after metadata (concurrent interference or storage corruption), recovery can allocate arbitrarily before eventually rejecting the length. title: same-seq delete after explicit seal+restatement must not fold a ghost live row
description: aubf restates a same-seq update after the creation has already sealed. A later same-seq delete then sees the restatement in pending and folds it away (zeay), leaving the sealed live creation as a durable ghost. title: Bound capsule recovery reads and reject trailing container bytes
description: CommitCoordinator::read_capsule uses Vfs::read, materializing the whole immutable capsule before framing validation. A corrupt or externally grown capsule can therefore allocate in proportion to arbitrary file size. Independently, decode_container returns success after parsing the declared symbol inventory without requiring EOF, so a fully valid capsule plus arbitrary trailing bytes recovers successfully and hides durable corruption. The format already has a finite maximum under its closed V1 capsule profiles and RFC source-symbol ceiling.
acceptance_criteria: Production recovery reads at most the maximum valid V1 capsule-container size plus one byte without trusting metadata; exact valid capsules recover; a stream/file larger than that bound is refused with a typed error after bounded consumption. decode_container rejects any bytes after a completely parsed declared inventory, while a genuinely truncated final symbol remains an erasure and continues to recover within budget. Planted declared-count/trailing-byte controls prove the canonical boundary. No claim of atomic protection from concurrent external writers.
close_reason: Bounded capsule recovery and strict container framing are implemented and mutation-proven; all acceptance criteria and the full repository gate pass.

So the same union_name anchored twice with overlapping arms collides at the ARM level. All five landed unions are single-anchor (MandatoryInventoryRef @ CheckpointStateVector.0x0001 etc.), and appendix_a.rs's expected_structural_keys comment calls per-anchor 'the right shape'.

(B) SINGLE ANCHOR AT THE DEFINING SITE: anchor at RemoteRetentionGrantSpec.target_ref only; the other two hosts carry ordinary [[field]] rows whose exact_wire_type = RemoteGrantTargetRef (no second anchor row). Smallest change; needs a validator answer for exact_wire_type naming a generated reference union from a non-anchor host.
(C) PER-HOST SPECIALIZED NAMES: violates the source's singular spelling — rejected unless the owner overrules the source text.

25 of the 73 closure kinds are NOT registered in logical_object_kinds.toml yet (LogicalDeltaBatch + W2 delta family, the backup certificate family, ack families, CanonicalStatementClassification, GraphIntentBatchProjection...). Their registrations belong to owning workstreams (W2/W11/W12).

(B) REGISTERED-ONLY NOW: land ~48 arms; defer 25 until their kinds register (reopens the union later; tag-permanence law says tags never renumber, so early reservation is cheaper).

title: The ADR's two enforcement lists are bound only by inspection; make the record cite violation codes and require each to be witnessed firing
notes:
Follow-up from fgdb-adr-doc-prose-unchecked-and-drifted-uyt2 (landed 60cb545).

## What is still unbound

docs/ARCHITECTURE_DECISION_RECORD.md is now generated from
registries/architecture_decisions.toml and byte-compared, so every count,
vocabulary row, and table cell is a projection that cannot drift. Two
statements in it are still bound only by inspection:

1. What the checker enforces --
   "`architecture-check` verifies the excerpts byte-for-byte against the
    master plan, pins the decision identity and semantic tables, validates
    live owner and claim references, prevents research citations from
    authorizing dependencies, regenerates this document, and emits
    deterministic decision-to-owner, owner-to-decision, and every-Bead-to-
    rationale NDJSON."

2. What fails the gate --
   "An unknown bet label, a shadowed override, an ambiguous rule, a missing
    decision, profile, or rationale, or an unresolved Bead fails the
    architecture gate."

All ten clauses were verified BY HAND on 2026-07-26 and every one maps to a
live mechanism: source_bytes_mismatch, id_table_hash_mismatch,
semantic_contract_hash_mismatch, owner_bead_unresolved,
live_verification_checker_missing, research_dependency_promotion,
document_drift, the three NDJSON emitters, bead_bet_label_set,
bead_override_shadowed, bead_family_ambiguous, provenance_rationale_missing,
bead_provenance_not_total. Nothing holds them there. Rename a code, delete a
rule, and the sentences keep reading correctly while describing a checker that
no longer exists -- which is the same defect uyt2 just closed, one level up.

## The proposed shape

Let the generator render the sentences WITH their violation codes, and require
every cited code to be one the test suite has WITNESSED FIRING -- not merely
one that appears as a string literal in architecture.rs. A source-text census
would be the fail-open version of this and should not be built (see
registry-check-metamorphic-harness: the hash layer is sound, every defect is
in a source-text reader).

That gives fgdb-validator-laws-never-witnessed-firing-xnxy its first consumer:
the document becomes the thing that CANNOT cite an unwitnessed law.

## Why this is its own bead, and not small

Measured 2026-07-26: architecture.rs emits 105 distinct violation codes.
Exactly 12 are witnessed by an assert_code call in
tools/registry-check/tests/architecture_decisions.rs. The ~13 codes the two
sentences would cite are NOT a subset of those 12 -- most notably
source_bytes_mismatch, bead_provenance_not_total, document_drift, and
research_dependency_promotion have no firing witness.

So the work is: write the missing witnesses first (each is a control plus one
typed mutation, the pattern already in tests/violation_witnesses.rs), then let
the document cite them, then add the guard that a cited code must be witnessed.
Doing it in the other order produces a citation list that looks enforced and is
not -- the exact failure this bead exists to prevent.

## Do NOT do the weak version

Rendering the codes without the witnessed-set guard is worse than the prose it
replaces: it reads as machine-checked and is not. If the witnesses are too
expensive to write, leave the sentences as prose and say in the document that
they are bound by inspection -- which is what uyt2 did for the four
statements that are not mechanically checkable at all.
