Semantic bindings and evidence rows are NOT derivable — they name owner bead, crate, checker, test/scenario/event IDs and gate. Those are per-owner knowledge.

PROPOSED SHAPE, for the other slice owners to adopt or contest:
 (a) Freeze the four row schemas and their pin mechanics ONCE, in one reviewed increment, before any slice authors a single row. Getting this wrong after 2000 rows exist is a mass migration.
 (b) Generate annotations from the census the way projections are generated today, with a sanctioned writer command and a byte-diff law, so annotation drift is impossible by construction. Do not hand-author 2136 rows.
 (c) Author semantic bindings and evidence per slice, by that slice's owner, since only they know the checker/test/gate IDs.
 (d) Sequence it AFTER the residual field/union/arm coverage of each slice, never before: an annotation binds to a target_row_id, so every target minted later needs its own four rows anyway. Front-loading it just means editing the same rows twice.
 (e) Nobody should flip definition_status="complete" until (a)-(d) are done for that slice, because the flip arms all of these laws simultaneously, plus source_complete_census_uncovered and source_complete_slice_ambiguity_unresolved.

=== 3. WHAT I PROPOSE TO DO NEXT, CONCRETELY ===
 - Land the two provably-landable ExportLeaf<T> rows (uncovered 12 -> 10). Small, no ruling, positional tags.
 - File the tracked items as beads in ONE batched br create pass with the architecture bead-provenance pins re-frozen in the SAME commit, under the catalog token, so architecture-check is never transiently red for the other five agents.
 - Add the dependency edge a01 -> a04 rather than inventing a ruling for two types the plan already defines.

=== RULING 1: THE a01:1443 vs a02:1449 DIVERGENCE. a02:1449 IS AUTHORITATIVE. THERE IS NO DIVERGENCE TO RECONCILE. ===

The two renderings:

ALL SEVEN of a01:1443's member names are ALREADY REGISTERED — as RootBootstrap FRAME fields: root_placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy_id, root_failure_domain_id, segment_id, offset, encoded_len, root_symbol_inventory_digest. a01:1443 is therefore a RECONSTRUCTION IDENTITY over rows that already exist, not a competing schema.

An active identity law over a mutable layout is the same hazard class as a derived structure outranking its source: today's placement_id and tomorrow's can differ for identical placements, with nothing detecting it.

comments.text:
COMPLETION-LAYER FINDING FOR ALL 21 SLICES: PARTIAL ANNOTATION SETS ARE LEGAL, AND THE GATE IS PER-TARGET, NOT PER-SLICE.

A slice at definition_status=declared may carry any number of annotation rows, including zero or a handful, because every mandatory-annotation law keys on a TARGET being complete: appendix_a.rs ~11137 emits complete_slice_annotation_missing only after the guard `if row.definition_status != "complete"` skips non-complete targets, and source_annotation_contract_ambiguous (verify_annotation_source_contracts, appendix_a.rs:7369, the check ~54 lines in) fires only when the source is non-exact AND target.definition_status == "complete". So you can annotate incrementally, target by target, without flipping anything.

THE ONE LAW THAT DOES APPLY REGARDLESS OF STATUS: if a field target's census source IS exact, any annotation you write for it must byte-match the census exact_type and cardinality — that check sits OUTSIDE the complete-gate. So partial is legal, but wrong is not: an annotation on a declared target is validated against the source the moment it exists.

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR SEQUENCING: it means the completion layer does NOT have to be an all-or-nothing per-slice campaign. Slices can land annotations progressively as their coverage closes, and a slice can pilot a handful of rows to prove the contract before committing to hundreds. That was the open question in my cross-slice proposal and it is now answered in the permissive direction.

A CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER PROPOSAL, because it will otherwise mislead planning. I argued annotations were "largely derivable" and should be GENERATED rather than hand-authored. Against the schema cod_1 actually froze, that is wrong. Annotation has NINETEEN fields, and only exact_type and cardinality are census-forced. The other seventeen - including posture, authority, locality, redaction_class, resource_bounds, compatibility, digest_recipe and retention_and_cut_rule - are per-row judgement, and there is no generator: ANNOTATION_CONTRACT is [AnnotationContractPin; 0] and each row additionally needs a reciprocal compiled pin with the same 19 fields. So the layer costs roughly two hand-authored 19-field records per target, not one generated row. My reality-check estimate of ~4 rows per target understated the effort per row; the row COUNT was right, the per-row cost was not. Anyone planning the layer should either build a generator for the derivable subset first or budget for hand-authoring.

ANNOTATION PILOT DESIGN (a01), complete enough that the hold is an apply. Designed off-token against HEAD 795830a. I will queue for catalog as pane3-a01pilot; cc_1 goes first with the bead-provenance split.

=== PILOT SET: FOUR ROWS, CHOSEN TO SPAN THE TRAP CLASSES RATHER THAN TO BE EASY ===
All four are a01 RootSlot field targets whose census source is EXACT, so their annotation exact_type and cardinality are FORCED and I am testing the contract rather than arguing about content.

Deliberately four, not one: a single-row pilot proves the plumbing but finds no traps, and traps are the whole reason to pilot before 227.

=== SCOPE FINDING THAT CHANGES THE a01 CLOSURE MAP ===
Of a01's field targets, 95 have an EXACT census source (annotation exact_type/cardinality forced) and 74 DO NOT. That second number is a completion blocker I had not quantified: a complete target MUST have an annotation (complete_slice_annotation_missing), and an annotation on a complete target whose source is non-exact fires source_annotation_contract_ambiguous. So a01 cannot reach complete until those 74 census sources are disambiguated - which is source work, in the same family as the ambiguous-candidate problem blocking CertificateSignerLock. Add it to the closure map: a01 needs 4 coverage keys + 2 adjudications + 74 source disambiguations + the annotation layer, not just the first two.

=== ANNOTATION TEMPLATE (19 fields; only the first two are forced) ===
  row_id                  derived - DO NOT hand-write, see trap 3
  target_row_id           the a01:field:... id above
  exact_type              FORCED, byte-match census
  cardinality             FORCED, byte-match census as_str()
  layout / role / posture / authority / locality            authored
  generic_expansions[] / role_expansions[]                  empty for these four (no generics, no role indexing)
  reference_semantics     "none" for all four (RootSlot scalars are not references)
  target_schema_ids[]     empty (follows from reference_semantics=none)
  construction_order / retention_and_cut_rule / digest_recipe / redaction_class / resource_bounds / compatibility   authored
Each row ALSO needs a reciprocal compiled AnnotationContractPin with the same 19 fields; ANNOTATION_CONTRACT is currently [AnnotationContractPin; 0], so I am the first consumer and there is no precedent row to copy.

=== LANDING ORDER ===
The four rows are mutually independent - an annotation binds only to its target_row_id, so there is no inter-row ordering law. Order is therefore: (a) splice all four TOML rows + four compiled pins together, (b) bump ANNOTATION_CONTRACT array 0->4 and EXPECTED_ANNOTATION_COUNT 0->4 TOGETHER (catalog_annotation_contract_pin_inconsistent fires if they diverge), (c) derive EXPECTED_ANNOTATION_SHA256 from the loader's own drift message, (d) gate. One increment, not four.

=== TRAPS I EXPECT, WITH THE MITIGATION ===
 1. CARDINALITY VOCABULARY. Cardinality::as_str() emits "one" | "optional" | "many" | "many-or-indexed". The annotation byte-match compares against THAT string, so database_id must carry "many-or-indexed". My own 2A-era note says census ManyOrIndexed maps to "many" in the FIELD-ROW vocabulary - that is a different row kind with a different vocabulary. Using "many" here will fail the byte-match. This is exactly why row 3 is in the pilot.
 2. QUOTED LITERAL. root-slot-magic's census exact_type is the four characters F G R T WRAPPED IN DOUBLE QUOTES, i.e. the quote characters are part of the value. The TOML must escape them. Getting this wrong looks like a trivial typo and fails a byte-match.
 3. ROW_ID DERIVATION. Per the a01 2G precedent, do not guess: land the row, read catalog_row_id_derived_mismatch, adopt the expected value it prints. lower_kebab mangles punctuation in ways that are not guessable.
 4. RUSTFMT BEFORE PATCH. The compiled pin entries must be rustfmt-canonical before the patch is derived, or cargo fmt --check fails the gate and the patch is stale the moment it is fixed. Fix the GENERATOR output, never run cargo fmt across appendix_a.rs - a whole-file reformat on a file several lanes edit can silently rewrite someone else's just-landed region. (Cost me a cycle in 2H.)
 5. THE FOUR INVISIBLE PIN SITES. I EXPECT none to apply: annotations add no target, move no epoch, and use no projection| fallback form. But expectation is not evidence - a green loader has never once been sufficient on this trail, so I will run g0_identity_e2e.sh and the composite regardless and report actual exit codes.
 6. STALE RLIB. Rebuild registry_check as the first action of the hold; three lanes have moved pins since my last build and cc_1 measured three stalenesses inside one hold.

=== WHAT THIS PILOT DELIVERS BEYOND FOUR ROWS ===
The first worked example of the completion layer for all 21 slices: a validated 19-field template, the reciprocal-pin mechanics, the two vocabulary traps, and a measured pin surface. That is the artifact - the rows are almost incidental.

title: Appendix A exact catalog: Filesystem, cipher, encoding, placement, and symbols
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the exact Appendix A catalog slice for Filesystem, cipher, encoding, placement, and symbols. This task embeds source-plan lines 1445-1463 verbatim, expands every generic and role-indexed family into stable registered rows, and assigns each row to its granular implementation owner. It is a format/ownership contract, not a substitute implementation.

## Exact normative contract
The following audited source-plan text is authoritative and self-contained:

**Filesystem durability and writer takeover.** `FilesystemDurabilityProfile` is a signed/checked-in artifact `{ profile_id, profile_version, os/kernel_range, allowed_filesystems_and_mount_predicates, forbidden_layers/options, required_lock_primitive, owner_death_rule, stable_inode_rule, slot_write_rule, file_sync_rule, directory_sync_rule, rename_no_replace_rule, cache_flush_assumption, probe_suite_oid }`. `FGFS-LINUX-LOCAL-V1` has exactly §5.1's ext4/XFS allowlist; a profile/mount not matching every predicate is not writable. A local `FilesystemInstanceRecord { profile_id, probe_suite_oid, mount_id, filesystem_type, canonical_mount_options, device_chain_digest, directory_device_inode, manifest_device_inode, checked_at, result_digest }` is diagnostic evidence, never a transferable proof or semantic root.

The takeover checker accepts only `NoGuard -> LeaseHeld(identity) -> ClosureRecovered(old_epoch) -> PendingFenceGuard(old_epoch+1) -> FenceRootDurableAndReread(old_epoch+1) -> WriterEnabled(FenceToken)`. Creation is `NoGuard -> StagingInodeLease -> PendingCreationGuard(epoch=1) -> CompleteStagingRootVerified -> RenameNoReplaceAndDirectorySync -> CanonicalRootReread -> WriterEnabled`. `PendingFenceGuard` is linear and can encode/seal exactly one fence-only `RootManifest` preserving the recovered state plus its inactive `RootSlot`; `PendingCreationGuard` can encode/seal only the registered Genesis closure and epoch-1 slot. Neither type implements user-segment, prepared-owner, receipt, Raft, canonical-transition, or general-root traits. `FenceToken` is nonserializable and nonconstructible outside the VFS/commit boundary; it binds the live lease handle, stable directory/root identity, profile, slot generation, and epoch. The fence-only root/slot must retain the exact prior canonical logical root, Raft/audit candidate, prepared root, and durable/applied/visible positions. Every immutable segment trailer records `{ database_security_namespace_id, cluster_incarnation, local_writer_fence_epoch, segment_id, sealed_len, inventory_digest, trailer_checksum }`; after promotion the local VFS refuses a seal, prepared-root update, receipt signature, Raft append acknowledgement/proposal, or root publication without the matching live token. Already receipted/ordered records from an older epoch remain strong obligations but cannot authorize new old-epoch publication. The crash matrix cuts after every lease/identity/recovery/object-sync/slot-write/slot-sync/staging-rename/directory-sync/reread step and includes owner death, path replacement, mount drift, stale descriptors, epoch overflow, competing creators, orphan staging, and a lying-sync profile that must be rejected.

**Cipher/encoding/placement records and SymbolRecord.** `CipherDescriptorWithoutDigest` is `{ logical_oid, object_kind, canonical_plaintext_len, codec_profile, compressed_len, data_crypto_profile, dek_id, object_nonce_or_siv, object_tag_len }`. Object AAD is the domain string plus logical OID and this canonical descriptor. `CiphertextRecord` is `{ descriptor, ciphertext_id, ciphertext_digest, object_tag_digest, protected_length }`; `CiphertextId` hashes descriptor+ciphertext+object tag. Immutable `EncodingDescriptorWithoutId` is `{ ciphertext_id, fec_profile, transfer_length, oti_common, oti_scheme, symbol_size, source_block_count, symbol_auth_profile }`, and `EncodingId` hashes the domain/version plus its **complete canonical bytes**. Separately, `PlacementDescriptorWithoutId` is `{ encoding_id, placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy, location_form }`, where `location_form = ContiguousSpan{failure_domain_id,segment_id,offset,encoded_len,symbol_inventory_digest} | Explicit{sorted_symbol_inventory_and_locators,failure_domains}`. `PlacementId` hashes the placement domain/version plus exactly that descriptor; immutable `PlacementRecord { placement_id, descriptor }` merely stores and cross-checks it. Moving/adding symbols creates a new placement record without changing encoding identity. KEK/wrap epoch is absent from both ciphertext and encoding identity. The authenticated local physical-realization index maps `CiphertextId`, `EncodingId`, and `PlacementId` to these records with nonretaining locators. An ordinary decoder obtains the complete descriptor/OTI/auth profile from an authenticated `EncodingDescriptorWithoutId` (or FGP's authenticated encoding prelude) before accepting any symbol; a bare `SymbolRecord` is never self-authorizing.

```text
SymbolRecord {
  magic="FGEC", format_version:u16, header_len:u16, record_len:u32,
  logical_oid:[u8;32], ciphertext_id:[u8;32], encoding_id:[u8;32],
  object_kind:u16, source_block:u32, esi:u32, symbol_len:u32,
  transfer_length:u64, oti_common:u64, oti_scheme:u32, flags:u32,
  symbol_mac_profile:u16, symbol_mac_len:u16,
  payload:[u8;symbol_len], symbol_mac:[u8;symbol_mac_len]
}
```

The symbol MAC key/transcript are exactly §5.1's domain-separated construction. All framing/OTI/length fields and payload are MACed. Truncated/noncanonical tails are ignored only in proved-unreferenced staging; a reachable sealed tail triggers authenticated repair or fail-closed recovery.

## Ownership, verification, and diagnostics
For every schema, field, tag, state, transition, reference, digest transcript, construction-order rule, and role restriction in this slice, generate a durable_fields.toml row with stable IDs; canonical encoding/version policy; concrete generic/role expansion; producer, owner bead/crate, and consumers; reference strength/target set; authority and redaction class; invariant/evidence/cost bindings; test/scenario/event IDs; and consuming gate. Cross-slice targets use stable catalog IDs and must resolve in the Appendix A epic closure. Downstream owners may add implementation detail but cannot abbreviate, alias, weaken, or contradict these bytes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The embedded line range is byte-complete, checksum-pinned, continuous with adjacent slices, and contains no truncation marker.
- Every exact named construct in the slice has one stable row and exactly one granular implementation owner; all references and consumers resolve.
- Unit tests cover canonical encode/decode, stable field/tag IDs, role/generic expansion, digest construction, state preconditions, and owner uniqueness.
- Property/mutation/fuzz tests remove, duplicate, reorder, retag, corrupt, weaken, or cross-role substitute every field/arm/reference class and prove rejection.
- Simulation tests exercise applicable crash, cancellation, retry, sent-unknown, receipt-first, recovery, authority/configuration rotation, compaction, and expiry boundaries.
- E2E scripts traverse each applicable public embedded/server/FGP/CLI path through durable publication, restart/replay, backup/restore, and terminal cleanup using isolated synthetic fixtures.
- Detailed versioned JSONL diagnostics carry schema_id, field_or_arm_id, role/group, object or public commitment, transition_id, state_before/state_after, checker, verdict, artifact refs, and replay command; secret/noninterference tests reject protected data or observable hidden state.
- Cross-version golden vectors and unknown-required-field fixtures enforce additive-minor/breaking-major policy; no gate passes with an uncovered row.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: family-level prose summaries, wildcard references, inferred fields, unregistered aliases, or treating the catalog slice as the implementation. Exactness is intentional; execution remains decomposed across the linked workstream beads.

    { encoding_id, placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy, location_form }
  location_form = ContiguousSpan{ failure_domain_id, segment_id, offset, encoded_len, symbol_inventory_digest }
                | Explicit{ sorted_symbol_inventory_and_locators, failure_domains }
Land the location_form union and both arms including Explicit. a02:1449 is AUTHORITATIVE; a01:1443 is a specialized root-bootstrap reconstruction over already-registered RootBootstrap frame fields, not a competing schema, so there is nothing to reconcile and nothing to wait for.

=== WHAT I ALREADY DID SO YOU DO NOT ===

a621c9e re-cited the wire row 0x001e encoding_context from "plan lines 1388-1444" (a01, wrong) to a02:1449, and records the a01/a02 relationship inline so the next reader does not re-litigate it. That row is a01-owned; do not touch it. Gate was green with ZERO pin movement — encoding_context is not part of the released assignment transcript, so the wire registry pin and epoch did not move and none of the four invisible sites applied. Useful precedent for you: descriptive context fields are free to edit, unlike codes/tags/names/lifecycle/union-arms.

=== WHAT IS STILL OPEN, AND WHO OWNS IT ===

The reserved-with-active-referent state is NOT yours to fix and NOT fixed. Do not flip PlacementDescriptorWithoutId to active as part of your work — its members are unregistered today, and activating an empty shell is strictly worse than the current transient.
The sequence is: YOU register the members -> the wire type then earns active status -> the anomaly disappears on its own. So your increment is what clears it, without you doing anything about the status directly.

=== ONE CORRECTION TO THE RECORD, IN YOUR FAVOUR ===

Your "only such row in the catalog" claim is CORRECT, and I have now verified it in both directions rather than just believing it. Exactly two physical kinds carry a canonical(X) transcript:
    EncodingRecord  [active] -> canonical(EncodingDescriptorWithoutId)   wire:active    clean
    PlacementRecord [active] -> canonical(PlacementDescriptorWithoutId)  wire:reserved  the one violation
What I corrected earlier was the MECHANISM, not the uniqueness: the referent is not a field row (there are zero field rows referencing it, controlled against ConsensusDomain=8 and RemoteObjectIdentity=12 so the zero is real) but an identity-bearing TRANSCRIPT — PlacementRecord's identity law is placement_id = BLAKE3("fgdb:placement:v1" || canonical(PlacementDescriptorWithoutId)). That distinction is what makes it dangerous rather than untidy: an active identity law over an unfrozen layout means placement_id can differ for identical placements.

=== THE DURABLE FIX, DELIBERATELY DEFERRED ===

The missing checker law — an ACTIVE physical kind's identity-bearing transcript may only name ACTIVE types — CANNOT land before your increment. Measured: it would fire on exactly one row, PlacementRecord, and that row is unfixable until you register the members. Landing it now reds the tree with a violation nobody can clear. After your increment it lands green and prevents recurrence.
Implementation note for whoever takes it: PhysicalKind.transcript is an opaque String (identity.rs:103) that is never decomposed, which is why no law exists. The extraction is narrower than it sounds — canonical\(([A-Za-z0-9_]+)\) is sufficient, not a general parser. Note the deliberate contrast to guard against over-reach: union_arm_lifecycle_mismatch permits RESERVED targets on purpose, which is right for a plain reference and wrong for an identity-bearing transcript. The new law must draw that distinction rather than banning reserved referents generally.

title: Appendix A exact catalog: Local logical state and durable transaction formats
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the exact Appendix A catalog slice for Local logical state and durable transaction formats. This task embeds source-plan lines 1464-1543 verbatim, expands every generic and role-indexed family into stable registered rows, and assigns each row to its granular implementation owner. It is a format/ownership contract, not a substitute implementation.

## Exact normative contract
The following audited source-plan text is authoritative and self-contained:

**LogicalStatePayload / LogicalStateRoot.** The following is a compact Local navigation projection of generated `LogicalStatePayload`, not a field-exhaustive alternate schema: `{database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,bootstrap_phase:Genesis|CheckpointInstalled|Operational|RecoveryReconciling|RecoveryAbandoned|OperationalPendingIndependentReopen,applied_logical_command_seq,applied_commit_seq,global_transaction_marker_head:StrongMarkerRef?,branch_head_map_root(entries carry StrongMarkerRef),branch_manifest_root,branch_key_epoch_registry_root,key_envelope/grant_registry_root,branch_merge_ledger_root,graph_partition_state_roots,catalog_root,schema_roots,id_allocator_root,identity_continuity_record_ref,constraint_state_roots,resource_ledger_root,privacy_ledger_root,privacy_continuity_record_ref,dp_request_index_root,txn_outcome_index_root:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeIndex>,local_begin_idempotency_index_root:StrongRef<LocalBeginIdempotencyIndex>,local_statement_index_root:StrongRef<LocalStatementIndex>,local_txn_outcome_summary_root:StrongRef<LocalTxnOutcomeSummaryRoot>,local_delta_batch_index_root:StrongRef<LocalDeltaBatchIndex>,local_delta_frontier,terminal_certification_reservation_root:StrongRef<TerminalCertificationReservationRoot<Local>>,recovery_checkpoint_ref:StrongRef<RecoveryCheckpoint>?,retained_stream_floor,retention_map_root:StrongRef<RetentionMap>,derived_generation_registry_root:StrongRef<DerivedGenerationRegistry>,replay_registry_root,logical_hlc_state,topology_epoch,policy_epoch,revocation_index,replicated_key_wrap/signing/capability-verifier roots,audit_ticket_index_root,audit_root,transparency_root,backup_registry_root,restore_state_ref:StrongRef<RestoreState>?,restore_retention_anchor:RestoreRetentionAnchor<Local>,gc_decision_root,remote_retention_authority_root:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionObligationRoot>,remote_retention_consumer_root:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionConsumerRoot>,remote_configuration_trust_root:StrongRef<RemoteConfigurationTrustRoot>,sharding_migration_state_ref:StrongRef<ShardingMigrationState>?,config_payload_floor_ref:StrongRef<ConfigPayloadFloor>?}`. Independent result/cursor/artifact delivery, the imported audit-continuity release head, and the audit visibility pipeline are protocol slots, not fields silently omitted from this semantic projection. The exact bounded `LocalDeltaBatchIndex` and cut lifecycle are defined with `LogicalDeltaBatch` below. `ShardingMigrationState` is `FreezePendingAudit{freeze_ref:StrongRef<ShardingFreezeRecord>}|FrozenVisible{freeze_ref,visibility_advance_maintenance_identity:MaintenanceAppliedRef}|RoleTransitionLocked{begin_ref:StrongRef<BeginRoleTransitionRecord>}|Resolved{terminal_identity}`; no variant names a future semantic command. Remote roots are empty reserved values before W12 preparation. Fresh bootstrap permits Genesis -> CheckpointInstalled -> Operational; restore/reopen/abandonment follow the exact later state machine and the retention anchor must match each phase. `LogicalStateRoot` is `{payload_ref:StrongRef<LogicalStatePayload>,logical_command_head:StrongCommandRef?}`; fresh genesis alone has no head.

For Local, the activated **semantic** state-slot closure additionally requires `security_state_binding_root`, `valid_time_slice_registry_root`, `constraint_reservation_index_root`, `escrow_ledger_root`, `allocation_reservation_and_disposition_root`, `txn_ownership_directory_root`, `txn_capability_lineage_root`, `artifact_output_request_registry_root`, `replay_manifest_registry_root`, `format_compatibility_state_ref`, `bulk_load_registry_root`, `derived_build_registry_root`, `audit_terminal_freeze_index_root`, and `restore_registry_root`. `local_result_delivery_index_root`, `result_independent_retention_index_root`, and `delivery_lease_registry_root` are obsolete alternate names for the one canonical Protocol slot `result_independent_retention_index`; none is encoded in `LogicalStatePayload`. Semantic owners store only delivery ID/detachment commitments, while RootManifest's protocol root owns the bytes. The audit pipeline is likewise not a payload slot, avoiding a content cycle. Feature-disabled semantic slots use registered empty/None recipes. `state_payload_fields.toml` supplies only semantic fields; `protocol_state_fields.toml` supplies the result/cursor/output/audit slots and forbids duplicate aliases.

The generated common header of every Local/Meta/Shard payload also contains `{incarnation_continuity_profile_id,cluster_incarnation_continuity_record_ref:StrongRef<ClusterIncarnationContinuityRecord>?,cluster_incarnation_continuity_digest,continuity_cas_version,service_visibility_epoch,time_authority_binding:Local{registry_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityRegistry<Local>>}|Meta{registry_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityRegistry<Meta>>}|Shard{active_projection_ref:StrongRef<ActiveMetaProjectionRoot>,projected_registry_digest,projected_selected_profile_oid,projection_meta_prefix},restore_registry_root:StrongRef<RestoreRegistry>,terminal_audit_freeze_index_root:StrongRef<AuditTerminalFreezeIndex>}`. `DirectoryBound` uses no external record ref and a fixed local continuity digest; `ExternalCas` requires `Some` and exact byte equality with the live authority. `restore_state_ref` is present only during a live restore, while `restore_registry_root` retains terminal projection/promotion/tombstone evidence. The audit-freeze index is active only in Local/Meta and is the canonical empty reserved value in Shard. Shards may validate only the exact current active/closing/draining profile projection certified in their active Meta projection; they cannot originate profile changes. RootManifest and RootSlot repeat and cross-check the same continuity/profile/digest/version/visibility tuple.

**Local 1.0 durable transaction formats.** Local and W12 deliberately share only embedded value schemas (`TxnCompletionState`, posture-tagged `SemanticTerminalDescriptor`, and `TerminalPublicOutcome`) plus public protocol semantics. They do not share durable registration, workspace, statement, result-owner, outcome, audit-owner, claim, or command objects. A Local decoder rejects every `Global*`, Meta, shard, certified-remote, or global-prefix identity in this family, and a W12 decoder rejects every Local identity. `LocalAuditTicketOwner` is `Operation{txn_token,registration_binding_digest}|Statement{registration_ref:StrongRef<LocalAttemptRegistration>,statement_seq,statement_idempotency_key}|Control{control_operation_tag,request_idempotency_key,request_basis_commitment}`. `LocalAuditTicketClaimRecord` is `{ticket_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicket>,owner:LocalAuditTicketOwner,claiming_control_ref:StrongRef<ControlCommand>,claim_applied_ref:AppliedControlRef,request_basis_commitment}` and is constructed during the registration/claim apply before its owning Local record. `LocalOperationAuditAdmission` is `NotRequired{evidence:NonRequiredAuditEvidence}|PendingUnclaimed{ticket_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicket>,ticket_admission_record_ref:StrongCommandRef,operation_request_basis_commitment}|Claimed{ticket_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicket>,claim_record_ref:StrongRef<LocalAuditTicketClaimRecord>,owner:LocalAuditTicketOwner::Operation,operation_request_basis_commitment}`. `LocalStatementAuditAdmission` has the analogous NotRequired/PendingUnclaimed/Claimed forms with `LocalAuditTicketOwner::Statement`; protected Local controls use the Control arm through their exact audit admission. No Local field can encode a global transaction ID, registration generation, GlobalControlRecord, or GlobalControlCommand.

The generated Local payload schema corrects the compact navigation list above by requiring `local_conflict_index_ref:StrongRef<LocalConflictIndex>` immediately after the statement/outcome roots. Genesis installs the canonical empty index. Its checkpoint vector, `ConfigPayloadFloor`, mandatory inventory, backup closure, restore transform/reconciliation, GC root inventory, key-destruction scan, and role-transition projection each have a generated required row; omission disables SERIALIZABLE operation and is a G0 failure, not a recoverable cache miss.

The same normative schema requires `policy_root_ref:StrongRef<SecurityPolicyRoot>`, `revocation_root_ref:StrongRef<RevocationRoot>`, `constraint_state_directory_root:StrongRef<ConstraintStateDirectoryRoot>`, `local_constraint_reservation_root:StrongRef<LocalConstraintReservationRoot>`, `resource_ledger_root:StrongRef<ResourceLedgerState>`, `escrow_ledger_root:StrongRef<EscrowLedgerRoot>`, and the valid-time contract/slice/temporal-constraint roots activated by the schema. Scalar policy/revocation fields are cross-checks only. Genesis installs canonical empty roots or DenyAll security policy as configured. Every generated checkpoint/floor/inventory/backup/restore/GC/key/transition row covers them; a generic `constraint_state_roots` or untyped `resource_ledger_root` rendering does not satisfy the registry.

`LocalConflictAttemptKey` is `{txn_token_digest,registration_identity}`. `LocalConflictEdge` is `{kind:wr|ww|rw,from:LocalConflictAttemptKey,to:LocalConflictAttemptKey,coordinate_or_predicate_domain,proof_ref:LocalConflictProofRef,first_observed_statement_seq,edge_digest}` where `LocalConflictProofRef` is a generated closed union over version, absence/range, path, constraint, and final-write proof objects. `LocalConflictEntry` is `{registration_ref:StrongRef<LocalAttemptRegistration>,registered_snapshot,start_logical_command_seq,terminal_logical_command_seq?,state:Active|PrepareAdmitted{admission_generation}|Committed|Aborted|ReadClosed,statement_frontier,workspace_generation_ref:StrongRef<LocalTxnWorkspaceGeneration>,cumulative_read_witness_root_ref:StrongRef<LocalCumulativeReadWitnessRoot>,cumulative_write_summary_ref:StrongRef<LocalWriteSummary>?,incoming_edges[LocalConflictEdge],outgoing_edges[LocalConflictEdge],overlap_interval:{start_prefix,closed_prefix?},detail_state:Detailed|Compacted{summary_ref:StrongRef<LocalConflictSummaryLeaf>}}`. Arrays/maps use canonical key/digest order and exact deduplication; an edge must appear byte-identically in both endpoint projections.

`LocalConflictIndex` is `{generation,basis_logical_command_seq,entries[LocalConflictAttemptKey->LocalConflictEntry],safe_snapshot_frontier,overlap_close_floor_ref:StrongRef<LocalConflictOverlapFloor>,root_digest:BodyDigest<LocalConflictIndex>}`. `LocalConflictIndexBasis` is the nonretaining typed `{basis_state:WeakStateIdentity,index_generation,index_root_digest,basis_logical_command_seq,safe_snapshot_frontier,overlap_close_floor_digest}` used by serialization/final-certification inputs; a bare `WeakStateIdentity` is insufficient. Registration atomically inserts Active with workspace zero. Every successful statement publication atomically replaces that exact entry with its successor statement/workspace/witness/write summary and all newly proved bidirectional edges. Prepare admission replays `may_affect` in both directions against every overlapping entry, reruns the registered SCC algorithm, and atomically selects PrepareAdmitted; commit, admitted abort, active cancel, or read close installs the terminal prefix and state in the same command as outcome/attempt changes. Terminal completion changes no serialization decision but retains the entry through its postcondition lifetime.

`LocalConflictOverlapFloor` is `{closed_through_start_prefix,safe_snapshot_frontier,oldest_live_overlapping_start,retained_detailed_attempt_key_commitment,retained_edge_proof_commitment,checker_version}`. `LocalConflictCompactionSpec {expected_index_basis:LocalConflictIndexBasis,sorted_selected_terminal_keys,sorted_summary_leaf_refs[StrongRef<LocalConflictSummaryLeaf>],no_future_overlap_edge_proof_ref:StrongRef<LocalNoFutureConflictEdgeProof>,expected_oldest_live_overlapping_start,expected_attempt_outcome_statement_workspace_retention_discharge,terminal_audit_gate}` may replace detail only when every possible future transaction has a start/snapshot beyond the selected entry's closed overlap interval and no live witness can add an edge; it never deletes the authenticated summary or changes public outcomes. Every follower reconstructs `may_affect`, verifies symmetric edges/proofs and workspace transport, and reruns SCC before signing `LocalSerializationCertificate`, whose `snapshot_and_conflict_index_basis` field is exactly `LocalConflictIndexBasis`. Missing/stale/asymmetric evidence, unsupported exact witness semantics, or resource exhaustion conservatively aborts/waits. Write-skew, multi-edge rw cycles, same-I/O-batch writers, read-only dangerous structures, statement-workspace transport, restart, checkpoint, compaction, and detail-retirement races are permanent oracle/model tests.

`LocalBeginIdempotencyIndex` maps `(database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,tenant,principal,scoped_begin_idempotency_key)` to exactly `Reserved{reservation_ref:StrongRef<LocalBeginReservationRecord>,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>}|BoundDetailed{registration_ref:StrongRef<LocalAttemptRegistration>,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>}|BoundCompacted{summary_root_ref:StrongRef<LocalTxnOutcomeSummaryRoot>,leaf_key_digest,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>}|NeverRegisteredDetailed{terminal_ref:StrongRef<LocalNeverRegisteredRecord>,public_projection_bundle_ref:StrongRef<NeverRegisteredPublicProjectionBundle<Local>>,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>}|NeverRegisteredCompacted{summary_root_ref:StrongRef<LocalTxnOutcomeSummaryRoot>,leaf_key_digest,public_projection_bundle_ref:StrongRef<NeverRegisteredPublicProjectionBundle<Local>>,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>}|ExpiredTombstone{scoped_key_digest,txn_token_digest,capability_commitment,expiry_evidence_digest}`. `LocalBeginReservationSpec` is `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>,canonical_begin_request_digest,operation_class:ReadOnly|ReadWrite,isolation_profile,transaction_error_policy,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>,read_your_writes_basis:None|Validated{validation_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence>,requested_floor_subset_digest,capability_floor_set_commitment},scoped_begin_idempotency_key,expected_index_absence:WeakAbsenceProof,staging_resource_reservation_ref:StrongRef<ResourceLedgerTransition>,operation_audit_admission:LocalOperationAuditAdmission::PendingUnclaimed|NotRequired,terminal_audit_gate:LifecycleScaffoldingNotRequired}`. The validated arm is required exactly when BEGIN presents a ReadYourWrites capability and must select the `ReadYourWritesBeginAdmission` Local row before any observation. The header is the sole namespace/incarnation/service/tenant/principal/ceiling/policy/revocation source and byte-matches the replay object, RYW basis, resource reservation, and audit admission. Apply constructs `LocalBeginReservationRecord {authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>,source_spec_ref:StrongRef<LocalBeginReservationSpec>,applied_control_ref:AppliedControlRef,canonical_begin_request_digest,txn_token,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>,capability_commitment,read_your_writes_basis,reserved_at_logical_command_seq,staging_generation}`, installs Reserved with the replay ref, and constructs `TxnOutcomeRecord::BeginStaging`; only that visible state permits BEGIN_ACCEPTED. Byte-identical retry returns the same identities. `LocalBeginTerminalSpec {reservation_ref,internal_reason_class,no_registration_or_effect_proof_ref,public_projection_bundle_ref:StrongRef<NeverRegisteredPublicProjectionBundle<Local>>,terminal_audit_gate}` alone consumes Reserved and creates `LocalNeverRegisteredRecord {reservation_ref,internal_reason_class,no_registration_or_effect_proof_ref,public_projection_bundle_ref,terminal_audit_gate,applied_control_ref}` plus NeverRegisteredDetailed. The bundle's internal subject/reason/request/domain byte-match the spec; deterministic apply invents no reason mapping, receipt, handle, or response bytes. A required ticket resolves directly from PendingUnclaimed with `AuditResolutionOrigin::Unclaimed`. Timeout, disconnect, or memory loss alone is not terminal evidence, and a terminal begin key can never later bind. The spec/record decode the replay object, require request_kind ExplicitBegin and exact request/domain/authority/profile/window equality, and derive txn_token/capability commitment from it; no duplicate inline capability encoding is trusted.

`LocalAttemptRegistrationSpec` has the closed binding `ExplicitBegin{reservation_ref:StrongRef<LocalBeginReservationRecord>,expected_index_value:Reserved,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>,read_your_writes_basis_from_reservation}|Autocommit{autocommit_idempotency_key,canonical_request_digest,classification_ref:StrongRef<CanonicalStatementClassification>,expected_absence_proof:WeakAbsenceProof,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>,read_your_writes_basis:None|Validated{validation_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence>,requested_floor_subset_digest,capability_floor_set_commitment}}` plus `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>,authority_permit_ref:AuthorityPermitRef<Local>,requested_snapshot_bounds,txn_operation_ceiling:TxnOperationCeiling,transaction_error_policy,initial_workspace_recipe,operation_audit_admission:LocalOperationAuditAdmission::PendingUnclaimed|NotRequired,terminal_audit_gate:LifecycleScaffoldingNotRequired}`. The ExplicitBegin basis must byte-equal the reservation field; an Autocommit validated basis selects `ReadYourWritesExecuteAdmission` before observation. Apply verifies the header, permit, replay object, begin reservation, RYW basis, audit admission, snapshot, and ceiling all name one complete Local binding; verifies any autocommit classification is within the ceiling; atomically claims the operation ticket when required; changes explicit Reserved -> BoundDetailed or creates the autocommit BoundDetailed lineage under the scoped client key; and constructs `LocalAttemptRegistration {authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>,source_spec_ref,applied_control_ref,reservation_ref?,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>,read_your_writes_basis,request_kind:ExplicitBegin|AutocommitExecute,txn_token,txn_operation_ceiling,autocommit_classification_ref?,registered_snapshot,authority_permit_ref,transaction_error_policy,operation_audit_admission:LocalOperationAuditAdmission::Claimed|NotRequired,registered_at_logical_command_seq}` followed by workspace generation zero and the succeeding `TxnOutcomeRecord::Registered`. A Local token has exactly one attempt; there is no Local attempt-family generation. No statement/storage observation may precede visible registration, with exactly one registered amendment: the fused single-statement autocommit write arm `LocalAutocommitWriteSpec` (§5.2), whose coordinator-local permit verification and admission precede every observation (FG-INV-20 preserved) while durable registration lands atomically with the commit in one sequenced semantic command carrying registration, prepare admission, the ordered final-certification reservation, and commit semantics. The amendment is scoped to exactly that arm and no other: a pre-order crash leaves no durable record, an exact retry re-executes from scratch, and the autocommit idempotency-key CAS at apply guarantees at-most-once durable effect. Both arms decode and byte-match the replay record; ExplicitBegin must match the reservation's same ref, while Autocommit requires request_kind AutocommitExecute and stores the scoped client key and classification before work. Exact lost EXECUTE retry returns the same registration/classification/outcome capability; body or authority drift fails.

`LocalTxnWorkspaceGeneration` is `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>,registration_ref:StrongRef<LocalAttemptRegistration>,authority_relation_to_registration:Exact|Narrowed{nonwidening_proof_ref:StrongRef<AuthorityNonwideningProof>},workspace_generation,predecessor_ref:StrongRef<LocalTxnWorkspaceGeneration>?,through_statement_seq,statement_registration_ref:StrongRef<LocalStatementRegistration>?,published_intent_batch_ref:StrongRef<GraphIntentBatch>?,overlay_root_ref:StrongRef<LocalWorkspaceOverlayRoot>,cumulative_effect_root_ref:StrongRef<LocalCumulativeEffectRoot>,cumulative_read_witness_root_ref:StrongRef<LocalCumulativeReadWitnessRoot>,cumulative_mutation_potential,branch_key_epoch_commitment}`. Generation zero contains the registration's exact header, canonical empty overlay, and ProvenReadOnly potential. Every successor carries the same or a proved narrower complete binding; a policy/revocation/service/principal/purpose/ceiling change without the registered nonwidening proof aborts before observation. `LocalStatementIndex` maps `(registration_identity,statement_seq)` and its scoped idempotency key to the same unique entry `Open{registration_ref:StrongRef<LocalStatementRegistration>}|Published{publication_applied_ref:AppliedControlRef,workspace_generation_ref:StrongRef<LocalTxnWorkspaceGeneration>,output:LocalStatementPublishedOutput}|Failed{abort_applied_ref:AppliedControlRef,stable_failure_class}|Abandoned{abort_applied_ref:AppliedControlRef,typed_reason}`. `LocalStatementRegistrationSpec` binds `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>,registration_ref,exact_next_statement_seq,statement_idempotency_key,classification_ref:StrongRef<CanonicalStatementClassification>,classification_digest,canonical_statement_digest,parameter_digest,requested_result_answer_contract,expected_prior_statement_frontier,expected_workspace_generation_ref,authority_nonwidening_proof_ref?,transaction_error_policy,statement_audit_admission:LocalStatementAuditAdmission::PendingUnclaimed|NotRequired,terminal_audit_gate:LifecycleScaffoldingNotRequired}`. Prepared ownership's typed closure inventory retains preparation, manifest, chunks, nonexpiring delivery policy, resource charge, security binding, and verifier before command order—never an absolute delivery window or already-running client lease. The object names no future command, outcome, applied record, lease, payload, or root; terminal completion consumes it and creates the publication hold, while visible activation later constructs the first lease.

`LocalPrepareAdmissionSpec` is `{registration_ref:StrongRef<LocalAttemptRegistration>,expected_registered_outcome_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeRecord>,admission_generation,expected_statement_frontier,expected_delivery_frontier,expected_statement_index_digest,expected_workspace_generation_ref:StrongRef<LocalTxnWorkspaceGeneration>,expected_cumulative_read_witness_root_ref:StrongRef<LocalCumulativeReadWitnessRoot>,expected_cumulative_effect_root_ref:StrongRef<LocalCumulativeEffectRoot>,local_serialization_certificate_ref:StrongRef<LocalSerializationCertificate>,global_authorization_decision_ref:StrongRef<AuthorizationDecisionRecord>,resource_transition_refs[StrongRef<ResourceLedgerTransition>],operation_audit_admission:LocalOperationAuditAdmission::Claimed|NotRequired,transaction_audit_basis_commitment,finalization_basis_digest,expected_branch_heads[WeakMarkerIdentity],expected_branch_key_epochs,expected_policy_epoch,expected_revocation_index,expected_conflict_index_basis:WeakStateIdentity,terminal_audit_gate:LifecycleScaffoldingNotRequired}`. Apply requires ReadWrite, no Open statement, contiguous terminal statement/delivery frontiers, exact workspace/witness/effect/SSI/security bases, and no prior admission. It constructs immutable `LocalTerminalAdmissionFence::Armed {registration_ref,admission_generation,admission_applied_ref:AppliedControlRef,frozen_statement_delivery_workspace_witness_effect_commitment,frozen_branch_heads,frozen_branch_key_epochs,frozen_resource_and_constraint_commitment,frozen_policy_epoch,frozen_revocation_index,frozen_conflict_basis,operation_audit_claim_commitment,transaction_audit_basis_commitment}` (with no future sequence/HLC), makes the succeeding `TxnOutcomeRecord::PrepareAdmitted` the unique canonical selector of that fence, and atomically replaces the token's Detailed entry.

Only then are the final rebased effect directory, optional `TerminalWriteResultPreparation`, and `TxnOutcomePreparationRecord` constructed. `TxnOutcomePreparationRecord` is `{txn_token,expected_prior_state:PrepareAdmitted{outcome_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeRecord>,terminal_admission_fence_ref:StrongRef<LocalTerminalAdmissionFence>,admission_generation,state_digest},proposed_terminal_kind,final_effect_digest,terminal_write_result:None|Prepared{preparation_ref:StrongRef<TerminalWriteResultPreparation>,required_posture:Local},authorization_decision_ref,resource_transition_refs,terminal_audit_gate}`. Before any terminal audit lock, `LocalFinalCertificationReserveSpec` revalidates the final rebased selection and installs the Active reservation/holds. The audit plan binds that reservation; the stable `CommittedEffectCapsule`, `LogicalDeltaTemplate`, and semantic D1 availability closure include the reservation but no HLC/order observation. After the audit triple is ready, each proposal builds a fresh D1-certified `LocalOrderAttemptInput`; the ordinary `CommitCommand` names both closures. Commit apply requires the exact selected Armed fence and Active reservation whose selection is LocalCommit, atomically consumes the reservation, constructs `LocalTerminalAdmissionFence::TerminalOrdered {predecessor_ref:StrongRef<LocalTerminalAdmissionFence>,final_certification_reservation_ref:StrongRef<LocalFinalCertificationReservation>,commit_command_ref:StrongRef<CommitCommand>,assigned_logical_command_seq,assigned_commit_seq}`, and makes the succeeding pending outcome select the terminal version. Admitted abort analogously requires an Active reservation whose selection is LocalAbort and a fresh terminal order supplement, consumes it, constructs `LocalTerminalAdmissionFence::Released {predecessor_ref:StrongRef<LocalTerminalAdmissionFence>,final_certification_reservation_ref:StrongRef<LocalFinalCertificationReservation>,applied_abort_ref:AppliedAbortRef::LocalTxn,assigned_logical_command_seq}`, and selects it through the succeeding aborted outcome. These are new immutable objects, never mutation of the Armed or reservation bytes; the outcome/reservation index CAS forbids a second successor.

`LocalTerminalCompletionSpec` is `{pending_outcome_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeRecord>,semantic_outcome:SemanticTerminalDescriptor::Local,terminal_public_projection_bundle_ref:StrongRef<TerminalPublicProjectionBundle<Local>>,prebuilt_read_your_writes_issuance_ref:None|Some{StrongRef<ReadYourWritesIssuanceBundle<Local>>},expected_required_postcondition_bitmap,observed_satisfied_postcondition_bitmap,configured_durability_evidence_ref,local_delta_frontier_evidence_ref,result_disposition:NoTerminalResult|ReadTerminalResult{delivery_disposition_proof_ref:StrongRef<ResultDeliveryDispositionProof>}|AutocommitWriteReturning{preparation_ref:StrongRef<TerminalWriteResultPreparation>,required_posture:Local,inline_activation_recipe:InlineResultDeliveryActivationRecipe<Local>?},resource_release_refs[],audit_visibility_evidence_ref,expected_conflict_overlap_floor,terminal_audit_gate}`. It monotonically adds verified bits, validates rather than manufactures the frozen public/capability artifacts, and creates `TerminalReady` only when the required bitmap is exactly satisfied; it cannot alter the semantic outcome. The autocommit-write arm uses `AtomicProtocolDetach` to create the owner, resource transfer/escrow, Protocol retention leaf, and only `{delivery_id,detachment_commitment}` in the semantic frontier. A legal visible inline recipe creates ActiveDeliverable; a visible candidate without one creates ReleasedAwaitingActivation; a hidden candidate creates PendingVisibility. All three satisfy the attempt's independent-retention bit, but only ActiveDeliverable can emit bytes or expire under a delivery lease.

`LocalReadCloseSpec` is `{registration_ref,operation_audit_admission,mode:AutocommitResult{read_access_admission_ref,read_result_release_decision_ref,buffered_result_manifest_ref,canonical_result_digest,result_answer_contract,delivery_policy_ref:StrongRef<ResultDeliveryPolicy<Local>>,inline_activation_recipe:InlineResultDeliveryActivationRecipe<Local>?}|ExplicitClose{expected_statement_frontier,expected_delivery_detachment_frontier,result_disposition_proof_refs[StrongRef<ResultDeliveryDispositionProof>],complete_publication_chain_digest,workspace_generation_ref,cumulative_read_witness_root_ref,zero_cumulative_write_effect_proof_ref,no_open_statement_proof_ref},local_serialization_certificate_ref,expected_conflict_index_basis,terminal_audit_gate}`. Apply advances LogicalCommandSeq/HLC but not CommitSeq, creates ReadClosed and, for autocommit, atomically detaches the result under the same pending/released/inline-active rule; semantic success waits for the later `LocalTerminalCompletionSpec`, whose now-known internal descriptor permits a prebuilt public projection bundle. It never waits for activation or client ACK.

Cancellation before prepare and admitted abort are distinct schemas. `TxnAbortSpec` is only the active/unadmitted lifecycle path `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>,registration_ref:StrongRef<LocalAttemptRegistration>,expected_prior:Registered{outcome_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeRecord>,state_digest},all_open_statement_abort_refs[],result_disposition_proof_refs[StrongRef<ResultDeliveryDispositionProof<Local>>],workspace_release_evidence_refs[],conflict_close_evidence_ref,terminal_abort_authority_ref:StrongRef<TerminalAbortAuthority<Local>>,required_abort_source:ClientRequested|Administrative,resource_release_refs[StrongRef<ResourceLedgerTransition<Local>>],operation_audit_admission,terminal_audit_gate}`. Its terminal-abort authority must use the registered `LifecycleOperation::RequestTerminalAbort{stage:Active}`, and it can never consume a PrepareAdmitted fence or final-certification reservation.

`AdmittedTxnAbortCommand` is the Local transaction-order peer of `CommitCommand`, not a generic ControlCommand: `{command_version,authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>,registration_ref:StrongRef<LocalAttemptRegistration>,terminal_admission_fence_ref:StrongRef<LocalTerminalAdmissionFence>,required_fence_state:Armed,final_certification_reservation_ref:StrongRef<LocalFinalCertificationReservation>,required_reservation_state:Active,required_selection:FinalCertificationSelection::LocalAbort,required_selected_terminal_digest,order_attempt_input_ref:StrongRef<LocalOrderAttemptInput>,required_order_subject:LocalOrderSubject::Terminal{final_certification_reservation_ref,required_state:Active,selected_terminal_digest},order_attempt_availability_certificate_ref:StrongRef<LocalOrderAttemptAvailabilityCertificate>,terminal_abort_authority_ref:StrongRef<TerminalAbortAuthority<Local>>,complete_no_effect_and_release_proof_ref:StrongRef<FinalAbortNoEffectAndReleaseProof<Local>>,resource_release_refs[StrongRef<ResourceLedgerTransition<Local>>],txn_outcome_preparation_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomePreparationRecord>,payload_availability_certificate_ref:StrongRef<PayloadAvailabilityCertificate>,terminal_audit_gate}`. It must byte-match `FinalCertificationSelection::LocalAbort`, including the exact selected-terminal digest; apply atomically marks the supplement Ordered, consumes the Active reservation, selects `LocalTerminalAdmissionFence::Released` with `AppliedAbortRef::LocalTxn` and the assigned logical sequence, terminalizes outcome/conflict state, and releases exactly the proved holds. It cannot race an ordered commit, create a marker/delta/effect, or be synthesized from timeout. The lifecycle matrix adds `RequestTerminalAbort{stage:Active|PrepareAdmitted}` with exact effect classes; the PrepareAdmitted client/admin source feeds `TerminalAbortAuthority`, while correctness-required aborts use their structural reason-specific authority. The later `LocalTerminalCompletionSpec` validates the frozen public projection after either abort outcome exists. The write-result preparation must equal the one retained by `TxnOutcomePreparationRecord`; completion cannot reevaluate or substitute RETURNING bytes.

`LocalOutcomeCompactionSpec` is `NeverRegistered{detailed_outcome_ref,terminal_begin_ref,public_projection_bundle_ref:StrongRef<NeverRegisteredPublicProjectionBundle<Local>>,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>,expected_outcome_index_entry:Detailed,expected_begin_index_entry:NeverRegisteredDetailed,summary_leaf_body,all_retention_and_audit_discharge_evidence}|TerminalReady{detailed_outcome_ref,terminal_public_projection_bundle_ref:StrongRef<TerminalPublicProjectionBundle<Local>>,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>,expected_terminal_public_outcome,expected_outcome_index_entry:Detailed,expected_begin_index_entry:BoundDetailed,summary_leaf_body,result_workspace_conflict_replay_retention_discharge_evidence}`. Apply requires the summary leaf copy the exact frozen public bytes/receipt from the referenced detailed bundle, writes the authenticated leaf, and atomically changes `TxnOutcomeIndex Detailed -> Compacted` together with `LocalBeginIdempotencyIndex NeverRegisteredDetailed -> NeverRegisteredCompacted` or `BoundDetailed -> BoundCompacted`; both compact arms retain the same replay/bundle evidence, and status/acceptance retry bytes remain identical. `LocalOutcomeExpirySpec` is the distinct ordered transition `{capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>,summary_root_ref:StrongRef<LocalTxnOutcomeSummaryRoot>,leaf_key_digest,expected_outcome_index_entry:Compacted,expected_begin_index_entry:BoundCompacted|NeverRegisteredCompacted,time_validation_evidence_ref:StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>,expected_verifier_key_and_profile_floors,expected_begin_retry_and_lookup_floors,permanent_tombstone_body,terminal_audit_freeze:AuditFreezeField::Required<LocalControl>,terminal_audit_gate}`. Evidence must classify the replay record's exact window Expired for this action and every advertised retry/lookup floor must be closed. Apply atomically changes both indexes to authenticated `ExpiredTombstone` values containing token/key/capability commitments and evidence digest, drops the replay/bundle edges only there, and permanently prevents key/token reuse; valid old bytes return TokenExpired while invalid/unauthorized input remains NotVisibleOrUnknown. The construction DAG is fixed: registration -> workspace zero -> outcome; statement successor workspace and manifest -> publication spec/command -> applied publication/detachment/outcome -> payload/record/root; prepare-admission outcome/fence -> final effect directory and optional terminal write-result preparation -> outcome preparation/capsule/prepared ownership -> unchanged `CommitCommand` -> marker/delta/pending outcome -> external audit batch and visibility release -> terminal projection bundle/completion -> optional output activation. No input names its future applied record, payload, command record, root, lease, marker, or summary leaf.

`GenerationRootRef` is the posture-closed union `Local{generation_root:StrongRef}` or `Distributed{manifest_ref:StrongRef<DistributedDerivedGenerationManifest>}`. `DerivedGenerationRegistry` maps a full `DerivedIdentity` strong reference to `{generation_root:GenerationRootRef,global_frontier?,answer_contract:AnswerContract,retention_class,status:Building|Active|Retiring}` and never reconstructs a singular graph/head/schema key. `ShardDerivedComponent` binds `{derived_identity_ref,shard_id,topology_epoch,input_global_batch_interval,resulting_global_frontier,partition_and_authority_coverage,answer_contract,component_root:StrongRef}`; `ShardDerivedComponentCertificate` adds `SameGroupCertificateHeader`, availability/retention floors, and quorum signatures. A meta-local `DistributedDerivedGenerationManifest` is `{derived_identity_ref,topology_state_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,exact_global_frontier,sorted_component_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardDerivedComponentCertificate>],complete_partition_and_authority_commitment,answer_contract,build_policy_epoch}`. Shard build/advance controls root components in `shard_derived_component_registry_root`; a meta activation control changes `Active` only after every required certified component at one topology/frontier exists. Partial, stale-topology, or mixed-frontier generations remain nonqueryable, and reads use the exact fallback path when the active manifest is missing. Checkpoint/configuration floors, remote grants, topology transfer, backup/replay, and GC retain every Building/Active/Retiring generation through its terminal transition.

## Ownership, verification, and diagnostics
For every schema, field, tag, state, transition, reference, digest transcript, construction-order rule, and role restriction in this slice, generate a durable_fields.toml row with stable IDs; canonical encoding/version policy; concrete generic/role expansion; producer, owner bead/crate, and consumers; reference strength/target set; authority and redaction class; invariant/evidence/cost bindings; test/scenario/event IDs; and consuming gate. Cross-slice targets use stable catalog IDs and must resolve in the Appendix A epic closure. Downstream owners may add implementation detail but cannot abbreviate, alias, weaken, or contradict these bytes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The embedded line range is byte-complete, checksum-pinned, continuous with adjacent slices, and contains no truncation marker.
- Every exact named construct in the slice has one stable row and exactly one granular implementation owner; all references and consumers resolve.
- Unit tests cover canonical encode/decode, stable field/tag IDs, role/generic expansion, digest construction, state preconditions, and owner uniqueness.
- Property/mutation/fuzz tests remove, duplicate, reorder, retag, corrupt, weaken, or cross-role substitute every field/arm/reference class and prove rejection.
- Simulation tests exercise applicable crash, cancellation, retry, sent-unknown, receipt-first, recovery, authority/configuration rotation, compaction, and expiry boundaries.
- E2E scripts traverse each applicable public embedded/server/FGP/CLI path through durable publication, restart/replay, backup/restore, and terminal cleanup using isolated synthetic fixtures.
- Detailed versioned JSONL diagnostics carry schema_id, field_or_arm_id, role/group, object or public commitment, transition_id, state_before/state_after, checker, verdict, artifact refs, and replay command; secret/noninterference tests reject protected data or observable hidden state.
- Cross-version golden vectors and unknown-required-field fixtures enforce additive-minor/breaking-major policy; no gate passes with an uncovered row.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: family-level prose summaries, wildcard references, inferred fields, unregistered aliases, or treating the catalog slice as the implementation. Exactness is intentional; execution remains decomposed across the linked workstream beads.

QUALIFIED-ARM IDENTITY CHECK — VERDICT: THE SIX ARE REFERENCES, NOT UNIONS. MINT NOTHING FOR THEM. Read-only, no token, run before writing a single row. Also corrects my own hypothesis about which class they belong to.

=== 1. WHAT THE SOURCE ACTUALLY SPELLS ===
Six a03 member unions came out of the census carrying ::-qualified arms. The plan text at their sites:
    1482  operation_audit_admission:LocalOperationAuditAdmission::PendingUnclaimed|NotRequired
    1484  operation_audit_admission:LocalOperationAuditAdmission::PendingUnclaimed|NotRequired
    1484  operation_audit_admission:LocalOperationAuditAdmission::Claimed|NotRequired
    1486  statement_audit_admission:LocalStatementAuditAdmission::PendingUnclaimed|NotRequired
    1486  statement_audit_admission:LocalStatementAuditAdmission::Claimed|NotRequired
    1488  statement_audit_admission:LocalStatementAuditAdmission::Claimed|NotRequired
    1528  operation_audit_admission:LocalOperationAuditAdmission::Claimed|NotRequired
And the parent, defined ONCE at plan line 1470:
    `LocalOperationAuditAdmission` is `NotRequired{evidence:NonRequiredAuditEvidence}
      |PendingUnclaimed{ticket_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicket>,ticket_admission_record_ref:StrongCommandRef,
        operation_request_basis_commitment}
      |Claimed{ticket_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicket>,claim_record_ref:StrongRef<LocalAuditTicketClaimRecord>,
        owner:LocalAuditTicketOwner::Operation,operation_request_basis_commitment}`
THE DECISIVE OBSERVATION: `NotRequired` — the SECOND arm at every one of the six sites — is itself one of the parent's three variants. The `::` qualifier is written once and the sibling relies on context. So each site is a 2-of-3 NARROWING of one existing closed union, not a new two-arm type. Three distinct subsets appear: {PendingUnclaimed,NotRequired} and {Claimed,NotRequired}.
Minting these as six [[union]] rows would create six duplicate types over two parents, and would also collide on names — my first naming pass produced OperationAuditAdmission x3 and StatementAuditAdmission x3, which duplicate logical schema names and fail G0 outright. The collision was the symptom; this is the cause.

=== 2. I HAVE TO CORRECT MY OWN FRAMING: THIS IS NOT THE fgdb-a9c8 CLASS ===
I flagged these as the a9c8 variant-qualified class. That was a hypothesis and inspection refutes it. a9c8 was about `StrongRef<Enum::Variant>` — a variant-qualified strong REFERENCE, which the plan normatively forbade and which was repaired by rewriting the source to `StrongRef<Family>` plus a mandatory arm predicate. Our six contain no StrongRef at all; they are member TYPE expressions naming a subset of a closed union's variants. Related in shape, different in kind, and the a9c8 remedy (rewrite the source) does not transfer — nothing here is prohibited. Also note a9c8's cited coordinate has drifted: grepping the current plan for its `Enum::Variant` prohibition text returns nothing, so that wording has moved or been reworded since 2026-07-22. Do not navigate by a9c8's line numbers.

=== 3. AN ASYMMETRY THAT SPLITS THE SIX, AND CHANGES THE REMEDY FOR HALF ===
The two parents are NOT in the same state, which is invisible unless you check both:
    LocalOperationAuditAdmission ... structurally defined at 1470; census emits it as a union
                                     candidate PLUS its three arms (4 census rows). MINTABLE as a
                                     parent union; the three operation_audit_admission sites can then
                                     be modelled as narrowed references to it.
    LocalStatementAuditAdmission ... defined ONLY by prose analogy at 1470 — "has the analogous
                                     NotRequired/PendingUnclaimed/Claimed forms with
                                     LocalAuditTicketOwner::Statement". NO structural body anywhere.
                                     Census emits ZERO union candidates for it.
    CONTROL, same probe, same run: LocalAuditTicketOwner returns 4 (union + 3 arms), so the probe
    does find parents that exist. A zero here is real absence, not a broken query.
So the three statement_audit_admission sites reference a parent that has no landable body — the same "referenced but never structurally rendered" class as RootManifest and LogicalCommandRecord in the epic's C4 bucket. They cannot be modelled against a landed parent union until that parent acquires a body, which is a source question and not a modelling choice. Had I minted, I would have invented LocalStatementAuditAdmission's three arms out of a prose sentence.

=== 4. WHAT THIS DOES TO THE a03 WORK-LIST ===
a03 is a from-scratch slice: 49 of 49 union candidates and 129 of 129 arm candidates unlanded.
    17  top-level unions, union_name = containing schema, mechanical
    26  nested member unions that are genuinely new types and need a chosen, globally unique union_name
     3  operation_audit_admission narrowings -> model as references to LocalOperationAuditAdmission
     3  statement_audit_admission narrowings -> BLOCKED on a parent with no structural body
The census pin (union_candidate_count = 49) does not move: these remain census CANDIDATES either way. What changes is how each is discharged — a target row for a real union, versus a reference/adjudication for a narrowing. The coverage law accepts a target, an approved adjudication, or a covering arm/wire interior contract, so the narrowings need one of the latter two rather than a [[union]] row.
NOT YET ESTABLISHED, and I am not guessing: which of those two discharge forms the checker actually accepts for a narrowing, and whether the catalog has an existing row shape that expresses "member admits a named subset of a parent union's variants". That is the next measurement and it should be made before any row is written. Also unresolved: `LocalAuditTicketOwner::Operation` and `::Statement` appear as single-variant pins inside the parent's own arm bodies at 1470 — a seventh site of the same construct, one variant rather than a subset, which the same answer should cover.

=== 5. WHY THIS CHECK WAS WORTH RUNNING BEFORE WRITING ===
It cost one read-only probe and no token. Without it the increment would have minted six duplicate union types over two parents, three of them with arms invented from a prose analogy, and the G0 name-collision failure would have surfaced only after the rows and their projections were written — i.e. after the expensive part. The naming collision was the tell, and the right response to a mechanical rule producing duplicates is to ask whether the things are actually distinct, not to disambiguate the names.

a03 UNION WRITE ATTEMPTED AND REVERTED — I MIS-SEQUENCED THE SLICE. The unions cannot land first; the identity kinds must. Measured with a rebuilt checker, catalog restored byte-identical to HEAD, token released. Not a u3gr-style wall — ordered work I put in the wrong order.

=== 1. WHAT I BUILT AND INSERTED ===
Generated the 17 top-level a03 unions (containing_schema == union_path, so union_name is mechanical and needs no naming judgment) plus their 46 arms in SOURCE order, plus the 63 matching [[target]] rows that catalog_projection_target_missing requires. Row-id derivation was controlled against three landed rows before generating anything: sha256("union|{cs}|{up}")[:16] and sha256("arm|{cs}|{up}|{arm}")[:16], kebab of union_name (not containing_schema) for the nested case, and generic signatures flattened into the kebab. All three controls exact. Arm tags came from ArmCandidate source positions, never the census's sorted arm_names print — that ordering differs and would have mis-tagged.
Counts after insertion reconciled exactly: union 32 -> 49, union_arm 77 -> 123, target 552 -> 615.

=== 2. WHY IT CANNOT LOAD — THE PREREQUISITE I MISSED ===
    17  projection_ordinary_union_unresolved_schema
    80  projection_ordinary_union_wire_contract_mismatch
     4  pin drift (projection_row_count, projection_registry_assignment_drift,
        projection_owner_assignment_drift, catalog_target_source_assignment_drift)
identity.rs:2018 requires a union's containing_schema to resolve in EXACTLY ONE identity class (logical, physical, bootstrap, prebootstrap, wire). Measured: 0 of my 17 owners resolve in ANY class. a03 has 89 top-level candidates and only 2 landed logical kinds, so essentially nothing this slice's unions hang off is registered yet.
identity.rs:2029-2074 then requires each top-level ordinary union to be backed EITHER by a same-name logical kind parent with identical lifecycle, a bound within the object bound, no broader role scope and self-only containing-schema closure, OR by a same-name union/discriminant WIRE parent with identical lifecycle, max size and closure — plus one wire variant per arm, with parent kind "discriminant" iff every arm is unit and "union" otherwise.
So the correct order for this slice is: MINT THE IDENTITY KINDS -> then the unions -> then the arms. That is exactly the order the a16 lane used ("mint the core time-plane logical kinds", then "mint the ten unreserved union hosts and complete all fourteen top-level role unions"). I went straight for the unions.

=== 3. THE REAL SHAPE OF THE NEXT INCREMENT ===
Per owner, two decisions that are NOT mechanical and should not be rushed:
  (a) IDENTITY CLASS — logical kind (an independently addressable durable object) versus wire type (an embedded value schema). This is a source-reading judgment per owner and it determines which of the two backing laws applies. Of the 17: names like LocalBeginIdempotencyIndex and LocalStatementIndex read as durable objects; DeliveryTransitionAppliedRef, ResultManifestRef, ResultActivationAppliedRef and LocalAuditTicketOwner read as embedded value schemas. I have NOT verified any of these against the source and am not guessing.
  (b) CODE ASSIGNMENT — fresh codes above 0x051d, minted directly, with no reservation for a non-StrongRef family (the reservation bijection law). Mint at status="reserved": activating a logical kind trips the compile-time assertions in crates/fgdb-types/src/refs.rs, which include_bytes! the projection and count active rows.
If the wire path is chosen for a union, its 46 arms additionally need one wire VARIANT row each, and the parent's kind must match the arm payload shape.

=== 4. METHOD NOTE — I NEARLY REPORTED MAIN AS RED OFF A STALE BINARY ===
My first run of the inserted catalog reported 105 violations including reservation epoch/assignment drift, and the reverted catalog still reported 7 against a tree that git said was byte-identical to HEAD. Both were artifacts: the probe binary was linked against an rlib built at the start of the session, which bakes in the EXPECTED_* counts and pin literals. Rebuilt from HEAD's own source, HEAD loads clean (LOAD_OK, 552 targets) and registry-check all exits 0, and the inserted catalog reports 101 rather than 105 — the four reservation/epoch entries were pure instrument noise.
The substantive 97 (17 + 80) are identical under both binaries, because they come from identity.rs structural logic rather than from pinned constants, which is why the conclusion survives. But the near-miss is the point: I was one step from filing "main is red" against a correct tree. Rule that caught it, and it is already on the a15/ovok trails: when a cached tool tells you the DATA is broken, control the TOOL first. Rebuild the rlib at the start of every hold and after every checker edit; never carry one across holds.

=== 5. STATE ===
registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml restored byte-identical to HEAD (git diff empty over registries/ and tools/). Catalog token released. Nothing half-applied. The generated 17 unions / 46 arms / 63 targets are staged off-repo and remain valid input for whoever does the mint increment first — they will need no regeneration, only the kinds landing ahead of them.
NOT ESTABLISHED, deliberately: the identity class of any of the 17 owners, and whether the checker accepts a narrowing (the six ::-qualified members from my earlier verdict) as a target, an approved adjudication, or a covering arm/wire interior contract. Both are read-only measurements and both should precede the next write.

description:
Five source-exact A03 fields under already registered non-wire hosts are rejected solely by the registered wire consumer closure:

- LocalAuditTicketClaimRecord.owner: LocalAuditTicketOwner
- ResultDeliveryPolicy<Role>.manifest_ref: ResultManifestRef
- ResultDeliveryPolicy<Role>.service_authority: ResultDeliveryServiceAuthority
- LocalResultDeliveryLease.owner: LocalResultDeliveryOwner
- LocalResultDeliveryLease.activation_applied_ref: ResultActivationAppliedRef

Each candidate was synthesized with the source-order field tag, identity_class inline under the settled l6xd law, reference_semantics none, and construction_order exactly equal to its containing logical kind. validate_identity returned only wire_context_mismatch for each. In the same probe, eight sibling source-exact fields passed and form the immediately landable A03 beneficiary tranche, so this is not a class convention or malformed-probe artifact.

The registered closures are append-only durable contracts: the first four types are self-only, while ResultActivationAppliedRef admits itself and ResultDeliveryLease but not LocalResultDeliveryLease. Do not widen these allowlists merely to make the source rows pass. Resolution requires an explicit source/census correction or an append-only consumer-contract repair/history witness, followed by the same candidate probe.

Exit: resolve all five source/registered-consumer contradictions explicitly; rerun validate_identity with the exact candidate rows; land only rows accepted without weakening the durable closure law.
close_reason: Resolved in 9056b2e: five source-forced inline fields landed after exact nonvacuous wire/ordinary-union consumer-closure repair; 5/5 narrow-removal and 5/5 unrelated-host controls fired wire_context_mismatch.
