title: Appendix A exact catalog: Key destruction, backup, publication, and release formats
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the exact Appendix A catalog slice for Key destruction, backup, publication, and release formats. This task embeds source-plan lines 2057-2156 verbatim, expands every generic and role-indexed family into stable registered rows, and assigns each row to its granular implementation owner. It is a format/ownership contract, not a substitute implementation.

## Exact normative contract
The following audited source-plan text is authoritative and self-contained:

**KeyWrap / KeyDestroyRecord / BackupManifest.** `KeyWrap` binds `{database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,logical_oid,ciphertext_id,dek_id,scope:Recipient|Database|BranchEpoch{graph,branch,write_epoch,object_creation_boundary:ObjectCreationBoundary}|Replica|Backup,wrap_algorithm,wrap_key_id,wrap_key_epoch,wrapped_dek,aad_bytes,aad_digest,issuer_signature}`; BranchEpoch AAD is exactly the branch-object transcript, while every other scope has its own registered transcript. Namespace-key escrow uses separately typed `ObjectIdKeyWrap` for `K_oid`. Rewrap creates only a new wrap; re-encryption creates a new CiphertextId and EncodingId realizations. `KeyDestroyFloorRef` is `Checkpoint{checkpoint_ref:StrongRef<RecoveryCheckpoint>}|Configuration{floor_ref:StrongRef<ConfigPayloadFloor>}` and `KeyDestroyExternalAckRef` is `Backup{ack_ref:StrongRef<BackupKeyReleaseAck>}|LegalHold{ack_ref:StrongRef<LegalHoldReleaseAck>}|RemoteConsumer{ack_ref:StrongRef<RemoteKeyConsumerReleaseAck>}`. `KeyDestructionTarget` is the closed union `KmsKeyVersion{kms_authority_id,key_uri,key_version}|HsmObject{hsm_cluster_id,slot_id,object_handle_digest}|StorageMemberReplica{consensus_domain,member_id,material_class,material_identity_digest}`; canonical target identity is `H(domain,canonical(target))`. `KeyDestructionOperationPlan` is `{operation_id,idempotency_token_digest,target:KeyDestructionTarget,canonical_request_transcript_digest,required_receipt_profile_oid}` and plans are sorted by target identity with no duplicate target or operation ID.

`KeyDestroyProposal` is the pre-order body `{key_identity,expected_key_state:RetainedDecryptOnly,basis_state:WeakStateIdentity,expected_current_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,expected_prospective_configuration_set_digest,exact_root_slot_generations,checkpoint_and_configuration_floor_refs[KeyDestroyFloorRef],generated_scanned_root_inventory_ref:StrongRef<KeyReferenceInventory>,zero_reference_proof_ref:StrongRef<ZeroReferenceProof>,backup_legal_hold_and_external_consumer_ack_refs[KeyDestroyExternalAckRef],threshold_authorization_ref:StrongRef<KeyDestructionAuthorization>,sorted_destruction_operation_plans[KeyDestructionOperationPlan],complete_target_set_digest,expected_state_conditions,terminal_audit_gate}`. The generated inventory includes every branch epoch, envelope node/root/grant, advancing-grant obligation, reachable ciphertext/wrap/opener, prepared/certificate/audit/outcome/result/workspace/replay/DP/backup, current or prospective configuration, and signing/verifier dependency. Apply atomically installs `KeyReferenceQuarantine {key_identity,quarantine_generation,proposal_identity:WeakDigest,installed_at_logical_command_seq,target_set_digest,no_new_reference_rule_id}` and one immutable Semantic `ExternalKeyDestructionOperationRecord {operation_id,key_identity,quarantine_ref:StrongRef<KeyReferenceQuarantine>,target:KeyDestructionTarget,idempotency_token_digest,canonical_request_transcript_digest,required_receipt_profile_oid,state:AuthorizedUndispatchedRecipe,source_command_ref:StrongRef<ControlCommand>,assigned_logical_command_seq}` for every and only plan, then moves the key to `DestroyPending`. This record is an authorization recipe, never a mutable physical-status record. The canonical operation-root map is keyed by target identity and proves a plan/record bijection.

Only after the quarantine's role-valid `CanonicalPublicationEvidence<Role>` exists may `KeyDestructionDispatchInitializeSpec` create one Protocol `IrreversibleDispatchAttempt<KeyDestruction>::Armed` per authorization recipe. `KeyDestructionDispatchMarkSentUnknownSpec` durably advances an attempt before transport eligibility. The generated `KeyDestructionDispatchGuard` then rereads both RootSlots, the complete current Semantic/Protocol/Prepared/Consensus inventory, the exact key quarantine and no-new-reference proof, current/prospective configurations, writer fence, continuity head, service/security authority, target provider profile, and time evidence, and acquires the registered destruction hold immediately before the byte-identical request is submitted. KMS, HSM, and storage-member provider profiles must expose authenticated idempotent registration/status and monotonic terminal evidence; an unsupported provider cannot be configured as a destruction target. Recovery queries the same operation ID first, and a signed NotRegistered response permits only the same request under a fresh guard. `KeyDestructionReceiptImportSpec` moves the Protocol attempt to TerminalReceiptImported. Timeout, local expiry, provider ambiguity, or process death neither retries with a new ID nor implies destruction.

Key-destruction terminal evidence is target-typed. `ExternalKeyDestructionProviderReceipt` is the KMS/HSM-issued portable `{external_request_binding:ExternalActionRequestBinding{action_kind=KeyDestruction},target:KmsKeyVersion|HsmObject,destruction_result:Destroyed{target_terminal_counter,provider_evidence_digest}|AlreadyDestroyed{matching_prior_operation_id,target_terminal_counter,provider_evidence_digest},completed_at:AuthorityInstant,time_authority_profile_oid,provider_key_id,provider_key_epoch,signature}`. `AlreadyDestroyed` is accepted only when provider evidence cryptographically binds the same target and canonical request lineage. A current member imports it through `ExternalKeyDestructionReceiptImportRecord {operation_record_ref,dispatch_attempt_identity,portable_receipt_ref:StrongRef<ExternalKeyDestructionProviderReceipt>,current_configuration_writer_fence_and_authority_commitment,imported_at_maintenance_index,body_digest}` before any completion transition.

`StorageMemberKeyDestructionReceipt` is the same-group member-issued `{header:FenceBoundIrreversibleReceiptHeader,operation_id,idempotency_token_digest,target:StorageMemberReplica,canonical_request_transcript_digest,key_material_identity_and_inventory_digest,pre_operation_physical_root_digest,post_operation_physical_root_digest,destroyed_or_crypto_erased_probe_digest,member_monotonic_counter,completion_counter,completed_at:AuthorityInstant,time_authority_profile_oid,member_signature}`. Its header proves the exact current configuration/member/writer/quarantine fence and that Started was durable before the first irreversible byte/key action; it is imported through `StorageMemberKeyDestructionReceiptImportRecord` under that same group. An external-provider receipt cannot stand for a storage member, and a member fence receipt cannot stand for KMS/HSM authority. `KeyDestructionTerminalReceiptRef` is the closed union `ExternalProvider{receipt_ref,import_record_ref}|StorageMember{receipt_ref,import_record_ref}` with target-discriminant equality. `TargetCompletionBijectionProof` binds the proposal target-set digest, canonical operation-root digest, sorted typed terminal receipt/import identities, and proves exactly one valid matching arm per target/operation with no missing, extra, duplicate, substituted, or conflicting result.

`PortableKeyDestructionDispatchTerminalEvidence` is the independently verifiable, Protocol-object-identity-free `{dispatch_contract_id,key_identity,quarantine_generation,source_publication_evidence_commitment,operation_plan_and_authorization_recipe_commitment,sorted_terminal_attempt_and_receipt_commitments,complete_target_bijection_commitment,provider_status_lineage_commitment,configuration_fence_continuity_and_authority_commitment,signer_set_epoch,canonical_signatures}`. Its source commitment is over the exact role-valid `CanonicalPublicationEvidence<Role>`; it is not hard-coded to a Local/Meta visibility certificate. `KeyDestroyFinalizeSpec` is `{proposal_ref:StrongRef<KeyDestroyProposal>,expected_quarantine_ref:StrongRef<KeyReferenceQuarantine>,quarantine_publication_evidence:CanonicalPublicationEvidence<Role>,sorted_operation_record_refs[StrongRef<ExternalKeyDestructionOperationRecord>],dispatch_terminal_evidence_ref:StrongRef<PortableKeyDestructionDispatchTerminalEvidence>,typed_terminal_receipt_refs[KeyDestructionTerminalReceiptRef],target_completion_bijection_proof_ref:StrongRef<TargetCompletionBijectionProof>,exact_current_role_payload_and_root_slot_identities,current_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,current_prospective_configuration_set_digest,current_complete_generated_root_inventory_ref:StrongRef<KeyReferenceInventory>,current_zero_reference_recomputation_ref:StrongRef<ZeroReferenceProof>,no_new_reference_since_quarantine_proof_ref:StrongRef<NoNewKeyReferenceProof>,expected_state_conditions,terminal_audit_gate}`. It requires current-root/configuration/slot equality or a registered quarantine-preserving successor proof, zero retaining references, byte-matching role-valid quarantine publication evidence, the exact proposal/recipe/Protocol-terminal/typed-receipt bijection, and no raw Protocol reference. Apply selects `DestroyedPendingCertificate` and creates compact `KeyDestroyRecord {key_identity,quarantine_generation,proposal_identity:WeakDigest,finalize_spec_identity:WeakDigest,complete_target_set_digest,operation_and_receipt_commitment,verified_current_inventory_digest,applied_finalize_identity:WeakAuthorityAppliedIdentity,terminal_audit_commitment}`; the record has no strong path to proposal, finalize, receipts, scanned inventories, old floors, Protocol attempts, or a future certificate.

Only after that record, its resulting durable root, and its required audit visibility advance exist may the current quorum create `KeyDestructionCertificate {SameGroupCertificateHeader,key_identity,quarantine_generation,key_destroy_record_ref:StrongRef<KeyDestroyRecord>,post_finalize_state_root_ref:StrongRef<LogicalStateRoot>,operation_and_receipt_commitment,verified_current_inventory_digest,finalize_visibility_certificate_ref:StrongRef<PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Local>>,certificate_attempt_ref:StrongRef<CertificateAttemptRecord>,canonical_signature_set}`. The Meta analogue uses `PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Meta>` through the generated role arm. `KeyDestroyCertificatePublishSpec {key_destroy_record_ref:StrongRef<KeyDestroyRecord>,certificate_ref:StrongRef<KeyDestructionCertificate>,expected_key_state:DestroyedPendingCertificate,expected_quarantine_generation,expected_current_state:WeakStateIdentity,terminal_audit_gate}` is the sole transition to final `Destroyed` and installs a compact certificate-index edge. Heavy inputs remain owned by the key lifecycle and certificate ledgers until publication's audit visibility advance plus an activated cut; compact result/receipt commitment/certificate remain through the crypto-erasure evidence floor. No state reaches final `Destroyed` if any reachable or independently obligated object can still require the key, any target lacks a receipt, or the certificate is absent.

Backup content and publication-envelope references are distinct identity classes. `BackupSourceIdentity<T> {source_authority_domain:ConsensusDomain,source_cluster_incarnation,object_kind,object_id,canonical_digest}` is nonretaining evidence and is never accepted by local or remote mark traversal. `BackupContentSubject<T>` is the closed union `SourceObject{expected_source:BackupSourceIdentity<T>}|RecoveryProjection{backup_id,projection_digest}`; generated type/kind rows make `RecoveryProjection` legal only for `T=BackupRecoveryProjection`. A manifest body, signature set, manifest, publication receipt, or transparency proof is never smuggled into this union: those objects are constructed only after the content-inventory root is fixed.

The root-free `BackupInventoryEntryRef<T>` is `{backup_id,archive_authority_id,inventory_key,subject:BackupContentSubject<T>,archived_byte_digest,archived_length,protection_profile,required_recovery_proof_class}`. It can be embedded while the final inventory root is not yet known. The externally resolvable content reference `BackupArchiveRef<T>` is `{entry:BackupInventoryEntryRef<T>,content_archive_inventory_root_digest,inventory_leaf_index,inventory_inclusion_proof}` and is constructed only after the final content inventory exists. Its proof must authenticate the exact entry under that root and a current matching archive-retention grant. Live source entries use `SourceObject`; the recovery projection uses its dedicated arm.

Publication-envelope artifacts use the disjoint portable `BackupPublicationArtifactRef<T> {backup_id,publication_bundle_id,archive_authority_id,artifact_kind:ManifestBody|ManifestSignatureSet|Manifest,expected_canonical_digest,expected_length,authenticated_locator,publication_receipt_digest,receipt_artifact_index}`. Generated type/kind rows make each artifact tag legal only for its exact `T`. Resolution requires the separately supplied authentic `BackupPublicationReceipt`, byte-equality with the indexed locator/digest/length row in that receipt, and a current matching `ArchiveRetentionGrant`; the reference is not a content-inventory leaf and contains no content-inventory inclusion proof. The receipt itself and any later transparency inclusion are carried by their own portable evidence types and cannot self-locate through a future receipt.

Portable recovery is specified by one plane-complete object rather than inferred from inventory names. `RecoverySlotDisposition` is the closed union `TransformCurrent|CarryPriorEvidence|RecreateCurrentAuthority|ReconcileExternal|SuspendProtocolOwner|DiscardReplicaLocal{registered_law_id}|Reject`. `PortableRoleRecoveryCut<Role>` is `{role_and_group,source_manifest_identity,source_slot_generation_and_digest,semantic_cut:{applied_state:BackupInventoryRoleStateRef<Role>,visible_state:BackupInventoryRoleStateRef<Role>,applied_and_visible_positions},protocol_cut:{protocol_state:BackupInventoryRoleProtocolStateRef<Role>,maintenance_generation_and_index,audit_pipeline_and_pending_queue_inventory:StructurallyInapplicable|Present{inventory_entry_ref},result_cursor_artifact_error_escrow_inventory,security_barrier_state},prepared_cut:{prepared_root:BackupInventoryRolePreparedRef<Role>,live_owner_inventory},consensus_cut:{applied_cut_snapshot,retained_suffix,configuration,certificate_and_attempt_ledgers,remote_obligation_floors},checkpoint_and_floor_cut,external_continuity_reconciliation_inputs,bootstrap_reconstruction_inputs,sorted_slot_dispositions[{slot:DurableStateSlotRef,disposition:RecoverySlotDisposition}],complete_durable_state_slot_coverage_proof,body_digest}`. The `BackupInventoryRole*Ref` families are generated closed role-specific unions over exact root-free `BackupInventoryEntryRef<T>` targets; no erased archive ref and no final inventory-root digest is legal inside the projection.

`BackupRecoveryProjection` is `Local{common,local_cut:PortableRoleRecoveryCut<Local>}|Sharded{common,meta_cut:PortableRoleRecoveryCut<Meta>,sorted_shard_cuts[PortableRoleRecoveryCut<Shard>],exact_global_barrier_and_partition_bijection_proof}`. Every activated `durable_state_slots.toml` row and mandatory inventory class has exactly one disposition. Same-identity recovery preserves applied/visible divergence, the exact pending audit queue, independent output owners, prepared owners, and maintenance suffix. Clone requires either a certified `CloneExportReady` cut with no applied-hidden barrier or an explicit exclude/transfer/reissue disposition for every hidden entry; it may never make source hidden state target-visible. Old transport leases/capabilities restore as suspended/no-send until fresh target authorization and time evidence, and source Raft hard state is historical evidence rather than current target consensus state.

`BackupManifestBody` is `{backup_id,database_id,database_security_namespace_id,source_cluster_incarnation,source_posture:Local|Sharded,barrier,backup_state:BackupState,exact_logical_commit_base_and_anti_rollback_ranges,content_archive_inventory_root_digest,content_archive_inventory_count,recovery_projection_ref:BackupArchiveRef<BackupRecoveryProjection>,recovery_projection_digest,branch_checkpoint_history_prepared_certificate_key_derived_trust_continuity_cursor_delivery_replay_inventories,object_id_key_escrow_policy,recipient_policy,format_matrix,canonical_semantic_digest,trust_policy,transparency_policy:NotRequired{policy_digest}|Required{log_id,minimum_checkpoint_policy_oid},prior_transparency_checkpoint?}`. Construction order is exact and acyclic: build/archive every source object and its root-free entry -> build/archive `BackupRecoveryProjection` from only those entries -> add its root-free RecoveryProjection entry -> compute the final content-inventory root and inclusion proofs -> construct all rooted `BackupArchiveRef` values -> construct `BackupManifestBody`. Publication-envelope objects are excluded from this content inventory and are built later. Body construction verifies the projection's slot bitmap/digest and every rooted ref proof against the fixed inventory. `BackupManifestSignatureSet` is `{body_ref:StrongRef<BackupManifestBody>,body_digest,signature_policy_oid,signer_set_epoch,configuration_chain_digest,canonical_sorted_signers[{signer_id,signing_key_id,key_epoch}],threshold,canonical_signing_transcript_digest,canonical_signature_set}`; the transcript binds the complete body bytes/digest and signer identities/keys/epochs. `BackupManifest` is exactly `{body_ref:StrongRef<BackupManifestBody>,signature_set_ref:StrongRef<BackupManifestSignatureSet>,body_digest,signature_set_digest,manifest_format_major,manifest_format_minor}` and contains no self digest, receipt, inclusion, grant, or reopen proof. Its canonical digest is computed only after encoding and becomes a later object's field.

`PortableRecoveryLocator` is the bounded reference-free signed closed union `ArchiveObject{provider_authority_id,locator_profile_oid,opaque_locator_bytes:BoundedBytes<4096>,target_artifact_kind,target_artifact_canonical_digest,expected_archived_byte_digest,expected_length,access_scope_commitment,locator_digest,provider_locator_signature}|KmsWrap{provider_authority_id,locator_profile_oid,opaque_locator_bytes:BoundedBytes<4096>,key_or_wrap_identity_commitment,recipient_and_ceremony_commitment,locator_digest,provider_locator_signature}|HsmObject{...same exact common fields plus nonexportable_object_commitment...}|ThresholdEscrow{...same exact common fields plus participant_set_and_threshold_commitment...}`. Opaque bytes are actionable provider input, not a digest masquerading as a locator; their digest, provider, kind, profile, target, scope, and signature are always present and cross-action substitution is invalid.

`BackupRecoveryBootstrapDescriptor` is constructed before publication and is the bounded portable public `{backup_id,publication_bundle_id,leakage_class:RestoreBootstrapMetadata,manifest_artifacts[{artifact_kind:ManifestBody|ManifestSignatureSet|Manifest,canonical_digest,length,ciphertext_id,encoding_id,archive_locator:PortableRecoveryLocator::ArchiveObject,key_opener_locators[PortableRecoveryLocator::KmsWrap|HsmObject|ThresholdEscrow],decoder_profile_oid}],recovery_projection_bootstrap:{content_inventory_entry_identity_and_digest,archived_byte_digest,length,ciphertext_id,encoding_id,archive_locator:PortableRecoveryLocator::ArchiveObject,key_opener_locators[PortableRecoveryLocator::KmsWrap|HsmObject|ThresholdEscrow],decoder_profile_oid},content_archive_inventory_root_digest,descriptor_digest}`. Locator bytes are deterministic/preallocated under the publication bundle and provider contract before the request is Armed; a provider that cannot honor them refuses without effect rather than substituting a location. The descriptor exposes only identities, sizes, cipher/encoding IDs, bounded opaque provider locators, wrapped-key/escrow locators, and decoder profiles—not plaintext, keys, graph contents, or the full object inventory. Restore must later byte-match it against the publication receipt and decrypted signed manifest/inventory; mismatch is a permanent acquisition failure.

`BackupPublicationRequestBinding` is the canonical external request `{external_request_binding:ExternalActionRequestBinding{action_kind=BackupPublishEnvelope},backup_id,publication_bundle_id,archive_authority_id,manifest_canonical_digest,manifest_body_digest,manifest_signature_set_digest,content_archive_inventory_root_digest,content_archive_inventory_count,recovery_bootstrap_descriptor_digest,required_durability_profile,authority_binding_public_commitment,service_visibility_epoch}`. `BackupPublicationReceipt` is the portable externally signed `{request_binding:BackupPublicationRequestBinding,publication_envelope_locations_and_byte_digests[{artifact_kind:ManifestBody|ManifestSignatureSet|Manifest,archive_locator:PortableRecoveryLocator::ArchiveObject,canonical_digest,length}],recovery_bootstrap_descriptor:BackupRecoveryBootstrapDescriptor,content_inventory_durability_commitment,publication_generation,archive_monotonic_counter,published_at,time_authority_profile_oid,signer_set_epoch,signature}`. The returned descriptor and every locator byte/digest must equal the request-bound prebuilt descriptor; provider substitution is impossible. It contains no local `StrongRef`; its transcript covers every field except `signature`, every status/result byte from the archive authority binds the same request, and exact retry returns the same generation/bytes. A different request under the same idempotency token is a permanent conflict. `BackupTransparencyInclusion` is the later portable `{external_request_binding:ExternalActionRequestBinding{action_kind=BackupAppendTransparency},backup_id,publication_bundle_id,publication_receipt_digest,manifest_canonical_digest,log_id,leaf_index,tree_size,root_hash,inclusion_path,checkpoint_bytes,checkpoint_signatures,cross_log_consistency_evidence?,included_at,time_authority_profile_oid}` and verifies the body-declared policy and prior checkpoint. Apply creates `ShardBackupPinRecord` strongly owning the generated-complete state/checkpoint/vector/config/floor/history/prepared/certificate/active-projection/key/derived/trust/retention closure at `P` and records `pin_generation`. `ShardBackupCopyVerification` is `{backup_id,pin_identity:WeakDigest,pin_generation,barrier_global_prefix:P,topology_and_configuration_identities,sorted_source_to_archive_entries,complete_inventory_bijection_proof_ref:StrongRef<BackupInventoryBijectionProof>,per_object_decode_results,recoverability_and_failure_domain_proof_ref:StrongRef<BackupRecoverabilityProof>,content_reopen_proof_ref:StrongRef<BackupContentReopenProof>,canonical_shard_semantic_digest}`. `ShardBackupClosureCertificate` is `{SameGroupCertificateHeader,backup_id,barrier_global_prefix:P,shard_id,source_domain,topology_and_configuration_identities,exact_partition_coverage,source_state:BackupSourceIdentity<ShardLogicalStateRoot>,archived_state_ref:BackupArchiveRef<ShardLogicalStateRoot>,copy_verification_ref:StrongRef<ShardBackupCopyVerification>,pinned_closure_digest,active_meta_projection_digest,key_derived_remote_obligation_digests,complete_archive_inventory_digest,inventory_bijection_proof_digest,recoverability_proof_digest,canonical_shard_semantic_digest,content_reopen_proof_digest,certificate_attempt_ref:StrongRef<CertificateAttemptRecord>,canonical_signature_set}` and contains no retaining source-pin edge. `ShardBackupClosurePublishSpec {pin_record_ref:StrongRef<ShardBackupPinRecord>,copy_verification_ref:StrongRef<ShardBackupCopyVerification>,closure_certificate_ref:StrongRef<ShardBackupClosureCertificate>,expected_registry_state:Pinned,expected_pin_generation,expected_barrier_topology_and_configuration,expected_current_root:WeakStateIdentity}` is the only `Pinned -> Certified` transition and byte-matches every field. Shard pins remain until Meta presents the post-publication artifact proof inside the release authorization; content proof alone never releases them.

`GlobalBackupSealSpec {intent_record_ref:StrongRef<GlobalBackupIntentRecord>,exact_sorted_shard_closure_certificate_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardBackupClosureCertificate>],meta_copy_verification_ref:StrongRef<MetaBackupCopyVerification>,backup_manifest_ref:StrongRef<BackupManifest>,expected_topology_and_configurations,exact_complete_group_and_partition_commitment,terminal_audit_gate}` accepts one certificate from every and only required shard, all at exact `P`; `MetaBackupCopyVerification` has the same typed bijection/recoverability/content-reopen fields and Meta scope as its Local/Shard counterparts.

Meta uses the same rooted sequence. `GlobalBackupPublicationAuthorizeSpec` is the sole Sealed successor and constructs the Meta publication operation; publication receipt import selects `PublicationReceiptedPendingTransparency` or `PublicationReceiptedPendingGrant`. Required transparency and grant issuance each receive their own Meta operation record, Protocol dispatch lineage, portable terminal evidence, and Semantic import. `GlobalBackupGrantIssueImportSpec` requires the intent, manifest, complete publication/transparency operation evidence, exact Active grant, direct current `ArchiveGrantAuthorityProjection<Meta>`, expected manifest body/signature digests, and the matching `GrantIssueAuthorizedUndispatched` state. It alone installs Published and never releases a source pin.

`GlobalBackupArtifactVerifySpec` consumes a current-use guard, verifies the exact post-publication artifact and complete operation/status lineage, and installs ArtifactVerified. `GlobalBackupReleaseAuthorizeSpec` names the intent, manifest, receipt, grant, artifact proof, Activated source-release hold, fresh action-bound observation import, exact shard set, expected ArtifactVerified state, and complete release commitment; apply installs Releasing, and only its later role-valid publication permits construction of the portable `GlobalBackupReleaseAuthorizationCertificate`. Every shard verifies that projection plus a new current hold observation import. `GlobalBackupAbortBeginSpec`, `GlobalBackupAbortFinalizeSpec`, and `ShardBackupAbortSpec` are the exact cleanup transitions only while every external operation is pre-SentUnknown or has provider-linearizable never-published cancellation evidence; otherwise they preserve the possibly advertised envelope and the ordinary required-inclusion, grant, artifact-verification, hold-backed source release, and hold-completion protocol is mandatory.

Abort has exact state-shaped no-publication evidence and is not a timeout shortcut. `BackupNoPublicationProof<Role>` is the closed union `PreSeal{backup_id,expected_registry_generation,zero_manifest_and_publication_operation_proof,current_source_pin_set,prepared/certificate/output roots_scanned,quiescence_barrier_id,checker_version}|SealedPublicationNeverEscaped{backup_id,expected_registry_state:Sealed|PublicationAuthorizedUndispatched,manifest_and_seal_identity,publication_bundle_id,publication_operation_record_identity?,publication_operation_disposition:NoOperationAuthorized|AuthorizedUndispatched{dispatch_never_initialized_proof}|ArmedAbandonedBeforeSend{attempt_identity,DispatchNeverSentProof}|ProviderCancelledBeforePublication{attempt_identity,canonical_full_request_digest,provider_linearizable_cancellation_tombstone},zero_transparency_and_grant_operation_proof,archive_publication_authority_head_and_counter,publication_receipt_nonmembership_proof,current_source_pin_set,prepared/certificate/output roots_scanned,quiescence_barrier_id,checker_version,authority_signatures}`. `ProviderCancelledBeforePublication` is a permanent authority tombstone that rejects any later registration or publication for that operation/idempotency/request lineage; signed NotRegistered after SentUnknown is insufficient and permits only exact retry. Because transparency and grant operations are legal only after a publication receipt, their existence makes no-publication false. A bare local absence, timeout, unavailable status, provider `Requested`, or unresolved SentUnknown cannot inhabit any disposition. Every extant operation ID, idempotency token, request digest, dispatch/status transcript, bundle ID, and authority head is mandatory; any successful receipt or ambiguous external state permanently makes abort illegal and forces roll-forward. `BackupStagingCleanupPlan<Role>` enumerates every staging object/realization/key opener/upload operation and pre-mints one idempotent cleanup operation per owner; each cleanup external effect uses the universal dispatch protocol. `BackupStagingCleanupCompletion` proves an exact one-to-one terminal receipt set and post-cleanup inventory. Neither proof may assert absence after a publication receipt, inclusion, or grant exists.

`LocalBackupAbortSpec {backup_id,expected_registry_state:Pinned|ClosureCertified|Sealed|PublicationAuthorizedUndispatched,source_pin_ref:StrongRef<BackupPinRecord>,no_publication_proof_ref:StrongRef<BackupNoPublicationProof<Local>>,cleanup_plan_ref:StrongRef<BackupStagingCleanupPlan<Local>>,cleanup_completion_ref:StrongRef<BackupStagingCleanupCompletion<Local>>,current_root_no_other_backup_owner_proof_ref:StrongRef<BackupPinAbsenceProof>,stable_reason,terminal_audit_gate}` atomically installs compact `AbortedBeforePublication` and releases only the enumerated Local pin/staging owners. If any publication evidence or unresolved SentUnknown exists, this command is permanently illegal and recovery follows the normal publication/verification/release path.

W12 abort is two-phase. `GlobalBackupAbortBeginSpec {intent_record_ref,expected_registry_state:Intent|CollectingClosures|Sealed|PublicationAuthorizedUndispatched,no_publication_proof_ref:StrongRef<BackupNoPublicationProof<Meta>>,meta_cleanup_plan_ref,exact_sorted_shard_pin_and_closure_commitment,abort_nonce,terminal_audit_gate}` installs `AbortAuthorized` while retaining every pin; only after its role-valid publication may a later certificate attempt create `GlobalBackupAbortAuthorizationCertificate`. Each `ShardBackupAbortSpec {authorization_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<GlobalBackupAbortAuthorizationCertificate>,own_pin_ref,own_closure_or_staging_state,own_cleanup_plan_ref,own_cleanup_completion_ref,current_root_no_other_owner_proof_ref,expected_abort_nonce}` removes only its own pin/staging closure and, after its own durable publication, permits creation of `ShardBackupAbortAck`. `GlobalBackupAbortFinalizeSpec {abort_begin_ref,authorization_certificate_ref,meta_cleanup_completion_ref,exact_sorted_shard_abort_ack_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardBackupAbortAck>],complete_required_group_and_pin_bijection_proof_ref,expected_registry_state:AbortAuthorized,terminal_audit_gate}` alone selects compact `AbortedBeforePublication`. Missing/duplicate/wrong-shard acks remain blocking. All abort states live in payload/checkpoint/configuration/backup/restore/GC inventories, and crash tests cut proof, begin, every cleanup dispatch/receipt, shard apply/publication/ack, Meta finalize, and lost response.

`ShardBackupReleaseSpec` is the closed inner union `Authorize{authorization_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<GlobalBackupReleaseAuthorizationCertificate>,own_pin_ref:StrongRef<ShardBackupPinRecord>,own_closure_certificate_ref:StrongRef<ShardBackupClosureCertificate>,manifest_ref:BackupPublicationArtifactRef<BackupManifest>,publication_receipt_ref:StrongRef<BackupPublicationReceipt>,archive_retention_grant_ref:StrongRef<ArchiveRetentionGrant>,activated_source_release_hold_ref:StrongRef<ArchiveSourceReleaseHold>,fresh_grant_authority_observation_import_ref:StrongRef<ArchiveGrantAuthorityObservationImport<Shard>>,required_observation_action:ShardSourcePinRelease{own_shard_id},expected_registry_state:Certified,expected_barrier_topology_configuration_and_pin_generation}|Finalize{authorization_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<GlobalBackupReleaseAuthorizationCertificate>,own_pin_ref:StrongRef<ShardBackupPinRecord>,own_closure_certificate_ref:StrongRef<ShardBackupClosureCertificate>,expected_registry_state:ReleaseAuthorized,current_root_no_other_pin_proof_ref:StrongRef<BackupPinAbsenceProof>,post_release_registry_body_recipe}`. `BackupPinAbsenceProof` binds the exact current role root, backup registry generation, backup ID/pin generation, complete scan commitment, and checker version; it cannot be a generic reachability assertion. `Authorize` verifies the current activated hold but keeps the pin and enters ReleaseAuthorized; `Finalize` alone removes it, installs shard Released, and permits a later certificate attempt to create the exact signed `ShardBackupReleaseAck` with authorization/hold/observation, post-release root/no-pin proof, applied index, and certificate-attempt closure.

`GlobalBackupReleaseFinalizeSpec` is `{authorization_record_ref:StrongRef<GlobalControlRecord>,authorization_certificate_ref:StrongRef<GlobalBackupReleaseAuthorizationCertificate>,exact_sorted_shard_release_ack_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardBackupReleaseAck>],activated_source_release_hold_ref:StrongRef<ArchiveSourceReleaseHold>,fresh_grant_authority_observation_import_ref:StrongRef<ArchiveGrantAuthorityObservationImport<Meta>>,required_observation_action:GlobalSourceReleaseFinalize,expected_registry_state:Releasing,exact_required_shard_commitment,meta_post_release_body_recipe,terminal_audit_gate}`. It drops the Meta pin and enters `ReleasedPendingArchiveHoldCompletion` only after every and only configured shard ack under the still-current Activated hold, and constructs the portable sharded `ArchiveSourceReleaseEvidence`. `ArchiveSourceReleaseCompletionImportSpec<Meta>` alone enters final Released. Meta states are `Absent|Collecting|Sealed|PublicationAuthorizedUndispatched|PublicationReceiptedPendingTransparency|PublicationReceiptedPendingGrant|TransparencyAuthorizedUndispatched|TransparencyIncludedPendingGrant|GrantIssueAuthorizedUndispatched|Published|ArtifactVerified|HoldPrepareAuthorizedUndispatched|HoldPrepared|HoldActivateAuthorizedUndispatched|HoldActivated|Releasing|ReleasedPendingArchiveHoldCompletion|Released`; shard states are `Absent|Pinned|Certified|ReleaseAuthorized|Released`. Reconfiguration, GC, key destruction, topology retirement, checkpoints, and floors retain every nonterminal state and every operation/dispatch/grant-head/hold/completion observation import needed for recovery. Renewal/revocation/expiry is raced before reopen, verification, authorization, every hold transition, shard authorize/finalize, Meta finalize, archive completion CAS, and completion import; stale generations always fail closed.

`BackupState` in the sealed manifest is the closed nonretaining posture tag `Local{barrier_coordinates,source_state:BackupSourceIdentity<LogicalStateRoot>,archived_state_ref:BackupArchiveRef<LogicalStateRoot>,checkpoint_configuration_history_inventory_digests,local_closure_certificate_identity}|Sharded{barrier_global_prefix,source_global_state:BackupSourceIdentity<GlobalStateRoot>,archived_global_state_ref:BackupArchiveRef<GlobalStateRoot>,topology_and_configuration_digests,sorted_shards[{shard_id,source_state:BackupSourceIdentity<ShardLogicalStateRoot>,archived_state_ref:BackupArchiveRef<ShardLogicalStateRoot>,closure_certificate_identity,partition_commitment}],complete_group_and_partition_commitment}`. Legacy Local manifests remain Local after activation and are never reinterpreted as Sharded. Unknown/mixed posture, group, inventory, trust, barrier, or configuration fields fail closed.

Same-identity write authority comes from one external linearizable chain. `AcquisitionRefinementState` is `None|BootstrapOpenersCommitted{refinement_generation=1,phase_a_plan_digest,archive_receipt_digest,refinement_digest,availability_certificate_digest,bootstrap_action_set_digest}|VerifiedObjectInventoryCommitted{refinement_generation=2,phase_a_plan_digest,bootstrap_refinement_digest,verified_manifest_and_projection_digests,refinement_digest,availability_certificate_digest,exact_inventory_count_and_root,phase_b_action_set_digest}`. `PortablePriorLeaseClosureContinuationPackage` is the reference-free threshold-signed `{restore_id,continuity_domain_and_target_identity,planned_target_incarnation,frozen_issuer_configuration_bytes_and_set_digest,sorted_issuer_and_cohort_recipe_bytes,sorted_contract_operation_idempotency_action_body_and_original_source_gate_bytes,sorted_completed_status_terminal_receipt_and_portable_evidence_bytes,completed_terminal_evidence_accumulator,remaining_issuer_and_cohort_bitmap,required_historical_time_profile_verifier_and_registry_ancestry_bytes,continuation_availability_certificate,continuation_retention_floor,no_service_until_complete:true,package_digest,signer_set_epoch,threshold_signatures}`. Its availability certificate proves the complete bytes—not merely a digest—exist in the continuity authority's declared failure domains through the retention floor. `PriorIncarnationLeaseClosureDisposition` is the closed union `NotApplicableNewIdentity|Complete{barrier_digest,complete_issuer_and_cohort_bijection_commitment,no_future_prior_incarnation_issue_or_renew:true}|PendingInheritedFromFence{continuation_package_bytes_and_digest:PortablePriorLeaseClosureContinuationPackage,no_service_while_pending:true}`. `RestoreAbandonmentAuthoritySeed` is the single pre-order reference-free `{restore_id,target_database_and_security_identity,target_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch,authority_profile,continuity_predecessor_class,source_lease_identity,source_access_cleanup_policy_id,stable_no_endpoint_reason,permanent_no_service_no_same_incarnation_successor_and_higher_incarnation_only_rules,seed_digest}`. It contains no journal/spec/operation record, action/cleanup recipe, request, manifest, skeleton, external result, tombstone body, publication evidence, or receipt. Both planes may bind the same seed only when every stable field matches; plane-specific authority is supplied outside it. `ClusterIncarnationContinuityRecord` is `{continuity_domain_id,database_id,database_security_namespace_id,predecessor_digest,cas_version,retired_incarnation_floor,active_or_reserved_incarnation,state:Operational{posture:Local|Sharded,writer_authority_digest,service_visibility_epoch,lease_policy:DirectOrdinary|PromotionReceiptRequired{promotion_manifest_digest,catalog_activation_receipt_digest,promotion_operation_id,complete_pre-finalization_lineage_commitment}}|RestoreFencePending{restore_id,source_backup_manifest_digest,planned_target_incarnation,lease_issuer_and_cohort_inventory_commitment,prior_lease_fence_operation_set_commitment,retiring_time_authority_profile_set_commitment,issuer_configuration_set_frozen:true,new_issuer_registration_forbidden:true,continuity_authority_direct_prior_incarnation_issuance_fenced:true,issuer_closure_status:Pending{complete_issuer_recipe_set_commitment,completed_terminal_evidence_accumulator,remaining_issuer_and_cohort_bitmap},acquisition_plan_and_operation_commitment}|RestoreReserved{restore_id,source_backup_manifest_digest,source_backup_incarnation,retired_through_incarnation,target_incarnation,recovery_writer_authority_digest,service_visibility_epoch,prior_lease_closure:Complete{prior_lease_barrier_digest,complete_issuer_and_cohort_bijection_commitment,no_future_prior_incarnation_issue_or_renew:true},source_acquisition_plan_and_operation_commitment,acquisition_refinement_state:AcquisitionRefinementState,lease_policy:RecoveryOnly}|CloneReserved{restore_id,source_database_and_security_identity,source_backup_manifest_digest,target_incarnation,recovery_writer_authority_digest,service_visibility_epoch,lease_policy:RecoveryOnly,new_identity_allocation_receipt_digest,source_acquisition_plan_and_operation_commitment,acquisition_refinement_state:AcquisitionRefinementState}|RoleTransitionReserved{migration_nonce,transition_certificate_digest,source_posture:Local,target_posture:Sharded,source_service_visibility_epoch,target_service_visibility_epoch,service_epoch_reservation_id,source_local_group_and_terminal_seal_commitment,target_group_topology_and_endpoint_commitment,transition_writer_authority_digest,lease_policy:RoleTransitionOnly}|PromotionCatalogPending{operation_kind:Restore|RoleTransition,operation_id,manifest_digest,catalog_reservation_id,catalog_reservation_digest_and_version,target_posture,target_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch,promotion_writer_authority_digest,lease_policy:PromotionOnly,no_ordinary_lease:true}|RestoreAbandoned{restore_id,target_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch,abandonment_basis:PreBootstrapNoRoot{abandonment_authority_seed_digest,prior_lease_closure_disposition:PriorIncarnationLeaseClosureDisposition}|CanonicalRooted{abandonment_authority_seed_digest,target_tombstone_skeleton_digest,prior_lease_closure_disposition:PriorIncarnationLeaseClosureDisposition},retired_through_incarnation,no_operational_successor_at_this_incarnation:true}|RoleTransitionAbandonedSealed{migration_nonce,target_service_visibility_epoch,catalog_tombstone_digest,terminal_local_seal_commitment,abandonment_receipt_digest,no_unfreeze_or_operational_successor:true},issued_at,signer_set_epoch,threshold_signatures}`. `RestoreFencePending` freezes the issuer universe and prevents the continuity authority from issuing directly, but it intentionally does **not** claim that independent online/offline issuers have all closed; only a complete signed barrier and `RestoreReserved` may make that global claim. `CommitAcquisitionRefinement` may only advance None -> BootstrapOpenersCommitted -> VerifiedObjectInventoryCommitted for the same restore/target/authority/recipient/profile under the deterministic rule precommitted by Phase A; every successor commits a phase-specific loss-tolerant availability certificate. It cannot widen or replace any other field. Only the returned direct-successor head authorizes introduced actions.

`RestoreAbandonableContinuityPredecessor` is the exact reference-free union `RestoreFencePending{head_bytes_digest_and_cas_version,planned_target_incarnation,frozen_issuer_set_and_pending_closure_projection}|RestoreReservedNone{head_bytes_digest_and_cas_version,acquisition_refinement_state:None,complete_prior_lease_closure_projection}|RestoreReservedBootstrapOpeners{head_bytes_digest_and_cas_version,acquisition_refinement_state:BootstrapOpenersCommitted,complete_prior_lease_closure_projection}|RestoreReservedVerifiedObjectInventory{head_bytes_digest_and_cas_version,acquisition_refinement_state:VerifiedObjectInventoryCommitted,complete_prior_lease_closure_projection}|CloneReservedNone{head_bytes_digest_and_cas_version,acquisition_refinement_state:None}|CloneReservedBootstrapOpeners{head_bytes_digest_and_cas_version,acquisition_refinement_state:BootstrapOpenersCommitted}|CloneReservedVerifiedObjectInventory{head_bytes_digest_and_cas_version,acquisition_refinement_state:VerifiedObjectInventoryCommitted}|PromotionCatalogPendingRestore{head_bytes_digest_and_cas_version,manifest_catalog_and_promotion_lineage_commitment}`. Every arm carries the same restore ID, target identity/incarnation, service epoch, acquisition plan, and recovery authority fixed by the abandonment action body.

`PreBootstrapRestoreContinuityCleanupDisposition` is the exact union `NoMutationOperationalUnchanged{mode:RecoverSameIdentity,current_operational_head_bytes_digest_and_cas_version,planned_target_incarnation,enter_restore_fence_pending_contract_and_operation_commitment,terminal_attempt:NeverArmed|AbandonedBeforeSend|ConflictNoEffect|PermanentRefusal,typed_prebootstrap_never_sent_or_zero_effect_evidence,proof_current_operational_head_is_unchanged_and_no_restore_descendant_exists,plan_and_operation_nonreuse_floor}|NoMutationAuthenticatedAbsentClone{mode:CloneNewIdentity,authenticated_empty_continuity_map_proof,target_identity_nonreuse_floor,enter_clone_reserved_contract_and_operation_commitment,terminal_attempt:NeverArmed|AbandonedBeforeSend|ConflictNoEffect|PermanentRefusal,typed_prebootstrap_never_sent_or_zero_effect_evidence,new_identity_and_allocation_reservation_burn_commitments,proof_no_clone_or_restore_descendant_exists}|AbandonedByCas{predecessor:RestoreAbandonableContinuityPredecessor,abandonment_authority_seed_digest,contract_id:PreBootstrapRestoreContinuityAbandonContract,terminal_import_artifact_ref:PreBootstrapArtifactRef<PreBootstrapExternalTerminalImportArtifact<PreBootstrapRestoreContinuityAbandonContract>>,portable_terminal_evidence_artifact_ref:PreBootstrapArtifactRef<PortableExternalActionTerminalEvidence<PreBootstrapRestoreContinuityAbandonContract>>,operation_id,action_body_digest,result_restore_abandoned_head_bytes_digest_and_cas_version,prior_lease_closure_disposition}`. `CanonicalRestoreContinuityCleanupDisposition<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` has the sole exact arm `AbandonedByCas{predecessor:RestoreAbandonableContinuityPredecessor,abandonment_authority_seed_digest,contract_id:CanonicalRestoreContinuityAbandonContract<Role>,terminal_import_ref:StrongRef<ExternalTerminalImportRecord<CanonicalRestoreContinuityAbandonContract<Role>,Role>>,portable_terminal_evidence_ref:StrongRef<PortableExternalActionTerminalEvidence<CanonicalRestoreContinuityAbandonContract<Role>>>,operation_id,action_body_digest,result_restore_abandoned_head_bytes_digest_and_cas_version,prior_lease_closure_disposition}`. The two no-mutation arms are prebootstrap terminal evidence, not fake continuity heads: same-identity cleanup leaves the pre-existing Operational incarnation and its older catalog endpoint untouched, while absent-clone cleanup relies on authenticated absence plus permanent allocation/nonreuse dispositions. The action kind `RestoreContinuityAbandon` has two statically distinct universal-dispatch rows: `PreBootstrapRestoreContinuityAbandonContract` uses `PreBootstrapAbandonmentCleanupGate`, while `CanonicalRestoreContinuityAbandonContract<Role>` uses the audit-visible canonical abandonment-operation candidate and ordinary Protocol publication evidence. Each requires the same-plane profile-valid catalog cleanup disposition and CASes only an actual `RestoreAbandonableContinuityPredecessor` to `RestoreAbandoned`; their attempts, request bindings, evidence, and imports cannot cross-decode. A `RestoreFencePending` predecessor transfers the complete `PortablePriorLeaseClosureContinuationPackage` into `PendingInheritedFromFence`; all other restore predecessors carry `Complete` or `NotApplicableNewIdentity` as appropriate. Already-applied is terminal only when the authority returns an authenticated existing equivalent `RestoreAbandoned` head for the same operation, seed, incarnation, plane, and closure disposition.

Same-identity recovery CASes `Operational{posture}(I_current) -> RestoreFencePending`, durably fences every online/offline prior-incarnation lease issuer, proves the complete cohort inventory expired or revoked, then CASes `RestoreReserved(J)` with `J > max(I_current,I_backup,retired_incarnation_floor)` and the exact barrier/acquisition-plan commitments. Clone recovery CAS-creates exactly one previously absent target database/security namespace into `CloneReserved(J)` under a nonreusable identity-allocation receipt whose claimed intended-use commitment already fixes the acquisition operation; it never traverses the source continuity chain as target authority. Promotion never jumps directly to Operational. It first acquires a nonexpiring hidden catalog reservation, then CASes `RestoreReserved|CloneReserved|RoleTransitionReserved -> PromotionCatalogPending`, activates the exact reserved catalog row, and only then CASes to `Operational{lease_policy=PromotionReceiptRequired}` using the composite four-lineage receipt. The catalog row remains admission-hidden until that final receipt exists. An irreconcilable no-endpoint conflict before finalization uses rooted catalog-tombstone and continuity-abandon operations; restore must choose a higher incarnation, while a role-transition source remains terminally sealed and can proceed only through fenced restore/clone. DirectOrdinary is reserved for fresh/direct service activation whose catalog and continuity publication are one externally atomic authority operation. Abandonment changes exactly the registered `RestoreAbandonableContinuityPredecessor` to `RestoreAbandoned`, advances the retired floor through the abandoned incarnation, and permanently forbids an Operational successor at that incarnation. A later same-identity recovery must move `RestoreAbandoned{retired through J} -> RestoreFencePending{target K}` for a new restore ID with `K > J` and a fresh recovery authority, inherit and finish any pending issuer closure, and only then enter `RestoreReserved` with one exact complete prior-lease barrier; no state at J is resurrected and no direct Abandoned -> Reserved shortcut exists. No other source or target posture is registered in v1. Checked overflow fails. Only one direct successor can win for a target identity, no acquisition send or recovery/transition write precedes its exact claimed plan, and continuity, lease/time guards, service-catalog reservation/activation, promotion receipts, and open/session admission all byte-match the active state/posture/incarnation/service epoch.

## Ownership, verification, and diagnostics
For every schema, field, tag, state, transition, reference, digest transcript, construction-order rule, and role restriction in this slice, generate a durable_fields.toml row with stable IDs; canonical encoding/version policy; concrete generic/role expansion; producer, owner bead/crate, and consumers; reference strength/target set; authority and redaction class; invariant/evidence/cost bindings; test/scenario/event IDs; and consuming gate. Cross-slice targets use stable catalog IDs and must resolve in the Appendix A epic closure. Downstream owners may add implementation detail but cannot abbreviate, alias, weaken, or contradict these bytes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The embedded line range is byte-complete, checksum-pinned, continuous with adjacent slices, and contains no truncation marker.
- Every exact named construct in the slice has one stable row and exactly one granular implementation owner; all references and consumers resolve.
- Unit tests cover canonical encode/decode, stable field/tag IDs, role/generic expansion, digest construction, state preconditions, and owner uniqueness.
- Property/mutation/fuzz tests remove, duplicate, reorder, retag, corrupt, weaken, or cross-role substitute every field/arm/reference class and prove rejection.
- Simulation tests exercise applicable crash, cancellation, retry, sent-unknown, receipt-first, recovery, authority/configuration rotation, compaction, and expiry boundaries.
- E2E scripts traverse each applicable public embedded/server/FGP/CLI path through durable publication, restart/replay, backup/restore, and terminal cleanup using isolated synthetic fixtures.
- Detailed versioned JSONL diagnostics carry schema_id, field_or_arm_id, role/group, object or public commitment, transition_id, state_before/state_after, checker, verdict, artifact refs, and replay command; secret/noninterference tests reject protected data or observable hidden state.
- Cross-version golden vectors and unknown-required-field fixtures enforce additive-minor/breaking-major policy; no gate passes with an uncovered row.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: family-level prose summaries, wildcard references, inferred fields, unregistered aliases, or treating the catalog slice as the implementation. Exactness is intentional; execution remains decomposed across the linked workstream beads.

Complete audited plan Appendix A lines 2057-2156.

FROM THE a16 LANE (cc-a16-pane8) — a queued catalog-token request, and one thing you should know BEFORE you land, because it touches the files you are holding.

THE THING WORTH KNOWING (full evidence is on fgdb-a16-time-authority-ytub): identity.rs:2680 resolves a field row's owner by EXACT name, but logical_by_name is keyed by BARE family. So every [[field]] row whose containing_schema carries a generic signature currently skips the ENTIRE construction-DAG block — dag_self_edge, dag_future_result, and the edge collection feeding dag_cycle. Measured at d0570ea: 15 of the 75 landed retaining field rows escape the law today. Proven by control: a strong self-edge on TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role> yields no dag_self_edge at all on an unpatched tree.

WHY THIS MATTERS TO YOUR INCREMENT SPECIFICALLY: if a15 lands any retaining field row (reference_semantics strong/conditional/weak_digest) on a generic-signed owner, it is currently UNCHECKED for self-edges and future results. It will pass your gate and still be wrong. If you have such rows, either derive their order by hand from both reference directions before landing, or land them after my fix so the checker actually verifies them. Purely non-retaining rows (reference_semantics = none/embedded) are unaffected.

My fix is one lookup normalised through generic_free_family(), matching the sibling law at identity.rs:1556, plus two negative tests and a corrected dag_self_edge message. It changes NO landed row's validity: registry-check identity and appendix both stay at 0 violations, and scripts/check.sh is ALL GATES GREEN at 7/7 with 831 tests passed / 0 failed. So it should be a clean rebase on top of whatever you land.

ALSO, WITH THANKS: I adopted your standalone-rustc technique for the catalog inner loop and can confirm it generalises past architecture-check to the TEST binary, which is the expensive part for checker-law work. Recipe, in case it is useful to you —
    rustc --edition=2024 --crate-type=lib --crate-name registry_check tools/registry-check/src/lib.rs -o libregistry_check.rlib      # 4.8s
    CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR=<abs>/tools/registry-check rustc --edition=2024 --test tools/registry-check/tests/identity.rs \
        --extern registry_check=libregistry_check.rlib -o probe_identity                                                              # 0.9s
    ./probe_identity                                                                                                                  # 67 tests, 23s
The CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR export is the whole trick: tests/identity.rs finds the registries through env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), which rustc reads from the compile-time environment, so the suite resolves the real registry files with no cargo involved. Full identity-suite signal in about 29 seconds from a cold rlib.

title: Ruling: KeyDestroyProposal field wire vocabulary is underspecified
description:
## What and scope

Eight otherwise-local A15 `KeyDestroyProposal` field candidates cannot be projected because Appendix A names a value, state predicate, digest, or gate but does not define the exact wire shape the durable-field registry requires. This is an owner vocabulary ruling, not permission to guess a schema or amend the normative plan. It is distinct from `fgdb-identity-class-record-wire-convention-l6xd`: that bead starts with a registered record/union wire type and asks which `identity_class` its containing field takes; this bead cannot yet name a legal `exact_wire_type` at all. A ruling here may subsequently consume the identity-class convention if it chooses a record or union wire shape.

## Exact unresolved vocabulary and blocked A15 rows

Each item blocks exactly one `KeyDestroyProposal` field row; total blocked rows: **8**.

1. `expected_key_state:RetainedDecryptOnly` — 1 row. The source supplies a required lifecycle-state value, not the containing enum/type name. `RetainedDecryptOnly` occurs as a state variant and is neither a builtin nor a registered wire type. Minting it as a standalone wire type would silently turn a value into a schema.
2. `basis_state:WeakStateIdentity` — 1 row. The source names `WeakStateIdentity`, but it is only a name-only Appendix candidate and is neither builtin nor registered. The source does not define whether this is a digest, an inline record, or another canonical state-identity wire shape.
3. `key_identity` — 1 row. No exact type, cardinality, identity class, or transcript recipe is stated at this occurrence. Other key identifiers in the plan have multiple noninterchangeable meanings, so name similarity cannot select one.
4. `expected_prospective_configuration_set_digest` — 1 row. The source says “digest” but not which durable digest class or canonical transcript/recipe produces it.
5. `exact_root_slot_generations` — 1 row. The source does not state the element/record type, whether it is scalar or collection-valued, the ordering rule, or cardinality.
6. `complete_target_set_digest` — 1 row. The source does not identify the digest class or the exact canonical target-set transcript/recipe.
7. `expected_state_conditions` — 1 row. The plan uses several semantically different condition families; this occurrence supplies neither a closed wire union/record nor exact cardinality.
8. `terminal_audit_gate` — 1 row. This recurring shorthand has no single registered wire type or exact local shape at this occurrence; choosing among gate/check/evidence forms would be semantic invention.

## Controlled measurement and interpretation

The lookup that found these absences also found the released `KeyDestructionOperationPlan` wire type and the released `expected_current_configuration_ref` field, and rejected a fabricated type/name. Thus the probe is working. Reading Appendix A A15 lines 2057-2059 establishes what the absence means: the proposal spells the eight member names but does not provide enough type/cardinality/transcript detail to emit legal `[[field]]` rows. The global landed-field precedent screen found no exact precedent for any of the six shorthand members. This is not an `identity_class`-only gap because the checker cannot first resolve a legal exact wire type.

## Required ruling

For each of the eight members, state the exact durable wire type and cardinality. For digest members, also state the digest class and canonical transcript/recipe. For `expected_key_state`, name the containing lifecycle enum/type and confirm `RetainedDecryptOnly` is a required value rather than a standalone type. For `basis_state`, define or bind `WeakStateIdentity`. For any newly chosen record/union type, apply the separate identity-class convention ruling rather than inventing an A15-only class.

## Success criteria

- Eight exact wire shapes/cardinalities are stated in a durable owner-visible rule or normative erratum.
- Each digest-like field has one unambiguous canonical recipe.
- The eight A15 field rows can be emitted without guessing and pass registry-check/G0 negative fixtures.
- No reservation is introduced for a non-StrongRef family; any required mints precede field/adjudication consumers.

## Provenance

Measured by pane5 against the post-I8 A15 state. I8 landed the three missing StrongRef prerequisites in `a8d7fcb`; these eight are the complete remaining `KeyDestroyProposal` field residue after that commit.
close_reason: Closed after c1e0317 landed the three source-forced consumers and comment 626 recorded the owner-ready five-fork matrix. WeakStateIdentity Branch B is disproved: CheckpointInstallSpec, GlobalCheckpointInstallSpec, ShardCheckpointInstallSpec, and DistributedSerializationCertificate co-locate WeakStateIdentity with a separate WeakDigest of that basis, so Branch A is source-distinct and landed. Remaining owner forks: (1) expected_key_state consumer +1 field/+1 target/+1 adjudication; a seven-arm carrier adds 16 projection and 16 exact-target shell rows before DestroyPending payload members, and depends on lifecycle carrier, seven tags, and payload-shape rulings; scalar branch has no union shell but needs the complete discriminant table. (2) key_identity consumer +1 field/+1 target/+1 adjudication, no union shell; opaque id256 has no producer rows, structured form adds one wire/target plus four member field/targets and depends on identity-domain/transcript versus member-shape ruling. (3) expected_prospective_configuration_set_digest +1 field/+1 target/+1 adjudication, no union shell; depends on digest class/transcript and identity-set versus body/membership/fence commitment. (4) exact_root_slot_generations +1 field/+1 target/+1 adjudication, no union shell; either record shape adds one wire/target plus two member field/targets and depends on fixed-pair versus exactly-two-entry cardinality/order ruling. (5) complete_target_set_digest +1 field/+1 target/+1 adjudication, no union shell; depends on sorted-identity transcript versus authenticated-set tree/root algorithm. No further implementation is authorized until those producer rulings are made.
