title: Appendix A exact catalog: Rollback-protected authority-time formats and rotation
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the exact Appendix A catalog slice for Rollback-protected authority-time formats and rotation. This task embeds source-plan lines 2157-2246 verbatim, expands every generic and role-indexed family into stable registered rows, and assigns each row to its granular implementation owner. It is a format/ownership contract, not a substitute implementation.

## Exact normative contract
The following audited source-plan text is authoritative and self-contained:

**Rollback-protected authority time.** Canonical logical HLC orders database state; it is never an expiry clock. Process-local monotonic time may enforce a short-lived in-memory use budget and drive advisory timers; ambient wall time is display-only. Any authorization, lease-validity, expiry, release, retirement, key destruction, archive downgrade, restore fencing, or retention-cut decision uses the following rollback-protected authority-time contract or fails closed.

`AuthorityInstant` is `{time_domain_id,authority_epoch,tick:u128}` and compares only within one domain/epoch; windows are closed-open: `not_before <= true_authority_time < expires_at`. `AuthorityInterval` is the exact `{earliest:AuthorityInstant,latest:AuthorityInstant}` with byte-identical domain/epoch fields and `earliest.tick <= latest.tick`; intervals from different domains/epochs are never ordered, intersected, or bridged by scalar conversion. `TimeAuthorityProfile` is the immutable threshold-signed `{schema_version,time_domain_id,authority_epoch,tick_scale,external_registry_id,ordered_signers[{signer_id,key_id,verification_key}],threshold,maximum_source_uncertainty_ticks,maximum_challenge_round_trip_ticks,maximum_guard_use_ticks,comparison_semantics:ClosedOpen,unavailable_policy:FailClosed,predecessor_profile_digest:WeakDigest?,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`.

External time evidence is reference-free. `PortableTimeAuthorityObservation` is the fresh challenged signed `{profile_oid,profile_digest,time_domain_id,authority_epoch,challenge_nonce,subject_digest,intended_use_digest,authority_sequence,possible_time_interval:AuthorityInterval,external_registry_head_digest,external_registry_cas_version,signer_set_epoch,threshold_signatures}`. It never claims process-local send/receive counters.

`ShardTimeAuthorityProjection` is the shard-local certified Meta projection `{source_meta_prefix,source_meta_configuration_identity,source_meta_time_registry_generation,selected_profile_oid,sorted_profile_projections[{profile_oid,profile_digest,issuance_state:ActiveForIssuance|ClosingRequested|IssuanceClosing|IssuanceQuiescent|Draining|Retired,verification_live_through_commitment}],time_authority_registry_head_digest,verifier_and_offline_issuer_floor_commitment,retention_grant_and_payload_availability_evidence,typed_projection_payload_identity_and_digest,projection_certificate_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<MetaControlProjectionCertificate>,body_digest}`. Its certificate's `TypedCertifiedMetaProjectionPayload` arm is exactly `TimeAuthorityRegistryProjection` and byte-matches the payload identity/digest and source prefix/effect. It is installed only through the exact contiguous ActiveMetaProjectionRoot time-authority slot and is invalid after that source prefix/configuration/trust or retention evidence ceases to be current.

`LocalChallengeRoundTripWitness` is the nonportable `{process_incarnation_id,challenge_nonce,send_monotonic_tick,receive_monotonic_tick,checked_elapsed_ticks,monotonic_source_profile_id,conversion_to_authority_uncertainty_ticks,body_digest}`. `TimeAuthorityObservationImport` is the closed role-local union `Local{role_and_group,current_configuration_writer_fence_and_publication_commitment,profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,portable_observation_ref:StrongRef<PortableTimeAuthorityObservation>,current_registry_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityRegistry<Local>>,local_round_trip_witness:LocalChallengeRoundTripWitness,exact_profile_registry_and_transcript_match_digest,imported_at_maintenance_identity}|Meta{role_and_group,current_configuration_writer_fence_and_publication_commitment,profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,portable_observation_ref:StrongRef<PortableTimeAuthorityObservation>,current_registry_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityRegistry<Meta>>,local_round_trip_witness:LocalChallengeRoundTripWitness,exact_profile_registry_and_transcript_match_digest,imported_at_maintenance_identity}|Shard{role_and_group,current_configuration_writer_fence_and_publication_commitment,profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,portable_observation_ref:StrongRef<PortableTimeAuthorityObservation>,current_meta_time_authority_projection_ref:StrongRef<ShardTimeAuthorityProjection>,local_round_trip_witness:LocalChallengeRoundTripWitness,exact_profile_projection_and_transcript_match_digest,imported_at_maintenance_identity}`. The import verifies the portable profile identity/digest, current registry or certified projection, role/group/configuration/fence, same-nonce local round trip, interval, subject, intended use, and signatures before any local validator may consume it. Challenge nonce, subject, and use are signed. Replay, wrong profile/domain/epoch, noncurrent registry head, excessive checked round trip/uncertainty, process-incarnation mismatch, role substitution, or signature failure is unusable.

`time_bound_subjects.toml` is the single exhaustive source for the closed `TimeBoundSubject` union. Each row names one concrete durable schema or one exact capability variant, its canonical pre-evidence transcript recipe, profile/window field tags, legal intended uses, evidence owner, expiry/retirement transition, and retention floor. It forbids raw refs, a generic object arm, a generic capability arm, and overlapping transcripts. `TimeValidationEvidence` is the already-built role-local immutable `{profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,observation_import_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityObservationImport>,subject:TimeBoundSubject,intended_use_digest,classification:Usable{not_before,expires_at,validated_process_incarnation_id,guard_deadline_local_monotonic_tick}|NotYetValid{not_before}|Expired{expires_at},validator_version,validation_digest}`. `Usable` exists only when the imported portable observation's `possible_time_interval.earliest >= not_before`, the local round-trip witness belongs to the current process incarnation, and `checked_add(possible_time_interval.latest.tick,maximum_guard_use_ticks)` succeeds in the same domain/epoch and is `< expires_at`; its local guard deadline is derived with checked arithmetic from the same receive tick and conservative remaining budget. A linear use guard can be constructed only in that same process incarnation while its current monotonic tick is strictly before the recorded deadline. Durable Usable bytes surviving restart therefore authorize nothing until a fresh observation/import/evidence exists. `NotYetValid` exists only when `possible_time_interval.latest < not_before`; `Expired` only when `possible_time_interval.earliest >= expires_at` and remains durable across restart. An interval overlapping either boundary yields no evidence and the uniform retryable `TimeAuthorityUnavailable`, before any protected lookup or disclosure. Tick addition, bound normalization, challenge-round-trip subtraction, and profile drain arithmetic are checked; overflow, saturation requirement, or domain/epoch mismatch yields `TimeAuthorityUnavailable` and never wraps.

The v1 arms bind the canonical pre-evidence body, never a future object that embeds the evidence, and are exactly: `TxnOutcomeCapabilityBytes`, `ResumeSubscriptionCapabilityBytes`, `ResumeBufferedResultCapabilityBytes`, `ResumeArtifactOutputCapabilityBytes`, `MergeOutcomeCapabilityBytes`, `ReadYourWritesCapabilityBytes`, `MacaroonTokenBytes`, `OfflineMacaroonIssuerEpochCohort`, `MutationPermitRecord`, `ReadPermitRecord`, `AuthorizationLease`, `TxnOwnershipLease`, `PrivacyExecutionLease`, `ResultDeliveryLeaseTimeBasis`, `SubscriptionDeliveryLeaseTimeBasis`, `ArtifactOutputLeaseTimeBasis`, `ProtectedErrorLeaseTimeBasis`, `ProtectedErrorReplayTimeBasis`, `TxnOutcomeLookupWindow`, `FollowerLeaseRead`, `IdRangeLease`, `ShardIdRangeLease`, `ClusterIncarnationLease`, `PriorIncarnationLeaseCohortWindow`, `RestoreSourceLeaseRecordLocal`, `RestoreSourceLeaseRecordMeta`, `ShardRestoreSourceLeaseProjection`, `NewDatabaseIdentityReservation`, `ServiceVisibilityEpochReservation`, `AllocationEpochReservation`, `ProfiledResourceReservationDeadline`, `ReplayArchiveRecord`, `ArchiveRetentionGrantWindow`, `ArchiveSourceReleasePreparedHoldWindow`, `KeyEnvelopeGrantWindow`, `BackupPublicationFreshness`, `BackupTransparencyFreshness`, `TransparencyCheckpointFreshnessBasis`, `CrossLogTransparencyFreshness`, `PayloadReceiptProposalFreshnessBasis`, `VerifierKeyWindow`, and `IrreversibleDispatchObservationWindow`. The three restore-source arms map exactly to `RestoreSourceLeaseRecord<Local>`, `RestoreSourceLeaseRecord<Meta>`, and the Shard projection schema; the prebootstrap owner belongs only to `prebootstrap_artifact_kinds.toml` and its prebootstrap time validator. Each row explicitly maps the arm to its exact schema and window field tags; aliases such as `FollowerReadLease`, `IdRangeIssuanceLease`, `RestoreSourceLease`, or `ReplayArchiveLease` are unregistered. Capability arms contain the exact capability kind plus header-and-body digest; they cannot overlap. `MacaroonTokenBytes` validates one presented root or attenuated token and therefore contains its exact token kind plus canonical header/body/caveat-chain digest. Output-basis arms contain role, owner/delivery generation, complete authority commitment, policy, and exact window.

The formerly shorthand window names above are generated exact schemas, not aliases for two loose timestamps. Their common canonical prefix is `{subject_kind,time_authority_profile_oid,not_before:AuthorityInstant,expires_at:AuthorityInstant,subject_body_digest,intended_use_set,owner_plane_and_slot,body_digest}`, with both instants byte-matching the profile domain/epoch and `not_before < expires_at`. Their subject-specific closed suffixes are: `ProtectedErrorReplayTimeBasis<Role>{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,error_delivery_id,error_generation,protected_error_policy_ref,replay_count_and_ceiling,public_error_digest}`; `TxnOutcomeLookupWindow<Role>{authority_bound_header,capability_commitment,outcome_index_key_commitment,lookup_floor_generation,verifier_key_ref}`; `ProfiledResourceReservationDeadline<Role>{authority_bound_header,reservation_kind,reservation_id,reservation_generation,resource_ledger_basis_digest,expiry_disposition}`; `PriorIncarnationLeaseCohortWindow{cohort_recipe_id,continuity_domain_id,database_security_namespace_id,prior_incarnation,issuer_id,issuer_configuration_identity_and_digest,issuer_authority_epoch,covered_generation_and_counter_ranges,issuer_fence_receipt_digest,cohort_closure_row_bytes_and_digest,time_domain_id,time_authority_epoch,last_legal_issuance_or_renewal_counter,maximum_issued_or_renewed_expires_at:AuthorityInstant,issuance_ledger_accumulator_and_range_completeness_commitment,window_digest}`; `ArchiveRetentionGrantWindow{archive_authority_id,grant_id,grant_generation,grant_subject_set_digest,grant_head_digest_and_cas_version}`; `ArchiveSourceReleasePreparedHoldWindow{archive_authority_id,hold_id,release_generation,participant_set_digest,prepared_head_digest_and_cas_version}`; `KeyEnvelopeGrantWindow<Role>{authority_bound_header,grant_id,generation,recipient_id,graph,branch,envelope_epoch,coverage_cut,grant_record_digest}`; `BackupPublicationFreshness{backup_id,publication_operation_id,publication_bundle_id,publication_authority_head_digest_and_cas_version,receipt_request_binding_digest}`; `BackupTransparencyFreshness{backup_id,transparency_operation_id,required_policy_digest,checkpoint_identity_and_digest,inclusion_subject_digest}`; `TransparencyCheckpointFreshnessBasis{log_id,security_domain_id,witness_policy_oid,checkpoint_body_digest,log_size,claim_class}`; `CrossLogTransparencyFreshness{source_checkpoint_digest,target_log_id,target_policy_oid,target_log_size,target_checkpoint_digest,cross_log_receipt_digest}`; `PayloadReceiptProposalFreshnessBasis{role_and_group,configuration_identity,payload_predicate_digest,storage_member,prepared_ownership_id,base_closure_inventory_digest,receipt_body_without_freshness_or_signature_digest}`; `VerifierKeyWindow{verifier_kind,key_id,key_epoch,verification_scope_digest,retention_floor_digest}`; and `IrreversibleDispatchObservationWindow<Role>{authority_binding_public_commitment,dispatch_contract_id,operation_id,attempt_generation,target_identity,source_gate_commitment,status_or_send_action_digest}`. The cohort window's common `expires_at` must byte-equal the exhaustive signed `maximum_issued_or_renewed_expires_at`; no lifetime, nominal duration, counter arithmetic, or derived expiry field exists. Generation rejects a suffix without its exact prefix, a prefix reused for another subject, an embedded future evidence ref, or a named window whose owner/expiry transition is absent.

`MacaroonRootIssuanceReceipt` is the portable signed `{issuer_id,mac_key_id,mac_key_epoch,root_token_id,root_issuance_sequence,canonical_issuance_request_digest,idempotency_key_digest,root_token_body_digest,canonical_root_token_digest,time_authority_profile_oid,root_not_before,root_expires_at,issuer_counter,authority_registry_head_digest_and_cas_version,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`. `MacaroonRootIssuanceRecord<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is the local durable root-issuance owner `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,root_token_id,issuance_receipt_ref:StrongRef<MacaroonRootIssuanceReceipt>,canonical_issuance_request_digest,idempotency_key_digest,root_token_body_digest,canonical_root_token_digest,canonical_root_token_bytes_ref:StrongRef<CanonicalCapabilityBytes>,replay_retention_floor,issuer_id,mac_key_id,mac_key_epoch,root_issuance_sequence,time_authority_profile_oid,root_not_before,root_expires_at,maximum_attenuation_expiry_equal_to_root_expiry,revocation_subject_commitment,state:Live|Revoked{revocation_evidence_ref}|Expired{time_validation_evidence_ref},body_digest}`. Online issuance creates exactly one record and publishes the matching reservation successor in the same RootManifest generation before returning canonical bytes; exact retry joins and returns the retained identical bytes. The root token ID, request/idempotency commitment, receipt sequence, and byte digest are permanent through the replay floor, while attenuated presentations are derived byte variants and never create inventory rows.

`OfflineMacaroonIssuerEpochFenceReceipt` is the portable signed result of moving one non-exportable counter-backed issuer epoch to verify-only/disabled-for-root-issuance: `{issuer_id,mac_key_id,mac_key_epoch,issuer_epoch_configuration_digest,permitted_root_sequence_range,permitted_hardware_counter_range,last_legal_root_issuance_sequence,returned_issuer_counter,issuer_epoch_state:VerifyOnly|Disabled,authority_registry_head_digest_and_cas_version,fenced_at:AuthorityInstant,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`. `OfflineMacaroonIssuerEpochCohort` is the signed bounded inventory subject `{issuer_id,mac_key_id,mac_key_epoch,issuer_epoch_configuration_digest,time_authority_profile_oid,cohort_not_before,permitted_root_sequence_range,permitted_hardware_counter_range,maximum_root_lifetime_ticks,derived_maximum_possible_expiry,last_legal_root_issuance_sequence,returned_issuer_counter,issuer_epoch_fence_receipt_digest,range_and_maximum_expiry_derivation_proof,issuance_scope_ceiling_commitment,attenuation_semantics_oid,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`. Its checker derives the maximum possible expiry from the configured maximum root lifetime, last permitted counter/sequence, and challenged fence interval; an asserted maximum without that derivation is invalid. It represents every root token that could have been issued by that epoch even when individual bytes are not locally enumerable; it does not validate a presented token. The offline issuer MAC/verify-only service and verification material remain rooted through the derived cohort maximum expiry. Post-fence attenuation of a pre-fence root is legal only under the exact narrowing law and does not create a new cohort member; post-fence root minting is rejected by the hardware counter/fence and by verification. `MacaroonTokenBytes` remains a use-time `TimeBoundSubject` so an individual presented token can be classified, but the rotation inventory tracks online `MacaroonRootIssuanceRecord` rows and offline issuer cohorts—not every possible attenuated byte string.

Each unsigned-body transcript includes its `time_authority_profile_oid`, both bounds when the object has a window, and every authority/domain/generation field, excluding only signatures/MAC and the later `TimeValidationEvidence` reference. Generation performs a two-way total check: every active `durable_fields.toml` time-bearing field set has exactly one nonoverlapping subject row, and every subject row resolves to one live schema/variant, owner floor, and transition. A status-only check may consume a runtime guard; an ordered expiry, release, tombstone, retirement, compaction, or reclamation must retain the exact durable evidence in its applied transition.

A successful Usable validation creates a linear, nonserializable `TimeUseGuard` bound to observation, subject, intended action, process incarnation, and remaining monotonic use budget. It is consumed immediately before the protected observation/irreversible step and cannot survive restart, over-budget suspend, clone, serialization, or replay. Local monotonic time measures only challenge/use age; it never establishes absolute time. Expired evidence is durable and monotone for its one bound canonical release/expiry action. Every canonical transition whose legality depends on expiry strongly retains the exact evidence; a scalar deadline or timeout alone never changes canonical state or cuts retention.

`TimeAuthorityRegistry<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is `{role,generation,profiles[profile_oid -> ActiveForIssuance{profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,issuance_generation}|ClosingRequested{profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,rotation_intent_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityRotationIntentRecord<Role>>,freeze_generation,reservation_index_ref:StrongRef<TimeSubjectIssuanceReservationIndex<Role>>}|IssuanceClosing{profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,rotation_intent_ref,closing_receipt_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityIssuanceClosingReceipt>,local_close_cut}|IssuanceQuiescent{profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,rotation_intent_ref,closing_receipt_ref,own_reservation_closure_ref:StrongRef<RoleTimeIssuanceReservationClosure<Role>>}|Draining{profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,transition_record_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityEpochTransitionRecord<Role>>,issuance_fence_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityIssuanceFence>,subject_inventory_closure_ref:StrongRef<RoleTimeBoundSubjectInventoryClosure<Role>>,drain_hold_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityDrainHold<Role>>,maximum_old_subject_expiry}|Retired{profile_identity_and_digest,terminal_summary_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityTransitionTerminalSummary<Role>>,retired_at_registry_generation}],selected_profile_oid,profile_retirement_floor,body_digest:BodyDigest<TimeAuthorityRegistry<Role>>}`. Profile keys are unique and canonical. In steady state exactly one selected profile is `ActiveForIssuance`; from ordered intent through quiescence there are zero Active profiles and exactly one selected `ClosingRequested`, `IssuanceClosing`, or `IssuanceQuiescent` profile. After activation exactly one successor is Active and the predecessor is Draining. No issuance encoder accepts ClosingRequested, IssuanceClosing, IssuanceQuiescent, Draining, or Retired. The registered body transcript excludes only `body_digest`. Every profile needed by a live window remains rooted, but Retired never retains the transition record, original administrator authorization, live authority binding, old subject objects, drain hold, or detailed dispatch attempts. `TimeValidationEvidence` resolves its profile through the current role registry or, on a Shard, the exact current certified Meta projection: ActiveForIssuance and Draining are valid for verification/use; ClosingRequested/IssuanceClosing/IssuanceQuiescent are valid only for a subject whose immutable reservation predates the freeze; Retired/foreign/unrooted profiles are invalid; and no non-Active state can authorize a new issuance reservation.

Closing issuance is an ordered, externally recoverable protocol, not a read-only guard. Each participating group first orders `TimeIssuanceAdmissionFreezeSpec {transition_id,retiring_profile_oid,expected_active_projection,freeze_generation,expected_reservation_index_ref,terminal_audit_gate:LifecycleScaffoldingNotRequired}`. Its applied record blocks new reservations locally and exports `GroupTimeIssuanceAdmissionFreezeCertificate {SameGroupCertificateHeader,transition_id,role_and_group,retiring_profile_oid,freeze_generation,last_admitted_local_sequence,reservation_index_digest,post_freeze_all_plane_root_and_slot_commitment,one_digest_signer_lock_ref,quorum_signatures}`. Local consumes its own certificate; Meta consumes its own plus one exact certificate from every current or prospective configured shard. `TimeAuthorityRotationIntentSpec<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is then the ordered Semantic authorization `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,admin_authorization_decision_ref:StrongRef<AuthorizationDecisionRecord<Role>>,transition_id,expected_registry_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityRegistry<Role>>,expected_registry_generation,expected_profile_state:ActiveForIssuance,retiring_profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,successor_profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,exact_current_and_prospective_group_freeze_certificate_set,exact_configured_offline_issuer_epoch_set,external_close_operation_recipe,external_fence_operation_recipe,external_registry_transition_operation_recipe,closure_resource_reservations,abort_before_external_fence_recipe,terminal_audit_gate}`. Apply atomically selects `ClosingRequested` and creates immutable `TimeAuthorityRotationIntentRecord<Role>` owning those exact sets, operation IDs/idempotency keys/transcripts, resource holds, authorization, and audit lineage. Only its durable `PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Role>` may initialize the universal external-effect dispatch for the close operation.

The external close request byte-matches the intent and all group floors. Status-first recovery returns portable `TimeAuthorityIssuanceClosingReceipt {external_request_binding:ExternalActionRequestBinding{action_kind=TimeAuthorityIssuanceClose},transition_id,retiring_profile_oid,closing_head_digest_and_cas_version,sorted_group_closing_floors[{role_and_group,issuance_epoch,last_admitted_local_sequence,reservation_inventory_digest,quiescence_certificate_digest:None}],configured_group_set_commitment,configured_offline_issuer_epoch_set_commitment,closed_at:AuthorityInstant,signer_set_epoch,threshold_signatures}` and atomically rejects any old-profile reservation beyond those group-local floors. Protocol receipt import produces portable terminal evidence; it never mutates Semantic state directly. `TimeAuthorityIssuanceCloseSpec<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` consumes the intent, receipt, dispatch terminal evidence, exact group-freeze set, and current registry and changes only `ClosingRequested -> IssuanceClosing`. A shard consumes the certified Meta close projection through `ShardTimeAuthorityIssuanceCloseApplySpec` and changes only its active projection/freeze state. Before the external close is known sent, a typed abort may select `ClosingRequested -> ActiveForIssuance` and release every unchanged group freeze and resource hold. Once the close dispatch is `SentUnknown` or receipted, reopen is illegal.

`TimeAuthorityTransitionCompletionAuthority<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is the non-widenable structural `{role_and_group,transition_id,rotation_intent_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityRotationIntentRecord<Role>>,original_admin_authorization_decision_ref:StrongRef<AuthorizationDecisionRecord<Role>>,original_authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,retiring_and_successor_profile_commitment,configured_group_offline_issuer_and_resource_commitment,close_fence_and_registry_operation_commitment,irreversibility_basis:CloseSentUnknown{attempt_ref:StrongRef<IrreversibleDispatchAttempt<TimeAuthorityIssuanceClose>>,canonical_full_request_digest}|ClosingReceipted{terminal_evidence_ref:StrongRef<PortableTimeAuthorityIssuanceCloseTerminalEvidence>}|FinalFenceSentUnknown{attempt_ref:StrongRef<IrreversibleDispatchAttempt<TimeAuthorityIssuanceFence>>,canonical_full_request_digest}|FinalFenceReceipted{terminal_evidence_ref:StrongRef<PortableTimeAuthorityIssuanceFenceTerminalEvidence>}|RegistryTransitionSentUnknown{attempt_ref:StrongRef<IrreversibleDispatchAttempt<TimeAuthorityRegistryTransition>>,canonical_full_request_digest}|RegistryTransitionReceipted{terminal_evidence_ref:StrongRef<PortableTimeAuthorityRegistryTransitionTerminalEvidence>},allowed_successor_spec_tags[TimeAuthorityIssuanceCloseSpec|TimeAuthorityIssuanceFenceAuthorizeSpec|TimeAuthorityRegistryTransitionAuthorizeSpec|TimeAuthorityProfileTransitionSpec],body_digest}`. It is constructible only from the rooted intent plus the exact current universal-dispatch attempt or terminal evidence at or beyond the listed irreversible state; a bare stage enum is insufficient. It cannot alter the successor, issuer/group sets, resources, operation IDs, request bodies, authority ceiling, or audit lineage, and cannot authorize abort, retirement, fresh issuance, or a new client choice.

`TimeAuthorityRetirementCleanupAuthority<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is the distinct structural `{role_and_group,transition_record_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityEpochTransitionRecord<Role>>,expected_registry_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityRegistry<Role>>,required_retiring_state:Draining,complete_subject_inventory_and_disposition_commitment,shutdown_and_verifier_floor_commitment,configuration_and_shard_retirement_floor_commitment,allowed_successor_spec_tag:TimeAuthorityProfileRetirementSpec,body_digest}`. It is constructible only after activation, from the exact Draining state and complete cleanup closure; it authorizes only deterministic retirement of that one predecessor profile and cannot change either profile, reissue a subject, or widen authority.

Every issuance already admitted owns a predecessor-linked immutable `TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role> {authority_binding:AuthorityBindingFor<Role>,stable_reservation_key:{profile_oid,role_and_group,issuance_epoch,issuance_sequence,idempotency_key_digest},generation,predecessor_ref:StrongRef<TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role>>?,transition_or_operation_id,subject_arm,canonical_pre_evidence_subject_digest,state:Reserved|Published{subject_identity,publication_cut,subject_membership_proof_ref}|Burned{typed_no_publication_proof_ref},body_digest}` indexed by `TimeSubjectIssuanceReservationIndex<Role>`. Reserved is generation one. Its sole terminal successor is generation two: Published is installed in the same RootManifest/RootSlot publication that installs the issued subject owner, while Burned requires a typed proof that no such owner/publication exists. Recovery may turn a lingering Reserved into Published only by proving exact current-root subject membership, otherwise into Burned only by proving nonpublication. A nonserializable `TimeIssuanceGuard` can be constructed only from one current Reserved row and is consumed by the matching Published/Burned successor; it cannot be acquired from an observation alone.

Prior-incarnation/archive edges use exact nonlocal types. `PriorIncarnationObjectRef<T> {restore_id,source_backup_manifest_digest,source_cluster_incarnation,target_cluster_incarnation,source:BackupArchiveRef<T>}` is legal only for content-inventory objects in restore plans/results/bridges/evidence/provenance and never enters the current mark set; `T=BackupManifest|BackupManifestBody|BackupManifestSignatureSet` is a generated negative. `RestoreSourceLeaseIdentity` is `{restore_id,source_backup_identity:{source_database_id,source_database_security_namespace_id,source_cluster_incarnation,backup_id,backup_manifest_digest,publication_bundle_id,archive_retention_grant_id,archive_grant_subject_set_digest,archive_inventory_root_digest,permitted_inventory_digest},target_holder_identity:{target_database_id,target_database_security_namespace_id,target_incarnation,target_service_visibility_epoch,recovery_authority_digest},archive_authority_id,lease_lineage_id,holder_authority_digest}`. Stable identity deliberately excludes grant and lease generations. `PortableRestoreSourceLeaseStateDigest` is `BLAKE3("fgdb.restore-source-lease-state.v1" || canonical(lease_identity,generation,selected_grant_generation_and_digest,window_profile_domain_epoch_and_bounds,archive_counter,holder_and_subject_set_commitment))`; it is derived entirely from portable archive-authority state and is never a keyed Local/Meta ObjectId or body digest. `PortableArchiveGrantLineageProof` is the reference-free signed `{archive_authority_id,grant_id,selected_generation,selected_grant_digest,ordered_predecessor_generation_and_digest_chain,current_head_digest_and_cas_version,unchanged_subject_set_digest,window_coverage,archive_monotonic_counter,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`. `RestoreSourceLeaseAcquireReceipt` and `RestoreSourceLeaseRenewReceipt` are distinct portable external receipts with `ExternalActionRequestBinding`, the stable lease identity, exact predecessor generation and portable lease-state digest for renewal, selected grant generation/digest, complete signed `PortableRestoreSourceLeaseLineageProof` bytes and digest, resulting lease generation/window/counter, resulting `PortableRestoreSourceLeaseStateDigest`, and signature. The lineage proof names request/result-head commitments but never its enclosing receipt digest, so receipt construction remains acyclic.

Before a target database exists, `PreBootstrapRestoreSourceLeaseOwner` is a registered prebootstrap artifact schema, not a logical object: `{identity:RestoreSourceLeaseIdentity,generation,portable_lease_state_digest:PortableRestoreSourceLeaseStateDigest,predecessor_owner_digest?,portable_plan_digest,source_gate_digest,record_kind:Acquire{receipt_artifact_ref:PreBootstrapArtifactRef<RestoreSourceLeaseAcquireReceipt>}|Renew{receipt_artifact_ref:PreBootstrapArtifactRef<RestoreSourceLeaseRenewReceipt>},selected_archive_grant_generation_and_digest,grant_lineage_proof_artifact_ref:PreBootstrapArtifactRef<PortableArchiveGrantLineageProof>,lease_window_successor_proof_artifact_ref:PreBootstrapArtifactRef<LeaseWindowSuccessorProof>?,lease_lineage_proof_artifact_ref:PreBootstrapArtifactRef<PortableRestoreSourceLeaseLineageProof>,time_authority_profile_oid,not_before,expires_at,archive_monotonic_counter,recovery_authority_public_commitment,journal_id,owner_publication_journal_head_generation_digest_and_cas_version,owner_publication_dispatch_state_generation_and_digest,relocation_chain_head_commitment,body_digest}`. It deliberately contains no inode, path, local mirror identity, or mutable dispatch-root locator. The acquire/renew terminal payload must journal the complete signed lineage proof before this owner can become Current; a digest-only result is invalid after restart or relocation. `PreBootstrapRestoreSourceLeaseCurrent` stores `owner_artifact_ref:PreBootstrapArtifactRef<PreBootstrapRestoreSourceLeaseOwner>` plus checked generation/portable-state/lineage commitment and resolves it only through the authenticated current journal head and relocation chain. Acquire creates generation one; registered prebootstrap renewal creates `g+1`, advances Current, and makes the prior artifact reclaimable only after the successor/head/capsule publication is durable. Relocating the cache inode changes neither owner identity nor authority; a stale mirror that cannot prove the current head/relocation chain is unusable. This owner is never a current-database authority record.

`LeaseWindowSuccessorProof` is an independently addressable registered logical schema with the closed body `SameEpochNonshrinking{lease_identity,prior_and_successor_generations,same_profile_domain_epoch,prior_and_successor_bounds,checked_nonshrinking_bounds_and_counter,archive_authority_signature}|CrossEpochHandoff{lease_identity,prior_and_successor_generations,old_and_new_profile_identities,dual_signed_transition_proof,no_gap_coverage_proof,checked_domain_mapping,archive_authority_signature}`. `PortableRestoreSourceLeaseLineageCheckpoint` is the reference-free signed contiguous-range summary `{lease_identity,start_generation_and_predecessor_head,end_generation_and_complete_head_bytes_digest_and_cas_version,ordered_operation_id_idempotency_request_result_head_and_outcome_accumulator,complete_generation_range_and_no_fork_proof,unchanged_holder_subject_archive_authority_and_permitted_inventory_commitment,start_and_end_archive_counters,predecessor_checkpoint:Genesis|Prior{complete_checkpoint_bytes_and_digest},provider_status_and_operation_nonreuse_floor,checkpoint_availability_and_retention_certificate,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`. It cannot omit a generation, summarize an unresolved operation, change subject/holder/inventory, or refer only to unavailable bytes. `PortableRestoreSourceLeaseLineageProof` is the reference-free signed `{lease_identity,selected_generation,selected_portable_lease_state_digest:PortableRestoreSourceLeaseStateDigest,lineage_basis:Genesis|Checkpointed{complete_prior_checkpoint_bytes_and_digest:PortableRestoreSourceLeaseLineageCheckpoint},ordered_generation_operation_request_and_result_head_commitments_after_basis,unchanged_holder_subject_and_archive_authority_commitment,current_head_bytes_digest_and_cas_version,archive_counter,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`; it never names a keyed Local/Meta record or body digest. Prebootstrap owner generations retain the complete checkpoint artifact; canonical `RestoreSourceLeaseLineageCheckpointImport<Role>` carries a full `AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>`, the complete portable checkpoint, current lease-lineage proof, and exact byte-match proof. The current canonical lease record and then its release operation summary retain the latest import through the provider status/nonreuse/retention floor; checked lease-history compaction may replace earlier details only when the checkpoint covers them and remains independently available.

Canonical `RestoreSourceLeaseRecord<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,identity:RestoreSourceLeaseIdentity,generation,portable_lease_state_digest:PortableRestoreSourceLeaseStateDigest,predecessor:Genesis|Prior{record_digest:WeakDigest},record_kind:AcquireImported{prebootstrap_owner_digest,receipt_ref:StrongRef<RestoreSourceLeaseAcquireReceipt>}|RenewImported{receipt_ref:StrongRef<RestoreSourceLeaseRenewReceipt>,lease_window_successor_proof_ref:StrongRef<LeaseWindowSuccessorProof>},selected_archive_grant_generation,selected_archive_grant_digest,grant_lineage_proof_ref:StrongRef<PortableArchiveGrantLineageProof>,lease_lineage_proof_ref:StrongRef<PortableRestoreSourceLeaseLineageProof>,lineage_basis:Genesis|Checkpointed{checkpoint_import_ref:StrongRef<RestoreSourceLeaseLineageCheckpointImport<Role>>},time_authority_profile_oid,not_before,expires_at,archive_monotonic_counter,body_digest}`. The portable state digest byte-matches the receipt, authority head, observations, proofs, checkpoint basis, and all portable projections; the keyed role-local `body_digest` and ObjectId remain separate. The first Local/Meta bridge imports the latest prebootstrap generation—not necessarily generation one—with the full current authority header. Later renewal constructs `prior+1`, preserves all stable identities/subject sets, advances the counter, and carries exact successor and lineage proofs; raw tick comparison across domains or authority epochs is invalid. The prior visible registry strongly owns the old record until renewal finalize becomes visible, after which the weak predecessor digest plus signed lineage proof/checkpoint avoids an unbounded strong chain without making historical status evidence disappear.

`ShardRestoreSourceLeaseProjectionSource` is the closed union `Bootstrap{bootstrap_certificate_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<RestoreShardBootstrapProjectionCertificate>,bootstrap_projection_identity_and_digest,source_lease_projection_payload_identity_and_digest}|Refresh{meta_control_projection_certificate_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<MetaControlProjectionCertificate>,typed_meta_projection_payload_identity_and_digest}`. `ShardRestoreSourceLeaseProjection` is `{source:ShardRestoreSourceLeaseProjectionSource,source_meta_prefix,source_meta_configuration_identity,lease_identity,generation,portable_lease_state_digest:PortableRestoreSourceLeaseStateDigest,selected_grant_generation_and_digest,window_profile_domain_epoch_and_bounds,archive_counter,holder_and_subject_set_commitment,retention_grant_and_payload_availability_evidence,body_digest}`. Bootstrap validates the exact `RestoreShardBootstrapProjectionCertificate` and its certificate-free payload; Refresh uses only `TypedCertifiedMetaProjectionPayload::RestoreSourceLease`, must name the same restore/plan/shard/lease lineage and unchanged holder/subject/inventory/recipient commitments, and may advance only `g -> g+1` with the exact successor proof. A Shard never owns a canonical lease record and cannot renew or release it.

`RestoreArchiveRef<T> {source:PriorIncarnationObjectRef<T>,lease_identity:RestoreSourceLeaseIdentity,permitted_inventory_leaf,leaf_proof}` contains no strong lease-generation edge. `RestorePublicationArtifactRef<T> {source:BackupPublicationArtifactRef<T>,lease_identity:RestoreSourceLeaseIdentity,permitted_grant_subject_leaf,grant_subject_leaf_proof,publication_receipt_binding}` is legal only for exact publication-envelope artifact kinds and proves the locator row against the lease-bound publication receipt/grant subject set. Every reference and registry common field must match both source and target identities. Before the bridge, resolution uses the current prebootstrap owner; afterward Local/Meta resolution requires the latest canonical live lease record and Shard resolution requires the exact current certified projection, plus subject-preserving grant lineage, `TimeValidationEvidence::Usable`, and the exact inventory/grant proof.

Source acquisition precedes canonical target creation and is externally recoverable. Pre-send `RestoreIdentityKeyPlan` is the closed union `PreserveSameIdentity{identical_namespace_basis,source_k_oid_identity_and_commitment,recover_and_rewrap_operation_recipe,target_rewrap_recipient_commitment,required_key_equality_proof_profile,required_zero_plaintext_persistence_proof_profile}|CloneFreshIdentity{distinct_namespace_basis,source_k_oid_source_open_only_commitment,recover_source_k_oid_for_decode_operation_recipe,create_target_k_oid_operation_recipe,target_k_oid_recipient_commitment,required_source_key_nontransplant_proof_profile}`. It contains only recipes, expected identities, and proof profiles. Post-provider `RestoreIdentityKeyDispositionEvidence` is the distinct closed union `PreservedSameIdentity{plan_digest,identical_namespace_proof,recover_and_rewrap_receipt_ref:RestoreKeyProviderReceiptRef,source_k_oid_commitment,target_rewrapped_k_oid_commitment,key_equality_proof,zero_plaintext_persistence_proof}|ClonedFreshIdentity{plan_digest,distinct_namespace_proof,recover_source_k_oid_receipt_ref:RestoreKeyProviderReceiptRef,create_target_k_oid_receipt_ref:RestoreKeyProviderReceiptRef,source_k_oid_source_open_only_commitment,target_k_oid_commitment,source_key_nontransplant_proof}`. Clone source `K_oid` and DEKs authorize source decoding only; every target ciphertext receives a fresh target DEK under the newly created target identity.

`RestoreClaimedTargetAuthorityRecipe` is the pre-claim closed union `RecoverSameIdentity{expected_operational_or_fence_predecessor_digest_and_cas_version,restore_id,source_backup_identity,planned_target_incarnation,recovery_writer_authority_digest,service_visibility_epoch,prior_lease_fence_plan_commitment}|CloneNewIdentity{identity_reservation_id,expected_reserved_head_digest_and_cas_version,claim_id,claimant_identity,target_database_and_security_identity,target_incarnation,recovery_writer_authority_digest,service_visibility_epoch,continuity_profile:DirectoryBound{filesystem_profile_id,mount_device_directory_and_target_manifest_inode_identity,target_manifest_staging_inode_creation_nonce_digest,whole_inode_fence_identity,parent_directory_durability_recipe,fixed_local_continuity_recipe_and_digest,zero_existing_root_slot_proof_recipe,directory_bound_creation_evidence_recipe_digest}|ExternalCas{expected_continuity_predecessor_digest_and_cas_version,enter_clone_reserved_operation_recipe,recovery_only_lease_recipe}}`. It contains no resulting claimed/reserved head and no plan digest field that would make the plan self-referential. DirectoryBound carries no external continuity head or CAS recipe; ExternalCas requires both.

## Ownership, verification, and diagnostics
For every schema, field, tag, state, transition, reference, digest transcript, construction-order rule, and role restriction in this slice, generate a durable_fields.toml row with stable IDs; canonical encoding/version policy; concrete generic/role expansion; producer, owner bead/crate, and consumers; reference strength/target set; authority and redaction class; invariant/evidence/cost bindings; test/scenario/event IDs; and consuming gate. Cross-slice targets use stable catalog IDs and must resolve in the Appendix A epic closure. Downstream owners may add implementation detail but cannot abbreviate, alias, weaken, or contradict these bytes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The embedded line range is byte-complete, checksum-pinned, continuous with adjacent slices, and contains no truncation marker.
- Every exact named construct in the slice has one stable row and exactly one granular implementation owner; all references and consumers resolve.
- Unit tests cover canonical encode/decode, stable field/tag IDs, role/generic expansion, digest construction, state preconditions, and owner uniqueness.
- Property/mutation/fuzz tests remove, duplicate, reorder, retag, corrupt, weaken, or cross-role substitute every field/arm/reference class and prove rejection.
- Simulation tests exercise applicable crash, cancellation, retry, sent-unknown, receipt-first, recovery, authority/configuration rotation, compaction, and expiry boundaries.
- E2E scripts traverse each applicable public embedded/server/FGP/CLI path through durable publication, restart/replay, backup/restore, and terminal cleanup using isolated synthetic fixtures.
- Detailed versioned JSONL diagnostics carry schema_id, field_or_arm_id, role/group, object or public commitment, transition_id, state_before/state_after, checker, verdict, artifact refs, and replay command; secret/noninterference tests reject protected data or observable hidden state.
- Cross-version golden vectors and unknown-required-field fixtures enforce additive-minor/breaking-major policy; no gate passes with an uncovered row.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: family-level prose summaries, wildcard references, inferred fields, unregistered aliases, or treating the catalog slice as the implementation. Exactness is intentional; execution remains decomposed across the linked workstream beads.

THE UNRESERVED-CANDIDATE CLASSIFICATION CALLS: SCOPED, EVIDENCED, AND PARTITIONED. Done off-token; no shared file touched.

FIRST, A COUNT CORRECTION. The standing trail says "15 unreserved unclassified candidates". The live figure is 33. A candidate needs a call when it has no [[target]], no [[reservation]], no [[source_symbol_disposition]], and no minted logical kind. The 15 was an earlier, narrower reading; plan on 33.

METHOD, and its limits stated up front. Two probes: one for definition-site evidence (census owner_statuses, definition_kinds, body_conflict, source locations, and whether the census renders a structural BODY), one for USAGE across the whole appendix field census (bare-type use, StrongRef target, nested/list use, arm-token match). Usage is the stronger signal — a symbol strong-referenced from anywhere MUST be a logical kind, and a symbol that appears in the census arm set is an arm token no matter how its brace body reads. THE LIMIT, stated because it changes how one bucket must be read: my usage scan covers Appendix A FIELD types only. It does not see references from command contracts, Appendix B intents, or ordering prose. So "no external use" means "no Appendix A field names it", NOT "not durable". Several symbols in that bucket are the command-contract-owned specs and authorities the trail already identified, and they will be referenced from the command_contracts registry instead. Do not classify anything in that bucket as not-a-durable-schema on this evidence alone.

ONE CALL IS DECIDED, WITH SOURCE PROOF. `Retired` is NOT a top-level schema — it is a union arm token of the TimeAuthorityRegistry profiles issuance-state union. The census flagged it as an AmbiguousUnownedStructure top-level candidate because the brace body `Retired{terminal_summary_ref}` parses like a definition, but the source at a16:2223 reads "deterministically creates TimeAuthorityTransitionTerminalSummary<Role>, SELECTS Retired{terminal_summary_ref}" — selection of an arm, not a definition. Disposition it as an arm, never mint it as a kind. That is the one call I would land today without further reading.

FIVE HAVE NO STRUCTURAL BODY AT ALL, which is the cleanest discriminator the census offers: CommitCx, MacaroonTokenBytes, PortableRestoreSourceLeaseStateDigest, PreBootstrapRestoreSourceLeaseCurrent, ReplayArchiveLease. CommitCx is an asupersync capability context (see AGENTS.md doctrine 3) and is categorically not a durable format — it is the Cx the writer holds, mentioned in ordering prose. MacaroonTokenBytes and PortableRestoreSourceLeaseStateDigest are byte/digest value types. PreBootstrapRestoreSourceLeaseCurrent and ReplayArchiveLease are named states/leases whose bytes live in another schema. None of the five should become a logical kind; each needs a value-type or not-a-durable-schema disposition, and the two prebootstrap ones must be settled with the a17 owner (still-open gotcha 3 on that bead).

ELEVEN ARE USED BARE AS A FIELD TYPE, which is what makes them the field-unblocking set: AuthorityInstant, AuthorityInterval, ClusterIncarnationLease, LocalChallengeRoundTripWitness, PortableRestoreSourceLeaseLineageCheckpoint, PortableRestoreSourceLeaseStateDigest, PriorIncarnationObjectRef<T>, RestoreSourceLeaseIdentity, TimeAuthorityProfileRetirementSpec<Role>, TimeAuthorityRetirementCleanupAuthority<Role>, TimeAuthorityTransitionCompletionAuthority<Role>. Each is a genuine fork: a named sub-record used bare is either (a) its own logical kind, with consumers holding a StrongRef, or (b) a WIRE TYPE, inlined into the consumer's bytes with no independent object identity. The evidence that decides it is whether the plan ever gives the symbol an independent lifecycle — its own publication, retention, or reference — and that is a per-symbol read of the source, not something a probe settles. AuthorityInstant and AuthorityInterval (3 and 2 members) are almost certainly wire types: they are time VALUES, inlined everywhere, with no lifecycle of their own. RestoreSourceLeaseIdentity (21 members) and TimeAuthorityTransitionCompletionAuthority<Role> (20 members, plus 1 union) are large enough that a logical kind with its own identity is the likely call. PriorIncarnationObjectRef<T>, RestoreArchiveRef<T> and RestorePublicationArtifactRef<T> are reference WRAPPERS by name and shape and belong in the wire class beside StrongRef/CertifiedRemoteStrongRef, not as logical kinds.

ONE IS USED ONLY NESTED: TimeAuthorityProfileTransitionSpec<Role>, inside a list. A list-of-X still needs X to be a named type, so it lands in the same fork as the eleven.

THE REMAINING TWENTY are in the "no Appendix A field names them" bucket and must be read against the command contracts before classification: ArchiveRetentionGrantWindow, ArchiveSourceReleasePreparedHoldWindow, BackupPublicationFreshness, BackupTransparencyFreshness, GroupTimeIssuanceAdmissionFreezeCertificate, IrreversibleDispatchObservationWindow<Role>, PreBootstrapRestoreSourceLeaseOwner, PreBootstrapTimeValidationEvidence, ProfiledResourceReservationDeadline<Role>, RestoreArchiveRef<T>, RestorePublicationArtifactRef<T>, TimeAuthorityRotationIntentSpec<Role>, TimeIssuanceAdmissionFreezeSpec, TimeObservationServiceContract, TxnOutcomeLookupWindow<Role>, VerifierKeyWindow and the four already named above. WHAT I DID NOT DO, and why. I did not mint or disposition anything. No adjudication needed.

WORKED OWNER: TimeAuthorityProfile, order 20, 15 flat members, all 15 currently uncovered. I did this one because it sits low in the DAG and has nine strong-ref consumers, so getting it wrong is expensive.

comments.text:
A LATENT UNSATISFIABLE CONSTRUCTION-ORDER CONSTRAINT IN A RELEASED KIND — found by designing TimeAuthorityRegistry's field body, and it must be settled before that body can be modelled at all.

THE FACTS, all probe-derived against the cf58ccb snapshot rather than the live tree. The source at a16:2181 reads: TimeAuthorityRegistry<Role:AuthorityOwningRole> is {role,generation,profiles[profile_oid -> ActiveForIssuance{profile_ref:StrongRef<TimeAuthorityProfile>,issuance_generation}|ClosingRequested{...}|IssuanceClosing{...}|IssuanceQuiescent{...}|Draining{...}|Retired{...}],selected_profile_oid,profile_retirement_floor,body_digest}. So `profiles` is an INDEXED MAP whose value is a closed six-arm union.

The census does NOT emit a union candidate for it. It emitted ZERO union candidates under TimeAuthorityRegistry and instead produced 23 nested FIELD keys at depth three: profiles.ActiveForIssuance.profile_ref, profiles.Draining.drain_hold_ref, profiles.Retired.terminal_summary_ref, and so on. The reason is a parser-coverage gap, not a source defect: the census recognises the `field:A|B` union spelling (that is what I2a/I6a/I6b modelled) but not the `field[key -> A|B]` indexed-map spelling. Evidence that both spellings really are in use: ShardTimeAuthorityProjection.sorted_profile_projections.record.issuance_state IS recognised as a union candidate, and it is written with an explicit `record.` segment.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS AN EMPTY ORDER WINDOW. Probing the order law from both directions, as the law requires: the strong references inside those arm interiors reach TimeAuthorityTransitionTerminalSummary<Role> (order 65), TimeAuthorityEpochTransitionRecord<Role> (60), TimeAuthorityDrainHold<Role> (55), RoleTimeBoundSubjectInventoryClosure<Role> (40) and others, so modelling them as field rows on TimeAuthorityRegistry demands construction_order >= 65. Its six strong-ref consumers (TimeAuthorityObservationImport at 23, plus the four unminted Spec/Authority symbols and TimeAuthorityEpochTransitionRecord) demand <= 23. TimeAuthorityRegistry is minted at 21. 65 > 23, so there is NO order that satisfies both directions. Nobody has hit this yet only because none of those 23 interior keys has a field row; the contradiction is latent, and the first agent to model `.profiles` as flat or nested strong fields will hit a wall that looks like a bad order rather than a modelling error.

FOUR RESOLUTIONS, with my reading of each. (a) TEACH THE CENSUS THE INDEXED-MAP UNION SPELLING so `.profiles` gets a union plus six arms; the interiors are then committed by arm payload digests, which create no DAG edge, and the registry stays at 21. Most faithful to the source, and it reuses the exact mechanism every other embedded union already uses — but it changes the census parser, which moves candidate counts and sha pins for EVERY slice, so it is a heavy catalog-wide change and emphatically not a unilateral one. (b) MINT THE MAP VALUE AS ITS OWN NAMED SCHEMA (a profile-registry-entry type) at an order >= 65 and have `profiles` hold entries INLINE, committed by the registry's own body digest; no DAG edge, registry stays at 21, and it needs no parser change. If instead the entries were held by StrongRef the constraint returns unsatisfiable, so the inline reading is the only workable form of this option. (c) WEAKEN the interior references to weak_digest or conditional. This removes the constraint but changes retention semantics — a registry pointing at the profiles it is currently administering plainly means to retain them — so I think this is wrong, and it would be the a01 identity-versus-reachability law applied backwards. (d) MOVE the registry's order: impossible, the window is empty.

I RECOMMEND (a) as correct and (b) as the pragmatic fallback if the census change is judged too expensive, and I am NOT deciding it. It is either a census/checker change with catalog-wide pin consequences or a change to the object graph of a released kind; both exceed what an increment inside a16 should settle alone. Escalating to the granular owner (w9-time-authority-0rv6) and whoever owns the census parser. This also warrants its own bead, which I did not create because bead creation moves the architecture bead-provenance pins and that needs the catalog token, currently held by cc_2 — file it on the next hold.

SCOPE OF THE BLOCK: TimeAuthorityRegistry has 6 flat members and 23 interior keys, 29 uncovered field keys in total, and it is the second-largest uncovered owner in a16. All 29 are blocked on this ruling. The same indexed-map spelling should be swept for across the other slices before the ruling is made, since the parser gap is not a16-specific.

A METHOD NOTE FOR THE NEXT AGENT, because it is the reason this surfaced at all: the owner probe prints the order window from BOTH directions — max order of anything the owner strong-refs (lower bound) and min order over every consumer that strong-refs it (upper bound). Reading only the consumer side, as the trail warned in I5, would have shown a comfortable `<= 23` and hidden the contradiction entirely.

COMPOSITE GATE RECORD — ATTRIBUTABLE TO COMMIT cf58ccb. This is the record that has been owed for three increments, and it is now taken in a form that needs no quiescence and is repeatable by anyone at any HEAD.

RESULT: scripts/check.sh exit 0, ALL GATES GREEN, all seven steps in sequence — cargo fmt --check, cargo check --all-targets, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test (822 tests across 30 binaries, zero failures), registry-check all, scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh, architecture-check. The recurring "error: unclosed table, expected `]`" lines in the log are the known asupersync deliberately-malformed test fixture (tests/fixtures/migration_readiness_planner/malformed/Cargo.toml), not failures.

METHOD, and why it beats waiting for a clean tree. In a six-agent shared checkout a clean working tree is not reliably obtainable — the window opened and shut twice while I was waiting for it, and the two composite runs I attempted against the live tree were both unattributable because another lane had uncommitted work in it. Instead:
  SNAP=/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/gate-snapshot-$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
  mkdir -p "$SNAP" && git archive HEAD | tar -x -C "$SNAP"
  cd "$SNAP" && CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/snapshot-target ./scripts/check.sh
`git archive HEAD` materialises exactly the committed state including tracked .beads/, with no agent's WIP. scripts/check.sh derives its own ROOT from its own location, so the whole run stays inside the snapshot; nothing can dirty the real tree and no concurrent commit can perturb the run mid-flight. The separate CARGO_TARGET_DIR means the run neither waits on nor holds the shared target-dir lock. architecture-check must run LOCALLY, not through rch, because remote workers do not sync .beads/ and it fails there with "issues.jsonl: No such file or directory".

ONE TRAP, PAID FOR AND WORTH RECORDING. My first snapshot run failed at clippy with "multiple workspace roots found in the same workspace" — and that was self-inflicted, not a real defect. I had earlier repointed a scratch probe crate's path dependency at the snapshot's tools/registry-check and, to make it build standalone, appended a [workspace] table to its Cargo.toml. That second workspace root inside the snapshot broke clippy for the whole run. THE RULE: a snapshot used as a gate record is READ-ONLY. Anything that mutates it invalidates the record. The fix was a fresh snapshot plus giving the probe its own private copy of registry-check, after which clippy passed — which is also the proof that the failure was mine and not the tree's.

WHAT THIS RECORD COVERS. cf58ccb is the tip of this session's a16 work: 0246145 (the fgdb-tfow reconstruction fix, the pipe-bearing union it unblocked, and the 19 forced I7 adjudications), 7cff9e6 (the 21 derivable strong-reference field rows), and the bead-evidence commits between them. RULING: generic-signed containing_schema on FIELD rows. Posting immediately and out of band because cc_1/pane2 has 8 Tier B generic-target rows blocked on it and currently holds the catalog token — cc_1, you can act on this inside your current hold; you do not need to wait for my 2G to land, and you should not re-derive any of it.

THE RULING IS: THERE IS NOTHING TO RULE. The contract you are waiting for already exists and is already law — YOUR OWN commit 4081560 ("feat(a16): generic-family field hosts and the five generic embedded unions") added it. identity.rs resolves a field row's containing_schema through the generic-free family:

    let containing_family = generic_free_family(f.containing_schema.as_str());
    let containing_logical = logical_by_name.get(containing_family);

so a field row whose containing_schema is `Foo<Bar>` resolves through the registered bare `Foo` kind row. The family is a LOOKUP ONLY: tag uniqueness, anchor matching and BodyDigest recipes all still key on the exact signed containing_schema, so two expansions never merge. I had this recorded as an open blocker on a01 and that was simply wrong — 4081560 predates my own 2D.

VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED. I spliced real generic-host field rows into a scratch copy of HEAD and validated: zero structural violations, specifically no field_unresolved_schema and no wire_context_mismatch. Then I landed two of them for real in 1828232 (ExportLeaf<T>.target_identity and ExportLeaf<T>.local_strong_ref_projection), gates green, e2e 94/0. So the path is proven end to end, not merely legal on paper.

WHAT YOU CAN DERIVE DIRECTLY, for your 8 Tier B rows:
 1. Write containing_schema as the EXACT census schema_owner, generic signature included — e.g. "TimeBoundSubjectInventory<Role:Local|Meta|Shard>", not the bare family. The target source_key must match the census key byte-for-byte, and the census key carries the signature.
 2. row_id derivation is the one real gotcha, and it will fail your first attempt if you guess. lower_kebab renders the signature's punctuation as separators, so `ExportLeaf<T>` becomes `export-leaf-t`. Do not hand-write these: land the row, read catalog_row_id_derived_mismatch, and adopt the expected value it prints. That is how I got mine.
 3. construction_order must equal the containing kind's, per identity.rs:1681 — forced, not chosen.
 4. If a row's exact_wire_type is a type that PREDATES the A10 erratum (a builtin, or a wire type like RemoteObjectIdentity), the frozen-history witness cannot see it via post_erratum_union(&field.exact_wire_type), because that predicate matches union NAMES. title: Appendix A exact catalog: Restore prebootstrap journal and source acquisition formats
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the exact Appendix A catalog slice for Restore prebootstrap journal and source acquisition formats. This task embeds source-plan lines 2247-2348 verbatim, expands every generic and role-indexed family into stable registered rows, and assigns each row to its granular implementation owner. It is a format/ownership contract, not a substitute implementation.

## Exact normative contract
The following audited source-plan text is authoritative and self-contained:

`RestoreSourceAcquisitionActionKey` is a plan key, not a second dispatch-action registry. Its generated total mapping selects exactly one live **RestorePreBootstrap contract row** in `irreversible_dispatch_contracts.toml`, whose action kind is one of `EnterRestoreFencePending|PriorIncarnationLeaseIssuerFence{issuer_key}|PriorIncarnationLeaseCohortRevoke{issuer_key,cohort_key}|EnterRestoreReserved|ReservationClaim{reservation_kind,reservation_id}|EnterCloneReserved|RestoreArchiveAcquire|CommitAcquisitionRefinementBootstrapOpeners|CommitAcquisitionRefinementVerifiedObjectInventory|RecoverAndRewrapPreservedObjectIdKey|RecoverSourceObjectIdKeyForDecode|CreateTargetObjectIdKey|RecoverSourceBootstrapDek{artifact_key}|RecoverSourceObjectDekForReprotect{inventory_ordinal}|RestoreArchiveLeaseRenew{family_id,ordinal}|RecoveryIncarnationLeaseAcquireOrRefresh{family_id,ordinal}|RestoreArchiveLeaseRelease|ReservationBurnBeforeUse{reservation_kind,reservation_id,claim_id?}|CatalogTombstoneRestoreTarget{catalog_profile}|RestoreContinuityAbandon|RevokeTransientRecoveryWrap{artifact_key}|DestroyFreshUnpublishedTargetObjectIdKey{artifact_key}|RestoreUnpublishedTargetPhysicalDelete{target_ordinal}`. Every key maps bijectively to one exact `dispatch_contract_id`, operation/body recipe, source-gate recipe, prebootstrap attempt/import type, resource relation, and cleanup disposition; a canonical-plane row for the same provider action is a different contract and cannot satisfy the mapping. No alias may rename or merge dispatch kinds. `EnterCloneReserved`, both refinement-commit actions, `RecoveryIncarnationLeaseAcquireOrRefresh`, and `RestoreContinuityAbandon` are ExternalCas-only. `CatalogTombstoneRestoreTarget` is inhabitable only for `ExternalCasCataloged|DirectoryBoundCataloged` and is forbidden for `DirectoryBoundEmbeddedNoCatalog`. DirectoryBound refinement and target-authority transitions are local authenticated journal/RootSlot publications, not transport keys. Source `K_oid` and source DEK destruction are uninhabited; cleanup may revoke only transient recovery wraps/grants. Destruction is legal solely for a clone-created target `K_oid` with key-origin plus zero-canonical-publication proofs. `RetainedTombstonedNoUse` is a local resource disposition, never an externally dispatched action.

Repeated prebootstrap operations use a bounded family fixed before the first member can be authorized. `PreBootstrapActionFamilyRecipe` is `{family_id,action_kind:RestoreArchiveLeaseRenew|RecoveryIncarnationLeaseAcquireOrRefresh,max_members,member_key_and_operation_id_recipe,member_idempotency_recipe,stable_subject_and_action_body_invariants,per_member_predecessor_and_window_recipe,resource_budget,terminal_history_and_nonreuse_floor,body_digest}`. A member key is exactly `{family_id,ordinal}` with `0 <= ordinal < max_members`; the operation/idempotency identities are deterministic from the sealed recipe and ordinal, and no member may change the lease/continuity subject, holder/writer, scope, target incarnation, first-root action digest, or other stable action bytes. The source-renew recipe derives member `n` only from the journal-durable terminal result of `n-1`, binding the then-current Active head/CAS, generation, portable lease-state digest, grant lineage/counter, and requested successor window. The recovery-lease recipe likewise binds the current lease generation/status and requested successor window produced or observed after `n-1`. The next ordinal may be authorized only after every prior ordinal is terminal and the resulting current head is journal-authority durable. Family exhaustion permanently abandons this restore attempt; recovery may start only a new `restore_id` under the profile's required fresh claim and, for same-identity recovery, a strictly newer incarnation—never mutate or extend the committed family. Source-lease renewal and ExternalCas recovery-incarnation-lease acquire/refresh are the only v1 families; fixed issuer/cohort/reservation/key/refinement/release/cleanup actions remain singleton keys. `RestoreBridgeFreezeSpec` closes the source-lease-renew family at an exact final ordinal, proves every created renew member terminal and no later renew member authorized, consumes all source/projection guards, and leaves only the separately bounded recovery-incarnation refresh family open. The sealed import, terminal accumulator, availability certificate, action/resource bijection, status API, and nonreuse floors retain every member—not merely the family name.

Availability construction is acyclic and does not assume that one local staging inode survives the declared failure model. `PortableRestorePlanRecipe` contains all Phase-A plan fields with one typed `AvailabilityCertificateDigest` hole and action recipes with their later `PlanDigest` holes. Before any target claim or dispatch-capable local root, recovery creates stable random `journal_id`, nonexportable `K_restore_journal`, and exact `PreBootstrapRestoreRecoveryCapsule {format_version,restore_id,journal_id,plan_recipe_bytes_and_digest,recovery_or_admin_authority_bytes_and_digest,journal_key_commitment,wrapped_journal_key_bytes_and_digest,wrap_recipient_and_profile,journal_mac_profile_oid,initial_generation_capsule_recipe_digest,availability_service_identity_and_locators,required_failure_domain_policy,recovery_and_relocation_policy,resource_ceiling,body_digest}`. The capsule contains no plaintext journal key and is itself encrypted/authenticated to the recovery authority.

`PreBootstrapJournalGenerationCapsule` is the exact complete encrypted state `{journal_id,restore_id,head_generation,dispatch_state_generation,predecessor_journal_head_digest_and_cas_version,plan_recipe_or_final_plan_digest,availability_certificate_digest?,current_staging_incarnation,complete_dispatch_root_body,dispatch_state_digest,complete_action_attempt_artifact_lease_and_resource_map,local_slot_generation_and_predecessor_digest,journal_mac_profile_oid,canonical_capsule_digest}`. Every journal-authority successor increments `head_generation` exactly once. `dispatch_state_generation` increments only when the plan/action/attempt/artifact/lease/resource state changes; a pure relocation preserves it and `dispatch_state_digest` while changing the staging incarnation and capsule bytes. The capsule contains only values known before the journal-head CAS—never a future authority head, receipt, status, or provider-result hole. In particular a generation that changes an ordinary target action to SentUnknown contains that complete SentUnknown state.

`prebootstrap_journal_publication_contracts.toml` has exactly two contracts, Bootstrap and SuccessorOrRelocation. It schedules exactly the lease release, reservation burns, profile-valid continuity abandonment or DirectoryBound zero-publication closure, transient-wrap revocations, clone-target-key destruction/tombstoning, and unpublished target-object disposition required by the resource inventory. If ArchiveAcquire was already RegisteredPending, drain recovery preserves its original request/source gate until it reaches Active, then the later cleanup plan immediately releases the returned lease and records `RegisteredArchiveAcquisitionRolledForwardThenReleased`. Release/status remains legal after lease expiry under its exact cleanup contract; claim/ordinary acquisition does not. No cleanup send is legal while the root remains Building, AcquiredProjectionAllowed, BridgeFrozenForCanonicalCreation, or AbandonmentDrainPending.

Terminal journal state is `TerminallyAbandoned{sorted_action_dispositions[PreBootstrapActionDisposition],complete_planned_action_and_family_member_bijection,sorted_resource_dispositions[PreBootstrapResourceDisposition],complete_claimed_acquired_created_resource_bijection,action_to_resource_disposition_relation,full_operation_idempotency_request_source_gate_status_and_typed_terminal_lineage_commitment,final_external_head_set_commitment,zero_canonical_publication_proof,terminal_body_digest}`. No two-receipt shortcut or duplicate release/burn row exists. Crash before Armed may use the typed never-sent proof; crash after SentUnknown must status-resolve the same bytes; crash after acquisition can only resume the same projection/creation until AbandonmentAuthorized is durable, after which it can only complete the exact disposition set. The plan availability capsule, claimed authorities, external heads, typed portable artifacts, and sealed journal—not an unrooted local file—are durable recovery authority.

Before `K_restore_journal` can be destroyed on the no-RootManifest path, recovery constructs unsigned reference-free `PortablePreBootstrapAbandonmentTerminalCertificateBody {restore_id,journal_id,predecessor_active_journal_head_bytes_digest_and_cas_version,predecessor_head_and_dispatch_state_generations,final_active_capsule_digest,plan_recipe_and_final_plan_digests,plan_and_refinement_availability_certificate_digests,terminal_journal_body_digest,complete_action_and_family_member_terminal_accumulator_root,complete_resource_disposition_accumulator_root,final_external_head_and_provider_operation_tombstone_set,permanent_operation_id_and_reservation_nonreuse_floors,zero_canonical_RootManifest_RootSlot_and_target_authority_publication_proof,profile_terminal_disposition:ExternalCasCataloged{catalog_tombstone_terminal_commitment,continuity_cleanup_disposition:PreBootstrapRestoreContinuityCleanupDisposition}|DirectoryBoundCataloged{catalog_tombstone_terminal_commitment,zero_publication_closure_commitment}|DirectoryBoundEmbeddedNoCatalog{zero_catalog_applicability_proof,zero_publication_closure_commitment},unpublished_target_object_terminal_disposition_commitment,journal_key_commitment,journal_key_destruction_authorization_digest,retention_floor,body_digest}`. It names only the already-existing Active predecessor, never the future terminal head. The profile arm, action accumulator, and resource accumulator must agree exactly on whether catalog and continuity actions existed; no generic “abandoned” bit can hide a missing cleanup stage.

The journal authority verifies and threshold-signs that body as `PortablePreBootstrapAbandonmentTerminalCertificate`, computes its digest, and atomically CASes the exact Active predecessor to `TerminalAbandoned{certificate_digest,retention_floor}` with `head_generation + 1`. It returns separate `PreBootstrapJournalAbandonmentTerminalizationReceipt {journal_id,publication_operation_id,publication_idempotency_digest,predecessor_active_head_bytes_digest_and_cas_version,certificate_digest,result_terminal_head_bytes_and_digest_and_cas_version,authority_counter,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`. The certificate never contains the result-head digest, and neither certificate nor terminal head embeds the later receipt. The receipt is retained outside the result capsule and may enter only a later immutable recovery package that does not name its own publication result. `PreBootstrapJournalKeyDisposition::AbandonedThenDestroyed` retains the certificate, receipt, and authenticated terminal head. None contains a local inode, artifact locator, journal MAC, or plaintext/key-dependent proof. Local zeroization or provider destruction evidence byte-matches the certificate and its key-destruction authorization. Thereafter recovery/status/nonreuse checks use the certificate, terminalization receipt/head, and authenticated provider heads/floors, never the destroyed MAC key. Successful creation instead imports and seals the complete journal lineage into the first canonical RootManifest.

For every schema, field, tag, state, transition, reference, digest transcript, construction-order rule, and role restriction in this slice, generate a durable_fields.toml row with stable IDs; canonical encoding/version policy; concrete generic/role expansion; producer, owner bead/crate, and consumers; reference strength/target set; authority and redaction class; invariant/evidence/cost bindings; test/scenario/event IDs; and consuming gate. Cross-slice targets use stable catalog IDs and must resolve in the Appendix A epic closure. Downstream owners may add implementation detail but cannot abbreviate, alias, weaken, or contradict these bytes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The embedded line range is byte-complete, checksum-pinned, continuous with adjacent slices, and contains no truncation marker.
- Every exact named construct in the slice has one stable row and exactly one granular implementation owner; all references and consumers resolve.
- Unit tests cover canonical encode/decode, stable field/tag IDs, role/generic expansion, digest construction, state preconditions, and owner uniqueness.
- Property/mutation/fuzz tests remove, duplicate, reorder, retag, corrupt, weaken, or cross-role substitute every field/arm/reference class and prove rejection.
- Simulation tests exercise applicable crash, cancellation, retry, sent-unknown, receipt-first, recovery, authority/configuration rotation, compaction, and expiry boundaries.
- E2E scripts traverse each applicable public embedded/server/FGP/CLI path through durable publication, restart/replay, backup/restore, and terminal cleanup using isolated synthetic fixtures.

- Cross-version golden vectors and unknown-required-field fixtures enforce additive-minor/breaking-major policy; no gate passes with an uncovered row.

## Risks & rejected alternatives

title: a18 exact field rows are rejected by registered consumer allowlists
description:
## Exact blocker

After the source-forced a18 increments in `329a50f` and `af3277c`, six
source-exact field candidates under already-landed logical owners remain
unlandable because the registered type's consumer contract rejects the
source-declared containing schema:

- `CatalogTombstoneRestoreTargetReceipt.predecessor:
  CatalogAbandonPredecessor` — `wire_context_mismatch` and
  `ordinary_union_field_mismatch`.
- `RestoreTerminalPinBasis.terminal_disposition: Operational` —
  `wire_context_mismatch`.
- `RestoreTerminalPinReleaseAuthorization.body:
  RestoreTerminalPinReleaseAuthorizationBody` — `wire_context_mismatch`.
- `RecoveryIncarnationTransformPlan.source_basis:
  RecoveryTransformSourceBasis<Role>` — `ordinary_union_field_mismatch`.
- `RestoreSourceLeaseReleaseOperationSummary.lease_operation_terminal_history:
  RestoreLeaseOperationTerminalHistory<Role>` —
  `ordinary_union_field_mismatch`.
- `RestoreTerminalPinBasis.abandonment_tombstone_ref:
  RestoreAbandonmentTombstoneRef<Role>` —
  `ordinary_union_field_mismatch`.

That is six unique rows: three fire `wire_context_mismatch`, four fire
`ordinary_union_field_mismatch`, and the first row fires both.

## Checker evidence

Each candidate was synthesized at the containing logical kind's exact
`construction_order` and passed through `validate_identity` for every tested
field class. All six were rejected by the type/consumer laws above. A
known-boring `u64` control on the same row shape accepted
`logical|physical|inline`; an unregistered-type control was rejected by
`field_unresolved_wire_type`. The result is therefore not an identity-class
convention and not a malformed-probe artifact.

The existing wire-type and ordinary-union rows are append-only durable
contracts. Their permitted consumer schemas/field names cannot be widened from
this slice merely to make the source candidates pass. Resolution needs an
explicit source/census correction or an append-only repair/history witness for
the registered consumer contract.

## Remaining a18 field radius

The a18 source slice still has 1,160 unlanded raw field occurrences:

- 838 have no `exact_type` in the source.
- 322 have a source `exact_type`.
- Of those 322, 82 have an unresolved owner; 152 have a landed logical owner;
  88 are under registered wire owners.
- Among the 152 exact rows under landed logical owners, 100 use unresolved
  non-reference types, 7 use unresolved reference-shaped types, 39 use
  registered reference-shaped types, 3 use registered non-reference wire
  types, and 3 use ordinary-union non-reference types.

The six rows above are the exact, non-wrapper candidates for which the current
checker supplies a specific blocking law. Do not infer permission for the
source-typeless or unresolved-type remainder from this blocker.

## Exit

Resolve the six source/registered-consumer contradictions explicitly, then
rerun the candidate probe with the `u64` positive control and the unregistered
negative control. No row may land by widening a durable allowlist without the
required append-only repair/history evidence.

The JSONL export itself follows in the immediately adjacent guarded repair commit after pane7 detected that external import had cleared SQLite dirty state and made flush-only a no-op.
