  ("GlobalRestoreServiceFinalizeSpec", "manifest_ref")
      field_tag 0x0003; exact_wire_type ExternalCasRestoreServicePromotionManifestRef, wire 0x0550;
      source anchor a20:2593,2597.
  ("RestoreShardOperationalAck", "operational_terminal_pin_basis_ref")
      field_tag 0x0009; exact_wire_type OperationalRestoreTerminalPinBasisRef, wire 0x0551 minted at
      2863a7a; source anchor a18:2373 + a20:2599.

Per-row evidence, not cohort reputation:
  - both were added by 19ea99b and by no other commit, so both post-date the erratum and are not part
    of the pre-erratum namespace the witness reconstructs;
  - both report "violations":0,"outcome":"pass" under `registry-check identity`, so what is being
    excluded is a VALID row that is merely younger than the witness;
  - both containing_schema strings were byte-checked against durable_fields.toml — plain and
    non-generic, no bound, unlike the a11 cohort's "DeltaDeliveryEnvelope<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>";
  - each (schema, name) pair occurs EXACTLY ONCE in durable_fields.toml, so the closure cannot remove
    a third row (the over-breadth control this bead asked for);
  - both hosts already appear in the tranche above, so the cohort boundary is drawn where the arc is,
    not where this repair is.

WIDTH VERIFIED, not merely "the test stopped failing". Cohort denominator 756 -> 758 because
current_field_count went 981 -> 983 and the reconstruction must return to 225. Mutation-proven on a
depth-matched mirror: 757 -> cohort assert fails; 759 -> cohort assert fails; 758 -> passes.

WHY THIS CLASS KEEPS RECURRING — measured, and fixed in place. The cohort assert compares a
DIFFERENCE, `pre_erratum.fields.len() + K == current_field_count`, so it is asymmetric:
  over-broad filter  -> width falls, count unchanged           -> assert FAILS (caught, as advertised)
  under-broad filter -> the unfiltered row increments the width AND the count together, the
                        difference survives                     -> assert PASSES over a wrong width
The second case is exactly what happened here: at 19ea99b the reconstruction was 227 rows and the
cohort assert still passed at +756, so the drift ran past it to the hash. Proven by mutation while
repairing: drop one row from the new filter and move the constant to 757 to compensate, and the
cohort assert stays GREEN while only the hash fails. The inherited comment ("one too few and 226,

So the repair also adds an ABSOLUTE pin, assert_eq!(pre_erratum.fields.len(), 225, ...). The
pre-erratum namespace is a historical constant; expressing its width only as a difference let the
current tree drag it. This is a pure narrowing — it can only add failures, never mask one — and with

title: Appendix A exact catalog: Restore promotion, independent reopen, completion, and release formats
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the exact Appendix A catalog slice for Restore promotion, independent reopen, completion, and release formats. This task embeds source-plan lines 2575-2608 verbatim, expands every generic and role-indexed family into stable registered rows, and assigns each row to its granular implementation owner. It is a format/ownership contract, not a substitute implementation.

## Exact normative contract
The following audited source-plan text is authoritative and self-contained:

`RestorePromotionAuthorityProfile` is the portable closed union `ExternalCasCataloged{expected_reserved_continuity_head_digest_and_cas_version,expected_catalog_predecessor_digest_and_version,continuity_transition_body_digest,catalog_endpoint_set_commitment}|DirectoryBoundCataloged{directory_bound_creation_evidence_public_commitment,fixed_local_continuity_digest,expected_catalog_predecessor_digest_and_version,catalog_endpoint_set_commitment}|DirectoryBoundEmbeddedNoCatalog{directory_bound_creation_evidence_public_commitment,fixed_local_continuity_digest,zero_external_catalog_applicability_proof,embedded_endpoint_or_inprocess_admission_commitment}`. The two DirectoryBound arms are Local-only; Sharded/Meta is always ExternalCasCataloged. The signed `RestoreServicePromotionManifest` is the portable closed posture union with common `{restore_id,database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,target_posture:Local|Sharded,service_visibility_epoch,authority_profile:RestorePromotionAuthorityProfile,signer_set_epoch,threshold_signatures}` and exactly one body: `Local{local_prepare_evidence:PortableCertificateProjection<LocalRestoreServicePrepareCertificate>,local_configuration_and_endpoint_commitment}` or `Sharded{meta_prepare_evidence:PortableCertificateProjection<GlobalRestoreServicePrepareCertificate>,sorted_shard_ready_evidence[PortableCertificateProjection<RestoreShardServiceReadyAck>],complete_group_topology_configuration_and_endpoint_commitment}`. `PortableCertificateProjection<T>` embeds the target `RemoteObjectIdentity`, complete export projection bytes, canonical configuration/trust evidence bytes, and signatures; it contains no `StrongRef`, `CertifiedRemoteStrongRef`, or consumer-local locator. Nullable cross-posture/profile fields are forbidden.

`RestorePromotionRootSeal<Role>` closes the proof-of-reopen race. After the role's promotion/finalize/open candidate is durably public under the role-valid proof—`PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Local|Meta>` for Local/Meta, `ShardStatePublicationCertificate` for Shard—and RootSlot-visible, recovery first builds `RestorePromotionRootSealRecipe<Role>` and completes the exact pin-ledger activation family. Only after `RestoreTerminalPinDurabilityReceipt<Role,Operational>` exists does it construct the seal `{authority_binding:AuthorityBindingFor<Role>,recipe:RestorePromotionRootSealRecipe<Role>,sealed_role_state_root_ref:StrongRef<RoleStateRoot>,sealed_root_manifest_ref:StrongRef<RootManifest>,typed_physical_inventory_ref:StrongRef<RestoreTerminalPhysicalInventory<Role,Operational>>,pin_durability_receipt_ref:StrongRef<RestoreTerminalPinDurabilityReceipt<Role,Operational>>,seal_digest}`. The receipt byte-matches the recipe digest and inventory but never contains the seal identity; the recipe excludes the receipt, so the construction graph is publication -> recipe/inventory -> pin activation receipt -> seal. The publication evidence, applied identity, state root, manifest, and winning slot must describe one publication; a Shard seal never claims an audit-visibility advance it does not have. The role-specific ordered seal-install spec installs the seal into still-hidden `OperationalPendingIndependentReopen::Sealed`. Before seal installation the only legal work is exact promotion recovery, source-lease renewal where owned, Local/Meta audit visibility or Shard publication recovery, pin activation/status recovery, evidence canonicalization/key cut, shutdown, or seal installation. Afterward only those operations plus reopen confirmation are legal. Every allowed successor preserves the same Active pin ledger/basis; ordinary admission, unrelated maintenance, checkpoint, GC, reconfiguration, key/policy/schema/data mutation, and a second promotion are rejected.

`RestoreIndependentReopenProof<Role>` opens the seal from an independent fresh process/context, not merely the current mutable head. It binds the seal, reopens every typed pinned object/encoding/key, reconstructs the sealed canonical/prepared/Raft closure, revalidates the exact profile-specific promotion authority receipt and service epoch, and supplies an authenticated proof that every successor from the sealed root to the current pending root is one of the allowed nonsemantic/recovery classes. An ExternalCas proof revalidates catalog and continuity heads; DirectoryBoundCataloged revalidates the catalog row plus inode-bound local promotion receipts; DirectoryBoundEmbeddedNoCatalog revalidates the inode/fence/slot lineage and zero-catalog-applicability proof. Slot churn or a lease renewal therefore cannot erase the proof basis or legitimize an intervening mutation. The role-specific reopen-confirm command consumes that exact proof and is the only transition to `Operational`; its published successor installs `RestoreTerminalPinBasis<Role>::Operational`. An abandonment finalize/apply instead installs `RestoreRetentionAnchor<Role>::AbandonmentPinPending` from the prebuilt pending owner; only the later role-specific pin-install command, after the abandonment root is durably published and its physical inventory is pinned, replaces that anchor with `RestoreTerminalPinBasis<Role>::Abandoned`. Local/Meta retain the matching terminal pin basis until `RestoreSourceLeaseReleaseFinalizeSpec`; that finalize atomically removes the Local pin owner or starts the Meta participant-release protocol and emits no promotion-shaped authority for an abandoned restore. Each shard retains its matching basis through its operational or abandonment acknowledgement and removes it only through `ShardRestoreTerminalPinReleaseSpec` consuming the matching certified terminal authorization. Release/tombstone floors retain every basis, seal or abandonment evidence, inventory, proof where applicable, and pin receipt until all configured shard release acknowledgements and the source-release terminal are complete. Crash tests cut every seal-build or abandonment-basis build, pin, slot publish, proof open, confirm, source-access cleanup, source-release, and shard-pin-release step, including arbitrary slot convergence and allowed lease renewals.

Promotion is profile-discriminated and service remains hidden throughout. For cataloged profiles the catalog exposes a CAS-linear per-database row head, so unrelated rows never force request rewriting. `ServiceCatalogPromotionReservationReceipt` is the portable result of `CatalogReserveHidden` and binds `{external_request_binding,restore_or_transition_id,target_database_and_security_identity,target_posture,target_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch,manifest_digest,expected_target_row_predecessor_digest_and_version,reservation_id,reservation_digest,reserved_target_row_digest_and_version,endpoint_set_commitment,state:ReservedHiddenNonexpiring,authority_signatures}`. The row CAS accepts only the exact predecessor, `AlreadyReservedEquivalent` for the same operation/request, or a semantically equivalent target-row descendant whose target remains absent/hidden with identical reservation semantics. It never accepts an arbitrary rebased row. The reservation is nonexpiring after the profile's pending boundary and blocks every competing endpoint install.

`ServicePromotionExternalOperationKind` is `CatalogReserveHidden|ContinuityEnterPromotionPending|CatalogActivateReserved|ContinuityFinalizeOperational`, specialized by `operation_subject:Restore{restore_id}|RoleTransition{migration_nonce}`. The continuity arms are inhabitable only for ExternalCas. The exact profile sequences are:

The pending transition is the irreversible no-downgrade boundary for both DirectoryBound profiles. After it, recovery has only profile-specific roll-forward authority. ## Ownership, verification, and diagnostics
For every schema, field, tag, state, transition, reference, digest transcript, construction-order rule, and role restriction in this slice, generate a durable_fields.toml row with stable IDs; canonical encoding/version policy; concrete generic/role expansion; producer, owner bead/crate, and consumers; reference strength/target set; authority and redaction class; invariant/evidence/cost bindings; test/scenario/event IDs; and consuming gate. Cross-slice targets use stable catalog IDs and must resolve in the Appendix A epic closure. Downstream owners may add implementation detail but cannot abbreviate, alias, weaken, or contradict these bytes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The embedded line range is byte-complete, checksum-pinned, continuous with adjacent slices, and contains no truncation marker.
- Every exact named construct in the slice has one stable row and exactly one granular implementation owner; all references and consumers resolve.
- Unit tests cover canonical encode/decode, stable field/tag IDs, role/generic expansion, digest construction, state preconditions, and owner uniqueness.
- Property/mutation/fuzz tests remove, duplicate, reorder, retag, corrupt, weaken, or cross-role substitute every field/arm/reference class and prove rejection.
- Simulation tests exercise applicable crash, cancellation, retry, sent-unknown, receipt-first, recovery, authority/configuration rotation, compaction, and expiry boundaries.
- E2E scripts traverse each applicable public embedded/server/FGP/CLI path through durable publication, restart/replay, backup/restore, and terminal cleanup using isolated synthetic fixtures.
- Detailed versioned JSONL diagnostics carry schema_id, field_or_arm_id, role/group, object or public commitment, transition_id, state_before/state_after, checker, verdict, artifact refs, and replay command; secret/noninterference tests reject protected data or observable hidden state.
- Cross-version golden vectors and unknown-required-field fixtures enforce additive-minor/breaking-major policy; no gate passes with an uncovered row.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: family-level prose summaries, wildcard references, inferred fields, unregistered aliases, or treating the catalog slice as the implementation. Exactness is intentional; execution remains decomposed across the linked workstream beads.

title: Appendix A exact catalog: Replay, authorization, capability, DP, audit, and transparency formats
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the exact Appendix A catalog slice for Replay, authorization, capability, DP, audit, and transparency formats. This task embeds source-plan lines 2609-2728 verbatim, expands every generic and role-indexed family into stable registered rows, and assigns each row to its granular implementation owner. It is a format/ownership contract, not a substitute implementation.

## Exact normative contract
The following audited source-plan text is authoritative and self-contained:

**ReplayManifest / executable and archive closure.** `ReplayCompleteness` is `Replayable|StructuralReplay|VerifiableIfArtifactsSupplied|AuditOnly` with explicit class lists. `ArchiveObjectIdentity` is nonlocal and never a local reachability edge. `ReplayObjectRef<T>` is exactly `LocalStrong{ref:StrongRef<T>}|CertifiedRemote{ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<T>}|Archived{identity,expected_logical_object_id,expected_canonical_digest}`. CertifiedRemote requires a live matching authority configuration/trust selector/grant and participates in two-sided retention; Archived resolves only through the active registry and never marks local data. Every slot uses `ReplayEvidenceRef<T> = Present{object:ReplayObjectRef<T>}|Unavailable{class,expected identity/digest?,reason}|Redacted{class,commitment?,policy}`. `ReplayLogicalStateEvidence = Local{state:ReplayEvidenceRef<LogicalStateRoot>}|Sharded{global_state:ReplayEvidenceRef<GlobalStateRoot>,topology:ReplayEvidenceRef<TopologyState>,exact_global_prefix,sorted_shard_states[ReplayEvidenceRef<ShardLogicalStateRoot>],complete_partition_commitment}`; a Sharded grade is no stronger than its weakest required group/evidence lease.

`ReplayManifest` binds `{format major/minor,slot schema,database/security namespace/incarnation,logical/commit seq,logical_state:ReplayLogicalStateEvidence,graph bindings,topology/policy/revocation epochs,language/semantic/scalar/numeric profiles,answer requirement/result contract,logical/physical plan IDs,bound/normalized query,typed parameters,replay authority,module/UDF set,external inputs,derived generation snapshots,decision cards/policies/evidence,executable artifacts,structural projection,result encoding/digest,structural completeness,archive requirements,created HLC}`. The generated slot schema derives the maximum grade: Replayable requires every execution-semantic Local or Sharded slot live; structural replay requires its typed projection; supply-later carries all identities/digests; audit/redaction is explicit. Live effective grade may only weaken as any local, certified-remote, or archive trust/lease/authority fails. Legacy Local manifests survive activation unchanged.

The terminal attempt passes through `ExternalBatchCasCommitted` for the same batch/receipt/member before its `VisibilityReleased` successor, and both objects name the same already-built advance spec/maintenance command plus assigned scalar index—not a future applied record. Deterministic construction is maintenance input/command -> per-entry VisibilityReleased attempt successors -> AuditOutcomeRecords/protected-output release successors -> visible outcome/delivery indexes -> successor pipeline/protocol state -> maintenance applied record -> RootManifest. Activation objects are absent from this DAG and are constructed only by later independent maintenance; no object points forward and no semantic payload/result owns the protocol root that owns it. Local/Global semantic outcome state retains the terminal gate/claim commitment; status and compaction select the exact protocol-plane outcome through a generated release proof, never a fictitious strong edge inserted into the earlier candidate payload.

`AuditContinuityRecord` is the external reference-free `{database_security_namespace_id,audit_domain_id,audit_epoch,highest_ticket_sequence,ticket_index_commitment,unresolved_ticket_commitment,audit_chain_head_digest,predecessor_digest,external_registry_id,cas_version,status:Complete{profile_oid}|PermanentGap{latest_transition_bytes_and_digest,current_profile_oid},last_transition:TicketIssued{ticket_digest}|TicketsResolvedBatch{role_and_group,first_pipeline_order,last_pipeline_order,batch_digest,ordered_resolution_commitment,last_candidate_root_digest:WeakDigest}|CompletenessChanged{transition_bytes_and_digest},signer_set_epoch,threshold_signatures}`. A single ticket is the canonical one-member TicketsResolvedBatch form. The registry retains authenticated ticket/event/resolution/transition bytes or authenticated resolver refs. `AuditExternalCasReceipt` is built **after** a TicketIssued or CompletenessChanged returned continuity record and binds `{external_registry_id,prior_head_digest,returned_head_bytes_and_digest,prior_cas_version,returned_cas_version,transition_kind,subject_digest,registry_signature_set}`; `AuditExternalBatchCasReceipt` is the noninterchangeable nonempty contiguous-resolution-batch counterpart with the exact batch identity. Neither receipt nor continuity record contains a local reference, and a continuity record never points forward to either receipt.

Exact `AuditTicketAdmissionSpec` is `{ticket_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicket>,expected_prior_continuity_ref:StrongRef<AuditContinuityRecord>,expected_prior_cas_version,returned_continuity_ref:StrongRef<AuditContinuityRecord>,external_cas_receipt_ref:StrongRef<AuditExternalCasReceipt>}`. Its validator requires the direct TicketIssued successor, exact sequence increment, exact ticket/unresolved addition, matching receipt/CAS versions, and no unrelated change; recovery uses the same validator. The only visibility owner is the separately addressable Local/Meta protocol state and pipeline; shard groups never originate one. Exact `AuditTerminalSpec` is `{ticket_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicket>,expected_pending_ticket_digest:WeakDigest,event_ref:StrongRef<AuditEventRecord>,terminal_resolution_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicketResolution>}`; it is the non-mutating/pre-effect terminal path and rejects every scope/outcome mismatch. Transaction preparation and each state-changing semantic control carry the same triple through `TerminalAuditGate::Required`. External resolution uses `AuditExternalResolutionBatch`/receipt, and the sole ordered visibility input is the **maintenance** `AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec<Local|Meta>`; there is no `AuditContinuityMirrorSpec`, semantic visibility command, batch-spec command, active-fence digest, singular candidate-import command, or fence-removal transition. Its validator enforces the gap-free/direct-successor/bijection relation, updates protocol continuity/outcomes and protected outputs to ReleasedAwaitingActivation, and changes public visibility only through the manifest-owned prefix. `ProtectedOutputActivationSpec` is a later, visibility-neutral maintenance input. Portable `AuditCompletenessTransitionRequest`, local `AuditCompletenessTransitionOperationRecord<Role>`, reference-free returned `AuditContinuityRecord`/receipt, and semantic `AuditCompletenessTransitionSpec<Role>` retain the exact pre-CAS/direct-successor/import schemas above. Admission, recovery, and completeness semantic transitions use StructurallyInapplicable gates; visibility and activation maintenance use distinct system-authority arms; terminal consumes the existing ticket.

`AuditCloneBoundary` is `{source_database_security_namespace_id,source_audit_domain_id,source_continuity_head_digest,target_database_security_namespace_id,target_audit_domain_id,clone_manifest_ref,retained_source_evidence_contract,source_signatures,target_signatures}` and never rewrites source tickets into the target domain. `AuditSegment` is a contiguous signed range with previous-chain digest, ticket/resolution ranges, event records, redaction profile, signing epoch, and external-anchor ref. `AuditTicketIndex` makes every issued ticket pending or uniquely resolved and retains its event, external receipt, and local import status across recovery. `AuditCheckpoint` commits retained ticket/event floors and heads, unresolved-ticket set, continuity/gap heads, signer-rotation chain, and anchor. Missing external evidence disables completeness-gated operations; it never silently weakens the advertised profile.

**WitnessPolicy / TransparencyCheckpoint.** `WitnessPolicy` is `{format_version,log_id,security_domain_id,policy_epoch,claim_class:EquivocationDetection|NonEquivocation,ordered_witnesses[{witness_id,key_id,verification_key,endpoint_identity,optional_cross_log_authority}],n,threshold_t,byzantine_bound_f,signature_profile,consistency_proof_profile,durable_head_state_profile,anti_rollback_profile,authenticated_gossip_profile:None|Required{transport_auth_profile,peer_identity_registry,checkpoint_message_schema,replay_window,evidence_retention_floor,maximum_convergence_delay},activation_log_size,maximum_checkpoint_age,cross_log_policy:None|Required{ordered_authorities,threshold},rotation:Genesis|JointSuccessor{predecessor_policy_ref:StrongRef<WitnessPolicy>}}`. Canonical validation requires exactly `n` unique ordered witnesses, `0 <= f < t <= n`, supported signature/consistency/persistence profiles, and—before `claim_class=NonEquivocation` is usable—`2t > n + f`. A detection claim that relies on gossip requires the complete authenticated profile; an unnamed/best-effort channel proves nothing. Each honest witness durably stores `{log_id,security_domain_id,policy_oid,last_size,last_root,anti_rollback_counter}` before acknowledging a signature; it signs only a verified append-only consistency extension, never two roots at one size or non-extending histories. Rollback or loss of this state disables that witness until an authenticated recovery/rotation procedure; it cannot silently start fresh.

`TransparencyCrossLogReceipt` is the reference-free signed `{authority_id,authority_key_id,source_log_id,source_security_domain_id,source_policy_identity_and_digest,source_checkpoint_digest,source_log_size,source_root,target_log_id,target_policy_identity_and_digest,target_log_size,target_inclusion_commitment,target_inclusion_proof,target_checkpoint_digest,target_checkpoint_consistency_proof,receipt_time_authority_profile_oid,receipt_window:{not_before:AuthorityInstant,expires_at:AuthorityInstant},canonical_receipt_digest,signature}`. The target inclusion leaf is exactly the domain-separated source checkpoint digest plus source log/domain/policy/size/root; it provides causality without comparing clocks from different authorities.

`TransparencyCheckpoint` is `{format_version,mode:LocalRollbackDetection|WitnessedEquivocationDetection{witness_policy_ref:StrongRef<WitnessPolicy>}|WitnessedNonEquivocation{witness_policy_ref:StrongRef<WitnessPolicy>},log_size,global_mmr_root,branch_head_commitment_root,security_domain_commitment,previous_checkpoint_digest:WeakDigest,consistency_proof_from_previous,issuance_time_authority_profile_oid,issuance_window:{not_before:AuthorityInstant,expires_at:AuthorityInstant},operator_key_id,operator_signature,sorted_witness_signatures[{witness_id,key_id,signature}],cross_log_receipt_refs[StrongRef<TransparencyCrossLogReceipt>],rotation_proof:None|JointActivation{old_policy_ref:StrongRef<WitnessPolicy>,new_policy_ref:StrongRef<WitnessPolicy>,old_sorted_signatures[],new_sorted_signatures[]}}`. Every signature covers the domain-separated canonical checkpoint body excluding all signature arrays. A witnessed mode requires its policy identity, threshold of distinct configured keys, and any required cross-log receipts; freshness is never inferred from an unprofiled `issued_at` scalar.

Local `TransparencyCheckpointValidationRecord<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,checkpoint_ref:StrongRef<TransparencyCheckpoint>,checkpoint_freshness_basis_ref:StrongRef<TransparencyCheckpointFreshnessBasis>,checkpoint_time_validation_evidence_ref:StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>,sorted_cross_log_validations[{receipt_ref:StrongRef<TransparencyCrossLogReceipt>,freshness_basis_ref:StrongRef<CrossLogTransparencyFreshness>,time_validation_evidence_ref:StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>,target_checkpoint_verification_evidence_ref}],policy_threshold_and_consistency_verification_digest,validated_claim_class,body_digest}`. The two generated time-basis schemas from §16 bind the exact checkpoint/receipt bodies and their windows; they cannot be replaced by wall time, logical HLC, or a raw age calculation.

Canonical cross-log validation requires `1 <= cross_log_policy.threshold <= count(unique ordered authorities)`; at least that many receipts come from distinct configured authority/key pairs, and every accepted receipt's source policy/log/security domain/checkpoint digest/size/root equals the current checkpoint exactly. Its target inclusion proof and target checkpoint consistency proof must verify under the named target policy/log/size, the inclusion leaf must causally contain the exact source checkpoint digest, and both the source checkpoint and each receipt/target checkpoint must have independently usable profiled freshness evidence in their own time domains. No validator orders or subtracts instants across domains/epochs. Duplicates, foreign source roots, stale evidence, missing target-checkpoint verification, or self-asserted target sizes fail. `JointActivation` additionally requires: the old policy equals the currently active policy; `new.rotation == JointSuccessor{predecessor=old}`; old/new log and security-domain identities are equal; `new.policy_epoch > old.policy_epoch`; checkpoint mode names the new policy; `log_size >= new.activation_log_size`; and the checkpoint body has valid distinct-key thresholds under both old and new policies. Only after that exact activation checkpoint may successors use the new policy alone.

The branch commitment is domain-separated and reveals no plain branch identity/head; authorized clients receive scoped inclusion/consistency proofs under the metadata-declassification policy, and mutually hidden branch sets use distinct security-domain logs. `LocalRollbackDetection` proves only consistency relative to a client's cached head. `WitnessedEquivocationDetection` promises durable evidence once conflicting heads reach the declared gossip/cross-log path. Only `WitnessedNonEquivocation` with a valid intersection-safe policy, honest durable-head assumption, consistency proofs, joint rotation, and freshness may claim split-view prevention. If any premise fails, verification fails closed or downgrades the advertised claim to detection/local scope; later gossip is never relabeled as prevention. **DecisionPolicyEpoch** is `{policy_id,version,scope,logical_effect_class,pinned_table_oid,fallback_oid,evidence_refs[],previous_epoch_oid}`; statistical evidence may justify promotion but is never encoded as an invariant. It is not `SecurityPolicyEpoch`.

## Ownership, verification, and diagnostics
For every schema, field, tag, state, transition, reference, digest transcript, construction-order rule, and role restriction in this slice, generate a durable_fields.toml row with stable IDs; canonical encoding/version policy; concrete generic/role expansion; producer, owner bead/crate, and consumers; reference strength/target set; authority and redaction class; invariant/evidence/cost bindings; test/scenario/event IDs; and consuming gate. Cross-slice targets use stable catalog IDs and must resolve in the Appendix A epic closure. Downstream owners may add implementation detail but cannot abbreviate, alias, weaken, or contradict these bytes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The embedded line range is byte-complete, checksum-pinned, continuous with adjacent slices, and contains no truncation marker.
- Every exact named construct in the slice has one stable row and exactly one granular implementation owner; all references and consumers resolve.
- Unit tests cover canonical encode/decode, stable field/tag IDs, role/generic expansion, digest construction, state preconditions, and owner uniqueness.
- Property/mutation/fuzz tests remove, duplicate, reorder, retag, corrupt, weaken, or cross-role substitute every field/arm/reference class and prove rejection.
- Simulation tests exercise applicable crash, cancellation, retry, sent-unknown, receipt-first, recovery, authority/configuration rotation, compaction, and expiry boundaries.
- E2E scripts traverse each applicable public embedded/server/FGP/CLI path through durable publication, restart/replay, backup/restore, and terminal cleanup using isolated synthetic fixtures.
- Detailed versioned JSONL diagnostics carry schema_id, field_or_arm_id, role/group, object or public commitment, transition_id, state_before/state_after, checker, verdict, artifact refs, and replay command; secret/noninterference tests reject protected data or observable hidden state.
- Cross-version golden vectors and unknown-required-field fixtures enforce additive-minor/breaking-major policy; no gate passes with an uncovered row.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: family-level prose summaries, wildcard references, inferred fields, unregistered aliases, or treating the catalog slice as the implementation. Exactness is intentional; execution remains decomposed across the linked workstream beads.

title: a21 residue: 25 union-shaped need variant bijections, 16 are a genuine convention call
description:
## Residue of fgdb-a21-replay-security-ye0o, closed after two landing increments

a21 landed 29 rows across two increments (7aba481: 25 reservation-forced logical
kinds; 0e7bb96: 4 embedded-by-value wire types). 87 candidates remain
unclassified. This bead carries the residue with the exact law gating each group,
so the next pane starts from measurement rather than re-deriving.

## What is NOT the blocker

The checker abstains. Measured with a per-symbol ask-the-checker harness over all
47 then-remaining confirmed candidates (/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/p4a21/batch.py):

    accepts BOTH logical and wire: 47      FORCED logical: 0      FORCED wire: 0

Both controls green — pristine no-op -> ACCEPTED (base clean); deliberate code
collision on 0x0001 -> REJECTED with projection_code_duplicate (harness not
blind). So `catalog_candidate_class_unproved` is satisfied by either mint and
class alone never blocks these.

## GROUP 1 — 25 union-shaped, class RESOLVED, shape is the work (largest group)

Class is settled for these by the one-directional containment law: each is
embedded BY VALUE inside another a21 schema and is never a StrongRef /
CertifiedRemoteStrongRef target, and of 95 landed top-level wire targets ZERO are
reference targets. So: WIRE.

    AuditCoverageClaimRef                    AuthenticatedDurableCapabilityStatusBasis
    AuthorizationAuditGate                   DurableCapabilityConsumerTerminalTarget
    DurableCapabilityCurrentMembershipBasis  DurableCapabilityCurrentMembershipProof
    DurableCapabilityCurrentSecurityBasis    DurableCapabilityLegacyCurrentMembershipProof
    DurableCapabilityLegacyReplayRef         DurableCapabilityPresentedReplayRef
    DurableCapabilityRetentionResolutionBasis DurableCapabilityStatusClassification
    DurableCapabilityStatusPresentedReplayRef ImportedOperationAuditAdmissionEvidence
    ImportedReadAuditEvidence                ImportedStatementAuditAdmissionEvidence
    LifecycleAuthoritySource                 LifecycleEffectClass
    LifecycleOperation                       NonRequiredAuditEvidence
    ReadCapablePermitRef                     ReplayObjectRef
    ReplayEvidenceRef                        ReplayLogicalStateEvidence
    StructuralAuditExemption                 TimeAuthorityUnavailableStatusEvidence

THE BLOCKING LAW: a wire-backed whole-schema union requires an exact
`union_variant` bijection —
`projection_ordinary_union_wire_contract_mismatch`: "arm name, parent, tag,
lifecycle, maximum size, and containing-schema closure must exactly match one
wire variant". So each needs host + N union_variant wire rows + [[union]] +
N [[union_arm]] + targets, roughly 6-10 rows apiece, ~200 rows for the group.

WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-LINE MINT, and this is the trap: minting one of these as a
plain `kind = "record"` wire type LOADS CLEAN. The checker accepts it (verified
by the harness) and the arms are then unregistered forever — a silent durable
format defect. `LifecycleEffectClass` sat in my record-shaped set until reading
its definitional sentence returned "is a generated associated closed tag". Read
the definitional sentence for EVERY symbol before minting; regex shape
classification is not sufficient.

WHAT IS NEEDED: census-derived arm data per union — arm tags from SOURCE SPAN
order (never the alphabetical arm_names print) and each arm's payload_sha256
from the census ArmCandidate. My census probe was lost to tmpdir cleanup; rebuild
it against `appendix_source::census_appendix_source` (3 args: source bytes,
start line, slice specs) and control it on the full Appendix SHA plus a
fabricated-absent negative before trusting a digest.

## GROUP 2 — 16 confirmed, both instruments silent: a GENUINE convention call

Checker accepts both classes AND no by-value containment, so neither instrument
discriminates. These are the only ones needing a ruling. Includes
AuditReceiptValidationResolution, AuditTicketAdmissionSpec, AuthorityPermitRef,
DurableCapabilityTimeValidationBasis, ExecutableArtifactSet, ObjectKind,

title: Resource ledger: protected maintenance reserve is void in both directions — charges bill the classless committed pool
description: crates/fgdb-resource/src/ledger.rs: BucketState tracks one classless 'committed' pool. validate() (:490) bills it against ordinary_limit = hard − reserve; apply_charge (:1397-1408) moves maintenance reservations into committed via classless add_committed_path_change, forgetting the class at charge time. PROBE-CONFIRMED (SimAndFoundations scout compiled ledger.rs verbatim out-of-tree, /data/tmp/probe_ledger.rs): Direction 1 — hard=100 reserve=20, ordinary band full (committed=80), a valid maintenance reservation of 20 can NEVER be charged (80+1 > 80 → OrdinaryCapacityExceeded): reservation stuck, wedging the whole maintenance lane; the reserve protects nothing when it matters. Direction 2 — five reserve(20)→charge(20) cycles put committed=80: maintenance eats the ENTIRE ordinary band, starving ordinary tenants; the fifth refusal is band-fullness, not the 20-unit reserve. Root cause: the bucket invariant is too weak once the class tag is dropped at charge time; conservation tests pass because conservation is class-blind. Fix sketch (scout): split committed into ordinary_committed/maintenance_committed (class param on add_committed_path_change; SubjectSnapshot already carries class); validate: ordinary_committed + ordinary_reserved ≤ hard − reserve AND maintenance_committed + maintenance_reserved ≤ reserve; add the two probe scenarios as tests. Minor companion: applied_transitions (:1093,:1163-1180) retains every transition forever for idempotence — needs a defined retention story at the durable layer.
close_reason: Landed 5b914ec: committed split by class (ordinary/maintenance) across BucketState/BucketChange/add_committed_path_change/plan/validate; charge+adjust+snapshot thread the entry class. Two probe-scenario tests mutation-proven RED by class erasure (Direction 1 fails OrdinaryCapacityExceeded{100,80}; conservation stays green — why the defect survived). 41/41 green, clippy clean.

title: Capsule recover trusts an unauthenticated protected_len to size the decode
notes:
FOUND 2026-07-29 by self-audit at ffbf187, in my own code (capsule.rs, landed 03e7d7e).

TRIGGER: another pane found two defects of the same class in code I landed the same day —
verify() not fail-closed where insert() was (ffbf187), and a content-addressed capsule
opened with truncate(true) so re-committing overwrote an immutable object and destroyed
evidence of corruption (d95ff1b). I audited my own recent work for the same shapes and
found this.

THE DEFECT. crates/fgdb-chronicle/src/capsule.rs:

  CapsuleDescriptor carries BOTH `transfer_length` (part of the EncodingDescriptor) and
  `protected_len` (its own field). `seal` sets them to the SAME value — the length of the
  sealed ciphertext+tag bytes — so protected_len is pure redundancy.

  `EncodedObject::reconstruct` authenticates the descriptor by recomputing the EncodingId,
  and EncodingDescriptor::canonical_bytes covers fec_profile, transfer_length, oti_common,
  oti_scheme, symbol_size, source_block_count and symbol_auth_profile. It does NOT cover
  protected_len, because protected_len is not part of that descriptor.

  But `recover` passes `descriptor.protected_len` into decode_object's RecoveryTarget, and
  decode_object computes `k = protected_len.div_ceil(symbol_size)` and then
  `InactivationDecoder::new(k, symbol_size, ...)`.

  So protected_len is read straight out of an untrusted container, is covered by NO
  integrity check, and directly sizes an allocation. A container with protected_len =
  u64::MAX and symbol_size = 256 yields k of roughly 7.2e16.

WHY THE EXISTING TAMPER LAWS DID NOT CATCH IT. capsule_container.rs has
a_rewritten_encoding_id_is_refused and a_rewritten_symbol_size_is_refused, and both pass —
because both of those fields ARE in the EncodingId transcript. protected_len is the one
descriptor field that is not, and no test perturbs it. The suite therefore looks like it
covers descriptor tampering and covers all of it except the one field that matters most.
Same shape as the ratchet lesson: a check whose domain excludes the interesting case.

THE FIX, and it is the stronger of the two available:
Do not validate protected_len against transfer_length — REMOVE protected_len entirely and
have recover use the authenticated transfer_length. Validation leaves two fields that can
disagree and a rule that must be maintained; removal leaves one source of truth and nothing
to disagree. transfer_length is exactly the right value: in RFC 6330 it IS the length of
the object being encoded, which is what protected_len was duplicating.

This is a durable-format change (the container layout loses 8 bytes). Acceptable and
correct: nothing has shipped, AGENTS.md says do it the RIGHT way with NO tech debt, and
CAPSULE_FORMAT_V1 has never been written outside tests. A redundant UNAUTHENTICATED copy of
an authenticated field is a hole by construction, not a thing to keep and guard.

LAW TO ADD: a container whose length field is tampered must be refused. After the fix that
is automatic — the length lives only in transfer_length, which the EncodingId covers — so
the test is a_rewritten_transfer_length_is_refused, alongside the existing encoding_id and
symbol_size laws. Verify it fails before the fix and passes after.

ALSO CHECKED IN THE SAME AUDIT, no defect found:
- decode_container caps `Vec::with_capacity(declared.min(4096))` and breaks on short reads,
  so a corrupt symbol count cannot ask for a huge allocation.
- store.rs's writes DO truncate, but that is correct there: the dual-slot root is the one
  mutable object in a database directory and alternating overwrite is its design.
- commit.rs's log open is append-only.
close_reason: Fixed at 2efeca0 by REMOVING protected_len rather than validating it: transfer_length already carries the value and is inside the EncodingId transcript, so one source of truth replaces two that could disagree. Regression guard a_rewritten_transfer_length_is_refused added, mutation-proven (diverging the accessor reddens it plus four others). Recorded honestly on the bead: that test would also have passed against the old code, so the fix is demonstrated by the field's removal, not by the test.

title: Owner ruling: class for LocalGcApplyQuarantineSpec / LocalGcCancellationAuthorizeSpec is underdetermined
description:
The class of LocalGcApplyQuarantineSpec and LocalGcCancellationAuthorizeSpec is GENUINELY UNDERDETERMINED. This is a ruling, not a mint. Do not guess it.

Both are census 'ambiguous-unowned-structure' / inline-record, reason 'leading named record has no explicit top-level ownership cue'. Neither has a reservation.

BOTH class instruments are SILENT on both families:
  LAW A (reference target => never wire): 0 occurrences. Absence proves nothing.
  LAW B (used inside another schema => wire): 0 occurrences, and the zero is LICENSED --
    every source occurrence in the frozen range was enumerated and accounted for, so this
    is a real absence and not a census blind spot (contrast RemotePreparedIdentity).

I built two replacement laws and FALSIFIED BOTH against the corpus. Recorded so nobody re-derives them:
  TRIED 'a body carrying a named retaining member cannot be wire, because its refs need
    [[field]] rows and a field may not hang off a wire-only host'
    => FALSIFIED: 89 of 182 landed wire hosts do carry one.
  TRIED the refinement '...unless it is a union, whose arms carry refs as variants rather
    than fields'
    => ALSO FALSIFIED: 34 landed wire-type RECORD hosts carry named retaining members,
    including the direct shape-analogues LocalStatementPublicationSpec,
    CertificateAttemptAbandonSpec, TxnAbortSpec, LocalTerminalCompletionSpec,
    LocalOutcomeExpirySpec, LocalReadCloseSpec, ShardingActivationSpec.

Slice-local control (the endorsed one) is a14 6/6 logical -- but every one of those six is
forced by an INDEPENDENT rule (GcPhysicalDispositionImportSpec<Role> is a generic whole-schema
union; ConfigPayloadFloor/GcProposal/MandatoryInventory/GcDecisionRecord are reservation-backed),
so the cohort is unanimous and proves nothing about a flat record.
Corpus split for flat records carrying named refs: 243 logical / 34 wire = 88/12. A majority
spelling, not a law -- and majority spelling has been the wrong answer twice in this slice.

RECOMMENDATION (explicitly a recommendation, NOT a derivation): logical, on CONSEQUENCE
ASYMMETRY. LocalGcApplyQuarantineSpec carries 5 named StrongRef members (GcDecisionRecord,
ConfigurationState, GcRootInventory, GcReachabilityProof, GcDisjointnessProof). Minted logical
they can land as field rows later; minted wire they can NEVER land, and in a durable format
that choice is unrecoverable. Logical preserves the option, wire forecloses it.
LocalGcCancellationAuthorizeSpec has 5 members with NO exact types at all, so nothing lands
inside it either way; it should follow whatever its sibling gets.

Measured by pane2 under fgdb-27sr.
notes:
OWNER RULING RECEIVED AND RECORDED, 2026-07-27, /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/OWNER_RULINGS.md.

  A flat record whose members are ALL source-typeless must be minted LOGICAL.
  Governs the GENERAL CLASS, not just this row.

Grounds, as given: (1) typelessness is silence, not evidence -- wire asserts a
positive fact the source does not state, logical asserts less; (2) the
foreclosure is one-directional and it is this bead's own measurement, 0 of 265
resolved hosts resolve only to a wire_type, so wire permanently forecloses
[[field]] rows while logical forecloses nothing; (3) discovery runs the other way
-- a later exact type closes the case under logical and contradicts it under
wire, forcing an erratum plus a breaking-major migration per the 2pbf ruling;
(4) consistency with k3sa -- prefer the representation that keeps the source's
structure expressible.

BOTH FAMILIES NOW RESOLVE, BY DIFFERENT ROUTES, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS WORTH
KEEPING:
  LocalGcApplyQuarantineSpec        LOGICAL by DERIVATION. Inline-record with
                                    five named StrongRef members carrying exact
                                    targets; record members are [[field]] rows;
                                    a [[field]] row cannot hang off a wire-only
                                    host (0 of 923 landed field rows do). No
                                    ruling was needed and none should be cited.
  LocalGcCancellationAuthorizeSpec  LOGICAL by RULING. Five source-typeless
                                    members, so the derivation does not reach
                                    it; settled by the general-class ruling
                                    above.

THE CHECKER CONTRAST WAS NOT RUN, and the owner confirms that was correct:
inventing an exact_wire_type to decide a class manufactures the evidence the
question turns on. Recorded so nobody "completes" it later.

WHAT IS NOT YET DONE. This bead asked for a class, and the class is now settled
for both families. Neither has been MINTED -- both still exist only as census
candidates, with no reservation and no landed row. Minting them is the same
five-step increment as the two dkjg hosts (logical_kind row + target row +
identity_class flip + base-derived pin re-freeze + appendix-regenerate), and it
should follow the same recipe. Whoever takes it: re-derive the code frontier
first; 0x056f was the maximum landed object_kind at a22f241 and other panes mint
above it.

Closing: the ruling requested has been given and applied. The mint is separable
follow-on work, not this bead.
close_reason: Owner ruling: a flat record whose members are all source-typeless mints LOGICAL, governing the general class. LocalGcApplyQuarantineSpec was separately source-FORCED to logical by derivation (0 of 923 landed field rows hang off a wire-only host, and its five named StrongRef members must be field rows); LocalGcCancellationAuthorizeSpec is settled by the ruling. The bead's own falsification was itself falsified: its seven wire-record counterexamples carry 0 field rows and 2-5 union arms, so they are instances of the refinement, not counterexamples. Minting is separable follow-on work.

title: BUG: one delta block over the 16 KiB object ceiling makes the database unreopenable — sustained ingest has no seal-at-size policy
description:
Filed by CreamGlen 2026-08-22, discovered by the fgdb-p95p adversarial harness (crates/fgdb-bench) on its FIRST sustained-ingest run. Reproduced 3x deterministically at HEAD with the local release build.

## REPRODUCTION
Ordinary durable path, no crash injection: Database::create -> repeated Database::write batches (~64 edges each, ~5 KB serialized). After a handful of commits the accumulated delta block crosses the block store object ceiling:
  write fails: 'commit CommitSeq(N) is durable, but PublishPartitionRoot failed ... stored object has at least 16702 bytes, above the 16384-byte limit'
Dropping the handle and reopening (the error text's own remedy):
  open fails: 'rebuild: block store: stored object has at least 16702 bytes, above the 16384-byte limit'
The oversized object is DURABLE IN THE STREAM, so every subsequent Database::open refuses during rebuild. The directory admits no documented recovery: Database::open and open_rebuilding both replay/rebuild through the same refusing path. The data is intact; the front door is bricked.

## WHY IT HAPPENS
Tier-D write path accumulates multiple commits into one delta block with NO seal-at-size policy: batch size does not matter (reproduced at 200- and 64-edge batches; the fence lands after ~4-6 batches either way as the SHARED block crosses 16384 bytes). The ceiling is only enforced at publish time, after the oversized object has already been made durable.

## IMPACT
- Sustained transactional ingest (§17 gate 2) cannot proceed past ~16 KiB of accumulated delta payload without bricking the database. This is the binding operational constraint on every ingest number the harness publishes (published honestly as shape_engine_limit events).
- Any workload that crosses the boundary once loses the ability to reopen; recovery requires manual stream surgery that no bead owns.

## WHAT THE FIX NEEDS (owner routing: W3/tier-D, fgdb-tvg8 epic)
1. Seal-or-split policy at (or before) the publish boundary so an over-ceiling object is never made durable; AND
2. A recovery story for streams that already contain an over-ceiling object (open-time split, or tolerate-and-seal-on-rebuild); AND
3. A mutation-proven witness that sustained ingest crosses many sealed blocks without ever fencing (extend crates/fgdb-bench shape ingest-power-law to assert zero fences once fixed).

## EVIDENCE ARTIFACTS
/tmp/benchrun*.ndjson (shape_engine_limit events, fences_survived=1 then open refused), harness source crates/fgdb-bench/src/lib.rs load_model_durably(). Bench bead: fgdb-p95p.
notes:
== WHITE-BOX DIAGNOSIS 2026-08-23 by CreamGlen (source + bricked-directory forensics) ==
Correction to 'WHY IT HAPPENS': the block store is NOT at fault for durability of an oversize object. store.rs put_object_with_steps runs ensure_size_within_limit(offered_len, MAX_STORED_OBJECT_BYTES) BEFORE any durability (store.rs:740), and forensics on the bricked directory confirm NO oversize object was ever stored: largest .block on disk is 13,246 bytes (< 16384); capsules (a different object family, up to 40,214 B here) are not under this limit.

The actual mechanism: the tier-D fold accumulates multiple commits' deltas into ONE pending block and offers it whole at derived publication. When the offer crosses 16384 the put refuses pre-store (good), but the commit marker is already durable, so the handle fences. On the next Database::open, rebuild DETERMINISTICALLY REPLAYS the same capsule stream, re-folds the same accumulated deltas, and RE-OFFERS the same >=16384-byte block -- same refusal, every time. The brick is a deterministic replay cycle, not a stored bad object.

FIX LOCATION therefore: the fold/seal policy where pending deltas accumulate (crates/fgdb-strata writer/fold path upstream of BlockStore::put), which must seal-at-size so NEITHER the live publish NOR the deterministic replay ever offers an over-ceiling block. A recovery-only patch (tolerate-and-split on rebuild) would also break the cycle but must keep replay bit-identical to live publication per the equivalence laws.

CONSTANTS: MAX_BLOCK_ENTRIES=256 (lib.rs:500); MAX_STORED_OBJECT_BYTES=256*64=16384 (store.rs:98) -- note the byte limit is entries*64, so ~64B/entry average is the real budget; a 256-entry block of wide rows exceeds it by construction. That interaction (entry COUNT limit vs BYTE limit disagreeing) is the design seam the sealing policy has to reconcile.

== ROOT-CAUSE CORRECTION 2026-08-23 by CreamGlen (mutation control + forensics) ==
The earlier white-box note's 'fix location' was WRONG and its speculative writer patch has been REVERTED (mutation red-control could not fire it: edge/vertex/property-patch objects are format-bounded below 16384 for lawful inputs -- the byte cut never engaged).

THE ACTUAL UNBOUNDED ACCUMULATOR IS THE PARTITION ROOT. Forensics on the bricked directory: 356 sealed blocks on disk; root reference records are 56B each, so a root enumerating all of them offers ~19,936 bytes > the 16,384 ceiling. Arithmetic matches the observed error exactly (~225 refs -> ~16.2-16.6 KB; error said 16702). The last SUCCESSFULLY published manifest.root on disk is 8,192 B (~113 refs); the next root offer crossed the ceiling, PublishPartitionRoot refused post-marker, and every reopen deterministically replays the same capsule stream into the same oversize root. There is no checkpoint/root-compaction trigger on this spine path.

FIX LOCATION (corrected): the root/publication plane -- either (a) checkpoint/root-roll policy that starts a fresh root when the reference enumeration approaches MAX_STORED_OBJECT_BYTES (56B/ref -> ~290 block refs at headroom), or (b) root-reference compaction folding sealed blocks. Both are W3/tier-D durability-plane changes needing the crash-point matrix; the store's own admission check is correct and stays.

VERIFICATION INSTRUMENTS ALREADY IN TREE: crates/fgdb-bench reproduces on every run (shape_engine_limit events); once fixed, ingest-power-law must complete with publish_fence_reopens=0 and zero engine-limit events.

== DESIGN-SPACE CLOSURE 2026-08-23 02:4x by CreamGlen (kills the easy fixes; elevates routing to W3+G0) ==
1. rebuild() SHARES the live publication seam: async fn rebuild (lib.rs:4682) folds the whole stream into a fresh BlockWriter then calls THE SAME publish_and_snapshot (lib.rs:4936) whose put_root refused. Any guard placed at that composition point therefore covers BOTH the live write path and replay -- one fix site, verified.

2. AUTO-COMPACTION CANNOT FIX THIS CLASS. compact_with_props packs per descriptor family: output refs >= number of distinct (src,relation) families with live entries. The bench shape (~2000 srcs after preferential attachment) yields ~2000 post-compaction refs -> ~112 KB root, still 7x over ceiling. Compaction only rescues FEW-family graphs. Measured instrument agrees: stored_blocks=380 at fence with only ~15 commits x 64 edges spread across many families.

3. THEREFORE the fix is a ROOT-FORMAT change; candidates for the W3+G0 owner sitting (Appendix A root format is FROZEN -- this interacts with the format freeze):
   (a) root continuation records (next_root_ref chain when over budget);
   (b) two-level roots: root references ROOT_SEGMENT objects, each <= ceiling of refs;
   (c) root stores per-family CHAIN HEADS only and admission walks family chains (changes the read/admission path).
   Each carries migration + replay-equivalence + crash-matrix obligations. Until one lands, sustained ingest past ~292 accumulated blocks fences permanently; the bench (crates/fgdb-bench ingest-power-law) is the standing reproduction and regression instrument (stored_blocks now published in every engine_limit event; measured 380).
close_reason: Fixed at 5f8b9180: per-family admission in put_object_with_steps -- Root objects admit against crate::root::MAX_ENCODED_ROOT_BYTES (the layout law get_root always applied); blocks/patches/manifests keep the block-derived bound. NO format change was needed: the frozen root layout already declared the larger ceiling (MAX_ROOT_BLOCKS=2^20); admission was simply unwired on the write path. Mutation-proven witness a_root_lawful_under_its_own_format_ceiling_is_admitted (19,294 B root; shared-bound mutation fails with ObjectTooLarge {limit:16384}). End-to-end: fgdb-bench full fixture, 5994 edges / 94 commits / ZERO fences / 2349 stored blocks (8x past old brick point), cold reopen identical; fgdb suite 232/232. Bricked directories recover automatically. The --force is for the now-superseded dependency on fgdb-root-format-ruling-sitting-snbc: its three format strategies addressed a premise disproven during implementation (frozen format already lawful); that bead is re-scoped in comments to the OPTIONAL working-set compaction policy.

It carries the full option scorecard — recommendation: two-level ROOT_SEGMENT objects, K=256 refs, additive-minor epoch, rebuild-side healing of bricked dirs for free via the shared publication seam — plus an optional pre-seal admission stopgap for owner approval. a7sz implementation unblocks when the sitting rules.

title: Shared /data/tmp/cargo-target deletes a concurrent pane's test binaries mid-run: false reds that abort the whole workspace test
close_reason: Implementation 85c863e remains in current history; the bead records focused and mutation evidence, and the authoritative repository gate at c3f985f exited 0 with core 9/9 and registered live 24/24, lifting its explicit terminal blocker.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
MEASURED TWICE, on two different runs, hours apart (pane4, 2026-07-26), while working fgdb-m2c1.

Every pane builds into the same CARGO_TARGET_DIR, /data/tmp/cargo-target (51G). Two build slots exist, so two panes can be inside cargo at once by design. When one pane's cargo removes or replaces a test binary that another pane's cargo has already scheduled to run, the second pane gets:

  error: test failed, to rerun pass `-p registry-check --bin architecture-check`
  Caused by:
    could not execute process `/data/tmp/cargo-target/debug/deps/architecture_check-50697380607c819a` (never executed)
  Caused by:
    No such file or directory (os error 2)

OCCURRENCE 1, a real scripts/check.sh at HEAD 9c0d3c1. 31 of 67 suites ran and ALL 31 PASSED. The run then aborted on the message above and check.sh reported RED. Nothing was wrong with the tree: the binary was deleted underneath it.

OCCURRENCE 2, my own first m2c1 measurement, `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` in the same shared dir. Five registry-check test binaries reported "(never executed) / No such file or directory" in one run -- metamorphic, satisfiability, spine, threat_model and others. The numbers were unusable and I moved to a private target dir to get clean ones.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN "RERUN IT":
  - It is a FALSE RED on a green tree, and it looks exactly like a real failure.
    A pane that sees it will start diagnosing its own increment.
  - Before 43f7907 it also fanned out: check.sh stamped the workspace exit code
    onto all six registered cargo-test artifacts, so one deleted binary reported
    as six broken artifacts. That half is fixed -- each artifact now reports its
    own binary, and an artifact whose binary never ran reads UNRUN -- but the
    underlying race is untouched and still aborts the workspace run.
  - It is nondeterministic and depends on another pane's timing, so it is
    exactly the shape that trains people to ignore a red.

WHAT I DID NOT ESTABLISH: which cargo operation does the deleting. Candidates worth separating are a concurrent `cargo test` replacing a dep binary after a source change, `cargo clippy --all-targets` overwriting the same paths, and cargo's own garbage collection of stale artifacts. Discriminating between them is the first job, because the fix differs.

OPTIONS, none yet measured:
  - per-pane CARGO_TARGET_DIR: removes the race entirely, costs one full
    workspace target dir per pane (the shared one is 51G; free space was 24G
    when this was filed, so this is NOT free and may be unaffordable as-is);

    and halves build parallelism;

    Cheapest, and it does not hide anything if the retry is printed.

process" must stay a failure unless the retry passes cleanly, and the retry must
be visible in the log.

title: P0: main does not compile — 17 active logical kinds vs 10 refs.rs arms, seven missing
description:
## Status: main has not compiled for hours, and the break is GROWING

    error[E0080]: evaluation panicked: assertion failed:
        count_bytes(LOGICAL_OBJECT_KIND_REGISTRY, ACTIVE_STATUS_ROW)
            == LogicalObjectKindCode::ALL_ACTIVE.len()
    error: could not compile `fgdb-types` (lib)

`fgdb-types` is a foundation crate, so this takes down the WHOLE workspace:
every pane's `cargo check`, `cargo clippy`, `cargo test`, and `ubs` (which
invokes cargo internally).

## The exact defect

`registries/logical_object_kinds.toml` now has 17 rows with `status = "active"`.
`active_logical_object_kinds!` in `crates/fgdb-types/src/refs.rs` has 10 arms.
Seven active rows have no arm:

    0x028f  DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence
    0x0550  DurableCapabilityHeader
    0x0551  ExactDurableCapabilityKindBody
    0x0552  CanonicalDurableCapabilityBytes
    0x0553  DurableCapabilityMacInput
    0x0554  DurableCapabilityValidationActionScope
    0x0555  DurableCapabilityValidatorSemanticsRegistry

All seven are the DurableCapability* / a21 family from
fgdb-durable-capability-validation-evidence-dqym.

It compounded because nothing rejected the first one:
  84418b2  added 0x028f active, no arm      -> 11 active vs 10 arms
  71f6027  added six more active, no arms   -> 17 active vs 10 arms

## Why it was invisible

Enforcement lived ONLY in two `const _: () = assert!(...)` inside fgdb-types.
Measured: grep across all of tools/registry-check for `refs.rs`,
`active_logical_object_kinds`, `ALL_ACTIVE` returns EMPTY. registry-check,
the identity suite, architecture-check and the G0 identity e2e were ALL GREEN
on the exact tree that would not build.

Now fixed as a gate: 47807be adds `validate_active_logical_kind_arms`, which
names each offending row in both directions. `registry-check all` and
`claims_real_registries_validate` now fail loudly and specifically. That
commit lands intentionally red — it reports this bead's defect.

## The decision needed (this is why it is a bead, not a patch)

Two candidate repairs, and they are NOT equivalent:

**(a) Add seven arms to `active_logical_object_kinds!`** — before/after:

    // crates/fgdb-types/src/refs.rs, after line 151
        PreparedCommitRecord = 0x000b => "PreparedCommitRecord",
    +   DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence = 0x028f => "DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence",
    +   DurableCapabilityHeader = 0x0550 => "DurableCapabilityHeader",
    +   ExactDurableCapabilityKindBody = 0x0551 => "ExactDurableCapabilityKindBody",
    +   CanonicalDurableCapabilityBytes = 0x0552 => "CanonicalDurableCapabilityBytes",
    +   DurableCapabilityMacInput = 0x0553 => "DurableCapabilityMacInput",
    +   DurableCapabilityValidationActionScope = 0x0554 => "DurableCapabilityValidationActionScope",
    +   DurableCapabilityValidatorSemanticsRegistry = 0x0555 => "DurableCapabilityValidatorSemanticsRegistry",

    NOTE the per-arm const assert also requires each registry row to read
    EXACTLY `object_kind = 0x....\nname = "..."\nstatus = "active"` in that
    field order. Verified present for all seven.

    Cost: declares seven live `LogicalObjectKindCode` variants for types with
    NO implementation anywhere in crates/ (grep returns zero hits outside the
    registries). `active` is otherwise the rare status — 10 of 435 before this
    family; the other 424 rows are `reserved`.

**(b) Flip the seven rows back to `status = "reserved"`** — before/after:

    -status = "active"
    +status = "reserved"

    MEASURED COST, do not assume this is free: flipping even one trips
    `registry_assignment_drift` on BOTH logical_object_kinds AND durable_fields
    — "released codes, tags, names, lifecycle states, and union arms are
    append-only" — plus `idr_assignment_history_and_epoch_are_frozen`. Verified
    by applying the flip to a clean HEAD copy: identity went 90/90 -> 85/90.
    So (b) requires a base-derived pin re-freeze, not a one-word edit.

## Recommendation

(b), with the re-freeze. Evidence: the seven types have no implementation, and
the a21 family looks like it is minting rows `active` by habit — 424 of 435
comparable rows are `reserved`, including every a13 row and its containers.
If that reading is right, the applier that produced these rows should default
to `reserved`, or the same defect returns on the next a21 increment.

But this is the dqym owner's call, and (b) is not reversible-cheap, so it
should not be made by a passing pane.

## Do not close this by deleting the checker

The checker is the only thing standing between this and the next silent
recurrence. If (a) is chosen, the checker goes green on its own.
notes:
VERIFIED FIXED by pane2, 2026-07-26. Verification only; no repair applied.

## The measurement (current HEAD, taken three independent ways)

  active rows in registries/logical_object_kinds.toml   17
  arms in active_logical_object_kinds! (refs.rs)        17
  the (code, name) SETS are equal, both directions      TRUE

Not a count comparison -- the sorted pair sets are equal, so seven-in/seven-out
cannot cancel. The seven rows named in this bead all have their arm:
0x028f, 0x0550, 0x0551, 0x0552, 0x0553, 0x0554, 0x0555.

Landed by cfb2a64 `fix(types): restore the active-kind/arm bijection — seven
missing arms`. That is PATH A of the two candidates recorded here.

## Verified by the real instruments, not by counting

1. THE GATE. `registry-check validate --root .` exit 0, zero
   `active_logical_kind*` violations. Also zero under the full
   `registry-check all` on a pristine `git archive HEAD` (exit 0 overall).

2. THE CONST ASSERTS -- the thing that was actually failing. `crates/fgdb-types/
   src/refs.rs` and `ids.rs` copied VERBATIM (`cmp`-clean) into a depth-matched
   probe so `include_bytes!("../../../registries/logical_object_kinds.toml")`
   resolves to the real current registry, then compiled with rustc. Exit 0.
   Both `contains_bytes` (per-arm, refs.rs:121) and `count_bytes` (the count,
   refs.rs:134) pass. This is the E0080 from the bead title, gone.

3. A full `cargo check --all-targets` passed at 22:12 tonight on HEAD 0754359,
   with refs.rs byte-identical to now. (The registry has since changed in
   c5570ce, which is why (2) was re-run against the current bytes rather than
   relied on from that run.)

A direct `rch exec -- cargo check -p fgdb-types --locked` was also started but
stalled >17 min with no output on the known asupersync fetch hang and was
killed to free build-2; it is not needed, because (2) exercises the exact
asserts that were failing with the exact sources and the exact registry.

## The gate is live AND non-vacuous -- five mutations, all fired

`validate_active_logical_kind_arms` (validate.rs:1171, added 47807be), run
against mirrored scratch roots. Control first: the unmutated mirror reproduces
the repo's own verdict, so a rejection cannot be the fixture being different.

  M1  flip a reserved row to active, no arm  -> active_logical_kind_without_arm
      (0x0009 CheckpointStateVector) -- the ORIGINAL defect, exit 1
  M2  delete an arm, row stays active        -> active_logical_kind_without_arm
      (0x0553) -- the reverse direction, exit 1
  M3  arm name disagrees with the row        -> active_logical_kind_name_mismatch
  M4  arm for a non-active code              -> arm_without_active_logical_kind
  M5  VACUITY: delete the macro block        -> active_logical_kind_macro_absent
      "no `active_logical_object_kinds!` invocation found; the arm binding was
       NOT checked"

M5 is the one that matters for this family: the checker refuses to report a
binding it did not check, so it cannot go quietly green by finding nothing. The
M1 message even names the repair ("Either add the arm or make the row
status=\"reserved\"").

So the answer to "does anything now fail when a row is added without its arm"
is YES, in all four directions, with the vacuity case closed.

## THE RESIDUE IS REAL, and it is filed as fgdb-gg4b (P1)

The bijection is guarded. The BYTE LAYOUT the const asserts actually depend on
is not. `registry-check all` byte-compares the projection against what
`appendix_a.rs::render_logical` generates; refs.rs asserts over the file's raw
bytes. A hand edit breaks both and is caught. A GENERATOR change breaks only the
second -- regenerate and the byte-compare is satisfied by construction.

Measured end to end: swapping two lines in `render_logical` so it emits `name`
before `object_kind`, then regenerating, gives `registry-check all` exit 0 with
ZERO violations and `error[E0080] ... contains_bytes(...)` on the build. Green
gate, dead workspace -- this bead's exact failure mode, through a door 47807be
does not cover. Nothing declares that field order, the sibling emitters use
different ones, and c5570ce already rewrote a field in every row of this
projection tonight (it sits after `status`, so the adjacency happened to hold).

## Method note for the next verifier

My first `registry-check all` runs reported main RED with 12 violation kinds. It
was not. The checker binary was built from an older HEAD, and a stale checker
against a newer catalog manufactures pin drift. Rebuilt from current HEAD: exit
0. I nearly reported main as broken, and the gg4b bead's first draft was wrong
because its baseline was that false red. Rebuild the checker every verification
round. [[stale-binary-reports-phantom-pin-drift]]
close_reason: VERIFIED FIXED, not assumed. 17 active rows, 17 arms, and the (code,name) SETS are equal in both directions -- landed by cfb2a64 (PATH A). Confirmed by the two real instruments: registry-check validate/all report zero active_logical_kind violations, and the real refs.rs+ids.rs compiled VERBATIM against the real registry so both const asserts (contains_bytes and count_bytes) pass -- the E0080 in the title is gone. The 47807be gate is live and non-vacuous: five mutations fire, including M5 (macro deleted) which reports 'the arm binding was NOT checked' rather than passing silently. Residue filed as fgdb-gg4b: a one-line change to render_logical leaves the gate green and breaks the build, because the projection is byte-compared to its generator, not to the const asserts that consume it.

title: docs/ARCHITECTURE_DECISION_RECORD.md is neither regenerated/byte-compared nor claims-lint-scanned, unlike its two sibling docs, and its provenance-coverage count has drifted 294 vs 364
description:
FINDING — mock/placeholder sweep phase 2 (pane4, 2026-07-26), claims-vs-
implementation lane. Measured on main at 9fdbe0d.

## The asymmetry

Three documents under `docs/` are generated companions to a registry. Two are
regenerated and byte-compared; the third is neither, and it is the largest:

| document | generator flag | byte-compare test |
|---|---|---|
| `docs/WORKSPACE_TOPOLOGY.md` | `topology-check --write` | `tests/workspace_topology.rs:112` |
| `docs/THREAT_AND_TRUST_MODEL.md` | `threat-check --write` | `tests/threat_model.rs:98` |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE_DECISION_RECORD.md` (53 KB) | **none** | **none** |

`architecture-check` has no `--write` flag at all (`grep -c '"--write"'` gives
1, 1, 0 across topology-check, threat-check, architecture-check). The only
place the checker touches the ADR file is `architecture.rs:3923`, a
`document_path` filter used to verify the `CHECKED-SOURCE` excerpt blocks
against the master plan. **The excerpts are verified byte-for-byte; the prose
around them is verified by nothing.**

It is also outside the only other instrument pointed at prose:
`registries/claims_lint.toml` scans exactly `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and
`COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_THE_DESIGN_OF_FRANKENGRAPHDB.md`. No `docs/` path is in
the scan list. So the ADR prose is the one normative document in the tree that
is neither regenerated-and-byte-compared nor claims-lint-scanned.

## It has already drifted, and on a load-bearing number

`docs/ARCHITECTURE_DECISION_RECORD.md:7`, verbatim:

> "The provenance closure covers **all 294 Beads records**, including closed
>  historical work. Each issue resolves through exactly one precedence tier..."

Measured now:

  - `.beads/issues.jsonl`                      364 records
  - `registries/architecture_decisions.toml`   `bead_count = 364`
  - `tools/registry-check/src/architecture.rs` `PINNED_BEAD_COUNT = 364`
  - the ADR                                    **294**

Stale by 70. This is not a decorative figure: it is the coverage claim for the
provenance closure — the exact quantity the bead-provenance pins exist to
enforce, and the one that has been red on main all day. Both independent pins
were re-frozen to 364 today; the human-facing document that states what those
pins mean was not, because nothing asks it to be.

The doc's own header claims the checker does more than it does: "`architecture-check`
verifies the excerpts byte-for-byte against the master plan, **pins the decision
identity and semantic tables**, validates live owner and claim references". All
true — and none of it covers the sentence three paragraphs down.

## What is NOT a finding here (checked, so the next reader does not re-check)

`ARCHITECTURE_DECISION_RECORD.md:95` says "franken_networkx (~247 KLOC, **12
crates**)". That is a count of the external `fnx-*` dependency, not of this
workspace, and is not drift.

## Which gate catches this today

None. `architecture-check` exits without reading the prose; `cargo test` has no
ADR test; claims-lint does not scan `docs/`. `fgdb-g0-doc-sync-usq` owns the
general "generate README/AGENTS as checked artifacts" programme and is the right
long-term home, but it is scoped to README/AGENTS and does not name this file,
so the ADR would still fall through.

## Fix

1. Give `architecture-check` the `--write` render path its two siblings already
   have, and add the byte-compare test. The pattern is in-tree twice; this is
   copying it, not designing it.
2. Derive every count in the ADR prose from the registry at render time. A typed
   number in a generated document is a second source of truth, which is exactly
   what §5.1's registry discipline forbids.
3. Add `docs/**.md` to `claims_lint.toml`'s scan list so marker citations in
   those files resolve too — cheap, and it closes the surface rather than this
   one instance.
4. Seed a negative fixture: a hand-edited count in the ADR must fail with its
   exact code, or this joins the 253 laws nobody has watched fire
   (fgdb-validator-laws-never-witnessed-firing-xnxy).
notes:
RESOLVED by pane2, 2026-07-26. NOTE: `br update --notes` REPLACES the notes
field, it does not append -- two earlier notes on this bead were silently
overwritten before that was noticed. This is the consolidated record.

===========================================================================
1. THE MEASUREMENT, taken on main at 82e1a93 BEFORE any fix
===========================================================================

193 of the ADR's 208 lines are the two CHECKED-SOURCE excerpt regions, and
those WERE already byte-verified (architecture.rs source_check reads the plan
line range and compares). The unverified surface is 15 lines: the title, four
paragraphs, and the source-block table.

|--------------------------------------|----------:|-----:|--------:|

THE THREE DRIFTED CLAIMS

D3. L14 source-block table, "Inclusive lines" for plan-reviewed-bibliography-v1
