title: Implement fgdb-bigint canonical signed-limb arithmetic kernel
description:
## What and scope
Create the first real engine crate at crates/fgdb-bigint and implement the final canonical signed-limb arithmetic kernel required by W1 and Ripple. The representation is private, normalized sign plus little-endian u64 magnitude limbs: zero has exactly one representation, nonzero values have no high zero limbs, and equality/order/hash therefore agree structurally. Implement exact signed add, subtract, multiply, negate, scalar construction, checked i128 conversion, magnitude inspection for codecs, and deterministic diagnostics.

This is a final subset of fgdb-w1-foundation-types-tjk, not a prototype. It deliberately does not invent a durable wire encoding: durable codec tags/bytes remain owned by the generated-format Bead. It also does not claim Ripple integration. All allocation-capable arithmetic accepts an explicit LimbLimit and fails before allocating above that limit, so later fgdb-resource accounting can wrap the kernel without an unbounded bypass.

## Why
The plan requires in-house canonical exact integers for ZWeight promotion and overflow-free STRICT rational comparisons. Producing this kernel now creates substantive reusable product code while the wider G0 registry work continues independently.

## Acceptance criteria
- Add crates/fgdb-bigint as a real workspace member with Rust 2024 and forbid unsafe code.
- Preserve the unique canonical representation across every constructor and operation.
- Exact signed addition, subtraction, multiplication, negation, total ordering, equality, hashing, and checked i128 conversion work across carry, borrow, sign change, zero, u64 boundaries, and i128 MIN/MAX.
- LimbLimit rejection reports operation, required limbs, and limit and occurs before result allocation beyond the declared bound.
- No external dependency or durable-format invention is introduced.
- Unit and deterministic property tests cover canonicalization, randomized i64 differential arithmetic against i128, multi-limb ring laws, order laws, carry/borrow chains, multiplication boundaries, limit failures, and conversion limits.
- A crate-scoped E2E script runs the complete test target twice from an isolated Cargo target and proves deterministic success.
- cargo fmt --check, cargo check --all-targets, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test, and UBS over changed files complete before closure.

## Boundaries
No parser, storage engine, mutable state, I/O, unsafe code, serde, or compatibility shim. Resource-ledger integration, spill, ZWeight, and the registered durable codec remain downstream work.

title: Migrate the shipped BoundPlan/gql_exec query slice onto the GLA operator family instead of letting it fossilize
description:
## Context

Between 2026-08-20 and 2026-08-22 the repository gained its first end-to-end
query capability, and it did so **without an algebra**:

- `crates/fgdb-gql/src/lib.rs` (one 3,186-line module) parses a bounded MATCH
  subset — labeled node scans, one-hop `-[:R]->`/`<-[:R]-`/`-[:R]-`, exactly
  two-hop chains, integer property predicates, at most two ANDed endpoint
  predicates, single-variable RETURN, SKIP/LIMIT — into a private AST and then
  `BoundPlan` (:97 binder :240, parser :386).
- `crates/fgdb/src/gql_exec.rs` (592 LOC) executes `BoundPlan` directly by
  rebuilding hop-1/hop-2 `BTreeMap<VId, Vec<VId>>` adjacencies from a full
  admitted-edge scan on **every query** (:29/:66/:97 builders, :505/:551 entry
  points), filtered in place, projected by one shared kernel
  (`execute_bound_plan_over`, crates/fgdb/src/lib.rs:904).
- Results are deduped ascending `Vec<VId>`; a `GqlPlanCertificate` hashes
  BoundPlan + snapshot seq (`crates/fgdb/src/gql_cert.rs`).
- Verification is strong: ~200 integration tests plus **86 differential oracle
  suites** in `crates/fgdb-sim/tests/*_oracle*.rs` against an independently
  replayed `fgdb-reference` graph.

Meanwhile the plan's Bet B3 (Loom) specifies one Graph-Logical Algebra with
registered operators, TrieCursor access over Strata tries, FreeJoin continuum,
factorized types. W5 stage beads exist: `fgdb-5vp9` (Stage 1: binary FreeJoin),
`fgdb-rz12` (Stage 2: run-trie WCOJ), `fgdb-gate-genesis-lce` (Genesis slice).
No bead mentions `BoundPlan` or `gql_exec` (searches return zero). The
2026-08-20 reality check explicitly warned: *"Keep it as the vertical slice,
not a fourth planner."* Without an owning migration bead, the bespoke executor
fossilizes into exactly that fourth planner — parallel to, rather than seeding,
Loom.

## Change

Design and land the lowering seam that turns the shipped slice into GLA's first
customer:

1. Introduce the minimal registered GLA operator set sufficient for the current
   grammar: vertex scan, edge-expand (oriented/undirected), filter/select,
   project, limit — typed over binding tables per plan §8.3 naming.
2. Lower `BoundPlan` → GLA DAG; delete the inline adjacency-building kernel in
   `gql_exec.rs` (clean cutover: no duplicate executor path may remain).
3. Execute over the W5 physical family once `fgdb-5vp9` lands its operator +
   TrieCursor contracts; until then the GLA DAG may interpret over the existing
   scan, but the *algebra boundary* must be the only seam.
4. Preserve, without regression:
   - the full differential contract with `fgdb-reference` (all 86 oracle suites
     stay green, assertions unweakened);
   - `execute_gql_at` temporal-selection semantics;
   - `GqlPlanCertificate`: continue hashing bound statement + snapshot seq, and
     extend the digest to the GLA plan hash in the same change that makes plan
     structure non-trivial (update the frozen fixture);
   - result determinism (today: deduped ascending VIds; reserve the CGSE
     tie-break-policy hook in the projection operator).
5. If Strata cursor pushdown (replacing per-query full edge scans with sealed /
   Tier-D cursor reads) fits the same diff, include it; otherwise split it into
   an immediate child bead referencing this one — but do not silently drop it.

## Acceptance

- No `Operator`-free executor: a debug `EXPLAIN`-style dump (even eprintln in a
  test) shows GLA operator names for a bounded MATCH query.
- `gql_exec.rs`'s standalone adjacency builders are gone or reimplemented as a
  GLA physical operator; `git grep gql_exec` finds no second execution path.
- All 86 fgdb-sim oracle suites pass unmodified in their assertions.
- Certificate fixture updated for the extended plan-hash digest; a negative
  test shows a mutated plan changes the digest.
- Complexity witness rows registered for each new physical operator (per
  Appendix C contract), even if bounds are provisional.

## Non-goals

- Parser breadth: variable-length/quantified paths, ORDER BY, DML-through-GQL,
  branch/time selector syntax — owned by the W5 language beads and
  `fgdb-g0-language-contracts-54g`.
- Cost-based optimization and statistics — later W5 stages.

This bead is currently blocked by fgdb-dbvf on the theory that the competing a01:1443 / a02:1449 bodies are what stop `location_form = ContiguousSpan{...} | Explicit{...}` from parsing. That theory is FALSE and I tested it directly. Rewriting the appendix in memory (line count held constant so slice ranges stay valid) and re-running census_appendix_source:
  BASELINE (HEAD)                              a02 unions=0 arms=0
  reconcile a01:1443 to the a02 rendering      a02 unions=0 arms=0
  rename a01:1443 to RootPlacementDescriptor…  a02 unions=0 arms=0

THE REAL CAUSE: the census union-name extractor `trailing_upper_identifier` (tools/registry-check/src/appendix_source.rs:1996-2004) ends with `(start < bytes.len() && bytes[start].is_ascii_uppercase()).then_some(...)`, so a union whose name does not start with an ASCII uppercase letter is never recognised at all. `location_form` is snake_case. Single-variable proof, sentence otherwise byte-identical:
  location_form (baseline)          unions=0
  zz_unique_form / qq_other_form    unions=0
  LocationForm / ZzUniqueForm       unions=1, arms=["ContiguousSpan","Explicit"]
  Location_form  (l -> L ONLY)      unions=1, arms=["ContiguousSpan","Explicit"]
The one-character flip settles it. Note what this means for your scope: the moment the initial is uppercase, BOTH arms parse — including `Explicit`, whose absence from the catalog you are chartered to fix. `Explicit` has zero rows today (the only "Explicit" strings in the catalog are RestoreExplicitRetentionOwnerRef, unrelated) not because anyone chose to omit it, but because the union it belongs to has never been visible to the census. ContiguousSpan exists standalone as a02 wire type 0x000a purely because someone registered the arm they could see.

IT IS A SOURCE ERRATUM, MEASURED: appendix-wide there are 11 backticked `Name = Arm{...} | Arm{...}` constructs; 10 are CapitalCase and location_form is the only lowercase-initial one. The checker convention parses all 10 others correctly, so the fix belongs in the plan, not in the checker — widening the extractor would re-interpret all 573 appendix unions to rescue one site.

PROPOSED NORMATIVE EDIT (a01/a02 owners' and the plan owner's call, not mine — filing, not editing). Minimal, idiom-conforming, single line 1449:
  BEFORE: where `location_form = ContiguousSpan{failure_domain_id,segment_id,offset,encoded_len,symbol_inventory_digest} | Explicit{sorted_symbol_inventory_and_locators,failure_domains}`
  AFTER:  where `LocationForm = ContiguousSpan{failure_domain_id,segment_id,offset,encoded_len,symbol_inventory_digest} | Explicit{sorted_symbol_inventory_and_locators,failure_domains}`
and, if the field should carry its type explicitly, `{ encoding_id, placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy, location_form:LocationForm }`. Any of these unblocks the Explicit arm registration this bead exists to do. None of them requires touching a01:1443, and none is a catalog edit.

title: Adopt fgdb-codec::identity in the Tier-D block entry encoding: the codec is built and unused, and strata is the caller it waits for
notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-04 at HEAD 41fb41b by JadeSnow while re-deriving fgdb-ge6a. Labels: b2, strata, w3.

THE FINDING. The Tier-D identity-column codec is NOT unbuilt. crates/fgdb-codec/src/identity.rs (145 KB) already implements the §6.2 normative layout: IdentityColumn / SortedIdentityColumn (order-preserving shared-prefix, fixed / FOR / delta-FOR slot suffixes), IdentityPrefix, ForSlots, DeltaForSlots, OriginBirthOrder, IdentityColumnLimits, typed IdentityColumnError. Its own doc states the FOR payload "retains exact typed identity reconstruction, canonical big-endian keys, binary-search order, and the 16-byte-per-entry upper bound", and then names exactly what is missing: "It is not a durable encoding until a caller supplies registered framing, counts, and a codec ID."

fgdb-strata IS that caller, and it does not depend on fgdb-codec at all. crates/fgdb-strata/Cargo.toml declares fgdb-crypto, fgdb-types, fgdb-delta-types only. So the delta block still writes ENTRY_LEN = 16+8+16+16+8+8 = 72 bytes per entry, of which 48 are three RAW 128-bit identities (src VId, dst VId, EId) -- the exact layout the §6.2 sentence exists to forbid.

THE COST, now measured rather than asserted (witnesses landed at 41fb41b in crates/fgdb-strata/tests/delta_block_format.rs, which encode real blocks and difference the output):
  72 B per entry, where §6.2 allows <=16.
  56 entries per 4 KiB block, where §6.2 wants 256. A 4.5x density shortfall.
Those two witnesses are written to FAIL when this bead lands; that failure IS the acceptance signal, and re-deriving the numbers downward is part of the work.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND DENSITY. This is the single edge that moves fgdb-ge6a from blocked to startable. ge6a cannot register DeltaBlockVersion/PartitionRoot in Appendix A because registering freezes the normative contract and the current shape would enshrine the regression -- a breaking-major change plus a catalog re-pin cycle to undo. Nothing else in the tier-D backlog is on that path.

SCOPE. Adopt the codec for the three identity columns in the block entry; supply the registered framing, entry counts, and codec ID the codec is waiting for; re-derive the 4 KiB / 256-entry constants against the result. This is a BREAKING-MAJOR block format change (BLOCK_FORMAT_V2 -> V3, §16.6), so it is one increment, not a trickle.

BLAST RADIUS, measured: crates/fgdb-strata/src/{lib,writer,store,compact,root}.rs; crates/fgdb-strata/tests/{delta_block_format,block_store,block_writer,compaction,complexity_witness}.rs; crates/fgdb-sim/tests/ (8 files read strata). MAX_BLOCK_ENTRIES is currently 1<<24 and must become the normative 256.

COORDINATION HAZARD observed 2026-08-04: crates/fgdb-strata/Cargo.toml was reserved by fgdb-4bxh (asupersync pin) and src/compact.rs by fgdb-1c9l (mutate-to-red verification) -- a format change invalidates in-flight mutation work. Take the whole crate reservation before starting, not file by file.

NOT IN SCOPE: the other five absent normative DeltaBlockVersion fields (partition_id, descriptor_key, stripe_range, property_patch_refs, predecessor, canonical_logical_digest) and skip-list nodes / hub striping. Those stay with fgdb-w3-tier-d-ctj. This bead is the entry ENCODING only, because that is the part ge6a is blocked on.
close_reason: Verified landed at HEAD 5ca2fb1 (successor-pane verify-or-close after fifth freeze; close was blocked by the schema-17 write freeze). Owner-ruled scope (PeachTiger msg 22269) is delivered: 70d6b6b adopts fgdb-codec::identity in the V3 durable frame (BLOCK_FORMAT_V3, MAX_BLOCK_ENTRIES=256, fgdb-codec now a real dependency of fgdb-strata), with the four hoists — src/relation at descriptor level, created_at/retired_at as run-length-coalesced visibility spans; 73cb3f0 reserves property_patch_refs fail-closed per the fgdb-2t7q ruling. Closure evidence chain green on fresh compile: cargo test -p fgdb-strata RC=0, all 9 suites (33/33 delta_block_format incl. the_v3_frame_is_thirteen_bytes_per_entry_and_visibility_amortizes_below_two = the 72->43->13 acceptance chain, and four_kibibytes_hold_the_normative_two_hundred_fifty_six_entries). comments.author: JadeSnow
comments.text:
SCOPE CORRECTED BY MEASUREMENT 2026-08-04 (JadeSnow). I filed this bead earlier today and its scope was WRONG. Landed 5500358 proves it, with the real codec rather than arithmetic.

MEASURED over the 256-entry run §6.2 talks about (crates/fgdb-strata/tests/delta_block_format.rs):
  raw layout today                      72 B/entry  (witnessed at 41fb41b)
  codec adopted, CURRENT entry shape    43 B/entry  a real 1.7x
  §6.2 own entry shape, same codec      13 B/entry  inside the 16 B law

So "adopt the codec for the entry encoding" -- this bead as filed -- lands at 43 B/entry, still 2.6x above the law. It would be a BREAKING format change that buys no unblocking: DeltaBlockVersion stays exactly as unregisterable as it is today, and a second breaking change would follow to finish the job. Two rewrites for one outcome.

THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL, NOT ENCODING. §6.2 entry is (dst_VId, EId, user_key_ref?, prop_row_ref, flags). No src, no relation, no inline created_at/retired_at -- a normative block is per (partition_id, descriptor_key) and visibility lives in the block own visibility_intervals[]. FOUR fields are hoisted OUT of the entry. No encoding of the identity columns can pay for a relation and two sequence numbers that should not be in the entry at all.

The 16 B ceiling is close to what TWO shared-prefix identity columns cost, which is why the normative entry carries exactly two. The second witness is the control for that claim and it holds: same codec, two normative columns, 13 B/entry -- with only 3 B left for user_key_ref?/prop_row_ref/flags. Tight rather than comfortable, and worth knowing BEFORE the shape is frozen.

REVISED SCOPE for this bead: adopt fgdb-codec::identity AND hoist the four non-entry fields (src -> block descriptor_key, relation -> block, created_at/retired_at -> visibility_intervals[]) in ONE breaking change V2->V3. That is a per-descriptor block, which is a genuine restructure of the writer, compaction and scan paths -- materially bigger than "adopt a codec" and arguably the core of fgdb-w3-tier-d-ctj rather than a separate bead. Whoever picks this up should decide with the orchestrator whether it stays standalone or folds into tier D; do not execute the original one-line scope.

fgdb-codec is now a DEV-dependency of fgdb-strata with a comment saying why: measuring what adoption buys is not adoption. The production edge lands with the format change. Workspace topology gate accepts it (59 passed).

title: fold must drop CreateEdge against a same-batch deleted/cancelled endpoint
description: fold_target_disjoint ignores CreateEdge only on the edge identity (cancelled/deleted/cascade_owned). DeleteVertex then CreateEdge to that vertex still emits both. title: registry-check validate is red on main: scripts/disk_hygiene.sh is an undeclared shell deliverable
description:
registry-check validate --root . exits 1:

  violation script_undeclared / checker_index / scripts/disk_hygiene.sh
  'shell deliverable is neither a registered checker artifact nor a
   [[script_disposition]] row; register it, or say why it is not a gate'

PRE-EXISTING, not from 2aa796a. scripts/disk_hygiene.sh is present in HEAD and HEAD's
registries/checker_index.toml carries ZERO declarations for it. It was added by the
cfg6 hygiene commits (ffb7b0e, a4f9d23). The a08 landing touches neither scripts/ nor
checker_index.toml.

This matters more than one red gate: the file-coverage closure in scripts/check.sh is
the gate that catches non-Rust deliverables, and validate is the checker that enforces
it. While validate is red, check.sh cannot pass for ANY pane, so nobody can run the full
mandatory chain even once disk recovers.

THE FIX IS A CLASSIFICATION, NOT A CODE CHANGE: either register disk_hygiene.sh as a
checker artifact, or add a [[script_disposition]] row saying why a hygiene script is not
a gate. The second is almost certainly correct -- it is an operator tool, not a checker
-- but that is the cfg6 owner's call to state, and the law is deliberately built so the
answer has to be written down rather than assumed.
close_reason:
FIXED in 953e31b. registry-check validate is GREEN: exit 0, checker_index 80 rows,
0 violations.

FIXED BY DECLARING, not by deleting or excluding. scripts/disk_hygiene.sh implements the
scratch inventory being used to escalate the reclaim, so removing it to green a gate
would have destroyed the artifact the gate was complaining about.

  BEFORE  exit 1 — checker_index violations 1
    code script_undeclared, row_id scripts/disk_hygiene.sh:
    "shell deliverable is neither a registered checker artifact nor a
     [[script_disposition]] row; register it, or say why it is not a gate"
  AFTER   exit 0 — checker_index violations 0, zero script_undeclared occurrences

THE DECLARATION: a [[script_disposition]] row with path/role/reason, role = advisory.
Not `candidate`: candidate means measured-and-promotable, a gate registered but for one
unverified assertion. This script asserts nothing about the repository — its own header
reads "Inventory only: this command never deletes or mutates artifacts" — so registering
it as a [[checker]] would make check.sh execute an inventory of a directory outside the
repo and then have no verdict to consume.

CONTROLS, both fire, so the row is load-bearing rather than incidentally green:
  path pointed at a non-existent file -> script_disposition_dangling AND script_undeclared
      BOTH fire, exit 1. A dangling row does not launder the file it was meant to cover.
  role set outside SCRIPT_ROLES       -> bad_field
Gates after: validate / identity / appendix / hash / lint all exit 0.

=== THE THREE MECHANISMS, WRITTEN DOWN ===
Requested explicitly because this cost two agents a wrong answer: the hazard was
predicted in mechanism 1, correctly falsified there, and then fired in mechanism 3. All
three re-verified directly rather than inherited.

  1. check.sh FILE-COVERAGE CLOSURE (coverage_of, scripts/check.sh:92)
     CLAIMS a .sh — by GLOB. The arm is `*.sh|*.bash) echo "bash -n + shellcheck (next
     step)"`. Any new shell file is claimed the instant it exists, so this closure can
     NEVER fire on a .sh. This is the mechanism that was predicted to break, and the
     falsification of that prediction was correct.
  2. check.sh SHELL-LINT GATE (scripts/check.sh:201)
     CLAIMS a .sh — by GLOB. `git ls-files '*.sh' '*.bash'`, then bash -n and shellcheck
     over each. It processes disk_hygiene.sh and PASSES; both re-run here, clean.
  3. registry-check validate script_undeclared (tools/registry-check/src/validate.rs:1101)
     DOES NOT claim a .sh. It requires an EXPLICIT per-file entry: a [[checker]] artifact
     row, or a [[script_disposition]] row in registries/checker_index.toml. This is the
     one that fired.

THE RULE THAT MAKES THIS PREDICTABLE: mechanisms 1 and 2 are GLOB-based, so a new .sh is
covered automatically and they are silent by construction. Mechanism 3 is
ENUMERATION-based, so a new .sh is UNcovered automatically and it is the only one able to
fire. "Is my new script covered?" has opposite answers depending which is asked — and the
two that answer yes are precisely the two that cannot detect anything. Any future shell
deliverable needs a checker_index entry and nothing else; the two check.sh mechanisms will
take care of themselves.

WHY IT MATTERED BEYOND ONE RED GATE: validate is a step of scripts/check.sh, so while it
was red no pane could complete the mandatory chain even once disk recovers.

title: CalibrationWindow permits invalid direct construction despite rejecting constructor
description:
## Finding

`crates/fgdb-evidence/src/lib.rs:667-683` documents `CalibrationWindow` as a closed half-open `[start_seq, end_seq)` window, and `CalibrationWindow::new` rejects `start_seq >= end_seq`. The two fields are nevertheless public at lines 670-672, so downstream code can bypass the constructor. `EvidenceEnvelope::new` at lines 777-793 accepts `Option<CalibrationWindow>` without revalidation, allowing the invalid value into the otherwise immutable envelope.

## Controlled evidence

The constructor census found the known `CalibrationWindow::new` production/example/test uses, so the probe was capable of finding the intended path. Direct source reading then established the bypass. A standalone external-crate probe compiled the actual `fgdb-evidence/src/lib.rs` against thin `fgdb_claim` and `fgdb_types` type stubs and successfully constructed `CalibrationWindow { start_seq: 9, end_seq: 2 }`. The stubs prove this module's public construction surface only; they do not prove claim-lattice or cross-crate integration behavior.

The existing `windows_reject_empty_and_inverted` test at lines 1417-1429 exercises only `CalibrationWindow::new`, so it cannot detect direct literal construction.

## Required closure

Make invalid windows unrepresentable or revalidate them at every accepting boundary. Prefer private fields plus read-only accessors, retain the fallible constructor as the sole admission path, add a `compile_fail` doctest for direct construction and a compiling constructor companion, and add an envelope regression proving empty/inverted windows cannot enter `EvidenceEnvelope`.
close_reason: Private bounds, paired doctests, and envelope regression landed in 4cee0b9 with scoped gates green

title: Prevent deterministic capsule dedup from overwriting immutable objects
description: W2 Chronicle reliability defect found during fresh-eyes review of fgdb-w2-commit-protocol-9w3u. Deterministic sealing maps identical plaintext under fixed keys to the same capsule ObjectId, but CommitCoordinator::commit_with_crash currently opens capsules/<oid>.capsule with create(true)+truncate(true). A retry or later commit of identical bytes can therefore truncate and rewrite an already-durable immutable capsule referenced by an earlier marker; any short write, I/O failure, or crash can corrupt previously committed history. Fix only this publication law: create a new capsule path without replacement; when the path already exists, compare its full encoded container to the deterministic candidate, refuse a mismatch with a typed error while preserving the file and pre-write coordinator state, and D1-sync an identical existing file before appending a marker. Acceptance: a sentinel at the exact target path is preserved and produces the typed conflict with no marker; committing identical plaintext twice reuses one capsule and leaves two restart-verifiable markers; focused Chronicle tests/clippy/fmt/UBS pass; repository scripts/check.sh is exit-code green or any environmental UNRUN is recorded without upgrading it. Parent-directory fsync, writer lease/takeover, and the broader nine-state protocol remain outside this bug.
close_reason: Fixed and repository-gated

title: Catalog targets CommitCapsule, a name absent from the plan, where the source says CommittedEffectCapsule
description:
## What & scope
`a11:field:commit-marker-capsule-ref` targets `CommitCapsule`, a name that appears **zero times** in the normative plan, while the source spells that member `capsule_ref:StrongRef<CommittedEffectCapsule>`. Repair the catalog so the a11 reference resolves to the symbol the source names. This is a CROSS-SLICE catalog correction, not a source erratum and not an a11-only edit, which is why it is filed rather than landed by pane4.

## THIS IS NOT A SOURCE ERRATUM — measured, and that distinction is the point
Unlike fgdb-normative-predecessor-ref-erratum-j00a (where two catalog laws are jointly unsatisfiable for any spelling the source uses) and unlike the u3gr result, here **the source is correct and the catalog is wrong**:
- `CommittedEffectCapsule`: 7 plan occurrences, 3 of them `StrongRef<CommittedEffectCapsule>` (plan:393, plan:1912, plan:1944), and the plan gives it a full structural body — `CommittedEffectCapsule { authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>, read_snapshot_basis, validated_appl... }`. It is a10-owned: reservation 0x0274 `reserved`, candidate `source_kind = "confirmed"` / `identity_class = "unclassified"`, disposition `appendix-structural-definition`, source a10:1910.
- `CommitCapsule`: **zero plan occurrences.** It is a g0 scaffold row (`g0:logical-kind:commit-capsule`, object_kind 0x000a, status ACTIVE) with **no top-level candidate and no `top|CommitCapsule` target at all** — i.e. nothing source-derived produced that name. It carries 4 member field rows of its own and is referenced by 2 field rows.

So no plan edit is needed and no owner ruling on the source text is required. Do NOT add this to the P0 source-ruling set.

## The repair measured CLEAN — zero structural violations
Staged out-of-tree on a `git archive HEAD` copy, verified with standalone rustc:
1. **Retarget alone FAILS**, as expected: changing `a11:field:commit-marker-capsule-ref` to `target_schema_id = "CommittedEffectCapsule"` with nothing else gives exactly one structural violation, `projection_ref_target_unresolved` — "target CommittedEffectCapsule resolves nowhere".
2. **Retarget + mint the source-named kind at a10's reservation SUCCEEDS**: mint `CommittedEffectCapsule` at its EXISTING reservation 0x0274 (disposition `reserved` -> `existing`, reservation-first), add the `top|CommittedEffectCapsule` logical-kind target, flip the candidate `unclassified` -> `logical`, then retarget the a11 field. Result: **only pin drift, zero structural faults** — no `ref_target_unresolved`, no `dag_*`, no class mismatch, no reservation collision, and no orphan (the g0 `CommitCapsule` row keeps its other consumer, so nothing is stranded).

Worth recording because it is counter-intuitive: retargeting an **active** row's `target_schema_id` does NOT trip the append-only law. That pin covers released "codes, tags, names, lifecycle states, and union arms"; a target change surfaces only as ordinary durable_fields assignment-pin drift and re-freezes normally. So this repair does not need the A10-CommandRef-style reviewed rename with a historical witness pin — that precedent applies to renaming a released NAME, which this does not do.

## Why pane4 filed instead of landing
Two reasons, both scope rather than feasibility:
1. The prerequisite mint is an **a10-owned** row (`slice_id = "a10"`, reservation/candidate/disposition all a10). Landing another slice's owner row silently is exactly the cross-pane collision the catalog token exists to prevent; the a10 owner should mint it, or explicitly delegate.
2. `construction_order` for `CommittedEffectCapsule` still needs deriving from BOTH reference directions. Partial measurement: the inbound consumer `CommitMarker.capsule_ref` puts an UPPER bound of 15 (CommitMarker's order), and the outbound lower bound from its own body was not completed. Order 10 satisfied the DAG law in the trial, but "no violation" is not the same as "derived", and a durable order should not be guessed.

## Acceptance criteria
- `CommittedEffectCapsule` is minted at 0x0274 with disposition flipped to `existing`, its candidate flipped to `logical`, and a construction_order derived from both reference directions with the derivation stated.
- `a11:field:commit-marker-capsule-ref` targets `CommittedEffectCapsule`; no field row in any slice targets a symbol absent from the plan.
- Whether the g0 `CommitCapsule` row is a scaffold duplicate of the same object, or a genuinely distinct object that merely needs a source-derived name, is decided explicitly by the g0/a10 owner and recorded.
- Gates: loader LOAD_OK, identity/lib/satisfiability/spine/claims green, registry-check all exit 0, appendix-regenerate zero violations.

## Provenance
Found while landing a11's union layer: `CommitMarker.effect_source` cannot register its Local arm's interior until this resolves, so it blocks the last unblocked a11 union. Discovered and measured by pane4-a11; full trail on fgdb-a11-delivery-markers-sdh6.

Two of the three open items are now settled by measurement; the third is a genuine ruling and I have

=== SETTLED BY MEASUREMENT 1: CommitCapsule and CommittedEffectCapsule are DISTINCT OBJECTS ===

=== THE FORK, COSTED. I am not choosing this one. ===
BRANCH A — mint at order <= 15 and retarget now.
  Cost to land: 1 logical kind at reservation 0x0274 (disposition reserved -> existing), 1 target,
  1 candidate class flip, 1 field retarget, plus the usual pin re-freeze. About ten minutes. Green
  today; unblocks a11's last union immediately.
  DEBT: a10 can then NEVER land CommittedEffectCapsule.authorization_decision_ref, because that row

BRANCH B — file it as an ordering erratum alongside fgdb-tuw1 and do not mint yet.
  Cost: a11's union layer stays blocked on its last union (the bead's own provenance note).
  Fix requires moving ONE of: CommitMarker's construction_order (15), AuthorizationDecisionRecord's

  tuw1 exists as a bead.

BRANCH C — leave a11 targeting CommitCapsule.
  Cost: a durable field row permanently asserts that the capsule is a 1-member g0 scaffold object

title: Recover the ENOSPC-torn catalog token without unsafe lease stealing
description: During fgdb-5ekk, scripts/token.sh acquire catalog PurpleSwan-5ekk 15 hit printf: write error: No space left on device after beginning its lease write. After shared cargo cleanup restored 324 GiB free, scripts/token.sh status catalog still reports HELD by ? with no holder PID and an indeterminate age, while build-1 and build-2 correctly report no tokens held. This is a torn lease, not evidence that no catalog writer exists. Do not steal, overwrite, remove, or edit the lock based only on this state. Completion requires (1) identify or obtain explicit coordinator confirmation that no catalog lane is active; (2) repair through the approved lease path; (3) prove acquire, status, and release work after recovery; (4) make token-file publication ENOSPC-safe or record why it already is; and (5) run the relevant shell checks. Provenance: fgdb-jagf capacity incident and fgdb-5ekk catalog validation.
close_reason: All five completion items verified met (successor-pane verify-or-close). (1)+(2) coordinator-confirmed and repaired through the approved path: PeachTiger reissued authorization, CreamStone executed token.sh steal under voucher 2026-08-04 (mail 22369; durable record = A20 bead comment 1172). (3) proven twice: JadeSnow scratch round-trip at 8df16a7, and a live-token round-trip today 2026-08-05 ~23:49Z (acquire catalog -> HELD pid-alive -> release -> no tokens held). (4) ENOSPC-safe publication landed at 8df16a7 (write_meta temp+5-line-verify+atomic mv, lock rollback on failure, TORN named state refused by acquire); /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/token.sh is a forwarder exec'ing the tracked scripts/token.sh, so the fix is live at the incident path. (5) bash -n + shellcheck --severity=warning rc=0 at 8df16a7. Residue: promoting scratch pub_rollback_test.sh to a tracked gate remains unfiled follow-up.

comments.author: JadeSnow
comments.text:
ITEMS 3/4/5 DONE at 8df16a7. Items 1/2 deliberately NOT done -- they need you, not me.

ROOT CAUSE, measured with a control rather than inferred. The tear is two defects:
 (a) acquire discarded write_meta exit status. mkdir takes the lock atomically, then printf >"$meta"
     CREATES the file and fails mid-write on a full filesystem. So acquire printed ACQUIRED and
     exited 0 with a zero-byte holder. Confirmed on disk: catalog.lock/holder is 0 bytes, against
     build-1.lock/holder at 45 bytes (three lines: name/epoch/ttl) as the healthy control.
 (b) hold_line derives age from ${M_EPOCH:-0}, so an empty epoch dates the hold to 1970. That is the
     "29764144m" -- fifty-six years, printed with the same confidence as a real answer and
     indistinguishable at a glance from a legacy three-line hold a human may legitimately vouch for.

ITEM 4 (ENOSPC-safe publication) DONE. write_meta now writes a temp file in the same directory,
verifies BOTH exit status and the exact 5-line count, then mv-renames it into place (same
filesystem, so atomic). The line count is not redundant: a short write can succeed per-call and
still truncate. On failure the lock is rolled back, so "acquire failed" and "no lease exists" are
the same observable state -- which is exactly the property that lets a later acquire proceed
WITHOUT anyone stealing a lease. acquire now reports FAILED and exits 1 instead of ACQUIRED.

ITEM 3 (prove acquire/status/release) DONE: round-trip green on a scratch FGDB_TOKEN_DIR
(ACQUIRED rc=0 -> status HELD ... pid alive -> RELEASED rc=0 -> "no tokens held").

ITEM 5 (shell checks) DONE: bash -n rc=0, shellcheck --severity=warning rc=0 -- the two gates
check.sh runs over tracked shell. I did not run full check.sh: the cache is cold post-outage and
the standing directive forbids new full-workspace runs. No new file was added, so file-coverage
closure is unaffected.

NEW: TORN is now a named state. A hold missing who/epoch/ttl reports TORN in status and is REFUSED
by acquire (exit 1) rather than being treated as reapable -- there is no pid to run the liveness
test on. Differential against a reproduced tear (lock dir + zero-byte holder):
  old: "catalog: HELD by ? for 29764147m (ttl ?m); liveness indeterminate"
  new: "catalog: TORN -- ... no age or liveness can be derived"
The old figure ticks with wall-clock and matched this bead reported 29764144m three minutes later,
so the reproduction is the real defect, not a lookalike. Acquire against the torn lock exits 1 and
leaves it intact -- nothing stolen. Live `token.sh status` now names the real catalog token
correctly while still reporting build-1 with its DEAD-holder verdict unchanged (no regression).

ROLLBACK HARNESS at scratchpad/pub_rollback_test.sh: it sed-extracts the REAL function bodies from
the script under test so it cannot drift from what ships, drives them against an unwritable lock
dir (same failure class as ENOSPC), and carries its own control -- the same helper on a WRITABLE
lock must publish a complete 5-line holder, so it cannot pass for a helper that only ever fails.
New code PASSES; old code fails on "the lock survived a failed publication". It is a reproduction,
not yet a tracked gate -- promoting it to one is worth a follow-up.

ITEMS 1 AND 2 REMAIN, AND THEY ARE YOURS. The live /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/tokens/catalog.lock is
UNTOUCHED. I did not remove, edit, overwrite, or steal it, per this bead own instruction and RULE 1.
Recovery needs (1) explicit coordinator confirmation that no catalog lane is active -- the bead
provenance says the torn acquire was PurpleSwan-5ekk at 06:12:48Z, so PurpleSwan is the one to
confirm -- and then (2) repair through the approved lease path. Note the repair is now cheap and
safe: with this commit, releasing the torn lock and re-acquiring produces a complete holder record
or no lock at all. Say the word and I will run it.

comments.author: JadeSnow
comments.text:
ITEM 2 (approved repair path) IDENTIFIED AND PROVEN ON A FIXTURE, 2026-08-04. The path is `token.sh steal`, and the script own doctrine names this exact case:

  "`steal` refuses a hold whose recorded process is alive, and remains THE MANUAL PATH FOR HOLDS
   WITH NO PID RECORDED (legacy or bare holds), WHERE A HUMAN VOUCHES THE HOLDER IS GONE and
   announces the steal in a bead comment."

A torn hold has no pid, so verdict falls to indeterminate and steal clears it. There is deliberately
no `force` (removed in fgdb-5j16 as an undocumented ceremony bypass), so steal is the ONLY sanctioned
route -- an `rm -rf` of the lock dir is not an alternative, it is the thing the ceremony exists to
prevent.

VERIFIED END-TO-END on a reproduced tear (scratch FGDB_TOKEN_DIR, lock dir + zero-byte holder), which
also confirms my own 8df16a7 did not break the repair path:
  status  -> TORN
  acquire -> REFUSED rc=1, lock left intact (nothing stolen)
  steal   -> "STOLEN catalog from ? ... you vouched the holder is gone" rc=0
  status  -> HELD by JadeSnow-faxs for 0m (ttl 45m); holder pid alive
  release -> RELEASED
So acquire refuses while steal repairs -- which is the correct split, and worth stating because I
added the TORN refusal to acquire and NOT to steal, deliberately.

ITEM 1 EVIDENCE (the "identify" branch of the requirement), measured at HEAD fd3eb39:
  - ZERO active file reservations on registries/**, tools/registry-check/**, or g0_identity_e2e.sh
    (checked the live reservation archive, filtering released).
  - Last commit touching those paths was ~2 hours before this note (fd3eb39 / 6c250f5, both the a20
    lane). Nothing since.
  - The catalog token has been UNUSABLE since 06:12:48Z, so no agent can have legitimately acquired
    it in the intervening ~9.5 hours; any catalog work in that window necessarily proceeded WITHOUT
    the token. That is itself worth noting: serialization has been absent, not merely stuck.
  - The torn acquire was PurpleSwan-5ekk per this bead provenance.

WHAT I AM NOT DOING. I am not self-vouching. The tool demands a human vouch by design, and clearing
a lock another agent created is a deletion under RULE 1. The exact command, stated verbatim so it can
be authorized or run directly:

    bash scripts/token.sh steal catalog <your-agent-name>

Affected: /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/tokens/catalog.lock (its zero-byte holder file and the directory),
replaced immediately by a complete 5-line hold for the named agent. Nothing else is touched, and
post-8df16a7 a failed re-publication rolls back rather than leaving a second tear.

title: Same-batch deletes of both endpoints assign the cascade once
description:
Deleting both endpoints of an edge in one WriteBatch can put that eid in two DeleteVertex cascades. NENF emits vertices in VId order, not evaluation order. The second apply then sees CascadeImageMismatch (declared contains an edge the first delete already retired) or an undercount if the first-applied vertex was not the one that claimed it.

## Background
17ht made the fold require declared == live incident. That is correct. Write-path cascade derivation still follows evaluation order: the first delete_vertex claims every remaining incident eid, including those a later delete_vertex also touches. NENF then sorts by VId. If the larger VId was deleted first in the batch, the smaller VId is applied first with an empty (or incomplete) cascade while the edge is still live.

Related to 17ht. Not parent-child to open `819`. Do not close `819`.

## Technical Approach
After building evaluation-order rows, rewrite DeleteVertex cascades: an incident eid is kept only on the smallest same-batch-deleted endpoint (src/dst from the prefix overlay or the fold's live map). Single-endpoint deletes are unchanged (that vid is the only owner), so the 17ht DeleteEdge-then-DeleteVertex case still carries the eid.

## Success Criteria
- One batch that deletes both endpoints (either order) commits; both vertices and the edge are gone.
- delete_edge then delete_vertex of one endpoint still commits (17ht).
- spine + spine_differential + block_writer stay green.
- `819` stays open.

## Test Plan
Spine: seed 1-2 edge, delete 2 then 1 in one batch; also 1 then 2. Existing checkpoint / if-present tests stay green.
close_reason: Same-batch dual-endpoint deletes assign each cascade eid to the smallest deleted endpoint so NENF VId order matches the fold incident-set check. Both delete orders commit; 17ht delete_edge+delete_vertex unchanged. spine 42/42, spine_differential 16/16. 819 stays open.

title: census_appendix_source merges two closed unions defined in one sentence, silently
description:
`appendix_source::census_appendix_source` attributes the arms of a SECOND closed
union to the FIRST when both are defined in one source sentence, and reports the
result as clean.

## The witness (a21:2651)

    `SubscriptionClosePrecondition` has exactly the stable `u16` tags
    `0x0001 NoOutstanding{...}|0x0002 Outstanding{...}`, and
    `CapabilityMigrationRetrySelector` exactly
    `0x0001 Initial|0x0002 ExactLiveSuccessorRetry{entry_digest}`;
    every other nested tag is reserved-invalid.

Two distinct top-level unions. What the census produces:

    owner="SubscriptionClosePrecondition" path="SubscriptionClosePrecondition"
    arms=["0x0001 Initial", "0x0001 NoOutstanding",
          "0x0002 ExactLiveSuccessorRetry", "0x0002 Outstanding"]
    unparsed_arm_count=0   arm_set_conflict=false

    CapabilityMigrationRetrySelector: 0 census unions

Both of the census's own health signals are GREEN on a four-arm set that belongs
to two different objects, and the second union vanishes entirely.

## Why this is severe, not cosmetic

The catalog's exactness laws take the census as ground truth. A landed union is
checked against the census owner/path/arm-set (`source_union_contract_mismatch`,
`source_union_arm_set_mismatch`) and each arm against the census payload digest
(`source_union_arm_contract_mismatch`). All three compare the projection to the
SAME wrong census record, so all three PASS on the merged arm set. The only law
that fires here is `ordinary_union_arm_duplicate_tag`, and only by luck: these
two unions happen to reuse 0x0001/0x0002. **Had the two unions used disjoint
tags, a four-arm union with two foreign arms would have landed clean, frozen
into the append-only durable_fields assignment pin.**

Consequences today: `SubscriptionClosePrecondition` cannot be landed correctly
(its correct two-arm shape is not what the checker will accept), and
`CapabilityMigrationRetrySelector` is structurally unlandable as an ordinary
union because no census union exists for it at all.

## Reproduce, lock-free, ~8s

Build the checker from a `git archive HEAD` snapshot and call
`appendix_source::census_appendix_source(source, manifest.start_line, specs)`;
filter `census.unions` on `schema_owner`. Probe preserved at
/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/p4/genchk2.rs (rebuild it; the tmpdir is pruned).
Control the run on the full Appendix sha256 and on a fabricated-absent symbol.

## Suggested shape of the fix

The arm scanner appears to keep consuming `|`-separated arms across a `` , and
`OtherName` exactly `` clause instead of terminating the first union's arm list
at the sentence's second definitional head. A second union head inside one
sentence must start a new UnionCandidate. A metamorphic relation states it
directly: splitting a sentence at `, and \`X\` exactly ` into two sentences must
not change the census union/arm transcript.

Owner: pane2 holds the tools/registry-check metamorphic suite; filed, not fixed,
to stay off that lane. Found by pane4 landing fgdb-a21-residue-union-shapes-afpl.
close_reason: Landed d2866ff: the one shared source reader now partitions all four same-sentence pairs into 8 unions/19 arms; split/join and erased-head controls discriminate, with exact locked focused gates green and whole-gate environmental reds recorded in the closeout.

title: Census truncates member-position slash tokens: one candidate whose name is a prefix and whose exact type begins with '/'
description:
The structural source census, asked for the member at a10:1920 source position 11,
returns ONE candidate:

    name  = required_prepared
    exact = ["/certificate/remote/key/audit/backup_obligation_floor"]
    ambig = true

It splits the slash-compressed token at the FIRST slash and makes the remainder the
"exact type" -- a string beginning with '/', which is not a type at all. The source
spells six members; the census emits one, whose name is a PREFIX and whose type is a
SLASH.

=== REPRODUCTION (measured 2026-07-27, HEAD d747cb8) ===

With the six correct rows written into registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml and all
four projection pins re-derived, `registry-check appendix --root .` emits EXACTLY six
violations, one per member, and nothing else:

  source_target_key_missing: target source_key
    "field|ConfigurationTransitionSpec|ConfigurationTransitionSpec.
     required_<D>_obligation_floor|required_<D>_obligation_floor"
    is absent from the structural source census

for D in prepared, certificate, remote, key, audit, backup.

So the census is the ONLY thing standing between the correct rows and a green
landing. Every other proposition on fgdb-hvfn is closed.

=== THE GATE IS SOUND; DO NOT WEAKEN IT ===

source_target_key_missing fails CLOSED and is doing exactly its job: it refuses a
[[target]] row whose source_key the census cannot produce. This bead is not a request
to relax that check. The census is the defect.

=== WHY MECHANICAL EXPANSION IS FORBIDDEN ===

Denominator, measured: 2,347 brace-balanced schema bodies, 15,679 top-level members,
13 distinct member-position slash tokens -- of which one (role/posture/
feature_predicate, plan line 292) is not a schema member at all but the plan
describing durable_fields.toml's OWN column set. True denominator 12.

The expansion rule is NOT uniform across those 12:

  shared suffix, 6 members  required_prepared/certificate/remote/key/audit/
                            backup_obligation_floor
  shared suffix, 2 members  incoming/outgoing_edges
  two independent names     labels/types, lease/status, schema/tag
  genuinely ambiguous       os/kernel_range        -> os_range + kernel_range?
                                                      or os + kernel_range?
                            expected_branch/key/allocation_epochs
                            base/current_closure_inventory
                            forbidden_layers/options
                            key_envelope/grant_registry_root
                            exact_grid/ceiling_carry_proof_ref
                            through_shard_index/global_prefix

An expander that guesses commits, at 12 sites, exactly the category of error
fgdb-hvfn exists to remove -- inventing structure the source does not state. That is
very likely WHY the census truncates rather than expanding: truncation is a visible
wrong answer, and guessing is an invisible one.

=== THE MECHANISM THAT ALREADY EXISTS ===

AMBIGUITY_ADJUDICATION_CONTRACT (tools/registry-check/src/appendix_a.rs:350) carries
450 pins, 390 of them field-type-ambiguous. A PER-TOKEN adjudication licenses one
expansion without inventing a general rule. It is the same table fgdb-ty4g is moving
450 -> 455, so the two beads share a mechanism.

=== MINIMUM VIABLE FIX, INDEPENDENT OF ADJUDICATION ===

Make the census REFUSE a member-position slash token, with its own violation code,
failing CLOSED -- instead of emitting a member whose name is a prefix and whose exact
type begins with '/'. That converts a silent wrong answer into a loud one and

title: a10: SequenceNeutralSpec is reserved with 0 arms and none of its 13 named inputs has a schema — the real block under 5uw2/d2ax
description:
## CORRECTED. I filed this bead 30 minutes ago with "0 outer role-command unions
## exist". That claim was mine, it was name-based, and it is FALSE.

Re-derived at HEAD 650c37d under a held catalog lease. The earlier number came
from searching union NAMES for `Command|Transition|LifecycleOperation|Maintenance`
-- inferring absence from spelling, which is the same move plan 5.1 forbids when
it says "a suffix conveys no semantics". The outer command types are not spelled
with "Command" in the place I looked.

## What is actually in the catalog for a10

  logical_kind rows, slice_id = "a10"  (6)
     CommitCommand              ACTIVE
     ControlCommand             ACTIVE
     LogicalCommandRecord       ACTIVE
     PreparedCommitRecord       ACTIVE
     CommittedEffectCapsule     reserved
     SequenceNeutralSpec        RESERVED
  union rows (1)     ExpectedStateCondition, version_status "reserved", 4 arms,
                     allowed_containing_schemas ["ControlCommand","KeyDestroyProposal"]
  plus              wire_type 5, field 17, reference_union 1 (+2 arms),
                    reservation 14, top_level_candidate 18, target 36,
                    source_symbol_disposition 14, ambiguity_adjudication 1

So four outer command schemas are ACTIVE. a10 is partially landed, not untouched.

## The real blocker, in one line

The outer union the 5.1 bijection quantifies over is `SequenceNeutralSpec`, it is
`status = "reserved"`, and it has ZERO union_arm rows. `GlobalSequenceNeutralSpec`
is likewise a reserved logical_kind with no arms.

Plan line ~1915 (a10's own source) names the required arms outright:

  "Required Local semantic rows include TxnOwnershipTransitionSpec<Local>,
   TxnOwnershipExpiryAbortSpec<Local>, every AllocationReservationTransitionSpec
   <Local> and FinalizationAllocationDispositionSpec<Local>, FormatTransitionSpec
   <Local>, EscrowRightsTransitionSpec, PrivacyContinuityImportSpec<Local>, the
   exact 12.7 DP semantic transitions, AuditTerminalPlanAbandonSpec<Local>,
   BulkLoadTransitionSpec<Local>, DerivedBuildTransitionSpec<Local>, and every
   exact semantic backup/restore/GC/key transition. Required Local maintenance
   rows separately include AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec<Local>,
   ResultResumeTransitionSpec<Local>, ..."

MEASURED, of those 13 named inputs, landed `logical_kind` rows: ZERO.

  TxnOwnershipTransitionSpec              0   no row of any kind
  TxnOwnershipExpiryAbortSpec             0   no row of any kind
  AllocationReservationTransitionSpec     0   no row of any kind
  FinalizationAllocationDispositionSpec   0   no row of any kind
  FormatTransitionSpec                    0   no row of any kind
  EscrowRightsTransitionSpec              0   no row of any kind
  BulkLoadTransitionSpec                  0   no row of any kind
  DerivedBuildTransitionSpec              0   no row of any kind
  PrivacyContinuityImportSpec             0   reservation 1, disposition 1
  AuditTerminalPlanAbandonSpec            0   top_level_candidate 1, wire_type 1
  AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec              0   reservation 1, disposition 1, candidate 1
  ResultResumeTransitionSpec              0   target 1, candidate 1, wire_type 1
  ConfigurationTransitionSpec             0   top_level_candidate 3

Eight of thirteen have no row at all; five exist only as candidates or
reservations. A `command_contracts.toml` row requires `input_schema_id`,
`body_schema_id`, `result_schema_id` and `applied_record_schema_id` to resolve to
REGISTERED schemas. None of these can be named today without inventing a referent.

## Also corrected: which direction the generation runs

fgdb-5uw2's note (mine) said command_contracts.toml "sits on the generated side"
of appendix_a_catalog.toml and must not be hand-authored. That reading was wrong.
Plan line 294 calls it "one further NORMATIVE REGISTRY", and the clause I leaned
on -- "hand-written lists IN THIS DOCUMENT are generated readability projections"
-- scopes to lists in the PLAN, not to the registry. a10 states the direction
explicitly:

  "The local SequenceNeutralSpec semantic union is generated from
   command_contracts.toml; it is exhaustive and has no hand-maintained allowlist."

So command_contracts.toml is an AUTHORED normative input and the SequenceNeutralSpec
union is its projection. 5uw2's verb "materialize" was right; my reason for
declining was wrong. The correct reason to decline is the one above: its referents
do not exist yet.

## What closing this bead requires

a10 must land, in this order, and each step is a real slice increment:
  1. the 13+ `*Spec` command-input schemas as logical kinds with fields
     (a10 declares field_candidate_count 180 and only 17 are landed)
  2. the `SequenceNeutralSpec` / `GlobalSequenceNeutralSpec` union rows moved off
     `reserved`, with one union_arm per concrete inner tag
     (a10 declares union_candidate_count 5 / arm_candidate_count 17; landed 1 / 4)
  3. the 110 declared ambiguity adjudications (1 landed)
Only then can command_contracts.toml name a real input/body/result/applied triple.

## Construction law for step 2, so it is not re-derived

A top-level wire-backed union's `allowed_containing_schemas` must name its
CONSUMER, not itself; the 69/69 self-only precedent strands its own anchor field
and "*" is banned. a10's one landed union already does this correctly --
`ExpectedStateCondition` names ["ControlCommand","KeyDestroyProposal"] -- so
`SequenceNeutralSpec` should name the command records that carry it. A generic
whole-schema union is always logical-backed and needs no variant rows; a
wire-backed one does.

Measured by pane2 under a held catalog lease. No build used -- greps and Python
reads over checked-in TOML and the plan. Nothing edited, nothing deleted.

title: checker_index status=live is proved by Path::is_file() alone: a registered live checker that no gate ever runs is indistinguishable from one that runs every commit
description:
FINDING — mock/placeholder sweep (pane4, 2026-07-26). Ranked #2, and it is the
ROOT CAUSE that makes the check.sh gap invisible.

## What it claims

AGENTS.md, "Spec-First Workflow" item 2: "**CI cross-checks that every ID has a
live checker.**" And the hard rule immediately below it: "**no subsystem ships
against an unenforced invariant.** A workstream exit gate (G1-G4, §19) cannot
pass while any invariant it depends on lacks a live checker in
`invariants.toml`. Promote a design assumption to enforced only after the
checker exists."

`registries/checker_index.toml`'s own header repeats it: rows may be
stub-registered pre-Genesis, "but the symbol must still be a registered,
reviewable row, and a \"live\" row's artifact must exist in-repo."

## What it actually does

`tools/registry-check/src/appendix_a.rs:6231`:

```rust
fn live_checker_artifact_exists(repo_root: &Path, checker: &model::Checker) -> bool {
    safe_repository_relative(&checker.artifact) && repo_root.join(&checker.artifact).is_file()
}
```

`status = "live"` is proved by `Path::is_file()`. Two consequences:

1. **Nothing binds a live checker to any gate that runs it.** A checker can be
   registered live, be cited by a clause as its enforcement mechanism, and be
   invoked by no wrapper, no CI step, and no test — and every registry gate
   stays green. This is not hypothetical: four live script rows and two live
   binary rows are in exactly that state right now (companion bead
   fgdb-gate-coverage-checksh-omits-live-gates-u7mw).

2. **The symbol->artifact binding is unverified at symbol granularity.** For
   `kind = "cargo-test"` rows the `symbol` is a test function name
   (`claims_neg_missing_checker`, `spine_neg_twenty_first_id`, ...), but nothing
   greps the artifact for it. Rename or delete
   `tests/claims.rs::claims_neg_waiver_present` and its row stays `status =
   "live"` and every gate stays green, because `tests/claims.rs` still exists.
   Verified by sweep: all `kind="cargo-test"` symbols DO currently resolve to
   real functions — by author discipline, not by enforcement. (The 11 live rows
   whose symbol is absent from its artifact are all scheme-prefixed or
   law-name symbols — `architecture_source_coverage`, `cargo-test:claims`,
   `topology_registry_source` — i.e. logical names, not code symbols. Those are
   fine; the point is that nothing distinguishes them from a rotted one.)

The `status = "stub"` rows are honest and should stay: 40 of them point at
files under `crates/fgdb-oracles/`, `crates/fgdb-reference/`, etc. that do not
exist yet, which is exactly what pre-Genesis stub registration is for. All 20
invariants in `invariants.toml` are `status = "stub"`. That part of the system
is telling the truth.

## Which gate catches this today

None. This IS the gate.

## Why it matters now

Nine planned subsystems exist only as plan text and every gate is green. The
only thing standing between "green" and "green because nothing ran" is this
predicate, and it currently answers a weaker question than the doctrine asks.

## Fix

Strengthen the live-checker proof from "the file exists" toward "the checker is
reachable from an executing gate":

1. Add a `runner` field (or equivalent) to each live row naming the gate that
   invokes it, and a law asserting that runner actually references the artifact
   — with `scripts/check.sh` parsed as the canonical runner manifest. Best form
   is to invert it: have `check.sh` derive its step list FROM `checker_index.toml`,
   which makes the law self-enforcing rather than a second list to keep in sync.
2. For `kind = "cargo-test"` rows, assert the symbol appears in the artifact
   (a `fn <symbol>` grep is enough to catch rename/delete rot).
3. Keep the existence check — it is necessary, just not sufficient.

title: appendix_a.rs holds 30% of its own subject's prose: every existence query resolves against a copy
description:
tools/registry-check/src/appendix_a.rs contains 302,724 characters of its own
subject's prose -- 30.3% of the file -- copied verbatim from
registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml.

  rationale             455 string literals   163,477 chars   16.4% of the file
  ambiguity_source_key  450 string literals   139,247 chars   14.0% of the file
                                              -------
                                              302,724         30.3%
  file total                                  997,854

Consequence: ANY QUERY OF THE FORM "does this rule/law/concept exist in the checker"
RESOLVES AGAINST A COPY OF THE THING BEING AUDITED. The checker cannot distinguish
"this rule is defined here" from "I am holding a copy of the sentence that cites it".

=== REPRODUCTION ===

Strip the mirrored literals and re-ask:

  python3: re.sub(r'(rationale|ambiguity_source_key):\s*"(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*"', '<M>', src)
  997,854 chars -> 702,224 chars

  law name              before strip   after strip
  flattened-rendering     RESOLVES          0
  compact-phrase          RESOLVES          0
  SequenceNeutralSpec     RESOLVES          0

=== I FELL INTO THIS ON THE FIRST PASS, AND THAT IS THE EVIDENCE ===

Working fgdb-law-citation-sweep-uzzh I ran the obvious test -- "is this cited law
mentioned in the plan or the checker" -- and it returned RESOLVES for three of the
eleven cited laws. All three were false. Their only appearances in the checker were
inside the mirrored catalog prose: the checker was agreeing with the citation because
it was holding a copy of the citation.

I caught it only because the RESOLVES verdicts were implausible against a corpus I
had already measured as having no law registry. An auditor without that prior would
have shipped "3 of 11 laws are real" and the sweep would have licensed the phantoms.
That 0-of-94 result should be trusted BECAUSE the first pass failed this way and the
failure was found, not because the first pass was clean.

=== SEVERITY, SCOPED HONESTLY ===

NOT LIVE IN A SHIPPED VALIDATOR. No gate does a textual existence query over checker
source: scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh contains no grep/rg/awk over
tools/registry-check/src, and the 450 pins are compared STRUCTURALLY, field by field,
by ambiguity_adjudication_contract_matches_with. That function is sound, and
`row.rationale == pin.rationale` makes the mirror load-bearing on purpose: the catalog
cannot silently rewrite the justification for an adjudication without a reviewed
checker edit. THE PIN MECHANISM IS NOT THE DEFECT AND MUST NOT BE REMOVED.

IMMINENT. The law-citation sweep this project just ruled to build (uzzh step 3) is
specified to resolve citations against the checker. Implemented the obvious way it
would pass on 100% of the citations it exists to catch -- including all 94.

DEMONSTRATED. Three false RESOLVES, above, by a careful reader.

=== THE PROJECT ALREADY HAS THE ANTIBODY, ONE FILE OVER ===

tools/registry-check/src/unsafe_ledger.rs:2519, inside #[cfg(test)]:

    /// The fixture must never be visible as real sites in this file. If this
    /// fails, the checker will fail its own crate -- and worse, a reader would
    /// see two "unsafe sites" in a std-only tooling crate that has none.
    fn fixture_is_not_visible_in_this_source() {
        let own_source = include_str!("unsafe_ledger.rs");
        assert_eq!(scan_sites("unsafe_ledger.rs", own_source), Vec::new(), ...);
    }

Somebody already recognised this exact class -- subject-like text embedded in the
checker corrupting the checker's own reading -- and guarded it for a fixture of a few
lines. appendix_a.rs carries 302,724 characters of subject prose with no equivalent
guard. The precedent is the argument: this is a known hazard in this codebase, left
unguarded at 30,000x the size.

=== PROPOSED INSTRUMENT (designed, not implemented) ===

1. SEPARATE THE MIRROR STRUCTURALLY. Move the 450 pins into their own module, e.g.
   appendix_a_adjudication_pins.rs. Then "the checker" and "the copy of the catalog"
   are different files, and a grep of the checker stops hitting the mirror by default.
   Cheapest change, largest share of the benefit, no behaviour change: the pins are
   still compiled, still compared structurally, still load-bearing.

2. A CANARY IN THE unsafe_ledger STYLE. Assert that a sentinel phrase occurring ONLY
   in catalog prose is not resolvable as a DEFINITION in checker source. Mutation-
   prove both directions: the canary must fire when the sentinel is present in a
   non-mirror region and stay silent when it is only in the mirror.

3. COMPLETENESS GUARD, FAILING CLOSED. Any resolution query over checker source must
   declare which regions it excludes and fail if it encounters a region it cannot
   classify as mirror-or-source. An unclassifiable region is exactly where a
   fabrication hides.

=== WHAT THIS BEAD IS NOT ===

Not a request to delete the mirror, shrink the pins, or relax
ambiguity_adjudication_contract_matches_with. The freeze is correct. The defect is
that the mirror is indistinguishable from source to every reader and every future
query.

Filed by pane2 at owner request, 2026-07-27, HEAD 1d19f02. Nothing deleted.
notes:
MEASURED AT HEAD 57610e9 (pane4). Numbers re-derived, not inherited.

=== 1. WHAT THE 296K IS: VERBATIM, 450/450, BOTH FIELDS ===
appendix_a.rs = 997,854 chars.
  rationale             455 literals  158,472 chars payload (163,477 with key prefix)  16.38%
  ambiguity_source_key  450 literals  129,347 chars payload (139,247 with key prefix)  13.95%
  MIRROR                              287,819 payload / 302,724 stripped              30.34%
Byte-identical to registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml for all 450 rows, both fields.
ZERO paraphrase. Bead's 302,724 reconciles exactly: it measured the strip incl.
the `field: ` prefix; payload alone is 28.84%.

MIRROR IS COMPLETE, NOT PARTIAL. The 4.46MB catalog holds exactly 450 `rationale =`
rows in total, all on [[ambiguity_adjudication]]. The checker pins every one. The
title understates it: the checker holds 100% OF THE CATALOG'S RATIONALE FIELD, and
that is 30% of the checker.

IT IS NOT 296K OF PROSE. Of the 129,347-char key field, 111,757 (86.4%) is
structural -- identifiers plus two 64-hex digests per key. Only 16,690 is prose,
from a closed 9-value enum. Real prose = 158,472 + 16,690 = 175,162 = 17.6%.

THE PROSE IS EVIDENCE, NOT LAW TEXT. 447/450 open with an aNN:LINE anchor.
411 distinct texts collapse to 102 skeletons under anchor/identifier masking.
ONLY 77 OF 450 ROWS (17.1%) CITE A LAW AT ALL: 82 real citations
(flattened-rendering x69, compact-phrase x12, SequenceNeutralSpec x1) plus the
one "No source law requires..." English over-match uzzh already corrected, which
this extractor independently reproduced as a control.

=== 2. WHO READS IT: EVERY CONSUMER NEEDS AN IDENTITY, NONE NEEDS THE PROSE ===
pin.rationale            -> exactly ONE reader: `==` at appendix_a.rs:11043
pin.ambiguity_source_key -> exactly ONE reader: `==` at appendix_a.rs:11031
Both inside ambiguity_adjudication_contract_matches_with. Its eight callers:
  :8200  census-coverage targeting      boolean gate -> reads row.resolved_source_keys
  :8367  complete-slice ambiguity closure boolean gate -> reads row.ambiguity_source_key
  :8476  annotation ambiguity discharge  boolean gate -> reads row.resolved_source_keys
  :11143 validate_readable_ambiguity_contract boolean gate -> violation code
  :12163 complete-slice top-level census boolean gate -> reads row.resolved_source_keys
  :11060 approved_final_ambiguity_keys_with boolean gate -> reads row.ambiguity_source_key
  :16404,:16426 tests                    boolean gate
All eight use it as a yes/no approval predicate, then read the CATALOG row's
fields -- never the pin's. NO CALL SITE ANYWHERE READS pin.rationale AS TEXT.

=== 3. CIRCULAR QUERY CLASSES: EXISTENCE IS NOT THE ONLY ONE ===
Strip the two fields, recount. FILE SCOPE (appendix_a.rs):
  registered law names      4 pop   4 PHANTOM (100%)   `shorthand` 767 hits all copy
  ambiguity reason phrases  9 pop   9 PHANTOM (100%)   388 hits for one phrase
  64-hex digests         1264 pop 766 PHANTOM (60.6%)  largest population
  plan anchors aNN:LINE    72 pop   7 PHANTOM (9.7%)   a01:1412 = 76 hits, 100% copy
  catalog `symbol` values 1599 pop   9 PHANTOM (0.6%)
  catalog `source_key`   3809 pop   0 PHANTOM          hazard assumed -> FALSIFIED
TWO NEW CIRCULAR CLASSES BEYOND EXISTENCE:
  COUNTING queries -- durable_fields.toml reads 72 vs 3 outside the mirror, 24x.
  ANCHOR-RESOLUTION queries -- a01:1412 is the anchor of FG-LAW-01 AND FG-LAW-02
    and is 100% copy, so resolving BY ANCHOR instead of by name is equally
    circular. That kills the obvious workaround.

CRATE-SCOPE CORRECTION, OWED AGAINST THE FILE-SCOPE NUMBER. Across all 20
modules only 1 of 4 registered laws is crate-wide phantom (compact-phrase).
Every non-mirror occurrence of the other three was inspected:
  flattened-rendering -> laws.rs:6, a doc comment QUOTING the problem
  shorthand           -> ordinary English ("shorthand field", "union shorthand")
  SequenceNeutralSpec -> test-corpus fixture strings in appendix_source.rs
ZERO of the four is defined, named or enforced by name anywhere in the checker.
File-scope 4/4 and crate-scope 1/4 are both true of different questions; the
crate-scope one is what supports "the checker cannot answer this at all".

=== 4. WHAT BREAKS UNDER LAW-ID + DIGEST ===
DOES NOT BREAK -- and this asymmetry is what makes the change small:
ambiguity_adjudication_contract_sha256 is computed over
&catalog.ambiguity_adjudications (:10684) -- the loaded TOML rows, NOT the pin
array. So swapping pin prose for a digest is CHECKER-ONLY: zero catalog bytes,
NO re-pin of EXPECTED_AMBIGUITY_ADJUDICATION_SHA256, no schema bump. The catalog
keeps its prose at its home. sha256(row.rationale)==pin.rationale_sha256 is
equivalent for all eight call sites. validate_ambiguity_adjudication_rows
(nonblank/non-placeholder) operates on catalog rows, untouched.

DOES BREAK -- three, one real:
(a) REVIEWER DIFF QUALITY. A catalog rationale rewrite becomes a hex diff, not a
    prose diff. The one genuine cost. Keeping source_locations, resolution and a
    new cited_laws readable preserves the DECISION; only the narrative moves.
(b) AN UNDECLARED DOCTRINE -- and a correction to pane4's own first report. The
    ":341-345 readable pins / opaque transcript digest is never authorization"
    comment does NOT govern this layer. Its subject is the four contracts
    declared immediately above it, and those four (annotation, semantic_binding,
    expansion_binding, evidence) are EXACTLY the four declared
    [[completion_layer]] rows carrying
    pin_policy = "compiled-count-sha256-readable-row-contract".
    ambiguity_adjudication IS NOT A DECLARED COMPLETION LAYER AT ALL. Its
    readability policy exists only in a function name
    (validate_readable_ambiguity_contract) and three violation strings. A
    450-row contract whose policy lives only in an identifier is a policy that
    is not pinned. FLAGGED, NOT ROUTED AROUND -- owner's call to declare or
    relax. Probably its own bead.
(c) The citation extractor must discriminate "No source law requires..." out.
    Red-prove both directions; do not allowlist the sentence.

ROW_ID ALREADY IS THE DIGEST. row_id = {slice}:ambiguity-adjudication:
sha256(ambiguity_source_key), enforced at :13036-13038, and the pin is FOUND by
row_id equality. So the 129,347-char key copy commits nothing pin.row_id does
not already commit. BUT both validators run in one validate_catalog pass and the
derivation check PUSHES rather than ABORTS, so the redundancy is a real
independent check: replace it with an explicit local
sha256(row.ambiguity_source_key) against the digest already inside pin.row_id.
Never a bare deletion.

=== REMOVAL CANDIDATES -- NAMED FOR OWNER AUTHORISATION, NOTHING REMOVED ===
1. The 450 `rationale:` literals, -158,472 chars. Replaced by rationale_sha256
   (450x64 = 28,800) + cited_laws: &[&str] (77 non-empty, ~1,200). NET -128,472.
2. The 450 `ambiguity_source_key:` literals, -129,347 chars, replaced by local
   re-derivation against the digest already in pin.row_id. NET -129,347, ZERO
   replacement bytes.
Combined -257,819: 30.3% -> ~3.0%, all four circular classes drop to zero in
appendix_a.rs, and the pin gains four registry-resolvable IDs. THE MIRROR
BECOMES UNNECESSARY, NOT SMALLER.
STAGING: (2) alone is the strictly-safer half -- pure redundancy against a law
the checker already enforces, no prose judgement, no doctrine question, and it
removes 766 of the phantom digests plus the whole 9-phrase enum. (1) is where
the readability trade-off and (b) live.

=== SAME FAMILY, ONE SCALE UP: THE SELF-DISABLING GUARD ===
Owner pairing: concurrent_bead_creation_cannot_red_another_panes_tree
(architecture_decisions.rs:950). Its control at :985 is
  assert!(write_and_validate(&corpus).is_empty(),
          "the unmodified fixture must be as green as the repo it mirrors")
-- the LIVE repo corpus. When the repo is red from a bead-provenance cause,
which is precisely the class this guard exists to catch, the control fires FIRST
and the k=1..5 growth loop and the vacuity control NEVER EXECUTE. The guard is
disabled by the condition it detects (fgdb-ft79 recorded exactly this).

THE SHARED DEFECT: a mechanism whose VERDICT or REACHABILITY is a function of
the very condition it validates is not a validator.
  23u1  VERDICT coupling by CONTAINMENT -- checker holds a copy of its subject,
        so "does the subject contain X" always agrees. It CANNOT RETURN NO.
  lzol  REACHABILITY coupling by DEPENDENCE -- guard preconditions on subject
        health, so when the subject is unhealthy it CANNOT RETURN AT ALL.

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE ACTIONABLE PART. lzol fails LOUDLY RED -- it panics on the
control, which is why it was found and cleared in one night. 23u1 fails SILENTLY
GREEN -- it reports RESOLVES, and a first law sweep shipped three false RESOLVES
until the mirror was stripped. The one that fails loudly gets fixed; the one
that fails green survives every gate. That is why 23u1 is P1 and not a cleanup.

The lzol CONTROL IS NOT THE DEFECT and must not be removed -- without it an
empty violation set could mean the fixture is not being read (same law as
license-the-zero-by-accounting). The defect is that a FAILED CONTROL IS
INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A FAILED GUARD in the report: the panic reads "the
unmodified fixture must be as green as the repo it mirrors", which an operator
parses as "concurrent bead creation reds the tree" when what happened is "this
guard never ran". UNRUN MUST NOT READ AS FAILED, AND MUST NOT READ AS PASSED --
same law as no-cargo-flag-recovers-a-compile-failure. Suggested separate bead.

=== STATE ===
Nothing edited. No file deleted. No token held (read-only measurement; catalog
is pane3-avex's). No gate run because nothing changed -- pane4 has introduced no
red, so the reported architecture 42/42 green stands unchallenged by this work.
Caveat recorded honestly: a crude corpus-side reimplementation of the bet-label
rule flags 8 records, but the real checker carries [[bead_override]] rows and
family rules, so those 8 are NOT claimed as a red -- ask the checker, not the
corpus. Awaiting explicit authorisation on removal candidates 1 and/or 2.

=== LANDED: CANDIDATE 2, COMMIT 2251f0e (owner-authorised) ===

The 450 mirrored `ambiguity_source_key` literals and the struct field they fill
are gone, replaced by a LOCAL re-derivation in
ambiguity_adjudication_contract_matches_with:

    pin.row_id == format!("{}:ambiguity-adjudication:{}",
                          row.slice_id,
                          sha256_hex(row.ambiguity_source_key.as_bytes()))

Local rather than leaning on validate_ambiguity_adjudication_rows, because that
derivation law PUSHES a violation, it does not ABORT -- a caller reaching this
function cannot assume it ran. Independence preserved, 129,347 chars of literal
payload retired.

MIRROR SHARE IS NOW A TRACKED NUMBER, NOT A ONE-TIME FINDING:
  30.40%  ->  19.18%
  303,492 ->  164,147 chars, of a file that went 998,476 -> 855,851
  removed 142,625 chars (the 450 literals plus the struct field, net of the

FOUR CIRCULAR CLASSES: TWO ZEROED, TWO SURVIVE.
  64-hex digests         1263 present -> 498;  765 mirror-only -> 0   ZEROED
  ambiguity reason phrases  9 present ->   0;    9 mirror-only -> 0   ZEROED
  registered law names      4 present ->   4;    4 mirror-only -> 4   SURVIVES
  plan anchor a01:1412      1 present ->   1;    1 mirror-only -> 1   SURVIVES

THE TWO SURVIVORS ARE EXACTLY WHAT CANDIDATE 1 IS FOR, and they are the ones
that originated this bead: the three false RESOLVES in the first law sweep were

SO THIS IS A PARTIAL CLOSE WITH THE RESIDUE MEASURED. Closing on candidate 2
