build-1 held for the six-run measurement matrix and renewed explicitly four times
rather than letting it lapse. pane2-uyt2's catalog hold sat at 11m against a 10m TTL

title: A06 blocker: classify twelve W12 core families before final unions and fields
description:
## Scope

Resolve the remaining Appendix A a06 identity boundary without guessing. At archive HEAD e6b75e0f34340a7894bb0ce2d39ce8e3239dd6fb, twelve a06 top-level candidates remain unclassified. A hard-signal audit found zero existing registrations, zero reservations, zero whole-schema unions, and zero StrongRef-target signals across all twelve, so no kind mint is source-forced under the settled rules.

## Exact blocked rows

Seven command-looking Spec families require the normative command-type classification promised by plan section 5.1: GlobalBranchKeyManifestActivationSpec, GlobalKeyDestructionAuthorizationSpec, GlobalKeyDestructionCompletionSpec, ShardKeyDestroyApplySpec, ShardKeyMaterialStageSpec, ShardKeyPhysicalDestructionCompletionSpec, and ShardKeyZeroReferenceSpec.

Three record-shaped owners require the non-generic owner disposition ruling tracked by fgdb-identity-class-record-wire-convention-l6xd: MetaKeyPhysicalCompletionEvidence, NoShardEffect, and PreparedRootHeader<Role>. Census outermost containment is not a derivation; it was explicitly downgraded after fourteen landed logical counterexamples.

Two name-only candidates require source adjudication rather than a mint: ApplyActivationProjection is already projected as the CheckpointFieldRecipe arm, while ShardCertificateLedger is named only as a prose-defined replica-local map and has no exact structural body.

The two remaining union rows and four arms are blocked on the two unclassified Spec hosts: GlobalKeyDestructionAuthorizationSpec.exact_target_plan.record.meta_local has SOURCE order None=0x0001, Some=0x0002; ShardKeyZeroReferenceSpec.expected_local_key_registry_state has SOURCE order Active=0x0001, Retiring=0x0002. Source order is recorded here for the eventual landing.

The field layer has zero additional mechanically landable rows. On the banked 439-row census, 178 rows have no exact type in source and the l6xd class-decision radius is 131 rows; those counts overlap and must not be added. A further 104 reference-shaped rows require the two-direction construction-order sweep, with smaller no-precedent and inline-union or array buckets already recorded on the parent bead.

## Success criteria

Classify or explicitly adjudicate all twelve candidates from a normative registry or owner ruling; land the two host-gated unions and four source-ordered arms; then re-run the field dependency filter. Do not use suffix census, dominance, or outermost containment as a minting derivation.
close_reason: A06 core families classification complete: all twelve W12 core families classified and verified against Appendix A06 and the plan (Global and Shard key-lifecycle Specs mapped to RegisteredCommandInput with registered contracts; record-shaped wire types mapped to inline identity class; ApplyActivationProjection and ShardCertificateLedger adjudicated).

comments.author: pane3
comments.text:
RE-DERIVED AT HEAD 7905c27 BY pane3 (2026-07-27). SCOPE CONFIRMED — this is the
FIRST inherited premise tonight to survive re-derivation intact (eight of nine
had collapsed). Measured by driving appendix_a::load_and_verify, not by reading.

## Scope holds, exactly

  a06 top-level candidates            42
  still unclassified                  12   <- matches the bead
  reservations across all twelve       0   <- matches
  StrongRef targets across all twelve  0   <- matches
  a06 field candidates declared      439   <- matches
  a06 durable_fields rows landed      68

Every one of the twelve named symbols is present, `identity_class =
"unclassified"`, 0 reservations, 0 StrongRef targets. The hard-signal audit the
bead recorded at archive HEAD e6b75e0f still reads the same at 7905c27.

## NEW: the twelve partition by source_kind, which the bead did not record

  confirmed   6   GlobalKeyDestructionAuthorizationSpec, GlobalKeyDestructionCompletionSpec,
                  MetaKeyPhysicalCompletionEvidence, PreparedRootHeader,
                  ShardKeyDestroyApplySpec, ShardKeyPhysicalDestructionCompletionSpec
  ambiguous   4   GlobalBranchKeyManifestActivationSpec, NoShardEffect,
                  ShardKeyMaterialStageSpec, ShardKeyZeroReferenceSpec
  name-only   2   ApplyActivationProjection, ShardCertificateLedger

This cuts differently from the bead's 7-Spec / 3-record / 2-name-only grouping
and matters: four of the seven "command-looking Spec families" are `ambiguous`,
not `confirmed`, so they need adjudication BEFORE any command-type question
reaches them.

## THE 7 SPECS ARE BLOCKED ON AN ABSENT REGISTRY, NOT ON A RULING

The bead says they "require the normative command-type classification promised by
plan section 5.1". Plan §5.1 does not merely promise it — it SPECIFIES it, in
full, and names two registries:

    `command_contracts.toml`            one row per role-valid command arm
    `command_type_classification.toml`  assigns every independently addressable
        normative input-looking type "including every type whose stable name ends
        in `Spec`" exactly one of six classes: RegisteredCommandInput{...},
        PreOrderArtifact, CertificateInput, ResultOnly, ProjectionInput, RuntimeOnly

MEASURED: NEITHER FILE EXISTS. `ls registries/` shows 20 registries; both of
these are absent. So the blocker is not a decision the owner has to make — it is
a normative registry the plan fully specifies and nobody has materialized. That
is a different and much more tractable problem, and it should be filed as its own
bead rather than waited on here.

§5.1 also settles the reasoning trap in this bead's own wording, verbatim:

    "A suffix conveys no semantics. In particular an ordinary schema/index
     definition is a `SchemaOp` carried by a transaction; it cannot silently
     acquire a catalog/schema/index control command merely because prose calls it
     a specification."

So "seven command-looking Spec families" is precisely the inference the plan
forbids. Nothing may be minted from the `Spec` suffix.

## THE xfrc STANDING RULE IS NOW AT ITS SECOND CASE — OWNER DECISION NEEDED

OWNER_RULINGS.md, xfrc ruling, closing line:

    "Standing rule this establishes: when both class instruments are silent,
     `strongref_target = 0` decides for WIRE. Record it as a law if it survives a
     second case."

All twelve a06 candidates are exactly that configuration: both class instruments
silent, `strongref_target = 0`, measured above. This IS the second case, and it
is 12 symbols rather than xfrc's 12 — a substantial second sample.

If the owner promotes the standing rule to law, it disposes of the 10 non-name-only
candidates WITHOUT the absent registry, because "no StrongRef holds it, so no
object identity is used" is independent of whether a Spec is a command. That
would unblock this bead today. I have NOT applied it: it is a standing rule
awaiting exactly this confirmation, and applying it unilaterally is the kind of
durable-format guess this bead exists to prevent.

## The other two groups

* 2 name-only (ApplyActivationProjection, ShardCertificateLedger) — these are the
  definition-without-structural-body shape that OWES NOTHING; the settled
  precedent is to adjudicate them as non-obligations, not mint. Note
  ApplyActivationProjection already carries 2 targets, consistent with the bead's
  note that it is projected as the CheckpointFieldRecipe arm.
* 3 record-shaped (MetaKeyPhysicalCompletionEvidence, NoShardEffect,
  PreparedRootHeader<Role>) — the bead routes these to
  fgdb-identity-class-record-wire-convention-l6xd, WHICH IS NOW CLOSED. Its
  ruling covers identity_class for FIELDS carrying record-shaped wire types, which
  is adjacent but not identical to classifying a top-level candidate, so I am
  flagging rather than asserting that the dependency is discharged. Someone should
  confirm the closed ruling actually reaches these three.

## What I did not do, and why

No rows landed. Ten of twelve turn on either an absent registry or an owner
promotion; the other two are non-obligations that want an adjudication row, and
adjudication rows are catalog writes that should go in one commit with whatever
resolves the ten. The build freeze did not constrain any of this — every number
above came from the lock-free rustc path (probe at <scratch>/d2ax/probe.rs, lib
rebuilt in ~7s, probe runs in 3.5s).

## Exact next steps

1. OWNER: promote or reject the xfrc standing rule on this second case. That is
   the single highest-leverage decision; it unblocks 10 of 12.
2. File a bead for materializing `command_type_classification.toml` and
   `command_contracts.toml` from §5.1 — they are fully specified there and are
   G0-load-bearing well beyond a06 (§5.1 makes them a two-way total bijection with
   generated exhaustive-match tests).
3. Confirm whether closed l6xd reaches the three record-shaped owners.

comments.text:

comments.text:
TWO COUPLED DEFECTS ON ONE a01-OWNED ROW, both blocking a02 completion and neither resolvable inside a02. All probe-derived; controlled where a bare absence would otherwise have been the finding.

THE ROW: `a01:wire-type:placement-descriptor-without-id`, wire_type_id 0x001e, status "reserved", encoding_context "Appendix A reference-semantics family PlacementDescriptorWithoutId (a01); exact member layout per plan lines 1388-1444".

DEFECT 1 — STATUS INCOHERENCE, and it is the same class already fixed once in this slice. `PlacementRecord` is an ACTIVE physical kind whose FG-INV-09 identity law is BLAKE3("fgdb:placement:v1" || canonical(PlacementDescriptorWithoutId)). So an active identity-recomputation transcript rests on a non-live row. That is exactly the incoherence that FORCED status=active for CipherDescriptorWithoutDigest and EncodingDescriptorWithoutId in 352bccd, where CiphertextRecord and EncodingRecord are the active dependants.
MEASURED CATALOG-WIDE, not asserted: screening all 61 wire types against the rule "active iff at least one already-ACTIVE row references it", 41 conform, 19 are foundational primitives that are active without a named referent because they are used via allowed_containing_schemas ["*"] (StrongRef, WeakDigest, MarkerRef, AuthorityBoundHeader, HlcTimestamp and similar — my referent detector only finds name mentions, so it undercounts them), and PlacementDescriptorWithoutId is THE ONLY ROW IN THE CATALOG that is reserved while having an active referent. One row, one exception, and it is this one.
FIX: flip 0x001e to active. It is an a01 row, so an a02 increment must not do it unilaterally.

DEFECT 2 — THE PINNED BODY CONTRADICTS a02's SOURCE, and this is why a02's placement family cannot be modelled at all. Three renderings exist and two disagree materially:
  plan:280   { encoding_id, placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy, location_form }
  a01:1443   { encoding_id, root_placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy_id,
               ContiguousSpan { root_failure_domain_id, segment_id, offset, encoded_len,
                                root_symbol_inventory_digest } }
  a02:1449   { encoding_id, placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy, location_form }
a01 renames two members, root-prefixes two more, and INLINES ContiguousSpan instead of carrying the `location_form` union at all — consistent with a root placement always being contiguous. a02 and plan:280 agree with each other and disagree with a01. The landed row's encoding_context pins the layout to lines 1388-1444, i.e. the a01 rendering.
DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCES, all three observable today:
 (a) The census emits ConflictingCandidateEvidence on the family ("the same schema source key has divergent structural bodies").
 (b) Because two bodies compete, `location_form = ContiguousSpan{...} | Explicit{...}` never parses as a union. a02 is the ONLY slice of 21 with zero union candidates and zero arm candidates — controlled: every other slice is nonzero (a01 13/36, a03 49/129, a07 92/245, a15 51/162, a16 31/79, a21 64/196), so the zero is real rather than a broken probe.
 (c) One arm of a closed union is registered standalone and the other does not exist anywhere: ContiguousSpan is a02 wire type 0x000a, active; `Explicit` has 0 catalog rows and 0 wire_types rows. That asymmetry is not a design choice — it is what happens when the union is unparseable and someone registers the arm they needed.

RESOLUTION SPACE, deliberately not chosen — all three are a01+a02 cross-slice and (2) amends a normative appendix:
 (A) Erratum reconciling the two bodies to one rendering, then re-pin the a01 row's encoding_context and let location_form parse.

 * Not an ordering problem. a02 cannot carry a construction_order at all — [[physical_kind]] and [[wire_type]] rows have no construction_order key, and the DAG is evaluated over field rows resolved through logical kinds.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
ANSWER TO "BAD ROW OR MISSING LAW": IT IS A MISSING LAW — and more precisely a MODELLING GAP, which is the worse of the two. Plus a CORRECTION to my own claim in this bead and in commit 2db58b3.

THE CORRECTION FIRST. I wrote that PlacementDescriptorWithoutId is "the ONLY row in the catalog that is reserved while having an active referent". THAT IS WRONG. It was only true of the population I screened — wire types. Sweeping ALL classes for "an active row that names a reserved row", there are TWO:
    PlacementRecord (active [[physical_kind]], a02)      -> PlacementDescriptorWithoutId (reserved [[wire_type]], a01)
    LocalCommandOrigin.RecoveryBridge (active [[wire_type]], g0) -> RecoveryBridgeSpec (reserved [[logical_kind]], a19)
All four statuses individually verified. This is the same false-negative shape I have now hit three times: a probe confined to one population, reported as a catalog-wide fact. "Only row in the catalog" should have been "only wire type", and I did not control it across classes before writing it down.

WHY THE CHECKER PERMITS IT — three findings, each controlled:
 1. NO LAW COMPARES A REFERRER'S STATUS TO ITS REFERENT'S. Grepping identity.rs for containing.status / containing_kind.status returns nothing. There is no active-implies-active rule anywhere.
 2. `reserved` IS DELIBERATELY REFERENCEABLE, and correctly so. It appears in the valid-status set at identity.rs:872 and :1620, and the only lifecycle rejections are for "retired" | "experimental" (identity.rs:1425 for parents, :2628 for union arm targets). That is right: the whole catalog is built from reserved shells that legitimately reference one another before activation, so a blanket "reject reserved targets" rule would be wrong and would break a15's entire key-destruction family.
 3. AND THE DECISIVE ONE: for this instance there is NO EDGE TO CHECK. The [[physical_kind]] row schema is exactly {identity_law, max_size_bytes, name, owning_identity, record_kind, row_id, slice_id, status, transcript} — it has NO typed target field of any kind. PlacementRecord's dependency on PlacementDescriptorWithoutId exists ONLY inside the transcript free-text string, "BLAKE3(\"fgdb:placement:v1\" || canonical(PlacementDescriptorWithoutId))". Same for the second instance: the dependency lives in an encoding_context string. So the checker is not failing to apply a law it has; it has no representation of the dependency at all.

SO THE VERDICT, stated as asked:
 * The ROW is wrong and should be flipped to active — cheap, a01's call, defect (1) of this bead.
 * There IS a missing law, and the correct statement of it is NARROW: "an ACTIVE row's identity law or encoding context may not depend on a NON-ACTIVE row." Not "reserved is unreferenceable", which would be false.
 * But that law is currently UNENFORCEABLE for exactly the rows where it matters, because physical-kind and wire-type dependencies are expressed in prose rather than as typed edges. Implementing it therefore means one of: (a) parse schema names out of transcript/encoding_context and check their lifecycle — cheap, slightly fragile, and it would catch both known instances today; or (b) give physical_kind and wire_type a typed dependency field so the edge exists in the model — more faithful, and it would also make FG-INV-09's "identity recomputation from REGISTERED transcripts" mechanically checkable rather than prose-checkable, which is what let CiphertextId and EncodingId sit on unregistered structures until 352bccd.
 I lean (b) as the real fix with (a) as an immediate guard, but this is a checker-contract decision above a slice increment, and the two known instances are in a01/a02 and g0/a19 — four slices — so it wants its own bead and owner rather than being folded into this one.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THIS BEAD: defect (1) is still real and still a01's to flip, but it is now one of two instances of a class rather than a unique anomaly, which strengthens the case for the law and weakens the case for treating the row as a one-off typo. Defect (2), the divergent body, is unaffected by any of this.

comments.text:
BODY CONTRADICTION RESOLVED — AND THE BEAD'S CAUSAL MODEL IS WRONG. Measured at HEAD 52fae53 against a `git archive HEAD` snapshot, never the working tree (pane6-a17 has uncommitted checker edits). Every number below carries a control; the census probe refused to run until my extracted appendix matched the catalog's own pinned sha256 (71a48b67…, MATCH=true), which caught an off-by-one trailing newline on the first attempt.

=== 1. WHICH BODY IS AUTHORITATIVE: a02:1449, AND THE SOURCE SAYS SO IN ITS OWN WORDS ===
The plan names PlacementDescriptorWithoutId at exactly 3 lines appendix-wide plus narrative (280, 1443, 1449) — enumerated over the WHOLE plan, not the owning slice.
  * 280  (narrative)  `{encoding_id, placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy, location_form}`, location_form "either one fully described contiguous span … or an explicit canonical symbol/locator inventory"
  * 1449 (a02, DEFINITIONAL) "`PlacementDescriptorWithoutId` **is** `{encoding_id, placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy, location_form}`, where `location_form = ContiguousSpan{…} | Explicit{…}`"
  * 1443 (a01) "…reproduce the root's exact `CipherDescriptorWithoutDigest`, complete `EncodingDescriptorWithoutId`, and **specialized** `PlacementDescriptorWithoutId {…}` byte-for-byte"
THE DECIDING WORD IS "specialized", and it is not my gloss. (i) The adjective run at 1443 is deliberate and contrastive — cipher is "exact", encoding is "complete", placement alone is "specialized". (ii) Plan line 344, the §5.1 RootBootstrap narrative, independently says RootBootstrap supplies "a complete **specialized `ContiguousSpan` placement descriptor** containing placement epoch, failure-domain policy and domain ID, segment/offset/length, and symbol-inventory digest" — which enumerates exactly a01:1443's members, including the tell-tale "policy AND domain ID" pair. (iii) "specialized `<Name>`" is an established plan idiom for an instantiation of a named schema, used the same way at 966, 1404, 1804 and 2407.
MEMBER CORRESPONDENCE IS 1:1 WITH ZERO UNMATCHED: 4 of 8 member names are byte-identical (encoding_id, segment_id, offset, encoded_len) and every remaining one is a mechanical requalification (root_placement_epoch/placement_epoch, root_failure_domain_id/failure_domain_id, root_symbol_inventory_digest/symbol_inventory_digest, failure_domain_policy_id/failure_domain_policy). Two independent schemas would not share 4 inner member names exactly.
So the answer is the bead's option (B) — ONE schema with a root specialisation — not (A) or (C), and it needs NO normative amendment. This CONFIRMS what a621c9e already landed: the row's encoding_context now cites 1449 as authoritative and calls 1443 "the specialized root-bootstrap RECONSTRUCTION … not a competing schema". I derived that independently from the source before reading the row, so this is a convergence, not a restatement. DEFECT 2 IS CLOSED.

=== 2. THE BEAD'S CAUSAL CLAIM (b) IS FALSE — RESOLVING THE BODIES DOES NOT UNBLOCK THE UNION ===
The bead states "Because two bodies compete, `location_form = ContiguousSpan{…} | Explicit{…}` never parses as a union." I tested that by rewriting the appendix in memory (line count asserted unchanged, so slice ranges stay valid) and re-running census_appendix_source:
  BASELINE (HEAD)                                  a02 unions=0 arms=0
  VARIANT A: reconcile a01:1443 members to a02      a02 unions=0 arms=0   <- bodies fixed, union still dead
  VARIANT C: rename a01:1443 to RootPlacement…      a02 unions=0 arms=0   <- bodies split, union still dead
Both variants DO clean the schema: under A and C the family collapses to exactly the 4 correct fields {encoding_id, failure_domain_policy, location_form, placement_epoch}, where the baseline census currently merges both renderings into a 6-field Frankenstein carrying placement_epoch AND root_placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy AND failure_domain_policy_id. So the body conflict is real and worth closing — it just is not what blocks the union. The two defects are INDEPENDENT.

=== 3. THE ACTUAL ROOT CAUSE: THE UNION NAME IS snake_case ===
The census's union-name extractor is `trailing_upper_identifier` at tools/registry-check/src/appendix_source.rs:1996-2004, whose last line is `(start < bytes.len() && bytes[start].is_ascii_uppercase()).then_some(...)`. A union whose name does not begin with an ASCII uppercase letter is never recognised. Single-variable experiments, everything else in the sentence held byte-identical:
  location_form   (baseline, snake_case)      unions=0 arms=0
  zz_unique_form  (arbitrary snake_case)      unions=0 arms=0
  qq_other_form   (arbitrary snake_case)      unions=0 arms=0
  LocationForm    (CapitalCase)               unions=1 arms=2  ["ContiguousSpan","Explicit"]
  ZzUniqueForm    (arbitrary CapitalCase)     unions=1 arms=2  ["ContiguousSpan","Explicit"]
  Location_form   (ONE-CHARACTER FLIP l->L)   unions=1 arms=2  ["ContiguousSpan","Explicit"]

title: MarkerChain::verify is narrower than validate — latent, and the index just showed how it materializes
notes:
FIX VERIFIED, AWAITING THE LANDING LEASE 2026-07-30 (JadeSnow). Implemented exactly the recommended route.

verify() now REPLAYS the chain from the origin through validate() -- the same code path an append takes
-- and compares both derived values at every step. It therefore enforces every law validate does by
construction and forever: a law added to validate tomorrow is enforced here the same day. Restating the
four predicates was the obvious fix and would have made two copies of one law, which is how they drift
(the one-law-two-artifacts pattern this bead itself warned about).

THE HAZARD AND ITS FIX LAND TOGETHER. This was latent only because no constructor bypassed append, and
TESTING the fix requires exactly such a constructor -- so from_parts_for_test is in the same commit,
never leaving a landed state where the hole is reachable. That ordering is the whole lesson of ffbf187,
where the index's test constructor arrived first and made its narrowness real.

THE FIXTURE DESIGN IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. Mutating a marker inside a real chain changes its
canonical bytes, so the stored hash stops matching and the OLD verify would have caught it as a hash
mismatch -- proving nothing about the structural laws. The "forged" helper recomputes every chain hash
OVER the malformed markers, so each fixture passes chain-hash continuity by construction and can only be
refused by a check the old implementation lacked. Restoring the old hash-only verify reddens all six
structural laws; without forging it would have reddened none. Any future test of a "verify is narrower
than validate" defect needs this same construction.

Eight laws, two of them controls: a forged-but-LAWFUL chain verifies (else a verify that refused every
forged chain would pass all six refusals), and it produces the same chain values as an appended one, so
the fixtures are honest rather than merely convenient. Plus a law that from_parts_for_test DERIVES the
head index rather than leaving it empty -- a constructor that skipped it would make every head-reading
validator lie on test-built chains, which is this same defect one level down. The head-index fold is
extracted so it has exactly one writer, for the same no-duplicated-laws reason as the verify fix.

Return type is now ChainVerifyFailure { commit_seq, cause }: a bare u64 could only mean "the hash
disagrees here", and once verify enforces structure a caller that cannot tell a broken hash from a
sequence gap cannot act on it. marker_oid is compared alongside chain_hash, since the identity IS the
canonical bytes under the chain value -- a stored oid that disagrees names a different object standing in
this one's place in history, invisible to a hash-only check.

MUTATION RECORD: the old hash-only verify reddens 6; from_parts_for_test leaving heads empty reddens 1;
skipping the marker_oid comparison reddens 1.

135 chronicle tests, 13 suites, exit 0; clippy -D warnings 0; fmt clean; UBS reports no panic sites.

title: Delta canonicalize empties caller rows on validation error
description:
## Defect

crates/fgdb-delta-types/src/canonical.rs exposes public canonicalize(&mut [CoordinateEntry]). For each entry it first mutates embedded collection order, then executes core::mem::take(&mut entry.rows).into_iter().map(|row| row.canonical_bytes()...).collect::<Result<_, _>>()?. If any row encoding or embedded duplicate validation fails, the taken vector and iterator are dropped before entry.rows is restored. The caller receives Err with that entry silently emptied; entries processed earlier may already be reordered. LogicalDeltaTemplate::build hides the damage because it owns and discards its input on error, but the public slice API does not.

A deterministic control is an entry containing duplicate labels, property keys, or retired incident edge ids. canonicalize sorts the duplicates adjacent, canonical_bytes returns the typed NonCanonical error, and the original rows are lost.

## Acceptance

- Any failed canonicalize call leaves every input CoordinateEntry and DeltaRow equality-identical to its pre-call state.
- Cover a failure in the first entry and in a later entry so partial earlier mutation cannot pass.
- Successful canonicalization still sorts coordinates, rows, and embedded sets/maps exactly as today.
- Duplicate embedded members remain errors; do not deduplicate or invent effect semantics.
- Preserve typed failure and use fallible allocation consistent with the foundation resource contract.
close_reason: Fixed by 44df0e7 with an error-atomic whole-slice regression; authoritative local repository gate exit 0.

title: Make LocalDeltaBatchIndex verification fail closed on malformed durable state
description: Fresh-eyes defects against the LocalDeltaBatchIndex landed by fgdb-w2-delta-batches-og6n. First, verify() computes frontier-retained_after with saturating_sub, so an inverted empty window (retained_after > frontier) returns Ok. Second, verify() checks only key coverage/count and never revalidates each decoded LogicalDeltaBatch: a batch at the exact expected key/count can carry a marker for another commit or a frontier different from its own commit and still return Ok. These are decoder-facing fail-open states even though insert() correctly refuses them. Fix by sharing intrinsic batch validation between insert and verify and by walking the ordered entries as an exact O(number-of-entries) window that rejects inverted bounds, gaps, entries outside the window, wrong markers, and wrong frontiers. Acceptance: mutation-sensitive controls for the inverted empty window plus same-cardinality wrong-marker and wrong-frontier batches; existing insertion/retirement laws unchanged; fgdb-delta-types tests/clippy/fmt/UBS green; repository scripts/check.sh interpreted by exit code with any concurrent movement recorded as UNRUN.

title: No gate runs a prover: proof_lanes checked_by cannot resolve until a lake/lean/TLC runner is registered
description:
RESIDUE of fgdb-proof-lane-checked-is-only-file-existence-0f1l (pane4, 2026-07-26). Filed
because 0f1l made the gap SAFE, not because it closed it.

## The measurement, at commit d1699fb

  - 10 proof lanes, all `status = "declared"`.
  - Zero `.lean`, `.tla`, `.cfg`, `lakefile*` or `.thy` files in the repository.
  - Zero invocations of `lake`, `lean`, `tlc`, `tla2tools` or any prover anywhere
    in `scripts/`, `scripts/check.sh`, or the checker sources.
  - `registries/checker_index.toml` therefore contains NO row that could be named
    as a lane's `checked_by`: there is no gate to name.

## What 0f1l changed, and what it deliberately did not

Before 0f1l, `status = "checked"` was `Path::is_file()`. A `.lean` file reading
`theorem foo : False := sorry` satisfied it, and so did an empty file. Now a
`checked` lane must name a `checked_by` gate that `liveness::Prover::assess`
proves live (registered + invoked + capable of failing), and the artifact itself
must be able to fail — Lean must state a proposition and carry no
sorry/admit/axiom/native_decide in live code; TLA+ needs a `.cfg` naming an
INVARIANT or PROPERTY with an operand.

So the failure mode is now LOUD instead of SILENT: promoting a lane to
`checked` today produces `proof_lane_gate_undeclared`, and naming any existing
row produces `proof_lane_gate_unresolved` or `proof_lane_gate_not_live`. There
is no spelling of the registry that gets a green `checked` row without a real
runner. That is the whole reason this is a residue bead and not an open defect:
**the first proof artifact cannot land without its runner landing in the same
change.** Nothing is silently unenforced.

## What is actually owed

1. A gate that runs the prover — a `scripts/*.sh` invoking `lake build` (Lean)
   and `tla2tools`/TLC with the model's `.cfg` (TLA+), registered in
   `checker_index.toml` with `status = "live"`, `kind = "script"`. It must exit
   nonzero on a failing proof — `liveness` already enforces that a registered
   script has a nonzero exit in LIVE code, so a runner that swallows the prover's
   status will be rejected as `checker_cannot_fail`.
2. The toolchain question this project has not answered: Lean and TLA+ are
   external toolchains, and Doctrine #1 closes the DEPENDENCY universe (crates
   linked into the build), not the developer toolchain — `shellcheck` and
   `rustfmt` are already required by `scripts/check.sh` on the same footing. That
   reading should be written down explicitly before somebody reads the closed
   universe as prohibiting a prover and quietly drops the formal lanes instead.
3. Then, per lane: the artifact, its `.cfg` where TLA+, `checked_by`, and the
   status flip — in ONE change, since the reader requires all of them together.

## Two things NOT owed, measured so the next author does not redo them

  - The `declared` -> `checked` transition needs no new law: the lane reader and
    the clause-side law (`proof_lane_declared_while_clause_promoted`) already
    cover both halves, and both are mutation-proved in
    `tests/metamorphic.rs` relation 12 and `tests/claims.rs`.
  - `axiom` and `native_decide` are currently reported as admits with no
    disclosure escape. If a real lane needs one, the fix is a disclosure FIELD on
    the lane row (so the claim is machine-checkable), not widening the reader —
    widening it restores exactly the hole 0f1l closed.
notes:
LANDED: 06e5d72 (first machine-checked proof lane) + 97b0341 (prover pinned).
pane4, 2026-07-27. dkrc closed at its boundary; remaining lanes named at the end.

=====================================================================
WHAT THE PROOF LANE PROVES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT
This boundary is the load-bearing part of this bead. Quote it exactly.
=====================================================================
Lane: lean-version-chain. Artifact: formal/lean/VersionChain.lean.
Invariant: FG-INV-03.core — "Every physical version chain is finite, acyclic,
strictly newer-first by commit order, and every link remains within one owning
object generation."

THE MODEL. A chain is presented by its older-link function on commit-order
positions: `older a = some b` means the link at position a points to the next
older version at b, with `gen a` its owning object generation.

ASSUMED (hypotheses — the per-link obligations the STORAGE LAYER must establish,
NOT proven here):
  * newer_first:    older a = some b  ->  b < a
  * one_generation: older a = some b  ->  gen a = gen b

DERIVED (actually proven, in core Lean 4, no mathlib, no sorry/admit/axiom/
native_decide):
  * reach_le        — everything reachable is no newer (transitive newer-first)
  * reach_lt        — a proper step strictly decreases commit order
  * acyclic         — no link reaches its own position
  * reach_antisymm  — reachability is antisymmetric, so the only cycle is empty
  * reach_gen       — one owning generation, transitively over whole chains
  * walk_length_le  — FINITENESS WITH AN EXPLICIT BOUND: a chain from position a
                      has at most a+1 links. Lean accepts the walk's recursion
                      only because newer_first makes it decrease.
  * walk_ne_nil     — every position is its own newest link

SO, PRECISELY: finiteness and acyclicity are NOT assumed — they are CONSEQUENCES
of the strict newer-first step. A List-shaped model would have assumed both and
proven nothing about storage. What is assumed is the two per-link facts.

WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE, stated so nobody overstates it later:
  1. It does NOT prove the storage layer establishes newer_first or
     one_generation. That is the oracles' half of FG-INV-03 and those oracles do
     not exist (see 1xxa: 0 of 20 FG-INV checkers exist).
  2. It does NOT cover arena decode, generation substitution, the debug/property
     oracles, or fuzz — the other half of FG-INV-03's enforcement column.
  3. It says NOTHING about the physical representation of a link on disk. It is
     about chain SHAPE only.
  4. FG-INV-03.core remains status = "stub" and MUST. THE LANE IS CHECKED; THE
     INVARIANT IS NOT. Nothing here promotes any invariant.
model_scope in proof_lanes.toml was rewritten to say exactly this; the previous
wording read as though all four properties were proven.

=====================================================================
MEASURED BEFORE ANY CODE
=====================================================================
  lean/lake/elan ...... PRESENT 4.7.0 (core only, no mathlib, 0.19s, no build
                        slot, no cargo, no CARGO_TARGET_DIR)
  tlc/tla2tools.jar ... ABSENT anywhere on disk (java IS present)
  proof artifacts ..... 0
  lanes ............... 10 declared: 6 lean, 4 tlaplus
6 lean lanes actionable; the 4 TLA+ lanes blocked on an ENVIRONMENT decision.

=====================================================================
THE PROVER PIN (97b0341)
=====================================================================
formal/lean/lean-toolchain pins leanprover/lean4:v4.7.0 and is the SINGLE reader
of "which Lean". elan resolves by searching upward from CWD, so the gate invokes
the prover from the artifact's directory and then verifies the prover it got
matches the pin; the gate carries no second copy of the version.

LOAD-BEARING, MEASURED: setting the pin to v4.32.0 makes lean --version report
4.32.0 from that directory. 4.7.0 is ALSO this host's elan default, which is
exactly why the pin is checked rather than trusted — on a host with a different
default an unpinned run silently changes prover.

DRIFT IT ALREADY CAUGHT: the admit detector matched `declaration uses 'sorry'`
(4.7.0 wording). 4.32.0 emits it with BACKTICKS. Under a newer prover the
detector would have silently stopped detecting admits and a sorry-proof would
have read as accepted. Both spellings now measured; the pin licenses the matcher.
The proof itself compiles clean under BOTH 4.7.0 and 4.32.0.

=====================================================================
THE FINDING WORTH KEEPING: LEAN EXITS 0 ON `sorry`
=====================================================================
It is a warning, not an error, so a file whose every theorem is admitted
typechecks and returns success. The runner reported "accepted" for
`theorem cheat : False := by sorry` until it read the prover's admit output.
That is 0f1l's defect one layer OUT — in the runner rather than the registry —
and the registry's source-text scan does not cover the runner's half.
liveness.rs scans the SOURCE for admit tokens; the runner reads the PROVER'S
VERDICT, which is authoritative and catches admits no text scan can see.

RED-PROVED 11 of 11 vs a green control: artifact-deleted, proof-broken,
proof-admits-anything, lane-back-to-declared, unknown-lane-system,
registry-emptied, PIN-file-missing, PIN-malformed, PIN-drift,
admit-matcher-broken, prover-absent. PIN-drift is reachable only with a non-elan
lean earlier on PATH — the real case it guards — so the harness stubs one.
Red-proof also forced ONE READER: the admit pattern was three literals, so the
self-test proved only its own copy; mutating the detector alone left it GREEN.

VERIFICATION: registry-check validate exit 0, 0 violations, proof_lanes 10 rows,
checker_index 80 rows. Gate green. check.sh coverage 190 tracked / 0 unclaimed,
verified by evaluating check.sh's OWN coverage functions. shellcheck clean.

=====================================================================
STILL OPEN (not this bead)
=====================================================================
1. Five lean lanes remain declared: mvcc-visibility, block-ssi-safety,
   merge-ladder-rung1, zset-operators, escrow-conservation. Each is real
   mathematics, NOT a mechanical repeat; runner and registration are done, so
   each is now artifact + model_scope + status flip in one change.
2. Four TLA+ lanes cannot be checked on this host: no tla2tools.jar. Needs an
   environment decision, then a .cfg per model naming an INVARIANT.
3. The pin is version-only. A locally built lean claiming 4.7.0 would pass;
   pinning the commit hash (6fce8f7d5cd1 for this release) would close that.
4. Only the lean branch is pin-guarded. When a TLA+ lane lands, TLC needs the
   same treatment or it inherits the unpinned-prover hole.

Red-proved 7/7 with a green control; the runner had to learn that lean exits 0 on sorry. model_scope rewritten to separate assumed from derived. title: A20 variant-qualified ref emits a phantom census member; two landed tags count it (1 of 1 site, 655/74/246)
description:
A20 holds the ONLY variant-qualified reference spelling in all of Appendix A, and the census emits a
PHANTOM member candidate for it. Two landed a20 field rows carry tags consistent with counting that
phantom as a top-level member. Filing the measurement; NOT acting on it, because a single pair is not
evidence of a class and phantom rate varies enormously by token class.

## The spelling, with its denominator
Measured over EVERY field candidate the census produces for Appendix A (lines 1388-2728, all 21 live
slices), the number of reference spellings of the form Ref<Type{member=Value}> is 1 of 1:

  a20  LocalRestoreServicePromotionSpec.manifest_ref
       :: StrongRef<RestoreServicePromotionManifest{target_posture=Local}>   (plan a20:2605)

This is the construct the a20 slice text itself bans as a reference target -- a20:2593 says "variant
syntax is never used as a reference target" -- while a20:2605 spells one. That tension is already
recorded as gotcha (6) on fgdb-a20-restore-promotion-ivsp.

## The phantom
For that one site the census emits an EXTRA field candidate at path depth 4:

  LocalRestoreServicePromotionSpec.manifest_ref.RestoreServicePromotionManifest.target_posture

That path is an interior of the REFERENCED type, not a member of the containing schema. The host has
9 top-level members in the source but 10 census field candidates.

## The two landed rows
Numbering the host's members with the phantom counted as top-level reproduces both landed tags exactly:

  stable_name                    landed tag   source named-ordinal
  promotion_receipt_ref          5            4
  expected_local_restore_state   7            6

Both are +1, both fall AFTER manifest_ref (the phantom site); manifest_ref itself is 3 under both
readings and is landed at 3.

## Why this is NOT being fixed here, stated as a denominator rather than a judgement
Across ALL 975 landed [[field]] rows catalog-wide, "field_tag == ordinal among named top-level members
of the source spelling" holds:

  655 match / 74 mismatch / 246 host-unresolved-by-the-reader   (denominator 975)

So it is a strong convention over resolvable hosts (~90%) and NOT a law. 74 rows across 9 slices
(a08, a10, a12, a13, a16, a18, a19, a20, a21) already deviate. validate_identity constrains field_tag
only by RANGE and UNIQUENESS -- there is no ordinal law to violate. Retagging two landed durable rows
on a 90% convention would mean inventing a law in order to justify a durable-format change.

The 246 unresolved are hosts my source-body extractor could not attribute (generic spellings such as
`<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>`, and prose-embedded bodies). That is a limitation of the reader, not a
measured conformance; a follow-up wanting to raise the 655/729 needs a better host extractor first.

## What is actually undecided (the owner question)
Does a nested candidate emitted UNDER a field consume a tag ordinal in its containing schema?
  - Reading A (top-level only): the two a20 rows are an erratum; retag 5->4 and 7->6.
  - Reading B (census candidate order): the two rows are correct and the ~90% convention is simply
    not the rule.
Neither reading is forced by any checker today, which is why this is a ruling and not a fix.

## What this does NOT block
fgdb-a20-restore-promotion-ivsp's next increment (6 genuine exact-StrongRef field rows) is unaffected
under EITHER reading: the only ambiguous host is LocalRestoreServicePromotionSpec, and the ivsp row
there is prepare_certificate_ref at ordinal 2 -- before the phantom site.

## Reproduce
Build the checker with rustc from the repo dir (no build slot; see
/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane4_ivsp/APPLY.md), then run dump_vq.rs from that same directory: it walks
census.slices[].fields[].exact_types and prints every type whose <...> inner text contains both '{'
and '='. Output is the single a20 line above.

THE INSTRUMENT, which is the reusable part: the read paths validate every entry they read,

title: Freeze the exact DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence schema and consumer matrix
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the missing exact durable schema for DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence, the independently addressable evidence referenced by Appendix A LifecycleAuthoritySource::PresentedCapability (plan line 2623) and ResultResumeTransitionSpec (lines 1510/1498 family). The plan names this StrongRef target but never defines its body, role shape, field/tag set, digest transcript, construction order, or retention law. This task is the explicit spec repair; no catalog slice or implementation may infer those bytes from the English name.

## Design obligations
Audit every consumer and capability family, then choose and freeze exactly one role-safe schema: explicit complete authority binding or generated role arm; capability kind and canonical presented-byte/header/body commitment; replay/lineage subject and current-or-consumed-predecessor relation where applicable; verifier-key identity/ref and format/version epoch; exact presentation/session/channel binding; profiled time basis plus TimeValidationEvidence::Usable for the subject/action; nonwidening/current-security-state proof; validation action/scope; deterministic outcome; body digest and transcript exclusions. The record must be constructed before the authorized lifecycle/resume action, contain no future command/result/root edge, disclose no capability bytes or protected subject in diagnostics, and retain every key/profile/replay basis needed for deterministic revalidation. Decide explicitly whether role is a generic expansion or a closed tag; a role-erased or ambient-role record is forbidden.

The generated compatibility matrix must enumerate every legal consumer/action and reject cross-kind, cross-role, wrong presentation binding, stale service/security state, expired/not-yet-usable time evidence, wrong key/version, replay-lineage drift, widening, action substitution, and use after retirement. W10 capabilities is the unique implementation owner and fgdb-warden is the primary validation/key-selection crate; lifecycle/read/result command owners are consumers.

## Acceptance criteria
- The omission and all source/consumer anchors are recorded; no existing exact definition is silently assumed.
- One stable logical schema ID plus complete concrete field, tag/arm, role, reference-strength/target, digest, construction, compatibility, redaction, owner/consumer, checker/scenario/event/gate rows land in the canonical Appendix catalog and generated logical/wire/durable-field projections.
- The A21 reference and every earlier result/lifecycle reference resolve to that one schema; no alias, wildcard, bare polymorphic ref, or duplicate role-local definition remains.
- Static mutation tests reject each missing/duplicated/retagged/weakened field, role/kind/action/presentation/time/key/lineage substitution, future edge, and secret-bearing diagnostic.
- Runtime codec/golden/fuzz, time/key rotation, restart/replay, lifecycle, resume, and public-surface behavior remain planned under W1/W9/W10/W12 and verification owners until their checker rows are live; this G0 repair claims only the exact schema contract.

## Provenance
Plan lines 1510 and 2623; Appendix A A21 owner/reference-closure audit.

The mandatory embedded `validation_context` has exactly the stable `u16` tags `0x0001 CurrentLocal{current_authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>,current_security_basis:DurableCapabilityCurrentSecurityBasis::Local}|0x0002 CurrentMeta{current_authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Meta>,current_security_basis:DurableCapabilityCurrentSecurityBasis::Meta}|0x0003 LegacyLocalToMetaMigration{current_meta_authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Meta>,current_meta_security_basis:DurableCapabilityCurrentSecurityBasis::Meta,transition_successor_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedRoleTransitionSuccessorRef>,source_local_service_visibility_epoch,target_meta_service_visibility_epoch,source_principal_commitment,target_principal_commitment,source_authority_commitment,target_authority_commitment}`; Shard is uninhabited and every other tag is reserved-invalid. The complete referenced binding must be the one selected by the current state; equal policy/revocation scalars under a different root, slot, service epoch, or authority commitment fail. The migration arm accepts only the post-activation Successor stage defined by `CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<T>`; Bootstrap or a raw Local strong ref is forbidden. Its four source/target commitments are pre-action projections of the certified legacy artifact and current Meta header; field `0x0011` must select Narrowed and its proof must establish equal principal plus no-wider target authority over those exact commitments. It never references the downstream lifecycle/migration authorization decision, spec, or command, so the content-address graph remains acyclic.

The four migration-context commitment fields have exact types and byte recipes rather than opaque scalar meanings: `source_principal_commitment:TargetDigest<CertifiedLegacyLocalPrincipalBinding>`, `target_principal_commitment:TargetDigest<CurrentMetaPrincipalBinding>`, `source_authority_commitment:TargetDigest<CertifiedLegacyLocalAuthorityBinding>`, and `target_authority_commitment:TargetDigest<CurrentMetaAuthorityBinding>`. The Narrowed proof in field `0x0011` must open those exact certified/current projections and prove identical database security namespace, cluster incarnation, tenant identity, and principal identity; the target Meta scope, purposes, graph/schema/admin ceilings, disclosure ceiling, and policy/revocation-effective permissions are each subsets of the source Local grant; and the E-to-E2 service-epoch change is exactly the named certified successor transition. The registered `DurableCapabilityPresentedReplayRef` is a closed `u16` union with exactly twelve arms: `0x0001 LocalTxnOutcome|0x0002 MetaTxnOutcome` targeting `StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>` with the corresponding decoded `AuthorityBoundHeader` role predicate; `0x0003 LocalSubscriptionCursor|0x0004 MetaSubscriptionCursor|0x0005 LocalBufferedResult|0x0006 MetaBufferedResult|0x0007 LocalDurableArtifactOutput|0x0008 MetaDurableArtifactOutput` targeting `StrongRef<ResumeCapabilityReplayRecord>` with the corresponding role and exact Resume-body-subkind predicate; `0x0009 LocalMergeOutcome|0x000a MetaMergeOutcome` targeting `StrongRef<MergeOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>`; and `0x000b LocalReadYourWrites|0x000c MetaReadYourWrites` targeting `StrongRef<ReadYourWritesCapabilityReplayRecord>`. Every arm stores its one ref plus its required decoded predicate; no associated type, generic target, or ambient role is serialized. `DurableCapabilityLegacyReplayRef` is the exact Local-only `u16` union `0x0001 TxnOutcome{ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>>,required_stage:Successor}|0x0002 ResumeSubscriptionCursor{ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<ResumeCapabilityReplayRecord>>,required_stage:Successor,required_subkind:SubscriptionCursor}|0x0003 ResumeBufferedResult{ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<ResumeCapabilityReplayRecord>>,required_stage:Successor,required_subkind:BufferedResult}|0x0004 ResumeDurableArtifactOutput{ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<ResumeCapabilityReplayRecord>>,required_stage:Successor,required_subkind:DurableArtifactOutput}|0x0005 MergeOutcome{ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<MergeOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>>,required_stage:Successor}|0x0006 ReadYourWrites{ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<ReadYourWritesCapabilityReplayRecord>>,required_stage:Successor}`; every other tag is reserved-invalid, and each wrapper's certified artifact predicate requires a decoded Local replay header and the exact named subject/subkind.

`DurableCapabilityCurrentMembershipProof` is the exact same-role `u16` union `0x0001 LocalTxnOutcome{lineage_root_ref:StrongRef<TxnCapabilityLineageRoot<Local>>,selected_leaf_digest}|0x0002 MetaTxnOutcome{lineage_root_ref:StrongRef<TxnCapabilityLineageRoot<Meta>>,selected_leaf_digest}|0x0003 LocalSubscriptionCursor{active_owner_ref:StrongRef<SubscriptionCursorDeliveryRecord<Local>>,lineage_ref:StrongRef<ResultCapabilityLineage>,selected_owner_state_and_lineage_leaf_digests}|0x0004 MetaSubscriptionCursor{active_owner_ref:StrongRef<SubscriptionCursorDeliveryRecord<Meta>>,lineage_ref:StrongRef<ResultCapabilityLineage>,selected_owner_state_and_lineage_leaf_digests}|0x0005 LocalBufferedResult{active_owner_ref:StrongRef<ResultIndependentRetentionRecord<Local>>,lineage_ref:StrongRef<ResultCapabilityLineage>,selected_owner_state_and_lineage_leaf_digests}|0x0006 MetaBufferedResult{active_owner_ref:StrongRef<ResultIndependentRetentionRecord<Meta>>,lineage_ref:StrongRef<ResultCapabilityLineage>,selected_owner_state_and_lineage_leaf_digests}|0x0007 LocalDurableArtifactOutput{active_owner_ref:StrongRef<ArtifactOutputDeliveryRecord<Local>>,lineage_ref:StrongRef<ResultCapabilityLineage>,selected_owner_state_and_lineage_leaf_digests}|0x0008 MetaDurableArtifactOutput{active_owner_ref:StrongRef<ArtifactOutputDeliveryRecord<Meta>>,lineage_ref:StrongRef<ResultCapabilityLineage>,selected_owner_state_and_lineage_leaf_digests}|0x0009 LocalMergeOutcome{ledger_root_ref:StrongRef<BranchMergeLedgerRoot>,selected_token_and_leaf_digest,required_header_role:Local}|0x000a MetaMergeOutcome{ledger_root_ref:StrongRef<BranchMergeLedgerRoot>,selected_token_and_leaf_digest,required_header_role:Meta}|0x000b LocalReadYourWrites{lineage_root_ref:StrongRef<ReadYourWritesCapabilityLineageRoot<Local>>,selected_floor_set_and_leaf_digest}|0x000c MetaReadYourWrites{lineage_root_ref:StrongRef<ReadYourWritesCapabilityLineageRoot<Meta>>,selected_floor_set_and_leaf_digest}`; every other tag is reserved-invalid. Each proof byte-matches the selected replay ref, current state root, subject identity, current capability commitment, generation, and complete authority header. `DurableCapabilityLegacyCurrentMembershipProof` is the migration-only `u16` union `0x0001 TxnOutcome{lineage_root_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<TxnCapabilityLineageRoot<Local>>>,selected_leaf_digest}|0x0002 ResumeSubscriptionCursor{active_owner_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<SubscriptionCursorDeliveryRecord<Local>>>,lineage_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<ResultCapabilityLineage>>,selected_owner_state_and_lineage_leaf_digests}|0x0003 ResumeBufferedResult{active_owner_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<ResultIndependentRetentionRecord<Local>>>,lineage_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<ResultCapabilityLineage>>,selected_owner_state_and_lineage_leaf_digests}|0x0004 ResumeDurableArtifactOutput{active_owner_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<ArtifactOutputDeliveryRecord<Local>>>,lineage_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<ResultCapabilityLineage>>,selected_owner_state_and_lineage_leaf_digests}|0x0005 MergeOutcome{ledger_root_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<BranchMergeLedgerRoot>>,selected_token_and_leaf_digest}|0x0006 ReadYourWrites{lineage_root_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedLegacyLocalArtifactRef<ReadYourWritesCapabilityLineageRoot<Local>>>,selected_floor_set_and_leaf_digest}`; every other tag is reserved-invalid. Every ref in that union must select `Successor`, the same `CertifiedRoleTransitionSuccessorRef`, source Local prefix, and legacy promise class as the selected legacy replay; together they byte-match the frozen Local current owner/lineage leaf, subject identity, capability commitment, generation, and complete Local authority header. `DurableCapabilityCurrentMembershipBasis` is the exact embedded union `0x0001 SameRole{proof:DurableCapabilityCurrentMembershipProof}|0x0002 LegacyLocalToMetaMigration{proof:DurableCapabilityLegacyCurrentMembershipProof}`. CurrentLocal/CurrentMeta accept only SameRole with the matching role; LegacyLocalToMetaMigration accepts only the migration arm, so a raw Local strong ref can never occur in a Meta-owned validation object. `ReadYourWritesCapabilityLineageKey` is exactly `{database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch,role_and_group,subject_basis_identity,capability_lineage_token_digest}`. `ReadYourWritesCapabilityTerminalTombstone<Role>` is exactly `{lineage_key:ReadYourWritesCapabilityLineageKey,terminal_authority_commitment:TerminalAuthorityCommitment<Role>,subject_basis_identity,public_floor_set_commitment,last_capability_commitment,last_generation,expiry_evidence_ref:StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>,required_subject:ReadYourWritesCapabilityBytes,required_classification:Expired,nonreuse_and_lookup_floor,body_digest:BodyDigest<ReadYourWritesCapabilityTerminalTombstone<Role>>}` and carries no replay ref or capability bytes. `ReadYourWritesCapabilityLineageState<Role>` is the exact `u16` union `0x0001 Current{current_replay_ref:StrongRef<ReadYourWritesCapabilityReplayRecord>,current_capability_commitment,current_generation,subject_basis_identity,floor_set_commitment}|0x0002 CurrentWithConsumedPredecessor{current_replay_ref:StrongRef<ReadYourWritesCapabilityReplayRecord>,predecessor_replay_ref:StrongRef<ReadYourWritesCapabilityReplayRecord>,current_capability_commitment,predecessor_capability_commitment,current_generation,consuming_request_digest,recovery_until:SuccessorAcknowledgedOrSubjectTerminal,subject_basis_identity,floor_set_commitment}|0x0003 ExpiredTombstone{tombstone_ref:StrongRef<ReadYourWritesCapabilityTerminalTombstone<Role>>}`; every other tag is reserved-invalid. `ReadYourWritesCapabilityLineageRoot<Role>` is exactly `{role_and_group,generation,entries:CanonicalMap<ReadYourWritesCapabilityLineageKey,ReadYourWritesCapabilityLineageState<Role>>,root_digest:BodyDigest<ReadYourWritesCapabilityLineageRoot<Role>>}`. For each grouped subject/action, generation emits one row for every listed concrete subject, row-declared validation context, and compatible concrete presentation tag; CurrentLocal pairs only with the corresponding Local presentation arm, CurrentMeta only with the corresponding Meta arm, and LegacyLocalToMetaMigration only with ReadyChannelMeta. ReadyChannel expands again over `NativeFgp|Http2|Grpc|WebSocket`. It then emits one row per allowed replay relation and outcome: Current -> `CurrentAccepted`; ConsumedImmediatePredecessor -> `ConsumedPredecessorExactRetry`; MigratedConsumedExactRetry -> the same-named outcome. Current Local/Meta rows allow only the row-declared `Exact|Narrowed` authority relation; every migration row requires `Narrowed`. Every row fixes the matching concrete `TimeBoundSubject` arm, `TimeValidationEvidence::Usable`, canonical action-scope recipe, current-state predicate named by the direct consumer, and exactly one retention class. Current rows for `TxnReattach`, `TxnRenew`, `ResultRotateResume`, `SubscriptionPause`, `SubscriptionResumeAfterPauseOrDisconnect`, all three subscription ACK actions, `ArtifactOutputResume`, and `ReadYourWritesWait` can select a successor and therefore use `ThroughInstalledSuccessorAcknowledgedOrSubjectTerminal`; their exact ConsumedImmediatePredecessor retry rows only return an already-installed successor and use `ThroughConsumerTerminal`. Other status, admission, merge, result ACK/release, subscription close, and artifact ACK/release Current rows also use `ThroughConsumerTerminal`; an action that terminally disposes its subject remains there until the exact receipt/tombstone resolution. Audit status uses `ThroughAuditReceiptResolution`. Initial `PostActivationCapabilityMigrate` Current rows can select a LiveSuccessor entry and use `ThroughCapabilityMigrationIndexTerminal`, while MigratedConsumedExactRetry rows only return that existing entry and use `ThroughConsumerTerminal`. The two selection classes require the downstream resolution arm above, so a post-validation CAS loser or other terminal consumer that selected no successor/index entry cannot leak its evidence. No generated row admits a management handle, embedded owner token, Bolt DISCARD/RESET, Shard context, negative-time status classifier, or a presentation class absent from the table.

Each concrete row ID is `dcv:v1:<subject-u16>:<action-u16>:<context-u16>:<presentation-outer-u16>-<presentation-nested-u16>:<replay-u16>:<authority-relation-u16>:<outcome-u16>:<retention-u16>`. Every `u16` is exactly four lowercase hexadecimal digits without `0x`; presentation nested is the ReadyChannel surface or Bolt request-kind tag and is `0000` only for Embedded. Thus the ID encodes the complete presentation cell, is at most 64 ASCII bytes (and therefore within the registered 128-byte field bound), and cannot collide across nested surfaces. Raw capability bytes, MAC bytes/material, protected subject fields, tenant/principal/public handles, and future command/result/root identities are forbidden.

- ResumeBufferedResult: rotate/resume current or exact predecessor retry; ACK and explicit release current only, with terminal retry authorized by the action-specific receipt/tombstone rather than reclassifying the capability.

ACK/release/client-control receipts are the later authority objects, but their construction rows must consume and retain this exact validation evidence when a durable capability is the presented source. I was asked to name the categories of transcript entry that no cohort assert

column, so ANY column change on a RETAINED (pre-erratum) row moves the hash with
every count intact.

  e0245f1bf4c183fd   + two post-erratum unions filtered
  236efa5babe190fe   the floor
  ----
  still 1 hash apart with EVERY line-level difference accounted for.

=== THE LARGER FINDING, STATED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER ===

NO ADMISSIBLE EXTENSION REACHES THE FLOOR, and the reason is structural rather
than a missing cohort.

The floor was computed over 8a704c2's RECONSTRUCTION — the raw registries put
through the filter and undo set AS IT STOOD AT THAT COMMIT. My diff compares
today's reconstruction against 8a704c2's RAW FILE, because the raw file is the
only artifact of that commit that still exists. Those are different objects, and
the 2 undo-touched fields plus 3 rename-touched unions are direct evidence of
the gap: they differ for no reason other than that a transform ran.

Reaching 236efa5b therefore requires reconstructing with 8a704c2's FILTER SET,
not today's. That set has been extended many times since — each extension is a
lossy narrowing, and nothing in the transcript or the registries records which
rows each one removed. The extensions are not invertible.

This is the same shape as fgdb-7yo9's answer one level up: 7yo9 proved the
PRE-REPIN value bdbcdc27ccd92518 is unrecoverable; this proves the FLOOR
236efa5babe190fe is likewise unreachable from today's namespace by any filter or
undo. The witness cannot be greened by extension.

WHAT I DID NOT DO, DELIBERATELY: move the pin, weaken the assert, or pick the
extension that happens to land closest. e0245f1b is not the floor and pretending
it is would repeat 8a704c2 exactly.

=== WHAT THE OWNER MUST NOW RULE ON ===

Three options, none of which an agent may take:
  (a) re-pin to the current reconstruction — repeats 8a704c2, destroys the
      remaining signal, and makes the assert say only "today equals today";
  (b) retire the assert and keep the witness as a pure drift DETECTOR between
      consecutive HEADs, which is what it has actually been since 8a704c2;
  (c) rebuild the historical namespace from an explicit, versioned manifest of
      what the pre-erratum set contained, rather than by subtracting cohorts
      from the present — the only option that restores it as a proof of history.

The red on main is real and will not clear by itself under (a)-forbidden rules.
