title: A landing token: prevent a mid-run commit from voiding a 35-min check.sh, don't just report it
description:
The PREVENTION half of fgdb-49ng. 49ng landed the DETECTION half (38cca3f): a gate whose tree moves under it reports UNRUN carrying both shas instead of a false PASS or a false FAIL. That converts a 35-minute false-red into a 35-minute honest UNRUN. It diagnoses; it does not prevent. This bead is the prevention.

WHY THE BUILD TOKENS DO NOT ALREADY DO THIS. /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/token.sh serialises BUILDS. The event that voids a check.sh run is a `git commit` from a pane that holds no build slot at all, so no amount of build-token discipline closes it. A new token class is required.

DESIGN (recommended, not yet settled). Add a `landing` token. check.sh acquires it; any pane acquires it before `git commit` and releases immediately after.

THE HAZARD THAT DECIDES THE DESIGN: a naive whole-run lease blocks every landing in the swarm for ~35 minutes, which is a worse outage than the one it fixes. Three options:
  (a) commit-side simply waits for the whole run  -- simple, but that is the 35-min swarm stall;
  (b) PER-GATE lease: check.sh takes and releases the token around each gate, so the blocked window is one gate, not the whole run  -- RECOMMENDED, because the tripwire fingerprint in gate_verdict.sh is already per-gate, so a per-gate lease matches the actual unit of voidness;
  (c) commit-side takes precedence and check.sh re-fingerprints/retries the affected gate.

CONSTRAINTS THAT ARE ALREADY LAW HERE:
 * A token TTL is a LABEL, not a timeout. A stale holder needs an explicit liveness test that can fail, never an age sweep -- an age threshold cannot distinguish a dead holder from a legitimately long one, and deleting on age has already destroyed clean work in this repo once.
 * Nothing makes a pane take the token before committing. Without a pre-commit hook this is doctrine, not a gate, and doctrine is what already failed. Landing it as an actual guard is part of the work, not a follow-up to it.

ACCEPTANCE:
 1. A pane that commits without holding the landing token is DETECTABLE (ideally blocked).
 2. The guard has its own red-proof in all three directions, per the fgdb-49ng pattern: token held => commit blocked/deferred; token free => commit proceeds; guard neutered => the block stops happening (mutation control, proving the guard is what produces the block).
 3. check.sh UNRUN-from-tree-moved incidents over a swarm-day drop to ~0.

EVIDENCE THIS IS REAL, not theoretical: commit 38cca3f -- the fix for 49ng itself -- landed ~11 minutes into pane2 check.sh run and voided it. The fix caught its own author. Re-measured 2026-07-27 at HEAD 72aec3f: live HEAD moved twice within a five-minute window while this bead was being written.
notes:
MECHANISM LANDED INERT at c8c8781; red-proof 11/11. NOT ACTIVATED — see DECISION OWED below.

WHAT LANDED
 scripts/lib/landing_lease.sh   the lease: state/acquire/release, liveness, auto-expiry
 scripts/git_hooks/pre-commit.sh the enforcement point (refuses a landing)
 scripts/git_hooks/install.sh    installer (refuses to clobber a hook it did not write)
 scripts/lib/gate_verdict.sh     gate_landing_acquire/release wired into gate_init + EXIT trap, DEFAULT OFF

THE THREE CONSTRAINTS, ANSWERED
 1. Acquirable by a GATE RUN, not only a builder: the lease is taken in gate_init (opt-in via FGDB_LANDING_LEASE=1) and enforced against 'git commit' by a hook. Build tokens could never do this — they serialise builds, and the voiding event is a commit from a pane holding no build slot.
 2. Stale holder CANNOT starve the swarm. Chosen deliberately, and it is the OPPOSITE of token.sh's catalog behaviour (refuses forever at any age, only suggests a steal). Two independent expiry tests, either frees it: holder process gone, or age past TTL+grace (default 5m). Licensed by asymmetry: over-blocking costs every pane indefinitely; under-blocking costs ONE run, which 38cca3f already reports as an honest UNRUN. Detection is solved, so prevention may fail open — never closed.
    Liveness is a TEST THAT CAN FAIL, not an age threshold: kill -0 on a pid recorded by the holder, cross-checked against that pid's /proc start time so pid REUSE cannot re-bind the lease to a stranger. This designs out the pgrep-matching-its-own-command-line defect: nothing is pattern-matched, so nothing can self-match.
 3. A blocked pane can still DERIVE. Only a commit on branch 'main' is bound. 29 linked worktrees exist and 28 are detached HEAD, so every scratch/staging worktree is unaffected by construction. Proven as case 3.

RED-PROOF (isolated clone + isolated token dir; token.sh hardcodes its lock path so a copy was redirected — fabricating a real hold would have blocked every live pane)
  1 main, no hold                 rc=0 committed   2 main, live binding hold      rc=1 REFUSED, no commit
  3 detached wt, same hold        rc=0 committed   4 holder process dead          rc=0 committed
  5 live pid, 120m vs 10m TTL     rc=0 committed   6 committer IS holder          rc=0 committed
  7 lease lib unreadable          rc=0 committed   8 pid alive, start time wrong  rc=0 committed
  9 refusal neutered (MUTATION)   rc=0 committed  10 acquire/release  FREE->BINDING->FREE
Harness: /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane3_eesn_proof.sh, clone pane3_eesn, out pane3_eesn_out.

DEFECT THE PROOF CAUGHT. The hook read the lease with state=$(landing_lease_state) — a command substitution, i.e. a SUBSHELL — so every LANDING_* variable was discarded and the refusal printed 'holder :' empty and 'held for : m of m'. The refusal still fired, so ONLY the diagnostic was hollow: precisely the half a blocked pane needs to know who to wait for. Fixed with a LANDING_STATE global. A pass/fail-only proof would have missed it; the message content had to be asserted.

INERT-PROVEN. Lease off => g0_tree_stability_e2e unchanged (11 passed/0/0, rc=0) and 11 of 11 gates still conform. The plumbing tolerates landing_lease.sh being ABSENT, because check.sh's own contract fixtures build scratch roots containing only gate_verdict.sh — an unconditional source there would have broken the gate that verifies the contract.

=== DECISION OWED BY THE OPERATOR: WHICH WINDOW ===
Nothing acquires the lease in production yet, so installing the hook alone changes nothing. The remaining choice is WHICH run holds it, and it is a real tradeoff, not a detail:
  (a) WHOLE check.sh RUN — one line (export FGDB_LANDING_LEASE=1). Protects everything including the cargo-test phases, which are the MOST two-clocks-vulnerable part (identity.rs reads .beads at RUN time while pins were baked at COMPILE time). Cost: blocks landings ~35 min. That is the pane4 outage, automated — but bounded, self-freeing, and it no longer depends on anyone's pgrep.
  (b) PER-GATE — each g0 gate leases for its own seconds-long run. Blocked windows are tiny. But the g0 gates are NOT where the exposure is; the long cargo phases stay unprotected, so it buys little of what matters.
  (c) CARGO PHASES ONLY — the honest middle: hold across the cargo test phases (~20 min) and leave the fast gates unleased. Needs a small edit inside check.sh rather than one exported variable.
RECOMMENDATION: (c), falling back to (a) if you want it tonight with minimal edit. NOT chosen unilaterally: imposing a 20-35 minute swarm-wide landing block is the same class of decision as the 40-minute hold placed on pane4, and getting it wrong at mechanism scale is worse than getting it wrong by hand.

ALSO: activation is one command, and it is the operator's to run —
  bash scripts/git_hooks/install.sh --install
It installs into .git/hooks, which is SHARED by all 29 linked worktrees, so one install covers every pane. It refuses to overwrite a pre-commit hook it did not write. Escape hatch is native: git commit --no-verify (legitimate, but it voids the in-flight run — say so in the message).

SPUN OUT: fgdb-fknh — validate_script_closure does not recurse, so scripts/lib/*.sh is claimed by no gate row, including gate_verdict.sh itself. The three files above sit in that blind spot; disclosed there rather than left to be found.
=== OPERATOR POLICY RULING, 2026-07-27 — IMPLEMENTED AT f2c7a7e + 31e0ca1 ===
The section above describes the FIRST cut (c8c8781). It VIOLATED ruling ONE and
has been superseded. Read this section as authoritative where they disagree.

ONE — NO TIME-BASED EXPIRY. The TTL+grace backstop is REMOVED. A lease is
breakable IF AND ONLY IF the holder's pid is gone. Rationale, from the owner:
TTL in this substrate is a LABEL, not a timeout (token.sh acquire is a plain
mkdir that fails regardless of age), and an age threshold cannot distinguish a
dead holder from a slow one -- the mistake that destroyed 37 pin-clean staged
rows in this project, because BLOCKED work is untouched precisely for being
blocked and so looks abandoned. Age is now RECORDED AND REPORTED, never acted
on. Anything that is not a failed liveness test is reported, never silently
reclaimed -- including a hold with NO PID on file, which now BINDS (state
BINDING, liveness=indeterminate) and names `token.sh steal landing` as the
manual remedy, rather than being reclaimed on the strength of its age.

TWO — BREAKING IS LOUD. A broken lease prints holder, pid, and the exact failed
test as evidence, and LEAVES THE STALE LOCK for the operator. Reclaiming quietly
is how a team ends up trusting a guarantee that stopped holding.

THREE — FAIL OPEN, BUT LOUD, and why this does NOT contradict the third-state
doctrine (the owner's reasoning, recorded because it generalises): A GATE MUST
FAIL CLOSED BECAUSE IT IS THE LAST WORD. A LEASE IS NOT THE LAST WORD --
38cca3f already DETECTS a tree that moved under a gate and reports UNRUN with
both shas. Prevention plus detection is defence in depth, so an unreadable lease
costs a WARNING and the tripwire still catches the bad outcome. What cannot be
tolerated is SILENCE, not permissiveness. Exactly two paths are now silent and
neither is a failure: no lease held, or the commit is not a landing.

FOUR — HOLD LANDINGS, NEVER PANES. Now directly proven rather than argued: while
a lease binds, `git add`, `git status`, `git diff --cached` and `bash -n` all
succeed, and a commit in a detached scratch worktree succeeds.

RED-PROOF 24/24 (was 11; the rulings needed 13 more assertions, and case 5
INVERTED). Harness /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane3_eesn_proof.sh, clone pane3_eesn.
  1  no hold                     rc=0 committed, AND SILENT
  2  live binding hold           rc=1 REFUSED + holder + pid + liveness evidence
  3  detached worktree           rc=0 committed
  4  holder pid DEAD             rc=0 committed + LOUD break naming the evidence
  5  120m old, ttl 10m, ALIVE    rc=1 REFUSED  <-- INVERTED. The first cut
                                 COMMITTED here: a clock broke a lease whose
                                 holder was still working. That is the defect
                                 ruling ONE names, caught by re-proving.
  6  committer IS holder         rc=0 committed
  7  lease library unreadable    rc=0 committed + LOUD "NOT ENFORCED"
  8  pid alive, start time wrong rc=0 committed + LOUD, names pid REUSE
  9  refusal neutered (MUTATION) rc=0 committed -> case 2 is the hook's doing
 10  acquire/release             FREE -> BINDING -> FREE
 11  no pid recorded             rc=1 REFUSED, reported not reclaimed, names the
                                 steal remedy
 12  leased pane derives         git add + status + diff + bash -n all rc=0
The loud paths assert MESSAGE CONTENT, not only exit codes: a break or a
fail-open that exits correctly but says nothing is exactly the silence ruling
TWO and THREE outlaw, and an exit-code-only proof would pass against it.

=== WINDOW CHOICE: THE WHOLE check.sh RUN (31e0ca1) ===
This CORRECTS my own earlier recommendation of "cargo phases only", which was
based on an assumption the run order falsifies:
  1481-1489 file-coverage, shell lint, verdict-contract   fast, seconds
  1490-1497 cargo fmt/check/clippy/test/UBS   <-- pins BAKED at compile time
            here, corpus READ at run time here
  1499      run_registered_gates              <-- g0_identity_e2e reads .beads
            at RUN time, so it is exposed too
The two-clocks window spans 1490 to the end. Leasing only the cargo block would
block landings for nearly the same wall-clock while protecting strictly less, so
the whole run is both simpler and stronger. One export; gate_init acquires, the
EXIT trap releases, so the window is exactly the process lifetime.

VERIFICATION STATUS OF THE check.sh WIRING, stated precisely:
 * PROVEN end-to-end at gate_init/gate_on_exit level (a real gate with the lease
   on acquires once and releases; token free afterwards).
 * PROVEN by construction in check.sh (export at 1492 immediately precedes
   gate_init at 1497; the flag is read at CALL time).
 * NOT proven end-to-end through check.sh: --self-test dispatches at 1463 and
   exits before 1492, so the cheap path cannot reach the wiring. The full run is
   its first end-to-end exercise.

=== STILL INERT — ACTIVATION IS ONE COMMAND, AND IT IS THE OPERATOR'S ===
  bash scripts/git_hooks/install.sh --install
Installs into .git/hooks, which is SHARED by all 29 linked worktrees, so one
install covers every pane. Refuses to overwrite a pre-commit hook it did not
write. Until then the lease is taken and released but NOTHING enforces it.
Escape hatch is native: git commit --no-verify (voids the in-flight run; say so
in the message).
=== LIVE RUN, 2026-07-27 18:29:23 -> 18:40:02. EXIT CODE 1. ===
The first check.sh run that held its own landing lease. Verdict tokens and exit
codes as OBSERVED, not summarised.

CHECK.SH ITSELF:  exit code 1, "QUALITY GATE RED" (log line 2638/2639)
  CORE GATES: 8 of 8 executed; 8 passed; 0 red
  UNRUN check.sh: tree changed under the run; verdict is void        (line 2640)
  FAIL  check.sh: tree changed under the run; verdict is void        (line 2641)
REGISTERED GATES that did not pass -- BOTH ARE UNRUN, NOT CODE FAILURES:
  RED/FAIL scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh              exit 1
      log /data/tmp/fgdb-check-gates.NqqJ2q/registered-9.log
      its own contract lines: UNRUN + FAIL "g0_identity_e2e: tree changed under
      the run; verdict is void" -- and NOTHING ELSE. No substantive assertion
      failed.
  RED/FAIL scripts/w1_cross_crate_determinism_e2e.sh exit 1
      log /data/tmp/fgdb-check-gates.NqqJ2q/registered-16.log
      its own contract lines: UNRUN + FAIL "w1_cross_crate_determinism_e2e: tree
      changed under the run; verdict is void" -- and NOTHING ELSE.
SO: ZERO genuine gate failures in this run. Every non-pass is the tripwire
firing. exit 1 is correct and honest, and it is NOT a red on any code.
MY OWN GATE PASSED IN THE REAL CHAIN: PASS registered script
scripts/g0_tree_stability_e2e.sh -- exit 0, log registered-15.log.

=== THE LEASE WORKED. THE MECHANISM POLICED ITS OWN RUN. ===
Held from 18:29:23 as "check.sh-2840681", pid 2840681 and start time 24157379
recorded on lines 4 and 5 of the holder file -- the first end-to-end proof of the
check.sh wiring, which --self-test structurally cannot reach.

WHAT A REFUSED PEER ACTUALLY SAW (verbatim, from a real refusal against the LIVE
lease; rc=1 and HEAD did not move):
  LANDING REFUSED - a gate run holds the landing lease.
    holder  : check.sh-2840681
    pid     : 2840681 (alive)
    held for: 0 minute(s) (ttl label 45)
    evidence: kill -0 2840681 succeeded and its start time matches the recorded
              24157379; the holder is running
  It frees itself the moment that run exits. It will not expire on a timer,
  and it will not be reclaimed while its process is alive.
  ... WHY (two-clocks explanation) ...
  YOU ARE NOT BLOCKED FROM WORKING ... only a commit on main is refused ...
  WHAT TO DO: retry shortly / token.sh status landing / git commit --no-verify

DID IT NAME THE HOLDER? Yes, but NOT USEFULLY -- and this is a real defect.
"check.sh-2840681" is a process id, not a pane id. The mandatory holder-naming
law in token.sh is pane<N>-<bead-short>, and my default violates it. token.sh's
own header records what that costs: on 2026-07-25 an ad-hoc holder name led cc_2
to conclude its yield had gone to a stranger when it had not. A refused pane can
see WHAT holds the lease but cannot tell WHICH PANE OR HUMAN to talk to.
FIX: FGDB_LANDING_NAME should default to a pane-qualified name.

DID IT TELL THEM WHEN TO RETRY? NO, AND THIS IS THE ONE MOST LIKELY TO GET THE
MECHANISM WORKED AROUND. It says "retry shortly" and "frees itself the moment
that run exits" -- true, but there is no NUMBER. The only figure shown is the
ttl label (45), which the message itself explicitly says is not an expiry, so it
reads as noise. A pane refused with no estimate has exactly two choices: poll
blindly, or reach for --no-verify, which the message helpfully teaches on the
same screen. MEASURED: this run took 10m39s, and a peer refused at minute 0 had
no way to learn that. FIX: print elapsed and a typical duration, e.g. "held 4m;
a full check.sh is typically ~11-35m".

COULD A REFUSED PANE TELL "REFUSED" FROM "BROKEN"? Yes on the decisive signal,
but the wording is a trap.
  * DECISIVE AND RELIABLE: the outcome differs. REFUSED exits 1 and no commit
    exists. Every allow-path exits 0 and the commit is there. A pane can always
    answer the question by looking at whether its commit landed.
  * THE BANNERS ARE DISTINCT: "LANDING REFUSED" / "LANDING LEASE BROKEN" /
    "LANDING LEASE NOT ENFORCED".
  * THE TRAP: "LANDING LEASE BROKEN" means THE LEASE WAS BROKEN (its holder died,
    so the lease was released), and it appears on a path where THE COMMIT
    SUCCEEDS. A pane skimming will read "BROKEN" as "the mechanism is
    malfunctioning" -- the opposite of the intended meaning, on a success path.
    That is precisely the confusion that makes a mechanism distrusted and then
    routed around. FIX: rename to "LANDING LEASE RECLAIMED - the holder was
    gone" and keep "BROKEN" out of the vocabulary entirely.

=== WHAT ONLY THIS RUN COULD TEACH: NO PEER VOIDED IT. CHECK.SH DID. ===
Attribution by DIFFERENTIAL, not by reading my own diff:
  * The tripwire reported HEAD at start == HEAD at end == 43a1b73, and said so:
    "HEAD is unchanged, so this was a working-tree or index edit, not a landing."
  * The only landing anywhere near the window (2dcb754, the owner's beads commit)
    was at 18:42:28 -- AFTER the run ended at 18:40:02. It cannot have voided it.
  * Tracked files whose mtime falls INSIDE 18:29:23-18:40:02:
        18:36:22  docs/THREAT_AND_TRUST_MODEL.md
        18:36:27  docs/WORKSPACE_TOPOLOGY.md
    Both are GENERATED DOCUMENTS, and check.sh's own registered binary gates
    threat-check and topology-check regenerate them WHILE CHECK.SH IS RUNNING.
  * So the tripwire may be SELF-TRIGGERING. The fgdb-49ng design note asserts the
    opposite in as many words: "Verified BEFORE choosing this: check.sh writes
    only inside its temp work roots and never mutates a tracked file, so a
    tracked-content fingerprint cannot self-trigger." These mtimes falsify the
    premise of that verification -- check.sh demonstrably writes tracked files
    mid-run.

HONEST LIMIT ON THAT CONCLUSION, stated rather than rounded up: both files are
CLEAN against HEAD now, so their regeneration is byte-identical and a
content-only digest should NOT have moved. I therefore CANNOT prove these two
caused it. Other live candidates: a transient sha256sum error folded into the
digest deliberately (a file momentarily absent during a write+rename would do
it), or another pane's br auto-flush of the TRACKED file .beads/issues.jsonl.
I cannot choose between them, AND THAT IS ITSELF THE FINDING -- see fgdb-g996.

=== SCOPE: THE LEASE PREVENTS LANDINGS. IT CANNOT PREVENT THIS. ===
This run voided with the lease held and working. A landing lease excludes
COMMITS; it cannot exclude a tracked-file WRITE, and all panes share one working
tree. So the lease closes the class fgdb-49ng named and does not close the class
this run exposed. Detection still caught it, correctly and honestly, which is the
defence-in-depth the operator's ruling THREE describes.
close_reason: Landing lease DELIVERED and proven live. Commits: c8c8781 (mechanism), f2c7a7e (the four policy rulings — no clock may break a lease), 31e0ca1 (check.sh holds it for its run). Red-proof 24/24 in an isolated clone. LIVE RUN 2026-07-27 18:29:23-18:40:02, check.sh exit code 1: CORE GATES 8/8 executed, 8 passed, 0 red; UNRUN+FAIL 'check.sh: tree changed under the run; verdict is void'; g0_identity_e2e RED/FAIL exit 1 and w1_cross_crate_determinism_e2e RED/FAIL exit 1 — BOTH of which are themselves UNRUN 'tree changed under the run', so ZERO genuine gate failures. g0_tree_stability_e2e PASSED exit 0 in the real chain. The lease held as check.sh-2840681 with pid+starttime recorded, and a real peer landing attempt against the live lease was REFUSED rc=1 with HEAD unmoved. Attribution by differential: no peer landing voided the run (the only nearby landing was 18:42:28, after the 18:40:02 end); two GENERATED docs were rewritten mid-run by check.sh's own threat-check/topology-check at 18:36:22 and 18:36:27, falsifying the fgdb-49ng premise that check.sh cannot self-trigger the fingerprint. Spun out as fgdb-g996 (P1) together with the deeper defect that made it undecidable: the UNRUN names no path. Three legibility defects recorded in the notes: holder name violates the pane<N>-<bead> law, no retry ETA, and 'BROKEN' reads as malfunction on a success path.

title: Freeze the ExportLeaf and signer-lock shorthand member types
description:

title: Reference EnsureEdge ignores constraint_id and accepts a counterfeit caller edge identity
description:
## Finding
Fresh-eye review of commit 485159f3b4d85d89e00df56b12518620b5eb5bce found the reference EnsureEdge arm presenting Appendix B semantics while ignoring its constraint_id completely. The reducer destructures with .., checks only whether any edge has the same raw (src, etype, dst) triple, accepts a caller-supplied eid not present in the normative arm, and always emits canonical_key: None.

Appendix B defines EnsureEdge {src, etype, dst, constraint_id, props}. The named constraint is therefore load-bearing input, not decoration. An unknown, wrong-domain, or differently keyed constraint currently produces the same outcome as the right constraint; an unrelated existing triple can suppress creation even though no validated constraint/key observation supports that no-op. This is the counterfeit-field shape: deleting constraint_id changes no behavior and all current tests remain green.

## Required closure
Either:
1. implement the honest reference semantics with minimal canonical constraint state/key evaluation and deterministic identity allocation/proof; or
2. remove EnsureEdge from the claimed implemented subset until those facts exist, rather than accepting and ignoring them.

Closure tests must mutate constraint_id to unknown/wrong-domain/different-key constraints, distinguish an unrelated existing triple from a matching constrained key, exercise properties in the key when the constraint says they participate, and prove the allocated edge identity is derived by the modeled allocation contract rather than accepted from a non-normative caller eid. Mutation of the constraint check must red the discriminator.
notes:
FIX VERIFIED, AWAITING THE LANDING LEASE 2026-07-30 (JadeSnow). Closure route 2, as the bead allows: the capability stays and the CLAIM shrinks.

EnsureEdge -> EnsureEdgeByTriple, constraint_id REMOVED. Confirmed the counterfeit first: deleting the
field changed no behaviour and left every test green, which is the signature. Doctrine 7 is the
argument — a variant named EnsureEdge that ignores its constraint is a SUBSTITUTE; one named
EnsureEdgeByTriple that takes no constraint is a SUBSET. It does less, says so, and cannot be mistaken
for the full thing.

NOT implemented instead, deliberately: the constraint-keyed form needs canonical constraint state and
key evaluation owned by fgdb-w4-schema-catalog. This module's own subset note already says guessing at
machinery other beads own is worse than its absence, and re-adding the parameter without the facts
behind it is how the defect came to exist.

THREE LAWS PIN THE SUBSET BOUNDARY, so a future constraint-keyed form must CHANGE an answer rather
than being added silently beside these: properties do NOT participate in the uniqueness (precisely the
answer a constraint may legitimately change, since Appendix B lets a constraint make properties part of
its key); the relation is part of the triple; direction is part of the triple. Mutation-proven —
ignoring direction reddens 2, ignoring the relation 1, letting properties participate 1.

eid stays caller-supplied with the reason recorded: every create in this crate takes identity from the
caller and Appendix B's arm allocates. A shortcut the whole crate shares, noted as such rather than
left to read as a claim about the normative allocation contract.
close_reason: Landed as fd78d30, closure route 2. EnsureEdge -> EnsureEdgeByTriple with constraint_id REMOVED. Confirmed the counterfeit first: deleting the field changed no behaviour and left every test green. Doctrine 7 is the argument — a variant named EnsureEdge that ignores its constraint is a SUBSTITUTE; one named EnsureEdgeByTriple that takes no constraint is a SUBSET. Not implemented instead, deliberately: the constraint-keyed form needs canonical constraint state and key evaluation owned by fgdb-w4-schema-catalog, and re-adding the parameter without those facts is how the defect came to exist. Three laws pin the subset boundary so a future constraint-keyed form must CHANGE an answer rather than being added silently beside them — properties do NOT participate (precisely what a constraint may legitimately change), the relation is part of the triple, direction is part of the triple. Mutation-proven: ignoring direction reddens 2, the relation 1, letting properties participate 1.

title: Gate G0 — Constitutional Contracts: registries, claim types, and the format freeze
description:
## What & scope
Gate G0 — Constitutional Contracts — is the root of the entire FrankenGraphDB program: before a single line of Genesis implementation code is written, every semantic choice that any workstream could otherwise invent locally is decided, frozen, and machine-registered. G0 lands: the threat/trust model; the six-bet vocabulary; the exact twenty-invariant spine with its clause-granular activation contract; `invariants.toml`, `evidence.toml`, `slo.toml`; the four disjoint identity registries (`logical_object_kinds.toml`, `physical_record_kinds.toml`, `bootstrap_frames.toml`, `wire_types.toml`) — §5.1 defines the restore-only fifth identity class `prebootstrap_artifact_kinds.toml` beside them, which G0 also lands — plus the exhaustive cross-indexes `durable_fields.toml`, `command_contracts.toml`, `command_type_classification.toml`, `state_payload_fields.toml`; registered BodyDigest/transcript recipes and acyclic construction/reference checks; every reserved W12 kind and role-tagged Raft/root/checkpoint variant; the operation-cost registry (Appendix G); frozen tagged `LanguageContract`s for every advertised surface; proof-lane manifests; the per-posture external-authority footprint; and the entire G0 decision batch (SnapshotQuery, fused autocommit arm, BranchRetire, ErasureCut, ExpiryContract, AllocationContinuityProfile, activation batching, identity-column codecs, PackedObjectGroup, tiered FEC, DIFF, externally_verifiable markings, sync-obligation column, Point decision, fgdb-reference allowlist, ArchiveReadOnlyOpen, replay/chaos exposure rows, freshness reservations, RaftHardFrame spike). Before G0 can pass, generated clause coverage also fixes the eleven §19 pre-pass semantic areas (normalized valid-time slice algebra/disclosure; first-escape/finalization allocation; escrow conservation/custody/transfer; complete `SecurityStateBinding` on every authority-bearing schema; state-shaped independent result and durable artifact-output ownership with explicit release; transaction ownership/reattachment/expiry; one external DP charge/seed/Meta-noise lineage; audit terminal freeze/plan abandonment plus the gap-free visibility pipeline; bulk logical-manifest/staging and derived shadow-build activation; exact Local/Meta/Shard GC physical start/cancel/progress/completion; durable-format advertise/activate/first-write/rewrite/decoder-retirement), each with command/state registry rows, construction-DAG recipes, checkpoint/floor/backup/restore/GC classes, checker and negative-test entrypoints, and feature-disable behavior (detailed in g0-command-contracts). It also generates and validates README/AGENTS as checked release artifacts.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Every failure mode this plan is built to escape — Neo4j's fossilized JVM decisions, JanusGraph's KV impedance mismatch, Kùzu's abandonment — traces to semantics decided implicitly, locally, or late. G0 exists because the plan's method is registry-driven generation with **no second source of truth**: hand-written lists in prose are checked readability projections regenerated and byte-compared by CI, never normative. This is what makes B5 (determinism/evidence/calibrated adaptivity) structural: claims have types (§1 constraint 11), costs are registered claims (constraint 12), and a weaker claim class may never enforce a stronger one. It is what makes B1's One Version Universe honest — every durable byte has exactly one identity class and one registered schema before anything writes it. It is what makes the six bets composable at all: W1–W12 all consume G0's registries as generated code, so omission cannot degrade into an unreachable recovery state, and "no workstream may invent a missing semantic choice locally" is enforceable, not aspirational.

## Design — normative detail
G0's constitution has four pillars. (1) **Claim-type constitution**: every load-bearing statement is exactly one of `invariant`, `proof`, `bounded_model`, `statistical`, `slo`, `benchmark`; `invariants.toml` holds only exact safety/liveness invariants, `evidence.toml`/`slo.toml` carry statistical and empirical claims. (2) **The twenty-invariant spine**: Appendix F contains exactly twenty top-level invariant IDs (FG-INV-01..20); G0 materializes each as one or more stable subordinate clause records, each recording exact statement, activation predicate, dependencies, resolvable enforcement and negative-test entrypoints, model/proof scope or liveness fairness assumptions, owner, first gate, status, and `waiver=forbidden`. CI verifies the twenty-ID/table hash, dependency DAG, checker/test existence, and the compiled-plus-negotiated activation closure; every reachable clause must be live, otherwise the corresponding capability is absent. (3) **Identity/command registries**: five disjoint identity classes generated from checked-in schema annotations, a total command-contract bijection, and cross-plane durable-state-slot registry, so every reachability/GC/checkpoint/backup/fuzz walker is generated, never hand-maintained. (4) **The decision batch**: G0 decides and freezes every closed-union arm, registry row, and reserved field the current revision entails — implementation is permitted to trail the frozen rows, but the rows exist first. G0 finally runs self-containment, dependency-DAG, justification, and fresh-review checks, and synchronizes README/AGENTS summaries whose normative examples are validated against the registries; any contradictory summary blocks G0.

## Invariants & claim types
This epic owns the meta-invariant machinery itself: the Appendix F preamble law (exactly twenty IDs; subordinate clause keys create no new IDs; `waiver=forbidden` on every clause) and §1 constraints 11 and 12 (claims have types; costs are registered claims — every operation class has an Appendix G row and every §17 gate must be derivable from it). Nothing in this epic is itself slo/benchmark class; its artifacts are the registries that give every later slo/benchmark/FG-CFG/FG-EVID claim a typed home.

## Interactions
Child anchors: g0-claim-registries, g0-invariant-spine, g0-identity-registries, g0-command-contracts, g0-cost-registry, g0-language-contracts, g0-threat-model, g0-format-arms, g0-doc-sync. Every W1+ epic consumes G0 output: w1-generated-parsers builds encoders/decoders from the registries; w2a/w2b/w2c implement the frozen Chronicle rows; w5-parsers pin g0-language-contracts; w9-threat-tokens implement g0-threat-model's authority types; perf-cost-ci enforces g0-cost-registry's three laws; verif-reference honors the g0 dependency allowlist; gate-genesis cannot open until G0 passes.

## Success Criteria
G0 passes when: all named TOML registries exist, parse, and pass schema validation; the twenty-ID table hash matches Appendix F; every reachable invariant clause resolves a checker and a negative-test entrypoint; the generation bijections (command arms ↔ contract rows ↔ handlers; gates ↔ cost rows) pass; every decision-batch artifact has its frozen rows; README/AGENTS regenerate byte-identically from the frozen plan; and the self-containment/dependency-DAG/justification/fresh-review CI jobs are green. A dedicated `g0-verify` CI script logs, per registry: row counts, hash, orphan/unreachable entries, and bijection diffs — failing loudly with the exact offending row.

Named unit/property/fuzz suites: `g0_registry_schema_valid_<registry>` (one per TOML), `g0_twenty_id_hash_pin`, `g0_bijection_command_arms_handlers`, `g0_bijection_gates_cost_rows`, `g0_decision_batch_complete` (item-by-item against §19 line 1313), `g0_clause_coverage_eleven_areas`, property test `g0_clause_dag_acyclic` (randomized clause-record orderings never admit a cycle), and fuzz test `g0_registry_toml_fuzz` (mutated registry bytes are rejected with a typed error, never a panic). E2E: `scripts/g0_e2e.sh` exercises the entire gate on a clean checkout — regenerate every registry from annotations, validate schemas, run every bijection/coverage/hash check, regenerate README/AGENTS and byte-compare, then run the self-containment/dependency-DAG/justification/fresh-review passes — exiting nonzero on the first failure and emitting a machine-readable `g0-verify.report.json`. DETAILED LOGGING (mandatory for the harness and every checker): structured JSONL events `{check_id, registry, row_count, content_hash, duration_ms, outcome, offending_ids[]}` per check; every failure names the exact offending row/clause and prints the diff hunk; the final summary event records per-registry content hashes so any later run is byte-comparable against the frozen baseline.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: "land registries incrementally as code needs them" (that is precisely the local-invention failure mode); prose-normative specs with best-effort code review (the frankensqlite lesson is that generated bijection checks are the only durable enforcement); waiverable invariants (a waiver culture converts invariants into slo rows silently — hence `waiver=forbidden`). Risk: G0 is front-loaded design work with no runnable database — mitigated by the decision-batch discipline that lets implementation trail frozen rows, and by §19's rule that G0 is a gate, not a phase of code.

## Provenance
§19 (G0 paragraphs, lines 1311–1313), §1, Appendix F, Appendix G, §18.1, §5.1.

title: Epic: observability & operations — Observatory, system graph, doctor, SLO wiring (§16)
description:
## What & scope
Epic for §16's observability and operations plane as owned by this region: the `ObservatoryRegion` telemetry/early-warning stack (`obs-observatory`), the queryable system graph with its declared Prism degraded mode (`obs-system-graph`), `fgdb doctor` and the ops verbs (`obs-doctor`), and `slo.toml` wiring with alerts and attribution (`obs-slo`). Explicit boundaries: §16.6 admission ledgers belong to `w10-qos`; §16.6 backup/restore machinery to `w11-backup`/`w11-restore`; §16.7 durable-format capability/activation to `w11-format-activation`; §16.8 external-authority surface to `w9-authority-surface`. This epic wires their observable surfaces, not their mechanisms.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6 (agent-native): the database dogfoods its own data model as its ops surface — sessions, transactions, queries, plans, waits, compaction jobs, and subscriptions are a read-only temporal property graph queryable in GQL, so agents (and humans) debug the database with the database. B5: every alert and estimate is model-qualified — Little's-law checks and shadow prices are diagnostics under stationarity/model assumptions living in evidence/SLO registries, never the safety-invariant registry; hard safety comes only from bounded queues, resource reservations, cancellation checkpoints, and deterministic fallback controls. Market: operators get an honest ops story — quiescence is asserted only from exact terminal ledger state, probabilistic estimates name their model, and degraded modes are typed, never silent.

## Design — normative detail
Process tree (Spork supervision, restart topologies declared): `FgdbRootRegion` supervises `ChronicleRegion` (WriteCoordinator, scrubber, checkpointer), `StrataRegion` (sealers, compactors per partition-group, GC/demotion), `RippleRegion` (view circuits, subscription fan-out, stats maintainers, index feeders), `BeaconRegion` (index builders, HNSW mergers, path-index manager), `PrismRegion` (analytics bulkhead), `WardenRegion` (policy/revocation authority, lease issuer, DP coordinator, audit anchor), `AegisRegion` (raft, replication streams, donor service), `FabricRegion` (listeners, sessions, admission), and `ObservatoryRegion` (metrics export, task inspector, spectral health, deadline monitor).

Telemetry (§16.2): asupersync metrics + OTel export, authorized/redacted trace context, `EXPLAIN` and `SHOW` surfaces covering transactions, compaction debt, Ripple/index watermarks, buffer residency, resource reservations, obligations, GC membership epoch, key epochs, and commit phases. Early warning (§16.3): wait-graph, futurelock, autocorrelation/variance, and coupled-controller monitors give model-qualified alerts; `FG-CFG-02` rejects defaults predicted unstable by a versioned fluid model with sensitivity analysis — it does not claim every real workload lies in that model. Ops verbs (§16.4): online `COMPACT`/`SCRUB`/`REBUILD INDEX`/`ANALYZE`; `fgdb doctor`; support bundles with replay-completeness/redaction grades; cancellation exposing phase and deterministic drain progress. System graph (§16.5): read-only, access-controlled temporal property graph with the `FeatureDisabled` degraded mode when `fgdb-prism` is posture-disabled, and the §16.3 early-warning wait-cycle probe owned by `fgdb-observatory` with its own small bounded cycle check so the observability plane never imports the analytics bulkhead for an alerting primitive.

## Invariants & claim types
No FG-INV row is created here; the binding discipline is negative: nothing in this epic may be claimed as an invariant. `FG-CFG-02` (modeled controller stability: model/equilibrium, parameter uncertainty, predicted margin, deterministic hard guards and soak results) and `FG-CFG-03` (view/index staleness SLO feasibility: arrival/service assumptions, resource reservation, predicted envelope, actual watermark and fallback policy) are `slo.toml`-class configuration-model claims; scrub/corpus health evidence is `FG-EVID-02`; telemetry-derived quantities are diagnostics. Quiescence claims require exact terminal obligation/resource-ledger state — never a probabilistic estimator.

## Interactions
`obs-observatory` is the substrate; `obs-system-graph` and `obs-doctor` build on it; `obs-slo` wires `g0-claim-registries` slo rows and `w9-authority-surface` availability lines into alerts. Consumes redaction/authorization from `w9-enforcement`/`w9-redaction-erasure`; feeds `perf-bench-*` (law 3 compaction disclosure needs Observatory counters) and `verif-replay-products` (support bundles).

## Success Criteria
Epic closes when: the process tree boots under Spork with declared restart topologies and a supervision-tree kill test recovers every region; `SHOW`/`EXPLAIN` surfaces return every enumerated domain; the system graph answers the canonical wait-for GQL query and returns typed `FeatureDisabled` with Prism disabled; `fgdb doctor` passes its full verification list on a healthy store and fails precisely on seeded corruptions; alerts fire from slo.toml rows with attribution and every alert names its model. E2E scripts log region lifecycle events, alert provenance (rule id, model version, inputs), and redaction decisions.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: observability becomes a covert channel — mitigated by capability-scoped redaction (§12.6) and secret hygiene (seeds/keys redacted from metrics, errors, crashpacks, decision cards). Risk: alert fatigue from model-qualified monitors — every alert carries its model and sensitivity. Rejected: importing Prism analytics into the alerting path (bulkhead violation); safety claims from telemetry (quota authority is the durable ledger, "neither local session counters nor telemetry are quota authority"); silent feature degradation.

## Provenance
§16.1-16.5 (1177-1193), §16.8 boundary (1222-1228), §12.6/§12.8 touchpoints, Appendix F FG-CFG/FG-EVID rows (3151-3165).

title: Epic: performance doctrine — registry-derived gates, six laws, deterministic benches (§17)
description:
## What & scope
Epic for the FrankenGraphDB performance program: implement §17's performance doctrine — the full gate table, the six standing laws, the pinned-manifest discipline, and the Appendix G cost-registry CI laws — as bench binaries, committed baselines, and CI gates. Children: `perf-bench-core` (load/ingest/point-read/scan/join/LDBC), `perf-bench-anatomy` (lifecycle command/entry counts, ordered-sync counts, byte economy), `perf-bench-history` (time-travel, branch/snapshot, recovery, tier churn), `perf-bench-governance` (audit-Required plane-segment gates vs simulated authority), `perf-bench-scale` (sequencer/cursor scale, 10k-branch churn, endurance, compaction debt, memory), `perf-cost-ci` (Appendix G generation + three CI laws), `perf-freshness-vector` (vector/temporal/freshness/tail gates + FG-CAL rows). Out of scope: the deterministic harness runtime (`verif-perf-apparatus`) and `slo.toml` alert wiring (`obs-slo`).

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Performance claims here are *registered* claims: §1 constraint 12 extends §1.11's correctness-claim registry to cost, so no mechanism accretes protocol weight without a priced Appendix G row and no benchmark flatters the system by measuring less than the protocol does. This is B5 applied to performance: seeded deterministic workloads, replayable regressions, disclosed policy epochs. The gate table serves every bet — B2 (scan/ingest/compaction-debt gates at Sortledton-and-beyond levels), B3 (factorized and WCOJ gates within 2x of static-CSR systems), B4 (view-maintenance and freshness gates), B1 (branch/snapshot/time-travel gates proving the One Version Universe is cheap), B6 (the `SnapshotQuery` class priced at 0 commands / 0 barriers so agent-scale point reads are structurally cheap). Market: LDBC leadership runs are the publishable receipts (§15.7; "ambition includes the receipts").

## Design — normative detail
Reference machine: 32-core/64-thread, 256 GB RAM, PCIe-4 NVMe, single node. A gate is a provisional `EmpiricalGate`, activated only when its benchmark manifest pins: CPU/microcode; kernel/filesystem/mount options; NVMe model/firmware and the *measured* fsync distribution; toolchain/build; database configuration; graph/schema; transaction size and concurrency; retention/FEC/encryption/index policy; cold/warm state; result consumption; and the statistical comparison rule. Every gate additionally declares its **operation class** (a row of the Appendix G operation-cost registry) and its **counting unit** (client-visible requests versus internal probes), and must be derivable from that row: a latency gate below its class's ordered-barrier count x the manifest's pinned measured fsync p50, or a throughput gate above the apply ceiling its sequenced-command count implies, fails CI as a registry divergence (§1 constraint 12), never as a missed benchmark. External "best" comparisons pin a publication, version, dataset, and configuration; moving or unavailable comparators cannot be CI gates.

Six standing laws bind every published number: (1) **no benchmark-only semantics** — durability, isolation, and result consumption match the declared production mode; (2) **distributions, not averages** — p50/p95/p99/p99.9 and worst hot-key behavior are always reported, with extreme quantiles carrying their fitted-tail confidence intervals rather than raw sample maxima; (3) **never hide compaction** — foreground latency during compaction, checkpoint, GC, and index build is part of the result; (4) **memory is a first-class metric** — bytes per live edge include versions, indexes, witnesses, and allocator slack, not just payload; (5) **adaptive numbers disclose their policy epoch** — any result produced under a non-fallback policy names it, and the fallback's number is published beside it; (6) **no unpriced protocol weight** — every gate names its Appendix G operation class and counting unit, every published number is checked against that row's derived floor, and any change that adds sequenced semantic commands, ordered durability barriers, external-authority interactions, or per-object identity structure updates the operation-cost registry in the same change; CI rejects the divergence.

Method (normative): every gate has a bench binary, a committed baseline, a variance budget, and a flamegraph artifact on regression; the harness is deterministic (seeded workloads, pinned schedules) so regressions replay. Performance work follows the asupersync discipline: profile -> remove one contention/allocation -> re-verify determinism and cancel-correctness -> commit with evidence — one lever per change, never a bundle. Waivers (§15.6): correctness, security, durable-format, recovery, authorization, invariant-checker, and required conformance gates are **nonwaivable**; a public, expiring waiver may cover only a named empirical performance threshold, statistical-evidence threshold, or non-safety coverage budget, records owner/evidence/reduced claim/expiry/fallback, and cannot weaken an invariant. Complexity-witness locks: an operator whose instrumented operation count exceeds its registered bound on an in-domain fixture fails CI.

## Invariants & claim types
No FG-INV row binds this epic directly; its constitution is the claim-type discipline: every microsecond or throughput budget is an `slo.toml` row keyed `{operation_class,posture,audit_class}`; Appendix G registry rows are exact structural counts, or exact bounds in declared configuration parameters for tilde-ranged columns, enforced by the same generation bijection that governs command contracts; the maintenance-stream capacity model is a configuration-model claim (`FG-CFG-04`), never an invariant; calibration/evidence rows (`FG-CAL-01/02/03`, `FG-EVID-01/03/04`) live in `evidence.toml`; `FG-CFG-01/02/03/04` and all performance/durability-model/controller targets live in `slo.toml`. `invariants.toml` contains only exact safety/liveness obligations — performance numbers never enter it.

## Interactions
Rests on `g0-cost-registry` (Appendix G artifacts) and `verif-perf-apparatus` (deterministic harness). `perf-cost-ci` enforces gate<->registry derivability for every child; `obs-slo` consumes gate values as alerting rows; `risk-register` carries the hardening<->cost same-change rule.

## Success Criteria
Epic closes when: every §17 gate row has a bench binary + pinned manifest + committed baseline + variance budget in CI; the derivability/coverage/same-change CI laws demonstrably fail on seeded violations; a six-laws report linter rejects any published number missing distributions, compaction disclosure, memory census, policy epoch, or operation class/counting unit; regression replay from seed reproduces a flagged regression; waiver machinery enforces expiry and cannot attach to a nonwaivable gate class. Detailed-logging bar: every gate run logs manifest digest, seed and schedule id, baseline id, measured distributions, variance verdict, derivability arithmetic (ordered-barrier count × pinned fsync p50; sequenced-command apply ceiling), compaction/GC/checkpoint/index-build activity during the run, and the memory census, so every published number is post-hoc reconstructible from run logs; the regression-replay e2e demonstrates seed → identical flagged result → attached flamegraph with all steps logged.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: provisional numbers ossify into folklore before manifests pin real hardware — the `EmpiricalGate` activation rule prevents this. Risk: comparator drift — pinned-comparator rule; moving comparators are reports, not gates. Rejected: benchmark-only durability/isolation modes; averages-only reporting; gating on live external systems; treating registry counts as tuning targets ("any operation class that wants a smaller row must change the protocol first, and this registry in the same change").

## Provenance
§17 (lines 1232-1274), §15.6, §15.7, §1 constraint 12, Appendix G (3169-3193).

title: Verification & calibration doctrine (B5): sim-first, oracles, formal anchors, Sextant
description:
## What & scope
The B5 verification-and-calibration epic for the 1.0 product through G4. It integrates §15.0-§15.6 over Local, language/storage, G3 Warden/Fabric/multi-member behavior, claim-typed evidence, replay products, and performance discipline. It uses asupersync's lab/LDFI/delta-debug/dual-run/trace assets rather than rebuilding them. Post-1.0 W12 Meta/Shard/global verification is explicitly excluded and owned by `fgdb-epic-w12-verification-bike`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5 (determinism, evidence, calibrated adaptivity) is a founding bet: every claim the system makes is claim-typed, every failure replays from a seed, every adaptive policy is inspectable and has a deterministic fallback. B6 depends on it — agents consume machine-checkable evidence, graded replay bundles, and honest conformance matrices, not prose. The other bets are enforced through this epic: B1's commit-stream invariants get crash matrices and TLA+ models; B2's seal/compaction gets metamorphic equivalence suites; B3's unified execution gets the reference-engine differential plus TCK/ISO matrices; B4's incrementality gets the derivative-equals-batch differential. §15.7's publishing ambition ("ambition includes the receipts") — six papers, including "Calibrated adaptivity: anytime-valid statistical governance of a self-tuning DBMS" — requires this stack to exist and be honest. §3.5 fixes the adopt/adapt/reject posture for every piece of statistical machinery used here.

## Design — normative detail
The claim-type constitution binds the whole epic. Every evidence envelope carries a `ClaimClass` from the closed union: `SafetyInvariant` (must hold on every execution; failure is a correctness defect) | `FormalModelClaim` (theorem or model-check result with abstraction, bounds, and refinement status) | `StatisticalClaim` (population, sampling/selection rule, alpha, power/effective sample size, and assumptions) | `ConfigurationModelClaim` (model version, fitted inputs, sensitivity, and validity domain) | `EmpiricalGate` (fixture, machine/profile, sample count, variance budget, and comparison rule). Registry split: `invariants.toml` contains only exact safety/liveness obligations; `evidence.toml` contains `FG-CAL-*` and `FG-EVID-*`; `slo.toml` contains `FG-CFG-*`, performance, durability-model, and controller targets. Never-mislabel law: sampled e-processes are statistical sentinels in `evidence.toml`, never the enforcement column of `invariants.toml`; a monitor that drives no named decision is dead code, but binding it to a decision does not make it an invariant. Independence law: every invariant has at least one checker outside the optimized component it checks, where practical. Appendix F holds exactly twenty top-level invariant IDs (FG-INV-01..20); G0 materializes each as stable subordinate clauses recording exact statement, activation predicate, dependencies, resolvable checker/negative-test entrypoints, proof/model scope and bounds, owner, first gate, status, and `waiver=forbidden`; every reachable clause must be live, otherwise the corresponding capability is absent. §15.6's waiver law: correctness, security, durable-format, recovery, authorization, invariant-checker, and required conformance gates are nonwaivable; only a named empirical performance threshold, statistical-evidence threshold, or non-safety coverage budget may carry a public, expiring waiver.

## Invariants & claim types
This epic owns the live enforcement side of every Appendix F clause activated by the 1.0/G0-G4 capability closure. It supplies independent Local SCC/history, root/recovery crash matrices, reference plus Lean visibility, obligation leak/quiescence, G3 external-authority/protocol/HA campaigns, and all 1.0 claim/evidence/configuration registries. The same twenty top-level IDs may contain W12-activated subordinate clauses, but those remain disabled/pending here and become live only through `fgdb-epic-w12-verification-bike`; registry presence is never coverage.

## Interactions
Children: verif-sim, verif-reference, Local verif-oracles, Local verif-torture, 1.0 differential/conformance/fuzzing, 1.0 formal anchors, Sextant, replay products, perf apparatus, plus `fgdb-g3-protocol-authority-oracles-w27f` and `fgdb-g3-protocol-ha-torture-jni4` for concrete W9-W11 integration. Genesis/G1-G4 cite this epic. Gate W12 cites only the separate W12 verification epic in addition to its implementation epic; it cannot inherit a green G4.

## Success Criteria
Epic closes when all eleven dependency tasks are complete and the 1.0 closure is green: twenty-ID/table hash and phase-aware clause DAG checks pass; every activated G0-G4 clause resolves to independent checker/negative/evidence symbols; disabled W12 clauses are provably absent from the 1.0 capability manifest; every G0-G4 gate cites correctly typed evidence; reference allowlist and chaos-facade boundaries pass; no statistical claim appears in `invariants.toml`; no invariant is enforced solely by its optimized subject.
- E2E rollup: boot a whole Local three-member server under sim and real-process modes, run a mixed reference-checked workload through each supported adapter, exercise one external authority, audit/DP/protected-output state, leader loss, and injected fault, then require legal recovery and an executable §15.1 replay artifact. A boundary negative attempts to import W12 evidence and must be rejected.
- Detailed-logging bar: every child emits structured JSONL `{claim_or_clause_id,ClaimClass,phase_owner_bead,first_required_gate,row_state,evidence_refs,seed_schedule_or_bounds,expected,actual,verdict}`. The rollup validates ancestry against registries; unlogged, phase-misattributed, pending-as-live, or unreplayable enforcement counts as unenforced.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: post-hoc QA, one monolithic suite, self-checking, unbounded formal ambition, statistics mislabeled as invariants, or letting the 1.0 epic absorb W12. Risks are controlled by nonwaivable gates, phase-aware ownership, trace export, dual runs, mutation tests, and the separate W12 epic.

## Provenance
§15 (lines 1102-1174), §3.5 (159-183), §18.1-18.2, §19 gates, Appendix F.


## Phase boundary
This epic ends at G4. `fgdb-epic-w12-verification-bike` is the sole W12 verification rollup. No dependency from G4 to that epic is permitted; Gate W12 must depend on it directly.

title: Epic W1: Bedrock + security foundations — the closed-universe crate layer
description:
## What & scope
W1 lands the foundation layer of the `fgdb-*` workspace, on which every later workstream (W2 Chronicle onward) is built: `fgdb-types`, `fgdb-bigint`, `fgdb-delta-types`, `fgdb-claim`, `fgdb-evidence`, `fgdb-resource` (foundation value/claim types), `fgdb-authz-types` + `fgdb-policy` (nonconstructible permits and the restricted verifier IR), `fgdb-crypto`, `fgdb-codec`, `fgdb-collections`, `fgdb-sketch`, `fgdb-calibrate`, the three unsafe islands `fgdb-unsafe-simd`/`fgdb-unsafe-arena`/`fgdb-unsafe-vfs` with their CI-enforced ledger, and the registry-generated format encoders/decoders with golden vectors and mutation corpora. W1 depends only on G0's frozen constitutional registries; it produces no durable database state itself.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
The foundation audit (§2) is the reason W1 is small enough to be credible. **asupersync (~580 KLOC)** is the operating system: region tree/obligations/`Outcome` lattice/three-lane scheduler (every background service and every parallel query is a region); `Cx` capability contexts (constraint 3: every function that performs I/O, takes a lock, allocates from a shared arena, or can block accepts `&Cx` — swap the `Cx` and the entire database runs under the lab runtime with virtual time, deterministic scheduling, and fault injection; this is what makes B5 structural); the lab runtime with DPOR/chaos/trace replay/crashpacks; the Lean/TLA+ formal layer; RFC 6330 systematic RaptorQ (never reimplemented here); ATP transport; the entire TCP/QUIC/HTTP/WebSocket/TLS/gRPC stack; cancel-correct channels and combinators; Spork/OTP supervision; `remote.rs` leases/idempotency/HLC; macaroons and authenticated types; fs/VFS/io_uring reactor, region heaps with generational handles, EBR; the e-process/conformal/decision-contract statistical governance machinery; SWIM+Lifeguard, Merkle anti-entropy, coded symbol distribution, CRDT ledgers; LDFI/delta-debugging/dual-run/~24-oracle verification tooling; e-graph rewrite certificates and the (min,+) latency algebra. **franken_networkx (~247 KLOC)** is the algorithm brain and semantics doctrine: 550+ algorithm functions as catalog and semantics oracle; the `GraphView` compatibility target (explicitly NOT a zero-copy match today); CGSE — 13 `TieBreakPolicy` variants, `ComplexityWitness {n,m,dominant_term,observed_count,policy,seed,decision_path_blake3}`, `WitnessLedger`, Strict/Hardened modes — the B5 determinism doctrine generalized from algorithms to queries; fuzz-hardened legacy-format parsers; deterministic generators; RaptorQ sidecar/scrub precedent; NetworkX-parity ordering reference. **frankensqlite (~1.28 MLOC)** is the architectural donor under the dissection-not-linking doctrine (§2.3): adopt its designs — page-granularity MVCC becomes block-granularity MVCC; page-SSI + first-committer-wins + eager locking is a donor pattern whose deadlock-freedom/soundness do NOT transfer by analogy; intent logs + deterministic rebase ladder; native-mode ECS (content-addressed objects, `SymbolRecord` envelopes, root publication, capsules/markers); `WriteCoordinator` shape; ARC pool mechanics; time-travel/checkpoint+delta thinking; Argon2id KEK hierarchy as a starting point only; the conformance/differential/metamorphic QA house style — and where a module is genuinely object-agnostic, fork it into an `fgdb-*` crate with attribution, never linking `fsqlite-*` and dragging SQLite's page/B-tree world along, because graph objects are not SQLite pages. §2.4/§18.2 then names what none of the foundations provide and W1 begins building: compression codecs, sketches, radix/succinct structures, crypto profiles, calibration scores/ledgers — the front edge of the estimated 275–440 KLOC of new Rust (smaller than frankensqlite). The closed universe (constraint 1: only `core`/`alloc`/`std`, nightly, asupersync, `fnx-*`, design-level frankensqlite reuse; no serde/tokio/rocksdb/arrow/tantivy/hnswlib) is the moat: the entire dependency surface is auditable, deterministic under lab, and owned. All six bets rest on this layer; B5 most directly.

## Design — normative detail
Workspace rules that W1 makes concrete: (1) constraint 2 — every ordinary crate root and the workspace default use `unsafe_code = "forbid"`; raw-pointer code lives only in `fgdb-unsafe-*` islands with `deny(unsafe_code)` roots plus narrowly scoped, ledgered `allow` sites. (2) Constraint 1's packaging boundary — the Python package may consume `fnx-python`, but `fgdb-*` crates may never add a direct PyO3 dependency; engine, server, CLI, and durable formats stay free of that boundary. (3) Constraint 9 (prohibited shortcuts, constitutional): no serde-derived enum as a durable format, no parser-interprets-AST engine, no detached background thread — early code may implement a subset of a final abstraction, never a substitute. (4) Nightly pinned per repo; portable-SIMD isolated behind `fgdb-codec`/kernel traits with scalar fallbacks (§20 risk row). (5) Layering per §18.1 with Cargo-enforced boundaries; foundation crates are the only crates `fgdb-reference` may import (its allowlist: foundation value/type/claim crates plus G0-generated registries and golden vectors, nothing else; the parser crates `fgdb-gql`/`fgdb-cypher` are §15.4's one recorded sharing exception, exercised end-to-end by the TCK and the differential corpora).

## Invariants & claim types
Constraint 11 (claims have types) is implemented by `fgdb-claim`: every load-bearing statement is exactly one of `invariant`, `proof`, `bounded_model`, `statistical`, `slo`, `benchmark`; a weaker class may inform policy but may not enforce or justify a stronger one; `invariants.toml` holds only exact safety/liveness invariants, `evidence.toml`/`slo.toml` carry the rest. FG-INV-12's scalar-coherence clause (canonical scalar equality, hashing, ordering, and encoding are coherent) binds `fgdb-types`. FG-INV-09's digest-class clause (every stored digest is explicitly Target, Transcript, WeakIdentity, or BodyDigest with one generated include/exclude recipe) binds the generated parsers. The unsafe-boundary ledger is itself a CI-enforced constitutional artifact materialized at G0.

## Interactions
Children: w1-foundation-types, w1-authz-policy, w1-crypto, w1-codecs, w1-collections, w1-sketch-calibrate, w1-unsafe-ledger, w1-generated-parsers, w1-format-test-corpora (the test-artifact half split from w1-generated-parsers). Consumers: every W2a/W2b/W2c/W3/W4/W5+ anchor; verif-reference (allowlist limited to these crates); verif-sim (runs everything under the lab `Cx`); perf-cost-ci (constraint 12 cost registry discipline applies to anything W1 ships that adds barriers or identity structure).

## Success Criteria
Workspace compiles with workspace-level `forbid(unsafe_code)` and pinned nightly; CI enforces the unsafe ledger bijection, the registry/codegen bijections, and the `fgdb-reference` dependency allowlist (the allowlist rule and CI job are defined here, but the check activates once `verif-reference` lands — that crate is not a W1 deliverable and is outside this epic's closure; enforced no later than gate-genesis); every child bead's own gates pass; no `fgdb-*` crate has a dependency outside the constraint-1 allowlist (automated dependency-universe CI check). E2E: `w1_foundation_e2e` — a workspace-level integration script that builds every W1 crate on the pinned nightly, then drives one value through the full foundation chain under the lab runtime with a fixed seed: construct canonical scalars (`fgdb-types`) -> encode with a registry-generated encoder -> keyed-BLAKE3 digest (`fgdb-crypto`) -> verify against the checked-in golden vector -> compress/decompress through `fgdb-codec` -> index/probe through `fgdb-collections` -> evaluate one `PolicyIr` decision to an `AuthorizedMutationPermit`; the run executes twice and the canonical outputs must be byte-identical. DETAILED LOGGING (required for post-implementation verification): every CI enforcement job emits a machine-readable manifest — unsafe-ledger bijection result (sites/rows/orphans), `fgdb-reference` allowlist verdict per import (emitted once `verif-reference` exists; an explicit `crate_absent` marker before then), dependency-universe scan listing each crate's resolved dependency set, registry epochs and generated-code digests — and the e2e run logs the seed, toolchain hash, and each stage's input/output digests so any cross-stage divergence is attributable from logs alone.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
§20 rows: in-house cryptography failing despite vectors (mitigation: prefer audited foundation primitives, mandatory constant-time/misuse verification, external release audit); nightly MSRV churn (pinned toolchain, SIMD isolation). Rejected: linking `fsqlite-*` wholesale (graph objects are not SQLite pages; correctness does not transfer by analogy); reopening the dependency universe for convenience crates (destroys auditability/determinism moat); JVM/GC/mmap-as-durability/generic-KV fossils (constraint 7).

## Provenance
§1 constraints 1–3, 9; §2.1–2.4; §3.5; §18.1–18.2; §19 W1 row; §20.
