title: Fabric (W10): embedded API, fgdbd, FGP protocol, adapters, and agent-native delivery
description:
## What & scope
W10 delivers every user-facing surface of FrankenGraphDB — the Fabric plane. Children: the embedded `fgdb::Database` API with its explicit ownership contract (`w10-embedded`); the `fgdb-python` binding that maps that contract onto Python idiom (`w10-python`); the FGP native wire protocol per Appendix D (`w10-fgp-core`), with wire-safe public projections and the taint checker (`w10-wire-projections`) and the flow-control/send-obligation write path (`w10-flow-send-obligations`); the four durable authority-bearing capabilities plus tombstones and lineage (`w10-capabilities`) and durable transaction-ownership leases with reattach/renew/expiry (`w10-txn-ownership`); the result, artifact-output, and protected-error delivery state machines (`w10-result-machines`); the `SnapshotQuery` ephemeral read class (`w10-snapshotquery`); HTTP/2+gRPC+WebSocket adapters (`w10-adapters`); the Bolt compatibility subset V1 plus the V2 write roadmap (`w10-bolt`); QoS/admission with `ResourceVector` and `ResourceLedgerState` (`w10-qos`); import formats, the in-house Arrow IPC export writer, and `fgdb-adbc` (`w10-formats`); `ArchiveReadOnlyOpen` single-file distribution (`w10-archive-open`); the deterministic UDF bytecode VM and native-procedure boundary (`w10-udf-vm`); CDC export (`w10-cdc`); and the `fgdbd` composition with drain choreography (`w10-server`). Crates (§18.1): `fgdb`, `fgdb-server`, `fgdb-cli`, `fgdb-protocol`, `fgdb-bolt`, `fgdb-formats`, `fgdb-udf-vm`, `fgdb-python`, `fgdb-adbc`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6 (agent-native) is the load-bearing bet: agents disconnect, retry, and resume constantly, so BEGIN, transaction reattach/renewal, autocommit, subscription creation, export, replay, result resume/ACK/release, unsubscribe, and E-to-E2 capability migration are all durably idempotent, and exactly four durable authority-bearing capabilities survive connection loss with explicit lineage, rotation, and tombstones. B5 (determinism/evidence): every protected result, baseline, delta, proof, replay/export byte, cancellation explanation, and data-dependent error of the durable classes is buffered until its exact authorization and audit-visible release evidence exists, then consumes a fresh linear `PublicFrameSendGuard` immediately before each frame write. B1 shows on the wire as `WireGraphReferenceSpec` branch/system-time/valid-time selectors. Market: Bolt-family drivers leave lost-COMMIT ambiguity, finalizer-driven leaks, and hidden-fact leakage through error surfaces; Fabric makes ownership explicit (Rust `Drop` cannot release; iterator exhaustion IS `finish()`), splits results into two honest classes (durable `PublishedResultStream` versus session-owned ephemeral `SnapshotQuery`), and makes every error either public-mechanics or a bounded durable protected output.

## Design — normative detail
One connection machine (`TransportEstablished -> VersionNegotiated -> Authenticated{AuthContext} -> Ready{ReadyBinding} -> Draining -> Closed`) for all surfaces; `DatabasePosture` is exactly `Local|Sharded` and every role-sensitive public identity is a closed opaque posture union. Adapters cannot weaken Appendix D: HTTP/2, gRPC, WebSocket, and Bolt preserve idempotency, posture, explicit release, output-guard, cancellation, result-resume, and cutover semantics. v1 restrictions: transaction-bound statements are serialized; unsupported savepoint, partial-rollback, or concurrent-statement profiles are rejected. Draining admits no new session-owned children and waits only for queued/writing transport obligations to become Sent/Failed, required audit publications, prepublication cancellations, admitted-decision recovery, terminal records, and durable detach/pause of senders; independently retained result/cursor/export/replay owners survive session/process close and never block drain. No `ObjectId`, reference tag, `WeakMarkerIdentity`, raw internal counter/frontier/generation, `ReplayManifest`, or storage-symbol type ever crosses the wire; a generated taint checker proves every wire path passes an exact projection constructor and fresh send guard.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-15 (independent retention): every result-producing feature uses one generated, noninterchangeable owner arm and the state-shaped independent-retention machine; QUERY_CANCEL, Drop, disconnect, drain, and process death cannot release it. FG-INV-16: no ownership lease, result/workspace/cursor/output lease, or obligation is lost, duplicated, refunded, released, or exposed while obligated. FG-INV-01: each scoped begin/autocommit key maps to at most one immutable semantic terminal outcome; matching retries return the recorded lineage. FG-INV-20: authorization precedes every observation; capability lookup/status/release is same-principal, same-or-narrower, current-epoch, uniformly nonrevealing on failure. Latency budgets for the durable command classes are Appendix G `latency_anatomy.toml` rows and §17 `slo.toml` gates (benchmark-class claims, never invariant clauses); protocol conformance transcripts are FG-EVID-class artifacts.

## Interactions
Consumes `w2-txn-lifecycle`/`w2-commit-protocol` transaction semantics, `w9-enforcement`/`w9-audit-release`/`w9-time-authority` security planes, `w6-subscriptions` cursor machine, `w5-binder`/`w5-determinism`/`w5-answer-contracts` statement and result contracts. Feeds `verif-differential`, `verif-torture`, `perf-bench-core`, `obs-observatory`.

## Success Criteria
All child beads closed. Appendix D closing suite green: state-model, golden, differential, fuzz, crash, and DPOR coverage of pre-auth database non-disclosure; missing/out-of-order AUTH_OK/READY; Local/Sharded dispatch parity; lost/duplicate/conflicting BEGIN, autocommit, subscription, result resume/ACK, unsubscribe, export, and replay requests; NotRequired versus RequiredVisible release; revocation/refresh/epoch change between every two chunks; protected-error silence; hidden zero-net provenance noninterference; E-to-E2 migration exclusivity; and adapter parity. No frame or state row ships without its exact generated wire tag, authorization/release rule, size bound, retry rule, and negative transition fixture. Epic-level e2e: one cross-surface agent-workload script (embedded, FGP, HTTP/2, gRPC, WebSocket, Bolt V1) that begins transactions, kills and reconnects mid-delivery, presents each of the four durable capability kinds, exercises SnapshotQuery beside the durable read path, and drains `fgdbd`, asserting identical durable outcomes and release-evidence classes across surfaces; every protected write in the run logs frame class, send-guard arm, obligation state, and capability-lineage transition so the transcript can be replayed against the generated frame-class and time-requirement matrices for post-implementation verification.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: Appendix D's surface is the largest single contract in the plan; mitigated by generated registries (`wire_types.toml`, frame-class and time-requirement matrices) and session types. Rejected: reusing Bolt or gRPC-only as the primary protocol (cannot express durable capabilities, buffered-until-release, posture unions); finalizer-based resource management (silent leaks and unauthorized releases); a single mushy result class (hides the durable/ephemeral trade instead of contracting it).

## Provenance
§13 (990-1060), Appendix D (2763-3119), §18.1.

title: Ship and verify installable release artifacts for CLI, server, Rust library, and Python wheels
description:
## What and scope
Own the release/distribution layer promised by README.md: installable `fgdb` and `fgdbd` artifacts, a verified curl installer at `scripts/install.sh`, the Rust library publication/install story, and ABI3 Python wheels installable as `frankengraphdb`. This task packages and proves the outputs of the existing CLI, server, embedded, and Python implementation beads; it does not duplicate those implementations.

## Why
The current README publishes executable installation instructions and claims signed release binaries, `cargo build --release` outputs, and `pip install frankengraphdb`, but the repository has no root installer, no product binary targets, no Python packaging manifest, and no bead whose acceptance criteria owns artifact signing/publication or makes every documented install path executable. A product that exists only in a source checkout has not met the W10/G4 product surface.

## Design and contracts
Produce a versioned release manifest that binds source commit, Rust toolchain, target triple, feature/capability manifest, artifact digests, signatures, SBOM/dependency-universe evidence, and durable-format/protocol compatibility declarations. `scripts/install.sh` must be production-grade: explicit supported platforms, HTTPS download, signature and digest verification before replacement, atomic install, deterministic destination selection, `--version`/dry-run/help, and typed nonzero failures; no silent PATH edits or partial overwrite. Rust publication must preserve the closed dependency universe and document whether crates.io, source archive, or signed binary distribution is the supported posture. Python wheels must be ABI3 where the plan requires it, built from the allowed fnx-python packaging boundary without adding a direct engine PyO3 dependency, and tested on the declared OS/architecture/Python matrix. Release automation is reproducible and may not bypass G4 capability, conformance, benchmark, recovery, security, or license gates.

## Acceptance criteria and tests
1. `cargo build --release` produces the documented product artifacts only after their owner crates are live; artifact names and versions match the release manifest.
2. A tracked `scripts/install.sh` installs a signed artifact into a clean sandbox, upgrades atomically, verifies digest/signature, rejects tampering, handles unsupported targets, preserves an existing working install on failure, and uninstalls only through a separately explicit documented action.
3. The Rust library has one tested, documented installation/publication path, including a clean external-consumer smoke project that creates/opens a database through a sanctioned production Cx path.
4. ABI3 wheels build for the declared platform matrix; clean-environment `pip install frankengraphdb` smoke tests open/write/read/reopen and reject ABI/platform mismatches cleanly.
5. CI/release evidence retains manifest, signatures, hashes, logs, and replay commands; every README install command is executed verbatim in a clean environment and the G4 gate rejects stale or non-existent commands.
6. Negative tests cover tampered archive, tampered manifest/signature, interrupted upgrade, unwritable destination, absent network, wrong architecture, incompatible Python, version downgrade, and partial mirror availability.

## Observability and risks
Emit stable robot-readable install/release events containing stage, artifact, version, target, digest, signature identity, destination, and typed failure class without secrets. Main risks are supply-chain substitution, partial-upgrade breakage, platform drift, and documentation rot; the manifest/signature/atomicity and verbatim README smoke gates are the controls.

title: Epic W11 - Aegis: multi-member replication, HA, GC, backup/restore, format activation
description:
## What & scope
W11 turns the single-node FrankenGraphDB (quorum-one Raft from W2) into a replicated, highly available database. Scope: multi-member consensus over the exact same commit state machine (`w11-raft-multi`), stable prepared-owner payload availability with donor receipts (`w11-payload-availability`), membership and joint-quorum reconfiguration with `ConfigPayloadFloor` (`w11-membership-config`), linearizable and lease-based read contracts (`w11-read-contracts`), writer-anywhere follower preparation (`w11-writer-anywhere`), ATP anti-entropy/seeding (`w11-anti-entropy`), fenced consensus GC with quarantine and physical-operation evidence (`w11-fenced-gc`, `w11-gc-physical`), the full §16 backup machinery (`w11-backup`, `w11-backup-publication`, `w11-backup-release`), restore/clone with hidden activation and service promotion (`w11-restore`, `w11-restore-lease`, `w11-restore-promotion`), and rolling durable-format activation (`w11-format-activation`).

## Why (bets, market, goals)
The Aegis doctrine (§14): **single-node correctness is the base product; replication adds crash-fault durability, availability, and read scale**. Canonical logical effects and digests agree across replicas, but repair ESIs, ciphertext encodings, cache state, and physical placement need not be byte-identical. Horizontal sharding is a post-1.0 protocol workstream (W12), not a configuration toggle — until the W12 gate passes, a database advertises `sharding=false` and rejects multi-shard topologies rather than weakening any 1.0 guarantee. This preserves B1 (One Version Universe): one `LogicalCommandSeq`/`CommitSeq`/HLC history, one commit state machine (§5.2) authoritative in one-member and multi-member configurations. B5 is served by evidence-first operation: every irreversible action (payload receipt, certificate, GC reclaim, backup publication, key destruction, format escape) is receipted, signed, and replayable; availability numbers are `slo.toml` rows, never invariants. B6 is served because agents get typed `Unknown` outcomes (capability-scoped, never a guess on leader loss) and a queryable ops surface. Market: the durability/HA story is what lets an embedded-first graph database compete with server-first incumbents without forking its semantics.

## Design — normative detail
The §19 W11 row fixes the deliverables: extend W2's quorum-one Raft to multi-member consensus; stable prepared-owner payload availability; joint/final/final-retirement-floor reconfiguration; current-root-recomputed, all-typed-root consensus GC with quarantine plus Requested/Started/Completed-or-cancelled physical-operation evidence, progress, and completion; anti-entropy/seeding; rolling durable-format activation and follower security/data fences; witnessed transparency. Dependencies: W2 commit/payload/Raft interfaces, W9 authority, W10 protocol/status contracts.

Structural laws that bind every child bead: (1) Raft persistence obeys the **no-extra-mutable-file doctrine** — all durable consensus state lives in Appendix A role-tagged objects (`RaftLogSegment`, `RaftHardState`, `RaftSnapshot`, `RaftStateRoot`, `ConfigurationState`, certificate/prepared-root/audit-visibility-pipeline formats) carrying the database/security-namespace/incarnation/role/group domain; no abbreviated ambient schema is normative. (2) A node syncs the new closure before vote/append/receipt/durability replies. (3) Truncation stops at visible audit-safe state and waits for the generated-complete floor including prepared transfers, cursors, replay, external continuities, remote trust/retention, backup, keys, and current/prospective configs. (4) Multi-member configurations must NOT fuse append-reply and post-apply publications (the Appendix G fusion law is one-member-only, because followers reply before commit). (5) SWIM+Lifeguard supplies suspicion/routing/donor evidence only; statistical suspicion never authorizes membership change, payload retirement, or GC. (6) Backup/restore follows §16, never a decode-proof shortcut. (7) Leader loss yields capability-scoped `Unknown`, never a guess.

## Invariants & claim types
This epic's children collectively enforce FG-INV-07 (acyclic durable reference graph, D1/D2 ownership, all-role Raft models), FG-INV-08 (contiguous sequences, exact-cut snapshots, gap-free audit pipeline), FG-INV-10 (two-slot root protocol, fencing, format activation), FG-INV-14 (GC follows every generated edge; obligations are roots), FG-INV-16 (no obligation lost/duplicated/exposed), and FG-INV-19 (replay grades across restore). Availability per operation class (apply-durability / visibility / delivery, §16.8) is `slo.toml` claim class; durability targets are `FG-CFG-01` (modeled MTTDL with sensitivity bounds); the writer-anywhere scaling claim is benchmark class per §14.4.

## Interactions
Consumes: `w2-order-raft` (quorum-one Raft core), `w2-commit-protocol` (§5.2 steps, D1/D2), `w2-gc-core` (single-node GC), `w2-continuity-profiles`/`w2-writer-takeover` (incarnation/fencing), `w9-key-lifecycle` (envelopes/DEKs), `w9-audit-release` (visibility certificates gating external dispatch), `w10-fgp-core` (protocol/status surfaces). Produces the substrate W12 (`epic-w12`) extends to Meta/Shard roles, the restore/backup surfaces `verif-torture` and the §19 deployment gates exercise, and the `ArchiveReadOnlyOpen` verification machinery `w10-archive-open` reuses.

## Success Criteria
Epic closes when: multi-member cluster passes the full §15.3 crash matrix and partition campaigns with zero invariant violations (the campaigns are executed by `verif-torture` over the matrices the w11 beads register — verif-torture is outside this epic's closure, so this criterion is validated at gate-g3, which joins the epic with verif-torture); Elle/SCC oracles pass on multi-member histories (the checkers are `verif-oracles` machinery hosted in those campaigns; likewise validated at gate-g3); reconfiguration ladder, GC pipeline, backup Released, restore-to-Operational, and format activation each survive every registered crash point idempotently; Local/Sharded restore drills and RPO/RTO gates (§16.6) pass; the three availability lines are measured and published per posture in `slo.toml`. Every child bead's e2e drill must emit structured logs — at minimum consensus positions (`term`/`raft_index`/`logical_command_seq`/`commit_seq`), configuration epoch and floor identity, operation/attempt IDs with dispatch states, certificate/receipt identities, and typed refusal reasons — and epic closure additionally requires a cross-workstream log-to-state verification pass: the generated log-to-state verifier replays those logs against final state for the reconfiguration-ladder, GC, backup, restore, and format-activation drills, proving post-implementation that each recorded transition occurred in the order logged; the same replay is additionally cross-checked through `fgdb doctor` once `obs-doctor` lands — obs-doctor depends on w11 deliverables, so the doctor cross-check is validated at gate-g4, not at epic close.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: federation of independently committed histories (breaks B1); vector clocks in Chronicle (§14.6 note — one scalar semantic clock even post-sharding); Calvin-style deterministic transaction lanes (§3.4 rejection — no second execution discipline); gossip as membership/GC authority (SWIM is evidence only); timeout-based prepared decision (blocked participants recover the decision, never guess). Risk: per-commit root-closure re-minting cost is priced via Appendix G (§17 gated number), not ambient; the `RaftHardFrame` spike (G0) may restructure publication cadence.

## Provenance
§14.1-14.5 (plan lines 1064-1078), §16.6-16.8, §19 W11 row, App A consensus/GC/backup/restore formats, App F.

title: W12 verification epic: independent sharding proofs and torture
description:
## What & scope
Post-1.0 W12 verification epic. Aggregate the dedicated W12 simulation/global-oracle and W12 formal/fuzz/fault/recovery evidence required before `sharding=true` can be advertised. This epic is deliberately separate from the 1.0 verification epic: G4 neither depends on nor inherits it, and W12 cannot reuse a G4 green bar as sharding evidence.

## Why
The plan reserves W12 identities in 1.0 but explicitly defers distributed atomic commit, global serializability/certification, Meta time, role transition, remote trust, distributed GC/key/backup/restore, and topology proof to their own gate. A separate epic makes that temporal and claim boundary mechanically visible in the dependency graph.

## Deliverables
- Live deterministic simulation and canonical Meta/Shard protocol-state machines over the completed W12 implementation.
- Independent global SCC/history oracle including every cross-shard/negative/gap/path/workspace edge and the registered virtual-serial batch-certification equivalence law.
- Ten scoped W12 TLA+/TLC model lanes with explicit abstractions, bounds, fairness, trace schemas, refinement status, and negative counterexample fixtures.
- Exhaustive generated crash matrices, distributed recovery/activation/remote/key/GC/backup/restore/topology campaigns, W12 format/protocol fuzzers, lab-vs-live and real-process E2E.
- Clause-to-checker/test/evidence/log ancestry audit for every activated W12 subordinate invariant; missing evidence keeps sharding absent.

## Success Criteria
- Both child tasks are complete and all registered unit, property, simulation, model, fuzz, real-process E2E, replay, and matrix-completeness gates exit green.
- `br dep cycles` remains empty and this epic is reachable from Gate W12 only; no G0-G4 gate or 1.0 epic depends on it.
- Every W12 result is claim-typed and model-qualified. Bounded model checking, statistical stopping, runtime monitoring, and trace conformance are not mislabeled as implementation proof.
- Gate W12 report is reproducible solely from structured JSONL evidence and artifact digests; every failed campaign has a minimized executable replay command.
- `sharding=true` remains absent unless the dedicated W12 gate consumes this epic and every live clause has complete evidence ancestry.

## Detailed diagnostics contract
The epic-level aggregator emits JSONL `{run_id,phase:"W12",child_task_id,evidence_manifest_digest,activated_clause_count,covered_clause_count,missing_clause_ids,unit_property_sim_model_fuzz_e2e_counts,replay_sample_verdict,dependency_boundary_verdict,overall_verdict}` and retains links/digests for every underlying row. It must reject incomplete, phase-misattributed, redacted-without-downgrade, or nonreproducible evidence.

## Provenance
Plan §14.6, §15, §19 Gate W12, Appendix F W12 clauses.

title: W12 epic: post-1.0 sharding — one universe, many shards
description:
## What & scope
Epic for workstream W12, the horizontal-sharding protocol. It owns the Meta/Shard consensus-role split and every distributed transaction, constraint, escrow, DP, allocation, recovery, GC, topology, backup/restore, and Local-to-Sharded conversion mechanism. Child anchors: `w12-meta-clock`, `w12-registration-snapshot`, `w12-statement-machine`, `w12-prepare`, `w12-certification`, `w12-final-reservation`, `w12-decision-visibility`, `w12-constraints-authority`, `w12-escrow-dp-alloc`, `w12-recovery-gc`, `w12-topology`, `w12-backup-restore`, `w12-conversion`.

**Doctrine (normative-now / implemented-post-1.0):** every W12 design choice in §14.6 and Appendix A is normative NOW — reserved kinds/tags/fields, role-tagged formats, closed unions with W12 arms (`GlobalOutcomeDirectoryValue::W12`, `AppliedAbortRef::MetaTxn`, `RootManifest` Meta/Shard/RetiredLocal payloads, `CertifiedRemoteStrongRef`, the `GlobalFinalCertificationReservation` batch arm) — only their *implementation* is post-1.0. Gate G4 (1.0) explicitly excludes W12 and its evidence cannot be reused as the W12 gate.

**The `sharding=false` refusal:** until the dedicated §19 Gate W12 passes — proving meta/shard reconfiguration, every crash/partition point, distributed SCC/constraint histories, cross-shard branch/merge/key/audit behavior, Ripple frontier atomicity, and topology moves — a database advertises `sharding=false` and *rejects* any topology with more than one data shard rather than weakening any 1.0 guarantee. Otherwise `sharding=true` is absent.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1 (One Version Universe) is the whole point: sharding preserves a single scalar semantic time through one database-wide meta-Raft order. W12 is explicitly **not** a federation of independently committed shard histories and does **not** switch Chronicle to vector time — reopening scalar time is a new architecture requiring new Chronicle/branch/Ripple/replay proofs, never an optimization (§20 risk row). B5: every step is evidence-carrying (certificates, typed acks, crash-DAG proofs); B6: agents get exact global snapshots, capability-safe `Unknown`, and byte-stable status across compaction. §3.4 rejected Calvin-style deterministic transaction lanes; W12's batching stays inside the existing certifier. SOTA context: Spanner/Calvin-style designs were mined for ideas (global order, deterministic certifiers) but the adopted shape is a single Meta sequencer with certified shard participation, priced honestly as a deliberate correctness/performance tradeoff.

## Design — normative detail
Doctrinal spine (§14.6): (1) **One scalar semantic clock** — `LogicalCommandSeq`, transaction-only `CommitSeq`, and logical HLC are Meta-issued global aliases; every canonical mutation passes through Meta; shard Raft indices order durability/apply only and never move time or heads. (2) I/O/group-commit batching of already-certified entries is allowed; same-basis certification is legal exactly and only under the registered virtual-serial batch-certification law (`w12-certification`); speculative certification and shard-local visible commit are forbidden. (3) The §5.2 commit state machine remains authoritative; W12 adds Meta/Shard roles, `GlobalTxnCommand`/`ShardPrepareCommand`/`ShardDecisionApplyCommand`/`ShardControlCommand` planes with exact `command_contracts.toml` rows (a compiled W12 build must contain the exact semantic and maintenance row sets; `AuditTicketResolutionBatchSpec` has no row in either union). (4) The one cross-consensus edge is `CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<T>` over consumer-local `ExportLeaf<T>`, configuration evidence, availability evidence, and two-sided retention grants; no raw cross-group `StrongRef` decodes. (5) Partitions may block; they cannot reverse decisions or reclaim uncertain state; no prepared participant times out or guesses. (6) Benchmarks must publish BOTH global sequencer ceilings — serial and batched under the §14.6 law — with the residual per-command Meta-apply ceiling stated.

Gate W12 ("One Universe, Many Shards", §19:1350-1354) is the exit: role-tagged logs/roots/floors/snapshots reject cross-role commands; fresh Sharded Genesis and audited Local freeze/seal/activation/RetiredLocal pass every crash point; every semantic mutation, including single-shard work, enters Meta Raft; BEGIN durably reserves key/outcome capability before response; the independent SCC/history oracle and the batch-versus-serial equivalence oracle are green; every cross-group edge passes two-sided CertifiedRemoteStrongRef trust/retention/GC tests; every compiled-and-negotiated subordinate clause of FG-INV-01..20 is live.

## Invariants & claim types
All twenty FG-INV rows in Appendix F carry W12 subordinate clauses (activation predicate: sharded posture); the gate requires every reachable clause live — otherwise the capability is absent, per the claim-type constitution (`invariants.toml`, `waiver=forbidden`). Sequencer-ceiling numbers are benchmark-class claims (Appendix G-derived §17 manifests), never invariants. Maintenance-stream capacity under sharding is FG-CFG-04 (model + measured saturation); durability of shard/meta payload is FG-CFG-01.

## Interactions
Consumes: multi-member Raft (`w11-raft-multi`), payload availability (`w11-payload-availability`), membership (`w11-membership-config`), read contracts (`w11-read-contracts`), the Local commit protocol (`w2-commit-protocol`) and txn lifecycle (`w2-txn-lifecycle`). Produces: the Meta/Shard planes consumed by `w6-delta-consumption` (Ripple frontier), `w10-cdc`, `w10-capabilities` (capability migration), and the verification spine (`verif-oracles`).

## Success Criteria
Epic closes only when Gate W12 passes in full: all child anchors done; `sharding=false` refusal path tested (topology with >1 data shard rejected with typed error, no partial admission); every failure artifact carries §15 structured replay fields; published benchmarks disclose both ceilings; rolling upgrade/donor-loss/checkpoint+suffix/status/backup/restore matrices green for Meta and every shard. Cross-cutting tests the epic itself tracks: `sharding_false_refusal` (unit: a topology with two data shards yields the typed refusal error, no partial admission, no shard state created), `cross_role_command_injection` (property: every role-tagged log/root/floor/snapshot rejects commands of every other role), and the gate-level batch-vs-serial and SCC/history oracle suites. E2E: a scripted full W12 gate drill on a 1-Meta/3-shard cluster — fresh Sharded Genesis, mixed txn/control load with crash/partition injection, one topology move, one backup-at-P/destructive-restore cycle, and one Local-to-Sharded conversion drill — asserting every §19:1350-1354 clause. DETAILED LOGGING (required of every child bead and verified at the epic): every Meta/Shard state-machine transition emits a structured record `{event, role, group_id, relevant ids (txn/registration/admission/decision/plan/grant), assigned prefix/seq, outcome}` carrying §15 replay fields; the gate drill fails if any transition the oracles observe in durable state is absent from the logs.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Meta sequencing may bottleneck (accepted, priced; §20). Rejected: vector clocks/federated shard histories (breaks B1, Chronicle, replay); Calvin-style deterministic lane (§3.4); speculative certification; shard-local visible commit; timeout-based presumed abort.

## Provenance
§14.6 (plan 1079-1097); §19 Gate W12 (1350-1354); §20 risk table (1379); Appendix A W12 formats (1386-1935).

title: Chronicle epic: one commit stream for durability, time, branches, replication (B1)
description:
## What & scope
Chronicle is FrankenGraphDB's ECS-native durability substrate — frankensqlite's Native mode born as the *only* mode, for graph objects (§5). This epic covers the full §5 surface: content-addressed object identity and the physical-protection pipeline plus the five disjoint identity-class registries (§5.1), `RootSlot`/`RootManifest` bootstrap and publication, filesystem durability profiles, writer takeover and fresh creation, incarnation/allocation continuity, the never-recycled ID allocator, the commit protocol with two durability barriers and quorum-one Raft (§5.2), snapshots and generation leases (§5.3), retention tiers/checkpoints/cuts (§5.4), compaction (§5.5), branch fork/merge/retire (§5.6), FEC scrub and self-healing (§5.7), and the MMR transparency layer (§5.8). Work splits into three groups: w2a substrate (`w2-object-identity`, `w2-object-packing`, `w2-root-bootstrap`, `w2-filesystem-profiles`, `w2-writer-takeover`, `w2-continuity-profiles`, `w2-id-allocator`, `w2-fec-scrub`, plus their split-out subtasks `w2-root-publication`, `w2-takeover-adoption`, `w2-scrub-coverage`, `w2-escape-bindings`); w2b ordering (`w2-order-raft`, `w2-commit-protocol`, `w2-fused-autocommit`, `w2-txn-lifecycle`, `w2-snapshots-leases`, `w2-recovery`, `w2-group-commit`, plus their split-out subtasks `w2-hlc-order-attempt`, `w2-prepare-terminal`, `w2-outcome-tokens`); w2c lifecycle (`w2-retention-checkpoints`, `w2-compaction`, `w2-delta-batches`, `w2-branch-fork`, `w2-branch-merge`, `w2-branch-retire`, `w2-transparency`, `w2-gc-core`, plus their split-out subtasks `w2-retention-cut-objects`, `w2-branch-grants`).

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Bet B1 (One Version Universe): one commit mechanism — capsule → marker → root publication — simultaneously serves MVCC visibility, time travel (`AS OF`), replication, subscriptions/CDC, and branches. No WAL-then-page dual write path, no separate temporal store, no separate replication log: retention tiers ARE the temporal database, `LogicalDeltaBatch` IS the subscription/Ripple feed (B4), and quorum-one Raft IS replication at one member. Agent-native workloads (B6) need cheap terminating branches, verifiable history, reproducible reads; regulated pipelines need externally checkable transparency. Foundations (§2.3): frankensqlite is the architectural donor (content-addressed objects, capsules/markers, root publication), but Chronicle re-specifies the root protocol, full-digest identity, encoding variants, final-capsule ordering, branch/global ancestry, and replicated payload availability — graph durability does not inherit correctness by analogy. §2.1: asupersync supplies RFC 6330 RaptorQ with per-symbol authentication (never reimplemented), the obligations model (a capsule publication is a two-phase obligation), and the lab runtime that turns interleaving bugs into seed-replayable failures (B5).

## Design — normative detail
Constitutional doctrines every Chronicle task inherits. (1) **No-mutable-file doctrine**: the only published durable bytes updated in place are the two 4 KiB `RootSlot`s of `manifest.root`; every other durable byte is an immutable content-addressed object assembled in uniquely named staging files, fsynced, sealed with an immutable trailer, renamed to final segment identity, and made directory-durable before publication; staging files are unreachable state cleaned only by a recovery procedure that proves it. (2) **Published-recovery-root constitution**: recovery discards slots failing structural/tear validation, selects the highest remaining generation; once structurally credible, authentication or mandatory-closure failure triggers symbol/replica repair and then fails closed — never silent rollback past an acknowledged commit; using an older generation requires §16's explicit restore protocol with fencing, incarnation advancement, and an audit/transparency record. (3) **Five disjoint identity classes** (`logical_object_kinds.toml`, `physical_record_kinds.toml`, `bootstrap_frames.toml`, `prebootstrap_artifact_kinds.toml`, `wire_types.toml`) plus the `durable_fields.toml` cross-index: a field absent from the table is unencodable. (4) **Layered state**: `LogicalStatePayload` (complete semantic state, no command head) + `LogicalCommandRecord { logical_command_seq, origin:LocalCommandOrigin, command, transaction_marker?, logical_command_hlc, resulting_state_payload_digest }` + `LogicalStateRoot { payload_ref, logical_command_head? }`; the canonical content graph is a DAG — no self, mutual, or future-result edges. (5) **Two durability barriers**: D1 (semantic capsule + entire mandatory strong closure under stable `PreparedOwnershipId`) and D2 (ordered `CommitCommand` + root publication), amortized by group commit; every durable database, embedded included, orders through the same internal Raft log — single node is a one-member/quorum-one configuration; only `:memory:` runs the state machine without a durability claim. (6) `MarkerRef { marker_oid, commit_seq }` is the transaction-history identity used by branch heads, version origins/retirements, checkpoints, MMR leaves, merges. (7) **Recovery equation** `state(L,C) = reconstruct_and_verify_install(RecoveryCheckpointProjection basis) + apply contiguous LogicalCommandRecord suffix (L0+1, L]`. (8) **Branches**: O(1) data-copy fork with key-envelope double rotation, squash-merge visibility with `MergeRecord`/`ImportedRangeKey` idempotency, first-class two-phase `BranchRetireSpec`/`BranchRetireFinalizeSpec`. (9) **Tiered FEC**: dynamic reconstructibility law + checkpoint-fold recode (§5.7).

## Invariants & claim types
Chronicle owns the largest share of the twenty-ID spine. FG-INV-07: the concrete durable strong/uncut-conditional graph is acyclic; every pre-order input excludes its future command/result/root; before receipt/order, D1 owns one exact closure under stable prepared ownership. FG-INV-08: logical-command predecessor order and the transaction-marker subsequence are contiguous; every role-tagged Raft snapshot matches its precise visible cut; only `AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec` moves the visible endpoint. FG-INV-09: keyed identity recomputation (`w2-object-identity`). FG-INV-10: two-slot protocol, fencing, fail-closed (`w2-root-bootstrap`/`w2-writer-takeover`). FG-INV-11: per-profile allocation monotonicity (`w2-continuity-profiles`/`w2-id-allocator`). FG-INV-13: immutable commits, atomic expected-head branch updates, fork closes parent envelope epochs. FG-INV-14: GC follows every generated strong/uncut-conditional edge; independent obligations remain roots. Scrub health is FG-EVID-02 evidence class; modeled durability is FG-CFG-01 configuration-model class — never invariants.

## Interactions
Blocked by the G0 registries and W1 crates (`w1-crypto`, `w1-codecs`, `w1-generated-parsers`, `w1-foundation-types`). Produces: object/snapshot interfaces for `w3-tier-d`/`w3-tier-r`/`w3-seal-compact`; the commit substrate for `w4-coordinator`/`w4-mvcc-locks`; canonical `LogicalDeltaTemplate`/`LogicalDeltaBatch` for `w6-delta-consumption`; quorum-one Raft that `w11-raft-multi` extends; backup/restore hooks for `w11-backup`/`w11-restore`; the transparency surface exercised by `verif-oracles`.

## Success Criteria
The epic closes when every w2a/w2b/w2c task closes and the Genesis-slice behaviors hold end-to-end under `fgdb-sim`: fresh `Genesis -> CheckpointInstalled -> Operational` with crashes before/after each checkpoint/floor command and no user operation admitted earlier; D1/D2 crash recovery from both slots and the installed checkpoint; G1 matrices green (accepted-filesystem conformance, lease-owner-death, fence-root-before-enable, torn-root, marker-tail, stale-writer, bootstrap/recovery); compaction and label changes preserve logical digests; scrub sweeps plus per-tier sampling e-processes reporting. E2E scripts log crash-point identity, both slot generations, recovered root-manifest identity, prepared-owner reconciliation decisions, and per-barrier fsync counts checked against Appendix G barrier-chain rows.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: WAL+page dual format (two sources of truth); mutable in-place trees; integer-only visibility without markers (branch ancestry unrepresentable, §2.3); a bespoke single-node commit path distinct from replication (violates B1; quorum-one Raft instead). Risks: fsync-latency floor per commit (group commit + Appendix G pricing); registry sprawl (generated bijection CI); correctness-by-analogy from the donor (re-specification plus independent models).

## Provenance
§5 (272-501), §2.1/§2.3, §19 W2 row, App A, App F.

title: Rewrite fgdb-chronicle crate-root docs so landed capsules/RaptorQ/CommitCoordinator are not described as future work
description:
## Context

The 2026-08-20 reality check (docs/REALITY_CHECK_AND_BRIDGE_PLAN.md, HEAD df733010) found a crate-root documentation lie in `crates/fgdb-chronicle/src/lib.rs`.

The header still says later increments will add RaptorQ symbolization, CommitCapsule/CommitMarker two-fsync, WriteCoordinator, retention tiers, and branches. On the same crate, `capsule`, `commit` (`CommitCoordinator`), `symbolize` (asupersync RaptorQ), `marker`, `root`, `scrub`, and `store` already exist and have crash/erasure tests.

This is not a missing feature. It is a false "not landed yet" claim sitting on the crate that already landed those features. Future agents treat crate-root docs as the no-claim boundary (doctrine 7); a stale header will cause them to re-implement or under-claim working machinery.

## Current state

- `crates/fgdb-chronicle/src/lib.rs` lines 9-20: "LANDED SO FAR" lists only `identity` and `symbol`, then "Later increments add the RaptorQ symbolization... CommitCapsule/CommitMarker... WriteCoordinator..."
- Landed modules in the same file: capsule, commit, identity, marker, pack, root, scrub, store, symbol, symbolize, validate.
- Retention-cooling tiers and product BranchManifest are still honestly absent; those absences must remain named.

## Implementation plan

1. Rewrite the crate-root "LANDED SO FAR" / "Later increments" split to match the modules and tests that exist today.
2. Keep an explicit **deliberately absent** list: retention-cooling as temporal DB, BranchManifest/product multi-branch API, replication/subscriptions, real SSI validator (PassThroughValidator is current), capsule-sealing of Strata derived objects.
3. Name `CommitCoordinator` as the coordinator that exists (do not resurrect the plan's WriteCoordinator name as if unimplemented).
4. Add a short test or registry-check prose pin only if the project already has a crate-doc/honesty checker; do not invent a new gate. A crate-level rustdoc doctest is enough if one already runs.

## Files to change

- `crates/fgdb-chronicle/src/lib.rs` (module docs only)

## Success criteria

- [ ] A reader of only the crate-root docs can list what is durable today vs what is not, without contradicting `commit.rs`, `capsule.rs`, or `symbolize.rs`.
- [ ] Retention tiers and product branches remain documented as absent.
- [ ] `cargo test -p fgdb-chronicle --doc` (or the crate's existing doc tests) still pass.

## Why this serves the vision

B1 is the commit stream. Agents already lose weeks to "is this real?" The crate header is the first answer. It must not lag the code.

title: Strata tiered storage engine: resolve the write/scan/space trilemma (Bet B2)
description:
## What & scope
Deliver **Strata**, FrankenGraphDB's storage engine and the whole of Bet B2: authoritative graph incidence and properties stored across temperature tiers with immutable published objects. Scope spans the vertex directory (§6.5), Tier I inline micro-adjacency (§6.1), Tier D delta blocks (§6.2), Tier R sealed runs (§6.3), the Tier A checkpoint feed (ECS cold: full compressed partition snapshots + logical effects for time travel/restore/replica seeding), property storage (§6.4), write-amplification/space discipline (§6.6), buffer & memory management (§6.7), the seal/compact pipeline, and bulk staging. Child anchors: `w3-tier-d`, `w3-tier-r`, `w3-identity-encoding`, `w3-properties`, `w3-vertex-directory`, `w3-write-amp`, `w3-buffer`, `w3-seal-compact`, `w3-bulk-staging`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Dynamic graph storage sits on a write/scan/space trilemma, and the 2025 "Revisiting DGS" study's headline — 4–9x CSR space overhead across the field — is the disease. Strata refuses to pick one point on the trilemma: each `(vertex, direction, edge_type)` adjacency descriptor exists across three tiers and migrates by temperature, so the hot minority pays delta overhead while the cold majority sits *below* CSR via compression. One per-descriptor representation choice under a single immutable-object law beats a representation zoo: there is exactly one merge semantics, one digest-validated equivalence rule for every physical transition, and one governed migration mechanism, instead of N engines with N consistency stories. The §3.1 SOTA verdicts are folded in deliberately: **CSR** adopted as sealed per-`(stable partition, edge_type, direction)` runs with explicit ordinal maps and per-list codecs; **Sortledton** adapted as the delta-tier layout (sorted 256-edge blocks, per-block version pointers, hub skip-list-of-blocks); **Teseo**'s PMA rejected as primary (rebalance storms conflict with p99 goals) while its lesson is adopted — the vertex directory is an index, not the store; **LiveGraph**'s append-only trick adapted as the *bounded* hot-burst overflow log; **Aspen**'s immutable structural sharing adopted at run granularity — the free-snapshot benefit at a fraction of the pointer overhead; **GTX/Spruce/RapidStore/RadixGraph** adapted for delta-chain-per-block concurrency and latch-free MPSC append; **AeonG** adopted-and-unified — our MVCC retirement path *is* the historical store, anchors are periodic sealed snapshots in ECS, deltas are the commit stream Chronicle already durably has. This serves B2 directly; B1 (every published Strata object is immutable and content-addressed — snapshots and branches are structurally free); B3/B4 (Loom scans and Ripple delta consumption get tier-shaped inputs); B5 (digest validators, decision cards, calibrated migration); B6 (agent workloads with thousands of branches ride structural sharing).

## Design — normative detail
Topology (§6.1): a per-stable-partition **vertex directory** maps snapshot ordinal to `{stable VId, label-set ref, prop locator, sparse descriptor-table ref}` with packed ordinal maps, membership indexes, and a canonical constraint map for external keys. Below the three tiers sits **Tier I**: a small bounded vector in the vertex row stores the first few active `(direction, edge_type, descriptor)` entries; a descriptor may inline up to eight `(dst_VId, EId, prop_locator)` incidences; mutable tiers never store a bare snapshot ordinal; overflow promotes to Tier D and demotion is a verified representation transition. **Tier D** (delta): immutable published versions, mutable staging only — sorted 256-edge blocks, per-block MVCC version chains, hub vertices as skip-lists of blocks, a bounded hot-burst overflow log, volatile latch-free staging, immutable roots at publication. **Tier R** (sealed runs, immutable): per-`(partition, type, dir)` runs with per-list codec tags, delta-varint neighbor gaps, stable-EId-keyed property chunks, zone maps, optional per-run hole bitmaps. **Tier A**: full compressed partition snapshots + logical effects in ECS. The governing law: **a logical adjacency list = merge(inline slot, delta blocks, [newest…oldest] sealed runs)** — exactly an LSM, except runs are graph-shaped and sorted by `(src_snapshot_ordinal, dst_snapshot_ordinal, EId)`; seal moves D to R0 and compact k-way-merges generations. Tombstones and run holes carry creation/retirement marker references or a lineage-pinned effective-interval sidecar; a branch-agnostic scalar retire sequence or current hole bitmap may never hide an edge from a sibling branch or older snapshot. Direction law: canonical forward runs always; reverse runs are declared synchronously maintained materializations, enabled by default, disableable per edge type only with the registered reverse-scan fallback; every present/required reverse family must equal the transpose of authorized forward incidence at each snapshot — disabling changes performance, never semantics. Partitioning law: runs are segmented by stable source partition and snapshot-ordinal ranges — the unit of compaction, buffering, statistics, checksums, and parallel scans; labels use separate membership bitmaps and derived Beacon projections; source-range ownership is an edge-cut/vertex-owner layout, and a future hub-splitting vertex-cut mode is a different protocol named separately in §14.6.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-03: every physical version chain is finite, acyclic, strictly newer-first by commit order, and every link remains within one owning object generation. FG-INV-04 binds visibility: snapshot high sequence, branch ancestry per graph-reference role, valid-time slices, create/retire and schema-coordinate rules, own-write overlays, the erasure-tombstone conjunct, the expiry predicate. FG-INV-11 (excerpt): canonical forward incidence, stable IDs, origin/birth/branch orders, properties, ordinal maps, holes, and any reverse materialization agree. FG-INV-12 (excerpt): every claimed answer-equivalent seal, compaction, codec/format rewrite preserves logical values, multiplicity, order, visibility, security projection, and AnswerContract. Per the claim-type constitution: compression-ratio and throughput numbers are benchmark-class claims tied to named corpora and encodings, never format truths (§6.1, §17); migration-policy evidence is FG-CAL-01/FG-EVID-01 class; durability modeling is FG-CFG-01.

## Interactions
Consumes the commit/effect stream and `LogicalDeltaTemplate`/`LogicalDeltaBatch` canonical deltas from `w2-delta-batches`; the ObjectId/AEAD/placement pipeline from `w2-object-identity`; snapshot/generation-lease pinning from `w2-snapshots-leases`; frozen identity/physical-record registries from `g0-identity-registries`. Produces the substrate for `w4-mvcc-locks`/`w4-ssi-witnesses` (block/stripe lock and witness granularity), `w5-executor` scans, `w6-delta-consumption`, `w7-index-core` builds, `w8-projection`, and the §17 gates in `perf-bench-core`/`perf-bench-scale`.

## Success Criteria
Epic closes when all nine anchors close and: the reference-graph differential (`verif-reference`) passes over ingest/seal/compact/scan for forward and reverse families (executed once `verif-reference` lands — it is a gate-genesis dependency outside this epic's closure; validated no later than gate-g1, which joins this epic with the genesis machinery); compaction metamorphics prove merge(inline, delta, runs) equals reference adjacency at every sampled snapshot/branch; crash matrices cover every publication barrier; §17 Strata gates (neighbor scans >=500M edges/s per core decoded-cache, point reads >=8M lookups/s across cores, p99 < 15us warm, cold bulk load >=40M edges/s — all provisional EmpiricalGates) are registered here with pinned manifests and run green on §15.6's deterministic apparatus once `verif-perf-apparatus`/`perf-bench-core` land — manifests-green is a gate-g4 requirement, not an epic-close-time run; an e2e script ingests a named corpus, forces seal+compact, and logs per-tier object counts, digests, generation IDs, and byte breakdowns.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: PMA as primary storage (rebalance storms), pure per-vertex logs (scan decay, awkward deletes), purely functional trees (3–10x CSR memory), a single-representation store (the 4–9x disease), and label-partitioned placement (mutable labels would force incidence rewrites). Risks: migration oscillation (dwell/hysteresis + SPRT guards in `w3-write-amp`/`w3-seal-compact`), hub skew (durable stripes), adversarial identity distributions (codecs degrade gracefully toward raw width, priced in the byte-economy metrics).

## Provenance
§6.1–§6.7; §3.1; §2.3; §4.5; §17; App A (`AdjRunSegment`).

title: Epic W4: Block-MVCC + Graph-SSI + semantic merge (transactions, state, secure view)
description:
## What & scope
Workstream W4 delivers FrankenGraphDB's transaction engine and semantic-state layer: block-granularity MVCC over Strata delta blocks, Graph-SSI with a logical witness algebra, the Local strict-serializability certification law, the semantic merge ladder, the WriteCoordinator choreography with final-certification reservations and holds, synchronous constraint state (`ConstraintStateRoot`), the two semantic-state algebras (valid time §4.6, escrow §4.7), element expiry contracts (§4.8), the FrankenGraph model surface — schema gradient, graph/branch catalog and coordinate objects, and reserved system slots (§4.1–§4.4), the bulk/DDL path (§7.5), the derived-index shadow lifecycle, and `fgdb-secure-view` — the sole authorized facade (§12.3). Child anchors: w4-secure-view, w4-mvcc-locks, w4-ssi-witnesses, w4-strict-serializability, w4-merge-ladder (+ w4-ladder-strengthenings), w4-coordinator (+ w4-cert-cancel), w4-schema-catalog, w4-constraints, w4-valid-time (+ w4-temporal-operators, w4-temporal-nonoverlap), w4-escrow (+ w4-escrow-transitions), w4-ttl-expiry, w4-bulk-ddl, w4-index-lifecycle.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
This is the concurrency thesis of the whole design. B1 (One Version Universe): MVCC version chains ARE the immutable content-addressed objects Chronicle publishes — no second version store; time travel, branches, and replication ride the same chains. B2: the versioning granule matches the storage granule (Strata's ~4KiB sorted blocks). B5: every accept/reject decision is a registered law with an oracle, and every performance-shaped claim (abort rate, merge hit rate) is a `benchmark`-class distribution, never an assumed fact. B6 (agent-native): agents fork branches, run massively concurrent sessions, and merge; the semantic merge ladder plus escrow convert same-granule conflicts into algebra instead of aborts — exactly what agent swarms writing to shared memory graphs need. Market: the 2026 synthesis (§3.3) flags governance/access control and derived-state freshness as the gaps buyers cannot fill; the mandatory secure-view boundary, synchronous constraints with disclosure contracts, and expiry-as-visibility answer the governance gap. Donor rationale (§2.3, frankensqlite): page-granularity MVCC is adopted as block-granularity MVCC, but branch ancestry is semantic visibility, not a donor integer-only TxnId rule; page-Cahill/Fekete SSI + first-committer-wins + eager locking is adapted with logical predicate witnesses because deadlock freedom and SSI soundness do not transfer by analogy; the intent-log + deterministic rebase merge ladder is re-instantiated for graph intents with hit rate measured rather than assumed. Rejections (§3.4): eventual consistency as a default; a second Calvin-style transaction lane unless measured aborts justify reopening it; Weaver-style refinable timestamps set aside for 1.0 because one global scalar commit order simplifies Chronicle, branches, Ripple, and replay (W12 preserves that contract or explicitly reopens the decision).

## Design — normative detail
Default isolation is SERIALIZABLE via SSI over canonical logical read/write dependencies, conservatively represented by §7.3 witness types, and strengthened in the Local posture to STRICT SERIALIZABLE by the registered strictness law (w4-strict-serializability). Granularity (§7.2): blocks (~256 edges, ~4KiB) are the graph analogue of frankensqlite's pages — fine enough that writers to different neighborhoods never touch (real-workload fan-out means concurrent writes mostly hit distinct vertices, let alone blocks), coarse enough that lock/siread tables stay small and cache-resident. Vertex-level would false-conflict on hubs; edge-level would drown in metadata. Hub blocks that do contend escalate to delta-chains (§6.2.3), converting conflict into commutative appends — contention is handled by changing the data structure, not by tuning locks. Writers conflict on final logical effects after the merge ladder, constraints, FCW, and SSI are reevaluated. The monotone transaction state machine is `Active -> Validating -> FinalPrepared -> PayloadDurable -> OrderSubmitted -> CommandCommitted -> Applied(MarkerRef) -> Acknowledged`, with `Aborted` legal only before the irreversible ordering boundary and externally reported `Unknown` an unresolved observer outcome, never an internal rollback state. Single-node mode collapses consensus substates but not their ordering. DDL and logical bulk effects never bypass ordinary transactions. Core local invariants (idempotent transaction-token outcomes, fenced unique block/constraint-lock ownership, finite correctly ordered version chains) do not alone prove SI or SSI: publication, branch visibility, deletes, own writes, witness soundness, and metadata lifetime are separate registry obligations (§15.5, Appendix F).

## Invariants & claim types
The epic pins: FG-INV-02 (for every exclusive block, constraint-owner reservation, resource hold, allocation offset, final-certification basis, and escrow custody unit, at most one legal live generation owns or may consume it; stale/cancelled/expired/prior-configuration owners can neither mutate nor release); FG-INV-03 (finite, acyclic, strictly newer-first version chains within one owning object generation); FG-INV-05 (acyclic dependency graphs, real-time edges for Local); FG-INV-06 (witness conservativeness under refinement); FG-INV-17 (capability-stripped deterministic rebase, extensional equality of incremental replay); FG-INV-18 (synchronous constraints, resource budgets, and escrow bounds hold before commit); FG-INV-20 (authorization precedes every observation or effect). Strictness abort cost and merge-ladder hit rate are `benchmark`-class registered distributions.

## Interactions
Consumes: w2-commit-protocol / w2-txn-lifecycle / w2-snapshots-leases / w2-group-commit / w2-order-raft (ordering, capsules, fences), w3-tier-d (DeltaBlockVersion objects), w1-authz-policy (nonconstructible permits), w5-intent-log (the intent vocabulary the ladder replays). Produces: the certification, constraint, temporal, and escrow state consumed by w6 (Ripple canonical deltas), w9 (enforcement planes), w12 (the virtual-serial batch law generalizes the local reservation), and verif-oracles (SCC/Elle histories); plus the schema/catalog/coordinate objects (w4-schema-catalog: `CoordinateSchemaBinding`, `GraphReferenceBinding`, `CoordinateSchemaTransition`, posture machine, reserved-slot rows) consumed by w5-binder, the plan-cache/permit/certificate keys, and w9-enforcement's reserved-slot masking.

## Success Criteria
Epic closes only when every child anchor is closed AND: the independent SCC/Elle-on-authorities oracle passes lab-generated histories including the real-time-edge strengthening; the strict-serializability abort-rate benchmark distribution is registered and published; the incremental-vs-full merge-ladder differential oracle runs in CI on sampled conflicts; the Lean escrow conservation/bounds lane is green (the lane itself lands in `verif-formal`, which depends on `w4-escrow`, so a dep here would invert the intended order; at epic close the proof obligations must be registered, and lane-green is validated at gate-g4); the valid-time reference matrix (system-time x valid-time x branch x schema) passes; secure-view noninterference and hidden-vs-removed differential rows pass; every w4 schema named above has its `command_contracts.toml` / registry row landed at G0. Epic-level e2e: a scripted agent-swarm scenario (N concurrent sessions on forked branches writing contended blocks through fgdb-secure-view, exercising merge-ladder rebase, escrow decrements, a Unique-constraint race, valid-time/TTL reads, and an online index activation mid-run) must complete with structured logs capturing per-transaction state-machine transitions, ladder rung decisions, reservation lifecycle events, and certification outcomes; the log stream is machine-checked against the SCC/Elle oracle verdicts so post-implementation verification requires no manual inspection.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risks: witness conservatism inflates aborts (mitigated by refinement under budget plus benchmark gates); merge-ladder hit rate disappoints on real workloads (measured, decision-carded, never load-bearing for correctness); strictness law raises long-lived-writer aborts under Required-audit visible-prefix lag (registered cost). Rejected: Calvin-style second lane, refinable timestamps, eventual consistency, per-hub lock tuning, generic KV underlay transactionality.

## Provenance
Plan §7 (577-652), §4.6-4.8, §12.3, §2.3, §3.4, Appendix A (constraint/reservation schemas), Appendix F.

title: Deliver Loom: languages, one algebra, optimizer, and execution engine (Bet B3)
description:
## What & scope
Workstream W5 builds Loom, the entire path from source text to canonical result bytes: the crates `fgdb-gql` + `fgdb-cypher` (syntax only), `fgdb-bind`, `fgdb-algebra`, `fgdb-planner`, `fgdb-exec`, `fgdb-linalg`, and `fgdb-datalog`, with all reads flowing through `fgdb-secure-view`. Scope: (1) parsers for GQL ISO/IEC 39075:2024, the openCypher compatibility layer, versioned FQL dialect extensions (including reserved `DIFF` syntax), and the validated Datalog subset — all hand-written recursive-descent/Pratt per the frankensqlite parser school, since the closed universe forbids parser generators; (2) the binder/normalizer producing `PreparedQueryTemplate`, `BoundQuery<Role>`, and the immutable `CanonicalStatementClassification` (including bind-time `SnapshotQuery` and fused-autocommit eligibility); (3) the Appendix B graph intent log — intents, `CapturedIntentObservation`, canonical effects, `NetEffectNormalForm`, `CommittedEffectSet`, `LogicalDeltaTemplate`; (4) the single typed Graph-Logical Algebra (GLA) with the Appendix C operator inventory and its total-contract discipline, including the `Diff` operator family end-to-end; (5) factorization as a recursive value algebra with per-operator preservation laws and COLT access paths; (6) the optimizer — DP enumeration to hybrid binary/FreeJoin plans, branch-aware base+delta `StatsSegment`s, conformal cost intervals as FG-CAL-02 evidence, registered safe replanning, `LogicalOrbitId`/`PhysicalPlanId` identity, view rewrite targets; (7) CGSE determinism contracts — `SemanticProfile`, `CanonicalScalarProfile` `STRICT_PORTABLE`, tie-break policies, and §8.8 canonical result encoding (`CanonicalResultChunk`); (8) the `AnswerRequirement`/`ApproximationProfile`/`AnswerContract` three-phase approximation typing with the orthogonal freshness constraint; and (9) `ReplayManifest` with evidence slots, replay grades, and the replay registry under FG-INV-19.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Bet B3: one execution fabric — pattern matching, relational operators, temporal slicing, path finding, and linear-algebra kernels share one algebra and one cost model; there is no "graph engine bolted to a SQL engine" seam (§3.2 SPJM verdict). The §3.2 SOTA adoptions define the shape: Kùzu/Graphflow vectorized factorized execution as executor baseline (with stable VId and snapshot-local `OrdinalMapId` projections instead of dense identity), WCOJ through declared trie cursor orders, Free Join for conjunctive inner joins with COLT for missing orders, factorized databases via a registered preservation matrix, morsel-driven HyPer/Umbra/LeanStore engineering, and GQL adopted with a content-addressed language contract publishing exact ISO feature IDs and gaps. Bet B5 (determinism, evidence, calibrated adaptivity) is enforced here: byte-identical canonical results within an evidence closure, calibrated-not-promoted cost estimates, adaptive replanning only at registered safe points. Bet B6 (agent-native) gets `DIFF` between any two branch/time endpoints, the semantic intent vocabulary, replayable answers, and answer contracts an agent can reason about. Bets B1/B2/B4 are served through branch-aware statistics, Strata-native access paths, and the incrementalizability column that Ripple consumes.

## Design — normative detail
The pipeline is staged and typed: parse (AST only — parsing never produces executable plans) → bind/normalize (templates, roles, classification) → snapshot acquisition resolves `GraphReferenceBinding`s → `BoundQuery` → optimizer over bound typed IR only → morsel-parallel push execution through `fgdb-secure-view` → canonical result encoding → delivery classes owned by Fabric. Statement execution captures Appendix B intents; finalization emits canonical effects and the `NetEffectNormalForm`. Every realized stream is typed with an `AnswerContract`; every operator has a complete Appendix C row or is unavailable. Ownership boundaries: witness algebra and SSI live in W4 (`w4-ssi-witnesses`), Ripple derivative execution in W6, Beacon index physicals in W7, Prism projections in W8, wire delivery in W10 — Loom defines the contracts (incremental derivative column, witness domain column, `IndexProbe`/`HybridSearch` rows, canonical chunk target) that those workstreams implement against.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12 binds the whole epic: canonical scalar equality/hashing/ordering/encoding are coherent, and every claimed answer-equivalent seal, compaction, codec rewrite, spill, factorize/flatten, workspace materialization, safe replan, and exact derived rebuild preserves logical values, multiplicity, order, visibility, security projection, and `AnswerContract`; approximate candidate/topology changes create a new pinned semantic generation. FG-INV-17 binds rebase/merge re-execution to capability-stripped deterministic contexts pinned to `IntentSemanticsOid`. FG-INV-19 binds replay grades. FG-INV-20 binds authorization-precedes-observation across storage, statistics, routing/scoring, temporal selection, workspace, errors, and derived state. FG-CAL-01/02/03 and FG-EVID-01 govern the optimizer's adaptive/calibration claims (evidence class, never invariants); §17 rows (LDBC SNB/Graphalytics/FinBench, triangle count, 2-hop factorized, neighbor scan) are benchmark-class gates.

## Interactions
Children — anchors: `w5-parsers`, `w5-binder`, `w5-intent-log`, `w5-gla-algebra`, `w5-diff-operator`, `w5-factorization`, `w5-planner`, `w5-branch-stats`, `w5-executor`, `w5-determinism`, `w5-answer-contracts`, `w5-replay`; split-out subtasks, equally blocking: `w5-prepare-protocol` (from `w5-binder`), `w5-effects-normal-form` and `w5-intent-merge-algebras` (from `w5-intent-log`), `w5-operator-matrix` (from `w5-gla-algebra`), `w5-replay-registry` (from `w5-replay`). Upstream: `g0-language-contracts` (frozen contracts), `g0-command-contracts`/`g0-identity-registries` (registries), `w4-secure-view` (sole read facade), `w3-tier-r` (run/cursor contracts), `w2-snapshots-leases` (snapshot acquisition). Downstream consumers: `w4-coordinator`/`w4-merge-ladder` (intent batches, effects), `w6-zset-circuits` (incremental derivative column), `w7-*` (IndexProbe/HybridSearch physicals), `w8-projection`, `w10-result-machines`/`w10-snapshotquery` (chunk delivery), `verif-differential` (TCK/ISO), `verif-replay-products`.

## Success Criteria
Epic closes when all twelve anchors and the five split-out subtasks (`w5-prepare-protocol`, `w5-effects-normal-form`, `w5-intent-merge-algebras`, `w5-operator-matrix`, `w5-replay-registry`) close and: the openCypher TCK manifest and ISO feature matrix are published with exact feature IDs, prerequisites, and gaps; determinism CI proves byte-identical canonical encodings across parallelism degree, spill decisions, factorization, and legal replan variants; every dispatched operator has a registry row with conformance tests; §17 Loom benchmark gates run with pinned manifests and committed baselines; replay CI reproduces canonical logical output across plan/target/artifact variation. Cross-cutting e2e: a scripted parse→bind→classify→plan→execute→encode→replay run over a seeded fixture graph exercises every anchor in one pipeline and asserts byte-identical canonical results across two legal physical-plan variants and one replay. Detailed logging (required of the pipeline and its tests): each stage logs language-contract OID, classification digest, `LogicalOrbitId`/`PhysicalPlanId`, statistics rung consumed, realized `AnswerContract`, canonical result digest, and replay grade, so post-implementation verification can be performed from the structured event stream alone.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: separate graph and relational engines (the seam destroys the shared cost model); a Cypher-to-GQL transpiler shortcut (parsers converge only after binding and semantic normalization); loose dialect strings or server defaults changing semantics after binding; treating approximation as a certificate footnote instead of a semantic type; promoting conformal/estimator properties into invariants. Chief risk is scope: the Appendix C total-contract discipline means an operator without complete contracts is *unavailable*, so partial rows silently shrink the language surface — tracked by the registry-coverage check.

## Provenance
Plan §8 (all of 8.1–8.8), Appendix B, Appendix C, §3.2, §4.2, §18.1/18.2.
