title: Freeze audit terminal-freeze, signer-attempt, abandonment, and visibility-input contracts
description:
## What & scope
Freeze exact audit terminal-freeze, terminal-plan abandonment, signer-attempt, supersession, and visibility-input durable contracts. This task owns the schema/registry/transition surface; W2 and W9 implementation tasks make the relevant clauses live.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Recovery must distinguish no signer ever locked a basis, partial shares exist, an attempt was superseded, and an external batch already advanced. Without a rooted freeze and attempt ledger, recovery can sign two terminal bases, leak a hidden candidate, or strand authority and retention holds.

## Design — exact normative contract
The complete normative paragraphs follow:
Every protected terminal—not only an admitted W12 write—first freezes exactly the state that its signed event will terminalize. `TerminalAuditOwner` is the closed union `Local{owner:LocalAuditTicketOwner}|LocalPendingBegin{reservation_identity,txn_token,request_basis_commitment}|Meta{owner:AuditTicketOwner}|MetaPendingBegin{reservation_identity,scoped_begin_key_digest,request_basis_commitment}`; pending-begin owner arms are legal only before registration for their exact role's BeginTerminal scope and resolve `AuditResolutionOrigin::Unclaimed`, while Local/Meta owner arms require the registered claim domain. Every tag must match group, ticket admission, request basis, and freeze scope. `ControlTerminalBasisHoldRoot {domain,freeze_scope,typed_held_predicates[ControlTerminalHeldPredicate],strong_dependency_refs[RegisteredStrongRef],coordinate_index_config_key_policy_resource_continuity_coverage_bitmap,conflict_matrix_version,body_digest}` is generated from the exact control spec/expected conditions. Every possibly conflicting mutation, checkpoint cut, GC, key/config/policy retirement, and restore/backup transition consults the active hold root and must wait, transfer it exactly, or reject.

`AuditTerminalFreezeRecord` is an immutable predecessor-linked Local-or-Meta object `{domain:{database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,group_role:Local|Meta,group_id},predecessor_ref:StrongRef<AuditTerminalFreezeRecord>?,state:Armed{freeze_scope,owner:TerminalAuditOwner,ticket_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicket>,expected_state_conditions_digest,terminal_semantic_basis_commitment,control_terminal_basis_hold_root_ref:StrongRef<ControlTerminalBasisHoldRoot>,scaffolding_applied_ref:AppliedControlRef}|Consumed{terminal_input_identity,assigned_role_order,hold_disposition:ConsumedByTerminal}|ReleasePending{release_admission_closed_at_role_order,control_terminal_basis_hold_root_ref:StrongRef<ControlTerminalBasisHoldRoot>,closed_terminal_attempt_index_generation,closed_signer_release_fence_vector[{signer_id,event_journal_generation,resolution_journal_generation,release_fence_receipt_ref}],blocking_set_proof_ref:StrongRef<AuditSignerBlockingSetProof>,begin_release_applied_ref:AppliedControlRef}|Released{typed_no_terminal_proof_ref:StrongRef<NoTerminalSignatureOrOrderProof>,hold_release_commitment,release_applied_ref:AppliedControlRef}}`; `AuditTerminalFreezeIndex` maps `(domain,owner,ticket)` to the unique latest version and forbids two successors. Prepared/configuration floors, backup/restore, and GC retain each live hold. The terminal apply or FinalizeRelease is the only operation that releases it.

`AuditTerminalFreezeSpec` is the closed lifecycle-scaffolding transition `Arm{group_role,freeze_scope,owner:TerminalAuditOwner,ticket_ref,expected_state_conditions_digest,terminal_semantic_basis_commitment,control_terminal_basis_hold_root_ref:StrongRef<ControlTerminalBasisHoldRoot>,expected_index_absence_or_matching_retry,terminal_audit_gate:LifecycleScaffoldingNotRequired}|BeginRelease{group_role,armed_freeze_ref:StrongRef<AuditTerminalFreezeRecord>,expected_index_value:Armed,expected_terminal_attempt_index_generation,sorted_signer_release_fence_receipts,blocking_set_proof_ref:StrongRef<AuditSignerBlockingSetProof>,expected_state_conditions_digest,terminal_audit_gate:LifecycleScaffoldingNotRequired}|FinalizeRelease{group_role,release_pending_freeze_ref:StrongRef<AuditTerminalFreezeRecord>,no_terminal_signature_or_order_proof_ref:StrongRef<NoTerminalSignatureOrOrderProof>,expected_index_value:ReleasePending,expected_closed_attempt_and_signer_journal_vector,exact_hold_release_recipe,terminal_audit_gate:LifecycleScaffoldingNotRequired}`. Arm scopes are `LocalControl`, `LocalBeginTerminal`, `MetaControl{registered_global_control_tag,spec_body_digest,expected_state_conditions_digest}`, `MetaBeginTerminal`, `MetaStatementPublishOrAbort`, `MetaActiveCancel`, and `MetaReadClose`; Arm apply atomically validates the complete basis, installs its hold, and freezes it before any terminal signature. BeginRelease first makes every signer in the complete eligible universe—or a registered blocking set proved to intersect every legal event and resolution threshold subset—durably reject new attempts/locks/shares for this freeze at the named journal generations, then selects ReleasePending without dropping the hold. FinalizeRelease byte-matches proof/freeze/ticket/domain/basis, unchanged generations, and exact hold release and alone produces Released; `Consumed` remains an atomic terminal output. Admitted Local mutation and W12 write use their ordered final-certification reservation holds instead.

`AuditTerminalFreezeRef` is the closed union `LocalMutation{fence_ref:StrongRef<LocalTerminalAdmissionFence>,required_fence_state:Armed,final_certification_reservation_ref:StrongRef<LocalFinalCertificationReservation>,required_reservation_state:Active}|LocalControl{freeze_ref:StrongRef<AuditTerminalFreezeRecord>,required_scope:LocalControl}|LocalBeginTerminal{freeze_ref:StrongRef<AuditTerminalFreezeRecord>,reservation_identity,txn_token,request_basis_commitment,required_scope:LocalBeginTerminal}|MetaControl{freeze_ref:StrongRef<AuditTerminalFreezeRecord>,required_scope:MetaControl{registered_global_control_tag,spec_body_digest,expected_state_conditions_digest}}|MetaBeginTerminal{freeze_ref:StrongRef<AuditTerminalFreezeRecord>,reservation_identity,scoped_begin_key_digest,request_basis_commitment,required_scope:MetaBeginTerminal}|MetaStatementPublishOrAbort{freeze_ref:StrongRef<AuditTerminalFreezeRecord>,required_scope:MetaStatementPublishOrAbort}|MetaActiveCancel{freeze_ref:StrongRef<AuditTerminalFreezeRecord>,required_scope:MetaActiveCancel}|MetaReadClose{freeze_ref:StrongRef<AuditTerminalFreezeRecord>,required_scope:MetaReadClose}|MetaAdmittedWrite{fence_ref:StrongRef<MetaTerminalAdmissionFence>,required_fence_state:Armed,final_certification_reservation_ref:StrongRef<GlobalFinalCertificationReservation>,required_reservation_state:Active}`. The exact SequenceNeutralSpec envelope field matrix makes this ref required on every final protected terminal tag and forbidden elsewhere; it is never silently injected into a body. An admitted-write plan byte-matches the reservation's one selected terminal. Final protected apply atomically consumes its unique reservation/freeze or constructs the terminal successor while Armed; release is legal only after ReleasePending with the typed proof that no signature share, quorum object, final command, or candidate root exists.

`NoTerminalSignatureOrOrderProof` is an authority-local quorum certificate `{SameGroupCertificateHeader,freeze_ref:StrongRef<AuditTerminalFreezeRecord>,required_freeze_state:ReleasePending,ticket_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicket>,owner:TerminalAuditOwner,terminal_semantic_basis_commitment,plan_disposition:NeverCreated{terminal_attempt_index_absence_path,signer_release_fence_and_attempt_absence_proofs_by_signer}|SemanticPlanAbandoned{terminal_plan_ref:StrongRef<AuditTerminalSigningPlan>,abandonment_ref:StrongRef<AuditTerminalPlanAbandonment>,all_event_attempt_disposition_refs[],no_event_or_resolution_object_proof,retired_attempt_epoch_floor},audit_terminal_attempt_index_root_digest,sorted_event_signer_journal_closures,sorted_resolution_signer_journal_closures,certificate_ledger_root_digest,complete_signer_set_and_key_epoch,raft_nonorder_evidence:{term,configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,read_barrier_index,commit_index,applied_index,closed_role_order,terminal_command_index_absence_path},candidate_root_and_audit_visibility_pipeline_absence_proof,external_audit_continuity_digest_and_cas_version,quiescence_barrier_id,checker_version,certificate_attempt_plan_ref,certificate_signer_lock_refs,quorum_signatures}`. All paths, release fences, attempt dispositions, signer-journal closures, and authority roots are observed at one linearizable quiescence barrier after BeginRelease selected ReleasePending; generations equal the closed vector in that state. A release fence covers every current eligible event/resolution signer or a proved blocking set intersecting every legal subset. NeverCreated is invalid if any matching semantic plan/signing attempt/lock/share existed. SemanticPlanAbandoned requires every concrete event attempt terminally superseded/abandoned with no event; a partial-share attempt needs quorum-impossibility and signer-closure evidence. The certificate is built after BeginRelease and before FinalizeRelease, names no future release command/result/root, and remains through freeze/audit retirement floors. Any missing signer/blocking proof, later-orderable command, candidate, stale Raft/configuration basis, or latent completable attempt makes release ineligible.

`AuditTerminalPlanAbandonSpec` is the exact freeze-backed Local-or-Meta maintenance input `{group_role,release_pending_freeze_ref:StrongRef<AuditTerminalFreezeRecord>,terminal_plan_ref:StrongRef<AuditTerminalSigningPlan>,expected_attempt_index_entry:PlanSelected|EventAttemptSelected|AttemptSuperseded,expected_per_signer_release_fence_vector,event_attempt_disposition_refs[],no_event_or_resolution_object_proof_ref:StrongRef<AuditStageNonpublicationProof>,complete_eligible_signer_universe,attempt_epoch_retirement_recipe,terminal_audit_gate:LifecycleScaffoldingNotRequired}`. It is legal only while the freeze is ReleasePending, every concrete event attempt is either share-free or quorum-impossible and durably closed, no event/resolution/terminal order/candidate exists, and every otherwise eligible signer is release-fenced. Apply creates `AuditTerminalPlanAbandonment {freeze_identity,terminal_plan_identity,closed_attempt_index_generation,closed_signer_journal_vector,event_attempt_disposition_commitment,retired_attempt_epoch_floor,maintenance_applied_index}` and marks the semantic plan AbandonedForFreezeRelease. It erases nothing and authorizes no replacement terminal. Any event, resolution attempt, prepared terminal, order, or candidate makes true plan abandonment permanently illegal. Admitted-write reservations cannot use this spec; they keep the selected terminal and use signing-attempt supersession until completion. All abandoned plan/attempt/lock/share evidence remains rooted through FinalizeRelease and the audit-retirement floor.

After the freeze/reservation, matching mutation/read/control/no-effect audit bytes use one acyclic, crash-recoverable signing pipeline; only the completed ticket/event/resolution triple becomes the final `TerminalAuditGate`. `SequenceNeutralAuditEventBody` is the pre-order immutable `{ticket_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicket>,owner:TerminalAuditOwner,chosen_terminal_kind,semantic_input_commitment,authorization_decision_digest,outcome:TransactionMutation|ControlMutation|ReadResult|Denied|Failed|Abandoned,event_attested_at,stable_ticket_domain_profile_epoch_and_unresolved_membership_commitment,body_digest}`. Its registered digest excludes only `body_digest` and contains no plan/attempt/lock/share/aggregate, mutable audit-continuity head/CAS version/append position, future role order/HLC/marker/candidate, or result root. `SequenceNeutralAuditResolutionBody` is `{ticket_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicket>,owner,terminal_class,expected_event_body_digest,stable_ticket_domain_profile_epoch_and_unresolved_membership_commitment,resolution_attested_at,body_digest}` with the same exclusions. `AuditTerminalSigningPlan` is the immutable semantic plan `{plan_id,plan_generation,predecessor_plan_ref:StrongRef<AuditTerminalSigningPlan>?,terminal_freeze_ref:AuditTerminalFreezeRef,ticket_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicket>,owner:TerminalAuditOwner,chosen_terminal_kind,semantic_input_commitment,event_body_ref:StrongRef<SequenceNeutralAuditEventBody>,event_body_digest,resolution_body_ref:StrongRef<SequenceNeutralAuditResolutionBody>,resolution_body_digest,event_signer_policy_ref,resolution_signer_policy_ref,event_threshold_rule,resolution_threshold_rule,signature_algorithm_and_encoding}`. It selects no concrete signer subset and binds only stable ticket/domain/profile/epoch/unresolved-membership facts; unrelated ticket issue/resolve and the mutable external audit head may advance without invalidating it.

Concrete subsets are replaceable attempts. `AuditEventSigningAttemptPlan {attempt_id,terminal_plan_ref:StrongRef<AuditTerminalSigningPlan>,event_body_digest,configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,canonical_signer_subset[{signer_id,signing_key_id,signer_set_epoch,key_epoch}],threshold,signature_algorithm_and_encoding}` is installed through nonsemantic maintenance before any event lock. For each selected signer, `AuditEventSignerLock {attempt_plan_ref:StrongRef<AuditEventSigningAttemptPlan>,terminal_plan_ref:StrongRef<AuditTerminalSigningPlan>,event_body_digest,signer_id,signing_key_id,signer_set_epoch,key_epoch,canonical_signing_transcript_digest,one_digest_only=true}` is signer-journal-published before `AuditEventSignatureShare`. `AuditEventRecord` deterministically adds `{terminal_plan_ref,event_attempt_plan_ref,event_body_ref,event_lock_refs,event_signature_share_refs,signer_subset_bitmap,threshold,canonical_aggregate_or_signature_set}` to the exact pre-order body; its signing transcript is `H(domain,terminal_plan_oid,event_attempt_oid,event_body_digest,signer identity/key/epochs)` and thereby binds the plan without a plan↔event cycle.

Only after the event exists may maintenance install `AuditResolutionSigningAttemptPlan {attempt_id,terminal_plan_ref:StrongRef<AuditTerminalSigningPlan>,event_ref:StrongRef<AuditEventRecord>,resolution_body_digest,configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,canonical_signer_subset[{signer_id,signing_key_id,signer_set_epoch,key_epoch}],threshold,signature_algorithm_and_encoding}`. Each selected signer publishes `AuditResolutionSignerLock {attempt_plan_ref:StrongRef<AuditResolutionSigningAttemptPlan>,terminal_plan_ref:StrongRef<AuditTerminalSigningPlan>,event_ref:StrongRef<AuditEventRecord>,resolution_body_digest,signer_id,signing_key_id,signer_set_epoch,key_epoch,canonical_signing_transcript_digest,one_digest_only=true}` before its share. `AuditTicketResolution` deterministically adds the terminal plan, resolution attempt, event ref, exact resolution lock/share bijection, signer bitmap, threshold, and canonical aggregate/signature set to the pre-order resolution body. Signer identity/key/epoch are part of every lock/share transcript, so selected signers cannot share a lock ObjectId. Missing, duplicate, unplanned, wrong-key, wrong-epoch, reordered, or aggregate-mismatched shares fail closed.

`AuditSigningAttemptSupersedeSpec` is the nonsemantic maintenance input `{stage:Event|Resolution,terminal_plan_ref:StrongRef<AuditTerminalSigningPlan>,old_attempt_plan_ref:StrongRef<AuditEventSigningAttemptPlan|AuditResolutionSigningAttemptPlan>,new_attempt_plan_ref:StrongRef<AuditEventSigningAttemptPlan|AuditResolutionSigningAttemptPlan>,required_identical_body_and_event_commitment,old_signer_release_fence_vector,old_share_state:ZeroShares|PartialShares{complete_share_bitmap,quorum_impossibility_proof_ref:StrongRef<AuditSignerQuorumImpossibilityProof>},no_completed_stage_object_or_terminal_order_candidate_proof_ref:StrongRef<AuditStageNonpublicationProof>,terminal_freeze_or_final_certification_reservation_ref,terminal_audit_gate:LifecycleScaffoldingNotRequired}`. Every old signer capable of completing the subset must close that attempt; the new attempt uses a higher ID, the identical terminal/event/resolution body, and a currently legal subset. Event supersession is illegal after an event exists; resolution supersession preserves the exact event. It never changes/release the terminal freeze, final-certification selection, ticket, semantic body, or result. Old attempts/locks/shares/closures remain rooted. Thus signer loss before or after partial shares cannot strand an admitted terminal, while two attempts can never both complete. True freeze release/terminal-plan abandonment remains the separate preterminal path below.

`AuditVisibilityAdvanceInputRef` is the closed same-group union `Local{spec_ref:StrongRef<AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec<Local>>,maintenance_command_ref:StrongRef<LocalMaintenanceCommand>}|Meta{spec_ref:StrongRef<AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec<Meta>>,maintenance_command_ref:StrongRef<MetaMaintenanceCommand>}`; each command must be the registered envelope whose sole body is the named spec. `AuditTerminalAttemptRecord` is a predecessor-linked durable stage chain `{predecessor_ref:StrongRef<AuditTerminalAttemptRecord>?,terminal_plan_ref:StrongRef<AuditTerminalSigningPlan>,state:PlanSelected|EventAttemptSelected{attempt_plan_ref:StrongRef<AuditEventSigningAttemptPlan>}|EventLocksPublished{attempt_plan_ref,event_lock_refs[StrongRef<AuditEventSignerLock>],complete_planned_lock_bijection}|EventSharesCollected{attempt_plan_ref,event_lock_refs,event_share_refs[StrongRef<AuditEventSignatureShare>],event_ref:StrongRef<AuditEventRecord>}|ResolutionAttemptSelected{event_ref,resolution_attempt_plan_ref:StrongRef<AuditResolutionSigningAttemptPlan>}|ResolutionLocksPublished{event_ref,resolution_attempt_plan_ref,resolution_lock_refs[StrongRef<AuditResolutionSignerLock>],complete_planned_lock_bijection}|Prepared{event_ref,resolution_attempt_plan_ref,resolution_lock_refs,resolution_share_refs[StrongRef<AuditResolutionSignatureShare>],resolution_ref:StrongRef<AuditTicketResolution>,terminal_gate_digest}|Ordered{terminal_input_identity,role_order}|CandidateApplied{candidate_root_identity}|ExternalBatchCasCommitted{batch_ref:StrongRef<AuditExternalResolutionBatch>,receipt_ref:StrongRef<AuditExternalBatchCasReceipt>,batch_member_ordinal}|VisibilityReleased{advance_input_ref:AuditVisibilityAdvanceInputRef,assigned_maintenance_index,pipeline_order,released_candidate_identity}|AttemptSuperseded{stage,old_attempt_identity,new_attempt_identity,supersede_evidence_ref:StrongRef<AuditSigningAttemptSupersession>}}`. Each successor retains its predecessor and needed artifacts. `VisibilityReleased` names only the already-built spec/maintenance command and the scalar index assigned while applying it; it never points to the future maintenance-applied record or resulting Protocol root. The matching prepared root plus generated `AuditTerminalAttemptIndex` maps `(domain,freeze_or_reservation_identity,terminal_plan_identity)` to the latest record and separately maps each concrete signing-attempt ID to Active|Superseded|Completed; exact absence/membership proofs are therefore available even at PlanSelected.

Before event locks, validation checks the Armed freeze/Active final-certification reservation rather than reserving semantic order. Immediately before ordering, the final transaction/control input consumes that hold, takes the then-next role order/HLC through the order supplement, and records Ordered. Candidate apply appends the RequiredPending pipeline entry, selects Semantic `AuditTicketIndexValue::TerminalPrepared`, and records CandidateApplied without exposing it. The external resolver selects only a gap-free prefix from the pipeline, builds `AuditExternalResolutionBatch`, CASes from the then-current continuity head to one direct-successor `TicketsResolvedBatch` record, and returns `AuditExternalBatchCasReceipt`; each included attempt records `ExternalBatchCasCommitted` with its exact member ordinal. `AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec` verifies that batch and releases exactly the same pipeline prefix, creates `VisibilityReleased` and `AuditOutcomeRecord` successors using its already-built maintenance command identity plus assigned maintenance index, and advances public visibility through `VisibleAuditOutcomeIndex`. Signed bodies never bind a stale expected continuity head. Crash resumes the selected or legally superseded signing attempt, locked digests, collected shares, durable stage, exact external batch/CAS, or pending visibility advance. A definitive external conflict triggers fail-closed recovery/permanent-gap handling and retains the attempt; it never exposes a candidate. Decision/shard apply and public-result guards verify the visibility-released audit outcome against the original TerminalPrepared claim and hold. Crash/DPOR suites race unrelated ticket issue/resolve operations, every scope/lock/share/supersede stage, alternate terminal, leader loss, reproposal, batch selection, external CAS, partial response loss, and visibility-advance recovery.

## Invariants & claims
Enforces FG-INV-03, FG-INV-16, FG-INV-17, and FG-INV-20. Freeze/attempt state is rooted authority, not telemetry. No plan is abandoned after an incompatible signer lock/share or order attempt exists; no protected candidate is visible before exact external resolution and gap-free visibility input.

## Interactions and ownership
Consumes exact authority bindings and identity registries. W2 Local audit core implements Local arms; W9 protected-order, pipeline, and release tasks implement signing/external-authority behavior. Final-certification cancellation must prove the separate no-signature/no-order condition.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every freeze, proof, abandon, signing plan/lock/share, supersession, attempt record/index, and visibility-input type has one stable row, exact reference strengths, construction DAG, floors, and role predicate.
- Unit/golden tests cover every arm/digest; mutation tests reject wrong terminal basis, signer set, attempt generation, predecessor, command position, ticket, candidate, external batch, visibility input, or role.
- Model/property tests prove one selected terminal basis, signer-lock monotonicity, no incompatible shares, justified supersession, and release only for the exact gap-free prefix.
- Crash/DPOR injects around freeze publication, plan selection, each lock/share, quorum, order attempt, candidate publication, external CAS, visibility input, apply, abandonment, supersession, and takeover.
- E2E runs no-signature abandonment, partial-share recovery, superseded attempt, lost external response, out-of-order completion, permanent gap, and successful release with restart at every phase.
- Structured JSONL emits {event_version,role_and_group,ticket_digest,terminal_basis_digest,freeze_id,freeze_state,attempt_id,attempt_generation,signer_id?,lock_digest?,share_digest?,superseded_attempt_id?,order_attempt_id?,candidate_pipeline_order?,external_batch_digest?,visibility_input_kind?,transition,recovery_action,replay_command}. Hidden event bodies and undisclosed reasons remain redacted.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: in-memory signer locks, no-response-means-no-signature, deleting abandoned plans, reusing transaction cancellation evidence, and deriving visibility from the latest external head without an exact input ref. Detailed attempts compact only after visibility and cut floors.

## Provenance
Plan Appendix A lines 1824-1846; G0 clause coverage; section 12.8 audit.

### Detailed diagnostic-event contract
Every checker and implementation transition emits versioned redacted JSONL keyed by `AuditTerminalEventId`: `event_version,event_id,run_id,role_group,audit_domain_public_commitment,subject_kind,subject_public_commitment,plan_or_freeze_generation,state_before,state_after,required_ticket_interval,visibility_prefix_before,visibility_prefix_after,signing_attempt_id?,dispatch_state?,abandonment_basis?,authority_binding_public_commitment,checker_id,verdict,failure_class,artifact_refs,replay_command`. Construction-order tests require exactly one ordered event for freeze, candidate construction, signer attempt/terminal evidence, import, visibility, abandonment, and terminal release as applicable; missing, duplicate, reordered, uncorrelated, secret-bearing, ticket-content-bearing, tenant/principal-bearing, or hidden-state-bearing events fail. Unit tests validate schema/cardinality/redaction; E2E crash/retry/abandon scenarios reconstruct the complete legal terminal path from logs alone.

title: Freeze exact role authority-binding formats and exhaustive substitution matrix
description:
## What & scope
Freeze and make executable the exact durable authority-binding format family used by every Local, Meta, and Shard object that can authorize observation, mutation, delivery, replay, retention, or external action. This task owns the canonical role-indexed schemas, generated reference unions, binding projections, and the exhaustive authority-bearing-schema matrix; later authz, command, wire, result, restore, and W12 work consumes these types and may not invent abbreviated bindings.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Authorization-before-observation is only structural when the complete authority state is an unforgeable typed input. Repeated scalar epochs are not enough: two states can share an epoch while differing in policy root, revocation root, service epoch, tenant, principal, purpose, ceiling, or role. The exact binding family prevents substitution, keeps cross-group authority portable without exposing raw local refs, and supplies the format-level foundation for FG-INV-20 and capability-safe replay.

## Design — exact normative contract
The following plan text is included in this bead so implementation never needs to consult the source plan:
Generated reference unions are exact rather than erased. For each containing schema and role, `durable_fields.toml` emits a finite tagged union such as `LocalCommandInputRef`, `MetaAppliedResultRef`, `ShardProtocolEvidenceRef`, or `MandatoryInventoryRef`; every arm names one top-level target schema and carries the target's canonical typed reference encoding. Bare `StrongRef`, `StrongRef<A|B>`, `StrongRef[]`, `result_refs[StrongRef]`, slash-separated pseudo-types, or a generic `RegisteredStrongRef` without a containing-schema-generated arm set are invalid in normative bytes. Compact renderings that use such shorthand are navigation-only and must expand through an exact field-table row. A generated construction-DAG test creates the concrete graph for every command tag and state slot and rejects self, mutual, or future-result edges.

Security binding is schema-enforced rather than name-enforced. `AuthorityOwningRole` is the closed set `Local|Meta`; Shards consume certified projections but never originate an authority record or permit. `AuthorityBindingRecord<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is the independently addressable `{role,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch,tenant,principal,non_widenable_authority_ceiling_digest,purpose_class,security_state_binding:SecurityStateBinding,authority_digest,body_digest:BodyDigest<AuthorityBindingRecord<Role>>}`; `AuthorityBindingRef<Role>` is the generated exact role arm that strongly selects it. `AuthorityBoundHeader<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is the embedded `{authority_binding_ref:AuthorityBindingRef<Role>,authority_digest,security_policy_epoch,revocation_index}` projection and every repeated value must byte-match the record.

`MetaAuthorityBindingProjection` is the portable certified projection `{source_authority_binding_public_commitment,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch,tenant_commitment,principal_commitment,non_widenable_authority_ceiling_commitment,purpose_class,exact_clipped_operation_read_write_disclosure_and_resource_scopes,security_policy_epoch,revocation_index,source_meta_prefix,source_configuration_and_retention_grant_evidence,projection_digest,signatures}`. `ShardAuthorityBindingProjection` is the shard-local exact `{security_state_projection:ShardSecurityStateProjection,certified_source_authority_projection_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<MetaAuthorityBindingProjection>,source_authority_binding_public_commitment,tenant_commitment,principal_commitment,non_widenable_authority_ceiling_commitment,purpose_class,exact_clipped_operation_read_write_disclosure_and_resource_scopes,source_meta_prefix,source_configuration_and_grant_commitment,projection_digest}`. The certified source projection and local security projection must agree on namespace/incarnation/service epoch/policy/revocation and cannot be recombined from different Meta prefixes or principals. `AuthorityBindingFor<Role>` is the generated closed role family `Local{header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>}|Meta{header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Meta>}|Shard{projection:ShardAuthorityBindingProjection}`; exactly one arm is inhabitable for a given containing role. Every durable field set marked `authority_bearing=true` must contain exactly one inline complete binding, one `AuthorityBoundHeader`, or—only for a shard consumer—the exact `ShardAuthorityBindingProjection`; scalar epochs/digests, a permit reference alone, the narrower `ShardSecurityStateProjection`, or an opaque “authority projection digest” alone fail G0. Public wire values cannot carry local refs, so their signed/MACed header contains `security_state_binding_public_commitment`; the durable issuance/replay record strongly retains the complete AuthorityBindingRecord and proves that commitment. The generated matrix covers permits, admissions/releases, audit-requirement decisions, prepared/final owners, intents/batches/effects, constraints/resources/escrow, derived identities/builds, plans/replay, result/cursor/output promises, DP, backup/export, descriptor views, cache keys, dispatch attempts, and every command authorization. Every Local/Meta outer command carries exactly one complete `AuthorityBoundHeader` that byte-matches its authorization object and frozen reservation; a Shard command instead carries the exact `ShardAuthorityBindingProjection` named by its imported authorization. Equal-scalar/different-root/service/tenant/principal/ceiling/role/purpose substitution is a mandatory negative fixture.

The sole authority-retention exception is a terminal, nonrevivable, nonpayload tombstone. `TerminalAuthorityCommitment<Role>` is the reference-free `{role,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch,authority_binding_body_digest,authority_digest,security_state_binding_public_commitment,tenant_principal_ceiling_purpose_commitment,final_disclosure_and_answer_contract_commitment,body_digest}`. It is derived byte-for-byte from the last live `AuthorityBindingFor<Role>` before that strong authority edge is released. A terminal commitment can prove identity, nonreuse, disclosure/answer compatibility, and tombstone equality only; it cannot authorize output, lookup of protected payload, resume, widening, mutation, resurrection, or a new capability. Any later status/lookup request must independently validate the caller against the exact current role binding/capability and compare its public commitments before returning a uniformly nonrevealing terminal projection. Any live/revivable/byte-owning state that substitutes this commitment for a full binding fails G0.

## Invariants & claims
This is G0 binding text for FG-INV-20 and the authority-bearing portions of FG-INV-13, FG-INV-15, FG-INV-16, and FG-INV-19. TerminalAuthorityCommitment<Role> is evidence about an irreversibly terminal, nonrevivable, payload-free subject; it is never an authorization token and cannot be used for lookup, result resume, output, mutation, key access, or renewed retention.

## Interactions and ownership
Consumes the G0 threat/trust model and identity registries. The command registry must use the exact role binding in every authority arm; fgdb-w1-authz-policy generates nonconstructible permits from it; wire projections expose only registered public commitments; result, audit, DP, restore, backup, GC, and W12 tasks must name the exact role type or certified projection. No consumer may duplicate namespace/incarnation/service/tenant/principal/policy/revocation fields as independently trusted scalars.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Registry generation emits AuthorityBindingRecord<Role>, AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>, AuthorityBindingRef<Role>, MetaAuthorityBindingProjection, ShardAuthorityBindingProjection, AuthorityBindingFor<Role>, and every complete generated reference union with stable IDs/tags.
- A generated matrix enumerates every authority-bearing schema and proves it carries exactly one complete legal binding or exact certified projection.
- Golden and cross-version vectors byte-freeze every role arm, field tag, projection, public commitment, and BodyDigest recipe.
- Unit tests cover canonical encode/decode, field inclusion/exclusion, exact/nonwidening relations, terminal commitment construction, and role-specific reference resolution.
- Property and mutation tests vary one field at a time and reject equal scalar epochs paired with different roots, service epoch, tenant, principal, purpose, authority ceiling, role, group, configuration, or certified projection.
- Compile-fail tests prove terminal commitments cannot construct permits or guards; fuzzing rejects cross-role tags, bare StrongRef arrays, slash pseudo-types, unresolved target kinds, and unknown required fields.
- E2E substitution corpus runs Local, Meta, and Shard requests through admission, restart, checkpoint, backup/restore, and service-epoch change; every mismatch fails before observation and produces the same public nonrevealing failure class.
- Structured JSONL diagnostics emit {event_version,schema_id,role_and_group,subject_kind,binding_digest,public_commitment,check_kind,verdict,mismatch_field?,expected_digest?,observed_digest?,source_projection_kind?,replay_command}. Logs never contain secrets, raw capability bytes, hidden graph facts, or DP seed material. Tests fail on missing, duplicated, secret-bearing, or out-of-order events.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: epoch-only checks, optional root fields, digest-only Shard authority, role-erased bindings, and terminal commitments reused as permits. Risk: pervasive type parameters add surface area; that cost is intentional because it makes wrong-role and incomplete-binding states unrepresentable.

## Provenance
Plan section 5.1 authority binding and Appendix A lines 328-334; FG-INV-20.

### Fidelity addendum — session authorization is a first-class authority owner
The plan's result/cursor receipts and `LifecycleAuthoritySource::AuthenticatedSession` require `SessionAuthorizationRecord<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` to be an independently addressable, registered exact role family before any consumer lands. Its minimum normative body is `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,session_binding,auth_context_generation,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch,server_process_incarnation,authentication_method_and_credential_commitment,exact_nonwidenable_operation_read_write_disclosure_and_resource_ceiling,issued_under_security_state_binding,issuance_time_basis_ref,not_before,expires_at,predecessor_or_refresh_commitment?,body_digest}`. Every repeated namespace/incarnation/epoch/authority value byte-matches the header; refresh creates a new generation proved equal-or-narrower, never mutates the record or widens it. Shard is uninhabited.

`durable_fields.toml` must give every receipt's `session_authorization_ref` an exact role-valid target arm. Unit/golden tests cover codec/transcript/tag stability; substitution negatives cover wrong role, session, process incarnation, auth generation, service epoch, principal, ceiling, time basis, and widened refresh. E2E authenticates, refreshes narrower, ACKs/releases a result and cursor, restarts the process, and proves old-process or old-generation receipts cannot be newly minted while exact retry of an already accepted receipt remains idempotent. Logs emit only commitments: `role`, `session_binding_commitment`, `auth_context_generation`, `service_visibility_epoch`, `process_incarnation`, `authority_body_digest`, `ceiling_digest`, and validation verdict; credentials and protected identifiers never appear.

title: Author invariants/evidence/slo registries, claim constitution, and activation contract
description:
## What & scope
Author the claim-type constitution and its three carrier registries: `invariants.toml` (exact safety/liveness invariants only), `evidence.toml` (statistical claims), `slo.toml` (empirical operational targets), plus the clause-granular twenty-ID activation contract over the FG-INV spine and the machine-readable restatement of §1's twelve constitutional constraints. It also lands two §19-listed G0 artifacts with no other home: the six-bet vocabulary (B1–B6) as registered identifiers that other registries and beads reference, and the proof-lane manifests — the asupersync-inherited formal-layer house style (Lean-checked invariants, TLA+ export discipline) binding every `proof`-class claim to a named lane, model scope, and checked artifact (§18's G0 materialization list). This bead defines the schemas, authors the initial content, and wires the CI that enforces the constitution; the per-invariant row text itself is materialized in g0-invariant-spine.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5 rests on never confusing a measured number with a proof. The 2026 market's unsolved problems — governance and freshness-of-derived-state — are unsolved partly because vendors state them as marketing claims with no type discipline. FrankenGraphDB's differentiator is outsider-verifiable evidence: that requires every load-bearing statement to carry a class, an owner, a checker, and an activation predicate from day zero.

## Design — normative detail
**The six claim classes (constraint 11):** every load-bearing statement is registered as exactly one of `invariant` (must hold on every execution), `proof` (theorem within a named formal model), `bounded_model` (checked only within declared bounds), `statistical` (confidence statement under named assumptions), `slo` (empirical operational target), or `benchmark` (measured on a pinned fixture). A weaker claim class may inform policy but may not enforce or justify a stronger one.

**The twelve constitutional constraints (§1), restated:** (1) the dependency universe is closed — `core`/`alloc`/`std`, nightly Rust, asupersync, `fnx-*`, design-level fork of frankensqlite into `fgdb-*`; everything else in-house; no serde/tokio/rocksdb/arrow/tantivy/hnswlib; PyO3 confined to the Python packaging boundary. (2) Memory safety is structural — workspace-default `unsafe_code = "forbid"`; raw-pointer code lives only in `fgdb-unsafe-*` boundary crates with `deny(unsafe_code)` plus narrowly scoped ledgered `allow` sites; every unsafe site gets a ledger row (path, invariant, evidence, scalar/safe fallback, no-claim boundary); CI rejects unledgered sites. (3) `Cx` everywhere — every function doing I/O, locking, shared-arena allocation, or blocking accepts `&Cx`, enabling lab-runtime substitution, cancellation-correct timeouts, and capability narrowing. (4) Deterministic by default with an explicit domain — same evidence closure (root object and branch head, normalized query and parameters, semantic/capability/policy epochs, executable artifacts, index generations, numeric profile, recorded external inputs) ⇒ byte-identical canonical logical-result encoding including order; transport chunking excluded; cross-machine strict mode uses the §8.6 portable numeric profile. (5) Single artifact, three postures — embedded `fgdb` library, `fgdbd` server (FGP/HTTP2/gRPC/WebSocket/Bolt subset), `fgdb` CLI; larger-than-memory first-class in all three. (6) The published recovery root is the source of truth — checkpoint projection plus complete contiguous `LogicalCommandRecord` stream; only the two fixed root-pointer slots are ever updated in place; every reachable object is immutable and content-addressed; derived indexes/views never become authoritative. (7) No JVM, no GC, no mmap-as-durability, no generic KV underlay, no eventual-consistency defaults. (8) Narrowed capability contexts — purpose-typed `QueryCx`/`TxnCx`/`CommitCx`/`MaintCx`/`ReplCx` wrappers exposing only legal effects; the merge ladder's intent-replay evaluator gets a `Cx` with no clock/entropy/network/filesystem capability. (9) Prohibited shortcuts (constitutional) — no global-lock interim transactions, no `HashMap<VId, Vec<EId>>` as storage, no snapshot isolation labeled ACID, no parser-interprets-AST engine, no non-durable benchmark mode reported as a result, no serde-derived enum as a durable format, no detached background thread; early code may implement a subset of a final abstraction, never a substitute. (10) Adaptivity is classified or it does not ship — every adaptive decision is exactly answer-preserving physical, answer-affecting execution (pinned inside `AnswerRequirement`/`AnswerContract`, decision cards emitted), or canonical-state-affecting (only via logical commands under stream-sequenced `DecisionPolicyEpoch`); statistical promotion evidence is `FG-EVID-*`, never an `FG-INV-*` proof; the deterministic fallback remains valid. (11) Claims have types — the six classes above. (12) Costs are registered claims — every operation class has an Appendix G row (sequenced commands, Raft entries, ordered barriers with amortization/fusion legality, external-authority interactions, minted objects); every §17 gate must be derivable from its row; same-change registry updates; structure in the registry, µs/throughput budgets in `slo.toml`, never invariants.

**Proof-lane manifests and bet vocabulary:** G0 materializes the proof-lane manifests beside these registries — each manifest names the formal lane (Lean lane, TLA+ export), the model scope, and the checked artifact for a `proof`-class claim, following the §2 formal-layer house style — and registers the six-bet vocabulary (B1–B6) whose identifiers the other registries reference.

**Activation contract:** every FG-INV clause record carries `{exact_statement, activation_predicate, dependencies, checker_entrypoint, negative_test_entrypoint, model_or_proof_scope, owner, first_gate, status, waiver=forbidden}`. CI verifies the twenty-ID/table hash, the clause dependency DAG, checker/test existence, and the compiled-plus-negotiated activation closure; every reachable clause must be live or the capability is absent.

## Invariants & claim types
This bead defines the taxonomy every other bead's "Invariants & claim types" section uses. `invariants.toml` rows are `invariant`/`proof`/`bounded_model` class; `evidence.toml` carries `FG-CAL-*`/`FG-EVID-*` statistical rows; `slo.toml` carries slo/benchmark rows keyed by fixture; FG-CFG configuration-model claims live beside FG-CAL in Appendix F's non-invariant table.

## Interactions
g0-invariant-spine materializes the twenty rows into this bead's schema. g0-cost-registry implements constraint 12's instrument. g0-doc-sync validates README/AGENTS against these registries. w1-unsafe-ledger implements constraint 2's ledger; w1-foundation-types implements the claim/evidence crates; verif-sextant consumes the FG-CAL rows; perf-bench-core consumes `slo.toml`; risk-register consumes the same-change rule.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
TOML schema validators for all three registries with negative fixtures (missing checker, waiver present, statistical row in `invariants.toml`, clause citing an unregistered dependency). A `claims-lint` CI job that greps merged prose artifacts for unregistered load-bearing claim markers and fails with file/line. Hash test pinning the twenty-ID table. A cross-class escalation test: a build that cites an `slo` row as justification for an `invariant` clause fails CI. Logged output: per-registry row count, activation-closure summary, and the exact diff on any hash mismatch.

Named suites: `claims_neg_missing_checker`, `claims_neg_waiver_present`, `claims_neg_statistical_in_invariants`, `claims_neg_unregistered_dependency`, `claims_hash_twenty_id_pin`, `claims_escalation_slo_cannot_justify_invariant`, `claims_proof_lane_manifest_resolves` (every `proof`-class row names a lane/model-scope/artifact triple that resolves), property test `claims_class_lattice_narrowing` (over all ordered claim-class pairs, only weaker-informs-stronger edges are representable, never enforce/justify), and fuzz `claims_registry_toml_fuzz` (mutated TOML fails closed with a typed parse error, never a panic). E2E: `scripts/g0_claims_e2e.sh` authors the three registries plus a seeded prose corpus containing one planted unregistered load-bearing claim and one planted cross-class escalation, runs schema validation, `claims-lint`, the activation-closure compiler for a sample capability manifest, and the twenty-ID hash pin, asserting each planted defect is caught with file/line. DETAILED LOGGING: JSONL events `{event: registry_validated|clause_checked|lint_hit|closure_computed, registry, row_id, claim_class, checker_symbol, negative_test_symbol, outcome}`; every lint hit logs file/line/marker text; closure computation logs reachable/live/absent clause counts and the exact clause IDs behind any capability declared absent; any hash mismatch logs the exact row-level diff.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: waiverable clauses (forbidden by construction); one merged registry file (classes must be structurally separate so a statistical claim cannot drift into the invariant namespace); free-text invariant statements without checker entrypoints (unenforceable). Risk: activation predicates rot as features land — mitigated by the reachable-clause-must-be-live CI rule.

## Provenance
§1 constraints 1–12; Appendix F preamble (line 3126); §19 G0 paragraph (line 1311); §18 G0 materialization list (line 1298); §2 formal-layer row (line 63).
