title: Materialize the twenty-invariant spine FG-INV-01..20 and the non-invariant gate table
description:
## What & scope
Materialize Appendix F's exactly-twenty top-level invariant rows into `invariants.toml` clause records, plus the separate statistical/evidence/configuration gate table (FG-CAL-01..03, FG-EVID-01..04, FG-CFG-01..04). Split out of g0-claim-registries so the row text is a first-class reviewable artifact.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
The spine is the safety contract every workstream builds against (B5): each row names both the property and its enforcement apparatus, so verification work is scheduled, not hoped for.

## Design — normative detail
Compressed normative statements (full text goes verbatim into the registry): **FG-INV-01** — within one security namespace/incarnation and capability domain, each scoped begin/autocommit key, durable token, and registered attempt maps to at most one immutable semantic terminal outcome and final-effect digest; retries return recorded lineage; `AttemptFamilyState` admits only generation-zero `First`, exact `prior+1 Successor` after a registered Terminal prior with proved release/overlap floor, or byte-identical `IdempotentRetry`; TerminalReady only after postcondition bitmap, audit visibility, and result detachment. **FG-INV-02** — for every exclusive block, constraint-owner reservation, resource hold, allocation offset, final-certification basis, and escrow custody unit, at most one legal live generation owns it; the batch-scoped `GlobalFinalCertificationReservation` is the single legal live owner of a shared basis with per-candidate sub-holds; escrow custody is a disjoint exhaustive partition with finite-side conservation equations at every transition. **FG-INV-03** — every physical version chain is finite, acyclic, strictly newer-first by commit order, links within one owning object generation. **FG-INV-04** — visibility obeys snapshot high sequence, branch ancestry per graph-reference role, valid-time slice intersection/boundary normalization, create/retire and schema-coordinate rules, own-write overlays, the erasure-tombstone conjunct (§12.6), and the expiry predicate (§4.8); applied state may lead public state only through the gap-free audit-visibility pipeline; `SnapshotQuery` reads only the visible candidate root. **FG-INV-05** — every committed SERIALIZABLE history has an acyclic dependency graph; the Local default additionally checks DSG-union-real-time cycles (strict serializability); dependency metadata retained until no overlapping attempt can add an edge. **FG-INV-06** — every witness conservatively represents all logically relevant positive/negative/gap/valid-time-slice/early-stop/path-cut observations; refinement preserves concretization and `may_affect`; missing coverage causes conservative failure, never a dropped edge. **FG-INV-07** — the durable strong/uncut-conditional reference graph is acyclic; every field/reference/digest is registry-resolved; pre-order inputs exclude their future command/result/root; `command_contracts.toml` is bijective with handlers; exact W12 read/write orders. **FG-INV-08** — logical-command order and the marker subsequence are contiguous; role-tagged Raft snapshots match exact cuts; only `AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec` moves the visible endpoint; provisional cuts authorize no new release until activation. **FG-INV-09** — `ObjectId` recomputes from the exact keyed namespaced canonical transcript; `CiphertextId`/`EncodingId`/`PlacementId` recompute from registered descriptors; every stored digest is exactly Target, Transcript, WeakIdentity, or BodyDigest with one generated recipe. **FG-INV-10** — the two-slot `manifest.root` protocol always selects the highest structurally credible authenticated role closure; one inode-bound publication sequencer plus external incarnation continuity fences stale writers; durable-format writes only under activated `FormatCompatibilityState`; failure repairs or fails closed. **FG-INV-11** — allocation epochs/leases/spent commitments are monotonic under the registered `AllocationContinuityProfile` (externally under `ExternalCas`, locally under `DirectoryBound`'s fenced journal); no VId/EId/key alias across crash/branch/merge/restore/topology; first-escape durable reservation; permanent spent tombstones. **FG-INV-12** — canonical scalar equality/hash/order/encoding coherent; every claimed answer-equivalent rewrite (seal, compaction, codec rewrite, spill, factorize/flatten, safe replan, exact rebuild) preserves values, multiplicity, order, visibility, security projection, and AnswerContract. **FG-INV-13** — commits immutable; branch heads move only by atomic expected-head updates; fork closes parent envelope epochs before opening successors; distributed key staging/destruction discipline; merge tokens pre-minted with one terminal outcome. **FG-INV-14** — GC follows every generated strong/uncut-conditional edge; independent obligations remain roots until exact terminal release; physical GC is Requested→Started→Completed or all-members CancelledBeforeStart with signed receipts. **FG-INV-15** — integrating ordered deltas equals batch evaluation for every registered exact derivative; retained batches own each payload exactly once; the state-shaped independent-retention result machine; cursor baseline/delta rules expose every gap. **FG-INV-16** — no obligation (task, lease, reservation, pin, prepared closure, DP charge/seed, audit entry, escrow hold, backup pin, quarantine, TerminalPending postcondition) is lost, duplicated, refunded, or exposed while obligated; bounded liveness under declared fairness. **FG-INV-17** — rebase/merge execute under capability-stripped deterministic contexts pinned to `IntentSemanticsOid`; drift regenerates everything before final-certification reservation; rung-1 reuse legal iff extensionally equal to full re-evaluation; a frozen Active reservation forbids rebase. **FG-INV-18** — base graph/bitemporal/schema/constraint semantics remain authoritative; committed effects equal logical before/after state; synchronous constraints/budgets hold before commit; derived state discardable without changing exact answers. **FG-INV-19** — replay manifests derive their structural maximum from the evidence-slot matrix; grades only weaken; erasure downgrades through the `Redacted` arm, never silently. **FG-INV-20** — authorization precedes every observation or effect everywhere, including `SnapshotQuery` coordinator-local admission; every authority-bearing schema binds one complete `SecurityStateBinding`; uniform nonrevealing failure. Non-invariant gates: FG-CAL-01 adaptive-policy evidence, FG-CAL-02 interval coverage, FG-CAL-03 ANN recall drift; FG-EVID-01 decision-card/OPE completeness, FG-EVID-02 scrub health, FG-EVID-03 endurance, FG-EVID-04 derived-state freshness; FG-CFG-01 MTTDL, FG-CFG-02 controller stability, FG-CFG-03 staleness feasibility, FG-CFG-04 maintenance-stream capacity.

## Invariants & claim types
All twenty rows are `invariant` class (with per-clause model/proof scopes); FG-CAL/FG-EVID rows are statistical; FG-CFG rows are configuration-model claims — never invariants.

## Interactions
Consumes g0-claim-registries' schema. Every enforcement column names apparatus later built by verif-oracles, verif-formal, verif-sim, and the per-workstream test beads; g0-format-arms registers the amended FG-INV-04/11/19/20 clauses.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Registry contains exactly twenty top-level IDs (hash-pinned); each clause resolves checker and negative-test entrypoints (may be stub-registered pre-Genesis but must be resolvable symbols); dependency-DAG acyclicity test; a negative fixture adding a twenty-first ID fails; a fixture marking a reachable clause inactive without disabling its capability fails.

Named suites: `spine_exactly_twenty_ids`, `spine_hash_pin`, `spine_clause_entrypoints_resolve`, `spine_dag_acyclic`, `spine_neg_twenty_first_id`, `spine_neg_inactive_reachable_clause`, `spine_gate_table_classes` (every FG-CAL/FG-EVID/FG-CFG row carries its required-disclosure fields and a non-invariant class), and property test `spine_clause_key_stability` (randomized subordinate-clause additions never mint a new top-level ID). E2E: `scripts/g0_spine_e2e.sh` materializes the registry from Appendix F, verifies the twenty-ID table hash, resolves every checker and negative-test symbol (stub-registered pre-Genesis but resolvable), compiles the activation closure for a sample capability manifest, and runs both negative fixtures, asserting each fails naming the exact clause. DETAILED LOGGING: JSONL events `{event: row_materialized|clause_resolved|closure_computed, invariant_id, clause_key, checker_symbol, negative_test_symbol, activation_predicate, status, outcome}`; the run logs the twenty-ID table hash, per-invariant clause counts, and the reachable/live/absent clause sets so later gates can diff activation drift against this baseline.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: more invariant IDs (clause records subordinate to twenty stable IDs keep the spine reviewable); folding FG-CFG rows into invariants (a modeled MTTDL is not a safety property). Risk: clause proliferation diluting review — mitigated by the stable-ID + subordinate-clause structure.

## Provenance
Appendix F (lines 3124–3165).

## Exact normative invariant and non-invariant gate payload
The earlier compressed summaries are navigation aids only. The following complete statements and enforcement columns are the binding registry payload; implementation must not consult an external plan to recover omitted qualifiers:
## Appendix F — Invariant and Evidence Registries

This table contains exactly twenty top-level invariant IDs. Every clause records its exact statement, activation predicate, dependencies, resolvable enforcement and negative-test entrypoints, model/proof scope or liveness fairness assumptions, owner, first gate, status, and `waiver=forbidden`. CI verifies the twenty-ID/table hash, dependency DAG, checker/test existence, and the compiled-plus-negotiated activation closure. | FG-INV-09 | `ObjectId` recomputes from the exact keyed, namespaced canonical logical transcript; `CiphertextId`, complete `EncodingId`, and non-self-referential `PlacementId` recompute from their registered descriptors and bytes/inventory. Root bootstrap reconstructs all identities without indexes; child-key AAD and symbol MACs cover their complete noncircular transcripts; collision buckets verify full identity and incompatible encodings never combine. Every stored digest is explicitly Target, Transcript, WeakIdentity, or BodyDigest with one generated include/exclude recipe. | Full keyed-identity/descriptor/AAD/body-transcript/root-bootstrap oracle; generated digest/field checker; mutation, golden, cross-version, collision, wrong-key/namespace, mixed-symbol, and FEC-wire fuzz campaigns. |
| FG-INV-10 | Under the accepted filesystem/crash profile, the two-slot `manifest.root` protocol always selects the highest structurally credible authenticated role closure with exact applied/visible/service positions, while one inode-bound publication sequencer plus external incarnation continuity fences every stale writer. Before the ordinary token, only the typed takeover, fresh-creation, or guarded restore publication may occur; every irreversible seal, receipt, Raft action, certificate, and slot write rechecks both authorities. Durable-format writes occur only under an activated `FormatCompatibilityState`: all current/joint voters and storage readers decode the active closure, first-target-write is irreversible, downgrade is refused after it, and old decoders retire only after exhaustive reachable/backup/restore/replay floors. Closure or capability failure repairs or fails closed, never rolls back or partially interprets. | Filesystem/lease/takeover/root-slot and external-CAS split-brain models; every-write/fsync-lie/path-replacement/rollback crash matrix; format advertise/activate/first-write/rewrite/rolling-upgrade/downgrade/decoder-retirement conformance gates. |
| FG-INV-11 | Allocation epochs, leases, and canonical spent commitments are monotonic under the registered `AllocationContinuityProfile` bound 1:1 to the incarnation-continuity posture — externally monotonic under `ExternalCas` (mandatory for W12/Meta), locally monotonic under `DirectoryBound`'s allocation-continuity journal beneath the same whole-inode fence — and prevent VId/EId/generated-key alias, overlap, or reuse across crash, label change, branch, merge, clone, restore, topology movement, and role activation; the registered residual-risk row applies to the whole closure: under `DirectoryBound`, block-level volume rollback is outside the declared threat model, allocation included. Any value is durably reserved no later than its first escape to a result, later workspace, procedure/UDF, provenance/audit, or terminal preparation; confined values are reserved by the finalization plan before capsule/effect construction. Rebase preserves prior bindings and may append only; disappearance/conflict/abort creates permanent spent tombstones. Canonical forward incidence, stable IDs, origin/birth/branch orders, properties, ordinal maps, holes, and any reverse materialization agree. | Per-profile `ExternalCas`/`DirectoryBound` continuity allocator and spent-range models; first-escape/finalization crash and lost-response tests; rebase/abort/expiry/restore/topology exhaustion campaigns; reference-graph and forward/reverse compaction metamorphics. |
| FG-INV-12 | Canonical scalar equality, hashing, ordering, and encoding are coherent. Every claimed answer-equivalent seal, compaction, codec/format rewrite, spill, factorize/flatten, workspace materialization, safe replan, and exact derived rebuild preserves logical values, multiplicity, order, visibility, security projection, and AnswerContract. Approximate candidate/topology changes create a new pinned semantic generation; no build progress or physical bulk/index artifact changes schema visibility before its ordinary transactional SchemaOp activation. | Scalar-law property/fuzz suite; digest/reference/workspace equivalence; answer-contract/type/security checker; exact rewrite/rebuild and approximate-generation metamorphic suites. |
| FG-INV-13 | Commits are immutable and branch heads move only by atomic expected-head updates. Fork closes the parent envelope/write epochs before opening independent parent/child successors; every envelope, object-DEK, grant, and wrap is bound to one authenticated root/cut/epoch. In W12, Meta first orders a certificate-free key distribution plan, each shard installs unusable Staged material and certifies it, Meta activates exactly one complete manifest, and only the matching typed shard projection makes material Active; Staged material cannot serve reads/effects/prepares or active backup. Distributed destruction requires current-root zero-reference certificates, durable shard authorization, physical member/KMS receipts and completion from every planned Meta target and shard/range, then Meta completion; any new root invalidates the zero proof. Merge tokens/nonces/capability generations are pre-minted, each has one terminal outcome, imported-range coverage prevents partial or repeated application across drift/cuts/restore/reconfiguration, and effects obey proved ACI algebra or their recorded total order. | Branch/fork/envelope/merge/imported-range and distributed-key phase models; cross-branch denial, wrong plan/manifest, stale-zero-basis, partial KMS, crash, retry, topology, and backup property tests. |
| FG-INV-14 | GC follows every generated strong and currently uncut conditional edge; only registered weak/locator/observation fields are nonretaining. Independent obligations—including state-shaped active result/output owners, allocation/escrow holds, transaction ownership/capability lineage, audit pipeline entries, DP seeds/charges, prepared/certificate state, backup/restore/format/bulk/derived state, remote grants, and keys—remain roots until their exact terminal transfer/release. Provisional cuts authorize no new reclaim. Physical GC uses Requested -> Started -> Completed or all-members CancelledBeforeStart, with signed exact receipts; any Started member makes cancellation impossible. W12 requires bounded preflight, Meta authorization, current-root disjoint quarantine, no resurrection, exact Meta/shard member completion, progress, and aggregate completion; missing participants remain blocking. Heavy detail retires only after visibility and an activated cut. | Generated reachability/mandatory-inventory/remote-release and GC models; state-arm liveness checker; mark-then-resolve, dedupe-resurrection, start-vs-cancel, partial-member, result/output, backup/restore, topology, and RetiredLocal crash storms. |
| FG-INV-15 | For every registered exact derivative, integrating ordered deltas equals batch evaluation, and retained Local/Global batches own each payload exactly once. W12 transaction records never name future batches; only complete post-visibility shard acknowledgements form one acyclic Global batch and its contiguous Meta publication advances Ripple. Every result-producing feature uses one generated, noninterchangeable owner arm and the state-shaped independent-retention machine: PendingVisibility and ReleasedAwaitingActivation retain manifest/policy/resource escrow, ActiveDeliverable additionally owns lease/replay/send authority, and ACK or explicit authenticated release/expiry atomically installs compact terminal evidence with no strong bulk predecessor. QUERY_CANCEL, Drop, disconnect, drain, and process death cannot release it. Resume/ACK/release/expiry CAS one delivery version with deterministic immediate-predecessor retry. Cursor baseline/delta rules forbid delta before baseline ACK and expose every gap. Public digests cover exact authorized canonical bytes/provenance, never keyed object IDs. | Derivative-vs-batch and global-publication differential; generated owner/state reachability; result release/resume/ACK/expiry and sender-death DPOR; public-digest/cursor/lease/gap/status-equivalence and exact/approximate derived-generation suites. |
| FG-INV-16 | No structured task, ownership lease, begin/allocation/finalization reservation, pin, scratch object, result/workspace/cursor/output lease, prepared closure, privacy charge/seed/result, audit freeze/plan/per-signer lock/share/pipeline entry, escrow/resource hold, backup pin, remote transition, GC quarantine, restore-source lease, or TerminalPending postcondition is lost, duplicated, refunded, released, or exposed while obligated. Transaction ownership is generation-fenced, durably reattachable/renewable only under the capability lineage, and becomes PrepareFenced atomically before finalization; expiry can only order the registered rollback/status-safe path. DP has one external charge request/tombstone/receipt lineage and noise is generated only by Meta after the charge is mirrored. Audit candidates remain hidden until their exact batch and gap-free visibility advance. Under declared quorum/storage/network/time/continuity/resource fairness, every obligation reaches one legal terminal or recoverable state. | asupersync leak/quiescence oracle; transaction ownership/reattach/expiry, allocation, result/output, prepared/resource/escrow, DP single-charge, audit signer/pipeline, backup/remote/GC/restore recovery tests; bounded-liveness models with explicit assumptions. |
| FG-INV-17 | Rebase and branch merge execute under capability-stripped deterministic contexts pinned to `IntentSemanticsOid`. Every semantic drift regenerates effects, workspace/read/write state, constraints, escrow/resource requirements, witnesses, logical deltas, allocation plan, RETURNING bytes, and capsule **before** final-certification reservation and terminal signing. Incremental rung-1 re-evaluation may reuse a prior intent's results only under unchanged-observation certificates closed transitively over the intra-transaction dependency DAG in intent-ordinal order, and such reuse is legal iff it is extensionally equal to full re-evaluation. Once an Active final-certification reservation freezes the basis, rebase is forbidden; conflicting drift must use the proved pre-signature cancel/restart path, while any terminal audit plan/lock/share requires completion of that selected basis. No mutable clock, entropy, filesystem, network, or policy lookup enters replay. | Type/capability boundaries; forced-drift and interleaved-head property tests; reserve/sign/cancel ordering model; wrong-semantics/unavailable-input fail-closed tests and final-effect/workspace/allocation/result digest oracle plus a sampled incremental-versus-full differential oracle. |
| FG-INV-18 | Base graph, bitemporal, schema, and constraint semantics remain authoritative: canonical committed effects equal logical before/after state over normalized valid-time slices; workspace finalization equals ordered published statements; synchronous constraints, resource budgets, and escrow bounds must hold before commit. Bulk ingestion commits only canonical logical batches through ordinary transactions, and index/build controls remain invisible until a transactional SchemaOp activates a validated generation. Rebuildable indexes/views/caches and optional staged runs can be discarded without changing exact answers or authorization. | Reference effect/workspace/valid-time differential; synchronous constraint/resource/escrow oracle; bulk row/source/effect bijection tests; index shadow-build/activation races; degraded-recovery and derived-state rebuild drills. |
| FG-INV-19 | A registry-rooted replay manifest derives its structural maximum only from its versioned evidence-slot matrix, and its effective grade may only weaken as leases, resolution, trust, configuration, or authority change. Replayable requires every semantic slot, including answer requirement, realized contract, authority, external inputs, executable artifacts, decisions, workspace-affecting statements, and exact approximate generations, to resolve through exactly LocalStrong, live CertifiedRemote, or active Archived evidence and reproduce canonical logical output. Sharded replay is no stronger than its weakest required group; activation/legacy evidence uses certified transition wrappers, never raw old-group refs. Missing, redacted, revoked, expired, or untrusted evidence yields only the declared weaker grade. Erased subjects downgrade replay through the `Redacted` arm with the erasure tombstone as typed evidence; an `ErasureCutSpec` never silently breaks a byte-identity claim — the effective grade weakens attributably instead. Answer-affecting and canonical-state policies are sequenced/pinned; proved physical equivalence cannot change strict output. | Cross-plan/target/artifact/workspace/approximation replay CI; generated slot-grade/local-remote-archive resolver and expiry/trust doctor; activation/posture-substitution tests and replica logical-digest oracle. |
| FG-INV-20 | Authorization precedes every observation or effect across storage, statistics, routing/scoring, temporal selection, workspace, errors, constraints/witnesses/prepares, derived state, Prism/UDFs, streams, capabilities, replay/export/backup, audit, and observability. `SnapshotQuery` admission obeys the identical authorization-before-observation rule — coordinator-local admission verifies the complete capability and policy binding before any statement or storage observation — with the same oracle coverage as the durable read classes. Every authority-bearing durable schema binds one complete `SecurityStateBinding` (or exact certified shard projection); equal epoch scalars with different roots/service epochs never substitute. W12 registration claims operation/statement tickets before observation; shard work carries only exact certified projections. One union-wide authorization decision covers the complete effect set. A protected candidate becomes observable only after its signer-locked terminal event, external resolution batch, and gap-free visibility advance; shard acknowledgements and streaming follow that visibility. Capability lookup/status/release is same-principal, same-or-narrower, current-epoch, and uniformly nonrevealing on failure. Hidden constraints follow one explicit disclosure contract and only named ticketed declassification is legal. | Generated authority-binding and pre-observation type matrices; raw-cross-group/equal-scalar-different-root/wrong-domain/config/grant/owner negatives; ticket claim, omitted participant, status/release noninterference, pre-visibility observation/ack, `SnapshotQuery` admission-before-observation, declassification, and continuity tests. |

### Statistical, evidence, and configuration gates (not invariants)

| ID | Qualified claim | Required disclosure/gate |
|---|---|---|
| FG-CAL-01 | Adaptive policy evidence versus pinned fallback | null/outcome filtration, alpha, support/overlap, effective sample size, loss and fallback; stream-sequenced promotion only |
| FG-CAL-02 | Cardinality/risk interval coverage | population, selection/window, exchangeability or nonexchangeability method, strata, marginal target, realized coverage and drift |
| FG-CAL-03 | ANN recall/drift evidence | authorized snapshot population, keyed sample, exact baseline, candidate policy, confidence interval and rebuild action |
| FG-EVID-01 | Decision-card/OPE completeness | state/actions/features, logged probabilities, zero-support exclusions, clipping/estimator, policy epoch and fallback |
| FG-EVID-02 | Scrub/corpus-health evidence | population, keyed stratified sampling, dependence assumptions, exhaustive-sweep position and observed corruption |
| FG-CFG-01 | Modeled durability target | CTMC/model version, fitted failure rates, failure domains, sensitivity bounds, repair/backup assumptions, and per-tier `fec_profile` reconstruction and checkpoint-fold recode paths |
| FG-CFG-02 | Modeled controller stability | model/equilibrium, parameter uncertainty, predicted margin, deterministic hard guards and soak results |
| FG-CFG-03 | View/index staleness SLO feasibility | arrival/service assumptions, resource reservation, predicted envelope, actual watermark and fallback policy |
| FG-CFG-04 | Maintenance-stream capacity model (Appendix G) | per-entry-class arrival/service assumptions, stated scale parameters (branch count, cursor count, delivery cadence, fan-out amplification factor, implied time-observation rate), predicted versus measured head-of-line saturation, reserved-capacity and fallback policy |
| FG-EVID-03 | Endurance-gate evidence (defined-duration sustained load) | duration and cadence, compaction-debt ceiling stated in §6.6 write-amplification-model terms, long-run memory stability bound, steady-state occupancy-model prediction versus observation — divergence is itself a finding |
| FG-EVID-04 | Derived-state freshness (slo-class, never an invariant) | bound expressed in watermark/commit-sequence units, audit-pipeline and time-evidence dependencies named, realized lag distribution, typed `FreshnessBreach` rate and fallback policy |

### Clause-level acceptance and diagnostics
For each FG-INV row, the generated clause manifest names: exact statement digest, activation predicate, checker symbol, independent negative-test symbol, proof/model/oracle scope, first gate that requires it live, and waiver=forbidden. Unit tests byte-compare the registry statement and enforcement column; mutation tests delete or weaken every material phrase and must fail. Each gate runs a compiled-capability-to-live-checker bijection and emits JSONL {event_version,invariant_id,clause_id,statement_digest,activation_predicate,checker_symbol,negative_test_symbol,gate,live,verdict,evidence_refs,replay_command}. Missing, disabled-but-advertised, duplicated, unresolvable, or waived clauses fail the gate. The same machinery covers FG-CAL, FG-EVID, and FG-CFG as qualified non-invariant claims without promoting them to safety invariants.


### Exact Appendix F attachment closure requirements
A checksum fixture pins this exact appendix range. Generation must enumerate every row/arm with stable IDs and map it bijectively to the owning implementation, unit/property/fuzz/simulation/E2E tests, detailed redacted diagnostic-event schemas, and consuming gate. Missing, duplicate, wildcard, silently weakened, or unowned rows fail CI and gate review.

Gate table FG-CAL-01..03/FG-EVID-01..04 (evidence.toml, statistical) and FG-CFG-01..04 (slo.toml, configuration_model bounded_model) verified by spine_gate_table_classes. All named suites green: spine_exactly_twenty_ids, spine_hash_pin, spine_clause_entrypoints_resolve, spine_dag_acyclic, spine_neg_twenty_first_id, spine_neg_inactive_reachable_clause, spine_gate_table_classes, spine_clause_key_stability. scripts/g0_spine_e2e.sh 10/10 incl. both negative fixtures naming exact clauses; closure baseline logged for activation-drift diffing.

title: Freeze irreversible-dispatch and sole prebootstrap-journal publication contracts
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the sole total contract system for irreversible external application/authority actions, including the ordinary canonical Protocol plane and the unique restore-prebootstrap plane. This task owns both registries, their exact closed unions and row schemas, attempt/hold/guard state machines, status-first recovery, terminal import, cross-plane noninterchangeability, and AtomicProtocolDetach conservation.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
A crash after transport escapes but before local import is the dangerous middle of DP debit, audit CAS, continuity fencing, key destruction, backup/restore lease operations, catalog promotion, time rotation, GC, and retention release. Call-after-commit cannot distinguish not-sent from sent-but-response-lost. The registered attempt machine makes every irreversible action idempotent, recovery-queryable, publication-gated, and replayable while admitting exactly one pre-first-root exception and no third substrate.

## Design — exact normative contract
The complete binding text follows:
4. **`prebootstrap_artifact_kinds.toml` — restore artifacts that necessarily predate target `K_oid`.** `PreBootstrapArtifactId = BLAKE3("fgdb:restore-prebootstrap:v1" ‖ target_claim_or_reservation_domain ‖ artifact_kind ‖ schema_version ‖ canonical_wrapper_bytes)` and `PreBootstrapArtifactRef<T> {artifact_id,authenticated_staging_locator,length,canonical_digest,dispatch_root_generation}` are legal only in the registered restore staging inode/root/capsule. The artifact's actual schema is the distinct wrapper `{import_target_schema_id_for_T,inner_canonical_bytes,inner_digest,artifact_metadata}`; `T` is a compile-time import-target phantom and does not make the inner target schema inhabit the prebootstrap identity class. Rows declare wrapper kind/schema, target claim domain, inner codec, authentication, bounds, lifecycle, exact allowed prebootstrap containers, canonical-import target kind, and cleanup floor. These IDs are never `ObjectId`, never accepted by `StrongRef`, never enter the current-database mark set, and never authorize ordinary reads. Contents are portable plans, status/receipt/refusal bytes, availability certificates, lease-owner generations, wrapped-key artifacts, and proof material only—never plaintext keys. Once target `K_oid` exists, generated canonical-import records decode/copy the inner bytes into the sole target-keyed logical identity and prove a total artifact-to-logical-object/disposition bijection; no canonical logical object retains a staging locator after the import floor closes.
External irreversible **application/authority actions** have one additional total registry, `irreversible_dispatch_contracts.toml`; ad-hoc “call after commit” code is forbidden. An action belongs here when transport may escape the process and the target can durably register, charge, reserve, publish, revoke, destroy, release, or advance a CAS-linear application authority—even when the operation is logically reversible later. The two publication substrates are not recursively modeled as application actions: ordinary state uses the fixed `RootSlot` protocol, and the sole pre-first-root exception uses the exact `prebootstrap_journal_publication_contracts.toml` protocol below. G0 permits no third substrate.

`DispatchSourceGateKind` is the closed union `PublishedSemanticAuthorization{authorization_record_kind,publication_evidence_kind,current_authorization_and_resource_checker}|PublishedExternalCasAuthorization{operation_record_kind,operation_publication_evidence_kind,authority_head_kind,current_operation_authorization_resource_and_direct_predecessor_checker}|PreBootstrapReservationAuthorization{prebootstrap_root_kind,reservation_body_and_head_kind,current_reserved_observation_plan_and_staging_inode_checker}|PreBootstrapClaimedAuthority{prebootstrap_root_kind,claimed_authority_kind,current_claim_plan_and_staging_inode_checker}|PublishedCancellationFence{fence_kind,publication_evidence_kind,current_fence_and_zero_start_checker}|SemanticQuarantine{quarantine_kind,publication_evidence_kind,current_root_and_no_new_reference_checker}|ActivatedReleaseHold{hold_kind,publication_evidence_kind,current_hold_and_participant_checker}|ReservationDisposition{reservation_kind,publication_evidence_kind,current_claim_or_pending_disposition_checker}`. DP/privacy, audit, continuity, catalog, and time-authority CAS operations use `PublishedExternalCasAuthorization`; a bare current external head without the exact published local operation and its publication evidence can never authorize them. `DispatchTerminalImportKind` is the closed union `SemanticImport{command_input_kind}|ProtocolFinalize{maintenance_input_kind}|ExternalCompletionImport{command_or_maintenance_input_kind}|PreBootstrapJournalImport{journal_transition_kind,canonical_bridge_import_kind}`.

`DispatchOriginPlane` is the closed tag `CanonicalProtocol|RestorePreBootstrap`. The unique registry key is `dispatch_contract_id`, not `action_kind`: one provider action kind may have a finite generated contract family when it is legally invoked from more than one origin plane or source-gate/profile class. Exact uniqueness is `(action_kind,origin_plane,role_and_group_predicate,source_gate_arm)`, and each member has a disjoint operation-ID namespace, attempt state slot, authorize/arm/import contracts, terminal schema IDs, and retention floor. `RestoreArchiveLeaseRenew`, `RestoreArchiveLeaseRelease`, reservation claim/consume/burn where applicable, transient cleanup, and any other dual-plane provider action therefore have distinct prebootstrap and canonical contract IDs even when their provider action-body schema is shared. No terminal evidence/import from one contract member can satisfy another.

`ExternalActionRequestBinding` is the portable, reference-free prefix every actual request, status result, refusal, and terminal receipt byte-matches: `{database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,role_and_group,service_visibility_epoch,dispatch_contract_id,origin_plane:DispatchOriginPlane,action_kind,authority_domain,target_identity,operation_id,idempotency_token_digest,canonical_action_body_digest,source_gate_kind,source_gate_publication_commitment,authority_binding_public_commitment,request_schema_major,request_schema_minor}`. The binding is constructed only after the registered source gate is durable. Pre-order action bodies and Semantic authorization records therefore contain an operation/idempotency identity plus a canonical action-body recipe, never a future publication commitment or full request. An external authority must key status and idempotency by at least `(authority_domain,target_identity,operation_id)` and permanently reject the same operation ID with different contract, plane, binding, or body bytes.

`AuthenticatedExternalStatusStep<Contract>` is the generated reference-free `{external_request_binding:ExternalActionRequestBinding{dispatch_contract_id=Contract},canonical_full_request_digest,status_query_nonce,status_observed_at:AuthorityInstant,status_time_authority_profile_oid,status_class:NotRegistered{authoritative_absence_counter,provider_operation-index-proof_digest}|RegisteredPending{registered_operation_digest,provider_progress_token_digest,provider_counter}|Applied{typed_receipt_digest,result_head_or_target_state_commitment,provider_counter_or_cas_version}|AlreadyApplied{typed_receipt_digest,result_head_or_target_state_commitment,provider_counter_or_cas_version}|PermanentlyRefused{typed_refusal_tombstone_digest,zero_effect_commitment,provider_counter_or_cas_version}|ConflictNoEffect{typed_conflict_evidence_digest,zero_effect_commitment,provider_counter_or_cas_version},prior_status_step_digest?,provider_status_key_id,provider_status_key_epoch,signature}`. Each contract row fixes the action kind, origin plane, admissible status classes, exact proof carried by `NotRegistered`, permitted monotonic step relation, and whether the provider uses a counter, CAS version, or both. A timeout, transport error, unsigned absence, locally elapsed deadline, or response for a different contract/request is not a status step.

`PortableExternalActionTerminalEvidence<Contract>` denotes a generated finite family, never an erased runtime generic. Every dispatch-contract row emits one distinct registered schema with `{external_request_binding:ExternalActionRequestBinding{dispatch_contract_id=Contract},canonical_full_request_digest,dispatch_attempt_generation,source_gate_publication_commitment,status_lineage:[AuthenticatedExternalStatusStep<Contract>],terminal_disposition:Applied{typed_receipt_digest,result_head_or_target_state_commitment}|AlreadyApplied{typed_receipt_digest,result_head_or_target_state_commitment}|PermanentlyRefused{typed_refusal_tombstone_digest,zero_effect_commitment}|ConflictNoEffect{typed_conflict_evidence_digest,zero_effect_commitment},provider_counter_or_cas_version,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`. It contains no local or Protocol object identity. `PortableTimeAuthorityIssuanceCloseTerminalEvidence`, `PortableTimeAuthorityIssuanceFenceTerminalEvidence`, `PortableTimeAuthorityRegistryTransitionTerminalEvidence`, and every other named terminal type are exact generated members keyed by contract ID with action-specific typed payloads; they are not aliases that permit cross-action or cross-plane decoding. Elsewhere, notation of the form `PortableExternalActionTerminalEvidence<Action>` is permitted only when the action has exactly one live contract; a dual-plane action must name its exact `Contract`.

At least one live contract row exists for every external action, and every legal origin-plane/source-gate specialization has exactly one row. The action inventory includes: DP charge and privacy-continuity freeze/retire/profile transitions; audit ticket issue, resolution-batch CAS, and completeness change; backup publication, transparency append, archive-grant issue/renewal, source-release-hold prepare/activate/completion; atomic restore archive acquisition whose typed terminal payload includes generation-one source-lease activation; separate source-`K_oid`/DEK recovery, target-`K_oid` creation, recovery-incarnation-lease acquire/refresh, later source-lease renew/release, reservation claim/consume/burn, pre-bootstrap continuity abandonment, prior-incarnation lease fencing, catalog reserve/activate/tombstone and ExternalCas continuity pending/finalize/abandon; time-authority issuance close/fence/registry transition/service shutdown; distinct GC member reclaim and cancel-before-start operations plus every deletion/crypto-erasure; and KMS/HSM/storage key destruction. There is no separate source-lease-acquire action: the prebootstrap `RestoreArchiveAcquire` contract alone performs Absent -> Registered -> Active and returns both archive acquisition and lease-acquire typed payloads under one request binding; key recovery/creation occurs only under its later refinement-authorized rows. The nonrecursive prebootstrap journal-head CAS publishes dispatch state but is not itself an application action row. Catalog/continuity/time/privacy/audit registries are not exceptions merely because they are CAS-linear. The only v1 **application/provider** transport permitted before a canonical RootManifest is the registered restore pre-bootstrap machine below, and it may send only after its complete SentUnknown generation is journal-head durable. Reservation-claim contracts use `PreBootstrapReservationAuthorization`; post-claim acquisition/use/consume/burn contracts use their exact `PreBootstrapClaimedAuthority`, `ReservationDisposition`, or registered successor gate. Every request, status, receipt, and terminal-evidence byte records its contract ID, origin plane, selected source-gate kind, and commitment; no unconditional “claimed target authority” field is inferred.

Each row declares `{dispatch_contract_id,action_kind,origin_plane:DispatchOriginPlane,operation_id_namespace,role_and_group_predicate,source_gate:DispatchSourceGateKind,operation_plan_kind,canonical_action_body_kind,target_identity_kind,idempotency_key_recipe,canonical_request_transcript_recipe,attempt_slot,authorize_contract_id,arm_contract_id,mark_sent_unknown_contract_id,abandon_before_send_contract_id,status_query_contract,authoritative_not_registered_evidence_kind,post_eligibility_not_registered_contract:Forbidden|RefusalOnly{provider_expiry_checker,permanent_refusal_tombstone_kind}|ExactCleanupRetry{eligibility_kind}|SeparateCleanupAction{action_kind},permanent_refusal_evidence_kind,terminal_receipt_kind,portable_terminal_evidence_kind,allowed_terminal_outcomes,current_root_or_prebootstrap_inventory_checker,configuration_and_writer_fence_checker,continuity_and_time_checker,dispatch_hold_class,terminal_import:DispatchTerminalImportKind,nonterminal_retention_floor,terminal_compaction_rule,status}`. A live row is required before an action encoder, provider adapter, or handler can issue or status-query the action. DP charge and audit ticket/completeness choose `RefusalOnly` when their admission window can expire; reservation consume and source-lease release choose only their exact registered cleanup eligibility. The generated matrix rejects duplicate contract keys, an action/plane/source-gate hole, missing authenticated idempotency/status semantics, timeout-as-success, changed operation/request bytes, a receipt/refusal not bound to the exact contract lineage, a future-receipt cycle, a Protocol object identity in portable evidence, and any send whose exact published source gate is absent or stale.

The generated canonical Protocol-plane machine is `IrreversibleDispatchAttempt<Contract> {dispatch_contract_id:Contract,action_kind,operation_id,idempotency_token_digest,target_identity,canonical_action_body_digest,canonical_request_transcript_digest,source_gate_kind_and_commitment,source_publication_evidence_commitment,authority_binding_public_commitment,service_visibility_epoch,nonretaining_predecessor_digest,state}` with the closed state `Armed{arm_generation,authorized_operation_plan_commitment,expected_predecessor_protocol_state_commitment,expected_source_gate_and_configuration_commitment}|SentUnknown{attempt_generation,arm_generation,arm_publication_evidence_ref:StrongRef<DispatchArmPublicationEvidence<Contract>>,mark_publication_basis_commitment}|AbandonedBeforeSend{attempt_generation,arm_generation,arm_publication_evidence_ref:StrongRef<DispatchArmPublicationEvidence<Contract>>,abandonment_proof_ref:StrongRef<DispatchNeverSentProof<Contract>>,terminal_reason}|TerminalImported{attempt_generation,terminal_outcome:Applied|AlreadyApplied|PermanentlyRefused|ConflictNoEffect,portable_terminal_evidence_identity,external_receipt_or_refusal_import_commitment,status_lineage_commitment}`. `Contract` must have `origin_plane=CanonicalProtocol`; prebootstrap uses its distinct journal-backed generated attempt type keyed by the prebootstrap contract ID. `Armed` and `AbandonedBeforeSend` contain only values known before their own publication; neither names its future Protocol state, RootManifest, slot, or publication generation. If a later consumer requires evidence that abandonment itself was published, it reconstructs `DispatchAbandonmentPublicationEvidence<Contract>` after the fact from authenticated current/historical Protocol-root membership and `RootPublicationEvidence`; that evidence is never embedded in the abandoning successor.

After the Armed-containing root is durable, recovery or the publisher constructs `DispatchArmPublicationEvidence<Contract> {dispatch_attempt_identity_and_commitment,containing_protocol_state_identity,containing_consensus_state_root_identity,containing_root_manifest_identity,winning_slot_index_generation_and_digest,root_publication_evidence:RootPublicationEvidence,source_gate_commitment,current_configuration_writer_fence_continuity_and_service_commitment,evidence_digest}`. `DispatchNeverSentProof<Contract>` binds that evidence, a current authenticated scan of both slots and the exact attempt lineage, and proves that no `SentUnknown` successor for the arm generation was ever published. Each row names the sole legal Armed-abandonment proof, NotRegistered proof, refusal/conflict evidence, typed receipt import, and portable terminal-evidence schema; absence is a G0 failure. `Armed -> SentUnknown` is durably RootSlot-published **before** request bytes can enter a transport. Recovery therefore treats every `SentUnknown` attempt as possibly delivered, first performs the registered authenticated status query, and never infers absence from a timeout. A definitive signed `NotRegistered` result permits only the byte-identical request under a fresh guard while the row's action-specific eligibility still permits first send; if eligibility has expired, it permits no send unless that contract explicitly registers a terminal-cleanup exception. Applied/AlreadyApplied imports the exact receipt; PermanentRefusal imports a signed zero-effect refusal tombstone; ConflictNoEffect imports signed evidence that the requested transition did not occur and cannot later appear under that operation ID. Any ambiguous result permits status/reconciliation only. `Armed -> AbandonedBeforeSend` is the sole no-send terminal and requires the registered proof; disconnect, cancellation, process death, or provider absence is insufficient. Construction-DAG and crash tests cut before/after authorization publication, Armed publication, arm-evidence construction, SentUnknown publication, transport submission, every status class, typed terminal import, and abandonment publication for every registered contract row.

Immediately before the first send or an allowed exact retry, `IrreversibleDispatchGuard<Contract>` rereads the winning RootSlot and both slot generations, the complete current all-plane root inventory, the still-current registered source gate and its checker, current/prospective configuration, writer-fence and continuity heads, service epoch, authority binding, and profiled time evidence. It also acquires a linear `IrreversibleActionHold<Contract>` that conflicts with invalidation of that authorization/quarantine/hold/reservation/CAS/cancellation gate, target resurrection where applicable, configuration/fence/continuity replacement, and authority widening while allowing unrelated database progress. The nonserializable guard is bound to the exact contract's `SentUnknown` attempt and request bytes, is consumed at transport submission, expires on any checked-observation budget breach, and cannot survive restart. A destructive target independently durably records Started under its own current fence before deleting or destroying its first byte/key; a CAS-style external authority durably registers the exact operation/request lineage before applying a terminal direct successor.

The pre-bootstrap analogue is generated from the exact row whose `origin_plane=RestorePreBootstrap`, not from a singular dual-use row and not from a parallel informal protocol. `PreBootstrapDispatchAttempt<Contract>` has the same request/status laws and `Authorized -> Armed -> SentUnknown -> TerminalImported|AbandonedBeforeSend` semantics, but its publication evidence is `PreBootstrapDispatchPublicationEvidence<Contract>` over the authenticated restore dispatch root, `journal_staging_inode_identity`, both mirror slot generations, whole-inode fence, selected prebootstrap source-gate kind/commitment, external journal-head commitment, and sealed plan/action bijection. `PreBootstrapExternalTerminalImportArtifact<Contract>` is the prebootstrap wrapper `{dispatch_contract_id:Contract,origin_plane:RestorePreBootstrap,action_kind,request_binding,dispatch_attempt_and_publication_commitment,terminal_artifact_bytes_and_digest,portable_terminal_evidence_bytes_and_digest,status_lineage,prebootstrap_time_and_source_gate_commitment,dispatch_root_generation,import_digest}`; it deliberately has no `FenceBoundIrreversibleReceiptHeader` or Protocol identity. `PreBootstrapIrreversibleDispatchGuard<Contract>` rereads all of those values plus current external claim/grant/continuity/time evidence immediately before send. The first canonical bridge copies/verifies each terminal-import artifact through a contract-specific canonical import record and imports a sealed, terminal-or-still-recoverable journal with an exact contract-to-attempt bijection. If a nonterminal prebootstrap attempt must be adopted into canonical Protocol for recovery, the Protocol owner is `AdoptedPreBootstrapDispatchAttempt<Contract>` and permanently retains `origin_plane=RestorePreBootstrap`, the prebootstrap operation-ID namespace, source-gate lineage, and prebootstrap terminal-import type; it never mutates into the canonical contract for the same action. No other subsystem may create a private outbox, retry ledger, or direct provider path. These rules are generated compile-time capability boundaries plus lab/runtime oracles, not review conventions.

The only v1 **cross-plane publication mode** is a registry-declared `AtomicProtocolDetach{cross_plane_conservation_recipe_id}` command-contract row; it is not one special command. For each result-producing Local/Meta command that uses this mode, one same-group Raft entry and one RootManifest slot generation publish (a) the semantic outcome/frontier containing only an opaque owner key and detachment commitment and (b) a Protocol PendingVisibility or legal inline-Active owner plus typed resource escrow. The row supplies a generated cross-plane conservation proof over owner key, byte digest, charge, audit candidate, and authority binding; ObjectId/reference edges across the planes are forbidden. All later activation/resume/ACK/release/expiry/send-completion work is Protocol maintenance and cannot write semantic slots. This narrow composite mode is used by ordinary query results, the **initial** subscription cursor/baseline owner, durable artifact outputs, protected errors, and DP results. Subsequent subscription deltas, coalesced replacements, and reset-required transitions are Protocol-only publications under the already-detached cursor identity. Any other multi-plane writer, any subscription-delta semantic rewrite, or a protocol-to-semantic back-edge is a G0 failure.

## Invariants & claims
Enforces FG-INV-01, FG-INV-10, FG-INV-13, FG-INV-14, FG-INV-16, FG-INV-20, and the G0 no-third-publication-substrate rule. A timeout, transport error, unsigned absence, stale external head, locally elapsed deadline, or response for another contract/plane is never terminal evidence.

## Interactions and ownership
Consumes G0 identity, threat, claim, and authority-binding contracts. command_contracts.toml classifies authorize/arm/import transitions; prebootstrap_journal_publication_contracts.toml owns the sole pre-first-root publication family. DP, audit, continuity, catalog, time, key, backup, restore, retention, and GC beads must resolve every provider action to one row. RootSlot publication itself is not recursively dispatched. Canonical and restore-prebootstrap families may share provider body schemas but never contract IDs, operation namespaces, attempt slots, terminal evidence, or imports.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Registries contain exactly one live row for every legal (action_kind, origin_plane, role/group predicate, source-gate arm) and none for illegal combinations.
- Generated Rust unions, schemas, codecs, handlers, guards, journal transitions, status adapters, and import tables are bijective with both registries.
- Unit/golden tests cover all eight DispatchSourceGateKind arms, every terminal status/disposition, exact request binding, row bounds, body digests, operation namespaces, and canonical/prebootstrap terminal imports.
- Property/model tests prove monotone attempt generations, one terminal disposition, operation-ID/body immutability, hold conservation, no action before durable source gate, and no terminal import before authenticated status lineage.
- Fuzz/mutation rejects cross-contract, cross-plane, cross-role, cross-provider, wrong-head, wrong-publication-evidence, wrong-body, stale-generation, unsigned-status, truncated-lineage, and third-substrate encodings.
- Crash/DPOR injects at authorization publication, attempt arm, request construction, first byte escape, provider registration, every status response, terminal receipt, journal publication, import, adoption, abandonment, and hold release.
- Simulated-provider E2E covers DP charge, audit CAS, key destruction, backup grant, restore lease acquire/renew/release, time transition, and catalog promotion with lost request, lost response, duplicate response, provider conflict, restart, relocation, and takeover.
- Structured JSONL emits {event_version,dispatch_contract_id,action_kind,origin_plane,role_and_group,operation_id,idempotency_digest,attempt_generation,source_gate_arm,source_gate_publication_commitment,request_digest,status_class,provider_counter_or_cas_version,prior_status_digest?,terminal_disposition?,journal_id?,journal_generation?,hold_state,recovery_action,replay_command}. Tests reconstruct every attempt and fail on missing, duplicated, nonmonotone, secret-bearing, or cross-contract events.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: ad-hoc post-commit calls, action-kind-only IDs, erased terminal evidence, inferred absence from timeout, raw provider receipts as local authority, shared canonical/prebootstrap namespaces, and any third publication substrate. Risk: the registry is large; generation and same-change CI prevent silent omissions.

## Provenance
Plan section 5.1 lines 287 and 300-324; G0 clause coverage; Appendix A restore dispatch.

title: Freeze the LanguageContracts: GQL ISO closure, openCypher, FQL, Datalog, Unicode bundle
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the complete versioned query-language contract family before parsers or binders ship: GQL ISO/IEC 39075:2024 minimum closure and selected optional feature IDs; the separate openCypher compatibility profile; explicitly versioned FQL extensions; the validated finite/stratified Datalog surface; synchronous Unicode/UTS #10/UAX #15/UAX #31 data; semantic and scalar profiles; advertised capability/feature-disable behavior; and the negative/deferred language decisions. This task owns canonical contract bytes and registry closure, not parser execution.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B3 requires every language to converge only after independent parsing, binding, and semantic normalization into one typed algebra. B5 requires a query's accepted grammar and semantics to be pinned, replayable artifacts rather than server defaults or host locale. Freezing exact ISO feature prerequisites, Unicode data, scalar equality/order, and dialect boundaries prevents accidental overclaiming and semantic drift. Explicit negative rows prevent future work from quietly installing rejected primary surfaces.

## Exact normative language and semantic contract
The following audited plan clauses are embedded verbatim and authoritative:

### 8.1 Language surface

- **Native: GQL (ISO/IEC 39075:2024)** — graph pattern matching including quantified path patterns, path modes (WALK/TRAIL/ACYCLIC/SIMPLE), the edition's registered shortest/count selectors, label expressions, `LET`/`FILTER`/`FOR`, composite queries, catalog/DDL, and transactions/sessions. The exact minimum closure and optional ISO feature IDs are frozen in `LanguageContract`; an in-flight edition/corrigendum is a different contract and never “lands” silently.
- **openCypher compatibility layer**: the pragmatic on-ramp. GQL and Cypher have separate lexer/parser/profile adapters but converge only after binding and semantic normalization; documented divergences and the openCypher TCK prevent a parser shortcut from changing meaning.
- **Versioned FQL dialect extensions**: temporal, branch, Prism, retrieval, materialized-view, subscription, certificate, branch-admin, and `CHEAPEST`/cost-selector syntax beyond the pinned 2024 ISO feature map is enabled only by an explicit `FQL <major.minor>` declaration or `FQL`-prefixed production. The plan does not call unprefixed future-standard-looking keywords “namespaced.” `DIFF <graph_ref_a> … <graph_ref_b>` — each endpoint an ordinary graph reference carrying the full `graph@branch AS OF <time|seq>` selector surface — is registered under this same dialect discipline as reserved 1.0 syntax producing canonical delta tables (insertions/retractions with element identity, slice, and period columns), composable with views and §9.5 subscriptions like any other typed stream; its evaluation, coverage, authorization, and answer-contract semantics are owned entirely by Appendix C's `Diff` operator-family row, and the syntax reservation makes the operator available only after that row's conformance tests exist.
- **Datalog surface**: `fgdb-datalog` compiles the validated finite/stratified subset in §9.3 to the same typed algebra. Recursion, negation, and aggregates are accepted only when their termination and incrementalization contracts are registered.

`LanguageContract` is a canonically encoded, content-addressed tagged union with common `{ grammar_oid, lexer_profile_oid, normalizer_oid, semantic_profile_oid, scalar_profile_oid, unicode_conformance_bundle_ref }` fields and one surface payload. A `UnicodeConformanceBundle` is `{ unicode_version, unicode_data_oid, uts10_collation_version, uts10_data_oid, uax15_normalization_version, uax15_data_oid, uax31_identifier_version, uax31_data_oid, synchronous_release_set_id, ucs_basic_profile }`; its validator requires Unicode ≥13.0.0 and proves that the UTS #10, UAX #15, and UAX #31 versions/data are the synchronous set claimed for that Unicode release. `Gql` carries `{ edition, corrected_printing, corrigenda[], conformance_profile, mandatory_feature_closure[], graph_type_conformance, selected_minimum_feature_ids[], optional_feature_ids[] }`; `graph_type_conformance` is exactly `Open{feature:GG01}` or `Closed{feature:GG02, element_type_feature:GG20|GG21|GG22|GG23}`. `OpenCypher` carries the exact language/specification revision, grammar and TCK commit, supported scenario manifest, and documented-divergence ObjectId; `Fql` carries its declared major/minor grammar, extension-feature closure, and GQL-base contract; `Datalog` carries the accepted finite/stratified grammar subset plus recursion, negation, aggregate, and operator-registry ObjectIds. The GQL 2024 contract includes the ISO minimum-conformance closure and every prerequisite of its selected feature IDs, supplies the required character-string, Boolean, signed-integer, and floating property types, and pins the common validated Unicode bundle plus mandated UCS_BASIC behavior; optional IDs are separate. Draft Edition 2 syntax can exist only under a visibly draft contract and cannot satisfy the 2024 claim. No loose dialect string or server default can change accepted syntax or semantics after binding.

Parsing never produces executable plans directly, and preparation never mistakes `@now` for a permanent head. `fgdb-bind` first constructs `PreparedQueryTemplate { language_contract_oid, catalog_contract, graph_reference_specs[{ binding_role_id, graph_id, branch_selector, system_selector_spec, valid_selector_spec, required_schema_contract }], parameter_types, non_widenable_authority_ceiling, typed_logical_template, output_schema_contract }`. It owns name/scope and correlated-reference resolution, deterministic role assignment, group variables, parameter inference/coercion, null and duplicate semantics, graph/table shape checking, path legality/termination, capability-domain injection, and incrementalizability classification. `PREPARE` therefore cannot freeze an execution option that it never received. At each execution the caller supplies an `AnswerRequirement` (default `Exact`); any query-language approximation clause narrows it, and an empty intersection is rejected. After parameters and both temporal selectors are known, snapshot acquisition resolves every spec into a concrete `GraphReferenceBinding`; binding then produces `BoundQuery<Role> {prepared_template_ref:StrongRef<PreparedQueryTemplate>,logical_state_root_identity:WeakStateIdentity,graph_reference_bindings[],normalized_valid_time_bindings[],topology_epoch,authority_binding:AuthorityBindingFor<Role>,authority_binding_body_digest,purpose_class,answer_requirement,instantiated_logical_plan,output_schema}`. Prepared handles pin the template and may be reused only while its catalog/schema compatibility predicates hold under same-or-narrower authority. Physical/logical plan-cache entries, certificates, and replay pin the concrete `BoundQuery`; their key includes the binding body digest, purpose, role, and service epoch. A cross-authority, cross-graph, historical, or valid-time self-join plan cannot substitute one reference's authority/head/schema/period for another. Optimizers consume only this bound typed IR.

Preparation is itself an authorized, idempotent child operation because even parameter/output schemas can reveal protected catalog facts. `SessionAuthorityBinding` is the Ready-bound closed union `Local{header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>,presentation_binding:SessionBound{session_binding,auth_generation}}|Meta{header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Meta>,presentation_binding:SessionBound{session_binding,auth_generation}}`; the role must match the selected database posture and Ready generation. `PrepareRequestRecord` is the session-scoped immutable `{ready_binding,session_binding,prepare_request_idempotency_key,canonical_prepare_request_digest,language_contract_oid,requested_parameter_contract?,session_authority_binding:SessionAuthorityBinding,catalog_contract_basis,resource_reservation_ref}`. It has no fictitious `AuthorityBindingRef<Session>` and no duplicate raw `SecurityStateBinding`. `PreparedStatementRecord` is `{request_ref:StrongRef<PrepareRequestRecord>,template_ref:StrongRef<PreparedQueryTemplate>,public_statement_handle:PublicHandle<PreparedStatement>,public_state_token:PublicStateToken<PreparedStatement>,authorized_public_parameter_schema,authorized_public_output_contract_commitment,compatibility_contracts,prepare_authorization_projection,response_commitment}`. The scoped idempotency index maps one key to exactly one request/record; byte-identical retry reproduces the same PREPARED bytes, while text, language, requested contract, Ready, or authority drift conflicts before protected catalog observation. Before PREPARED, a `PublicFrameSendGuard::PreparedMetadata` arm revalidates the complete current binding, the record's non-widenable ceiling, catalog compatibility, and exact frozen response digest. EXECUTE must present both public handle and state token, resolve them through the session index, reauthorize same-or-narrower, and then construct the concrete `BoundQuery`; prepared metadata never grants execution authority. Session drain fences unsent PREPARED, retires unescaped records after their send obligations join, and never turns socket success into durable semantic state.

Clients declare ceilings and expectations, never the semantic class. `TxnOperationCeiling` is exactly `ReadOnlyOnly|ReadWriteAllowed`. `CanonicalMutationPotential` is `ProvenReadOnly|MayMutateGraph|MayMutateSchema|MayInvokeReplicatedProcedure`; `CanonicalOutputClass` is `NoRows|Rows`. The derived `CanonicalStatementClass` is `ReadOnly{output}` only for ProvenReadOnly, `WriteReturning` for any mutation potential plus Rows, and `WriteNoResult` for any mutation potential plus NoRows. A write-capable semantic no-op remains write-classified because admission, authorization, witnesses, and retry semantics cannot be inferred from the final zero effect.

`CanonicalStatementClassification` is the immutable binder object `{classification_version,prepared_template_ref:StrongRef<PreparedQueryTemplate>,bound_query_ref:StrongRef<BoundQuery>,prepared_template_digest,canonical_bound_query_digest,parameter_digest,language_contract_oid,binder_and_normalizer_semantics_oid,exact_graph_reference_bindings,exact_write_coordinate_set,sorted_procedure_udf_module_effect_contract_refs[StrongRef<ExecutableEffectContract>],mutation_potential,output_class,derived_statement_class,required_txn_operation_ceiling,required_warden_operation_classes,determinism_and_external_effect_profile,classification_digest:BodyDigest<CanonicalStatementClassification>}`. It is constructed after parameters, graph roles, schemas, modules/procedures, and temporal selectors resolve and before statement registration. Every executable artifact has one immutable bounded effect contract; parameters cannot choose an undeclared class. The generated statement-kind matrix maps every bound-IR tag and effect-contract arm to exactly one mutation/output row. Unknown tags, wildcard fallback, or an unclassified procedure fail binding.

Attempt registration stores only the client ceiling. Statement registration specs remove client `statement_class` and instead strongly name the classification plus repeated digest projections that must byte-match it. Statement registrations, intent batches, statement audit bases, authorization decisions, owner/result/no-result selection, workspace generations, and idempotent request digests all name the same classification. Workspace generation zero starts `cumulative_mutation_potential=ProvenReadOnly`; successful statement publication takes the monotone join, so a mutation-capable statement can never be reclassified away. A class exceeding the attempt ceiling rejects before storage observation. Read-close is legal only from cumulative ProvenReadOnly; otherwise the write terminal path applies even if all effects normalize to no-op. Rebase regenerates effects/results but cannot reinterpret the stored classification; missing or incompatible semantics requires a fresh bind/request. Exact retry returns the stored classification across ambient schema/policy/module drift, while a newly bound different class conflicts under the old idempotency key. Generated malicious-underclassification tests cover every GQL/openCypher tag, subquery, DDL, mutating CALL/UDF/module, output/no-output form, dynamic graph role, adapter, and PREPARE-versus-EXECUTE_TEXT path.

### 8.2 Semantics discipline

GQL's formal-semantics literature is tracked; where the standard leaves latitude (result ordering, path enumeration order, duplicate semantics under morphism modes), FrankenGraphDB pins behavior via CGSE tie-break policies (§8.6) and documents each pin. Temporal clauses get algebraic semantics (snapshot-relativized pattern matching; `BETWEEN` yields per-binding validity intervals with interval-algebra predicates).

Each pin set is a versioned **SemanticProfile** referenced from `LanguageContract`—not an ambiguous name such as bare `gql-2024-strict`—fixing null/UNKNOWN handling, duplicate semantics per morphism mode, ordering defaults, coercion rules, and tie-break bindings. Two results are comparable only under the same language+semantic+scalar contracts, and corrigendum/dialect drift becomes a new content-addressed artifact.

`CanonicalScalarProfile` defines equality, hashing, total ordering, collation, coercion, and durable/result encoding for every value, with property tests enforcing `equal ⇒ same_hash`, comparator totality/transitivity, and encode/decode/order coherence. `STRICT_PORTABLE` canonicalizes NaNs and signed zero; fixes decimal scale/rounding/overflow; stores timestamp instant, zone/offset semantics, and a content-addressed tzdb version; pins Unicode data/normalization/segmentation and each non-binary collation by ObjectId; fixes map-key order over canonical bytes; and rejects unavailable profile artifacts rather than consulting host locale/tzdb. Floating execution uses fixed logical reduction trees independent of SIMD width, fixes denormal/rounding behavior, forbids target-dependent contraction, and uses pinned math kernels. A scalar/SIMD fast path ships in strict mode only after bit-identity testing on every supported target; otherwise it is RELAXED and the certificate names target/build behavior.

Path expressions carry a rewrite-protected `PathSemantics { mode, selector, hops, cost, temporal, enumeration, tie_break }`. `All + WALK` requires a finite hop bound. Every potentially infinite enumeration requires a finite selector or explicit `MaxResults`/resource budget; truncation is visible result status and certificate state, never silent success. NaN/infinite weights, arithmetic overflow, and a reachable negative cycle that makes the requested WALK optimum unbounded have defined errors. Negative finite weights are legal only for mode/selector combinations with a registered exact algorithm and termination contract. Dijkstra/bidirectional kernels require nonnegative costs; the matrix below governs other cases.

Executor state is `PathStateKey { automaton_state, vertex, mode_state, capture_state_id, feasible_valid_time, cost_state }`, where `CaptureStateId` is a full content digest whose lookup verifies canonical capture bytes on collision; TRAIL carries persistent used-edge state and SIMPLE/ACYCLIC carry persistent visited-vertex state. Coalescing is allowed only through a mode-specific proved dominance relation. The same abstraction defines §7.3 path witnesses. The physical registry names valid combinations: bounded RPQ WALK uses NFA-product BFS/DFS; nonnegative shortest uses BFS/Dijkstra/bidirectional variants; hop-bounded negative WALK uses dynamic programming over hops; unbounded WALK may use Bellman–Ford-class logic only to prove a finite optimum or report a reachable negative cycle. Negative TRAIL/SIMPLE/ACYCLIC uses exact finite history-aware search with an exponential complexity/resource contract or is unavailable. Yen/Eppstein is used only where its preconditions match; temporal paths include the feasible interval in product state.

## Exact rejected/deferred surface decisions
### 3.4 What we deliberately reject

Generic KV underlays (JanusGraph/Nebula tax); Gremlin as the primary language (imperative, optimizer-hostile — provided only as a later compat shim if ever); RDF-first modeling (property graph first; RDF import/view later); JVM anything; mmap-as-the-durability-story; PMA global rebalancing; eventual consistency as a default; external crates (constraint #1).

Four seductive alternatives were evaluated in depth and rejected with recorded reasons: (a) native hyperedges; (b) an unbounded per-fragment representation zoo; (c) a separate full GraphBLAS executor; and (d) plan racing as the default. Racing survives only behind deterministic-output buffering and registered safe cutovers (§8.5). Weaver-style refinable timestamps were set aside for 1.0 because one global scalar commit order simplifies Chronicle, branches, Ripple, and replay; post-1.0 sharding workstream W12 must preserve that contract through a meta-Raft global transaction record or explicitly reopen the decision.

Further rejections: (e) a second Calvin-style transaction lane unless measured aborts justify reopening it; (f) WASM as a foreign UDF runtime; (g) external-codegen JIT; (h) TrueTime-class infrastructure for 1.0—HLC plus consensus-fenced read contracts supplies the semantics actually specified, not arbitrary follower linearizability; (i) FHE/MPC/ORAM in the initial threat model; (j) learned indexes as authoritative access paths; and (k) a spatial index in 1.0 — `Point(2D/3D)` values are storable scalars but are not orderable and not indexable, a declared index over a `Point` property fails closed as a typed error, and the canonical `Point` byte encoding exists for digests and equality only and is explicitly not a spatial order; the recorded post-1.0 route is a Z-order/Hilbert-curve mapping over the existing B-tree machinery, with an in-house R-tree admitted only if profiling defeats the curve mapping, and the Neo4j differential corpus documents the divergence (`point()`, `distance()`, point indexes) as a registered non-goal. DP and leakage measurements remain scoped mechanisms, not substitutes for noninterference.

## Registry, boundaries, and ownership
`language_contracts.toml` has stable nonreusable IDs for the common contract header and each exact Gql/OpenCypher/Fql/Datalog arm, grammar/lexer/normalizer/semantic/scalar/Unicode artifact, ISO feature/prerequisite row, divergence row, capability-manifest bit, and rejected/deferred surface. A generated closure checker proves the GQL 2024 selected set contains the minimum closure and every prerequisite; graph-type selection is exactly GG01 or GG02 plus one applicable GG20-GG23 arm; the Unicode bundle is one synchronous release set; no draft Edition 2, loose dialect string, server default, host locale/tzdb, or unprefixed FQL-looking syntax satisfies the 2024 claim.

Gremlin is not a primary language, optimizer authority, or 1.0 LanguageContract arm. A later compatibility shim, if ever approved, is a separate post-1.0 profile and gate. RDF-first modeling is rejected: the property graph remains canonical; RDF may later exist only as a typed import/view with explicit conversion, loss, identity, disclosure, and answer contracts, never a second storage truth. Spatial Point values remain storable/equality-comparable but nonorderable/nonindexable in 1.0. Native hyperedges, a separate GraphBLAS executor, WASM/native foreign semantics, and external-codegen JIT remain rejected as stated in the decision record.

Parser/binder/GLA tasks consume these bytes. G0 format/field registries own durable encoding; W5 parser/binder/scalar/determinism tasks own execution; W6 Datalog recursion owns validated incrementalization; verification owns ISO-ID, openCypher TCK, grammar fuzz, semantic differential, and out-of-contract refusal corpora; Fabric advertises only enabled contract rows. A missing checker or operator row makes the feature absent, not partial.

## Invariants & claims
Supports FG-INV-12 semantic generation identity, FG-INV-19 replay closure, and FG-INV-20 authority-safe preparation/binding. Conformance claims are scoped to the exact contract OID and feature matrix. openCypher parity applies only to supported scenarios minus documented divergences. Datalog acceptance never implies termination outside the registered subset.

## Interactions
Depends on G0 registries/claim constitution and the architecture decision record. Feeds W5 parser, binder, GLA, scalar, determinism, answer-contract, and replay work; W6 recursion/Diff/subscription surfaces; Fabric negotiation and robot schema; conformance/differential verification; and G1/G4 capability gates.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Canonical rows and golden vectors cover every common field, surface arm, ISO feature/prerequisite, Unicode artifact, semantic/scalar profile, FQL extension, Datalog restriction, divergence, and rejected/deferred surface with stable IDs/tags.
- Unit tests validate exact encode/decode, ISO closure/prerequisites, GG01 versus GG02+GG20-GG23 selection, synchronous Unicode release compatibility, profile availability, scalar totality/hash/encoding laws, and version negotiation.
- Property/mutation tests delete prerequisites, mix Unicode release data, substitute grammar/semantic/scalar artifacts, drift corrigenda, inject host locale/tzdb, or smuggle unprefixed/draft syntax and prove failure.
- Grammar/parser fuzzing covers all accepted and rejected tokens without direct AST execution; unknown tags and disabled rows fail before planning.
- Conformance tests key every GQL feature and openCypher TCK scenario to its exact contract/divergence row; unsupported features are rejected and documented rather than silently approximated.
- E2E scripts negotiate embedded and FGP sessions for GQL/openCypher/FQL/Datalog, prepare and execute representative accepted statements, then attempt Gremlin, RDF-first, draft-edition, unavailable Unicode, and out-of-contract features; only registered enabled surfaces reach binding.
- Replay tests prove the same contract/template/binding inputs remain byte-identical across restart and host locale/tzdb changes; a changed contract produces a new identity.
- Detailed versioned JSONL diagnostics emit contract_oid, surface/tag/version, requested and expanded feature IDs, Unicode bundle OIDs, semantic/scalar profiles, capability decision, divergence/rejection code, parser/binder stage reached, verdict, artifact refs, and replay command. Logs never expose protected catalog facts or query payloads beyond authorized public commitments, and tests fail on missing/out-of-order events.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: ISO corrigenda and Unicode releases evolve. Mitigation: each is a new content-addressed contract with explicit compatibility evidence; nothing lands silently. Rejected: one permissive parser, implicit server dialect, host-dependent scalar behavior, Gremlin/RDF as primary surfaces, and advertising syntactic support before binder/operator/checker closure.

## Provenance
Plan §3.4 and §8.1-§8.3; Gate G0/G4 language clauses; Appendix C operator ownership.
