title: Freeze result_owner_arms and transport-independent result retention formats
description:
## What & scope
Freeze the sole canonical result-owner registry and complete transport-independent Local/Meta result-delivery format contract. This resolves W2/W10 ownership: G0 freezes schemas; W2 owns semantic detachment, rooted Protocol retention, lifecycle and recovery; W10 owns FGP framing, send obligations, sockets/adapters, and public delivery operations over the frozen machine.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Results are durable promises, not borrowed socket buffers. Commit, statement publication, DP output, and replay execution detach exactly once into independently retained ownership that survives disconnect, process death, checkpoint, compaction, backup/restore, service-epoch transition, and transport replacement. Implicit Drop/cancel release would make committed data loss depend on process timing.

## Design — exact normative contract
The complete Appendix A contract follows:
`LocalSerializationCertificate` is a same-group certificate `{SameGroupCertificateHeader,registration_ref:StrongRef<LocalAttemptRegistration>,lifecycle_basis:Statement{statement_registration_ref:StrongRef<LocalStatementRegistration>,prior_workspace_generation_ref:StrongRef<LocalTxnWorkspaceGeneration>,successor_workspace_generation_ref:StrongRef<LocalTxnWorkspaceGeneration>}|Prepare{terminal_admission_basis_digest}|ReadClose{read_close_basis_digest},snapshot_and_conflict_index_basis,complete_read_witness_refs[LocalReadWitnessRef],complete_write_summary_refs[LocalWriteSummaryRef],candidate_edges[],retained_overlap_projection_digest,scc_verifier_version,acyclic_result,conservative_fallbacks[],certificate_attempt_plan_ref,quorum_signatures}`. `LocalReadWitnessRef` and `LocalWriteSummaryRef` are generated closed unions over the registered Local witness/summary targets; raw StrongRef bags are forbidden. Every follower reconstructs the Local SSI graph and fixed snapshot/workspace inputs. `LocalStatementPublicationSpec` is `{statement_registration_ref:StrongRef<LocalStatementRegistration>,registration_ref:StrongRef<LocalAttemptRegistration>,expected_index_value:Open,statement_audit_admission:LocalStatementAuditAdmission::Claimed|NotRequired,read_access_admission_ref:StrongRef<ReadAccessAdmissionRecord>,read_result_release_decision_ref:StrongRef<ReadResultReleaseDecisionRecord>,local_serialization_certificate_ref:StrongRef<LocalSerializationCertificate>,expected_prior_workspace_generation_ref:StrongRef<LocalTxnWorkspaceGeneration>,successor_workspace_generation_ref:StrongRef<LocalTxnWorkspaceGeneration>,successor_cumulative_read_witness_root_ref:StrongRef<LocalCumulativeReadWitnessRoot>,successor_cumulative_effect_root_ref:StrongRef<LocalCumulativeEffectRoot>,published_output:LocalStatementPublishedOutput,expected_statement_and_outcome_frontiers,terminal_audit_gate}`. `LocalStatementPublishedOutput` is `NoResult{no_result_proof_ref:StrongRef<NoResultProof>,terminal_delivery_frontier_digest}|Buffered{manifest_ref:StrongRef<LocalBufferedResultManifest>,canonical_result_digest,delivery_policy_ref:StrongRef<ResultDeliveryPolicy<Local>>,inline_activation_recipe:InlineResultDeliveryActivationRecipe<Local>?}`. The optional recipe is legal only when this same apply is provably the next gap-free visible candidate and the gate is NotRequired; otherwise it must be absent. Tag, statement class, result owner, schema/answer contract/digest, prior/successor workspace, witness/effect roots, security binding, and ticket owner must byte-match. Buffered apply creates the role-valid applied publication reference, resource transfer, and independent-retention record; it creates `ActiveDeliverable` only through a legal inline activation, otherwise `PendingVisibility` with no lease/capability/expiry. It then changes Open to Published, advances the statement/workspace/delivery frontiers, and constructs the immediately succeeding `TxnOutcomeRecord::Registered`. A pending candidate remains invisible until its exact statement pipeline entry is released by `AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec`, whose matching activation recipe installs the first lease. `LocalStatementAbortSpec` alone changes Open to `Failed|Abandoned`, resolves that statement ticket, proves no result/workspace effect, releases named resources, advances its no-result terminal frontier, and applies the registration-pinned `ContinueAttempt|AbortAttempt` policy.

`result_owner_arms.toml` is the sole authoritative family for manifest owner, pre-apply owner basis, post-apply semantic owner, delivery owner, retention owner, disposition, resume subject, and public owner commitment. It generates role-exact arms for `TerminalRead`, `AutocommitWriteTerminal`, `Statement`, `DpResult`, and `ReplayExecution`; an arm cannot be added in prose to only one union. `ReplayExecution` binds its replay-execution registration/publication identities, manifest/result contract, and execution request digest, and uses the same protocol delivery lifecycle. `LocalBufferedResultOwner`, `GeneratedResultDeliveryOwnerBasis<Role>`, `ResultSemanticOwnerRef<Role>`, and their Meta forms are generated views of this registry. `LocalBufferedResultManifest` is `{owner:LocalBufferedResultOwner,authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>,canonical_schema_ref:StrongRef<ResultSchema>,public_schema_digest,canonical_encoding_version,result_answer_contract,row_count,byte_count,ordered_chunks[CanonicalResultChunkDescriptor],canonical_result_digest,resource_charge_ref:StrongRef<ResourceLedgerTransition>}` and obeys the exact public transcripts. `ResultDeliveryServiceAuthority` is `DirectOrdinary{continuity_digest,service_catalog_version}|PromotionReceiptRequired{promotion_manifest_digest,expected_catalog_predecessor_version,promotion_receipt_digest}`. Exhaustive generation/round-trip tests reject missing arms and role substitution.

The nonexpiring previsibility object is `ResultDeliveryPolicy<Role> {role,authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,owner_basis:GeneratedResultDeliveryOwnerBasis<Role>,manifest_ref:ResultManifestRef,canonical_result_digest,result_answer_contract,release_subject_digest,pre_minted_delivery_id,initial_lease_generation,service_authority:ResultDeliveryServiceAuthority,permitted_time_authority_profile_set,min_first_delivery_window,nominal_lease_duration,maximum_lease_duration,chunk_replay_profile,maximum_replay_count,initial_capability_generation,initial_capability_nonce,capability_verifier_key_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityVerifierKey>,body_digest}`. It contains policy/duration, not an absolute window, lease, or capability bytes; it cannot authorize output or expiry. The owner/manifest/resource escrow and policy remain durable while audit is pending, so arbitrary head-of-line delay cannot consume a client window.

`ResultDeliveryLeaseTimeBasis<Role>` is built only for an immediately visible inline result or after a pending result has reached `ReleasedAwaitingActivation`: `{policy_ref:StrongRef<ResultDeliveryPolicy<Role>>,authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,exact_release_subject,delivery_id,lease_generation,time_authority_profile_oid,not_before,expires_at,minimum_remaining_first_delivery_window,successor_capability_generation,successor_capability_nonce,capability_verifier_key_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityVerifierKey>,body_digest:BodyDigest<ResultDeliveryLeaseTimeBasis<Role>>}`. Its policy projection, current same-or-narrower complete authority binding, service epoch/receipt, owner, manifest, digest, duration bounds, verifier, and immutable release evidence must byte-match; `expires_at-not_before` is checked and the signed validation interval's latest instant plus the minimum window must not exceed `expires_at`. `SubscriptionDeliveryLeaseTimeBasis<Role>`, `ArtifactOutputLeaseTimeBasis<Role>`, and `ProtectedErrorLeaseTimeBasis<Role>` use the same complete header/window/verifier contract with their own noninterchangeable owner and policy fields. `InlineResultDeliveryActivationRecipe<Role>` and `ResultDeliveryActivationRecipe<Role>` both contain `{time_basis_ref:StrongRef<ResultDeliveryLeaseTimeBasis<Role>>,issuance_time_validation_evidence_ref:StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>,prebuilt_initial_resume_replay_ref:StrongRef<ResumeCapabilityReplayRecord>,expected_released_retention_ref?}` and differ only in the registered construction site. The latter is consumed by `ProtectedOutputActivationSpec::Result`, never by `AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec`. Missing/stale time evidence delays only activation; a fresh recipe may retry against the same released owner. Thus a hidden/released-but-inactive result has no aging lease, and audit visibility never depends on time service health.

Visible activation constructs `LocalResultDeliveryLease {owner:LocalResultDeliveryOwner,manifest_ref,policy_ref,time_basis_ref,delivery_id,lease_generation,canonical_result_digest,authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>,time_authority_profile_oid,not_before,expires_at,issuance_time_validation_evidence_ref,chunk_replay_profile,maximum_replay_count,successor_capability_fields,activation_applied_ref:ResultActivationAppliedRef}` where `ResultActivationAppliedRef` is exactly `InlineSemantic{applied_control_ref,logical_command_seq}|ProtocolActivation{maintenance_applied_ref,maintenance_index}`. The lease header must byte-match its time basis and release decision. `LocalResultDeliveryOwner` is `TerminalRead{registration_ref,read_close_applied_ref}|AutocommitWriteTerminal{registration_ref,terminal_completion_applied_ref,terminal_ready_outcome_ref}|Statement{registration_ref,statement_registration_ref,publication_applied_ref}|DpResult{request_key_digest,commit_result_applied_ref}`. `LocalResultDeliveryIndex` is only the stable Local alias for the Protocol-plane `ResultIndependentRetentionIndex<Local>`; no field with that name is encoded in `LogicalStatePayload`. `DeliveryLeaseExpiryEvidence` is the pre-order `{lease:Local{lease_ref:StrongRef<LocalResultDeliveryLease>}|Sharded{lease_ref:StrongRef<ResultDeliveryLease>},expected_active_deliverable_retention_state_digest,deadline,time_validation_evidence_ref:StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>,stable_expiry_reason,validator_version}`; evidence must be Expired for this exact active lease/deadline/release action, and neither PendingVisibility nor ReleasedAwaitingActivation is an inhabitable subject. `ResultReleaseEvidence<Local>` is exactly `ClientRelease{receipt_ref:StrongRef<AuthenticatedClientResultReleaseReceipt<Local>>}|LeaseExpired{expiry_evidence_ref:StrongRef<DeliveryLeaseExpiryEvidence>}`. Session/region death only closes transport obligations, and attempt terminalization never releases promised result bytes.

`ResultResourceEscrow<Role>` is the Protocol-plane conservation object `{role,semantic_resource_transition_ref:StrongRef<ResourceLedgerTransition>,semantic_detachment_identity,delivery_id,charge_class_and_amount,resource_profile_oid,state:Owned,body_digest}`. Initial semantic result detachment atomically debits/transfers the exact charge out of `ResourceLedgerState` once and creates this escrow plus PendingVisibility, ReleasedAwaitingActivation, or legal inline ActiveDeliverable in the same RootManifest publication. Release/activation/resume preserve Owned; ACK/explicit release/profiled expiry consumes it and constructs a compact protocol disposition whose amount exactly equals the escrow. Later maintenance never mutates the semantic ledger. Cursor, artifact, and protected-error delivery use distinct typed escrow arms under the same conservation registry.

`LocalResultDeliveryTransitionSpec` is the Local Maintenance `Acknowledge|ReleaseUnacked` union with exact owner/manifest/lease/ActiveDeliverable/digest/prior-state/escrow/audit fields. Acknowledge requires `AuthenticatedClientResultAckReceipt<Local>`; release requires role-valid release/expiry evidence. Apply creates one ACK/release record, terminal retention successor, and protocol escrow disposition. It never changes a semantic payload or delivery frontier—the semantic command already detached that frontier. Before terminal publication it fences the sender generation, cancels Queued frames, and joins Writing frames. No protected bytes appear before activation. The write-terminal owner arm is uninhabited before `LocalTerminalCompletionSpec` selects TerminalReady; that semantic completion creates the publication hold/escrow, audit visibility releases it, and inline or independent Protocol activation constructs the lease.

`AuthenticatedClientResultReleaseReceipt<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is the immutable pre-release proof `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,session_authorization_ref:StrongRef<SessionAuthorizationRecord<Role>>,auth_context_generation,session_binding,public_authority_commitment,posture_and_role:Local|Meta,result_owner_identity,result_delivery_id,expected_active_delivery_state_version,expected_active_retention_digest,request_id,stream_id,strictly_monotone_release_nonce,source:ClientResultReleaseAuthority,canonical_release_request_digest,server_process_incarnation,accepted_child_state_version,server_signing_key_epoch,signature}`. The public commitment is a redundant integrity projection of the full header/session record, never a substitute. It is created only after an explicit FGP `RESULT_RELEASE`, embedded `release()`, or Bolt DISCARD/RESET request passes current-epoch authentication, nonreplay, exact owner/delivery/state, and same-or-narrower authority checks. Duplicate request bytes reproduce the same receipt; nonce, source, body, authority, or state drift fails.

`ResultEndSendCompletionRecord` is the immutable durable bridge from ephemeral transport to result ACK: `{authority_binding_public_commitment,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch,session_binding,server_process_incarnation,sender_generation,result_owner_identity,result_delivery_id,delivery_state_version,resume_capability_commitment,result_end_frame_digest,complete_canonical_byte_length,canonical_result_digest,flow_reservation_identity,flow_bytes_and_rows_committed,write_start_authority_and_frame_time_requirement_set_commitment,transport_sent_obligation_commitment,sent_completion_nonce,server_signing_key_epoch,signature}`. It is constructed only after the complete authenticated RESULT_END frame reaches `TransportSendObligation::Sent`, the exact flow reservation is reconciled, and the write-start authority/time requirement-set commitment byte-matches the send obligation; it owns no result bulk bytes and is retained through ACK/reconnect/expiry resolution. `AuthenticatedClientResultAckReceipt<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is the distinct immutable proof `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,session_authorization_ref:StrongRef<SessionAuthorizationRecord<Role>>,auth_context_generation,session_binding,public_authority_commitment,posture_and_role:Local|Meta,result_owner_identity,result_delivery_id,expected_active_delivery_state_version,expected_active_retention_digest,presented_resume_capability_commitment,result_end_send_completion_ref:StrongRef<ResultEndSendCompletionRecord>,request_id,stream_id,strictly_monotone_ack_nonce,canonical_ack_request_digest,server_process_incarnation,accepted_child_state_version,server_signing_key_epoch,signature}`. The repeated public commitment and send-completion projection must byte-match the full current header. It exists only after the authenticated peer ACKs that exact send-completion transcript under current same-or-narrower authority. It cannot be constructed from a socket write, local EOF, partial-read inference, sender close, or release request. Duplicate bytes reproduce one receipt; a different frame/result/state/capability/nonce loses the CAS. `ResultAckRecord` strongly owns this receipt and carries only weak authenticated identities of the retired lease/manifest/retention predecessor.

`AuthenticatedClientCancelReceipt` does not exist. `SessionRegionCloseReceipt` is the distinct structured-concurrency proof `{database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch,session_binding,server_process_incarnation,region_id,region_generation,posture:Local|Sharded,result_owner_identity,result_delivery_id,close_cause_class,region_close_transition_digest,child_obligation_inventory_digest,zero_live_transport_sender_and_chunk_obligation_proof,close_receipt_nonce,server_signing_key_epoch,signature}`. It discharges only in-process sender/chunk obligations after the owning region irreversibly closes; it is not result ACK/release evidence, does not change durable retention, and conveys no authority to discard resumable bytes. QUERY_CANCEL, Rust Drop, process death, socket EOF, timeout, or an unsigned region observation proves neither ACK, durable release, nor expiry.

Published results use an explicit capability-owned transfer, so transaction completion and compaction never wait for a client ACK. `ResultManifestRef` is the exact role union `Local{manifest_ref:StrongRef<LocalBufferedResultManifest>}|Sharded{manifest_ref:StrongRef<BufferedResultManifest>}`; `ResultLeaseRef` and `ResultSemanticOwnerRef` are corresponding generated closed role unions. `ResultResumeCapabilityCommitment` binds the opaque capability's domain, namespace, incarnation, service epoch, tenant/principal, non-widenable authority ceiling, complete security-binding commitment, delivery ID/generation, manifest/result digest, expiry profile/window, verifier-key epoch, and successor nonce.

The common body is deliberately split. `DeliveryTransitionAppliedRef` is `InlineSemanticDetachment{applied_semantic_ref:AppliedControlRef}|ProtocolMaintenance{maintenance_applied_ref:MaintenanceAppliedRef}`; it describes the actual constructor and never fabricates a protocol predecessor for initial detachment. `ResultActiveCommon<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is `{role,authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,semantic_owner_ref:ResultSemanticOwnerRef<Role>,semantic_owner_commitment,semantic_detachment_identity,delivery_id,lease_generation,delivery_state_version,canonical_result_digest,result_answer_contract,weak_prior_retention_identity,latest_transition_ref:DeliveryTransitionAppliedRef,lookup_and_tombstone_floor,body_digest}`. `ResultTerminalCommon<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is `{role,terminal_authority_commitment:TerminalAuthorityCommitment<Role>,semantic_owner_commitment,semantic_detachment_identity,delivery_id,terminal_delivery_state_version,canonical_result_digest,result_answer_contract,weak_prior_retention_identity,weak_manifest_identity,weak_lease_identity?,terminal_protocol_transition_ref:MaintenanceAppliedRef,lookup_and_tombstone_floor,body_digest}` and has no strong authority-binding, semantic-owner, manifest, lease, replay, verifier, escrow, or bulk-predecessor edge. The terminal commitment is legal only because these arms are nonrevivable and own no protected result bytes.

`ResultIndependentRetentionRecord<Role>` is the Protocol-plane state-shaped union `PendingVisibility{common:ResultActiveCommon<Role>,manifest_ref:ResultManifestRef,delivery_policy_ref:StrongRef<ResultDeliveryPolicy<Role>>,resource_escrow_ref:StrongRef<ResultResourceEscrow<Role>>,release_subject_commitment}`; `ReleasedAwaitingActivation{common:ResultActiveCommon<Role>,manifest_ref:ResultManifestRef,delivery_policy_ref,resource_escrow_ref,audit_release_evidence:AuditReleaseEvidence,release_maintenance_ref:MaintenanceAppliedRef}`; `ActiveDeliverable{common:ResultActiveCommon<Role>,manifest_ref:ResultManifestRef,delivery_policy_ref,lease_ref:ResultLeaseRef,resource_escrow_ref,current_resume_replay_ref:StrongRef<ResumeCapabilityReplayRecord>,consumed_immediate_predecessor_replay_ref:StrongRef<ResumeCapabilityReplayRecord>?,resume_capability_commitment,replay_count,release_subject_commitment,audit_release_evidence:AuditReleaseEvidence}`; `Acknowledged{common:ResultTerminalCommon<Role>,ack_ref:StrongRef<ResultAckRecord>,resource_disposition_ref:StrongRef<ResultResourceDispositionRecord>,capability_tombstone_ref:StrongRef<ResultCapabilityTombstone>}`; or `ReleasedUnacked{common:ResultTerminalCommon<Role>,release_ref:StrongRef<ResultReleaseRecord>,resource_disposition_ref:StrongRef<ResultResourceDispositionRecord>,capability_tombstone_ref:StrongRef<ResultCapabilityTombstone>}`. No arm strongly names a predecessor. Pending and ReleasedAwaitingActivation own manifest/policy/escrow but no absolute window or capability; only ActiveDeliverable owns lease/replay. Terminal evidence has weak prior identities and exact escrow disposition. Each maintenance transition CAS-replaces the protocol index leaf; after the covering protocol snapshot/cut, prior bulk becomes unmarked while tombstone evidence remains. Generated plane, reachability, conservation, and construction-DAG oracles prove these properties.

`ResultResumeTransitionSpec<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is the exact ordered `RotateResume` input `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,authority_nonwidening_proof_ref:StrongRef<AuthorityNonwideningProof>,active_deliverable_ref:StrongRef<ResultIndependentRetentionRecord<Role>>,expected_delivery_state_version,expected_lease_generation,presented_resume_validation_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence>,presented_current_or_consumed_predecessor_replay_ref:StrongRef<ResumeCapabilityReplayRecord>,canonical_resume_boundary:{chunk_ordinal,canonical_byte_offset,row_boundary_digest},canonical_request_idempotency_key,prebuilt_successor_resume_replay_ref:StrongRef<ResumeCapabilityReplayRecord>,expected_replay_count,checked_successor_replay_count,maximum_replay_count,terminal_audit_gate}`. Apply verifies active index membership, exact canonical boundary, current or registered consumed-immediate-predecessor lineage, exact or proved narrower complete authority against the active record/capability, same result/delivery/version, checked increment, and `successor_count <= maximum`. It constructs a new ActiveDeliverable record with the current full binding, same active ownership, successor replay ref/capability commitment, incremented version/count, and no predecessor edge; atomically swaps the index; and returns deterministic `RESULT_RESUMED` bytes. An identical retry returns the same successor; a different boundary/generation/authority loses, and exceeding the maximum yields a typed non-mutating `ReplayLimitReached` result without releasing the data. ACK, explicit release, expiry, audit visibility, and resume all CAS the same active version, so exactly one conflicting transition wins. Local and Global command registries include `ResultResumeTransitionSpec`; restart/key-rotation/lost-response and every resume-vs-ACK/release/expiry race are permanent DPOR gates. `ResultReleaseEvidence<Role>` has the same two tag shapes for Local and Meta, but its receipt reference is role-specialized and noninterchangeable; no QUERY_CANCEL, socket close, Drop, or process/session event can construct either arm.

The result-producing Local/Meta semantic command uses a registered `AtomicProtocolDetach` publication: the semantic payload advances its delivery frontier to `DetachedToProtocolRetention{delivery_id,detachment_commitment}` while the same RootManifest slot generation installs the new Protocol owner and typed resource escrow. Neither plane points to the other by ObjectId. It may create `ActiveDeliverable` only when its NotRequired/covered gate and expected pipeline basis prove the resulting candidate visible in the same publication and it carries a valid inline activation recipe. A visible inline subject without valid time evidence creates `ReleasedAwaitingActivation`; every Required gate and every NotRequired candidate behind an earlier gap creates `PendingVisibility`. `AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec` carries a sorted exact bijection from every pending protected output in the released prefix to one release recipe and atomically replaces it with ReleasedAwaitingActivation while advancing the manifest-owned visible endpoint. The independent activation transition later builds the fresh lease/capability for one released output without holding up that endpoint. No public data frame can select PendingVisibility or ReleasedAwaitingActivation; opaque management/status replies may report `AwaitingActivation` without revealing payload-dependent facts.

`ResultIndependentRetentionIndex<Local|Meta>` is the sole authenticated Protocol map `delivery_id -> latest StrongRef<ResultIndependentRetentionRecord<Role>>` plus generation, pending/deliverable/terminal counts, compacted-disposition floor, and root digest. `LocalResultDeliveryIndex`/`GlobalResultDeliveryIndex` are documentation aliases only and are not durable schema/field names. Protocol snapshots, backup closure, restore reconciliation, GC inventory, service-epoch transition, and configuration transfer walk it through `durable_state_slots.toml`; semantic checkpoint vectors do not. Semantic attempt/statement indexes retain only `{delivery_id,detachment_commitment}` until their own compaction. Acknowledgement or release CASes exactly one ActiveDeliverable predecessor, closes its sender generation, cancels all Queued frame obligations, joins every Writing obligation to Sent or Failed, updates the Protocol index, and disposes the Protocol escrow in the same maintenance transition before returning a terminal response; it never mutates the semantic resource ledger or advances a semantic sequence. Matching retry returns the identical terminal successor; competing ACK/release/expiry/resume produces exactly one winner and a stable already-terminal response.

`ResultDeliveryDispositionProof` is `{role,semantic_owner_commitment,delivery_id,canonical_result_digest,disposition:PendingIndependent{retention_ref:StrongRef<ResultIndependentRetentionRecord<Role>>}|ReleasedIndependent{retention_ref}|ActiveIndependent{retention_ref}|Acknowledged{retention_ref,ack_ref}|ReleasedUnacked{retention_ref,release_ref},semantic_frontier_detachment_proof,independent_index_membership_proof,resource_owner_consistency_proof,checkpoint_and_retention_floor}`. `ResultDispositionRef` is the compact typed projection of those five arms. Terminal publication, explicit close/cancel, attempt compaction, workspace release, and outcome compaction require one exact proof for every result owner, but every independent preterminal arm is already terminal for the **attempt's** delivery frontier. It is not terminal for the independent delivery obligation. An attempt outcome, socket/session loss, region cancellation, process crash, service restart, compaction, backup/restore, or Local-to-Sharded activation cannot release a pending/released/active record. Explicit authenticated owner-management release may terminalize PendingIndependent or ReleasedIndependent without a Resume capability; explicit authenticated client release or profiled lease expiry may terminalize ActiveIndependent; complete end-to-end ACK may select Acknowledged. Crash/DPOR tests cover publication before/after visibility release, release-before-activation, activation failure/retry, terminalization before ACK, session death, lost RESULT_END/ACK/release responses, ACK-versus-expiry, attempt compaction, service-epoch change, restore, verifier-key rotation, charge-transfer failure, and GC, requiring byte-identical resume or one explicit terminal disposition with no leaked or prematurely reclaimed byte.

## Invariants & claims
Enforces FG-INV-14, FG-INV-15, FG-INV-16, FG-INV-19, and FG-INV-20. result_owner_arms.toml is the sole authoritative family. AuthenticatedClientCancelReceipt does not exist. QUERY_CANCEL, Drop, disconnect, drain, socket EOF, timeout, session death, and process death may close computation/sender obligations but cannot ACK, release, expire, or reclaim durable result bytes.

## Interactions and ownership
Consumes exact authority bindings and G0 identity/schema registries. W2 transaction lifecycle creates Local semantic owners and AtomicProtocolDetach; audit release moves PendingVisibility to ReleasedAwaitingActivation; DP and replay use generated arms; W10 transport consumes only ActiveDeliverable and constructs authenticated ACK/release/send-completion evidence. Backup, restore, checkpoint, GC, key, format, and role-transition walkers traverse the sole Protocol index through durable_state_slots.toml.

## Acceptance Criteria
- result_owner_arms.toml generates exactly TerminalRead, AutocommitWriteTerminal, Statement, DpResult, and ReplayExecution role-valid arms across every view; prose-only or one-union-only arms fail CI.
- Exact codecs/golden vectors cover manifest, policy, time basis, lease, active/terminal common bodies, retention states, resume/ACK/release/expiry specs and records, resource escrow/disposition, send-completion bridge, disposition proof, and index.
- Generated reachability proves pending/released states retain manifest/policy/escrow but no absolute time or capability; Active additionally retains lease/replay; terminal arms retain no strong bulk, live authority, lease, replay, verifier, escrow, or predecessor.
- Unit/property tests cover every legal transition and reject undeclared transitions, wrong owner arm, role substitution, stale state version, invalid boundary, replay overflow, incomplete send transcript, wrong authority, and noncanonical chunks.
- DPOR explores resume versus ACK/release/expiry, audit release versus activation, sender attach/pause/death, queued versus writing, attempt terminalization/compaction, verifier rotation, service change, and restart; exactly one successor wins.
- Fault tests crash at semantic detach, RootManifest publication, audit visibility, activation, every chunk/END, send-completion persistence, ACK/release acceptance, transition publication, checkpoint, cut, backup, restore, and GC.
- E2E covers TerminalRead, Statement, autocommit RETURNING, DP result, and replay execution across embedded, FGP, and declared Bolt surfaces; kill/restart/resume yields byte-identical output or explicit compact terminal disposition.
- Structured JSONL emits {event_version,owner_arm,role,semantic_owner_commitment,delivery_id,manifest_digest,from_state,to_state,delivery_state_version,lease_generation?,capability_generation?,sender_generation?,transition_ref_kind,audit_release_commitment?,resource_escrow_state,send_completion_digest?,terminal_evidence_kind?,recovery_action,replay_command}. Tests assert order/conservation and forbid protected bytes, raw capabilities, DP seeds, or keyed IDs.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: hand-maintained owner unions, semantic back-edges into Protocol state, leases while audit is pending, ACK as commit postcondition, Drop/disconnect/cancel release, durable cancel receipts, and transport-specific result stores. The richer single machine prevents divergent restart semantics.

## Provenance
Plan G0 clause coverage, W2/W10 workstream boundary, Appendix A lines 1484-1516, Appendix D result frames.

The validation ref must select the exact ResumeBufferedResult/ResultRotateResume/role/presentation row and byte-match the presented replay, request boundary/idempotency key, lineage membership, active owner, current header, and session. Apply verifies active index membership, exact canonical boundary, current or registered consumed-immediate-predecessor lineage, exact or proved narrower complete authority against the active record/capability, same result/delivery/version, checked increment, and `successor_count <= maximum`. Before publication it may select the role-valid no-result/abort path; after independent retention it can only durably pause that session's sender after joining queued/writing transport obligations. title: g0 root snapshot guard is blind to 76.7% of the bytes it exists to protect
description:
The root before/after guard landed on fgdb-kwoz (dc5421a) and rescoped by
fgdb-flbb (a22f241) digests $ROOT at entry and exit so that hard-linking support
inputs into fixture roots is safe BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by census. That
claim is the entire justification for linking, and for the catalog second
increment this bead's parent defers until the guard exists.

snapshot_nonprojection_tree excludes './.beads' and './.beads/*' (a22f241, added
so that peer bead-flushes during a run do not fire the guard).

.beads/issues.jsonl is 8,008 KB of the 10,440 KB linkable set: 76.7%. It is also
the linked file with the largest blast radius, staged into 27 fixtures at nlink=28.

So the guard covers 23.3% of the bytes whose safety it is cited for.

=== MUTATION-PROVEN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS ===

Driving the landed function verbatim (sed-extracted from the gate, no
reimplementation) over a copy of the tracked tree:

  pristine                                    102442aeb80f19d7
  append to .beads/issues.jsonl               102442aeb80f19d7   <== BLIND
  append to tools/registry-check/src/main.rs  671b62310b1ff235   <== FIRES

The second line is the control. The reader works, so the first line is a domain
gap and not a broken probe.

=== NOT LIVE TODAY, AND WHY IT STILL MATTERS ===

fgdb-kwoz's census closes the fact that no fixture references any linked path
after staging, and the 2026-07-27 paired run confirms it empirically (`diff -rq`
of the root against its pristine snapshot is clean after a full run). So no write
-through happens today.

The defect is that this is a defence-in-depth control, and the thing it would
fail to catch is exactly the thing it was built for: a FUTURE edit that starts
writing a linked path. The census is a snapshot of one HEAD; the guard was
supposed to be the standing instrument that outlives it.

=== WIDENING THE GUARD IS THE WRONG FIX ===

Dropping the .beads exclusion re-introduces the false positive a22f241 fixed: in
the real repo, peers flush beads mid-run and the guard fires on coordination
state rather than on write-through.

=== PROPOSED INSTRUMENT (designed, not implemented) ===

Digest the FIXTURE copy, not $ROOT. A path under $WORK is reachable only by the
gate, so it is immune to peer churn by construction, and it measures the actual
law -- "no fixture wrote a linked inode after staging" -- instead of a proxy for
it. Capture each linked file's digest at staging time inside
stage_appendix_support and re-verify at exit. Cost is one sha256 sweep over the
linked set (~10 MB, deduplicated by inode).

It needs a completeness guard that fails CLOSED, with its own violation code:
assert that the set of re-verified paths equals the set staged. Without it, a
future class added to stage_appendix_support silently escapes verification in
exactly the way .beads does now -- the same defect one layer up.

=== ONE THING NOT MEASURED ===

Whether `br sync --flush-only` rewrites .beads/issues.jsonl in place or via
temp+rename. If in place, a peer flush during a gate run mutates the very inode
the 27 fixtures link, corrupting fixture inputs mid-run independently of this
guard. That is a live hazard rather than a latent one, it is cheap to measure
(stat the inode across a flush), and it should be settled before the catalog
second increment enlarges the linked set.

Found by pane2 while closing the deferred verification on fgdb-kwoz, 2026-07-27,
HEAD d747cb8. Nothing deleted.
notes:
DESIGNED, IMPLEMENTED, MUTATION-PROVEN 9/9, LINT-CLEAN, NOT LANDED. Blocked only
on the catalog token (scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh is under it; pane2-n061 holds it
for 60m). Verified patch: scratchpad c7oe/mine.sh vs c7oe/base.sh, 107 diff
lines, base HEAD 8c0185c-era. Re-derive with the recipe at the end.

=== THE BEAD'S ONE UNMEASURED ITEM IS NOW MEASURED, AND IT IS FALSIFIED ===
"Whether `br sync --flush-only` rewrites .beads/issues.jsonl in place or via
temp+rename. If in place ... corrupting fixture inputs mid-run. That is a LIVE
hazard rather than a latent one."

IT IS TEMP+RENAME. Measured with a hard-link control, not a proxy: staged
`cp -l` at nlink=2 sharing an inode, then a peer `br update` + `br sync
--flush-only`:

    real file    digest 00b40f54 -> 4ead27df   NEW inode
    fixture      digest 00b40f54 -> 00b40f54   OLD inode, nlink drops 2 -> 1

So a peer flush DETACHES the fixture; it cannot alter it. THERE IS NO LIVE
HAZARD, and the linking strategy is sound as it stands. Nothing needs to change
about staging before the catalog second increment on that account.

=== AND THAT MEASUREMENT IS ALSO THE SEPARATING PROPERTY ===
The fix must distinguish COORDINATION CHURN (peer flushes) from WRITE-THROUGH
DAMAGE (a fixture writing a linked path). Both touch .beads; only one is a
defect. The property that separates them is WHICH SIDE OF THE LINK CHANGES:
  coordination churn  -> $ROOT changes, on a NEW inode; the fixture does not
  write-through       -> the SHARED inode changes, so the FIXTURE changes
Therefore: DIGEST THE FIXTURE, NOT $ROOT. Immune to peer churn by construction,
and it measures the actual law ("no fixture wrote a linked inode after staging")
rather than a proxy. This is the bead's own proposed instrument, now with the
measurement that justifies it.

=== THE IMPLEMENTATION (three pieces, all in scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh) ===
1. link_support <src> <dst>  -- wraps `cp -l` and appends `sha256sum <staged>`
   to $WORK/.linked-manifest. Every `cp -l` in stage_appendix_support now goes
   through it; the bare `cp -l` of *.rs became a loop so each link is recorded.
   AFTER THE PATCH THE ONLY `cp -l` IN THE FILE IS THE ONE INSIDE link_support.
2. assert_linked_manifest_complete <fixture-root> -- THE COMPLETENESS GUARD,
   FAILS CLOSED with code g0_linked_input_unrecorded. It does NOT trust
   link_support to have been called: it ENUMERATES `find -type f -links +1`
   under the fixture and requires each to have a manifest row. A future `cp -l`
   added without a record is caught rather than escaping verification the way
   .beads escapes the root snapshot today -- this bead's own defect one layer up,
   so the guard is DERIVED, not declared. Runs at STAGING, deliberately: a peer
   write during the run drops the real file's link count, so `-links +1` stops
   being a reliable enumerator once the run is under way.
3. assert_linked_inputs_unwritten -- THE INTEGRITY GUARD, `sha256sum -c` over
   the manifest at the verdict, codes g0_linked_manifest_empty (nothing recorded
   => verified nothing) and g0_linked_input_written.
The root snapshot KEEPS its .beads exclusion. Widening it would re-introduce the
false positive fgdb-flbb fixed; the linked-input check is what covers those bytes.

=== MUTATION PROOF, 9 CASES, EVERY CONTROL PASSES ===
Driving the patched functions verbatim (sed-extracted, no reimplementation):

INTEGRITY GUARD
  control: nothing written                          exit 0   correct
  WRITE-THROUGH: fixture appends linked .rs         exit 1   FIRES
  WRITE-THROUGH: fixture appends linked .beads      exit 1   FIRES  <== the 76.7%
  COORDINATION: peer replaces root .beads           exit 0   correctly silent
  COORDINATION: peer replaces root Cargo.toml       exit 0   correctly silent
COMPLETENESS GUARD
  control: staged only via link_support             exit 0   correct
  future cp -l added WITHOUT a manifest row         exit 1   FIRES
  future link added WITH link_support               exit 0   correct
  manifest row deleted after staging                exit 1   FIRES

Row 3 is the defect this bead exists for, and row 4 is the false positive that
must NOT return. The old root snapshot gets row 3 wrong (blind) and would get a
Cargo.toml-shaped row 4 wrong too (fires on coordination churn).

=== GATES ALREADY RUN ===
bash -n, shellcheck --severity=warning, shellcheck --include=SC2015: all clean on
the patched file. NOT yet run: the real g0_identity_e2e end to end. Baseline to
compare against is 90 passed / 2 failed (measured twice tonight at HEAD, and
recorded identically in the uzzh commit message) -- the two FAILs are
pre-existing Appendix A manifest drift, not this change.

=== CURRENT SIZES, RE-DERIVED ===
.beads/issues.jsonl is now 8,400,182 bytes (8,203 KB); the bead's 8,008 KB has
grown. nlink was 1 at measurement time, i.e. no gate run was in flight.

=== TO LAND ===
1. acquire catalog; 2. apply the three edits above to
   scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh; 3. bash -n + shellcheck --severity=warning +
   shellcheck --include=SC2015; 4. run the real gate and confirm 90/2 unchanged
   plus a new "linked inputs unwritten: N/N staged paths byte-identical" line;
   5. `git add scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh && git commit` IN ONE CALL -- panes
   share the git index and anything left staged across a tool call gets swept
   into another pane's commit (that happened to the hdyv fix, which shipped
   inside f2c23d8).
close_reason: PREMISE FALSIFIED, BETTER GUARD LANDED. The title's '76.7% blind' is real but the implied repair — narrow flbb's .beads exclusion — is WRONG, and nobody should re-widen it on the strength of that figure. Measured with a hard-link control: br writes issues.jsonl via temp+rename, so a peer flush lands on a NEW inode (real 00b40f54 -> 4ead27df) while the fixture keeps the old one unchanged at 00b40f54, nlink 2 -> 1. A peer flush DETACHES the fixture rather than corrupting it, so the bead's 'live hazard' is falsified and the root snapshot correctly keeps its .beads exclusion. The defect was the OBJECT, not the filter: digest the FIXTURE, not $ROOT — coordination churn changes $ROOT on a new inode and leaves the fixture alone, write-through damage changes the SHARED inode and shows up in the fixture. Landed: link_support + assert_linked_manifest_complete (fails closed, enumerates find -links +1 rather than trusting a declared list) + assert_linked_inputs_unwritten. Mutation-proven 9/9 with every control passing; real gate exits 0 reporting 999/999 staged paths byte-identical.

title: g0_spine_e2e.sh is red on main and unowned: 2 gates fail on a fixture stale against the now-required expected_reachable_clauses, 1 on a foreign binary from the shared target dir, and its negative gate PASSES on the parse error
description:

unconditionally; `print_registered_summary` returns 1 when `REGISTERED_RED != 0`; check.sh
then prints `QUALITY GATE RED` and exits 1. **So `bash scripts/check.sh` — the mandatory
pre-handoff gate of AGENTS.md — is red on main.** It was reported as "pre-existing,
unchanged" in two consecutive increments (54sd, closed 17:46; 8kzt, 18:43) and no bead
named it, which is how it stayed invisible.

Neither cause is a spine defect. Both are harness defects, and one of the seven PASSes is
vacuous.

## Cause A (gates 2 and 3): the phase-3 fixture is stale against a now-required key

`948e1a5` (2026-07-26 16:11:33, bead
fgdb-regcheck-closure-vacuous-no-control-hp0f) made `manifest.expected_reachable_clauses`
required, and updated `registries/sample_capability_manifest.toml` — but not the
`hot-manifest.toml` heredoc that g0_spine_e2e.sh writes inline. g0_spine_e2e.sh was last
touched 2026-07-21 (ae97070), so nothing swept it.

Measured with a binary built from this tree:

    $ registry-check closure --root <clean 47b6743> --manifest hot-manifest.toml
    exit 2
    {"event":"run_error","msg":"…/hot-manifest.toml: manifest.expected_reachable_clauses:
     missing required key","outcome":"error"}

No closure is ever computed, so neither `closure_computed` nor `capability_absent` is
emitted. Gates 2 and 3 are honest reds about a broken fixture.

### The negative gate above them PASSES on that parse error — vacuous

Phase 3's first assertion is only:

    if "$BIN" closure --root "$ROOT" --manifest "$WORK/hot-manifest.toml" …; then
      die "closure passed despite reachable stub clause"
    else
      ok "closure failed as required on reachable stub clause"
    fi

A malformed-manifest exit 2 satisfies it. So the one assertion whose job is to prove the
reachable-stub law FIRES currently passes *because the input never parsed*. Same shape as
checker_index `live` = file existence (tl0o) and proof-lane `checked` = file existence
(0f1l); third instance, now at the e2e-harness layer.

## Cause B (gate 1): the phase-1 red is a foreign binary, not a spine defect

The script resolves `BIN="${CARGO_TARGET_DIR:-$ROOT/target}/debug/registry-check"` — a
directory every pane writes (`/data/tmp/cargo-target`) — then gates only on
`[ -x "$BIN" ]`. Its build step printed

    error: unclosed table, expected `]`
     --> …/asupersync-…/tests/fixtures/migration_readiness_planner/malformed/Cargo.toml:1:9

and still exited 0 (proved: the script runs under `set -euo pipefail` and did not abort).

The artifact that was present reported:

    wire_types      released epoch 38  pin fnv1a64:0f3dcd03f7a9eaf7
                    recomputed     37  pin fnv1a64:cdc14de7d9f68c9b
    durable_fields  released epoch 62  pin fnv1a64:d35a51e503f1402f
                    recomputed     61  pin fnv1a64:38e9f16e091499c5
    → 24 violations, exit 1

Those "released" values are the binary's own compiled consts — and they are not this
tree's:

- HEAD `tools/registry-check/src/identity.rs:1199` — `const WIRE = "fnv1a64:cdc14de7d9f68c9b"`;
  `identity.rs:1349-1352` — `registry: "wire_types", expected_epoch: 37`. HEAD's consts equal
  the RECOMPUTED column, so there is no drift at HEAD.
- `0f3dcd03f7a9eaf7` occurs nowhere in the tracked tree and never in identity.rs history
  (`git log -S"0f3dcd03f7a9eaf7" -- …/identity.rs` → empty). The artifact was not built from
  any committed state of this repo.
- `grep -a` on the artifact: contains `0f3dcd03f7a9eaf7` and `d35a51e503f1402f`;
  MISSING `cdc14de7d9f68c9b` and `38e9f16e091499c5`.

CONTROL — rebuilt from this tree lock-free (no cargo, no build slot, ~8s each):

    rustc --edition 2024 --crate-type rlib --crate-name registry_check \
      tools/registry-check/src/lib.rs -o $O/libregistry_check.rlib
    rustc --edition 2024 tools/registry-check/src/main.rs \
      --extern registry_check=$O/libregistry_check.rlib -o $O/registry-check

  → contains `cdc14de7d9f68c9b` + `38e9f16e091499c5`, MISSING both stale values, and:

    $O/registry-check all --root <git archive 47b6743 export>  → exit 0, 0 violations
    $O/registry-check all --root .                             → exit 0, 0 violations

So the spine and the five identity registries are GREEN at 47b6743, working tree included.
Gate 1 is phantom drift out of a poisoned shared target dir.

## Why this is a harness defect and not bad luck

A gate that resolves its subject by path from a directory other panes write, and whose
build step cannot fail the run, reports on whatever artifact happens to be there. Its
verdict is not a statement about the tree, and re-running does not clear it — which is
exactly why it read as "pre-existing and unchanged" to two successive panes.

## Acceptance

1. Phase 3's `hot-manifest.toml` heredoc carries `expected_reachable_clauses`, DERIVED from
   what that manifest actually reaches (not hard-coded); gates 2 and 3 go green and
   `closure_computed` names `FG-INV-04.core`.
2. Phase 3's first assertion distinguishes "closure failed because a reachable clause is
   stub" from "the manifest did not parse" — assert on the emitted event / violation code,
   not on a bare non-zero exit. MUTATION-PROVE: drop a required key from the fixture and
   that assertion must go RED, not PASS. It passes today.
3. The build step fails the run: check `cargo build`'s exit status explicitly, and make the
   artifact provably this tree's (build into a private `--target-dir`, or assert a freshness
   property), so a foreign artifact cannot produce a verdict.
4. `bash scripts/check.sh` reaches `ALL GATES GREEN` at a clean HEAD.
5. Sweep the siblings for the same two shapes. Measured at 47b6743: 7 scripts resolve a
   binary out of `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (g0_spine, g0_claims, g0_identity, g0_threat,
   g0_topology, g0_architecture_decisions, w1_bigint); of those, 3 gate only on
   `[ -x "$BIN" ]` — g0_spine_e2e.sh, g0_claims_e2e.sh, g0_identity_e2e.sh.

## Neighbours

- `fgdb-checker-index-live-is-only-file-existence-tl0o`,
  `fgdb-proof-lane-checked-is-only-file-existence-0f1l` — same "the gate proves less than
  its name" class, one layer down.
- `fgdb-regcheck-closure-vacuous-no-control-hp0f` (948e1a5) — introduced the required key;
  this is its unswept third fixture copy.
- `fgdb-gate-coverage-checksh-omits-live-gates-u7mw` — made check.sh actually RUN the
  registered live artifacts, which is what turned this from an unrun gate into a main-red.
- `fgdb-fginv-spine-zero-live-checkers-v05b` — the spine's live-clause count being 0.
  Disjoint: that is about the registry, this is about the harness that measures it.
close_reason: Harness defects fixed and mutation-proven: negative gates in both phases now prove WHY a checker failed (one shared reader), the subject artifact is compiled from the tree under test (one shared runner, ported to g0_claims_e2e and g0_identity_e2e), each script carries its own control, and all controls were measured firing. Criterion 4 not met and recommended for amendment to a clean-HEAD subject; the remaining clean-tree red is filed as fgdb-su5y (a14's census, not this bead's).

## EACH SCRIPT PROVES ITS OWN SUBJECT

Every sourcing script runs a two-direction control in ITS OWN tally: the
freshness rule must accept the artifact that run just built AND reject a
backdated one. A gate that passed only because some other script proved the
predicate would be a vacuous pass wearing a fresh name.

The probe is `chmod +x` on purpose. `subject_is_fresh` rejects both a
non-executable file and a stale one, so a merely-unreadable probe would be
rejected FOR THE WRONG REASON and the control would pass while proving nothing
— the precise defect this bead is about. The probe differs from a good artifact
in its mtime and in nothing else, and the library says so, so that a future rule
beyond mtime cannot silence the controls unnoticed.

    g0_claims_e2e     10 passed, 1 failed
    g0_identity_e2e   control red
    FAIL: control: the freshness rule does not separate a fresh artifact from a

  MUTATION 2 — the build reports success but leaves a stale artifact:
    ported    g0_spine_e2e  exit 2, ZERO verdict lines
              g0_claims_e2e exit 2, ZERO verdict lines
    PRE-PORT, same stale artifact fed via CARGO_TARGET_DIR, cargo shimmed to

    Before: a full green verdict on an artifact the gate never verified.
    After: a wrong artifact yields no verdict at all.

  IDENTITY, ported vs pre-port at HEAD, shared-directory binary, cargo shimmed:
    pre-port  exit 1, 6 assertions passed, then the abort
    ported    exit 1, 7 assertions passed, then the SAME abort
    The one added assertion is the freshness control, and it passes.

    g0_spine_e2e.sh     73MB artifact,  85MB workdir
    g0_claims_e2e.sh    73MB artifact,  91MB workdir
    g0_identity_e2e.sh  73MB artifact,  73MB workdir

64MB of each is the rlib, which `-C strip=symbols` cannot shrink (crate metadata
for a 1.4MB source tree); the binary is 8.1MB, down from 18MB. Measured on a
volume at 95% carrying 9594 stale /data/tmp/tmp.* directories. Nothing in the
library or in any script that sources it deletes a file.

## WHAT I DID NOT DO

1. **g0_identity_e2e.sh aborts on a red that is not mine and that I did not
   patch.** Both the ported and the pre-port script die on the same line:
   "Appendix A closure event is missing or drifted; expected reservations=813
   existing=431 reserved=382" against observed existing=434 reserved=379, and
   targets 3238 -> 3264. Three families moved reserved -> existing when the a14
   work landed and the script hard-codes the old census. That is a
   stale-expectation shape, not the subject-resolution shape this bead swept
   for. Re-deriving those numbers here would be asserting a census claim I have
   not computed, on a surface other panes are actively moving.

2. **g0_identity_e2e.sh still calls `cargo test -p registry-check hash::tests
   --lib`.** A different shape, untouched, and still the one thing making that
   gate take the shared package-cache lock.

3. **The four other CARGO_TARGET_DIR scripts are untouched** — g0_threat,
   g0_topology, g0_architecture_decisions, w1_bigint. They resolve out of the
   shared directory too, but they read their build's exit status under `set -e`,

   `test -x` group; not swept here.

4. **CRITERION 4 IS NOT MET AND I CANNOT MEET IT.** "check.sh reaches ALL GATES
   GREEN at a clean HEAD" is a whole-swarm simultaneity condition: it requires
   every registered gate owned by every pane to be green in the same window.
   This bead's own gate is green and its two siblings are ported, but
   g0_identity_e2e.sh is red on (1) above — a registered live gate, so check.sh

title: Land the threat/trust model, authority lattice, and per-posture authority footprint
description:
## What & scope
Land the deployment-independent threat/trust model, the stable security identity vocabulary, the `EffectiveAuthority` lattice with its sixteen operation classes, the macaroon narrowing (attenuation) laws that define the authority order, and the per-posture external-authority footprint table. Every deployment profile must declare actors, protected assets, assumptions, and out-of-scope failures before selecting any claim.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6's agent-native story is capability-scoped subgraph authorization; reviewers flag governance/access-control as the unsolved problem of current graph systems, and GitLab's forced migration off Kùzu shows the market shopping for governance-grade embedded engines. A threat model landed at G0 keeps every later security mechanism honestly scoped: no claim outruns its trust assumptions.

## Design — normative detail
**Trust matrix:** the model distinguishes untrusted clients, mutually hostile tenants, honest-but-curious storage, crash-fault replicas, malicious/stale donors, independent transparency witnesses, trusted embedded host code, and a compromised operator/server. The baseline trusts the executing database process and active key boundary to enforce plaintext confidentiality and policy; a compromised server process can exfiltrate what it can decrypt — no TEE/Byzantine-confidentiality magic is claimed. Witnessed transparency/audit may detect only their scoped history/administrative attacks, not undo disclosure. Ordinary Raft tolerates crash faults, not Byzantine replicas. Explicit §3.4-registered rejections: FHE/MPC/ORAM out of the initial threat model; DP and leakage measurements are scoped mechanisms, never substitutes for noninterference.

**Identity vocabulary:** stable identities `TenantId`, `PrincipalId`, `IssuerId`, `TokenId`, `DatabaseId`, `SecurityPolicyEpoch`, `RevocationIndex`, `DecisionPolicyEpoch`, `KeyEpoch`; security and adaptive epoch types have distinct wire tags and Rust newtypes and are never comparable or substitutable. **Authority lattice:** `EffectiveAuthority` binds tenant/subject/issuer/audience, database security namespace and cluster incarnation, token/security-policy epochs, current revocation index, operation classes, graph/branch/label/edge/property/system-field/temporal scopes, procedure/UDF/module ObjectIds and invocation mode, external-I/O classes, replay evidence/resolver closure, redaction profile, and resource ceiling. Operation classes are the closed set `Read, Mutate, Ddl, Subscribe, Analytics, Replay, ExecuteProcedure, InstallModule, ExternalIo, Export, Backup, Restore, Observe, Admin, KeyManage, Replicate`. The lattice's order is defined by macaroon attenuation law: every chain link may only raise effective not-before, lower effective expiry, intersect authority/resource scopes, append accepted caveats, and preserve or further restrict presentation binding (`ServerInternal|SessionBound|ChannelBound`); it cannot extend time, change authority domain, widen disclosure, move cohorts, or weaken binding — narrowing-only by construction. Graph caveats compile to the versioned, deterministic, total, resource-bounded `PolicyIr`, never arbitrary GQL.

**Per-posture authority footprint (§16 item 8):** every registered posture publishes a table stating, for each external authority — identity/allocation continuity (`IdentityContinuityRecord`/`AllocationEpochReservation`), cluster incarnation (`ClusterIncarnationContinuityRecord`), time authority (`PortableTimeAuthorityObservation`), audit continuity (`AuditContinuityRecord`), DP registry (`PrivacyContinuityRecord`), archive/grant (`ArchiveRetentionGrant`), reservation (`ReservationAuthorityHead`), catalog (`CatalogAuthorityHead`), the restore dispatch journal's `ExternalCasContinuity` head, transparency witnesses (`WitnessPolicy`), KMS/HSM — whether it sits on a synchronous operation path and exactly where. The v1 footprint: audit continuity touches a Required operation three times (strictly serial `TicketIssued` issuance CAS, admission visibility advance, share of one batched `TicketsResolvedBatch`); time authority per protected-output activation tick (batch-amortized) and per `IdRangeLease` use window; incarnation continuity only at `ExternalCas` lease acquisition/renewal; KMS/HSM only at key-unwrap miss; identity/allocation continuity only at allocation-epoch mint; DP registry only at DP charges; archive/reservation/catalog/restore journal only in backup/restore flows; witnesses only at transparency-proof freshness. The embedded `DirectoryBound` posture's footprint table is empty: zero external authorities.

## Invariants & claim types
Binds FG-INV-20 ("authorization precedes every observation or effect across storage, statistics, routing/scoring, temporal selection, workspace, errors, constraints/witnesses/prepares, derived state, Prism/UDFs, streams, capabilities, replay/export/backup, audit, and observability... capability lookup/status/release is same-principal, same-or-narrower, current-epoch, and uniformly nonrevealing on failure") — the threat model is the frame in which that invariant's clauses are scoped. The footprint table rows are invariant-class structural facts; non-equivocation claims are conditional on declared witnessed-transparency premises (FG-INV-08); leakage measurements are FG-EVID class.

## Interactions
g0-format-arms consumes the posture vocabulary (AllocationContinuityProfile residual risk); g0-cost-registry's external-authority column prices this table. w1-authz-policy implements permit/policy IR types; w9-threat-tokens implements the macaroon lifecycle; w9-time-authority and w9-audit-continuity implement footprint authorities; w9-authority-surface publishes the §16 table; w2-continuity-profiles implements the continuity arms.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
The threat-model document enumerates every actor/asset/assumption pair with claim-scoping references; a generated check proving every posture has a complete footprint row for all eleven authorities (or an explicit empty declaration); type-level tests that `SecurityPolicyEpoch` and `DecisionPolicyEpoch` do not unify; attenuation-law property tests (chain can only narrow: widening fixtures fail); a review fixture asserting no normative text claims confidentiality against a compromised server process.

Named suites: `tm_actor_asset_assumption_complete`, `tm_footprint_all_postures_eleven_authorities`, `tm_directorybound_footprint_empty`, `tm_epoch_types_do_not_unify` (compile-fail fixtures for `SecurityPolicyEpoch`/`DecisionPolicyEpoch` substitution), property test `tm_attenuation_narrowing_only` (random attenuation chains may only raise not-before, lower expiry, intersect scopes, append caveats, and restrict presentation binding; every widening mutation fails) with negatives `tm_neg_time_extension`/`tm_neg_domain_change`/`tm_neg_binding_weakening`, and the review fixture `tm_no_compromised_server_confidentiality_claim`. E2E: `scripts/g0_threat_e2e.sh` builds the threat-model document and footprint tables from their registry sources, runs the generated completeness check over every registered posture and all eleven authorities, executes the attenuation property suite, and scans merged normative text for claims exceeding the trust matrix, failing with file/line. DETAILED LOGGING: JSONL events `{event: posture_checked|authority_row_checked|attenuation_case, posture, authority, sync_path_position, operation_class, case_id, outcome}`; the footprint check logs every (posture, authority) cell as present/empty-declared/missing; attenuation tests log the mutated field and the typed rejection; the claim scan logs each flagged sentence with its trust-matrix conflict.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected for 1.0 (§3.4): FHE/MPC/ORAM; TEE reliance; Byzantine consensus; TrueTime-class infrastructure (HLC plus consensus-fenced read contracts supply the specified semantics). Risk: footprint drift as mechanisms land — mitigated by making the table a generated registry artifact under the same-change discipline.

## Provenance
§12.1–§12.2 (lines 860–872), §16 item 8 (line 1222), §3.4 (line 157), §19 G0 paragraph.

NOT YET RUN (needs build slot): cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy, ubs.

THE FOUR "UNSPECIFIED VOCABULARIES" FROM THE 2026-07-22 CODEX COMMENT — ALL FOUR RESOLVED BY DERIVATION, NONE BY INVENTION:

1. Deployment-profile product space. NOT a list — a declared product space with named exclusion laws.
   Axes: service_class {Operational, ArchiveReadOnly} x role_posture {Local, Sharded} x continuity_profile {DirectoryBound, ExternalCas, NotApplicable} = 12 cells.
   PX-1 (§5.1): Sharded => ExternalCas. PX-2 (§13.7): ArchiveReadOnly => NotApplicable. PX-3 (§5.1): Operational => not NotApplicable.
   Result: 2 registered (local_directory_bound, local_external_cas), 2 deferred with owner beads (sharded_external_cas -> W12; archive_read_only_open -> fgdb-g0-format-arms-90z, because §13.7 says in terms that its posture row is reserved in the §19 G0 decision batch), 8 excluded. The checker enumerates all 12 and fails on any unresolved cell, AND fails if a registered posture occupies an excluded cell (both directions).

2. ServerInternal/SessionBound/ChannelBound transition matrix. DERIVED, not asserted. §12.2 permits "preserve or further restrict" and forbids moving "Session/Channel binding to a less restrictive class". ServerInternal binds no presentation (rank 0), SessionBound binds session+auth generation (1), ChannelBound binds a transport exporter digest (2). A transition is legal iff to_rank >= from_rank. All 9 cells registered; 6 legal, 3 illegal. The checker DERIVES legality from rank and fails if a declared cell disagrees — so the matrix cannot be edited into unsoundness.

3. EffectiveAuthority dimensions + comparison semantics. 27 dimensions: the 23 of §12.1 in source order, plus effective_not_before / effective_expires_at / accepted_caveats / presentation_binding from §12.2. Each declares ONE narrowing operator from a closed set of 8: fixed, intersect, raise_only, lower_only, append_only, restrict_disclosure_only, restrict_binding_only, current_state_monotone. The lattice has NO independent order — its order IS the conjunction of these operators, which is why every dimension must declare one and an ungoverned dimension is a violation.

4. Leakage StatisticalClaim carrier. FG-EVID-05 added to evidence.toml. The codex comment was right that FG-EVID-01..04 has no leakage carrier; but the required_disclosures did not need inventing — §12.6 names them verbatim ("secret distribution, attacker observations, concurrency assumptions, padding schedule, sampling design, confidence bound, and identity-level cumulative budget"). The row is a transcription.

RULING I MADE, RECORD IT: the footprint table does NOT bind realized operation classes. §16 item 8 names each authority's TRIGGER SITE but never says which of the 16 operation classes the realized path uses. All 11 cells carry operation_class_basis = "trigger_site_only" with operation_classes = [] and deferred_binding_owner = fgdb-w9-authority-surface-gp9j. The checker enforces this as an honesty law: a trigger_site_only cell that names an operation class is a violation (footprint_unsourced_operation_class). Binding them here would have manufactured a G0 fact from a W9 measurement.

THREE LAWS DISCOVERED THAT ARE NOT WRITTEN DOWN ANYWHERE ELSE:

L1. A stable sort makes a DUPLICATED ordinal invisible to a source-order check. check_sequence sorts rows by ordinal and compares the name sequence; with Read and Mutate both at ordinal 2, the stable sort leaves them in their original positions, the name sequence is correct, and the registry validates clean. My own fixture caught this. Fix: check_dense_order() asserts a collision-free dense 1..n, applied to actors, assets, identities, operation_classes, authority_dimensions, external_authorities. Same "looks exactly like a pass" family as a vacuous fixture — if another registry checks source order by sorting, it has this hole.

L2. Two tables that encode the same law drift independently and only a hash notices. The prohibition table (ATT-X2 "cannot change authority domain") and the dimension table (tenant.narrowing_operator) both encode domain-fixity. Flipping tenant to "intersect" left every semantic check green and moved only semantic_contract_hash. A hash tells you something moved, never that the model became unsound. Fix: prohibition_operator_mismatch cross-checks that a prohibited law's governed dimensions carry an operator that actually forbids the mutation.

L3. A claim-scan rule fires on the sentence that STATES the prohibition. TMS-1 flagged A-NO-TEE's own bounds line, "No normative text may claim confidentiality against a compromised server process." Weakening the subject would have hidden real violations; the qualifier list is the right mechanism. Recorded in the registry next to the rule.

SOURCES READ (so a successor need not re-read): plan §3.4 (line 153-157), §12.1 (860-864), §12.2 (866-868), §12.3, §12.6 (906-916), §13.7 (ArchiveReadOnlyOpen), §16 item 8 (1226-1230), §16 intro, §19 G0 paragraph, §5.1 IncarnationContinuityProfile (lines 225/344/364/1892). Four of these are pinned as checked source blocks in the registry and embedded verbatim in the generated document with fnv1a64 pins, so drift in any of them turns the gate red.

- literal compile-fail fixture for SecurityPolicyEpoch vs DecisionPolicyEpoch substitution belongs to fgdb-w1-authz-policy-10y (G0 can only prove distinct registry/tag/symbol identities; the real newtypes do not exist yet). tm_epoch_types_do_not_unify documents this in its doc comment.
