title: Pass Gate G1 'The Engine Lives': single-node engine exit criteria
description:
## What & scope
Integration Gate G1 — "The Engine Lives." The first convergence gate proper: certifies the single-node engine (W1 bedrock, W2 Chronicle durability core, W3 Strata, W4 transactions/Secure View, plus the *declared* W5 subset) live end to end, with every exit clause below demonstrably green. Nothing past G1 may build on unproven engine behavior. This bead is the gate checklist itself; each clause must be independently demonstrable, logged, and reproducible.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
§19's gate discipline exists because the crown-jewel risks (§20: graph-SSI soundness — "central correctness risk"; root/checkpoint recovery closure — "catastrophic") must be retired before W6-W8 fan out in parallel. B1 rests on the commit/recovery machinery certified here; B5's evidence discipline requires the strict canonical replay closure and formally validated witness families *now*; B2's claim that representation changes never change semantics is pinned here as "compaction/label changes preserve logical digests." Full strength before breadth is the market position: the Kùzu-shaped hole is filled by proofs, not features.

## Design — normative detail
Exit criteria, complete: (1) fresh-creation three-phase bootstrap and the embedded authorized path; (2) bounded resources; (3) the declared GQL/Cypher feature subset with its synchronous Unicode bundle and conformance matrix — **full language breadth is not claimed until its binder/operator rows exist**; (4) acyclic durable-object construction; (5) final-capsule/command/pre-minted-merge coherence; (6) stable D1 prepared-root ownership and quorum-one ordered-command crash recovery; (7) generated complete projected checkpoint-vector (`CheckpointStateVector`) plus mandatory genesis or paired-operational checkpoint-floor install plus logical-command/transaction-marker suffix recovery with **no historical-floor retention chain** — including inherited absent bytes under a dominating replacement Provisional cut and proof that it authorizes no new reclamation before separate activation; (8) exact Raft snapshot cut binding; (9) serializable witness families **formally and independently validated**; (10) accepted-filesystem conformance plus the lease-owner-death, fence-root-before-enable, torn-root, marker-tail, stale-writer, bootstrap, and recovery matrices all green; (11) constraint state authoritative; (12) compaction/label changes preserve logical digests; (13) strict canonical replay closure works; (14) every clause reachable by the compiled/negotiated G1 capability manifest is live — otherwise that capability is absent from the manifest.

G1 additionally requires **executable reference/oracle coverage** for: normalized valid-time slices; first-escape and finalization allocation under forced rebase; resource/constraint/escrow atomicity; complete security-root binding (`SecurityStateBinding` on every authority-bearing schema); generation-fenced transaction ownership and prepare handoff; and the Local audit visibility pipeline exercised with multiple unresolved candidates, out-of-order external completions, batch release, restart, and bounded backpressure. The command/state registries (`command_contracts.toml`, `state_payload_fields.toml`) must demonstrate that **every active Local transition owns an exact rooted result and recovery path**. Hard-failure list — any one fails the gate: a pre-rebase capsule, post-filter authorization, an ambient allocator counter, an implicit result release, or an optional audit fence.

## Invariants & claim types
Binding invariant text (Appendix F): FG-INV-05 — every committed SERIALIZABLE history has an acyclic logical dependency graph; for the Local default the checked graph additionally contains real-time precedence edges, or applies the registered dangerous-structure rule proved to reject every DSG-union-real-time cycle, so the default Local contract is **strict serializable**. FG-INV-06 — every witness conservatively represents all logically relevant positive, negative, gap, valid-time slice, early-stop, and path-cut observations, and refinement preserves their concretization and `may_affect` behavior. FG-INV-07 — before receipt/order, D1 owns one exact closure under stable prepared ownership; every pre-order input excludes its future command/result/root. FG-INV-08 — logical-command predecessor order and the transaction-marker subsequence are contiguous at their respective sequences; every retained checkpoint suffix begins with its exact install command. FG-INV-10 — the two-slot root protocol selects the highest structurally credible authenticated closure; one inode-bound publication sequencer plus external incarnation continuity fences every stale writer. FG-INV-11 — any value is durably reserved no later than its first escape; confined values are reserved by the finalization plan before capsule/effect construction; rebase preserves prior bindings and may append only. FG-INV-04 — applied state may advance ahead of public state only through the rooted gap-free audit visibility pipeline. Claim class: G1 evidence is invariant-clause conformance with resolvable checker and negative-test entrypoints and `waiver=forbidden`; no slo/benchmark claim qualifies as G1 evidence (those are G4's).

## Interactions
Blocked by gate-genesis and epics epic-w1..epic-w4. Consumes the declared-subset W5 anchors (w5-parsers, w5-binder, w5-gla-algebra, w5-planner, w5-executor, w5-determinism, w5-answer-contracts, w5-replay); verif-oracles supplies the SCC/Elle/obligation-leak oracles used for witness and history validation; w9-audit-pipeline supplies the Local audit visibility pipeline scenario. Produces the foundation gate-g2 assumes.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
- All seven named crash matrices (lease-owner-death, fence-root-before-enable, torn-root, marker-tail, stale-writer, bootstrap, recovery) green under the lab with per-row seeds; logs record matrix row id, injected fault, recovered root generation, and pass/fail decision.
- Witness-family validation bundle per family: formal concretization/may-affect proof artifact, independent small-model histories, gap/negative/path mutation tests; negative test that SERIALIZABLE **rejects** an unverified family.
- Suffix-recovery run with dominating replacement Provisional cut plus reclaim ledger proving zero new reclamation before the separate activation command; exact Raft snapshot cut-binding check.
- Logical-digest differential across compaction and label mutation.
- Strict canonical replay-closure e2e reproducing byte-canonical output from the manifest.
- Audit-pipeline scenario: >1 unresolved candidates, out-of-order external completions, batch release, restart mid-batch, backpressure bound observed and logged.
- Registry CI proof mapping every active Local transition to an exact rooted result and recovery path.
- Five executable negative gates for the hard-failure items, each failing closed.
- Clause-to-evidence map: the gate report carries one row per exit clause (1)-(14) and per G1-additional coverage item, naming the demonstrating artifact (matrix, suite, oracle run, or registry CI check). The clauses not already named above map as follows: (1) the fresh-creation three-phase-bootstrap crash-matrix rows plus an embedded authorized-path walk through `fgdb-secure-view`; (2) a bounded-resources run — reservation ceilings enforced and obligation quiescence reached under the lab; (3) the declared GQL/Cypher subset conformance-matrix run with its synchronous Unicode bundle; (4) the acyclic durable-object construction check from the registry CI; (5) final-capsule/command/pre-minted-merge coherence fixtures; (6) stable-D1-prepared-root-ownership fixtures plus the quorum-one ordered-command rows of the crash matrices; (11) the constraint-authority fixtures (synchronous enforcement authoritative before commit; unavailable or corrupt constraint state fails closed for affected writes); (14) a capability-manifest liveness audit proving every reachable clause of the compiled/negotiated G1 manifest is live and every capability with a dead clause is absent from the manifest. The remaining G1-additional oracle-coverage items — normalized valid-time slices; first-escape/finalization allocation under forced rebase; resource/constraint/escrow atomicity; complete `SecurityStateBinding`; generation-fenced ownership and prepare handoff — each map to their executable reference/oracle runs. A clause or coverage item without a mapped artifact row does not count as passed.
- Detailed logging: every matrix/suite/oracle/audit run above logs {run_id, scenario or matrix-row id, seed, injected fault where applicable, per-clause verdict}; failures carry §15.1 structured replay fields; the gate report must be regenerable from these logs alone, and a criterion whose log chain is incomplete does not count as passed.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Graph-SSI unsoundness is retired inside this gate: unverified witness families are rejected rather than shipped; SNAPSHOT remains an explicit weaker contract, never containment for a false serializable claim (§20). Rejected: performance gating here; language-breadth claims beyond existing binder/operator rows; any waiver path (constitutionally forbidden).

## Provenance
§19 Gate G1 (plan lines 1334-1336); Appendix F rows cited; §20 risk rows.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Pass Gate G2 'One Version Universe': branches, Ripple, backup/restore exit criteria
description:
## What & scope
Integration Gate G2 — "One Version Universe." Certifies that B1's central promise is real: MVCC publication, retained history, branches, change subscriptions, views, indexes, projections, and backup/restore all ride one append-only commit mechanism with distinct retention/proof products. This bead is the gate checklist; every clause below must be demonstrably green.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1 is the bet "nobody else can make" — it needs the ECS-style durability substrate designed in from byte zero. B4 (Ripple incrementality) and B6 (branch-per-agent isolation, GraphRAG-grade governed retrieval) are certified here: agent-memory workloads demand git-grade branches with real key isolation (sibling non-decryption), subscriptions with no silent gaps, and capability-safe ANN — exactly what reviewers flag as unsolved (governance/access-control, freshness-of-derived-state). G2 is where those market claims acquire evidence.

## Design — normative detail
Exit criteria, complete: (1) verified generated-complete checkpoint-install + logical-command suffix recovery and per-graph retention over **mixed transaction/control commands**; (2) branch fork **double rotation**, exact envelope DAG/AAD and `StrongCiphertextRef` realization retention, snapshot/advancing handoff, re-encryption/movement under live grants, **sibling and post-fork-parent non-decryption**, and pre-minted merge-token/imported-range-idempotent explicit-base merges across history cuts; (3) conditional source templates plus self-contained retained Ripple batches; (4) publicly authenticated baseline results and atomic/coalesced delta provenance/output; (5) durable cursor-generation plus tagged baseline/delta lease, with baseline-ACK/delta-ACK/resume/lost-response/expiry recovery and **no delta-before-baseline and no silent gap**; (6) table/graph views with explicit read policies; (7) watermark/tail-correct indexes; (8) historical/capability-safe ANN roots with exact fallback; (9) authorized Prism projections; (10) exact Local backup: barrier/pin -> copy, then independent archive reopen -> closure certificate -> seal -> publication receipt/archive grant -> ordered pin release; (11) exact Local restore: `RestoreSourceLease` -> exhaustive leaves-first incarnation transform/re-encryption -> guarded RecoveryReconciling bridge -> identity/privacy/audit/cluster-incarnation reconciliation -> hidden activation and service preparation -> continuity-then-catalog CAS receipt -> Local service promotion -> independent target reopen -> completion/audit visibility advance -> lease release, with stale incarnation/service epochs and old capabilities **rejected**; (12) Sharded round-trip remains reserved for W12; (13) empirical/statistical gates reported **with assumptions**.

G2 also proves the **state-shaped independent result, DP-result, and replay-execution owner machines**: only Active arms retain bulk bytes; explicit authenticated release/expiry or complete ACK creates compact terminal evidence; disconnect/Drop/cancel can never do so. Bulk import's source-row/chunk/logical-effect **bijection** survives retry/crash and commits only through ordinary transactions. Derived shadow builds catch up to one exact frontier, validate, and become visible only through a transactional SchemaOp. Exact format rewrites are semantic no-ops, while durable-format activation/first-write and decoder floors are recovery-safe.

## Invariants & claim types
Binding invariant text: FG-INV-13 — commits are immutable and branch heads move only by atomic expected-head updates; fork closes the parent envelope/write epochs before opening independent parent/child successors; merge tokens/nonces/capability generations are pre-minted, each has one terminal outcome, and imported-range coverage prevents partial or repeated application across drift/cuts/restore/reconfiguration. FG-INV-15 — for every registered exact derivative, integrating ordered deltas equals batch evaluation; retained batches own each payload exactly once; every result-producing feature uses one generated, noninterchangeable owner arm with the state-shaped independent-retention machine (PendingVisibility and ReleasedAwaitingActivation retain manifest/policy/resource escrow; ActiveDeliverable additionally owns lease/replay/send authority; ACK or explicit authenticated release/expiry atomically installs compact terminal evidence); QUERY_CANCEL, Drop, disconnect, drain, and process death cannot release it; cursor rules forbid delta before baseline ACK and expose every gap. FG-INV-12 — every claimed answer-equivalent seal, compaction, codec/format rewrite, spill, factorize/flatten, workspace materialization, safe replan, and exact derived rebuild preserves logical values, multiplicity, order, visibility, security projection, and AnswerContract; no build progress changes schema visibility before its transactional SchemaOp. FG-INV-18 — bulk ingestion commits only canonical logical batches through ordinary transactions; rebuildable indexes/views/caches can be discarded without changing exact answers or authorization. FG-INV-14 — backup pins and restore-source leases remain GC roots until exact terminal release. Claim types: ANN recall evidence is FG-CAL-03 (authorized snapshot population, keyed sample, exact baseline, candidate policy, CI and rebuild action); view/index staleness feasibility is FG-CFG-03; freshness is FG-EVID-04 slo-class, never an invariant.

## Interactions
Blocked by gate-g1 and epics epic-w5..epic-w8. Consumes the W2c anchors: w2-retention-checkpoints, w2-compaction, w2-delta-batches, w2-branch-fork, w2-branch-merge, w2-branch-retire, w2-transparency, w2-gc-core; plus w11-backup and w11-restore for the Local backup/restore drills. Feeds gate-g3.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
- Mixed transaction/control suffix-recovery and per-graph retention matrix, logged per command class.
- Branch crypto matrix: fork double rotation, envelope DAG/AAD verification, live-grant re-encryption/movement, sibling and post-fork-parent non-decryption negatives, merge-token idempotency across history cuts (retry, drift, restore).
- Subscription/cursor campaign: baseline-ACK/delta-ACK/resume/lost-response/expiry with fault injection; assertion of zero delta-before-baseline and zero silent gaps, with gap accounting in logs.
- Owner-machine DPOR: disconnect/Drop/cancel/sender-death cannot release retained results; terminal evidence compaction checked.
- Bulk-import crash/retry bijection test (source-row/chunk/logical-effect).
- Shadow-build race suite: catch-up to exact frontier, validation, SchemaOp-only visibility.
- Format-rewrite no-op digest differential; activation/first-write/decoder-floor recovery matrix.
- Full Local backup and restore drills executing every arrow of the two pipelines above, with stale-epoch/old-capability rejection negatives; every empirical claim in the report names its assumptions.
- Detailed logging: every matrix/campaign/drill row logs {run_id, scenario_id, seed, crash/fault point id, per-clause verdict}; the backup and restore drills log each pipeline arrow with its evidence identity; failures carry §15.1 structured replay fields; the gate report must be regenerable from these logs alone, and a criterion whose log chain is incomplete does not count as passed.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: filtering unauthorized ANN candidates after retrieval — output filtering and exact rerank cannot repair missed candidates (§20 HNSW row); the gate demands authorized historical topology roots with exact fallback. Rejected: treating restore as ordinary open — the receipt-first hidden machine is mandatory. Risk: statistical gates degenerating into ornaments — every one must bind to an `evidence.toml`/`slo.toml` row or be removed.

## Provenance
§19 Gate G2 (plan lines 1338-1340); Appendix F rows cited; §20 HNSW/calibration rows.


## Integrated G2 E2E and evidence contract
- Unit/property rollup verifies that every G2 clause maps to a live child checker and negative fixture: mixed-command suffix recovery, branch cryptographic isolation and idempotent merges, derivative-equals-batch, cursor state, owner retention/release, shadow activation, exact-format rewrite, and backup/restore inventories. A missing mapping keeps the criterion red.
- Full E2E on isolated fixtures: open an embedded database and the server/CLI surfaces against the same Chronicle state; create branches, perform double key rotation, mutate/merge across a retained-history cut, run incremental view/index/ANN/projection and subscription baseline/deltas, lose and resume responses, retain/release protected and DP/replay outputs, bulk import through ordinary transactions, perform exact Local backup publication, independently reopen the archive, restore into a fresh isolated target through the hidden/service/receipt-first machine, independently reopen the target, and prove canonical results/proofs/cursors/branch isolation before and after compaction/restart. Fault injection covers every pipeline arrow and stale epoch/capability rejection; tests simulate source loss inside disposable fixtures only.
- Structured JSONL gate evidence: `{run_id,phase:"G2",criterion_id,child_bead_id,scenario_id,seed,command_or_pipeline_step,branch_graph_snapshot_commit_ids,cursor_generation_and_frontier,result_owner_arm,dp_replay_owner_arm,backup_restore_operation_ids,service_visibility_epoch,crash_fault_point,expected,actual,checker_ids,evidence_refs,verdict}`. Every arrow records before/after state and evidence identity; failures add full §15.1 replay artifacts. The gate report is generated from these rows, and incomplete or phase-misattributed ancestry cannot pass.

### Phase boundary correction — what the G2 DP-result criterion proves
The G2 DP-result criterion is limited to exact owner-arm reachability, atomic semantic/protocol detachment, retention/resource conservation, audit-pending/activation state shape, retry/recovery, authenticated release/ACK/expiry, compaction, and nonrelease on disconnect/cancel/Drop. It uses the registered verification-only structurally valid candidate constructor and reports `mechanism_evidence=NotActivated`; G2 neither advertises DP nor claims external debit, budget continuity, seed/noise correctness, or Warden noninterference. Those capabilities require W9 and Gate G3, which consume this already-proved owner machine. The G2 gate evaluator rejects any report that counts W9/G3 evidence or advertises DP.

title: Pass Gate G3 'Verified & Networked': protocol, Warden, multi-member Raft exit criteria
description:
## What & scope
Integration Gate G3 — "Verified & Networked." Certifies the networked, governed system: bounded FGP protocol machines with adapter parity, end-to-end Warden governance, Local receipt-first restore, and multi-member Raft replication with all-typed-root GC. This bead is the gate checklist; every clause below must be green before any networked/governed guarantee is advertised.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6's agent-native claim is worthless without governance that survives the wire: capability-scoped authorization, revocation, DP, and audit must hold across every adapter, frame, cursor, and failure mode. B1 extends to replication here (one commit mechanism, now multi-member). §0's market read: reviewers flag governance/access-control as *the* unsolved problem of current graph systems, and enterprise agent-memory adoption hinges on it; G3 is where FrankenGraphDB's governance becomes demonstrated rather than described. The §20 row "planner-only authorization leaks through another path" is retired here by cross-capability differential matrices.

## Design — normative detail
Exit criteria, complete: (1) bounded FGP connection; explicit multi-statement transaction ownership/reattachment; query/state-shaped result-delivery, durable-output, subscription, and FEC machines with adapter parity — including durable BeginStaging reservation and lost-BEGIN recovery; (2) statement sequence/key/class and workspace generations; (3) exact `SymbolRecord`; (4) RESULT_BEGIN/CHUNK/END plus terminal-or-statement ACK and typed release; (5) read-close/write-commit outcomes; (6) the sole wire-safe `PublicTxnStatusProjection` mapping: unreleased semantic terminal state is `FinalizingOpaque`; released terminal state with incomplete typed postconditions is `TerminalVisiblePendingPostconditions`; complete state is `TerminalReady`; internal `TxnCompletionState::TerminalPending` descriptors and bitmaps **never serialize**; (7) NeverRegistered detailed/compacted and terminal detailed/compacted status are **byte-identical**; (8) canonical baseline/delta transport and ACK/resume, and cluster-incarnation/service-visibility binding cover **every** authenticated frame, handle, cursor, capability, and adapter; (9) uniform `NotVisibleOrUnknown` is limited to invalid/unauthorized/wrong-epoch lookup; (10) end-to-end Warden: noninterference, declared constraint declassifications, revocation, externally monotonic irreversible-before-access DP debit/rollback reconciliation, Local two-stage current-root-recomputed key destruction, and exact audit `PendingUnclaimed -> Claimed(owner) -> Resolved` plus per-signer lock/candidate/external-batch-CAS/gap-free visibility recovery; lifecycle gates are nonrecursive and permanent gaps are durable; (11) Local receipt-first restore requires continuity/catalog fencing, hidden direct-endpoint negatives, independent archive and target reopen, completion, and source-lease release; (12) multi-member Raft proves prepared-root payload ownership/availability **before ordering**, exact stable/joint/final-retirement-floor semantics, paired checkpoint/floor replacement, exact-cut snapshots, leader loss at every phase, two-prefix fenced reads, Local/multi-member all-typed-root GC with exact current-root recomputation and physical-retirement evidence, and idempotent unknown/abort outcomes; W12 quarantine/aggregate GC remains W12-only; (13) rollback, witnessed-detection, and witnessed-non-equivocation claims remain **distinct**, with quorum-intersection, durable-witness, consistency, freshness, cross-log, and joint-rotation matrices green wherever prevention is claimed; (14) raw versus filtered proof scopes, formal/model bounds, and implementation bridges land **before** their advertised guarantees.

**Protocol matrix**, complete: explicit `TXN_REATTACH`/renewal; `QUERY_CANCEL` as compute/sender control only; `RESULT_RELEASE` as the **sole** client-directed durable release; output ACK/release/resume; exact cumulative flow-credit accounting; public proof/FEC schemas; Bolt's declared read-only downgrade. Every protected frame is bound to one release/send-guard arm and current complete security binding. **DP E2E:** arm-before-send external charging, exact receipt import, Local authority-owning-role noise at G3 (the Meta-only arm is W12 and excluded), charged-crash recovery, no seed/result leakage. **Rolling mixed-version:** advertise, joint support, write activation, first target write, refusal to downgrade, rewrite, decoder retirement.

## Invariants & claim types
Binding invariant text: FG-INV-01 — TerminalReady is exposed only after its exact postcondition bitmap, audit visibility, and independent result detachment are complete; detailed and compacted proofs return byte-identical public outcomes. FG-INV-16 — DP has one external charge request/tombstone/receipt lineage and noise is generated only after the charge is mirrored; audit candidates remain hidden until their exact batch and gap-free visibility advance; transaction ownership is generation-fenced, durably reattachable/renewable only under the capability lineage. FG-INV-20 — capability lookup/status/release is same-principal, same-or-narrower, current-epoch, and uniformly nonrevealing on failure; only named ticketed declassification is legal. FG-INV-10 — durable-format writes occur only under an activated `FormatCompatibilityState`; first-target-write is irreversible; downgrade is refused after it; old decoders retire only after exhaustive reachable/backup/restore/replay floors. FG-INV-08 — transparency claim grades remain distinct and non-equivocation requires the declared intersection, durable-witness, rotation, and freshness premises. Claim types: gate evidence is invariant-clause conformance; posture availability lines are slo.toml rows (§16 authority-surface pricing); no statistical claim substitutes for a matrix.

## Interactions
Blocked by G2 and completed W9/W10/W11 implementations. `fgdb-g3-protocol-authority-oracles-w27f` supplies live external-authority, protocol, noninterference, and independent-history evidence; `fgdb-g3-protocol-ha-torture-jni4` supplies live frame/adapter fuzzing, fault matrices, and real-process HA evidence. The reusable Local verifier beads are prerequisites, not substitutes. W12 is excluded. G3 feeds G4.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
- Protocol conformance suite covering every frame/machine above on every adapter (HTTP/2, gRPC, WebSocket, Bolt), with byte-level logs; adapter-parity differential.
- Status-projection tests: serialization fuzzers proving `TerminalPending` internals never appear on the wire; byte-identity checks for detailed/compacted NeverRegistered and terminal outcomes.
- Warden E2E: noninterference matrix, declassification-ticket tests, revocation propagation, DP debit/rollback with charged-crash recovery, two-stage key-destruction drill, audit claim/resolve recovery with per-signer locks and gap-free visibility.
- Restore drill with hidden direct-endpoint negative probes and stale service-epoch rejection.
- Multi-member Raft campaign: leader loss at every phase, two-prefix fenced reads, joint/final-retirement-floor reconfiguration, all-typed-root GC with physical-retirement evidence; idempotent unknown/abort outcome tests.
- Transparency matrices (quorum intersection, durable witnesses, consistency, freshness, cross-log, joint rotation) wherever prevention is claimed.
- Rolling mixed-version drill through all seven format stages; downgrade-refusal negative.
- DP leakage tests: no seed/result observable at any failure point.
- Detailed logging: every suite/campaign/drill emits JSONL `{run_id,phase:"G3",evidence_owner_bead,scenario_id,adapter,connection_stream_id,member_role,configuration_epoch,authority_kind,cas_version,seed,crash_or_fault_point,positions,obligation_owner_ids,clause_id,expected,actual,verdict,evidence_ref}`. Warden/restore/member steps carry evidence identities; failures carry complete §15.1 replay fields. The gate aggregator rejects base-fixture evidence presented as live G3 evidence and rejects any W12 row.
- Integrated G3 E2E: boot three Local members plus every configured simulated external authority; run all adapters through authentication, durable writes/reads/subscriptions/protected result resume, DP/audit/key/backup-restore status; inject authority fork, revocation, leader partition and joint reconfiguration; assert adapter parity, no leak, legal recovery, gap-free visible audit, exact owner retention/release, and executable replay artifacts.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: conflating rollback-prevention with detection claims — the grades stay distinct or the claim is removed. Rejected: adapter-specific status vocabularies — one wire-safe projection only. §20 row retired here: external authorities as availability ceiling is priced per posture in slo.toml, batched resolutions amortize round trips, and the embedded DirectoryBound posture requires zero external authorities.

## Provenance
§19 Gate G3 (plan lines 1342-1344); Appendix F rows cited; §16/§20 authority-surface row.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Pass Gate G4 'Leapfrog, Published': benchmarks, conformance, and 1.0 exit criteria
description:
## What & scope
Integration Gate G4 — "Leapfrog, Published." The 1.0 gate: every activated benchmark manifest green and public, full language-contract conformance, production-grade recovery/restore drills, correctly qualified evidence, and publications that match proven scope. Passing G4 *is* shipping 1.0. W12 sharding is excluded and cannot reuse G4 evidence as its gate.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
The leapfrog thesis (§0) is a *composition* claim, and G4 is where composition is published as verifiable artifacts: B5 demands that every empirical number carry its assumptions and every replay claim its closure; B6's market position (abandonment-proof, governance-grade embedded engine for the GraphRAG/agent-memory wave) requires outsider-verifiable proofs, not marketing. Cloud GQL gravity (Microsoft Fabric Graph GA with native ISO GQL, Spanner Graph GQL-compatible, Neo4j converging via Cypher 25/Neo4j 6) makes ISO GQL conformance table stakes — hence the 100% contract-closure clause. Honesty rules ("a disabled feature is absent, not partial") are the anti-Kùzu continuity posture.

## Design — normative detail
Exit criteria, complete: (1) **all activated §17 benchmark manifests green and public**; (2) 100% of G0's 1.0 `LanguageContract` — the ISO minimum closure, `GG01` or `GG02` plus one of `GG20`-`GG23` as applicable, all prerequisites, the required scalar profile, the validated synchronous Unicode/UTS #10/UAX #15/UAX #31 bundle and UCS_BASIC behavior, and the named optional IDs — passes its ISO-ID/TCK corpus, while **every out-of-contract feature is rejected/documented**; (3) canonical replay/archive/answer-requirement/approximation-profile/result-contract and security matrices; (4) production-format recovery plus Local receipt-first restore, continuity split-brain, stale service epoch, independent archive/target reopen, and source-lease-release drills; (5) crash-fault multi-writer preparation and globally ordered commitment; (6) evidence reports correctly qualified; (7) papers match proven scope; (8) 1.0.

G4 additionally publishes: the durable-format compatibility matrix and completed upgrade/downgrade drills; allocation/escrow/valid-time/security/transaction-ownership/result-retention/DP/audit-pipeline **invariant clause reports**; bulk and derived-build conformance; and exact backup/restore/GC inventory coverage for **every newly activated state slot**. Documentation, robot schemas, and benchmark claims are generated or checked against the frozen registries. **A feature whose command/state/checker row is disabled is absent from the 1.0 capability manifest, not described as partial.**

## Invariants & claim types
This gate is where the claim-type constitution is enforced in public. Appendix G's three CI laws bind every published number: **Derivability** — every §17 gate names its operation class and counting unit and must be arithmetically consistent with its registry row (a latency gate >= the class's ordered-barrier count x the manifest's pinned measured fsync p50; a throughput gate <= the apply ceiling implied by its sequenced-command count and measured serial apply cost); a gate failing the check is a registry error and fails the build, not the benchmark. **Coverage** — every stated scale objective must be covered by a registered `stream_capacity.toml` scenario. **Same-change** — any change adding sequenced semantic commands, ordered durability barriers, external-authority interactions, or per-object identity structure updates `latency_anatomy.toml`/`stream_capacity.toml` in the same change. Statistical/evidence/configuration claims publish only under their registered classes with full disclosures: FG-CAL-01 (adaptive policy vs pinned fallback: null/outcome filtration, alpha, support/overlap, effective sample size, loss and fallback), FG-CAL-02 (interval coverage), FG-CAL-03 (ANN recall), FG-EVID-01 (decision-card/OPE completeness), FG-EVID-02 (scrub/corpus health), FG-EVID-03 (endurance: duration/cadence, compaction-debt ceiling in §6.6 write-amp terms, memory stability, occupancy-model divergence is itself a finding), FG-EVID-04 (freshness: watermark/commit-sequence units, realized lag distribution, typed `FreshnessBreach` rate), FG-CFG-01 (MTTDL durability model incl. per-tier `fec_profile` reconstruction and checkpoint-fold recode paths), FG-CFG-02 (controller stability), FG-CFG-03 (staleness SLO feasibility), FG-CFG-04 (maintenance-stream capacity model). FG-INV-19 binds replay claims: the manifest's effective grade may only weaken as leases/resolution/trust/configuration/authority change; missing/redacted/revoked/expired/untrusted evidence yields only the declared weaker grade.

## Interactions
Blocked by gate-g3; epic-perf supplies bench binaries/manifests, governance-profile and scale gates, and cost-registry CI; epic-obs supplies the observatory, doctor, and slo.toml wiring behind qualified evidence; verif-formal supplies the Lean/TLA+ anchors whose bounds must land before advertised guarantees; g0-doc-sync supplies the generated README/AGENTS synchronization that makes docs a checked release artifact. Feeds gate-w12 (as sequencing only — W12 must produce its own evidence).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
- Public benchmark publication pipeline: every activated §17 manifest runs green with pinned environment, seeds, fsync p50 measurement, and Appendix G derivability check logs attached.
- ISO-ID/TCK corpus run for the full frozen contract; out-of-contract rejection corpus with documented errors.
- Replay/archive/answer-requirement/profile/result-contract matrices and security matrices executed and archived.
- The five named operational drills (production-format recovery; receipt-first restore; continuity split-brain; stale service epoch; independent archive/target reopen + source-lease release) with structured drill logs.
- Multi-writer crash-fault campaign proving globally ordered commitment.
- Registry-vs-docs CI: documentation, robot schemas, and claims regenerate or diff-check cleanly against frozen registries; capability-manifest audit proving disabled rows are absent.
- Invariant clause reports generated for the eight named domains; backup/restore/GC inventory coverage check for every state slot activated since G3.
- Detailed logging: every gate run (benchmark manifest, conformance corpus, matrix suite, drill, campaign) logs {run_id, manifest/corpus digest, seed, environment-pin digest, per-criterion verdict}; drills log per-step structured events (step name, evidence identities, verdict); failures carry §15.1 structured replay fields; the gate report must be regenerable from these logs alone, and a criterion whose log chain is incomplete does not count as passed.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: shipping "partial" features (constitutionally absent instead); publishing benchmark numbers without registry derivability (a build failure, not a footnote); claiming replay strength beyond resolvable evidence slots. §20 rows live here: statistical guarantees rest on modeling assumptions — every claim names assumptions and scope; monitoring can trigger fallback but never retroactively restores invalid coverage.

## Provenance
§19 Gate G4 (plan lines 1346-1348); Appendix G CI laws; Appendix F statistical/evidence/configuration gate table.


## Release-candidate E2E and evidence reproducibility
- Unit/property release audit validates registry derivability arithmetic, feature-ID closure, capability-manifest absence for disabled rows, replay-grade weakening, backup/restore/GC inventory coverage, public-document claim links, and every invariant-clause report. Mutation fixtures remove one checker/log/ref/format row and must make the release candidate fail.
- Full release E2E on pinned isolated environments: build embedded/server/CLI artifacts; run the frozen ISO/TCK and answer/security matrices; execute durable multi-writer workloads through all 1.0 transports; inject a crash during prepared ownership and audit visibility; recover production-format state; publish a Local backup, independently reopen it, perform receipt-first restore into a fresh target, independently reopen the target, reject stale service epochs/capabilities, run a subscription and replay bundle across restart, execute all activated benchmark manifests, and regenerate docs/robot schemas/capability/evidence reports from registries. Repeat the canonical workload at the same seed and require byte-identical exact outputs/certificates where the declared grade permits.
- Structured JSONL release ledger: `{release_candidate_id,run_id,phase:"G4",criterion_id,child_bead_id,claim_class,manifest_or_corpus_digest,environment_pin_digest,seed,scenario_step,format_version,positions,benchmark_registry_row,measured_and_derived_values,evidence_refs,public_artifact_digest,expected,actual,verdict}`. Operational steps include all evidence identities and before/after positions; failures carry complete §15.1 replay fields. The public gate report is reproducible from the ledger and signed artifact digests alone; missing ancestry, an unqualified claim, or any W12 evidence presented as G4 evidence is fatal.
- W12 boundary negative: compile/registry inspection proves `sharding=true` and every W12-only clause remain absent from the 1.0 manifest. `fgdb-epic-w12-verification-bike` is not a G4 dependency and cannot be used to repair a failed 1.0 criterion.

title: Pass the Genesis slice: first W1-W5 end-to-end integration under the lab runtime
description:
## What & scope
The Genesis slice is the first W1-W5 integration milestone and the entry ticket to Gate G1. It proves, on real code under asupersync's lab runtime, the exact lifecycle `Genesis -> CheckpointInstalled -> Operational` — including crashes injected before and after each checkpoint/floor command — and admits **no user operation earlier**. It then proves a checkpoint-replacement experiment and one complete end-to-end walk through every final abstraction. This bead is the gate itself: an executable, logged, reproducible demonstration, not a code deliverable.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
§0's anti-goals forbid an MVP, a "v1 simplification", or a temporary RocksDB phase: §19 sequences *integration*, not ambition, and every workstream is specified at full strength. The Genesis slice is where the six bets first compose: B1's One Version Universe (D1/D2 append-only publication, checkpoint/floor machinery), B3's Loom pipeline (binder -> GLA -> planner -> authorized cursor), B5's determinism/evidence (post-rebase capsule under `IntentSemanticsOid`, canonical result, executable `ReplayManifest`, typed decision card), and B6's authorization-first access. The market rationale is Kùzu's fate — an excellent single-vendor embedded engine acquired by Apple, its repo archived read-only 2025-10-10, with GitLab forced into migration: FrankenGraphDB's differentiator is outsider-verifiable composition, and the Genesis slice is the first artifact an outsider can replay. The academic frontier solved every subproblem in isolation; no shipping system composed them — this slice is the first composition proof.

## Design — normative detail
**Phase 1 — lifecycle.** Prove `Genesis -> CheckpointInstalled -> Operational` with crash injection before/after each checkpoint/floor command. No user operation is admitted before `Operational`.

**Phase 2 — checkpoint replacement.** Replace an operational checkpoint with bytes already absent under the inherited activated cut. Required outcomes: recovery must succeed; the replacement Provisional cut must **dominate** that inherited absence; and **no new reclaim may occur until its distinct activation command**.

**Phase 3 — the end-to-end walk**, in this exact order: authenticated authority -> pinned GQL `LanguageContract`/Unicode bundle/binder/role-bearing graph references -> typed GLA subset -> planner -> authorized Strata cursor -> positive/absence/path witness -> SSI/constraint validation -> forced base drift and a **new post-rebase capsule** under `IntentSemanticsOid` -> D1/D2 logical/local-root publication -> crash recovery from **both** root slots and from the installed checkpoint -> canonical result plus an executable `ReplayManifest`. The slice additionally includes: stable IDs under label mutation; factorized/flat equivalence; spill; one safe replan class; and a correctly typed decision card. The lab explores declared bounded interleavings (DPOR) and runs differentials against independent semantics/oracles.

**Prohibitions (each disqualifies the slice):** no stub transaction, no post-filter security, no pre-rebase capsule, no parser-interpreted execution qualifies.

## Invariants & claim types
Binding invariant text (Appendix F): FG-INV-08 — every retained checkpoint suffix begins with its exact install command; Provisional cuts authenticate inherited absence but authorize no new release until activation. FG-INV-10 — the two-slot `manifest.root` protocol always selects the highest structurally credible authenticated role closure with exact applied/visible/service positions, while one inode-bound publication sequencer plus external incarnation continuity fences every stale writer. FG-INV-17 — every semantic drift regenerates effects, workspace/read/write state, constraints, witnesses, logical deltas, allocation plan, RETURNING bytes, and capsule **before** final-certification reservation and terminal signing. FG-INV-19 — a registry-rooted replay manifest derives its structural maximum only from its versioned evidence-slot matrix; Replayable requires every semantic slot to resolve and reproduce canonical logical output. FG-INV-20 — authorization precedes every observation or effect. Claim types: slice evidence is invariant-clause conformance (checker plus negative-test entrypoints, `waiver=forbidden`); the decision card is FG-EVID-01 class (state/actions/features, logged probabilities, zero-support exclusions, clipping/estimator, policy epoch and fallback); no slo/benchmark claim is made here.

## Interactions
Consumes w2-root-bootstrap (dual-slot frames, publication sequencer), w2-commit-protocol (D1/D2, capsules), w2-recovery (recovery equation), w2-retention-checkpoints (checkpoint/floor install, Provisional cuts), w2-id-allocator (stable IDs under label mutation), w3-tier-d (Strata cursor substrate), w4-secure-view (authorized cursor), w4-ssi-witnesses (witness families), w4-merge-ladder (rebase), w5-parsers/w5-binder/w5-gla-algebra/w5-planner/w5-executor (pipeline), w5-planner additionally supplying the typed decision card, w5-determinism (canonical result), w5-replay (`ReplayManifest`), verif-sim (lab harness), verif-reference (independent semantics). Produces the prerequisite for gate-g1.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
- Deterministic lab script for Phase 1 with per-crash-point seeds; structured logs record each command, slot write, fence action, and recovery decision; assert user operations rejected pre-`Operational`.
- Phase 2 script with a reclaim ledger proving zero new reclamation before the distinct activation command, and a dominance check of the replacement Provisional cut over inherited absence.
- Phase 3 e2e script logging per stage: authority id, contract hash, GLA plan digest, witness inventory (positive/absence/path), capsule digest under `IntentSemanticsOid`, root-slot generations, replay grade. Forced-drift assertion: the pre-rebase capsule is never signed; a new post-rebase capsule exists.
- Both-slot recovery matrix (corrupt/lag each slot alternately) plus recovery from the installed checkpoint.
- Label-mutation stable-ID test; factorized-vs-flat differential; spill trigger with equivalence check; one replan-class equivalence test; decision-card schema validation.
- Bounded-interleaving DPOR exploration report and differential runs against verif-reference, archived with seeds.
- Prohibition negatives: executable checks that stub transactions, post-filter security, pre-rebase capsules, and parser-interpreted execution are structurally impossible or fail the gate.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: any MVP slice with stubbed transactions or a substitute storage engine — it would validate nothing about the composition, which §20 identifies as the actual risk (Free-Join/factorization interplay; graph-SSI soundness). Rejected: admitting the slice with post-filter security "for now" — FG-INV-20 is constitutional. Risk: slice scope creep; bounded by exactly the walk enumerated above, nothing more.

## Provenance
§19 "The Genesis slice" (plan line 1332); §0 thesis and anti-goals; Appendix F rows cited.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: GQL certificate stub over snapshot seq + bound MATCH
description:
G1 slice of Genesis criterion 5 (docs/REALITY_CHECK_AND_BRIDGE_PLAN.md): a replayable certificate over snapshot seq + bound statement for the pinned GQL MATCH.

This is NOT full EXPLAIN (CERTIFICATE), NOT FG-INV-19 promotion, NOT a planner, NOT G0 language freeze, NOT Appendix A, NOT 176-row freeze, NOT Graph-SSI.

## Why this is a capability, not ceremony

Genesis: "Result includes a replayable certificate over snapshot seq + bound statement." Wave 3 landed `Database::execute_gql` returning `Vec<VId>` with no certificate. Same statement + same snapshot must be auditable; a write that advances seq must change the certificate.

## Architecture (do not invert)

- Do NOT change `execute_gql`'s signature (Wave 3 tests pin `Vec<VId>`).
- Additive: `Database::execute_gql_certified(&self, src, bind) -> Result<(Vec<VId>, GqlCertificate), GqlError>`. Rows MUST equal `execute_gql` on the same inputs.
- `GqlCertificate { snapshot_seq: CommitSeq, statement_digest: Digest, bind_digest: Digest }` (field names may match landed Digest type from fgdb-crypto).
- Statement digest hashes the source text (as parsed — same bytes the caller passed, not a pretty-print). Bind digest hashes a canonical encoding of RelationBind (sorted name→RelationId). Snapshot seq is `Database::frontier`.
- Deterministic: same db state + same src + same bind ⇒ byte-identical certificate.
- Off-grammar still `GqlError::Parse` and produces no certificate.
- No-claim: not plan-cost, not operator tree, not FG-INV-19 replay of the whole engine, not bumping `expected_enforced_invariants`.

## Required behavior

Positive:
1. certified rows == execute_gql rows on the pinned statement.
2. two calls without an intervening write: certificates are equal (including seq).
3. a WriteBatch commit between calls: snapshot_seq (and thus the certificate) changes.
4. Off-grammar: Parse error, no certificate.

Planted negative:
5. A certificate that hashed only the statement (omitting seq) MUST fail test 3. Assert seq is in the struct and differs after commit.

## Owned files

1. `crates/fgdb-gql`: `RelationBind::canonical_bytes(&self) -> Vec<u8>` sorted pairs, no crypto dep.
2. `crates/fgdb/src/gql_cert.rs` (new): `GqlCertificate` + digest helpers using fgdb-crypto.
3. `crates/fgdb/src/lib.rs`: `mod gql_cert`; `execute_gql_certified`. Do not edit execute_gql body except to share a private helper if needed.
4. `crates/fgdb/tests/min_gql_certificate.rs` (new).

## Code-first

`cargo check -p CRATE` only. No cargo test, no check.sh, no rch exec. Commit immediately. Do not br close. Orchestrator batch-verifies and closes.

title: 13 SC2015 sites in the gate scripts are fail-closed by accident, not by construction
description:
## The residue

Carried from `fgdb-shell-lint-silent-no-op-xi8p`, item 3 of its remaining work,
so that bead can close.

The gate scripts use `check && ok "..." || die "..."` in 13 places. shellcheck
flags each as **SC2015** (note severity, so it does not fail the gate today).

They are all fail-CLOSED right now, and that was verified rather than assumed:
`ok()` returns the status of a log `echo`, which succeeds, so the `||` branch is
not reached on success; and both scripts whose `die()` does not itself `exit` end
in `[ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ] || exit 1`. A spurious trip therefore yields a false RED,
never a false GREEN.

## Why it is still worth removing

The safety is incidental, not structural. It rests on `ok()`'s last statement
happening to return 0. Any future `die()` or `ok()` that gains a
non-zero-returning first statement flips these 13 sites from fail-closed to
**fail-open** — the gate would report success on a failed check — and nothing in
the tree would notice, because SC2015 is advisory and the flip is invisible in a
line-level diff.

That is the same silent-green shape as the parent bead: an enforcement mechanism
whose correctness depends on an unstated, unchecked property.

## The fix

Convert each site to the explicit form:

    if check; then ok "..."; else die "..."; fi

Mechanical, local, and it removes the dependency on `ok()`'s return value
entirely. 13 sites across the `scripts/` gate scripts.

Per AGENTS.md "No Script-Based Changes", do these by hand or with parallel
subagents — not with a regex sweep.

## Acceptance

1. `shellcheck` (no `--severity` filter) reports **0** SC2015 in `scripts/`.
2. `scripts/check.sh` still passes; the 13 converted checks still fail on the
   conditions they were guarding.
3. At least one converted site is mutation-audited: force its condition false and
   confirm the script exits non-zero.
4. Optional follow-on once the count is 0: tighten the shell-lint step in
   `scripts/check.sh` from `--severity=warning` to the default so notes fail too,
   which makes the class non-recurring rather than merely absent.
close_reason: Landed in 2f2862a. Count was 14, not 13 (g0_claims_e2e 9, g0_spine_e2e 5). PARTITION: 0 of 14 fail open, 14 of 14 fail closed. Every site is 'check && ok || die', and since ok() ends in a printf returning 0, a passing check never reaches die -- there is no path that turns a failure into a green. The real exposure is the inverse and is a DIAGNOSTIC defect: break ok() and all 14 emit a FAIL line attributed to an assertion that actually PASSED. Proved with an 8-cell truth table replicating the exact preamble (set -euo pipefail, ok/die, VERDICT_REACHED trap, trailing [ $FAIL -eq 0 ] || exit 1): both forms exit non-zero in every broken cell, but if/then/else turns a broken ok() into an honest 'ABORTED before the verdict' via the existing trap instead of a misattributed FAIL. All 14 converted by hand; diff is purely mechanical (zero lines outside the pattern in either direction) and ok/die call-site counts match HEAD (claims 16/16, spine 13/20). CLASS PINNED, not merely removed: run_shell_lint gains a 'shellcheck --include=SC2015' pass, which enforces one code regardless of severity -- SC2015 is only a note, so --severity=warning never saw it and 14 accumulated unnoticed, with ubs exiting 0 on .sh without checking. Mutation-proven at the gate: clean tree prints '0 SC2015 across 15 file(s)' exit 0; reintroducing ONE site exits 1 naming g0_spine_e2e.sh:329 while --severity=warning still passed in the same run. Acceptance items 1, 3 and 4 met; item 2 met for every gate a .sh-only change can touch (run_shell_lint and run_file_coverage driven verbatim from check.sh, 187 tracked = 176 inspected + 11 exempt, exit 0; both e2e scripts re-run). The full check.sh cargo chain was NOT run: its asupersync fetch alone is ~505s, which exceeds the 10m build-1 TTL in force. Six unrelated notes remain out of scope by design (3x SC1091, 2x SC2016, 1x SC2012). Cross-cutting finding recorded on fgdb-ia2b: the checker_index script census is filesystem-based too (script_undeclared on an untracked scripts/g0_proof_lanes_e2e.sh), so ia2b is wider than the claims lint.

title: Pass Gate W12 'One Universe, Many Shards': post-1.0 sharding exit criteria
description:
## What & scope
Gate W12 — "One Universe, Many Shards" (post-1.0). The dedicated sharding gate: `sharding=true` may be advertised only when every clause below is green. W12 cannot weaken single-node/replicated contracts and cannot reuse G4 evidence as its gate.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
§0 is explicit: 1.0 formats reserve the identities and fencing fields sharding needs, but distributed atomic commit, distributed SSI, and global time are **not** configuration-only activations — they get their own workstream and proof gates. B1 extends to shards only through Meta-ordered semantics; B5's honesty discipline demands that the deliberate correctness/performance tradeoff (global Meta sequencing, §20) is published as two ceilings, never hidden. The gate encodes the plan's constitutional bet: no shard-local semantic bypass, ever; reopen scalar time only as a new architecture with new proofs.

## Design — normative detail
Exit criteria, complete: (1) every reserved kind/tag/field has an exact registry row; (2) role-tagged Local/Meta/Shard logs, roots, floors, and exact-cut snapshots **reject cross-role commands**; (3) fresh Sharded Genesis and audited Local freeze/seal/activation/authority transfer/RetiredLocal finalization/reclamation pass **every crash point**; (4) every semantic mutation — including single-shard work — enters Meta Raft for one global logical/transaction/HLC order; (5) BEGIN durably reserves its key/outcome capability **before response**; registration atomically claims the operation ticket and roots workspace zero before every serializable read; (6) every explicit statement is Meta-registered against one sequence/key/class/error policy and workspace generation; every routed shard reads registered snapshot plus the exact certified overlay for every previously touched shard; Meta publication atomically advances statement/delivery/workspace/witness/effect state and constructs the successor Registered outcome; (7) no result streams before its distinct statement/read-close audit visibility release and typed delivery lease; terminal/autocommit and statement results share exact ACK/typed-release transitions; (8) cancellation proves open-statement, result, overlay, and remote-grant discharge; read close is a Global control; (9) ReadWrite admission names complete statement/delivery/workspace frontiers; effect-only bases feed **one union-wide authorization decision**, while terminal audit remains a separately signer-locked event/resolution; (10) fence-free prepares, constraint/serialization certificates, pre-command availability, Meta applied-hidden candidate/external batch CAS/visibility advance, decision-certificate publication, shard decision, typed visibility projection, post-visibility acknowledgements, complete `GlobalLogicalDeltaBatch` publication, and TerminalReady status pass **exact DAG/crash proofs**; (11) detailed/compacted NeverRegistered and terminal outcomes are byte-identical; attempt compaction's build/attest/publish protocol proves every result/workspace/remote-grant/public-status obligation before release.

Additional proofs: certified shard allocation reservations with permanent spent commitments; Meta escrow custody with staged/active shard grants and a conservation bijection; complete security-state projections; transaction ownership generation transfer; DP clipped fragments with one Meta charge/noise/result owner; format support across Meta plus current/joint shard groups; exact role payload-root coverage. Meta/Shard GC passes Requested/Started/Completed-or-all-cancelled state machines before aggregate completion. Local-to-Sharded capability migration is exclusive and service-epoch fenced; outstanding Local results/cursors either follow their certified transition policy or require a new baseline — **never reinterpret an old ObjectId**.

Distributed correctness: every cross-group edge passes two-sided `CertifiedRemoteStrongRef` trust/retention/GC tests; every participant prepare has durable availability and one terminal decision; **no timeout fractures atomicity** under crash/partition/leader loss/reconfiguration. The independent global SCC/history oracle finds no committed cycle across local, cross-shard, negative/gap/path, read-only, workspace, and batch interleavings — including same-certification-basis batches under §14.6's registered **virtual-serial batch-certification law**: two-writer, rw-cycle, aggregate-overflow, and same-head cases — and the batch-versus-serial equivalence oracle proves batched certification yields the **identical admitted set, identical abort set, and identical committed history** as serial certification of the same submission order; deterministic constraint owners/reservations agree with the single-threaded reference. Branch/key/ID/security/resource/privacy/audit authority and activation state is Meta-atomic; shard-local key material changes only through certified Staged-to-Active or destruction protocols. Cross-shard reads use one retained registered snapshot plus exact workspace generation and overlays. Remote configuration trust and the six-stage grant release, replacement Provisional cuts with no-new-reclaim before activation, current-root staged key zero/destroy/member-KMS completion, and GC preflight/quarantine/no-resurrection/member/aggregate completion pass models and physical evidence gates. Exact backup at barrier P proves per-shard copy/reopen/closure, portable Global manifest publication, archive grants, ordered shard release acks, and Meta finalize. Restore proves continuity reservation, exhaustive leaves-first readdress/re-encryption, hidden activation/visibility/service preparation, receipt-first continuity/catalog publication, Meta finalize, shard open, independent reopen, operational acknowledgements, completion, and source-lease release. Three-phase topology copy/cutover/retire proves no ambient evidence, straddled epoch, or premature byte/key retirement. Every failure artifact carries §15's structured replay fields. Meta and every shard pass payload/certificate loss, checkpoint+suffix, donor loss, rolling upgrade, and exact status/backup/restore matrices; every compiled-and-negotiated subordinate clause of FG-INV-01-20 is live; published benchmarks disclose **both global sequencer ceilings** — serial and batched under the §14.6 law, with the residual per-command Meta-apply ceiling stated. Otherwise `sharding=true` is absent.

## Invariants & claim types
Binding W12 clause text: FG-INV-01 — W12 reserves the begin key and outcome-capability bytes before response; no shard creates or reverses the semantic decision. FG-INV-02 — under the batch-certification law the batch-scoped `GlobalFinalCertificationReservation` is the single legal live owner of a shared certification basis with per-candidate sub-holds; exclusivity is per generation, not per candidate. FG-INV-05 — W12 Meta state contains every local, cross-shard, read-only, statement-workspace, positive/negative/gap/path `wr`/`ww`/`rw` edge; Meta histories remain plain serializable unless Meta registers the certification rule. FG-INV-07 — the exact W12 read and write orders (begin reservation through TerminalReady) are normative; timeout releases no prepared, certificate, audit, result, allocation, escrow, or retention owner. Claim types: sequencer ceilings are Appendix G registry rows plus slo/benchmark disclosures; the gate itself is invariant-clause conformance.

## Interactions
Sequenced after G4 and blocked by the complete W12 implementation epic plus `fgdb-epic-w12-verification-bike`. The latter supplies live W12 global/protocol oracles and formal/fuzz/fault/recovery evidence. Base/G4 verifier results are reusable infrastructure only and never substitute for W12 evidence; no G0-G4 gate depends on the W12 verification epic.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
- Registry audit for every reserved kind/tag/field; cross-role command rejection negatives per role.
- Sharded Genesis and Local activation crash-point matrix (every phase).
- Full read/write order DAG/crash proofs per FG-INV-07's W12 orders; attempt-compaction build/attest/publish obligation proofs.
- SCC/history oracle campaign including the four named batch cases; batch-versus-serial equivalence oracle (admitted set, abort set, committed history identical).
- Escrow conservation bijection, DP single-owner, capability-migration exclusivity, and ObjectId non-reinterpretation tests.
- Backup-at-barrier-P and restore pipelines executed arrow by arrow; topology copy/cutover/retire drills with epoch-straddle negatives.
- Matrix suite: payload/certificate loss, checkpoint+suffix, donor loss, rolling upgrade, status/backup/restore — per shard and Meta.
- Published ceiling disclosure check: serial + batched + residual per-command Meta-apply ceiling in the benchmark report.
- Full W12 E2E: boot Meta plus at least three shards from fresh Sharded Genesis; execute begin reservation, multi-statement cross-shard read/write and read-only transactions, workspace overlays, batch certification with injected cycle/aggregate/constraint/escrow cases, union-wide authorization, DP fragments, protected delivery, branch operation, remote references, key rotation/destruction, distributed GC, topology move, exact backup and receipt-first restore. Inject partitions, leader loss, lost responses, stale epochs/capabilities, and crashes at every selected DAG phase; then independently reopen archive and restored target, verify global-oracle/reference/batch-serial equivalence, one Meta semantic order, complete global deltas, no timeout-fractured decision, no hidden/unauthorized observation, no old ObjectId reinterpretation, and legal physical retirement.
- Unit/property evidence rollup: every activated reserved kind/tag/field, role command/root/floor/payload, state transition, global dependency-edge constructor, batch-law arm, and release/reclamation condition maps to a live checker plus negative fixture. Mutation/removal of any mapping must fail and keep `sharding=true` absent.
- Phase-boundary E2E negative: present a valid G4 artifact without the W12 verification epic's evidence or present a base pending row as live; the gate must reject both deterministically and log the exact missing W12 clause IDs.
- Detailed logging: every matrix/oracle/model/fuzz/drill/E2E row emits JSONL `{run_id,phase:"W12",evidence_owner_bead,scenario_id,seed,model_bounds,crash_point_id,role,group_id,configuration_topology_service_epochs,global_logical_txn_hlc_meta_index,shard_applied_visible_audit_positions,attempt_statement_workspace_decision_ids,remote_grant_key_gc_backup_restore_ids,clause_id,expected,actual,verdict,evidence_ref}`. Failures carry complete §15.1 artifacts, minimized schedules, first divergences, and executable replay commands. Passing rows use the same schema; the gate report and ceiling disclosure are regenerated from logs/registry digests alone.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected constitutionally: shard-local semantic bypass; scalar-time reopening as an "optimization" (new architecture with new Chronicle/branch/Ripple/replay proofs, or nothing); reusing G4 evidence. §20 row: the Meta sequencer may bottleneck — the mitigation is honesty (publish both ceilings) plus the registered batch law, never weakened semantics.

## Provenance
§19 Gate W12 (plan lines 1350-1354); §14.6 batch-certification law; Appendix F W12 clauses; §0 anti-goals.


## Dedicated verification requirement
`fgdb-epic-w12-verification-bike` is mandatory gate input. Its child tasks `fgdb-w12-sim-global-oracles-p1cl` and `fgdb-w12-formal-torture-ejx0` must both be green. W12 does not inherit Gate G4 verification.

description:

The accrual half of geo2 HELD ENTIRE and grew. Its prescribed fix does not
survive contact with why the script is the way it is.

## The accrual, re-derived

  g0_identity_e2e $WORK pool   36 dirs   11.45 GB   mean 326 MB/run
    span 07:34:08 -> 21:28:19 on 2026-07-27 = 13.90 h

  /data/tmp/fgdb-subject       28 subject-<sha> dirs   2.05 GB, no reaper

  (geo2 filed 34 dirs / 10.50 GB and 24 dirs / 1.8 GB; both grew as it predicted,
   and its rate claim of "~one every 22 min, ~860 MB/h, ~20 GB/day" re-derives.)

Classifier: a `/data/tmp/tmp.*` dir containing `neg-appendix-bead/`. It is
positive-marker based, and it separates this pool from the other gate pools.

Disk is 88% used with 114 GB free. geo2's context of 95% / 52 GB has EASED, so
this is an accrual bead with ~5 days of headroom from this pool alone, not an
emergency.

## disk_hygiene.sh removes nothing — CONFIRMED. That is not the same claim as
## "it is a failed reaper".

31 lines; no `rm`, `unlink` or `delete` anywhere. Line 4: "Inventory only: this
command never deletes or mutates artifacts." Last line states a POLICY:
"status+ownership+recoverability liveness; never age-only".

Its three commits are all [fgdb-cfg6], and the FIRST is titled

  669a77d  feat(hygiene): inventory per-pane artifacts WITHOUT DELETION

and cfg6 is CLOSED on exactly that deliverable. The non-deletion is a decision
taken under its own bead, not an omission.

geo2's "it names no pool" is FALSE as written: line 5 is
`root=${1:-/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm}`, which names one. What IS true: it names none
of the gate work-dir pools, and it has no REAPABLE-AFTER input to honour.

## Why this is a ruling, not a patch

geo2's attribution is verbatim correct: 1j16 option 2 asked for "one accountable
reaper (the orchestrator's scripts/disk_hygiene.sh) that honours it". But 1j16
ALSO says "Nothing in the library deleting a file is CORRECT under RULE 1 and
must stay: a gate script must never be the thing that removes data."

AGENTS.md RULE 1 is unscoped — no file may be deleted without express written
permission. A schedulable reaper is a STANDING DELEGATION of deletion authority,
and age-only sweeping is the specific failure mode that has already destroyed
work in this project (a prior age sweep deleted 37 pin-clean staged rows,
because BLOCKED work is untouched precisely for being blocked).

## The unblocked half: the LIFETIME

Have the gate (or scripts/lib/private_subject.sh) write a REAPABLE-AFTER stamp
and a byte count into each `$WORK` dir, and have disk_hygiene.sh REPORT the
reapable set with its existing per-path classification. That is 1j16 option 3
plus the accounting half of option 2, breaks no rule, and reduces the eventual
deletion to a one-line human decision over a named list. It also gives the
liveness test the POLICY line already demands and today cannot evaluate.

BLOCKED ON: an owner ruling on whether any script in this repo may delete under
RULE 1. Do not implement geo2's fix option 3 ("MAKE disk_hygiene.sh ACTUALLY
REAP") before that ruling.

## Provenance

Successor to fgdb-geo2, closed on re-derivation.

title: Strata's two durable formats are outside the Appendix A catalog, and nothing in the object graph reaches a partition — so no database can be reopened
notes:
FILED 2026-07-31 from the reality check, then SPLIT OUT of fgdb-w3-tier-d-ctj during Phase 5
refinement. Filed as a BUG rather than a task: this is not missing future work, it is an active
dangling reference in a durable format that is already marked active.

THE DEFECT. RootSlot is an ACTIVE row in registries/bootstrap_frames, and it carries
root_manifest_oid. No object kind anywhere defines what that OID resolves to. So recovery can select
a structurally credible root slot, authenticate it, read an OID out of it -- and then has nothing to
resolve. There is no durable path from "here is a database directory" to "here are its partitions",
which means NO DATABASE CAN BE REOPENED, by anyone, today. Everything that currently looks like it
reopens is a test holding a PartitionRoot identity in memory across the close.

WHY IT WAS SPLIT OUT. It was first recorded as a comment on fgdb-w3-tier-d-ctj and fgdb-j0vu was
blocked on that whole bead. That edge was COARSER THAN THE TRUTH: tier D is a large bead with several
in-flight children, and the spine does not need most of it -- fgdb-strata already writes, reads,
verifies and reopens blocks. It needs exactly this one object. Blocking the first runnable engine on
all of tier D would have delayed it behind work it does not depend on, which is the same
throughput-allocation failure the reality check was written to correct. fgdb-j0vu now blocks on this
bead instead.

WHAT IT HAS TO CARRY, and the point is how little. fgdb-strata already guarantees a partition reopens
from a 32-byte block identity alone: BlockStore::get verifies content-addressing on read, PartitionRoot
carries the full BlockRef list, and decode_root reconstructs the span. So the manifest does NOT
describe partition contents. Per live partition it needs the (graph, partition) coordinate and the
PartitionRoot's object id. Plus a branch->head binding, since the root slot is per database and
branches are per graph.

DECISIONS TO RESOLVE, none of them free:
1. IDENTITY CLASS. It is referenced by OID from RootSlot, which per the reservation bijection law makes
   it a StrongRef target and therefore logical-backed. VERIFY THIS BY RUNNING validate_identity ON A
   SYNTHESIZED ROW rather than by reasoning from this comment -- "ask the checker, not the corpus".
2. GROWTH. The manifest is rewritten on every partition publish. If it is one object listing every
   partition, publish cost is O(partitions) and it becomes the write-amplification hot spot the moment
   there is more than one partition. Consider a two-level shape (manifest -> per-graph roots), and
   note this interacts directly with fgdb-lc1t: if the manifest is a persistent structure, a branch
   fork shares it and stays O(1); if it is a flat list, the fork copies it and O(1) forking dies here
   rather than in tier R.
3. It is a durable format, so it owes an Appendix A catalog row.

NAME THE COST HONESTLY: this puts a piece of G0 catalog work on the critical path of the first
runnable engine. That is the ONE place where "catalog blocks engine" is true, as opposed to the
general case where it is not -- see the Track E steering note in
docs/REALITY_CHECK_AND_BRIDGE_PLAN.md. Do not let it become a precedent for the general case.

LAWS THIS BEAD OWES:
- a manifest written, closed and re-read resolves every partition it names, with the store having no
  in-memory state carried across (the fgdb-sim/tests/partition_lifecycle.rs shape);
- a manifest naming a partition whose root object is ABSENT fails closed with a typed error naming the
  missing OID -- it must not silently return a smaller graph, which is the failure mode that would
  look exactly like correct operation;
- a torn manifest write is either fully applied or fully absent (it rides the same two-fsync protocol
  as everything else; do not invent a second durability mechanism for it);
- and the round-trip law must use DISTINCT values per field. Two decoder offset defects have already
  been shipped and caught in this subsystem precisely because equal field values made a
  wrong-offset read indistinguishable from a right one.
close_reason: The defect is fully discharged and every piece is chain-certified. MECHANISM: a database directory durably reaches its partitions — RootSlot (PLAIN opener, ruled) -> FGSM manifest (fgdb-63w2) -> FGSR V2 root -> blocks/patches; checkpoint-selected open authenticates the slot's root against Chronicle's complete prefix (checkpoint_matches_stream) before accepting it, falls back to authoritative rebuild on a missing slot, refuses foreign/disagreeing slots, heals lagging ones, and republishes when the suffix advances the fold. Durable compaction survives reopen; the generated differential pins engine==oracle at every epoch across reopen and compaction; the v3 element-version heads are witnessed equal across every open path incl. post-compaction (the GoldBarn review's missing instrument, landed 452d926). REGISTRATION: all five formats in Appendix A kind-through-field — increment 1 kinds at reminted codes (d495385), increment 2 reachability edges (c328fb3), increment 3 full field tables + wire vocabulary incl. the catalog's first 128-bit spelling and the block digest's transcript recipe (06a08e0); epochs logical 63 / wire 47 / fields 82; each increment quiet-root-certified GATE_RC=0 with 33 PASS zero FAIL/UNRUN. RESIDUALS ROUTED: stripe_range tag reserved (fgdb-n90t w4); root additive fields split to fgdb-6lyc (first tier-d increment) and fgdb-w3-tier-d-ctj (premise re-derived + root-shape ruling recorded there); the RootSlot.root_manifest_oid opener-dependent target divergence is fgdb-clbr on fgdb-lc1t's persistence contract. Executed under the user's blanket delegation ('take over whatever you need to and make the optimal decisions').
