comments.text:
PREMISE RE-DERIVED 2026-08-01 BY ITS OWN AUTHOR, AND THE STATED FACT IS WRONG. The conclusion
survives, for a different and considerably larger reason. Read this before acting on the notes above.

WHAT I CLAIMED: "RootSlot.root_manifest_oid points at an object kind NOBODY HAS DEFINED."

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE. RootManifest is a LANDED, ACTIVE logical object kind — object_kind 0x0007,
status "active", golden_corpus corpus/logical/root_manifest/ (registries/logical_object_kinds.toml).
The whole chain resolves:

    RootSlot.root_manifest_oid  (field_tag 0x000d, oid256, reference_semantics "external_root")
      -> RootManifest.logical_state_root_ref   (StrongRef, its ONLY field)
        -> LogicalStateRoot.payload_ref        -> LogicalStatePayload
           LogicalStateRoot.logical_command_head -> LogicalCommandRecord

Nothing dangles. I wrote the original claim from a code grep, and the definition lives in the
registries — the exact mistake the "ask the checker, not the corpus" rule exists to prevent, made by
someone who had already written that rule down.

THE REAL DEFECT, which is worse. Follow the chain to its end and it terminates in
LogicalStatePayload, whose ENTIRE field set is two scalars: applied_logical_command_seq and
applied_commit_seq. So a recovered database learns WHICH SEQUENCE IT HAD APPLIED and nothing whatever
about where its graph data lives. Measured:

 - `grep target_schema_id = "PartitionRoot"` over registries/durable_fields.toml: ZERO hits. No field
   of any schema references a Strata partition root.
 - PartitionRoot appears in NO registry at all — not as a kind, not as a wire type, not even as a
   reservation.
 - DeltaBlockVersion has a RESERVATION ONLY: row plan:reservation:delta-block-version, code 0x04d4,
   disposition "reserved". It is not among the 555 landed [[kind]] rows.
 - Neither `FGSB` (BLOCK_MAGIC) nor `FGSR` (ROOT_MAGIC) appears anywhere under registries/.

So fgdb-strata writes TWO durable on-disk formats with magic numbers, versioned headers and canonical
encodings, and NEITHER is in the Appendix A catalog. That is the finding. "No database can be
reopened" is still exactly right, but the cause is not a dangling pointer in the manifest — it is that
the entire Strata tier sits outside the durable object graph and outside the normative format
contract.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND REOPEN. Appendix A is the normative on-disk contract and AGENTS.md's rule is
that no subsystem ships against an unenforced invariant. Every format law fgdb-strata currently
enforces, it enforces on its own authority in its own crate; the catalog does not know these objects
exist, so none of the catalog's cross-cutting machinery — identity class, construction order,
retention and cut rules, golden corpora, GC reachability under FG-INV-14 — applies to them.

REVISED SCOPE. This is no longer "add a field to the manifest". It is:
 1. Land DeltaBlockVersion at its reserved code 0x04d4 (the reservation exists, so per the bijection
    law mint AT that code and flip disposition to "existing" — do NOT allocate a fresh one).
 2. Reserve and land PartitionRoot, which has no code at all.
 3. Register the durable fields of both, matching the SOURCE spelling and ordinals in
    crates/fgdb-strata/src/{lib,root}.rs rather than alphabetical census order.
 4. Only THEN add the binding that makes reopen possible — a partition inventory reachable from
    LogicalStateRoot or LogicalStatePayload. This is the step my original notes described, and it is
    the last one, not the first.

Steps 1–3 are pin-re-freezing catalog work in a lane several panes are already in. Step 4 is the one
the spine (fgdb-j0vu) actually needs. They should probably be separate beads; I have not split them
because whoever picks this up should decide that with the catalog lane's current state in view.

WHAT I GOT RIGHT AND WHY IT STILL HOLDS: the interaction with fgdb-lc1t (a flat copy-on-fork
partition inventory kills O(1) forking), the "distinct values per field in the round-trip law" warning
(two decoder offset defects have already shipped here), and the fail-closed law for a manifest naming
an absent partition. Those were about the SHAPE of the eventual object and are unaffected by the
correction.

comments.text:
EXECUTABLE PLAN, 2026-08-01 (JadeSnow). Everything below was MEASURED at HEAD, not inferred. I held
the catalog token, scoped the work, and released it without editing — the pin cycle is multi-round and
I did not have the budget to finish it in one sitting, and abandoning it half-applied while holding
the token would be worse than not starting. Nothing here needs re-deriving.

=== THE COUPLING THAT MAKES THIS A TWO-ARTIFACT CHANGE ===

An `active` row in registries/logical_object_kinds.toml is NOT free. crates/fgdb-types/src/refs.rs
carries `active_logical_object_kinds! { ... }`, and the macro emits, per arm:

    const _: () = assert!(contains_bytes(LOGICAL_OBJECT_KIND_REGISTRY,
        concat!("object_kind = ", stringify!($code), "\nname = \"", $name, "\"\nstatus = \"active\"")));

plus ONE count assert:

    const _: () = assert!(count_bytes(LOGICAL_OBJECT_KIND_REGISTRY, ACTIVE_STATUS_ROW)
        == LogicalObjectKindCode::ALL_ACTIVE.len());

So adding an active TOML row WITHOUT a matching macro arm stops the whole workspace compiling, while
every registry gate stays green. This is not hypothetical: validate.rs:1195 records that 84418b2 did
exactly this with DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence (0x028f), took the count 10 -> 11, and left main
broken for hours. A checker now names the offending symbol in both directions
(validate_active_logical_kind_arms), so the failure is at least legible — but the two edits must land
in ONE commit.

Note the const assert matches EXACT BYTES including newlines, so the three keys must appear in that
order and adjacently in the TOML row.

=== STEP 1: DeltaBlockVersion ===

MINT AT THE RESERVED CODE. Do not allocate a fresh one — the reservation exists:

    [[reservation]]
    row_id = "plan:reservation:delta-block-version"
    slice_id = "plan"
    symbol = "DeltaBlockVersion"
    row_kind = "logical-kind"
    identity_class = "logical"
    code_reservation = "0x04d4"
    disposition = "reserved"          <- flip to "existing" in the same commit

Add the [[kind]] row at 0x04d4 with status = "active", and add the macro arm in refs.rs. The arm list
is in ascending code order, so 0x04d4 goes between 0x028f
(DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence) and 0x0550 (DurableCapabilityHeader).

max_size_bytes: take it from the SOURCE, not from a neighbour row. fgdb-strata already derives its
ceilings (root.rs has MAX_ENCODED_ROOT_BYTES = HEADER_LEN + MAX_ROOT_BLOCKS * REF_LEN); use the block
equivalent from crates/fgdb-strata/src/lib.rs rather than copying 16777216 off RootManifest.

golden_corpus: declare the path. VERIFIED that the directory need not exist — corpus/logical/ is
absent entirely today and every landed kind declares a path under it, so no checker requires the
directory. Declare corpus/logical/delta_block_version/ for consistency and do not create files.

construction_order: DeltaBlockVersion is a LEAF — it holds AdjacencyEntry rows and references no other
durable object. PartitionRoot references IT (by block_id). So its order must be strictly below
PartitionRoot's. Derive from both reference directions rather than from one consumer; the order law is
non-strict and re-ordering a landed kind is cheap, so this is not the risky part.

=== STEP 2: PartitionRoot — CHECK THE RESERVATION LAW FIRST ===

PartitionRoot has NO code anywhere: not a kind, not a wire type, not a reservation. Verified by
grepping every file under registries/.

BEFORE reserving one, resolve this: the reservation bijection law says never reserve a NON-StrongRef
family. Nothing references PartitionRoot today, so at this instant it is not a StrongRef target — it
only becomes one when step 3 lands the binding. Either the law permits reserving in anticipation, or
steps 2 and 3 must land together so the referent exists when the code is minted. ASK THE CHECKER
(synthesize the row and run validate_identity) rather than reasoning it out; that is what settled
three previous "open conventions" that turned out to be laws already.

=== STEP 3: THE BINDING, which is what the spine actually needs ===

Only after 1 and 2. Today the chain is:
    RootSlot.root_manifest_oid -> RootManifest.logical_state_root_ref
      -> LogicalStateRoot.{payload_ref, logical_command_head}
        -> LogicalStatePayload { applied_logical_command_seq, applied_commit_seq }   <- ends here

LogicalStatePayload's ENTIRE field set is those two scalars, so recovery learns which sequence it
applied and nothing about where the graph lives. The binding must carry, per live partition, the
(graph, partition) coordinate and the PartitionRoot's object id — Strata already guarantees a
partition reopens from a 32-byte identity, so nothing more is needed.

WHERE IT HANGS interacts with fgdb-lc1t's persistence contract (routed there by MistyJay): the root
object "must reach a persistent content-addressed directory from graph and branch bindings to
partition leaf roots" rather than "a flat copy-on-fork partition inventory". A flat list makes fork
O(partitions) and kills O(1) branching here rather than in tier R. Read that comment on fgdb-ge6a and
fgdb-w3-tier-r-0tj before choosing the shape.

=== PIN EXPOSURE, measured ===

Four test files read logical_object_kinds: tools/registry-check/tests/{identity,metamorphic,
violation_witnesses,workspace_topology}.rs, and identity.rs carries sha256 digest pins. Expect a
multi-round re-freeze. Follow the established procedure: parse new pin values from the loader's own
drift messages, never hard-code them; re-derive from the BASE each round because HEAD moves several
times per increment; and regenerate any generated artifact LAST because it fail-closes.

=== ORDER OF WORK ===

Steps 1 and 2/3 are separable and 1 is self-contained, so land 1 first as its own commit — it converts
"a format nobody registered" into "a registered format", which is worth having even if the binding
takes longer. Consider splitting this bead at that seam once someone starts.

STEP 1. I took the catalog token to start it, measured the format first, released the token without

WHAT I GOT WRONG. My plan said "land DeltaBlockVersion at its reserved 0x04d4" as a self-contained

freezes it as the normative contract, and the format fgdb-strata writes today is NOT the format the
plan specifies — it is an early subset that the plan explicitly rules out.

MEASURED, field by field. The plan's normative unit (fgdb-w3-tier-d-ctj, Design section) is:

    DeltaBlockVersion { format, partition_id, descriptor_key, stripe_range, sorted_entries[],
                        visibility_intervals[], property_patch_refs[],
                        predecessor: ConditionalCoordinateRef<DeltaBlockVersion>?,
                        canonical_logical_digest }

What crates/fgdb-strata/src/lib.rs actually writes:

    HEADER_LEN = 4 + 2 + 4                      // magic, format, entry count. That is all.
    ENTRY_LEN  = 16 + 8 + 16 + 16 + 8 + 8 = 72  // src, relation, dst, eid, created_at, retired_at

So SIX of the nine normative fields are absent: partition_id, descriptor_key, stripe_range,
property_patch_refs, predecessor, canonical_logical_digest. Visibility exists only as inline
created_at/retired_at rather than the specified interval array.

AND THE ENTRY ENCODING IS THE ONE THE PLAN NAMES AS WRONG. It requires entries "encoded under the
registered identity-column codec (w3-identity-encoding; <=16 B/entry -- raw 128-bit identities would
cap near 95 entries)" in a block of "about 4 KiB ... at most 256 entries". Today's entry is 72 bytes
of RAW 128-bit identities -- precisely the layout that sentence exists to forbid, and at 72 B/entry a
4 KiB block holds 56 entries, not 256. Freezing this in the catalog would enshrine a >4x density
regression as the normative on-disk contract, and undoing it later is a breaking-major format change
plus a catalog re-pin cycle.

SO THE DEPENDENCY IS RIGHT AND I SHOULD NOT HAVE REMOVED IT EARLIER. fgdb-w3-tier-d-ctj gates this
bead because you cannot register a format before the format exists. Note its rollup reads
"closed (3 closed)" -- that counts CHILD BEADS, not scope. Its own normative surface (skip-list
nodes, per-block MVCC predecessor chains, bump arenas + EBR, the bounded hot-burst overflow log and
its drain actor, hub striping, DeltaPartitionRoot's descriptor_map_ref and overflow_state) is
substantially unbuilt. A closed rollup is not a finished bead.

WHAT SURVIVES, and it still matters: a durable format IS in production use today with no catalog row,
so none of the catalog's cross-cutting machinery reaches the only place graph data lives. That is a
real exposure and it is what this bead should track. But the remedy is to FINISH THE FORMAT and
register it once, not to register the interim shape and churn it.

REVISED SEQUENCING:
 1. fgdb-w3-tier-d-ctj brings the block to its normative field set and the w3-identity-encoding
    codec. (This is also where the 4 KiB / 256-entry density target is either met or renegotiated
    with evidence.)
 2. Register DeltaBlockVersion at the reserved 0x04d4 AND PartitionRoot together, once the shapes
    are settled. The two-artifact coupling in my earlier comment (TOML row + active_logical_object_kinds!
    arm in crates/fgdb-types/src/refs.rs, in ONE commit) is still accurate and still the trap -- keep
    that part.
 3. Then the partition binding the spine needs.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE REALITY CHECK's framing, which I also had slightly wrong: I called this "the one
place where catalog blocks engine". It is the reverse. The ENGINE format is unfinished, and
registration is correctly waiting on it. There is no catalog work on the critical path here that
could be started today; the critical path runs through tier D itself.

IN THE MEANTIME the exposure should be visible rather than silent. Worth considering: a note at the
BLOCK_MAGIC/BLOCK_FORMAT_V2 definition stating that this format is deliberately unregistered pending
fgdb-w3-tier-d-ctj, so a reader does not assume catalog coverage that does not exist.

title: Owner ruling: 10 generated closed unions have no source-spelled arm set, so line 328 forbids landing them — 7 are outside ww9g
description:
MEASURED at d9d4e28. Successor/sibling of fgdb-ww9g, whose 3 remaining union-shaped pairs are
3 of the 10 symbols below. Filed because deciding ww9g's 3 pairs alone would settle, on
identical evidence, a question 7 co-shaped siblings leave open.

## THE GOVERNING LAW is source line 328 -- OUTSIDE the Appendix A range (1388-2728)
"Generated reference unions are exact rather than erased. For each containing schema and role,
 `durable_fields.toml` emits a finite tagged union such as `LocalCommandInputRef`,
 `MetaAppliedResultRef`, `ShardProtocolEvidenceRef`, or `MandatoryInventoryRef`; EVERY ARM NAMES
 ONE TOP-LEVEL TARGET SCHEMA and carries the target's canonical typed reference encoding. Bare
 `StrongRef`, `StrongRef<A|B>`, `StrongRef[]`, `result_refs[StrongRef]`, slash-separated
 pseudo-types, or A GENERIC `RegisteredStrongRef` WITHOUT A CONTAINING-SCHEMA-GENERATED ARM SET
 ARE INVALID IN NORMATIVE BYTES."

So an arm set is a precondition for landing one of these, and it must be source-derived.

## THE MEASUREMENT -- total, zero slack, 13 of 13
Population: every symbol appearing in a "generated closed ... union" definition sentence.
19 matched the pattern. RaftLogSegment is a FALSE POSITIVE (L1560 says it "CARRIES ... a
generated closed command union" -- carrier, not union). 5 have no [[top_level_candidate]] row.
That leaves 13 real candidates:

  arm set SPELLED INLINE in the source  ->  3 of 3 CLASSIFIED
      ContinuityAuthorityCurrentBasis<Role>   L2225  logical
      LifecycleAuthoritySource<Role>          L2697  logical
      DurableCapabilityConsumerTerminalTarget L2657  WIRE
  arm set NOT SPELLED                   -> 10 of 10 UNCLASSIFIED

The wire/logical discriminator among the classified 3 is legible: the one that went WIRE is the
one whose source declares a TAG ENCODING -- "a generated closed `u16` union" with explicit
`0x0001`/`0x0002` arm codes -- and it carries a [[union]] row plus a wire_type row. The two
logical ones spell arms but declare no tag width, and have logical_kind projections and no
[[union]] row. Consistent with the corpus split: of 385 distinct [[union]] union_names, 101 are
also wire types (92 kind="union", 9 kind="discriminant") and 32 are also logical kinds.

DETECTOR CAVEAT, stated because it bit me: a first inline-arm regex with a 400-char window
returned False for ContinuityAuthorityCurrentBasis and LifecycleAuthoritySource, both of which
spell arms inline -- the window truncated before the closing backtick. The corrected detector
runs to the close of the backtick span and passes that eyeball control. Keep the control if you
re-run this: an under-detecting matcher turns the law into a fake 4/4-vs-10/10, and the
conclusion happens to survive, which is worse than a clean failure.

## A ZERO I LICENSED AND THEN REJECTED -- do not repeat it
The catalog holds 5 [[reference_union]] rows and 8 [[reference_union_arm]] rows, and 5 of 5 have
NO wire_type row and NO logical_kind row. That looks like "a reference union is never
projected". IT IS NOT A LAW, it is a SELECTION ARTIFACT: none of those 5 has a
[[top_level_candidate]] row either, because 4 are named only at line 328 and
LogicalCommandInputRef appears in the source ZERO times -- generated names outside the census
range. catalog_candidate_class_unproved never applied to them. Their missing projection is
evidence about NON-candidates. There is also no checker law forbidding a reference-union name
from carrying a projection row (the only reference_union logic in appendix_a.rs is source-key
reconstruction at 12180-12295). A zero at n=5 over a self-selected set licenses nothing.

## WHAT PROVES A CLASS -- for anyone tempted to fix this by authoring union rows
appendix_a.rs:9265 `fn projection_identity_class` is the whole authority, a closed five-way map:
logical-kind=>logical, physical-kind=>physical, bootstrap-frame=>bootstrap,
prebootstrap-kind=>prebootstrap, wire-type=>wire, _=>None. So [[union]], [[reference_union]],
[[union_arm]], [[reference_union_arm]], [[field]] and [[target]] rows prove NOTHING. Authoring
a union's entire structure does not classify its candidate.

## THE 10, and what the source gives for each arm set
Three are fgdb-ww9g's (with their B twins, which share the same definition sentence and
therefore the same status; the population regex captures only the first backticked symbol of
an "`A` and `B` are ..." sentence, which is why the twins do not appear as separate rows):
  LocalReadWitnessRef | LocalWriteSummaryRef        a04:1488  arm set UNKNOWN
  ResultLeaseRef | ResultSemanticOwnerRef           a04:1510  arm TAGS derivable, targets not
  RestoreReconciliationEvidenceRef<Role> | RestoreExplicitRetentionOwnerRef<Role>
                                                   a19:2547  14 class names, targets not

SEVEN are outside ww9g and are the reason this is a separate bead:
  DeltaRetentionObligationRef<Role>
  LocalConflictProofRef                    a04:1476 -- the cleanest specimen of the shape:
      "a generated closed union over version, absence/range, path, constraint, and final-write
      proof objects" -- five classes named, zero targets named.
  RecoveryBridgeDependencyRef<Role>
  RemoteGrantTargetRef
  RestoreReadyClosureRef<Role>
  RestoreSourceKeyAccessTerminalProjection<Role>
  ShardReadWitnessRef                      -- the Shard sibling of ww9g's LocalReadWitnessRef:
      same family, same missing registry, NOT in ww9g's 13.

## A GENUINE SOURCE TENSION the owner must resolve (not guessable)
`ResultSemanticOwnerRef` is given two different arm sets:
  a04:1490 -- a generated VIEW of result_owner_arms.toml, arms TerminalRead |
              AutocommitWriteTerminal | Statement | DpResult | ReplayExecution  (FIVE)
  a04:1510 -- a closed ROLE union corresponding to `ResultManifestRef`, arms Local | Sharded (TWO)
The generic differs too: `<Role>` at 1490 and 1512, bare at 1510.

## THE ASK
A ruling on the family, in this order:
 1. Is "no source-spelled arm set => stays unclassified" the intended terminal rule, or is the
    missing arm set an erratum to be supplied in the source? (Line 328 says these are emitted
    by durable_fields.toml per containing schema + role, which reads like the arm set is
    GENERATED rather than prose-declared -- in which case the generator, not the prose, is the
    authority and this whole cohort is waiting on it.)
 2. If arm sets are to be supplied: where do "the registered Local witness/summary targets"
    live? The phrase occurs ONCE in the source. There is no witness-target registry, and the
    only two *_arms.toml families named anywhere are result_owner_arms.toml (@1490) and
    resume_capability_arms.toml (@1010).
 3. Resolve the ResultSemanticOwnerRef arm-set contradiction above.

## DO NOT
Do not invent an arm set to unblock a mint, and do not classify one of these by inventing a
type. Both are the same error as the one fgdb-ww9g's "Do not" section forbids, and line 328
makes the invented-arm-set version a normative-bytes violation rather than merely a guess.
close_reason: Owner ruled all three asks (Q1 wait-on-generator terminal rule, Q2 moot, Q3 two-objects/1510-renames via amendment queue); the cohort's unclassified state is now the ruled steady state

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
RULED 2026-08-02 (mv6g sitting rounds 1 and 5, owner direct). All three asks answered:

Q1 - TERMINAL RULE CONFIRMED: "no source-spelled arm set => stays unclassified" is the
intended terminal rule for this cohort. The 10 unions WAIT ON THE GENERATOR (the
durable_fields.toml emission machinery line 328 describes); no source amendments, no
hand-minting. Consistent with the I-0 ruling that made command_contracts.toml the normative
arm-set authority for the command family unions - the same generator-normative principle,
one registry over.

Q2 - MOOT under Q1: arm sets are not to be prose-supplied, so "where do the registered
Local witness/summary targets live" has no pending consumer. If the generator's inputs
someday need a witness-target registry, that is the generator lane's design work.

Q3 - TWO OBJECTS; 1510 MUST RENAME: the five-arm generated owner-kind view (a04:1490,
<Role>, result_owner_arms.toml) keeps the name ResultSemanticOwnerRef. The two-role closed
union at a04:1510 is a DIFFERENT object wrongly sharing the name and gets renamed in a
source amendment (a role-qualified sibling of ResultManifestRef). The rename rides the
amendment queue opened by the I-7 ruling (source amendments held for owner confirmation).

Closing: the family ruling this bead asked for exists. The 10 stay unclassified BY RULE
(not by neglect); the rename is tracked in the amendment queue. Nobody should reopen this
to "fix" an unclassified member of the cohort - that is now the ruled steady state until
the generator emits.
Full record: /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/OWNER_RULINGS.md, mv6g rounds 1 and 5.

title: g0_identity_e2e stages 114 fixtures at 326MB per run — 69% of it 27 unshared copies of .beads/issues.jsonl — and disk_hygiene.sh reaps nothing
description:

building on it. 1j16's filed subject is FIXED (3caaeb0) and its pool reclaimed;
this is what replaced it, and per run it is LARGER than the defect 1j16 named.

  Live pool: 34 such dirs, 10.50 GB, spanning 07:34:08 -> 20:00:07 on 2026-07-27

## What re-derivation established, stated because a negative is a result

 * private_subject.sh dirs: FILED 113 / 18.5 GB -> MEASURED 0 / 0.00 GB.
 * The classifier was CONTROLLED before the zero was believed: post-3caaeb0 the
   subject lives in the shared cache and bin/ holds only `stale-probe`, so
   `bin/registry-check` correctly reports absence rather than being broken by a
   layout change. The population is gone; the instrument is not.
 * 1j16's premise "reclaiming this pool alone ends the disk emergency" is
   FALSIFIED: it was reclaimed, the fix landed, and disk is STILL 95% / 52 GB.
   Real consumers: /data/tmp/claude-1000 121 GB, cargo-target 60 GB.

## scripts/disk_hygiene.sh EXISTS AND REAPS NOTHING

31 lines. Measured by five independent greps, each read by its own exit code:
absent `fgdb-subject`, absent `tmp.`, absent `appendix-baseline`, absent
`fgdb-check-gates`, absent `reap|delete|rm `. 1j16 option 2 pointed at this
script as "one accountable reaper"; it names no pool and removes nothing, so the
deferral-to-hygiene is still a deferral to nobody. That is a SEPARATE defect from
the staging cost and is the reason the pool accrues at all.

## The fix that landed has its own unreaped accumulation

/data/tmp/fgdb-subject: 24 subject-<sha> dirs, 1.8 GB. Correct by design -- one
per distinct checker-source tree state -- but unbounded over time and covered by
no reaper. Small today; name it now rather than re-discover it at 100%.

## Fix options, cheapest first (NOT implemented; this bead is the measurement)

1. SHARE THE CORPUS ACROSS FIXTURES. Only 27 of 114 fixtures read
   .beads/issues.jsonl, and every one of them reads the SAME bytes. Hard-link or
   symlink it instead of copying: -224 MB per run, ~69%, with no behaviour change
   for the 87 fixtures that never open it. CAUTION: a fixture that MUTATES the
   corpus to prove a negative must keep a private copy -- classify by whether the
   fixture writes it, not by whether it reads it, and prove the split.
2. DECLARE A LIFETIME on the $WORK dir, as 1j16 asked for and did not get.
3. MAKE disk_hygiene.sh ACTUALLY REAP, with the pools named. Today it is a
   31-line file that satisfies the letter of "an accountable reaper exists".

## CONTROL THE FIX (it must be able to fail)

Count bytes written per run BEFORE and AFTER: the 27-copy figure is the
prediction, so a fix that does not move it did not do what it claims. Then run
g0_identity_e2e and confirm the SAME assertion set passes -- a staging change
that silently drops a fixture buys disk by losing a test. And neuter the sharing
to confirm the 326 MB returns; a saving that survives the fix being disabled was
never the fix.

## Provenance

Successor to fgdb-1j16 (closed on re-derivation, not on repair). Do not re-file
1j16's numbers: they were true at HEAD eda507f and are dead at 6dd12eb.

title: A one-line change to render_logical leaves registry-check all GREEN and makes fgdb-types fail to compile: the projection is byte-compared to the generator, not to the const asserts that consume it
notes:
FINDING from verifying fgdb-active-kind-arm-bijection-break-cuvx (pane2,
2026-07-26). cuvx itself is FIXED and its gate is live and non-vacuous; this is
the door that gate does not cover.

CORRECTION FIRST. An earlier version of this bead claimed a hand-added COMMENT
in registries/logical_object_kinds.toml was invisible to the gate. That was
WRONG, and wrong for an instructive reason: it was measured with a checker
binary built from an older HEAD, which reported 12 phantom pin-drift violations
on a tree that was actually clean, so the "no new violation" delta was taken
against a false red baseline. Rebuilt from the current HEAD, `registry-check
all` is GREEN on main, and a hand-edited comment IS caught -- `projection_byte_diff`
fires immediately. See [[stale-binary-reports-phantom-pin-drift]]. The real
finding survives and is narrower and sharper.

## The gap

`registries/logical_object_kinds.toml` has TWO consumers with different laws.

  * `registry-check all` byte-compares the file against what
    `appendix_a.rs::render_logical` regenerates. Law: "the file equals the
    generator's output."
  * `crates/fgdb-types/src/refs.rs` embeds it with `include_bytes!` and asserts
    over its raw BYTES at compile time. Law: "`status = \"active\"` occurs
    exactly ALL_ACTIVE.len() times (refs.rs:134), and for every arm the three
    fields `object_kind = <code>\\nname = \"<name>\"\\nstatus = \"active\"` are
    ADJACENT IN THAT ORDER (refs.rs:121)."

A hand edit violates both, so it is caught. A GENERATOR change violates only the
second -- regenerate, and the file matches the generator by construction, so the
byte-compare is satisfied while the const assert is not. The gate cannot see it,
not because it is weak, but because the property it checks is no longer the
property being broken.

## MEASURED end to end, on a pristine `git archive HEAD` with a HEAD-built checker

Baseline: `registry-check all` exit 0, zero violations. Probe compiles clean.
(Probe = real refs.rs and real ids.rs copied VERBATIM, `cmp`-clean, into a
depth-matched tree so `include_bytes!(\"../../../registries/...\")` resolves to
the tree under test. No Rust source was edited.)

MUTATION -- swap two lines in `render_logical` (appendix_a.rs:13650) so it emits
`name` before `object_kind`. Same data, valid TOML, no row changed:

        write_string(&mut out, \"name\", &row.name);
        writeln!(&mut out, \"object_kind = {:#06x}\", row.object_kind)

Then `registry-check appendix-regenerate` to produce the projection the mutated
generator wants, and:

    registry-check all --root <archive>   ->  exit 0, ZERO violations
    compile the probe                     ->  exit 1
        error[E0080]: evaluation panicked: assertion failed:
        contains_bytes(LOGICAL_OBJECT_KIND_REGISTRY, ...)

Green gate, broken workspace. That is precisely cuvx's failure mode, reached
through a door 47807be does not cover.

## Why this is P1 and not theoretical

  * `fgdb-types` is a foundation crate, so this takes down every pane's
    `cargo check`, `clippy`, `test`, and `ubs`.
  * The diagnostic is an opaque const-eval panic naming `contains_bytes`, with
    no file, no row, and no hint that a generator refactor caused it.
  * NOTHING DECLARES THE ORDER. There is no comment in `render_logical`, no
    test, and no assertion tying its field order to refs.rs. The sibling
    emitters already disagree with it: `render_physical` puts `identity_law`
    BETWEEN `name` and `status`; `render_bootstrap` puts `status` right after
    `name`. The orders are per-projection accidents, not a convention anyone is
    holding.
  * `appendix_a.rs` is under active edit by several panes. A near miss already
    happened tonight: c5570ce rewrote `construction_order` values in every row.
    That field sits AFTER `status`, so the adjacency held. Had the same
    increment moved a field between `name` and `status`, main would have gone
    down again with a green gate.
  * The same class covers `projection_header`: adding a lifecycle sentence
    mentioning `status = \"active\"` to the generated header would break
    refs.rs:134's count with the gate green.

## Candidate repairs (fgdb-types / appendix_a owners decide)

1. RECOMMENDED, and small: assert the byte-layout contract where the generator
   lives. In validate.rs beside the existing arm checker, require that every
   `status = \"active\"` occurrence in the projection is inside a `[[kind]]`
   row, and that `object_kind`/`name`/`status` are adjacent in that order.
   Turns an undeclared coupling into a declared one that fails with a named row
   instead of E0080.
2. Make the compile-time law match the gate's law -- parse `[[kind]]`-scoped
   status in the const fn instead of counting a raw substring. Costs a const
   TOML scanner; removes the adjacency requirement entirely.
3. Decouple: have refs.rs consume a generated Rust const table rather than
   `include_bytes!` of a TOML projection.

## Do not fix by deleting the const asserts

They are the only thing that has ever caught this class. The 47807be gate exists
because they fire too late and too opaquely -- not because they are redundant.
It provably cannot see this mutation.

## Reproduction recipe (~2s, no build slot, no cargo)

  cp crates/fgdb-types/src/{refs.rs,ids.rs} <probe>/crates/fgdb-types/src/
  printf 'pub mod ids;\npub mod refs;\n' > <probe>/crates/fgdb-types/src/lib.rs
  cp registries/logical_object_kinds.toml <probe>/registries/
  rustc --edition 2024 --crate-type rlib --crate-name probe \
        <probe>/crates/fgdb-types/src/lib.rs -o <probe>/probe.rlib

Both const asserts are exercised, `refs.rs` stays verbatim, and only the
registry bytes vary. Any fix here should carry this as its witness.
close_reason: Added explicit generator-to-fgdb-types logical projection layout validation; identity remains green and the documented generator mutation now has a named checker law.

title: Strata durable merge and compaction accept EId rebirth or topology drift across blocks
description: Fresh-eyes audit of 8d651fa (fgdb-0trr) at HEAD 3d7475a. BlockWriter permanently spends EId, but merge_neighbours keys versions by (EId, created_at) only after filtering to the requested (src, relation), and compact keys by (src, relation, dst, EId, created_at). Therefore individually canonical blocks can restate one EId/version with changed topology without superseding the old adjacency, or introduce a later non-overlapping birth for a permanently spent EId. The reader can silently keep the old edge live, expose the moved edge under another query, or accept non-overlapping identity reuse; compaction emits rather than refuses the malformed history. Repair must validate one immutable (src, relation, dst, created_at) identity per EId across publication order before answering or compacting, return a typed error with both identities, keep lawful retirement restatements and parallel EIds working, and mutation/regression-test topology drift plus non-overlapping EId rebirth. Compaction should become fallible rather than emit a root the read path rejects; update all callers directly (early development, no compatibility wrapper).

title: Strata-side incremental publish: publish_and_reopen is O(blocks) per commit (45.9ms @ 96 commits), next dominant write-cost term after fujt
notes:

ORIGINAL PREMISE: publish_and_reopen grows 0.5ms@8 -> 15.3ms@96 (ffe05f6 attribution), 45.9ms@96 replica; fix direction strata-side incremental publish; INTERACTS with fgdb-2t7q sitting (ruling pack /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/s62_amendment_pack.md). title: The durable-fields epoch is hardcoded in tests/identity.rs in two places; every epoch bump silently reproduces un4g's 12 failures
notes:
Filed by pane2 from landing fgdb-a03-local-state-txn-rxjg (7e71af6). Third
occurrence tonight of the same coupling; the first two were repaired in silence.

## The coupling

`registries/durable_fields.toml` is a GENERATED projection whose
`registry_epoch` is declared in `registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml`
(`[[projection_epoch]] registry = "durable_fields"`). Adding any field row
requires bumping it, because a released row set is append-only.

`tools/registry-check/tests/identity.rs` hardcodes that same epoch in TWO
places inside `ordinary_top_level_union_fixture`:

    line 177   registry_epoch = 70      <- inside the fixture's TOML text
    line 219   assert_eq!(epoch, 70);   <- and asserted again in Rust

Nothing ties either to the registry. So every epoch bump makes the fixture
stale, and the fixture is consumed by eleven ordinary-union tests plus the
historical witness.

## The signature, which is exact and now reproduced three times

    105 passed / 12 failed, the SAME twelve names every time:

      idr_assignment_history_and_epoch_are_frozen
      idr_ordinary_top_level_union_parses_and_validates
      idr_ordinary_union_arm_bound_must_fit_union_bound
      idr_ordinary_union_embedded_field_requires_exact_anchor
      idr_ordinary_union_rejects_duplicate_arm_tag
      idr_ordinary_union_rejects_invalid_inline_record_hash
      idr_ordinary_union_rejects_reference_union_name_collision
      idr_ordinary_union_rejects_unresolved_containing_schema
      idr_ordinary_union_rejects_wire_type_name_collision
      idr_reference_union_rejects_ordinary_union_name_collision
      idr_wire_backed_top_level_union_requires_exact_cross_index
      idr_wire_backed_top_level_union_validates_every_consumer

Occurrences:
  1. epoch 68 -> 69. Filed as fgdb-un4g. Fixed incidentally by 8e5cd57
     (`test(a15): carry key identity into release witnesses`), which bumped the
     fixture for its own reasons. Nobody recorded it as a fix.
  2. epoch 69 -> 70. Same silent path; the fixture was at 70 by the time I
     measured, with no bead naming the repair.
  3. epoch 70 -> 71, mine, in 7e71af6. I reproduced all twelve exactly and
     repaired both sites in the same commit.

FIXING ONLY LINE 177 IS A TRAP AND I FELL IN IT. That took 12 failures to 15,
not to 0 -- three MORE tests fail, because the Rust `assert_eq!(epoch, 70)` at
line 219 then contradicts the fixture text it just parsed. The intermediate
state is strictly worse than the original and its failure set does not look
like this bead's. Anyone repairing this must change BOTH sites.

## Why a guard, not another repair

Every occurrence has been repaired by hand, and two of the three were repaired
without anyone recording that they had been. The next epoch bump reproduces it.
The failure lands on whoever bumps the epoch, is not obviously about the
fixture, and reads exactly like they broke the ordinary-union laws.

## Candidate guards (owner's call; I did not implement one)

1. SMALLEST: derive the fixture's epoch from the registry at test time --
   read `identity::load_identity(...).fields_epoch` and interpolate it into the
   fixture text rather than hardcoding, dropping the line-219 assert or
   asserting equality against the same source. The fixture's purpose is the
   UNION shape; the epoch is incidental to it.
2. Assert the coupling explicitly: one test that
   `ordinary_top_level_union_fixture`'s declared epoch equals
   durable_fields' released epoch, failing with a message that names the two
   files and both line numbers. Cheap, and it makes the next drift self-naming
   instead of arriving as twelve unrelated-looking union failures.
3. Reject the general shape: no test fixture may hardcode a released registry
   epoch. That is the real law, and it likely has siblings -- I did NOT sweep
   for other hardcoded epochs in the fixtures, and that sweep is part of this
   bead.

(1)+(2) together are recommended: derive it, and assert the derivation, so the
guard cannot itself go quietly stale.

## Verification note for whoever takes it

The whole loop is lock-free and needs no build slot or cargo:
  CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR=<repo>/tools/registry-check rustc --edition 2024 \
    --crate-type rlib --crate-name registry_check tools/registry-check/src/lib.rs -o <sp>/l.rlib
  CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR=<repo>/tools/registry-check rustc --edition 2024 --test \
    --crate-name identity tools/registry-check/tests/identity.rs \
    --extern registry_check=<sp>/l.rlib -L <sp> -o <sp>/t
Parallel run ~41s, serial ~279s. Both runners give the same 12; this has never
been a race.
close_reason: PREMISE FALSIFIED ON AXIS A (EXISTENCE), per fgdb-rhvi's procedure. THE DEFECT IS ALREADY FIXED. Commit 47df9c4 'test(identity): derive the union fixture's epoch instead of retyping it [fgdb-un4g]' landed glo0's OWN recommended candidate 1, and effectively candidate 2 as well: ORDINARY_UNION_FIXTURE_SOURCE now carries the placeholder 'registry_epoch = @EPOCH@', interpolated at identity.rs:319 from identity.fields_epoch, and @EPOCH@ is deliberately NOT VALID TOML so a substitution that stops happening is a loud parse error. The line-219 literal assert is gone; identity.rs:2954 now asserts against catalog.identity.fields_epoch, i.e. the registry itself. glo0's blocker fgdb-un4g is CLOSED. CLASSIFIER CONTROLLED BOTH DIRECTIONS before believing the collapse (rhvi step 2): at the pre-fix commit 5328b64 the same grep FINDS 'registry_epoch = 72' (line 177) and 'assert_eq!(epoch, 72)' (line 219) - the two sites glo0 names, at the epoch they had reached by then; at HEAD it finds ZERO. EMPIRICAL CONFIRMATION OF THE PREMISE ITSELF: glo0's claim was 'every epoch bump silently reproduces un4g's 12 failures'. durable_fields has gone 71 -> 77 since glo0 was filed, SIX BUMPS, with no recurrence and no bead. AXIS E (COMPLETENESS) - glo0's own unfiled step zero, the sweep it says it did NOT do, is NOW DONE AND CLEAN: across all 11 tools/registry-check/tests/*.rs there are ZERO asserts against a literal epoch, and only 2 literal 'registry_epoch =' occurrences, both = 1 and both replacen SEARCH STRINGS in a negative-fixture builder rather than fixture declarations. Candidate guard 3's claim that the shape 'likely has siblings' is FALSIFIED: zero siblings. NO REPAIR OWED - a standing guard would guard an empty population, and the landed fix is self-proving via the invalid-TOML placeholder. RESIDUAL FILED as fgdb-fixture-literal-epoch-search-wps6: those 2 replacen search strings are a literal released epoch, matching today only because physical_record_kinds and prebootstrap_artifact_kinds are both still at epoch 1. Measured, not assumed, by reading the harness: the consumer is .expect_err(), so if both bump the test PANICS LOUD rather than going vacuous - the opposite of glo0's filed failure mode, hence P3 not P1.

title: The state-value field class is 190 candidates across 18 slices with exactly 1 landed precedent: rule it or it blocks every remaining slice
description:
A large, uniform, appendix-wide class of field candidates declares its type as a STATE VALUE rather
than a type: either a `Union::Variant` path or a bare name that the catalog knows only as a
`source_arm_name`. Nobody has ruled on how such a row lands, so almost none of them have landed, and
the class is now the single largest blocker on slice completion closure.

## The measurement, at HEAD 43a1b73

One reader (standalone rustc over appendix_source.rs + hash.rs, full Appendix lines 1388..2728, all
21 live slice boundaries from the catalog's own [[slice]] rows): 11740 field candidates over 1020
owners.

A candidate is in the class if its exact type is `X::Y`, OR is a bare CamelCase name that appears in
the catalog as a `source_arm_name` and is NOT itself a registered identity (not a `name`,
`union_name`, or `symbol` anywhere).

    TRUE state-value field candidates:   190
      landed as a [[field]] row:           1
      unlanded:                          189
    slices affected: 18 of 21
      a01 1, a03 24, a05 14, a06 1, a07 52, a08 17, a09 1, a10 4, a11 1, a13 3,
      a14 1, a15 12, a16 4, a17 1, a18 6, a19 2, a20 6, a21 40

THE ENTIRE PRECEDENT BASE IS ONE ROW:
    a01  RemoteRetentionGrantRecord.state :: Active
         -> exact_wire_type = "u8", identity_class = "inline", max_size_bytes = 1

Two guards on that number, because a loose classifier makes this look solved when it is not. A first
sweep that did not exclude registered identities reported 303 candidates and 22 landed; 20 of those
22 are `WeakStateIdentity` / `WeakMarkerIdentity` / `StrongRef` / `StrongCommandRef` — real
registered types that merely also occur as an arm name somewhere. They are not precedent for
anything. And a strict `X::Y`-only sweep reports 94 candidates and 0 landed. Whichever way the
boundary is drawn, the precedent base is 0 or 1 rows against 94–190 candidates.

## Why the one precedent should not simply be copied

`u8` + `inline` encodes the discriminant but DROPS the constraint. Every a20 member of this class is
an `expected_*` precondition field — `expected_meta_pending_state:OperationalPendingIndependentReopen::Sealed`
names ONE admissible variant, and the whole point of the field is that the command is rejected in any
other state. A bare `u8` cannot express "only 0x02 is admissible here", so the durable format would
silently lose the precondition the source states. That is a format defect, not a style choice, which
is why this needs a ruling and not a pattern-match.

The shape the source seems to want is a tag-refined scalar — the same instrument already minted for
references (`OperationalRestoreTerminalPinBasisRef` admits only arm 0x0001 of its union). Whether the
answer is that, or `WeakStateIdentity` plus a documented refinement, or something else, is the
ruling.

## What it blocks in a20 specifically (fgdb-a20-restore-promotion-ivsp)

a20's field partition is 182 = 50 landed + 68 top-level source-typeless + 55 interior + 9 residue.
SEVEN of the 9 are this class:
    CatalogActivatedHidden.admission                                   :: CompositePromotionReceiptRequired
    GlobalRestoreServiceCompletionSpec.expected_meta_pending_state     :: OperationalPendingIndependentReopen::Sealed
    GlobalRestoreServiceCompletionSpec.expected_restore_registry_state :: PromotedAwaitingReopen
    LocalRestoreServiceCompletionSpec.expected_pending_state           :: OperationalPendingIndependentReopen::Sealed
    LocalRestoreServiceCompletionSpec.expected_restore_registry_state  :: PromotedAwaitingReopen
    ServiceCatalogPromotionReservationReceipt.state                    :: ReservedHiddenNonexpiring
    ShardRestoreReopenConfirmSpec.expected_pending_state               :: OperationalPendingIndependentReopen::Sealed
The remaining 2 are blocked on fgdb-qh3r. So a20 cannot reach completion closure on either count,
and its [[slice]] row is still definition_status = "declared".

Note two of the four type names are registered NOWHERE in the catalog — `ReservedHiddenNonexpiring`
and `CompositePromotionReceiptRequired` have zero occurrences in any role. The other two occur
exactly once each, as a landed `source_arm_name`: `OperationalPendingIndependentReopen` on a05
GlobalStatePayloadBootstrapPhase arm 0x0004, `PromotedAwaitingReopen` on a18 LocalRestorePhase arm
0x0003. So even the ruling's inputs are not uniformly present, and the two unregistered names may be
a separate defect worth checking before the ruling is written.

## Do not resolve it slice by slice

18 slices are affected and a21 alone holds 40. If each slice invents its own shape the durable format
acquires 18 dialects for one construct, and unlike a construction_order that is cheap to redo, a
landed field tag and wire type are append-only. One ruling, applied everywhere, is the only version
of this that is repairable.
design:
=== STANDING RULE (orchestrator, 2026-07-27) — recorded on the design field so it survives
rotation without touching this bead's ruling in --notes (br update --notes REPLACES).

A pane does NOT need permission for read-only work. Run probes, census reads, measurements,
differentials, quiet-root builds, and br filings on your own initiative and report what they showed.
Ask the owner ONLY before something that MUTATES THE TREE — a splice, a pin re-freeze, a commit, a
revert — or for a genuine owner ruling where the source underdetermines the answer and no instrument
in domain can settle it.

If you are waiting on the owner for anything, say what in ONE line. A pane deep in valuable work and
a pane blocked look identical from the orchestrator's seat, and that ambiguity has cost this swarm
hours. Surface in the three-way form: landable now / mid-derivation and N minutes out with what you
are deriving / blocked on X. Release any token you are not actively writing with — catalog held
across a long read starves peers for nothing.

COROLLARY: a measurement that FAILS TO DISCRIMINATE is a RESULT. Report the negative rather than
silently moving on; a discarded negative is how your successor re-chases the same dead end. Two from
this session, both recorded rather than dropped:
  * the role-token disagreement scan over the 31 bare-name candidates fired on 2, and one of those
    two was a false positive (a05 required_floor_arm:MetaSuccessor -> ShardingMigrationRetentionFloor,
    where the ARM is Meta-named and the union need not be). The heuristic is NOT the law; it found
    the real a20 case by luck. Do not rebuild it.
  * the hypothesis that qh3r-style census loss hides the class's referents is FALSIFIED for the bare-
    name subset: S4 = 0 of 96, i.e. every bare arm name in the class has at least one real source arm
    site. The 17 S4 cases are all in the '::' subset and are heads absent from the source census.
notes:
THE RULING, by pane2 at HEAD dbaab71 (2026-07-27). This note REPLACES every earlier one.
The ruling is MADE and ENFORCED. Its application is fgdb-5uj5. Zero of the 190 have landed under it.

=== 1. THE MEASUREMENT RE-DERIVED, NOT INHERITED ===
Filed at 43a1b73; re-derived at dbaab71 with the same instrument (dump_all_fields.rs over plan lines
1388..2728 and the catalog's own 21 [[slice]] rows, which still match pane4_ivsp/slices.txt exactly):
  11740 field candidates over 1020 owners                                   MATCHES
  a20: 182 = 127 top-level (68 typeless + 59 typed) + 55 interior;

reproduce 190. Read faithfully — split a multi-type cell on '|' and test each part — it yields 346

tag-refined strong reference the source already blesses.

The source rules the reference case itself, at a20:2593: 'ExternalCasRestoreServicePromotionManifestRef
and ExternalCasRestoreServicePromotionReceiptRef are generated tag-refined strong references whose
validators require respectively the Sharded/ExternalCas manifest arm and the ExternalCasCataloged
receipt arm; VARIANT SYNTAX IS NEVER USED AS A REFERENCE TARGET.' A field whose declared type is
`Union::Variant` in a VALUE position is the same construct one column over, and gets the same answer:
mint a wire type that names the admitted arm, and give the field that type.

  exact_wire_type      a wire_types row with kind = "discriminant", encoding_context in the enforced
                       grammar below, allowed_containing_schemas = the exact consuming schemas
  identity_class       "inline"   -- FORCED, not chosen: non_reference_wire_identity_class_mismatch
                       already rejects scalar/logical/physical on a registered non-reference wire tag
                       with reference_semantics = none
  reference_semantics  "none"     cardinality  "one"
  max_size_bytes       the REFINED UNION'S tag width (its [[union]] tag_wire_type), not the arm's
                       payload bound -- a precondition carries the discriminant, never the payload

WHY NOT THE ONE PRECEDENT. a01's u8+inline row is not wrong for a01 (a RECORD in a state), but
copying it to an `expected_*` PRECONDITION drops the constraint that is the whole point of the field:
u8 carries the discriminant and cannot say 'only 0x03 is admissible here'. Confirmed by the source's
own vocabulary — it writes `expected_local_restore_state:WeakStateIdentity` (7 landed rows) when the
precondition is UNCONSTRAINED, and `Union::Variant` when it is pinned. Those are two different asks
and u8 answers only the first.

WHY NOT THE union_variant WIRE TYPE (347 already minted). Two independent reasons. It is the arm's
PAYLOAD type — LocalRestorePhase.promoted_awaiting_reopen is max_size_bytes 16777216 for an
inline-record arm, and a precondition carries one byte. And its allowed_containing_schemas names only
its own union, so reusing it forces a cross-slice widening of a landed row in another lane.

=== 3. THE RULING'S PRECONDITION, WHICH WAS NOT MET, AND IS NOW ===

ones. NOTHING DID. MEASURED at dbaab71: 6 wire rows carry a refinement claim; encoding_context was
read only for non-emptiness (identity.rs:1580). A claim naming a nonexistent arm, or a real arm under
the wrong arm_tag, read exactly like a correct one. Multiplying an unenforced claim by 100 is the
doctrine violation the bead was trying to prevent, one layer down.

LANDED THIS SESSION — the law, in identity.rs::validate_identity, with four codes:
  refinement_claim_unparseable   refinement_union_unresolved
  refinement_arm_unresolved      refinement_arm_tag_mismatch

    admits only the <SourceArmName> arm (arm_tag 0x<hex>) of the <Union> union

dialect ('the Sharded/ExternalCas RestoreServicePromotionManifest arm' — no tag, no union clause)
which parses to None, so a law that validated only what it could parse would have skipped exactly the
rows that motivated it. One construct in two dialects at n=6 is gpms's own forecast at n=190.

Both a20 rows were canonicalized into the grammar (0x054f -> ExternalCasCataloged arm_tag 0x0001 of
RestoreServicePromotionReceipt; 0x0550 -> Sharded arm_tag 0x0002 of
RestoreServicePromotionManifestTargetPosture, the union that actually carries that arm). Both files
that mirror the row were edited: registries/wire_types.toml and registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml.

code and nothing else:
  (a) arm_tag 0x0001 -> 0x0002 (the SIBLING arm, both real)  -> refinement_arm_tag_mismatch
  (b) union -> NoSuchUnion                                   -> refinement_union_unresolved
  (c) arm -> Operationall                                    -> refinement_arm_unresolved
  (d) revert 0x054f to its PRE-CHANGE prose spelling         -> refinement_claim_unparseable
  (e) conformant control: re-point the same row at the union's OTHER real arm at its real tag
      (Abandoned 0x0002) -> stays green, so (a)-(d) are the law firing and not the law rejecting
      every edit
The domain is pinned at 6 in the test, so a new tag-refined wrapper must be added deliberately rather
than discovered by a green run. Gates: cargo fmt --check 0, clippy -D warnings 0, registry-check
identity 131 passed / 0 failed (was 130). validate_identity over the live registries: 0 violations
with 6 rows in the law's domain.

Referent registration is. Of the 190, only 22 have a referent that resolves today (type is U::V with
both registered). 31 more are bare arm names owned by exactly one union — and global-uniqueness
resolution is UNSOUND, proven at a20: PromotedAwaitingReopen occurs exactly once as a source_arm_name
so it resolves unambiguously, but a20:2601's META-path field then binds to the LOCAL union, because

REFERENT FROM THE CANDIDATE'S OWN SOURCE LOCATION, NEVER BY GLOBAL NAME LOOKUP.

title: gql_cert hashes BoundPlan.projection so RETURN a != RETURN b
description:
Plan certificates must hash BoundPlan.projection so RETURN a and RETURN b at the same seq produce different digests.

Wave 31 landed ReturnProjection on BoundPlan and the MATCH kernel, but gql_cert::certify still hashes only relation + src_var + dst_var + seq. title: MATCH live/as_of one edge-table pass (no neighbours second scan)
description:
Gap 3 leftover after RETURN a (fgdb-gql-return-src-g7g5): live/as-of MATCH still does **two scans** — `Database::edges()` (or `edges_at`) to collect sources, then `neighbours`/`neighbours_at` per source. The matching-relation dests are already on those edge records. One pass must feed the shared kernel.

NOT Graph-SSI, NOT G0, NOT 5uw2, NOT grammar, NOT WriteTxn overlay (it already expands from its overlay map), NOT GLA crate.

## Why

`gql_exec::execute` materializes the whole edge table, filters the bound relation, then asks Strata again for each source's neighbours. That second lookup can drift from the table that chose the sources (a dest visible in `edges()` but not `neighbours()`, or the reverse). Genesis MATCH is an edge-table projection: sources and dests of the bound relation, then `execute_bound_plan_over` for CGSE sort+dedup and RETURN a/b.

## Behavior

- `gql_exec::execute` / `execute_at`: one pass over `edges()` / `edges_at`. Build the bound-relation adjacency (src → dests). Hand that map to `crate::execute_bound_plan_over` as the expansion. Do **not** call `neighbours` or `neighbours_at`.
- `RETURN b` still unique dests; `RETURN a` still unique sources with at least one matching out-edge. Same answers as today.
- `write_txn.rs` overlay path unchanged.
- Planted negative: a source witness that `gql_exec.rs` contains `neighbours(` must fail once the second scan is gone.

No-claim: not a Strata relation postings cursor, not Loom, not streaming row APIs.

## Owned files

title: Pinned MATCH equals fgdb-reference; BoundPlan certificate hashes plan+seq
description:
G1 leftover of Gap 3 / Genesis 4–5 after `fgdb-w5-parsers-nje.1` (CLOSED: pinned MATCH executes). This leaf adds the two missing proofs:

1. Engine `execute_gql` rows equal `fgdb-reference` neighbour expansion over the same durable stream.
2. A plan certificate stub: hash of bound plan + snapshot seq; same inputs ⇒ byte-identical digest.

NOT full EXPLAIN, NOT G0 language-contracts, NOT Appendix A, NOT TCK, NOT SSI.

## Why this is a capability

`min_gql_match` proves the engine agrees with itself. Genesis still requires reopen/oracle agreement and a replayable certificate over snapshot seq + bound statement. Without this leaf, MATCH is a Rust neighbour scan with a parser glued on.

## Architecture

- Certificate lives in `fgdb` (has `fgdb-crypto`), not in `fgdb-gql` (do not add crypto to the parser crate). Input is `BoundPlan` + `CommitSeq` (healthy frontier). Domain-separated BLAKE3 (existing `fgdb_crypto::Hasher`), not serde.
- Differential lives in `fgdb-sim` only (§15.2: engine and oracle may both be visible there; never make `fgdb` depend on `fgdb-reference`).
- Oracle expansion: after drop(Database), independent `CommitCoordinator` + `fgdb_sim::replay`, then for every `reference.vertices()` collect `neighbours(vid, RelationId)`, flatten dest vids, sort+dedup — same kernel `gql_exec` uses. Compare to `execute_gql` captured BEFORE drop (or reopen engine and query).
- `execute_gql` signature stays. Add `gql_plan_certificate(&self, src, bind) -> Result<GqlPlanCertificate, GqlError>` (name may match style).

## Acceptance (orchestrator closes)

Positive:
- Sim test: spine graph with two `:R` edges written descending dest order; engine rows == oracle dest-set (sorted). Off-relation edge in oracle is absent from both.
- Certificate: same statement+bind+seq ⇒ equal digest; different seq OR different bound RelationId ⇒ different digest.

Planted negative:
- A sim test that compared engine to itself (reopen only) must not be the oracle test — the oracle path must call `fgdb_sim::replay` / `ReferenceDatabase`.
- Certificate digest must include seq: mutating only the seq in the hasher input changes the digest (unit test).

No-claim: not a query planner, not FG-INV promotion, not CLI.

title: A guard whose precondition is the negation of its trigger: concurrent_bead_creation_cannot_red_another_panes_tree cannot fire when the tree is red
description:
tools/registry-check/tests/architecture_decisions.rs carries a test named
`concurrent_bead_creation_cannot_red_another_panes_tree`. It exists to prove that
one pane filing a bead cannot red the shared tree for every other pane.

IT CANNOT FIRE WHILE THE TREE IS RED FROM EXACTLY THAT CAUSE.

    thread 'concurrent_bead_creation_cannot_red_another_panes_tree' panicked at
    tools/registry-check/tests/architecture_decisions.rs:985:5:
    the unmodified fixture must be as green as the repo it mirrors

The test mirrors the repo into a fixture, and its first act is to assert the
unmodified mirror is green. When the repo is red because a pane filed a bead
without a bet label, that precondition fails and the test aborts before it can
exercise the property it was written to defend. The guard is available in exactly
the circumstances where nothing is wrong, and unavailable in exactly the
circumstances it was built for.

=== MEASURED, 2026-07-27, HEAD dee62ef ===

Five of the 42 tests in the suite were failing, and ALL FIVE reduced to two beads
carrying no labels at all -- fgdb-wzyl and fgdb-h6kr:

    architecture_bead_provenance_is_total_pinned_and_bidirectional
    architecture_registry_parses_and_validates
    architecture_neg_semantic_change_with_stable_id
    concurrent_bead_creation_cannot_red_another_panes_tree
    architecture-check (the registered binary) and g0_architecture_decisions_e2e

After labelling those two beads b5 under owner authorisation: 42 passed, 0
failed. So the population is confirmed at two, and the guard's unavailability is
confirmed to have been caused by the very class it detects.

I HIT THIS MYSELF, WHICH IS THE POINT. Earlier the same day I filed three beads
(uzzh, avex, 23u1) with labels g0,verification,appendix-a and no b1..b6 bet
label, redding the shared tree for every pane. The guard that exists to prevent
precisely that was already disabled -- by two earlier unlabelled beads -- so it
could not warn me, and I found the breakage only by reading a full check.sh
transcript afterwards.

=== WHY THIS SITS NEXT TO fgdb-checker-mirrors-subject-prose-23u1 ===

Same defect family, different mechanism:

  23u1  a validator holds a copy of its own subject, so an existence query
        resolves against the copy and cannot return "absent".
  this  a guard's precondition is the negation of the condition it detects, so
        it cannot return "violated".

In both cases the instrument is structurally incapable of producing the answer it
was built to produce, and in both cases every gate stays green -- or in this case
merely red for a different-looking reason -- while the specific protection is
absent. A precondition that is the negation of the trigger is a fail-open, and it
should be reported as one rather than as a cascading failure.

=== WHAT A FIX HAS TO PRESERVE ===

The green-mirror precondition is not gratuitous: without it the test cannot tell
its own planted mutation from ambient repo breakage, and would report a false
pass. So it must not simply be deleted.

The shape that keeps both properties is to make the precondition SCOPED rather
than global: assert the mirror is green *with respect to the property under
test* -- i.e. that the set of bead-provenance violations in the unmodified mirror
is exactly the set in the repo -- and then assert that planting a new bead adds
none. That is a differential formulation: it tolerates ambient red, and still
fails if bead creation contributes a violation. It also needs a control proving
it goes red when a planted bead does contribute one, or the fix reintroduces the
same class one level down.

Filed by pane2 at owner request, 2026-07-27, after the orchestrator authorised
labelling the two beads. Nothing deleted.

reporting it and is the only one that needs no new reporting channel. I have a preference

title: br close on a BLOCKED issue exits 0 and hints 'already closed or not found', contradicting its own first line
notes:
Found while closing fgdb-ty4g; it is the same defect that made me report fgdb-dbta CLOSED to the orchestrator three times when it was still IN_PROGRESS.

REPRODUCTION, exact:
  $ br dep add A B          # B blocks A
  $ br close A --reason "..."
  Warning: Skipped A: blocked by: B
  Error: Nothing to do: all 1 issue(s) skipped
  Hint: All specified issues were already closed or not found.
  $ echo $?
  0

THREE SEPARATE PROBLEMS, in order of harm:
 1. EXIT 0 ON A NO-OP THAT PRINTS 'Error:'. Any automation, guard script or agent that
    branches on exit status reads SUCCESS while the issue is untouched. This is the
    same failure family as 'ubs exits 0 without scanning' and 'grep -c exits 1 on the
    success case': the status does not carry the outcome.
 2. THE HINT CONTRADICTS THE WARNING TWO LINES ABOVE IT. Line 1 states the true cause
    (blocked by B). The Hint then asserts a different, mutually exclusive cause --
    already closed, or not found. A reader who trusts the last line, which is where
    CLIs conventionally put the actionable summary, concludes the issue is CLOSED. I
    did exactly that on dbta and reported it closed three times before verifying.
 3. 'blocked by' IS A POLICY REFUSAL, NOT AN ERROR. Refusing to close a blocked issue
    is defensible, but it should be a distinct exit code and a distinct message, so
    'refused, here is the blocker' is never confusable with 'nothing matched'.

SUGGESTED FIX: exit non-zero when zero issues were modified; make the Hint conditional
on the actual skip reason (blocked / already-closed / not-found are three different
hints); and print the blocker id in the summary line rather than only the warning.

DETECTION RULE FOR AGENTS UNTIL IT IS FIXED, and it is cheap: never believe a br
mutation from its own output. Re-read the record -- 'br show <id> | head -1' or the
JSONL at HEAD -- before reporting a state change. A tool's message about what it did is
not evidence that it did it. Same family as [[stale-binary-reports-phantom-pin-drift]]:
when a tool tells you about the data, control the tool.
close_reason: Fixed and pushed in beads_rust: 86750ae6 (fix), 8d367d28 (regression tests), merged as 2965b3aa, plus 1691d0a7 restoring their pre-existing clippy red first and separately. Headline claim FALSIFIED: a single blocked close exits 3 on every binary measured; the real defect is the PARTIAL BATCH — close.rs gated its terminal error on closed_count==0, so one success swallowed every refusal and 'br close <blocked> <closeable>' exited 0 with the refused id absent from stdout. Now CLOSE_INCOMPLETE, exit 3. Problems 2 and 3 of this bead were already fixed upstream by 480a412d (#380) and are merely UNDEPLOYED — see fgdb-204h for the 0.2.16-vs-0.2.19 skew, which is why we saw a fixed defect. Regression tests, both mutation-proven to FAIL on the pre-fix predicate: e2e_partially_applied_close_batch_does_not_exit_zero (process-level, asserts real ExitStatus) and execute_with_args_reports_partial_batch_as_error_not_success (library-level). ERRORS.md stdout/stderr contradiction filed upstream as beads_rust-806e.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
=== OWNER RULING, 2026-07-27: KEEP THE INDEPENDENT THIRD PIN COPY. DO NOT CONVERT. ===

Do not convert these four literals to `catalog_manifest_value` lookups. The reason is
the validator-coupling principle applied to a pin: if the script derived its pins FROM
the catalog, a catalog corruption would be invisible to it, because the script would
always agree with whatever the catalog says. A mechanism whose verdict is a function of
the condition it validates is not a validator. The third copy exists in order to be
ABLE TO DISAGREE; a copy that cannot disagree is not a copy.

This is demonstrated, not theoretical, on a live example in this very bead: the one
manifest pane3 DID move -- target_manifest -- is read from the catalog at run time
(lines 328-329) and absorbed the change automatically, detecting nothing. That is the
conversion's behaviour. These four literals are the half that still works.

exactly what this bead is. Mitigation is the recipe below -- derive from the tool's
emitted NDJSON, never hand-copy, and re-derive at the applier's HEAD. A mechanical

    301  byte_count                    317-323  the reference_manifest block
    302  sha256                        320      occurrence_count
                                       321      occurrence_transcript_sha256

`grep '^FAIL'` returned 0 on a red run of nine of ten gates, so no grep-for-failure is

assuming: `die()` at line 132 does `FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); log "FAIL: $*"`, and `log()` at

If you are here because hand-re-freezing four literals felt like pointless toil and you
are about to replace them with `catalog_manifest_value` lookups the way lines 328-329
already do: that conversion is FORBIDDEN by owner ruling, and here is the reason it is
not mere conservatism.

A pin derived from the artifact it validates cannot ever disagree with that artifact.
It will report green against a corrupted catalog just as cheerfully as against a correct
one, because its expected value IS the catalog's value. That is not a weaker check; it
is not a check. The whole purpose of a third, independent copy is the capacity to
DISAGREE -- with the catalog and with the loader at once, so that a catalog change plus
a matching loader change cannot authorise themselves.

ALREADY derived at run time from the catalog. When pane3 withdrew a target row in

script that still works, and the 156-byte / 13-occurrence drift they caught (introduced
by 65a21da and invisible to every loader-visible pin) is them doing precisely the job
the derived half could not have done.

The maintenance cost is real and was accepted with open eyes. It is bounded by the
recipe above: derive from the tool's emitted NDJSON, never hand-copy, re-derive at your
own HEAD, ~8s with no cargo and no build slot. A mechanical re-freeze of an independent
pin is cheap. An automatic one is not a pin at all.

SETTLED. Do not re-litigate, do not file the conversion as an improvement.

title: HAZARD: du apparent-vs-actual cannot detect hard links and per-link byte summation invents them — the control that produced geo2's phantom 224MB
description:
Banked 2026-07-27 ~22:30 by pane2 at HEAD 1a6fdc2. REFERENCE record, not a work
item. One instrument pair produced a P1 bug bead whose headline quantity does
not exist.

## What happened

fgdb-geo2 claimed: "27 of them carry a FULL COPY of .beads/issues.jsonl @
8.29 MB => 224 MB, 69% OF THE RUN COST", and offered a control for it:

  "Not hard-linked: apparent 322 MB vs actual 326 MB, so the copies are real bytes."

MEASURED at HEAD 1a6fdc2 on the same work dir: all 27 paths are ONE inode
(51953358) at nlink=27. Their true footprint is 8.28 MB — 2.5% of the run, not
69%. And 27 x 8,684,836 B = 223.6 MB reproduces "224 MB" to the decimal, so the
number was produced by summing a size per LINK.

## The control, run BOTH directions (scratch dir, ext4, same volume)

  10 hard links to one 8 MB file : du actual  9   apparent  8   per-file sum 80 MB
  10 real 8 MB copies            : du actual 81   apparent 80   per-file sum 80 MB

`du` de-duplicates by inode in BOTH modes, so `apparent < actual` is block
rounding and appears identically in both worlds. The per-file size sum reports
80 MB in both worlds. NEITHER instrument can tell a copy from a link.

  discriminating instruments: `stat -c %h` -> 11 vs 1; `find -printf '%n %i'`.

## The rules

- To ask "is this shared", read nlink/inode. Never `du`, never a size sum.
- Genuinely unshared bytes: `find $D -type f -links 1 -printf '%s\n'` summed.
- Shared bytes: `find $D -type f -links +1 -printf '%i %s\n' | sort -u -k1,1n`
  summed. The two partition the tree and must equal `du --apparent-size`. On the
  geo2 dir: 310.82 + 10.36 = 321.18 MB vs du apparent 322 MB.
- The DENOMINATOR needs the same care. geo2's "114 neg-* / staged fixtures per
  run" is a real count of depth-1 entries named `neg-*`, but it is 38 fixture
  DIRS + 39 `.jsonl` + 35 `.err` + 2 `.sha256` OUTPUT files. Staged fixture roots
  are 40 (dirs containing `registries/`), of which 27 carry `.beads/`. The ratio
  that read as a minority — 27 of 114 — is a majority: 27 of 40.
- A code comment can settle this before any measurement. The staging function
  says, in the tree at geo2's own filed HEAD: "These support inputs are read-only
  after staging. Hard-linking them avoids duplicating ~10 MB per fixture;
  registries and the plan remain real copies because fixtures mutate those paths."

Related: fgdb-rhvi (the re-derivation procedure), fgdb-geo2.
close_reason:
REFERENCE RECORD, COMPLETE — closed on filed scope per its own header ('REFERENCE record, not a work item') and per fgdb-rhvi output discipline (close on filed scope with the measurement in the reason). Nothing in it was unimplemented: it banks a measured hazard, its discriminating instruments (stat -c %h, find -printf '%n %i'), and a both-directions control, and its successor work was already routed to fgdb-geo2.

CONTRIBUTED BEFORE CLOSING (2026-08-04, JadeSnow): one NEW instrument trap in the same family, verified — in this environment `du` is ALIASED TO `dust` (which du -> 'du: aliased to dust'). Every rule this bead states is phrased in coreutils du semantics ('du de-duplicates by inode in BOTH modes'), and a reader typing du interactively does not get coreutils du. The defence is \du / command du / /usr/bin/du. This is a real gap in the bead's own coverage, not a restatement.

ALSO RECORDED, and it is the honest part: during the 2026-08-04 ENOSPC outage I reported a large apparent-vs-actual discrepancy on /data/tmp/cargo-target to the orchestrator, then COULD NOT REPRODUCE IT — the directory was cleared during recovery, so the subject no longer existed. I withdrew the number rather than keep it. That is this bead's own standard applied to my own claim, and it adds a rule worth having: a disk subject can vanish within hours, so run the discriminating check (which du, stat -c %h) AT THE MOMENT OF OBSERVATION, not afterwards.

Reopen freely if anyone wants the du-alias trap tracked as its own work item; the closure is a queue-hygiene judgment on a completed reference record, not a claim that disk measurement is a solved problem.

comments.text:
NEW INSTRUMENT TRAP IN THIS EXACT FAMILY, verified 2026-08-04 at HEAD fd3eb39: IN THIS ENVIRONMENT `du` IS ALIASED TO `dust`.

  $ which du
  du: aliased to dust

Every rule this bead states is phrased in terms of du behaviour -- "du de-duplicates by inode in
