title: Rename the bead-provenance floor pins so their names stop claiming equality
description:
## What

4a01ce8 (fgdb-lzol) turned the bead-provenance cardinality pins into monotone
FLOORS and re-keyed `binding_hash` by rule instead of by bead. The semantics
changed; the names did not. Rename them:

  registries/architecture_decisions.toml, [bead_provenance]
    bead_count            -> bead_count_floor
    direct_owner_count    -> direct_owner_floor
    bet_label_count       -> bet_label_floor
    exact_override_count  -> exact_override_floor
    family_rule_count     -> family_rule_floor
    binding_hash          -> rule_binding_hash

  registries/architecture_decisions.toml, every [[bead_family]]
    expected_match_count  -> min_match_count

  tools/registry-check/src/architecture.rs
    PINNED_BEAD_COUNT           -> PINNED_BEAD_COUNT_FLOOR
    PINNED_DIRECT_OWNER_COUNT   -> PINNED_DIRECT_OWNER_FLOOR
    PINNED_BET_LABEL_COUNT      -> PINNED_BET_LABEL_FLOOR
    PINNED_EXACT_OVERRIDE_COUNT -> PINNED_EXACT_OVERRIDE_FLOOR
    PINNED_FAMILY_RULE_COUNT    -> PINNED_FAMILY_RULE_FLOOR
    PINNED_BEAD_BINDING_HASH    -> PINNED_RULE_BINDING_HASH
  plus the matching `BeadProvenanceConfig` / `BeadFamily` struct fields and the
  `exact_keys(...)` lists that validate the TOML key set.

## Why

"count" and "expected" both assert equality in English. A pane reading
`bead_count = 401` next to a 402-record corpus reads a stale pin and
re-freezes it — which is precisely the behaviour fgdb-lzol removed, and
putting it back reds every other pane. The words are now the only thing left
pointing at the old design.

`expected_match_count` is the worst of them: "expected" is what the checker
compared with `!=` before, and the field is now a lower bound.

## What breaks if this is not done

Nothing mechanically — the tree is green and the checker is correct. The risk
is a human one and it is the same defect returning by hand: someone
"repairs" a floor that was never broken, or writes a new negative test as
`declared + 1` (which goes vacuous the moment the corpus grows — see the
comment on fgdb-lzol). Mitigations already in place, and why they are not
enough: explicit FLOOR comment blocks at every pin site, a doc comment on
PINNED_BEAD_COUNT, and a warning in scripts/bead_provenance_preflight.sh
("If you find yourself editing bead_count after a `br create`, stop"). Those
are all comments. The name is what gets read.

## Files carrying the old name

  registries/architecture_decisions.toml                    TOML keys
  tools/registry-check/src/architecture.rs                  consts, struct
                                                            fields, exact_keys,
                                                            parse fns, use sites
  tools/registry-check/tests/architecture_decisions.rs      imports + assertions
  scripts/g0_architecture_decisions_e2e.sh                  bead_policy_value
                                                            lookups (awk key
                                                            match) and the
                                                            python POLICY dict
  scripts/bead_provenance_preflight.sh                      prose only

## How to do it safely

The compiler covers the Rust side and `exact_keys` covers the TOML key set, so
completeness is enforced rather than eyeballed — this is a mechanical rename,
not a design change. Two things it must NOT do: change any comparison operator,
and change any pinned value. Verify with `bash scripts/check.sh` plus
`scripts/g0_architecture_decisions_e2e.sh`, and confirm
`concurrent_bead_creation_cannot_red_another_panes_tree` still passes.

Needs the catalog token (registries/**, tools/registry-check/**). It is ~40
sites across two heavily contended files, so take it at a quiet point and
stage the whole edit in a `git archive HEAD` copy first.
notes:
LANDED a4d60fc. The bead's scope was measured accurate -- the first inherited
claim tonight that survived re-derivation intact. Its file list of five is
right, including the omission of tools/registry-check/src/bin/architecture-check.rs:
that file's `bead_count` and `bead_binding_hash` are NDJSON fields carrying
OBSERVED values, so "count" is correct there and renaming them would have broken
the grepped contract in scripts/g0_architecture_decisions_e2e.sh, which reads
registry["bead_count"] (observed) and POLICY["bead_count_floor"] (declared) on
the SAME line. That asymmetry is now a two-line comment at the site.

PARTITION of the 40 renamed sites: TOML 20 (6 [bead_provenance] keys + 14
[[bead_family]] rows); architecture.rs consts 6, struct fields 7, exact_keys
entries 7, parse calls 7, use sites 21, doc/comment/message text 9; tests 21;
g0 script 12; preflight prose 2. NOT renamed, each for a stated reason: the two
NDJSON field names, `recompute_bead_binding_hash` (genuinely keyed by bead), and
the violation codes `bead_count_pin` / `bead_family_expected_total` (they are
the contradiction_class contract, not prose).

NO PINNED VALUE MOVED, NO OPERATOR CHANGED: 7 comparison sites in the diff, all
keeping `!=`, `<` or `==`. The rule-binding hash recomputes to
fnv1a64:66a303ca1f79e606, unchanged -- confirmed by reading
recompute_rule_binding_hash (its transcript keys are the literals "rule.id" and
"rule.decision_ids", never a TOML key name) and then measured on the real tree.
recompute_semantic_contract_hash quantifies over decisions only. The generated
docs/ARCHITECTURE_DECISION_RECORD.md is unchanged because generate_document
renders field VALUES, not key names -- architecture_document_matches_registry
passes.

VERIFIED WITHOUT CARGO (orchestrator froze builds at 9.9G disk), on the
standalone rustc path, ~10s per round, no target tree:
  baseline at HEAD before the change   42 passed / 0 failed
  after the change                     42 passed / 0 failed
  architecture-check --root .          violations 0, outcome pass,
                                       observed bead_count 422 vs floor 401
                                       (slack 21), rule hash unchanged
  rustfmt --check clean; bash -n + shellcheck clean

MUTATION CONTROLS, both directions, on synthetic roots (registries symlinked,
architecture_decisions.toml a real file):
  control, unmutated copy                loads, 0 bead_provenance violations
  old key `bead_count` planted           LOAD_ERROR bead_provenance: unknown
                                         key(s) in closed schema: bead_count
  old key `expected_match_count` planted LOAD_ERROR bead_family[0]: unknown
                                         key(s): expected_match_count
  g0 awk POLICY lookup of an old key     exit 42, no value
  g0 python block on an old-key TOML     AssertionError: bead_provenance is
                                         missing bead_count_floor
exact_keys is a CLOSED schema, so a stale old name is a hard load error, not a
silent pass. The g0 script's own 110-line python block, extracted verbatim and
run against rustc-built NDJSON, PASSES.

UNRUN, and why: scripts/check.sh and scripts/g0_architecture_decisions_e2e.sh
both begin with a cargo invocation, and `ubs` shells out to cargo too. All three
are blocked by the build freeze, not by anything in this change. The g0 script's
assertions were exercised against an rustc-built binary as described above; the
script itself has not been executed end to end.

TWO RESIDUES FOUND, both out of this bead's stated scope, filed separately:
(1) g0_architecture_decisions_e2e.sh line 41 states the script "is not in
    check.sh". Measured false at this HEAD: checker_index.toml carries two live
    `kind = "script"` rows for it, live_gate_inventory sorts -u to one, and
    run_registered_gates executes it. The comment and the wiring landed in the
    same commit (8ea2055), so the present tense was wrong on arrival.
(2) The words "count"/"expected" survive in the violation codes
    `bead_count_pin` and `bead_family_expected_total` and in the local
    `expected_family_total`. Renaming a code is an NDJSON contract change and
    was deliberately not bundled into a prose rename.

INCIDENT, self-inflicted and fully repaired: while building the first mutation
fixture I redirected sed output into a path that was a symlink to the real
registries/architecture_decisions.toml, which truncated it to 0 bytes before sed
read it. Restored from HEAD and the 20-line rename re-applied; `git diff` then
showed exactly the intended 20 insertions / 20 deletions and nothing else. No
other file was a redirect target. The rule: when a fixture root symlinks a
registry, write the mutant file FIRST and never create the symlink you are about
to redirect into.

title: Transaction commit silently rebinds snapshot effects to a newer schema epoch
description: At immutable commit ba5606928f373385529a696bccf111a09898a33c, Transaction::begin_at materializes its workspace from the transaction snapshot (crates/fgdb-reference/src/txn.rs:358-381), and CoordinateEntry.schema_epoch is explicitly the schema binding under which rows were validated (crates/fgdb-delta-types/src/lib.rs:237-247). The li8d fix instead reads db.graph(...).schema_epoch() from the LIVE database at commit (txn.rs:738-758). Race: begin and execute at epoch 0; a concurrent durable schema transition installs epoch 1; the old transaction commits afterward. It now stamps epoch 1 onto effects evaluated under epoch 0, so preflight accepts them instead of reporting invalidation. The new test covers only transition-before-begin and cannot see this. This contradicts plan lines 205 and 213: per-coordinate schema binding is part of snapshot identity and old snapshots keep their epoch interpretation. Required closure: capture the exact schema binding at begin (root plus epoch, not merely a live scalar), and treat a post-snapshot Schema/Constraint root move as an asymmetric shared-vs-exclusive CoordinateRoots conflict; do not put the shared dependency into the ordinary write set, which would serialize two disjoint ordinary writers. Controls: transition before begin commits; transition after begin conflicts/refuses without apply; a constraint-root-only move also invalidates; two disjoint ordinary transactions under one unchanged binding remain independently committable. title: Historical witness: the union and arm cohort asserts claim a total domain but are blind to a newly landed row — only the re-baseline-able pin guards them
description:
Derived 2026-07-27 by pane3 at HEAD 59a1d81, re-deriving the fgdb-pqnr premise
per fgdb-rhvi. pqnr's own failure is GONE (131 passed / 0 failed); this is the
residue, and it is a different defect from the one pqnr filed.

THE SHAPE: a check whose STATED domain is wider than its ACTUAL one.
tools/registry-check/tests/identity.rs:9798 asserts
    pre_erratum.ordinary_unions.len() + 378 == current_union_count
under the message "the historical witness must remove EVERY post-erratum union".
That message is a total claim over all unions. The assertion is not. Because
`current_union_count` is captured from the same vector BEFORE the retain, the
predicate reduces to "the filter removed exactly 378", so a union that NO filter
names increments both sides together and is invisible.

The same holds for all four relative cohort asserts:
  L9798  ordinary unions        pre.len() + 378   == current_union_count
  L9803  reference unions       filtered count    == current - 0
  L9819  reference union arms   sum(arms)         == current_reference_arm_count
  L9828  ordinary union arms    sum(arms) + 1_108 == current_ordinary_arm_count

FIELDS ARE ALREADY FIXED; UNIONS AND ARMS WERE NEVER GIVEN THE SAME FIX.
L9883 pins the reconstruction width ABSOLUTELY (`pre_erratum.fields.len() == 225`,
landed at e4f2428) and its own comment states the mechanism verbatim: "A newly
landed field row that was not added to a post_erratum_* filter widens it and is
INVISIBLE to the cohort assert above, because it increments that assert's two
sides together." No equivalent absolute pin exists for
`pre_erratum.ordinary_unions.len()` or for either arm sum.

PROVEN BY MUTATION, BOTH DIRECTIONS, ON QUIET ROOTS AT 59a1d81 (rustc path, repo
never touched; registries/durable_fields.toml carries 983 [[field]], 385 [[union]],
1130 [[union_arm]] rows at this HEAD).

  BLIND — append ONE [[union]] named by no filter (PqnrBlindnessProbeUnion):
    passes L9798, L9803, L9814, L9819, L9828 and the absolute field pin L9883.
    Fails ONLY at L9929, the hash:
      left  fnv1a64:d524cd1012b49c70   right fnv1a64:e0245f1bf4c183fd
    Re-run with 2 [[union_arm]] rows added to the same probe union: still passes
    L9828, the ordinary-ARM cohort assert, and still fails only at L9929:
      left  fnv1a64:f1cbf253862aee1f   right fnv1a64:e0245f1bf4c183fd

  FIRES — rename an existing union the filter DOES name
  (BoltBookmarkRequestKind -> ...RenamedProbe, 10 occurrences) so the filter stops
  matching it: L9798 fires immediately, left 386 right 385.

  So the assert is a live predicate, not constant-true; its real domain is "the
  filter's matched count moved", i.e. the OVER-filter direction only. The
  UNDER-filter direction it is written to catch is exactly the one it cannot see.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A MISSING ASSERT
The pin at L9929 is the SOLE guard for the union and arm cohorts. The pin is also
the artifact that gets re-baselined when it goes red — legitimately, under the
fgdb-e55p owner ruling, which requires full published accounting. Every such
re-baseline therefore resets the only detector these two cohorts have, and any
under-filtered union that landed before it is absorbed silently into the new
baseline. fgdb-pqnr's instinct ("re-pinning erases the signal") was RIGHT about
the mechanism and WRONG about the remedy: the remedy is not a ban on re-pinning
(the owner has ruled that accounted re-baselines are legitimate), it is to give
unions and arms the absolute width pin fields already have, so the hash stops
being the only thing standing between an under-filtered row and a green suite.

ACCEPTANCE
  - add absolute width pins beside L9883 for pre_erratum.ordinary_unions.len(),
    pre_erratum.unions.len(), and both arm sums, derived from the CURRENT
    reconstruction and base-derived from the test's own drift, never hard-coded
  - each must be mutation-proved to fire on the append probe above, which today
    reaches only L9929
  - keep the relative cohort asserts: they catch the over-filter direction the
    absolute pins do not
  - correct the L9798 message so it states the domain it actually has
close_reason: FIXED. Four absolute width pins added beside the field pin: ordinary_unions.len()==7, unions.len()==5, ordinary arm sum==22, reference arm sum==8 — all four derived from the reconstruction itself, and each reconciles with the corpus (7+378=385, 22+1108=1130, 5 and 8 exact). Red-proved BOTH ways on a quiet root against the pre-fix and post-fix binaries: pristine GREEN/GREEN; +1 unfiltered [[union]], +1 [[reference_union]], +1 [[reference_union_arm]], +1 arm on a pre-erratum union all went RED-at-a-hash before and RED-at-a-named-width-pin after (left 8/6/9/23 vs right 7/5/8/22); restored corpus GREEN/GREEN. L9798's total-domain message corrected to state the over-filter domain it actually has. WIDER THAN FILED, recorded in the commit body: the two reference cohorts are not blind in one direction, they are len()==len() and vacuous for any corpus — pre_erratum.unions is never retained.

title: Implement the fgdb CLI with human and versioned robot modes
description:
## What & scope
Implement the shipped `fgdb` binary as the agent-first and human-friendly command surface over the same embedded/session and FGP contracts as the library and server. Own command parsing and discovery, endpoint/embedded selection, capability authentication, explicit transaction/session commands, query and streaming-result control, SnapshotQuery, CDC/subscription, backup/archive/restore/status surfaces, and stable output/error behavior. Robot mode is a frozen versioned NDJSON protocol; human mode may be ergonomic and decorative but can never contaminate robot stdout.

## Why
B6 is a product property only if agents can operate the database without scraping prose or terminal decoration. Durable results, explicit ACK/release/resume, typed failures, replay identities, and service epochs lose their value if the CLI collapses them into an ambiguous exit code or socket lifetime. Humans still need excellent discoverability and safe defaults, so both postures share one command model while keeping distinct renderers.

## Design and public contract
- `fgdb robot schema` emits the complete canonical schema bundle for the requested supported robot protocol version, including event discriminants, field types, redaction rules, exit-code table, feature/capability requirements, ordering rules, and compatibility policy. Output is data-only NDJSON on stdout with no color, progress bars, prompts, banners, or log decoration.
- Every robot invocation begins with a versioned invocation/result envelope and emits line-oriented canonical events. Event order is deterministic whenever semantics permit; nondeterministic operational observations carry explicit sequence/time/source fields rather than relying on arrival prose. Unknown versions and unavailable capabilities fail before database observation.
- Freeze explicit exit classes for success, usage/schema error, authentication/authorization refusal, unavailable feature, semantic query/transaction failure, retryable transport/leadership condition, sent-unknown/reconciliation required, partial client-side consumption with durable owner retained, and internal corruption. Exit status never substitutes for the terminal event.
- Provide commands for connect/open, prepare/execute, explicit begin/statement/commit/abort/reattach/renew, query cancel, result/artifact ACK/release/resume, status, snapshot query, CDC/subscription, archive open, backup/restore inspection, capability inspection, replay and explain/certificate retrieval. Each command projects the owning canonical API type; it does not invent a CLI-only state machine.
- Human mode supplies concise help, shell completion data, TTY-aware tables/streaming, explicit confirmations only for genuinely dangerous administrative operations, and secret-safe input. Noninteractive human use remains pipe-correct. Configuration precedence and endpoint/profile selection are deterministic and printable; secrets, macaroons, locators, protected facts, DP seeds, and raw internal identities are never logged.
- Structured CLI diagnostics use a separate stderr or explicitly selected JSONL diagnostic sink; robot stdout remains contract data. Broken pipes, disconnect, Drop, SIGINT/cancellation, and terminal rendering cannot ACK or release an independent owner.
- Robot schema fixtures and docs are generated or checked from the same registries/closed unions as FGP and the Rust API. Additive robot-minor changes and breaking robot-major changes follow the durable compatibility discipline; human wording is not a machine contract.

## Interactions and ownership
Consumes `fgdb-embedded`, `fgdbd`/FGP, transaction ownership, capability, result/artifact/error delivery, SnapshotQuery, CDC, and archive-open contracts. W10 specialized beads own their semantic/protocol state machines; this bead owns CLI command projection, rendering, schema/versioning, process exit, configuration, and end-to-end operator ergonomics. The W10 epic and G3 prove the live CLI; G4 checks generated robot schemas and documentation against frozen registries.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Unit tests exhaustively cover command grammar, option/config precedence, endpoint/profile selection, robot-version negotiation, every exit-code mapping, every event encoder/decoder, canonical field ordering, redaction, TTY/non-TTY branching, broken-pipe behavior, and invalid/unavailable-capability refusal. Golden fixtures freeze each robot event and `fgdb robot schema` bundle.
- Property/model tests generate legal and illegal command/event sequences, arbitrary chunk boundaries and Unicode, stale/cross-session handles, config conflicts, and terminal/disconnect races; emitted robot streams validate against the selected schema and never imply ACK/release absent the canonical transition.
- Fuzz parsers, NDJSON decoders, schema negotiation, shell completion generation, and hostile terminal/control characters under strict resource budgets.
- E2E script starts an embedded database and a real `fgdbd`, runs human smoke flows and robot flows for open/connect, write/read, explicit multi-statement transaction, reattach, cancel, result resume/ACK/release, artifact output, SnapshotQuery, CDC/subscription, archive/restore status, authorization refusal, lost response, leader change, and broken pipe; it validates stdout against frozen schemas and asserts byte-equivalent public outcomes across embedded and FGP paths.
- Agent-usability E2E executes only schema-discovered commands from a clean process, verifies every response is actionable without prose scraping, and checks deterministic replay of a captured robot transcript.
- Detailed versioned diagnostics record `{run_id,cli_version,robot_schema_version,invocation_id,command_kind,endpoint_profile,posture,capability_public_commitment,cluster_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch,session_txn_statement_result_or_artifact_public_ids,event_seq,transition,exit_class,bytes_or_rows,backpressure,cancel_or_disconnect,verdict,evidence_refs,seed,replay_command}` with secrets/protected facts redacted. Tests fail on stdout decoration, missing events, unbounded fields, secret leakage, or an incomplete diagnostic chain.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: scraping human output as robot mode; one unversioned JSON blob; implicit release on process exit; CLI-only transaction/result semantics; logging credentials or protected errors; silently retrying SentUnknown. Risk is schema drift across CLI/FGP/Rust; generated fixtures and cross-surface E2E make drift a gate failure.

## Provenance
Plan Product Shape item 3, Agent Ergonomics Requirements, §13 Fabric/W10, §16.6 compatibility, §19 W10/G3/G4, and B6.

title: a10 ERRATUM in the i1rx mint: ConfigurationTransitionSpec.required_prepared is a census truncation of a 6-member slash-compressed token, typed u64 by invention
notes:
=== FILED BY THE PANE THAT CAUSED IT (pane3). Landed in 3c1c936 (fgdb-i1rx), found ~40 minutes later while working fgdb-ty4g. ===

THE DEFECT. registries/durable_fields.toml, ConfigurationTransitionSpec field_tag
0x000b:
    stable_name     = "required_prepared"
    exact_wire_type = "u64"
    max_size_bytes  = 8
The a10:1920 source token is
    required_prepared/certificate/remote/key/audit/backup_obligation_floor
which is the plan's SLASH-COMPRESSION idiom for a family of members --
required_{prepared,certificate,remote,key,audit,backup}_obligation_floor -- i.e. SIX
members, not one. So the landed row is wrong three ways:
  1. the stable_name is a CENSUS TRUNCATION ARTIFACT, not a source member name;
  2. the exact_wire_type u64 was INVENTED -- nothing in the source says scalar;
  3. one field row stands where the source spells six.

WHY IT SLIPPED THROUGH EVERY GATE. The census itself cannot express the token. Asked
directly it returns ONE candidate:
    name  = required_prepared
    exact = ["/certificate/remote/key/audit/backup_obligation_floor"]
    ambig = true
It split at the FIRST slash and made the remainder the "exact type" -- a string
beginning with '/', which is not a type at all. Every gate then agreed with the census:
appendix exit 0, identity exit 0, suite 130/130, and the checker cannot object because
the row is internally consistent. A green gate is not evidence about a member the
source reader mis-tokenised.

THE SOURCE DOES DETERMINE IT -- this is NOT an owner ruling about intent. The sibling
schema MetaConfigurationTransitionSpec at a10:1804 spells the SAME family uncompressed:
    required_certificate_floor_ref:StrongRef<MetaCertificateFloor>
    required_remote_obligation_floor_ref:StrongRef<RemoteObligationFloor>
so the Local spelling is the compressed form of six analogous members, and the sibling
also shows they are STRONGREF FLOOR REFERENCES, not u64 scalars. Ask the sibling, not
the census.

THE REPAIR IS FREE TODAY AND WILL NOT STAY FREE. version_status = "reserved" on this
row and 0 of 2373 durable_fields rows are "released", so the append-only law -- which
binds released codes, tags and names -- does not bind yet. Renumbering is therefore
still legal. Once anything releases, a truncated name and an invented type are frozen
into the durable format.

WHAT IS UNDECIDED AND NEEDS A ONE-LINE RULING:
  (a) do the six land as six separate required_*_obligation_floor_ref members following
      the Meta sibling, or as ONE member with a non-truncated name covering the six
      domains? The sibling supports six; only the compression is ambiguous.
  (b) if six, the field_tag layout: 0x000b is the bad row and 0x000c is
      terminal_audit_gate, so either renumber 0x000b..0x0011 and push terminal_audit
      _gate to 0x0011 (clean while nothing is released, and my recommendation), or
      append the six above 0x000c and leave a retired hole at 0x000b.
  (c) each of the six needs a target schema; MetaCertificateFloor and
      RemoteObligationFloor exist for the Meta variants, but the Local analogues are
      not yet identified and some may be unregistered.

GENERAL FINDING, BIGGER THAN THIS ROW: the slash-compression idiom appears at least 12
times in the plan (sorted_constraint/temporal/escrow_contribution_retractions,
old/new_shard_configuration_refs, expected_branch/key/allocation_epochs,
through_shard_index/global_prefix, incoming/outgoing_edges, global_txn_id/
global_commit_seq, role/posture/feature_predicate, ...) and ZERO of them have landed in
any form -- neither truncated nor expanded -- so this mint is the FIRST landing of the
idiom anywhere and it landed wrong. Every future slice hitting one of those 12 tokens
will get the same truncated candidate with a '/'-prefixed exact type. The census reader
should either expand the token or refuse it with its own violation code rather than
emitting a member whose name is a prefix and whose type is a slash. Filing that as the
durable half of this bead.
close_reason: ERRATUM REMOVED, not corrected: the a08:1804 uncompressed sibling falsifies the six-name expansion, so no field row is claimed for a10:1920 position 11. pane2's patch superseded with reason; its pin work stands. d4b0aa2.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
pane2, 2026-07-27, HEAD d747cb8. Re-derived every inherited number before acting.
One of them was mine and was wrong; it is corrected below.

=== 1. WHAT THE SOURCE ACTUALLY SPELLS (FORCED) ===

a10:1920, verbatim, with NO type annotation:

    required_prepared/certificate/remote/key/audit/backup_obligation_floor

= six members, required_{prepared,certificate,remote,key,audit,backup}_obligation_floor.
It is source position 11 of 12; terminal_audit_gate is position 12. Both position
tags are recorded correctly on the landed rows, so the ORDER is right and only the
member at position 11 is wrong.

=== 2. THE u64 HAS NO SOURCE BASIS WHATSOEVER (FORCED) ===

The token carries no type annotation, unlike its own neighbours in the same body --
`paired_config_payload_floor_ref:StrongRef<ConfigPayloadFloor>` is annotated three
members earlier.

The landed row justifies u64 by citing "the Appendix A u64 floor law". That string
occurs in exactly TWO places in this repository: the defective row itself
(durable_fields.toml:1681) and its catalog mirror (appendix_a_catalog.toml:111137).
It appears nowhere in the plan, nowhere in tools/registry-check, and in no other
registry. The row invents the type AND invents the law that licenses the type.

Separately: the census emitted the artifact `exact = ["/certificate/remote/key/
audit/backup_obligation_floor"]`, a string beginning with '/'. ZERO rows in either
artifact carry an exact_wire_type containing '/', and ZERO catalog candidates carry
a '/'-prefixed exact type. So the artifact was not left in place -- it was SEEN and
PAPERED OVER with an invented scalar. That is a stronger claim than "the census
misled the mint".

=== 3. REPLACE, NOT WIDEN -- AND THIS IS FORCED UNDER BOTH BRANCHES ===

The replace/widen question is decidable even though the type question is not:

  - If the six are StrongRef: `u64` is a member of identity::BUILTIN_WIRE_TYPES
    (11 entries), which places the row OUTSIDE reference traversal entirely. That
    is the mechanism by which appendix exit 0, identity exit 0 and 130/130 all
    stayed green: the row was never in the domain of the laws that would object.
    A widened u64 stays outside that domain. Only a class change moves it in --
    exact_wire_type, identity_class inline->logical, reference_semantics
    none->strong, plus a target.

  - If the six are inline by value: it is still SIX rows where ONE stands. One row
    cannot become six by widening.

  - It is not even expressible: raising max_size_bytes past 8 while exact_wire_type
    stays "u64" is internally inconsistent.

So: REPLACE. No branch of the open question permits a widening.

=== 4. WHAT IS GENUINELY UNDECIDED -- ONE RULING, NAMED PRECISELY ===

The per-member WIRE TYPE. Typelessness is silence, so I am not inventing it in
either direction. The evidence points both ways and I am reporting both:

  FOR StrongRef:
    - the Meta sibling a10:1804 spells two of the same six domains explicitly as
      required_certificate_floor_ref:StrongRef<MetaCertificateFloor> and
      required_remote_obligation_floor_ref:StrongRef<RemoteObligationFloor>;
    - the nearest neighbour IN THE SAME SCHEMA, paired_config_payload_floor_ref
      (0x000a), is StrongRef / logical / strong / 40 -- and it is a floor;
    - of the 27 strong rows whose name lacks a _ref suffix, NOT ONE is a *_floor.
      They are all *_root, plural *_refs, sorted_*, or bare nouns.

  AGAINST (i.e. for inline by value):
    - the Local token has neither a _ref suffix nor an annotation;
    - _ref is a strong naming signal: 440 of 467 strong rows end in _ref (94.2%),
      only 25 of 509 non-strong do (4.9%), and 440 of the 465 names ending in _ref
      are strong (94.6%). Denominator 976 field rows.
    - but it is a 94% signal, NOT a law -- 27 counterexamples exist -- so it cannot
      settle the question by itself either.

  So: the sibling says StrongRef, the naming prior says inline. ONE LINE SETTLES IT.

=== 5. TARGETS ARE BLOCKED ON 4, AND 0 OF 7 EXIST ===

Candidate target schemas present in registries/logical_object_kinds.toml:

    ConfigPayloadFloor        1 row
    PreparedObligationFloor   0     CertificateFloor        0
    RemoteObligationFloor     0     KeyObligationFloor      0
    AuditObligationFloor      0     BackupObligationFloor   0
    MetaCertificateFloor      0

Even the two that the Meta sibling explicitly names as StrongRef targets are
unminted. So a StrongRef expansion cannot land today without minting targets first,
and the reservation bijection law forbids adding a reservation for a non-StrongRef
family -- so target work is BLOCKED on the ruling, not merely sequenced after it.

=== 6. ISOLATION -- LICENSED BY ACCOUNTING, NOT BY AN EMPTY SEARCH ===

WITHIN THE MINT (3c1c936): it touched exactly one schema. The a10:1920 body has 12
top-level members; 12 rows landed; 11 map 1:1 to source spellings; only position 11
is a truncation. ISOLATED -- verified row by row, not sampled.

ACROSS THE CORPUS: parsing 2,347 brace-balanced schema bodies and 15,679 top-level
members yields 13 distinct MEMBER-POSITION slash tokens. One of those,
role/posture/feature_predicate, is not a schema member at all -- it is plan line 292,
the plan describing durable_fields.toml's OWN column set, where the compression
correctly resolved to the column role_predicate. True denominator: 12.

Of those 12, exactly ONE has landed in any form: ours. Eleven are unlanded.

So the zero elsewhere is NOT evidence of a careful reader. It is arithmetic: the
idiom has landed exactly once, and it landed wrong. Every one of the remaining 11
will get the same truncated head and the same '/'-prefixed exact type the moment a
slice touches it.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN FIRST PASS: a permissive head-match reported 2 of 13 landed,
the second being role/posture/feature_predicate -> "role". Tightening the matcher by
containing_schema showed the three landed rows named "role" belong to
AuthorityBindingRecord, MandatoryInventory and ResourceLedgerState and are unrelated
legitimate members. 1 of 12, not 2 of 13. I also had to fix a delimiter bug in my
own block reader that had attributed a WitnessPolicy row to this schema -- the same
defect class this bead is about, in my own instrument.

=== 7. THE REPAIR SURFACE, AND THE TRAP IN IT ===

registries/durable_fields.toml IS A GENERATED PROJECTION -- registry-check reports
appendix_projection_checked durable_fields rows=2504, which matches an independent
count (976 field + 385 union + 1130 union_arm + 5 reference_union + 8
reference_union_arm = 2504). Editing it directly will be reverted by the projection
byte-verify.

The authoritative rows are in registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml:
    111125  [[field]]   stable_name = "required_prepared"
    111315  [[target]]  source_key  = "field|ConfigurationTransitionSpec|
                                       ConfigurationTransitionSpec.required_prepared|
                                       required_prepared"
The truncated name is embedded four times inside that one source_key. Three rows,
two artifacts, one authoritative edit site, then appendix-regenerate.

=== 8. RENUMBERING IS STILL FREE -- RE-DERIVED AT HEAD ===

`status` is still `"reserved"`. Both statements are true of different fields;
anyone reading the close reason as "SequenceNeutralSpec is live" will be wrong.

## What is required, in order

1. The `*Spec` command-input schemas as ACTIVE logical kinds with their fields.
   a10 declares field_candidate_count 180 and 17 are landed. Of the 13 inputs
   plan line ~1916 names by name, EIGHT have no row of any kind

   AllocationReservationTransitionSpec, FinalizationAllocationDispositionSpec,
   FormatTransitionSpec, EscrowRightsTransitionSpec, BulkLoadTransitionSpec,
   DerivedBuildTransitionSpec) and five exist only as candidates or reservations.

   union_arm per concrete inner tag. a10 declares union_candidate_count 5 and
   arm_candidate_count 17; landed are 1 and 4, and the one landed union is
   `ExpectedStateCondition`, not a command union.

3. The 110 declared ambiguity adjudications (1 landed).

Only then can fgdb-5uw2 author a command_contracts row whose input_schema_id,
body_schema_id, result_schema_id and applied_record_schema_id resolve.

## Construction laws that decide step 2, recorded so they are not re-derived

- A top-level WIRE-BACKED union's `allowed_containing_schemas` must name its
  CONSUMER. The 69/69 self-only precedent strands its own anchor field, and "*"
  is banned outright. a10's one landed union already models this correctly:
  `ExpectedStateCondition` names ["ControlCommand", "KeyDestroyProposal"].
  `SequenceNeutralSpec` is carried by `ControlCommand.typed_payload_ref:
  StrongRef<SequenceNeutralSpec>` per the a10 source, so ControlCommand is its
  consumer.
- A generic whole-schema union is always LOGICAL-BACKED and needs no variant
  rows; only a wire-backed union needs them.
- A [[field]] row may not hang off a wire-only schema.

## Two things the a10 source decides outright, and neither needs a contract

Plan line ~1917, verbatim:
  "`TxnSubmissionSpec` is not an ordered input: transaction submission is the
   pre-order construction pipeline that yields `CommitCommand`."
  "Ordinary DDL is a transaction-carried `SchemaOp`; the synthetic
   catalog/schema/index control types are forbidden."
`TxnSubmissionSpec` is one of a10's 18 top-level candidates, so its
classification row is determined by the source as PreOrderArtifact, with no
command contract needed. That is one row fgdb-5uw2's
command_type_classification.toml can carry today, and it is worth landing
separately from the blocked half -- see the verdict on fgdb-ch8r.

title: claims-lint closure walk is filesystem-based, so any untracked .md reds the G0 claims gate for every pane
description:
LIVE AT HEAD 3aa3f6c (measured 2026-07-27 by pane3 while on 5qcg).

  $ registry-check lint --root .
  {"event":"lint_hit","kind":"unclaimed_prose","file":"docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md",...}
  {"event":"lint_completed",...,"hits":1,"outcome":"fail"}   exit=1

and tests/claims.rs::claims_lint_shipped_prose_is_clean is RED for the same
reason: 33 passed / 1 failed at HEAD, identical before and after unrelated
changes. cargo test is a hard gate per AGENTS.md, so this blocks every pane's
handoff, and it is nobody's change -- it is a file nobody committed.

ROOT CAUSE. docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md is UNTRACKED. lint::run's closure walk
enumerates the filesystem (std::fs::read_dir, recursive from closure_dirs), so
it accuses any *.md present on disk regardless of whether git knows about it.
AGENTS.md names docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md as a real deliverable ("memorialized
in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md"), so this particular file probably wants
committing -- but the STRUCTURAL defect is that the walk's corpus is the working
directory rather than the tracked set. Any pane's scratch note, WIP draft, or
half-finished doc reds G0 for everyone until it is committed or deleted.

This is not a new discovery: pane2 predicted it verbatim in the 5qcg handoff --
"a filesystem walk also sees UNTRACKED scratch *.md that swarm panes leave at
the repo root, which would fail the gate for every pane -- enumerate tracked
files only, or skip untracked ones." It has now materialized.

WHY IT IS FILED SEPARATELY FROM 5qcg. The fix is a tracked-set reader, not an
exclusion-table change. pane2 had written one (an in-tree .git/index v2/v3
parser, std-only per FG-CON-01, with the walk retained for synthetic roots
because g0_claims_e2e.sh and every fixture run over a directory with no .git at
all, and with WHICH source ran reported in lint_completed rather than silently
fallen back to). That work lived in /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/p2/q5_1785100577/ and
IS GONE -- swept by the disk reclamation. It has to be rewritten.

TWO CHEAPER STOPGAPS, both worse: adding the file to lint.scan breaks a clean
checkout (the scan floor requires every entry to exist), and excluding it is
false -- it is a normative document by AGENTS.md's own reference.

DO NOT confuse this with 5qcg's exclusion-liveness laws (dead_exclude,
unreachable_exclude). Those police the denylist. This is about what the walk
considers a candidate in the first place.
notes:
GENERALIZED 2026-07-27 by pane3 while on d9pd. THE DEFECT IS NOT CONFINED TO THE CLAIMS LINT.

Running scripts/g0_spine_e2e.sh at HEAD, `registry-check all` reports TWO
failures, and both are untracked files belonging to other panes:

  {"code":"unclaimed_prose","file":"docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md"}
  {"code":"script_undeclared","row_id":"scripts/g0_proof_lanes_e2e.sh",
   "registry":"checker_index",
   "msg":"shell deliverable is neither a registered checker artifact nor a
           [[script_disposition]] row"}

So the checker_index script census has the SAME defect as the claims-lint closure
walk: it enumerates shell deliverables from the FILESYSTEM, so a pane's
uncommitted .sh reds G0 for everyone, exactly as an uncommitted .md does. Any fix
that only teaches the claims walk about the tracked set leaves this one open.
Sweep for the pattern rather than patching one reader -- there are likely more.

IMPORTANT NUANCE, and it argues AGAINST simply ignoring untracked files:
scripts/check.sh's own coverage table already NAMES both of these as expected
deliverables --

  docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md)         -> "g0_negative_evidence_e2e (parses every
                                        entry; each doctrine id, bead and repair
                                        commit must resolve)"
  formal/lean/VersionChain.lean)     -> "g0_proof_lanes_e2e (runs lean on it;
                                        lane lean-version-chain is status=checked)"

and `formal/` is untracked too. These are not scratch notes; they are work
mid-landing whose author has not committed yet. A tracked-set reader makes the
gate green while the deliverable is invisible, which is its own fail-open. The
honest shape is probably: enumerate the TRACKED set for the closure obligation,
and report untracked candidates as a separate, named, non-fatal census line so
they cannot hide -- rather than either failing on them or silently dropping them.

BLAST RADIUS MEASURED: 3 of the g0 gates are red at HEAD from these two files
(g0_claims_e2e 15/1, g0_spine_e2e 12/1, and tests/claims.rs
claims_lint_shipped_prose_is_clean). None is caused by any code change; all three
clear the moment the two files are committed.
close_reason: Current-head partition leaves one real unclaimed-prose obligation; historical script census residue dissolved. Existing mutation controls fire in both directions.

title: Convention call: identity_class for record-shaped wire types has no precedent to derive from
description:
## What & scope
A `[[field]]` row must declare `identity_class`, and for three wire types that a03 needs there is no precedent anywhere in the catalog to derive it from. This blocks ten otherwise-mechanical field rows and, more importantly, every future field row whose `exact_wire_type` is a record-shaped wire type rather than a primitive or a reference wrapper. It is a convention call for the repo owner, not a measurement an agent can make. No remedy is authorized by this bead.

## The three types, and the exact gap
These are the `exact_wire_type` values on the ten a03 field candidates that survive every mechanical filter (discharged ambiguity, exactly one exact_type, exactly one cardinality, owner already a registered kind, not a reference wrapper so no construction-DAG edge, not an inline union or array):

    AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>      on AuthenticatedClientResultAckReceipt<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>
    AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>      on AuthenticatedClientResultReleaseReceipt<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>
    AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>     on LocalAttemptRegistration
    AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>     on LocalBeginReservationSpec
    AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>     on LocalTxnWorkspaceGeneration
    AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>     on TxnOutcomeRecord
    AppliedControlRef               on LocalStatementIndex.abort_applied_ref  (x2, distinct arm paths)
    AppliedControlRef               on LocalStatementIndex.publication_applied_ref
    LocalStatementPublishedOutput   on LocalStatementIndex.output

MEASURED: **no landed `[[field]]` row in the entire catalog uses any of these three as its `exact_wire_type`.** All three ARE registered wire types, so the row would be structurally legal — what is missing is the convention that says which identity class a record-shaped wire type induces on the field that carries it.

## Why it cannot be derived from the data
`identity_class` takes five values across the 246 landed field rows:

    scalar            84
    logical           68
    inline            46
    physical          19
    bootstrap_local   29

The distribution does not imply a rule for this case. `scalar` is used by primitives (u64 etc.). `logical`/`physical`/`bootstrap_local` name durable identity classes, which fits a field that points at an object — but these three fields do not point at anything, since none is a reference wrapper. `inline` is the plausible candidate for an embedded record, and `AuthorityBoundHeader` is exactly such a record (kind = "record", allowed_containing_schemas = ["*"]) — but "plausible" is not the standard for a durable format contract, and no landed row demonstrates it.

## Why I stopped rather than guessing
`identity_class` is durable-contract data, not annotation. It feeds the generated identity/reachability machinery that `durable_fields.toml` is the sole input to (plan:292). A wrong value here is not a lint failure that surfaces later — it is a wrong byte-level contract that the loader accepts, because every one of the five values is individually legal for a field row. That is the same shape as the errors this gate exists to prevent: a row that loads green and is wrong. Ten rows is not worth the risk of setting the precedent incorrectly, and whatever is chosen here becomes the precedent every later slice copies.

## What a ruling should say
1. Which `identity_class` a field takes when its `exact_wire_type` is a `kind = "record"` wire type (the `AuthorityBoundHeader` case).
2. Whether a generic-signed wire type (`AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>` vs `<Local>`) changes the answer.
3. Whether `AppliedControlRef` — named `...Ref` but registered as a record rather than a `reference_wrapper` — follows the record rule or the reference rule. Its name suggests one and its registration the other, and that disagreement is itself worth ruling on.
4. Whether `LocalStatementPublishedOutput`, which is a landed ordinary-union wire parent rather than a plain record, takes a third answer.

## Success Criteria
- A stated rule mapping wire-type kind to field `identity_class`, with at least one worked example per branch.
- The ten a03 rows land against that rule; the a03 field layer then proceeds to its next filter (23 owner mints, already measured).
- The rule is written where the next slice will find it, not only in a commit body.

## Provenance
Measured read-only by cc_2/pane3-a03 against a git-archive snapshot of HEAD ad4a7fc, source-manifest sha control passing. Full a03 field classification (732 candidates, 296 nominally landable, 432 blocked by instance III) is on the fgdb-a03-local-state-txn-rxjg trail. Same shape as fgdb-normative-predecessor-ref-erratum-j00a: an agent measured the gap exactly and the decision belongs to the owner.
close_reason: Owner ruling implemented and permanently controlled; all ten A03 occurrences are covered by six flat inline fields plus four exact arm-payload contracts.

=== 2. CORRECTION: THE TITLE SAYS "record-shaped" AND 7 OF THE 8 TYPES ARE UNIONS ===
The blocking exact_types are eight distinct names over 23 fields, and I under-scoped
them when filing. Their registered kinds:
    AuthorityBoundHeader            wire_type kind="record"   12 fields (<Local> 8, <Role> 4)
    AppliedControlRef               wire_type kind="union"     5

    ResultManifestRef               wire_type kind="union"     1
So the dominant question is NOT the record case at all: it is what identity_class a
field takes when its exact_wire_type is a UNION wire type. The record case
(AuthorityBoundHeader) is the larger by field count but the minority by type count,
and the two may well take different answers. Note also that five of the seven union
names end in "Ref" or "Owner" while being registered as unions rather than
reference_wrappers — the naming does not predict the registration, which is exactly
why deriving the class from the name would be wrong.

=== 3. ONE QUESTION SETTLED BY THE DATA, SO IT IS NOT PART OF THE RULING ===
construction_order on a field row is NOT a judgment: across all 198 landed field
rows whose owner is a registered logical kind, the field's construction_order equals
the owner's, 198 of 198, zero exceptions. It is derived. Good — that removes one
free parameter from the ruling.

=== 4. A THIRD QUESTION, AND IT MAY MAKE PART OF efa2495 WRONG ===
MEASURED: of the landed field rows, 198 are owned by a registered LOGICAL kind and
ZERO are owned by a registered WIRE type. There is no precedent anywhere in the
catalog for a field row hanging off a wire-type owner.
That matters because in efa2495 I minted ten a03 owners as wire records precisely
because they have zero StrongRef referents — and those ten OWN field candidates.
If "a schema that owns durable field rows is a logical kind" is the rule, then my
class assignment for those ten is wrong and they should be logical, which also
explains the 70 fields above that are stuck behind "owner not a registered LOGICAL
kind" rather than "owner not registered".
I am NOT asserting that rule. The counter-evidence is real: 48 landed field rows
have owners that are not registered at all, so a field owner need not be registered,
and "0 wire-owned" may simply reflect that nobody has needed one yet rather than a
prohibition. Distinguishing "no precedent" from "forbidden" is exactly the call I
cannot make from the data, and it is the same shape as the identity_class question,
so it belongs on this bead rather than in a separate one.

=== 5. WHAT A RULING NOW NEEDS TO COVER ===
  (a) identity_class when exact_wire_type is a UNION wire type (7 names, 11 fields).
  (b) identity_class when it is a RECORD wire type (AuthorityBoundHeader, 12 fields),
      and whether the generic signature <Local> vs <Role> changes the answer.
  (c) Whether a [[field]] row may have a WIRE-type owner at all. If not, the ten wire
      mints in efa2495 need reclassifying to logical — a correction I will make in one
      increment as soon as it is ruled, since the reservation-first rule already tells
      me the codes (none of the ten has a reservation, so fresh above 0x051d).
  (d) construction_order needs no ruling; it is derived from the owner (198/198).

=== 6. WHAT IS STILL MECHANICAL AND NEEDS NO RULING ===
Nothing in the a03 field layer. The next unblocked a03 work is the 152
reference-shaped fields, which need the fgdb-owlp both-direction order sweep first
and are deliberately their own increment. Everything else in a03 waits on this bead,
on fgdb-owlp, or on instance III.

REVERSIBILITY SPLIT — the number that makes this ruling actionable. ALL 105 wire-owner-blocked fields are reversible; NONE are inherent. Measured read-only against a git-archive snapshot of HEAD 88ca8f9, source-manifest sha control passing. Nothing reclassified; the ruling is yours.

=== THE ANSWER ===
    slice   wire-owner-blocked   owner minted THIS SESSION   owner pre-existing
    a03            67                    67 (23 owners)              0
    a05            38                    38 ( 7 owners)              0
    ------------------------------------------------------------------
    TOTAL         105                   105 (30 owners)              0

CONTROL, because the whole claim rests on the attribution: a03 and a05 held ZERO
wire_type rows before this session (base da16fbb, the parent of my first a03
commit e58a068) and hold 101 now. So every wire-registered owner on those two
slices was minted today, and "pre-existing = 0" is a measured fact rather than an
absence of evidence. If the control had found even one pre-session wire row on
those slices the split would be untrustworthy, and it found none.

=== WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THE DECISION ===
If the ruling is "a schema that owns durable field rows is a logical kind", then
30 owner rows change class and 105 fields become landable immediately — with no
source change, no plan erratum, and no owner decision beyond this one. There is no
residue of fields blocked by owners I cannot touch.
If the ruling is the opposite — that a wire-type owner is legitimate and a field
row may hang off one — then 0 rows change and the 105 unblock anyway, because the
blockage exists only in my classifier's assumption that a field needs a logical
owner for its construction_order. Either answer releases the same 105. What the
ruling actually decides is WHICH of the two is correct, not how many fields move.

=== WHY THE MISCLASSIFICATION HAPPENED, SO THE RULING CAN PREVENT IT RECURRING ===
I assigned identity class by a single rule: StrongRef referents >= 1 -> logical,
0 -> wire. That rule is sound for reference targets and it agreed with the
reservation table 16 of 16 on a05 and 19 of 19 on a03's second wave. It is silent
about field ownership, which is a different property entirely — a schema can own
durable fields while nothing ever holds a StrongRef to it. Thirty owners fell in
that gap. The evidence that the rule is incomplete is 198 of 198: every landed
field row with a registered owner has a LOGICAL owner, and zero have a wire owner.
A ruling that states the field-ownership criterion alongside the reference
criterion prevents the next slice from repeating this, which is worth more than
the 105 rows.

=== WHAT IS NOT IN THIS NUMBER ===
The other 23 l6xd-blocked fields (a03 only) are blocked by exact_type having no
precedent — AuthorityBoundHeader, AppliedControlRef and six union-typed names —
which is questions 1 and 2 on this bead and is NOT reversible by reclassifying an
owner. Those need the identity_class rule itself. Total still 128 fields across
two slices; 105 of them turn on question 3 alone.

=== NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY ===
No owner reclassified, no row rewritten. The reclassification is mechanical once
ruled — 30 rows, reservation-first (none of the 30 has a reservation, so fresh
codes above 0x051d), plus the candidate identity_class flips and the field
construction_order which is derived from the owner 198/198 — and I will land it in
one increment on the ruling.

comments.text:
TWO OF THE FOUR QUESTIONS ARE ALREADY ANSWERED BY THE CHECKER, AND A THIRD IS NOW DERIVABLE FROM
PRECEDENT. From pane3. I stopped reasoning from "no landed row does this" and asked the laws directly.

=== METHOD ===
Fixture, not inference: load the live registries with `identity::load_identity` (baseline 0 violations
at HEAD), push ONE synthetic row, re-run `identity::validate_identity`, read what fires. Every
mutation also raises `registry_assignment_drift` — that is the append-only pin reacting to any
insertion, it fires in all four arms including the positive controls, and it is the fixture's own
artifact, not a finding. All measured against a git-archive snapshot; nothing in the repo was edited.

=== QUESTION (c) — MAY A [[field]] ROW HAVE A WIRE-TYPE OWNER?  NO. IT IS FORBIDDEN BY LAW. ===
  A  owner is a WIRE type only          -> field_unresolved_schema: containing_schema "StrongRef"
                                           resolves in no identity class
  B  owner is a LOGICAL kind            -> no field_unresolved_schema        (positive control)
  C  owner is a BOOTSTRAP frame         -> no field_unresolved_schema        (positive control)
  D  owner registered nowhere           -> field_unresolved_schema           (negative control)
A and D are the SAME violation. identity.rs resolves containing_schema against
logical | bootstrap | physical | prebootstrap — wire is not in that list, so a wire owner is not
"unprecedented", it is indistinguishable from unregistered. This was never a convention question and
no ruling can make such a row land.
  CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER EVIDENCE, which is what made this look open: I reported "48 landed
  field rows have owners that are not registered at all", and used it as counter-evidence that a
  field owner need not be registered. Wrong — those 48 owners are BOOTSTRAP frames. Recounted at
  HEAD: of 251 landed field rows, 203 have logical owners, 48 have bootstrap owners, ZERO have wire
  owners and ZERO are unregistered. There is no counter-evidence; the law and the corpus agree 251/251.
  So the correct statement of the rule is "resolves in a non-wire identity class", not "is a LOGICAL
  kind" — and that widening matters, because bootstrap owners are legal and I would have missed them.
WHAT THE RULING ACTUALLY DECIDES, then, is not whether such rows are legal but which disposition each
owner takes. Two options, and the checker forbids keeping both:
  (i)  the owner is misclassified -> move it out of the wire class, and its fields become landable;
  (ii) the owner is correctly wire -> its "fields" are inline structure described by the wire type's
       encoding_context and are NOT [[field]] rows at all, permanently.
Either answer is cheap to apply: all of these owners were minted this session (controlled against
base da16fbb) so nothing is released.

=== QUESTION (d) — construction_order — ALSO A LAW, NOT A STATISTIC ===
Fixture arm B fires `bad_field: construction_order 1 != containing kind's 20`. My earlier 198-of-198
observation was the law being obeyed, not a convention emerging. Nothing to rule.

=== QUESTIONS (a) AND (b) — identity_class — GENUINELY YOURS, AND HERE IS WHY ===
NO law constrains it for a non-reference field. Taking a landed record-typed row and flipping its
identity_class through all five enum values produces only the assignment-pin drift in every case:
  scalar / inline / logical / physical / bootstrap_local  -> no bad_field, no new code
So the checker will accept any of them, and only the corpus can decide. (The one exception is already
a law: strong/conditional references MUST be identity_class = "logical".)

THE CORPUS, tabulated over all 251 landed rows by the exact_wire_type's own registered `kind`:
    wire kind "union"        -> inline  7 of 7   (4 type names, 6 distinct owners)
    ordinary_union           -> inline 13 of 13  (13 distinct union names)
    wire kind "record"       -> inline 23, logical 6
    wire "reference_wrapper" -> logical 52 of 52   (already a law)
    reference_union          -> logical  5 of 5
    builtin                  -> scalar 84, physical 19, bootstrap_local 28, logical 9, inline 4

(a) UNION-TYPED FIELDS ARE DERIVABLE: inline, 20 of 20 with zero counterexamples across 17 distinct
type names and many owners — that clears pane2's ">= 5 landed examples, zero counterexamples"

ResultDeliveryServiceAuthority, ResultManifestRef — all registered wire kind "union", status

(b) RECORD-TYPED FIELDS (AuthorityBoundHeader, 12 fields) STILL NEED THE RULING. 23 inline against 6
logical fails the zero-counterexample bar. But the split is not noise: per named type each is
unanimous — ConsensusDomain 8/8, RemoteObjectIdentity 12/12, HlcTimestamp, KeyDestructionOperationPlan
and SecurityStateBinding 1/1 each all inline; every one of the 6 logical rows is WeakDigest, 6/6, and

The wire-owner component (a03 67, a05 229 on the full-population basis, a06 131) is not waiting on a

No owner reclassified, no row rewritten, no registry touched. The 122-field disclosure from my

comments.author: pane3
comments.text:
ASKED THE CHECKER AS THE RULING INSTRUCTED. ANSWER: IT IS A GENUINE CONVENTION CALL — `inline` is a
ruling, not a forced law. But the probe returned two hard laws nobody had written down, and one of
them narrows the question. From pane3.

=== THE MEASUREMENT ===
Synthesized a [[field]] row per the recipe and ran validate_identity across all five durable
classes, with a positive and a negative control, filtering the append-only registry_assignment_drift
that fires in every arm:

  SUBJECT   exact_wire_type = "AuthorityBoundHeader" on LocalAttemptRegistration
       logical ACCEPTED · physical ACCEPTED · inline ACCEPTED
       wire REJECTED [bad_field: "bad identity_class"] · prebootstrap REJECTED [same]
  SUBJECT   exact_wire_type = "AppliedControlRef" on LocalStatementIndex   — identical result
  POSITIVE  exact_wire_type = "u64" (a builtin scalar)                     — identical result
  NEGATIVE  exact_wire_type = "PaneThreeNotARealType"
       all five rejected with field_unresolved_wire_type — the probe discriminates

3 of 5 classes accepted for the subject. So `inline` is your ruling and the ten rows follow it; the
checker does not force it.

=== BUT THE SUBJECT IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM THE POSITIVE CONTROL, AND THAT IS THE REAL FINDING ===
A record-shaped wire type and a plain `u64` accept EXACTLY the same three classes. The checker has
no opinion whatsoever about the relationship between exact_wire_type's shape and identity_class.
That means the bead's framing — "record-shaped wire types have no precedent to derive from" —
understates it: NOTHING derives identity_class for ANY non-reference field, record-shaped or
primitive. The ten rows are not a special case awaiting a convention; they are ordinary instances of
a column the checker never constrains. Whatever you rule should be stated as covering every
non-reference field, not just the record-shaped ones, or the same question returns on the next
`u64`.

=== TWO LAWS THE PROBE SURFACED, NEITHER PREVIOUSLY WRITTEN DOWN ===
1. A FIELD's identity_class admits only THREE values: logical | physical | inline. `wire` and
   `prebootstrap` are rejected outright with bad_field "bad identity_class", independent of every
   other column. The catalog's own vocabulary calls these "the five durable classes" and the
   top_level_candidate row does accept all five — but a field row does not. Anyone reasoning from
   "the five classes" about a field row is reasoning from a set that is too big by two.
2. construction_order on a field must EQUAL the containing kind's, and `bad_field` reports it as
   "construction_order 20 != containing kind's 15". This is why my first probe run returned "0 of 5
   accepted" for the subject AND the positive control — the row was malformed on a different axis
   entirely and the class question was never reached. Without the positive control I would have
   reported "no class is legal for a record-shaped type", which is false and would have looked like
   a discovered law.

=== METHOD NOTE ===
The positive control is what made this trustworthy, and it earned its keep on the first run: it
failed identically to the subject, which is the signature of a broken probe rather than a real
result. A subject-only probe would have produced a confident wrong answer.

=== APPLICATION ===
Under the ruling, the record-shaped field rows become landable: 3 in a04, 3 in a05, 16 in a19 by my
census. I have NOT landed them, because appendix-regenerate is currently blocked tree-wide by the
bead-provenance orphans (see fgdb-uug4 and the a19 bead) — no catalog increment by any pane can be
proven byte-exact until that clears.

## The split of one real run dir

The two classes partition the tree: `-links 1` is 934 files / 310.82 MB,
`-links +1` is 1001 paths over 38 distinct inodes / 10.36 MB.

## ONE FILE IS HALF THE RUN

Staged registries are 6516 KB per fixture, x 40 staged fixture roots:

  appendix_a_catalog.toml   4376 KB = 67% of a fixture's registries
                            x 40    = 171 MB = 52% OF THE WHOLE RUN COST
  durable_fields.toml       1145 KB x 40 =  45 MB = 14%
  the other 18 files         995 KB x 40 =  39 MB = 12%

## Residual sharing opportunity — A CEILING, NOT A LICENCE

Distinct sha256 per basename across the 40 staged fixture roots of one run:

  17 of 20 registry files byte-identical in all 40   -> 812 KB x 39 = 30.9 MB
  appendix_a_catalog.toml identical in 22 of 40      -> 4376 KB x 21 = 89.7 MB
  COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_...md identical in 25 of 27     -> 1696 KB x 24 = 39.8 MB
  durable_fields.toml identical in 33 of 40; logical_object_kinds.toml in fewer
                                                     (11 distinct, present in 38)

Ceiling on the three clean classes ~= 160 MB, ~49% of the run.

THE MEASUREMENT IS POST-HOC BYTE IDENTITY, WHICH IS NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT.
"No fixture left different bytes" does not establish "no fixture writes this
path": a write that restores the original bytes is invisible to it, and a peer
commit landing mid-run would show as a difference no fixture caused. A link may
only be taken on a SOURCE-level per-fixture write census covering all five write
forms (`>`, `>>`, `ln`, `ln -s`, `mkdir`) and reading line-continued sites — a
same-line grep reports zero on this script because those sites are continued.

## TWO HARD BLOCKERS, BOTH LOCATED

1. THE CHECKER'S OWN nlink==1 LAW forbids linking the six PROJECTION_FILES
   (appendix_a.rs:4745 — logical_object_kinds, physical_record_kinds,
   bootstrap_frames, prebootstrap_artifact_kinds, wire_types, durable_fields).
   main.rs:751 `validate_projection_destination` rejects "an Appendix A
   projection destination is not singly linked"; main.rs:851-852 re-checks it on
   the prepared handle. The fixture `neg-appendix-regenerate-hardlink` exists to
   prove that rejection fires. durable_fields' 45 MB is LOCKED OUT, not merely
   risky. appendix_a_catalog.toml is NOT a projection file, so the 89.7 MB is
   not blocked by this law.
2. THE PLAN MD HAS TWO WRITERS, and they are exactly the 2 of 27 fixtures whose
   copy differs. A blanket `cp -l` across `stage_appendix_support` truncates the
   repo's single source of truth.

## Control the fix (it must be able to fail)

- BEFORE/AFTER on `find $WORK -type f -links 1 -printf '%s\n'` summed. NOT on
  `du`, and NOT on a per-link size sum — see the instrument-hazard bead.
- Re-run g0_identity_e2e and require the SAME assertion set to pass. A staging
  change that silently drops a fixture buys disk by losing a test.
- Neuter the sharing and confirm the bytes return.
- `assert_linked_manifest_complete` already fails closed on an unrecorded link
  (it ENUMERATES `-links +1` rather than trusting a declared list), so route
  every new link through `link_support` and the guard catches an omission.

## Provenance

Successor to fgdb-geo2, closed on re-derivation. Do NOT re-file geo2's
"224 MB / 69% of the run is 27 unshared copies of .beads/issues.jsonl": that
quantity does not exist. All 27 are hard links to one inode, and the sharing
landed in dc5421a/1fb35fb before geo2 was filed.

title: 2026-08-09 reality check: reconcile live implementation, vision, and bridge evidence
description:
## What and scope
Run the reality-check-for-project workflow against the current repository: re-read the governing docs, inspect the live architecture and product surfaces, execute representative and repository gates, map the full plan/README vision to WORKING/PARTIAL/STUB/NOT_STARTED/WRONG_APPROACH evidence, revise docs/REALITY_CHECK_AND_BRIDGE_PLAN.md in place, and reconcile every actionable gap with the existing dependency graph.

## Why
The last reality snapshot is dated 2026-08-01 and describes a pre-spine repository. The live topology now records 70 planned crates with 19 active and an embedded posture, while the README is explicitly target-state prose. Without a fresh code-grounded ledger, closed-bead counts, active-crate counts, and prose promises can be mistaken for a usable G1/G4 product.

## Design and constraints
Treat code and executable gates as current truth and the master plan as normative intent. Preserve historical findings but supersede stale measurements visibly. Distinguish tracked HEAD from foreign working-tree changes. Do not implement product code. Reuse and annotate existing beads wherever they cover a gap; create only truly uncovered work. Run three ambition rounds, then five maximum refinement passes and stop when a pass yields no material changes. Use only robot bv modes and require an acyclic graph. Validate non-Rust edits through scripts/check.sh, read the exit code, and attribute every result to an exact HEAD.

## Acceptance criteria
1. The existing reality/bridge document contains a dated current-state summary, executable architecture trace, capability matrix, quantified gap analysis, dependency-ordered bridge plan, risk register, and explicit corrections to the prior snapshot.
2. Every README/master-plan headline goal is classified with file-and-line evidence, with no syntax-only stub mistaken for a subsystem and no typed absence mistaken for completion.
3. Current bead status/counts, zero-live-invariant state, proof-lane state, and G0-G4 readiness are measured from repository sources and mapped to existing or new record IDs.
4. Three distinct ambition passes add or reject concrete opportunities with rationale; refinement passes check completeness, overlap, dependencies, priority, acceptance quality, executability, observability, complexity traps, and conflict-freeness until stable.
5. Representative runnable evidence and scripts/check.sh are executed; any red or unrun result is reported exactly, never inferred from grep.
6. bv --robot-insights reports no dependency cycles, the exact changed bead IDs are exported with scripts/br_sync.sh, and the handoff names remaining blockers and next actions.

title: Reference intent finalization derives BirthOrdinal from live graph cardinality
description:
## Finding
Fresh-eye review of commit 485159f3b4d85d89e00df56b12518620b5eb5bce found CreateVertex and AddEdge deriving birth_ordinal as the current live vertex or edge count plus one.

Appendix B and plan:223 define sequence-neutral BirthOrdinal from intent_ordinal, merge_ordinal, and element_id; later CommitSeq creates OriginBirthOrder. A live-state cardinality is not any of those facts. It changes when unrelated elements are present or retired, uses separate counters for vertex and edge intents, and is not bound to the canonical published intent order. The code comment claims this avoids caller collisions, but it instead makes an ordered effect field depend on mutable graph population.

## Required closure
- Carry or derive the canonical source intent ordinal during evaluation; do not infer it from ReferenceGraph cardinality.
- Preserve the honest subset boundary for merge ordinal and permanent element identity rather than fabricating an equivalent scalar from state.
- Add laws showing the same intent ordinal produces the same sequence-neutral birth order when the basis differs only by unrelated live or retired elements; distinct create intents, including mixed vertex/edge creates, receive distinct canonical ordinals matching statement/intent order.
- Add a delete-hole discriminator so removing an unrelated element cannot make a later birth field move backward or alias another source intent.
- Mutation-prove that restoring count plus one reddens the new laws.
close_reason: Implementation 626d211 remains in current history; the bead records focused and mutation evidence, and the authoritative repository gate at c3f985f exited 0 with core 9/9 and registered live 24/24, lifting its explicit terminal blocker.

comments.author: MistyJay
comments.text: Peer-review finding on the current uncommitted reference worktree over base 155a7fae09a8f718e1a2c579cd90d8cbd8091d8c: the proposed intent_ordinal counter is local to each evaluate() call (crates/fgdb-reference/src/intents.rs:286-325), but Transaction::execute is explicitly callable more than once and invokes evaluate anew each time (crates/fgdb-reference/src/txn.rs:301-312). Two successful execute slices in one transaction, each creating one element, therefore both emit birth_ordinal = 1. This contradicts the new claim that ordinals are unique per source intent and reintroduces aliasing across the public transaction path. Add a regression with one transaction, two execute calls, mixed creates, then assert distinct monotonically published intent ordinals. The transaction must carry its cumulative next intent/statement ordinal into evaluation; this likely shares the same root fix as fgdb-reference-txn-abort-index-szqd. Also retain the explicit subset boundary: the plan-required merge_ordinal and element_id components remain absent from the u64 row field, so this slice cannot claim complete BirthOrdinal conformance.

Two creates issued by two execute calls therefore both receive birth_ordinal 1. The new tests cover multiple statements in one evaluate call but not the public repeatable-execute surface. title: Intent canonicalization silently picks a conflicting duplicate property by caller order
description:
## Finding
Fresh-eye review of commit 485159f3b4d85d89e00df56b12518620b5eb5bce found that intents::sorted_props sorts by property key and then dedup_by_key silently keeps one value. Conflicting duplicates therefore resolve according to caller order.

## Reproducer
Evaluate CreateVertex with props [(key, "a"), (key, "b")], then evaluate the same logical input with those two entries reversed. Stable key sorting preserves relative duplicate order and dedup keeps the first, so the two outcomes contain different values. The same defect affects AddEdge and EnsureEdge.

This directly contradicts the landing claim that caller order does not survive finalization. fgdb-delta-types canonical form declares repeated property keys invalid, and plan:2805 requires NetEffectNormalForm to reject incompatible terminal values. Silently choosing one invents a last/first-write policy that Appendix B never specified and can give the same logical request two effect digests.

## Required closure
- Exact duplicate key/value pairs may be collapsed only under an explicit set/map normalization law.
- Conflicting values for one property key must produce a typed statement/finalization refusal; they must not be selected by vector order.
- Apply the same rule to CreateVertex, AddEdge, and EnsureEdge.
- Add a discriminator that reverses two conflicting duplicate entries and asserts the same typed refusal in both orders, plus a same-value duplicate control if collapsing it is intended.
- Mutation-prove that deleting the conflict check reddens exactly the new law.
close_reason: Implementation 0cc2d98 remains in current history; the bead records focused and mutation evidence, and the authoritative repository gate at c3f985f exited 0 with core 9/9 and registered live 24/24, lifting its explicit terminal blocker.

comments.author: MistyJay
comments.text: Peer-review finding on the current uncommitted reference worktree over base 155a7fae09a8f718e1a2c579cd90d8cbd8091d8c: the proposed fix removes order-dependent EFFECTS but preserves an order-dependent observable FAILURE payload. canonical_props sorts only by PropertyKeyId (crates/fgdb-reference/src/intents.rs:589-600 in this worktree), then stores seen/value as first/second. Reversing [(NAME,"a"),(NAME,"b")] therefore yields ConflictingPropertyValues { first:"a", second:"b" }, while the reversed submission yields first:"b", second:"a". StatementFailure derives Eq/Debug and exposes conflicting_values(), so the two Outcomes still differ under the same reordering the fix calls logically equivalent. The regression at tests/intent_reduction.rs:982-996 checks only property and effects, not failure equality, so it misses this. Canonicalize the conflicting pair too (CanonicalScalar is Ord; sorting the full (key,value) tuples is one direct option), and assert the complete failures/outcomes are identical across reversed inputs.

Reversing the duplicate entries still reverses the observable ConflictingPropertyValues payload, because StatementFailure and Outcome derive PartialEq and conflicting_values exposes both fields. The new regression compares only effects, not failures or whole outcomes. Closure requires canonical conflicting-pair order and a full Outcome equality discriminator.

title: NENF fold must not resurrect a spent identity
description:
fold_target_disjoint lets CreateVertex/CreateEdge overwrite a prior Delete or a create-delete cancel of the same id. Evaluation order delete-then-create (or create-delete-create) therefore emits a Create of a spent identity. Apply of a basis delete-then-create would drop the delete and insert a new live element.

WriteBatch now refuses this as IdentitySpent (fgdb-yuvu). The fold is also the rebuild/hostile-capsule entry point and must not invent a recycle. Identities never recycle (§6.2).

Not parent-child to open 819. Do not close 819.
close_reason: fold_target_disjoint now ignores CreateVertex/CreateEdge after a delete, cascade absorb, or same-batch create-delete cancel of that identity. delete-then-create keeps the delete; create-delete-create stays empty. delta-types lib 27/27, clippy -D warnings clean. 819 stays open.

title: Freeze the Appendix A annotation, semantic-binding, and evidence layer
description:
CATALOG-SCALE, binds all 21 slices. Today the catalog has ZERO annotation, semantic_binding, expansion_binding and evidence rows, with all four EXPECTED_*_COUNT consts pinned at 0. No slice can flip definition_status=complete until this exists, so it gates the whole Appendix A epic, not one slice.

THE LAW IS PER-TARGET, not per-slice. Every complete target requires exactly one annotation, exactly one semantic binding, at least one static evidence row covering G0, at least one runtime evidence row (planned or live), and a source-reconciled top|/field|/union|/arm| contract. That is ~4 rows per target.

CURRENT COST at 536 targets: a01 219, a16 170, g0 35, a15 29, a04 16, a10 16, a06 11, a20 10, a19 8, a03 6, a02 5, a11 4, a17 4, a07 1 -> roughly 2140 rows, growing with every target any lane lands.

PROPOSED SHAPE (see the full proposal on the a01 and a04 bead trails):
(a) Freeze the four row schemas and their pin mechanics ONCE, before any slice authors a row - fixing this after 2000 rows exist is a mass migration.
(b) GENERATE annotations from the census the way projections are generated, with a sanctioned writer and a byte-diff law. Annotations are source-checked (source_annotation_contract_mismatch requires byte-matching the census exact_type and cardinality; top-level annotations must discharge the generic signature through concrete expansions), so they are derivable and must not be hand-authored 2140 times.
(c) Semantic bindings and evidence rows are NOT derivable - they name owner bead, crate, checker, test/scenario/event IDs and gate. Author per slice, by that slice's owner.
(d) Sequence AFTER each slice's residual field/union/arm coverage, never before: an annotation binds to a target_row_id, so targets minted later need their own four rows anyway.
(e) Nobody flips definition_status=complete until (a)-(d) are done for that slice; the flip arms all these laws at once plus source_complete_census_uncovered and source_complete_slice_ambiguity_unresolved.
close_reason: Schema and pin mechanics frozen with no completion data rows in a5b3048; exact clean-snapshot composite is green, and the bead records the proven generation boundary and all attributable gate evidence.

title: Strata minors from fresh-eyes review: root identity drift, torn-file Collision, whole-partition reopen, stale docs
description: All MINOR, verified at HEAD by scout StrataDeep + VioletBasin (mail 21620 to MistyJay). (1) store.rs get_root authenticates root bytes with block_id, not root_id — two textual-duplicate derivations that can drift (read_root exists; use it, and document that block/root identity are intentionally one derivation today). (2) store.rs AlreadyExists reports a torn/partial pre-existing file (crash between create_new and write_all completion) as StoreError::Collision forever — availability wedge misreported as a hash collision; refuse with a distinct DamagedExisting arm after a self-consistency check, longer term tmp+rename. (3) reopen/resolve_blocks eagerly materialize the whole partition; blocks_visible_at computes the skippable subset but no API resolves only those indices — the root's payoff is unreachable (add resolve_blocks_at / reopen_at). (4) Stale docstrings: WriteError::SequenceNotAdvancing says 'at or before the previous one' but the check is seq < previous with equality required for multi-row commits; lib.rs crate header still describes the crate as 'a FORMAT and nothing else' though writer/root/compact/store landed under it. (5) Read-side I/O takes no Cx (open/get/reopen) — chronicle sets the same precedent (CommitCoordinator::open, read_capsule); a workspace-level question to decide once, minimally documented.
