title: THE SPINE: a minimal end-to-end vertical slice a human can actually run, long before W10
notes:
FILED 2026-07-31 from the reality check (docs/REALITY_CHECK_AND_BRIDGE_PLAN.md). This is the single
most important finding of that pass, and it is a SCHEDULING gap rather than a coverage gap.

THE FINDING. Measured: 19 of 71 crates are activated, 274 of 600 beads are closed, 2150 tests pass --
and there is NO WAY FOR A HUMAN TO USE ANY OF IT. No library entry point, no binary, no query. The only
bead for the embedded API is fgdb-w10-embedded-54r: the FULL fgdb::Database surface with the explicit
ownership contract, correctly scoped and correctly late, sitting at P2 in workstream 10.

So the vertical slice is scheduled LAST, after every horizontal layer. That is the classic shape of a
project that is 46% "complete" while 0% usable, and it hides integration risk until the most expensive
possible moment. Chronicle, Strata and the oracle are three islands today; the ONLY place they meet is
inside test files in fgdb-sim.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS. The thinnest possible thing a person can run, built EARLY and deliberately
incomplete:

    let db = Database::open(path)?;          // Chronicle coordinator + recover + Strata store
    db.write(|txn| { txn.create_vertex(..); txn.add_edge(..); })?;   // real commit, two fsyncs
    let n = db.neighbours(v, rel)?;          // served from Strata, at the current frontier
    drop(db); // reopen and get the same graph back

Nothing else. No sessions, no prepared statements, no query language, no ownership leases, no
capability scoping, no server, no CLI.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS NOT, and this matters for doctrine 7. It is a SUBSET of fgdb-w10-embedded-54r, never
a substitute. The module doc must say so and name what is missing: no explicit transaction ownership
contract, no epoch guard, no capability narrowing, no result-stream lifecycle. A slice that stubs the
transaction model is a prototype, and prototypes are prohibited -- so this must use the REAL commit
path (fgdb-chronicle::CommitCoordinator, two fsyncs, real capsules) and the REAL storage
(fgdb-strata tier D). It is thin in SURFACE, not in mechanism.

WHY IT PAYS FOR ITSELF IMMEDIATELY:
 - It is the first production code where the islands meet, so integration defects surface now rather
   than in W10. Every such defect found today is found against 4 crates instead of 40.
 - It gives fgdb-p95p (the benchmark harness) something to measure. Right now there is nothing to
   benchmark, which is part of why no numbers exist.
 - It gives fgdb-z5y0 (the model-based generator) an engine-side target that is a real API rather than
   a test helper.
 - It makes the project demonstrable, which is worth more than it sounds when the honest answer to
   "can I try it" has been no for the entire project.

DEPENDENCIES AND ORDER:
 - BLOCKED BY the root manifest problem: RootSlot.root_manifest_oid points at an object nobody has
   defined, so a reopened database cannot find its partitions. See the comment on fgdb-w3-tier-d-ctj.
   The Strata side already guarantees a partition reopens from a 32-byte identity, so the manifest only
   needs to carry that per partition -- but it is a durable format and therefore needs an Appendix A
   catalog row (G0 territory).
 - RELATES TO fgdb-w10-embedded-54r, which supersedes this. When 54r lands, this slice should be
   ABSORBED into it, not left beside it -- doctrine forbids parallel APIs for the same thing.

LAWS THIS BEAD OWES:
 - open -> write -> read -> drop -> reopen -> read returns the same graph, with nothing held across the
   drop except the path (the shape fgdb-sim/tests/partition_lifecycle.rs already proves at the test
   level -- lift it into production code);
 - a crash between the write and the reopen leaves either the whole transaction or none of it;
 - the result equals fgdb-reference's answer for the same history, reusing the existing differential
   rather than writing a new one;
 - opening a directory that is not a database FAILS CLOSED with a typed error naming why.
close_reason: All four thin-spine laws and both durable/recovery blockers are implemented; current production-runtime example and full gate are green through 53fb871

  ubs over every file I added                           -> 0  (0 criticals)

THE FOUR LAWS:
 1. open->write->read->drop->reopen returns the same graph, at the same frontier
    AND the same content-addressed PartitionRootVersion.
    crates/fgdb/tests/spine.rs::open_write_read_drop_reopen_returns_the_same_graph
 2. a crash between write and reopen leaves the whole batch or none.
    ::a_crash_at_any_protocol_instant_leaves_the_whole_batch_or_none plus
    ::a_crash_on_the_first_commit_covers_the_parent_directory_instant -- the
    seventh instant exists only on the first commit into a fresh capsule dir.
 3. the result equals fgdb-reference's answer for the same history, REUSING the
    existing differential rather than a new oracle.
    crates/fgdb-sim/tests/spine_differential.rs (12 probes; parallel edges,
    self-loop, two relations, hub).
 4. opening a directory that is not a database FAILS CLOSED with a typed error
    naming why -- plus absent path, occupied dir, and existing database.

MUTATION EVIDENCE, every law proven capable of failing:
 M-A never persist blocks       -> 4 laws red, Store(RootBlockLoad{Io(NotFound)})
 M-B never fold the stream      -> both content laws red with left: []
 M-C stop folding past commit 2 -> differential red, engine and oracle disagree
                                   for VId(1) over RelationId(2)
M-B SURVIVED the determinism law (an empty fold is perfectly deterministic), so
that law now also pins the root away from the empty-partition root. M-C survived
agreement_survives_a_reopen, which probes only a batch-1 vertex -- the 12-probe
law carries the weight.

THE BLOCKER EDGE WAS COARSER THAN THE TRUTH. Dep-blocked on fgdb-ge6a, but ge6a's
own newest comment retracts its framing and CommitCoordinator::open recovers the
whole stream from the directory alone. Reopen REBUILDS tier-D from the commit
stream -- doctrine 5 / FG-INV-18's primary path, not a workaround. ge6a adds the
FAST path later; this stays as the authority it is checked against. Cost is in the
module doc, not hidden: rebuild is O(history), on open and after every write.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, so remaining scope is legible: no incremental publish
(fgdb-w3-tier-d-ctj); no properties/labels/vertex reads, tier D being adjacency
only (fgdb-w3-properties-gou); no deletes, their before-images being finalization's
job (fgdb-w5-effects-normal-form-819); one graph/branch/partition; no CLI or server
posture. All named in the crate doc as a SUBSET of fgdb-w10-embedded-54r.

fgdb-sim, because fgdb-sim/src/lib.rs was leased by another pane throughout.

title: write_cost_attribution's chronicle-only timing control false-reds under neighbour machine load
description: Verdict 3 of the_o_history_term_lives_in_rebuild_not_in_the_commit_protocol pins the chronicle-only control's late/early mean ratio at 4x. Under concurrent pane load (cargo builds, sibling test runs) the wall-clock ratio exceeded 4x THREE times this session (27ms->227ms once, similar twice) with the test green in isolation and green on clean re-runs each time — the regression lock is sound, the MEASUREMENT is load-sensitive. Costs a full 149-suite re-run per false red. Candidate fixes: interleave early/late control batches (A/B/A/B) so load skew cancels; use a paired ratio-of-medians; or count I/O operations instead of wall time (the lock is about O(history) WORK, not milliseconds). Do not weaken the 4x bound without one of those — a looser bound is how a real regression hides.
close_reason: Control sentinel-normalized: verdict is on median commit/sentinel ratios, so machine load cancels and only a real O(history) term fires (ratio 2.72->2.89 measured vs 4x bound while wall time drifted 1.5x).

title: The shared cargo target dir reached 325G and twice hit ENOSPC: build slots are disabled, so fgdb-a9tg's documented mitigation cannot run
notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-04 ~12:35Z by CalmSwan during the second ENOSPC of the session.

THE NUMBERS (/usr/bin/du -sh; note the shell aliases du to dust, which does not accept -sh and
silently prints its help instead -- a real trap when measuring under pressure):
  /data/tmp/cargo-target                 325G    <- the SHARED dir every pane builds into
  /data/tmp/fgdb-uy5x-workspace-target   4.3G
  /data/tmp/fgdb-uy5x-target             1.5G
  /data/tmp/cargo-target-calmswan        1.3G
  filesystem: 906G total, 140M free at time of measurement, single mount for /, /tmp and /home.

WHY THIS IS FILED AS A BUG AND NOT A CLEANUP CHORE. The orchestrator advisory attributed the
emergency to the fgdb-uy5x target dirs and asked their owner to reclaim them. That is 5.8G, or
0.6% of the disk. The shared target dir is 56x larger than both of them combined. Reclaiming
uy5x cannot end the emergency and the next workspace build refills it within minutes, so the
advisory as written buys minutes and costs a rebuild.

THE ROOT CAUSE, which is what makes it recurrent rather than a one-off:
  1. Every pane shares CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/tmp/cargo-target (AGENTS.md build-environment
     note; bead fgdb-a9tg documents the contention hazard).
  2. fgdb-a9tg's mitigation is acquire_build_slot via Agent Mail.
  3. acquire_build_slot RETURNS AN ERROR IN THIS ENVIRONMENT: "Build slots are disabled. Enable
     WORKTREES_ENABLED to use this tool." MEASURED this session.
So the documented control for concurrent cargo is unavailable, panes concurrently build many
profiles and targets into one unbounded dir, and nothing prunes it. Growth is unbounded BY
CONSTRUCTION. It will recur after any cleanup.

SECOND, INDEPENDENT SYMPTOM OF THE SAME CAUSE, already cost real debugging time this session:
the shared dir produced a PHANTOM "unresolved import fgdb_crypto::argon2id" while the lib built
clean and the module was present on disk -- another pane's concurrent run clobbering artifacts.
An isolated CARGO_TARGET_DIR gave the true answer immediately. Anyone debugging that class of
red in the source is chasing a ghost. (See also the memory note: a neighbour test run hands you
a false red.)

CANDIDATE FIXES, in rough order of leverage. NOT chosen here -- this bead records the
measurement and the causal chain; the remediation is an owner decision:
  (a) Enable WORKTREES_ENABLED so build slots work, restoring fgdb-a9tg's mitigation.
  (b) Per-pane CARGO_TARGET_DIR by default (isolates artifacts AND removes the clobbering
      class), with a size cap or periodic prune per pane.
  (c) A janitor with a real budget: prune debug/incremental/ and stale debug/deps/ on a
      threshold, rather than ad-hoc emergency cleanups under ENOSPC.
  (d) At minimum, a disk-headroom precondition in scripts/check.sh so a gate refuses to start
      rather than dying mid-write. A half-written artifact under ENOSPC is worse than no build,
      and this session hit exactly that: a git commit failed with the filesystem full.

NOT DONE AND DELIBERATELY SO: nothing was deleted. RULE 1 removes deletion authority from an
agent, and dcg blocked an rm -rf earlier in this session (correctly). Every number above is
read-only measurement.
close_reason: Recovered externally: shared /data/tmp/cargo-target measured 325 GiB before cleanup and 1.2 GiB after; 324 GiB free; build-1/build-2 report no holds. fgdb-uy5x private targets remain 1.5 GiB and 4.3 GiB under SageRidge ownership. Filed fgdb-catalog-token-enospc-recovery-faxs for the distinct malformed catalog lease left by ENOSPC.

title: Pin-cycle tool is blind to every CATALOG-side mint: it greps the wrong subcommand and the values it needs are unprintable
notes:
FIXED and LANDED. Repo half: 303042c. Tool half: /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/refreeze_identity_pins.sh (v2, full text below).

=== THE DEFECT, RED-PROVED ===
v1 ran `registry-check identity` and grepped its drift message. `identity`
validates the CHECKED-IN registries/*.toml projections; a mint edits the CATALOG.
Until appendix-regenerate runs, the projections still agree with the OLD pins, so
identity exits 0 and v1 printed "no pin movement: the six assignment pins already
match the tree" on a tree whose pin was genuinely stale. FALSE GREEN -- the one
failure mode that makes a tool worse than no tool.
The drift exists only over catalog-derived identity, reached at appendix_a.rs:11442
where validate_identity is called on catalog.identity and every code is re-emitted
with a `projection_` prefix.

NOT LOGICAL-KINDS-ONLY -- CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED. One row of each minted class added
to a pristine git-backed quiet root at HEAD 303042c, same binary, both subcommands:
    logical_object_kinds   identity=0  appendix=1  assignment_drift seen
    wire_types             identity=0  appendix=1  assignment_drift seen
    durable_fields         identity=0  appendix=1  assignment_drift seen
The mechanism is structural, so physical_record_kinds / bootstrap_frames /
prebootstrap_artifact_kinds are blind by the same route; they simply never receive
mints. (First durable_fields probe returned catalog_row_id_derived_mismatch because
the synthetic row_id was malformed: row_id must derive as
{slice}:{kind}:{kebab(containing_schema)}-{kebab(stable_name)}. Recorded because it
aborts the run BEFORE any pin is reached, so a malformed probe reads as "no drift".)

SECOND, INDEPENDENT BLOCKER, fixed in-tree at 303042c: main.rs collapsed EVERY
appendix violation message to "Appendix A contract check failed", so even the right
subcommand printed no value to parse. v2 REQUIRES that fix and detects its absence.

=== CONTROLS, ALL AGAINST THE FINAL SCRIPT ===
  A   clean tree                  -> "no pin movement", 0 rewritten, exit 0
  B(i) stale logical-kind pin      -> reports AND corrects, restoring the exact
        (const corrupted)             pre-plant value, reaches CLEAN, exit 0
  B(ii) stale pin via CATALOG MINT -> DETECTED and corrected: 6 values rewritten.
        (the case v1 called green)    This is the defect class itself.
  C4  end-to-end replay of the real lquj mint onto pristine b4e50d9:
        reproduced 6 of 6 values derived BY HAND, and the resulting appendix_a.rs
        is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the hand-written commit 6b12cff. Ends PIN CYCLE
        COMPLETE, exit 0. Only identity.rs delta is expected_epoch -- see the gap.
  C5  idempotence                 -> re-run on the tool's own output: 0 rewritten
  C6  prerequisite regression     -> revert the main.rs fix and the tool exits 2
                                     rather than silently mis-parsing
  refuse: dirty identity.rs       -> exit 1 before building anything
  refuse: dirty appendix_a.rs     -> exit 1  (NEW: v1 guarded only identity.rs,
                                     while v2 also writes appendix_a.rs)
  allow:  dirty CATALOG           -> does NOT refuse, correctly: that file is the
                                     operator's working file and holds the mint
  bash -n OK; shellcheck --severity=warning clean.

ANTI-FALSE-GREEN IS THE POINT. When the gate is still red and a round rewrites
nothing, v2 prints the remaining codes and EXITS 1. Demonstrated live: a probe mint
with a DAG-illegal construction_order left census_dag_future_result standing, and
the tool re-pinned correctly and then REFUSED to call the cycle finished.
The one exception is projection_byte_diff alone, which is not a pin and not a
failure -- it means "now run appendix-regenerate", which v2 names as the NEXT STEP.

=== KNOWN GAP, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN ===
THE EPOCH BUMP IS UNDETECTABLE IN PRINCIPLE. registry_epoch lives in both the
catalog [[projection_epoch]] row and the expected_epoch const, and the checker only
compares those two against EACH OTHER. Bump neither and NO code fires, so no tool
can find it from checker output. v2 therefore prints the doctrine on every run that
rewrites a value. Adding/retiring a row owes the bump in BOTH places (precedent
e7b6f09; doctrine identity.rs:1206).

=== WHERE IT LIVES ===
/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/refreeze_identity_pins.sh, unchanged path. NOT promoted into
scripts/: a new tracked .sh owes a file-coverage-closure declaration row and a
shell-lint pass, which is an owner decision, not a side effect of this bead.
Full text below against the /data/tmp sweep.

=== FULL SCRIPT TEXT (v2) ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# refreeze_identity_pins.sh — the base-derived pin cycle, once, for everyone
# (fgdb-1j16 shape: fix the repeated procedure at the source, not per holder)
#
# HISTORY. Built at f9c8578 for fgdb-y5m1. Rewritten at fgdb-jkvc after fgdb-lquj
# proved the v1 tool BLIND TO EVERY CATALOG-SIDE MINT — the exact failure mode a
# tool must not have, because the beads that depend on it reported success while
# leaving the pin stale.
#
# WHAT WAS WRONG WITH v1, measured not inferred (fgdb-jkvc controls C1..C3):
#   v1 ran `registry-check identity` and grepped its drift message. But `identity`
#   validates the CHECKED-IN registries/*.toml projections, and a mint edits the
#   CATALOG. Until appendix-regenerate runs, the projections still agree with the
#   old pins, so `identity` exits 0 and v1 printed
#       "no pin movement: the six assignment pins already match the tree"
#   on a tree whose pin was genuinely stale. FALSE GREEN.
#   The drift exists only over catalog-derived identity, reached at
#   appendix_a.rs:11442 where validate_identity is called on catalog.identity and
#   every code is re-emitted with a `projection_` prefix.
#   NOT logical-kinds-only. Measured on one row of each minted class against a
#   git-backed quiet root:
#       logical_object_kinds  identity=0  appendix=1  assignment_drift seen
#       wire_types            identity=0  appendix=1  assignment_drift seen
#       durable_fields        identity=0  appendix=1  assignment_drift seen
#   The mechanism is structural, so the three static registries
#   (physical_record_kinds, bootstrap_frames, prebootstrap_artifact_kinds) are
#   blind by the same route; they simply never receive mints.
#
#   SECOND, INDEPENDENT BLOCKER: main.rs collapsed EVERY appendix violation
#   message to "Appendix A contract check failed", so even the right subcommand
#   printed no value to parse. That is fixed in-tree by fgdb-jkvc; this script
#   REQUIRES that fix and checks for it rather than silently mis-parsing.
#
# WHY IT PARSES RATHER THAN ACCEPTS A VALUE. HEAD moves several times per
# increment in this swarm, so any pin read a minute ago is already suspect. This
# script never takes a pin from its caller: every NEW value below is read out of
# the checker's own message.
#
# EXIT 0 = the appendix gate is clean (it may have written).
# EXIT 1 = refused to start, or drift survives. NEVER exit 0 with drift outstanding.
# EXIT 2 = the checker could not be built, or emitted a verdict this cannot parse.
# =============================================================================
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="${FGDB_ROOT:-/data/projects/frankengraphdb}"
PINS="$ROOT/tools/registry-check/src/identity.rs"
APX="$ROOT/tools/registry-check/src/appendix_a.rs"
CAT="$ROOT/registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml"
CACHE="${FGDB_PIN_CACHE:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fgdb-pin-cycle}"
MAX_ROUNDS="${FGDB_PIN_ROUNDS:-6}"
mkdir -p "$CACHE"

log() { printf '[refreeze-pins] %s\n' "$*"; }

# --- refuse to absorb a peer's edit ------------------------------------------
# Checked BEFORE anything is built, so a refusal costs nothing.
#
# SCOPE, and why it is not "every file I touch": identity.rs and appendix_a.rs
# are pure pin-carriers here — nobody should have them dirty while you re-freeze.
# The CATALOG is deliberately EXCLUDED: it is the operator's working file and it
# is *expected* to be dirty, because it is holding the mint you just applied.
# Guarding it would refuse on every legitimate invocation.
if (cd "$ROOT" && git rev-parse --git-dir) >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  for guarded in "$PINS" "$APX"; do
    rel="${guarded#"$ROOT"/}"
    if [ -n "$(cd "$ROOT" && git status --porcelain -- "$rel")" ]; then
      log "REFUSING: $rel already has uncommitted changes."
      log "  This script cannot tell your pin edit from a peer's in-flight work."
      log "  Commit or hand back that edit first, then re-run."
      exit 1
    fi
  done
else
  # A non-repo root has no peers to absorb, so the guard is vacuous rather than
  # skipped-in-silence. Said out loud because a guard that quietly does nothing
  # is the defect this whole swarm keeps closing.
  log "NOTICE: $ROOT is not a git worktree; the peer-edit guard does not apply here."
fi

# --- build the checker, every round, from the tree under test ----------------
# A stale binary and a real drift are indistinguishable from the output; this is
# measured, not hypothetical (a binary a few commits old reported five drift
# codes on a tree a fresh build called clean).
build_checker() {
  CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR="$ROOT/tools/registry-check" rustc --edition=2024 \
    --crate-type=lib --crate-name registry_check -C strip=symbols \
    "$ROOT/tools/registry-check/src/lib.rs" -o "$CACHE/libregistry_check.rlib" \
    >"$CACHE/build.log" 2>&1 || return 1
  CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR="$ROOT/tools/registry-check" rustc --edition=2024 \
    -C strip=symbols "$ROOT/tools/registry-check/src/main.rs" \
    -L "$CACHE" --extern "registry_check=$CACHE/libregistry_check.rlib" \
    -o "$CACHE/registry-check" >>"$CACHE/build.log" 2>&1 || return 1
}

# The APPENDIX path, not identity — see the header. Raw text, parsed per family.
appendix_report() {
  "$CACHE/registry-check" appendix --root "$ROOT" 2>&1
}

# Rewrite exactly one literal in one file, or refuse. Never a regex over a file.
rewrite_one() {
  local file="$1" old="$2" new="$3" label="$4"
  [ "$old" = "$new" ] && return 0
  python3 - "$file" "$old" "$new" "$label" <<'PY'
import sys
path, old, new, label = sys.argv[1:5]
text = open(path).read()
count = text.count(old)
if count != 1:
    print(f"FATAL: {label}: {old!r} appears {count} times in {path}; refusing to guess")
    raise SystemExit(2)
open(path, "w").write(text.replace(old, new))
PY
  local rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] && return "$rc"
  log "  rewrote  $label  $old  ->  $new"
  moved_total=$((moved_total + 1))
  return 0
}

moved_total=0
epoch_warned=0

for round in $(seq 1 "$MAX_ROUNDS"); do
  log "round $round: building the checker from the current tree"
  if ! build_checker; then
    log "FATAL: cannot build the checker (see $CACHE/build.log)"
    exit 2
  fi

  report="$(appendix_report)"
  if ! printf '%s' "$report" | grep -q '"event":"violation"'; then
    if [ "$round" -eq 1 ]; then
      log "no pin movement: the appendix gate is already clean"
    else
      log "appendix gate is CLEAN after $((round - 1)) rewrite round(s)"
    fi
    log "SUMMARY: $moved_total value(s) rewritten"
    [ "$moved_total" -gt 0 ] && [ "$epoch_warned" -eq 0 ] && \
      log "REMINDER: an added/retired row also owes a registry_epoch bump in BOTH the catalog [[projection_epoch]] row and the expected_epoch const (identity.rs doctrine; precedent e7b6f09). Nothing detects a missing bump, so it is on you."
    exit 0
  fi

  # Guard against the swallowed-message regression: if the fixed string is back,
  # every parse below silently finds nothing and we would loop to a false FATAL.
  if printf '%s' "$report" | grep -q 'Appendix A contract check failed'; then
    log "FATAL: the binary is emitting the collapsed message 'Appendix A contract check failed'."
    log "  main.rs appendix_violation_message must return violation.msg (fgdb-jkvc)."
    log "  Without it no recomputed value is printable and this script cannot be base-derived."
    exit 2
  fi

  before="$moved_total"

  # --- family 1: the six assignment pins (identity.rs) ----------------------
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r old new; do
    [ -z "${old:-}" ] && continue
    rewrite_one "$PINS" "\"$old\"" "\"$new\"" "assignment-pin" || exit 2
  done < <(printf '%s' "$report" \
    | grep -o 'released assignment pin "[^"]*" != recomputed "[^"]*"' \
    | sed 's/released assignment pin "//; s/" != recomputed "/\t/; s/"$//' | sort -u)

  # --- family 2: projection row count + row-id transcript (appendix_a.rs) ---
  # Message carries BOTH sides, so both are base-derived.
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r oldn olds newn news; do
    [ -z "${oldn:-}" ] && continue
    rewrite_one "$APX" "EXPECTED_PROJECTION_ROW_COUNT: usize = $oldn;" \
                       "EXPECTED_PROJECTION_ROW_COUNT: usize = $newn;" "projection-row-count" || exit 2
    rewrite_one "$APX" "\"$olds\"" "\"$news\"" "projection-row-ids-sha256" || exit 2
  done < <(printf '%s' "$report" \
    | grep -o 'must contain [0-9]* rows with sha256 [0-9a-f]*; found [0-9]* rows with sha256 [0-9a-f]*' \
    | sed 's/must contain //; s/ rows with sha256 /\t/; s/; found /\t/; s/ rows with sha256 /\t/' | sort -u)

  # --- family 3: target/source assignment (appendix_a.rs + the catalog) -----
  # This message carries only the RECOMPUTED side. The OLD side is therefore
  # located by its const name / TOML key rather than parsed — the VALUE is still
  # the checker's, which is what "base-derived" protects.
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r newcount newsha; do
    [ -z "${newcount:-}" ] && continue
    # `grep -o` suppresses -A context, so the const name and its value must be
    # matched in two stages or the value is silently never found (measured: the
    # one-stage form rewrote the catalog and left appendix_a.rs stale).
    oldsha="$(grep -A1 'EXPECTED_TARGET_SOURCE_ASSIGNMENT_SHA256' "$APX" \
              | grep -oE '[0-9a-f]{64}' | head -1)"
    [ -n "$oldsha" ] && rewrite_one "$APX" "\"$oldsha\"" "\"$newsha\"" "target-source-sha256" || true
    oldcount="$(grep -A1 '^\[target_manifest\]$' "$CAT" | grep -oE 'target_count = [0-9]+' | grep -oE '[0-9]+')"
    if [ -n "$oldcount" ] && [ "$oldcount" != "$newcount" ]; then
      rewrite_one "$CAT" "[target_manifest]
target_count = $oldcount" "[target_manifest]
target_count = $newcount" "catalog-target-count" || exit 2
    fi
    oldcatsha="$(grep -oE '^target_source_assignment_sha256 = "[0-9a-f]{64}"$' "$CAT" | grep -oE '[0-9a-f]{64}' | head -1)"
    [ -n "$oldcatsha" ] && [ "$oldcatsha" != "$newsha" ] && \
      rewrite_one "$CAT" "\"$oldcatsha\"" "\"$newsha\"" "catalog-target-source-sha256" || true
  done < <(printf '%s' "$report" \
    | grep -o 'must remain pinned at [0-9]* targets, [0-9]* projection fallbacks, and sha256 [0-9a-f]*' \
    | sed 's/must remain pinned at //; s/ targets, [0-9]* projection fallbacks, and sha256 /\t/' | sort -u)

  if [ "$moved_total" -eq "$before" ]; then
    # projection_byte_diff is NOT a pin and NOT a failure: it says the checked-in
    # projections have not been regenerated yet, which is the documented NEXT step
    # (this script runs BEFORE appendix-regenerate by design). Exiting 1 here would
    # report a completed pin cycle as a failed one. Anything else is a real stop.
    remaining="$(printf '%s' "$report" | grep -oE '"code":"[a-z_0-9]+"' | sort -u)"
    if [ "$remaining" = '"code":"projection_byte_diff"' ]; then
      log "PIN CYCLE COMPLETE: every assignment/count/sha pin is frozen and re-verified."
      log "SUMMARY: $moved_total value(s) rewritten"
      log "NEXT STEP, required, this script deliberately does not write projections:"
      log "    registry-check appendix-regenerate --root $ROOT"
      log "REMINDER: an added/retired row also owes a registry_epoch bump in BOTH the catalog [[projection_epoch]] row and the expected_epoch const (identity.rs doctrine; precedent e7b6f09). Nothing detects a missing bump, so it is on you."
      exit 0
    fi
    log "FATAL: the appendix gate is red but this round rewrote NOTHING."
    log "  These violations are outside what this tool knows how to re-pin:"
    printf '%s' "$report" | grep -oE '"code":"[a-z_0-9]+"' | sort -u | sed 's/^/    /'
    log "  Repair them by hand. Exiting NONZERO on purpose: a pin cycle that"
    log "  cannot finish must never look like one that did."
    exit 1
  fi
done

log "FATAL: drift still present after $MAX_ROUNDS rounds; something else is moving the pins"
exit 1
close_reason: Both halves landed: main.rs message fix at 303042c, tool v2 rewritten to the appendix path. Blindness measured class-wide (logical/wire/fields all identity=0 appendix=1). Controls fire both directions: clean tree 0 rewrites exit 0; stale pin reported AND corrected, via const AND via catalog mint. Plus idempotence, prerequisite-regression, and two refusals.

title: Bead-provenance violation codes still say count/expected after the floor rename
description:
## What

fgdb-hcvx (landed a4d60fc) renamed every bead-provenance PIN so its name states
a floor. Three names it deliberately did not touch still say "count"/"expected":

  tools/registry-check/src/architecture.rs
    violation code  "bead_count_pin"              -> the declared-vs-code-pin
                                                     equality; both sides are
                                                     now *_floor
    violation code  "bead_family_expected_total"  -> fires when the
                                                     min_match_count values do
                                                     not sum to family_rule_floor
    local           expected_family_total         -> that sum

## Why it was deferred, not an oversight

A violation code is not prose. It is the `code` field of the NDJSON
contradiction stream, and tests/architecture_decisions.rs asserts on both
strings literally (`codes.contains("bead_count_pin")` twice,
`!codes.contains("bead_family_expected_total")` once). Renaming one is a change
to a machine-read contract and belongs in its own commit with its own sweep, not
bundled into a rename whose whole claim was "no behaviour moved".

## What must be measured first, before renaming anything

The fgdb-hcvx sweep found no consumer of these two codes outside
architecture.rs and its test file -- but that sweep was `grep` over the repo,
which is exactly the instrument that misses a code assembled at runtime or read
from a registry row. Before renaming, check registries/claims_lint.toml,
registries/invariants.toml and the other g0 e2e scripts for the literal, and
re-run the grep including .beads/ (10 bead records mention `bead_count`).

## Cost

Small: 2 codes x (1 emit site + 1-2 test assertions), plus a 3-line local
rename. Needs the catalog token; the compiler covers the local, nothing covers
the string literals, so the test assertions are the only guard and they must be
edited in the same commit.

## Judgement call this bead is asking for

It may be correct to leave them. `bead_count_pin` describes a pin over counts
and both operands really are equal-compared; the misleading word is "expected"
in `bead_family_expected_total`, which is the one fgdb-hcvx called "the worst of
them" in the TOML. A partial rename -- just `bead_family_expected_total` ->
`bead_family_floor_total` -- may be the whole fix.

Found while landing fgdb-hcvx (a4d60fc).
close_reason: Renamed the two stale floor-era NDJSON codes and local to floor terminology; 42/42 ADR suite plus mutation controls pass.

title: nrx3's three new witness cohort guards are red on main: two denominators conflate unions with arms
description:
tools/registry-check/tests/identity.rs is RED on main. The witness test
idr_assignment_history_and_epoch_are_frozen aborts at guards added by the nrx3
transcript-coverage work, before any of its own asserts run.

  1. expected_reference_unions = 13, ACTUAL 5.
     Both HEAD and the current tree carry 5 [[reference_union]] rows in
     durable_fields.toml. 13 is 5 unions + 8 arms -- a TRANSCRIPT-LINE count pinned
     against a UNION count. The very next guard counts reference arms separately, so

  2. the ordinary-union arm cohort asserts
         pre_erratum.ordinary_unions.iter().map(|u| u.arms.len()).sum() + 44
             == current_ordinary_arm_count

title: 2b94eef0 + 470da664 residue: historical witness and allowed-containing-schema baselines not updated for the 2 new logical_kind rows and 2 new ordinary union rows
description:
## What & scope

Two registry-check tests fail on main after the 2b94eef0 and 470da664 commits by PearlAnchor landed the d2ax residue (GlobalKeyDestructionAuthorizationSpec, ShardKeyZeroReferenceSpec) and the host Spec kinds:

- idr_allowed_containing_schema_catalog_domain_is_nonempty_and_fail_closed: expected (625, 439) but got (625, 441). 2 new ordinary_union citations landed but the baseline wasn't bumped.
- idr_assignment_history_and_epoch_are_frozen: expected 7 but got 9. 2 new ordinary unions widened the historical witness reconstruction.

Both are P0 because the test suite is a hard gate (cargo test must exit 0 per AGENTS.md).

## Exact site

tools/registry-check/tests/identity.rs:3822 (first failure; count baseline)
tools/registry-check/tests/identity.rs:12496 (second failure; historical witness filter)

## Established fix pattern

Per fgdb-a20-historical-witness-red-opc5, fgdb-tsfs, fgdb-bbqq (slice 1+2 landings), the fix is two coordinated edits:
1. Add a `post_erratum_*` filter clause for the two new ordinary union names in idr_assignment_history_and_epoch_are_frozen, so the historical witness stays a frozen historical width.
2. Update the count baseline in idr_allowed_containing_schema_catalog_domain_is_nonempty_and_fail_closed to reflect the 2 new ordinary_union citations (439 -> 441).

Both edits land in ONE commit. The accepted evidence path: replay idr_assignment_history_and_epoch_are_frozen with the erratum filter applied; observe the cohort assert reads `left: 7, right: 7` (or whatever the filtered denominator becomes). Mutation control: removing the erratum entry for either new name must make the cohort assert read `left > right` and the test red.

## Reproducer

```
RCH_CARGO_WRAPPER_BYPASS=1 cargo test -p registry-check --test identity \
  idr_allowed_containing_schema_catalog_domain_is_nonempty_and_fail_closed \
  idr_assignment_history_and_epoch_are_frozen -- --nocapture
```

Observed at HEAD 470da664 (uncommitted working tree has the same state).

## Acceptance

- Both tests pass on main.
- Adding a third new ordinary union after this lands must make the test red at the cohort assert (nonvacuous), not pass silently.
- The fix is ONE commit, attribution clear.

title: Field rows carry no source path: the owner law already fails closed (0 of 923), but 117 landed rows sit inside union arms with no mechanism that can tell
notes:
Filed by pane4 2026-07-27 ~04:3x at HEAD ccae08d, at the orchestrator's request
after pane3 surfaced the symptom on a05. Re-derived before filing, and the
reported defect does not reproduce — but the investigation that falsified it
found the real one.

=== THE REPORTED DEFECT IS FALSIFIED AT HEAD ===

Reported: "validate_identity ACCEPTS a [[field]] row on a UNION owner, so an arm
payload member lands silently as a field."

It does not. `field_unresolved_schema` (identity.rs:1762-1800) resolves a field's
`containing_schema`, by generic-free family, against an ALLOWLIST:

    resolves = logical || bootstrap || physical || prebootstrap

An allowlist fails CLOSED by construction: an unrecognised owner kind is a
violation, not a skip. That is exactly the property the law was to be built for,
and it is already there — including a dedicated message for the wire sub-case,
which the code comments say was added because "resolves in no identity class"
read as a missing mint and invited authors to re-mint the owner as a logical
kind.

CENSUS, denominator = EVERY landed [[field]] identity row, 923 of them:

    logical       849
    bootstrap      48
    physical       26
    ---------------------
    total         923      union owners: 0   wire owners: 0   unresolved: 0

Zero counterexamples, and the partition is total.

WITNESS — planted rows, both directions, positive control PASSES:

    baseline                                          0 violations
    ordinary-union owner  ActivatedRetentionCutSet...  REJECTED field_unresolved_schema
    reference-union owner MandatoryInventoryRef        REJECTED field_unresolved_schema
    wire-type owner       StrongRef                    REJECTED field_unresolved_schema
                                                       (with the wire-specific message)
    nonsense owner        ZzNoSuchOwnerZz              REJECTED field_unresolved_schema
    logical owner         CommitMarker                 ACCEPTED   <- control passes

Without that last line the four rejections would only prove the probe rejects
everything. Building the requested law again would duplicate a live mechanism.

=== THE REAL GAP, WHICH IS WHAT pane3 ACTUALLY HIT ===

pane3's report was "the PATH rejected what the CHECKER could not — 49 dropped to
42 only because a human noticed", and that is precise. The owner is not the
problem; the PATH is, and a durable_fields row does not have one.

A [[field]] identity row carries `containing_schema` + `stable_name` and nothing
else about where the member sits in the source. The source path survives only in
the sibling `[[target]].source_key`
(`field|Owner|Owner.state.Arm.member|member`), and NO law reads it for depth.

Joining every landed field row to its target source_key:

    depth 1   762    a direct member,  Owner.member
    depth 2    62 )  an INTERIOR: Owner.state.Arm.member and deeper
    depth 3    54 )
    depth 5     1 )
    ------------------
    joinable  879    (44 of the 923 rows have no field target to join, itself
                      worth a look and NOT covered by this bead)

**117 landed rows are at depth >= 2.** Examples, all live today:

    AttemptFamilyState.latest_state.Active.registration_ref
    AuditTerminalFreezeRecord.state.Armed.scaffolding_applied_ref
    CommitMarker.effect_source.Local.capsule_ref
    DistributedSerializationCertificate.lifecycle_basis.ReadWrite.routing_certificate_ref
    GlobalBeginIdempotencyIndex.Reserved.reservation_ref

Whether each of those 117 is legitimate is exactly the question NOTHING in the
checker can answer, and that is the defect: the catalog relies on a rule with no
mechanism that can fail. The only governing artifact is
`STRONGREF_ONLY_ARM_PAYLOAD_SHAPES` (identity.rs:203), a hard-coded table of
exactly TWO named shapes with a completeness guard. Two, against 117.

=== WHAT A FIX HAS TO DECIDE FIRST, AND WHY THIS IS NOT A ONE-LINER ===

The 117 are not obviously wrong. A union arm whose payload is a single StrongRef
is precisely the shape `STRONGREF_ONLY_ARM_PAYLOAD_SHAPES` licenses, and most of
the 117 look like exactly that. So the law cannot be "depth >= 2 is a violation";
it has to be "depth >= 2 is a violation UNLESS the arm it sits in is licensed",
and licensing is currently a two-row hand-written table.

Sequence I would follow, and did not because the ruling is the owner's:
  1. Partition the 117 by the arm they sit in and by whether that arm is a
     StrongRef-only payload. That is a census, no ruling needed, and it turns
     "117 unknown" into "N licensed by the existing rule, M needing one".
  2. Only then choose the mechanism. If M is small the table grows and gains a
     completeness guard over the whole 117. If M is large the table is the wrong
     instrument and the law belongs on the path itself.
  3. Either way the enforcement point has to be a law that READS
     `[[target]].source_key`, because that is the only place the path exists.
     identity.rs cannot see it at all — it never receives the targets.

That last point is the structural finding: `validate_identity` takes
`&IdentityRegistries` and the catalog's targets are not in it, so this law CANNOT
live where the sibling field laws live. It has to be an appendix_a.rs law, or
identity.rs has to be given the path. Grepped both artifacts first, as instructed:
appendix_a.rs has `field_owner_and_name` (:12014) keyed by owner+name and drops
the path, so neither artifact currently retains what the law needs.

=== NOT IN SCOPE ===

pane3's second finding — field_tag has no derivable law (flat census rank agrees
774/837, depth-1 rank 668/720; only range and per-owner uniqueness enforced) —
stays on fgdb-uug4 and is deliberately not duplicated here.

Nothing deleted. Census and witness are standalone-rustc probes under
/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane4_owner_law; no cargo, no catalog token was needed or
taken for any of the above.

=== THE 117, CENSUSED BY ARM. THE POPULATION IS HETEROGENEOUS — NO LAW YET ===

Denominator 117. Partition is TOTAL and splits into two shapes that share no
mechanism, so a single law over 117 would be exactly the thing we keep catching:

  106  ARM INTERIOR, backed by a landed [[union_arm]] row at that exact path,
       and EVERY ONE has payload_kind = "inline-record". SOURCE-FORCED: the
       source spells an arm whose payload is an inline record, the arm row is
       landed, and these field rows ARE that record's members. Nothing invented.
   11  NOT AN ARM AT ALL. Every one has `.record.` as the segment before the
       member — the collection-element marker of a repeated field:
         KeyEnvelopeNode.inherited_roots.record.source_root_digest
         LocalConstraintReservationRecord.owner.record.registration_ref            (x3)
         NoTerminalSignatureOrOrderProof.raft_nonorder_evidence.record.configuration_ref
         PriorIncarnationLeaseBarrierBootstrapImport<Role>.sorted_*_imports.record.*_ref  (x4)
         RemoteGrantRetirementPlan.sorted_entries.record.old_grant_evidence_ref
         KeyEnvelopeNode.inherited_roots.record.source_root_ciphertext_digest
       11 of 11, no exceptions. Depth >= 2 here means "element of a repeated
       field", which is a different question from "member of a union arm".
  ---
  117

  depth 2  62   depth 3  54   depth 5  1
  86 distinct (owner, union_path, arm) keys: 62 carry 1 member, 17 carry 2,
  7 carry 3  (62 + 34 + 21 = 117).
  102 of 117 are strong/conditional StrongRef; the other 15 spread over
  AppliedControlRef 6, AppliedAbortRef 2, digest256 2, and one each of
  Operational, RemoteObjectIdentity, RestoreAbandonmentTombstoneRef<Role>,
  WeakDigest, u64.

THE TWO-ENTRY TABLE NAMES 0 OF THE 117, AND THAT IS NOT A GAP IN THE TABLE.
STRONGREF_ONLY_ARM_PAYLOAD_SHAPES governs the COMPLEMENT: arms whose payload is
a single StrongRef and NO inline record, i.e. arms that correctly have no field
rows at all. It licenses an ABSENCE. Reading it as an under-populated licensing
table for these 117 is the wrong model and would grow it in the wrong direction.

A CONTROL THAT CAUGHT MY OWN PROBE. The first run of this census reported
117 of 117 "no landed union arm at that path" — a clean, alarming, and FALSE
result. `OrdinaryUnion.union_path` is the FULL dotted path INCLUDING the owner
("AttemptFamilyState.latest_state"); my key used the tail only, so nothing ever
matched. Caught by dumping four real landed union rows before believing a
near-total negative. The corrected join is 106/11.

=== THE CONSEQUENCE, STATED FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP ===

THIS IS A DATA-FLOW CHANGE BEFORE IT IS A LAW.

  identity.rs   validate_identity(&IdentityRegistries). The registries DO carry
                paths — OrdinaryUnion.union_path and OrdinaryUnionArm.union_path
                are full dotted paths, and OrdinaryUnionArm.source_arm_name is
                the arm. The UNION side has everything. The FIELD side has none
                of it: FieldRow is containing_schema + stable_name and no path.
  appendix_a.rs has the path, in [[target]].source_key, and drops it —
                field_owner_and_name (:12014) keys by owner+name only.

So neither artifact retains what the law needs, but they fail differently, and
that decides the fix. It does NOT need a third place. The asymmetry is the
defect: [[union_arm]] rows carry union_path + source_arm_name and [[field]] rows
do not, though both are members of the same source tree. Give the [[field]]
projection row the same two columns the arm row already has, and the law becomes
a local check inside validate_identity with no cross-artifact plumbing at all:

    a field row whose union_path/arm_name are set must match a landed
    [[union_arm]] at that path whose payload_kind is inline-record;
    a field row with them unset must be a direct member.

That is a durable-format change to durable_fields.toml — additive-minor under
§16.6, which is the one exception to the no-compat-shim rule — and it is the
reason this is not a one-turn fix. 117 rows would need the two columns
backfilled from their [[target]].source_key, which is mechanical and verifiable
(the join above is exactly it, and it is already written).

WHAT I DID NOT DO, DELIBERATELY: author the law. The population is two shapes,
not one; the 11 repeated-record rows need their own ruling (is `.record.` depth
even in scope?), and a law written over the mixed 117 would be wrong for 11 of
them by construction.

Census: /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane4_owner_law/arms.rs, standalone rustc, no cargo,
no catalog token taken.

=== THE 11 `.record.` ROWS, ASKED OF THE CHECKER. MOSTLY FORCED; ONE RULING LEFT ===

STRUCTURAL CONSEQUENCE, FIRST, BECAUSE IT DECIDES WHERE ANY FIX GOES:
validate_identity takes &IdentityRegistries and the catalog's targets are not in
it, while appendix_a.rs keys field_owner_and_name at :12014 by owner+name and
DROPS the path — so neither artifact retains what a path law would need, which
makes this a data-flow change before it is a law. The right home is NOT a third
place: [[union_arm]] rows already carry union_path + source_arm_name, so giving
the [[field]] projection row those same two columns puts the law inside
validate_identity with no cross-artifact plumbing at all.

Shape of the 11, uniform: the REPEATED FIELD ITSELF has no landed row anywhere —
inherited_roots, owner, raft_nonorder_evidence, sorted_issuer_fence_imports,
sorted_expired_cohort_imports, sorted_revoked_cohort_imports, sorted_entries are
each unlanded — and only their element members are landed, every one at
cardinality = "one" on the top-level owner.

READINGS, run through validate_identity on the representative row
RemoteGrantRetirementPlan.sorted_entries.record.old_grant_evidence_ref:

  A  flatten the element member onto the owner   (what is landed)   0 violations
  B1 mint the element type as a WIRE type        REJECTED
       field_unresolved_schema: "resolves as a WIRE type, which can never own a
       field row" — this is reference_semantics being forced by the source: the
       member is StrongRef, and a StrongRef member cannot hang off a wire host.
  B2 mint the element type as a LOGICAL kind     0 attributable violations
  CONTROL unminted element host                  REJECTED (control fires)

So the checker forbids B1 and admits both A and B2. Applying that across the 11:

   9 rows are StrongRef with a real target (LocalAttemptRegistration,
     LocalPrepareAdmissionSpec, ConfigurationState,
     PriorIncarnationLeaseIssuerFenceReceipt, PriorIncarnationLeaseCohortWindow,
     PreBootstrapPortableTimeExpiryAttestation,
     PriorIncarnationLeaseCohortRevocationReceipt, RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence,
     plus LocalConstraintReservationRecord.owner.record.admission_generation
     which is u64/inline in the same three-member element).
     For these B1 is FORBIDDEN. Two readings remain.
   2 rows are the KeyEnvelopeNode digests — source_root_digest and
     source_root_ciphertext_digest, digest256 with digest_class = "target",
     reference_semantics = none. These are ALREADY the correct resolution of a
     plan-named digest: digest256 plus digest_class on the carrying field, not a
     minted wire type, so that half is source-forced and settled. But because
     they carry no reference, B1 is not forbidden for them, so their option set
     is WIDER than the other nine, not narrower.

WHAT IS UNDECIDED, AND IT IS ONE QUESTION, NOT ELEVEN:

  Does the durable format record that these seven fields are COLLECTIONS at all?
  Under reading A — what is landed and green today — the repeated field has no
  row in any registry and its members are scalar `cardinality = "one"` rows on
  the owner, so nothing in the format says there are N of them. Under B2 the
  element becomes a logical kind and the owner carries one repeated field
  pointing at it, which records the repetition but costs 7 new logical kinds for
  element types that nothing references — and since none of them is a StrongRef
  target, the reservation bijection law forbids reserving them, so each would
  need a fresh code above the live frontier.

  That is a durable-format question about representation, not a checker question,
  and the checker has said everything it can: it accepts both. Naming it to you
  rather than inferring it.

  (The two KeyEnvelopeNode digest rows ride on the same answer for their parent
  `inherited_roots`; their own digest resolution is already correct either way.)

=== OWNER RULING: B2, RECORD THE COLLECTIONS. DESIGN DERIVED, NOT LANDED ===

Ruled by the owner (/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/OWNER_RULINGS.md): mint the 7 element
types as LOGICAL kinds at fresh codes and land the repeated field rows with
their true cardinality. Grounds are on the ruling; the decisive one is that
under A the repeated field is not in the durable format AT ALL, so every walker
plan 5.1 generates from durable_fields.toml reads "one" where the source says
"many".

EVERYTHING BELOW IS DERIVED AT HEAD b7effc2, TOKEN-FREE. Nothing is landed: the
catalog lease was held by pane3-bw2x throughout.

CARDINALITY VOCABULARY (measured, 923 rows): one 885, many 26, optional 12.
So the repeated field takes cardinality = "many".

PRECEDENT FOR THE SHAPE, from the corpus, two forms already in use:
  ConstraintValidationEvidence.owner_reservation_refs
    card=many wire=StrongRef sem=strong target=LocalConstraintReservationRecord
      -> a repeated StrongRef to a LOGICAL kind. This is our form.
  ConstraintMutationBatch.sorted_mutations
    card=many wire=ConstraintStateMutation sem=none target=None
      -> a repeated inline record whose element is a registered WIRE type. NOT
         our form, and the checker already said why: a wire host can never own a
         field row, and 6 of our 7 elements carry StrongRef members.

FRESH CODES: max landed logical is 0x0570; the next ten free of BOTH landed and
reserved are 0x0571..0x057a. Take 0x0571..0x0577 for the seven, in the order
listed below. Re-derive the frontier at the moment of the edit — other panes are
minting.

THE SEVEN, WITH THEIR ORDER WINDOWS — EVERY ONE SATISFIABLE, AND EVERY ONE
ADMITS THE OWNER'S OWN ORDER, which is the tightest defensible choice (the upper
bound IS the owner's order, and it clears every lower bound):

  owner (order)                                    repeated field                     window        take
  KeyEnvelopeNode (50) 0x02e1                      inherited_roots                    (-inf, 50]    50
  LocalConstraintReservationRecord (30) 0x056d     owner                              [20, 30]      30
  NoTerminalSignatureOrOrderProof (6) 0x0373       raft_nonorder_evidence             [5, 6]        6
  PriorIncarnationLeaseBarrierBootstrapImport<Role:AuthorityOwningRole> (30) 0x039a
                                                   sorted_expired_cohort_imports      [27, 30]      30
                                                   sorted_issuer_fence_imports        [20, 30]      30
                                                   sorted_revoked_cohort_imports      [20, 30]      30
  RemoteGrantRetirementPlan (40) 0x03af            sorted_entries                     [24, 40]      40

  Lower bound = max construction_order over that element's member targets; upper
  bound = the owner's order, because the owner's new repeated field references
  the element and target.order <= containing.order. Equality is legal — the law
  fires only on `>`.

WHAT LANDS, PER ELEMENT TYPE (x7):
  1. [[logical_kind]] <Owner><Field>Record at its fresh code, status "reserved",
     construction_order per the table, role_predicate and max_size_bytes copied
     from the owner.
  2. [[field]] on the OWNER for the repeated field itself — the row that is
     missing today and is the whole point of the ruling:
       cardinality = "many", exact_wire_type = "StrongRef",
       reference_semantics = "strong", target_schema_id = the new element kind,
       identity_class = "logical", construction_order = the OWNER's order.
  3. RE-KEY the existing element-member rows from the owner to the new element
     kind: containing_schema becomes <Owner><Field>Record and construction_order
     becomes the element kind's order (the field-order-equals-kind-order law).
     Their field_tags are free to restart at the element, but re-keying moves
     released names, so check the append-only assignment pin before assuming.
  4. One [[target]] row per new [[field]], plus re-pointed source_keys for the
     re-keyed members.

SCOPE LIMIT HELD: the two KeyEnvelopeNode members keep digest256 + digest_class
= "target". A plan-named digest never becomes a minted wire type; B2 governs the
CONTAINING field row, not those element resolutions.

PIN COST — SPLIT THE INCREMENT. This adds 7 logical kinds + 7 field rows + 7
targets and re-keys 11 rows, so it moves at least: [target_manifest] target_count
and target_source_assignment_sha256, EXPECTED_PROJECTION_ROW_COUNT and
EXPECTED_PROJECTION_ROW_IDS_SHA256, the durable_fields assignment pin, and — new
this time, because kinds are minted — the LOGICAL assignment pin
(identity.rs:1211) and very likely the logical registry_epoch and its e2e drift
fixture at g0_identity_e2e.sh:637. BASE-DERIVE EVERY ONE from the loader's own
drift at the moment of the edit; do not copy a value from this note. Suggested
split: (i) the 7 kinds alone, (ii) the 7 repeated field rows, (iii) the 11
re-keys — each a separate pin round, each verifiable on its own.

AND CHECK refs.rs BEFORE COMMITTING: minting at status "reserved" does not trip
the fgdb-types compile-time assert, but ACTIVATING would. These land reserved.

=== INCREMENT (i) PROVEN TOKEN-FREE, WITH (ii) SYNTHESIZED ON TOP TO VALIDATE
    THE ORDER CHOICE, AND A CONTROL THAT FIRES ===

Script: /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane4_owner_law/inc1.rs — re-runnable, derives the
frontier and PARSES the drift every run rather than restating one.

  baseline validate_identity                              0 violations
  frontier re-derived                 max landed 0x0570 -> 0x0571..0x0577
  name collisions across all 7 namespaces + 813 reservations   0
  (i) 7 logical kinds minted          1 violation, 0 ATTRIBUTABLE
  (i)+(ii) + 7 repeated field rows    2 violations, 0 ATTRIBUTABLE
  CONTROL element order 99 > owner order 40
      -> dag_future_result FIRED on RemoteGrantRetirementPlan#sorted_entries

WHY (ii) IS SYNTHESIZED HERE THOUGH IT LANDS SEPARATELY: increment (i) alone
CANNOT validate the order values, because nothing references the new kinds until
the owner's repeated field row exists — the DAG law has no edge to check. Proving
(i)+(ii) together and landing them separately is the only way the orders in (i)
are anything but assertions. The control at order 99 is what shows the check is
live rather than vacuous.

A DEFECT THE PROBE CAUGHT IN MY OWN SYNTHESIS, worth carrying into the edit:
three of the seven repeated fields share one owner
(PriorIncarnationLeaseBarrierBootstrapImport<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>), and my
first pass allocated each one `max existing tag + 1` from the pristine catalog,
so all three took tag 26 and the checker returned two code_duplicate rows. They

from the base.

ALSO NOTE THE PIN ALREADY MOVED UNDER ME: identity.rs:1211 read
LOGICAL = "fnv1a64:9853f4c21f65ce17" when I first opened it; the loader now
reports the released pin as "fnv1a64:5bf6e0e768c4d939". Other panes minted in

  a12:logical-kind:local-constraint-reservation-record-owner-record          0x0572 order 30 role role-local
  a08:logical-kind:no-terminal-signature-or-order-proof-raft-nonorder-evidence-record
                                                                            0x0573 order  6 role true
  a19:logical-kind:prior-incarnation-lease-barrier-bootstrap-import-sorted-expired-cohort-imports-record
                                                                            0x0574 order 30 role true

title: ReferenceDatabase rejects same-coordinate multi-relation templates
description: Measured while closing fgdb-yk6e at HEAD 07fba7b. LogicalDeltaTemplate keys entries by (graph, branch, relation), so one atomic template may legally carry multiple relation entries for the same graph/branch. ReferenceDatabase::apply_template checks SequenceNotAdvancing against the mutating candidate and writes applied_through after each entry; the second legal relation entry therefore sees the same commit_seq as already applied and is refused. Compare per-coordinate sequence against immutable pre-template applied_through (or equivalently once per graph/branch), retain all-or-nothing application, and add a control proving two relations for one coordinate land at one commit. Normative anchor: plan:740 and plan:1924 coordinate entries are graph/branch/relation keyed; only duplicate triples are invalid. Found as a prerequisite discriminator for fgdb-yk6e.
notes: IMPLEMENTED, NOT CLOSED. Source commit 2c30b6001ce5b9d87537fcd45fedfa375f4a9be2. Per-coordinate SequenceNotAdvancing now reads immutable pre-template applied_through rather than the mutating candidate, so distinct graph-branch-relation entries share one atomic commit sequence. recorded_commits now counts distinct CommitSeq values because history stores one record per relation entry. The control applies two relations to one graph-branch at CommitSeq 1, materializes both vertices, leaves applied_through at 1, and reports exactly one recorded commit. Live cargo test -p fgdb-reference passed 159 tests in /data/tmp/fgdb-yk6e-kfe5-live-package-final.log; cargo fmt --all -- --check and cargo clippy -p fgdb-reference --all-targets -- -D warnings passed. instinct and is wrong: prepare_capsule takes &LogicalDeltaTemplate, and
fgdb-chronicle does NOT depend on fgdb-delta-types (checked its Cargo.toml).

puts composition at 13 and verification at 14, so fgdb-sim (verification) may
depend on fgdb (composition). No cycle: fgdb depends on chronicle/strata/
delta-types/types/crypto and on neither fgdb-sim nor fgdb-reference.

Agent-Mail lease held by MaroonCanyon for the whole window I had. I would rather
file the duplication loudly than edit a file another pane holds.

and commit_capsule), so either update those imports or surface the names once via

and is thin, and fgdb calls coordinator.commit directly; decide whether it moves
too or fgdb-sim keeps it.

apart precisely so the differential cannot be gutted by code sharing, so those

title: repair_symbols is the one unauthenticated capsule descriptor field
notes:
FOUND 2026-07-29 by systematic audit at def2938, in my own code (capsule.rs).

WHY THIS AUDIT HAPPENED: four defects were found in code I landed the same day, and four of
the five were one class — a canonicality or authentication claim that does not cover every
case (ffbf187 verify narrower than insert; d95ff1b truncate on an immutable object;
fgdb-a6cv unauthenticated protected_len; def2938 embedded collections not canonicalized).
Only one of those four was found by me. So instead of writing more features I enumerated
every CapsuleDescriptor field against every integrity transcript. This is the one result.

THE FINDING. Every field of CapsuleDescriptor is authenticated EXCEPT repair_symbols:
- the 8 cipher fields (object_kind, canonical_plaintext_len, codec_profile, compressed_len,
  data_crypto_profile, dek_id, object_nonce, object_tag_len) ride the AEAD's AAD via
  CipherDescriptor::canonical_bytes, so tampering makes the open fail;
- the 7 encoding fields (fec_profile, transfer_length, oti_common, oti_scheme, symbol_size,
  source_block_count, symbol_auth_profile) plus ciphertext_id ride the EncodingId transcript
  that EncodedObject::reconstruct recomputes;
- encoding_id is itself checked by that recomputation;
- repair_symbols rides NOTHING. A rewritten container can name any budget it likes.

WHY IT CANNOT BE FIXED BY REMOVAL, unlike fgdb-a6cv's protected_len. That one was a
duplicate of an authenticated value, so deleting it left one source of truth. This one is
NOT derivable: the surviving symbol count of a damaged container cannot distinguish "eight
repair symbols, all lost" from "no repair symbols at all". A scrub needs the declared figure
precisely to say how many symbols are MISSING. Deleting it would lose real information.

SEVERITY TODAY: LOW, and stated so rather than inflated. The accessor has no production
consumer — measured, only tests call it, and symbolize::erasure_budget is a separate free
function taking a parameter rather than reading the descriptor. Nothing decides Degraded vs
Lost from it yet.

DONE NOW (2efeca0 follow-up): renamed erasure_budget -> claimed_erasure_budget and
documented it as UNAUTHENTICATED and advisory, so the next caller cannot mistake it for a
durability fact. A name that says "claimed" is the cheapest guard available until the real
fix lands.

THE REAL FIX: get repair_symbols inside an authenticated transcript. The natural home is
EncodingDescriptor, since that is what the EncodingId covers — but that type is SHARED with
root.rs's RootBootstrap and with symbolize, so adding a field changes the EncodingId of
every object including the root, and re-freezes the root bootstrap fixtures. That is why it
is filed rather than done inline: it is an identity-pipeline change, not a capsule change.
Check whether the plan already assigns repair overhead to a reconstructibility tier (§5.1
mentions the repair budget as a policy decision per tier) — if the tier is authenticated
elsewhere, the descriptor may only need to name the tier rather than the count.

CONTROL FOR THE FIX: capsule_container.rs already has a_rewritten_encoding_id_is_refused and
a_rewritten_transfer_length_is_refused. Add a_rewritten_repair_symbols_is_refused alongside
them and verify it FAILS before the fix — otherwise the fix is untested. Note that the

title: STREAM POISONING: a lawful-looking WriteBatch can commit bytes whose own fold/replay refuses — canonical row order is not program order
description: FOUND BY the fgdb-ls5b generated differential (seed 11, minimized to a 2-row repro): LogicalDeltaTemplate::build canonicalizes rows by ENCODED BYTE ORDER within a coordinate, so the durable fold order differs from submission order. Compositions that are lawful in program order but unlawful in canonical order commit durably and THEN refuse at the incremental fold — and would refuse identically at every future reopen: the database is poisoned by its own write API. Reproduced: [set_vertex_property(v), delete_vertex(v)] in one batch → canonical order [DeleteVertex, Property] → UnknownVertex AFTER the two-fsync commit. Same class: two updates of one exact field in one batch (canonical order of the two Property rows is byte order — the engine folds them reordered and the ORACLE refuses the second before-image at replay, i.e. at the differential/reopen); an update on an edge a later delete_vertex cascades; identity reuse across or within batches (writer spent-set refusals fire only at fold, post-commit). THE FIX PRINCIPLE: the spine must refuse at BUILD TIME everything the fold would refuse after commit — WriteError::OrderSensitiveBatch for order-sensitive compositions (update+delete of one element incl. via cascade; two updates of one exact field), and build-time spent/live refusals on creates (new writer accessors is_edge_spent/is_vertex_spent). Program-order-equivalent compositions (create+update, create+delete, commuting distinct-field updates) stay lawful — they are the same-batch folds the spine already laws.
close_reason: The write API can no longer poison the stream: order-sensitive compositions and identity reuse refuse before the two-fsync commit, proven by the refusal law and three seeded generated histories (34f0fb4).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: FIXED 34f0fb4. Build-time refusals now cover everything the fold refuses post-commit: OrderSensitiveBatch (update+delete one element incl. cascade route; double touch of one exact field — distinct fields commute and stay lawful), AlreadyLive/IdentitySpent on creates (new writer accessors is_edge_spent/is_vertex_spent). Refusal law pins all five shapes + commuting control + nothing-durable (frontier/reopen). The finder — the seeded model-based generated differential (3 seeds, 8 batches each, all op families, per-epoch oracle comparison with count closure) — landed in the same commit; its model refuses to propose what the engine refuses to commit. Differential seventh epoch's same-key double touch was lucky-lawful by byte order and became commuting fields. NOTE for the future txn layer: the underlying truth stands — durable row order within a commit is canonical byte order; any higher-level statement pipeline must serialize order-dependent effects into SEPARATE commits or coalesce before building the template. title: Gate evidence dirs are 9.84GB of the tmp pool — same lifetime defect, different producer
description:
## The half of the pool fgdb-1j16 does not cover

fgdb-1j16 attributes 18.01 GB across 113 `/data/tmp/tmp.*` dirs to
scripts/lib/private_subject.sh. Partitioning each dir into `bin/` (what that
library writes) versus everything else (what the SOURCING GATE writes), measured
2026-07-27 02:3x:

  bin/  -- the subject private_subject.sh builds     8.17 GB   45.4%
  rest  -- gate evidence                             9.84 GB   54.6%

So fixing private_subject.sh at the source, even perfectly, leaves 9.84 GB of
the same defect standing. This bead is that remainder.

## Shape of it

Per-dir totals: min 72.3 MB, median 88.4 MB, mean 163.2 MB, max 627.5 MB. The
subject is a flat 75 MB, so everything above ~75 MB is gate output. The mean dir
carries 88 MB of it.

The largest single occupants are whole-registry COPIES made for negative
controls. /data/tmp/tmp.Q9JWAqKb1p alone holds five at 17.2 MB each:

  neg-appendix-unrelated-bindings   17.2 MB
  neg-appendix-unknown-key          17.2 MB
  neg-appendix-semantic-owner       17.2 MB
  neg-appendix-maintenance          17.2 MB
  neg-appendix-annotation-reference 17.2 MB

That is the appendix-baseline harness pattern: copy the registry tree, mutate one
row, run the checker, assert it fires. Correct as a method; the copies just never
had a lifetime. registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml is 4.0 MB and
registries/durable_fields.toml is 1.0 MB, so each control copy is dominated by
registry bytes that are identical across all five.

## Why it is a separate bead and not part of 1j16

Different producer, and a different fix. private_subject.sh writes ONE artifact
that is a pure function of the checker sources, so it can be content-keyed and
shared -- that is 1j16's fix. Gate evidence is per-run BY CONSTRUCTION: it is the
output being asserted on, and two runs must not share it or the gate stops
measuring its own run. Content-keying is the wrong instrument here.

## What to measure before choosing a fix

1. How much of the 9.84 GB is registry COPIES versus genuine per-run output.
   A copy that differs from the shipped registry in one row could be a
   copy-on-write clone, a symlink farm with one real file, or an in-memory
   mutation -- the checker already accepts a synthesised registry (see how
   tests/architecture_decisions.rs mutates a parsed ArchitectureRegistry rather
   than copying files). If most of the 9.84 GB is near-duplicate registry bytes,
   the fix is to stop copying, not to reap.
2. Which gates produce the biggest dirs. The 627.5 MB maximum is 8x the mean and
   is worth naming on its own.
3. Whether any of it is EVIDENCE someone is relying on. /data/tmp/tmp.G5czm7QFIs
   is already flagged on fgdb-1j16 as the recorded evidence for fgdb-ia2b and
   must not be reaped.

## Constraint inherited from 1j16

No external sweeper, and nothing in a gate deletes a file (RULE 1). If the answer
turns out to be retention rather than not-writing, it needs an owner with delete
authority -- 1j16 option 2 -- and this bead should be merged into that decision
rather than growing its own reaper.

Found while working fgdb-1j16 (pane2, 2026-07-27). Nothing has been deleted.
notes:
pane4, 2026-07-27 ~03:2x. Pool measured at HEAD 6c379ed with 7.1G free; written
up at HEAD 47a8c00, by which point fgdb-1j16 had landed (3668d69). MEASURED AND
DESIGNED; the code change is NOT LANDED and the reason is stated at the end.

=== THE CLAIM IN THIS BEAD THAT COLLAPSES ===

This bead says: "Gate evidence is per-run BY CONSTRUCTION: it is the output being
asserted on, and two runs must not share it or the gate stops measuring its own
run. Content-keying is the wrong instrument here."

Genuine per-run output is 0.272 GB of the 9.84 GB -- 2.8%. MEASURED: 2443 loose
files (.jsonl/.err/.sha256) sitting directly in the 113 marker dirs. Everything
else is INPUT, copied per fixture. 4.10 GB of it (41.7%) is four file classes
that no fixture and no checker code path ever writes.

Content-keying is indeed the wrong instrument. So is reaping. The instrument is
`cp -l`.

=== THE PARTITION OF THE 9.84 GB (measured, sums to 9.83) ===

  class                                       copies      GB      %   disposition
  registries/*.toml                              837    4.75   48.3%  MUST COPY
  .beads/issues.jsonl                            441    3.08   31.3%  LINKABLE
  tools/registry-check/src/*.rs                  441    0.93    9.4%  LINKABLE
  COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_...md                       453    0.71    7.2%  MUST COPY
  per-run evidence (.jsonl/.err/.sha256)        2443    0.27    2.8%  irreducible
  crates/ + scripts/ + Cargo.toml                441    0.09    0.9%  LINKABLE
                                                       -----
                                                        9.83

Cross-check on 1j16's half from the same census: libregistry_check.rlib 113
copies = 7.151 GB, registry-check 113 copies = 1.033 GB, total 8.18 GB -- 1j16
says 8.17 GB. The two halves are measured by one reader and agree.

Also from the same pass, unrelated to either bead: the /data/tmp pool is 10719
entries, not 165. 165 are directories (22.16 GB); 10554 are stray `tmp.*` FILES
totalling 0.04 GB. Negligible bytes, 10554 inodes, different producer.

=== Q1 (this bead's first question): copies vs genuine per-run output ===

87.1% of the 9.84 GB is copies (8.57 GB), 2.8% is genuine per-run output. The
three hypotheses this bead offered for the copies:

  - copy-on-write clone: FALSIFIED ON THIS MACHINE. / is ext4 on /dev/nvme0n1p4.
    `cp --reflink=always` -> "Operation not supported" (probed in scratchpad).
  - symlink farm: unnecessary. Repo and /data/tmp are the same device (st_dev
    66308 both), so HARD links work and are invisible to the checker's laws.
  - in-memory synthesis: correct in principle (that is what
    tests/architecture_decisions.rs does) but it is a rewrite of a 72 KB gate
    script, not a fix.

=== Q2: which gates produce the biggest dirs ===

The 113 marker dirs attributed by positive child marker:

  gate           dirs      GB   mean      max
  g0_identity      17    9.98  601.3MB  627.5MB (tmp.Q9JWAqKb1p)
  g0_spine         61    5.12   86.0MB   92.4MB
  g0_claims        22    1.97   91.7MB   93.1MB
  unattributed     13    0.94   73.8MB   81.8MB

Subtracting each dir's 75 MB subject (1j16's half) leaves 8.71 GB of evidence in
g0_identity and 1.01 GB in everything else. **88.5% of this bead is one script,
scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh, and the 627.5 MB maximum is simply one run of it.**
The other three producers are ~zero evidence and ~all subject: they are 1j16.

Per run, that script stages 26 complete roots (23 stage_appendix + 3
stage_appendix_except) at 17.61 MB each = 458 MB, plus 14 registries-only roots
(3 stage + 11 stage_except) at 6.07 MB each = 85 MB, plus 0.27 GB/17 of evidence
and the 75 MB subject. 627 MB predicted, 627.5 MB observed.

AND IT GROWS. The two dominant copied files are the two files the swarm itself
appends to. MEASURED from git history:

  .beads/issues.jsonl          5.02 MB (07-22) -> 7.86 MB (now)   +57% in 5 days
  registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml
                               1.59 MB (07-24) -> 4.32 MB (now)  +171% in 3 days

Those two are copied 26x per identity run: 317 MB today, 172 MB five days ago.
The gate's disk cost is a linear function of the beads export size times 26, and
every bead any pane files raises it.

=== Q3: is any of it evidence someone relies on ===

9 distinct pool dirs are cited by name in .beads/issues.jsonl. 6 are PRESENT
(AJuYPC46f4, ECFKRWvum9, G5czm7QFIs, Q9JWAqKb1p, Z33uC7OtE5, qIVyqY2uko); 3 are
ALREADY ABSENT (04yme8fWMO, 1mDaWQL5Za, CB9K3IaRcE) and all three are cited by
one bead, fgdb-a15-key-backup-n77c, whose recorded evidence has therefore already
evaporated. G5czm7QFIs (89 MB, fgdb-ia2b) is present and must not be reaped.

That is the honest answer to "does anything rely on it": the citation practice
has a 33% dangling rate after one day, so a sweep must be checked against this
list, and citing a tmp path is not a durable record.

=== THE FIX, AND WHY IT IS SAFE ===

One function, scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh:551 stage_appendix_support(). Change
`cp` to `cp -l` for the four never-written classes; leave registries/ and the
plan md as real copies:

  cp -l   .beads/issues.jsonl                  7676 KB   never written
  cp -l   tools/registry-check/src/*.rs        2308 KB   never written
  cp -l   scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh             76 KB   never written
  cp -l   Cargo.toml + crate/tool manifests      60 KB   never written
  ------------------------------------------- 10120 KB = 56.1% of a root
  cp      registries/*.toml                    6220 KB   36 mutation sites + law
  cp      COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_...md             1696 KB   2 mutation sites

Saves 26 x 9.88 MB = 257 MB per identity run, 41.0% of a 627 MB run. Retroactively
4.10 GB of this bead's 9.84 GB, 41.7%. Two independent derivations of the same
fraction: today's source sizes give 56.1% of a root linkable, and the historical
depth-2 census of a real fixture gives 9716/17396 KB = 55.9%.

Four propositions, all closed statically, no build:

1. THE GATE NEVER REFERENCES A LINKED FILE AGAIN, READ OR WRITE. Exhaustive
   census of every `$WORK/<fixture>/...` path in the script, by tail:

     registries/logical_object_kinds.toml        19
     registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml          18
     registries/durable_fields.toml              13
     registries/{wire_types,prebootstrap_artifact_kinds,
                 physical_record_kinds,bootstrap_frames}.toml  6 each
     COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_...md                     2   (both writes: 1120, 1532)
     registries, registries/                      8   (staging dests)
     .beads, .beads/, scripts, scripts/,
       tools/registry-check/src{,/}               6   (all inside
                                                      stage_appendix_support
                                                      itself, lines 551-568)

   Nothing outside registries/ and the plan md is touched after staging. This
   covers every write form, not just truncating `>`: there are appending `>>`
   writers (1126, 1144, 1221, 1328), an `ln -s` (1350), a bare `ln` (1378) and a
   `mkdir -p` (1401), and all six land on registries/logical_object_kinds.toml
   or registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml. An earlier same-line-only grep of mine
   reported "zero ln/mv/mkdir writers", which was wrong -- those six are
   line-continued. The conclusion is unchanged and stronger: the linkable set has
   zero post-staging references of any kind.

2. NO CHECKER WRITE CAN LAND OUTSIDE registries/. The whole production write
   surface of tools/registry-check is main.rs:808 (create a
   .appendix-regenerate-*.prepared inside registries/), main.rs:819 (write_all to
   it) and main.rs:1009 (rename it onto a projection destination inside
   registries/). main.rs:725 opens the catalog READ-ONLY for an advisory lock.
   Every other fs::write in the tool is inside `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`
   (unsafe_ledger.rs:2415).

3. THE CHECKER'S HARD-LINK LAW DOES NOT REACH THE LINKED SET. main.rs:638
   metadata_has_one_link is called at main.rs:746 (projection destination) and
   main.rs:846-847 (prepared projection). PROJECTION_FILES (appendix_a.rs:5058)
   is 6 files, all in registries/, which stays a copy. The gate's own
   neg-appendix-regenerate-hardlink fixture (line 1371) proves that law fires
   with exit 2 / code 6 -- linking a projection would break the POSITIVE
   appendix-regenerate fixture, which is exactly why registries/ is excluded.
   snapshot_nonprojection_tree (line 583) records %y|%m|%p|%l and sha256, none of
   which move under a hard link.

4. WRITE-THROUGH IS DETECTABLE AND DOES NOT HAPPEN. Probe (scratchpad, no repo
   file touched, no build, runs in under a second) builds a stand-in ROOT, stages
   it, applies all five write forms the census found, and digests the source:
     A today, all copies      -> source intact,  0 of 10 staged inodes shared
     B proposed               -> source intact,  5 of 10 shared
     C control: ALSO link the plan md, then truncate it
                              -> source CORRUPT, 6 of 10 shared
        136311807998a261 -> 6750d368e7325049; source plan reads "MUTATED plan"
     D control: append `>>` through the linked .beads/issues.jsonl
                              -> source CORRUPT, 5 of 10 shared
        136311807998a261 -> dea1c2313f0632e8; source reads
        "SENTINEL beads APPENDED beads"
   Both controls FIRE. Without C and D, A and B would prove only that the probe
   is blind. D exists because the gate has four `>>` appenders and a truncation-
   only probe cannot see them.

   The probe's own per-file reporter had this bug and it was caught by D: it
   classified a file as intact if its content still STARTED with the sentinel,
   which is true after an append. Fixed to a byte compare against a pristine
   rebuild. The case verdict was always driven by the tree digest and was correct
   throughout; the per-file line was the thing that lied.

THE FOOT-GUN THIS EXPOSES, INDEPENDENT OF THE FIX: two fixtures
(neg-appendix-source at line 1120, neg-appendix-reference-source at line 1532)
truncate-redirect into COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_THE_DESIGN_OF_FRANKENGRAPHDB.md
inside a staged root. It is the repo's single source of truth. Anyone who reaches
for the obvious `cp -l` across the whole staging function -- which is what both
this bead and 1j16 gesture at -- destroys it. That is case C above, and it is not
hypothetical: it is the first thing a reader of these two beads would try.

=== THE SECOND INCREMENT, AND THE GUARD IT NEEDS FIRST ===

registries/ is 4.75 GB, half this bead, and it is "MUST COPY" only in aggregate.
