title: Poison or recover the Database handle after any post-D2 derived-publication failure
description:
## What and scope
Harden the integrated fgdb spine at the authority-to-derived-state boundary. After CommitCoordinator returns success, the Chronicle marker is durable, but any later fold, Strata object, manifest, root-slot, decode, or snapshot-refresh failure currently returns WriteError::Rebuild while the same Database handle remains callable with its pre-commit writer and snapshot. Introduce an explicit state transition that prevents reads or writes from using stale derived state and provides one authoritative recovery path.

## Why
At tracked commit 62cb9797, write_with_crash commits at crates/fgdb/src/lib.rs:1438-1446, performs fallible derived publication through :1448-1663, and updates self.writer/self.snapshot only at :1664-1665. WriteError::Rebuild documents that the commit may already be durable. Because Chronicle open uses PassThroughValidator, no transaction validator closes this gap. A second write after a post-D2 error can fold only its new template over stale state and publish a derived root that omits the prior durable commit until reopen. This is an inferred code-path correctness risk that requires a deterministic reproducer.

## Design and contracts
Model the live handle explicitly as Healthy or NeedsAuthoritativeRecovery carrying at least the committed sequence and typed failure evidence. Once D2 succeeds, every later error must atomically enter NeedsAuthoritativeRecovery before returning. In that state, writes and reads that would claim the current frontier fail with a typed recovery-required error; they never use the stale writer or snapshot. Recovery must rebuild or verify from the authoritative retained checkpoint plus complete logical-command suffix, or fail closed when that basis is unavailable. Reopen remains a valid recovery route. Do not make Strata authoritative and do not silently roll the Chronicle head back. Where pre-D2 validation can eliminate fold refusals, wire it into the real validator, but retain the state machine for unavoidable post-D2 I/O failures.

## Acceptance criteria and tests
1. Deterministic fault injection at every fallible boundary after D2 and before self.writer/self.snapshot replacement proves the returned handle cannot serve stale reads or accept another write.
2. For every injected failure, drop and reopen reconstructs the durable commit exactly once and agrees with fgdb-reference; a same-handle repair path, if provided, yields the identical root/frontier.
3. A two-write regression proves the second write can never publish a root omitting the first already-durable commit.
4. Typed errors distinguish pre-commit refusal, commit outcome unknown, committed-needs-recovery, and recovery failure without claiming rollback.
5. Simulation/crash tests cover failure, cancellation, ENOSPC, fsync lies, and root-slot publication around the D2-to-snapshot window, with structured events naming durable sequence, prior snapshot frontier, failed stage, handle state, and replay command.
6. Mutation evidence removes the poison transition or permits one read/write in NeedsAuthoritativeRecovery and demonstrates the regression test fails.
close_reason: All post-D2 recovery-fence acceptance is implemented and mutation/gate proven through 53fb871

title: Fail-closed citation guard: every law citation must resolve to a registries/laws.toml ID
description: Step 3 of the fgdb-law-citation-sweep-uzzh ruling. registries/laws.toml now exists (57610e9), so citations finally have something to resolve against. The guard must key on the law ID, carry its own violation code, and have a COMPLETENESS GUARD FAILING CLOSED: an unrecognised citation-shaped phrase must FAIL, never be skipped, because a fabricated law is by definition the one the extractor has no entry for. Resolve by the registry's `name` field rather than rewriting catalog prose -- all 69 flattened-rendering citations live in `rationale`, which is byte-compared against the 450 compiled adjudication pins, so rewriting means 138 coordinated edits and enlarges the 23u1 mirror. A citation resolving to a row whose status is `fabrication-candidate` or `unadjudicated` must NOT be licensed. BLOCKED ON 23u1: the guard resolves citations through a namespace that is 30% mirrored catalog prose, so the obvious implementation passes on 100% of the citations it exists to catch. Filed by pane2 2026-07-27.

title: Sweep every law-citation string in the catalog against the laws that actually exist, fail-closed
description:
ORIGIN. fgdb-hvfn. The row ConfigurationTransitionSpec.required_prepared justified an
invented u64 by citing "the Appendix A u64 floor law". MEASURED at HEAD d747cb8: that
string occurs in exactly TWO places in this repository -- the row itself
(durable_fields.toml:1681) and its catalog mirror (appendix_a_catalog.toml:111137).
It appears nowhere in COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_THE_DESIGN_OF_FRANKENGRAPHDB.md, nowhere
in tools/registry-check, and in no other registry. The row invented the type AND
invented the law that licensed the type.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A WRONG VALUE. A wrong value is a value; the next reader can
re-derive it. A fabricated citation MANUFACTURES AUTHORITY. Every later reader
inherits a rule that was never adopted, and the next mint can cite the same phantom
law as precedent in perfect good faith. The failure is silent by construction: the
row was internally consistent, so appendix exited 0, identity exited 0, and the suite
was 130/130. No gate can object to a citation it never resolves.

THE ASK. Sweep EVERY law-citation string in the catalog against the set of laws that
actually exist. Own violation code. Fail closed.

=== DESIGN ===

1. BUILD THE LAW SET. Candidate sources, to be measured not assumed:
     - named laws in the plan (Appendix A prose, the doctrine, FG-INV-01..20)
     - violation codes the checker can emit
     - owner rulings with a stable id
   The set must include PROHIBITION laws, not only affirmative ones. Per the
   doctrine finding already on the board, a bare "citations must resolve" rule
   inverts the doctrine unless it classifies prohibitions -- a row citing a law that
   FORBIDS something must not be read as licensed by it.

2. EXTRACT EVERY CITATION-SHAPED PHRASE from catalog free text. retention_and_cut_rule
   is the dominant carrier but NOT the only one: rationale strings on ambiguity
   adjudications also cite laws and rulings (appendix_a.rs:4882 is a live example --
   "the owner ruling therefore selects the builtin opaque id256 form").

3. REQUIRE EACH TO RESOLVE, with its own violation code.

4. COMPLETENESS GUARD, FAILING CLOSED. The extractor must ACCOUNT FOR every
   citation-shaped phrase it sees. A phrase the extractor does not recognise must
   FAIL, not be skipped -- otherwise the sweep is vacuous in exactly the region where
   a fabricated citation lives, since a fabricated law is by definition the one the
   extractor has no entry for. This guard is the whole instrument; without it the
   sweep passes on the very row that motivated it.

=== MEASURE BEFORE BUILDING ===

State the denominator first: how many citation-shaped phrases exist in the catalog,
and how many resolve against the law set, BEFORE writing the checker. If the
unresolved count is large the design is wrong (the extractor is over-matching); if it
is zero on a corpus known to contain at least one fabrication, the extractor is
under-matching and the control cannot fire. Prove both directions with a mutation:
plant a fabricated citation and confirm it is caught, and confirm a real citation is
not.

=== KNOWN INSTANCE TO USE AS THE POSITIVE CONTROL ===

"the Appendix A u64 floor law" -- 2 occurrences, 0 supporting definitions. Note that
fgdb-hvfn's repair removes both occurrences, so capture the fixture BEFORE that lands
or the control disappears with it.

Filed by pane2 at owner request, 2026-07-27. Nothing deleted.
close_reason: Steps 1 and 2 delivered and landed (57610e9, dee62ef). registries/laws.toml exists with a fail-closed validator and 15 mutation fixtures; all 10 cited law names adjudicated -- 4 registered covering 86 of 93 citations, 2 unadjudicated for owner decision, 3 fabrication-candidates recorded and NOT struck. flattened-rendering is real: plan a01:1412 states it verbatim. Step 3 extracted to fgdb-law-citation-guard-ld8f, which now carries the 23u1 dependency.

pane2, 2026-07-27, HEAD a7ea5ce. DENOMINATOR MEASURED BEFORE ANY CHECKER WAS WRITTEN,
as this bead requires. The result changes the bead's premise and I am reporting it
before building.

=== THE CORPUS ===

registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml, prose-carrying keys identified by mean value
length rather than by guess: retention_and_cut_rule (984 values), rationale (450),
transcript_recipe (20), encoding_context (942), plus 8 small keys. 2,440 prose values,
404,560 characters scanned.

=== THE MEASUREMENT ===

  11 distinct cited law names
  94 occurrences
   0 of 11 defined as a law anywhere in the plan or the checker

  n   cited law name                       referent exists?  defined as a law?
  69  flattened-rendering                  no                NO
  12  compact-phrase                       no                NO
   2  StrongRef-only arm-payload-shape     no                NO
   2  ConsensusDomain per the shorthand    no                NO
   2  SequenceNeutralSpec                  YES               NO
   2  Appendix A u64 sequence              no                NO
   1  SequenceNeutralSpec wrapper          no                NO
   1  No source                            YES               NO
   1  Appendix A u64 index                 no                NO
   1  D1 closure                           YES               NO
   1  Appendix A u64 floor                 no                NO

THE SET OF LAWS THAT ACTUALLY EXIST IS EMPTY. There is no law registry in this
repository -- no table, no enumeration, no artifact that defines a named law and its
statement. So a sweep "against the set of laws that actually exist" resolves 0 of 94
citations, and the checker this bead asks for would flag every one of them.

=== "the Appendix A u64 floor law" IS NOT THE OUTLIER; IT IS THE SMALLEST INSTANCE ===

It has ONE occurrence. The dominant citation is "the flattened-rendering law" at 69
occurrences -- 73% of all law citations in the catalog -- and it has no referent under
any of four spelling variants tested (flattened-rendering, flattened rendering,
flattened_rendering, flatten). The bare verb "flatten" appears 10 times in the plan;
no artifact anywhere defines a flattened-rendering LAW.

It also has two siblings nobody had looked at: "the Appendix A u64 sequence law" (2)
and "the Appendix A u64 index law" (1). So the u64 family is 4 occurrences across 3
invented variants, not one row.

=== TWO CLASSES, AND THEY NEED DIFFERENT REPAIRS ===

  Class A -- cites a REAL referent, invents its legal status (3 of 11):
    SequenceNeutralSpec (a real schema, 12 plan mentions), D1 closure, "No source".
    Repair: rewrite the citation to name the thing without calling it a law, or
    promote it to a real law with a statement.

  Class B -- cites nothing that exists (8 of 11, 88 of 94 occurrences):
    flattened-rendering, compact-phrase, StrongRef-only arm-payload-shape,
    ConsensusDomain-per-the-shorthand, SequenceNeutralSpec wrapper, and the three
    Appendix A u64 variants.
    Repair: define the law, or retract the citation.

=== WHY THIS WAS NEVER NOTICED -- A CIRCULARITY WORTH ITS OWN NOTE ===

tools/registry-check/src/appendix_a.rs MIRRORS the catalog's prose: its 450
AMBIGUITY_ADJUDICATION_CONTRACT pins embed rationale strings verbatim. Stripping those
mirrored literals takes the file from 997,854 to 702,224 characters -- 296K chars,
30%, is copied catalog text.

So the obvious test, "is this law mentioned in the checker", RESOLVES A CITATION
AGAINST ITS OWN COPY. My first pass fell into exactly this: flattened-rendering,
compact-phrase and SequenceNeutralSpec all read "RESOLVES" until the mirror was
stripped, after which all three read 0. Any future implementation of this sweep MUST
strip the mirror or it will pass on every citation it is built to catch.

=== CONSEQUENCE FOR THE DESIGN ===

Building the fail-closed checker now would be correct and would immediately red the
tree on 94 occurrences, which is not landable in one increment. The bounded form is:

  1. Seed a law registry with these 11 rows. Each row is either DEFINED (name +
     statement + where it is enforced) or RETRACTED (citation rewritten).
     That converts an unbounded prose problem into an 11-row adjudication.
  2. Then land the checker: every citation-shaped phrase must resolve against that
     registry, own violation code, and a COMPLETENESS GUARD FAILING CLOSED -- an
     unrecognised citation-shaped phrase must FAIL, never be skipped, because a
     fabricated law is by definition the one the extractor has no entry for.
  3. Positive control is banked at
     /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane2_uzzh_control_fixture.txt, captured before fgdb-hvfn
     removes both occurrences of the u64 floor law. Negative control: any Class A
     citation, which must NOT fire once its referent is registered.

Step 1 is an owner-facing adjudication (11 rows, several of which are load-bearing
prose across 69 rows), so I am naming it rather than deciding it.

Nothing deleted. No repo file touched by this measurement.

title: URGENT before Tier R: Strata structures must be PERSISTENT (structural sharing) or O(1) branch forking is dead
notes:
FILED 2026-07-31 from the reality check (docs/REALITY_CHECK_AND_BRIDGE_PLAN.md, Phase 4 Round 2a).
P0 because the cost of acting is small NOW and is a rewrite LATER. Nothing is broken today; this is a
window that is closing.

THE REQUIREMENT, verbatim from the plan. plan:451: branch creation "adds only metadata and key wraps,
so its data-copy complexity is O(1)", and "reads select the branch head and follow explicit
branch-parent links atop structurally shared objects".

WHAT WE HAVE. fgdb-reference::fork_branch materializes the parent's fold at the boundary -- O(n) -- and
says so honestly at the definition, because §15 licenses that crate to be simple and never optimized.
That licence does NOT extend to the engine. fgdb-strata tier D (def35d6..3fb7b94) stores immutable
content-addressed blocks, which is a good start and is NOT the same thing: immutability gives you safe
sharing, but nothing in tier D yet lets a forked branch SHARE a partition root's blocks without
re-listing them, and nothing at all exists for tier R.

WHY THIS IS URGENT RATHER THAN IMPORTANT. Retrofitting persistence into a mutable or copy-on-fork
structure is not an optimization, it is a rewrite of the structure and everything that reads it. Tier
D is young enough to absorb the decision. Tier R (fgdb-w3-tier-r-0tj) is NOT YET WRITTEN, so it can be
born persistent at no extra cost. Once tier R exists in a non-persistent shape, B1's git-style
branching and B6's branch-per-agent isolation are both economically dead -- an agent-per-branch product
whose branch creation is O(graph) has no product.

THE TECHNIQUE, named so it can be argued with. Driscoll, Sarnak, Sleator and Tarjan, "Making Data
Structures Persistent" (JCSS 1989). Two usable shapes:
  - PATH COPYING: fork copies only the nodes on the path from root to change, O(log n) per write,
    O(1) per fork. Simplest, and the standard choice for immutable tries.
  - FAT NODES with version stamps: O(1) amortised space per change, more complex reads.
CONFLUENT persistence (Fiat & Kaplan) is the harder relative and is what a branch MERGE needs; scope it
separately rather than pretending fork and merge are one problem.

WHAT TO ACTUALLY DECIDE AND RECORD:
1. Is a partition root's block list shared structurally on fork, or copied? (Today: copied -- a forked
   branch would get a new root listing the same block identities. That is O(blocks), not O(1). It may
   be acceptable if block counts stay small, and that is a MEASUREMENT, not an assumption.)
2. Does tier R's run structure admit path copying? Decide before the layout is frozen, because
   Elias-Fano-coded runs (see the tier R bead) are monotone sequences whose sharing granularity is a
   layout decision.
3. Where does the branch-parent link live so a read can follow it without loading the parent's data?

LAWS THE CLOSURE OWES:
- forking a branch touches O(1) durable objects, measured by counting objects written -- not by timing,
  which hides the asymptote behind constant factors;
- a forked branch and its parent SHARE block identities (assert the identity sets overlap, so sharing
  is proved rather than hoped);
- the observable semantics are unchanged: every existing branch_fork law in fgdb-reference and every
  Strata differential stays green;
- and a control that the sharing is real: mutating the child does not change any object the parent
  reads.

DO NOT let this bead become a general "make it fast" task. The deliverable is a DECISION plus the
laws that hold it, recorded before tier R is written.
close_reason: Decision already normative; exact persistence laws routed to fgdb-ge6a and fgdb-w3-tier-r-0tj, with existing architecture, fork-semantic, and Strata suites green.

comments.author: MistyJay
comments.text:
DECISION RESOLVED 2026-08-01 by MistyJay.

FIND-WHAT-ALREADY-EXISTS-FIRST audit: the requested design decision is already normative, so this bead must not create a second ADR or a redundant test surface.

Existing authority:
- plan:451 requires O(1) data-copy complexity at fork and reads through explicit branch-parent links over structurally shared objects.
- plan:453 fixes the mechanism as a frozen path-copied parent root in BranchForkBundle.
- plan:2000 fixes the ancestry link in BranchManifest::Fork with parent_branch, parent_head, fork_boundary_logical_command_seq, and boundary_reservation_identity.
- frozen FG-ADR-SOTA-STORAGE-ASPEN adopts immutable structural sharing at run granularity and already registers cargo-test:run-sharing-snapshots as planned implementation evidence.

Resolved decision:
1. Fork does not create a child PartitionRoot or copy parent block/run inventories. It publishes branch and key metadata plus the frozen parent-head ancestry binding. PartitionRoot V1 remains a branch-local leaf object, not the cross-branch directory.
2. Shared durable objects remain immutable. The first divergent child write creates new affected leaf objects and path-copies only the persistent directory route needed to publish the child head. Fat-node or version-stamped mutation is rejected.
3. Tier R shares whole immutable AdjRunSegment ObjectIds. Elias-Fano and codec payloads are neither copied at fork nor patched in place. Child compaction publishes replacement runs only into the child route.
4. Merge remains the separately specified squash-difference operation; physical confluent persistence is not introduced.

Implementation laws routed to the owning beads:
- Fork data-object writes equal zero. Metadata and key-wrap writes are counted separately and reported with their bounded-fanout qualification, never mislabeled O(1) for arbitrary recipient lists.
- At the fork boundary, resolved parent and child partition/run ObjectId sets are equal, which is stronger than merely proving a nonempty overlap; the child local overlay is empty.
- After a child write, the parent head and every object identity and byte sequence resolved by the parent are unchanged.
- Existing fgdb-reference branch_fork laws and Strata differential laws stay green.
- Fresh-store reopen follows BranchManifest ancestry and never depends on an in-memory copied partition list.

Ownership: fgdb-ge6a owns the persistent root-directory and fresh-reopen laws. fgdb-w3-tier-r-0tj owns whole-run sharing plus cargo-test:run-sharing-snapshots. This P0 bead is the decision gate only; those implementation beads must not claim these laws before executable evidence exists.

title: Mint LocalGcApplyQuarantineSpec and LocalGcCancellationAuthorizeSpec as logical kinds (a14), per the source-typeless ruling
description:

## Class, settled, do not re-derive

  LocalGcApplyQuarantineSpec        LOGICAL by DERIVATION. Inline-record with five

deliberately on a71s and the owner confirmed it: inventing an exact_wire_type to
decide a class manufactures the evidence the question turns on.

Both are slice a14, exist ONLY as [[top_level_candidate]] rows, identity_class
"unclassified", no reservation, no logical kind, no wire type.

  a14:top-level-candidate:local-gc-cancellation-authorize-spec-55ad14b03f73e5e4

This is the part that would have been wrong from one direction:

     inbound 0, and its five members are source-typeless so there are no outbound

Per host, following the seven e7b6f09 a20 mints:

The frontier was max object_kind 0x0570 at HEAD adaddfb, giving 0x0571/0x0572.
It was 0x056f forty minutes earlier. Panes mint above it continuously, so take

title: SPINE increment: edge property UPDATES — per-statement content chains on FGSB (the proven FGSV V2 model applied to edges)
description: The last CRUD gap: vertices update (stb6), edges cannot — the writer liveness-checks DeltaRow::Property on edges then explicitly unstores it, so a durable update the oracle applies is invisible to the engine. THE MODEL (mirror stb6 exactly): an EId's durable history becomes a chain of content statements keyed (eid, created_at) — same (src,relation,dst) birth-immutability across the chain, contiguity (successor.created_at == predecessor.retired_at; gap = resurrection refused, overlap = aliasing refused), retirement final, tombstone restates the CURRENT row. FORMAT: FGSB V7 relaxes the uniqueness/order law from strictly-ascending (dst,eid) to strictly-ascending (dst,eid,created_at) so one block can carry a retire+successor pair; spans already encode per-statement visibility. VALIDATOR: EdgeHistoryValidator re-keyed by statement with cross-block chain admission (VertexHistoryValidator is the template); EdgeIdentityMismatch narrows to birth-field drift; new discontinuity/aliasing arms. MERGES: collapse keyed (eid,created_at); contiguity makes at most one statement visible per eid per as_of, so merge_neighbours/merge_edge_with_props/merge_all pick the visible statement — and SYSTEM-TIME reads then answer the OLD row at old as_of, which is the whole payoff (a naive restatement model would leak the new row into history; the per-epoch differential would catch it, and with chains it will not). WRITER: fold Property(edge) as retire-live-statement-at-seq + successor with updated row; same-commit create+update folds in place (vertex precedent); pending key gains created_at. SPINE: WriteBatch::set_edge_property with prefix-overlay before-image derivation validated by the oracle at replay; fold_version edge-update arm. LAWS: chain refusals both directions (vertex_patch_format is the template), spine update law with as_of sweep (old row at old seq), differential seventh epoch updating edge props compared vs oracle per epoch, compaction answer-preservation over chains (mid-chain floor drops admit as chain-start — FGSV precedent). Compaction/props carry and V6 predecessor chains are orthogonal and compose.
close_reason: Edge properties update durably as retire+content-successor chains; every content version answers in its own interval, proven by boundary laws and the seven-epoch oracle differential (f8f7ef8). Full CRUD on both element kinds.

title: Bead-provenance pins are a count over a file every pane writes: any br create invalidates every other pane's just-frozen pins
close_reason: Provenance pins are monotone floors and binding_hash is re-keyed by rule (4a01ce8). The defect was the quantification domain, not the count form: the already-content-addressed binding_hash broke identically on one legal create. Concurrent reproduction fails under the old scheme (4 violations) and passes under floors (0) across all interleavings and 2/3/5 concurrent creators; loss still trips the floors (deletion 2, owner-bead deletion 6, 198-record wipe 178). Rename follow-up filed as fgdb-hcvx.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FILED BY ORCHESTRATOR at pane2's request; pane2 surfaced it and declined to file unilaterally, correctly, since it is a design question rather than a defect in any one increment.

THE DEFECT. The bead-provenance pins are a COUNT over .beads/issues.jsonl -- a file every pane writes. So the pin is a global assertion about shared mutable state, and any pane running 'br create' invalidates every other pane's just-frozen pins. pane2 hit this TWICE in one session. It is not a bug in any pane's behaviour; correct panes racing correctly still break it.

OBSERVED COST TONIGHT, all from this one root cause:
  - repeated 'chore(beads): re-freeze provenance' commits that carry no product change
  - a 398->399 re-freeze sitting in one pane's tree while another pane's closed bead depended on it
  - seven CREATED records stranded in local .beads/beads.db, exposed to deletion by any 'br sync --import-only' (relayed swarm-wide 23:12Z; closed by a flush at 23:20Z)
  - the standing rule that a bead CREATION costs a pin re-freeze while an equal-insert/delete MODIFIED sweep does not -- a rule every pane must be told, because nothing enforces it

WHY IT IS A DESIGN FIX, NOT A REPAIR. Each occurrence is individually cheap to fix and collectively unbounded: the repair is O(number of concurrent creators) forever. A pin that quantifies over a file with N writers cannot be stable under N>1 by construction.

DIRECTIONS WORTH COSTING (do not assume one): make the pin per-record or content-addressed rather than a count; scope it to the records the freezing commit actually owns; derive it from committed HEAD rather than the working-tree export; or serialise creation behind the existing beads token and make that mandatory rather than advisory.

Related: the bead-provenance re-pin cycle is already known to break 5 tests on any creation. This bead is the root cause of that tax.

At b938141: `.beads/issues.jsonl` holds 401 distinct records while both pins declare 398.

So `architecture-check` — scripts/check.sh stage 8 — is red on main for every pane, and

I derived +1 (398->399, bet_label 243->244, binding fe035bf5->a0d87d7a), applied it to both
the TOML and the four compiled consts, recomputed PINNED_SEMANTIC_CONTRACT_HASH from the
edited TOML (db71fd98->b2a59643), and verified architecture-check at 0 violations and

moved twice and the record count went 399 -> 401. **Every value I had just frozen was
correct for a tree that no longer existed** — and a stale pin is indistinguishable at the
exit code from a correct one, which is what makes this expensive rather than merely annoying.

I have therefore REVERTED my pin edits rather than commit them (the two files are byte-
identical to HEAD again) and am not re-freezing. Re-freezing here is a race I cannot win
and would only move the red by one commit; it is also your bead. Nothing of mine is left
unflushed — pane4's sweep already committed my k2mj CREATE, my fgdb-8kzt close, and my two
comments, so this is not a case of me holding records hostage.

TWO THINGS MY ATTEMPT SUGGESTS FOR THE FIX, offered as data not design:
1. The orphan violation DOES NOT NAME THE BEAD. With 401 records and 61 lacking a b1..b6
   label (most legitimately resolved by family rule or exact override), "one of them is an
   orphan" is not actionable, and the obvious probe is wrong: the per-bead
   `architecture_bead_provenance_indexed` events are not emitted at all on this failure
   path, so you cannot diff indexed-vs-present to find it. Naming the bead in the message
   is a small change that turns a 10-minute hunt into a glance. This is the same gap
   already filed as fgdb-bead-provenance-orphan-workstream-tag-7u5m.
2. The count is only half the churn. `bead_count` and the four class counts move on any
   CREATE, but `binding_hash` and `semantic_contract_hash` also move, and the semantic hash
   can only be computed AFTER the TOML edit lands — so the re-freeze is inherently two
   passes over a base that is moving under both of them. Any fix that keeps a literal count

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
pane2 DESIGN FINDING. Costed all four named directions plus a fifth, built a working prototype, and ran a mutation matrix on both. Nothing landed: `catalog` is held by pane6-dsi3 and this change alters a procedure every pane uses, so it wants scheduling, not a unilateral write. Everything below is measured, not estimated.

INSTRUMENT. Base state = 60439d7, the last commit where records == PINNED_BEAD_COUNT (398 == 398). Fixture symlinks every path from that snapshot and materialises only `.beads/issues.jsonl`, so a difference in the report is attributable to the corpus mutation and nothing else. Checkers driven lock-free by plain rustc against `validate_architecture`. Base is 0 violations under both checkers, so the instrument is not vacuous.

=== 1. THE DEFECT STATEMENT NEEDS SHARPENING ===

The bead says the pin is a COUNT. That is true but it is not the defect, and taking it literally sends you to a fix that does not work. `binding_hash` is ALREADY content-addressed and it breaks exactly as hard:

  mutation create1 (one bead, resolves via an existing bet label -- legal under every provenance law):
    bead_source_count, bead_resolution_class_count, bead_binding_hash_mismatch, independent_bead_binding_hash_mismatch   = 4 violations

The problem is not count-vs-hash. It is the QUANTIFICATION DOMAIN: the change-detector quantifies over a set the freezing commit does not own. Any equality over corpus-derived data is unstable under insertion, whatever its form.

The second half of the sharpening: the provenance machinery is TWO things fused, and only one of them is broken.

  (A) PER-RECORD LAWS -- orphan, not_total, family_ambiguous, bet_label_unknown, decision_unresolved/superseded, override_shadowed, override_target_missing, owner_bead_unresolved. Every one is a predicate over a single record. They are ALREADY stable under N writers. A pane creating a bead with a home does not move any other bead's resolution. These are not the defect and must not be touched.

  (B) CORPUS-CARDINALITY CHANGE-DETECTOR -- bead_count, 4 class counts, 14 expected_match_counts, binding_hash, each pinned twice (TOML + code const). This is the whole of the tax.

=== 2. THE MEASUREMENT THAT MATTERS MOST: THE PINS DESTROYED THE SIGNAL THEY RIDE ON ===

`recompute_semantic_contract_hash` takes `&ArchitectureRegistry` and no `&Path` -- it CANNOT read the bead file. It is the registry's "did the ADR contract move" tripwire. But the corpus counts and `binding_hash` are laundered into its transcript, so every `br create` moves it.

Walking all 49 commits that touch architecture.rs:

  PINNED_SEMANTIC_CONTRACT_HASH moved in                45 commits
    ...of which ALSO moved PINNED_BEAD_COUNT            44   <- bead churn, not a semantic edit
    ...genuine semantic-only edits                       1
  PINNED_BEAD_COUNT moved without the semantic hash      0   <- 100% laundering

44:1 noise-to-signal on the registry's most load-bearing tripwire. Independent confirmation: the rule-side content of the registry is BYTE-IDENTICAL between 60439d7 and HEAD (rule hash fnv1a64:c4e66b12a1e31d91 at both) -- every registry edit in that window was corpus-pin churn wearing a semantic-hash change as a disguise.

Rate: 44 re-freezes over 2026-07-22..07-26 (~9/day); 26 commits whose SUBJECT LINE is nothing but pin churn.

=== 3. DIRECTION VERDICTS ===

D1 per-record / content-addressed pins -- FALSIFIED. Content-addressing over the whole set is what `binding_hash` already is (4-violation result above). Making it genuinely per-record means a ~400-row table in the TOML that `br create` must append to, which converts a one-line conflict into a shared-table conflict and still costs a registry edit per create. Strictly worse; moves the race one hop.

D2 scope the pin to records the freezing commit owns -- COLLAPSES INTO D1. There is no "freezing commit" at check time; the checker runs on a working tree. Expressing ownership requires per-record attribution, i.e. D1. The useful CONTENT of this direction survives inside D5.

D3 derive from committed HEAD -- FALSIFIED, and strictly worse. HEAD moves too, so the race is unchanged; but the red now appears in a tree the pane never touched, with no local reproduction, and it puts a git dependency inside a checker that is deliberately git-free and cargo-free (that property is what makes `bead_provenance_preflight.sh` work while the workspace is mid-repair).

D4 mandatory beads token -- ALREADY DEPLOYED, ALREADY MEASURED AS INSUFFICIENT. token.sh's own header records that the `beads` token was added 2026-07-24 for exactly this failure. Since then:

  re-freeze commits before 2026-07-24    9
  re-freeze commits on/after             40
  growth transitions since               47

The token removes SWEEP collisions, which is what it was built for. It removes none of the tax, because the tax is per-create, not per-collision. Serialising a cost does not eliminate it. Keep the token for what it does; it is not this fix.

=== 4. D5 -- THE RECOMMENDATION: MAKE THE CORPUS PINS MONOTONE, MOVE THE EQUALITY TO THE RULES ===

Rules are not shared-mutable; the corpus is. Pin each with the form that suits it.

  (a) corpus cardinality: every `!=` becomes `<`. bead_count, the 4 class counts and the 14 family counts become FLOORS. Creation can never trip a floor; loss always does.
  (b) `binding_hash` stops being H(every bead's binding) and becomes H(rule_id -> sorted decision_ids) over direct owners, the six labels, every override and every family. Pure function of the registry; `.beads/issues.jsonl` is never read.
  (c) the floors and the rule hash come OUT of the semantic-contract transcript. That hash goes back to meaning what its name says.
  (d) per-record laws unchanged.
  (e) a ratchet (raise floors to observed) is available but never required for green -- raising a floor to the current count is arithmetic, not a judgement call, unlike assigning provenance.

The corpus/registry boundary turns out to be exactly three comparisons plus one hash function. One reader, no second implementation of the family rules.

MUTATION MATRIX (records; violations TODAY -> violations FLOOR):

  base                    398   0 -> 0     control, both green
  create1                 399   4 -> 0     THE TAX, gone
  create2                 400   4 -> 0
  create10                408   4 -> 0
  delete1  (bead loss)    397   4 -> 2     distinct *_below_floor codes
  delowner (owner lost)   397   8 -> 6
  swap     (equal +1/-1)  398   2 -> 0     MISSED by the fix
  grow10_del1 (stale)     407   4 -> 0     MISSED by the fix
  grow10_delowner         407   9 -> 5
  wipe     (198 lost)     200 180 -> 178

The line that indicts today's design: create1 and delete1 produce THE SAME FOUR CODES. A pane filing a bead and the corpus silently losing a bead are indistinguishable to the checker. That is why the alarm gets re-frozen reflexively -- it carries no information about which happened. Under floors they are different codes, and only one of them fires.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS ON THE PROTOTYPE -- all four FIRE:
  raise a class floor 98->99       -> bead_resolution_class_count_below_floor + bead_count_pin + bead_class_count_total
  raise a family floor 7->8        -> bead_family_match_count_below_floor + bead_family_expected_total
  tamper a family match pattern    -> rule_binding_hash x2 + semantic_contract_hash + 7 orphans + not_total
  silently drop an ADR from a
    family's decision_ids          -> rule_binding_hash x2 + semantic_contract_hash, and NOTHING ELSE

That last one is the control I ran against my own recommendation, and it is the one that matters: a pure re-binding that changes no count and leaves every bead resolvable. It is precisely what the corpus hash was for. The rule-keyed hash catches it. So (b) is not a weakening on that hazard class.

The existing negative tests survive: `direct_owner_count += 1` and `expected_match_count += 1` both still fire (renamed codes).

=== 5. WHAT THE RECOMMENDATION BREAKS -- BOTH GAPS NAMED ===

  swap        equal insert+delete inside one class. Today: 2 (hash). Floor: 0.
  grow10_del1 a bead lost while the floor is stale by 10 creates. Today: 4. Floor: 0.

Both gaps are the same shape: a lost bead that NO decision owns and NO override targets. Every bead the registry actually references is still covered, by `owner_bead_unresolved` and `bead_override_target_missing` -- and those are per-record, so they are already race-free. Scale check from the wipe run: 169 of today's 180 violations come from `owner_bead_unresolved`. The cardinality pins contribute 6. The anti-loss protection people think the count pin is providing is overwhelmingly already coming from a guard that does not have this defect.

Residual exposure is bounded by ratchet cadence and shrinks to zero if ratcheted. Also worth naming: a floor can be silently lowered to 0, which equality cannot be. Mitigated but not eliminated by the TOML-vs-const equality (`bead_count_pin`) forcing a two-file edit -- today's equality pins are lowerable the same way, so this is not a regression.

  record-count transitions   57

comments.text:
pane2 CLOSEOUT. Fixed in 4a01ce8. Follow-up filed as fgdb-hcvx (rename only, no semantics).

=== THE RESULT THAT MATTERS, BECAUSE IT IS THE LEAST OBVIOUS ===

THE DEFECT WAS THE QUANTIFICATION DOMAIN, NOT THE COUNT FORM. This bead was
filed saying "the pin is a COUNT over a file with N writers". True, but taken
literally it sends you to a fix that does not work, and three of the four
directions named here follow from that misreading.

The proof is that `binding_hash` was ALREADY content-addressed -- a BLAKE-style
digest over every bead's (id, resolution_class, rule_id, decision_ids) -- and
it broke exactly as hard. One legal `br create`, a bead that resolves cleanly
through an existing bet label and violates no provenance law:

  bead_source_count, bead_resolution_class_count,
  bead_binding_hash_mismatch, independent_bead_binding_hash_mismatch   = 4

The count and the content-addressed hash fail together, in the same trial, for
the same reason. So the form of the pin was never the variable. What made it
unstable is that the assertion QUANTIFIES OVER A SET THE FREEZING COMMIT DOES
NOT OWN. Any equality over corpus-derived data is unstable under insertion
whatever its shape -- count, hash, per-record table, or anything else.

That reframe is what selects the fix: stop trying to make the equality
survive, and change the QUANTIFIER. A floor (`>=`) is the weakest predicate
that still catches loss, and creation cannot violate it.

The machinery was also two things fused, and only one was broken. The
PER-RECORD laws -- orphan, not_total, family_ambiguous, bet_label_unknown,
decision_unresolved/superseded, override_shadowed, override_target_missing,
owner_bead_unresolved -- are predicates over a single record and were ALREADY
race-free under N writers. They are untouched. Only the corpus-cardinality
change-detector was the tax.

=== THE CONCURRENT REPRODUCTION: FAILS OLD, PASSES FLOORS ===

Two real concurrent processes, pane A freezing pins while pane B runs a
create. One read racing one append has exactly TWO interleavings, so both are
forced rather than sampled -- an earlier jitter harness drew the same order
20/20 times, and keeping it would have let "0 reds" stand as false proof. Both
fixture roots symlink ONE corpus, so a single race is judged by both checkers
and neither scheme gets its own trials.

  create lands AFTER the freeze   OLD 4 violations   NEW 0
  create lands before A's read    OLD 4 violations   NEW 0
  2 / 3 / 5 concurrent creators   OLD 4 each         NEW 0 each

CLOSED, NOT NARROWED, and by monotonicity rather than timing: every state
reachable from any interleaving of creates is a SUPERSET of what the freezing
pane read, and a floor is a lower bound, so no interleaving can trip it. That
is an argument over the whole space, not an observation about one run.

Locked permanently by `concurrent_bead_creation_cannot_red_another_panes_tree`
(tools/registry-check/tests/architecture_decisions.rs), mutation-proven both
directions: PASSES against the landed checker, FAILS against the pre-change
one with exactly bead_source_count, bead_resolution_class_count and both hash
mismatches. A test that cannot fail under the old scheme locks nothing.

=== WHAT LOSS STILL TRIPS -- THE FLOOR IS NOT A VACUOUS GUARD ===

A floor that never fires would pass every assertion above while protecting
nothing, so this is stated as measurement, not intent:

  one bead deleted        NEW 2 violations
                          bead_source_count_below_floor,
                          bead_resolution_class_count_below_floor
  a direct-owner bead     NEW 6 (the two above plus 4 owner_bead_unresolved)
  198 records wiped       NEW 178

Raising any floor above the observed corpus fires: bead_count ->
bead_source_count_below_floor, a class floor ->
bead_resolution_class_count_below_floor, a family floor ->
bead_family_match_count_below_floor. All three are asserted in
architecture_neg_rule_tables_and_resolution_pins.

The rule-keyed hash is not vacuous either: silently dropping an ADR from a
family's decision_ids -- a rebinding that changes NO count and leaves every
bead resolvable -- fires bead_rule_binding_hash_mismatch,
independent_bead_rule_binding_hash_mismatch and semantic_contract_hash_mismatch,
and nothing else. That was the case the corpus-wide hash existed for, and it
is still caught.

KNOWN GAPS, NAMED: an equal insert+delete swap inside one class, and a plain
bead lost while the floor is stale. Both are beads that no decision owns and
no override targets; every bead the registry actually references is still
covered by owner_bead_unresolved and bead_override_target_missing, which are
per-record and were always race-free. Scale check: on a 198-record wipe,
owner_bead_unresolved produced 169 of 180 violations and the cardinality pins
produced 6 -- the anti-loss protection people attribute to the count pin was
already coming from a guard without this defect.

=== WHY THE OTHER THREE OPTIONS LOST ===

PER-RECORD OR CONTENT-ADDRESSED PINS -- falsified twice over. Content-addressed
is what binding_hash already was (the 4-violation result above). Genuinely
per-record means a ~400-row table in the TOML that every `br create` must
append to: it converts a one-line conflict into a shared-table conflict, still
costs a registry edit per create, and needs its own completeness guard to stop
a missing row failing open. Strictly worse, and it moves the race one hop --
the failure mode this project keeps hitting.

SCOPE THE PIN TO RECORDS THE FREEZING COMMIT OWNS -- collapses into the above.
There is no "freezing commit" at check time; the checker runs against a working
tree. Expressing ownership requires per-record attribution, which is the
option already rejected. Its useful content -- "assert only over what you own"
-- survives inside floors, where what you own is a LOWER BOUND you established
rather than a set of rows you enumerate.

DERIVE FROM COMMITTED HEAD -- falsified, and strictly worse than doing nothing.
HEAD moves too (it moved several times per increment tonight), so the race is
unchanged; but now the red appears in a tree the pane never touched, with no
local reproduction. It also puts a git dependency inside a checker that is
deliberately git-free and cargo-free -- the property that lets
bead_provenance_preflight.sh work while the workspace is mid-repair.

MANDATORY BEADS TOKEN -- not a hypothesis. It was ALREADY DEPLOYED on
2026-07-24, for exactly this failure, per token.sh's own header. Measured
since: 40 of the 44 pin re-freezes happened AFTER it landed, across 47 growth
transitions. It removes SWEEP collisions, which is what it was built for, and
removes none of the tax, because the tax is per-create and not per-collision.
Serialising a cost does not eliminate it; it converts a correctness problem
into a throughput problem and leaves creation a global lock across the swarm.
Keep the token for what it does. It is not this fix.

=== A SECOND COPY OF THE DEFECT LIVED IN THE GATE ===

scripts/g0_architecture_decisions_e2e.sh asserted the emitted provenance-event
count and registry bead_count `-eq` the TOML pin, and compared the corpus hash
to it. Converting only the checker would have produced a race-free checker
behind a gate that still redded for every pane on any create -- green, and
wrong. Those are floors now; the exact assertion is the rule hash (newly
emitted as bead_rule_binding_hash); and a closure assert plus a sum check stop
a fifth resolution class hiding behind the per-class floors.

=== LIVE MEASUREMENT AT CLOSE ===

Filing the follow-up bead fgdb-hcvx was itself the test. The corpus is now 404
records against a floor of 401 -- my create plus two more from other panes
since the commit, i.e. the N>1 case unstaged and unsimulated:

  under the landed floor checker      0 violations   GREEN
  under the pre-change equality one   5 violations

Before 4a01ce8 that state cost a 7-value re-freeze across two files and redded
five tests for every pane. It now costs nothing.

=== GATES ===

scripts/check.sh: CORE 6 of 7 -- fmt, check --all-targets, clippy -D warnings,
test --workspace, file-coverage closure, shell lint ALL PASS; the one core red
is the whole-tree UBS scan (pre-existing false-positive class). REGISTERED LIVE
GATES 18 of 19, up from 17: w1_cross_crate_determinism_e2e.sh now passes,
confirming its earlier red was the shared-target-dir race. The single remaining
red is scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh, unchanged cause and not mine -- the
reservation split from e7b6f09 (a20, fgdb-5cgb), observed existing=434
reserved=379 against pinned 431/382; repair is scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh:210
-> 434 and :211 -> 379, left for pane5 because those numbers ratify their
adjudication.

=== HANDOFF ===

OPEN, filed: fgdb-hcvx -- rename the pins so their names stop claiming
equality (bead_count -> bead_count_floor, expected_match_count ->
min_match_count, binding_hash -> rule_binding_hash, and the matching consts).
Mechanical, compiler-checked, no semantics; wants the catalog token at a quiet
point. Nothing breaks mechanically if it waits -- the risk is a pane re-reading
"count" as equality and re-freezing a floor by hand.

FOR THE NEXT AUTHOR, two traps this turn hit:
  - Under floors, a negative test written as `declared + 1` goes VACUOUS the
    moment the corpus grows past the floor. The staged tree at 401-vs-401
    passed; the real tree at 402-vs-401 silently stopped firing it. Derive
    every floor mutation from the OBSERVED count. Staging alone cannot catch
    this, because the staged copy is exactly the state where observed ==
    declared.
  - When converting an equality pin anywhere, grep the GATES as well as the
    checker. The e2e carried an independent copy and would have kept the race
    alive on its own.

Evidence, both prototypes and the race harness survive in this session's
scratchpad; the permanent artefacts are the new test and the floor negatives.

title: Strata BlockStore reads persisted objects without a byte ceiling
description: Fresh-eyes finding at HEAD dbc1103. BlockStore::put compares an existing canonical file with read_to_end, while get and get_bytes also materialize the entire file before identity or format validation. A corrupt or externally planted oversized regular file at a content-derived path can therefore drive an unbounded allocation before the store can return Collision, IdentityMismatch, or a typed format refusal. The durable block and root formats already have finite cardinality ceilings, so the storage boundary must enforce a finite object-byte ceiling as well. Closure: add one bounded reader used by every persisted-object materialization path; reject oversized inputs and existing objects with a typed error; retain identity-before-format diagnostics for in-range damage; use an early file-length check plus a bounded stream read so concurrent growth cannot bypass the ceiling; add a small-limit red control that proves rejection occurs before materialization; keep idempotent put, collision, root reopen, and crash-durability laws green.
close_reason: Implementation aa2e61b remains in current history; focused and mutation evidence is preserved on the bead, and the authoritative repository gate at c3f985f exited 0 with core 9/9 and registered live 24/24. Durable exact-record export is attempted separately and is not implied by this local close.

title: Wire the README's :memory: promise: MemVfs + Database<MemVfs>::open_memory over the real two-fsync path
description: README's embedded 1.0 snippet promises Database::open(":memory:"). The embedded spine had exactly one VFS posture (disk). comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
MEASURED 2026-08-04 while landing the lab VFS (fgdb-1xtp, crates/fgdb-sim/src/vfs.rs).

Plan section 15 names five fault classes for the lab VFS: "injectable latency, torn
writes, bit flips, ENOSPC, fsync lies". Four landed and are witnessed by tests. LATENCY
DID NOT, and this bead exists so that absence is a tracked gap rather than a quiet one.

WHY IT WAS HELD BACK RATHER THAN STUBBED. A latency knob that records an intended delay
without awaiting one is a placebo: every test passes, no test is stronger, and the plan's
claim reads as satisfied. This repo already carries one of those (fgdb-4bxh: a crashpack
replay command whose emitted env vars nothing reads). Shipping a second was the worse of
the two available errors.

WHAT MAKES IT REAL, and the exact obstacle. asupersync's timer is
asupersync::time::sleep(now: Time, duration: Duration) -> Sleep -- an ABSOLUTE deadline
built from a caller-supplied `now`. The Vfs/VfsFile trait methods take no Cx, so a
FaultVfs has no clock to read. Cx::current() inside Runtime::block_on is the candidate
(block_on installs an ambient Cx with the timer driver, per its own comment at
runtime/builder.rs:3398), but that was NOT verified, and under the LAB runtime the whole
point is that the clock is virtual and advanced by the scheduler. So the question this
bead has to answer before writing any code is:

    where does a FaultVfs get its Time, such that the delay is virtual under the lab
    runtime and real under the live one?

Three candidate answers, none measured yet:
  (a) FaultVfs holds a Cx handed in at construction -- couples the VFS to a Cx, but that
      is doctrine 3's shape anyway;
  (b) read Cx::current() per operation inside block_on -- no coupling, unverified, and it
      silently degrades to "no delay" outside a runtime, which is the placebo again
      unless the absence hard-errors;
  (c) a LatencyClock trait the caller supplies, with the lab runtime's clock as one impl.

ACCEPTANCE -- the shape the other four classes already meet:
  * a per-class Trigger plus a duration, seeded from the same SplitMix64 stream, so the
    same plan injects the same delays (crates/fgdb-sim/src/vfs.rs holds the pattern);
  * a FaultEvent recording the delay actually awaited, not the one intended;
  * A TEST THAT FAILS IF THE DELAY IS NOT AWAITED. This is the whole bead. Asserting "an
    event was recorded" would pass against the placebo; the test has to observe ordering
    or elapsed virtual time. Under the lab runtime, two concurrent operations with
    different injected delays completing in delay order is the cheapest real witness.
  * the faultless-plan control stays byte- AND timing-transparent.

CONSUMER: the publication sequencer needs injectable latency (named in fgdb-1xtp's own
"why it matters" list). Until then the four landed classes cover the durability faults
and none of the timing ones.

comments.text: MEASURED 2026-08-05 (SageForge, read-only, pre-claim): the three candidate answers checked against asupersync 3e8d08e. (a) is VIABLE and doctrine-3-shaped: Cx::current() exists (cx/cx.rs:619) and Cx carries a clock (Cx::now, cx/cx.rs:2490) plus timer_driver() access - a FaultVfs holding a construction-time Cx clone gets virtual time under the lab Cx and real time under a live one, with no per-op ambient lookup. title: Merge-algebra suites do not constrain their kernel: any confusable operator pair passes (three families)
description:
START HERE: `label_counts` already contains the discriminator. `merge_is_deliberately_not_idempotent` (crates/fgdb-sketch/src/label_counts.rs) is the relation that separates an additive merge from an absorbing one, and it was written independently before this defect was known. A reader who finds that test does not need to re-derive anything — copy its shape.

THE GUARD, which is the durable part and survives any change in how many families are affected:
**Commutativity and associativity cannot distinguish sum from max, so an algebra suite asserting only those constrains nothing.** Max is itself commutative and associative, so a merge kernel that silently used max instead of addition satisfies both properties and every test built on them. Any mergeable sketch with an additive kernel therefore needs at least one relation that separates the operators:
  * NON-IDEMPOTENCE — merging a value with itself must double it; under max it is a no-op.
  * MASS CONSERVATION over a disjoint split — partitioning a stream and merging must equal accumulating it whole. Assert on canonical bytes, not on a total, or a merge that moves mass between buckets while preserving the sum still passes.
And verify it the only way that counts: MUTATE THE KERNEL TO MAX AND WATCH THE SUITE GO RED, then revert and watch it go green. A suite that has never been observed to fail is not evidence that it constrains anything.

WHAT WAS FOUND AND FIXED. Two families carried a counter-addition kernel where this confusion is expressible, and both are now fixed:
  * `count_min` — was unconstrained; fixed by d7c4ff1 (split/merge equivalence on canonical bytes plus monotone accumulation).
  * `degree_histogram` — was unconstrained; fixed by 1d75e8f (`merge_is_additive_and_not_idempotent`, asserting both relations above). Proven: GREEN at 113 with the real kernel, RED with the kernel mutated to max and exactly that test failing.

WHAT WAS MEASURED, NOT INFERRED — the survey behind the scope, so nobody re-derives it and nobody overstates it. All eight families were probed.
  * Targeted addition/max mutation, applicable only where the kernel is counter-additive: count_min RED (constrained), degree_histogram RED after the fix (was GREEN before), label_counts RED via its existing non-idempotence test, distinct RED under max->overwrite. `distinct`'s kernel IS max and that is correct — proposing otherwise would be a defect, not a fix.
  * `bottom_k`, `exact_quantiles`, `path_correlation` merge COLLECTIONS, not counters — their `checked_add` calls operate on lengths — and `zone_map` merges bounds. The addition/max confusion is not expressible in those kernels, so the targeted mutation does not apply to them.
  * UNIVERSAL BASELINE, run so that the four non-additive families were not merely classified by reading: making `try_merge` a no-op fails 2-4 tests in EVERY one of the eight. So every suite constrains merge at the coarsest level; the gap was specifically at the operator-identity level, and only in additive kernels.

STATUS: no family currently carries this defect. This record exists for the guard, not for outstanding remediation. The action it implies is forward-looking: any NEW mergeable sketch with an additive kernel must ship a discriminating relation and a witnessed red run, not a commutativity/associativity pair.

METHOD NOTE that made this affordable: fgdb-sketch modules depend only on `fgdb_collections::hash_table`, and fgdb-collections has zero dependencies, so it links as a REAL rlib under standalone `rustc --test` — no stubs, hashing stays faithful. That gives the whole eight-family suite in about a second against a ~15 minute remote gate, which is what made mutating eight kernels and re-running everything cheap enough to attempt. One trap worth repeating: DELETE THE PROBE BINARY BETWEEN RUNS. A stale binary once reported a green result for a mutation that had failed to apply, which would have entered this record as a false finding.
close_reason: All three affected families fixed and proven by witnessed red/green: count_min d7c4ff1, degree_histogram 1d75e8f, exact_quantiles 06f29ae. Guard recorded for future additive/confusable kernels.

comments.author: pane4-calibrate
comments.text:
GENERALISATION AND CORRECTED COUNT — the title and scope of this bead are now wider than when I filed it, because I measured further and my original scope was wrong. Three families, not two, and the guard is not about addition versus max specifically.

WHAT I GOT WRONG. I probed every family with ONE mutation — counter addition to max — found it inapplicable to the families whose merge unions collections rather than adding counters, and concluded no further family was affected. That was a scope error, not a measurement error: the right question is not "does the addition/max confusion apply here" but "does this suite constrain ITS OWN kernel", and every kernel class has its own confusable pair. Asking the narrow question and generalising the negative is the mistake.

THE GENERALISED GUARD, which is the durable content of this bead:
**Commutativity, associativity and idempotence cannot distinguish between operators that all satisfy them. An algebra suite asserting only those properties constrains nothing about WHICH operator the kernel implements.**
Confusable pairs observed in this crate, each pair being commutative, associative and idempotent on both sides: sum vs max (counter kernels); min vs max (bounds kernels); keep-k-smallest vs keep-k-largest (selection kernels); ascending vs descending (ordered-merge kernels). A suite built only on the three algebraic properties admits either member of any of these pairs.
THE FIX SHAPE, per kernel: add at least one relation that SEPARATES the pair. Non-idempotence under self-merge separates sum from max. Mass conservation over a disjoint split separates sum from any absorbing operator. An explicit ordering assertion over INTERLEAVED runs separates ascending from descending — non-overlapping runs merge identically under both and cannot discriminate. Assert on canonical bytes rather than on a derived scalar, since two different internal states can agree at the value you sampled.
AND WITNESS IT: mutate the kernel to the confusable operator, watch the suite go RED, revert, watch it go GREEN. A suite never observed to fail is not evidence that it constrains anything. This is the step that found all three.

THE THREE AFFECTED FAMILIES, each fixed and each proven by that RED/GREEN cycle:
  * `count_min` — counter addition confusable with max. Fixed by d7c4ff1 (monotone accumulation plus split/merge equivalence on canonical bytes). Before the fix all thirty tests passed under the mutation.
  * `degree_histogram` — same counter-addition kernel, same confusion. Fixed by 1d75e8f (`merge_is_additive_and_not_idempotent`). Proven GREEN 113 / RED 112+1 with only the new test failing.
  * `exact_quantiles` — ordered-merge kernel confusable with descending. Fixed by the commit carrying this comment (`merge_preserves_sorted_order_and_is_split_exact`). Proven GREEN 114 / RED 113+1. Order is not cosmetic here: `select` and `quantile` index into the values array, so an unsorted merge silently returns the WRONG QUANTILE rather than failing.

FAMILIES PROVEN CONSTRAINED, so nobody re-derives them: `label_counts` via its pre-existing `merge_is_deliberately_not_idempotent` — still the best starting point for anyone writing one of these; `distinct`, whose kernel IS max and correctly so, caught under max-to-overwrite; `zone_map`, caught under min-bound-to-max; `path_correlation`, caught under reversed sample selection; `bottom_k`, caught under keep-k-smallest-to-largest.

TWO INVALID PROBES, recorded so the evidence is not overcounted. I first probed `exact_quantiles` and `path_correlation` with "return early when the other operand is empty". Both passed, and that proves NOTHING — merging an empty operand should be identity, so the mutation is semantically equivalent and passing is correct. A mutation that does not change behaviour is not evidence in either direction. The real `exact_quantiles` defect only surfaced under a mutation that genuinely changes the result. Same discipline as a compile_fail doctest needing a must-compile companion.

STATUS: all three fixed; no family currently unconstrained under a class-appropriate mutation. The forward-looking action is the guard: any NEW mergeable sketch must ship a discriminating relation for its kernel's confusable pair, with a witnessed red run — not a commutativity/associativity/idempotence triple, which is satisfied by the wrong operator too.

title: No durable regression test for the tree-stability tripwire: land the fgdb-49ng red-proof as an enumerated gate
description:
Outstanding item 2 from fgdb-49ng. The tripwire in scripts/lib/gate_verdict.sh (gate_tree_fingerprint / gate_tree_head / gate_check_tree_stable, landed 38cca3f) is proven in all three directions, but the PROOF LIVES IN /data/tmp, NOT IN THE REPO. Until it is a registered gate, the fix is protected only by a transcript: anyone can neuter gate_check_tree_stable and every gate in the repo stays green.

That this is a live hazard is measured, not assumed. The mutation control run twice (38cca3f and again at HEAD 72aec3f) shows that neutering gate_check_tree_stable makes the tree-moves case report PASS rc=0 -- a green verdict over a moving tree -- while cases A and B are unchanged. Nothing else in the repo notices.

WHAT TO LAND. The existing harness is /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane3_49ng_r2_proof.sh (3 cases) and its predecessor pane3_49ng_proof.sh. It drives scripts/g0_negative_evidence_e2e.sh inside an isolated `git clone --local` and asserts:
  A  tree static, gate green           -> PASS  rc=0
  C  real commit lands mid-run         -> UNRUN rc=1, both shas present AND DIFFERENT in the stderr diagnostic
  B  tree static, gate genuinely red   -> FAIL  rc=1, and ZERO UNRUN lines (the third state must not swallow a real failure)
Case B is made red by CONTENT ONLY (an AGENTS.md edit that stops the plannerV2.rs line saying NEVER, tripping law 1 prohibition classification), committed BEFORE the run so the tree is static throughout. Nothing is deleted.
Strongly consider also landing case D (uncommitted tracked edit mid-run -> UNRUN): D is the case that kills a HEAD-only fingerprint design, since HEAD is identical at both ends.

THE REGISTRATION TRAP -- this is the part that is easy to get wrong. A new .sh is claimed by THREE mechanisms in this repo and TWO OF THEM CAN NEVER FIRE: they answer "covered" by GLOB. Only the ENUMERATION-based `script_undeclared` check actually fires. So the gate MUST be enumerated by name in registries/checker_index.toml. Dropping the file into scripts/ and assuming the glob claims it produces a file that no gate has ever opened -- which is the exact failure mode AGENTS.md documents for ubs on non-Rust files.

TOKEN: registries/** is under the CATALOG token, and catalog is a WRITE token -- take it BEFORE editing, not at commit time, or the whole editing window is unprotected.

OTHER CONSTRAINTS:
 * The gate MUST source scripts/lib/gate_verdict.sh and report under the udco contract (PASS/FAIL/RED/UNRUN, verdict on stdout, exit 0 iff zero FAIL and zero UNRUN), or the verdict-contract closure gate in check.sh turns it red.
 * It MUST run in an isolated clone. Committing inside /data/projects/frankengraphdb to prove this would void whatever real check.sh is in flight -- the exact harm fgdb-49ng is about.
 * It must clean up after itself or declare its temp root. The g0 e2e scripts compile with standalone rustc and DO NOT clean up (~70MB per run); /data/projects/frankengraphdb/rc/ is accumulated litter from exactly that. Do not add to it.
 * Budget: the three-case run at HEAD 72aec3f completed in well under a minute against a g0 gate, which costs NO build slot. This is cheap enough for check.sh.

ACCEPTANCE: the gate is enumerated in registries/checker_index.toml, is green on a settled tree, and a mutation of gate_check_tree_stable turns it RED. The last clause is the whole point -- a regression test that stays green when the thing it guards is removed is not a regression test.

title: Extend Local backup to multi-member Aegis with configuration-fenced pins and release
description:
## What & scope
Extend the exact Local backup barrier/pin/copy/reopen/closure/publication/release machinery into a multi-member Aegis consensus group without changing its manifest, inventory, recovery-projection, or independent-reopen semantics. This task owns configuration-fenced distributed barrier acquisition, member source-inventory/payload receipts, joint-configuration coverage, donor/failure-domain recoverability, all-member pin/GC coordination, leader-loss adoption, multi-member publication/release/abort, and the reusable group-level basis consumed by W12's separate Meta-plus-shard global backup.

## Why
Gate G2 needs a complete Local backup and must not wait for multi-member Raft. G3 needs the same guarantee across storage members and joint configuration. Separating the extension prevents reserved Sharded rows from forcing Aegis into G2 while preserving one format and one proof vocabulary: distribution adds certified participants and obligations, never a second backup truth or weaker reopen standard.

## Design — normative detail
A `ConsensusGroupBackupBarrierSpec` binds the Local-format semantic barrier plus exact `ConfigurationState`, stable or joint voter/storage-member sets, `ConfigPayloadFloor`, applied/visible/durable indexes, prepared-root generation, certificate ledger, GC epoch, key-wrap/signing epochs, payload predicate, failure-domain map, and required member set. Ordering it creates one group barrier identity and per-storage-member `MemberBackupPinRequest`; each accepted request roots the exact local physical/logical inventory under that member's current writer fence and configuration and returns a signed `MemberBackupPinReceipt` with inventory digest, durable index, fsync generation, encoding/placement coverage, and failure domain.

The coordinator forms `GroupBackupPinCertificate` only from the exact required stable/joint member predicate and a recoverable union of authenticated receipts. Joint configuration requires the registered old/new quorum and storage predicates; a bare majority or same epoch/member list is invalid. Prepared payload ownership and base closures remain rooted. A leader change adopts the durable operation by backup ID/configuration/fence and cannot issue a second barrier or lose a pin. Reconfiguration cannot retire a required member/configuration/key/payload floor while the group operation is live; consensus GC sees every member pin and terminal operation state as typed roots.

Copy and independent reopen use the existing content inventory, `BackupRecoveryProjection`, manifest, closure, and publication objects. The group certificate adds certified source coverage but does not enter the content inventory as a future/self edge. Publication/receipt/archive grant is one external operation over the sealed group manifest. Ordered release first proves independent archive recoverability and durable archive hold, then imports publication completion, releases every member pin through idempotent typed receipts, advances GC floors, and records one terminal group completion. Abort is legal only before publication send or with exact provider no-effect/terminal evidence; it releases all pins or none logically, with partial physical progress recovered to convergence.

W12 consumes this as the per-group layer. Its Meta intent, exact global prefix P, one certificate per required shard, and Global seal/finalize remain owned by `fgdb-w12-backup-restore-msk`; this task never claims cross-group atomicity.

## Invariants & claims
FG-INV-01 structured ownership/adoption; FG-INV-02 exclusive live generation; FG-INV-07 acyclic construction; FG-INV-09 same-group configuration binding; FG-INV-14 pins remain roots; FG-INV-15/16 exact obligation bijection and no lost/duplicate release; FG-INV-18 derived inventories remain subordinate. Recoverability and failure-domain calculations are bounded/configuration evidence, not universal invariants.

## Interactions
Depends on the Local backup core/publication/release tasks, W11 multi-member Raft, payload availability, membership configuration, fenced GC/physical execution, anti-entropy, W9 key/audit/time authority, and W2 transparency. W11 epic and Gate G3 consume it. W12 backup consumes its group certificate/pin/release interface but supplies separate cross-group sequencing and verification.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Unit tests cover stable/joint required-member calculation, receipt signature/config/fence binding, recoverability union, certificate canonical order, adoption/idempotency, typed-root registration, release/abort state totality, and exact reuse of Local manifest/reopen formats.
- Property/model tests vary member/configuration/failure-domain/receipt sets and prove certificate formation exactly matches the independent quorum+payload predicate oracle.
- Simulation explores leader loss, donor loss, member crash/restart, joint reconfiguration, GC pressure, key/time rotation, external sent-unknown publication, partial physical pin release, and cancellation at every obligation boundary; all runs converge to one terminal state with no unrooted required bytes.
- Negative tests reject mixed configurations, stale fences, duplicate member/failure-domain evidence, incomplete old/new joint coverage, nonrecoverable receipt sets, release-before-hold, GC of live pins, and accidental cross-group/W12 claims.
- E2E runs a three-member Local group under writes, takes a backup across leader change and joint reconfiguration, independently reopens it after simulated donor loss, publishes it through a simulated archive authority, releases pins, and proves current-root GC can retire only then. A second campaign aborts safely at each prepublication boundary.
- Detailed versioned JSONL diagnostics emit backup/group/configuration IDs, barrier positions, required/received member sets, member fence/fsync/inventory public commitments, failure-domain/recoverability calculation, prepared/payload floors, leader/adoption transitions, pin/GC roots, external dispatch/receipt state, per-member release state, checker verdict, artifact refs, seed, and replay command. Logs contain no keys, credentials, plaintext, protected locators, or hidden tenant facts.
- W12 conformance fixture proves this group layer composes under a Meta barrier without claiming or implementing the global layer here.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: making Local backup depend on multi-member Raft, one-leader copy without member receipts, majority-only payload assumptions, release on socket/provider timeout, and a separate distributed manifest. Risk: long backup pins impede reconfiguration/GC; explicit SLOs, admission, abort, and resumable adoption bound the operational cost without weakening safety.

## Provenance
Plan §14/W11 multi-member ownership and GC, §16.6 backup, §19 W11/G3 boundary, Appendix A backup/configuration/payload/GC formats.

title: Owner ruling: safe region-backed collection storage versus std Allocator boundary
description:
## Problem

`fgdb-og31` requires the existing byte-oriented `RegionAlloc` seam to back persistent `Vec` storage in ART, the deterministic hash table, and succinct vectors. The current contract cannot do that honestly: it is handle-based, mutably borrowed, and does not implement `std::alloc::Allocator`. A shadow allocation/accounting layer would leave the real storage on `Global` and is explicitly not an integration.

The direct Rust allocator bridge is mechanically feasible, but `Allocator` necessarily exposes the foreign trait's `unsafe fn deallocate` and returns `NonNull<[u8]>`. The live safe-facing checker intentionally treats foreign-trait impl items as public and rejects every reachable unsafe function (`island_public_unsafe_fn`); its own no-claim note says the raw-pointer check does not cover `NonNull`. The arena charter also says "No public raw pointers and no public unsafe fn." Landing the bridge by exploiting that `NonNull` scanner gap or weakening the assertion merely until it passes would violate the current constitutional boundary.

## Owner ruling required

Choose and freeze one integration architecture:

1. Admit a narrowly specified standard-allocator boundary: update the arena charter and safe-facing checker with an exact allowlist for the `std::alloc::Allocator` contract, explicitly cover `NonNull`, require fail-closed finalization while allocator owners remain, and require a ledger row plus differential/reclamation evidence; or

- The checker can mechanically reject a broader unsafe API than the selected route.
