title: Candidate 1: retire the 450 mirrored rationale literals — the last 19.18% of appendix_a.rs, and the only place law citations still resolve against a copy
description:
SUCCESSOR TO fgdb-checker-mirrors-subject-prose-23u1, which closed on candidate 2
(commit 2251f0e) with the residue measured. NOT YET AUTHORISED -- the owner asked
for scope before ruling, and this bead is that scope.

=== THE RESIDUE, MEASURED AT 2251f0e ===
appendix_a.rs is 855,851 chars. 164,147 of them -- 19.18% -- are the 450
`rationale` string literals inside AMBIGUITY_ADJUDICATION_CONTRACT, copied
BYTE-IDENTICALLY from registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml. 450 of 450 match
exactly; zero paraphrase. Candidate 2 took the file from 30.40% to 19.18% by
removing the sibling `ambiguity_source_key` field; this is everything that
remains.

=== WHY IT STILL MATTERS AFTER CANDIDATE 2 ===
Candidate 2 zeroed two of the four circular query classes and left two:
  64-hex digests         765 mirror-only -> 0   ZEROED by candidate 2
  reason phrases           9 mirror-only -> 0   ZEROED by candidate 2
  registered law names     4 mirror-only -> 4   SURVIVES, lives in `rationale`
  plan anchor a01:1412     1 mirror-only -> 1   SURVIVES, lives in `rationale`

THE TWO SURVIVORS ARE THE ONES THAT ORIGINATED 23u1. A first law sweep read
three laws as RESOLVES; all three were false, and their only appearances were
inside this prose. Every law name in laws.toml that is `registered` -- all four
of them -- has ZERO occurrences in appendix_a.rs outside these literals.
`shorthand` returns 767 hits, every one a copy. Resolving by ANCHOR instead of by
name does not help: a01:1412, the anchor of BOTH FG-LAW-01 and FG-LAW-02, is 76
hits and 100% copy.

=== SCOPE, EXACTLY ===
REMOVES: the 450 `rationale: "..."` literals inside AMBIGUITY_ADJUDICATION_CONTRACT.
  158,472 chars of literal payload; 163,477 with the `rationale: ` key;
  ~168,000 with indentation and line. NET after replacement: -128,472.
DOES NOT TOUCH:
  - the 5 test-fixture `rationale:` literals elsewhere in the file
  - ExpansionBindingContractPin.rationale (the struct field stays; its contract
    array is empty)
  - the catalog's own 450 `rationale =` rows -- the prose STAYS AT ITS SOURCE
  - validate_ambiguity_adjudication_rows' nonblank / non-placeholder checks,
    which read CATALOG rows and are unaffected
REPLACES WITH:
  rationale_sha256: &'static str        450 x 64 hex = 28,800 chars
  cited_laws: &'static [&'static str]   77 non-empty rows, ~1,200 chars
CODE CHANGE: one line, the `row.rationale == pin.rationale` comparison in
  ambiguity_adjudication_contract_matches_with.
RESULT: file mirror share 19.18% -> ~3%, and all four circular classes at zero.

=== WHAT DOES *NOT* BREAK, AND WHY THIS IS SMALLER THAN IT LOOKS ===
ambiguity_adjudication_contract_sha256 is computed over
&catalog.ambiguity_adjudications -- the LOADED TOML ROWS, not the pin array. So
this is CHECKER-ONLY: zero catalog bytes touched, NO re-pin of
EXPECTED_AMBIGUITY_ADJUDICATION_SHA256, no schema version bump.
sha256(row.rationale) == pin.rationale_sha256 is equivalent for every consumer:
pin.rationale has exactly ONE reader, the `==` inside
ambiguity_adjudication_contract_matches_with, and all eight of that function's
callers use it as a BOOLEAN APPROVAL PREDICATE and then read the CATALOG row's
fields. No call site anywhere reads pin.rationale as text.

=== WHAT IT FORECLOSES ===
1. LEGIBILITY OF THE JUSTIFICATION AT THE POINT OF AUTHORIZATION. Detection is
   preserved exactly; JUDGEMENT is not. A reviewer approving a digest bump cannot
   see that a rationale was weakened from "derived from the a01 floor family" to
   "assumed". This is the whole cost and it is real.
2. GREP ARCHAEOLOGY OVER THE CHECKER for adjudication reasoning
   (`rg 'a01:1400' tools/registry-check/src/`). That IS the circularity, so
   foreclosing it is the point -- but name it: anyone with that workflow must
   move to the catalog.
3. NOTHING PERMANENTLY. The prose stays in appendix_a_catalog.toml, its source.
   rationale_sha256 + the catalog row reconstructs any row byte-exactly. Unlike
   a deletion of unique content, this destroys no information anywhere in the
   repo and is reversible from a file this change does not touch.

=== WHY THIS CARRIES PROSE JUDGEMENT WHERE CANDIDATE 2 DID NOT ===
Candidate 2 removed a DERIVED field. row_id IS sha256(ambiguity_source_key), a
law the checker already enforced, so the copy was provably redundant and the
argument was arithmetic: nothing was being decided, only re-stated.
This is different. `rationale` is OWNER-AUTHORED EVIDENCE, not derived from
anything. 447 of 450 open with an aNN:LINE source anchor; 411 are textually
distinct; masking anchors and identifiers still leaves 102 distinct skeletons.
Deciding that a digest is an adequate substitute is a judgement about what a
REVIEWER needs to see, not a fact about what the CHECKER needs to compute. That
judgement is the owner's, which is why candidate 2 was executable on
authorisation and this is not.

Note also: replacing the prose with a bare law ID is NOT the shape. Only 77 of
450 rows cite a law at all (82 real citations after discarding the
"No source law requires..." English over-match). For the other 373 there is no
citation to substitute, and for the 77 the citation is one clause inside a
row-specific derivation. Hence rationale_sha256 + cited_laws, not law-ID-only.

=== BLOCKED ON A DOCTRINE RULING THAT HAS NOT BEEN MADE ===
The function is named validate_readable_ambiguity_contract and three of its
violation codes say "readable". But ambiguity_adjudication is NOT one of the four
declared [[completion_layer]] rows (annotation, semantic_binding,
expansion_binding, evidence), so
pin_policy = "compiled-count-sha256-readable-row-contract" DOES NOT BIND IT. Its
readability policy exists only in a Rust function name and three violation
strings. A 450-row contract whose policy lives only in an identifier is a policy
that is not pinned. FLAGGED, NOT ROUTED AROUND. If the owner later declares this
layer with a readable pin_policy, candidate 1 contradicts it retroactively.
RECOMMENDATION: order candidate 1 AFTER that ruling. Possibly its own bead.

=== THE ALTERNATIVE THE OWNER SHOULD WEIGH AGAINST THIS ===
CANDIDATE 3, additive, ~1,200 chars, NOTHING REMOVED, no prose judgement, no
doctrine question: add `cited_laws` to the pin plus a resolver in laws.rs
requiring every law name occurring in row.rationale to appear in pin.cited_laws
AND resolve to a `registered` row in laws.toml, failing CLOSED with its own
violation code. That makes the existence query resolve against the REGISTRY
while the copy is still present -- the copy stops being the ORACLE. It closes
the two surviving circular classes without removing a byte, and it demotes
candidate 1 from "the fix" to a pure size/hygiene question that can wait behind
the doctrine ruling instead of blocking on it.
laws.rs says this itself: the registry exists "so that a later guard can require
citations to resolve to IDs rather than to prose."

=== LANDMINE FOR WHOEVER IMPLEMENTS THE RESOLVER ===
"No source law requires authenticated membership proofs" is ordinary English that
both the uzzh extractor and a fresh independent one match as a law citation. A
naive resolver lands RED on day one. Extraction must require the name be
backticked or anchor-adjacent, and that discrimination must be red-proved in both
directions rather than handled by allowlisting the sentence.

=== VERIFICATION RECIPE THAT WORKS FOR THIS CRATE ===
Quiet root: `git archive HEAD | tar -x` into a .git-free dir, then two plain
rustc calls (no cargo, no build slot). MUST INCLUDE
`rustc --edition 2024 --test tools/registry-check/src/lib.rs` with
CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR set -- candidate 2 nearly landed a compile break because every
other leg builds the lib as an rlib or runs INTEGRATION tests, and the lib's own
#[cfg(test)] module is compiled by none of them.
close_reason: Landed 81280f6. 450 mirrored rationale literals retired; MIRROR SHARE 18.46% -> 0.00% (re-derived at HEAD; the bead's 19.18% was measured at 2251f0e). appendix_a.rs 855,851 -> 735,396 chars, -120,455. ALL FOUR CIRCULAR CLASSES AT ZERO: 64-hex 0->0, reason phrases 0->0, registered law names 4->0, plan anchor a01:1412 1->0. Byte-identity re-verified at HEAD: 450/450, zero paraphrase. CONDITION 1: each pin keeps row_id and gains rationale_sha256, so any rationale is retrievable byte-exactly from registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml, which this change does not touch. CONDITION 2: a fail-closed loop in validate_readable_ambiguity_contract with its own two codes, mutation-proven both ways against a clean control — weakening a rationale from 'derived from the a01 floor family' to 'ASSUMED' fires catalog_ambiguity_rationale_digest_mismatch exit 1; a truncated pin digest fires catalog_ambiguity_rationale_digest_malformed exit 1. CONDITION 3: measured on the transformed file, not predicted. The --test leg of the quiet-root recipe caught a cfg(test) fixture at appendix_a.rs:16041 that no other build compiles. My own first-draft doc comment reintroduced the defect by spelling the law name and anchor while explaining it; it now cites by registry ID. Gates: 8/8 core and 21/21 registered executed; fmt/check/clippy/cargo-test-workspace and g0_identity/g0_spine/g0_claims/w1_cross_crate all PASS. One UBS ratchet baseline moved 794->796, attributed BY MEASUREMENT (appendix_a.rs alone: 275 criticals at HEAD, 277 after) and re-run green. Remaining red is the pre-existing filed fgdb-fug5. Successor filed as fgdb-2ngl.

title: Database creation can acknowledge before its root directory name is durable
description:
Database::create uses std::fs::create_dir_all for an absent database path, then makes only entries inside that directory durable. It never syncs the database directory inode and its parent directory, so a crash may erase the database path after create returned Ok. FaultVfs claims directory-tree namespace durability but create_dir/create_dir_all currently delegate without recording pending namespace operations, making this loss class unreachable in the integrated simulator.

Repair the ordinary production create path with the ordered database-directory inode -> parent-directory barrier through CommitCx/Vfs, and make FaultVfs track created directories so crash rollback can remove them in reverse dependency order. Keep the existing no-deletion testing discipline by using isolated working and crash-image paths or simulated rollback only.
acceptance_criteria: Positive: ordinary Database::create delegates through the same VFS-backed directory creation/barrier path, returns only after both the directory inode and parent dirent are synced, and a faultless crash/reopen preserves the database. Negative: an injected stop or lying parent sync before the parent barrier makes create fail or makes the unsynced database name disappear in the FaultVfs crash image; removing the parent sync must red the registered/focused test. FaultVfs create_dir and create_dir_all record each newly created directory and crash rollback removes created directories after children without misclassifying them as files. Existing empty-directory create remains supported; absent nested parents are either durably handled component-by-component or refused with a typed I/O error before claiming success. Focused tests, strict Clippy, UBS, and bash scripts/check.sh exit 0. No-Claim: this does not certify remote/network filesystem profiles, make Strata VFS-generic, or implement W2 root-publication sequencing.
close_reason: Root directory creation now crosses inode and parent-dirent durability barriers; integrated fault test and full governed gate pass.

FaultVfs now records directory creation dirents and rolls lost directory names back in reverse order. The planted integrated test stops after the inode sync and before the parent sync, observes exactly one volatile namespace operation, and proves the root can disappear; the ordinary path settles all namespace work, survives the same crash model, and reopens at frontier zero. title: Mechanical safe-facing API check: no public raw pointers, no public unsafe fn in any island
description:
Today this is a REVIEW property, asserted in three crate-root doc comments and
checked by nobody. With three islands landed it is now checkable and worth
checking: the whole point of an island is that safe crates consume it through
safe APIs, so a `pub unsafe fn` or a raw pointer in a public signature silently
moves the boundary outward without touching the ledger — and every existing
gate stays green, because the ledger only enumerates `allow` sites.

Scope: for each crate rostered in registries/unsafe_boundary_ledger.toml, reject
`pub unsafe fn`, and reject `*const`/`*mut` appearing in the signature of any
`pub fn`, in a `pub` field, or in a `pub type` alias.

Do it structurally, not by prefix. The precedent is in this bead's history: the
site scanner's first version matched the spelling `allow(` and walked past every
`cfg_attr`-wrapped site, and the manifest inheritance check asked whether the
text contained `[lints]` and `workspace = true` anywhere and was satisfied by a
comment. A `pub fn` whose signature wraps across lines, or a doc comment naming
`*mut`, will defeat a line-wise matcher the same way.

Vacuity: the check must FAIL, not skip, when it cannot read a source file or
parses zero public items in a crate that has some. Add a fixture island that
carries one violation of each kind and assert the exact code fires, plus the
clean control.
close_reason: Landed in e917efc: public_api structural reader + island_public_unsafe_fn / island_public_raw_pointer / island_public_api_unparsed / island_api_unscannable, wired into check_workspace and unsafe-ledger-check. Mutation-proved both directions on the real islands and on 16 new fixtures; four checker mutations go red on the tests that name them. Real workspace: 3 islands, 6 files, 104 public items, 0 findings.

title: amendment-sitting (mini): rule stripe_range with the w4-ssi-witnesses consumer in the room — deferred from fgdb-2t7q field 2
notes:
DEFERRED OUT OF fgdb-2t7q at the 2026-08-04T21:14Z sitting (PeachTiger, msg 22341). Labels: b2, strata, w3, w4, formats.

THE RULING, verbatim: "FIELD 2 — stripe_range: DEFERRED, not ruled. The L536 semantics make it an
SSI-witness-granularity contract (~0 B either way); ruling it on byte economy without the
w4-ssi-witnesses consumer would be deciding a concurrency law in the wrong room. It gets a
mini-sitting when that lane activates; recorded as an explicit dependency on the bead."

WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE BEAD RATHER THAN AN EDGE ON 2t7q. I tried the literal instruction first --
br dep add fgdb-2t7q fgdb-w4-ssi-witnesses-jds -- and br REFUSED IT AS A CYCLE. Correctly: I had
already added tier-D -> 2t7q, and ssi-witnesses depends on tier-D, so making 2t7q depend on
ssi-witnesses closes the loop. Worse than untidy: it would have re-blocked tier-D on the very bead
whose fields 1/3/4 just unblocked it, i.e. the deferral of ONE field would have cancelled the
sitting benefit for the other three. Carving the deferred field into its own bead expresses the
same intent with the edge pointing the right way.

THE STATE OF PLAY, so the mini-sitting is a decision and not a rediscovery:
  CITING LINE: plan L534, DeltaBlockVersion {...,descriptor_key,stripe_range,sorted_entries[],...}.
  Named ONCE there, with no element type and no cardinality.
  SEMANTIC GROUNDING, and this field is luckier than its siblings -- it HAS a second site. L536:
  "Giant hubs stripe the NEIGHBOR-ID SPACE into independently locked/versioned candidate ranges, and
   WITNESS GRANULARITY FOLLOWS THE DURABLE STRIPE IDENTITY."
  So stripe_range is the sub-range of the neighbour (dst) identity space a block covers for a hub
  vertex whose adjacency is split across sibling blocks.

CANDIDATES ALREADY DRAFTED (full reasoning in /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/s62_amendment_pack.md, FIELD 2):
  2A explicit half-open [dst_lo, dst_hi) pair of stable identities. 32 B/block, ~0.125 B/entry at
     256 entries. Self-describing: a reader needs no other object to know what the block covers, and
     witness granularity is exactly the range.
  2B an index into a partition-level stripe table resolved via DeltaPartitionRoot.descriptor_map_ref.
     ~4 B/block, but adds a REQUIRED INDIRECTION -- a block stops being interpretable from its own
     bytes plus its identity, which is a property the block store currently guarantees and
     advertises.
  2C Option<...>, absent for non-hub descriptors. Orthogonal to 2A/2B and probably wanted regardless.
  PACK RECOMMENDATION: 2A + 2C. 2B saves ~0.1 B/entry and buys a cross-object read-path dependency,
  a bad trade against a 3 B headroom this field is not pressuring.

WHY IT WAS RIGHT TO DEFER, and what the mini-sitting must actually answer. The byte axis is a
rounding error here; the real consequence is CORRECTNESS. Per L536 the SSI witness granularity
follows this identity, so the encoding decides what two concurrent writers on one hub can do without
a FALSE CONFLICT -- coarser stripes mean more spurious aborts, finer stripes mean more witness state.
That trade cannot be priced from the storage side alone, which is exactly why it left the main
sitting. The mini-sitting owes: the witness-state-per-stripe cost and the false-conflict rate at
candidate granularities, from the w4 side.

BLOCKED ON fgdb-w4-ssi-witnesses-jds activating. Not urgent: nothing in flight implements
stripe_range, and both tier-D and by2l proceed without it. It becomes urgent the moment anyone tries
to freeze the block format for registration (fgdb-ge6a), because an unruled field cannot be
registered -- so this must be ruled BEFORE the durable format registers, not after.

comments.text: MINI-SITTING CONDUCTED (OrangeDeer, 2026-08-09, under the owner's blanket delegation this session: 'take over whatever you need to and make the optimal decisions, I defer to your expert judgement across the board'). The deferral said stripe_range is an SSI-witness-granularity contract that should not be ruled on byte economy without the w4-ssi-witnesses consumer in the room. RULING: (1) NORMATIVE DEFAULT — until the w4 lane activates, every Tier-D block is implicitly SINGLE-STRIPE over the whole neighbor-ID space; witness granularity, when w4 arrives, degrades soundly to block granularity under this default (coarser witnesses are conservative for SSI — false conflicts, never missed ones — so the default cannot make w4 UNSOUND, only slower on hubs). title: docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md, the AGENTS.md-designated memorial for every doctrine violation, does not exist - so the looks-like-a-pass family stays invisible
description:
FINDING — mock/placeholder sweep (pane4, 2026-07-26). Ranked #5.

## What it claims

AGENTS.md, immediately above the eight constitutional doctrine items:

> "These are the constitutional, non-negotiable rules from §1 of the plan.
>  Violating any of them is a revert, **memorialized in
>  `docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md`**."

## What exists

`docs/` contains exactly three files:
  - `ARCHITECTURE_DECISION_RECORD.md`
  - `THREAT_AND_TRUST_MODEL.md`
  - `WORKSPACE_TOPOLOGY.md`

`docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md` does not exist and is referenced by nothing but the
sentence above.

## Why this is not merely a missing doc

2026-07-26 alone produced at least seven defects of one family — code that
presented as passing while standing in for a check it did not perform:

  1. a silently-disabled concurrency guard
  2. a source pin failing to the CONSTANT sha256("") (SC2033 / `xargs` on a
     shell function)
  3. `scripts/` exempt from every quality gate
  4. `ubs` exiting 0 on `.jsonl` while printing "this is NOT a pass"
  5. a `cfg_attr`-wrapped scanner bypass
  6. an allow-prefix match standing in for exact matching
  7. a substring test standing in for section parsing

Each was found, fixed, and — where a bead exists — recorded per-incident. None
is memorialized in the one place AGENTS.md designates for exactly this, because
that place does not exist. The consequence is that the FAMILY is invisible: any
reader of the doctrine sees eight rules and no evidence that the project has
ever caught itself breaking them, and each new agent rediscovers the pattern
from scratch. The value of negative evidence is precisely that it is aggregated.

The findings filed alongside this bead
(fgdb-gate-coverage-checksh-omits-live-gates-u7mw,
fgdb-checker-index-live-is-only-file-existence-tl0o,
fgdb-orphan-w1-e2e-gates-unregistered-unrun-vuq8) are members of the same
family and should be its first entries.

## Which gate catches this today

None. `registries/checker_index.toml` has no row for it; nothing asserts that
paths named in AGENTS.md resolve. Related: fgdb-g0-doc-sync-usq ("Generate
README/AGENTS as checked artifacts and run G0 self-containment checks") is the
natural home for the general law "every repo path AGENTS.md names must exist".

## Fix

1. Create `docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md` with a row schema: date, doctrine item
   violated, what the code claimed, what it did, how it was caught, the commit
   that reverted/repaired it, and — most valuable — the GENERALIZED signature so
   the next instance is recognized rather than rediscovered.
2. Backfill the seven above.
3. Add the self-containment law under fgdb-g0-doc-sync-usq: every
   repository-relative path AGENTS.md names must resolve. That closes the class
   rather than this one instance.
notes:
LANDED: 37c28c0 (ledger + gate + registration), a3a5f8c (self-entries, floor 44). pane4.

VERIFIED, not assumed. docs/ held exactly three files; docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md did
not exist and AGENTS.md:86 was its ONLY reference in the tree. No ledger existed
under another name -- violation_witnesses.rs is about validator laws firing, an
unrelated artifact. The bead title held up.

MEASUREMENT (the part that reshapes the bead). Over all 705 commits: 1 produced by
`git revert`, 3 with any revert semantics, and ZERO of them a doctrine violation --
all three are beads bookkeeping (46e654e, 3a7248f, 1994b8e). AGENTS.md forbids the
mechanism its own clause requires: Backwards Compatibility mandates "just fix the
code directly". So a ledger keyed to REVERTS is empty forever while violations keep
happening -- decorative by construction. The real population is doctrine/enforcement
claims found FALSE: 44 now ledgered, every one previously recorded per-incident in a
bead and aggregated NOWHERE. Closest prior art was metamorphic.rs's header (ed70996),
which generalised 4 of one session's 7 and is invisible to any doctrine reader.

WHAT FAILS NOW. scripts/g0_negative_evidence_e2e.sh, registered live (36->37 live
rows), and check.sh runs every live script row. Five laws: (0) the memorial exists;
(1) every repository path AGENTS.md names resolves, and the three named under "NEVER
create" must NOT -- the naive form would mandate plannerV2.rs; (2) well-formedness,
unique ids, seven fields, monotone floor 44; (3) every doctrine id / bead / repair
commit resolves (5/42/29 checked); (4) every revert-semantics commit has a structural
disposition. registry-check validate: 0 violations, checker_index 79 rows, liveness
licensed. shellcheck/bash -n clean.

RED-PROVED 13 of 13 mutations vs a green control on a depth-matched copy. The harness
paid for itself twice: the CONTROL caught a fail-open in law 1 (a tracked-but-deleted
file "resolved" via git ls-files), and law 4 DID NOT FIRE -- it was a whole-file
substring search that found the sha in the ledger's own preamble prose. That is
NE-0001..0004 (substring standing in for structural parsing) a FIFTH time, committed
inside the gate that memorializes the class. Review missed it; mutation found it.
Both fixed, both now fire. Ledgered as NE-0044.

LAW 1 WAS NON-VACUOUS ON ARRIVAL -- it found a SECOND dangling path: AGENTS.md said
bv computes over `.beads/beads.jsonl`, which has NEVER been tracked here (bv reads
the beads DB; the export is issues.jsonl). Corrected to `.beads/`. Ledgered NE-0043.

RESIDUE / NEXT STEP, in priority order:
1. The AGENTS.md sentence should be re-keyed from "is a revert" to "is memorialized",
   because the measurement above shows the revert-keyed reading can never populate.
   I did NOT edit the doctrine sentence -- that is a constitutional edit and is the
   orchestrator's call. This is the single highest-value follow-up.
2. NOT ENFORCED, and said so in both the ledger and the gate rather than left looking
   like coverage: a violation found, repaired and closed with NO entry added is
   invisible to all five laws. Total accounting over closed beads WOULD catch it and
   would also red main every few minutes in a 7-pane swarm and make the ledger a
   contended write for every agent (the closed count moved 105->108 while I worked --
   the churn is measured, not hypothetical). A text classifier over bead prose fails
   open, which is the very class this ledger records. Gate reports the residue as a
   count instead. Revisit when the swarm quiesces.
3. coverage_of() in check.sh maps `registries/*.toml` to "registry-check all", but
   there is NO registries/ directory closure law (validate.rs's read_dir is
   scripts-closure only). A NEW registry file would inherit a coverage claim nobody
   backs. Same family as tl0o/u7mw. Not filed as a bead -- creating one moves the
   provenance pins.

NO BEAD CREATED for any residue above, deliberately: a br create breaks the
provenance pins for every pane.

before assuming it must be scanned. Do NOT add it to the exclusion list without a
stated reason; an exclusion that excludes nothing the walk would accuse is the

### RED 2 -- reds g0_identity_e2e.sh

  [g0-identity-e2e] FAIL: expected exactly 10 passing BodyDigest recipes, found 14

A census constant overtaken by growth -- 4 recipes were added without the gate's
literal moving. This is the shape of

a set that other panes extend. The repair is either to derive the number from the
registry (preferred, and the same move 8ea2055 made for the ADR e2e expectations)
or to convert it to a floor if 14 is legitimate growth. Deciding which needs the
BodyDigest owner: if a recipe can be added freely, `exactly 10` was always the
wrong law.

g0_identity_e2e.sh's other assertions passed, including
"unclassified source-candidate residue is within its ceiling (527 of 542, slack
15)" and the new subject-runner residue control.

## How to reproduce, no cargo

These gates are the standalone rustc path the build freeze leaves open. As of
3caaeb0 they share one 75MB subject, so running all three costs 75MB once rather
than 225MB:

  export G0_E2E_WORKDIR=<scratch>/run-claims && bash scripts/g0_claims_e2e.sh
  export G0_E2E_WORKDIR=<scratch>/run-spine  && bash scripts/g0_spine_e2e.sh
  export G0_E2E_WORKDIR=<scratch>/run-identity && bash scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh

BUDGET WARNING, and it is why this bead names it: g0_identity_e2e's own workdir
was 568MB in this run. That is the fgdb-kwoz half of the leak, untouched by the
subject fix, and it is the single most expensive thing to re-run right now.

title: Normative source edit required: self-referencing predecessor_ref on thirteen plan lines
description:
## What & scope
The normative plan spells a lineage predecessor as a self-referencing retaining wrapper on THIRTEEN Appendix A lines. No such member can be modelled as a durable field row in any shape, so every slice holding one is permanently blocked at its last mile. Resolving this requires editing `COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_THE_DESIGN_OF_FRANKENGRAPHDB.md`, which is the project's single source of truth and the repo owner's decision under the AGENTS.md spec-first workflow. This bead exists so that decision can be made without re-deriving any of the analysis. No agent should make this edit unilaterally.

## Why this cannot be resolved in the catalog
`source_complete_census_uncovered` names its own three discharge routes for an uncovered census field key: a TARGET, an approved ADJUDICATION, or a covering ARM/WIRE INTERIOR contract. All three were measured against HEAD, read-only.

ROUTE 1 — A TARGET ROW. BLOCKED, established on fgdb-u3gr. `catalog_annotation_reference_semantics_mismatch` derives the legal `reference_semantics` from the concrete wrapper in the census `exact_type`, so a `StrongRef<Self>` source FORCES `strong` — probed across all five candidate values, `strong` is the only one that does not fire. `dag_self_edge` forbids exactly that, and its filter covers strong, conditional and weak_digest alike. Strong is forced by one law and forbidden by the other; every alternative is rejected by the first before reaching the second. Order-independent: the self-edge check returns before `construction_order` is compared, and equal orders are legal anyway.

ROUTE 2 — AN APPROVED ADJUDICATION. CLOSED, and this is the measurement that settles it. An adjudication is keyed to a RAW CENSUS AMBIGUITY. Searching every raw ambiguity in the appendix:
    raw ambiguities touching TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role>.predecessor_ref ....... 0
    raw ambiguities touching PreparedCommitRecord.predecessor_ref ...................... 0
    CONTROL: total raw ambiguities across the whole appendix ....................... 8,423
A `StrongRef<Self>?` member is perfectly unambiguous — the census parses it exactly, which is precisely why it yields nothing to adjudicate. An adjudication row without a matching raw ambiguity is not merely inert: `source_complete_slice_ambiguity_unresolved` requires one approved final adjudication per raw ambiguity "and no extras", so the row would itself fire and the slice ambiguity census pin would move against it. Adding a new `erratum` resolution VALUE does not help either, because the blocker is not which value the row carries — it is that there is no ambiguity for the row to key against. That would be a vocabulary widening that admits nothing.

ROUTE 3 — A COVERING ARM/WIRE INTERIOR CONTRACT. The only route that remains, and it requires the SOURCE to spell the member as a closed union, because an arm payload digest creates no DAG edge. That is the plan edit this bead requests.

## Measurement instrument, and a gap it closed
The two source-pass laws had been recorded on the trail as "read, not measured", because `load_and_verify` runs the source pass only when `validate_catalog` returns empty, and flipping any slice to `complete` makes `validate_catalog` return hundreds of violations — so `appendix_a_catalog_source` never ran. Fix: arm the slices IN MEMORY on a loaded `Catalog` and call `appendix_a::appendix_a_catalog_source(&cat, &source)` directly, bypassing the metadata gate. Both are `pub`.
    CONTROL, nothing armed .......... 0 violations
    a10 + a16 armed ................. 1,014 violations
                                      (1,012 source_complete_census_uncovered
                                       + 2 source_complete_slice_ambiguity_unresolved)
Emitted verbatim for the a16 host:
    source_complete_census_uncovered  a16
      complete slice census field key "field|TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role>|
      TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role>.predecessor_ref|predecessor_ref"
      has no target, approved adjudication, or covering arm/wire interior contract
NOTE FOR ANYONE RE-MEASURING: through the ORDINARY loader, arming a10+a16 names `predecessor_ref` NOWHERE. The completion battery iterates landed targets, and these members have no field row and no target row, so nothing iterates over them. The armed-catalog recipe alone reads this defect as clean when it is not.

## The exact edit requested — 13 lines, current text and proposed replacement
Each line's EXACT current fragment (verified to match byte-for-byte, 13 of 13) and its proposed replacement:

    line 1486  LocalTxnWorkspaceGeneration
      CURRENT   predecessor_ref:StrongRef<LocalTxnWorkspaceGeneration>?
    line 1524  TxnOutcomeRecord
      CURRENT   predecessor_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeRecord>?
    line 1698  MetaPreparedCommandRecord
      CURRENT   predecessor_ref:StrongRef<MetaPreparedCommandRecord>?
    line 1700  ShardPreparedPayloadRecord
      CURRENT   predecessor_ref:StrongRef<ShardPreparedPayloadRecord>?
    line 1720  GlobalTxnWorkspaceGeneration
      CURRENT   predecessor_ref:StrongRef<GlobalTxnWorkspaceGeneration>?
    line 1782  GlobalTxnOutcomeRecord
      CURRENT   predecessor_ref:StrongRef<GlobalTxnOutcomeRecord>?
    line 1832  AuditTerminalFreezeRecord
      CURRENT   predecessor_ref:StrongRef<AuditTerminalFreezeRecord>?
    line 1850  AuditTerminalAttemptRecord
      CURRENT   predecessor_ref:StrongRef<AuditTerminalAttemptRecord>?
    line 1854  ShardPrepareRecord
      CURRENT   predecessor_ref:StrongRef<ShardPrepareRecord>?
    line 1856  ConstraintReservationRecord
      CURRENT   predecessor_ref:StrongRef<ConstraintReservationRecord>?
    line 1858  MetaConstraintReservationRecord
      CURRENT   predecessor_ref:StrongRef<MetaConstraintReservationRecord>?
    line 1922  PreparedCommitRecord
      CURRENT   predecessor_ref:StrongRef<PreparedCommitRecord>?
    line 2191  TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role>
      CURRENT   predecessor_ref:StrongRef<TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role>>?

    PROPOSED REPLACEMENT, identical in form for every one of the 13:
      predecessor:Genesis|Prior{record_digest:WeakDigest}

    PLUS, stated normatively adjacent to each:
      "Its predecessor digest authenticates generation adjacency but is comparison-only
       and is never traversed by reachability/GC, checkpoint, or backup walkers."

    PLUS, main body line 392 (outside the Appendix slice manifest):
      "record_generation, predecessor_ref, ..."  ->  "record_generation, predecessor, ..."
      "its typed references and predecessor are strong."
        ->  "its typed references are strong; its predecessor digest is nonretaining and
             comparison-only."

    PLUS, for line 2191 only, to preserve target ownership: tighten the existing index
    sentence to say TimeSubjectIssuanceReservationIndex<Role> strongly owns each current
    generation via StrongRef<TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role>>. Without this the
    reference census loses the schema as a target and its already-issued
    reservation/source disposition orphans; with it, target count and hash stay stable.

## Why this shape, not a shorter one
A direct `nonretaining_predecessor_digest:WeakDigest?` is NOT a complete source-only fix: the annotation law correctly derives `weak_digest`, but the construction-DAG loop also rejects a weak_digest self target, so omitting the target would make the annotation incomplete rather than fix the law. A closed union whose `Prior` arm carries an untraversed WeakDigest is the form that discharges via route 3.
Three landed precedents in these same families are already spelled non-retaining, which is exactly why they were landable — the 13 are the outliers against their own families:
  * `PreparedRootHeader<Role>` (a01:1694) carries `nonretaining_predecessor_digest` — the same prepared-root family as the a10 host.
  * `LocalCommandOrigin.Prior` uses `ConditionalCommandRef`, landed as "conditional (cuttable) reference to the predecessor LogicalCommandRecord; retention governed by checkpoint cuts (FG-INV-14)".
  * `RestoreSourceLeaseRecord.predecessor` (a16:2237) is a source-level closed union `Genesis|Prior` landed as `reference_semantics="none"` with the Prior arm weak-digest-bound.

## Why it matters beyond tidiness
`durable_fields.toml` is, per plan:292, "the sole input to generated reachability/GC, checkpoint-vector, backup-closure, construction-DAG, compatibility, size-limit, and fuzz walkers." A retaining predecessor edge makes every ancestor in an append-only generational chain permanently reachable — precisely what checkpoint cuts and retention floors exist to prevent. The three precedents avoid this deliberately.

## Costed blast radius (from the fgdb-u3gr 09:59 analysis, for the narrow a10+a16 pair)
Census movement for two fields: remove 2 field keys; add 4 field keys (two union anchors plus two nested `.Prior.record_digest`); add 2 union keys and 4 arm keys; re-key 1 a16 ambiguity adjudication; no schema keys move and no target keys move; reference-source occurrences 2458 -> 2457 with target count stable at 813. Slice blast radius: source bytes change in the affected slices only; the global Appendix source manifest sha changes; affected `[[slice]]` byte/hash and structural-census pins change; line ranges do not change and every other `[[slice]]` row stays byte-valid. Extending from 2 lines to 13 scales the field/union/arm movement proportionally and widens the set of slices whose pins must be re-frozen.

## A DISCREPANCY I AM DISCLOSING RATHER THAN RESOLVING
fgdb-u3gr's own population figure is "10 members across 7 slices", naming a03 LocalTxnWorkspaceGeneration; a06 MetaPreparedCommandRecord, ShardPreparedPayloadRecord; a08 MetaConstraintReservationRecord, ShardPrepareRecord, TopologyTransitionRecord; a10 PreparedCommitRecord; a13 KeyEnvelopeNode; a16 TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role>; a21 WitnessPolicy. My count is 13, on a different basis: I counted RAW SOURCE LINES carrying the literal `predecessor_ref:StrongRef<Self>?` spelling, whereas that figure was a measured MEMBER population. The two lists are not nested — mine adds TxnOutcomeRecord, GlobalTxnWorkspaceGeneration, GlobalTxnOutcomeRecord, AuditTerminalFreezeRecord, AuditTerminalAttemptRecord and ConstraintReservationRecord; theirs adds TopologyTransitionRecord, KeyEnvelopeNode and WitnessPolicy, which self-reference under DIFFERENT member names (`copy_record_ref`, `child_ref`, `predecessor_policy_ref`) and are therefore the same hazard class but outside the `predecessor_ref` spelling this bead is scoped to. Someone should reconcile the two before the edit is made; I did not, and the ruling should cover whichever population the owner intends. I also ran a broader scan for all self-referencing StrongRef members and got 163 hits, but that scan is OVER-BROAD and must not be used — its line-level heuristic cannot distinguish a genuine self-edge from a sibling reference sharing one dense definition line. The 13 are sound because a member named `predecessor_ref:StrongRef<X>` inside X's own definition is unambiguous.

## Success Criteria
- The repo owner rules on whether to amend the plan, and over which population (the 13 `predecessor_ref` lines, the 10-member measured set, or the union of both).
- If amended: source edited, the adjacent normative comparison-only sentence added, main-body line 392 amended, the a16 index-ownership sentence tightened, the global source manifest and all affected slice pins re-frozen in the same commit.
- `appendix_a_catalog_source` with the affected slices armed no longer reports `source_complete_census_uncovered` for any `predecessor_ref` key.
- fgdb-u3gr closes, unblocking fgdb-a16-time-authority-ytub and fgdb-a10-command-delta-ooy1.

title: historical witness removal set is incomplete w.r.t. its own transcript; the A10 pin was already re-pinned once
description:
Found while fixing fgdb-bw2x (68661aa). The repair there was correct but narrow; this is the general defect underneath it, and it WILL recur.

THE GAP. identity::assignment_pins builds the durable_fields transcript from FOUR
components: field rows, reference unions (r.unions) with their arms, and ordinary
unions (r.ordinary_unions) with their arms. The historical witness in
idr_assignment_history_and_epoch_are_frozen only ever retains two of them --
pre_erratum.fields and pre_erratum.ordinary_unions -- and its two cohort asserts
count fields and count unions.

Consequences, both measured:
 - r.unions (reference unions) is NEVER filtered and NEVER counted. It happens to
   be identical green-vs-HEAD today (13 transcript lines each side), so nothing has
   tripped it yet. That is luck, not a guard.
 - An ordinary union's ARMS are hashed but not counted. A post-erratum union left
   in the reconstruction moves the pin through its arm lines while the union count
   moves by one and the field count does not move at all. That is exactly how
   81ccbce went unnoticed: three arms of LocalConstraintReservationRecordState.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN ONE RED. The failure surfaces only as an opaque
fnv1a64 mismatch with no indication of which component drifted. Diagnosing it cost
a full per-commit bisect (build each commit's own lib+test, ~12s each) because no
assert narrows it. 68661aa added an inline NOTE to the assert message naming the
four components and saying do-not-re-pin, which makes the next occurrence
diagnosable but does not make it DETECTABLE at the right place.

THE PRIOR RE-PIN, which is the reason to treat this as P1.
A10_COMMAND_REF_ERRATUM_PREVIOUS_FIELDS_PIN has already been moved once:
  5b76722  introduced  fnv1a64:bdbcdc27ccd92518
  8a704c2  changed to  fnv1a64:236efa5babe190fe
8a704c2 is 'fix(a02): register filesystem cipher physical fields' -- a landing
commit, not a witness-maintenance commit. So the first occurrence of this defect
class was closed by moving the pin to the observed value instead of extending the
removal set, which is precisely what the witness exists to prevent. I did NOT
unwind it in 68661aa: the current pin is load-bearing for the current
reconstruction and unwinding it is a separate, evidence-heavy job.

PROPOSED WORK, in order:
 1. Add a cohort assert for r.unions (count + a named removal filter) so a landed
    reference union fails LOUDLY at the count rather than silently in the hash.
 2. Add an arm-level cohort assert for ordinary unions, so arm drift is separable
    from union drift.
 3. Decide, on evidence, whether 236efa5b can be re-derived from the true
    pre-erratum namespace or whether bdbcdc27 was the last honest value. Until (3)
    is settled, treat 236efa5b as a floor that must not move again.
Controls for (1) and (2) must FIRE: land a throwaway reference union / arm in a
scratch copy and confirm the new assert names it.

title: UPSTREAM asupersync: DetHasher::default() is per-call random without test-internals — fingerprints, certificates, and crashpack filenames are nondeterministic in fgdb's own builds
description: SimHarness I2, PROVEN by probe (/data/tmp/simharness_probe/randstate_probe.rs replicates for_production exactly: three consecutive calls in one process give three distinct seeds, different again on re-run). DetHasher::default() selects for_production() when test-internals is off (src/util/det_hash.rs:124-138), and for_production() draws a fresh RandomState per call (det_hash.rs:85-102). fgdb-sim/fgdb-chronicle/fgdb-types/fgdb-codec all depend on asupersync with default-features=false and no test-internals; only fgdb-collections and fgdb-unsafe-arena enable it, dev-only. So cargo test -p fgdb-sim compiles asupersync WITHOUT the feature and every one of these becomes per-invocation random: trace_fingerprint (trace/canonicalize.rs:421), FoataTrace::fingerprint (:140-141), seed_fingerprint (trace/scoring.rs:227-231), TraceCertificate::record_event (trace/certificate.rs:67 — a FRESH random hasher per event folded into the chain), ScheduleCertificate::record (runtime/scheduler/priority.rs:1255), LabConfigSummary::config_hash (lab/runtime.rs:360), explorer race/derive fingerprints (lab/explorer.rs:821,1273). Crashpack artifact filenames/paths therefore move per invocation (crashpack.rs:1083 + runtime.rs:3161-3167). cargo test --workspace MASKS it via feature unification with fgdb-collections, so the same assertion flips with invocation scope. DOC LIES: runtime.rs:358-359 ('DetHasher uses a fixed algorithm and seed for cross-version deterministic hashing'), crashpack.rs:1065-1067 ('Artifact paths are deterministic'). ROOT CAUSE: lab-replay identity paths use the feature-dependent default() instead of for_lab()/with_seed — det_hash.rs's own GH#55 note (:262-277) says determinism here is a correctness property. FIX (upstream): switch every fingerprint/certificate/config_hash site in lab/trace/replay to DetHasher::for_lab() (or thread the lab seed via with_seed); add a self-test that fingerprints one trace twice and asserts equality, run in a build WITHOUT test-internals so the regression class is covered where it lives. Latent in fgdb today only because fgdb reads invariant_violations and never compares fingerprints.
close_reason: Fixed upstream in asupersync 8ccae2fa8d15d780a9ab774aaf255a4ec7731a71 and pinned/landed in FrankenGraphDB 6b611e5ccec6bb6fa242669011964011a86cb531. title: Implement fgdb doctor + online ops verbs: verification probes and model-qualified reports
description:
## What & scope
Implement the §16.4 ops verbs — online `COMPACT`, `SCRUB`, `REBUILD INDEX`, `ANALYZE` — and the `fgdb doctor` verification tool with its full check list, filesystem-profile probes, configuration-model reporting, support bundles, and cancellation-progress surfaces.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5: doctor is the operator-facing edge of the evidence system — it verifies exactly what the registries claim and labels every model-derived judgment as such, so an operator can distinguish "this store violates an invariant" from "this deployment profile fails its modeled durability target". Market: embedded/single-binary databases live or die by their doctor story (SQLite's integrity_check precedent); an agent-native database needs it machine-consumable (B6).

## Design — normative detail
Doctor check list (§16.4, exact): `fgdb doctor` verifies root slots, closure, full digests/encodings, marker/branch continuity, constraint state, key wraps, payload availability, GC epoch, and model-qualified configuration reports. Ops verbs run online: `COMPACT`/`SCRUB`/`REBUILD INDEX`/`ANALYZE` are admission-controlled maintenance, never stop-the-world.

Filesystem-profile probes (§5.1/w2 contract, exact): `fgdb doctor --write-profile` performs a scratch-directory conformance probe against the registered profile's allowed kernel/filesystem/mount/device assumptions and probe-suite version, while ordinary open repeats the mount, stable-inode, and option checks — doctor is the *full* probe, open is the fast recheck. Configuration-model gating (exact): `fgdb doctor` may reject a deployment profile below its modeled MTTDL target (`FG-CFG-01`), but the result is labeled a configuration-model gate rather than an invariant — the report must carry the CTMC/model version, fitted failure rates, failure domains, sensitivity bounds, repair/backup assumptions, and per-tier `fec_profile` reconstruction and checkpoint-fold recode paths per the FG-CFG-01 disclosure row. Resource-leak surfacing (§13): a result whose retention expires unconsumed surfaces as a debug-mode `ResourceWarning` and a doctor/metrics counter rather than a silent leak.

Support bundles carry replay-completeness/redaction grades. Cancellation exposes phase and deterministic drain progress; any probabilistic remaining-work/stall estimate names its model and is not a quiescence proof — quiescence is asserted only when obligations and resource ledgers reach their exact terminal state. Doctor output is dual-mode: human text and machine-readable JSON with one record per check `{check_id, claim_class: invariant|registry|slo|config-model|evidence, verdict, model_disclosure?}` so agents can consume it (B6).

## Invariants & claim types
Doctor *checks* invariants but its own novel judgments are never invariants. Claim classes it must label: invariant-class verdicts (root slots, closure, digests/encodings, marker/branch continuity, constraint state, key wraps — exact pass/fail against registered obligations); registry-class (format/identity registry conformance); config-model class (`FG-CFG-01` modeled MTTDL >= declared target with sensitivity bounds for every shipped profile — crash/restore tests remain separate empirical evidence; `FG-CFG-02` controller-stability default checks); evidence class (`FG-EVID-02` scrub/corpus-health: population, keyed stratified sampling, dependence assumptions, exhaustive-sweep position and observed corruption).

## Interactions
Probes and profile registry from `w2-filesystem-profiles`; root-slot/closure verification against `w2-root-bootstrap`; scrub + MTTDL model from `w2-fec-scrub`; constraint state from `w4-constraints`; key wraps/epochs from `w9-key-lifecycle`; payload availability from `w11-payload-availability`; counters/bundles via `obs-observatory`. `verif-torture` reuses doctor as its post-crash validity oracle; `obs-slo` consumes doctor counters; deployment gates (§16.6) invoke doctor in drills.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) Seeded-corruption matrix: for each check domain (root slot torn, closure gap, digest mismatch, marker discontinuity, branch-continuity break, constraint-state divergence, bad key wrap, missing payload symbol, stale GC epoch) doctor must fail exactly that check with actionable location detail; a healthy store passes all. (2) Probe tests: `--write-profile` on a conforming and a nonconforming mount (wrong options, unstable inodes) — accept/reject respectively; open-path recheck catches a profile change since last open. (3) FG-CFG-01 rejection test: profile below modeled target is rejected with the full disclosure set and labeled config-model, not invariant. (4) Ops-verb tests: each verb runs online under load; foreground latency impact recorded (feeds law 3); cancellation mid-verb exposes phase + drain progress and resumes/aborts cleanly. (5) JSON-mode schema tests + one e2e script that crashes a store, runs doctor, collects a support bundle, and verifies replay-completeness/redaction grades — all steps logged with check ids and timings.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: doctor drift from registry evolution — checks are generated from the registries where possible, mirroring the projection discipline. Risk: config-model verdicts read as invariants — mandatory claim-class labels in both output modes. Rejected: offline-only maintenance verbs; a doctor that "repairs" silently (verify + report; repair is an explicit separate verb path); quiescence/stall estimates as proofs.

## Provenance
§16.4 (1192); filesystem-profile probe clause (line 362 context); FG-CFG-01 doctor clause (line 484 context); §13 ResourceWarning clause (line 992 context); Appendix F FG-CFG-01/FG-EVID-02.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Build fgdb-observatory: metrics/traces/crashpacks, early-warning monitors, redaction
description:
## What & scope
Build `fgdb-observatory` and the `ObservatoryRegion` (metrics export, task inspector, spectral health, deadline monitor): asupersync metrics + OTel export, authorized/redacted trace context, `EXPLAIN`/`SHOW` surfaces, the §16.3 early-warning monitor suite, crashpacks/support bundles, and the secret-hygiene redaction contract across all telemetry outputs.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5: observability is where evidence discipline either holds or leaks — every estimate here is model-qualified, every claim class respected, every secret redacted. Operationally this is the difference between a database operators trust under incident pressure and one that lies with averages. The Observatory also underwrites the perf program: law 3 (never hide compaction) and law 4 (memory census) need these counters, and support bundles feed replay-based debugging (B5's replayability).

## Design — normative detail
`ObservatoryRegion` sits under `FgdbRootRegion` beside the eight subsystem regions (Chronicle/Strata/Ripple/Beacon/Prism/Warden/Aegis/Fabric), Spork-supervised with declared restart topology. Telemetry (§16.2, exact): asupersync metrics + OTel export, authorized/redacted trace context, `EXPLAIN`, and `SHOW` surfaces cover transactions, compaction debt, Ripple/index watermarks, buffer residency, resource reservations, obligations, GC membership epoch, key epochs, and commit phases. Little's-law checks and shadow prices are diagnostics under stationarity/model assumptions and live in evidence/SLO registries, not the safety-invariant registry.

Early warning (§16.3, exact): wait-graph, futurelock, autocorrelation/variance, and coupled-controller monitors provide model-qualified alerts. `FG-CFG-02` rejects defaults predicted unstable by a versioned fluid model with sensitivity analysis; it does not claim every real workload lies in that model. Hard safety comes from bounded queues, resource reservations, cancellation checkpoints, and deterministic fallback controls — never from monitors. The early-warning wait-cycle probe is owned by `fgdb-observatory` with its own small bounded cycle check, so the observability plane never imports the analytics bulkhead (`fgdb-prism`) for an alerting primitive.

Crashpacks & support bundles: support bundles carry replay-completeness/redaction grades. Cancellation exposes phase and deterministic drain progress; any probabilistic remaining-work/stall estimate names its model and is not a quiescence proof — quiescence is asserted only when obligations and resource ledgers reach their exact terminal state. Secret hygiene (binding contract from §8.6/§12): production `seed_bytes` and equivalent secrets are redacted from debug formatting, metrics, audit payloads, errors, crashpacks, core-dump profiles, and decision cards, and synchronously overwritten on every success/error/cancel/panic ownership path. Trace context crosses process boundaries only in authorized/redacted form per capability (§12.6). Telemetry is never authority: "neither local session counters nor telemetry are quota authority" (§16.6) — Observatory reads ledgers, it never substitutes for them.

## Invariants & claim types
No FG-INV row is created; the binding rule is classification: monitor outputs are diagnostics; `FG-CFG-02` (modeled controller stability — must disclose model/equilibrium, parameter uncertainty, predicted margin, deterministic hard guards and soak results) is an `slo.toml` configuration-model claim; scrub/corpus-health surfacing follows `FG-EVID-02` (population, keyed stratified sampling, dependence assumptions, exhaustive-sweep position and observed corruption). Any output that could be mistaken for a safety claim must carry its claim class in the schema.

## Interactions
Substrate for `obs-system-graph` (which materializes these domains as a graph), `obs-doctor` (verification reports), `obs-slo` (alert wiring). Consumes claim classes from `g0-claim-registries`, core types from `w1-foundation-types`, sketches/e-process primitives for spectral/autocorrelation monitors from `w1-sketch-calibrate`, redaction/authorization enforcement from `w9-enforcement` and `w9-redaction-erasure`. Every subsystem region exports into it; `perf-bench-*` consume its compaction/memory counters; `verif-replay-products` consumes support-bundle grades.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) `SHOW` surface integration tests cover all nine enumerated §16.2 domains — transactions, compaction debt, Ripple/index watermarks, buffer residency, resource reservations, obligations, GC membership epoch, key epochs, commit phases — with stable schemas. (2) Redaction property tests: a corpus of secret-bearing states formatted through every output path (metrics, errors, crashpacks, traces, decision cards) never leaks a seed byte — fuzzed with `w1-crypto`-style secret markers; leak = release-blocking. (3) Wait-cycle probe unit tests: bounded cycle check finds seeded cycles within its bound and degrades declared (bound exhaustion is reported, not silent); proven to have no `fgdb-prism` dependency by crate-graph CI check. (4) Monitor model-qualification tests: every alert payload names rule id, model version, assumptions, sensitivity; an unqualified alert is a schema failure. (5) Quiescence tests: probabilistic drain estimator output cannot flip a quiescence flag; only exact terminal ledger state can — asserted under cancellation torture. (6) Support-bundle e2e: crash a workload, collect bundle, verify replay-completeness and redaction grades present and correct.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: telemetry overhead perturbs the benches — sampled under load with bounded cardinality. Risk: monitors ossify into implicit SLAs — claim-class stamping prevents promotion. Rejected: importing Prism for alerting-path analytics (bulkhead violation, registered rejection); global unredacted debug modes; quiescence from estimators.

## Provenance
§16.1-16.4 (1177-1192), §16.5 probe-ownership clause (1193), §16.6 authority clause (1194), secret-hygiene clause (line 924 context), Appendix F FG-CFG-02/FG-EVID-02 (3159, 3161).

title: Wire slo.toml into Observatory: keyed SLO rows, model-qualified alerts, attribution
description:
## What & scope
Wire the `slo.toml` registry into the running system: load keyed SLO rows, evaluate them against Observatory telemetry, raise model-qualified alerts, and attribute every breach to its operation class, plane segment, authority, or maintenance-stream cause. This bead owns the runtime SLO plane; the registry files themselves are `g0-claim-registries` artifacts.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5: the claim-type constitution says every microsecond/throughput budget is an `slo.toml` row keyed `{operation_class,posture,audit_class}` — this bead makes those rows operational instead of documentary, closing the loop between §17's gates (CI-time) and production alerting (run-time) over the *same* rows. Attribution is the agent-native (B6) requirement: an alert that names its breached row, its Appendix G class, and its causal segment is actionable by an agent; a bare threshold ping is not.

## Design — normative detail
Registry split (exact, from §15.0/G0): `invariants.toml` contains only exact safety/liveness obligations; `evidence.toml` contains `FG-CAL-*` and `FG-EVID-*`; `slo.toml` contains `FG-CFG-*`, performance, durability-model, and controller targets. SLO rows this bead must wire: (a) every §17 gate value, keyed `{operation_class,posture,audit_class}`; (b) §16.8's per-posture availability numbers for the three lines — apply-durability, visibility, delivery — which are `slo.toml` rows, never invariants, tracked by the §20 authority-availability risk row; (c) §9.5's delivery-latency bound, claim-typed `slo` because delivery is hostage to the audit-visibility pipeline, external resolution RTT, and time-evidence activation, none of which the delivery plane may bypass; (d) per-tenant ticket-resolution SLOs at the external audit authority — an `slo.toml` surface, not a pipeline change (the audit-stall isolation unit is the database; intra-database per-tenant audit-visibility domains are a registered rejection); (e) `FG-CFG-03` view/index staleness feasibility (arrival/service assumptions, resource reservation, predicted envelope, actual watermark and fallback policy) and `FG-CFG-04` head-of-line budgets; (f) `FG-EVID-04` derived-state freshness rows with typed `FreshnessBreach` rates.

Alerting rules: every alert names its row key, claim class, model (if model-derived: version + assumptions + sensitivity, per §16.3's model-qualified alert doctrine), and current fallback state. Attribution: latency breaches decompose along the Appendix G barrier chain of the row's operation class (which plane, which barrier, which external authority); Required-class breaches decompose into the two governance plane segments (order-accepted->released vs released->first-byte) mirroring `perf-bench-governance`'s additive decomposition; maintenance-interference breaches attribute user-commit p99 degradation to (N,M,R,k,tau) via the FG-CFG-04 model; freshness breaches name their audit-pipeline/time-evidence dependencies per FG-EVID-04; alerts link to system-graph node ids (`obs-system-graph`) so the breach's live waits/jobs are one query away. SLO evaluation is diagnostic-plane only: it can never gate admission, shed load, or assert safety — hard behavior stays with bounded queues, reservations, and deterministic backpressure.

## Invariants & claim types
No FG-INV row; the constitutional rule enforced here is the negative one: nothing evaluated by this bead may be represented, logged, or exported as an invariant, and an `slo.toml` row can never migrate into `invariants.toml` via alert config. FG-CFG-03/04 disclosure text as above; FG-EVID-04 (slo-class, never an invariant): bound in watermark/commit-sequence units, audit-pipeline and time-evidence dependencies named, realized lag distribution, typed `FreshnessBreach` rate and fallback policy.

## Interactions
Rows/claim classes from `g0-claim-registries`; operation classes + barrier chains for attribution from `g0-cost-registry`; telemetry substrate from `obs-observatory`; three-line availability doctrine and footprint table from `w9-authority-surface`; `FreshnessBreach` events from `w6-freshness`; breach->graph links into `obs-system-graph`. `perf-bench-*` beads and this bead share row definitions — CI baseline and production alert must reference the same row id, so a gate change automatically retunes alerting.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) Loader round-trip: every `slo.toml` row parses to a typed key `{operation_class,posture,audit_class}`; unknown operation classes fail startup (registry coherence). (2) Alert e2e: inject latency at a named barrier (fault-injection via the sim harness); alert fires naming row, class, barrier-level attribution; logs carry row id, measured vs budget, decomposition table. (3) Governance decomposition test: stall the simulated audit authority; visibility-line alert fires attributed to the audit authority while the apply-durability line stays green — verifying the three-lines-never-one-product rule. (4) Freshness test: induce watermark lag; FG-EVID-04 alert carries realized lag distribution and FreshnessBreach rate. (5) Negative test: SLO evaluator provably cannot trigger admission/shedding paths (no such dependency edge, CI crate check) and its outputs are stamped diagnostic. (6) Head-of-line test: raise N x M until the FG-CFG-04 budget breaches; alert attributes to maintenance-stream parameters.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: alert storms under correlated breaches — attribution collapses correlated child alerts under their common cause. Risk: silent divergence between CI gate rows and alert rows — single row-id source. Rejected: SLO-driven automatic remediation (safety stays deterministic); availability as one multiplied product (three lines mandated); per-tenant audit-visibility pipelines (registered rejection — W12-scale redesign, not an additive registry change; the mitigation is per-tenant ticket-resolution SLOs at the authority plus §12.8's reserved capacity and pipeline limits).

## Provenance
§15.0 registry split (line 1118 context); §16.2-16.3 (1190-1191); §16.8 (1222-1228); §9.5 slo clause (line 802 context); §17 gate values; Appendix F FG-CFG-03/04, FG-EVID-04; §20 authority-availability row (line 1378 context).

title: Expose the system graph: queryable ops surface + Prism FeatureDisabled degraded mode
description:
## What & scope
Implement §16.5 as the dedicated `fgdb-system-graph` crate (§18.1, Surface/operations layer): the database's own runtime exposed as a read-only, access-controlled *temporal property graph* queryable in GQL, with Prism-powered analyses over it, the declared `FeatureDisabled` degraded mode, and the Observatory-owned wait-cycle probe kept independent of the analytics bulkhead.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6 made concrete: the database dogfoods its data model as its ops surface. Agents and operators debug FrankenGraphDB with FrankenGraphDB — `MATCH (q:Query)-[:WAITS_FOR]->(x) WHERE q.elapsed_ms > 250 RETURN q, x` — instead of learning a bespoke admin API. B4/B1: incidents become subgraphs you can diff across time because the graph is temporal. B5: the degraded mode is typed and registered, never silent, preserving evidence discipline even when features are off.

## Design — normative detail
Graph contents (exact): sessions, transactions, queries, plans, operators, snapshots + leases, obligations, segments, compaction jobs, subscriptions, replication streams, repairs, decision cards — a read-only, access-controlled temporal property graph, queryable in GQL like any other graph. The wait-for graph is literally a graph: deadlock and contention analysis run Prism's own cycle detection and centrality over it, and incidents become subgraphs diffable across time. Cardinality is bounded, sampled under load, redacted per capability (§12.6).

Degraded mode (exact, normative): with `fgdb-prism` disabled by its posture/feature activation predicate, the system graph remains a queryable read-only temporal property graph, while the fnx-backed analyses over it — wait-for cycle detection, centrality, incident diffing — return a typed `FeatureDisabled` error rather than degrading silently, with the corresponding feature-disable registry row recorded per G0's per-clause rule. Nothing safety-bearing degrades with them: deadlock and starvation safety come from §16.3's bounded queues, resource reservations, cancellation checkpoints, and deterministic fallback controls, and the §16.3 early-warning wait-cycle probe is owned by `fgdb-observatory` with its own small bounded cycle check, so the observability plane never imports the analytics bulkhead for an alerting primitive.

Separation of duties: `fgdb-system-graph` is a *projection* of Observatory state (`fgdb-observatory` is the substrate; the crate holds no second bookkeeping system); queries run through the ordinary Loom path under ordinary authorization, so plan certificates, decision cards, and redaction apply to ops queries exactly as to user queries. Prism analyses run inside the `PrismRegion` bulkhead (`w8-scheduling`) so an expensive centrality run over a huge wait graph cannot starve user work.

## Invariants & claim types
No FG-INV row is created. Binding rules restated: (a) safety never depends on this surface — deadlock/starvation safety is carried by bounded queues, reservations, cancellation checkpoints, deterministic fallbacks; (b) the `FeatureDisabled` behavior plus its feature-disable registry row is claim-typed under G0's per-clause activation contract (each disabled clause records which registered claims deactivate with it); (c) all exposed quantities inherit their source claim classes (diagnostics stay diagnostics even when rendered as graph properties).

## Interactions
Deliverable crate: `fgdb-system-graph` (§18.1). Builds on `obs-observatory` (source domains, wait-cycle probe stays there); GQL execution via `w5-executor`; Prism analyses gated by `w8-scheduling`'s bulkhead; access control and capability-scoped redaction from `w9-enforcement`; feature-disable registry rows per `g0-claim-registries`' clause-activation contract. `obs-slo` links alerts to system-graph node ids for attribution; incident tooling and `verif-replay-products` consume incident subgraphs.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) E2E: run a contended workload, execute the canonical wait-for GQL query, verify returned waits match ground truth from the scheduler's own records; logs include query text, capability, redactions applied. (2) Degraded-mode e2e: disable `fgdb-prism` via its activation predicate; plain GQL over the system graph still answers; cycle-detection/centrality/incident-diff calls return typed `FeatureDisabled` (assert error type, not a generic failure); the feature-disable registry row is present; re-enabling restores analyses. (3) Crate-graph CI: `fgdb-observatory` has no dependency edge to `fgdb-prism`; the wait-cycle probe passes its bounded-cycle unit tests independently. (4) Redaction tests: a low-capability session sees redacted query text/parameters in the graph; property fuzzing for leak paths. (5) Temporal diff test: capture incident subgraph at t1/t2, diff, verify changed edges. (6) Bulkhead test: a deliberately expensive centrality run is admission-bounded and cannot degrade user-commit p99 beyond the declared budget (logged both sides).

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: ops-surface cardinality explosion under incident load — bounded cardinality with declared sampling, so the graph degrades by disclosure rather than by OOM. Risk: the surface becomes a privilege-escalation channel — ordinary authorization path, capability redaction, read-only. Rejected: bespoke admin RPCs instead of the graph (violates B6 dogfooding); silent no-op when Prism is off (must be typed `FeatureDisabled` + registry row); Observatory importing Prism for its probe (registered rejection).

## Provenance
§16.5 (line 1193); §16.3 hard-safety clause (1191); §12.6 redaction; §18.1 `fgdb-system-graph` crate row (1293); G0 per-clause feature-disable rule.

title: Seven of nine §12.1 security identities declare a rust_newtype that does not exist: the law the registry says a type system must enforce has no type
notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-04 at HEAD 6202588 by JadeSnow while verifying the A21 acceptance clause of fgdb-w1-sketch-calibrate-tpj. Labels: b5, security, w1, verification.

THE CLAIM. registries/threat_model.toml §12.1 header, verbatim:
  "Nine identities. The security and adaptive epoch types have distinct wire tags and distinct Rust
   newtypes and are never comparable or substitutable -- THE ONE LAW IN THIS BLOCK THAT A TYPE
   SYSTEM, NOT A REVIEWER, MUST ENFORCE."
So the registry names the Rust type system as the enforcement mechanism for identity separation.

THE MEASUREMENT. Of the nine declared rust_newtype values, SEVEN have no definition in any crate
(grep for "pub struct X" / "pub enum X" over crates/**/*.rs):
    TenantId              ABSENT
    PrincipalId           ABSENT
    IssuerId              ABSENT
    TokenId               ABSENT
    DatabaseId            EXISTS  crates/fgdb-types/src/ids.rs:66
    SecurityPolicyEpoch   ABSENT
    RevocationIndex       ABSENT
    DecisionPolicyEpoch   EXISTS  crates/fgdb-calibrate/src/policy_epoch.rs:543
    KeyEpoch              ABSENT
A law enforced by a type that does not exist is enforced by nothing. For seven of nine identities
there is no type to make them "never comparable or substitutable", so nothing prevents a consumer
from passing a tenant where a principal is expected -- they would both be whatever primitive the
call site picked.

WHY THE EXISTING CHECKER DOES NOT CATCH IT, and this is the interesting part.
tools/registry-check/src/threat.rs:1860 DOES enforce a law here:
    if !newtypes.insert(identity.rust_newtype.as_str()) { ... "rust_newtype is shared with another
    identity; the epoch types must never unify" }
That checks UNIQUENESS OF THE REGISTRY STRINGS. It reads exactly like the separation law and is
not: two names that exist only as TOML strings are trivially distinct. The check passes at maximum
strength while the property it stands for is unenforced in code. Same fail-open-by-vacuity shape as
the cases this swarm has closed repeatedly (unpinned splits, inert exclusions, unenforced SC2015);
here the tell is that the checker constrains the REGISTRY and the header claims the TYPE SYSTEM.
tools/registry-check/tests/threat_model.rs:340 asserts security.rust_newtype != decision.rust_newtype
-- again string inequality, not type distinctness.

CONSEQUENCE FOR A21 (fgdb-w1-sketch-calibrate-tpj). That bead owns DecisionPolicyEpoch and its
acceptance says "DecisionPolicyEpoch is byte- and type-distinct from SecurityPolicyEpoch; equality,
aliasing, or ambient policy-version inference fails closed." That clause CANNOT be tested today:
SecurityPolicyEpoch has no type, so there is nothing to prove distinct from. DecisionPolicyEpoch
itself is fully implemented (policy_epoch.rs, 2875 lines, canonical bytes, try_root/try_promote/
try_revert_to_fallback, exercised in sextant_e2e.rs) -- the gap is entirely on the counterpart.

WHERE THE FIX BELONGS: crates/fgdb-types/src/ids.rs (174 lines) already hosts DatabaseId and
DatabaseSecurityNamespaceId and carries newtype macros at lines 35/43, so it is the established home
for the six missing security identities. That makes this fgdb-w1-foundation-types-tjk territory, not
this bead. NOT DONE HERE for that reason and because tjk is in_progress under another pane -- do not
let two panes define the same seven types.

DERIVE THE SHAPES FROM THE PLAN, not from the summaries. Each identity has a one-line summary in
threat_model.toml that constrains it (e.g. TokenId "the immutable root token identity and the
RevocationSubject::Token identity; attenuation never creates a new token ID"; SecurityPolicyEpoch
"advances once per applied policy transition with checked arithmetic" -- so it owes checked
increment, like CommitSeqExhausted at ids.rs:86). §12.1 is the anchor.

SUGGESTED CLOSING TEST, so the law stops being reviewer-enforced: a registry-check test that reads
the nine rust_newtype values and asserts each names a type the workspace actually defines. That
turns the header claim into a gate. It will be RED for seven rows until they land, so land the types
first or land the test with the census pinned and tighten it as they arrive.
close_reason:
FIXED by 45f5c56 (feat(types): §12.1 security identity newtypes and fail-closed policy epochs), landed by another pane after this was filed and mailed. Re-censused at that HEAD: all nine §12.1 identities now resolve. TenantId/PrincipalId/IssuerId/TokenId are u128_id! macro-generated at crates/fgdb-types/src/ids.rs:66-77 with §12.1 doc anchors; SecurityPolicyEpoch carries ORIGIN + checked_successor with SecurityPolicyEpochExhausted (no wrap/saturate) per the commit; RevocationIndex and KeyEpoch cover the revocation/key-rotation epoch domains; DatabaseId and DecisionPolicyEpoch were already present. All eight are exported from crates/fgdb-types/src/lib.rs (verified 1 occurrence each). The A21 distinctness clause on fgdb-w1-sketch-calibrate-tpj is now testable: SecurityPolicyEpoch finally has a type to be distinct FROM.

METHOD NOTE worth keeping: my original census grepped 'pub struct X' and would have reported these seven ABSENT even after they landed, because they are macro-generated and the name appears bare inside the macro invocation. I re-ran it that way first and got a false negative on my own fixed bug. A name-presence census over Rust source must account for macro generation, or it under-reports in exactly the direction that manufactures phantom defects.

RESIDUE, not part of this bug: the suggested closing test (assert every declared rust_newtype names a type the workspace defines) is still unwritten, so the registry->code direction remains reviewer-enforced. threat.rs:1860 still only checks uniqueness of the TOML strings. Now that all nine exist that test would be GREEN on landing rather than red for seven rows, so it is cheap to add and worth doing before the next identity is declared.
