title: Engine delta window is queryable since a cursor
description:
Wire the live frontier-stream face: `since(cursor)` over the retained delta window.

## Background
`fgdb-w2-delta-batches-og6n` names three things: template construction, the ordered batch, and the **delta index and frontier stream**. The type layer already has `LocalDeltaBatchIndex` (insert + frontier in one transition, `iter` over the whole window, `retire_prefix`). The engine now owns that index (`fgdb-og6n-engine-delta-index-ltji`). Ripple/CDC (`fgdb-w6-delta-consumption-iyc`) is the consumer, and it is blocked on retention cuts, valid-time, TTL, and Z-set circuits.

What is missing is the **stream primitive itself**: "give me every retained batch after this cursor, or refuse." `iter()` walks the whole window and cannot tell a caller their cursor was retired out from under them. A consumer that filters `commit_seq > after` by hand would silently skip a cut prefix and emit a gapped CDC feed. Plan:1928's window is `(retained_after, frontier]`; a cursor below `retained_after` is unanswerable, a cursor above `frontier` is the future.

This bead is that live subset: `LocalDeltaBatchIndex::since` plus `Database::delta_since`, both fail-closed. It does **not** land retention-cut activation, ShardFragment/Global indexes, or Ripple adapters. Derived state is never more authoritative than the commit stream (FG-INV-18).

Do **not** parent-child this to open `og6n` — that edge made 819.2 unready. This is `related` to `og6n`. Closing this does **not** close `og6n` or `iyc`.

## Technical Approach
- Add `IndexError::BeyondFrontier { asked, frontier }` and `IndexError::CursorRetired { asked, retained_after, frontier }`.
- `LocalDeltaBatchIndex::since(after)` yields every retained batch with `commit_seq > after`, in commit order.
  - `after > frontier` → `BeyondFrontier` (never clamp).
  - `after < retained_after` → `CursorRetired` (the prefix is gone).
  - `after == frontier` → empty success (caught up).
  - `after == retained_after` (including origin on a fresh index) → the full window.
- Overflow-safe: walk `BTreeMap::range((Excluded(after), Unbounded))`, never `after + 1`.
- `Database::delta_since` checks `Healthy` then delegates. Map `BeyondFrontier` onto the existing `ReadError::BeyondFrontier`; add `ReadError::DeltaCursorRetired` for the cut-cursor case.
- Do not persist anything. Do not invent a second stream type.

## Success Criteria
- Type-layer: three inserts, `since(origin)` is `[1,2,3]`; `since(2)` is `[3]`; `since(3)` is empty; `since(4)` is `BeyondFrontier`; after `retire_prefix(1)`, `since(0)` is `CursorRetired` and `since(1)` is `[2,3]`.
- Engine: after two writes, `delta_since(ORIGIN)` has length 2 and `delta_since(first)` has length 1, naming the second seq.
- Empty create: `delta_since(ORIGIN)` is empty, not an error.
- Future cursor on a healthy handle is `ReadError::BeyondFrontier`.
- Independent reconstruction: after drop, `Database::open` and `fgdb_sim::replay` produce **equal** `LocalDeltaBatchIndex` values (same frontier, same batches). `fgdb` does not import `fgdb-reference`.
- A fenced post-D2 handle refuses `delta_since` the same way it refuses other reads.
- `cargo test -p fgdb-delta-types --test delta_batch_index` exit 0; `cargo test -p fgdb --test spine` exit 0; `cargo test -p fgdb-sim --test spine_differential` exit 0. clippy `-D warnings` on the three crates exits 0.

## Test Plan
- Unit (`delta_batch_index.rs`): empty/full/suffix/caught-up/future/retired-cursor, plus "refusal leaves the index byte-identical".
- Spine: two commits, assert seqs and counts by name; empty create; future cursor.
- Differential: reopen vs replay `assert_eq!` on the indexes; fence `delta_since` in the existing post-D2 fence sweep.
- Logging: assertions name `asked`, `frontier`, `retained_after`, and the yielded seqs.

## Considerations
- `since` is a read. It must not retire, insert, or otherwise mutate the window.
- Retention cuts remain og6n/`cn1l`. This only makes an already-retired floor observable as a refusal.
- Do not parent-child to `iyc`. Ripple will call this; this is not a fake Ripple.
acceptance_criteria: since(origin)/suffix/empty/future/retired-cursor; engine delta_since after two writes; reopen index equals sim replay; spine + delta_batch_index + spine_differential exit 0; og6n and iyc stay open
close_reason: LocalDeltaBatchIndex::since and Database::delta_since are live. Type-layer: origin/suffix/caught-up/future/retired-cursor (delta_batch_index 18/18). Engine: two-write stream + future refusal (spine 34/34). Independent reopen index equals fgdb_sim::replay (spine_differential 11/11). clippy -D warnings on fgdb-delta-types, fgdb, fgdb-sim exit 0. og6n and iyc stay open.

title: Engine maintains LocalDeltaBatchIndex on write and rebuilds it at open
description:
Wire LocalDeltaBatchIndex into the engine so apply and frontier advance in one transition.

## Background
`fgdb-w2-delta-batches-og6n` is the full committed-delta stream: template construction, `LogicalDeltaBatch<LocalCommitted>` at apply, `LocalDeltaBatchIndex` + `local_delta_frontier`, and retention-cut machinery. It is blocked on G0 identity registries, txn lifecycle, retention checkpoints, and the six-step commit protocol.

The *type* layer already exists in `fgdb-delta-types` (`LogicalDeltaTemplate`, `LogicalDeltaBatch::order`, `LocalDeltaBatchIndex::insert`). Replay in `fgdb-sim` already inserts a batch in the same step as `apply_template` (plan:397). The live engine `Database` does **not**: after D2 it folds the template into Strata and publishes, and the index is never touched. Same-handle and reopen have no window over committed deltas. Ripple/CDC cannot consume what is not there.

This bead is the live subset: put the index on `Database`, insert on every successful write, rebuild the window from the marker chain at open. It does **not** land retention cuts, ShardFragment/Global role schemas, or a durable index object. Derived state is never more authoritative than the commit stream (FG-INV-18): crash after D2 before the in-memory insert is healed by reopen rebuild.

Do **not** parent-child this to open `og6n` — that edge made 819.2 unready. This is `related` to `og6n`. Closing this does **not** close `og6n`.

## Technical Approach
- Add `delta_index: LocalDeltaBatchIndex` to `Database`.
- After D2, in the same write that applies the template to the retained writer: `CommittedMarker::attest(marker_ref, cx)`, `LogicalDeltaBatch::order(&template, digest, marker)`, `delta_index.insert(batch)`. Insert failure after D2 is `CommittedNeedsRecovery` (derived), not an uncommitted write.
- On every open/rebuild path that already walks the chain (`bind_with_vfs`): rebuild the index from the full recovered marker chain (not only a checkpoint suffix — the index must cover `(0, frontier]`).
- Public read accessors: `delta_index()` / `delta_frontier()`. Reads check `Healthy` like other graph reads.
- Do not persist the index as a second source of truth.

## Success Criteria
- After `write` returns, `delta_frontier()` equals the new `CommitSeq` and `delta_index().get(seq)` is `Some`.
- Two writes produce a gap-free window of length 2.
- Drop + `open` reconstructs the same frontier and the same number of entries.
- A write that D2s then fails derived publication still rebuilds the batch on reopen (index is derived from the chain).
- Existing spine / differential tests stay green.
- `cargo test -p fgdb --test spine` exits 0. clippy `-D warnings` on `fgdb` exits 0.

## Test Plan
- Unit/spine: seed write, assert frontier and `get`.
- Two commits: both sequences present, `next_commit_seq` is the successor of the second.
- Reopen: frontier and `len()` match the pre-drop handle.
- Empty create: frontier is origin, index empty.
- Logging: each assertion names seq, frontier, and entry count.

## Considerations
- Checkpoint-selected open only folds the suffix into the writer. The index rebuild must still walk the whole chain or the window would start at `published_at` and `insert` on the next write would see a gap.
- `LogicalDeltaBatch` stores entries by value (og6n subset note). Fine for the live window; retention cuts remain og6n's.
- Do not import `fgdb-reference` into `fgdb`.
acceptance_criteria: After write, delta_frontier equals commit seq; reopen reconstructs the window; cargo test -p fgdb --test spine exit 0; og6n stays open
close_reason: Engine Database now owns a derived LocalDeltaBatchIndex: insert after D2 in the same write, rebuild from the full marker chain at open (not the checkpoint suffix). Public delta_index()/delta_frontier() check Healthy. cargo test -p fgdb --test spine exit 0 (34 passed, including delta_index_is_maintained_on_write_and_rebuilt_at_open and a_post_d2_publication_failure_still_rebuilds_the_delta_index_on_reopen). clippy -p fgdb --all-targets -D warnings exit 0. og6n stays open.

title: Systemic: 42 symbols carry a jointly-unsatisfiable construction_order, 35 already frozen
description:
A sweep of every symbol the Appendix A source constrains in BOTH reference directions finds 42 whose
construction_order is jointly unsatisfiable: the maximum order among the targets its own body
StrongRefs exceeds the minimum order among the rows that StrongRef it. No value satisfies
`projection_dag_future_result` in both directions.

  42  total
   4  BIND TODAY — the loader already rejects every value
  38  LATENT — the loader accepts values today that the source forbids
  35  are ALREADY-LANDED logical kinds, so the contradiction is frozen behind the append-only
      assignment pin and cannot be corrected by choosing a different order

WHY LATENT IS THE DANGEROUS HALF. `projection_dag_future_result` evaluates the LANDED field-row
graph. A kind minted before its field rows exist has no outbound edges the checker can see, so any
order below its ceiling passes every gate. The contradiction only surfaces when someone lands that
kind's own body — at which point the order is pinned and the correction is expensive. Two beads were
already parked as individual errata for exactly this, fgdb-tuw1 (GlobalTxnCommand, floor 40 against
ceiling 30) and fgdb-capsule-ref-target-name-drift-cq4x (CommittedEffectCapsule, floor 40 against
ceiling 15). They are instances 1 and 2 of the 42.

ROOT CAUSE, structural rather than careless: the established increment shape mints kinds with an
order first and lands their fields later, so the order is chosen against a reference graph the
checker cannot yet see. Every slice following that shape manufactures more instances, and each is
frozen on landing. Three kinds minted tonight by pane3 are in the list and passed every gate.

THE FOUR THAT BIND TODAY are the ones to look at first; the full list is reproducible in seconds
with the sweep at /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/p3-tuw1-probe.rs, which also carries a known-good control
(ShardingFreezeSpec, window 29..=29) so a broken harness cannot report a silent all-clear.

OPTIONS, costed on fgdb-tuw1's latest comment: rule each bead individually (leaves 40); require a
source-derived two-directional window at mint time (stops new instances, does not fix the 35);
extend the DAG check to source edges (makes the invariant true, but turns 42 red and needs a
remediation plan for the 35 frozen); or document that construction_order is a landed-graph invariant
only (free now, leaves the generated reachability/GC and checkpoint-vector walkers keyed on an order
the source contradicts).
close_reason: Mechanical class discharged (331862c, 109d21a, 5b484ec). Re-measured at 7f60e5f: 3 cycles -> fgdb-2lch; 16 source self-edges + the last 3-symbol/6-row entangled batch (AuditTerminalAttemptRecord/AuditEventRecord/AuditTicket, one weakly-connected component blocked by AuditTerminalAttemptRecord.predecessor_ref:StrongRef<Self>) -> fgdb-suhb, recorded there with both bounds; mint-time latency and the applier window guard -> fgdb-owlp. Every remainder has an open, durable home.

comments.text:
RE-MEASURED AND RE-COSTED. From pane3, against HEAD d80c942, checker rebuilt from that same HEAD.
Three of this bead's load-bearing claims do not survive, and the cheapest option is not the one the
bead recommends.

=== CORRECTION 1: THE 42 IS 39 + 3, AND THE 3 ARE A WORSE CLASS ===
Reconciled my sweep against the original one, deliberately, because a harness disagreement is exactly
the "looks like a pass" family. My list is a STRICT SUBSET: 39 vs 42, with 0 symbols in mine that are
not in theirs. The 3 in theirs only:
  AuditTerminalAttemptRecord, GlobalTxnWorkspaceGeneration, RemoteAuthorityConfigurationEvidence
All three are symbols with a source SELF-EDGE. The original sweep let the self-edge act as the
symbol's own inbound ceiling, so it reported an unsatisfiable order window. They are not order
defects -- they are dag_self_edge defects, which no integer can fix in any direction. Counting them
here understates their severity.

=== CORRECTION 2: THE ORDER LAW IS NON-STRICT, SO MOST OF THIS IS SATISFIABLE ===
dag_future_result fires on `target.order > containing.order`. Strictly greater. Equal orders are
legal, and 18 landed retaining edges in the live green catalog already sit at equal order (of 184
with both ends ordered). A non-strict relation over an ACYCLIC graph is satisfiable by construction.
So "no value satisfies it in both directions" is only truly unfixable where the SOURCE GRAPH CYCLES.
Full Tarjan SCC over the source StrongRef graph (963 symbols, 532 owners):
   3 nontrivial SCCs trapping 7 symbols   <- genuinely unfixable by any assignment
       GlobalPrepareAdmissionSpec@60 <-> GlobalTxnOutcomePreparationRecord@60 <-> GlobalTxnOutcomeRecord@60
       AuditTerminalFreezeRecord@6   <-> NoTerminalSignatureOrOrderProof@6
       KeyEnvelopeNode@50            <-> KeyEnvelopeRoot@50
  18 source self-edges                    <- also unfixable by any assignment
Splitting the 39 by that test:
   2  trapped in a source cycle  -> a reference SPELLING must change; a real owner ruling
  37  source is satisfiable      -> the FROZEN INTEGERS are wrong; mechanical, no plan edit
Note all three SCCs currently sit at co-equal orders, which is why they are green: co-equality
satisfies dag_future_result. It does NOT satisfy dag_cycle, which fires on the edge set alone. They
go red the moment their field rows land, and no order will save them.

=== CORRECTION 3, THE ONE THAT CHANGES THE DECISION: THE 35 ARE NOT EXPENSIVELY FROZEN ===
This bead says the contradiction is "frozen behind the append-only assignment pin and cannot be
corrected by choosing a different order". construction_order is NOT in the pin. The pin's own message
enumerates its scope: "released codes, tags, names, lifecycle states, and union arms".
Measured, not read: moving GlobalFinalCertificationReservation 40->30, TopologyState 40->30 and
TopologyState's 3 landed field rows, in appendix_a_catalog.toml plus both projections, gives
LOAD OK / 0 violations -- not even pin drift.
NEGATIVE CONTROL, same copy same harness: TopologyState status reserved->active fires
projection_registry_assignment_drift instantly. The harness is live; the orders simply are not pinned.
(Editing only the projection and not the catalog yields projection_byte_diff -- the catalog is the
source of truth and the projections regenerate from it.)

=== WHAT THAT DOES TO THE FOUR OPTIONS ===
Option C -- extend the DAG check to source edges -- was rejected as "highest cost, needs a
remediation plan for the 35 frozen". Remediation is row edits with no re-freeze. C is now the
cheapest option that makes the invariant TRUE rather than merely unviolated, and it is the only one
that catches the 2 cycles and 18 self-edges, which are the genuinely dangerous residue and which no
amount of B-style discipline at mint time will ever fix.
Recommended: C, scoped as
  1. fix the 37 assignment defects mechanically (each is a small verified edit; two are already
     verified green on fgdb-tuw1 and fgdb-capsule-ref-target-name-drift-cq4x)
  2. rule the 2 cycle-trapped symbols and the 18 self-edges as source errata -- these are the only
     genuine owner decisions in the whole set
  3. then land the source-edge DAG rule, which can now go green
B remains worth doing to stop new instances, but B alone leaves every existing defect in place.

=== BLOCKING ===
This bead blocks fgdb-tuw1 and fgdb-capsule-ref-target-name-drift-cq4x, so `br update --status
in_progress` refuses to claim either. Both are nonetheless fully measured and settled on their own
comments; tuw1's value is forced at 30 and needs no ruling at all.
Instruments (rebuild the lib from the tree you are measuring, or you WILL get phantom violations --
a stale binary reported 24 against a clean HEAD for me):
  ~/.claude/projects/-data-projects-frankengraphdb/tools/source-order-satisfiability.rs
  ~/.claude/projects/-data-projects-frankengraphdb/tools/source-order-scc.rs
  ~/.claude/projects/-data-projects-frankengraphdb/tools/source-order-landing-plan.rs
  ~/.claude/projects/-data-projects-frankengraphdb/tools/source-order-repair-cost.rs
All four carry positive, negative and known-boring controls inline.

comments.text:
REPAIRED, IN TWO TRANCHES, AND THE HEADLINE COUNT IS NOW 19. pane3, against 109d21a.
43 of the 60 symbols this bead's class covers are landed at corrected orders; 23 remain,
every one of them inside a slice another pane holds or entangled with a self-edge.

=== WHAT THE PREDECESSOR'S RULING GOT RIGHT, RE-CONFIRMED ===
construction_order is NOT inside the append-only assignment pin. Both tranches moved
landed kinds and their landed field rows with LOAD OK / 0 violations and no pin drift.
The negative control was run on a copy of each post-repair tree: flipping one lifecycle
status still fires projection_registry_assignment_drift AND registry_assignment_drift,
exit 1. The green is a real green, not a check that stopped looking.
dag_future_result is non-strict, witnessed by 71 landed equal-order edges.

=== WHAT WAS MISSING, AND IT IS THE WHOLE DELIVERABLE ===
Every prior probe on this bead MEASURED. None of them REPAIRED, and a per-edge patch is
not a repair: raising one referrer to clear one violated edge pushes it through its own
ceiling, and the contradiction moves one hop instead of dying. The constraint system is

    o(target) <= o(referrer)    for every retaining edge

over a totally ordered label set. That is a monotone labelling problem, so with a
per-symbol cost for changing a value the MINIMUM-COST consistent assignment is exactly a
min-cut in Ishikawa's construction -- solved, not approximated. Chain node (v,l) means
"o(v) >= L[l]"; an infinite arc (t,l) -> (a,l) encodes o(t) <= o(a). Lexicographic
objective in one scalar, which Ishikawa admits because only the PAIRWISE term must be
convex and a hard monotone constraint is:
    1. fewest symbols moved       (1_000_000 each)
    2. fewest catalog rows edited (1_000 per landed field row that moves with its kind)
    3. shortest distance moved    (|new-old|, <= 75, tie-break only)
Term 3 is not cosmetic. Without it the cut is indifferent between two legal values and
parks symbols at the bottom label -- formally optimal, semantically vandalism, since
construction_order names a construction phase. It is what turns "AuditTicket 40 -> 5"
into "AuditTicket 40 -> 6".

Constraints come from BOTH populations, deliberately:
  S1 every retaining source reference between two symbols that carry an order, INCLUDING
     paths whose interior is still unminted -- each interior is forced into the window
     when it lands, so repairing direct-only re-manufactures this bead;
  S2 every retaining edge already in the catalog's landed field rows. The landed graph is
     not a subset of the source graph, and an S1-only repair can turn the loader RED.

=== THE MATCHER DEFECT, WHICH COST ME ONE LANDED VALUE ===
Tranche 1 (331862c) read a reference with strip_prefix. A repeated member's census
exact_type is spelled `[StrongRef<T<Local>>]`, starts with `[`, fails the prefix test,
and its edge is dropped -- the same under-reading fgdb-suhb traces to a frozen violation
already in the tree (a12 minted ResourceLedgerTransition against a ceiling computed from
five of its six consumers). A matcher that misses an edge reports a WIDER window than
exists and looks exactly like a pass.
Tranche 2 (109d21a) scans for every retaining wrapper ANYWHERE in the type, requires the
preceding byte to be a non-identifier so CertifiedRemoteStrongRef< is never read as a
bare StrongRef<, and takes the inner type with a BALANCED angle scan. +50 constraint
edges, +5 symbols.
CONSEQUENCE, stated plainly: 17 of tranche 1's 18 values survive the wider reading
unchanged. ONE did not -- GcDecisionRecord went 15 -> 25 and 25 was still below its
floor; it is now 40. Nothing was landed in a wrong direction; one value was an
under-correction, caught before its field body froze it.

=== MEASURED (balanced-scan reading throughout) ===
                          865ecfb   331862c   109d21a
  violated edges             81        68        28
  unsatisfiable windows      38        35        19
  symbols still to move      60        48        23
  catalog rows still to edit 118       99        49
  independent components     21         8         5

=== THE RESIDUAL, EXACTLY, FOR ITS OWNERS ===
Five components. Every move below is verified consistent with the whole system; a
component may be landed WHOLE and in any order (partial-within-a-component is NOT safe --
it can violate an edge that was fine before).

  a16 -- pane7's lane, 19 symbols across three components
    C1  RestoreSourceLeaseRecord            45 -> 30   (5 landed field rows)
    C2  ShardRestoreSourceLeaseProjection   50 -> 30
    C5  TimeAuthorityRegistry               21 -> 30      TimeAuthorityObservationImport  23 -> 30
        TimeValidationEvidence              25 -> 30      DeliveryLeaseExpiryEvidence     27 -> 30  [a03]
        ReservationDispositionEligibility   30 -> 50 [a19] OfflineIssuerVerificationServiceFloor 32 -> 30
        TimeBoundSubjectInventory           33 -> 30      TimeBoundSubjectInventoryProof  34 -> 30
        ShardTimeBoundSubjectInventoryCertificate 35 -> 30 GroupTimeIssuanceQuiescenceCertificate 39 -> 30
        DurableCapabilityVerifierKey        40 -> 20 [a21] RoleTimeBoundSubjectInventoryClosure   40 -> 30
        RoleTimeIssuanceReservationClosure  41 -> 30      TimeAuthorityDrainHold          55 -> 30
        TimeAuthorityRegistryTransitionReceipt 57 -> 30   TimeAuthorityEpochTransitionRecord 60 -> 30
        TimeAuthorityTransitionTerminalSummary 65 -> 30
        (17 symbols, 35 catalog rows. This is fgdb-ovok's cluster: the registry's own
         window is [65..23], empty in both directions, and the whole cluster collapsing
         to 30 is the minimum-churn resolution.)

  a08 -- pane6's lane, 2 components
    C3  TopologyRetirementAck                6 -> 30   (demand 30 <- TopologyRetirementFloor)
    C4  AuditTerminalAttemptRecord           6 -> 40   AuditEventRecord 40 -> 6   AuditTicket 40 -> 6
        !! ENTANGLED: AuditTerminalAttemptRecord also carries a SOURCE SELF-EDGE, so the

        Land the self-edge ruling (fgdb-suhb / fgdb-u3gr) FIRST or these three are wasted.

=== NOT MECHANICALLY REPAIRABLE, AND NOT MINE TO RULE ===
No integer assignment can satisfy these; they need a reference SPELLING change.
  3 constraint cycles, 7 symbols
    GlobalPrepareAdmissionSpec@60 <-> GlobalTxnOutcomePreparationRecord@60 <-> GlobalTxnOutcomeRecord@60
    AuditTerminalFreezeRecord@6   <-> NoTerminalSignatureOrOrderProof@6

  All three sit at co-equal orders today, which is why they are GREEN: co-equality

This class grew 42 -> 60 in ONE DAY on this board, because the established increment

against a reference graph the checker cannot yet see. Repair alone loses that race. The
guard has to go in the APPLIER, not the loader: the loader cannot see it, since a kind

comments.author: pane3
comments.text:
THE METHOD, WRITTEN OUT SO pane6 DOES NOT RE-DERIVE IT. pane3 handing off the residual.
This is the whole reasoning chain behind 331862c and 109d21a. Everything below is measured on
this tree, not argued.

=== 0. WHY THE PROBLEM IS NOT WHAT THE BEAD TITLE SAYS ===
"N symbols carry a jointly-unsatisfiable construction_order" describes symptoms. There is one
system underneath, and once you write it down the whole class is solved at once instead of 60
times. Three facts turn it from an erratum pile into an assignment defect:

  (a) construction_order is NOT inside the append-only assignment pin. The pin's own violation
      message enumerates its scope: "released codes, tags, names, lifecycle states, and union
      arms". Orders are not in it. Both my tranches moved landed kinds AND their landed field
      rows with LOAD OK / 0 violations and no pin drift.
  (b) dag_future_result is NON-STRICT. It fires on `target.order > containing.order` -- strictly
      greater. EQUAL ORDERS ARE LEGAL, witnessed by 72 landed equal-order retaining edges in the
      live green catalog, not by reading the code. A non-strict relation over an ACYCLIC graph is
      satisfiable by construction (give every symbol the same integer), so "no ordering exists"
      can only be true where the SOURCE GRAPH CYCLES.
  (c) therefore every non-cyclic instance is a MECHANICAL REPAIR: edit integers, no plan edit,
      no erratum, no owner ruling.

=== 1. WHY EDGE-AT-A-TIME PATCHING IS NOT A REPAIR ===
The obvious move -- find a violated edge, raise the referrer above its target -- is wrong, and it
is wrong in a way that looks like progress. Each symbol is bounded in BOTH directions:
    demand(v)  = max order among the targets v's own body retains   (its floor)
    ceiling(v) = min order among the rows that retain v             (its ceiling)
Raising the referrer to clear one edge pushes it through its OWN ceiling and manufactures a new
violation one hop up. Lowering the target pushes it under its own floor. You can chase this
around a component indefinitely. That is why 42 became 60 in a day.

=== 2. THE SYSTEM, AND THE FACT THAT MAKES IT SOLVABLE EXACTLY ===
Write down every constraint at once:

    o(target) <= o(referrer)      for every retaining edge

That is a MONOTONE LABELLING PROBLEM over a totally ordered label set (the existing
construction_order vocabulary, 59 distinct values). With a per-symbol cost for changing its
value, the MINIMUM-COST CONSISTENT ASSIGNMENT is exactly a MIN-CUT in Ishikawa's construction --
solved, not approximated, not heuristic.

Construction, concretely:
  * label set L = the sorted distinct existing orders. Chain node (v,l) means "o(v) >= L[l]".
  * chain per symbol: s -> (v,1) -> (v,2) -> ... -> (v,k-1) -> t. Cutting the arc entering
    level l sets o(v) = L[l-1]. Give that arc capacity = the unary cost of assigning L[l-1] to v.
    Add an INFINITE reverse arc (v,l+1) -> (v,l) so exactly one arc per chain is ever cut.
  * one constraint arc per edge, per level: for `o(b) <= o(a)`, an INFINITE arc
    (b,l) -> (a,l) for every l. It encodes "o(b) >= L[l] implies o(a) >= L[l]".
  * min-cut value = minimum total unary cost. Decode: o(v) = the largest L[l] whose chain node
    is still on the source side.

Ishikawa admits an ARBITRARY unary term -- only the PAIRWISE term must be convex, and a hard
monotone constraint is -- so the whole lexicographic objective rides in one scalar:
    1. fewest symbols moved        1_000_000 each
    2. fewest catalog rows edited  1_000 per landed field row that must move with its kind
                                   (field_construction_order_mismatch forces a field's order to
                                   EQUAL its containing kind's, so they move together)
    3. shortest distance moved     |new-old|, <= 75, tie-break only
TERM 3 IS NOT COSMETIC. Without it the cut is indifferent between two legal values and parks
symbols at the bottom label. Formally optimal, semantically vandalism -- construction_order names
a construction phase. It is exactly what turns "AuditTicket 40 -> 5" into "AuditTicket 40 -> 6".

=== 3. WHICH EDGES GO IN. BOTH POPULATIONS, DELIBERATELY ===
  S1 every retaining reference the Appendix A SOURCE spells between two symbols that already
     carry an order -- INCLUDING paths whose interior is still unminted. Contract the unminted
     interior out and keep the endpoint constraint: that interior is forced into the window when
     it lands, so a direct-only repair re-manufactures this bead's next generation.
  S2 every retaining edge already in the catalog's LANDED field rows. The landed graph is NOT a
     subset of the source graph, and an S1-only repair can turn the loader RED.

=== 4. THE BALANCED-SCAN FLOOR, WHICH COST ME A LANDED VALUE ===
Tranche 1 read a reference with `strip_prefix("StrongRef<")`. A repeated member's census
exact_type is spelled `[StrongRef<T<Local>>]` -- it starts with `[`, fails the prefix test, and
its edge is DROPPED. fgdb-suhb traces exactly that under-reading to a violation already frozen in
the tree (a12 minted ResourceLedgerTransition against a ceiling computed from five of its six
consumers). A MATCHER THAT MISSES AN EDGE REPORTS A WIDER WINDOW THAN EXISTS, AND IT LOOKS
EXACTLY LIKE A PASS.
The floor, use nothing weaker:
  * scan for a retaining wrapper ANYWHERE in the type string, not as a prefix;
  * require the preceding byte to be a NON-IDENTIFIER, so `CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<` is never
    read as a bare `StrongRef<`;
  * take the inner type with a BALANCED ANGLE SCAN, so `StrongRef<T<Local>>` yields `T<Local>`
    and not `T<Local`;
  * the nine RETAINING wrappers (from fgdb-owlp, not re-derived): StrongRef,
    CertifiedRemoteStrongRef, StrongCommandRef, StrongMarkerRef, StrongCiphertextRef,
    StrongGlobalCommandRef, StrongShardCommandRef, ConditionalCoordinateRef, ConditionalMarkerRef.
    MarkerRef, CommandRef, WeakDigest and the *Identity wrappers are EXCLUDED -- bare identity
    imposes no ordering obligation (the a01 identity-is-not-reachability law).
Consequence, measured: widening the matcher added 50 constraint edges and 5 symbols. 17 of
tranche 1's 18 landed values survived it unchanged; ONE did not. GcDecisionRecord went 15 -> 25
under the narrow reading and 25 was still below its floor of 40. Nothing landed in a wrong
direction; one value was an under-correction, caught before its field body froze it.

=== 5. THE BATCHING LAW: WHOLE COMPONENTS, NEVER PART OF ONE ===
Batch = weakly connected component of the constraint graph restricted to the moved symbols. Any
SUBSET OF COMPONENTS is safe, and here is the proof, because it is what lets you defer another
pane's slice without deferring the whole repair:
  * an edge between two moved symbols is INSIDE one component, so both ends move together;
  * an edge from a moved symbol to an unmoved one still holds -- the unmoved value is unchanged
    and the full solution satisfied it;
  * two unmoved symbols cannot be on a violated edge, since a violated edge forces at least one
    end to move.
PARTIAL-WITHIN-A-COMPONENT IS NOT SAFE: it can violate an edge that was fine before, and if that
edge is landed the loader goes RED.

=== 6. WHAT NO INTEGER CAN FIX ===
Tarjan the source graph. Symbols in a NONTRIVIAL SCC and symbols with a SOURCE SELF-EDGE are not
assignment defects -- a reference SPELLING must change, which is an owner ruling. Note the trap:
all three current cycles sit at CO-EQUAL orders and are therefore GREEN, because co-equality
satisfies dag_future_result. It does NOT satisfy dag_cycle, which walks the EDGE SET alone. They
go red the moment their field rows land and no order will save them. Do not "fix" them with
integers.

=== 7. VERIFY LIKE THIS, AND KEEP THE NEGATIVE CONTROL ===
Rebuild the lib FROM THE TREE YOU ARE MEASURING -- a stale rlib silently passed and then failed
on byte-identical inputs for me today, and reported 7 phantom pin drifts against a clean HEAD.
    rustc --edition=2024 --crate-type=lib --crate-name registry_check -O \
        tools/registry-check/src/lib.rs -o lib.rlib            (~15s)
    <build src/main.rs against it> ; ck all --root <tree>       (~0.6s, covers every projection)
    rustc --edition=2024 --test tests/identity.rs --extern registry_check=lib.rlib   (~9s)
    rustc --edition=2024 --test src/lib.rs                      (~2.5s -- the aNN binding-contract
                                                                 tests hard-assert orders and fire
                                                                 ONLY here)
NEGATIVE CONTROL IN EVERY BATCH, non-negotiable: on a COPY of the exact post-repair tree, flip one
released lifecycle status. projection_registry_assignment_drift and registry_assignment_drift must
fire, exit 1. A batch that passes because the check stopped looking is the failure mode this
codebase produced repeatedly. `order-repair-apply.py --negative-control <Kind>` does it.

=== 8. THE TEST PINS MOVE WITH THE CORRECTION ===
Slice-landing tests hard-assert orders as landing witnesses. They are landing evidence for a
slice, not a durable contract, so they move with the repair and carry the reason inline. Four so
far, in tools/registry-check/tests/identity.rs and src/appendix_a.rs (the aNN
binding_contract_tests). Watch for SHARED literals: a12's table asserts one `construction_order`
value for four rows across two owners, which is only correct while those owners share an order.

=== 9. TOOLS, ALL WITH CONTROLS INLINE ===
  ~/.claude/projects/-data-projects-frankengraphdb/tools/order-mincut-repair.rs
      <root>                  measurement + batches
      <root> --emit           NAME<TAB>OLD<TAB>NEW
      <root> --explain <Sym>  the exact source field spellings behind BOTH bounds, so no move
                              rests on an unread census
      Controls C1-C8 inline, including C6 (the emitted assignment satisfies EVERY edge), C7 (the
      min-cut value equals the recomputed cost of the decoded labelling -- the flow did not lie)
      and C8 (nothing moves that has no constraint path to a violation). ~0.5s.
  .../tools/order-repair-apply.py       asserts the expected OLD value at every site and the total
                                        row count against the plan, so a partial application is
                                        impossible; carries --negative-control <Kind>
  .../tools/order-repair-testpins.py    the four test literals moved so far, with reasons
  .../tools/oicl-order-repair/          movesA2.tsv, movesB2.tsv, all9.tsv, and
                                        residual-at-7290298.txt (the 23 remaining moves, by
                                        component, with the a08 self-edge sequencing warning)

title: OWNER RULING: tag_wire_type is u8 on 340/340 landed unions, including two the source calls u16
description:
A systematic divergence between the source spelling and the registry, surfaced
by landing 19 a21 unions. I followed precedent and am flagging it rather than
settling it silently in either direction.

## The measurement

* Landed ordinary unions with `tag_wire_type = "u8"`: 340. With `"u16"`: 0.
  The checker admits both (`bad_field` rejects anything else), so the u16
  vocabulary exists and has never been used.
* Ten of the nineteen unions landed in 3f34b52 are spelled `u16` in the source:
  AuthenticatedDurableCapabilityStatusBasis,
  DurableCapabilityConsumerTerminalTarget,
  DurableCapabilityCurrentMembershipProof, DurableCapabilityCurrentSecurityBasis,
  DurableCapabilityLegacyCurrentMembershipProof, DurableCapabilityLegacyReplayRef,
  DurableCapabilityPresentedReplayRef, DurableCapabilityStatusClassification,
  DurableCapabilityStatusPresentedReplayRef,
  TimeAuthorityUnavailableStatusEvidence.
* The divergence PREDATES this landing. Two a05 symbols the source also spells
  `u16` -- `PostActivationCapabilityMigrationInitialSubject` ("the exact
  creation-only `u16` union") and `PostActivationCapabilityMigrationSpec` ("the
  disjoint outer `u16` union") -- are landed at u8.

## Why I landed at u8

`PostActivationCapabilityMigrationInitialSubject` embeds
`prebuilt_successor_replay:DurableCapabilityPresentedReplayRef` by value. Landing
the embedded union at u16 while its embedder is u8 would have made an object
disagree with the object it contains, on a field inside the append-only
durable_fields assignment pin. Every arm tag in the tranche fits u8 (max 0x000c),
so u8 is not lossy today.

## The ruling needed

Either (a) `tag_wire_type` on an ordinary-union row denotes the CATALOG's tag
encoding for a closed-tagged union and the source's `u16` describes the object's
own tag field elsewhere -- in which case 340/340 u8 is correct and this bead
closes with that sentence written down; or (b) it is the wire tag width, in which
case 12 landed rows (2 a05 + 10 a21) are a durable-format defect and need
re-tagging together, with the a05 embedder/embedded pair moving as one.

## Cost of (b)

`tag_wire_type` IS inside the durable_fields assignment pin
(`ordinary-union|...|{tag_wire_type}|...`), so re-tagging is a 12-row edit plus
one pin re-freeze -- cheap while all 12 rows are `status = "reserved"`, and it
only gets expensive after activation. Deciding this before any of them activates
is the whole point of filing it now.

Filed by pane4 from fgdb-a21-residue-union-shapes-afpl.

=== now points hard at option (b)

--- 1. RE-MEASURED POPULATION: "0 u16" IS NO LONGER TRUE ---

      tag_wire_type = "u8"     371
      tag_wire_type = "u16"      1   <-- BoltBookmarkRequestKind

The bead says "340 u8 / 0 u16 ... the u16 vocabulary exists and has never been
used". It has now been used. `BoltBookmarkRequestKind` landed at u16 in dec248a
(pane7, feat(a21), fgdb-replay-security-residue-class-rulings-xfrc), hours after

source — the tree now contains BOTH spellings, chosen by two different panes on
the same undecided field within one night. That is the concrete harm of an
unpinned durable-format choice, demonstrated rather than predicted.

    max arm_tag across all 372 unions: 0x000c   (u8 ceiling 0x00ff)
    most arms on any one union:        12
So nothing in the tree NEEDS u16 today, by a factor of 21.

--- 2. WHAT ENFORCES A WIDTH: NOTHING ---

Every reader of `tag_wire_type` in the checker:
  identity.rs:2469  vocabulary only — `bad_field` unless u8|u16. Both accepted.
  identity.rs:2605  maximum_arm_tag — u8 -> 0xff, u16 -> 0xbfff. The only
                    semantic consequence.
  identity.rs:1293  inside the durable_fields assignment-pin transcript.
  appendix_a.rs:13865 written to the projection; four inline test sites assert
                    `== "u8"` on specific unions, i.e. on their own fixtures,
                    not as a registry-wide law.

MUTATION-PROVED, both directions, against the real registry:

    CONTROL   real registry, raw                        0 violations
    CONTROL   real registry, after re-freeze            0 violations
    MUT A     flip a landed union u8 -> u16
                raw                                     ["registry_assignment_drift"]
                after re-freeze                         []            <-- accepted
    MUT B     a NEW ordinary union authored at u16
                after re-freeze                         []            <-- accepted
    VACUITY   tag_wire_type = "u32"                     ["bad_field"] <-- reader is live
    CONSEQ    u8 union, arm_tag 0x0100                  ["code_invalid"]
    CONSEQ    same arm_tag under u16                    []

Read the last two together: the field is NOT inert. It decides whether 0x0100 is
a legal arm tag. So the choice is load-bearing durable format, and the only thing
standing between it and a silent wrong answer is the assignment pin — which
reports THAT a row changed, never that its width is wrong, and which the author
re-freezes as the normal part of landing. After that re-freeze, u16 is accepted
with zero violations. Nothing anywhere compares tag_wire_type against a required
value.

--- 3. THE SOURCE EVIDENCE, AND IT DECIDES (a) vs (b) ---

I classified every non-nested occurrence of all 13 symbols. Where the source
states a width, it states it about the symbol ITSELF, in its own clause:

  u16  L2693  AuthenticatedDurableCapabilityStatusBasis      "is the embedded role-closed `u16` union"
  u16  L2657  DurableCapabilityConsumerTerminalTarget        "is a generated closed `u16` union with one catalog-stable arm per ..."
  u16  L2635  DurableCapabilityCurrentMembershipProof        "is the exact same-role `u16` union"
  u16  L2635  DurableCapabilityLegacyCurrentMembershipProof  "is the migration-only `u16` union"
  u16  L2633  DurableCapabilityLegacyReplayRef               "is the exact Local-only `u16` union"
  u16  L2633  DurableCapabilityPresentedReplayRef            "is a closed `u16` union with exactly twelve arms"
  u16  L2695  DurableCapabilityStatusClassification          "is the inline `u16` union"
  u16  L2693  DurableCapabilityStatusPresentedReplayRef      "is the exact `u16` union"
  u16  L2695  TimeAuthorityUnavailableStatusEvidence         "is the embedded closed `u16` failure union"
  u16  L1642  PostActivationCapabilityMigrationInitialSubject "is the exact creation-only `u16` union"
  u16  L1642  PostActivationCapabilityMigrationSpec          "is the disjoint outer `u16` union"
  --          DurableCapabilityCurrentSecurityBasis          "is the exact embedded two-arm union"  (NO width)
  --          BoltBookmarkRequestKind                        "exactly 0x0001 Begin|0x0002 Run; all other NESTED TAGS are reserved-invalid"  (NO width)

  CONTROLS: the reader finds the sentence the source literally calls "the exact
  creation-only `u16` union", and finds zero occurrences of a fabricated symbol.

  A METHOD CORRECTION, because I got this wrong first and it matters. My initial
  read of four symbols found them as `field:Symbol` payload references inside an
  enclosing u16 union, and I was about to report that the source's `u16` always
  belongs to the ENCLOSING union — which would have argued for (a). That was a
  sampling error: those were later, nested occurrences. Each of those symbols
  ALSO has its own dedicated declaring sentence, quoted above. Checking the
  matched windows instead of trusting the first hit reversed the conclusion.

THE RESULT: in all 11 cases where the source states a width, the registry
contradicts it. And the single row that uses the u16 vocabulary is one of the two
where the source states NO width. Source and registry agree in ZERO of the 13
cases where either speaks.

That is very hard to read as (a). Under (a) — "tag_wire_type denotes the
catalog's tag encoding, and the source's u16 describes something else" — one
would expect the source's u16 to attach to a different subject. It does not; it
attaches to these symbols by name, in the copula, eleven times.

--- 4. THE OBJECTION THAT MOTIVATED u8 DISSOLVES UNDER (b) ---

pane4 landed at u8 partly because `PostActivationCapabilityMigrationInitialSubject`
embeds `DurableCapabilityPresentedReplayRef` by value, and landing the embedded
union at u16 under a u8 embedder would make an object disagree with the object it
contains. Under (b) that mismatch does not arise: the source declares BOTH at u16
(L1642 and L2633). Consistency and source-fidelity point the same way.

--- 5. COST, RESTATED AT TODAY'S TREE ---

  (a) u8 is correct, source `u16` means something else:
      0 rows change. Cost is one sentence written down — PLUS a decision about
      BoltBookmarkRequestKind, which is now u16 and would become the only row
      violating the sentence. So (a) is no longer free: it is 1 row + 1 pin
      re-freeze.

  (b) `u16` is the wire tag width:
      11 rows u8 -> u16 (the list above), and BoltBookmarkRequestKind is the
      open question in the other direction — the source states no width for it
      and its tags are 0x0001..0x0002, so it either stays u16 by author's choice
      or moves to u8 for consistency with every other width-silent union.
      Either way: 11 or 12 rows + one durable_fields pin re-freeze.
      All rows are `status = "reserved"`, so this is still cheap. It stops being
      cheap at activation.

  Either ruling costs a pin re-freeze now. Doing nothing costs the next pane a
  third arbitrary choice.

--- 6. WHAT I DID NOT DO ---

I did not re-tag anything and did not add a width law. Both would settle the
ruling, and the ruling is not mine. I also did not "fix" BoltBookmarkRequestKind:
pane7 landed it deliberately under xfrc and it is defensible under (a).

Verified by the standalone rustc path only; no cargo, no target tree.

title: Five scripts/ deliverables present as gates but are in no runner and no registry, carrying hard-pinned counts that silently rot
description:
FINDING — mock/placeholder sweep (pane4, 2026-07-26). Ranked #3.

## What they claim

Five shell deliverables under `scripts/` present as gates. They carry every
signal of one: `set -euo pipefail`, a banner comment describing what they prove,
`mktemp -d` evidence directories, PASS/FAIL counters, and hard-pinned expected
counts. Reading the directory, they look like the W1 half of the gate suite.

## What they actually are

Nothing runs them and nothing registers them. Cross-referencing every tracked
`scripts/*.sh` against all in-repo references (excluding the file itself):

  - `scripts/w1_bigint_e2e.sh`                  -> referenced by NOTHING
  - `scripts/w1_codec_scalar_e2e.sh`            -> referenced by NOTHING
  - `scripts/w1_codec_pipeline_scalar_e2e.sh`   -> referenced by NOTHING
  - `scripts/bead_provenance_preflight.sh`      -> referenced by NOTHING
  - `scripts/w1_foundation_types_e2e.sh`        -> referenced only by
        `crates/fgdb-delta-types/examples/foundation_transcript.rs` (a doc
        mention, not an invocation)

None of the five appears in `scripts/check.sh`. None has a row in
`registries/checker_index.toml` — unlike the seven registered script artifacts,
these are absent from the registry entirely, so they are not even covered by
the (weak) file-existence liveness proof.

## Why this is worse than dead code

They carry hard-pinned magic numbers that silently rot as the crates they
"gate" evolve, and nothing will ever notice:

  - `w1_codec_pipeline_scalar_e2e.sh:62`  `wc -l` must equal 67
  - `w1_codec_pipeline_scalar_e2e.sh:71`  `grep -c` must equal 64
  - `w1_codec_pipeline_scalar_e2e.sh:79`  `grep -c` must equal 2
  - `w1_codec_pipeline_scalar_e2e.sh:103` `wc -l` must equal 68
  - `w1_codec_scalar_e2e.sh:55`           `wc -l` must equal 5

    move it out of `scripts/` into a clearly-labelled evidence directory.

`checker_index.toml` row. That law is cheap and closes the class.

title: seal/publish must chunk pending by MAX_BLOCK_ENTRIES, not only the property-row ceiling
description: The aubf/wlxe early-seal skip lets same-seq pending grow past 256 and claims publish/seal already splits oversized pending into conforming blocks. seal() only splits a descriptor family on MAX_PROPERTY_PATCH_ROWS (255 propertied). A 257-entry same-family propertyless run (the aubf fixture) therefore hits encode_block ImplausibleEntryCount. seal_vertices() dumps the whole pending map into one encode_patch, so 257 vertices fail the same way. compact.rs pack_retained already cuts on both ceilings; the writer must match.
close_reason: seal() now cuts a descriptor family at MAX_BLOCK_ENTRIES or MAX_PROPERTY_PATCH_ROWS, matching pack_retained. seal_vertices() chunks at MAX_PATCH_ROWS and sorts by span before commit. Publish tests lock 257 same-family edges and 257 vertices.

Every one becomes a hard violation the moment its field body is modelled.

  OWNER TimeAuthorityRegistry<Role:AuthorityOwningRole> @21 — six distinct violating targets, all reached through the .profiles indexed-map interiors: TimeAuthorityIssuanceFence@27, RoleTimeBoundSubjectInventoryClosure<Role>@40, RoleTimeIssuanceReservationClosure<Role>@41, TimeAuthorityDrainHold<Role>@55, TimeAuthorityEpochTransitionRecord<Role>@60, TimeAuthorityTransitionTerminalSummary<Role>@65. No order satisfies both, so the interiors CANNOT become flat or nested strong field rows at any order. They must either be covered by union arms (no DAG edge is created by an arm payload digest) or held indirectly.

  OWNER ControlCommand @10 -> PayloadAvailabilityCertificate@20. This one is NOT a16 and NOT mine. It is an independent instance of the same class in another slice, and it is the evidence that the hazard is structural rather than an a16 quirk — whoever owns ControlCommand should be told before they model its body. I am not touching it.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND a16: the checker cannot warn about any of these today. The DAG law is enforced over field ROWS, and a census key with no row contributes no edge, so a slice can look completely clean while carrying an unsatisfiable ordering that only detonates when someone does the honest modelling work. A cheap standing guard would be to run this latent-violation probe as a checker law over census strong references rather than only over landed rows — that would surface the contradiction at mint time, when the order is still free to choose, instead of at field-body time when it is frozen. I would file that as its own bead, but bead creation needs the pin re-freeze and therefore the catalog token.

THE RESOLUTION SPACE IS UNCHANGED but the preferred option is now clearer. (a) Teach the census the `field[key -> A|B]` indexed-map union spelling so .profiles yields a union plus six arms, whose payload digests cover the interiors and create no DAG edges; the Registry stays at 21 and no new kind is minted. This is the most faithful to the source and it reuses the exact mechanism I2a/I6a/I6b already rely on, but it perturbs the frozen census and therefore every slice's candidate counts and sha pins. (b) Mint the map value as its own entry schema at order >= 65, held INLINE by the Registry and committed by its body digest — no parser change, no DAG edge, Registry stays at 21. Holding entries by StrongRef instead would reintroduce the contradiction, so inline is the only workable form. (c) Weakening the interior refs is wrong: a registry administering live profiles plainly means to retain them, and that would be identity-is-not-reachability applied backwards. I recommend (a), with (b) as the fallback if the census change is judged too expensive, and I am still not deciding it — it is either a catalog-wide parser change or a change to a released kind's object graph.

SCOPE OF THE BLOCK, unchanged: all 29 of TimeAuthorityRegistry's uncovered field keys (6 flat plus 23 interior) wait on this ruling. It is the second-largest uncovered owner in a16.

title: Arena budget: alignment padding derives from runtime heap base address — fit decisions nondeterministic across heap states
description: crates/fgdb-unsafe-arena/src/region.rs alloc_block (~:777-798): pad = (align − (chunk.as_ptr().addr() % align)) % align uses the RUNTIME BASE ADDRESS of the globally-allocated chunk. Global allocator guarantees only 16-byte alignment; MAX_BLOCK_ALIGN is 64. PROVEN by out-of-repo probe: a 512B chunk lands at base%64 ∈ {0,16,32,48} depending on live chunks, producing BOTH fit outcomes for one (512B/align=64, len) request — a pre-existing design flaw (predates e1k6's contract tests, whose observed padding is itself heap-history-dependent). Fix sketch (ArenaBudget scout): canonical chunk window — over-allocate by MAX_BLOCK_ALIGN−1, record base_pad once, set bump origin at base_pad so usable base ≡ 0 (mod 64); charge prologue as fixed MAX_BLOCK_ALIGN−1 constant to alignment_padding_bytes. Also makes len>chunk_bytes pre-check fully decide BlockLargerThanChunk BEFORE allocation. Needs RoseForest's sign-off (their e1k6 contract lane). Minors: BlockLargerThanChunk reports len: pad+len conflating padding into block length; tombstone pop before fallible reserves in best-effort shrink.

PROPOSAL: add a checker law over CENSUS strong references, not just landed rows — for every census field whose exact_type strong-references a minted kind, require target.construction_order <= owner.construction_order even when no field row exists yet. Expect it to fire on the 14 above, so landing it means resolving or explicitly waiving those first; the waiver list is the honest interim state and is far better than silence.

EXHAUSTIVE CATALOG-WIDE CONSTRUCTION-ORDER SWEEP — complete result, all slices, read-only analysis off the token, measured against the cf58ccb snapshot.

METHOD, and the gap it closed in my own earlier number. Three reference populations were swept, because each is enforced differently: (A) landed field rows, (B) landed reference-union arms — both already enforced by dag_future_result — and (C) census references with no landed row, which NOTHING enforces. My first measurement matched only the literal `StrongRef<` spelling; this sweep matches all nine retaining wrapper spellings (StrongRef, CertifiedRemoteStrongRef, StrongCommandRef, StrongMarkerRef, StrongCiphertextRef, StrongGlobalCommandRef, StrongShardCommandRef, ConditionalCoordinateRef, ConditionalMarkerRef). Non-retaining identity spellings — MarkerRef, CommandRef, WeakDigest, the *Identity wrappers — are deliberately EXCLUDED: they are bare identity with no traversal, so they impose no ordering obligation. That is the a01 identity-is-not-reachability law used as the sweep's own admission rule.

THE LAW, stated exactly, because the brief slightly overstated it: dag_future_result fires on `target.construction_order > containing.construction_order`. Strictly greater. EQUAL orders are legal and common — a16 alone has twelve kinds at order 27 — so a sweep for `>=` would report false positives. I report strict violations as the defect set and equal-order pairs separately as zero-slack information.

RESULT 1 — STRICT VIOLATIONS: 14 witnesses, 7 DISTINCT EDGES, 2 HOSTS, 2 SLICES. (Each edge appears twice because the census records both the aggregate member type and the specific nested path; they are one edge counted at two granularities.)
  a10  ControlCommand@10 -> PayloadAvailabilityCertificate@20
       via ControlCommand.payload_availability_certificate_ref
  a16  TimeAuthorityRegistry<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>@21 -> six targets, all through the .profiles indexed map:
         TimeAuthorityIssuanceFence@27, RoleTimeBoundSubjectInventoryClosure@40,
         RoleTimeIssuanceReservationClosure@41, TimeAuthorityDrainHold@55,
         TimeAuthorityEpochTransitionRecord@60, TimeAuthorityTransitionTerminalSummary@65
ZERO violations came from populations (A) or (B). Every one is census-latent. That is the headline: the checker is doing its job perfectly on everything it can see, and 100% of the defect lives in the population it cannot see.

RESULT 2 — CLASSIFICATION, and it is the same verdict for both, reached independently.
  * NOT an ORDER error. I checked whether either host can simply be re-ordered, deriving the window from BOTH directions as required. ControlCommand needs >= 20, but it is retained from above by CommitCapsule@10 and LogicalCommandRecord through landed reference-union arms, so it is pinned <= 10. TimeAuthorityRegistry needs >= 65, but its consumers pin it <= 23 (TimeAuthorityObservationImport@23 in census; TimeAuthorityEpochTransitionRecord@60 landed). BOTH windows are empty. NEITHER violation is fixable by re-ordering, and there is no minimal re-assignment to compute — that is the answer to the re-ordering question, and it is a negative one.
  * a16 is a SCHEMA-SHAPE error: `.profiles` is written `profiles[profile_oid -> A|B|...]`, an indexed map the census does not recognise as a union, so its six retained targets surface as nested field keys instead of arm interiors. Arms would create no DAG edge at all. Fix is fgdb-ovok: teach the census the indexed-map spelling, or mint the map value as an inline entry schema.
  * a10 is REFERENCE-STRENGTH, most likely. ControlCommand is a command; a payload-availability certificate is evidence ABOUT a command's payload, produced independently and later. A command retaining a certificate that is constructed after it is precisely the "future result" the law names. The natural reading is that the command should carry the certificate's IDENTITY, not reachability to it — a weak digest or a bare identity rather than a StrongRef. That is an a10 call and I am not making it; flagging it to the a10 owner.

RESULT 3 — THE GRAPH: 68 nodes, 76 edges, and it does NOT layer cleanly. Kahn leaves three nodes undrained, and the reason matters:
  * PreparedCommitRecord.predecessor_ref -> PreparedCommitRecord (SELF-EDGE)
  * TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role>.predecessor_ref -> TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation (SELF-EDGE)
  * CheckpointStateVector is NOT itself defective — it is merely DOWNSTREAM of the first, through a landed reference-union arm CheckpointStateVector@35 -> PreparedCommitRecord@12 which is perfectly legal (12 <= 35). It never drains only because its predecessor never does.
The two self-edges are the banked `predecessor_ref` hazard, and this sweep shows it is not an a16 quirk: the identical pattern exists in PreparedCommitRecord in another slice. Per the cycle rule these are schema-shape errors, not ordering errors, and the fix is the same a01 law — a predecessor link is lineage to be COMPARED, never traversed, so it must be weak_digest or conditional, never a flat strong field. Modelled as strong it trips dag_self_edge. Once both are reclassified the retaining graph is acyclic and layers cleanly.

RESULT 4 — ZERO-SLACK EQUAL ORDERS: 4, all legal, all worth knowing because they have no room to absorb a future change: CommitCapsule@10 -> CommitCommand@10, CommitCapsule@10 -> ControlCommand@10, RemoteRetentionGrantSpec@20 -> PayloadAvailabilityCertificate@20, RootManifest@40 -> LogicalStateRoot@40.

WHO MUST CHANGE WHAT

MECHANISM 1 — GENERIC-SIGNATURE ESCAPE (mine, fixed, gated). identity.rs:2680 resolves a field row's owner by EXACT name while logical_by_name is keyed by BARE family, so every [[field]] row whose containing_schema carries a generic signature silently skips the ENTIRE construction-DAG block: dag_self_edge, dag_future_result, and the edge collection feeding dag_cycle. This is a plain defect, not a design gap — the sibling field-resolution law at identity.rs:1556 already normalises through generic_free_family(); the DAG law simply failed to.
  MEASURED at d0570ea: 75 retaining field rows are landed and 15 of them escape the law today, over 5 owners (TimeAuthorityEpochTransitionRecord<Role:AuthorityOwningRole> 6, ContinuityAuthorityObservationImport<Role> 3, TimeAuthorityDrainHold<Role:AuthorityOwningRole> 3, RestoreSourceLeaseRecord<Role:AuthorityOwningRole> 2, MacaroonRootIssuanceRecord<Role:AuthorityOwningRole> 1).

Zero change to any landed row's validity — registry-check identity and appendix both stay at 0 violations, which independently CONFIRMS the sweep's population-(A) result that those 15 rows were all genuinely clean.
  ALSO MEASURED AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED: the same exact-name spelling appears on the reference-union arm path (the containing lookup guarding the arm-side dag_future_result). I wrote a test for it and the test PASSED UNPATCHED, which means that path is already subsumed: the field DAG loop expands union arm targets through the anchor field, and union anchors are REQUIRED to be strong/conditional with no target_schema_id. So arm targets always reach the DAG through the anchor, and once the field-side lookup is normalised they are covered. I dropped the change rather than ship an untestable one-liner.

MECHANISM 2 — CENSUS LATENCY (THIS BEAD, NOT FIXED BY ME, STILL FULLY OPEN). The DAG law is enforced over landed field ROWS and landed reference-union ARMS. A census strong reference with NO landed row contributes no edge, so a slice can look completely clean while carrying an unsatisfiable ordering that only detonates when someone does the honest modelling work — at which point the order is already frozen and the window may be empty. My fix does NOTHING for this. It makes the law see generic-signed rows THAT EXIST; it does not make the law see references that have no row yet. Those are orthogonal, and closing owlp requires the second.

WHY THE DISTINCTION IS LOAD-BEARING RATHER THAN PEDANTIC: the sweep found ZERO violations in the landed populations and 100% of the defect in the census-latent population. So after my fix the checker will still be silent on every one of the 7 distinct violating edges and both self-edges. The measured pass rate does not improve at all. What improves is that the wrong shape can no longer LAND silently once someone does model it — the hole was the mechanism by which a bad row would have been accepted, which is why I fixed it first. But the early-warning property this bead asks for is untouched.

THE HONEST WAIVER SET TO LAND WITH THIS BEAD, so whoever implements it is not surprised by a red gate — expect exactly these to fire, and note that only ONE is an ordering problem at all:
  STRICT FUTURE-RESULT EDGES (7 distinct, 14 witnesses; each edge appears twice because the census records both the aggregate member type and the specific nested path):
    a10  CommitCommand@10 -> PayloadAvailabilityCertificate@20  (via the flat payload_availability_certificate_ref at a10:1912; the sweep originally mis-attributed this to ControlCommand, whose member is a closed union None|Some and therefore takes the no-DAG-edge union route instead)
    a16  TimeAuthorityRegistry<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>@21 -> six targets, all through the .profiles indexed map:
           TimeAuthorityIssuanceFence@27, RoleTimeBoundSubjectInventoryClosure@40, RoleTimeIssuanceReservationClosure@41,
           TimeAuthorityDrainHold@55, TimeAuthorityEpochTransitionRecord@60, TimeAuthorityTransitionTerminalSummary@65
  SELF-EDGES (2): PreparedCommitRecord.predecessor_ref (a10:1922), TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role>.predecessor_ref (a16:2210)
  ZERO-SLACK EQUAL ORDERS (4, all LEGAL — a sweep written for >= instead of > will report these as false positives): CommitCapsule@10 -> CommitCommand@10, CommitCapsule@10 -> ControlCommand@10, RemoteRetentionGrantSpec@20 -> PayloadAvailabilityCertificate@20, RootManifest@40 -> LogicalStateRoot@40.

TWO IMPLEMENTATION WARNINGS FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS BEAD:
 1. STATE THE LAW AS STRICTLY GREATER. dag_future_result fires on target.construction_order > containing.construction_order. Equal orders are legal and common — a16 alone has twelve kinds at order 27. A census-level sweep written with >= will produce four false positives on the list above.
 2. ADMIT ONLY RETAINING WRAPPERS. Match all nine retaining spellings (StrongRef, CertifiedRemoteStrongRef, StrongCommandRef, StrongMarkerRef, StrongCiphertextRef, StrongGlobalCommandRef, StrongShardCommandRef, ConditionalCoordinateRef, ConditionalMarkerRef) and EXCLUDE the non-retaining identity spellings (MarkerRef, CommandRef, WeakDigest, the *Identity wrappers): those are bare identity with no traversal and impose no ordering obligation. That is the a01 identity-is-not-reachability law used as the sweep's own admission rule. Matching only the literal "StrongRef<" spelling undercounts, which is how the first pass on this got a smaller number.

Enforcing at mint time is valuable precisely BECAUSE the order is still free then; enforcing at field-body time, which is all we have today, arrives after the choice is frozen. TerminalWriteResultPreparation's own window is > 20 (it references
LocalPrepareAdmissionSpec@20 and LocalAttemptRegistration@15) with no upper bound
from any landed row, so 25 satisfies every constraint derivable when it landed and
is not the defect. The infeasibility is inherited from CommitCommand sitting at 10
while its body reaches a construct at 20. Fix (a) and (b)+(c) become satisfiable;
change my 25 and (a) is still violated.

=== 3. THE INSTRUMENT, BECAUSE THE FIRST ANSWER WAS WRONG ===
I first read (c) as a false positive — plan line 1530 also NARRATES
"the final rebased effect directory, optional TerminalWriteResultPreparation, and
TxnOutcomePreparationRecord are constructed", and a line-granular reference probe
cannot tell narration from membership when one line defines several schemas. So I
built a BODY-SCOPED extractor: match `Name` is `BODY` and read StrongRefs only
from inside that backtick-quoted body. 927 definitions, 952 sites.
It refuted me. The member is real — `terminal_write_result:None|Prepared{...}` is

    TxnOutcomePreparationRecord -> TxnOutcomeRecord   expect present  PASS

this defect class. These plan lines routinely define several schemas and narrate

line will produce both false positives and false negatives. Scope to the body.

The extractor makes a catalog-wide sweep cheap: for every landed logical kind,

title: SPINE increment: delete_edge/delete_vertex on WriteBatch — engine-derived before-images, oracle-validated at replay
description: Split out of fgdb-w5-effects-normal-form-819 at the seam the j0vu/3xoi precedent names: strata is delete-ready (9bce55b) but the spine's WriteBatch exposes creates only, so nothing can be deleted end-to-end. This bead adds the thinnest REAL surface: WriteBatch::delete_edge/delete_vertex whose DeltaRows carry ENGINE-DERIVED before-images — an independent reimplementation of the element-version chain (domain fgdb.reference.element-version.v1: hash(domain||pred-tag||prev||len||canonical row bytes)) folded in rebuild() and per-commit, and vertex cascades taken from the tier-D writer's live map (both directions, ascending EId). title: Canonical row order is not applicability order: multi-write transactions deterministically fail at commit (NetEffectNormalForm absent)
description:
PROBE-PROVEN at HEAD by VioletBasin (fresh-eyes scout RefDelta IMPORTANT-1, independently reproduced). Effects are emitted and workspace-applied in EVALUATION order, but LogicalDeltaTemplate::build's canonicalize (delta-types/src/canonical.rs:1010-1041) byte-sorts rows before apply_template replays them against live state. Byte order is a total order over row identity, NOT a topological order over effect dependencies: when they disagree on one target, the sorted replay's first row declares a before-image the live graph does not have, and apply refuses with the error whose own doc calls reaching it a defect.

EXACT PROBE (regression-shaped, run and watched red): basis vertex 1 with PROP=Int(5); one transaction [SetProp(v,p,3), SetProp(v,p,7)]. Evaluation emits r1={before:5, after:3}, r2={before:3, after:7} and the workspace ends p=7. The template sort orders by tag/elem/property-key/BEFORE-scalar: Int(3) < Int(5), so sorted = [r2, r1]. apply_template applies r2 first: declared before=Int(3), actual=Int(5) -> TxnError::Apply(PropertyBeforeMismatch{elem: Vertex(VId(1)), property: 100, declared: Some(Int(3)), actual: Some(Int(5))}). An ordinary 'SET p=3; SET p=7' transaction can NEVER commit whenever the first write DECREASES the value (increasing chains sort safely by accident, which is why the suite is green).

Same class, same root: LabelMembership remove-then-re-add (before:false sorts before before:true); two Counter rows on one (elem,property) sort by operation-key bytes (arbitrary vs evaluation order, and Counter before-images chain); CreateVertex+SetProp+DeleteVertex on one vid sorts Create(0x01) < DeleteVertex(0x03) < Property(0x06) -> NoSuchVertex on replay.

ROOT CAUSE: NO NetEffectNormalForm exists anywhere in the tree (grep-confirmed). canonical.rs:275 says merging same-coordinate entries 'is NetEffectNormalForm's job', delta-types/lib.rs:4-5 assigns it, and the intents layer emits raw per-intent rows — the canonicalizer's precondition (a repeat means the input never went through the normal form) is one nothing satisfies. OWNED BY: fgdb-w5-effects-normal-form-819 (open, unassigned) — this bug is that workstream's absence manifesting; dep-linked.

FIX SKETCH (the 819 design, per plan:2805 and §9.1 'finalization emits only canonical effects'): fold at finalization before canonicalize — collapse sequential Property rows per (elem,property) to {first before, last after}; same for LabelMembership per (vid,label) and ValidTime per elem; erase create-then-delete pairs and fold post-create writes into the create payload; counters collapse with Σdelta carrying the first operation key deterministically (or preserve evaluation order explicitly). After the fold the remaining rows are target-disjoint and byte-sorting is applicability-safe. DO NOT land a partial fold-only-Property patch as the answer — that is a substitute convention beside 819's assigned design; the full form is the fix.
close_reason: Owner slice fgdb-w5-effects-normal-form-819.1 closed. Probe SET p=3; SET p=7 after p=5 commits as one Property{before:5,after:7}. Engine multi-write is now fgdb-w5-effects-normal-form-819.2, not this bug.

title: Adversarial benchmark harness: publish honest §17 numbers including hostile shapes
notes:
FILED 2026-07-31 from the reality check (Phase 1 goal 11, Phase 4 Round 2c).

THE MEASURED FACT: there is NO benchmark harness anywhere in this repository. No benches/ directory,
no criterion, no timing test. §17 sets hard numeric gates -- >=8M point-reads/s across cores, p99 <15us
warm -- and the README repeats performance claims throughout. Not one of those numbers has ever been
measured. Every performance claim in this project is currently unfalsifiable, which means we cannot
even tell whether an optimization helped.

WHY THIS IS P1 AND NOT LATER. The longer we go without numbers, the more design decisions get made on
intuition and the more expensive they are to unmake. The persistence decision (fgdb-lc1t), the tier-R
layout, and the merge path all have performance consequences that are currently arguments rather than
measurements.

THE HARNESS MUST BE ADVERSARIAL, NOT CONFIRMATORY. A benchmark that measures what we happened to build
measures nothing. Required shapes, each a known way for a graph engine to fall over:
  - POWER-LAW DEGREE SKEW, so the supernode path is exercised. A uniform-degree benchmark is the single
    most common way graph databases publish numbers that do not survive contact with real data.
  - DEEP BRANCH CHAINS, since reads follow branch-parent links and the cost is per-ancestor.
  - LONG VERSION CHAINS on one key -- which currently FORCES one block per version, so this shape is
    also a block-count amplifier.
  - COLD PARTITION REOPEN, the path that reads from the store rather than from memory.
  - COMPACTION UNDER LOAD, because a compactor that is fast when idle is not a compactor.

PUBLISH THE BAD NUMBERS. A measured 400k point-reads/s against a target of 8M is PROGRESS -- it says
where we are and makes the next change measurable. An unmeasured claim of 8M is a liability. Doctrine 7
forbids reporting a non-durable benchmark mode as a result, so the harness must run against the real
durable path, and any in-memory-only figure must be labelled as such at the point of publication.

LAWS THIS BEAD OWES: the harness itself needs a correctness check -- every benchmark run must also
assert the result it computed, or a "fast" path that returns nothing looks like a win. Reuse the
fgdb-reference differential for that; it is the same instrument.

fgdb-bench is a PLANNED crate in the verification layer -- activate it rather than putting benches in
an engine crate, so the benchmark dependency surface never leaks into a shipping crate.

== FIRST HARNESS LANDED by CreamGlen 2026-08-22 at HEAD+bench (crate crates/fgdb-bench, topology row activated active/owner_bead=this bead) ==
Production runtime authority (RuntimeBuilder -> PurposeContexts::commit), real two-fsync path, every measured read asserted against the deterministic model inside the measurement region. NDJSON publication with empirical_gate_activated=false on every event: machine-local baselines, not gates (no pinned manifest yet).

PUBLISHED NUMBERS (AMD EPYC 7282, release build; /tmp/benchfinal*.ndjson):
- version-chain: 65 exact versions through 65 durable commits; 6620 bytes/version on disk; historical probe p50=11-20us p99=23-40us across all versions; cold-reverified.
- compaction-under-load: compaction publishes a replacement root in 55-64ms while a pinned reader thread completes 71-86 FULL verified history traversals concurrently — answer isolation holds under load.
- ingest-power-law / point-reads-supernode / cold-reopen: BLOCKED BY ENGINE LIMIT, see below.

## FINDING (filed as fgdb-a7sz, P1 bug)
Sustained ingest crosses the block store's 16 KiB object ceiling after ~4-6 commits REGARDLESS of batch size (blocks accumulate multiple commits; no seal-at-size policy). The over-ceiling object is made durable, the write fences, and EVERY later Database::open refuses during rebuild: the directory becomes unreopenable. Reproduced 3x. Published as shape_engine_limit events (fences_survived=1 then open refused); harness treats it as a first-class outcome per publish-the-bad-numbers.

## HARNESS MECHANICS WORTH KEEPING
- Deterministic LCG + preferential attachment (no rand in the closed universe); workload replayable, degree skew real (true supernode).
- load_model_durably() survives publish fences by reopen-and-probe and counts them as a published metric (publish_fence_reopens).
- Correctness is checked INSIDE measured regions for read shapes and immediately after load for ingest, against the model — no fast-path-that-returns-nothing can look like a win.

## REMAINING FOR THIS BEAD
- After fgdb-a7sz fixes sealing: re-run ingest/point-read/cold-reopen shapes to full completion and publish sustainable edges/s + warm p99 under skew (the §17-relevant numbers this bead exists for).
- Deep branch chains remain absent (no spine branch API).
- Manifest pinning (§16/§17 EmpiricalGate activation) is a later increment.

== PRE-a7sz NUMBERS PUBLISHED 2026-08-23 by CreamGlen (commit after fence telemetry) ==
Fixture scaled to 150 vertices / ~450 edges so root refs stay under the a7sz ceiling; config strings carry the exact fixture. ALL FIVE SHAPES NOW COMPLETE (rc=0, zero fences on the scaled fixture, zero engine-limit events):

- point-reads-supernode (FIRST PUBLISHED): 2,400 verified ops under degree skew, warm decoded cache from a real cold open. vertex lookup p50 <1us (sub-resolution). BOTH one-hop faces measured and mid-measurement verified: outbound p50=122us p95=134-135us p99=152us; inbound p50=122us p95=135us p99=152us. ops_per_s=11,967 for the full vertex+out+in probe mix, single-threaded.
- cold-reopen: open-to-first-VERIFIED-answer p50=40.5ms p95/p99=141.7ms over 5 rounds.
- version-chain: unchanged (6620 B/version; probes p50=12us p99=33us).
- compaction-under-load: 103.8ms publish with 130 full verified pinned-reader traversals concurrent.
- ingest-power-law: completes with ZERO fences at this scale (444 edges, 7 commits, 180 stored blocks); edges_per_s=23 and commit p50~976us are fsync-dominated honest durable numbers on a loaded box.

HARNESS BUG FIXED en route: the model was UNDIRECTED while Database::neighbours is OUTBOUND-only -- the stricter whole-graph warm check caught the drift; the model now tracks both faces separately and the shape measures/verifies both.

REMAINING for this bead: re-run ingest/point-reads/cold-reopen at §17-scale fixtures once fgdb-a7sz's root-format fix lands; deep branch chains still absent (no branch API); manifest pinning.

== FULL-SCALE NUMBERS 2026-08-23 by CreamGlen (post fgdb-a7sz fix, commit 5f8b9180) ==
The a7sz per-family admission landed, so the skew shapes re-ran at FULL fixture (2000 vertices / ~5994 edges / 94 durable commits) and ALL FIVE SHAPES COMPLETE with zero fences and zero engine-limit events:

- ingest-power-law: edges_per_s=162 (fsync-dominated durable path), commit p50=390us p95=454us p99=566us, bytes_per_edge=1178, stored_blocks=2349 -- 8x past the old brick point, zero fences.
- point-reads-supernode at full skew: vertex p50=6us p99=33us; BOTH faces p50~2.25ms p99~3.7ms (the supernode's neighbour list is now hundreds of entries -- honest heavy-scan reads), ops_per_s=640 for the verified vertex+out+in mix.
- cold-reopen: p50=219ms p99=223ms (full-generation decode from 2349 blocks).
- version-chain + compaction-under-load: unchanged.

The a7sz closure also means bricked pre-fix directories recover on plain Database::open. Remaining for this bead: manifest pinning toward EmpiricalGate activation (fgdb-epic-perf-4xe); deep branch chains still await a branch API.

LANDED: crates/fgdb-strata/tests/complexity_witness.rs — four witnesses over blocks_visible_at.

THE DESIGN DECISION WORTH KEEPING: op counts, not wall clock. AGENTS.md line 243 already requires exactly this — 'complexity-witness regression locks (an operator whose observed op-count exceeds its declared bound fails CI)'. A stopwatch cannot gate CI here: nondeterministic (B5 forbids it as a result) and load-sensitive on a box where ten panes compile at once. An op count is exact, diffable, and fails naming the defect. This also means the closed dependency universe costs us nothing — no criterion, no harness crate, no fgdb-bench activation needed for this half.

ONE BOUND IS DELIBERATELY BAD AND SHOULD FAIL LATER. blocks_visible_at filters on first_seq <= as_of, so it skips only blocks created AFTER the snapshot; at the frontier nothing is skipped and a point read is O(blocks in partition). That is the read amplification §6.2 answers with skip-list nodes and hub striping, unbuilt under fgdb-w3-tier-d-ctj. The witness records it as the CURRENT bound and its doc says it should fail when that lands — a witness that only ever tightens silently is not a lock.

POWER MEASURED rather than assumed, two mutations with root.rs restored byte-identical: removing the skip kills 2 of 4; the plausible WRONG skip (also filtering last_seq >= as_of — the optimization a real person would try, which silently drops old blocks still holding live entries) kills 3 of 4 including the monotonicity witness. Each witness measures a distinct property.

WHAT REMAINS ON THIS BEAD, still genuinely blocked on fgdb-j0vu: the §17 numbers themselves (>=8M point-reads/s, p99 <15us warm) and the adversarial SHAPES from the original notes — power-law degree skew, deep branch chains, long version chains, cold partition reopen, compaction under load. Those need something runnable. Consider splitting at that seam.

NOT YET WITNESSED though unblocked: decode_block and merge_neighbours have no declared bound. merge_neighbours is the more interesting one — it builds a BTreeMap keyed (eid, created_at) over every entry of every visible block, so its cost is the product of the two, and nothing pins that.
