THERE IS NO WAY TO OBTAIN A PRODUCTION Cx, SO THE SECTION 17 THROUGHPUT GATES
CANNOT BE HONESTLY MEASURED TODAY.

  - fgdb::Database::open/write/neighbours all require &CommitCx.
  - CommitCx comes only from PurposeContexts::narrow_runtime_root(&root), which
    needs a Cx<cap::All>.
  - The ONLY constructor is asupersync's Cx::for_testing(), gated
    #[cfg(any(test, feature = 'test-internals'))] (cx/cx.rs:4652). Its doc says
    outright: 'production consumers of the asupersync crate cannot construct a
    Cx<cap::All> out of band'.
  - asupersync's [features] table (Cargo.toml:77) does NOT define
    'test-internals'. So the opt-in the doc describes is not available at the
    pinned revision 3e8d08e.
  - Consequently every Cx in this repository comes from run_async_under_lab.
    RuntimeBuilder::new().build().block_on(..) exists and is used in
    fgdb-sim/tests/lab_vfs.rs, but it hands out no Cx.

WHY THAT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A DETAIL. Section 17's gates are
'>=8M point-reads/s across cores' and 'p99 <15us warm'. Both are THROUGHPUT AND
TAIL-LATENCY UNDER CONCURRENCY. The lab runtime is deterministic and
schedule-serialized, so a number produced under it cannot speak to either: real
syscalls do take real time, so std::time::Instant inside a lab run measures
something real, but it is single-threaded-under-a-deterministic-scheduler, an
understatement of unknown size. Publishing it against the section 17 targets
would compare two different quantities and would be exactly the confirmatory
benchmark this bead exists to forbid.

THE DECISION THIS BEAD NOW NEEDS, and it is a scoping decision rather than an
implementation one:
  (a) fund a production-Cx path first -- either an upstream asupersync change to
      expose 'test-internals' (or a real runtime-root API), or an fgdb-side
      runtime entry -- and only then measure the section 17 gates; or
  (b) build the harness now against the lab runtime, publish LAB-SERIALIZED
      wall-clock numbers, and label them at the point of publication as not
      comparable to the section 17 concurrency gates.
Option (b) still delivers the bead's headline value (the project's first measured
numbers, and hostile shapes exercised) but it CANNOT discharge the section 17
gates, and the bead should say so rather than appearing to.

title: Payload-bearing Union::Arm value fields cannot use tag-only gpms discriminants
description: The fgdb-gpms ruling assumes every field typed as Union::Arm is a precondition carrying only the refined tag. AuditTicketClaimRecord.owner is a counterexample: AuditTicketOwner::Operation carries global_txn_id, registration_generation, and operation_request_basis_commitment, while the record has no independent fields for the first two. Classify value-position refinements into tag-only preconditions versus payload-bearing arm values; freeze a representation and checker law that preserves the complete selected-arm payload; mutation-prove that dropping the payload fails. title: Build lifecycle-anatomy benches: command/entry counts, ordered-sync counts, byte economy
description:
## What & scope
Extra subtask split from perf-bench-core: the protocol-anatomy gates — durable read/write lifecycle counts, ordered-sync-operation counts, and the three byte-economy rows — measured by decoding the actual Chronicle stream and Raft log per operation class and byte-matching Appendix G.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Law 6 (no unpriced protocol weight) is only enforceable if something *measures* the protocol: these benches are the empirical half of the Appendix G constitution (B5). They make "the counts above are protocol counts, not aspirations" true in CI, and they price B1's identity machinery (identity-column bytes) and B2's stream economy honestly.

## Design — normative detail
Gate rows (exact): **Durable read/write lifecycles** (per Appendix G class, client-visible operations): sequenced semantic commands and total Raft log entries per operation, measured by operation class, must *equal* the Appendix G registry row where the row declares an exact count and fall within the row's declared configuration-dependent bounds where it declares a range — a measured excess is a protocol regression, not a tuning miss; durable-autocommit-read and fused-autocommit-write latency distributions reported p50/p95/p99 against the registry-derived barrier floor. Reference counts: durable autocommit read = 3 commands (`LocalAttemptRegistrationSpec::Autocommit`, `LocalReadCloseSpec`, `LocalTerminalCompletionSpec`), ~6-10 Raft entries, ~6-10 objects minted; fused autocommit write = 2 commands NotRequired / 3 Required, ~4-8 entries, ~15-20 objects; explicit N-statement commit = 5+N commands, ~2-3x(5+N) entries; `SnapshotQuery` = 0/0/0. The read is 3 because read-close semantic success waits for `LocalTerminalCompletionSpec` and no terminal result returns before `TerminalReady`; the fused write floor is 2 because `TerminalCompletion` consumes durability/visibility evidence of the commit's own publication and FG-INV-07 forbids any pre-order input naming its future applied record.

**Ordered sync operations**: count per commit and per append batch, by posture (single-node/replicated) and audit class (NotRequired/Required); must byte-match the Appendix G barrier chain *including its fusion-legality column* — in quorum-one the append-reply hard-state publication and post-apply D2 protocol publication MAY fuse into one ordered slot update; in any multi-member configuration they MUST NOT fuse; a legal fusion counts as **one** ordered sync operation, never zero.

**Byte economy**: (a) metadata bytes per small durable object, measured on the pinned small-commit fixture with component breakdown (symbol headers, MACs, index entries, key wraps); gate value provisional, derived from Appendix G's minted-object census; (b) Chronicle stream bytes per user commit, reported by class — semantic payload, maintenance, audit — for the pinned transaction mix, wired into §6.6's component breakdown; (c) identity-column bytes per live edge, by tier (Tier D and sorted sealed runs) under the canonical stable-key encoding; reverse-family blocks reported separately.

Pinned-manifest discipline: each gate is a provisional `EmpiricalGate`, activated only when its manifest pins CPU/microcode, kernel/filesystem/mount options, NVMe model/firmware + measured fsync distribution, toolchain/build, database configuration, graph/schema, transaction size and concurrency, retention/FEC/encryption/index policy, cold/warm state, result consumption, and the statistical comparison rule — plus the gate's Appendix G operation class and counting unit (client-visible requests vs internal probes). Derivability: a latency gate below its class's ordered-barrier count x pinned measured fsync p50, or a throughput gate above the apply ceiling its sequenced-command count implies, fails CI as a registry divergence (§1 constraint 12), never as a missed benchmark. The six laws bind every published number: (1) no benchmark-only semantics — durability/isolation/result consumption match the declared production mode; (2) distributions, not averages — p50/p95/p99/p99.9 + worst hot-key always reported, extreme quantiles carrying fitted-tail confidence intervals, never raw sample maxima; (3) never hide compaction — foreground latency during compaction/checkpoint/GC/index build is part of the result; (4) memory is a first-class metric — bytes per live edge include versions, indexes, witnesses, allocator slack; (5) adaptive numbers disclose their policy epoch, with the fallback's number published beside; (6) no unpriced protocol weight — every gate names its Appendix G operation class and counting unit, is checked against that row's derived floor, and any protocol-weight change updates the registry in the same change (CI rejects divergence).

## Invariants & claim types
Registry counts are exact structural claims (registry class, generation-bijection enforced); latency/byte values are `slo.toml`/`benchmark` rows keyed `{operation_class,posture,audit_class}`. FG-INV-07's text as it binds here: no pre-order input may name its own future applied record — which is why no one-command write arm can exist and the count floor is 2.

## Interactions
Consumes classes/floors from `g0-cost-registry` via `perf-cost-ci`; exercises `w2-commit-protocol` (D1/D2, certificates) and `w2-group-commit` (fusion law, per-group amortization); identity-column codecs from `w3-identity-encoding`; feeds §6.6 breakdowns owned by `w3-write-amp`. Shares the small-commit fixture with `perf-bench-core`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) A stream/log decoder harness counts sequenced commands, Raft entries, and ordered sync points per operation class; equality/range assertions against regenerated registry rows. (2) Posture matrix: quorum-one with fusion, quorum-one without, three-member — the MUST NOT fusion case is asserted to fail closed at the G0 conformance gate. (3) Latency distributions vs registry-derived floor (barrier count x pinned fsync p50); a below-floor result fails as registry divergence. (4) Byte-economy reports carry full component breakdowns; unexplained bytes > budget fail. Logging: per-operation trace of every barrier (plane, what synced, amortization credit). (5) E2E: a scripted anatomy run in CI on a small pinned fixture executes every operation class once per posture, decodes the streams, and emits a machine-readable anatomy report; each row logs {operation_class, posture, command/entry/ordered-sync counts, registered row values, verdict}, so registry conformance is auditable from the report alone.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: counting harness drifts from the real decoder — reuse `w1-generated-parsers` golden decoders. Rejected: treating counts as tunables; reporting fused barriers as zero; benchmarking marker-only paths.

## Provenance
§17 rows "Durable read/write lifecycles", "Ordered sync operations", "Byte economy" x3 (1242, 1264-1267); Appendix G (3173-3193).

title: Build core bench binaries + pinned manifests: load, ingest, point-read, scan, join, LDBC
description:
## What & scope
Implement the nine headline §17 gates as bench binaries — bin targets of the `fgdb-bench` verification crate (§18.1), built on `verif-perf-apparatus`'s deterministic harness — with pinned manifests and baselines committed as repo artifacts, variance budgets, and flamegraph-on-regression artifacts: cold bulk load, transactional ingest, point reads, sealed-run neighbor scans, 2-hop factorized count, WCOJ triangle count, LDBC SNB Interactive SF-100, LDBC Graphalytics, LDBC FinBench.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
These are the numbers the design is publicly judged by. B2: Strata's tiered adjacency must beat the Sortledton bar on transactional storage. B3: factorized/WCOJ execution within 2x of static-CSR specialists while transactional. B6: `SnapshotQuery` exists so agent-scale point reads pay zero protocol weight; this bead proves the throughput. Market: LDBC leadership runs back §15.7's papers; honest anatomy (no marker-only commit latency) differentiates from vendors who benchmark less than they durably do.

## Design — normative detail
Gate rows (exact, all provisional `EmpiricalGate`s on the 32-core/64-thread, 256 GB RAM, PCIe-4 NVMe single-node reference machine):
- **Cold bulk load** (CSV/Parquet-lite -> sealed runs): >= 40M edges/s sustained; I/O-bound framing: >= 60% of NVMe sequential-write ceiling. Counting unit: internal edge appends on the fenced bulk path.
- **Transactional ingest**: provisional >= 2M edge inserts/s for the pinned batch/txn mix; reported latency MUST include final rebase/constraint work, payload D1, root D2, configured encryption/FEC, and in replicated mode payload quorum + Raft. **No marker-only benchmark is reported as commit latency.** Operation classes: Appendix G fused-autocommit-write and explicit multi-statement commit rows.
- **Point reads** (vertex by key, 1-hop existence; `SnapshotQuery` class, client-visible requests): >= 8M lookups/s across cores; p99 < 15 us warm. Appendix G row: 0 sequenced semantic commands, 0 Raft entries, no ordered barrier — executes against the pipeline's visible endpoint under an existing admission/lease — no external authority, 0 durable objects minted (sampled Sextant decision cards are telemetry, not durable protocol objects).
- **Neighbor scans, sealed runs** (decoded-cache path): >= 500M edges/s per core; >= 10B edges/s node aggregate; memory-bandwidth-bound framing: EF+varint decode >= 4 B/edge effective.
- **2-hop factorized count** (10^8-flat-row equivalent): < 50 ms; factorization gate — the plan must NOT materialize flat rows.
- **Triangle count** (WCOJ over compressed runs, com-Orkut-class): within 2x of best published static-CSR WCOJ systems; >= 20x any pointer-chasing GDBMS. Comparators pin publication, version, dataset, configuration.
- **LDBC SNB Interactive SF-100**: full compliance run; throughput >= 3x Neo4j, >= 1.5x best published embedded engine on the reference class.
- **LDBC Graphalytics** (BFS/PR/WCC/CDLP/LCC/SSSP): within 1.5x of dedicated static analytics engines *on transactional storage* — the Sortledton bar, beaten.
- **LDBC FinBench** (write-heavy, temporal-flavored): publishable leadership run.

Pinned-manifest discipline: each gate is a provisional `EmpiricalGate`, activated only when its manifest pins CPU/microcode, kernel/filesystem/mount options, NVMe model/firmware + measured fsync distribution, toolchain/build, database configuration, graph/schema, transaction size and concurrency, retention/FEC/encryption/index policy, cold/warm state, result consumption, and the statistical comparison rule — plus the gate's Appendix G operation class and counting unit (client-visible requests vs internal probes). Derivability: a latency gate below its class's ordered-barrier count x pinned measured fsync p50, or a throughput gate above the apply ceiling its sequenced-command count implies, fails CI as a registry divergence (§1 constraint 12), never as a missed benchmark. Moving or unavailable external comparators cannot be CI gates.

The six laws bind every published number: (1) no benchmark-only semantics — durability/isolation/result consumption match the declared production mode; (2) distributions, not averages — p50/p95/p99/p99.9 + worst hot-key always reported, extreme quantiles carrying fitted-tail confidence intervals, never raw sample maxima; (3) never hide compaction — foreground latency during compaction/checkpoint/GC/index build is part of the result; (4) memory is a first-class metric — bytes per live edge include versions, indexes, witnesses, allocator slack; (5) adaptive numbers disclose their policy epoch, with the fallback's number published beside; (6) no unpriced protocol weight — every gate names its Appendix G operation class and counting unit, is checked against that row's derived floor, and any protocol-weight change updates the registry in the same change (CI rejects divergence).

## Invariants & claim types
No FG-INV row binds directly. Every gate value here is `benchmark`/`slo` class: an `slo.toml` row keyed `{operation_class,posture,audit_class}`; none may enter `invariants.toml`. Adaptive results name their policy epoch and publish the fallback number beside them (FG-CAL-01 governs any adaptive-policy promotion behind those numbers).

## Interactions
Consumes: deterministic harness + baseline discipline from `verif-perf-apparatus`; operation-class rows and derived floors from `g0-cost-registry` (checked by `perf-cost-ci`); bulk path from `w3-bulk-staging` + readers from `w10-formats`; commit anatomy from `w2-commit-protocol`; `SnapshotQuery` surface from `w10-snapshotquery`; sealed-run scan/intersection contracts from `w3-tier-r`; factorized/WCOJ/LDBC plans from `w5-executor`. Produces gate rows for `obs-slo`; shares fixtures with `perf-bench-anatomy`/`perf-bench-scale`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) Each bench binary emits machine-readable results with manifest digest, p50/p95/p99/p99.9 + worst hot-key, per-component latency anatomy, compaction/GC/checkpoint/index-build activity during the run (law 3), and full memory census (law 4). (2) CI compares against the committed baseline within the variance budget and runs the derivability check; a seeded registry-divergent gate fails as a registry error. (3) Ingest report schema makes D1/D2/encryption/FEC/rebase fields mandatory; a marker-only latency field is a lint failure. (4) 2-hop bench asserts the materialization counter is exactly 0. (5) LDBC harness produces compliance artifacts and a comparator manifest; gating on a non-pinned external number is a lint failure. (6) A replayed regression (same seed/schedule) reproduces the flagged result; flamegraph attached automatically. (7) E2E gate-pipeline script: a scaled-down pinned manifest (same schema, small corpus) runs all nine bench binaries end-to-end in CI — cold load, ingest, point reads, neighbor scans, 2-hop, triangle, and the three LDBC harnesses in smoke mode — validating report schemas, baseline comparison, and the derivability check on every gate row before any reference-machine run. (8) Detailed logging: every bench run logs {gate_id, manifest_digest, operation_class, counting_unit, seed, baseline_digest, per-law fields (latency-anatomy components, compaction/GC/checkpoint/index-build activity, memory census, policy_epoch plus fallback number where adaptive), verdict vs variance budget}; a report missing any law-mandated field is a schema failure, and a flagged regression must be reproducible from the logged manifest digest plus seed alone.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Numbers are provisional until manifests pin real hardware; the fsync-distribution pin prevents both flattery and false alarms. Rejected: benchmark-only durability/isolation modes (law 1); averages (law 2); warming away compaction (law 3); LDBC official audit as a blocking prerequisite — a compliance run with pinned comparators is the gate; audit is a later publication step.

## Provenance
§17 gate rows 'Cold bulk load' through 'LDBC FinBench', excluding the tier-churn and durable-lifecycle rows owned by perf-bench-history/perf-bench-anatomy (1238-1239, 1241, 1243-1248) + activation and method paragraphs (1234, 1273); Appendix G rows (3177-3180).

title: Build governance-profile benches against a pinned simulated audit authority
description:
## What & scope
Implement the three §17 governance-profile gates measuring the audit-Required pipeline: commit(order-accepted)->released, released->ActiveDeliverable->first-result-byte, and end-to-end commit->streamable — all against a pinned deterministic *simulated* audit authority under `fgdb-sim`, always reported beside the no-audit baseline.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
The governance plane (Warden's audit-visibility pipeline) is the compliance differentiator, and B5 demands its cost be measured honestly. Real external authorities have arbitrary RTTs, so gating on them would make CI hostage to a third party; the pinned simulated authority makes the *protocol's* cost deterministic and replayable while real-authority numbers remain reported, never gated. This bead operationalizes §16.8's three availability lines as measurable segments.

## Design — normative detail
Gate rows (exact): **commit(order-accepted)->released**: p50/p99 against the pinned deterministic simulated audit authority under `fgdb-sim` with a declared RTT/throughput distribution, reported beside the no-audit baseline; real-authority numbers are reported, never gated. **released->ActiveDeliverable->first-result-byte**: p50/p99 under the same pinned simulated authority and time-evidence fixture, reported beside the no-audit baseline. **End-to-end commit->streamable (Required class)**: p50/p99; must decompose additively into the two plane segments above within the variance budget, reported beside the no-audit baseline.

Operation class under test — the Appendix G audit-Required write row: fused/explicit commands plus the ordered `AuditTicketAdmissionSpec`; 7-10 ordered sync points: external ticket-issuance CAS (strictly serial per `AuditDomainId`) -> ordered admission + admission audit visibility -> event/resolution signing under `CertificateAttemptPlan` quorum-rooting + per-signer `CertificateSignerLock` installs for both payload and order-attempt certificates -> D1 prepared-root publication -> Raft closure sync -> D2 apply publication (quorum-durable maintenance entry + protocol-root slot update: two ordered publications) -> external resolution-batch CAS (per-batch) -> `AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec` + visible-endpoint publication (again entry + slot) -> `ProtectedOutputActivationSpec` (per output; fresh time evidence) -> terminal completion. External-authority interactions: >= 2 external RTTs — ticket issuance synchronous per operation; resolution batch amortized per contiguous batch; time authority per activation (batch-subject amortized under `TimeBoundSubject::ActivationBatch`).

§16.8 framing the segments measure: **apply-durability availability** is local storage plus Raft only — applies continue behind a stalled Required entry up to §12.8's pipeline limits, then degrade to deterministic backpressure; **visibility availability** multiplies in the audit authority's availability under Required profiles (only `AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec` can release a Required entry); **delivery availability** multiplies in the time authority's per-tick availability, deliberately kept off the audit prefix. The v1 footprint: audit continuity touches a Required operation exactly three times — the strictly serial one-at-a-time `TicketIssued` issuance CAS, the admission visibility advance, and its share of one batched `TicketsResolvedBatch` resolution.

Pinned-manifest discipline: each gate is a provisional `EmpiricalGate`, activated only when its manifest pins CPU/microcode, kernel/filesystem/mount options, NVMe model/firmware + measured fsync distribution, toolchain/build, database configuration, graph/schema, transaction size and concurrency, retention/FEC/encryption/index policy, cold/warm state, result consumption, and the statistical comparison rule — plus the gate's Appendix G operation class and counting unit (client-visible requests vs internal probes). Derivability: a latency gate below its class's ordered-barrier count x pinned measured fsync p50, or a throughput gate above the apply ceiling its sequenced-command count implies, fails CI as a registry divergence (§1 constraint 12), never as a missed benchmark. Manifests here additionally pin the simulated authority's RTT/throughput distribution, audit batch size k, activation tick tau, and the time-evidence fixture. The six laws bind every published number: (1) no benchmark-only semantics — durability/isolation/result consumption match the declared production mode; (2) distributions, not averages — p50/p95/p99/p99.9 + worst hot-key always reported, extreme quantiles carrying fitted-tail confidence intervals, never raw sample maxima; (3) never hide compaction — foreground latency during compaction/checkpoint/GC/index build is part of the result; (4) memory is a first-class metric — bytes per live edge include versions, indexes, witnesses, allocator slack; (5) adaptive numbers disclose their policy epoch, with the fallback's number published beside; (6) no unpriced protocol weight — every gate names its Appendix G operation class and counting unit, is checked against that row's derived floor, and any protocol-weight change updates the registry in the same change (CI rejects divergence). Law 6 requires this bead's numbers to reconcile with the audit-Required registry row.

## Invariants & claim types
No FG-INV created; per-posture availability numbers for the three lines are `slo.toml` rows, never invariants (the §20 authority-availability risk row tracks them). Gate values are `benchmark` class keyed `{operation_class=audit-required-write,posture,audit_class=Required}`. The additive-decomposition requirement is a report-consistency law, not a semantic invariant.

## Interactions
Consumes the deterministic simulated authority from `verif-sim` and harness from `verif-perf-apparatus`; exercises `w9-audit-release` (visibility advance, release recipes) and `w9-time-authority` (activation time evidence); restates and measures `w9-authority-surface`'s footprint/availability lines; classes/floors from `g0-cost-registry`; `obs-slo` consumes the segment rows; `perf-bench-scale` reuses the authority fixture for head-of-line runs.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) Three bench binaries + a combined run; report schema forces the no-audit baseline column and the additive decomposition check (|e2e - (seg1+seg2)| within variance budget) — violation fails the run. (2) Sweep simulated-authority RTT distributions; verify apply throughput is unaffected up to pipeline limits, then deterministic backpressure engages (logged with limit values) — a stalled authority never blocks durable ordering. (3) Ordered-sync counter byte-matches the 7-10-point chain per audit class. (4) Real-authority mode produces report-only output; CI gating on it is a lint failure. Logging: per-segment timestamps keyed by ticket id, `AuditDomainId`, pipeline entry index, activation tick.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: simulated authority too kind — the declared RTT distribution is pinned in the manifest and varied in sweeps. Rejected: gating on real external authorities; single end-to-end number without plane decomposition; treating availability products as one line (§16.8 mandates three lines, never one product).

## Provenance
§17 governance rows + ordered-sync row (1261-1264); §16.8 (1222-1228); Appendix G audit-Required row (3181).

title: Build history/lifecycle benches: time-travel, branch/snapshot, recovery, tier churn
description:
## What & scope
Extra subtask split from perf-bench-core: the Chronicle/Strata lifecycle gates — time-travel query overhead, branch create / snapshot open, recovery, and tier-migration churn — as bench binaries with pinned manifests.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1 (One Version Universe) is only credible if history is nearly free: these gates price time-travel against the current path, prove branch creation is O(1) data-copy, and bound recovery. B5: the tier-churn gate applies calibrated-adaptivity honesty to Strata's promote/demote controller instead of hand-waving stability.

## Design — normative detail
Gate rows (exact): **Time-travel query overhead**: measure current OLTP cost by retention policy plus historical latency by checkpoint distance and suffix bytes; provisional targets are < 8% current-path overhead and < 2.5x for the declared recent-history fixture — explicitly *not* universal guarantees. **Branch create / snapshot open**: snapshot open is O(1) metadata and provisional < 100 us warm; durable branch creation is O(1) data-copy complexity but includes root publication/fsync or Raft and has a *separate* latency distribution. Appendix G branch-create row: 2 sequenced semantic commands — ordered `BranchEpochBoundaryReservation`, then `BranchForkSpec` installing the pre-built `BranchForkBundle` — ~4-6 Raft entries; barriers: bundle D1 (availability certificate over the closed inventory, per-op) + append (per-batch) + D2 root publication (per-batch); durable objects proportional to bounded envelope-root fanout, O(1) data copy; identity-continuity authority episodic per allocation-epoch advance, nothing synchronous. **Recovery** (clean shutdown / crash @ 1 TB): < 1 s / < 30 s to first query (anchor-mapped, capsule tail replay). **Tier-migration churn**: report promote<->demote reversals per descriptor, minimum-dwell violations (must be zero), conversion-cost regret, and soak-test limit cycles; SPRT type-I/type-II bounds apply only to its declared decision hypotheses — they are not reversal-rate bounds.

Pinned-manifest discipline: each gate is a provisional `EmpiricalGate`, activated only when its manifest pins CPU/microcode, kernel/filesystem/mount options, NVMe model/firmware + measured fsync distribution, toolchain/build, database configuration, graph/schema, transaction size and concurrency, retention/FEC/encryption/index policy, cold/warm state, result consumption, and the statistical comparison rule — plus the gate's Appendix G operation class and counting unit (client-visible requests vs internal probes). Derivability: a latency gate below its class's ordered-barrier count x pinned measured fsync p50, or a throughput gate above the apply ceiling its sequenced-command count implies, fails CI as a registry divergence (§1 constraint 12), never as a missed benchmark. The time-travel and recovery manifests must additionally pin retention/FEC/encryption policy and checkpoint distance since the gates are parameterized by them. The six laws bind every published number: (1) no benchmark-only semantics — durability/isolation/result consumption match the declared production mode; (2) distributions, not averages — p50/p95/p99/p99.9 + worst hot-key always reported, extreme quantiles carrying fitted-tail confidence intervals, never raw sample maxima; (3) never hide compaction — foreground latency during compaction/checkpoint/GC/index build is part of the result; (4) memory is a first-class metric — bytes per live edge include versions, indexes, witnesses, allocator slack; (5) adaptive numbers disclose their policy epoch, with the fallback's number published beside; (6) no unpriced protocol weight — every gate names its Appendix G operation class and counting unit, is checked against that row's derived floor, and any protocol-weight change updates the registry in the same change (CI rejects divergence).

## Invariants & claim types
No FG-INV row binds directly; all values are `benchmark`/`slo` class. The churn gate's statistical framing is calibrated-claim discipline: SPRT bounds are claims about declared hypotheses only (B5), and minimum-dwell violations are a hard zero because dwell is a deterministic guard, not a statistical one.

## Interactions
Exercises `w2-recovery` (recovery equation, capsule tail replay), `w2-branch-fork` (fork bundle path), `w2-snapshots-leases` (snapshot open), `w2-retention-checkpoints` (retention-policy parameterization of time-travel cost), `w3-seal-compact` (SPRT churn guards under soak). Recovery crash points coordinate with `verif-torture` crash matrices; `perf-bench-scale`'s endurance fixture feeds the churn soak.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) Time-travel bench sweeps retention policy x checkpoint distance x suffix bytes and reports the overhead surface; the two provisional targets gate only the declared fixture. (2) Branch bench reports snapshot-open and durable-create as separate distributions; conflating them is a report-schema error; command/entry counts byte-match the Appendix G branch row. (3) Recovery bench: scripted clean-shutdown and kill-at-random-phase crash at 1 TB, time-to-first-query measured to a successful `SnapshotQuery`; logs recovery phases with timestamps. (4) Churn bench: soak fixture with adversarial temperature oscillation; asserts zero minimum-dwell violations, reports reversals/descriptor and conversion-cost regret, detects limit cycles via the pinned detector. (5) E2E + logging: one scripted CI pass runs scaled-down variants of all four benches back-to-back on a shared fixture and validates every report schema; each bench logs {bench_id, manifest_digest, seed, phase timestamps, measured distributions, verdict}, and the recovery/churn logs (phases, dwell decisions, reversals, regret) must suffice to reconstruct each reported number without rerunning.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: time-travel targets read as universal SLAs — the row text explicitly scopes them to the declared fixture. Rejected: benchmarking snapshot open as "branch create" (hides root publication); universal time-travel guarantees; SPRT bounds marketed as reversal-rate bounds.

## Provenance
§17 rows "Tier-migration churn", "Time-travel query overhead", "Branch create / snapshot open", "Recovery" (1240, 1249, 1252-1253); Appendix G branch-create row (3183).

title: Build scale/endurance benches: sequencer cursors, 10k branches, compaction debt, memory
description:
## What & scope
Implement the §17 scale and endurance gates: sequencer & maintenance-stream scale (N=10k cursors), Ripple view maintenance, the 10k-branch churn covering scenario, and the three endurance gates (sustained ingest, compaction-debt ceiling, memory stability) on one shared fixture.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B4 and B6 collide here: thousands of agent subscriptions and branches share one ordered log with user commits, so the honest question is head-of-line interference, priced by the `FG-CFG-04` capacity model. B2: compaction debt is Strata's failure mode under sustained ingest; endurance gates make law 3 a defined-duration obligation. B5: model-predicted vs measured divergence is itself a finding (`FG-EVID-03`).

## Design — normative detail
Gate rows (exact): **Sequencer & maintenance-stream scale**: provisional N = 10k live cursors each sustaining M = 1 coalesced delivery/s with subscription end-to-end p99 < 10 ms AND user-commit p99 degradation within the declared head-of-line budget; N/M and the budget are provisional values derived from the `FG-CFG-04` capacity model (Appendix G), which the manifest pins together with the fan-out amplification factor and implied external time-observation rate. **Ripple view maintenance**: delta application >= 1M input-changes/s per circuit worker; subscription end-to-end p99 < 10 ms. **Endurance: sustained ingest**: defined-duration ingest at a stated fraction of the transactional-ingest gate — 2h run on merge to main, 24h nightly — on the shared endurance fixture that also feeds the §6.6/tier-migration soak. **Endurance: compaction-debt ceiling**: steady-state compaction debt bounded in §6.6's write-amplification-model terms — debt bytes and generation count at sustained ingest at the stated gate fraction; exceeding the ceiling fails the run even when point latencies pass. **Endurance: long-run memory stability**: RSS and allocator-slack drift bounds over the same endurance run; unexplained monotonic drift fails.

`stream_capacity.toml` model (restated): total same-group ordered-log entries/s as registered functions of scale parameters — live cursors N, per-cursor coalesced delivery cadence M, durable result rate R, live branch count B, audit batch size k, activation tick tau. Governing law — fan-out amplification: a commit matching C cursors mints ~3*C per-subject protocol transitions in Required postures (~2*C NotRequired) — publish, activation, ACK — because the `Coalesced` provenance arm (§9.5) reduces commits per delivery, never transitions per delivery; ordered-log entries amortize below transitions under §12.8's batch rows — `PublishDeltaPending` across one Ripple flush tick, `ProtectedOutputActivationBatchSpec`/`ProtectedOutputDispositionBatchSpec` per activation tick, audit release across a pipeline range inside one `AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec` — so entries/s scale with tick rates while per-subject transitions scale with N x M. The model publishes the implied external time-observation rate — N x M challenge-nonce-fresh threshold-signed observations/s under per-lease subjects, amortized to one per activation tick under the registered `TimeBoundSubject::ActivationBatch` arm — and derives head-of-line cost for user commits: semantic commands and maintenance entries share one role/group ordered log, so user-commit p99 degradation is a stated function of (N,M,R,k,tau); that derived figure is what the sequencer row gates. The §5.6 10k-branch objective must have a registered covering scenario (Appendix G coverage law); per §5.6 it is an empirical gate parameterized by retained deltas, key wraps, subscriptions, lease cost, per-branch `StatsSegment`/Ripple-maintainer cost (§8.5), and sustained create+retire churn at steady state — meaningful only with retirement in the loop — so the branch-churn soak runs sustained create+retire (fork plus branch retirement) against the registered scenario, never create-only.

The six laws bind every published number: (1) no benchmark-only semantics — durability/isolation/result consumption match the declared production mode; (2) distributions, not averages — p50/p95/p99/p99.9 + worst hot-key always reported, extreme quantiles carrying fitted-tail confidence intervals, never raw sample maxima; (3) never hide compaction — foreground latency during compaction/checkpoint/GC/index build is part of the result; (4) memory is a first-class metric — bytes per live edge include versions, indexes, witnesses, allocator slack; (5) adaptive numbers disclose their policy epoch, with the fallback's number published beside; (6) no unpriced protocol weight — every gate names its Appendix G operation class and counting unit, is checked against that row's derived floor, and any protocol-weight change updates the registry in the same change (CI rejects divergence). Pinned-manifest discipline binds as in perf-bench-core; scale manifests additionally pin the fan-out amplification factor, implied time-observation rate, endurance cadences (2h merge, 24h nightly), and the stated gate fraction.

## Invariants & claim types
`FG-CFG-04` (maintenance-stream capacity model, `slo.toml` class): must disclose per-entry-class arrival/service assumptions, stated scale parameters (branch count, cursor count, delivery cadence, fan-out amplification factor, implied time-observation rate), predicted versus measured head-of-line saturation, reserved-capacity and fallback policy — it gates configuration acceptance and CI fixture design, never correctness; §12.8's deterministic backpressure remains the honest overload behavior when assumptions fail. `FG-EVID-03` (endurance-gate evidence, `evidence.toml` class): duration and cadence, compaction-debt ceiling stated in §6.6 write-amplification-model terms, long-run memory stability bound, steady-state occupancy-model prediction versus observation — divergence is itself a finding. No FG-INV row binds; nothing here is an invariant.

## Interactions
Exercises `w6-subscriptions` (cursor machine), `w6-zset-circuits` (circuit workers), `w9-activation-batching` (batch amortization), `w2-branch-fork` plus `w2-branch-retire` (branch create+retire churn — §5.6 requires retirement in the loop), `w3-write-amp` (debt model terms), `w3-seal-compact` (churn guards). Consumes `stream_capacity.toml` scenarios from `g0-cost-registry` via `perf-cost-ci`'s coverage law; reuses `perf-bench-governance`'s simulated authority for Required-posture fan-out; `obs-slo` consumes the head-of-line budget row; `perf-bench-history`'s churn soak shares the endurance fixture.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) Cursor-scale bench at pinned (N,M,R,B,k,tau): subscription e2e p99 < 10 ms, user-commit p99 degradation within budget, measured entries/s and per-subject transitions vs model prediction — divergence is a reported finding. (2) Transition-count audit: a commit matching C cursors mints ~3*C (Required) / ~2*C (NotRequired) per-subject transitions; entries amortize per tick as registered. (3) Time-observation-rate audit under per-lease vs ActivationBatch subjects. (4) Endurance harness: 2h/24h cadences wired to CI; continuous logging of debt bytes, generation count, RSS, allocator slack; run fails on ceiling breach or unexplained drift even with green latencies. (5) 10k-branch churn soak against the registered scenario with sustained create+retire at steady state, sweeping the declared §5.6 parameters (retained deltas, key wraps, subscriptions, lease cost, per-branch stats/maintainer cost); logs per-branch lifecycle events — fork, retire, key-wrap and maintainer-instantiation counts.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: capacity-model flattery — divergence is a finding and backpressure is tested at saturation. Rejected: per-delivery accounting that hides fan-out (the Coalesced arm reduces commits per delivery, never transitions); unpinned soaks; payload-only memory accounting.

## Provenance
§17 rows "Ripple view maintenance", "Sequencer & maintenance-stream scale", "Endurance" x3 (1251, 1260, 1268-1270); Appendix G stream_capacity (3189); Appendix F FG-CFG-04/FG-EVID-03 (3163-3164); §5.6, §6.6, §9.5, §12.8 touchpoints.

title: Implement Appendix G cost-registry CI: generation, derivability, coverage, same-change
description:
## What & scope
Implement the CI machinery that makes Appendix G constitutional: generation of `latency_anatomy.toml`/`stream_capacity.toml` from `command_contracts.toml`, byte-comparison of the appendix's readability projections, and the three CI laws — derivability, coverage, same-change — enforced on every change and every benchmark manifest.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
§1 constraint 12: costs are registered claims — §1.11 gave correctness claims a registry; Appendix G does the same for cost, so no mechanism can accrete protocol weight without a priced row. This is B5's enforcement arm for performance: it welds the §17 gate table to the protocol so "the gates and the protocol remain mutually derivable" — without it, gate numbers and protocol reality drift apart silently.

## Design — normative detail
Two machine-checkable artifacts constitute the registry. `latency_anatomy.toml`: one row per operation class stating five structural quantities — (i) sequenced semantic commands; (ii) total Raft log entries including order-attempt and certificate maintenance; (iii) the ordered durability-barrier chain, per barrier: the plane from `DurableStateSlotRef` (`SemanticPayload|Protocol|PreparedOwnership|Consensus|Bootstrap`), what syncs, the amortization law (`per-txn|per-group|per-batch|deferrable`), and the fusion-legality column; (iv) external-authority interactions classified `synchronous|episodic`; (v) durable objects minted. `stream_capacity.toml`: the maintenance-stream capacity model (`FG-CFG-04`). Both are generated where possible from `command_contracts.toml`: a class's command count derives from its registered command arms, and its barrier chain from their `publication_mode` and consumed/written state slots; hand-declared rows exist only where structure is not yet expressible there (external RTT class, group-commit amortization) and each names the contract rows it summarizes. Per §5.1's registry discipline, the tables in Appendix G are checked readability projections — CI regenerates and byte-compares them — never a second source of truth. Claim types fixed: registry rows are exact structural counts, or exact bounds in declared configuration parameters where a column is configuration-dependent (the tilde-ranged columns), enforced by the same generation bijection that governs command contracts; every microsecond or throughput budget is an `slo.toml` row keyed `{operation_class,posture,audit_class}`; the capacity model is a configuration-model claim (`FG-CFG-04`, registered beside `FG-CFG-03` in Appendix F), never an invariant. Counts are stated for the single-node quorum-one posture at concurrency 1; group commit amortizes every barrier marked per-group or per-batch; the replicated posture changes barrier behavior (follower append/reply), never command counts.

The three CI laws (exact): **Derivability** — every §17 gate names its operation class and counting unit (client-visible requests versus internal probes) and must be arithmetically consistent with its row: a latency gate >= the class's ordered-barrier count x the benchmark manifest's pinned measured fsync p50, a throughput gate <= the apply ceiling implied by its sequenced-command count and the measured serial apply cost; a gate that fails the check is a registry error and fails the build, not the benchmark. **Coverage** — every stated scale objective in the plan must be covered by a registered `stream_capacity.toml` scenario: the §5.6 10k-branch objective, §17's cursor-scale gate, the governance-profile gates, and any future objective that names a scale parameter; an objective without a covering scenario is a G0 failure. **Same-change update** — any change that adds sequenced semantic commands, ordered durability barriers, external-authority interactions, or per-object identity structure updates `latency_anatomy.toml`/`stream_capacity.toml` in the same change; CI regenerates the derivable portions from `command_contracts.toml`, diffs them against the registered rows and the appendix's projections, and rejects a divergence.

Fusion legality is a normative registry column, not an implementation option discovered under load: quorum-one MAY fuse append-reply hard-state publication with post-apply D2 protocol publication into one ordered slot update (both sides land in the same `RootManifest`/`RootSlot` closure; the crash window is exactly §5.2's two abandonment arms); multi-member MUST NOT fuse (followers reply to append before commit, so hard-state publication is an independently observable protocol obligation); a build fusing against a MUST NOT row fails closed at the G0 conformance gates; a legal fusion counts as one ordered sync operation, never zero.

## Invariants & claim types
No FG-INV row; this bead enforces claim-type boundaries themselves: registry class (exact counts/bounds, generation bijection), `slo` class (all budgets), `FG-CFG-04` (capacity model disclosure per Appendix F: per-entry-class arrival/service assumptions, stated scale parameters, predicted vs measured head-of-line saturation, reserved-capacity and fallback policy).

## Interactions
Consumes `g0-cost-registry` (registry artifacts + law specs), `g0-command-contracts` (`command_contracts.toml`, publication modes, state slots, bijection CI), `g0-claim-registries` (claim-type constitution, slo/evidence toml split). Validates manifests from `perf-bench-core` and all other perf-bench-* beads; `perf-bench-anatomy` supplies the empirical counts the registry rows are checked against; `obs-slo` consumes the keyed slo rows.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) Generator regenerates derivable rows from `command_contracts.toml` and byte-compares registered rows and Appendix G projections; a seeded divergence (extra command arm, changed publication_mode) fails CI naming the row. (2) Derivability checker runs over every gate manifest; a seeded impossible gate (latency below barrier-count x fsync p50) fails as a registry error with the arithmetic in the message. (3) Coverage checker enumerates scale objectives; deleting the 10k-branch scenario is a G0 failure. (4) Same-change detector rejects a synthetic PR adding a sequenced command without a registry diff. (5) An orphan hand-declared row (naming no contract rows) fails. (6) Fusion conformance: a multi-member build with fusion enabled fails closed at the G0 conformance gate. (7) E2E CI-pipeline script: on a fixture repo carrying `command_contracts.toml` plus registered registry rows, run the whole chain end-to-end — generation, byte-compare of registered rows and Appendix G projections, derivability over a sample gate-manifest set, coverage enumeration, same-change detection — once green, then once against each of the six seeded defects above, asserting each fails with its own distinct error class. (8) Detailed logging: every checker run emits structured events {checker (generation|derivability|coverage|same-change|orphan|fusion), row_or_gate_id, operation_class, derived_value, registered_value, verdict}; the seeded-defect e2e asserts the failing row/gate id and the offending arithmetic appear in the log record, so every CI verdict is verifiable from logs alone.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: generation gaps force hand rows to proliferate — each must name its contract rows, keeping the exception enumerable. Rejected: Appendix G tables as a second source of truth (they are checked projections); treating a below-floor gate as a benchmark win (it is a registry error); putting budgets in the registry (budgets are slo rows) or the capacity model in invariants.

## Provenance
Appendix G complete (3169-3193); §1 constraint 12; §17 activation/derivability paragraph (1234); Appendix F FG-CFG-04 (3163).

title: Build freshness/vector/tail/temporal gates + FG-CAL calibration evidence rows
description:
## What & scope
Implement the statistically-qualified §17 gates: vector search, temporal connectivity, cardinality-interval evidence, tail evidence, derived-state freshness, and the adaptive-policy audit — each wired to its Appendix F calibration/evidence row (FG-CAL-01/02/03, FG-EVID-01/04) so the disclosure obligations are machine-enforced parts of the benchmark reports.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5's core promise is *calibrated* adaptivity: numbers that depend on sampling, extrapolation, or learned policies must carry their statistical passports or revert to conservative behavior. B4: derived-state freshness is Ripple's user-facing promise, promoted here from reported to gated. B6: agents consuming vector/hybrid retrieval need recall claims scoped to *authorized* snapshots, not raw corpora — a differentiator no mainstream vector store offers.

## Design — normative detail
Gate rows (exact): **Vector** (10M x 768-d f32, HNSW): provisional >= 20k QPS at measured recall >= 0.95 on a pinned authorized-snapshot corpus; publish exact-baseline sampling and confidence interval; separately report logical commit->delta-tail-searchable and commit->merged-generation latency; no sample can "certify" each insert. **Temporal connectivity** (`CONNECTED ... AS OF`, sealed history): provisional < 100 us per probe over every sequence sampled by the pinned sealed-history fixture; the result is exact only for a matching `sealed-exact` projection/root — branch overlays or uncovered tails must be compensated or fall back (§10.7). **Cardinality-interval evidence**: report realized marginal coverage, stratum counts, selection/window policy, drift alarms, and any nonexchangeability penalty; failure reverts to conservative costing — this is `FG-CAL-02`, not a correctness gate. **Tail evidence**: p99.9 is empirical when sufficiently observed; any POT/GPD extrapolation separately reports threshold, exceedance count, dependence/stability diagnostics, fit uncertainty, and sensitivity; a model failure blocks the extrapolated claim rather than "certifying" the tail. **Derived-state freshness**: commit->delta-tail-searchable and commit->merged-generation p50/p99 promoted from reported to gated numbers (values provisional), plus watermark lag under sustained ingest; claim class `slo`/`benchmark`, never an invariant. **Adaptive-policy audit**: promotion requires the registered `FG-CAL-01` evidence rule, overlap/effective-sample checks, and deterministic fallback; reports never claim arbitrary-policy OPE.

Appendix F disclosure rows (restated, enforced in report schemas): `FG-CAL-01` (adaptive policy evidence versus pinned fallback): null/outcome filtration, alpha, support/overlap, effective sample size, loss and fallback; stream-sequenced promotion only. `FG-CAL-02` (cardinality/risk interval coverage): population, selection/window, exchangeability or nonexchangeability method, strata, marginal target, realized coverage and drift. `FG-CAL-03` (ANN recall/drift evidence): authorized snapshot population, keyed sample, exact baseline, candidate policy, confidence interval and rebuild action. `FG-EVID-01` (decision-card/OPE completeness): state/actions/features, logged probabilities, zero-support exclusions, clipping/estimator, policy epoch and fallback. `FG-EVID-04` (derived-state freshness; slo-class, never an invariant): bound expressed in watermark/commit-sequence units, audit-pipeline and time-evidence dependencies named, realized lag distribution, typed `FreshnessBreach` rate and fallback policy. The adjacent config rows `FG-CFG-01` (modeled MTTDL >= declared target with sensitivity bounds per shipped profile; crash/restore tests remain separate empirical evidence — owner `w2-fec-scrub`) and `FG-CFG-02` (defaults outside the named model's predicted instability region with sensitivity margin plus no limit cycle in pinned soak fixtures — surfaced via `obs-observatory`/`obs-doctor`) appear in the same §17 gate table; this bead wires their gate-table presence, not their models.

## Invariants & claim types
No FG-INV row binds. Everything here is `evidence.toml` (FG-CAL-01/02/03, FG-EVID-01) or `slo.toml`/`benchmark` (freshness values, vector QPS, temporal probe latency) class per the claim-type constitution: e-processes may be anytime-valid under their named filtration/null assumptions; conformal coverage is marginal under its stated population — none of these are invariants, and a failed disclosure reverts the number to its conservative fallback rather than shipping an unqualified claim.

## Interactions
Exercises `w7-vector` (HNSW, quantizers, authorized recall story) and `w7-path-temporal` (temporal connectivity index); freshness machinery from `w6-freshness` (`FreshnessBreach`) and watermarks from `w6-views`; calibration plane and FG-CAL row registration from `verif-sextant`; harness from `verif-perf-apparatus`; operation classes/floors from `g0-cost-registry`. `obs-slo` consumes FG-EVID-04 rows for alerting; `perf-bench-scale`'s sustained-ingest run supplies the watermark-lag environment.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) Vector bench: pinned authorized-snapshot corpus; keyed sampling against exact baseline; report carries CI and rebuild action per FG-CAL-03; recall measured under authorization (an unauthorized-corpus number is a schema violation); the two freshness latencies reported separately. (2) Temporal bench: probes over every fixture-sampled sequence; asserts exactness only under `sealed-exact` match and verifies compensation/fallback on overlay fixtures. (3) Cardinality/tail report validators: missing disclosure field fails the run; seeded GPD misfit blocks the p99.9 extrapolated claim while the empirical quantile still publishes. (4) Freshness gate: p50/p99 vs provisional values + watermark lag under sustained ingest; `FreshnessBreach` rate and fallback policy in the report. (5) Adaptive-policy audit: a promotion without FG-CAL-01 evidence or without a deterministic fallback is rejected; decision-card completeness per FG-EVID-01 spot-checked on sampled cards. (6) E2E script: one pipeline run on a scaled-down pinned corpus exercises all four gate families in sequence — vector recall under authorization, temporal probes over sealed and overlay fixtures, cardinality/tail report validation, and the freshness gate under sustained ingest with an induced watermark stall — followed by one adaptive-policy promotion attempted with and then without FG-CAL-01 evidence, asserting the former promotes and the latter is rejected. (7) Detailed logging: each gate run logs {gate_id, manifest_digest, corpus/authorized-population id, seed, measured quantiles with CI fields, FreshnessBreach count, fallback decisions, decision-card ids}; validator rejections log the exact missing disclosure field; the e2e asserts every claim in the emitted report traces to a logged evidence row, so calibration verdicts are auditable from logs alone.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: statistical passports become boilerplate nobody reads — validators make them load-bearing (missing/failed disclosure changes the published claim). Rejected: per-insert recall "certification" (impossible claim, explicitly forbidden); universal temporal-probe guarantees (fixture-scoped); freshness as an invariant (it is hostage to audit-pipeline and time-evidence dependencies, hence slo-class); raw sample maxima as p99.9.

## Provenance
§17 rows "Vector", "Temporal connectivity", "Cardinality-interval", "Tail evidence", "Adaptive-policy audit", "Derived-state freshness", "Durability model", "Controller stability" (1250, 1254-1259, 1271); Appendix F (3151-3165); §9.5/§10.7 touchpoints.

title: RestoreServicePromotionManifest's posture BODY union is registered nowhere: 5 source members, 0 rows, and the 2 in a20's residue cannot land as field rows
notes:
MEASURED at HEAD 7dd2aa6 by pane2 while re-deriving fgdb-a20-restore-promotion-ivsp against the
owner's EMBED ruling for section 8.

THE SHAPE. a20:2575 declares TWO constructs on RestoreServicePromotionManifest, and only one is
registered.

  (1) THE TAG, LANDED AND CORRECT. The common member `target_posture:Local|Sharded`. Catalog has
      [[union]] RestoreServicePromotionManifestTargetPosture (union_path
      RestoreServicePromotionManifest.target_posture, field_tag 0x0005, tag_wire_type u8,
      max_size_bytes 1) plus TWO [[union_arm]] rows, Local 0x0001 and Sharded 0x0002, both
      payload_kind = "unit", max_size_bytes 1. That is faithful: target_posture carries only the tag.

  (2) THE BODY, REGISTERED NOWHERE. The same sentence continues '...and exactly one body:
      `Local{local_prepare_evidence:PortableCertificateProjection<LocalRestoreServicePrepareCertificate>,
      local_configuration_and_endpoint_commitment}` or `Sharded{meta_prepare_evidence:
      PortableCertificateProjection<GlobalRestoreServicePrepareCertificate>,sorted_shard_ready_evidence
      [PortableCertificateProjection<RestoreShardServiceReadyAck>],
      complete_group_topology_configuration_and_endpoint_commitment}`.'
      ZERO [[union]] rows, ZERO [[union_arm]] rows for that body. The only three union/union_arm rows
      in the entire catalog whose union_path starts with `RestoreServicePromotionManifest` are the
      three in (1). a20 has 6 [[union]] rows total and none of them is this one.
      The five body member names have ZERO occurrences in registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml AND
      ZERO in registries/durable_fields.toml.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE SAME BEAD AS fgdb-qh3r, AND WHY IT CHANGES THE ivsp RESIDUE SHAPE.
ivsp's residue of 9 counts two of these members as owed [[field]] rows:
    Sharded.meta_prepare_evidence        :: PortableCertificateProjection<GlobalRestoreServicePrepareCertificate>
    Sharded.sorted_shard_ready_evidence  :: [PortableCertificateProjection<RestoreShardServiceReadyAck>]
That is the WRONG SHAPE for them, on a measurement rather than a preference:
  * `Sharded` is a [[top_level_candidate]] symbol (a20:top-level-candidate:sharded-484eb28941778afb)
    ONLY because the census reads the body alternation as a top-level definition. It is an ARM.
    `Local` is not a registered symbol at all -- exactly because qh3r drops its body.
  * OF 983 LANDED [[field]] ROWS OVER 279 DISTINCT HOSTS, the number whose containing_schema is an
    arm name that is neither a union_name nor a top_level symbol is ZERO. A field row may not hang
    off an arm.
  * And it cannot land as an arm payload member either, because the arm does not exist.
So the real obligation is ONE union + TWO arms + FIVE members, not two field rows. a20's actionable
residue is better read as 7 field rows + this union, not 9 field rows.

THE EMBED RULING DOES NOT UNBLOCK THEM -- MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED.
The owner ruled (2026-07-28) that an unwrapped `name:Type` member is not per se invalid under plan
line 328, so no re-spelling is owed and no construction-order edges appear. Line 328's prohibition
list is bare `StrongRef`, `StrongRef<A|B>`, `StrongRef[]`, `result_refs[StrongRef]`, slash-separated
pseudo-types, and generic `RegisteredStrongRef` -- an unwrapped `name:Type` is indeed not in it, and
the source independently confirms the embed reading: 'PortableCertificateProjection<T> ... contains
no StrongRef, CertifiedRemoteStrongRef, or consumer-local locator' (a20:2575).
That removes the SPELLING objection and leaves TWO standing:
  * no host union exists for the body (above), and
  * `PortableCertificateProjection` IS REGISTERED NOWHERE: 0 occurrences in
    registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml, 0 in registries/wire_types.toml, 0 in
    registries/durable_fields.toml. An embed still needs a registered target type to carry an
    exact_wire_type. The ruling legitimizes the spelling; it does not mint the type.

THE FIX, stated exactly so it is not re-derived.
  1. Register PortableCertificateProjection<T> as a type. The source gives its exact contents in the
     same sentence: 'embeds the target RemoteObjectIdentity, complete export projection bytes,
     canonical configuration/trust evidence bytes, and signatures'. It is a generic over the
     projected certificate; three instantiations are used in a20 alone
     (LocalRestoreServicePrepareCertificate, GlobalRestoreServicePrepareCertificate,
     RestoreShardServiceReadyAck). Follow the appendix's existing generic-expansion convention rather
     than inventing one.
  2. Register the posture body as a union with its two arms. Both arms are payload-carrying
     (inline-record), NOT unit -- this is the construct target_posture is not. Arm tags must come from
     the SOURCE spelling order, Local first then Sharded, which is also the target_posture order, so
     Local 0x0001 / Sharded 0x0002.
  3. Only then do the five members land as arm payload members.

A COMPETING READING, named so whoever takes this rules on it rather than discovering it late: one
could instead argue the two LANDED target_posture arms should have been payload-carrying, and the
`payload_kind = "unit"` on them is the defect. Two things weigh against it. The source writes
`target_posture:Local|Sharded` as a COMMON member alongside the body, i.e. two constructs in one
sentence; and the landed union and both arms carry max_size_bytes = 1, which is the tag width and is
faithful to a bare discriminant. Re-tagging a landed arm is also append-only damage where minting a
new union is not. I did not act on either reading -- registering the body is a20/a19 lane work and
this is filed, not landed.

BLOCKING RELATION TO fgdb-qh3r. qh3r remains real and remains a blocker on COMPLETING this: the
census drops the `Local` body, so its 2 members (local_prepare_evidence,
local_configuration_and_endpoint_commitment) are invisible to the entire appendix closure and cannot
be derived from the census at all. Under this bead the Sharded half is derivable from the source
text but the Local half is not, so a fix here without qh3r lands half a bijection. Sequence qh3r
first, or derive the Local half from the source sentence directly and say so.

NOT MINE TO LAND. Filed with the exact fix; ivsp records it.

title: Measurement record: nine-subsystem claims-vs-implementation table (40 declared crates, 0 exist), FG-INV checker exists=0 seen-to-fail=0, and 12 unregistered performance budgets
description:
MEASUREMENT RECORD — phase-two mock/placeholder sweep (pane4, 2026-07-26),
measured on main at 9fdbe0d. Filed as a bead so the numbers survive a session
restart. This is a measurement, not a defect; the defects it found are filed
separately and linked at the bottom.

=============================================================================
Q1. THE SUBSYSTEM GAP — nine rows, all "NO CODE"
=============================================================================
Method: `registries/workspace_topology.toml` declares 70 crates across 14
layers. Intersected the declared crate set per subsystem layer with what
actually exists in `crates/`.

  Subsystem                              declared crates   exist on disk
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  Chronicle          (layer "chronicle")               7               0
  Strata             (layer "strata")                  4               0
  Loom               (layer "loom")                    8               0
  Ripple             (layer "ripple")                  3               0
  Beacon             (layer "beacon")                  5               0
  Prism              (layer "prism")                   1               0
  Warden             (layer "warden")                  3               0
  Fabric             (layer "surface_operations")      6               0
  Aegis              (layer "aegis")                   3               0
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  TOTAL                                               40               0

All 13 crates that exist are in `foundation` (10: types, bigint, delta-types,
claim, resource, codec, sketch, collections, calibrate, evidence) or
`unsafe_islands` (3: unsafe-simd, unsafe-arena, unsafe-vfs).

VERDICT: no substitutes. Doctrine 7's "subset yes, substitute no" is not
violated anywhere. Probed three ways rather than trusting a name scan:
  (a) no struct/enum/trait/mod named for any subsystem (the single "strata"
      hit is `strata_oid()` in fgdb-calibrate/src/ope.rs:256, an OPE
      stratification identifier);
  (b) Doctrine 7's named prohibitions absent — no `HashMap<VId, Vec<EId>>`,
      no parser/AST engine, no global lock, no detached thread, no external
      crate outside the closed universe;
  (c) the two crates most likely to substitute both decline the role in their
      own module docs — `fgdb-delta-types/src/lib.rs:24` ("the subset both
      will consume, never a substitute for them") and `fgdb-codec/src/run.rs:8`
      ("stops below AdjRunSegment framing ... a Strata owner must supply those
      registered fields").

Note for whoever re-runs this: Fabric IS mapped, under the layer name
`surface_operations` (title "Fabric + operations", workspace_topology.toml:547).
It is not a missing subsystem; do not re-file that.

=============================================================================
Q2. FG-INV-01..20 — CHECKER "EXISTS" = 0, CHECKER "SEEN TO FAIL" = 0
=============================================================================
All 20 clauses are `status = "stub"`. Each names a `checker_entrypoint` AND a
`negative_test_entrypoint`; all 40 symbols resolve to `checker_index.toml`
rows whose artifacts DO NOT EXIST — they point into `crates/fgdb-oracles/`,
`fgdb-reference/`, `fgdb-observatory/`, `fgdb-secure-view/`, `fgdb-ecs/`, none
of which is a crate yet.

So the distinction between "has a checker" and "has a checker that can fail"
COLLAPSES here: both numerators are zero. That is correct and correctly
declared (`waiver = "forbidden"` on all 20, enforced as a literal at
validate.rs:231 plus a registry-level policy check at :360 — stricter than
AGENTS.md's "public, expiring waiver").

The guard that stops a capability being enabled while its clauses are stub IS
proven to fire: `tests/spine.rs::spine_neg_inactive_reachable_clause`, and
`scripts/g0_spine_e2e.sh` phase 3 asserts the failure NAMES `FG-INV-04.core`.

WHY THIS MATTERS ANYWAY: pane2 proved this hour that the distinction is real
on this repo — two G0 enforcement checks measured vacuous (a substring test
satisfied by a prose comment in Cargo.toml, and a quote scan reporting
crates_scanned=0 as a clean pass while an unledgered unsafe fn existed). A
checker exactly that vacuous would satisfy every promotion law in the tree:
`validate_clause` enforces `negative_test_entrypoint` only as a NON-EMPTY
STRING (validate.rs:281). 18 of the 20 clauses carry `first_gate = "G1"`, so
~18 promotions land in one window. See fgdb-clause-promotion-to-live-is-unguarded-nllh.

10 of 20 clauses also cite a formal proof lane; all 10 lanes are `declared`,
zero `.lean`/`.tla` artifacts exist, and `status = "checked"` is `is_file()`.
See fgdb-proof-lane-checked-is-only-file-existence-0f1l.

=============================================================================
Q3. BENCHMARK CLAIMS — no false measurement; 12 unregistered budgets
=============================================================================
Doctrine 7's "no non-durable benchmark mode reported as a result" is NOT
violated: there is no benchmark mode at all (no `benches/`, no criterion, no
`#[bench]`, no `black_box`), and README §17 frames its numbers honestly as
"provisional CI gates ... activated only under pinned benchmark manifests".
No number is presented as measured.

The gap is registry coverage: README's Performance section states 12 numeric
throughput/latency budgets citing ZERO claim markers, while `registries/slo.toml`
holds 4 rows, ALL `bounded_model` (FG-CFG-01..04) — zero `claim_class = "slo"`
rows and zero `claim_class = "benchmark"` rows — against slo.toml's own header
law that "every µs or throughput budget is an slo.toml row keyed
{operation_class, posture, audit_class}".
See fgdb-claims-lint-one-directional-unmarked-budgets-sdpv.

Checked and DISCARDED as non-findings (recorded so they are not re-filed):
  - README's present-tense "Every gate has a bench binary, a committed
    baseline, a variance budget, and a flamegraph artifact on regression" is
    the design register of the whole document and is quoted verbatim from open
    bead fgdb-verif-perf-apparatus-dv6p, which tracks building it.
  - `fgdb-calibrate` genuinely implements the deterministic-fallback doctrine
    (`PinnedFallback`, `pinned_fallback_oid`, and a `CandidateEqualsFallback`
    error rejecting a candidate identical to its own fallback).
  - assertion strength is real, not decorative: across all 13 crates,
    `is_ok()`-only assertions are 0-8% of 3,537 total, `assert_eq!` dominant.
  - `docs/ARCHITECTURE_DECISION_RECORD.md:95` "12 crates" is franken_networkx's
    count, not this workspace's.

title: CAS expected=None on a gone element is a match, then Unknown*
description: Reference property_of on a gone element is None. CompareAndSet expected=None therefore MATCHES and reduces to a Property after=Some, which apply refuses (unknown element). title: private_subject cache key omits toolchain, build recipe, paths, and framing
description: Fresh-eyes audit at HEAD 3d7475a plus the current uncommitted completeness follow-up. subject_key hashes only the raw concatenation of src/*.rs and src/bin/*.rs and truncates it to 64 bits. It excludes relative paths and file boundaries, scripts/lib/private_subject.sh as the compilation recipe, and rust-toolchain.toml or the resolved rustc identity. subject_is_fresh independently compares only checker-source mtimes. Therefore a tree that changes the pinned toolchain or compilation recipe while keeping checker source bytes unchanged can accept and execute a cached binary that this tree never compiled. Raw concatenation also admits trivial cross-file boundary collisions when mtimes do not force a rebuild. This contradicts the library contract that the artifact under test is the artifact THIS TREE compiles. The immediate I5 change already exposed the recipe-key problem: subject_build grew three named binaries without changing the cache key, requiring a separate fast-path completeness repair for old cache entries.
