title: proof_lanes status=checked is proved by Path::is_file(): no Lean or TLC ever runs, a 'sorry' proof would pass, and the declared-lane-only-while-stub rule has no implementation
description:
FINDING — mock/placeholder sweep phase 2 (pane4, 2026-07-26). Deepening of
question 2 into the strongest claim class in the system: formal proof.

## What it claims

`registries/proof_lanes.toml` header defines the two lane statuses:

>   declared — the lane and its artifact path are registered; the artifact
>              does not exist yet (pre-Genesis). A proof-class clause may cite
>              a declared lane **only while its own status is "stub"**.
>   checked  — the artifact exists in-repo and **is CI-checked**; registry-check
>              verifies the file is present.

and the binding law: "Every `proof`-class claim binds to exactly one named lane
here: the lane names the formal system, the model scope (exactly what is and is
not proven), and the checked artifact."

AGENTS.md, Testing Policy: "**Formal anchors (scoped, honest):** Lean for MVCC
visibility, block-level SSI safety, merge-ladder rung-1 soundness, and the Z-set
operator subset; TLA+/TLC for the two-fsync commit + recovery, compaction
publish/retire, Raft-marker interaction, and branch fork/merge."

## What it does

`tools/registry-check/src/validate.rs:661`:

```rust
"checked" => {
    if !root.join(&lane.artifact).is_file() {
        out.push(Violation::new("artifact_missing", reg, &lane.id, ...));
    }
}
```

`status = "checked"` is `Path::is_file()`. Two laws in that header have no
implementation:

1. **Nothing checks the proof.** No `lake build`, no `lean`, no TLC invocation
   exists anywhere in the repo — confirmed across `scripts/`, `check.sh`, and
   the checker sources. A `.lean` file consisting of `theorem foo : False :=
   sorry` satisfies `status = "checked"`. So does an empty file. `sorry` is
   Lean's admit-anything tactic and is THE standard failure mode of a formal
   lane: the file typechecks, the build is green, and nothing is proven. For
   TLA+ it is worse — a `.tla` model without a `.cfg`, instance bounds, and an
   actual TLC run proves nothing at all, and none of those is even a registry
   field.
2. **The "declared lane only while stub" rule does not exist in code.**
   `validate.rs:305-334` checks only that a cited `proof_lane` RESOLVES to a
   lane id. There is no cross-check that a clause promoted to `live` cites a
   lane whose status is `checked` rather than `declared`. The registry states
   this combination is illegal; nothing rejects it.

## Current exposure, measured

  - 10 of the 20 invariant clauses cite a proof lane (6 Lean, 4 TLA+).
  - All 10 lanes are `status = "declared"`.
  - Zero `.lean`, `.tla`, `.cfg`, `lakefile*` or `.thy` files exist in the repo.
  - All 20 clauses are currently `claim_class = "invariant"`, so the `proof`-class
    branch at `validate.rs:305` is not even reached yet.

So today the check is VACUOUS — there is nothing for it to be wrong about. That
is precisely why it should be fixed now: the defect fires at the moment the
first proof artifact lands, which is also the moment it stops being reviewable,
because a green `checked` row is indistinguishable from a real proof.

## What is honest here, and worth preserving

`proof_lanes.toml` is otherwise one of the best-written registries in the tree.
Every one of the 10 lanes carries a genuine negative scope clause — "Does not
cover the audit-visibility pipeline's distributed behavior", "Does not cover
W12 Meta histories or the runtime SCC oracle", "Bounded model checking within
declared instance sizes; not a full-system proof". That is exactly the "scoped,
honest" discipline AGENTS.md asks for, and the schema even rejects an empty
`model_scope`. The gap is only in what `checked` is allowed to mean.

## Which gate catches this today

None. `registry-check validate` runs `validate_proof_lanes` and passes, because
all lanes are `declared` and the `declared` arm is literally `{}`.

## Fix

1. Rename the enforcement, or enforce the name. If `checked` is to keep its
   word, `status = "checked"` must require a recorded CI run of the checker for
   that lane — `lake build` exit 0 for Lean, a TLC run with its `.cfg` and
   declared instance bounds for TLA+ — recorded the way
   `unsafe-ledger-check` records its scanner self-test before licensing any
   zero-site conclusion (`bin/unsafe-ledger-check.rs:52-70`). Until that
   machinery exists, the honest move is to rename the status to `present` so no
   reader infers a checked proof from a checked-in file.
2. Add an explicit `sorry`/`admit` scan over Lean artifacts, and require a
   `.cfg` + instance bounds field for every TLA+ lane. An axiom or `sorry` in a
   lane must fail closed and name the lane.
3. Implement the header's own stub rule: reject a `live` proof-class clause
   citing a `declared` lane. That is a five-line cross-check today and an audit
   later.
4. Give each of the three a seeded negative fixture, or they join the 253 laws
   nobody has watched fire (fgdb-validator-laws-never-witnessed-firing-xnxy).

Related: fgdb-clause-promotion-to-live-is-unguarded-nllh is the same failure
shape on `negative_test_entrypoint`; fgdb-checker-index-live-is-only-file-existence-tl0o
is the same `is_file()` primitive standing in for liveness in a third registry.
Three registries now prove three different kinds of "this is enforced" with the
same call. That pattern is worth fixing once, centrally.
close_reason:
FIXED (pane4, 2026-07-26). `status = "checked"` is now adjudicated by `liveness::Prover::assess_lane` — the SAME reader that adjudicates `status = "live"`, not a second copy of it.

WHAT LANDED
  liveness.rs   assess_lane: path safety on EVERY lane (declared included —
                Path::join discards the root on an absolute path, so an unsafe
                artifact passes is_file() the instant somebody promotes it),
                artifact presence, the DELEGATED gate read, and the artifact's
                own capacity to fail. New registry field `checked_by` names the
                checker_index symbol of the gate that runs the prover; that row
                must be status=live AND survive Prover::assess in full. Lean: a
                proposition must be stated and no sorry/admit/axiom/native_decide
                may appear in live code. TLA+: a companion .cfg must name an
                INVARIANT/PROPERTY with an operand. mask_formal is the one new
                reader and serves BOTH languages (Lean and TLA+ differ in three
                comment tokens and both nest) — two maskers would be this bug in
                miniature. Completeness guard: a lane naming a system no reader
                adjudicates is reported, never passed.
  validate.rs   both call sites delegate; self-test consulted FIRST so a reader
                that stopped reading cannot produce a clean sweep. The header's
                second law is enforced: proof_lane_declared_while_clause_promoted.

MUTATION PROOF, BOTH DIRECTIONS
  Positive: every mutant asserted to satisfy legacy_lane_is_file_predicate —
  the pre-fix predicate kept verbatim — so each test states the old reader could
  not tell the cases apart.
  Negative (measured on a depth-matched scratch copy): reverting the lane body to
  root.join(artifact).is_file() turns FIVE tests red (38/43 green) —
  a_lane_whose_gate_is_not_live_is_not_checked,
  a_proof_that_admits_its_conclusion_is_not_checked,
  a_model_that_checks_no_property_is_not_checked,
  a_lane_of_an_unreadable_system_is_not_silently_checked,
  a_lane_artifact_path_is_checked_before_it_is_joined.
  Deleting the clause law turns ONE red: claims_proof_lane_declared_requires_a_stub_clause.
  Under BOTH reversions every control stays green — including
  claims_real_registries_validate and the pre-existing
  claims_proof_lane_manifest_resolves, which is exactly why nothing caught this.

VACUITY CONTROL THAT FIRES
  All 10 lanes are declared; zero .lean/.tla/.cfg/lakefile* exist, so the checked
  arm is quantified over nothing. proof_lane_checked_arm_is_vacuous_today_and_this_is_what_licenses_it
  promotes a REAL shipped lane the way a future author would and requires the
  readers to produce a real defect from real registry data. The checker binary
  also reports checker_liveness_self_test cases=52 failed=0 licensed=true.

GATES  metamorphic 43/43, claims 14/14 (standalone rustc, lock-free); check.sh
  reports registry_validated proof_lanes rows=10 violations=0 pass; cargo fmt
  clean; cargo test --workspace passed; ubs 0 critical on the 5 changed files.

PROVENANCE ERRATUM  the change was swept into d1699fb 'chore(beads): close l6xd
  on inline field ruling' by a concurrent pane while my files were staged. The
  content is intact and complete (1350 insertions, exactly my six files); only the
  commit subject misattributes it. Not amended — d1699fb is another pane's commit
  object and rewriting it in a swarm is the hazard git-amend-races-other-panes names.

RESIDUE (not a defect in this fix)  no gate yet RUNS a prover: no lake/lean/TLC
  invocation exists. That is now SAFE rather than silent — a lane cannot be
  'checked' without naming a live gate, so the first real proof artifact must land
  with its runner. Filing that as its own bead is deliberately deferred: a CREATED
  bead record moves the provenance pins and costs a re-freeze cycle.

title: Produce the six §15.7 papers/technical reports with executable receipts
description:
## What & scope
Produce the six standing papers/technical reports promised by §15.7 from the implemented, verified, and benchmarked system. This is not a prose-only marketing pass: each publication is a versioned claim bundle backed by executable artifacts, stable registry rows, negative evidence, benchmark manifests, replay commands, and an explicit proof-scope/no-claim boundary. The six deliverables are:
1. **Strata: temperature-tiered transactional adjacency** — versioned delta blocks, sealed compressed CSR runs, archived anchors, label-independent descriptors, migration decision cards, representation equivalence, larger-than-memory scans, and honest ingest/scan/churn trade-offs.
2. **One Version Universe** — MVCC publication, retained temporal history, branches, replication order, change subscriptions, and their distinct retention/proof products over one content-addressed, RaptorQ-protected commit stream.
3. **Refinable predicate witnesses** — graph serializability with positive, negative, gap, and path observations; concretization and may-affect laws; refinement budgets and conservative abort; optimizer/workspace transport; false-conflict measurements without per-edge read tracking.
4. **Plan certificates and decision cards** — deterministic and auditable execution, answer-requirement/answer-contract binding, policy epochs, replay closure, pinned fallbacks, propensity and expected-benefit disclosures, and byte-reproducible STRICT results.
5. **The externally verifiable graph database** — transparency checkpoints, WitnessPolicy epochs, MMR inclusion/consistency proofs, filtered-changefeed delta commitments, proof-scope labels, and computed durability certificates over the fountain-coded stream.
6. **Calibrated adaptivity** — anytime-valid statistical governance for self-tuning tiering/planning/pacing, assumption-scoped FG-CAL/FG-EVID claims, promotion/fallback rules, and evidence that statistical machinery controls named decisions rather than becoming ornamental telemetry.

## Why and over-arching intent
§15.7 says the ambition includes the receipts. Public trust comes from making the novel claims falsifiable by outsiders, not from describing architecture after the fact. These reports also defend B1–B5 against accidental claim inflation: each separates proved safety, model-checked bounded behavior, executable differential evidence, empirical performance, calibration assumptions, configuration policy, and unproved scope. Publication is therefore part of Gate G4 “Leapfrog, Published,” not post-release collateral.

## Required artifact contract
Each deliverable owns a versioned `PublicationClaimManifest` with:
- publication ID/title/version, source revision, registry-table digests, active capability/posture/format profile, datasets/workloads, toolchain and machine manifest;
- claim ledger partitioned into `FG-INV`, `FG-PROOF`, `FG-EVID`, `FG-CAL`, `FG-CFG`, and `FG-COST`, with one resolvable checker/proof/model/benchmark/replay artifact per claim;
- negative-evidence ledger and rejected-alternative record, including failing/degenerate cases and limits;
- reproduction bundle with commands, deterministic seeds, crashpacks/traces, golden vectors, raw distributions, baseline/fallback policy results, and artifact checksums;
- independence disclosures for reference oracles, external comparators, reviewers, and any foundation-library behavior relied upon;
- exact no-claim boundary: proof abstractions/bounds, empirical population and confidence method, model assumptions, unsupported features/postures, and what a result does not establish;
- archival and link-integrity manifest so the report remains reproducible if an external comparator or project disappears.

A shared cross-report glossary pins terms such as logical versus physical state, durability versus availability, detection versus prevention, membership-only proof scope, reference oracle, differential comparator, STRICT determinism, and replay. Cross-report claims cite one canonical claim record rather than drifting copies. Report text and tables are generated or checked against claim manifests; a stale registry hash, missing artifact, moved claim scope, or unpriced protocol change fails publication CI.

## Evidence requirements by report
- Strata binds W3 representation-equivalence/crash tests, tier-migration churn and dwell evidence, workload manifests, bytes-per-live-edge accounting, and fallback/static-policy comparisons.
- One Version Universe binds Chronicle D1/D2/root recovery, retention/GC/branch/Ripple/replication evidence, and explicitly shows where one mechanism still has distinct proof and retention products.
- Predicate witnesses bind formal lane manifests, independent small-model histories, mutation families, optimizer transport, and false-conflict/cost distributions.
- Certificates/cards bind canonical byte vectors, replay across schedules, answer-equivalence tests for physical choices, and answer-affecting/canonical-state sequencing proofs.
- External verification binds marked format-registry rows, WitnessPolicy rotation, MMR/changefeed/durability golden vectors, attack/tamper fixtures, and independent-verifier differential results.
- Calibrated adaptivity binds named decision cards/evidence.toml/slo.toml rows, anytime-valid simulations, assumption violations, fallback activation, regret/churn, and policy-coverage disclosures.

## Unit and conformance tests
- `six_publication_manifests_complete`: exactly six live manifests, titles/scopes match this inventory, IDs are unique, and every required section is present.
- `claim_has_resolvable_receipt`: every claim resolves to an immutable evidence artifact and checker command; dangling or mutable-only references fail.
- `claim_type_scope_is_honest`: fixtures that promote FG-EVID/FG-CAL to an invariant, omit assumptions, or overstate a bounded model are rejected.
- `cross_report_claims_do_not_drift`: duplicated claim IDs byte-match the canonical record and no report carries a divergent paraphrased threshold.
- `negative_evidence_and_no_claim_boundary_required`: each report has at least its registered adverse cases and explicit exclusions.
- `reproduction_bundle_hashes_verify`: commands, inputs, outputs, seeds, environment manifests, and checksums form a closed bundle.
- `published_costs_match_appendix_g`: every performance claim resolves to an operation-cost class/counting unit and passes the same-change law.
- `external_links_are_not_evidence_roots`: removing all network links still leaves a locally verifiable evidence closure.

## E2E and adversarial proof
In a clean, isolated release fixture, build all six reports from pinned registries and evidence; verify the bundle offline; replay at least one canonical success and one negative/adverse fixture per report; regenerate plots/tables from raw artifacts; and compare every generated claim/table against the committed report. Then inject a stale registry digest, delete a referenced local artifact from the fixture, change an empirical threshold without its raw distribution, relabel a calibrated claim as an invariant, and alter a cross-report term: every mutation must fail with the exact owning claim/report. An independent reviewer follows only the published reproduction index and reaches the declared results without consulting the design-plan prose.

## Detailed logging and observability
The publication pipeline emits deterministic JSONL events `publication_started`, `claim_resolved`, `artifact_verified`, `replay_started`, `replay_finished`, `negative_case_verified`, `scope_checked`, `report_rendered`, and `publication_sealed`. Every event includes `publication_id`, `claim_id?`, `claim_type?`, `source_revision`, registry/evidence digests, command ID, seed/environment ID, outcome, elapsed/resource summary, and failure code. Sensitive/internal paths are redacted through the ordinary observability policy. The E2E suite proves the event stream alone can reconstruct which claims were checked, which artifacts/replays supported them, and why a failed publication was blocked.

## Risks and rejected alternatives
Rejected: six essays with a shared bibliography but no executable receipts; benchmark cherry-picking; treating a published design as an inherited proof; collapsing proof, model, differential, calibration, and empirical claims; depending on live external URLs for reproduction; publishing only successful cases; moving thresholds without Appendix G updates. If evidence does not support a planned claim, narrow or remove the claim—never weaken the gate or invent a narrative.

## Completion and provenance
Complete only when all six sealed report bundles, offline reproduction indexes, negative-evidence records, claim-scope reviews, and publication CI gates are green. Source: §15.7 “Publish the design”; §§15.1–15.6 verification doctrine; §17 benchmark honesty laws; Appendix F claim/invariant registry; Appendix G cost registry.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Exactly six versioned publication manifests and report bundles exist, matching §15.7's six subjects with no omissions or merged-away claim surface.
- Every published claim resolves offline to typed evidence, negative evidence, scope/no-claim boundaries, and a reproducible command bundle; all publication unit/adversarial/E2E/log-reconstruction tests pass.
- Cross-report terminology/claim IDs, active registry digests, Appendix G costs, raw benchmark distributions, and archived link-integrity closure are current.
- Gate G4 consumes the sealed publication digest; no unsupported or failed claim is narrated as complete.

title: CAS NoOp and clear-label on a gone element must not fail the batch
description: WriteMismatchPolicy::NoOp on a live vertex with the wrong expected continues the batch (existing spine test). On a missing or prefix-deleted element it still returns UnknownVertex/UnknownEdge before the policy is consulted, so a sibling create is lost. Reference property_of on a gone element is None, so expected=Some is a mismatch and NoOp is Nothing. set_vertex_label(..., false) on a gone vertex is the same vacuous absence (not a member). AbortWrite and set(..., true)/set(..., Some) still refuse Unknown*.
close_reason: CAS NoOp on a missing or prefix-deleted element continues; AbortWrite still Unknown*. set_vertex_label(..., false) on a gone vertex is Nothing; adding a label still UnknownVertex. Spine locks sibling creates and the AbortWrite/add-label refusals.

title: Fence Database::compact across cancellable root-slot publication
description: Database::write marks the borrowed handle NeedsAuthoritativeRecovery before any cancellable post-D2 publication await, but Database::compact remains Healthy while awaiting RootStore::publish_evidenced. If the future is dropped after the new slot is durable but before publish_evidenced returns, the handle retains the old snapshot and slot_generation. A later write can reuse the already-published generation for different content, provoking non-monotonic or divergent root selection. This is a same-handle cancellation-correctness defect at the sole mutable root authority.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic lab-VFS regression cancels compact at the root-slot sync and proves the borrowed handle is fenced, graph/identity reads refuse, and recover_authoritatively reopens the compacted state. Ordinary compaction and write behavior remain green; no new publication substrate is introduced.

title: G0 erratum: plan:1990 bucket shape/law is internally contradictory — resolved by class-scoped committed (fgdb-a61t)
description:
NORMATIVE CONFLICT (found by MistyJay review of fgdb-a61t). COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN...md:1990 spells each bucket as {hard_limit,protected_maintenance_reserve,ordinary_reserved,maintenance_reserved,committed} with law 'ordinary use satisfies committed+ordinary_reserved <= hard_limit-protected_reserve', and the IMMEDIATELY FOLLOWING sentence says 'registered maintenance consumes only its named reserve'. The two are jointly unsatisfiable whenever maintenance usage is committed: the single classless committed pool is billed against the ordinary band, so maintenance committed usage eats the band (contradicting sentence 2), and a full band makes a valid maintenance reservation unchargeable (voiding the reserve the shape exists to protect — probe-confirmed pre-fix, fgdb-a61t).

RESOLUTION LANDED (5b914ec + review follow-ups): BucketState splits committed into ordinary_committed/maintenance_committed; the laws become ordinary_committed+ordinary_reserved <= hard-reserve and maintenance_committed+maintenance_reserved <= reserve (total <= hard follows and is kept as explicit backstop). The summed committed() view is retained. Charge/adjust/release/transfer/expire thread the entry's class so the split holds across the whole lifecycle; transfer netting across shared ancestors is class-scoped on both sides. This resolution satisfies sentence 2 (the semantic intent) and keeps sentence 1's law shape per class.

PLAN AMENDMENT PROPOSED (for the G0/catalog lane — not landed by this bead): replace the bucket shape at plan:1990 with {hard_limit,protected_maintenance_reserve,ordinary_reserved,maintenance_reserved,ordinary_committed,maintenance_committed} and the law with 'ordinary use satisfies ordinary_committed+ordinary_reserved <= hard_limit-protected_reserve, and maintenance use satisfies maintenance_committed+maintenance_reserved <= protected_reserve, so registered maintenance consumes only its named reserve and a reservation always guarantees chargeability'.

PROVENANCE: defect + probe — SimAndFoundations scout (fgdb-a61t); fix — VioletBasin (5b914ec); normative-conflict identification — MistyJay (mail 21533). Registry rows citing the five-vector shape need the erratum marker convention (post_erratum_*).

title: NENF dual-delete cascade is apply-safe on both fold and reference
description:
The engine fold and the reference graph-diff are both supposed to emit apply-safe NENF. Two holes remain after cczg/s9ja.

1. `fold_target_disjoint`: absorb_edge clears a later DeleteEdge by setting deleted=None, but a DeleteEdge *after* DeleteVertex writes deleted back. The fold then emits both rows. Apply is tag-ordered (DeleteVertex 0x03 before DeleteEdge 0x04), so the standalone delete hits UnknownEdge. Same hole for a later Property/ValidTime on a cascade-owned durable edge.

2. `normalize` (reference): each deleted VId is emitted with the full basis incident set. A shared eid therefore appears on both endpoints. apply_template is byte-sorted (VId order for DeleteVertex); the second apply fails CascadeImageMismatch. The engine fold already partitions to min VId; the oracle does not.

Related to cczg / s9ja / 17ht / 819.2. Not parent-child to open 819. Do not close 819.

## Success Criteria
- DeleteVertex then DeleteEdge of a cascade member folds to only the DeleteVertex.
- DeleteVertex then edge property/valid-time does not re-emit the mutation.
- Reference dual-delete of both endpoints emits the shared eid only on the smaller VId, and those rows apply to the basis graph.
- 819 stays open.
close_reason: fold_target_disjoint now keeps cascade-owned durable eids from re-emitting DeleteEdge/Property/ValidTime after DeleteVertex (apply is tag-ordered). Reference normalize assigns a shared cascade eid only to the smallest deleted VId so apply_template matches the live incident set. fold 7 + reference lib 15 + spine 42/42 + spine_differential 16/16 + clippy -D warnings on delta-types/reference/fgdb. 819 stays open.

title: Recover owner-bound supplemental posture unions in a18/a20; split the a03 anonymous-owner gap
description:
The structural source census drops the BODY of any braced arm whose head name is exactly one of the
role tokens `Local`, `Meta`, or `Shard`. Mutation-proven with a name-swap control and two conformant
controls. 110 of 114 role-token arm-head sites in Appendix A are affected; at 5 of them NO member of
the body appears anywhere in the census, so 11 real source-spelled members are invisible to the
entire Appendix A closure and cannot be landed by anyone.

## The mechanism, proven by mutation not by reading

One reader: standalone rustc over tools/registry-check/src/appendix_source.rs + hash.rs, full
Appendix source lines 1388..2728, all 21 live slice boundaries. Baseline at HEAD 72aec3f is
byte-exact against every released pin (a20 = 182 field / 26 top / 6 union / 17 arm / 146 ambiguity;
11740 field candidates over 1020 owners appendix-wide).

Subject: the `RestoreServicePromotionManifest` posture body at a20:2575, spelled

    ... and exactly one body: `Local{local_prepare_evidence:PortableCertificateProjection<
    LocalRestoreServicePrepareCertificate>,local_configuration_and_endpoint_commitment}` or
    `Sharded{meta_prepare_evidence:...,sorted_shard_ready_evidence[...],complete_group_topology_
    configuration_and_endpoint_commitment}`.

BASELINE: owner `Sharded` carries the second arm's 3 members. Owner `Local` is absent, and both of
its member names are absent from all 182 a20 candidates and from all 11740 appendix-wide candidates.

CONTROL 1 — paired name swap, member lists untouched. Rewrite the one sentence so the FIRST arm is
named `Sharded` and the SECOND is named `Local`:
    a20 182 -> 181; owner `Sharded` now carries local_prepare_evidence and
    local_configuration_and_endpoint_commitment; owner `Local` is absent.
The loss followed the NAME, not the position. "First arm of an alternation" is therefore FALSIFIED
as the mechanism.

CONTROL 2 — rename the second arm only, one name at a time:
    Sharded -> Meta     a20 182 -> 179   body DROPPED
    Sharded -> Shard    a20 182 -> 179   body DROPPED
    Sharded -> Local    a20 182 -> 179   body DROPPED
    Sharded -> Global   a20 182 -> 182   body kept
    Sharded -> Zebra    a20 182 -> 182   body kept      <- conformant control
    Sharded -> Sharded  a20 182 -> 182   body kept      <- identity control
So the filter is the role-token set {Local, Meta, Shard} exactly. `Global` is NOT in it, which is
itself a tell: whatever list this is, it is not the full role vocabulary.

CONTROL 3 — rename the first arm `Local` -> `Sharded` (both arms then share a name):
    a20 182 -> 184, recovering exactly the 2 lost members.
Renaming `Local` to anything outside the set recovers its body in full.

## Denominator, and the recovered/lost split

Sweeping the Appendix source for `` `?\b(Local|Meta|Shard|Global)\{ `` arm heads:

    Local 47   Meta 32   Shard 31   Global 4      = 114 sites
    dropped: 110 of 114 (every Local/Meta/Shard site), across 18 of the 21 slices
    upper bound on affected member positions (brace-matched, top-level comma split): 367

Those 367 are NOT all invisible. For many sites the same members are also emitted under the correct
`Union<Role>.Arm.member` depth-2 path, so the pseudo-owner drop is a duplicate loss. Measured
directly: of the 107 sites whose body has at least one lowercase member name,

    102  at least one member name appears somewhere in the 11740 candidates  (recoverable)
      5  NO member of the body appears anywhere in the 11740 candidates      (fully lost)

The five fully-lost sites, 11 member candidates in total:

    a03:1468  `Local{registry_ref}`                                              1
    a03:1468  `Meta{registry_ref}`                                               1
    a03:1468  `Shard{active_projection_ref,projected_registry_digest,...}`       4
    a18:2443  `Local{target_tombstone_skeleton_recipe,no_target_observation_...}`3
    a20:2575  `Local{local_prepare_evidence,local_configuration_and_endpoint_...}`2

NOTE the direction of the error bar: the "recoverable" test matches on the member's LAST PATH
SEGMENT only, and common names like `command_ref` collide across the whole appendix. It is therefore
PERMISSIVE. 5 sites / 11 members is a LOWER bound on the fully-lost population, not an estimate.

## Second, separable defect at the same sites: the pseudo-owner shape

Where the body is not dropped, it is often attached to a bare arm name as if that name were a
top-level schema. 19 of the 1020 census owners are a bare name the catalog also carries as a landed
`source_arm_name`: Abandoned, Acknowledged, Commit, CompactedTerminal, Consumed,
DetachedToProtocolRetention, InstallProvisionalCut, NotRequired, Operational, Published,
ReleasedUnacked, RequestTerminalAbort, Retired, Sharded, StrongCommandRef, StrongGlobalCommandRef,
StrongRef, StrongShardCommandRef, WeakMarkerIdentity.

For `Abandoned` (a18) BOTH forms are emitted — 3 members under the pseudo-owner at depth 1 AND 8
under the correct `RestoreTerminalPinBasis<Role>.Abandoned.*` path at depth 2 — so there the
pseudo-owner is redundant. For a20's `Sharded` only the pseudo-owner exists: a20's union census is 6
and all six are accounted for by other unions, so the manifest posture body union is not censused at
all, and there is no `RestoreServicePromotionManifest.Sharded.*` or `.Local.*` candidate.

## Why a20 is blocked on this today

a20's actionable field residue is 9 once the two ww9g-unblocked rows land (182 = 50 landed + 55
interior + 68 source-typeless + 9). Two of the 9 are `Sharded.meta_prepare_evidence` and
`Sharded.sorted_shard_ready_evidence`. Their only census host is the bare name `Sharded`, and a20's
settled adjudication (gotcha 1, which resolved a05's flag) is that `Sharded` is the manifest posture
arm and must NOT be minted top-level. Those two cannot land until the posture body is censused as a
union with arms.

`Local`'s two members are worse than blocked: they are not in the residue at all, because nothing
counts them. A closure reporting itself complete over 182 candidates is complete over a source that
has 184.

## Relationship to the closed predecessor

Same class as fgdb-2qb6 (census drops the FIRST name of every "`A` and `B` are ..." definition,
13 of 13 sites, fixed at 30eb809) but a different construction and a different reader path: that fix
distributed a prose DEFINITION across a conjunction; this is a structural BODY alternation keyed on
the arm's head name. 30eb809 did not recover these — every measurement above was taken at HEAD,
after it.

## Where to start

The reader path is the arm-head/owner branch in tools/registry-check/src/appendix_source.rs. Look for
where a role token is recognized: the {Local, Meta, Shard} / not-Global asymmetry says the list is
hard-coded and is being consulted at a position where it does not belong. Fixing it moves the a20
field candidate count 182 -> 184 and every slice census pin in the 18 affected slices, so it is a
whole-appendix re-pin, not a local repair — the same shape as 30eb809, which is the precedent to
follow for sequencing.

title: WriteBatch refuses edges whose endpoints are not live
description:
`add_edge` / `ensure_edge_by_triple` can commit a CreateEdge whose src/dst are not live. The reference apply refuses that as `DanglingEndpoint`. A durable stream the oracle cannot replay poisons the spine.

## Background
`fgdb-reference::ReferenceGraph::apply_row` checks referential integrity before inserting a CreateEdge. `Database::write` and `BlockWriter` do not. The generated mixer never proposes this (it requires two live vertices), so the spine differential stays green while a caller can commit a graph that capsule replay cannot materialize.

This is a write-path preflight, same discipline as AlreadyLive (fgdb-kokz): refuse before D2. Related to the live WriteBatch line. Do **not** parent-child to open `819`. Closing this does not close `819`/`og6n`.

## Technical Approach
- After the ensure-noop continue, before emitting CreateEdge, require both endpoints live at that point in the batch (prefix create, not prefix-deleted, or fold-live).
- Missing src is checked before missing dst (deterministic).
- Typed `WriteError::DanglingEndpoint { eid, endpoint }`. Not UnknownVertex — the write is an edge create.
- Same-batch create-then-add_edge stays lawful.

## Success Criteria
- add_edge / ensure of a new triple with a missing endpoint refuses before D2; frontier unchanged.
- Both endpoints missing names src.
- Only dst missing names dst.
- Existing same-batch create+edge fixtures stay green.
- Independent: engine refusal agrees with reference `ApplyError::DanglingEndpoint`.
- `819` stays open.

## Test Plan
- Spine: the three refusals above plus frontier unchanged.
- `cargo test -p fgdb --test spine -- dangling`
- `cargo test -p fgdb-sim --test spine_differential -- dangling`
close_reason: add_edge/ensure of a new triple now refuse WriteError::DanglingEndpoint before D2 when src/dst are not live. Same-batch create+edge still lawful. Engine refusal matches reference ApplyError::DanglingEndpoint. spine 41/41, spine_differential 16/16. 819 stays open.

title: g0 ADR e2e comment claims the script is not in check.sh; it is
description:
## What

scripts/g0_architecture_decisions_e2e.sh line 41 reads:

  # Bead-dependent expectations are DERIVED from the declared registry, not
  # hand-copied. Every bead filing moves them, and a hand-copied literal drifted
  # unnoticed for ~15 filings precisely because this script is not in check.sh.

The last clause is false at HEAD a4d60fc.

## Measured

registries/checker_index.toml carries TWO live rows naming this artifact:

  symbol = "g0_architecture_decisions_e2e"   kind = "script"  status = "live"
  symbol = "e2e:g0_architecture_decisions"   kind = "script"  status = "live"

scripts/check.sh live_gate_inventory() emits (kind, artifact) pairs for every
`status = "live"` checker and pipes them through `sort -u`, so the two rows
collapse to one; run_registered_gates() then dispatches `kind = script` to
`run_registered_command "$kind" "$artifact" bash "$root/$artifact"`. The script
is therefore executed by check.sh.

`git log -S` puts the comment and the wiring in the SAME commit, 8ea2055
("fix(g0): derive the ADR e2e bead expectations and wire it into the composite
gate"), so the present tense "is not" was wrong on arrival -- the sentence is a
correct PAST explanation of why the literal drifted, wearing the wrong tense.

## Why it matters

It is a load-bearing claim in the argument for deriving the expectations rather
than hand-copying them. A reader who believes the gate is unrun will also
believe a drifted literal there is cheap, which is precisely the defect 8ea2055
fixed.

## Repair

One clause, in the file the fgdb-hcvx rename already touched. Past-tense it
("...drifted unnoticed for ~15 filings while this script was not yet in
check.sh") or drop the causal clause. No code change. Needs the catalog token
only because scripts/ is contended, and no build: the claim is verified by
reading checker_index.toml and check.sh, both of which this bead quotes.

Found while landing fgdb-hcvx (a4d60fc).

  2026-07-25  8ea2055            wrote the comment AND added a hard-coded
                                 `scripts/g0_architecture_decisions_e2e.sh` line
                                 to check.sh, "step 7 of 8". Its own commit

comments.author: JadeSnow
comments.text:
PREMISE RE-DERIVED 2026-08-04 at the PINNED REV. The headline HOLDS; the second clause in this bead title is FALSE, and correcting it narrows the defect to something actionable.

MEASURED against /home/ubuntu/.cargo/git/checkouts/asupersync-b12181f74b36652e/3e8d08e (the rev
Cargo.lock pins, 4 occurrences). METHOD NOTE FIRST, because I nearly filed a false report: my initial
grep hit checkout 3339812 and found NOTHING -- no request_cx_with_budget, no test-internals -- which
would have "confirmed" the bead for entirely the wrong reason. FOUR asupersync checkouts coexist
under one cargo dir. Always resolve the rev from Cargo.lock before grepping a git dependency.

CLAIM 1 -- "the documented path Runtime::request_cx_with_budget is pub(crate)": TRUE.
  src/runtime/builder.rs:3453
    pub(crate) fn request_cx_with_budget(&self, budget: Budget) -> crate::cx::Cx
  And no public method on Runtime returns a Cx at all (grepped src/ for pub fn returning Cx).

CLAIM 2 -- "the test-internals feature the cfg-gates reference is not declared": FALSE AT THIS REV.
  It IS declared, Cargo.toml:109-114, verbatim:
      # Enable internal test helpers for integration tests.
      # This exposes private APIs like Cx::new() and is NOT for production use.
      test-internals = [ "dep:tracing", "dep:tracing-log", "dep:tracing-subscriber", "dep:visibility" ]
  and it is consumed at Cargo.toml:234 and :613 (required-features). So an external crate CAN enable
  it. This clause also appears in crates/fgdb/examples/open_a_database.rs ("asupersync [features]
  table does not define test-internals") -- that doc comment is stale/incorrect at the pinned rev and
  should be corrected wherever the bead is cited.

WHAT SURVIVES, and it is the real defect, now narrower: there is NO PRODUCTION path for an external
crate to originate a capability-bearing Cx. Enumerated every public origination in src/:
  Cx::for_testing / for_testing_with_budget / for_testing_with_io  -- cx.rs:4657/4689/4718, all
    #[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-internals"))]. Reachable, but ONLY by opting into a feature whose
    own comment says "NOT for production use".
  Cx::restrict, RequestRegion::cx_narrow/cx_readonly, grpc cx_narrow/cx_readonly -- these NARROW an
    existing Cx or hang off a web/grpc region; none originates one for an embedded library consumer.
  net/atp/test_utils::test_cx() -- pub mod, but delegates to the gated for_testing_with_budget.
  Cx::detached_cancel_context() -- cx.rs:3964, PUBLIC AND UNGATED, and I record it because it is the
    one counterexample to a bare "no public constructor" phrasing. It is not a counterexample to the
    SUBSTANTIVE claim: it deliberately returns Cx<cap::None> with an empty runtime capability mask --
    its own doc says it "cannot provide spawn, timer, random, I/O, or remote authority" and exists
    for "adapters and CLI diagnostics". A database cannot run on it.

SO THE CORRECTED DEFECT, one sentence: asupersync sanctions request_cx_with_budget as (its own words)
"the only ambient-free way to mint a Cx in production" and then declares it pub(crate), leaving every
external consumer to choose between a test-only feature and a capability-less diagnostic context.

SCOPE. This is UPSTREAM (/dp/franken... the asupersync repo), not a frankengraphdb code change --
the fix is a visibility change plus whatever ambient-freedom argument justified pub(crate), and it
must be made and re-pinned upstream the way fgdb-4bxh handled its upstream repairs. Nothing in
crates/ can route around it: fgdb::Database takes &CommitCx, which comes from
PurposeContexts::narrow_runtime_root(&Cx<cap::All>), and cap::All is exactly what no public
production path yields. The spine example is honest about this already -- it states it proves the
spine is "consumable from a program" but NOT that "the database runs on a production runtime".

NOT DONE BY ME: no upstream edit. I hold no lease on the asupersync repo and this bead is filed
against frankengraphdb; someone with the upstream lane should take the visibility change, and the
title of this bead should drop the test-internals clause when they do.

title: Chronicle decode panics on self-consistent oversized transfer length
description: Fresh-eyes review found decode_object constructing asupersync InactivationDecoder with InactivationDecoder::new(k, symbol_size, seed), where k is derived from the capsule header transfer_length. The header is untrusted: an attacker can change transfer_length and recompute the unkeyed EncodingId, after which capsule recovery filters every now-invalid symbol but still reaches decoder construction. The pinned asupersync API explicitly documents that new panics for k == 0 or k > 56,403 and requires try_new on attacker-influenced FEC/OTI paths. Thus a self-consistent oversized descriptor converts malformed durable input into a process panic instead of typed fail-closed recovery. Replace new with try_new mapped to SymbolizeError::InvalidParameters. Add a regression that forges transfer_length to 56,404 * symbol_size, recomputes EncodingId using public reconstruction inputs, supplies no authentic symbols, and proves recovery returns CapsuleError::Recovery(SymbolizeError::InvalidParameters) without unwinding. Mutation back to new must red the discriminator.

title: Concurrent genesis transactions both create the same branch
description: Fresh-eye review of commit 4f860e9. Transaction::begin_genesis (crates/fgdb-reference/src/txn.rs:136-144 at that commit) checks coordinate absence only when the transaction begins. commit at lines 243-284 never revalidates that the genesis coordinate is still absent and conflict_keys_since has no coordinate-creation key. Reproducer: on an empty ReferenceDatabase, begin two genesis transactions for the same G/B; first creates v1 and commits at seq 1; second creates disjoint v2 and commits at seq 2. Its write set does not intersect the first creation, so both succeed even though both claimed to be the FIRST transaction that creates the branch. Closure: carry genesis-vs-existing intent into commit certification and first-committer-win on coordinate creation, with a negative concurrent-genesis law proving the loser cannot append disjoint effects to the winner-created branch.
close_reason: Landed as e75d9a5. Same shape underneath: a transaction's claim is not only 'these elements were unwritten' but 'my basis was the state at snapshot.high of this lineage', and the conflict rule only checked the first half. re6w: conflict_keys_since now walks the LINEAGE with a per-ancestor cap, so inherited records in (snapshot.high, boundary] are conflicts; a historical child transaction gets Conflicted instead of TxnError::Apply. dfk3: ConflictKey::CoordinateExistence, named by a genesis claim and by any coordinate created after a transaction's basis, so two racing genesis transactions with DISJOINT effects can no longer both commit. Five laws; each revert reddens exactly its closure law. Three of the five exist to stop the fix overshooting — a child at the current boundary must NOT conflict with the parent's post-fork commits (else branch isolation becomes branch serialization), an uncontested genesis must still commit, and no ROW may name CoordinateExistence. The Apply doc no longer claims the conflict rule is complete; that claim of completeness is what made this class hard to see.

title: ReferenceDatabase accepts gapped and globally reversed CommitSeq histories
description:
## Finding
Fresh-eye review of commit 24497213a66680e5dbbd22c4e3cd940c9c2617bd found that ReferenceDatabase::apply_template enforces CommitSeq only against each touched coordinate. It has no database-wide replay frontier.

## Reproducer
Starting from ReferenceDatabase::new():
1. apply a template at CommitSeq(2) to coordinate A: accepted;
2. apply a template at CommitSeq(1) to previously untouched coordinate B: accepted;
3. CommitSeq(0) is also accepted on a fresh coordinate;
4. an empty LogicalDeltaTemplate is valid and applies without recording any sequence at all.

This admits histories the new comments explicitly call gap-free and monotone. Chronicle MarkerChain starts at 1 and requires the exact next sequence; LocalDeltaBatchIndex likewise has one global frontier and rejects gaps/duplicates. Per-coordinate applied_through is still useful because intervening commits can touch other coordinates, but it cannot substitute for the stream frontier.

## Required closure
- Add a distinct database-wide applied stream frontier initialized to CommitSeq(0).
- Require apply_template to carry exactly frontier + 1 and advance it once, atomically, including for an empty/no-effect template.
- Retain per-coordinate applied_through and update it only for touched coordinates, so commit 1 on A, commit 2 on B, commit 3 on A remains valid while a global gap or reversal is refused.
- Preserve all-or-nothing refusal.
- Add discriminator tests for first seq 0, first seq 2, cross-coordinate 2 then 1, empty templates, duplicate/lower sequences, and the valid cross-coordinate skip case.

If apply_template is intentionally a prevalidated low-level operation, narrow its contract and type the proof instead of claiming it materializes a gap-free stream while accepting arbitrary sequences.
notes:
RE-DERIVED 2026-07-30 (JadeSnow) — PREMISE CONFIRMED, all four parts, by reading apply_template rather than trusting the report.

apply_template compares commit_seq only against candidate.applied_through for each coordinate the
template touches (crates/fgdb-reference/src/lib.rs, the SequenceNotAdvancing guard). There is no
database-wide frontier, so:
1. seq 2 to coordinate A then seq 1 to a previously untouched B is accepted — globally reversed;
2. a gap is accepted, since a fresh coordinate has no applied_through to compare against;
3. CommitSeq(0) is accepted on a fresh coordinate;
4. an EMPTY template applies successfully and records nothing — the entry loop never runs, so no
   sequence is consumed and *self = candidate is a no-op.

Part 4 is the one worth naming separately: it contradicts a law that already landed. The write-path
laws in fgdb-sim assert that a transaction with no effects appends NO marker at all ('not an empty
capsule, not a marker with no effects — nothing'). A template that applies while recording nothing is
the same shape one layer down, and the oracle currently accepts it.

WHY THIS IS EXACT-NEXT AND NOT MERELY MONOTONE. Chronicle's MarkerChain starts at 1 and requires the
exact next sequence; LocalDeltaBatchIndex keeps one global frontier and rejects gaps AND duplicates.
A gapped history therefore cannot come from the commit stream, so the oracle admitting one lets a
differential pass on a history the durable layer could never produce — which is the specific way an
oracle becomes useless: it stops being able to reject.

PER-COORDINATE applied_through IS STILL NEEDED and must not be replaced. Intervening commits can
touch other coordinates, so a coordinate's own frontier is genuinely below the global one; the fix is
a SECOND frontier beside it, not a substitution. Deleting the per-coordinate check would break the
fork boundary derivation and the conflict window (see
fgdb-reference-historical-fork-conflict-lineage-re6w).

SCOPED HONESTLY: NOT ATTEMPTED IN THIS PASS. The fix changes the sequence discipline every test
fixture in the crate relies on — three test files apply templates at hand-chosen sequences — and it
must land with its fixtures corrected in the same commit or the suite is red. Left open with the
analysis rather than half-applied, which would leave the tree worse than an open bead does.

LAWS THE CLOSURE OWES: globally reversed across two coordinates; a gap on a fresh coordinate;
CommitSeq(0); an empty template; a template touching TWO coordinates at one sequence (must still be
accepted — the multi-coordinate case is the reason a per-coordinate check existed at all); and a
control that an ordinary sequential multi-coordinate history is still admitted, so the fix cannot be
'refuse everything'. Mutation-prove each against the restored per-coordinate-only check.
close_reason: Re-closed after counterexample invalidation: current write-terminal semantics intentionally admit a rowless coordinate for mutation-capable semantic no-ops.

title: Historical child transaction ignores inherited commits after its snapshot
description:
At 4f860e9b6dfd816fbfea0914defea78985429c7d, ReferenceDatabase::conflict_keys_since consults only the child coordinate own records (crates/fgdb-reference/src/lib.rs:1446-1473). Transaction::begin_at explicitly permits a historical child snapshot and commit uses that incomplete set for first-committer-wins (crates/fgdb-reference/src/txn.rs:152-166, 240-305).

Concrete history: parent seq1 creates v=0; parent seq2 changes v=1; fork child at boundary seq2; begin_at(child snapshot high=seq1); transaction changes v=2 and commits to child. The parent seq2 write is visible through the child lineage and occurred after the transaction basis, but it is absent from the child own history. The conflict check says disjoint, then applying the stale before-image fails as TxnError::Apply(PropertyBeforeMismatch), even though Apply is documented as an internal contradiction rather than a concurrency outcome.

Required closure: conflict detection over a historical child basis must include every inherited lineage record in (snapshot.high, fork boundary], without treating parent commits after the boundary as child conflicts. Add positive and negative controls for the exact history above, nested forks, a parent commit after the fork boundary, and a child transaction begun at the current fork boundary. The stale transaction must return an explicit conflict/stale-basis outcome and must not mutate state.
close_reason: Landed as e75d9a5. Same shape underneath: a transaction's claim is not only 'these elements were unwritten' but 'my basis was the state at snapshot.high of this lineage', and the conflict rule only checked the first half. re6w: conflict_keys_since now walks the LINEAGE with a per-ancestor cap, so inherited records in (snapshot.high, boundary] are conflicts; a historical child transaction gets Conflicted instead of TxnError::Apply. dfk3: ConflictKey::CoordinateExistence, named by a genesis claim and by any coordinate created after a transaction's basis, so two racing genesis transactions with DISJOINT effects can no longer both commit. Five laws; each revert reddens exactly its closure law. Three of the five exist to stop the fix overshooting — a child at the current boundary must NOT conflict with the parent's post-fork commits (else branch isolation becomes branch serialization), an uncontested genesis must still commit, and no ROW may name CoordinateExistence. The Apply doc no longer claims the conflict rule is complete; that claim of completeness is what made this class hard to see.

title: SI oracle misclassifies concurrent edge-create versus vertex-delete race
description:
At 4f860e9b6dfd816fbfea0914defea78985429c7d, collect_conflict_keys maps CreateEdge only to its edge ID, while DeleteVertex maps the vertex and only the incident edge IDs captured in its snapshot (crates/fgdb-reference/src/lib.rs:1239-1260). Therefore a concurrent transaction that creates a new edge incident to the vertex and a transaction that deletes the vertex have disjoint write sets. Depending on commit order, first-committer-wins admits the second commit until apply_row rejects stale endpoints/cascade images, which Transaction::commit exposes as TxnError::Apply. That path is documented as an internal contradiction, so the oracle reports a legal concurrency/constraint race as an implementation failure.

Required closure: represent the endpoint/adjacency predicate or an equivalent deterministic constraint-certification key so the race aborts through an explicit conflict or constraint outcome before mutation. Add both commit orders, directed and undirected edges, a control using an unrelated vertex, and assertions that the losing commit leaves database state and history unchanged. Keep the existing documented limitation on general neighbour phantoms honest; do not claim broad predicate locking if the mechanism is endpoint-specific.
notes:
RE-DERIVED 2026-07-30 (JadeSnow) — PREMISE CONFIRMED, and the obvious fix is wrong.

MistyJay's post-landing re-review at 155a7fa is correct: collect_conflict_keys gives CreateEdge only
Element(Edge(eid)) and DeleteVertex the vertex plus its PRECOMPUTED cascade, so a concurrent edge
with a fresh eid incident to the deleted vertex is in neither write set. Both commit orders reach
apply_template and surface as TxnError::Apply. Confirmed by reading the code, not taken on trust.

WHY I DID NOT PATCH IT IN THE SAME PASS AS re6w/dfk3. The tempting fix — give CreateEdge an
adjacency key for its endpoints, so a vertex delete collides — is WRONG for this database, and
silently so. Two transactions adding different edges to one vertex would then conflict, which makes
every supernode a serialization point. For a property graph that is a worse defect than the one it
closes, and it would pass every law lmtc asks for.

THE CORRECT MODEL IS ASYMMETRIC, and it is a design change rather than a patch. An edge create takes
a SHARED dependency on its endpoints' existence; a vertex delete takes an EXCLUSIVE one. Shared
against shared does not conflict; shared against exclusive does. That needs two kinds of key rather
than one set — the conflict rule becomes (my writes ∪ my existence-reads) against (their existence-
writes), which is a second, asymmetric domain beside first-committer-wins and is the beginning of
constraint certification proper.

WHAT THE FIX MUST NOT CLAIM. Endpoint existence is specific; it is not predicate locking. The
neighbour-phantom limitation documented on Transaction::read_neighbours and in fgdb-oc8y stays
exactly as narrow as it is — an edge create's dependency on its endpoints existing says nothing about
a dependency on an edge that does not exist.

LAWS THE CLOSURE OWES, from the bead plus two more the asymmetry demands: both commit orders;
directed and undirected; an unrelated-vertex control; the losing commit leaves state AND history
unchanged; PLUS two concurrent edge creates on the SAME vertex must still both commit (the
over-strictness control), and a delete whose cascade is stale must report a conflict rather than
TxnError::Apply.

RELATED WORK THAT LANDED: the Apply doc comment no longer claims the conflict rule is complete — it
says the arm is EXPECTED to be unreachable and that a new reachable path is a defect in the rule.
That claim of completeness is what made this class hard to see; lmtc is now the named counterexample
to it rather than a contradiction of it. See the re6w/dfk3 fix for the lineage window and the
coordinate-existence key, which are the same shape (the conflict rule must cover the transaction's
BASIS, not only the elements it touched).

title: Snapshot capability is transferable across ReferenceDatabase instances
description: Fresh-eye review of commit 006005f. crates/fgdb-reference/src/lib.rs:1155-1165 claims Snapshot makes the SI bound structural because only snapshot/snapshot_at can mint it. But Snapshot carries only graph, branch, and high, while ReferenceDatabase::read at lines 1357-1380 neither binds the capability to the database/history that minted it nor revalidates high against the receiving database frontier. Reproducer: database A advances coordinate G/B through seq 2 and mints a snapshot; independent database B has the same G/B only through seq 1; B.read(&snapshot_from_A) silently returns B state instead of refusing the future snapshot. With equal frontiers but divergent histories it silently returns the wrong database state. Closure: bind snapshots to an authoritative database/history/head identity (or model that identity and revalidate it on read), add cross-instance and divergent-clone negative laws, and narrow the structural claim to what the type actually enforces.
notes: Peer review at 4f860e9b6dfd816fbfea0914defea78985429c7d confirms the same missing provenance now amplifies into writes: Transaction::begin_at(db_a, snapshot_a) copies graph/branch/high and a workspace, but Transaction::commit(self, db_b, ...) accepts an arbitrary mutable ReferenceDatabase with no database/history identity binding. If before-images happen to match, a capability minted from A can commit its effects into B. genesis_snapshot likewise creates a freely transferable high=0 capability for an absent coordinate. Closure must bind both Snapshot reads and Transaction commits to the issuing database/history identity, cover equal-frontier divergent instances, cross-instance begin/commit, cloned/same-state controls, and prove refusal is side-effect-free.

title: Transaction abort index resets across execute batches
description:
At 4f860e9b6dfd816fbfea0914defea78985429c7d, Transaction::execute is explicitly repeatable so statements may be issued over time (crates/fgdb-reference/src/txn.rs:187-205), but Outcome::Aborted.statement is stored directly in aborted_at and is local to the latest execute slice. TxnOutcome::Aborted and TxnError::AlreadyAborted later expose that bare index as though it identified a statement in the transaction (txn.rs:55-59, 75-77, 195-205, 243-251).

Repro: execute one successful statement, then execute a second one-statement slice whose guard aborts. commit reports Aborted { statement: 0 }, indistinguishable from an abort in the first transaction statement; the transaction-global position is 1. More generally every execute batch resets the observable index. The unused IndexedFailure alias at txn.rs:323-325 also promises statement identity without supplying a batch coordinate.

Required closure: define and implement one stable indexing contract. Prefer a transaction-global statement ordinal maintained across execute calls; alternatively return an explicit batch/statement coordinate and document it. Add controls covering abort in a later batch, prior StatementError and no-op statements, AlreadyAborted, and a single-batch index so existing semantics stay pinned.

title: A conjunctive arm-refinement is inexpressible in the landed grammar: X::Sealed needs two locations, parse_refinement_claim admits one
description:
Derived 2026-07-27 by pane3 at HEAD 1a6fdc2 while re-deriving fgdb-6v86 per
fgdb-rhvi. 6v86's facts and diagnosis all hold; this is the gap between its
PRESCRIPTION and the instrument that landed after it was written.

WHAT 6v86 ESTABLISHES (re-verified, see its note)
`OperationalPendingIndependentReopen::Sealed` is not a path into one union. The
phase arm is registered FLAT and BODYLESS — durable_fields.toml carries it as
union_arm of GlobalStatePayloadBootstrapPhase, arm_tag 0x0004,
payload_kind = "unit", max_size_bytes = 1 — and a05:1650 declares the union with
no body on that arm. The seal state is a SEPARATE anonymous inline sub-union
declared at a01:1390 on an arm payload member. So `X::Sealed` is a CONJUNCTION
over two registered locations, and 6v86 prescribes landing it "as TWO field rows
or one composite".

THE INSTRUMENT THAT LANDED AFTER THE BEAD CANNOT SPELL THAT
4fcc68a (feat(identity): enforce arm-refinement claims) introduced the
value-position refinement grammar and four codes. Its parser is
tools/registry-check/src/identity.rs:157

    fn parse_refinement_claim(encoding_context: &str) -> Option<(&str, i64, &str)>

returning exactly ONE (arm, tag, union) triple, off the single marker
`admits only the <Arm> arm (arm_tag 0x<hex>) of the <Union> union`
(REFINEMENT_CLAIM_MARKER, identity.rs:140). It further rejects any multi-word arm
or union name by design — the in-source comment says a multi-word phrase "is the
prose dialect, not this grammar". There is no conjunction, no second location,
and no composite form. A two-location precondition has no representation.

THE COVERAGE TRAP IF IT IS LANDED ANYWAY — same class as
fgdb-witness-census-named-not-witnessed-11fo,
fgdb-historical-witness-cohort-asserts-blind-38tv and
fgdb-complete-census-law-vacuous-twice-54jf
Splitting `X::Sealed` into two independent single-arm refinement claims makes
each one individually parseable and individually valid, so all four codes report
clean — while the thing actually being asserted, that BOTH hold simultaneously,
is enforced by nothing. The law would certify two unrelated facts and read as
having certified the conjunction. That is stated coverage exceeding actual
coverage, introduced by the repair rather than found in the tree, which is the
cheapest possible moment to prevent it.

THE RULING NEEDED, WHICH 6v86 DOES NOT MENTION
Before 6v86's option (i) can be applied, decide one of:
  A extend the grammar to a conjunctive form with its own code, so a
    two-location precondition is expressible AND checkable as one claim
  B land one composite location (register seal_state as a two-arm ordinary union
    per 6v86, then refine against THAT union alone) so the claim stays
    single-location and the existing grammar suffices
  C land the two claims separately and state explicitly, in the row and here,
    that the conjunction is unenforced — the honest but weakest option
B looks preferable on the same reasoning 6v86 uses to prefer its (i): it needs no
new grammar and no source erratum. It is not free — it requires ruling that the
refinement target is the seal_state union rather than the phase arm, which is a
different referent from the one the source spells at a20:2599/2601/2605.

READINESS NOTE. 4fcc68a states the claim population was pinned at 6 at dbaab71
"so a new wrapper is added deliberately". The live marker count is now 9
(7 in wire_types.toml, 2 in durable_fields.toml). Landing the three a20 rows adds
more, so whatever pins that population must move in the same increment. I did not
locate the pin's assertion site and did not verify it is currently stale — the
identity suite was 131 passed / 0 failed when last run.

ACCEPTANCE
  - pick A, B or C and record the reasoning on this bead
  - if B, mutation-prove that a claim refining the seal_state union fires
    refinement_arm_unresolved when pointed at a nonexistent arm and stays green
    on the real one, per 4fcc68a's own non-vacuity standard
  - whichever is picked, do not let the three a20 rows land while the conjunction
    is silently unenforced
close_reason: Option A landed in 9911ca9 with exact immutable full-gate evidence; conjunctive refinement grammar and mutation witness are complete. Downstream fgdb-6v86 remains separate.

title: reference_semantics is not forced by exact_wire_type: a StrongRef field can declare none and pass every gate
description:
## The gap

A `[[field]]` row's `reference_semantics` is not constrained by its
`exact_wire_type`. A row typed `StrongRef` may declare `reference_semantics =
"none"`, keep its `target_schema_id`, and pass every gate in the stack.

Every downstream law keys off `reference_semantics`, not off the wire type:
`projection_dag_future_result`, `bare_strong_ref`, and the generated
reachability / GC / checkpoint-vector walkers whose sole input is `durable_fields`.
So declaring `"none"` on a StrongRef-typed member silently switches ALL of them
off at once for that member, and then freezes behind the append-only field pin.

## Measurement (six arms on a clean tree, one axis at a time)

Subject: the row landed by fb0cc32,
`ResourceLedgerTransition<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>.authorization_decision_ref`
-- `exact_wire_type = "StrongRef"`, `identity_class = "logical"`,
`reference_semantics = "strong"`, `target_schema_id =
"AuthorizationDecisionRecord"`, construction_order 15. Base tree: 0 violations.
Only `registry_assignment_drift` is filtered out (it fires in every arm including
the control, because the probe mutates without re-freezing the pin).

  A  untouched (control)                        0 real violations
  B  reference_semantics -> "none", target kept 0 real violations   <-- THE GAP
  C  reference_semantics -> "none", target dropped  0 real violations
  D  target dropped, semantics kept "strong"    bare_strong_ref
  E  identity_class -> "inline", rest untouched bad_field
       "strong/conditional references must have identity_class = logical"
  F  target retargeted to a later-ordered kind  dag_future_result
       "target RetentionMap (order 25) is constructed after
        ResourceLedgerTransition (order 15)"

So D, E and F show the neighbouring guards are all live and precise. Only the
`exact_wire_type -> reference_semantics` direction is unguarded, in both the
target-kept and target-dropped spellings.

Probe: ~/.claude/projects/-data-projects-frankengraphdb/tools/p4-a12/refsem.rs
(~40 lines, links against a standalone registry_check rlib, runs in seconds, needs
no cargo and no build slot).

## Why this matters more than a lint

It is the same LATENCY class as fgdb-oicl, and the same signature as the six bugs
found on 2026-07-26 whose common property was "looks exactly like a pass": a
silently-disabled guard. An author who mis-types one field row gets a green
loader, a green lib suite, a green tests/identity.rs, and a green
g0_identity_e2e.sh -- and ships a durable format whose construction DAG and
reachability closure are wrong. The mutation audit for fb0cc32 carries this as a
standing arm (`mutate3.sh`, `m7_gap`) that asserts the gap is still open, so a
future fix is noticed rather than assumed.

## Suggested repair

`validate_identity` already resolves `exact_wire_type` against
`BUILTIN_WIRE_TYPES` / `wire_names` / ordinary unions. Add the reciprocal law:
a field whose resolved `exact_wire_type` is a reference wrapper
(`StrongRef`, `WeakRef`, `ConditionalRef`, `StrongCiphertextRef`,
`CertifiedRemoteStrongRef`, `Strong*Ref`, `Conditional*Ref`) MUST carry a
reference `reference_semantics`, and conversely a non-wrapper type must carry
`"none"`. Run it against the 506 landed rows first: this bead does not claim the
existing corpus is clean, only that nothing enforces it.

It is the same LATENCY class as fgdb-oicl, and the same signature as the six bugs
found on 2026-07-26 whose common property was "looks exactly like a pass": a
silently-disabled guard. An author who mis-types one field row gets a green

reachability closure are wrong. The mutation audit for fb0cc32 carries this as a

record existed and br assigned `-gls4`. The commit is not amended: `--amend`

title: registry-check: claims-lint scan set is an unverified allowlist and its exclusion table is dead code
description:
FILES: tools/registry-check/src/lint.rs:53-86 (load_config), :126-151 (run),
registries/claims_lint.toml.

RELATION VIOLATED: adding a normative prose artifact that cites an unregistered
claim marker must change the violation set. It does not.

TWO FACTS, BOTH VERIFIED:

1. lint::run() iterates config.scan ONLY. registries/claims_lint.toml declares
   scan = [README.md, AGENTS.md, COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_...md] — a hard-coded allowlist
   of three files. Nothing checks that the set is complete. A new normative document
   (a new appendix, a merged spec) gets zero claim-marker enforcement, silently, and
   no gate notices the omission. This is the same exemption shape as the known
   "scripts/ was exempt from every mandated check" defect.

2. LintConfig.excludes is DEAD. It is parsed, and schema-validated hard enough that
   an exclusion without a reason is an error (lint.rs:78-82), then never read by any
   code path — verified: `grep -rn "\.excludes" src/ tests/` returns nothing outside
   its own construction at lint.rs:23/70/83/85.

The two interact badly. claims_lint.toml preamble says "Historical review artifacts
are excluded WITH RECORDED REASONS", and six [[exclude]] rows carry carefully written
reasons. That describes denylist semantics over an implicit scan-everything default.
The implementation is an allowlist, so those rows exclude nothing, the reasons
document nothing, and the schema rule polices a field with no effect. A reader
auditing the claim surface is told the design is "scan all prose minus these six",
which is false in a way that hides fact 1.

GATE COVERAGE: none. tests/claims.rs has no test referencing exclude at all.

FIX: pick one design and make the config match it. Either (a) enumerate the prose
artifacts by walking the repo for normative *.md and apply excludes as a real
denylist — which makes the six reasons load-bearing and closes the new-file hole —
or (b) keep the allowlist and delete the exclude table, adding a check that every
tracked normative document appears in scan. (a) is the shape the config already
claims.
notes:
RE-DERIVED AT HEAD 3aa3f6c BY pane3 (2026-07-27). BOTH FILED FACTS ARE NOW
STALE, AND THE HEADLINE NUMBER ("dead excludes") IS FALSIFIED.

## What the bead said vs what is true today

FACT 2 as filed -- "LintConfig.excludes is DEAD, parsed and never read" -- was
fixed by 4f37495 (sdpv). lint.rs now reads config.excludes at :610 (the closure
`claimed` set) and :706 (the DeadExclude liveness law). Not dead.

FACT 1 as filed -- "scan is a hard-coded three-entry allowlist and a new
normative document gets zero enforcement" -- was fixed by fd7d169 + 1245f89. The
closure walk is now RECURSIVE from closure_dirs = ["."], scan has grown 3 -> 6,
and an unaccounted prose file raises `unclaimed_prose`. Proof it works: it is
firing right now (see the LIVE RED below).

## The measurement asked for: how many excludes, how many still match anything

Three different questions, three different numbers, all taken by driving the
real `lint::run` (delete-and-rerun, not by reading the config):

  excludes declared ....................................... 6
  Q1  path still exists on disk ........................... 6/6   ZERO dead
  Q3  exclusion suppresses an unregistered-marker hit ..... 2/6
  Q2' exclusion is load-bearing for the CLOSURE law ....... 6/6

  path                                                    marker-hits  closure-hits
  COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_REVIEW_BY_KIMI_K3.md                       0           1
  META_ANALYSIS_OF_KIMI_K3_REVIEW_BY_FABLE.md                   0           1
  PLAN_AUDIT_BY_SOL_ULTRA.md                                    1           1
  ENHANCEMENT_PROPOSALS_FOR_THE_COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN.md          16           1
  COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_..._FRANKENGRAPHDB__FABLE.md               0           1
  COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_..._FRANKENGRAPHDB__SOL.md                 0           1
  (marker-hits = move the row into `scan` and count unregistered_marker on that
   file; closure-hits = delete the row and count unclaimed_prose on that file)

THERE ARE ZERO DEAD EXCLUDES. Every one of the six narrows something: removing
any single row raises `unclaimed_prose` for its file. The tempting law -- "an
exclusion that suppresses no marker hit is dead" -- is WRONG and I did not
land it: it would condemn the four correctly-classified historical documents
(KIMI_K3, META_ANALYSIS, __FABLE, __SOL) and force them into `scan`, which is
the exact opposite of what their recorded reasons say. Their reasons are
classification claims ("historical external review", "retained for
provenance"), not suppression claims, and a hit count cannot falsify them. Only
the two rows whose reasons ARE specific ("references pre-adjudication FG-INV-2x
numbering") suppress anything, and those two reasons are accurate.

## The real hole, and what landed

`dead_exclude` asks only `path.exists()`. Existing is not the same as
narrowing: `unclaimed_prose` accuses only files the closure walk FOUND, so a row
naming a path inside a `[[closure_prune]]` subtree, under a hidden directory, or
outside every closure_dir excuses a hit that could never have been raised.

NAMED-NUMBER MUTATION PROOF, identical mutation, two binaries, real tree:
  append `[[exclude]] path = "target/PHANTOM.md"` (pruned subtree), file CREATED
  on disk so the existence law cannot be what fires:
    PRE-CHANGE  (HEAD rlib): base_hits=1 -> 1   kinds=[unclaimed_prose]
    POST-CHANGE            : base_hits=1 -> 2   kinds=[unclaimed_prose,
                                                        unreachable_exclude]
  and dead_exclude = 0 in the post-change run, confirming the NEW law fired and
  not the old one.

Landed as HitKind::UnreachableExclude / code `unreachable_exclude`, keyed on the
walk's own `found` set -- one reader, no second reachability derivation.

Controls, all four run:
  base    real shipped config, 6 excludes -> unreachable_exclude = 0 (the law
          does not fire on the tree it ships with)
  vacuity same row pointed at a REACHABLE path -> 0 accusations, and 0
          unclaimed_prose for that file, i.e. it can be made to go quiet
  absent  presence="optional" + path absent -> 0 (a fresh clone must not fail)
  fixture claims_neg_unreachable_exclude: hidden `.private/OLD.md` -> 1 hit with
          dead_exclude EMPTY; same file moved to a reachable path -> 0 hits, so
          location is the only difference between the two verdicts.

Suite: 34 passed / 1 failed, and the 1 is the pre-existing red below -- the
failure SET is byte-identical to a HEAD-built claims binary, so this change
regresses nothing.

## LIVE RED AT HEAD, FILED AS fgdb-ia2b -- NOT CAUSED BY THIS WORK

`registry-check lint --root .` exits 1 at HEAD and
tests/claims.rs::claims_lint_shipped_prose_is_clean is red, because
docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md is UNTRACKED and the closure walk enumerates the
filesystem rather than the tracked set. Any pane's scratch .md reds G0 for
everyone. This is pane2's predicted hazard, materialized; its fix is a
tracked-set reader, and pane2's implementation of one was swept off disk with
/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/p2/q5_1785100577/. Filed separately because it is about
what the walk CONSIDERS, not about the denylist this bead polices.

## Still owed (not landed here)

* The same reachability hole exists for `[[closure_prune]]`: `dead_closure_prune`
  also asks only `is_dir()`. Not fixed here to keep the change one law wide.
* Metamorphic relation 12 (the bead's original reproducible pair) is still owed
  in tests/metamorphic.rs.
close_reason: Both filed facts stale; headline number falsified; the real hole found and closed in 70cd298. excludes is no longer dead (4f37495) and scan is no longer an unchecked 3-entry allowlist (fd7d169+1245f89). Measured by driving the real lint::run per row: 6 excludes, 6/6 exist, only 2/6 suppress a marker hit, but 6/6 are load-bearing for the closure law -- so there are ZERO dead excludes and the tempting 'must suppress a marker' law would have condemned four correctly-classified historical documents. The actual hole is that dead_exclude asks only path.exists(): a row the closure walk never REACHES excuses a hit that could not be raised. Proven with one mutation on two binaries -- inert target/PHANTOM.md exclusion, file created so the existence law could not fire: pre-change 1 hit -> 1, post-change 1 -> 2 with unreachable_exclude and dead_exclude=0. Four controls including a vacuity control that goes quiet when the same row is aimed at a reachable path. Still owed: the identical reachability hole in dead_closure_prune, and metamorphic relation 12. SEPARATE LIVE RED filed as fgdb-ia2b: the walk is filesystem-based so the untracked docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md reds G0 for every pane.
