## Authoritative post-d96bf0f contract reconciliation

The post-G4 Bolt V2 profile has its own exact BoltV2 result-release arm and cannot reuse the V1 or generic Bolt rendering.

The following current plan text is authoritative and supersedes any older rendering in this Bead:

**Authoritative v1 delivery and control corrections.** `QUERY_CANCEL` controls computation and the current sender only. Before publication it may select the role-valid no-result/abort path; after independent retention it can only durably pause that session's sender after joining queued/writing transport obligations. It never ACKs/releases a result, changes capability lineage, or frees durable charge. `ClientResultReleaseAuthority` is the closed source union `ReadyChannel{surface:NativeFgp|Http2|Grpc|WebSocket,presented_authority:ResumeCapability{validation_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence>,capability_commitment}|ManagementHandle{validated_management_handle_commitment},session_binding,auth_context_generation,surface_request_digest,canonical_fgp_request_digest}|Embedded{stream_release_token_commitment,host_session_generation,explicit_release_call_digest}|BoltV1{bolt_session_binding,qid,request_kind:DISCARD|RESET,request_message_digest}|BoltV2{bolt_session_binding,negotiated_profile_oid:BoltCompatProfileV2,qid,request_kind:DISCARD|RESET,request_message_digest}`. Only ReadyChannel ResumeCapability validation selects the exact ResumeBufferedResult/ResultReleaseUnacked row and byte-matches the capability commitment, surface/canonical request pair, current result lineage, role, header, and session. The ReadyChannel management-handle arm, embedded stream token, and Bolt V1/V2 authenticated DISCARD/RESET arms cannot populate a capability-validation ref. `AuthenticatedClientResultReleaseReceipt<Role>` binds the complete role/domain/service/principal/authority/result ID/state version/digest/release nonce/source/authentication attestation and thereby strongly retains validation evidence only in the ReadyChannel ResumeCapability source arm. `ResultReleaseEvidence` is exactly `ClientRelease{receipt_ref:StrongRef<AuthenticatedClientResultReleaseReceipt<Role>>}|LeaseExpired{expiry_evidence_ref}`. Rust Drop, transport loss, QUERY_CANCEL, drain, and process/session death cannot construct it.

Implementation, tests, retained evidence, and public-surface behavior must use this exact corrected contract. No Markdown plan edit is required or authorized by this reconciliation.

title: Build the dependency-free external verifier SDK
description:
## What & scope
Build the registered post-1.0 **dependency-free external verifier SDK** for every `externally_verifiable` surface. It is a small auditable implementation (several-KLOC budget) that verifies evidence without linking FrankenGraphDB, asupersync, or third-party packages. Implement only BLAKE3 required by marked transcript/identity recipes; registered threshold-signature verification and policy-epoch lineage; MMR leaf/checkpoint plus inclusion/consistency proofs; canonical bounded decoders for `TransparencyCheckpoint`, `WitnessPolicy`, marked proof encodings, filtered-changefeed delta commitments, and marked durability-certificate envelopes; and exact domain-separated transcript recipes/golden vectors.

## Proof-scope and compatibility contract
Reproduce scope labels verbatim, including `membership_only` and detection-versus-prevention. Local-only verification never claims non-equivocation; witness-policy verification establishes only encoded scope. A verifier pinned to a WitnessPolicy epoch verifies every checkpoint legally issued within that epoch. Marked format transitions use existing dual-quorum policy rotation; operators cannot force-upgrade an external verifier inside an epoch. Unknown required flags/tags, noncanonical bytes, resource-limit violations, untrusted signer transitions, epoch gaps/forks, and unsupported algorithms fail closed.

The implementation is genuinely independent: no shared parser, hash/signature wrapper, MMR code, generated decoder, or runtime library with proof-producing code. Shared **data** is limited to normative format descriptions and golden/adversarial vectors. This makes it a §15.4 differential oracle rather than another facade over producer bugs.

## API and distribution
Provide a tiny stable library API and CLI/robot mode for inspecting policy/checkpoint; verifying signature/policy lineage; verifying inclusion/consistency proofs; verifying marked changefeed/durability evidence; and printing exact scope/no-claim results. Inputs are bounded streams/files with no ambient network. Every result binds verifier/schema version, format/policy epoch, checkpoint/root identity, proof kind, scope label, signer result, transcript digest, resource counts, and terminal verdict. Human text never mixes with versioned NDJSON.

## Unit, golden, mutation, and differential tests
- `marked_format_inventory_is_exact`: cover every and only active externally-verifiable registry row.
- `golden_vectors_cross_implement`: producer and independently constructed SDK vectors agree byte-for-byte.
- `canonical_decoding_rejects_malleability`: overlong encodings, duplicates/order variants, unknown required flags, truncation, overflow, oversized allocation, trailing bytes.
- `threshold_policy_epoch_and_rotation`: threshold, wrong/duplicate signer, rotated set, dual quorum, stale/future epoch, fork.
- `mmr_inclusion_and_consistency`: empty/singleton/boundaries, wrong leaf/index/size/root, splicing, fork attacks.
- `scope_labels_are_not_upgraded`: membership/local/detection evidence cannot yield stronger text/codes.
- `dependency_scan_is_empty`: only language core/runtime plus SDK source.
- Fuzz every decoder/verifier; malformed input cannot panic, over-allocate, leak, or return ambiguous success.

## E2E/adversarial corpus
From an independently reopened archive and live witnessed stream, export a policy/checkpoint chain, inclusion/consistency proofs, filtered changefeed commitment, and marked durability evidence. Transfer only public bytes to a clean offline environment, compile from source, and verify exact verdicts/scopes. Mutate bytes, signers, epochs, roots, leaf order, proof nodes, filters, rotations, and claimed scope; every attack fails at a typed stage. Differentially compare producer/SDK across the whole corpus and retain disagreements. Test an old verifier across legal same-epoch additive evolution and dual-quorum rotation; no within-epoch force-upgrade.

## Detailed logging
Robot events `verifier_input_opened`, `format_decoded`, `policy_lineage_checked`, `signature_share_checked`, `threshold_reached`, `mmr_proof_checked`, `scope_assigned`, `verification_terminal`. Fields include SDK/schema version, bounded length, format/proof/policy/checkpoint IDs/digests, signer-set epoch and public signer IDs, transcript/root digests, scope, resource counters, verdict, failure code/offset. No private material or protected data. Identical input yields deterministic logs except explicitly separate diagnostics.

## Supply-chain/release evidence
Require reproducible builds, source archive, checksums/signatures, SBOM proving zero dependencies, pinned toolchain, target matrix, CLI schema, golden/adversarial corpus, and independent security review. Crypto follows constant-time/misuse and agility discipline with target/toolchain no-claim boundaries.

## Completion / no-claim boundary
Close only when all marked formats are covered, zero-dependency proof machine-checked, independent differential/adversarial/fuzz suites green, epoch compatibility proven, and release reproduces offline. Do not claim database correctness, data availability, global non-equivocation in local-only mode, or anything stronger than encoded scope.

## Provenance
§5.8 externally verifiable formats; §15.4 independence discipline; §19 post-1.0 roadmap. Post-1.0 only; do not feed G4/1.0.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every and only marked externally-verifiable format is covered by canonical bounded decoding, cryptographic/policy/MMR verification, exact scope labels, and golden/adversarial vectors.
- Dependency scan proves zero project/foundation/third-party linkage; independent differential, fuzz, mutation, old-verifier epoch, offline E2E, reproducible-build, and security-review gates pass.
- Robot output/logs are stable and deterministic, and no verdict exceeds its encoded detection/prevention/non-equivocation scope.
- No dependency from this post-G4 task into G4 or a 1.0 epic exists.

title: Specify and implement the post-APFS Windows Local durability profile
description:
## What & scope
Specify, implement, and activate the explicit post-1.0 Windows Local filesystem durability profile after APFS. Windows rename, share-mode, handle, directory durability, and lock-owner semantics are harder and must be measured and registered rather than inferred from POSIX/APFS. Deliver the exact profile ID/epoch, supported filesystem/OS envelope, foundation-reactor binding, durable-publication primitives, writer lease/takeover mapping, doctor probes, crash evidence, and capability-manifest activation.

## Discovery-before-freeze contract
The plan records Windows roadmap work without pretending its exact primitives are proven. Begin with a reproducible matrix over intended Windows versions and local filesystem candidates: file flush, directory metadata persistence, replace/exclusive-create/rename collision, open-handle/share flags, delete/rename while open, durable file identity, links, volume snapshots, abrupt process/host loss, and stale-handle behavior. Freeze a row only for the subset satisfying common RootSlot, exclusive publication, whole-file/inode-equivalent fencing, takeover, checkpoint, backup, and restore laws. Unsupported configurations are explicit doctor failures, never best-effort writes.

## Architecture constraints
All blocking/I/O paths remain behind `Cx` and the pinned asupersync Windows-capable reactor; no detached threads, private runtime, Tokio, external WAL/database, or semantic compatibility shim. Reuse canonical logical/durable formats and state machines. Platform-specific code lives only in the registered VFS/unsafe boundary; every unavoidable raw-handle/FFI site has a narrow ledger row, SAFETY argument, negative tests, and safe deterministic lab model. Added barriers update Appendix G in the same commit.

## Required profile row
Record stable ID/format epoch, OS/build/filesystem/volume probes, reactor capabilities, file-data/metadata flush rules, namespace/parent durability rule or unsupported boundary, exclusive and replacement publication semantics, durable file identity, lock/lease primitive and owner death, handle share flags, takeover/fence recipe, root/bootstrap/checkpoint/backup/restore recipes, unsupported modes (network/removable/cloud-synced/filter-driver variants unless proven), doctor/checker symbols, and evidence digest. Writes activate only when every required probe succeeds.

## Unit, model, and conformance tests
- `windows_profile_row_complete_after_empirical_freeze`: no placeholder or unknown durability law is active.
- `windows_name_publication_never_overwrites`: racing create/rename/replace preserves exact no-overwrite/idempotency.
- `windows_file_identity_and_lock_scope_match`: alternate paths, links, handles, and share flags cannot create two writers.
- `windows_flush_error_mapping_is_fail_closed`: ambiguous/partial/unsupported outcomes never advance durability.
- `windows_owner_death_requires_takeover_fence`: restart/stale-handle cases obey fence-root-before-enable.
- `windows_unsupported_volume_is_read_only_or_rejected`: every unregistered fixture fails predictably.
- `cross_profile_logical_equivalence`: Windows, APFS, and Linux histories yield identical canonical logical output/replay.
- Bounded lab models/reference traces cover the selected recipes without claiming the model proves kernel behavior.

## Real-host E2E
For every supported profile cell run fresh bootstrap, writes, checkpoint/suffix recovery, dual-slot tears, abrupt process/VM power loss at each barrier, concurrent writers, owner death/takeover, stale handle, name collision, disk-full/I/O/permission failures, backup/independent reopen, restore staging/hidden promotion/reopen, and upgrade/downgrade fixtures. Preserve raw traces and volume/OS manifests. Hostless CI cannot activate support; rerun cells whenever the support envelope changes.

## Detailed logging
Stable events: `windows_profile_probe`, `windows_reactor_probe`, `windows_handle_open`, `windows_flush_attempt`, `windows_namespace_publication`, `windows_writer_lease_transition`, `windows_takeover_fence_transition`, `windows_recovery_probe`, `windows_profile_activation`. Log profile/build/filesystem envelope, recipe ID, redacted file identity, handle/share class, barrier/slot generation, result/error class, evidence digest, and fail-closed reason. Never log keys or protected path contents.

## Completion / no-claim boundary
Close only when the profile is exact, empirical real-host evidence archived, foundation support pinned, crash/takeover/restore matrices green, and activation fail-closed. Do not claim network filesystems, arbitrary filter drivers, future builds, or filesystems outside the registered envelope.

## Provenance
§19 platform roadmap: Windows follows APFS because its rename/lock semantics are harder, and absence from 1.0 is an explicit decision. Post-1.0 only; do not feed G4/1.0.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Empirical Windows/filesystem evidence has produced one exact registered profile with no placeholder durability primitive; all unsupported envelopes fail doctor.
- Unit/model/cross-profile tests and every supported real-host crash, handle/lease, publication, backup, and restore E2E cell pass with archived evidence.
- Foundation reactor/unsafe-ledger/cost-registry requirements are green and structured logs reconstruct activation.
- The task remains post-APFS/post-1.0 and does not feed G4.

title: OWNER RULING: partition-root reference budget under sustained ingest — pick two-level ROOT_SEGMENT objects vs continuation chain vs per-family chain heads (Appendix A frozen format)
description:
## Context

CreamGlen's mutation-proven closure on fgdb-a7sz established: the unbounded
accumulator is the PARTITION ROOT (56 B/ref; ceiling 16384 B => ~290 refs);
compaction cannot rescue many-family graphs (~2000 post-compaction refs);
rebuild() shares the live publication seam (lib.rs:4682 -> publish_and_snapshot
lib.rs:4936), so ONE fix site covers live + replay; and every candidate repair
is a change to the FROZEN Appendix A root format. Per AGENTS doctrine and the
G0 format freeze (durable formats are versioned additive-minor/breaking-major,
section 16.6), this choice belongs to an owner sitting, not to whichever agent
is nearest the keyboard.

This bead IS that sitting. It blocks fgdb-a7sz implementation.

## What the owner must decide

Pick exactly one root-format strategy (analysis in comments):

(a) root CONTINUATION records — root carries K refs + next_root_ref chain;
(b) TWO-LEVEL roots — root references bounded ROOT_SEGMENT objects;
(c) root stores per-family CHAIN HEADS only; admission walks family chains.

Each carries: format-epoch mechanics under section 16.6, replay-equivalence
obligations through the shared publication seam, crash-matrix rows,
registry/appendix regeneration, and a recovery story for already-bricked
directories. Recommendation summary lives in the first comment; the sitting
may override it.
notes:
== SUPERSEDED IN PART 2026-08-23 by CreamGlen (fix landed at 5f8b9180) ==
The sitting's gating premise -- "every candidate repair is a change to the FROZEN Appendix A root format" -- was DISPROVEN during implementation: the root layout ALREADY declares its own large ceiling (crate::root::MAX_ROOT_BLOCKS = 2^20 refs; MAX_ENCODED_ROOT_BYTES derived beside the layout, doc'd 'Storage applies this before materializing a root'). get_root always admitted that bound; only put_object_with_steps applied the block-derived 16 KiB instead. The fix (per-family admission, one match arm + witness a_root_lawful_under_its_own_format_ceiling_is_admitted, red-control proven) required NO format change, NO section 16.6 epoch, NO migration: the frozen format was lawful all along; admission was unwired.

Consequences for THIS bead's scope: options (a)/(b)/(c) are no longer needed for correctness -- sustained ingest past ~292 refs works today at full bench scale (5994 edges / 94 commits / zero fences / 2349 blocks / cold reopen identical). What REMAINS is an OPTIONAL working-set policy: root byte size now grows unbounded with sealed-block count (perf/economics, not correctness), so a threshold-triggered compaction decision card under the adaptive-decision contract is a legitimate future workstream item at lower priority.

Recommendation: re-scope this bead to that policy design (or close as superseded-by-enforcement) at the next triage.
close_reason: Ruling recorded and ratified; superseding discovery made the frozen format lawful — governs re-scoped future policy

comments.author: SwiftDuck
comments.text:
DECISION ANALYSIS — prepared for the sitting (SwiftDuck, 2026-08-23)

RECOMMENDATION: option (b), two-level ROOT_SEGMENT objects, segment budget
K = 256 refs.

Byte math: 56 B/ref x 256 = 14,336 B payload; fits the 16,384 ceiling with a
>=2 KB margin for header/digest growth. K mirrors MAX_BLOCK_ENTRIES=256 — one
bounded-fanout mental model for every interior object. Root then holds one ref
per segment: 356 blocks -> 2 segments (~112 B root). Root size grows O(blocks
/ K); it would itself need the same treatment near ~290 segments (~74k blocks)
— far horizon; document the recurrence rather than solving it now.

PER-OPTION SCORECARD

(a) Continuation chain (next_root_ref):
+ Smallest diff; one additive optional field on the root record.
- Open-time read becomes an O(chain length) sequential object walk on every
  snapshot load; chains grow without bound under sustained ingest.
- Commitment semantics get awkward: published_chain_hash binds the head only;
  tail-mutation rules would need new law rows to stay auditable.
- New crash points mid-chain publication ordering.

(b) Two-level segments:
+ O(1) hops; clean digest layering (root binds ordered segment digests;
  segment binds its refs). FG-INV-08/09/10 decode-proof surface extends to the
  new kind naturally.
+ Deterministic seal-at-K in the fold means live publication and replay split
  identically through the SHARED publish_and_snapshot seam — preserves
  CreamGlen's one-fix-site property.
+ Heals already-bricked directories for free: rebuild re-folds the stream and
  now emits budgeted segments, so the deterministic replay cycle breaks and
  open_rebuilding recovers existing bricks without stream surgery.
- Costs a new physical record kind (registry + Appendix A row + golden corpus
  entry): more machinery than (a).

(c) Per-family chain heads:
- Breaking-major: changes what a root IS; admission walks per-family chains,
  read amplification proportional to chain depth, collides with MVCC
  visibility walks and Warden masking, and Tier R sealed runs will collapse
  families anyway. REJECT this sitting; revisit when Tier R lands.

FORMAT EPOCH (either (a) or (b)): additive-minor per section 16.6 — new
optional fields / new kind; old roots parse with defaults; writers emit the new
format from activation epoch; no migration backfill.

OBLIGATIONS CHECKLIST (whoever implements):
1. Registries: appendix_a_catalog regenerate; physical_record_kinds row;
   durable_fields slots; wire_types if FGP-exposed.
2. Invariants: extend FG-INV-08/09/10 checker+negative pairs to the new kind
   (promotion only with live checkers per law).
3. Crash matrix: crash after segment put before root swap; (a) adds mid-chain
   rows; extend durability_semantics_e2e.
4. Equivalence: metamorphic — pattern results invariant across a re-seal at a
   segment boundary + reopen.
5. Bench flip: ingest-power-law asserts publish_fence_reopens=0 and zero
   engine_limit events (existing instrument).
6. ADR row with b2 bet label; claims-lint green.

OPTIONAL STOPGAP for owner approval (hardening, NOT the fix): pre-seal
predictive admission on the LIVE write path only — the writer knows pending
root refs, so refuse the batch with a typed PartitionRootBudgetExhausted BEFORE
capsule seal. Converts future irreversible bricks into clean backpressure while
(b) lands. Tradeoffs: new typed error surface + bench loader behavior change;
does NOT heal already-bricked dirs (that rides the format fix). Reasonable to
skip if (b) lands within days.

OPEN QUESTIONS FOR THE OWNER:
1. Confirm K = 256 or pick another budget.
2. Root-segment list recurrence: solve now or documented-horizon deferral?
3. Take or leave the stopgap during format implementation?

comments.author: MagentaShore
comments.text:
OWNER RULING (MagentaShore, 2026-08-23, HEAD 224a4922): **option (b), two-level ROOT_SEGMENT objects, K = 256 refs** — the recommendation is ACCEPTED with the following determinations on the open questions:

1. **K = 256 CONFIRMED.** The byte math holds (56 x 256 = 14,336 B payload; >= 2 KB margin under 16,384 for header/digest growth), and mirroring MAX_BLOCK_ENTRIES gives every interior object one bounded-fanout mental model — the same property that makes the block ceiling auditable.

2. **Recurrence: DOCUMENTED-HORIZON DEFERRAL.** Do not build three levels now. Obligations: the ADR row must state the recurrence explicitly (root grows O(blocks/K); at ~290 segments (~74k blocks) the root itself crosses budget and promotes to the same segment treatment — one additional indirection level, same instrument); add ONE law line pinning that horizon so a future crossing cannot land silently. Speculative third-level machinery before Tier R collapses families would be format churn without a witness.

3. **STOPGAP: TAKE IT.** '(b) lands within days' underestimates the obligation set this bead itself enumerates — registry regeneration, FG-INV-08/09/10 checker extensions with negative pairs, crash-matrix rows, metamorphic equivalence, golden corpus. That is a multi-session format landing, and until it ships EVERY sustained-ingest run past ~292 blocks bricks an irreversible directory. The predictive pre-seal refusal (typed PartitionRootBudgetExhausted BEFORE capsule seal, live path only) converts future bricks into honest backpressure, is mutation-testable, and its bench-visible behavior change is exactly what fgdb-p95p publishes honestly anyway. Land stopgap FIRST as its own commit so the protection window opens immediately; the format fix supersedes it and the stopgap's typed error retires with a registry retirement row when rebuild-side healing proves out.

RATIFICATION DETAIL on (b) over (a)/(c): I concur with the scorecard — (a)'s unbounded sequential walk + awkward head-only commitment semantics buy nothing over segments; (c) is breaking-major against MVCC visibility walks and Warden masking and stays rejected per the analysis until Tier R forces the conversation.

OBLIGATIONS CHECKLIST: ratified as written, with one addition — item 1 must also update registries/workspace_topology.toml if ROOT_SEGMENT warrants a named crate-row mention, and the file-coverage closure table if any new non-.rs deliverable lands (the .yml precedent).

Implementation ownership: fgdb-a7sz (CreamGlen holds the lane + the bench instrument). Stopgap may proceed independently and immediately.

comments.text: CLOSING AS DELIVERED: owner ruling recorded above (option b, two-level ROOT_SEGMENT K=256; recurrence documented-horizon deferral with pinned horizon law; stopgap approved first). Subsequent development (0df77b17) established the frozen root format was LAWFUL all along — the a7sz brick was unwired admission, fixed by 5f8b9180/dfdb960d — so this ruling now governs the RE-SCOPED question (optional working-set policy / future budget pressure) rather than the immediate fix. Reopen if sustained ingest ever approaches the ~292-ref horizon or Tier R forces the family-chain conversation.

## THE THREE ROWS (all source-pinned, all unblocked by closed predecessors)
- ShardRestoreReopenConfirmSpec.expected_pending_state = OperationalPendingIndependentReopen::Sealed (a20:2599)
- GlobalRestoreServiceCompletionSpec.expected_meta_pending_state = OperationalPendingIndependentReopen::Sealed (a20:2601)

The conjunctive refinement grammar (9911ca9, fgdb-refinement-claim-grammar-cannot-conjoin-78tr Option A) parses 'admits only when both the A arm (arm_tag) of the U1 union and the B arm (arm_tag) of the U2 union' and resolves BOTH clauses through ordinary unions only (identity.rs resolve_refinement_clause).

Clause 1 resolves: bootstrap-phase arm OperationalPendingIndependentReopen @ 0x0004 (a05 GlobalStatePayloadBootstrapPhase).
Clause 2 does NOT: the ONLY registered Sealed arms tree-wide are RoleTransitionActivationState{MetaPhase Finalized,ShardPhase Opened}PendingIndependentReopenSealState @ 0x0002 (fgdb-6v86 landing) — the TRANSITION path. The a20 ::Sealed is the RESTORE path (seal = RestorePromotionRootSeal<Role> installed over bootstrap_phase=OperationalPendingIndependentReopen; lifecycle Unsealed after finalize -> Sealed after seal install -> completion selects Operational, per a20:2577/2597/2601). No union for it exists and NONE IS SOURCE-DECLARED: 'Sealed|Unsealed' appears exactly twice in the whole plan (both at a01:1390, transition context). Per source-silence law, inventing a restore seal_state union or conflating with the transition unions would make each row individually parseable while asserting what the source never said — the exact trap 6v86's notes warn about.

title: W5 Stage 2: implement and prove run-trie WCOJ
description:
## What & scope
Implement and independently close Loom stage two: worst-case-optimal multiway FreeJoin over Strata runs that are already tries. Own variable/trie order, leapfrog intersection, seek/advance, multi-relation multiplicity, cyclic-pattern handling, witness propagation, cancellation, spill, and AGM/declared complexity evidence. Factorized columns and adaptive replanning remain disabled until later stages.

## Why
Binary correctness does not prove multiway worst-case optimality. The plan explicitly requires run-trie WCOJ evidence before factorization and adaptivity so semantic, witness, and complexity failures can be localized rather than hidden inside an all-at-once executor benchmark.

## Design and phase contract
Extend the same GLA/FreeJoin operator family and authorized cursor abstractions from stage one; do not add a second WCOJ engine. Canonical variable order and CGSE tie breaks make output/witness bytes deterministic. Each leapfrog/seek action increments registered counters and emits a complexity witness against the named query hypergraph/bound; conservative resource exhaustion aborts without partial publication. The stage supports flat canonical output only; factorized representation and answer-affecting adaptivity are unconstructible in its capability manifest.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Unit tests exhaust variable-order, seek/advance/intersection, duplicate/multiplicity, empty/skewed/high-degree, triangle/clique/cycle/path, early-stop, witness, cancellation, resource, and invalid-cursor arms.
- Property/model tests generate query hypergraphs and graphs, compare flattened results/witness concretization against `fgdb-reference`, and prove binary-stage equivalence for two-relation cases.
- Complexity regression tests assert registered AGM/operation-count bounds on adversarial families; exceeding a declared bound fails CI rather than becoming a benchmark note.
- Mutation/fuzz suites attack trie order, seek monotonicity, relation/variable substitution, corrupt runs, cardinality overflow, spill/restart, and obligation cancellation.
- E2E executes authorized triangle, clique, cyclic, path, negative/gap, and valid-time patterns through GQL -> binder -> WCOJ -> SSI/constraint -> canonical result/replay, across Tier-D/Tier-R and compaction; factorization/adaptivity requests are rejected as inactive.
- Detailed JSONL diagnostics record `{run_id,stage:"run-trie-wcoj",query_hypergraph_and_plan_digest,variable_and_trie_order,input_cursor_commitments,leapfrog_seek_advance_counts,declared_bound,witness_digest,rows_and_multiplicities,bytes,memory_spill,cancel_or_fault,oracle,verdict,evidence_refs,seed,replay_command}` with protected facts redacted.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: pairwise hash-join chaining labeled WCOJ, borrowing factorized/adaptive output, or reporting only friendly datasets. Risk is witness drift under variable reordering; independent concretization and adversarial mutation suites gate every order.

## Provenance
Plan §§8.1-8.4, §15, §17, §20 crown-jewel build order, B3/B5, FG-INV-05/06/09/19/20.

comments.text:
FROM THE 2026-07-31 REALITY CHECK (Phase 4 Round 3). One cross-cutting dependency worth stating
explicitly, because it is a STORAGE decision that determines whether this bead can succeed.

THE JOIN AND THE LAYOUT ARE ONE DECISION. Generic Join (Ngo-Porat-Re-Rudra 2012) is worst-case optimal
because it runs in time proportional to the AGM bound -- the fractional-edge-cover bound on the output
size -- and it achieves that by INTERSECTING TRIE LEVELS, not by pairwise joining. Its cost model
assumes the relations are already tries with efficient seek/next per level. §2 says exactly this: Loom
runs "over Strata runs that are already tries".

That is only true if tier R (fgdb-w3-tier-r-0tj) is BUILT as that trie. Tier R is not yet written. If
it lands as a flat CSR with offsets and the WCO join is added afterwards, the join walks a structure
that was not designed for it, the seek/next primitive degrades, and the AGM-optimality claim becomes
marketing -- a normal hash join with a fancy name. The triangle query is the canonical witness: WCO
gives O(n^1.5), binary joins give O(n^2), and that gap is the whole B3 bet.

CONCRETE ASK: before tier R freezes its layout, state here what seek/next primitive this bead needs
from it -- per-level seek to a key, next-sibling, and the cost each must have. A note has been added to
the tier-R bead pointing back here. Elias-Fano coding of the offsets (recommended there) is compatible
with trie seek via its select structure, so the two requirements do not conflict.

ALSO WORTH PINNING HERE: worst-case optimality is a THEOREM, so it is testable as one. A law that
generates a triangle query over a graph with a known AGM bound and asserts the operator touches
O(bound) tuples -- counting tuples, not timing -- turns "we implemented WCOJ" into "we implemented WCOJ
and it is optimal on the case that distinguishes it". Timing hides the asymptote behind constants;
counting does not.

title: Reference oracle admits identity recycling: create-after-delete of the same VId/EId is accepted, but plan:221 says spent slots 'remain spent forever'
notes:
FOUND 2026-07-31 while re-deriving fgdb-0trr's FIX SKETCH (not its premise, which holds exactly as
written). The sketch justifies its new canonical key with "since identities never recycle (6.2), each
key has exactly one interval". That premise is TRUE OF THE PLAN and FALSE OF OUR CODE, and 0trr
cannot be fixed soundly until this is resolved -- so this bead is a precondition for that one, not a
side note.

THE LAW, and it is stated more than once so it is not an off-hand remark:
  plan:221 "VId is label-independent and never recycled ... deleted or abandoned leased slots remain
           spent forever."
  plan:225 "never recycled even when partly unused ... a create that becomes a no-op or an aborted
           transaction leaves an authenticated spent tombstone and never returns the slot."
  plan:553 "IDs are never recycled (§4.5)."

WHAT THE ORACLE ACTUALLY DOES. Uniqueness is checked against the LIVE map only --
`if self.vertices.contains_key(vid)` (lib.rs:934) and `if self.edges.contains_key(eid)`
(lib.rs:959) -- while deletion REMOVES the entry (`self.edges.remove(eid)`, lib.rs:1019 and
lib.rs:1049). So the sequence

    CreateEdge  e10 (1->2)      -- accepted
    DeleteEdge  e10             -- accepted, e10 leaves the map
    CreateEdge  e10 (3->4)      -- ACCEPTED. Should be refused: e10 is spent forever.

is accepted end to end, and the same hole exists for VId. MEASURED: `grep -n 'spent'` over
crates/fgdb-reference/src/lib.rs returns ZERO hits -- there is no spent set, no tombstone, no
high-water mark. This is not a weak enforcement, it is an absent one.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A NORMAL ORACLE BUG. fgdb-reference is not one implementation among two; §15
makes it the DEFINITION of "what should this return". An illegal history it accepts is an illegal
history the whole verification ladder believes in:
 - fgdb-z5y0 (the model-based generator, filed the same day) will emit recycled-identity histories and
   score them legal, and the engine -- which must honour never-recycle -- will diverge. Every such
   divergence is a FALSE FAILURE, and false failures are how a generator gets switched off.
 - fgdb-0trr's per-eid keying is only sound if an eid has one interval. Today it can have several.
 - any Strata "forced seal" reasoning about re-creation is reasoning about a case whose legality
   nobody has decided.

THE SCOPE DEFENCE, and why it does not dispose of this. It is arguable that the oracle does not model
ALLOCATION at all: it receives identities in intents rather than minting them, so allocator state
(IdAllocatorState, IdRangeLease, spent-range commitments) is legitimately out of scope. Accept that.
It still does not settle this, because never-recycle is not a fact about the allocator -- it is a fact
about which HISTORIES ARE LEGAL, and legality is exactly what this crate is for. The defect is that
the oracle currently answers neither way: it does not enforce the law, and it does not document that
it declines to.

TWO ADMISSIBLE RESOLUTIONS. Pick one deliberately; do not let it be decided by whichever is easier.
 A. ENFORCE. Keep a spent set per element kind, check uniqueness against live-or-spent, and add
    ApplyError arms distinguishing "already exists" from "identity is spent". Cost: the spent set
    grows without bound in a long-running oracle, which is acceptable for a crate that is explicitly
    licensed to be simple and never optimized (§15), and is arguably the honest model anyway --
    the real system's spent commitments are also permanent.
 B. DECLARE OUT OF SCOPE, at the type level rather than in prose. State at the definition that the
    oracle does not model identity allocation, and make the GENERATOR (fgdb-z5y0) structurally unable
    to emit a recycled identity, so the gap cannot reach a differential. A comment alone is not
    enough: it would leave a hand-written test free to encode a history the engine must reject.

A is preferred. It makes the oracle answer the question, and B's guarantee is only as good as every
future history source remembering to honour it.

LAWS THE CLOSURE OWES:
- create-after-delete of the same VId is refused, with an error naming the spent identity;
- likewise for EId;
- a spent identity stays spent across a branch fork -- a child branch may not re-mint an identity its
  parent spent, or two branches could mint conflicting meanings for one id and merge could not
  reconcile them;
- and the negative control that keeps this honest: creating a FRESH identity after a delete still
  succeeds. Without it, "refuse everything after a delete" passes all three laws above.
close_reason: Implemented in b6a399c89769c3e611191a76273b3850ceaf3310: the reference oracle now permanently spends retired VId/EId identities within a lineage and across the graph-wide branch allocator namespace; all required positive and negative controls and the full Rust gate pass.

title: Strata concurrent identical puts can observe a partial winner and report a false collision
description: Measured at HEAD a79d79a67c8ecbde98089556c0a07959973457fd in crates/fgdb-strata/src/store.rs. BlockStore::put publishes the create_new destination inode before write_all completes. A second writer of identical bytes can lose create_new, immediately open and read the zero-length or partial winner, compare it with the complete input, and return StoreError::Collision even though both callers derived the same content identity. The source comment claims the two-writer identical case succeeds, but every existing block_store test is serial. The fgdb-zy8o durability patch preserves this behavior and does not pretend to solve it. Closure needs either a typed single-writer publication owner or a staging/no-replace publication protocol with an explicit completed-winner observation; bounded sleeps or blind retry loops are not sufficient. Add a deterministic interleaving control that pauses the winner after create_new and proves the identical loser cannot produce Collision, while different bytes at the same derived path still fail closed.
notes:
Implemented and landed as aafa9f9. BlockStore now creates and durably records one empty publication-lock inode. Every put opens that inode independently, acquires its whole-file lock through CommitCx, and receives a private non-clone BlockPublicationPermit. While the permit is held, new bytes are written to the sole noncanonical staging pathname, synced, atomically moved to the content-derived canonical pathname, then inode and containing-directory synced. Existing equal bytes are observed only under the permit and re-enter the durability barrier; different bytes remain a collision. An interrupted or failed staging write can be safely rewritten by the next permit owner. Reuse fails closed unless an existing staging name is a regular single-link inode, preventing an external hard link from turning staging truncation into canonical-block corruption.

Dedicated controls: the channel-ordered interleaving pauses the winner after staging sync, starts an identical loser immediately before permit acquisition, then releases the winner; both return the same ObjectId and the loser never sees partial bytes. A staging crash proves the canonical path remains absent and a subsequent permit owner completes publication. A multiply-linked staging control proves canonical bytes remain bit-identical.

Mutation evidence: replacing only File::lock with a successful no-op made cargo test -p fgdb-strata --lib store::durability_tests::an_identical_loser_observes_only_the_complete_winner -- --exact exit 101; the loser failed with NotFound while racing the shared staging pathname. Restoring the lock made the exact test exit 0.

Focused evidence on landed content: cargo fmt --all -- --check exit 0; cargo test -p fgdb-strata --lib --test block_store exit 0 with 4 library and 15 integration tests; cargo test -p fgdb-strata --all-targets --no-fail-fast exit 0 with 86 tests; cargo clippy -p fgdb-strata --all-targets -- -D warnings exit 0; exact-path UBS exit 0 with zero critical findings; git diff --check exit 0.

Authoritative bash scripts/check.sh completed with logs in /data/tmp/fgdb-check-gates.sKUm5p and exited 1: core 9 of 9 executed, 8 passed, 1 red; registered 24 of 24 executed, 23 passed, 1 red; zero unrun. Unsafe-tool lanes passed. The sole registered red was scripts/w1_cross_crate_determinism_e2e.sh, whose retained diagnostics explicitly say determinism was not reached: foreign tools/registry-check/src/unsafe_ledger.rs inline-table fixtures trigger unclosed table in registry-check --lib, 115 passed and 1 failed. This bead remains in_progress until a clean repository hard gate exits 0.

title: NENF assigns shared cascade eids to the smallest deleted VId
description:
`fold_target_disjoint` is the net-form. Shared cascade eids currently get partitioned only in `Database::write` (`assign_cascade_owners`). A second caller of the fold, or a rebuild of evaluation-order rows, would still emit two DeleteVertex rows that both list the same eid. The fold applies vertices in VId order; the second apply then fails CascadeImageMismatch.

## Background
cczg fixed this on the write path. The law belongs in NENF: after 17ht, evaluation-order derivation puts a shared incident eid on every same-batch DeleteVertex. The net must keep it only on the smallest VId, which is the first applied. Topology is not required — an eid listed on two delete rows is incident to both.

Related to cczg / 17ht / 819.2. Not parent-child to open `819`. Closing this does not close `819`. Remove the write-path pre-pass so there is one owner.

## Technical Approach
- After folding vertex nets, before emit: each cascade eid is claimed by the smallest deleted VId that lists it; other deletes drop it.
- Delete `assign_cascade_owners` from `write()`.
- Unit test: two DeleteVertex both listing EId(10) emit (1, [10]) then (2, []).
- Spine dual-delete test stays green.

## Success Criteria
- fold_target_disjoint unit test names the owner.
- `deleting_both_endpoints_in_one_batch_retires_the_edge_once` still passes with no write-path assign.
- spine + spine_differential green.
- `819` stays open.

## Test Plan
`cargo test -p fgdb-delta-types --lib fold` and the spine dual-delete + full spine/differential.

title: FG-INV-12 scalar docs falsely state hash equality implies encoding equality
description:
## Finding

`crates/fgdb-types/src/scalar.rs:3-13` states the FG-INV-12 law as:

`a == b` implies `hash(a) == hash(b)` implies `encode(a) == encode(b)`.

The second implication is false: hashes are not injective, and equality of hash outputs cannot prove equality of canonical encodings. The normative plan at line 680 states the intended pair of obligations instead: equal values have the same hash and equal values have the same canonical encoding. The test `equal_implies_same_hash_and_same_encoding` at lines 1162-1208 likewise proves those two consequences independently; it does not and cannot prove hash equality implies encoding equality.

## Controlled evidence and interpretation

The identical implication-chain grep found this line as the only Rust doc claim using the chained arrow form; the positive control found the plan's known `equal ⇒ same hash` statement. Reading the implementation and test supplies the interpretation: behavior implements the intended coherence law, while the module documentation overclaims an impossible stronger law.

## Required closure

Rewrite the bullet as two implications from semantic equality (or an explicit conjunction), keep it aligned with plan line 680 and FG-INV-12, and add a documentation assertion or review guard that cannot regress to treating a hash as an injective identity.
close_reason: Corrected the FG-INV-12 implication and added an executable hash-collision guard; all scoped gates passed.

- The implementation and tests do not rely on that false converse. The intended law appears independently in the plan and in `scalar.rs:1162-1208`: scalar equality must imply equal hashes, and scalar equality must independently imply equal encodings.
- A controlled chained-arrow grep found this as the only Rust claim of that form, while the known plan wording was found by the same probe. Reading the code establishes that this is a documentation/invariant-statement defect, not a demonstrated hash or encoding behavior defect.

Required fix shape: rewrite the claim as two independent consequences of scalar equality, preserve FG-INV-12 wording consistently across nearby docs/tests, and add or retain tests that assert both implications from equality without asserting any implication from hash equality.

title: Shell deliverables need bash -n + shellcheck; cargo and ubs are silent no-ops on them
description:
## The rule

Shell deliverables need `bash -n` + `shellcheck`. The mandated checks
(`cargo check --all-targets`, `cargo clippy`, `cargo test`, `ubs`) are ALL
no-ops on a `.sh` file, and `ubs` reports **exit 0** while doing nothing.

## Why this is a silent-green class, not a style nit

`ubs scripts/foo.sh` prints:

    no supported languages detected in /data/projects/frankengraphdb
    UBS did not run any scanner: nothing was checked (this is NOT a pass).

and exits 0. A shell script that has never been examined by any tool is
indistinguishable, at the exit code, from one that passed every gate. AGENTS.md
mandates `ubs $(git diff --name-only)` after substantive changes, so following
the documented process exactly still leaves shell deliverables unchecked.

Same family, found by pane7 the same hour: `ubs` reports `.jsonl` as
UNSUPPORTED, so it is a silent no-op on everything under `.beads/`.

Operational note: `ubs` invokes cargo internally, so take build-1 or build-2
before running it or you stall other panes on the shared package-cache lock.

## Concrete evidence: a load-bearing guard was disabled and nothing noticed

`scripts/w1_cross_crate_determinism_e2e.sh` had:

    sha256() { sha256sum "$@"; }
    find crates tools ... | xargs sha256 | sha256 - | cut -d' ' -f1

`xargs` cannot invoke a shell function. shellcheck flags this as SC2033
(warning). The failure mode is the worst available:

  - `xargs sha256` writes NOTHING to stdout
  - the trailing hash then digests an EMPTY STREAM
  - the "source pin" comes back as `e3b0c442...b855` = sha256("")
  - that is 64 valid hex characters, IDENTICAL on every tree

So the pin passed a length check, and every before/after comparison of it
succeeded. The guard it powered — detect a concurrent agent committing to the
tree mid-run, so a foreign edit is not misreported as nondeterminism — was
dead, with no error, no output, and no symptom.

Measured differentially against a faithful reconstruction of the buggy code:

    buggy   before=e3b0c442...b855  after=e3b0c442...b855  -> guard silent
    fixed   before=f4ce29f3...c5f5  after=6e703cc0...5791  -> guard fires

While proving the fix, a SECOND constant-digest hazard surfaced: GNU `xargs`
runs its command once even with no input, so `find | xargs sha256sum` over an
empty tree ALSO yields a tree-independent constant (`abcfa6a9...`) that passes
both the length and empty-digest checks. Both are now guarded (03e498c).

## What landed

- 03e498c — the two guards, mutation-proven three ways
- 482f806 — `scripts/check.sh` now runs `bash -n` + `shellcheck
  --severity=warning` over every tracked shell file, FIRST, before any cargo
  step (fast, needs no build slot). Errors and warnings fail; notes advisory.
  Refuses to be vacuously green two ways: an empty file list is an error, and
  a missing shellcheck binary is an error rather than a skip.

Sweep of the 10 existing scripts: bash -n clean, 0 errors, 0 warnings. 13
SC2015 notes, all the `check && ok "..." || die "..."` idiom, all verified
FAIL-CLOSED (ok() returns a log echo's status; both scripts whose die() does
not exit end in `[ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ] || exit 1`). A spurious trip gives a false
RED, never a false GREEN. No fixes were needed — the gap was that nobody had
ever looked.

## Remaining work

1. AGENTS.md still documents only the cargo-based checks. Its "Mandatory
   Checks After Substantive Changes" block should say that `ubs` does not
   cover `.sh` or `.jsonl` and that `scripts/check.sh` is the gate that does.
2. Decide whether `.beads/*.jsonl` deserves an analogous real check, since
   `ubs` is a confirmed no-op there and those files carry provenance pins.
3. The 13 SC2015 notes are safe today but the idiom is fragile: any future
   `die()` that gains a non-zero-returning first statement flips them from
   fail-closed to fail-open. Converting to `if ...; then ok; else die; fi` is
   a cheap permanent removal of that footgun.

## What landed

`scripts/check.sh` now enforces **file-coverage closure** before any cargo step.

    ADR mutated inside markers -> architecture-check exit=1

which is pane6's, and I left them alone. Commented there.

M6 is the one that matters: without it, M3 could have been passing for an
unrelated reason.

## Two findings the first run produced

1. `.beads/.write.lock.stale-1784298410` is **tracked** — a stale beads lock
   committed by accident. Declared exempt with that reason (printed every run)
   rather than deleted; AGENTS.md Rule 1 reserves deletion to the user.
2. `registry-check` silently passes a brand-new `.md` carrying unregistered claim
   markers: claims-lint scans a static list of 3 and nothing closes the set. The
   new check.sh step is a backstop for the tracked case, but the law belongs in
   the checker. Filed separately.

## Verification

    lib tests (rustc --test)   76/76
    tests/identity.rs         105/105
    claims-lint               green on the edited AGENTS.md
    shellcheck                clean at severity>=warning across all 13 tracked
                              shell files, including this script's own new code
    ubs scripts/check.sh AGENTS.md  -> "nothing was checked", exit 0
                                       (the defect, reproduced on this commit)

title: fgdb-sim whole write path fixture bypasses head CAS and durable transaction authority
description:
## Finding
Fresh-eye review of landed commit 4065eba947cdab54a122a333a7c12240b3082e65 found a useful verification composition fixture exported and claimed as the whole user transaction write path even though it bypasses load-bearing transaction and visibility authority.

## Concrete defects
- commit_transaction accepts an arbitrary caller-supplied &ReferenceGraph while its docs claim CURRENT materialized state. The test helper happens to replay first, but the public API does not enforce that premise.
- commit_capsule is called with empty head_updates. A marker and capsule exist, but no coordinate branch head CAS advances; reference replay ignores that missing visibility authority, so the E2E can report a graph a real branch head never selected.
- final certification, SSI, authorization, resource/constraint/escrow checks, audit ownership, durable txn outcome/idempotency, and plan:397 same-transition LocalDeltaBatchIndex publication are absent.
- source_intent_root_digest and SchemaEpoch are fabricated zero constants.
- a build/finalization error is mislabeled ReplayError::Decode.
- TxnAbort/no-effect returns assert nothing durable. plan:399 instead gives abort/outcome lifecycle durable semantic control state that advances LogicalCommandSeq/HLC but not CommitSeq; no marker is not the same claim as no durable outcome. A statement-error-only transaction also loses its failure/outcome across restart.

This is the AGENTS doctrine-7 prohibited shape: an early subset may implement a slice of a final abstraction, never a substitute transaction model. The composition test is valuable; the production-like API and evidence claim are not.

## Required closure
Choose one honest boundary:
1. make this explicitly a verification-only composition fixture, not an exported user transaction API: name it for reference-effects-to-Chronicle composition, state the exact missing authorities, and ensure no feature/gate cites it as transaction-path evidence; or
2. defer a real commit_transaction path until the owning W2/W5 transaction, final-certification, outcome, head-CAS, audit/resource, and local-delta publication types exist, then require those types in the signature.

Discriminator tests must show an arbitrary/stale basis cannot commit, a successful graph commit advances the exact coordinate head via CAS, abort/no-op retains a recoverable durable terminal outcome without falsely consuming CommitSeq, and materialization follows visible heads rather than every marker indiscriminately. The bead note and any gate evidence must call the current slice a fixture until those laws exist.

At focused snapshot 18043dd993391c72afc6d7ee105a27fb5ceb626b over base e9bfaaf1295f68ad364dec181a10ad2d2b8b16ac: cargo test -p fgdb-sim passed 17/17, cargo clippy -p fgdb-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings passed, and cargo fmt --all -- --check passed. title: Require one sealed storage-read Cx across Strata and Chronicle
description: Doctrine 3 requires every filesystem read to accept a purpose-typed context, but Strata BlockStore get/get_bytes/get_root/reopen paths and Chronicle CommitCoordinator read_capsule/capsule_exists plus RootStore recovery reads perform synchronous I/O without one shared read-authority contract. Acceptance: fresh and selective Strata reopen tests, Chronicle capsule recovery and root-store crash suites, strict workspace fmt/check/clippy/test, local .beads identity coverage, and exact-path UBS all exit 0. title: Prove private W1 token boundaries with negative and positive doctests
description:
## Finding

Three public contracts say illegal states are structurally unavailable, and source reading confirms their private fields/sealed traits currently enforce the claims, but no permanent compile-fail test names the boundary:

- `crates/fgdb-resource/src/lib.rs:218-225`: `Admitted` is constructible only through `ResourceCeiling::admit`; forgetting the budget check is documented as unrepresentable.
- `crates/fgdb-types/src/context.rs:949-1018`: `PurposeObligation<State>` makes transfer/publication/cleanup order unrepresentable out of sequence.
- `crates/fgdb-codec/src/kernel.rs:63-72` together with `crates/fgdb-codec/src/evidence.rs:218-235`: private `KernelOutput` construction plus sealed dispatch traits prevent evidence callers from relabeling arbitrary bytes.

## Controlled evidence and interpretation

The compile-fail census found the known controls for purpose-context role isolation, the claim lattice, logical-delta ordering, private evidence envelopes, bigint operations, and the sealed identity-column marker. The identical probe found no block naming `Admitted`, the obligation state order, or `KernelOutput`. That passing control licenses the absence measurement. Reading each implementation supplies the interpretation: these are presently sound type boundaries with missing regression proof, not demonstrated construction bypasses.

## Required closure

For each boundary add one external-crate `compile_fail` doctest that exercises the forbidden construction or transition and one companion doctest that compiles on the legal side. Pin the expected compiler error where stable. Do not weaken or redesign the APIs unless a negative case unexpectedly compiles; if it does, split that behavior defect into its own bug.
close_reason: Added compile-fail and compiling companions for all three private W1 boundaries; all scoped gates passed.

title: SymbolRecord verifier accepts unauthenticated trailing bytes
description:
Fresh-eyes trace at HEAD 4f860e9b6dfd816fbfea0914defea78985429c7d confirmed the unresolved finding already noted on fgdb-w2-object-identity-t0f: crates/fgdb-chronicle/src/symbol.rs parse_framing rejects only bytes.len() < record_len. A canonical, MAC-valid SymbolRecord followed by arbitrary bytes therefore verifies successfully; the suffix is outside record_len and outside the MAC transcript. This contradicts the module contract that the transcript is total and every declared length agrees with the supplied buffer. It is reachable from the capsule container because the outer per-symbol length can include the unchecked suffix.

Required closure: exact-record verification must reject bytes.len() > record_len as InconsistentLengths (while preserving Truncated for shorter input), and a mutation-sensitive regression must append a nonempty suffix to a freshly serialized valid record and require refusal. Run the full Chronicle suite plus repository gates; do not widen the parser into a prefix-consuming API unless it returns explicit consumption and every caller proves canonical framing.

notes:

not fixed by me -- filed so the red is owned rather than lingering, and so the next pane to see it
does not re-derive the attribution from scratch.

THE STATE OF THE TREE. `bash scripts/check.sh` exits nonzero for EVERY pane right now. 22 steps PASS;
exactly one fails:

    ERROR: UBS critical ratchet drift in "panic!/unreachable!/todo!/unimplemented!":
      baseline 137, observed 132.
    RED  core: UBS over every tracked Rust source (exit 1)
    FAIL core: UBS over every tracked Rust source (exit 1)

ATTRIBUTION, and it is exact rather than circumstantial:
 - the drifting class is `panic!/unreachable!/todo!/unimplemented!`, and the OTHER TWO classes in
   UBS_CRITICAL_BASELINE (scripts/check.sh:911) matched their pins exactly (817 and 122), so this is
   one class moving, not a scan-wide shift;
 - HEAD is 9e11f4a "test(types): remove scanner-critical panic branches [fgdb-storage-read-cx-srta]",
   whose stated purpose is exactly this class;
 - the count moved DOWN (137 -> 132), which is the direction a fix moves it;
 - it landed WHILE this gate run was in flight, so the run observed the post-commit tree;
 - and the ratchet's own error text says what was owed: "update UBS_CRITICAL_BASELINE in the SAME
   commit and say in the message which findings moved and why."

WHY I DID NOT JUST RE-PIN IT, which is the tempting one-line fix:
1. UBS_CRITICAL_BASELINE lives in scripts/check.sh, which I was concurrently editing for an unrelated
   coverage row. Two panes editing one file to land two unrelated changes is how a change gets lost.
2. A DOWNWARD move is not self-evidently safe. The pin is per-class, which is much better than a
   single aggregate, but 137 -> 132 within one class is still a NET. It is consistent with "5 removed"
   and equally consistent with "7 removed, 2 added". Re-pinning to 132 without splitting it would
   bless any new finding hiding inside the net. The authoring pane already has that evidence; I would
   have to reconstruct it.
3. The bead id in that commit (fgdb-storage-read-cx-srta) names the owner.

WHAT CLOSING THIS ACTUALLY REQUIRES -- not just editing the number:
 - the per-finding split, so the message can say which findings moved and why (the ratchet demands
   this in prose, and it is the only thing that distinguishes a fix from a masked regression);
 - the pin updated to the observed value in the same commit;
 - a re-run of `bash scripts/check.sh` read BY EXIT CODE, not by grepping the log.

GENERAL POINT WORTH KEEPING. A ratchet that must be updated in the same commit as the fix is a
two-artifact change, and the second artifact is easy to forget precisely because the first one felt
complete and the gate that would have caught it takes ~35 minutes to run. This is the same failure
shape as landing a new docs/*.md without registering it in claims_lint.toml -- the work is done, the
gate is red, and nobody notices until someone pays for a full run.

title: Structural source keys mis-parse when a generic signature contains a pipe
close_reason: Fixed in 0246145: structural source keys now match by byte-exact reconstruction from the typed catalog row instead of an ambiguous split('|') parse. Proven against a pristine control binary (only the five catalog_target_source_identity_mismatch violations differ; zero difference on the unmodified catalog) plus three negatives covering the exact row, four tampered components, and a re-segmented key. The blocked union TimeBoundOnlineMacaroonRootProjection minted in the same commit.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
`validate_target_source_identity` (tools/registry-check/src/appendix_a.rs, the "field" / "union" / "union-arm" arms around lines 10133 / 10157 / 10173) recovers a structural source key's components with `row.source_key.split('|')` plus a fixed expected part count. The census's own key grammar uses `|` as the separator — `field|{schema_owner}|{path}|{stable_name}`, `union|{schema_owner}|{union_path}`, `arm|{schema_owner}|{union_path}|{arm_name}` — but a schema owner may legally carry a generic signature that itself contains `|`, e.g. `TimeBoundSubjectInventory<Role:Local|Meta|Shard>`. For those owners the split mis-segments the key and the law rejects a row whose bytes are exactly correct.

REPRODUCED (a16 I6b, 2026-07-24): staging the anchor field + union + three arms for `TimeBoundSubjectInventory<Role:Local|Meta|Shard>.online_macaroon_roots` produced exactly 5 `catalog_target_source_identity_mismatch` violations (1 field, 1 union, 3 arms) with EVERY other structural law passing — census bijection, arm payload digests, anchor contract, coverage, adjudication projection. The rows were dropped from I6b and the union remains unminted for this reason alone; see the a16 bead trail.

FIX: stop parsing the ambiguous string. Reconstruct the expected key from the typed catalog row, which already holds the components separately (`containing_schema`, `union_path`, `stable_name`, `source_arm_name`), and compare byte-for-byte against `row.source_key`. That is strictly stronger than the current parse — it cannot be satisfied by a differently-segmented key — and it removes the grammar dependency entirely. `validate_target_source_identity` currently receives only `ProjectionRowMeta`, whose `canonical_symbol` is dot-joined and cannot recover the `path` component for nested fields, so the typed row (or the catalog) has to be threaded to the call site.

BLAST RADIUS (probed over the full frozen census, 2026-07-24): exactly ONE census owner catalog-wide carries an interior pipe — `TimeBoundSubjectInventory<Role:Local|Meta|Shard>`, holding 26 field + 1 union + 3 arm keys. Two further owners have pipe-bearing generic signatures but own zero structural keys (`RecoveryBridgeSpec<Local|Meta>`, `ResultIndependentRetentionIndex<Local|Meta>`). `top|` candidate keys are immune because they are prefix-stripped rather than split, which is why three such top-level candidates have been in the catalog for many increments without surfacing this.

NEGATIVES TO ADD WITH THE FIX: a pipe-bearing owner whose row is exact must PASS; the same row with any component altered (schema, path, stable name, arm token) must still FAIL; and a hand-crafted key that re-segments to the same `split('|')` parts as a legal key must FAIL under the reconstruction comparison.

UNBLOCKS: a16 `TimeBoundSubjectInventory<Role:Local|Meta|Shard>.online_macaroon_roots` (1 field + 1 union + 3 arms), plus its 26 interior field keys once the field-coverage closure reaches them. Owner lane: Appendix A catalog / registry-check. Needs the `catalog` write token.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FIXED AND LANDED. The defect is real, the fix is proven against a control, and the union it blocked now mints.

ROOT CAUSE, confirmed exactly as diagnosed: `validate_target_source_identity` (appendix_a.rs, the field/union/union-arm arms) recovered a structural source key's components with `source_key.split('|')` against a fixed expected part count. `|` is both the key separator and legal inside a generic signature, so `TimeBoundSubjectInventory<Role:Local|Meta|Shard>` — four interior pipes — segments into seven parts instead of three and the law rejects a byte-exact row.

THE FIX SHIPPED: reconstruction, not parsing. Expected keys are rebuilt from the typed catalog row and compared byte-for-byte; the key is never split. Unions and arms reconstruct exactly from (containing_schema, union_path[, source_arm_name]). Fields have no `path` column in the catalog, so the field arm anchors on the two components that ARE columns — owner prefix and stable-name suffix — plus a requirement that the interior path be rooted at the owning schema. The path itself is validated by the source pass, which independently requires the whole key to exist in the frozen census, so the two laws compose to full validation. Strictly stronger than the old parse and free of any grammar dependency.

THREADING SOLVED (the obstacle flagged in the original bead): the single call site sits in `validate_catalog_metadata`, which holds the catalog but not the census, and `ProjectionRowMeta.canonical_symbol` is dot-joined so it cannot recover `path` for nested fields. Resolution: build the expected keys once per run from `catalog.identity` into an `ExpectedStructuralKeys` index, keyed by the same projection symbol those components derive. No signature churn beyond one added parameter, and only one call site exists.

EVIDENCE, from a pristine CONTROL binary built from the pre-fix source so the comparison is isolated:
  * control vs patched on identical staged input: the ONLY difference is the five catalog_target_source_identity_mismatch violations (1 field + 1 union + 3 arms) disappearing. Every other reported code is identical pin drift.
  * control vs patched on the UNMODIFIED live catalog: both report zero failures. The fix changes no existing verdict — no regression.
  * three negatives (appendix_a_pipe_bearing_owner_keys_match_by_reconstruction): the exact pipe-bearing row PASSES; four tampered variants FAIL (owner, union path, arm token, field stable name); and a re-segmented key with owner and path swapped — same split('|') parts as the legal key — still FAILS. That last assertion is the one the old parse was incapable of making.

BLAST RADIUS held at the probed value: exactly one census owner carries an interior pipe. RecoveryBridgeSpec<Local|Meta> and ResultIndependentRetentionIndex<Local|Meta> have pipe-bearing signatures but own zero structural keys, and `top|` keys were always immune because they are prefix-stripped rather than split — which is why three such candidates sat in the catalog undetected for many increments.

UNBLOCKED AND MINTED IN THE SAME COMMIT: TimeBoundOnlineMacaroonRootProjection on TimeBoundSubjectInventory<Role:Local|Meta|Shard>.online_macaroon_roots — anchor tag 7, construction order 33, arms Local|Meta|Shard in census source order with exact payload digests. Cardinality is `one`, not `many`: there is exactly one role-selected union value per inventory; the repeated record_refs live inside the Local/Meta arm payloads and the Shard arm is deliberately uninhabited-empty. The census reports ManyOrIndexed for this member because of the `[...]` inside those arm payloads, which is why the honest field-row cardinality had to be decided rather than copied.

METHOD NOTE worth reusing: the whole fix was written, compiled, and gate-rehearsed OFF the catalog token in a scratch copy of tools/registry-check rooted so `include_bytes!("../../../PLAN.md")` and `repo_root()` both resolve, with the registries as real file copies so regeneration could never write through to the live tree. All 65 identity tests plus registry-check all (513 targets, 0 violations) were green in that scratch tree before the token was acquired, which turned the hold into a mechanical apply. Two defects were caught there rather than under the token: a rustfmt violation in generated pin entries, and a second in the new test.

title: topology-check reports required_edge_coverage outcome=pass with 7 of 8 edges deferred; the ratchet that says so lives only in a script no runner invokes
description:
FINDING — mock/placeholder sweep (pane4, 2026-07-26). Ranked #6.

## The measurement

Running the prebuilt gate binary read-only against the live tree:

```
$ topology-check --root .
{"event":"required_edge_coverage","declared":8,"evaluated_live":1,"deferred":7,"outcome":"pass"}
{"event":"posture_closure_checked","posture":"embedded","entry_crate":"fgdb","closure":[],"illegal":[],"outcome":"deferred"}
{"event":"posture_closure_checked","posture":"server","entry_crate":"fgdb-server","closure":[],"illegal":[],"outcome":"deferred"}
{"event":"posture_closure_checked","posture":"cli","entry_crate":"fgdb-cli","closure":[],"illegal":[],"outcome":"deferred"}
```
exit 0.

Seven of the eight named architectural edges cannot be evaluated (no active
crate on one side), all three posture closures are deferred, and the aggregate
`required_edge_coverage` carries `outcome: "pass"`. The single live edge is
`calibrate-over-asupersync`. Every one of the seven design-only capabilities
(merge ladder, Native/ECS, WriteCoordinator, ARC buffer pool, time travel,
encryption, verification posture) also reports `outcome: "pass"` with
`disposition: "design_only"`.

## What is honest here, and what is not

Honest, and worth preserving: the gate REPORTS its own deferral rather than
hiding it. The counts are in the NDJSON. `topology.rs:1725` states the
condition plainly in its docstring ("With no composition crate active every
posture resolves to `deferred`"), and `g0_topology_e2e.sh:87-101` prints the
coverage line explicitly under the banner "report what is deferred rather than
letting a green bar imply coverage", plus an anti-vacuity ratchet:

```
if ! grep -q '"event":"required_edge_coverage".*"evaluated_live":1' "$FIRST"; then
  echo "ERROR: the named-edge law is vacuous — no edge has both endpoints active" >&2
```

That is the right instinct and it is well built.

NOT honest, as currently wired: **that ratchet lives only in
`g0_topology_e2e.sh`, which no runner invokes** (see
fgdb-gate-coverage-checksh-omits-live-gates-u7mw). In the green bar that
actually executes — `scripts/check.sh` — `topology-check` is never run at all,
so neither the coverage line nor its ratchet is ever produced or read. The
result is a topology law that is 7/8 unevaluated, with the instrument that says
so sitting outside every executing path.

Second gap, independent of the wiring: there is no RATCHET ON THE DEFERRED
COUNT. `deferred: 7` is reported but not pinned. When a subsystem crate lands
and its edge should go live, nothing fails if the edge stays `deferred` because
of a crate-name mismatch or a stale registry row. The transition
deferred -> evaluated is exactly the moment a silent miss becomes permanent, and
it is unguarded. The existing ratchet only asserts `evaluated_live` is
non-zero — and note it is an unanchored substring grep, so `"evaluated_live":1`
also matches 10-19, 100-199; harmless while the intent is "at least one", but it
cannot be repurposed as a count pin without anchoring.

## Which gate catches this today

None, on both counts.

## Fix

1. Depends on fgdb-gate-coverage-checksh-omits-live-gates-u7mw: get
   `topology-check` and `g0_topology_e2e.sh` into an executing runner. That
   alone restores the existing instrument.
2. Pin `declared`/`evaluated_live`/`deferred` in `registries/workspace_topology.toml`
   the way `crate_count`/`capability_count`/`required_dependency_count` are
   already pinned, and derive the expectation from the registry (the e2e's
   `registry_scalar()` helper already does exactly this for the other four
   counts, so the pattern is in hand). Then a deferred edge that should have
   gone live fails loudly at the moment of transition.
3. Anchor the substring greps in `g0_topology_e2e.sh:98` while there.

attribute to EOF. architecture.rs has its test module at 1320-1383 with ~4900

`Violation::new("registry_name", ...)` into the "already witnessed" set. The
script that does it correctly is in the xnxy.1 working notes; it is ~90 lines of
Python and it is the difference between 13 and 14.

WHY THIS SHARE WAS NOT TAKEN WITH THE OTHER 122
  registries/appendix_a_catalog.toml and tools/registry-check/src/appendix_a.rs
  were under another pane's catalog write hold for the whole xnxy.1 window. Nothing
  about the method is harder here; the file was simply not available.

THE METHOD, WHICH IS ALREADY PROVEN ON THIS EXACT OWNER
  tools/registry-check/tests/violation_witnesses.rs already holds three Appendix A
  witnesses that work exactly this way, and they are the template:
    control:  appendix_a::parse_catalog(real catalog text) must succeed AND
              appendix_a::validate_catalog / verify_projections must return ZERO
              violations -- so no row can fire without its mutation
    mutation: ONE field on ONE Catalog row, on a fresh clone
    assertion: the EXACT code, never a string-only or count-only match
  The 122 laws closed in xnxy.1 are table-driven for the same reason and the table
  shape carries over verbatim: `struct Witness { code, fact, mutate: fn(&mut T) }`.

ACCEPTANCE
  - every reachable Appendix A code witnessed with its exact code, or declared
    unreachable-by-input WITH THE REASON (see below)
  - mutation-prove both directions with named numbers: forward is the suite green;
    reverse is a scratchpad copy of src/appendix_a.rs with its `Violation::new`
    constructor rewritten to prefix every code, which must turn every new witness
    RED while the other suites stay GREEN. The repo is never touched and
    CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR is a compile-time value, so repo_root() still resolves.
  - do not let the genuinely-unwitnessed count increase

EXPECT SOME "CANNOT FIRE", AND TREAT THAT AS THE FINDING
  xnxy.1 found three such laws in the other modules: a predicate that compares a
  reader's answer on a COMPILED-IN fixture against a compiled-in constant is
  unreachable from any input, and is the opposite of vacuous -- it is the control
  that licenses every zero below it. The honest disposition is to declare it, say
  why, and witness that the GUARD is a live predicate rather than constant-true
  through the same public reader on perturbed text. The five production-dead pin
  diagnostics the parent bead lists are a second, weaker class: they compare two
  compile-time constants and should become compile-time invariants or documented
  exclusions.

TRAPS ALREADY PAID FOR
  - REBUILD THE RLIB EVERY VERIFICATION ROUND. A test binary built against an
    rlib from an earlier HEAD reported 12 phantom Appendix A pin drifts (a15
    byte_count, durable_fields epoch 72->73, 3319 vs 3327 projection rows) on a

    GlobalTxnRecord.command_ref : StrongRef<GlobalTxnCommand>

    Same law, other direction.

  inside a08 changes it, because both bounding kinds are outside a08 and already landed.

lines within a05 and a08, both are plain StrongRef members rather than digests or weak references,
and neither was introduced by any catalog decision. A command that names topology state must be
constructed after topology; the record that names the command sits before topology. That is a
contradiction in the specification, not in the catalog.

  2. GlobalTxnRecord moves to >= 40. It is landed at 30 in a05 and is itself referenced; a05's field

     plan text should say which it is.
  4. GlobalTxnRecord.command_ref stops being a StrongRef, same reasoning in the other direction.
I am not choosing between them: 1 and 2 move landed rows on another slice, and 3 and 4 change what

title: Strata store: block and root identities are both bare ObjectId, so get_root(block_id) compiles
notes:
SELF-REPORTED 2026-07-31 (JadeSnow). A defect I introduced in 7e189cb/ca69ab9, with a working fix
PARKED rather than landed -- read the collision note at the bottom before picking it up.

THE DEFECT. BlockStore holds two kinds of object -- delta blocks and partition roots -- and every
identity in its surface is a bare ObjectId. So all of these compile:

    store.get_root(a_block_identity)
    store.get(a_root_identity)
    store.reopen(a_block_identity)
    store.contains(a_root_identity)

Each answers with a runtime refusal (Malformed or MalformedRoot), so this is a mistake the caller is
told about rather than a wrong answer -- which is why it is P2 and not higher. But it is a mistake the
COMPILER could prevent, and the store is the one place in the crate where two object kinds share a
namespace, so it is exactly where a newtype earns its keep.

plan:2000-era Strata already names the block one: DeltaBlockVersion. This bead is the remaining
typing item on fgdb-w3-tier-d-ctj.

THE FIX, WHICH IS WRITTEN AND STASHED. Two newtypes in fgdb-strata/src/lib.rs --
DeltaBlockVersion(ObjectId) and PartitionRootVersion(ObjectId) -- with the store surface typed:
put -> DeltaBlockVersion, put_root -> PartitionRootVersion, get/get_bytes/contains take a block, and
get_root/reopen take a root. The library compiles clean under it.

CRITICALLY: the newtype WRAPS and does not redefine. The identity stays §5.1 logical_object_id over
the object canonical bytes, so the same block has the same identity whether or not it is wearing the
type. Anything else forks the identity domain and a root naming a block stops being resolvable. Keep
that property; it is the one way this change could do real damage.

WHY IT IS PARKED, and this is the part worth reading. crates/fgdb-strata/tests/block_store.rs is
under active development by another pane -- put_with_crash and BlockStoreCrashPoint appeared in
2fceaf7/aafa9f9/aa2e61b while I was working, and strata went from 78 to 100 tests in that window. A
newtype necessarily touches every call site in that file, so landing it would mean rewriting a file
someone else is actively writing, for a benefit that is compile-time hygiene rather than a behaviour
fix. My first attempt at the mechanical rewrite also mangled two of their assertions
(store.path(id.0) where id was already an ObjectId), which is exactly the damage the collision rule
exists to prevent.

The work is in `git stash` on this repo: "JadeSnow: DeltaBlockVersion/PartitionRootVersion newtypes,
parked (block_store.rs is contested)". Whoever takes this should re-derive it rather than trusting the
stash to still apply -- the store has moved since -- but the shape above is right and the library-side
edit is small. Do it when block_store.rs is quiet, and do the call sites by reading each one rather
than by pattern replacement.
