title: Milestone W3/G1: Strata transactional storage core
description:
## What & scope
Aggregate the exact W3 Strata subset required by Gate G1: the independent reference oracle, bounded extent buffer and scratch discipline, canonical identity/property encodings, Tier-I vertex-directory and inline adjacency, Tier-D immutable MVCC delta blocks, Tier-R sealed CSR-class runs, seal/compaction equivalence, and write/space-amplification decision-card accounting. It deliberately excludes only the registered bulk-staging construction path, whose first public activation is the G2 bulk-load/DDL surface.

## Why
The W3 workstream crosses two convergence gates. Requiring bulk staging at G1 made the engine gate wait for a capability Gate G1 does not advertise; omitting final Strata abstractions would instead create a prohibited prototype. This aggregate preserves the complete transactional storage abstraction while keeping the later bulk ingestion capability disabled until its ordinary-transaction, schema, source-bijection, crash, and replay contracts land at G2.

## Design and phase contract
The generated G1 storage capability manifest admits ordinary authorized reads and writes over Tier-I/Tier-D/Tier-R representations, bounded spill, sealing, compaction, and governed migration. Every representation exposes the same logical digest and authorized cursor semantics. Bulk-staging kinds and formats remain frozen in G0 and decodable where required, but construction, publication, and user-visible bulk-load commands are unconstructible at G1. The full W3 epic adds bulk staging and closes at G2.

## Success Criteria
- Every child task passes its unit, property/model, mutation/fuzz, simulation/fault, and E2E rows under the universal verification-evidence contract.
- Unit tests cover every canonical encoder/decoder, boundary, checksum, extent state, tier transition, and invalid capability/format arm.
- Representation-equivalence properties compare Tier-I, Tier-D, Tier-R, seal, compaction, and spill results against fgdb-reference after every operation and under every retained snapshot.
- Lab E2E proves authorized commit -> Tier-D visibility -> seal/Tier-R scan -> compaction -> restart with byte-identical logical digest and bounded resource ledgers.
- Compile/registry negatives reject bulk-staging construction and publication at G1 while preserving its frozen format/command rows as inactive.
- Structured JSONL diagnostics name run/scenario/seed, graph and snapshot identity, representation/tier, input/output logical digests, resource reservations, decision-card/policy epoch, fault point, oracle/checker verdict, evidence references, and replay command; protected values are redacted.
- No HashMap-of-vectors storage substitute, mutable-primary authority, post-filter authorization, unbounded materialization, or non-durable benchmark path can satisfy this milestone.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
The principal risks are representation drift, premature retirement under open snapshots, unbounded spill/buffer use, and adaptive tier thrash. Exact logical-digest equivalence, snapshot-aware retirement models, resource-ledger assertions, dwell/hysteresis cards, and deterministic pinned fallbacks are mandatory. Rejected: a special G1 storage implementation or a silent bulk-load stub.

## Provenance
Plan §§6, 15, 17, 19 W3; Gate G1 compaction/label-digest and bounded-resource clauses; Gate G2 bulk-import/derived-build clauses; Doctrine §§1, 5, 7, 8.

title: Inject the lab VFS into Strata BlockStore so post-D2 derived publication is faultable
description:
## Context

Doctrine 3 (`Cx` everywhere) and W1 ("the lab VFS exists before the first fsync") are load-bearing for B5. Chronicle's commit/root path is VFS-generic. The 2026-08-20 reality check confirmed Strata's production `BlockStore` still writes canonical files through ordinary filesystem paths (`crates/fgdb-strata/src/store.rs`, and the admission in `crates/fgdb/src/lib.rs` around the `open_with_vfs` comments: Strata does not yet accept a VFS).

Consequence: lab torn-write / ENOSPC / fsync-lie / cancel campaigns that claim to cover "the database" currently cover Chronicle and `manifest.root`, then a second, unfaultable path publishes derived Tier-D objects. Crash matrices on the capsule/marker protocol do not prove Strata publication fencing.

This is not "add more tests". It is wiring the existing lab VFS into the derived-object store so FG-INV-08/09-class recovery claims can be about one I/O plane.

## Current state

- Chronicle: `CommitCoordinator` + `RootStore` take a VFS.
- Strata: `BlockStore` content-addressed `strata-blocks/` via `std`/`Unix` paths; staging + publication lease exist; capsule sealing of those bytes is a sim-only composition proof (`fgdb-sim/tests/strata_blocks_are_durable_objects.rs`).
- `fgdb::Database::open_with_vfs` documents the seam.

## Implementation plan

1. Give `BlockStore` (and the publication lease) the same VFS trait Chronicle uses; no second filesystem abstraction.
2. Keep storing canonical plain bytes (doctrine 5 derived-state rule). Do not sneak capsule wrapping into this bead; that is a separate composition decision already named as deliberately absent.
3. Extend `fgdb-sim` crash-point coverage so a fault during Strata publication after D2 still leaves the handle fenced (`NeedsAuthoritativeRecovery`) and reopen agrees with the oracle.
4. A bit-identical scalar/path fallback is not relevant here; the fallback is the existing UnixVfs.

## Files to change

- `crates/fgdb-strata/src/store.rs`
- `crates/fgdb/src/lib.rs` (open/create wiring)
- `crates/fgdb-sim/tests/` (publication-fault matrix)

## Success criteria

- [ ] `open_with_vfs` injects the same VFS into Chronicle and Strata.
- [ ] A deterministic FaultVfs test tears or lies on a Strata block fsync after D2; product reads/writes refuse; authoritative reopen matches `fgdb-reference`.
- [ ] Existing incremental-publish ≡ rebuild tests stay green.
- [ ] No new `unsafe`. No HashMap storage substitute.

## Tests

- Unit: BlockStore put/get/identity-mismatch through UnixVfs and FaultVfs.
- Integration: post-D2 Strata publication crash/cancel/ENOSPC; handle fenced; reopen.
- Logging: structured crash-point name, object id, and whether the marker survived.

## Why this serves the vision

B5 requires the whole database to run under lab. A lab that cannot bite Strata cannot claim FoundationDB-class recovery for the graph store, only for the commit log.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FOUND WHILE CLOSING fgdb-claims-lint-scan-set-not-total-nldg (pane4, 2026-07-27), and deliberately NOT fixed there.

fd7d169 made the closure walk recursive, so every non-hidden `*.md` anywhere under a `closure_dirs` root must be scanned or excluded. That closes the depth hole. It does not close the hole one level up: **`closure_dirs` is declared data and nothing validates that it covers the repository.**

THE MUTATION THAT SHOULD FIRE AND DOES NOT. Edit registries/claims_lint.toml:

    closure_dirs = ["."]        ->      closure_dirs = ["docs"]

Every law in lint.rs still holds. The walk is still recursive, the prune list is still live, every exclusion still names an existing path, and the three docs/ artifacts are all in `scan`. The eight root `.md` -- including AGENTS.md and the merged plan -- simply stop being closure obligations, and a new root document is invisible again. This is the same defect the bead just closed, moved from the WALK to the ROOTS.

WHAT PARTIALLY CATCHES IT TODAY, and why it is not enough. `claims_lint_shipped_prose_is_clean` asserts `census.prose_files_seen >= 12`, so narrowing to `["docs"]` (3 prose files) would red that test. That is a real backstop and it is why this is P3, not P1. But it is a NUMBER IN A TEST, not a law in the checker:
  - it is a floor measured on today's corpus, so it says nothing about which
    directories were walked, only how many files were found;
  - a narrowing that keeps the count at or above 12 -- e.g. adding a root that
    happens to hold enough prose -- passes it;
  - `registry-check lint --root .` alone, which is what a pane runs and what
    `registry-check all` runs, never evaluates it.
Compare `[[closure_prune]]`: a prune that narrows nothing is `dead_closure_prune`, a law in the checker. A root that covers nothing has no equivalent.

THE LAW THAT SHOULD EXIST, stated as the fix, not as a preference:

    the repository root must be a closure root, transitively --
    `closure_dirs` must contain "." or a set whose union is "."

The simplest honest form is: require `"."` to be present, and emit a violation naming the config if it is not. If a future tree genuinely needs several disjoint roots, the law becomes "every top-level non-hidden, non-pruned directory is reachable from some root", which is checkable with the same walk that already exists.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. `closure_dirs = ["docs"]` makes `registry-check lint --root .` exit non-zero
   and name registries/claims_lint.toml.
2. The shipped config is unchanged and stays green.
3. Mutation audit: removing the new law makes case 1 pass again.
4. The law must be in lint.rs, not in a test floor -- the test floor already
   exists and is exactly what this bead says is insufficient.

NOT INVESTIGATED: whether the same "declared roots are unvalidated" shape exists in the other registries that carry a directory list. I did not look.

  appendix_a.rs:6342        Cargo.toml [workspace] members             no, manifest
  liveness.rs:409           <member>/src and <member>/src/bin          no, manifest

SO THE NUMBER IS 1 OF 7. Five roots are manifest-derived and one is a code constant. That is a CATEGORY, not five more holes, and I proved it rather than asserting it:

  MANIFEST-DERIVED, proven self-enforcing. Removing one line -- "crates/fgdb-bigint"
  -- from Cargo.toml [workspace] members and running the checker built from that
  same tree:
      topology-check --root .  ->  exit 1

      "code":"active_manifest_missing"
  Narrowing a manifest root removes a crate from the build and an existing law
  names it. Four of the five go through one shared roster reader
  (appendix_a::workspace_member_paths), so there is one place to narrow and it is
  already guarded.

  CODE CONSTANT, already guarded against its own vacuity. validate.rs's scripts
  closure carries `script_scan_empty`: if the directory yields nothing it FAILS
  rather than reporting a clean tree. Changing the constant is a code change under
  review, and tests/metamorphic.rs drives the same closure from fixtures.

WHY lint.rs's EXISTING GUARD IS NOT ENOUGH, since it has one. The walk already errors with "closure directory holds no prose — the closure law would be vacuous here" when a root holds no `*.md`. THE TOP-LEVEL SURFACE the law has to account for: 5 non-hidden directories (crates, docs, registries, scripts, tools) plus the repository root's own files.

DESIGN DECISION, and a rejected alternative. The bead proposed "closure_dirs must contain '.'". I am not implementing that as a standalone rule, because a second rule "every top-level directory is covered" would then be UNREACHABLE -- it can only fail when the first already has -- and a check that cannot fail reports enforcement that is not happening. One law instead: every non-hidden top-level entry that could hold prose must be reachable from some closure root or excused by a `[[closure_prune]]`. comments.text:
ERRATUM IN THE NORMATIVE APPENDIX, not in the catalog. Filed for the repo owner and the a10 owner. Blocks fgdb-a16-time-authority-ytub and fgdb-a10-command-delta-ooy1. This is NOT an ordering problem and cannot be fixed by re-ordering; see the last section.

THE DEFECT. Two Appendix A schemas spell a lineage predecessor as a self-referencing retaining wrapper:
  a16:2210  TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role> {... predecessor_ref:StrongRef<TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role>>? ...}
  a10:1922  PreparedCommitRecord            {... predecessor_ref:StrongRef<PreparedCommitRecord>? ...}
Neither member can be modelled as a [[field]] row in ANY shape, because two live checker laws are jointly unsatisfiable for that spelling.

PROBE EVIDENCE, measured against the real catalog, not reasoned. All five candidate annotations were tested with exact_type = StrongRef<TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role>>:
      reference_semantics   catalog_annotation_reference_semantics_mismatch
      strong                does NOT fire   <- the ONLY accepted value
      weak_digest           FIRES
      none                  FIRES
      conditional           FIRES
      identity              FIRES
That law derives the legal reference_semantics from the concrete reference wrapper in the census exact_type, so the source's own `StrongRef<...>` spelling FORCES `strong`.

And dag_self_edge forbids exactly that: it fires when the target resolves to the owner. Critically, ITS FILTER IS NOT LIMITED TO `strong` — it covers strong | conditional | weak_digest alike, even though its message historically said "strongly reference itself". That wording is what invited a reclassification fix that cannot work, and it has since been corrected in 6316ab5 to name the real filter.

NET: `strong` is forced by the annotation law and forbidden by the DAG law; every non-retaining alternative is rejected by the annotation law before it ever reaches the DAG. THERE IS NO LANDABLE FIELD ROW IN ANY SHAPE. Do not spend a catalog-token hold rediscovering this.

WHY THIS IS A SOURCE DEFECT RATHER THAN A MODELLING CHOICE. The plan spells one family's predecessor three different ways, and the other two are both non-retaining:
  * PreparedRootHeader<Role> (a01:1694) carries `nonretaining_predecessor_digest` — the SAME prepared-root family as the a10 host, spelled correctly.
  * LocalCommandOrigin.Prior uses ConditionalCommandRef, whose landed wire_type row reads "conditional (cuttable) reference to the predecessor LogicalCommandRecord; retention governed by checkpoint cuts (FG-INV-14)".
  * RestoreSourceLeaseRecord.predecessor (a16:2237) is a source-level closed union Genesis|Prior, landed as reference_semantics="none" with the Prior arm weak-digest-bound.
All three were landable PRECISELY BECAUSE they are spelled non-retaining in the source. The two predecessor_ref members are the outliers against their own families. plan:392 doubles down for the a10 host ("its typed references and predecessor are strong"), so the inconsistency is internal to the spec.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. durable_fields.toml is, per plan:292, "the sole input to generated reachability/GC, checkpoint-vector, backup-closure, construction-DAG, compatibility, size-limit, and fuzz walkers." A retaining predecessor edge therefore makes every ancestor in an append-only generational chain permanently reachable, which is exactly what checkpoint cuts and retention floors exist to prevent. The other two spellings in the same family avoid this deliberately.

TWO CANDIDATE RESOLUTIONS. I am deliberately NOT choosing between them; both are above an agent's level and the first amends the normative appendix.
  (A) AMEND THE APPENDIX so the two members are spelled non-retaining, matching their own families — e.g. `nonretaining_predecessor_digest` (the PreparedRootHeader precedent, and the most direct fit for a10 since it is the same family), or a source-level closed union Genesis|Prior with the Prior arm weak-digest-bound (the RestoreSourceLeaseRecord precedent). Consequence: this moves the affected slices' pin sha256 values, so it must be done as an explicit erratum with the slice pins re-frozen, and it touches at least two slices.
  (B) NARROW THE dag_self_edge FILTER so a declared lineage self-edge is admissible — on the argument that the construction DAG is a schema-level approximation, and an immutable generational chain is acyclic at the INSTANCE level (generation N is constructed after N-1, so the predecessor is always already known). Consequence: the retaining-reachability concern above is then real and unmitigated, so (B) would need a separate mechanism to keep predecessor chains cuttable — otherwise it trades a checker complaint for a retention defect.
My own read is that (A) is more consistent with the doctrine, because the family's other two spellings already encode the intended answer and (B) leaves the GC/reachability consequence unaddressed. But (A) edits the normative spec, which is the repo owner's call.

RE-ORDERING IS THE INTUITIVE FIX AND IT IS WRONG — for both hosts, and this is the single most useful sentence here. A self-edge is ORDER-INDEPENDENT: identity.rs compares `target == containing` and `continue`s BEFORE it ever compares construction_order, and equal orders are legal anyway (a16 alone has twelve kinds at order 27). No order assignment whatsoever changes the outcome. There is no minimal re-assignment to compute and no better number to find; the search is pure waste.

ENFORCEMENT STATE, so nobody is surprised. Until 6316ab5 the a16 host ESCAPED dag_self_edge entirely, because the DAG law resolved a field row's owner by exact name while logical_by_name is keyed by bare family, so every generic-signed row skipped the whole block. That is fixed: both hosts now fail honestly the moment their field body is modelled. PreparedCommitRecord is spelled bare and always failed. So a red gate on dag_self_edge for either member is the checker working correctly — read this bead, do not work around it.

REPRODUCE THE PROBE IN ~30 SECONDS, no cargo:
    rustc --edition=2024 --crate-type=lib --crate-name registry_check tools/registry-check/src/lib.rs -o /tmp/libregistry_check.rlib
    CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR=$PWD/tools/registry-check rustc --edition=2024 --test tools/registry-check/tests/identity.rs \
        --extern registry_check=/tmp/libregistry_check.rlib -o /tmp/probe_identity && /tmp/probe_identity
(the --extern path must be named lib*.rlib, and CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR must be set at COMPILE time because tests/identity.rs resolves the registries through env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")). Push an appendix_a::Annotation with the exact_type above and vary reference_semantics to reproduce the table.

OWNER DECISION SUPPORT — costed u3gr resolution options (read-only analysis; no
choice made).

BASELINE AND METHOD

This analysis is frozen against commit
`fdbe8e88f727500eb3a1022f99adcd67c234a0ba`.  I paired an immutable
`git archive` of that commit with a registry_check rlib rebuilt from the same
archive.  I did not reuse the rlib after HEAD moved: registry_check bakes the
shared EXPECTED_* counts and assignment pins into the rlib, so an rlib from a
different catalog state can report false violations.  Live HEAD had already
moved to `e251b28caf8dd92ffdc42f3b9dff6b260283d5fe` while this note was being
written.  Every hash below is therefore a costed fdbe8e8 baseline value, not a
landing value.  The chosen implementation must rebuild the rlib from live HEAD
at the start of its catalog hold and recompute every dependent pin.

Positive-control evidence for the measurement:

* My first self-reference census returned zero because the probe mishandled the
  trailing `?`.  The identical probe also failed to find the certainly-present
  `PreparedCommitRecord.predecessor_ref`, so I rejected the result and fixed the
  parser.
* The corrected probe asserted both known u3gr members before reporting a
  count.  It found 23 direct source fields whose concrete type is
  `StrongRef<their-own-family>`.
* The catalog-row lookup was controlled against the known landed
  `RootSlot.cluster_incarnation` field.  That control resolved; none of the 23
  self-reference field keys did.  In particular, neither u3gr predecessor has
  an already-landed [[field]] row.

Code-reading evidence for the interpretation:

* 20 of the 23 are predecessor-shaped.  The other three are an intentionally
  recursive key-envelope child tree (a13) and two ReservationUseRecord
  self-family references (a19).  Several predecessor-shaped entries also have
  explicit retaining semantics in their surrounding prose (remote-authority
  trust chain, same-epoch key chain, persistent key tree, witness-policy
  rotation).  Thus “23 self references” is a trustworthy measurement, but it
  does NOT mean “rewrite all 23 as weak.”  The two named outliers remain a
  spec-owner classification decision.

ONE IMPORTANT OPTION BOUNDARY

A direct source edit to
`nonretaining_predecessor_digest:WeakDigest?` is not a complete source-only
resolution under the live checker.  The annotation law correctly derives
`reference_semantics=weak_digest`, but the current construction-DAG loop also
rejects a weak_digest self target.  Omitting the target would make the
annotation incomplete rather than fix the law.  Therefore:

* a genuinely source-only form of Option A needs a closed source union whose
  `Prior` arm contains an untraversed WeakDigest, following the already-landed
  RestoreSourceLeaseRecord precedent; or
* the shorter direct WeakDigest spelling must be paired with the safe,
  weak-self narrowing described under Option B.  That is A+B, not B instead of
  A.

OPTION A — AMEND THE NORMATIVE APPENDIX

The narrow, source-only, controlled shape I costed is:

1. At a10 (fdbe8e8 line 1922), replace
   `predecessor_ref:StrongRef<PreparedCommitRecord>?` with
   `predecessor:Genesis|Prior{record_digest:WeakDigest}`.
2. Immediately state normatively:
   “Its predecessor digest authenticates generation adjacency but is
   comparison-only and is never traversed by reachability/GC, checkpoint, or
   backup walkers.”
3. At a16 (fdbe8e8 line 2191; the bead's original 2210 coordinate drifted as
   other plan changes landed), make the analogous replacement:
   `predecessor:Genesis|Prior{record_digest:WeakDigest}`.
4. Preserve TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation's target/reservation ownership by
   tightening the existing index sentence to say that
   `TimeSubjectIssuanceReservationIndex<Role>` strongly owns each current
   generation via `StrongRef<TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role>>`, while the
   record's predecessor digest is comparison-only and is never traversed by
   reachability/GC, checkpoint, or backup walkers.
5. Amend the main-body paragraph at fdbe8e8 line 392:
   `record_generation, predecessor_ref, ...` becomes
   `record_generation, predecessor, ...`; and
   “its typed references and predecessor are strong” becomes
   “its typed references are strong; its predecessor digest is nonretaining
   and comparison-only.”

The explicit index ownership in step 4 is load-bearing.  Without it the full
Appendix reference census loses TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation as a target and
its already-issued reservation/source disposition becomes an orphan.  With it,
the target count and target hash remain stable.

Census movement for exactly those two fields:

* remove 2 old field keys;
* add 4 field keys (the two union anchors plus the two nested
  `.Prior.record_digest` members);
* add 2 union keys and 4 arm keys (`Genesis` and `Prior` for each host);
* re-key 1 a16 ambiguity adjudication because the source expression changes;
* no schema keys move and no target keys move;
* reference-source occurrences move 2458 -> 2457, while target count remains
  813.

Slice blast radius:

* The narrow erratum changes source bytes in a10 and a16 only.  The global
  Appendix source manifest changes.  The a10 and a16 [[slice]] byte/hash and
  structural-census pins change.  Their line ranges do not change, and every
  other [[slice]] row remains byte-for-byte valid.  The main-body line-392 edit
  is outside the Appendix slice manifest.
* The controlled full census found 18 other predecessor-shaped keys across
  a01, a03, a06, a07, a08, a13, and a21.  A universal
  “all predecessor links are nonretaining” policy would additionally touch
  those seven slices.  If the policy were broadened to all recursive
  self-family references, a19 also joins the blast.  Code reading shows this
  would weaken several expressly retaining structures, so none of those
  additional slices should be swept into the narrow erratum mechanically.

Exact fdbe8e8 pin cascade measured by the paired probe:

* Appendix: 1,020,717 -> 1,021,099 bytes;
  sha256 `71a48b67304f94568590f79c5b1c1ee4731819aee022c57fece78a7e72bce7f1`
  -> `99bdbabe4879da6de05708b44941caafffe90e1b318ba486fac3e32ead204777`.
* a10: 16,579 -> 16,737 bytes;
  sha256 `7bad384e377f49ef7d102eefda083260874790f6af47f85d0b344ea4c0854e9e`
  -> `38243eb255379374822f14fce9f39e1a21e8cd696b1534319df26eb0d29562ef`.
* a16: 69,768 -> 69,992 bytes;
  sha256 `9fc751b96c0539ad956995a3e0bde2fe71e58fe4103aa80cbce9d1c687273427`
  -> `999b75d2355fa5ca846befb717845d4dfd2dedd633d7fd3c2888b47d2dc9a674`.
* a10 structural pins:
  fields 134/`afd046a5...1042` ->
  135/`32a798afbb82395ea5089be311a455a78f691935689946375473d715dab5d1e9`;
  unions 4/`75ebe16c...7211` ->
  5/`9ea05919a371a153187922c8f8d24c655730637a177ba5218bdc8b7ee7fe69b3`;
  arms 13/`442fae0a...fe7` ->
  15/`271ef85b272629296c6299f8fa0444752941636b6b9c90414f798f500a1fd563`.
* a16 structural pins:
  fields 1066/`558e4fe8...c43` ->
  1067/`58a70cc32050123f8ad4ea5382c5323f82d3f586c4f1dd4b5b406bf8954fb592`;
  unions 31/`8811f886...a3d` ->
  32/`1b9b97b9be811daa05f5f317f43d33e856af21c079597c5fa828f79ed1621a6c`;
  arms 79/`4396cd4a...ed7` ->
  81/`5b0540e12ce1bec8822ad8f34938dd2d0b8e8c505fcc305e8d15c48dd83a5a55`;
  ambiguities remain 825, but hash moves
  `bf9119647ec4065423958f4721e6cdead82b9b90ef4327313621c8940565c152`
  -> `012ae799c8d02a7fda418c0475a7fa39c27296d3bc936e151468d840fb74e45d`.
* Reference manifest:
  813 targets and target hash
  `84276b6d97342e9ec1619424ddacb5b429e98e1862e03359afc837b65bb3392e`
  stay fixed; occurrences become 2457 with hash
  `eb737c879b0dd5fb447762a299c383805317961981444ec1fb2047eeaa2c1c96`.
* The new a16 ambiguity adjudication row suffix is
  `6a0fd7cffdf6dde5214eb5d38913ccd83b886aad5a6ccee3acef54366b93b1a3`;
  the static ambiguity-contract hash moved
  `1b6db0abb881dc7e9530421748f7a3f53dd6e0b115c4ebd6f88b7afbdf5de0b0`
  -> `9dc37edffeac1fd779762650723ee2f3c25a4f6c9eb7480c2a9573569d264ffe`.

Already-landed-row effects:

* Neither obsolete predecessor field has a landed projection row, so no field
  row becomes invalid.
* The PreparedCommitRecord reference-source disposition must drop the removed
  a10 occurrence: locations `["a06:1694","a10:1922"]` become
  `["a06:1694"]`.
* The one a16 ambiguity adjudication must be re-keyed.
* PreparedCommitRecord kind/other fields, TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation kind,
  and the already-landed TimeSubject state union/arms remain valid.
* With the explicit index ownership sentence, the TimeSubject reservation and
  source-disposition rows remain valid.
* The controlled simulation did not move target-source assignment
  (`8be4e34c...6b6c0`) or reservation assignment
  (`ccd889a3...8865`), and it required no projection-registry epoch bump.
  Minting the newly exposed union/field/arm rows in the same commit would be a
  separate scope and would move those epoch/pin cascades.

Mechanical file blast at fdbe8e8 is ten existing files: the plan; the catalog;
`tools/registry-check/src/appendix_a.rs`; `scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh`; and the
six generated registry header comments in bootstrap_frames, durable_fields,
logical_object_kinds, physical_record_kinds, prebootstrap_artifact_kinds, and
wire_types.  The catalog itself also carries the header.  Only a10/a16 slice
constants change in the checker.

Epoch-fixture warning: the erratum-only simulation did not move an epoch, but
the landing pin chase still must inspect every old value in tools/ and scripts/.
If the implementation also mints rows and moves an epoch, update all three
known loader-invisible sites: the identity.rs fixture literal/assert, the g0
target-source-assignment pin, and phase 2h's exact awk rewrite of current
logical epoch -> next epoch.  Also audit sibling negative fixtures and the
e2e existing/reserved reservation literals.  A phase-2h miss exits 42 without
a named assertion.

Blast/reversibility/silent risks for A:

* Blast is broad mechanically (ten pinned files) but narrow semantically (two
  source definitions, two slice rows, one ambiguity row, one source
  disposition).
* It is reversible as one explicit spec erratum before durable-format release,
  although reversing after projection rows are minted requires the inverse
  re-pin/re-key operation.
* Silent risks are: omitting the main-body line-392 contradiction; weakening
  every self predecessor instead of the two owner-approved outliers; losing
  TimeSubject target ownership by omitting the index sentence; trusting stale
  fdbe8e8 pins or a stale rlib; updating only the global sha but not slice
  structural pins; and a negative epoch fixture matching nothing.

OPTION B — NARROW dag_self_edge

There are two materially different meanings of “narrow the filter,” and only
one is safe:

1. Safe weak-self narrowing: keep the outer construction-DAG filter as
   `strong | conditional | weak_digest`.  In the
   `if target == containing_family` branch only, accept/skip a self edge when
   `f.reference_semantics == "weak_digest"`; continue rejecting strong and
   conditional self edges.  Keeping weak_digest in the outer loop is necessary
   so weak mutual cycles, weak future results, and unresolved weak targets
   remain checked.
2. Unsafe shortcut: remove weak_digest from the outer filter.  Do not do this.
   My controlled mutation made a weak mutual cycle and a weak future reference
   completely invisible, while every existing construction-DAG negative test
   still passed because those fixtures all use strong references.  That is the
   exact “law passes for the wrong reason” failure mode.

The safe checker edit is localized to
`tools/registry-check/src/identity.rs`'s self-edge branch plus tests.  A
controlled probe produced this boundary:

* shipped DAG: clean (positive control);
* weak self: accepted;
* strong self and conditional self: `dag_self_edge`;
* weak mutual and strong mutual: `dag_cycle`;
* weak future and strong future: `dag_future_result` (and cycle where the
  fixture creates one);
* unresolved weak target: still `ref_target_unresolved`.

Required regression boundary, not merely one happy case:

1. a positive weak_digest prior-instance self link compiles/validates;
2. ordinary strong self remains rejected (existing test);
3. conditional self remains rejected (new; conditional is retaining in the
   registry discipline);
4. generic-signed strong self remains rejected (existing test);
5. weak mutual links still produce `dag_cycle`;
6. weak future links still produce `dag_future_result`;
7. unresolved weak target still produces `ref_target_unresolved`; and
8. a strong field merely named `nonretaining_predecessor_digest` is rejected,
   proving semantics rather than spelling controls the exception.

However, this safe narrowing alone does NOT resolve the present Appendix:
StrongRef forces `reference_semantics=strong` before the DAG law runs.  It only
makes the direct WeakDigest version of Option A landable.  Its blast is two
checker files, no catalog pin or epoch movement, and it is readily reversible,
but it is complementary rather than a complete alternative.

For Option B to be a standalone resolution while leaving the two source
StrongRefs unchanged, the checker must instead admit a genuinely retaining
self edge.  The smallest code diff would hard-code the exact owner/field pairs
in the self-edge branch:

* `PreparedCommitRecord#predecessor_ref`; and
* `TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role>#predecessor_ref` after generic-family
  normalization.

That is cheap in lines but not cheap in semantics: generated reachability/GC,
checkpoint, and backup walkers still traverse the strong edge and can retain
the complete predecessor chain.  The checker would go green by exception while
the retention defect identified by plan line 292 remains.  It is also an
untyped allowlist: there is no current FieldRow attribute proving “this target
is an already-existing prior instance rather than the object under
construction.”

A robust retaining-self version of B therefore needs an explicit registered
relationship discriminator such as `prior_instance`, validated independently
of field name.  That expands beyond one filter:

* add/parse/validate the discriminator on `identity::FieldRow`;
* include it in exact-key and transcript/robot output contracts;
* add corresponding Appendix catalog annotation evidence and projection
  comparison in appendix_a.rs;
* annotate only the approved lineage fields; and
* specify how generated GC/checkpoint/backup walkers cut such an edge.  Without
  the last item it is merely a construction exception, not a complete
  retention design.

That robust form moves durable-field/catalog contracts and likely their epoch
and assignment pins once rows are minted.  It therefore inherits the full
epoch-fixture and stale-rlib audit described above; it is no longer the
apparently tiny checker-only change.

Tests required for a retaining-self exception are stricter:

* ordinary and generic strong self cycles still fail;
* the exact approved prior-instance field succeeds;
* the same stable name on another schema fails;
* a different self field on the approved schema fails;
* conditional behavior is explicit;
* strong/weak mutual and future-result cases remain rejected; and
* a reachability/GC/backup closure test proves the approved predecessor is cut
  as specified.

One existing test is directly affected:
`idr_neg_self_edge_through_generic_family` uses the exact TimeSubject
`predecessor_ref`.  A standalone-B exception would make that fixture cease to
be negative.  It must be replaced with a different generic-signed strong
self-edge and paired with a positive approved-lineage fixture.  Weakening or
deleting it would let the generic-owner-normalization regression start passing
for the wrong reason.

Blast/reversibility/silent risks for B:

* The safe weak-only branch edit is tiny and reversible but not standalone.
* A hard-coded strong exception is tiny in files but system-wide in semantic
  blast because every generated retaining walker consumes durable_fields.
* A typed prior-instance/retention-cut design is safer than an allowlist but is
  a registry-schema change with an epoch/pin cascade and new generated-walker
  law; it is no longer cheaper than A.
* A checker exception is easy to revert before data exists, but poor to reverse
  after records rely on the admitted format.  A strong predecessor chain can
  silently defeat retention floors without producing a loader violation.
* The principal silent failures are removing weak_digest from the outer loop,
  keying the exception on a suggestive field name, preserving a green generic
  test by weakening its assertion, and validating construction order while
  never testing reachability retention.

COSTED VIEW, NOT A DECISION

The hard-coded standalone B has the smallest textual diff, but it is not the
cheapest complete engineering resolution: it leaves unbounded strong
reachability and therefore owes a second design.  The safe weak-self narrowing
is the cheapest checker change, but it only complements a source amendment.

For the two named outliers, I believe the source-only closed-union form of A is
cheaper in complete-system cost and safer: its pin blast is mechanical and
bounded, it follows the already-landed RestoreSourceLeaseRecord precedent, and
it makes non-retention true in the sole source consumed by GC/checkpoint/backup
walkers.  That is a recommendation about engineering risk, not authorization
to amend the normative Appendix.  Whether these two fields are spec errata,
whether the direct WeakDigest+A/B form is preferable, or whether the project
wants a first-class prior-instance relationship class is the repository
owner's decision.

comments.text:
THE ADJUDICATION ROUTE IS CLOSED — MEASURED, NOT REASONED. There is no catalog-only erratum record for this defect, and I can now say that with a number instead of an argument. Also closes the "read, not measured" gap that has been open on this trail all day.

=== 1. THE SOURCE PASS IS NOW MEASURABLE. IT WAS NOT BEFORE. ===
Every previous attempt to see which law binds predecessor_ref failed for a structural reason: load_and_verify runs the source pass ONLY if validate_catalog returns empty, and flipping any slice to complete makes validate_catalog return hundreds of violations, so appendix_a_catalog_source never ran. That is why source_complete_census_uncovered (:7182) and source_complete_slice_ambiguity_unresolved (:7311) have been recorded as READ, not measured.
Fix: arm the slices IN MEMORY on a loaded Catalog and call appendix_a::appendix_a_catalog_source(&cat, &source) DIRECTLY, bypassing the metadata gate entirely. Both are pub. Controls: nothing armed -> 0 violations; a10+a16 armed -> 1014 violations (1012 source_complete_census_uncovered + 2 source_complete_slice_ambiguity_unresolved). Zero-to-1014 on a two-slice flip is the positive control.
FIRST RESULT, and it corrects an assumption I had been carrying: arming a10+a16 through the ORDINARY loader names predecessor_ref NOWHERE. The completion battery iterates landed targets, and these members have no field row and no target row, so nothing iterates over them. Anyone measuring this defect with the armed-catalog recipe alone will conclude it is already clean. It is not; the law that binds it lives in the other pass.

=== 2. THE LAW NAMES ITS OWN THREE DISCHARGE ROUTES, AND I TESTED ALL THREE ===
    source_complete_census_uncovered   a16
      complete slice census field key "field|TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role>|
      TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role>.predecessor_ref|predecessor_ref"
      has no TARGET, approved ADJUDICATION, or covering ARM/WIRE INTERIOR contract
The a10 twin fires identically for field|PreparedCommitRecord|...predecessor_ref.
  ROUTE 1, a target row — BLOCKED. Already proven on this trail: strong is forced by
      catalog_annotation_reference_semantics_mismatch and forbidden by dag_self_edge; every
      alternative is rejected by the annotation law first. Nothing here changes that.
  ROUTE 2, an approved adjudication — CLOSED, and this is the new measurement. An adjudication
      is keyed to a RAW CENSUS AMBIGUITY. I searched every raw ambiguity for either member:
          ambiguities touching TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role>.predecessor_ref ... 0
          ambiguities touching PreparedCommitRecord.predecessor_ref ................. 0
          CONTROL: total raw ambiguities across the appendix ..................... 8,423
      A `StrongRef<Self>?` member is perfectly unambiguous — the census parses it exactly, which
      is precisely why it produces no ambiguity to adjudicate. And an adjudication without a
      matching raw ambiguity is not merely useless: source_complete_slice_ambiguity_unresolved
      requires one approved final adjudication per raw ambiguity "and no extras", so the row
      would itself fire, and the slice's ambiguity census pin would move against it.
  ROUTE 3, a covering arm/wire interior contract — THE ONLY ROUTE LEFT. It discharges the key
      because an arm payload digest creates no DAG edge, which is exactly the mechanism ovok
      established for the .profiles interiors. But it requires the SOURCE to spell the member as
      a closed union. That is Option A, a normative plan edit.

=== 3. WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE INSTRUCTION "LAND THE ADJUDICATION RECORD" ===
It cannot be done, and not for want of vocabulary. The catalog's resolutions are exactly
maps-to-source (373 rows) and not-a-durable-schema (16); dispositions are the seven structural
classes. Adding an "erratum" resolution would not help either, because the blocker is not which
VALUE the row carries — it is that there is no raw ambiguity for the row to key against. A new
resolution value would be a vocabulary widening that admits nothing, which is the exact failure
shape that cost this swarm a full increment on category (A) earlier today. I stopped before
designing it, for that reason.

=== 4. SCOPE CORRECTION — THIS IS FIVE PLAN LINES, NOT TWO ===
The bead title cites a16:2210 and a10:1922. Grepping the whole plan for the self-referencing
spelling finds FIVE hosts, consistent with the epic's 10-member / 7-slice u3gr population:
    1524  TxnOutcomeRecord.predecessor_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeRecord>?
    1698  MetaPreparedCommandRecord.predecessor_ref:StrongRef<MetaPreparedCommandRecord>?
    1700  ShardPreparedPayloadRecord.predecessor_ref:StrongRef<ShardPreparedPayloadRecord>?
    1922  PreparedCommitRecord.predecessor_ref:StrongRef<PreparedCommitRecord>?
    2191  TimeSubjectIssuanceReservation<Role>...   (the a16 host; 2210 drifted to 2191)
Amending only a10 and a16 unblocks those two slices and leaves the same defect standing in a03,
a06, a08, a13 and a21 — i.e. it fixes the blocker without fixing the doctrine. Whoever rules on
this should rule on all five spellings at once or say explicitly that the narrow fix is intended.

=== 5. WHERE I STOPPED, AND WHY ===
Route 3 means editing COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_THE_DESIGN_OF_FRANKENGRAPHDB.md — the normative
source — which moves the global source manifest sha256 and the a10/a16 slice pins, and which the
original filing explicitly reserved to the repo owner. The costed shape is already on this trail
(the 09:59 comment): replace with `predecessor:Genesis|Prior{record_digest:WeakDigest}`, add the
normative comparison-only sentence, preserve TimeSubjectIssuanceReservationIndex ownership so the
target census does not lose the schema, and amend the main body at line 392. Census movement is
-2 field keys, +4 field keys, +2 union keys, +4 arm keys, 1 a16 adjudication re-keyed.
I have NOT made that edit. I was asked for an adjudication record; the adjudication record is
provably impossible, and the remaining route is a materially larger and different action than the
one authorized. Holding for an explicit go-ahead on the source edit, and on whether it covers two
hosts or all five. Everything else is measured and ready.

REPRODUCE, ~20 seconds, no cargo and no token:
    rustc --edition=2024 --crate-type=lib --crate-name registry_check \
        tools/registry-check/src/lib.rs -o /tmp/libregistry_check.rlib
then a bin that loads the catalog, sets slice.definition_status="complete" for a10/a16 in memory,
and calls appendix_a::appendix_a_catalog_source(&cat, &plan_bytes). Give the census the APPENDIX
LINE RANGE only, not the whole plan, and re-append the trailing newline after joining the lines —
otherwise the range reads one line short and the census rejects it as SliceOutsideSource. Verify
census.source_sha256 == catalog.source_manifest.sha256 before trusting any of it.

title: Sim verdicts must not confuse harness I/O, detail text, or workload seed with product failure
description:
Closed q97e left three fail-closed holes in the sim harness.

1. Lab fixture adapter authenticates ReplayTrace.metadata.seed against the workload seed (cfg.seed / receipt.seed). asupersync records LabConfig.seed. 3. spine_durability and observe_spine_durability treat vfs.crash() Err as AcknowledgedCommitLost / InvariantViolated. FaultVfs::crash documents rollback Err as harness breakage.

Related to closed q97e. Not parent-child to open 819. Do not close 819.

- completed_task_dispatch_steps / matches_lab_replay_trace bind the scheduler seed.
- materialize compares kind + typed evidence, never detail.
- crash() Err is IoFailed / not a durability violation when the commit is still present.
- 819 stays open.

title: UBS core gate scans a directory, not the tracked set: 965MB of untracked tool state has disabled it
description:
The check.sh core gate "UBS over every tracked Rust source" is currently
inspecting ZERO Rust. It does not fail on a finding; it refuses to start:

    ℹ Scan size after ignores: 1003MB (limit 1000MB)
    ✗ Directory too large (after ignores): 1003MB exceeds limit of 1000MB
    RED core: UBS over every tracked Rust source (exit 2)

A 0.3% overshoot. MEASURED 2026-07-27 at HEAD b0f9041.

=== FULL ACCOUNTING OF THE 1003 MB ===

    .beads/.br_history                812 MB   81.0%   br command history
    .beads/.br_recovery                87 MB    8.7%   rolling beads.db backups
    libregistry_check.rlib (repo root) 66 MB    6.6%   stray build artifact
    .beads/beads.db                    16 MB    1.6%
    everything else                   ~22 MB    2.2%
                                     -------
                                     ~1003 MB

    tracked content, for contrast      24 MB   (191 files)

So the gate is disabled by ~965 MB of untracked tool state -- 96% of what it
scans -- while the thing it is named for is 24 MB. `.br_recovery` holds ten-plus
beads.db snapshots at 15-28 MB each (largest:
.beads/.br_recovery/beads.db.20260726_153739_148524848.bak, 27.8 MB).

The stray root artifact `libregistry_check.rlib` (66 MB, mtime 2026-07-27
03:01:36) is untracked and no commit owns it -- a rustc `-o` that landed in the
repo root instead of a scratch dir. NOT MINE: my builds this session wrote to
/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane2_laws_build.

=== WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE ONE GATE ===

The gate's NAME is "UBS over every tracked Rust source" but it scans a
DIRECTORY, not the tracked set. Those differ by 40x here. That mismatch is why
untracked tool state can disable a source-quality gate at all, and it is the same
shape as the other reporting defects found tonight: the instrument's stated domain
and its actual domain are not the same set.

It currently fails CLOSED, which is correct and is why it was visible. But the
failure mode is fragile in a specific way: the limit is a size threshold on
churning untracked state, so the gate can flip green again -- without anything
about the Rust changing -- the moment `.br_history` is rotated or a backup ages
out. A gate whose colour tracks the size of a log file is not measuring the code.

=== FIXES, IN ORDER OF PREFERENCE, NONE REQUIRING A DELETION ===

  1. Scan the tracked set, matching the gate's own name: feed UBS the output of
     `git ls-files '*.rs'` rather than the repo directory. 24 MB, no threshold
     anywhere near it, and the domain then matches the label.
  2. Add `.beads/.br_history` and `.beads/.br_recovery` to whatever ignore list
     UBS consults, so tool state cannot enter a source scan.
  3. Raise UBS_MAX_DIR_SIZE_MB. Weakest -- it restores the gate without fixing
     the domain mismatch, and the number will be crossed again.

NOTHING HAS BEEN DELETED and nothing should be without an owner ruling.
`.beads/.br_history` and `.beads/.br_recovery` are br's own recovery state; the
recovery backups in particular are the durable home for DB rows if a JSONL import
ever drops them, so reaping them is a decision with consequences, not cleanup.
Named here for the orchestrator rather than acted on.

ALSO NOTED, not acted on: `.beads/.write.lock.stale-1784298410` is TRACKED in git
(`git ls-files .beads/` lists it), and there are 2 `.write.lock*` files present. A
stale lock committed to the repository is at least a curiosity and may be a
second defect.

Filed by pane2, 2026-07-27, found while reading the full check.sh output after
the wzyl/h6kr labelling. Nothing deleted.
notes:
LANDED. Code is at HEAD and verified byte-identical to what was lint-proved --
but see PROVENANCE below: it shipped inside another pane's commit.

=== RE-DERIVED AT HEAD (the bead's numbers had already moved) ===
    .beads/.br_history        816.2 MB   78.2% of the scan   (bead said 812)
    .beads/.br_recovery       121.1 MB   11.6%               (bead said 87 -- grew 39%)
    libregistry_check.rlib     66.1 MB    6.3%
    .beads/beads.db            16.3 MB    1.6%
    untracked tool state     1019.6 MB   97.7%
    tracked Rust (the name)     6.6 MB   119 files
    all tracked                23.5 MB   194 files
    non-.git tree            1043.3 MB

STATED vs ACTUAL DOMAIN IS 159x, NOT 40x. The bead's 40x used all tracked
content (23.5 MB) as the denominator, but the gate's name says "every tracked
RUST source", and that is 6.6 MB. 1043.3 / 6.6 = 159.

THE SCAN IS GROWING. .br_recovery went 87 -> 121 MB in the hours between the
bead being filed and this measurement. The gate's input is a monotonically
growing pile of tool state, which is the colour-coupling claim demonstrated
rather than argued.

=== BEFORE -> AFTER, BOTH MEASURED ===
    HEAD   exit 2   "Directory too large (after ignores)"   0 files inspected
    now    exit 1   119 files inspected                     1049 crit / 14769 warn / 5349 info
The gate was ALREADY RED at HEAD (measured twice in full check.sh runs). The
reason moved from "refuses to start" to "1049 findings in the code it is named
for". Not a regression -- the first reading this instrument has ever taken. The
1049 are filed as fgdb-uz5e rather than smuggled in.

=== THE GUARD IS GENERAL ===
`gate_tracked_sources` states the input-set law for ANY gate, not just UBS: the
domain must be DERIVED from `git ls-files`, and if it cannot be -- not a work
tree, git unavailable, enumeration fails, or the set is empty -- the gate FAILS.
Deliberately no fallback. Proceeding on a different, smaller input set while
reporting the same verdict is the defect one level up, and is the same shape as
a test that returns PASS when the corpus it reads is absent (70q9 / identity.rs).

MUTATION-PROVED, CONTROLS THAT FIRE:
    positive  in-repo             -> 119 paths, exit 0, scan runs, no refusal
    negative  not a git worktree  -> gate_tracked_sources 1, run_ubs 1, NO scan
    negative  git repo, 0 .rs     -> gate_tracked_sources 1, run_ubs 1, refusal msg

CAUGHT IN REVIEW, WOULD HAVE FAILED OPEN: `readarray -t x < <(cmd)` reports
READARRAY's status, not cmd's. The first draft's guard would therefore have
succeeded whenever git failed -- a fail-open guard against fail-open, which is
this bead's own subject. It now writes through a file and checks git's own exit
status. Same wrong-command-attribution trap check.sh already documents for
SC2015.

=== GATES ===
bash -n, shellcheck --severity=warning, shellcheck --include=SC2015 all clean on
the STAGED content (not merely the worktree). Tracked file set unchanged, so the
file-coverage closure verdict cannot move. run_ubs proven directly rather than
through a ~35-minute full check.sh run.

=== PROVENANCE: THE FIX SHIPPED INSIDE f2c23d8, NOT UNDER THIS BEAD ===
All panes share ONE git index. This change was staged with `git apply --cached`,
lint-checked in a second tool call, and committed in a third. Between calls two
and three, pane3 ran `git commit` -- and swept the staged hunk into f2c23d8
("a guard that cannot run must not borrow the passing token", 70q9), whose stat
shows `scripts/check.sh | 70 +++`. My own `git commit` then reported "no changes
added to commit", which reads like failure when the change had already shipped.

Content verified byte-identical to what was lint-proved
(`gate_tracked_sources` and `run_ubs` both diff-clean against HEAD), and HEAD's
check.sh passes bash -n + shellcheck. NOTHING WAS LOST. Only the attribution is
wrong, and it is not fixable without amend/rebase, which is forbidden -- hence
this note is the record.

LESSON, GENERAL: staging is not private in this swarm. `git add` and
`git commit` must be ONE tool call; verification must happen BEFORE staging,
from a scratchpad copy or `git show :path`. A scoped commit protects the FILE
from a concurrent editor; it does not protect the INDEX from a concurrent
committer. That needs atomicity, not scoping.

=== NAMED FOR OWNER AUTHORISATION, NOT REMOVED ===
  libregistry_check.rlib  repo root, 66.1 MB, untracked, gitignored
                          (.gitignore:16 `*.rlib`), mtime 2026-07-27 03:01:36,
                          owned by no commit. Not mine -- my builds wrote to the
                          session scratchpad. The fix does NOT require removing
                          it; with the domain corrected it is simply out of
                          scope for the gate.
  .beads/.br_history      816.2 MB. NOT rotated, NOT deleted. With the domain
                          corrected its size no longer has any bearing on the
                          gate's colour, which was the whole point.
close_reason: Domain fixed: the gate now scans git ls-files '*.rs' (119 files) instead of a 1043MB directory, and fails closed via gate_tracked_sources if the input set cannot be derived from the tracked set. Gate went from exit 2 / 0 files inspected to exit 1 / 119 files inspected. Code landed at HEAD inside f2c23d8 due to the shared-index sweep (recorded in notes); content verified byte-identical to what was lint-proved. The 1049 criticals it revealed are filed as fgdb-uz5e.

title: Gate failure tokens are three different strings on two streams; grep '^FAIL' returns 0 on a red run of 9 of 10 gates
description:
Every gate script in this repo reports failure under a token, indentation and
stream of its own. There is no shared verdict contract, so no single grep
answers "did this gate fail" across the set, and the one grep the swarm
actually uses answers NO on a red run of every one of them.

MEASURED 2026-07-27 at d4b0aa2. Method: each script's failure emitter was
EVALUATED (not read) in a controlled shell with its streams captured to
separate files, so the token and the stream are observations, not inferences.
Denominator: scripts/check.sh plus the 9 live `kind = "script"` artifacts in
registries/checker_index.toml -- 10 gates a pane runs and reads directly.

  gate                                 failure token emitted     ^FAIL?  stream
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  check.sh (before fgdb-...-vbhd)      "RED core: <label>"         no    stderr
  check.sh (after)                     "RED ..." + "FAIL ..."     YES    stdout
  g0_claims_e2e.sh                     "[g0-claims-e2e] FAIL: "    no    stdout
  g0_identity_e2e.sh                   "[g0-identity-e2e] FAIL: "  no    stdout
  g0_spine_e2e.sh                      "[g0-spine-e2e] FAIL: "     no    stdout
  g0_negative_evidence_e2e.sh          "    FAIL  " (4-sp indent)  no    stderr
  g0_proof_lanes_e2e.sh                "    FAIL  " (4-sp indent)  no    stderr
  g0_architecture_decisions_e2e.sh     "ERROR: ..."                no    stderr
  g0_threat_e2e.sh                     "ERROR: ..."                no    stderr
  g0_topology_e2e.sh                   "ERROR: ..."                no    stderr
  w1_cross_crate_determinism_e2e.sh    "ERROR: ..."                no    stderr

THE TWO NUMBERS.

  `grep '^FAIL' <log>` returns 0 on a red run of 10 of 10 gates before vbhd,
  and 9 of 10 after. It has NEVER worked anywhere in this repo. The habit is
  not a misreading of check.sh -- three gates do say FAIL, and none of them
  says it at column 0, so the habit was taught by a token that was always
  prefixed.

  7 of 10 write the failure to stderr only. `gate.sh > log` then grepping log
  yields a complete-looking all-green transcript of a red run for those seven.

Three tokens (RED / FAIL / ERROR), two indentation conventions (column 0 /
4-space), two streams. No consumer can be right about all of them at once.

WHAT IS NOT BROKEN, and it matters for ranking. The EXIT CODE is authoritative
on all 10: each gate either forces `exit 1` from a `[ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ] || exit 1`
tally or runs under `set -e` with an explicit `exit` on every error path.
check.sh consumes the 9 registered scripts by exit code with the streams merged
(`if "$@" >"$log" 2>&1`), so check.sh's own aggregation is SOUND and was never
under-reporting. This defect is entirely in the human/agent reading path -- and
that path is the one AGENTS.md tells every pane to use.

SCOPE NOTE / WHY THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED IN THE SAME COMMIT.
vbhd fixed check.sh only. Uniforming the other nine touches g0_identity_e2e.sh,
which is inside the `catalog` write token's scope, and each of the nine has its
own self-test that greps its own output shape (g0_negative_evidence_e2e.sh and
g0_proof_lanes_e2e.sh both assert on the indented form). That is a bead with a
token and a gate run, not a drive-by.

PROPOSED FIX, same shape as the one vbhd landed and for the same reason:
  1. One shared emitter in scripts/lib/, so there is ONE reader to drift rather
     than ten. scripts/lib/private_subject.sh is the precedent.
  2. Every per-assertion verdict ANCHORED at column 0 and on STDOUT; stderr
     keeps the diagnostics only. This is the project's own robot-mode contract
     (AGENTS.md: "stdout is data-only, stderr diagnostics") applied to gates.
  3. Both tokens on a failure -- a `RED` line and a `FAIL` line -- so neither
     existing habit returns a silent zero.
  4. Per script, a control that captures the two streams SEPARATELY. Every
     existing self-test merges them with `2>&1`, which is why all of them
     passed over this for months: a merged log cannot see a stream defect.
     In vbhd four independent mutations were each required to produce a
     distinct named failure before the control was believed.

Filed by pane2, 2026-07-27. Nothing deleted.
close_reason: Fixed and landed at e5ee59f. One shared verdict contract in scripts/lib/gate_verdict.sh, sourced by all ten gates: ONE STREAM (verdicts on stdout, stderr is diagnostics), ONE TOKEN (anchored ^FAIL at column 0 for every failure; RED/UNRUN are refinements emitted BESIDE it, never instead), THREE STATES (ran-and-passed / ran-and-failed / DID NOT RUN — only the first is green; gate_verdict and the EXIT trap both refuse green over zero executed assertions), ONE EXIT DISCIPLINE (0 iff zero FAIL and zero UNRUN, and the exit code stays authoritative). Attribution: 1 of 10 already conformant (check.sh, vbhd), 9 of 10 made conformant. Denominator 10 gates / 3 tokens / 2 indentations / 2 streams. The class fix is the verdict-contract closure CORE GATE in check.sh: it enumerates the gate set from checker_index.toml at run time so a gate registered next month is in scope immediately, and it fails closed on an unreadable registry, a list shorter than 2, or an unreadable gate. Eleven mutations across the guard laws and the three states, each applied alone on a path-correct mirror, each producing a distinct named failure; one assertion (L1b gate_init) was found UNCONTROLLED by the matrix and its fixture added; the gate_unrun control found a real bug in the trap I had just written. Behavioural proof: a rogue planted in a REAL registered gate is named and reds 1-of-10 while a byte-identical clean copy reports 10/10. Two full check.sh runs; all reds attributed to other panes (UBS scan size, fgdb-fug5, and identity's write-through guard firing on two commits landed mid-run).

title: Identity fixtures stale at durable-fields epoch 69: 12 deterministic failures

    idr_assignment_history_and_epoch_are_frozen
  11 ordinary-union fixture consumers:

    idr_ordinary_union_arm_bound_must_fit_union_bound
    idr_ordinary_union_embedded_field_requires_exact_anchor
    idr_ordinary_union_rejects_duplicate_arm_tag
    idr_ordinary_union_rejects_invalid_inline_record_hash
    idr_ordinary_union_rejects_reference_union_name_collision
    idr_ordinary_union_rejects_unresolved_containing_schema

Every consumer therefore gets an extra registry_epoch_mismatch; the nominal positive also gets assignment drift.
  - the historical witness reconstructs durable-fields pin fnv1a64:987b7a7f7824d2ba, while A10_COMMAND_REF_ERRATUM_PREVIOUS_FIELDS_PIN is fnv1a64:236efa5babe190fe.

Controls and scope:

and the patch below is mechanical once it is accepted.

## THE ANSWER: 11 of the 12 were STALE FIXTURES. 1 was REALITY, correctly caught.

Not one or the other — the twelve split, and the split is what makes both fixes
correct. Establishing it took one experiment: hold `registries/durable_fields.toml`
at its shipped epoch and move ONLY the fixture's hardcoded literal back one step
(exactly the pre-8e5cd57 state). Snapshot a6077a0, lock-free rustc, no cargo:

No more and no fewer. So those eleven are a STALE FIXTURE — one retyped number,
reproducible on demand — and re-baselining them is correct because reality was
never wrong about them. They were never testing the epoch at all; the fixture
overwrites `identity.fields_epoch` with its own literal, so every consumer
inherited a `registry_epoch_mismatch` that had nothing to do with the union rule
each one exists to check.

The TWELFTH is the other kind and must not be re-baselined:

    idr_assignment_history_and_epoch_are_frozen

It is absent from the eleven above, so its cause is disjoint. It was REALITY
correctly caught: `KeyDestroyProposal.key_identity` landed as a new durable field
and the historical post-erratum REMOVAL COHORT was not extended, so the witness
reconstructed a different pre-erratum namespace. 8e5cd57 repaired it the right
way — extend the cohort (field delta 569 -> 570), PRESERVE the pre-erratum fnv
pin `fnv1a64:236efa5babe190fe`. Re-pinning the witness instead would have erased
the only signal that a field had landed unrecorded. That is the standing law:
extend the filter, never re-pin the witness.

## THE 12 ARE GREEN AT HEAD — and the repair is a treadmill, not a fix

Independent corroboration: 117 passed / 0 failed at b77982e AND at f95210f,
default parallel runner. pane6's close was right; my own earlier 12 and pane4's 12
were both measured on trees between the break (91d14c2) and the fix (8e5cd57).

proof that it is a treadmill arrived on its own WHILE I WAS MEASURING IT: pane6's
`bf9604c` had to bump the same literal **69 -> 70** the same night. Three hand
bumps of one number in one session.

Derive the epoch instead of retyping it. The fixture TOML becomes a const with an
`@EPOCH@` placeholder substituted from `real_identity().fields_epoch`; `@EPOCH@`
is not valid TOML, so a substitution that stops happening is a loud parse error
rather than a silent divergence. There is then no literal to get wrong and no
next bump.

    control (HEAD, literal)   117 passed; 0 failed
    mine    (derived)         117 passed; 0 failed

comment claims "the synthetic fixture union stays at index 0", and
`wire_backed_top_level_union_fixture` and the embedded-union fixtures all reach
for `ordinary_unions[0]` by index. Nothing checked it. Stitching the synthetic
union AFTER the real ones instead:

    against the patch      103 passed; 14 failed     <- the guard fires, naming it

So the patch adds `assert_eq!(identity.ordinary_unions[0].union_name,
"FixtureTopLevelUnion", ...)` after stitching.

## HANDOFF — the single next step

the index-0 hole = 4 vs 14.

IN FLIGHT: nothing running.

3316`). That is another pane's catalog work between commits, NOT this bead — it

title: Calibration outside-window refusals are unreachable
description: Measured at HEAD ae1ed98c07236911931603daf63f33c14a1fe96a. AnnRecallLedger::record and OpeLedger::record compare the supplied sequence with the exact next sequence before checking whether it exceeds the immutable window. Because every sequence above the window necessarily differs from the exact next in an incomplete ledger, both dedicated SequenceOutsideWindow error arms are unreachable and above-window input is misclassified as an ordinary gap. No test or live bead covers either arm. Add mutation-red laws for above-window input in both modules, give the domain violation precedence over in-window exact-next ordering, and preserve atomic refusal. Scope is the two existing fgdb-calibrate source files only.

MEASURED AT PINNED SHA e14563e BY pane3 (2026-07-27), rebuilt from the preserved
partition.rs. TOTAL PARTITION OF ALL 720 a05 FIELD CANDIDATES, plus a negative
result that matters more than the counts.

## Method note worth keeping

The probe kept failing against the live worktree because other panes were
mid-landing. Fix: build a SHA-PINNED snapshot — registries, .beads AND
tools/registry-check/src all extracted from ONE `git show <sha>:` — then compile
with CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR pointing at it. Both halves must come from the same
commit: registries from HEAD with a lib built from the modified worktree reports
phantom pin drift, and the inverse reports it backwards. BASE violations = 0 on
that snapshot, so every number below is against a clean base.

## The partition (total: 720)

  0  already landed                                          10
  1  no exact type in source                                392
  2  type conflict                                            4
  3  ambiguous                                               45
  4  owner not a census schema                                8
  6  exact type + bodied owner                              261
  ---------------------------------------------------------------
  bucket 5 (owner is definition-without-structural-body)       0
     <- the "owes nothing" shape does NOT occur among a05 field owners

  refinement of bucket 6:
     6a owner is a WIRE type (field_unresolved_schema)       133
     6b owner not a registered field host                     17
     6d exact type not a registered wire type                 33
     6e REFERENCE (needs target + construction DAG)           71
     6f NON-REFERENCE                                          7

Against the bead's own figures: 10 landed CONFIRMED, 392 no-exact-type CONFIRMED,
4 type-conflict CONFIRMED. Three differ — ambiguous is 45 not 26; the wire-owner
bucket is 133 not "~90"; and the reference-shaped population is 71, of which the
lost tranche's 37 were the subset that also had a resolvable target and satisfied
the DAG.

## The 7 non-reference candidates split 5 / 2, and the split is load-bearing

  FLAT record-typed (l6xd's actual shape — its close reason says "six FLAT inline
  fields plus four exact arm-payload contracts"):
    LegacyRetentionAuthorityTransferPlan.consumer_domain      : ConsensusDomain      (record)
    LegacyRetentionAuthorityTransferPlan.target_identity      : RemoteObjectIdentity (record)
    LocalToGlobalProjection.source_local_basis                : WeakStateIdentity    (record)
    LocalToShardProjection.source_local_basis                 : WeakStateIdentity    (record)
    ShardingFreezeRecord.source_basis_identity                : WeakStateIdentity    (record)

  UNION-typed, NOT flat, so l6xd does not reach them:
    GlobalControlRecord.origin                                : GlobalControlOrigin       (union)
    RetentionAuthorityTransferAdoptionSpec.transfer_evidence_ref : LegacyTransferEvidenceRef (union)

"every non-reference field takes inline" is too coarse by exactly these two. The
inline-union shape is its own case and is not settled by l6xd.

## THE NEGATIVE RESULT: validate_identity CANNOT DECIDE identity_class HERE

Synthesized the five flat rows and asked the checker. Then ran the vacuity
control — the SAME five rows with identity_class set to "logical", "scalar" and
"physical" instead of "inline".

  inline    -> 11 new violations
  logical   -> 11 new violations, IDENTICAL code set
  scalar    -> 11 new violations, IDENTICAL code set
  physical  -> 11 new violations, IDENTICAL code set

Only the recomputed assignment hash differs. **THE CONTROL DID NOT FIRE.**
`validate_identity` does not discriminate identity_class for a non-reference
field: all four values are equally accepted. So "ask the checker, not the corpus"
returns NO ANSWER for this question — which is precisely why l6xd had to be an
owner ruling, and it means landing these five as `inline` rests entirely on that
ruling with nothing enforcing it afterwards.

THAT IS THE SAME SHAPE CLOSED THREE TIMES TONIGHT (a7c8's unpinned split, 5qcg's
inert exclusions, d9pd's unenforced SC2015): a rule exists, and no checker holds
it. A wrong identity_class on a non-reference field is accepted silently and is
durable-format data. The l6xd ruling should become a CHECKER LAW —
"a field whose exact_wire_type resolves to a non-reference_wrapper wire type and
whose reference_semantics is none must have identity_class = inline" — with the
usual completeness guard so an unclassified wire kind fails closed rather than
escaping. I have NOT authored it: it is a new law over durable-format data and
belongs in its own bead beside the ruling, not smuggled into a field tranche.

## Two real defects in my synthesized rows, useful to whoever lands them

Independent of the class question, the checker DID reject two things, so the
eventual rows must fix both:
  * `cardinality = "required"` -> `bad_field ... "bad cardinality"`. The
    cardinality vocabulary is not what I guessed; read it off landed rows.
  * `construction_order = 0` -> `field_construction_order_mismatch:
    "construction_order 0 != containing kind ... order 29"`. A field's
    construction_order must EQUAL its containing kind's order, not be zero and not
    be derived from the target.
Both are mechanical and neither depends on any ruling.

## Status

Nothing landed. The five flat rows are landable in principle and blocked on
nothing but the two mechanical fixes above — but I am not landing durable-format
rows whose one semantically load-bearing column no checker can verify, in the
same turn that I discovered no checker can verify it. That ordering is the whole
lesson of tonight.

title: Extend the generated-history differential to branches, transactions, and DPOR schedules
notes:
FOLLOW-UP TO fgdb-z5y0, which landed the generator in 8c53adb. This bead is the REMAINDER, named
precisely so nobody has to diff the bead against the code to find out what is missing.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS (crates/fgdb-sim/tests/generated_histories.rs) -- build on it, do not restart:
 - an INTENT-LEVEL generator maintaining live model state, so every emitted history is reachable;
 - SplitMix64 seeding, with a law that a seed reproduces its history exactly;
 - a greedy shrinker that preserves the failure KIND, not merely "some error";
 - failure reports printed as a pasteable #[test];
 - asserted coverage counters, so a distribution that goes tame fails instead of passing;
 - the shared harness in tests/common/mod.rs driving the REAL BlockWriter and the oracle from one
   history.
It is proven to have power: the fgdb-0trr defect, reintroduced deliberately by re-keying
merge_neighbours on destination, was caught at seed 4.

WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER, and each is a separate axis rather than "more of the same":

1. BRANCHES. The generator drives ONE BranchId. fgdb-reference has fork_branch_at, branch lineage,
   and conflict_keys_since walking ancestors with a per-ancestor cap; none of it is generated
   against. This is the highest-value gap: branch fork/merge is B1's headline claim, its cost is
   per-ancestor, and fgdb-1xqd (the genesis-vs-fork race) is exactly the kind of defect a
   branch-aware generator finds and a single-branch one cannot. Generating a FOREST of branches with
   forks at varying depths is the shape to aim for.

2. TRANSACTIONS. Nothing generates Transaction begin/commit/abort, so the SSI machinery
   (fgdb-reference::ssi, dangerous structures, rw-antidependencies) has no generated subject. My
   bead's stated bias list included "transactions that abort after writing" and that shape is not
   reachable from the current Step vocabulary at all -- it needs a second, transaction-level
   generator layered above this one, not a new Step arm.

3. DPOR. asupersync ships deterministic partial-order reduction; generated histories explored under
   scheduled interleavings turn concurrency bugs into seeds. BLOCKED ON the lab VFS work
   (fgdb-1xtp) -- deliberately not blocked on 1 and 2, which are single-threaded and available now.

4. PROPERTIES AND TEMPORAL SELECTORS. The generator sets one property at birth and never updates
   one; valid_time is always None. Both are in the oracle's semantics and neither is generated.

A NOTE ON WHY THE SHRINKER MATTERS MORE AS THIS GROWS. At 24 steps a failure is almost readable
without shrinking. At branch-and-transaction scale it will not be, and the shrinker will be doing the
work that decides whether anyone can act on a failure. Extend its removal moves along with the
vocabulary -- dropping a whole branch, dropping a transaction, and lowering fork depth are all
shrink moves that do not exist yet, and a shrinker that cannot remove the new dimensions will
produce counterexamples that are minimal only in the dimension it happens to know about.

DO NOT let this bead become "add more Step arms". Each numbered item above changes what the
generator is generating, not how much.

notes:

(landing lease held by check.sh-1752222, 17m in). CalmSwan, 2026-08-04.

spine CODE landed at 42b4b0d and Database::create/write/open/neighbours exist. The end-to-end
half is therefore startable even though the bead edge is not retired. Child bead carries it;
the edge stays because it is true for whatever else j0vu owes.

FILE: crates/fgdb/tests/hostile_shapes.rs (reserved before writing; the surface was free —
GentleCat's crates/fgdb/** lease had lapsed). complexity_witness.rs was NOT touched: it is
released to ChartreuseSalmon for by2l.

THE FIRST END-TO-END §17 NUMBER IN THE PROJECT, and it is a bad one, published deliberately:
  298 BYTES PER LIVE EDGE (37,920 bytes for 127 live edges)
measured on a real directory, after a real Database::create + write + drop + open. §17's
sealed-run target is an effective >=4 B/edge, so this shape sits about 75x above it. Nothing is
sealed, nothing is compressed, and the directory carries a manifest and a root beside the
blocks. fgdb-by2l is the slice that should move it.

LAW 1 IS WHY THE FILE EXISTS. §17's first standing law is no-benchmark-only-semantics, and
doctrine 7 forbids reporting a non-durable mode as a result. Every number here comes off the
ordinary durable path with a cold reopen in the middle. This is the first place in the project
where that distinction could actually have been got wrong.

BYTES NOT SECONDS, same argument as the op counts: a wall clock is nondeterministic (B5 forbids
it as a result) and load-sensitive on a box where a dozen panes compile. Bytes on disk after a
fixed history are exact and diffable, and law 4 asks for bytes per live edge INCLUDING what the
payload does not cover — which a directory walk gives and an in-memory estimate does not.

I TIGHTENED MY OWN CEILING AFTER MEASURING. First draft asserted <=4096 B/edge, chosen before
measuring. The engine does 298, so that ceiling was 13x reality and would have sat green through
a TENFOLD regression. Now 512, just under 2x measured. A ceiling loose enough never to fire is a
comment drawing a test's salary. Also added a control (the_byte_measurement_responds_to_history_
size): a 64-edge history must cost more bytes than a 4-edge one, or the instrument is reading a
fixed-size manifest and reporting a stable meaningless number.

SHAPE COVERAGE, stated in the file because 3-of-5 silently reads exactly like 5-of-5:
  COVERED: power-law degree skew; cold partition reopen (every witness reads after drop+open).
  NOT REACHABLE, with reasons: long version chains (WriteBatch exposes create_vertex/add_edge
    only — no retirement, so a second version of one edge cannot be expressed end-to-end; the
    shape IS witnessed one layer down in fgdb-drwe); deep branch chains (no branch API on the
    spine — the branch-parent walk this shape exists to expose does not exist to call);
    compaction under load (compact is tier-D-internal, no spine trigger; fgdb-drwe measures the
    cost compaction REMOVES, the foreground-latency-during half remains owed by p95p).

(3 hostile-shape + 11 spine + others); ubs rc=0, 0 critical.

comments.text:
bd49860 LANDED (CalmSwan, 2026-08-04): §17 recovery gate as a SCALING measurement.

MEASURED (batches -> reopen, per batch, first query):
   1    5.30 ms   5.30 ms/batch    5.6 us
   4   18.12 ms   4.53 ms/batch    9.2 us
  16   65.65 ms   4.10 ms/batch   23.4 us
  64  271.20 ms   4.24 ms/batch   89.9 us

RECOVERY IS LINEAR IN THE CAPSULE TAIL. Per-batch cost flat at ~4.1-5.3 ms across a 64x
range => reopen is O(commits). NOT superlinear (the shape assertion passes, correctly), but
linear is already fatal at the scale §17 states the gate: "@1 TB, <1 s to first query". At
~4.2 ms/commit a one-second budget buys ~238 COMMITS. A 1 TB database has incomparably more
history. The gate is missed by whatever ratio real commit count bears to 238 -- no
constant-factor optimisation closes that. Anchor mapping and checkpointing, which §17's own
parenthetical names, are the mechanisms that make recovery sublinear; neither exists yet.

THE EXPERIMENT IS THE SWEEP VARIABLE. Recovery is capsule TAIL replay, so tail length is the
independent variable -- I swept BATCH COUNT, not edge count. Edges inside one batch grow the
graph without lengthening what recovery walks, and would have produced a flat, reassuring,
WRONG curve. Anyone re-deriving this must keep that distinction.

Reopen and first-query timed SEPARATELY: an open that defers work to the first read has not
recovered, it has postponed, and §17 gates time to FIRST QUERY. First query grows 5.6 -> 89.9
us, roughly linear in commit count -- consistent with the tier-D witnesses (more commits, more
blocks, read path examines all of them).

SECONDARY, NOT PROMOTED: the 85 commits take ~163 ms each, almost certainly fsync-dominated.
Says nothing directly about §17's >=2M edge-inserts/s (a per-EDGE rate a batched write would
amortise). Labelled not-the-ingest-gate so it is not quoted as one.

CROSS-LAYER PICTURE now assembled from three independent instruments, all agreeing that fixed
per-operation cost dominates and per-edge work does not:
  - tier-D op counts (fgdb-drwe): examined-entry count FLAT across a 64x answer-size spread.
  - end-to-end latency (f2ede2e): 64x degree -> 1.5x p50.
  - recovery (this): O(commits), per-commit cost flat.
CONSEQUENCE FOR fgdb-by2l: that slice targets per-EDGE encoding. Three instruments say the
time is not there. Worth re-scoping before it lands, or it will move a number nobody feels.

UBS: 2 CRITICALs on this file, Instant::now() flagged as token-generation randomness. Both
false positives (keys() is fixed fixture bytes; nothing derives from the clock). Reviewed,
REJECTED, and the reasoning written into the module doc rather than suppressed -- satisfying
the scanner would mean obscuring the timing calls that are the point of the file.

rc=0 (3 tests). Lease checked free before committing; re-verified against 79b4499.
