title: Implement fgdb-types/bigint/delta-types/claim/evidence/resource foundation crates
description:
## What & scope
Implement the value/type spine of the workspace: `fgdb-types` (core scalar values, identity newtypes, typed references), `fgdb-bigint` (canonical exact integers), `fgdb-delta-types` (the G0/W2 delta schema only), `fgdb-claim` (the claim-type constitution as a Rust type system), `fgdb-evidence` (evidence envelopes), and `fgdb-resource` (typed resource vectors/ceilings). These are pure-type crates: no I/O, no durable state, `forbid(unsafe_code)`, and they sit inside `fgdb-reference`'s dependency allowlist.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5 (determinism/evidence) begins with value semantics: if equality, hashing, ordering, and encoding are not provably coherent, byte-identical canonical results (constraint 4) are impossible. B1 (One Version Universe) needs typed references (`StrongRef<T>`, conditional refs, weak digests) as first-class values so the durable content graph can be checked as a DAG. B4 (Ripple) needs an exact integer domain: Z-set weights must live in the true integer additive group, not a bounded imitation. B6 needs resource types so agent workloads are admission-controlled by construction. The claim-type constitution (constraint 11) is the anti-benchmarketing weapon this market lacks: measured numbers can never quietly become correctness claims.

## Design — normative detail
`fgdb-types`: identity newtypes (`ObjectId` full 256-bit, `VId`/`EId`, `DatabaseSecurityNamespaceId`, epoch/sequence scalars), the typed reference family (`StrongRef<T>`, `Conditional*Ref<T>`, weak-digest target types — all of which must resolve to `logical_object_kinds.toml` rows), `BoundedBytes<N>`, and the canonical scalar value union governed by `CanonicalScalarProfile`: equality, hashing, total ordering, collation, coercion, and durable/result encoding for every value, with property tests enforcing `equal ⇒ same_hash`, comparator totality/transitivity, and encode/decode/order coherence. The `STRICT_PORTABLE` profile canonicalizes NaNs and signed zero; fixes decimal scale/rounding/overflow; stores timestamp instant plus zone/offset semantics and a content-addressed tzdb version; pins Unicode data/normalization/segmentation and each non-binary collation by ObjectId; fixes map-key order over canonical bytes; and rejects unavailable profile artifacts rather than consulting host locale/tzdb. (Executor-side numeric/reduction-tree rules are w5-determinism; the value types, orderings, and encodings live here.)

`fgdb-bigint`: in-house canonical signed-limb exact integers with a unique (canonical) representation so compare/hash/encode are coherent; checked arithmetic throughout; designed as the promotion target for Ripple's `ZWeight`, which uses checked `i128` as the fast representation and promotes before overflow; limb allocation/spill is resource-accounted so exhaustion aborts or lags a derived computation without publishing partial state.

`fgdb-delta-types` (G0/W2 delta schema ONLY — the differential machinery itself is w2-delta-batches): exact typed delta rows — create/delete/property/valid-time/counter/escrow/sketch/schema/constraint deltas; the sequence-neutral `LogicalDeltaTemplate` keyed by graph/branch/relation/schema/`IntentSemanticsOid`; and the rule that only a committed `MarkerRef` turns a template into an ordered `LogicalDeltaBatch`.

`fgdb-claim`: two closed vocabularies. Registry claim classes per constraint 11: `invariant | proof | bounded_model | statistical | slo | benchmark`, with the lattice law that a weaker claim class may inform policy but may not enforce or justify a stronger one, and the routing law (`invariants.toml` only exact safety/liveness; `evidence.toml` and `slo.toml` for the rest). Evidence-envelope `ClaimClass` per §15.0: `SafetyInvariant` (must hold on every execution; failure is a correctness defect), `FormalModelClaim` (theorem/model-check with abstraction, bounds, refinement status), `StatisticalClaim` (population, sampling/selection rule, alpha, power/effective sample size, assumptions), `ConfigurationModelClaim` (model version, fitted inputs, sensitivity, validity domain), `EmpiricalGate` (fixture, machine/profile, sample count, variance budget, comparison rule).

`fgdb-evidence`: envelope types binding a `ClaimClass` to an immutable evidence identity — calibration windows, selection policy, strata, propensity support, regime epochs, fallback, and failure behavior are immutable evidence identities. `fgdb-resource`: typed resource vectors/ceilings consumed later by permits, `FrameLimits`, and W10 admission.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12 (binding clause): "Canonical scalar equality, hashing, ordering, and encoding are coherent." The claim-type constitution itself: a weaker claim class never enforces a stronger one — this crate makes that a type error, not a review comment. Everything here is `invariant`-class scaffolding; no slo/benchmark rows originate in this bead.

## Interactions
Consumes g0-claim-registries (claim vocabulary), g0-identity-registries (reference/field classes), g0-command-contracts (delta-row field registry). Produces types consumed by literally every other bead; specifically: w1-generated-parsers (encoders over these types), w1-authz-policy (binding types), w2-delta-batches (delta machinery over `fgdb-delta-types`), w6-zset-circuits (`ZWeight` promotion into `fgdb-bigint`), w5-determinism (`CanonicalScalarProfile` execution rules), verif-reference (allowlisted import), verif-sextant (evidence envelopes).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Property suites: `equal ⇒ same_hash`, comparator totality/transitivity, encode/decode/order coherence for every scalar type under `STRICT_PORTABLE`; bigint ring laws (associativity/commutativity/distributivity), canonical-representation uniqueness (no two byte encodings of one value), checked-overflow behavior at `i128` promotion boundaries, and encode/compare coherence under randomized + adversarial limb patterns; delta-row golden vectors and exhaustive per-arm encode/decode round trips; claim-lattice negative tests (constructing an invariant from statistical evidence is a compile error or typed rejection); tzdb/collation-artifact-unavailable tests reject rather than fall back to host locale. Fuzz: scalar decode with malformed bytes under length-before-allocation bounds. Logging: property-test failures must emit the exact seed and canonical byte encodings of counterexamples. E2E: `foundation_types_e2e` — one lab-runtime script that constructs representative values of every canonical scalar type under `STRICT_PORTABLE`, round-trips encode/hash/order coherence, promotes a `ZWeight` across the `i128` boundary into `fgdb-bigint` and back, builds every delta-row arm into a `LogicalDeltaTemplate` and (with a synthetic committed `MarkerRef`) an ordered `LogicalDeltaBatch`, and constructs one evidence envelope per `ClaimClass`; outputs must be byte-identical across two seeds, and a scripted claim-lattice violation must produce the typed rejection. DETAILED LOGGING (required for post-implementation verification): in addition to counterexample seed/byte logging above, coherence suites log {scalar_type, profile_oid, value_digest, comparator outcome} per checked pair class, bigint tests log {limb_count, promotion boundary hit}, and tzdb/collation rejection paths log the missing artifact ObjectId, so every failure is reproducible from logs alone.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: serde-derived enums as durable formats (constraint 9 — encoders come from the registries, w1-generated-parsers); floating-point or saturating Z-weights (breaks the integer-group semantics B4 requires); host locale/tzdb consultation (destroys cross-machine determinism); a single flat "claim" type without the lattice (would let benchmark numbers justify invariants). Risk: canonical scalar profile churn after G1 would invalidate golden vectors — mitigated by freezing the profile artifacts by ObjectId at G0.

## Provenance
§1 constraints 4, 9, 11; §8.6 (scalar profile); §9.1 (ZWeight); §18.1–18.2; App B (delta rows); §15.0.

## Fresh-eyes contract addition — narrowed Cx obligation vocabulary
The purpose-typed context surface is exact and load-bearing, not merely a naming convention. Subsystems receive only `QueryCx`, `TxnCx`, `CommitCx`, `MaintCx`, or `ReplCx` wrappers over asupersync `Cx`; the registered obligation vocabulary includes `pin_snapshot`, `reserve_prepared_bytes`, `reserve_raft_payload_space`, and `publish_segment`, plus the complete owner-specific set generated from command/resource registries. Compile-fail unit tests prove each wrapper cannot invoke another role's effects. Simulation/E2E tests cancel each obligation at acquisition, transfer, publication, and cleanup boundaries and assert zero leaks with ordered redacted lifecycle events. The merge evaluator's narrowed Cx has no clock, entropy, network, or filesystem capability, and a compile-fail surface proves that negative capability set.

THE SIX PROPERTIES, chosen to be gaps rather than duplicates. I read the existing 20 tests first: commutativity, associativity, DISTRIBUTIVITY, negation, the i64 oracle for add/sub/mul and ordering, randomized q*d+r=n, ordering totality/transitivity and limb budgets are ALREADY covered, so none of those are repeated.

This is the crate's durable-shape identity: that pair is the only canonical external rendering, so a consumer persisting the limbs would read back a different number if it failed. This is the one I would want re-run first if the limb representation ever changes.
 2. comparison_is_translation_invariant_under_addition — a.cmp(b) == (a+c).cmp(b+c). Note I deliberately stated it for ANY addend rather than "addition of a positive" as briefed: addition here is over signed integers, so translation invariance is total and the documented boundary is the limb budget, not the addend's sign. Pinning the weaker positive-only form would have under-tested it.
 3. subtraction_inverts_addition_on_random_values — (a+b)-b == a and (a+b)-a == b.
 4. division_inverts_multiplication_with_zero_remainder — (a*b)/b == a with r == 0 exactly. This is the direction the existing randomized test does NOT pin: q*d+r=n is satisfied by a truncating bug, whereas exact-inverse-with-zero-remainder is not.
 5. identity_and_absorbing_elements_are_ordinary_inputs — v+0, v*1, v*0, v-v, v/1 and --v over zero, 1, -1, u64::MAX, u128::MAX, i128::MIN and i128::MAX, using the same operators and the same budget as any random value rather than special-casing the edges.

SCOPE ANNOUNCEMENT #2, cc_1/pane2 -> cod_3 as crate owner: crates/fgdb-delta-types, TEST-ONLY. Announced BEFORE writing this time. Nothing written yet; this is the plan and a correction to the brief I was given.

THE BRIEF DOES NOT FIT THE CRATE, and I would rather say so than write tests against a surface that does not exist. I was asked to pin: a delta composed with its inverse is the identity; composition associative; the empty delta a two-sided identity; application order-independent; encode-decode round-trips. Measured against the actual code:
  * There is NO composition operator anywhere in the crate — `rg 'fn (compose|apply|invert|inverse|merge|concat)'` over crates/fgdb-delta-types/src returns nothing.
  * There is no `apply`, so "application order-independent" has no subject.
  * There is no encode/decode surface, so there is no encode-decode round trip to pin.
delta-types is two layers, neither of which is a composition algebra: lib.rs (559 lines, 3 tests) is the TYPE layer — DeltaRow's nine families, DeltaTemplateKey, LogicalDeltaTemplate, CommittedMarker, LogicalDeltaBatch; zweight.rs (675 lines, 11 tests) is the multiplicity arithmetic. Composition presumably lives in the unbuilt Ripple crate, not here.

AND THE HEADLINE CONCERN IS ALREADY PINNED. The brief's strongest point was that "a Z-set weight that silently saturates would corrupt an incremental view without ever failing a test". That exact hazard already has tests: `addition_promotes_before_overflow_and_demotes_after_cancellation` and `subtraction_promotes_below_min_and_demotes_back_to_min`. ZWeight is a two-variant Repr — Fast(i128) and Promoted(BigInt) — and the existing suite pins promotion BEFORE overflow rather than saturation, plus demotion on the way back. Also already covered: `additive_group_laws_hold_across_storage_boundaries` (inverse, identity and associativity ACROSS the Fast/Promoted boundary, which is the real version of "delta composed with its inverse is the identity" for this crate), `multiplication_is_commutative_and_distributes_over_addition`, `equality_order_and_hash_are_numeric_not_variant_based`, `importing_bigints_always_demotes_when_possible`, `limb_limits_fail_with_exact_operation_and_requirement`, and `every_arm_maps_into_the_nine_families` in lib.rs. So this crate is ALREADY well property-tested, and I am not going to restate its existing laws with new names to look productive.

THE RESIDUAL GAPS I INTEND TO PIN, four, all genuine and all narrow:
 1. CROSS-PATH AGREEMENT: `checked_mul_i128(f)` must equal `checked_mul(&ZWeight::from_i128(f))` for the same inputs and budget, including across the promotion boundary and for f = 0, 1, -1, i128::MIN, i128::MAX. Two independent code paths computing the same product is precisely the divergence shape that 8487dcd was — a second path that forgot the caller's constraint — and the existing multiplication tests exercise only `checked_mul`.
 2. CANONICALITY IS PRESERVED BY EVERY OPERATION, not only by construction. The existing test pins `is_canonical()` on constructed values; I will assert it on the RESULT of add, sub, neg, mul and mul_i128 over randomized boundary-crossing operands. A non-canonical intermediate that compares equal today would break Hash/Eq consistency later.
 3. OBSERVER AGREEMENT: `is_promoted()`, `to_i128().is_none()` and `magnitude_limb_count()` must tell one consistent story about the same value. Three observers of one representation that can disagree is a latent bug surface, and nothing currently ties them together.
 4. PROMOTION ROUND TRIP: a value pushed over the i128 boundary and brought back by the inverse operation must equal the original AND be demoted again, i.e. representation is a function of VALUE not of history. `equality_order_and_hash_are_numeric_not_variant_based` pins that equality ignores the variant; this pins that the variant itself returns.

DISCIPLINES I AM HOLDING TO, from the bigint round: TEST-ONLY, verified with `git diff -U0` rather than by eye; standalone rustc --test harness for the fast loop; no trait impl added and no visibility relaxed to make a test compile. You predicted delta-types has a BigInt-no-Clone equivalent and it does — `CommittedMarker`'s field is private and `attest` requires a `&CommitCx`, so a bare `MarkerRef` cannot be promoted into a batch, and there are already compile_fail doctests pinning both halves. I will not weaken that; if a test needs a CommittedMarker it goes through the lab-runtime CommitCx the existing tests use.
Any source-level defect goes to you as owner rather than being fixed here. I will report back whether each property passed first try or found something.

Existing context.rs coverage was 8 tests, each walking ONE hand-picked path with ONE hand-picked id. The new tests quantify over the whole acquisition surface: all 9 acquisition methods across the 5 obligation-bearing roles (merge_eval acquires nothing), and all 5 terminal depths the affine chain admits.

=== MUTATION AUDIT — THE PART THAT MAKES IT WORTH LANDING ===
A passing test proves nothing on its own, so each law was audited against a mutation designed so the PRE-EXISTING 8 tests stay green. That measures what the increment ADDS rather than what it restates.
  M1 stage not recorded for PublishSegment only ....... old 0 failed / NEW 1 (L1)
  M2 generations start at 2 instead of 1 .............. old 0 failed / NEW 1 (L2)
  M3 QueryCx role view reports 0 ...................... old 0 failed / NEW 1 (L3)
  M4 free-form "acme_corp/graph_7" leaks into evidence  old 0 failed / NEW 1 (L4)
  M5 raft reservation drops requested units to 1 ...... old 0 failed / NEW 1 (L5)
5 of 5 caught, each by exactly its intended law, none by the pre-existing suite. Harness controlled in both directions: the null mutation reports 0 failures, and an absent pattern reports MUTATION-DID-NOT-APPLY rather than silently mutating nothing (the 'guard that matched nothing' shape).

=== TWO THINGS THE AUDIT CHANGED IN THE TESTS THEMSELVES ===
1. L2 originally asserted gens[0] == FIRST_OBLIGATION_GENERATION. That is method-note trap #4 — a witness derived from the same constant the law tests. Under M2 the expectation would have moved WITH the mutation and the law would never have fired. The literal 1 is now written out, with the constant checked against it separately. I found this while designing the mutation, not while writing the test: designing the falsification is what exposed the tautology.
2. L4 began as a forbidden-substring scan extending the existing test's ["path","tenant","payload","description"]. It failed immediately on a TRUE NEGATIVE: the legitimate kind name ReserveRaftPayloadSpace contains "payload", and the legitimate stage Publication contains "public". A blacklist cannot express this property. It is now a WHITELIST over identifier tokens — every identifier in the rendered evidence must belong to the closed vocabulary of record names, field names and enum variants; digits are free. That is both correct and strictly stronger: M4 leaks a string containing none of the four blacklisted words and the old approach cannot see it, while any newly added free-form field trips the whitelist automatically. Worth noting for the owner: the pre-existing complete_lifecycle_is_ordered_and_redacted has this blacklist weakness, and it passes today only because it exercises ReservePreparedBytes rather than the raft kind.

Fast loop: standalone `rustc --test` on a #[path] harness against the module, linked to the REAL prebuilt libasupersync rlib (not a stub) — 1.2s compile, 13/13 green, whole cycle ~1.3s versus 15-45 min for cargo test. title: Generate durable encoders/decoders, field tables, digest recipes, and walkers
description:
## What & scope
Build the code-generation pipeline that turns G0's frozen registries — the five identity-class registries `logical_object_kinds.toml`, `physical_record_kinds.toml`, `bootstrap_frames.toml`, `prebootstrap_artifact_kinds.toml`, and `wire_types.toml`, plus the cross-index and contract registries `durable_fields.toml`, `command_contracts.toml`, `command_type_classification.toml`, and `durable_state_slots.toml` with its backing plane registries (`state_payload_fields.toml`, `protocol_state_fields.toml`, `prepared_state_fields.toml`, `consensus_state_fields.toml`), and the registered BodyDigest/transcript recipes — into canonical Rust encoders/decoders, field tables, and digest-recipe implementations. Every durable schema in the system gets its serialization from this pipeline; no hand-written durable encoder exists outside it. (The generated golden vectors, mutation corpora, cross-version fixtures, and fuzz targets are split into w1-format-test-corpora.)

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Constraint 9 bans serde-derived enums as durable formats; constraint 6 makes published bytes constitutional. The only way to keep hundreds of durable schemas honest across a decade is to make the registry the single source of truth and generate everything — encoder, decoder, checker, test — from the same rows, so a schema cannot drift from its registration and FG-INV-07/FG-INV-09 checkers are generated rather than hand-maintained. This is B5's evidence discipline applied to bytes; B1 depends on it (content addressing is only sound if canonical encoding is unique and reproducible); B6 rides it (robot-readable schemas/docs are generated from the same registries per G4).

## Design — normative detail
Registry law (restated): each registry has its own 16-bit code space with `0x0000` and `0xffff` permanently invalid, `0x0001..=0x7fff` permanent core assignments, `0x8000..=0xbfff` negotiated extension assignments, and `0xc000..=0xfffe` test/experimental assignments that production readers reject. A released code changes status to `Retired` but is never reassigned; removed experimental bytes remain reserved in the golden corpus. `registry_epoch` changes only when rows are added or retired, not when prose moves. Every class requires the appropriate canonical encoder/decoder, construction-order annotation, version/feature/posture compatibility rule, size/resource limits, and fuzz/golden corpus; a missing, duplicated, cross-class, untyped-field, or orphan row is a build failure. G0 enforces four separate bijections (logical schema↔logical-object row, physical record↔physical identity row, bootstrap frame↔bootstrap row, embedded durable type/tag↔wire-type row) plus disjointness across all five identity classes and code-range/nonreuse rules — the generator consumes those validated registries and re-verifies them. The fifth identity class, `prebootstrap_artifact_kinds.toml` (restore artifacts that necessarily predate target `K_oid`), has its own identity law — `PreBootstrapArtifactId = BLAKE3("fgdb:restore-prebootstrap:v1" ‖ target_claim_or_reservation_domain ‖ artifact_kind ‖ schema_version ‖ canonical_wrapper_bytes)` — whose IDs are never `ObjectId` and never accepted by `StrongRef`; its wrapper encoders/decoders and canonical-import record generation belong to this pipeline like every other class. `durable_state_slots.toml` is the total cross-plane registry whose rows each point to exactly one backing field registry (`state_payload_fields.toml` for canonical semantic payloads; `protocol_state_fields.toml` for the protocol plane; `prepared_state_fields.toml`/`consensus_state_fields.toml` for prepared ownership and Raft hard/snapshot/configuration state), and every required checkpoint/snapshot/floor/backup/restore/GC/transition walker is generated from it; a feature with no slot, a slot with no writer, or an unclassified protocol mutation is a G0 failure.

Encoding baseline (App A, normative for all generated code): declared format major/minor; little-endian fixed integers; canonical unsigned LEB128 only where the field says varint; length-before-allocation; checked arithmetic; per-kind maximum sizes. Unknown additive-minor fields are length-delimited and skipped; unknown required flags fail closed. Readers authenticate/validate headers and resource bounds before allocating or decompressing.

Digest generation: stored digest fields are never defined by naming convention — every `durable_fields.toml` digest row declares exactly one semantic class: `TargetDigest` (of separately identified bytes), `TranscriptDigest` (with a registered transcript recipe), `WeakIdentityDigest`, or `BodyDigest`. A `BodyDigest<T>` row fixes `{domain_separator, schema_major, included_field_tags, excluded_field_tags}` with default recipe `BLAKE3(domain_separator || canonical(schema_major, T excluding exactly the one BodyDigest field))`; signatures/MACs are excluded only when the row explicitly lists their stable tags. Unknown exclusions, two body-digest fields, an implicit zero placeholder, or computing over bytes that include the digest itself are G0 errors. Encoder, decoder, field-table, golden-vector, mutation, and cross-version tests all use the same generated recipe.

DAG law enforced by generated encoders: the canonical content graph is a DAG — every strong, conditional, and weak-digest value in newly encoded bytes must already be known; a future applied result may be described only by a sequence-neutral spec, body recipe, or assigned scalar order, never by its not-yet-computable ObjectId/digest; self IDs, mutually strong cycles, and an input command that names its own applied result are invalid and unencodable.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-07 (binding clauses): "every field, typed reference, transcript digest, and weak identity is registry-resolved and names already identified bytes, and every pre-order input excludes its future command/result/root. `command_contracts.toml` is bijective with every role command arm/handler and `state_payload_fields.toml` roots every written state class." FG-INV-09 (binding clause): "Every stored digest is explicitly Target, Transcript, WeakIdentity, or BodyDigest with one generated include/exclude recipe" — with its enforcement column requiring the generated digest/field checker plus mutation, golden, cross-version, collision, and fuzz campaigns. All invariant-class; generation determinism itself is an invariant of the build.

## Interactions
Consumes: g0-identity-registries (the five identity-class registries + durable_fields + the durable_state_slots/plane field registries + BodyDigest recipes), g0-command-contracts (command/state field registries + bijection CI), g0-format-arms (frozen decision-batch rows: identity-column codec registrations, `PackedObjectGroup`, `externally_verifiable` markings, activation-batch specs — all of which must have rows before generation), w1-foundation-types (target types), w1-codecs (varint/framing primitives), w1-crypto (BLAKE3/keyed digest implementations behind the recipes). Produces generated encoders consumed by every durable-schema owner (all w2a/w2b/w2c beads, w3-tier-d/w3-tier-r, w9-audit-*, w10-fgp-core wire types, w11-*), by w1-format-test-corpora (test artifacts), and by verif-reference (generated registries under its allowlist).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Generation determinism: identical registry inputs produce byte-identical generated code (CI diff check). Round-trip: generated encode∘decode is identity on arbitrary valid values (property tests per kind). DAG enforcement: encoding a self-referential or forward-referencing value is a compile-time or typed construction error with a negative fixture. Digest recipes: generated BodyDigest implementations match hand-computed BLAKE3 transcripts on reference examples for every recipe class. Registry-law negatives: retired codes rejected; test/experimental-range (`0xc000..=0xfffe`) codes rejected by production-configured readers; unknown required flags fail closed; additive-minor unknown fields skipped (length-delimited). Bounds: no generated decoder allocates before validating declared sizes (length-before-allocation assertions). Bijection re-verification: generator fails on missing/duplicated/cross-class/orphan rows with diagnostics naming the row. Logging: generator emits a per-build manifest (registry epochs, row counts, output digests) for provenance. E2E: `codegen_pipeline_e2e` — run the generator on the frozen G0 registries from a clean tree, compile the generated crates, re-run and diff (byte-identical); then drive one encode -> digest -> decode -> field-table-walk cycle for a representative kind of each of the five identity classes, plus the negative path (retired code, test-range discriminant, unknown required flag) against a production-configured reader — wired as a single CI job. DETAILED LOGGING (required for post-implementation verification): beyond the per-build manifest above, codegen logs per kind {kind_id, identity class, encoder/decoder symbols, recipe_id}; decoders log rejections as {kind_id, offending field/tag, rejection class} and the negative tests assert those records; a generation-nondeterminism failure must log the first differing output file and byte offset.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: serde/derive-based durable encoding (constraint 9 — no transcript control); hand-written per-schema encoders (guaranteed drift at this schema count); digests defined by field-naming convention (a G0 error class); generated code depending on engine crates (generation stays in the foundation layer so `fgdb-reference` can consume it). Risk: generator bugs become correlated bugs across all formats — mitigated by the independent `fgdb-reference` decode path and the ground-truth hierarchy placing appendices + golden vectors above both implementations.

## Provenance
§5.1 (registry classes, code spaces, DAG law, digest classes); §19 G0/W1 rows; App A preamble; App F FG-INV-07/09.

title: Implement sealed RegionVec over the private allocator boundary and query-region lifecycle contract
description:
## Decision source

Implements the architecture selected by `fgdb-mz8u`. This is route 1, but narrower than a public allocator API: `core::alloc::Allocator` is admitted only on one sealed, private adapter inside `fgdb-unsafe-arena`. Every consumer sees only a safe typed container.

## Scope and public contract

Add a safe `RegionVec<T>`-class container whose actual element buffer is `Vec<T, PrivateRegionAllocator>`; a `Vec<T, Global>` shadow plus region accounting is forbidden. The private allocator type, its `Allocator` impl, `NonNull`, raw pointers, allocator handles, and the allocator-parameterized `Vec` type must be absent from every reachable public signature and re-export. Do not implement `Deref<Target = Vec<...>>` or expose an escape hatch that can call allocating `Vec` methods without the capability contract.

The allocation-capable safe methods (`try_reserve`, `try_push`, `try_insert`, fallible extend/resize/clone equivalents) accept `&QueryCx` or a purpose-typed allocation permit minted from it, checkpoint before mutation, reserve before mutating, and return structured refusal without partial success. Nonallocating slice/read/pop/truncate/clear/remove operations may omit the context. Do not add an allocating `Clone`, `FromIterator`, `Extend`, or equivalent trait path that lacks context. The sealed foreign-trait callbacks do no I/O, clock, entropy, network, blocking, or lock acquisition; they are synchronously reachable only beneath an already-admitted safe operation. The first slice is task-local and makes no concurrent-allocation claim.

## Ownership, drop, and reclamation

A non-clone region owner/scope outlives every `RegionVec` through the type system. Ordinary close and cancellation may reclaim typed backing storage only after all typed containers have dropped; no API may invalidate storage while a safe owner can still access it. If any dynamic-owner path is added, finalization must refuse with a typed `OwnersRemain` error and retain the storage. Generic `T`, recursive node shapes, and arbitrary collection `K`/`V` run normal Rust drop glue exactly once. Reallocation uses the standard `Vec<T, A>` move/drop contract rather than a local `RawVec` reimplementation.

Support zero-sized types explicitly and refuse unsupported layouts, including alignment above the arena bound, before mutation. Make chunk growth fallible. Close and cancellation each produce a non-vacuous audit with `bytes_reclaimed == bytes_allocated` and `blocks_released == blocks_allocated`; a leaked/live owner is fail-closed, never reported balanced.

## Product-boundary ruling

`fgdb-unsafe-arena::Region` is a W1 allocation kernel, not a second product query heap. At the workspace-pinned asupersync revision `e464a484cb65c1a55be0d9c925e6e9c20318edcb`, `RegionRecord`/`RegionHeap` owns admission, quiescence, finalizers, generational handles, and close-time reclamation, while its current typed storage is global `Box<dyn Any + Send + Sync>`. The FrankenGraphDB query-memory adapter must bind this kernel audit to the asupersync query-region close/cancel path after quiescence; it must not replace or race that lifecycle authority. `fgdb-w3-buffer-g2v` owns the product integration.

## Mechanical boundary checks

Refine `unsafe-ledger-check` with an exact allowance for the pinned `Allocator` trait impl only when all of these hold: the self type is the one registered private adapter; it is not public, re-exported, or reachable through a public field/signature; the trait path and unsafe method set exactly match the pinned toolchain contract; and each local unsafe site has its own ledger row and safety proof. Add public-signature coverage for `NonNull` and allocator-parameterized types. Mutants must turn the gate red when they publicize/re-export the adapter, expose `NonNull`, raw pointers, `Allocator`, or `Vec<_, Adapter>`, add an unrelated public unsafe function or unsafe trait impl, broaden the allowed self type/method set, or add an allocating safe method/trait path without the purpose context.

## Evidence and acceptance

- Differential tests compare all supported `RegionVec` operations and reallocations against ordinary `Vec` values/refusals across multiple fixed seeds.
- Drop-counter tests cover growth, replacement, normal drop, close, and cancellation; every initialized `T` drops exactly once.
- Recursive ART-like nodes with generic `V`, hash-like `K`/`V`, and succinct integer vectors use the actual region allocator type.
- Tests cover ZST, alignments through the supported bound, over-aligned refusal, capacity/size overflow, budget exhaustion with no partial mutation, stale/foreign region use, and finalization with a live owner.
- Close and cancel logs reconstruct allocation/reclamation equality under real typed reallocations.
- Miri runs the complete checked unsafe workload or the ledger records an honest exclusion; ASAN/TSAN status remains explicit.
- `bash scripts/check.sh` exits 0 after the registry, ledger, source, and tests land.
- No latency, throughput, ART, probe, or other consumer benchmark claim is attached.

title: Implement the canonical durable resource-ledger and accounting transition contract
description:
## What & scope
Implement the canonical durable resource-accounting contract: split ephemeral versus durable requests, fixed charge vectors, authority roles, quota paths/policies/owner keys, ledger state/basis/transition/spec/applied record, and exact Reserve/Charge/Release/Expire/Transfer/Adjust laws. Runtime QoS is a consumer, not the ledger definition.

## Why
Admission estimates and durable ownership are different. If a process-local budget is mistaken for a durable charge, restart can refund work; if a prepared/result/backup owner is expired or partially transferred, obligations leak or bytes are reclaimed early. One exact ledger makes accounting atomic with object ownership.

## Design — exact normative contract
**Resource accounting.** `ResourceRequest` is `{ephemeral:EphemeralResourceBudget,durable:DurableChargeVector}`. Ephemeral budget is `{cpu_ns,resident_bytes,temp_bytes,read_iops:WindowedRateBudget,write_iops:WindowedRateBudget,egress_bytes,output_bytes,output_rows,max_snapshot_age,maximum_subscription_backlog}` and is enforced by cancel-correct runtime obligations, never canonical state. Durable vector is the fixed versioned checked nonnegative `{canonical_durable_bytes,retained_history_bytes,branch_count,index_count,view_count,subscription_count}`. Replica/FEC/cache/placement bytes are operational capacity, not semantic tenant charges. Only `ResourceAccountingRole::Local|Meta` authors canonical durable quota; shards enforce ephemeral local capacity.

`QuotaPath` is a canonical nonempty root-to-leaf path of `Database|Tenant|Graph|Branch|Feature`. `ResourceLimitPolicy` fixes the path tree, per-bucket hard vectors, protected maintenance reserve, class rules, and `ResourceLimitPolicyEpoch`. Every transition updates the exact leaf and each unique ancestor once. `ResourceOwnerKey` is `Attempt{posture,registration_identity}|Statement{posture,registration_identity,statement_seq}|ResultDelivery{posture,result_delivery_id}|Subscription{cursor_id}|DurableObject{object_class,stable_logical_owner_key}|Replay{replay_manifest_key}|BackupPin{backup_id,scope}|PreparedClosure{prepared_ownership_id}|Maintenance{job_id,registered_class}` and never a future ObjectId.

`ResourceLedgerState` is `{format_version,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,role,ledger_generation,limit_policy_ref:StrongRef<ResourceLimitPolicy>,limit_policy_epoch,bucket_state_root,reservation_entry_root,charge_entry_root,applied_transition_index_root,body_digest}`. Each bucket is `{hard_limit,protected_maintenance_reserve,ordinary_reserved,maintenance_reserved,committed}`. All arithmetic is checked; ordinary use satisfies `committed+ordinary_reserved <= hard_limit-protected_reserve`, and registered maintenance consumes only its named reserve. The transition index maps a transition ID to immutable body digest and applied outcome, making exact retry idempotent and body drift invalid.

`ResourceLedgerBasis` is the nonretaining `{role,state_identity:WeakStateIdentity,ledger_generation,ledger_root_digest,limit_policy_oid,limit_policy_epoch}`. `ResourceLedgerTransition<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is the sequence-neutral pre-order object `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,transition_id,idempotency_key_digest,basis:ResourceLedgerBasis,owner:ResourceOwnerKey,resource_class,quota_path,operation,exact_sorted_before_buckets,exact_sorted_after_buckets,checked_arithmetic_commitment,authorization_decision_ref:StrongRef<AuthorizationDecisionRecord<Role>>,release_or_measurement_evidence_ref?,body_digest}`. `operation` is exactly `Reserve{reservation_id,reservation_generation:0,vector,expiry:None|ProfiledDeadline}|Charge{reservation_id,expected_reservation_generation,charge_id,vector,release_unused_reservation:true,stable_subject_key}|Release{subject:Reservation|Charge,expected_generation,exact_vector,release_authority_ref}|Expire{reservation_id,expected_generation,exact_vector,owner_quiescence_proof_ref,time_validation_evidence_ref:StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>}|Transfer{subject:Reservation|Charge,expected_generation,source_owner,source_path,target_owner,target_path,exact_conserved_vector,transfer_authority_ref}|Adjust{charge_id,expected_generation,before_vector,after_vector,stable_subject_key,measurement_or_logical_change_proof_ref}`. The header, basis role, owner, decision, and containing command must byte-match. Expire evidence must be `Expired` for the exact subject/action.

Reserve creates one active reservation. Charge consumes it completely, creates one charge, and releases the deterministic unused remainder. Release/Expire/Transfer operate on a whole entry; partial changes use Adjust. Transfer conserves the vector globally and checks destination ancestors after netting shared ancestors. No timeout, disconnect, process death, logical delete, or stale cache releases an entry, and expiry fails while prepared ownership, final certification, result delivery, backup, or remote grants retain the subject. `ResourceLedgerTransitionSpec {expected_basis,sorted_transition_refs,complete_transition_id_set_commitment,semantic_subject_basis,terminal_audit_gate}` is the standalone-control wrapper; transactions and exact lifecycle specs embed transition refs directly. A generated enclosing-command matrix fixes legal operation tags.

Apply verifies one common basis, IDs, exact before buckets, canonical net deltas, policy/authorization/evidence and constructs the new state, then `ResourceLedgerAppliedRecord {command_ref,assigned_role_logical_position,transition_refs,before_root_ref,after_root_ref}`, then payload/command record. Pre-order transitions never name the applied record or after payload. `ResourceChargeEffect` is exactly `{transition_ref:StrongRef<ResourceLedgerTransition>,stable_subject_key,before_vector,after_vector}` and the effect set requires a generated bijection with transaction-owned transition refs. Graph/object and ledger state apply atomically. Tests exhaust arithmetic boundaries, ancestor races, idempotency drift, remainder release, shared-ancestor transfer, destination insufficiency, every hold/release/expiry race, every crash/root/audit publication cut, Local/Meta differential replay, and checkpoint/backup/restore/activation/GC coverage.

## Invariants & interactions
Enforces FG-INV-16 and resource portions of FG-INV-17/18/20. Consumes authority bindings, command/state slots, foundation exact arithmetic and time evidence. W4 coordinator/constraints/escrow, W9 DP/audit, W10 QoS/result/output, backup/restore/GC and W12 Meta custody consume it. Shards may hold only certified ephemeral allocations; durable authority is Local or Meta.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Exact schemas/rows/codecs exist for every request/vector/role/path/policy/owner/state/basis/transition/spec/applied type and operation arm.
- Unit/golden tests cover checked arithmetic, ancestor quota aggregation, idempotency/body drift, charge class, whole-entry transfer/release, state basis and atomic object+charge publication.
- Property/model tests prove nonnegative conservation, every live durable object has exactly one owner/charge, release once, transfer without split/loss, prepared-owner nonexpiry, and current-authority enforcement.
- Mutation/fuzz rejects overflow/underflow, wrong role/tenant/path/owner, stale basis, duplicate key with drift, partial transfer, expiry of protected owner, Shard durable charge and object-without-charge publication.
- Crash/DPOR E2E races reserve/charge/transfer/release/expiry with result activation/ACK, prepare/commit/abort, backup/restore, GC and service restart; ledger and rooted owner remain bijective.
- JSONL emits {event_version,role_and_group,operation,request_key,owner_key,quota_path,charge_class,amount_vector,basis_generation,transition_id,from_state,to_state,ancestor_balances_digest,object_publication_digest?,time_evidence_digest?,verdict,recovery_action,replay_command}; principal-safe IDs only, no hidden query/data.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: process counters as durable truth, floating charges, partial owner transfer, timeout expiry of prepared/result obligations, and Shard-local durable authority. Conservative quota refusal is correct on stale/missing evidence.

## Provenance
Plan Appendix A lines 1980-1990; sections 7.6 and 13.3.

I read all 3,492 lines / 111,363 bytes of `src/ledger.rs` plus `src/lib.rs`
before judging the result.  The existing implementation is real: its six-axis
checked vectors, ancestor-closed quota tree, policy/class rules, exact retry
idempotence, whole-entry Reserve/Charge/Release/Expire/Transfer/Adjust
semantics, deterministic charge remainder release, shared-ancestor transfer
netting, protected-owner expiry rejection, and atomic failure behavior are
substantive and tested.

  legal, no command reference type can populate ResourceLedgerAppliedRecord,
  and no durable state-slot row can prove atomic graph/object + ledger-root

LogicalObjectKindCode enum.  TimeValidationEvidence and all resource kinds are
still reserved/unavailable there; AuthorizationDecisionRecord is not even
projected.  Inventing local marker types or leaving ObjectIds in place would
make the exact-reference and by-construction claims advisory, which is a
prohibited prototype rather than a subset of the final abstraction.

authorization, time, or command API.  ConfigurationState is the authority
configuration being retained; it is not AuthorityBoundHeader, an authorization
decision, or the command/state-slot constitution.  The new edge is useful
upstream evidence but does not supply any type consumed by ResourceLedgerTransition.

1. `fgdb-g0-authority-bindings-1xrl` must land the executable role family:
   AuthorityOwningRole, AuthorityBindingRecord/Ref<Role>, and the
   AuthorityBoundHeader<Role> Rust type + codec/substitution laws.  The active

2. `fgdb-w1-authz-policy-10y` plus its a21 catalog work must project/activate and

   writer/atomic-publication slot.
5. `fgdb-a12-checkpoint-resources-m9jz` (or an explicit owner-approved transfer
   of that catalog scope into ym2g) must mint the ResourceLimitPolicy,
   ResourceLedgerState, and ResourceLedgerTransition families and resolve the
   Basis/Spec/AppliedRecord/Effect candidates.  Their activated kind codes must
   then enter fgdb-types before exact StrongRef wrappers can compile.

Once 1-5 provide those typed seams, the next ym2g increment is mechanical and
well-bounded: replace TransitionHeader with exact ResourceLedgerBasis +
AuthorityBoundHeader, add the evidence fields to all six arms, expose
before/after bucket plans as committed values, add State/Spec/AppliedRecord/
Effect wrappers and codecs, then bind the operation matrix and atomic state
slot.  Until then, extending those surfaces inside fgdb-resource would duplicate
their owners or encode the wrong final type.

No Cargo gate was run because this re-test changed no repository code and both

the controlled Rust/file searches, the two landing diffs, and the full ledger

title: Build fgdb-sketch and fgdb-calibrate over asupersync's e-process core
description:
## What & scope
Build `fgdb-sketch` — the graph-statistics sketch library feeding `StatsSegment`s and synopses — and `fgdb-calibrate` — the Sextant calibration plane's graph-specific scores and ledgers, implemented as wrappers over asupersync's existing e-process/test-supermartingale monitors, conformal calibration + exploration budgets, decision-contract runtime (Bayesian regime posterior, Lyapunov governor), deterministic no-regret (EXP3/Hedge) scheduler adaptation, and Freedman/Azuma drain-progress evidence. Per §2.4, `fgdb-calibrate` wraps the runtime's machinery rather than reimplementing it.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5's third leg is calibrated adaptivity: constraint 10 says adaptivity is classified or it does not ship — every adaptive decision is exactly one of answer-preserving physical, answer-affecting execution, or canonical-state-affecting, and statistical promotion evidence is `FG-EVID-*`, never an `FG-INV-*` safety proof, with the deterministic fallback remaining valid when assumptions fail. §3.5's adopt/adapt verdicts govern the toolbox: conformal prediction is adopted as assumption-bearing evidence for optimizer intervals and approximate-maintainer risk, never as semantic enforcement; e-processes are adopted for policy trials and health sentinels and stay in `evidence.toml`; SPRT/Shiryaev–Roberts/BOCPD are adopted conditionally (an SPRT may add evidence to migration cards but never replaces hard dwell/hysteresis guards; one versioned BOCPD+SR regime signal feeds controllers without being treated as ground truth); empirical Bayes/Good–Turing/Catoni are "evaluate" status for per-block selectivities and cold-predicate floors; OPE is adopted conditionally with logged probabilities, support exclusions, effective sample size, deterministic fallback, and explicit deployment evidence. This discipline is the moat against the industry's "adaptive = unaccountable" failure mode.

## Design — normative detail
`fgdb-sketch`: sketch families for `StatsSegment` content — label/type counts, authorized degree histograms, property sketches (distinct-count, quantile, frequency), zone maps, and sampled path correlations. Every sketch profile fixes its merge/delete algebra, precision/error contract, canonical state, duplicate-operation behavior, and fallback; a sketch without exact deletion either rejects delete/update workloads or rebuilds, and never becomes authoritative constraint state (App B law — this also serves the intent-log sketch merge modes). Sketch state must have canonical encoding (deterministic bytes for identical logical state) because sketches ride delta rows and digests.

`fgdb-calibrate`: Sextant (§15.0) as code. Every evidence envelope carries `ClaimClass` (from `fgdb-claim`): `SafetyInvariant | FormalModelClaim | StatisticalClaim | ConfigurationModelClaim | EmpiricalGate`. Routing law: `invariants.toml` contains only exact safety/liveness obligations; `evidence.toml` contains `FG-CAL-*`/`FG-EVID-*`; `slo.toml` contains `FG-CFG-*`, performance, durability-model, and controller targets. Validity conditions are explicit in the types: e-processes may be anytime-valid under their named filtration/null assumptions; conformal coverage is marginal under its named exchangeability or online-validity conditions; drift alarms do not retroactively preserve a broken assumption; OPE requires positivity/overlap and sufficient effective sample size. Every adaptive policy retains a deterministic fallback valid without the statistical model. Calibration windows, selection policy, strata, propensity support, regime epochs, fallback, and failure behavior are immutable evidence identities. Everything is a deterministic transformation of logged inputs — same logs, same outputs — so calibration itself replays under the lab. A monitor that drives no named decision is dead code, but binding it to a decision does not make it an invariant.

## Invariants & claim types
This bead ships evidence-class machinery, not invariants. Registry rows it must implement/serve verbatim: FG-CAL-01 "Adaptive policy evidence versus pinned fallback — null/outcome filtration, alpha, support/overlap, effective sample size, loss and fallback; stream-sequenced promotion only"; FG-CAL-02 "Cardinality/risk interval coverage — population, selection/window, exchangeability or nonexchangeability method, strata, marginal target, realized coverage and drift"; FG-CAL-03 "ANN recall/drift evidence — authorized snapshot population, keyed sample, exact baseline, candidate policy, confidence interval and rebuild action"; FG-EVID-01 "Decision-card/OPE completeness — state/actions/features, logged probabilities, zero-support exclusions, clipping/estimator, policy epoch and fallback". The type system must make constructing an `FG-INV` claim from this crate impossible.

## Interactions
Consumes: g0-claim-registries (claim constitution, evidence/slo toml schemas), w1-foundation-types (`fgdb-claim`/`fgdb-evidence` types), w1-codecs (canonical sketch encodings). Produces machinery consumed by: w5-branch-stats + w5-planner (StatsSegment content, optimizer intervals, decision cards), w3-write-amp (§6.6 migration cards with SPRT evidence + hard dwell guards), w6-freshness (breach evidence), w7-vector (FG-CAL-03 recall ledgers), verif-sextant (the §15.0 calibration-plane verification), obs-slo (controller targets), perf-freshness-vector (calibration gate rows).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Sketch accuracy harnesses on named fnx-generator fixtures with declared error contracts (observed error within contract at stated confidence; violations are findings); merge-algebra property tests (commutativity/associativity/idempotence exactly as each profile claims); delete-incapability enforcement tests (delete workload against a non-deletable sketch profile ⇒ typed rejection or rebuild, never silent wrongness); canonical-encoding determinism (same logical sketch state ⇒ identical bytes). Calibration: simulation suites validating e-process type-I control under the null at declared alpha (anytime validity via Ville's inequality over long adversarial stopping rules), conformal marginal coverage under exchangeability plus documented, measured degradation under injected drift; OPE estimator tests with known ground truth, positivity-violation detection, and ESS gating; determinism test — identical logged inputs produce byte-identical evidence envelopes under the lab runtime; immutability test — evidence identities cannot be mutated post-construction. Logging: every envelope records its full assumption set; test failures print the envelope and the seed. E2E: `sextant_e2e` — under the lab runtime: generate a fixture workload stream, maintain a sketch family over it (merges plus one delete event against a non-deletable profile asserting typed rejection/rebuild), drive an e-process policy trial against a pinned fallback through to a promotion decision, emit the FG-CAL-01 evidence envelope, replay the identical logged inputs asserting byte-identical envelopes, then inject drift and assert reversion to the fallback through a stream-sequenced `DecisionPolicyEpoch`. DETAILED LOGGING (required for post-implementation verification): beyond envelope assumption-set logging above, monitors log {monitor_id, claim class, filtration/window id, e-value or coverage statistic, regime_epoch, decision consumed} per observation batch and sketches log {sketch_profile_oid, merge op, canonical state digest} per merge; the e2e asserts the replay's log stream is byte-identical to the original's.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: reimplementing the e-process/conformal core (asupersync owns it — deterministic implementation does not make assumptions true, and neither does reimplementation); treating fitted extreme quantiles as "certified" (§3.5 CVaR/EVT row); letting an SPRT replace dwell/hysteresis hard guards; graph-workload slogans substituting for fixture-specific risk evidence (§3.5 empirical-Bayes row). Risk: assumption erosion in production (exchangeability breaks silently) — mitigated by drift alarms wired to fallback, with the honest caveat that alarms do not retroactively preserve coverage.

## Provenance
§1 constraint 10; §2.1 statistical-governance row; §2.4; §3.5; §6.6; §8.5 (StatsSegments); §15.0; App B (sketch algebra law); App F FG-CAL/FG-EVID rows.
acceptance_criteria:
### A21 DecisionPolicyEpoch ownership

This bead is the unique implementation owner for DecisionPolicyEpoch {policy_id,version,scope,logical_effect_class,pinned_table_oid,fallback_oid,evidence_refs,previous_epoch_oid}. It owns its stable catalog row and field tags, canonical codec and identity, predecessor/promotion validation, binding to deterministic pinned fallback, evidence-reference validation, replay determinism, and negative fixtures proving StatisticalClaim evidence cannot be encoded as an invariant or substituted for the fallback. DecisionPolicyEpoch is byte- and type-distinct from SecurityPolicyEpoch; equality, aliasing, or ambient policy-version inference fails closed. W3/W5/W6/W7 controllers are consumers and may not define local variants.
notes: 2026-08-12 bounded delivery at HEAD 2a1015a6f5dc086c5073824d809a616b61ae832e (commits f23ccf7, 49400ef, 2a1015a): wired all four named graph-accuracy fixtures through the pinned fnx-generators GraphGenerator API; added deterministic 8,192-trial e-process optional-stopping and conformal exchangeability/drift campaigns with explicit statistical no-claim boundaries; added production StatisticalLogRecord to EvidenceEnvelope conversion with exact FG-CAL-01/02/03 and FG-EVID-01 disclosure/binding validation; added keyed DecisionPolicyEpoch production object identity; persisted and replay-checked all decision-bearing statistical log records, including real DrainProgress prefix emissions; exhaustively rejected every unknown LogicalEffectClass byte; promoted six exact governed verification selectors; and removed compile-time registry-file coupling to preserve topology. Full bash scripts/check.sh on unchanged HEAD exited 0: core 9/9, registered live 31/31, file coverage 326/337 with 11 declared exemptions, including Miri and whole-tree UBS critical ratchet. Focused fgdb-sketch plus fgdb-calibrate suites, clippy, fmt, claims, architecture, topology, and independent false-green review also passed. Scope boundary: this establishes empirical fixture evidence, governed envelope/log plumbing, and production DPE identity. It does not claim general formal Ville/conformal validity, a production golden corpus, BOCPD/Shiryaev-Roberts regime detection, or full downstream Sextant controller integration. Keep this Bead in_progress for those broader original criteria; fgdb-verif-sextant-ss83 owns the broader verification/integration tranche and fgdb-w1-format-test-corpora-lyf owns corpus materialization.

LANDED 24c15ef — the sketch/E2E integration this bead has listed as remaining since the 2026-07-23 22:41 comment.

The E2E maintained only count-min, whose deletion is refused with a typed rebuild requirement. That is half the App B sketch law. The other half — a family that supports exact deletion and therefore must APPLY it — had no coverage, and a StatsSegment carries both kinds. run_label_counts_maintenance is the counterpart: 11 observations over three keys, exact deletion (Person 5->3, City dropped entirely so the key disappears rather than retaining a zero), then a merge asserting the summed result. Its deletion asserts the exact opposite outcome from the count-min twin: Ok with the canonical state moving, versus Err(RebuildRequired) with the state pinned.

ONE DESIGN CALL WORTH RECORDING. The deletion is ordered BEFORE the merge. The maintenance log vocabulary is Merged | RebuildRequired, so an APPLIED deletion has no record of its own; ordering the merge last keeps the family's logged after_digest an accurate description of its final canonical state instead of a stale one. I checked whether this was forced: it is not. Records carry no digest chaining — the only cross-digest rule is that a RebuildRequired record's before and after must be equal (maintenance_log.rs validate_outcome). So this is an evidence-honesty choice, not a codec requirement. Extending SketchMaintenanceOutcome with an applied-deletion arm would change a canonical record contract, and nothing here demonstrates that need, so I deliberately did not. If a future consumer needs to reconstruct every state transition of a deletable family from the log alone, THAT is the trigger to revisit — note it rather than assume it.

Free coverage worth knowing about: SketchFixture derives PartialEq, so adding label_counts_final_state_bytes means the existing first.sketch == replay.sketch assertion now requires the exact-deletion family's canonical bytes to be byte-identical across the lab replay — the determinism claim this bead asks the E2E to make, with no extra assertion.

LANDED 234d04e — finishing the draft. Its estimator test asserted only `candidate > fallback`. This module is exact fixed-point arithmetic end to end, so an ordering assertion leaves the arithmetic unproved at exactly the magnitude the envelope is declared against: a wrong value that kept its sign would pass. I derived the exact values from the source rather than adopting them from a failure, and they held first run:
  candidate numerator = 4 * PROBABILITY_SCALE * MAX_ABS_OUTCOME_UNITS = 4e21
  fallback numerator  = -4e21, shared denominator 4 * PROBABILITY_SCALE * OUTCOME_SCALE = 4e15
  advantage numerator = 8e21
All three estimators agree on this fixture because the direct model predicts the selected action's logged outcome exactly, zeroing every importance-weighted residual. The advantage assertion is the load-bearing addition: `validate_arithmetic_envelope` compares exactly ONE derived quantity against `i128::MAX`, and that quantity is the advantage — driving it at the declared bound is what makes this a test OF the envelope rather than merely near it.

LANDED 1e2ee24 — the construction-time validations. 32 of ope.rs's 37 `OpeError` variants had zero test references; the five covered were the ones the estimator path forces. Seven tests now cover 25 of those 32, grouped by rule rather than by variant: canonical action tables (empty/descending/duplicate, including the NON-ADJACENT repeat — the uniqueness check only compares against the immediately preceding action, so it is monotonicity that closes that hole, and that case is what makes the pair sufficient rather than suggestive); selected-action presence and positive logging probability (a silent-wrongness guard, not tidiness: `clipped_weight` answers a zero behavior probability with the FULL clipping limit, so admitting one would enter both estimates at maximum weight instead of being refused); candidate-versus-fallback identity; window construction and closure; every profile bound including that each declared maximum is itself admissible; and the three cross-object rules where identity meets profile, each individually legal and jointly impossible so neither constructor can catch them. ope.rs goes from 5/37 to 30/37 variants exercised. Every non-trivial guard was mutation-confirmed: disabling it fails exactly the new test that names it and leaves the rest green.

FINDING — A DEAD BRANCH IN THE SHARED VALIDATION TEMPLATE, in TWO modules. `OpeError::SequenceOutsideWindow` (ope.rs:1016) and `AnnRecallError::SequenceOutsideWindow` (ann_recall.rs:1120) are both unconstructible, by identical algebra:
  `record` guards on `is_complete()` (len == capacity), so past that guard len <= capacity-1;
  `expected = first + len`, so expected <= first + (last-first) = last;
  the equality check `sequence != expected` rejects everything else;
  therefore the `sequence > last_sequence` branch below can never be true.
Proven empirically too: I patched ope.rs's branch body to `panic!` and drove sequences 104, 105, 999, u64::MAX, 99 and 0 against window 100..=103, plus a filled ledger pushed past its end. Every route is intercepted first by `UnexpectedSequence` or `WindowAlreadyComplete`; the panic never fired. Neither variant is constructed anywhere else.
NOT a bug — redundant defence, never a wrong answer — but it is tech debt in public error types that are part of the evidence contract, and `UnexpectedSequence{expected, actual}` is strictly more informative than what the dead branch would have reported. Because it appears identically in two modules it is a TEMPLATE defect, so fix the template, not one site. I checked policy_epoch.rs and it is a FALSE POSITIVE: its `RegimeFallbackSequenceOutsideWindow` is a different variant with a genuinely reachable two-sided range check.

comments.text:
LOG.RS SLICE — three increments landed (718b0fd, bec6ca3, 374e967). Author identity: pane4-calibrate, the crate lane (same agent as the earlier cc-sketch-calibrate comments).

A CENSUS CORRECTION FIRST, because I got it wrong and caught it. My initial census reported log.rs as 1270 code / 4848 test lines, which would have made it the BEST-covered module in the crate and the wrong thing to work on. It is wrong: log.rs has TWO `#[cfg(test)]` markers — one at line 1270 on a test-only helper INSIDE production code, and the real `mod tests` at 4528. Splitting on the first truncates the body and inflates the tests. Split correctly it is 4526 code / 1590 test = 0.35, exactly the predecessor's ranking. Anyone censusing a module in this crate must split on the LAST top-level `#[cfg(test)]`, not the first.

SECOND CORRECTION, to the plan rather than the measurement: the determinism properties this bead cares about most were ALREADY COVERED before I started — log_replay_is_byte_identical, record_round_trip_covers_every_closed_statistic_variant, ordered_append_rejections_are_atomic, distinct_monitors_share_a_batch_in_canonical_order, record_limit_rejection_is_atomic, plus two strict-decoder tests. The 0.35 ratio means "4526 lines of code per 1590 lines of test", NOT "replay is untested". The real gap is the COMPLEMENT of what exists: the suite proved valid inputs round-trip and never proved invalid ones are refused. 66 of 99 error variants across the four enums had zero test references.

718b0fd — CLOSED TAG VOCABULARIES. Eight decoders (conformal mode, monitor kind, OPE estimator/failure-behaviour/selection-reason, ANN sample design/action/action-reason). Each asserts every valid tag maps to its own distinct variant, which also pins the discriminants against silent reordering, and that 0, one past the last valid tag, and 255 are rejected carrying the offending tag. Tag 0 is asserted separately everywhere because it is the byte a zeroed or padded buffer supplies and must never resolve to a live variant. The single-variant vocabulary (OPE failure behaviour) earns its own case for the opposite reason: a decoder that ignored the tag entirely would satisfy any test that only ever supplies the one valid value. This is canonicity, not politeness — an accepted unknown tag lets two byte strings denote one logical state and replay stops being bit-identical.

bec6ca3 — THE CLAIM-CLASS LAWS ARE STRUCTURAL, and now proven so. log.rs opens by claiming "no claim-class field a caller can change, no invariant constructor, and no conversion to an invariant claim". The only thing testing that was one positive assertion that claim_class() returns Statistical, which proves the law was not violated in the case tried and cannot prove the illegal state is unconstructible. Two compile_fail doctests now assert the complement, each PAIRED with a companion that must compile — a lone compile_fail also passes when it fails for an unrelated reason such as a typo or a renamed item, so the pairing is what makes it evidence. The conversion pair is the sharp one: identical signatures, differing only in `record.claim_class()` versus `record.into()`. I verified all three claims hold BEFORE writing, so these pin an accurate doc comment rather than exposing a defect. I deliberately did NOT duplicate fgdb-claim's justify::<Statistical,Invariant> compile_fail — that law is already proven where it is defined — and I dropped a "no invariant constructor" doctest because it would fail on arity or a missing name, which a typo also produces, so it would not have been attributable.

TRAP WORTH BROADCASTING: `cargo test --lib` DOES NOT RUN DOCTESTS. These are the first doctests in fgdb-calibrate, so `--doc` previously passed by running ZERO tests. Landed under the `--lib` gate everyone (including me) had been using all session, the compile_fail assertions would have been silently unexecuted forever. Gate any doctest work with plain `cargo test -p <crate>`. Proof it ran: the gate printed `Doc-tests fgdb_calibrate` then 2 + 2 = 4 passing.

374e967 — THE FIVE FLOAT DOMAIN RULES AND THE CANONICAL-BITS GATE. None of the five had a direct test. The accept/reject sets were MEASURED, not inferred from names, and two boundaries read the opposite way round: validate_finite_or_positive_infinity constrains MAGNITUDE not sign, so it admits negative finite values and refuses only negative infinity; and positive infinity splits the two non-negative rules, admitted by the ..._or_positive_infinity form and refused by plain ..._finite. Zero is the entire difference between the non-negative and positive rules. The second test covers the shared gate: NEGATIVE ZERO compares EQUAL to positive zero yet has a different bit pattern, so admitting it would let two distinct byte strings denote one logical value — inadmissible in a log whose purpose is bit-identical replay. NaN is refused for the companion reason. Because the gate runs before each domain check the rejection must be uniform, so all five are asserted; a validator that checked its own domain first would report the wrong error and, for negative zero, would wrongly ACCEPT under both non-negative rules.

METHOD — log.rs DEFEATS the standalone harness, but its validators do not. log.rs pulls 8 sibling modules and all but ope.rs bind asupersync behaviourally (regime.rs even `pub use`s asupersync types), so stubbing would mean asserting my own stubs. Measured, not assumed: a harness attempt produced 25 errors, ALL unresolved imports and zero type errors, so the modules do compose — the blocker is fidelity, not compilability. What DOES work: the domain validators are pure functions, so I copied the five predicates verbatim into a throwaway probe and RAN them to build the truth table. That caught the two counter-intuitive boundaries above, which I would otherwise have asserted backwards and discovered only after a 30-minute gate.

First I checked whether the ordering law is STRUCTURAL or merely advisory, because if it were advisory that would be a defect rather than a coverage gap. It is structural: decode_canonical routes every decoded record back through append (log.rs:1949), so a decoded log passes the identical duplicate, strictly-after-per-monitor and canonical-order checks as a built one, and `records()` hands out an immutable slice with no other mutator anywhere. The doc comment claiming "replays its append checks" is accurate — verified in the code, not taken from the comment.

A decoder trusting wire order would deserialise an out-of-order log, and "nothing is dropped or reordered" would hold only for logs assembled in-process — not the guarantee a replayable decision log makes. The test splices two hostile streams from a valid two-record encoding at REAL frame boundaries (the frame walk asserts it consumed the whole encoding, so the offsets are true boundaries rather than ones that merely parse): the records reversed, and the same frame twice. Reversed must fail RecordNotInCanonicalOrder; repeated must fail DuplicateRecord — a stream that would otherwise silently double-count one monitor observation. Both vocabularies carry the same canonicity obligation: this log is the audit trail for sketch maintenance, so a decoder admitting an unknown tag lets two distinct byte strings denote one logical event. LANDED ae3a55d — batch-range ordering and identity-window containment, the log-level ordering surface. Author: pane4-calibrate.

Both `ReversedBatchRange` and `BatchOutsideIdentityWindow` had ZERO test references (control: `NonCanonicalFloatBits` returns 2, so the probe finds covered variants). `eprocess_record_in_window` already existed but was used only for APPEND-level overlap tests, never for record-construction containment — a good example of a helper's existence not implying the rule is covered.

WHY THESE TWO ARE ONE INCREMENT: together they are the ordering guarantee at construction time. `StatisticalBatchRange` is INCLUSIVE, so `first == last` is a legal single-sequence batch and only `first > last` is reversed; both sides are pinned because a `>=` slipped into that comparison would silently outlaw every one-observation batch and nothing else in the suite would notice. Containment is the other half: batches are ordered and nonoverlapping WITHIN a declared window, so a batch escaping its identity window would be ordered against a range the identity never covered. Equality is asserted legal at both ends (a batch may span the whole window) and escape by exactly one at either end is asserted refused — the case that separates a correct pair of strict comparisons from an off-by-one admitting a straddling batch.

DE-RISKING, because log.rs cannot use the standalone rustc harness (it pulls 8 sibling modules, all but ope.rs binding asupersync behaviourally) and a wrong assertion costs a full ~17 minute gate. Before writing I confirmed the fixture tolerates window != batch — `ordered_append_rejections_are_atomic` already drives batches (10,19)/(19,25)/(1,9) against window (1,30) — and that `eprocess_statistic` carries no window of its own, so `statistic.validate()` at log.rs:3165 cannot pre-empt the containment check at :3167 for this monitor. Both held; the gate passed first attempt.

comments.text:
STANDING RECOMMENDATION, endorsed by the operator and recorded here so the next agent does not helpfully defeat it: DO NOT WRITE TESTS FOR THE IDENTITY AND ALLOCATION ERROR VARIANTS.

In log.rs these are `EvidenceIdentityAllocationFailed`, `EvidenceIdentityIssuanceFailed`, `MonitorIdentityIssuanceFailed`, `EvidenceIdentityLengthOverflow`, `HistoryAllocationFailed`, `ExclusionAllocationFailed`, and the `ArithmeticOverflow`/`ArithmeticEnvelopeUnrepresentable` pair; in maintenance_log, `AllocationFailed` and `EncodedLengthOverflow`.

They can only be driven by real fault injection — an allocator that fails, an issuer that refuses, a length that genuinely overflows. A test that fabricates the condition to reach the arm proves nothing about the arm: it asserts that a hand-built error value equals itself. Worse, it makes the variant LOOK covered, so the next coverage census scores it green and nobody writes the real fault-injection harness. That is a substitute for an abstraction rather than a subset of one, which the doctrine prohibits outright.

The honest disposition is to leave them uncovered and visible until the lab runtime's fault injection exists, at which point they become a genuine crash-point-matrix item rather than a unit test. Any coverage census over these crates should EXCLUDE this set rather than report it as a gap — counting them inflates the deficit and invites exactly the faking this note forbids.

Separately and for the same reason: the SIX unconstructible variants recorded earlier (both `SequenceOutsideWindow`s, `ObservationLimitUnrepresentable`, both `SequenceOverflow`s, `ProfileTooLarge`, `RecordCountTooLarge`) must not be tested either. Those are not merely hard to reach, they are unreachable — an infallible width conversion or a range check already implied by an equality check above it. They need an API change, not a test.

LANDED 137e0d8 (conformal config admission) and ae3a55d (batch ordering + window containment), plus a FINDING of the shape the operator asked me to watch for while writing them. Author: pane4-calibrate.

137e0d8 — CONFORMAL ALPHA IS HALF-OPEN, CALIBRATION BOUNDS ARE ORDERED. Neither rule had a test. Alpha lives in `[0.0, 1.0)`: zero is a legal target miscoverage, one is not, because an alpha of one asks for zero coverage. BOTH ends are asserted because the openness at exactly one end IS the rule — a `..=` slipped into that range would admit 1.0 with nothing else in the suite noticing. Calibration bounds refuse a zero minimum (a coverage claim over no calibration samples is not a claim) and refuse maximum < minimum, but equality is asserted LEGAL: a fixed-size calibration set is a valid configuration, not a degenerate one, so a `<=` there would be as wrong as the `..=`. Every case perturbs exactly ONE field of a fixture asserted to construct first. GATE: rch cargo test -p fgdb-calibrate --lib --locked = 191 passed 0 failed (190 + 1, exact); rustfmt clean; ubs exit 0. Run under an exclusive build-1 hold as pane4-calibrate, released immediately after.

FINDING — A GUARD CLAUSE THAT CANNOT DECIDE, at three sites. This is the code-side twin of cod_2's FG-INV-12 shape (a doc asserting what nothing checks): here it is a CHECK that can never be the deciding one.
  Sites: the conformal alpha check (log.rs ~604), the exploration alpha check (~640), and `validate_unit_interval` (~4008). All three are written `!value.is_finite() || !(0.0..1.0).contains(&value)` — but a BOUNDED range check already excludes both infinities, and NaN is caught upstream by `validate_canonical_float`. So `!is_finite()` can never change the outcome at those three sites.
  MEASURED, NOT REASONED. I ran each predicate with and against the clause removed over eight values (+0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, -1.0, +inf, -inf, MAX): removing `!is_finite()` changed the outcome in 1 of 24 cases. The single difference is the CONTRAST case — in `validate_nonnegative_finite` removing it flips `+inf` from rejected to ACCEPTED, because `+inf` is not `< 0.0`.
  So the clause is load-bearing exactly where the comparison is ONE-SIDED, and dead exactly where the range is BOUNDED. That asymmetry is what makes this a finding rather than a style note: someone copied a guard from a rule that needs it into two that do not.
  NOT A CORRECTNESS DEFECT — behaviour is right at all three sites. It matters because it invites a test asserting "the is_finite clause rejects infinity here", which would assert a clause that never fires. My existing 374e967 test correctly asserts the OUTCOME (infinity refused), which stays true whichever clause gets there.
  NOT FIXED BY ME: removing a clause from a live validator is a PRODUCTION edit, a different risk class from adding tests, and the redundancy is harmless. Recorded for whoever owns a validator cleanup.
  Second instance of this family in these crates today: the six unconstructible error variants are BRANCHES that cannot be reached; this is a CLAUSE that cannot decide. Machinery that looks like it is working and is not.

REMAINING CROSS-CHECKS, with reasons rather than omissions so nobody re-derives them:
  exploration alpha — needs a record fixture whose known-good argument set I do not have, and log.rs has NO fast loop (it pulls 8 sibling modules, all but ope.rs binding asupersync behaviourally), so guessing costs a full ~17 minute gate per attempt.
  InvalidEProcessConfiguration — delegates to asupersync's `EProcessConfig::validate`, so the rejecting input must be MEASURED, not assumed. Same discipline the predecessor applied to regime.rs.
  InvalidOpeProfile / InvalidAnnRecallProfile — thin delegations to `OpeProfile::try_new` and `AnnRecallProfile::try_new`, both already covered DIRECTLY in 1e2ee24 and 77cf424. Driving them again through the record path would assert the delegation, not the rule.
  Still outstanding and genuinely worth writing: the OPE cross-checks (10) and ANN cross-checks (9), where embedded evidence must agree with the claimed trial profile.

TWO OPERATIONAL FACTS FOR EVERY CRATE LANE, both paid for today.
  THE CATALOG AND CRATE LANES ARE NOT INDEPENDENT. `crates/fgdb-types/src/refs.rs:29` include_bytes! the `logical_object_kinds.toml` projection and asserts on it AT COMPILE TIME (active-row count at :136), so everything downstream of fgdb-types fails to build while a catalog edit is in flight. An `error[E0080]` inside `refs`, or an ACTIVE_STATUS_ROW assertion, is NOT your crate: likeliest a catalog increment legitimately changed an active row, else the projection was regenerated with a different field order (the per-kind check demands exactly object_kind, name, status), else an incidental `status = "active"` byte run moved the whole-file count. The guard is TIGHT (seven transitions tested with a control, no silent disagreement), so both modes are over-strict — false alarm, never a miss. Wait for the catalog lane and re-gate. NEVER revert a registry edit to go green.
  `beads_safe_to_commit.sh` VALIDATES AGAINST THE WRONG BASELINE. It compares working-tree pin to working-tree records, but committing `.beads/` alone pairs working-tree records with HEAD's pin. Observed live this tick: the script said `pin=315 records=315, exit=0` while HEAD held pin 314 against 315 records — architecture-check (check.sh stage 8) was ALREADY failing at HEAD and the outstanding repair was the pin, not the export. 49ba164 has since landed it and HEAD is coherent again. Check `git show HEAD:` for both values before believing the script. This is its SECOND defect (the first: it inspects only unstaged changes), and both are the same shape — the tool answered a question, just not the one that decides safety.
