`SubscriptionCreationIndex` durably maps the scoped subscription key and canonical request digest to exactly one semantic cursor creation plus its Protocol pending owner. Exact retry reproduces `SUBSCRIBE_ACCEPTED` while PendingVisibility/ReleasedAwaitingActivation and reproduces the frozen `SUBSCRIBE_READY` only after BaselineDeliverable; drift fails. No creation entry owns an absolute lease or Resume capability before activation. `SUBSCRIBE_CLOSE` presents the exact authenticated outstanding disposition, orders `CloseCursor`, stores a capability-safe tombstone, and makes lost close-response replay deterministic. Generic STREAM_END, socket loss, or drain is not unsubscribe; ordinary disconnect merely detaches the runtime sender, while an explicit durable pause is a separate authenticated policy transition. `FLOW_CREDIT` is a versioned cumulative grant: the next client-owned credit sequence and expected grant generation must match; server debit generation is private. Exact duplicate is idempotent; conflicting duplicate, gap, decrease, overflow, wrong stream generation, or closed stream rejects. `GAP` is emitted only from ResetNoticeDeliverable; `GAP_ACK` durably completes that notice before the separately activated successor baseline receives a fresh lease. `GAP`, explicit `AUTHORITY_RESET`, reset-baseline readiness, and `SUBSCRIPTION_ENDED` are protected data-dependent output and require the matrix-assigned fresh guard immediately before every write; socket disconnect itself emits no durable application frame.

The complete internal delta provenance remains in `DeltaDeliveryEnvelope` and its `InternalDeliveryDigest`; it is never a wire type. Every `baseline_digest` frame field above means `PublicBaselineDigest`, and every baseline ACK validates that public digest; internal baseline identity/coverage/frontier are likewise server-side only. `AuthorizedDeltaPublicProvenance` and `PublicDeliveryDigest` are separately derived after authorization. The default Opaque arm reveals only delivery sequence and authorized cursor position. Atomic/coalesced source ranges, batch IDs/digests, source count, zero-net cadence, and hidden commits appear only in the explicitly authorized and audited Declassified arm. Hidden-commit differential tests require byte-identical public streams, timings within the declared deterministic envelope, and digests under the Opaque policy.

Local dispatch uses `LocalStatementAbortSpec`, `TxnAbortSpec`, `LocalResultDeliveryTransitionSpec`, Local read-close/prepare/terminal-completion, and Local status/index types. Sharded dispatch uses `GlobalStatementAbortSpec`, `GlobalAttemptCancelSpec`, `GlobalResultDeliveryTransitionSpec`, Global read-close/prepare/terminal-completion, and Meta outcome/directory types. After publication, QUERY_CANCEL can only pause the current sender; only RESULT_RELEASE or lease expiry releases independently retained delivery, and neither retracts Published. After prepare admission, semantic cancellation returns TooLate or Unknown and recovery completes the admitted terminal. `CANCEL_EXPLANATION` and data-dependent cancellation errors are protected output.

`CAPABILITY_MIGRATE` is legal only under a fresh Sharded E2 Ready binding and the exact six-arm `PostActivationCapabilityMigrationSpec`, including DurableArtifactOutput. The E capability is checked solely as proof with the same principal, no-wider authority, immediately preceding Local epoch, and certified transition. It grants no E read, delivery, lookup, or existence authority. Exact retry returns the same prebuilt E2 successor; ineligible or invalid proof is a uniform nonrevealing failure. Subscription migration requires no outstanding or pending Local output and creates a new pending baseline; no Local-to-Global delta range is emitted. PendingVisibility and ReleasedAwaitingActivation promises have no legacy capability, so `RoleTransitionProtectedPromiseInventory` and `PostActivationProtectedPromiseTransferSpec` transfer them by exact owner commitment before capability migration can complete.

Frame-order validity never substitutes for value, authorization, decompression, time, or resource validation. Every `*_BEGIN`, chunk, end, proof, replay/status projection, exported byte, protected error, and cancellation explanation consumes the one fresh `PublicFrameSendGuard` arm assigned by the generated frame-class matrix; `DataOutput` is not valid for status, terminal outcomes, audit receipts, or protected errors. Canonical chunking uses deterministic record/row boundaries; oversized legal rows use `DATA_FRAGMENT` after bounded spill reservation, and nothing is exposed until row and envelope verification completes. ACK is legal only after the matching END transcript. Incomplete unacked output replays from its declared canonical boundary or releases through a typed transition; it is never silently acknowledged.

A ReplayManifest ObjectId is internal and never a wire selector; only an opaque public replay handle plus current scoped Replay authority can select a typed public projection. Replay execution results use the ordinary result lifecycle. `WireFecSymbolRecord` is a channel-bound transfer record, never the at-rest SymbolRecord, and is verified against `PublicFecTransferDescriptor` before admission. Compression/FEC is negotiated only after authenticated public metadata and resource reservation. HTTP/2, gRPC, WebSocket, and Bolt adapters preserve the same idempotency, posture, explicit release, output-guard, cancellation, result-resume, and cutover semantics; Bolt exposes only its declared read-only downgrade in 1.0; `BoltCompatProfileV2` (§13.5) is the registered 1.x write profile.

State-model, golden, differential, fuzz, crash, and DPOR suites cover pre-auth database non-disclosure; missing/out-of-order AUTH_OK/READY; Local/Sharded dispatch parity; lost/duplicate/conflicting BEGIN, autocommit, subscription, result resume/ACK, unsubscribe, export, and replay requests; NotRequired versus RequiredVisible release; revocation/refresh/epoch change between every two chunks; protected-error silence; hidden zero-net provenance noninterference; E-to-E2 migration exclusivity; and adapter parity. No frame or state row ships without its exact generated wire tag, authorization/release rule, size bound, retry rule, and negative transition fixture.

## Invariants & interactions
Enforces FG-INV-03, FG-INV-15, FG-INV-16, FG-INV-19, FG-INV-20 and robot-mode determinism. Consumes wire projections, authority bindings, capabilities, result-owner formats, transaction lifecycle, subscription delivery/reset contracts, audit receipts, replay/artifact/error contracts and flow control. FGP core, adapters, server, Bolt, CDC and protocol verification consume the generated catalog.

## Acceptance Criteria
- One registry row exists for every exact frame including SubscriptionCreationIndex, SUBSCRIBE_PAUSE/PAUSED/RESUME_AFTER_PAUSE, AuditReceiptSubject with seven arms, and current-scoped Replay authority lookup.
- Each row fixes direction, legal connection/request state, exact body schema/tag, required header/binding, idempotency key, state token/capability, guard arm, time requirements, flow/size charge, success/error frames, retry semantics, disclosure class and feature predicate.
- Generated codec/state-machine/golden tests byte-freeze all frames and reject unknown required tags, illegal state/direction, internal keyed refs, stale epochs/tokens, duplicate IDs with body drift, unbounded lengths and partial bodies.
- Property/model tests prove connection/request state totality, one terminal response or resumable state, current authority before every observation/write, flow conservation, no result/cursor delta before legal release, and exact retry response.
- Fuzzing covers arbitrary frame streams, fragmentation/coalescing, size overflow, cross-frame body substitution, FEC/wire versus at-rest symbols, handle/token confusion, audit-subject substitution and every forbidden transition.
- E2E script exercises handshake/auth, SnapshotQuery, explicit transaction, statement result, cancel versus release, result resume/ACK, subscription baseline/delta/pause/resume/reset, artifact/error/replay, FEC reconnect, audit receipt, reauth/service epoch change and graceful drain across every adapter.
- Detailed JSONL emits {event_version,connection_id,connection_state,request_id,stream_id,frame_tag,direction,body_digest,header_binding_digest,auth_generation,service_epoch,request_state_before,request_state_after,guard_arm?,state_token_generation?,flow_rows?,flow_bytes?,time_requirement_set?,response_commitment?,terminal_or_resume_state?,rejection_class?,recovery_action,replay_command}. Public logs exclude protected payloads, raw capabilities, internal ObjectIds, DP seeds and hidden provenance; tests assert every accepted/rejected frame has one complete event.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: hand-written duplicate frame lists, wildcard body families, adapter-specific semantics, internal IDs as selectors, numeric internal generations leaked on wire, and permissive unknown-tag handling. Registry growth is managed by generation and explicit protocol epochs.

## Provenance
Plan Appendix D lines 2763-3118; FGP section 13.2 and G3 protocol gate.
design:
## Authoritative post-decomposition contract delta (d96bf0f)

The capability-status and audit-receipt authorization references below are required fields of the exact frame/send-guard catalog; digest-only or wildcard status authority is invalid.

`CapabilityStatusAuthorizationRef` is the exact `u16` union `0x0001 LocalTxn{ref:StrongRef<LifecycleAuthorizationDecisionRecord<Local>>,required_operation:StatusLookup<TxnOutcome>}|0x0002 MetaTxn{ref:StrongRef<LifecycleAuthorizationDecisionRecord<Meta>>,required_operation:StatusLookup<TxnOutcome>}|0x0003 LocalMerge{ref:StrongRef<MergeCapabilityOperationAuthorizationRecord<Local>>,required_authority:StatusLookup}|0x0004 MetaMerge{ref:StrongRef<MergeCapabilityOperationAuthorizationRecord<Meta>>,required_authority:StatusLookup}|0x0005 LocalUniformUnknown{session_authorization_ref:StrongRef<SessionAuthorizationRecord<Local>>,canonical_status_request_digest}|0x0006 MetaUniformUnknown{session_authorization_ref:StrongRef<SessionAuthorizationRecord<Meta>>,canonical_status_request_digest}`; every other tag is reserved-invalid. The UniformUnknown arms are legal only after invalid/unclassifiable capability input and authorize exactly `NotVisibleOrUnknown`, no index lookup or other status class. `AuditReceiptStatusAuthorizationRecord<Role>` is the same-group immutable `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,validation_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence>,audit_subject:0x0001 TxnOutcome|0x0002 ResumeSubscriptionCursor|0x0003 ResumeBufferedResult|0x0004 ResumeDurableArtifactOutput,audit_subject_handle_commitment,expected_receipt_index_leaf_digest,canonical_audit_receipt_request_digest,request_nonce,body_digest}`; all other subject tags are reserved-invalid, and the validation selects only `AuditReceiptStatus`, ReadyChannel presentation, Current lineage, and the matching subject. `AuditReceiptStatusAuthorizationRef` is the exact `u16` union `0x0001 Local{ref:StrongRef<AuditReceiptStatusAuthorizationRecord<Local>>}|0x0002 Meta{ref:StrongRef<AuditReceiptStatusAuthorizationRecord<Meta>>}`; every other tag is reserved-invalid, and the selected ref is rooted through receipt resolution and frame completion. `PendingOutcomeStatusAuthority` is the exact `u16` union `0x0001 Authenticated{status_authorization_ref:CapabilityStatusAuthorizationRef,validated_outcome_capability_commitment}|0x0002 UniformUnknown{status_authorization_ref:CapabilityStatusAuthorizationRef}`; every other tag is reserved-invalid, and this is the normative type of `PublicFrameSendGuard::PendingOutcomeStatus.authority` even where the later compact rendering elides its type name.
`FrameSubjectVersion` is the closed type-specific union `PreparedStatement{statement_handle:PublicHandle<PreparedStatement>,state_token:PublicStateToken<PreparedStatement>}|ResultDelivery{delivery_handle:PublicResultDeliveryHandle,state_token:PublicStateToken<ResultDelivery>}|ArtifactDelivery{delivery_handle:PublicArtifactOutputHandle,state_token:PublicStateToken<ArtifactDelivery>}|CursorOutput{cursor_handle:PublicCursorHandle,output_handle:PublicHandle<CursorOutput>,state_token:PublicStateToken<CursorOutput>}|ProtectedError{delivery_handle:PublicErrorDeliveryHandle,state_token:PublicStateToken<ProtectedErrorDelivery>}|TxnStatus{txn_handle:PublicTxnHandle,state_token:PublicStateToken<TxnProgress>}|MergeStatus{merge_handle:PublicMergeHandle,state_token:PublicStateToken<MergeProgress>}|AuditStatus{subject_handle:PublicAuditSubjectHandle,state_token:PublicStateToken<AuditStatus>}|SnapshotStream{admission_commitment:OpaquePublicCommitment<SnapshotQueryAdmission>,stream_ordinal}`; a naked numeric version or cross-kind token cannot decode. `PublicFrameSendGuard` is the closed queue-admission union `PreparedMetadata{prepare_authorization_digest,catalog_compatibility_digest}|DataOutput{read_release_authorization_digest,audit_release_digest,active_delivery_authorization_digest}|SnapshotEphemeralOutput{admission_record_commitment,visible_endpoint_binding_commitment,read_release_authorization_digest}|CapabilityTerminalOutcome{status_authorization_ref:CapabilityStatusAuthorizationRef,validated_capability_commitment,terminal_projection_authorization_digest,audit_release_digest}|PendingOutcomeStatus{authority:Authenticated{status_authorization_ref:CapabilityStatusAuthorizationRef,validated_outcome_capability_commitment}|UniformUnknown{status_authorization_ref:CapabilityStatusAuthorizationRef},opaque_status_projection_digest}|ProtectedOutputManagementStatus{validated_management_handle_commitment,output_kind:Result|SubscriptionInitial|SubscriptionDelta|SubscriptionReset|Artifact|ProtectedError,released_state_token,release_authorization_digest}|AuditReceiptStatus{authorization_ref:AuditReceiptStatusAuthorizationRef,audit_subject_handle_commitment,current_scoped_audit_authority_digest,receipt_status_projection_digest}|ProtectedError{error_delivery_authorization_digest,audit_release_digest}` plus common `{auth_generation_use_guard,ready_binding,session_binding,stream_id,frame_subject_version:FrameSubjectVersion,exact_frame_class_and_digest_or_byte_range,frame_time_requirement_set_ref:StrongRef<FrameTimeRequirementSet>,queue_frame_time_guard_set:FrameTimeUseGuardSet}`. `PreparedMetadata` queues only the frozen PREPARED parameter/schema contract after current catalog and authority revalidation. `DataOutput` queues bytes only from the exact ActiveDeliverable cursor/output arm. `SnapshotEphemeralOutput` is the sole arm that queues `SNAPSHOT_RESULT_CHUNK`/`SNAPSHOT_RESULT_END` bytes from a live `LocalSnapshotQuery` admission (Appendix A) under the `SnapshotStream` subject arm; it never queues a lease, resume capability, or durable-outcome projection. `CapabilityTerminalOutcome` alone queues `NeverRegistered`, `TerminalVisiblePendingPostconditions`, `TerminalReady`, or `MERGE_STATUS_RESULT::{Committed,Rejected}` after exact audit-visible terminal authorization and retains the Usable status source through send. `PendingOutcomeStatus` alone queues `BeginStaging`, `InProgress`, `FinalizingOpaque`, `MERGE_STATUS_RESULT::InFlight`, `TokenNotYetValid`, `TokenExpired`, `TimeAuthorityUnavailable`, or `NotVisibleOrUnknown`; none may encode a semantic terminal kind. Authenticated requires a non-UniformUnknown ref containing Usable for a state-bearing projection or the byte-matched negative classifier for the three public time classes. UniformUnknown requires exactly a LocalUniformUnknown or MetaUniformUnknown ref and can emit only NotVisibleOrUnknown; it carries no capability commitment. TokenExpired additionally requires the exact durable-expired requirement arm. `ProtectedOutputManagementStatus` queues only a frozen ACCEPTED/AwaitingActivation projection for a PendingVisibility or ReleasedAwaitingActivation owner and can never queue payload bytes, a lease, or a Resume capability. `AuditReceiptStatus` queues only the projection selected by its rooted authorization record, and `ProtectedError` uses its bounded owner lifecycle. The generated public-frame-class and time-requirement matrices assign every protected frame or byte range to exactly one arm/set and reject aliases or wildcard classes. `OutputSendGuard` is the legacy alias for `DataOutput`, not a generic escape hatch.
**Authoritative v1 delivery and control corrections.** `QUERY_CANCEL` controls computation and the current sender only. Before publication it may select the role-valid no-result/abort path; after independent retention it can only durably pause that session's sender after joining queued/writing transport obligations. It never ACKs/releases a result, changes capability lineage, or frees durable charge. `ClientResultReleaseAuthority` is the closed source union `ReadyChannel{surface:NativeFgp|Http2|Grpc|WebSocket,presented_authority:ResumeCapability{validation_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence>,capability_commitment}|ManagementHandle{validated_management_handle_commitment},session_binding,auth_context_generation,surface_request_digest,canonical_fgp_request_digest}|Embedded{stream_release_token_commitment,host_session_generation,explicit_release_call_digest}|BoltV1{bolt_session_binding,qid,request_kind:DISCARD|RESET,request_message_digest}|BoltV2{bolt_session_binding,negotiated_profile_oid:BoltCompatProfileV2,qid,request_kind:DISCARD|RESET,request_message_digest}`. Only ReadyChannel ResumeCapability validation selects the exact ResumeBufferedResult/ResultReleaseUnacked row and byte-matches the capability commitment, surface/canonical request pair, current result lineage, role, header, and session. The ReadyChannel management-handle arm, embedded stream token, and Bolt V1/V2 authenticated DISCARD/RESET arms cannot populate a capability-validation ref. `AuthenticatedClientResultReleaseReceipt<Role>` binds the complete role/domain/service/principal/authority/result ID/state version/digest/release nonce/source/authentication attestation and thereby strongly retains validation evidence only in the ReadyChannel ResumeCapability source arm. `ResultReleaseEvidence` is exactly `ClientRelease{receipt_ref:StrongRef<AuthenticatedClientResultReleaseReceipt<Role>>}|LeaseExpired{expiry_evidence_ref}`. Rust Drop, transport loss, QUERY_CANCEL, drain, and process/session death cannot construct it.

title: Implement flow control, TransportSendObligation, and socket write-start guards
description:
## What & scope
Implement the FGP write path below queue admission: `FlowState` credit accounting, `FLOW_CREDIT` handling, the linear `FlowReservation`, the bounded `TransportSendObligation` lifecycle, and the second linearization point `SocketWriteStartGuard`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5/B6: revocation and authority narrowing must fence unsent protected bytes even under backpressure; queue admission must never carry validity across a stall. Two nested linear guards (queue admission, write start) with no ordinary lock held across `await` give a structural argument instead of a scheduling hope.

## Design — normative detail
`FlowState` is `{key:{session_binding,stream_id,stream_generation},grant_generation,next_credit_sequence,cumulative_granted_bytes,cumulative_granted_rows,reserved_queued_bytes,reserved_queued_rows,committed_sent_bytes,committed_sent_rows,internal_debit_generation,state:Open|Closing|Closed}` with checked `available = granted - reserved - committed`. `FLOW_CREDIT` carries expected grant generation, next credit sequence, and cumulative nondecreasing byte/row totals; server debits never invalidate the client's expected grant generation; exact duplicate is idempotent; conflicting duplicate, gap, decrease, overflow, wrong stream generation, or closed stream rejects. A generated frame-cost matrix charges final encoded bytes and logical rows exactly at each row's final fragment (factorized multiplicity included; FEC symbols charge zero rows). Credits never move between streams; bounded mechanics frames use a separate control reserve.

Queue-admission guard consumption atomically copies exact authenticated frame bytes into `TransportSendObligation {session_binding,queued_auth_context_generation,frame_subject_version,frame_digest,encoded_len,logical_row_charge,frame_time_requirement_set_commitment,required_release_and_audit_commitments,flow_reservation:FlowReservation{stream_key,internal_debit_generation,reserved_encoded_bytes,reserved_logical_rows,frame_cost_rule_id},state:Queued|Writing{write_start_generation,write_start_authority_commitment,write_start_frame_time_guard_set_commitment,minimum_remaining_guard_ticks_at_start,bytes_written}|Sent{committed_encoded_bytes,committed_logical_rows}|CancelledBeforeWrite{refunded_reservation_digest}|Failed{bytes_written,consumed_reservation_digest,transport_poisoned:true}}` under the authority and FlowState CAS, then releases both queue-admission guard sets — the obligation retains the canonical requirement-set commitment, not an ephemeral guard. `SocketWriteStartGuard<Role>` is acquired only while CASing `Queued -> Writing`; it reruns the complete arm-specific authority, subject-state, audit-release, lease/capability/freshness/expiry, service-epoch, and flow checks against current rooted state. Failure before the CAS selects `CancelledBeforeWrite` and refunds without emitting bytes. Once Writing, the guard set is consumed into the one transport writer; the complete authenticated frame must reach `Sent` within the committed minimum monotonic budget. Any write failure or budget overrun after the Writing CAS — including zero bytes or a partial prefix — selects `Failed`, consumes the reservation, permanently poisons the connection, and forces close without `AUTH_REFRESHED` or a later application frame; a peer accepts only complete frames, so a partial prefix is never application-visible, and the independently retained owner resumes on a fresh connection from its canonical boundary. A narrowing/revoking refresh cancels every still-Queued old-generation obligation and waits for every Writing obligation to become Sent or Failed; it emits `AUTH_REFRESHED(new_generation)` only if all such obligations reached Sent and the transport remains usable, otherwise it closes; drain/close performs the same join. Refresh/revocation, epoch/receipt drift, subject-version change, ACK/release, audit mismatch, lease/capability expiry, flow-generation drift, or authority-generation change before write start cancels the queued frame. No guard is serialized as durable evidence; durable END-send records name the terminal Sent obligation and reconciled reservation, and every durable END-send completion byte-matches the write-start authority and full requirement-set commitments.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-16: obligations are never lost, duplicated, refunded twice, or left obligated; under declared fairness every obligation reaches one legal terminal state. FG-INV-20: write start re-verifies authorization against current rooted state — queue admission never carries validity. Flow-credit and budget parameters are configuration rows; DPOR transcripts are FG-EVID artifacts.

## Interactions
Consumes `w10-fgp-core` (guard unions, frame-class matrix), `w9-time-authority` (monotonic budgets), `w9-enforcement` (revocation fencing). Produces the write path used by `w10-result-machines`, `w10-snapshotquery`, `w10-cdc`, `w10-adapters`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
DPOR suite that blocks and fails the socket while interleaving refresh/revocation/drain/credit/expiry at: queue guard acquisition, byte-copy, reservation, queue admission, write-start guard acquisition, Queued->Writing CAS, every partial-write boundary, completion, and reconnect/resume. Property tests: reservation conservation (reserved+committed never exceeds granted; refund exactly once); poison-on-Failed with no subsequent application frame. Fuzz FLOW_CREDIT sequences (gaps, decreases, overflow, stale generations). e2e: throttled-socket run logging every obligation transition with digests; assert no protected byte written under a narrowed generation.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: budget tuning causing spurious Failed poisoning — start conservative, measure via Appendix G rows. Rejected: revalidating only at queue admission (backpressure staleness); per-byte revocation checks (cost); credit sharing across streams (priority inversion and accounting ambiguity).

## Provenance
Appendix D 2776-2786, 2802, 3084-3093.

title: Build fgdb-formats readers, the in-house Arrow IPC export writer, and fgdb-adbc
description:
## What & scope
Build `fgdb-formats`: bounded import readers (fnx legacy formats, CSV, JSONL, Parquet-lite), the in-house Arrow IPC stream export writer with its minimal FlatBuffers emitter, the `.fgdb` archive container definition, and the `fgdb-adbc` C-ABI packaging crate.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Data gravity: agents and analysts live in Arrow/ADBC ecosystems; emitting Arrow IPC without importing the `arrow` crate keeps §1's closed dependency universe intact while meeting the ecosystem where it is. B5: the canonical logical-result encoding stays the single digest target — interchange formats are registered projections, never second identities, so determinism and replay claims survive format diversity.

## Design — normative detail
Import: the declared fnx/CSV/JSONL/Parquet-lite profiles are read under explicit size, recursion, schema, and decompression limits (decoder validates declared sizes and reserves resources before allocation, mirroring `FrameLimits` discipline). Bulk ingestion feeds §7.5's canonical logical batches — readers never write storage directly. Export: the surface additionally emits Arrow IPC stream bytes written in-house — §1's closed dependency universe bans the `arrow` crate, not the wire format, so the writer carries its own minimal FlatBuffers emitter, priced like the Parquet-lite reader — as a deterministic projection of canonical result rows/columns attached to `DurableArtifactOutputKind=Export` and the HTTP bulk export endpoints. Logical result identity is unchanged: the canonical logical-result encoding remains the digest target, and Arrow IPC bytes are a registered projection format contract — a `public_format_contract_oid` value whose deterministic emission from the canonical rows is golden-vector tested — never a second logical identity. `fgdb-adbc` ships as a C-ABI packaging crate at the same boundary as `fgdb-python`; engine crates gain no new dependency. A `.fgdb` archive is a signed `BackupManifest` plus exact root/head, object inventory, base dependencies, key wraps, format/profile epochs, and transparency checkpoint; decode proofs alone do not establish backup completeness or semantic validity (§16) — completeness is the backup subsystem's claim, not the format's.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12: every claimed answer-equivalent codec/format rewrite preserves logical values, multiplicity, order, visibility, security projection, and AnswerContract — the Arrow projection must reproduce exactly the canonical rows. FG-INV-19: exported artifacts referenced by replay resolve through registered evidence slots; a projection format cannot upgrade a replay grade. Golden vectors for the Arrow writer and reader-limit fuzz corpora are FG-EVID artifacts; import limits are configuration rows; writer throughput belongs to §17/Appendix G bench rows (benchmark-class, not invariant).

## Interactions
Consumes `w1-codecs` (compression/varint primitives), `w5-determinism` (canonical result encoding as source of truth), `w10-result-machines` (Export artifact kind and delivery), `w4-bulk-ddl` (bulk manifest ingestion), `w10-embedded` (`fgdb-adbc` packages the embedded boundary). `.fgdb` container consumed by `w10-archive-open` and `w11-backup`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Golden vectors: canonical result rows -> Arrow IPC bytes byte-stable across platforms and releases; digest recorded against `public_format_contract_oid`. Round-trip differential: export via Arrow, reimport via reader, compare canonical logical rows (multiplicity/order preserved). Fuzz every reader under limit profiles: decompression bombs, recursion, schema lies — zero allocation before validation, uniform typed failures. ADBC smoke: connect from a stock ADBC client, run reads, verify results equal embedded-API results. Archive: sign/verify `BackupManifest` fixtures including tamper negatives (flipped inventory entry, stale transparency checkpoint). Logged e2e: bulk export -> ACK/release lifecycle through the artifact registry with chunk digests verified.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: hand-rolled FlatBuffers emitter drift vs. Arrow consumers — pinned golden vectors against reference readers in CI (test-only dependency, not shipped). Rejected: linking the `arrow` crate (closed-universe violation); making Arrow bytes a digest target (two logical identities); full Parquet writer in 1.0 (scope; Parquet-lite read-only suffices).

## Provenance
§13.7 (1055), §18.2, §16 (backup completeness).

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement the bounded durable protected-error delivery state machine
description:
## What & scope
Implement protected errors as their own bounded durable output machine: frozen padded manifest, disclosure class registry, semantic request owner, Protocol pending/released/active/sent-replayable/acknowledged/expired states, policy/time basis, resource escrow, send-completion bridge, same-request replay and nonrecursive mechanics failure.

## Why
Constraint/existence/authorization errors are observable data. Emitting them from an exception path can leak hidden causes, vary timing/size, lose committed error outcomes on disconnect, recursively fail, or release charges without authenticated ACK/expiry.

## Design — exact normative contract
   **Protected errors are bounded durable outputs, not an exception path.** A data-dependent error is first canonicalized to `ProtectedErrorManifest {error_format_version,public_reason:PublicReasonProjection,padded_public_fields,canonical_error_bytes,error_digest,disclosure_contract_digest,maximum_replay_window,body_digest}`. The canonical bytes contain exactly that frozen projection; `protected_error_classes.toml` maps hidden constraint/existence/authorization details to `PublicReasonProjection::Opaque{OperationDidNotComplete,...}` unless the bundle carries the exact portable receipt for one registered disclosed code. No internal reason class, policy counter, existence fact, or raw digest is serialized. Semantic `ProtectedErrorRequestRecord<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` stores only `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,request_key_digest,error_manifest_ref:StrongRef<ProtectedErrorManifest>,delivery_policy_ref:StrongRef<ProtectedErrorDeliveryPolicy<Role>>,semantic_resource_transition_ref,audit_gate_commitment,detachment_commitment}`. `ProtectedErrorActiveCommon<Role>` is `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,request_key_digest,error_delivery_id,delivery_state_version,error_digest,disclosure_contract_digest,semantic_detachment_identity,nonretaining_predecessor_digest}`; `ProtectedErrorTerminalCommon<Role>` replaces the header with `terminal_authority_commitment:TerminalAuthorityCommitment<Role>` and retains only terminal/public identities. The same publication creates `ProtectedErrorResourceEscrow<Role>` and Protocol `ProtectedErrorDeliveryRecord<Role> = PendingVisibility{common:ProtectedErrorActiveCommon<Role>,manifest_ref,policy_ref,escrow_ref,audit_gate_commitment}|ReleasedAwaitingActivation{common:ProtectedErrorActiveCommon<Role>,manifest_ref,policy_ref,escrow_ref,audit_release_evidence,release_maintenance_ref}|ActiveDeliverable{common:ProtectedErrorActiveCommon<Role>,manifest_ref,lease_time_basis_ref,lease_generation,sender_generation,escrow_ref}|SentReplayable{common:ProtectedErrorActiveCommon<Role>,send_completion_ref:StrongRef<ProtectedErrorSendCompletionRecord>,replay_time_basis_ref:StrongRef<ProtectedErrorReplayTimeBasis<Role>>,escrow_ref}|Acknowledged{common:ProtectedErrorTerminalCommon<Role>,ack_commitment,escrow_disposition_commitment}|Expired{common:ProtectedErrorTerminalCommon<Role>,expiry_evidence_commitment,escrow_disposition_commitment}`. Pending/released states have no clock or send authority; SentReplayable owns the exact profiled replay basis rather than a raw `replay_until`. Terminal arms retain no manifest, lease, replay basis, escrow, or live authority edge. `ProtectedErrorDeliveryIndex<Role>` indexes both request key and delivery ID, so exact request retry returns the same padded public error while a conflicting request digest fails uniformly. Audit visibility only releases; independent activation installs a fresh bounded lease. `ProtectedErrorSendCompletionRecord` is the durable maintenance bridge from the exact ephemeral `TransportSendObligation::Sent` transcript to SentReplayable. `ERROR_ACK` or profiled expiry alone disposes escrow; socket loss, cancellation, drain, and Rust Drop do not. Errors have no fifth durable capability: replay requires the original scoped request key under a fresh same-principal Ready binding, exact current disclosure authority, and fresh `TimeValidationEvidence::Usable` for the retained replay basis. A failure in this delivery path closes or returns a fixed protocol-mechanics failure and never recursively creates another protected error.

## Invariants & interactions
Enforces FG-INV-16 and FG-INV-20. Consumes disclosure/noninterference policy, audit release/activation, authority binding, resource/time/send obligations and public projections. It shares generic delivery mechanics with result machines but has no durable resume capability and distinct terminal arms.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Exact rows/codecs cover manifest/classes, request, active/terminal common, delivery/index, policy/time/replay basis, escrow/disposition, send completion, ACK and expiry.
- Golden/unit tests freeze padded bytes/reason mapping/digests and every state/reference rule.
- Differential noninterference proves hidden causes map to byte-identical public bytes/timing class unless an exact portable disclosure receipt authorizes one code.
- Property/DPOR proves pending/released no send authority, one SentReplayable transcript, socket/cancel/Drop no disposition, only ERROR_ACK or profiled expiry releases escrow, and delivery failures never recurse.
- Fuzz rejects internal reasons/counters/digests, wrong receipt/profile/principal/state, raw replay_until, result/artifact arm substitution and malformed padding.
- E2E triggers all registered hidden classes, stalls audit/time, loses connection after send, retries same scoped key under fresh Ready binding, ACKs/expires and restarts at every phase.
- JSONL emits {event_version,request_key_digest,error_delivery_id,public_reason_class,disclosure_profile,from_state,to_state,state_version,error_digest,byte_length,timing_class,send_completion_digest?,ack_or_expiry?,escrow_state,recovery_action,replay_command}; hidden reason, protected fields and raw error bytes never logged.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: exception-path emission, plaintext hidden causes, recursive protected errors, general Resume capability, raw replay deadline, and socket close as ACK. Fixed mechanics failure may close a connection by design.

## Provenance
Plan section 13.2 line 1023 and Appendix D.

title: Build fgdb-python: map the ownership contract onto Python idiom explicitly
description:
## What & scope
Build `fgdb-python` on the allowed `fnx-python` binding boundary: context managers, iterator semantics, the `__del__`-equals-Drop rule, ResourceWarning surfacing, the short-expiry profile, NumPy view pinning, and Jupyter/asyncio guidance.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Python is the agent-framework lingua franca (B6). The classic failure mode — finalizers silently rolling back transactions or leaking cursors — is replaced by an explicit mapping: Python idiom is made to express the Rust ownership contract rather than accidentally subvert it. No PyO3 in engine crates keeps the durable/runtime layers isolated from ABI churn.

## Design — normative detail
`fgdb-python` consumes the allowed `fnx-python` binding boundary rather than adding PyO3 directly to engine crates; ABI3/NumPy support remains isolated from durable/runtime layers. The ownership mapping is explicit, never by finalizer accident: (1) context managers perform explicit authenticated `release()`/`finish()` on `__exit__` for sessions, transactions, and result streams — never in `__del__`; (2) iterator exhaustion IS `finish()` and emits ACK after complete consumption; (3) `__del__`/GC finalization is defined as exactly Rust `Drop` — local structured cancellation and sender detachment with no durable release authority — with the documented consequence that an abandoned result or cursor lives to profiled expiry holding its retention and escrow, surfaced as a debug-mode `ResourceWarning` and a doctor/metrics counter rather than a silent leak; (4) embedded and interactive sessions default to a documented short-expiry result-retention profile; (5) a claimed NumPy view is zero-copy only for matching contiguous authorized buffers and otherwise returns an explicit copy; the view pins its authorized buffer through the ordinary cursor/borrow rule and releases that pin on view drop; (6) a GC-abandoned open transaction terminates through the ordinary `TxnOwnershipExpiryAbortSpec<Local>` ownership-lease expiry abort — never through a finalizer-invented rollback; (7) Jupyter and asyncio consumers get explicit with-block and `aclose()` guidance in the binding documentation.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-15: `__del__`/GC cannot construct release evidence; abandoned owners survive to profiled expiry. FG-INV-16: the GC-abandoned transaction path is exactly the registered expiry abort — complete cancellation/terminalization evidence, legal only before PrepareFenced. The short-expiry profile value and ResourceWarning policy are configuration rows; binding-parity transcripts are FG-EVID artifacts.

## Interactions
Consumes `w10-embedded` (the API being bound), `w10-result-machines` (finish/release semantics), `w8-fnx-upstream` (fnx-python boundary work). Surfaced counters feed `obs-doctor`/`obs-observatory`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Behavior tests under CPython GC: abandon a partially consumed cursor -> ResourceWarning in debug mode, doctor counter increments, bytes resumable until expiry, no ACK emitted. Iterator exhaustion emits exactly one ACK (idempotent under double-exhaust). `with` blocks: exception inside block still performs authenticated release/finish; `__exit__` failure surfaces, never swallows. NumPy: contiguity/authorization matrix — zero-copy only on exact match, explicit copy otherwise; view lifetime pins buffer (use-after-free fuzz under gc.collect()). Abandoned-transaction e2e: open txn, drop all references, force GC, assert lease-expiry abort path in logs (no finalizer rollback frames). asyncio/Jupyter smoke tests with `aclose()`.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: users perceive expiry-held resources as leaks — mitigated by warnings, counters, short default profile. Rejected: finalizer-driven release/rollback (unauthorized, nondeterministic ordering under interpreter shutdown); PyO3 in engine crates (ABI coupling); implicit zero-copy with silent aliasing (authorization bypass).

## Provenance
§13.1 (992), §18.1 (`fgdb-python`).

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement QoS admission: ResourceVector reservations and ResourceLedgerState quotas
description:
## What & scope
Implement the QoS/admission plane separating ephemeral runtime reservations from durable quota state: the hierarchical `ResourceVector`, obligation-scoped reservation/release, the Chronicle-sequenced `ResourceLedgerState`, capsule-coupled charges, emergency reserves, and the hedging rules.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6: multi-tenant agent workloads are bursty and adversarial-adjacent; admission must be enforced before work, and durable footprint (branches, indexes, views, subscriptions, history) must be charged transactionally so crash recovery can never separate an object from its quota charge. This is also the enforcement point for §16's noisy-neighbor story.

## Design — normative detail
A hierarchical `ResourceVector { cpu_ns, resident_bytes, temp_bytes, durable_bytes, read_iops, write_iops, egress_bytes, output_bytes, output_rows, snapshot_age, branch/index/view/subscription counts, subscription_backlog }` is reserved before transient work and released by obligation — no fire-and-forget accounting. Durable bytes/branches/indexes/views/subscriptions/history are enforced by an authoritative Chronicle-sequenced `ResourceLedgerState`; every create/grow/delete/expiry carries a `ResourceReservationId` plus canonical `ResourceChargeEffect`/release in the same final capsule as the durable object change (§5.2), so concurrent sessions serialize quota validation with publication and crash recovery replays charge and object atomically. Maintenance has protected emergency reserves (compaction/scrub/audit can always make progress). Hedging is allowed only within ephemeral reservations and never chooses strict logical order by wall-clock race; DP work forbids independent hedges entirely (a second execution would consume privacy budget or reveal timing). Connection admission (§13.2) composes semaphore + rate-limit combinators ahead of session creation. Result/output escrow interplay: independently retained outputs hold escrowed charges (see `w10-result-machines`); expiry/ACK disposal releases them through the same ledger.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-16: no resource hold or escrow is lost, duplicated, refunded, or released while obligated; under declared fairness every hold reaches a legal terminal. FG-INV-02: escrow custody is a disjoint exhaustive partition with finite-side conservation equations at every transition; only registered transitions mint or burn rights. FG-INV-07/§5.2: charge and object change ride one capsule. Quota values and reserve sizes are configuration rows; conservation-equation checks are Lean-lane/oracle FG-EVID artifacts; admission latencies belong to Appendix G rows.

## Interactions
Consumes `w1-foundation-types` (`fgdb-resource`), `w2-commit-protocol` (capsule coupling), `w2-txn-lifecycle` (per-attempt reservations). Consumed by `w10-server` (connection admission), `w10-fgp-core` (resource_request fields on BEGIN/EXECUTE/EXPORT), `w10-result-machines` (escrow), Ripple/Beacon builders for durable footprint charges. Observed via `obs-slo` attribution.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Property: reservation conservation per vector dimension under randomized concurrent admit/release/crash (no negative available, no orphaned holds after recovery). Crash matrix: kill between reservation, capsule submit, and publication — recovery yields charge-and-object atomicity (both or neither). Ledger serialization test: two sessions racing the last quota unit — exactly one wins at publication. Hedging tests: hedged read never determines commit order (inject wall-clock skew); DP-labeled work refuses hedge admission. e2e: tenant-quota exhaustion script logging admission decisions, ledger sequence numbers, and emergency-reserve maintenance progress under saturation.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: ledger becomes a hot spot — mitigated by hierarchical ephemeral reservations with only durable-footprint changes sequenced. Rejected: best-effort metering with async reconciliation (crash divergence between object and charge); wall-clock hedge racing for ordered operations (nondeterminism, B5 violation); global locks for quota (serializes unrelated tenants).

## Provenance
§13.6 (1054), §13.2 (993), §5.2 coupling.

title: Implement replay execution and exact wire-safe public projection bundles
description:
## What & scope
Implement exact replay-execution indexing/ownership and all wire-safe public projection/bundle schemas: replay handle lifecycle, PublicProjectionDomain/handles/tokens/commitments, disclosure receipts, marker/logical/snapshot/result/digest/reason projections, graph/RYW sets, terminal/never-registered/merge bundles, RYW issuance and frozen response construction.

## Why
Internal ObjectIds, counters and replay manifests are not wire selectors. Public bytes must be prebuilt under a scoped projection domain, survive reconnect/compaction exactly, resist dictionary/correlation attacks, and never be recomputed differently after policy change. Replay execution must use the ordinary result owner, not an ad-hoc stream.

## Design — exact normative contract
   Internal `ReplayManifest` ObjectIds are never wire selectors. `ReplayPublicHandleRecord<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is state-shaped: `Active{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,replay_handle:OpaquePublicNonce,manifest_ref:StrongRef<ReplayManifest>,disclosure_contract_digest,handle_generation,created_at_role_command_seq}|Revoked{terminal_authority_commitment:TerminalAuthorityCommitment<Role>,replay_handle,terminal_generation,revocation_commitment}|Expired{terminal_authority_commitment:TerminalAuthorityCommitment<Role>,replay_handle,terminal_generation,expiry_evidence_commitment}`. Terminal arms retain no manifest, executable/archive evidence, replay bytes, verifier, or live authority edge. It is indexed by `ReplayRegistry`; every active use reauthorizes the opaque handle and emits only a typed `PublicReplayManifestProjection` through the artifact-output registry. Replay execution is separate: `ReplayExecutionIndex<Role>` uniqueness-serializes its request and `ReplayExecutionRecord` owns execution state under its own full header. Its query output uses the ordinary result owner arm `ReplayExecution{registration_ref,publication_applied_ref}`, result manifest, independent retention, resume, ACK, and release machinery—never an ad hoc stream or the artifact-output registry. Public replay evidence contains commitments only and cannot expose a DP seed.

   **Wire-safe public types.** Incoming graph selection is `WireGraphReferenceSpec {client_binding_ordinal,graph_selector,branch_selector,system_time_selector,valid_time_selector,required_public_schema_contract}`. Every opaque value is built under `PublicProjectionDomain {database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch,posture,principal_scope_commitment,non_widenable_authority_commitment,projection_key_epoch}`. `PublicHandle<Kind>` is a pre-minted random 128-bit nonce plus a domain-separated MAC over domain/kind/nonce; it is never derived from an ObjectId, marker, counter, name, or low-entropy hidden fact. `PublicStateToken<Kind>` is a separately pre-minted random CAS nonce plus the same scoped MAC for one externally addressable state transition; it is not a serialized internal generation/version. `OpaquePublicCommitment<Kind>` is `PRF(projection_key, "fgdb:opaque:" || domain || kind || per_subject_random_salt || canonical_internal_subject_commitment)` and therefore cannot be used as an offline dictionary or cross-principal/cross-epoch correlation oracle. Replay retains the exact bytes and verifier-key floor; key rotation never recomputes a live public token.

   The sole portable field-declassification proof is `PortablePublicDisclosureReceipt {receipt_version,projection_domain_commitment,disclosure_profile_oid,stable_projection_subject_commitment,allowed_public_field_bitmap,receipt_free_projection_digest,signer_id,signing_key_id,signer_epoch,signature}`. Its signature covers every preceding field and the digest of the **receipt-free** projection body, never itself. It contains no session/Ready binding, local reference, state root, topology identity, policy/revocation counter, or internal position, so frozen bytes survive reconnect and compaction. The later `PublicFrameSendGuard` separately binds those stable bytes to the current Ready/session/auth generation immediately before write.

   The closed public projections are posture-tagged and noninterchangeable: `PublicMarkerProjection = Local|Sharded{handle:PublicHandle<Marker>,commitment:OpaquePublicCommitment<Marker>,disclosure:Opaque|Disclosed{public_comparison_domain:PublicHandle<CommitComparisonDomain>,public_ordinal,receipt}}`; `PublicLogicalPositionProjection = Local|Sharded{handle:PublicHandle<LogicalPosition>,commitment:OpaquePublicCommitment<LogicalPosition>,disclosure:Opaque|Disclosed{axis:LocalLogical|GlobalLogical,public_comparison_domain:PublicHandle<LogicalComparisonDomain>,public_ordinal,receipt}}`; `PublicSnapshotProjection = Local|Sharded{snapshot_handle:PublicHandle<Snapshot>,snapshot_commitment:OpaquePublicCommitment<Snapshot>,logical_position:PublicLogicalPositionProjection,normalized_valid_time_projection,selector_echo_commitment,receipt:None|Some{PortablePublicDisclosureReceipt}}`; and `PublicResultOwnerProjection = Local|Sharded{owner_handle:PublicHandle<ResultOwner>,owner_commitment:OpaquePublicCommitment<ResultOwner>,disclosure:Opaque|Disclosed{owner_class:TerminalRead|AutocommitWriteTerminal|Statement|DpResult|ReplayExecution,receipt}}`. A disclosed ordinal exists only in a registered public comparison domain/epoch with an authenticated server-side map and retention floor; otherwise v1 emits Opaque.

   Digest projections have distinct wire tags and transcripts: `PublicEffectProjection`, `PublicPublicationProjection`, `PublicResultDigestProjection`, and `PublicOutputDigestProjection` are each `Omitted{commitment:OpaquePublicCommitment<ExactKind>}|Disclosed{digest_of_authorized_public_bytes,receipt}`. A disclosed digest is recomputed from the registered authorized public transcript, never copied from an internal final-effect, publication-chain, result-manifest, or storage digest; cross-kind substitution fails decoding. `PublicReasonProjection` is `Opaque{coarse_class:OperationDidNotComplete,reason_commitment:OpaquePublicCommitment<Reason>}|Disclosed{public_reason_code:RegisteredPublicReasonCode,reason_commitment,receipt}`. `protected_error_classes.toml` maps every hidden constraint/existence/authorization cause to the Opaque arm unless the receipt permits one exact public code, with padded byte/timing classes and differential noninterference tests. `StablePublicReasonClass` and generic `PublicDigestProjection` are invalid types.

   `PublicEffectiveSnapshotSet` is `{set_handle:PublicHandle<SnapshotSet>,sorted_bindings[{client_binding_ordinal,graph_binding_handle,branch_handle,effective_snapshot:PublicSnapshotProjection}],set_commitment}`; `PublicRywFloorSet` is `{set_handle:PublicHandle<RywFloorSet>,visibility_floor:PublicLogicalPositionProjection,sorted_branch_floors[{client_binding_ordinal,graph_handle,branch_handle,head:PublicMarkerProjection}],set_commitment}`. Arrays are unique and sorted by client binding ordinal. Outgoing graph selection is `PublicGraphBindingProjection {public_binding_role_id,graph_handle,branch_handle,effective_snapshot:PublicSnapshotProjection,public_schema_contract_digest,disclosure_decision_digest}`; normalized valid time has exactly one owner inside the snapshot. `PublicMarkerSelector` is a capability-safe handle plus expected marker commitment backed by the server's retained mapping/floor; a display commitment alone cannot select a merge basis.

   Signed/random public artifacts are prebuilt, never invented by deterministic apply. `TerminalPublicProjectionBundle<Role>` is `{role,internal_terminal_descriptor_digest,authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,receipt_free_terminal_core,receipt_free_projection_digest,portable_disclosure_receipt,frozen_public_progress_bytes,frozen_terminal_outcome_bytes,prebuilt_result_capability_commitments[],prebuilt_read_your_writes_issuance_ref?,original_response_commitment,bundle_digest}`. It remains a byte-owning, capability-gated live object even though its internal subject is terminal, so a `TerminalAuthorityCommitment` is insufficient until later compaction removes every protected byte and replay promise. The non-self-referential response commitment covers version, frozen terminal core, and listed prebuilt capability commitments, excluding itself and later audit/send evidence. `NeverRegisteredPublicProjectionBundle<Role>` and `MergePublicProjectionBundle<Role>` use the same shape with their exact internal subject. Construction is internal subject + pre-minted handles/salts -> receipt-free public body -> digest -> signed portable receipt -> frozen bytes -> bundle -> semantic completion/publication input. Apply only byte-matches and installs. Detailed values and compact summaries retain/copy the same frozen bytes and receipt; current authority either permits them exactly or returns uniform `NotVisibleOrUnknown`, never recomputes a redacted variant.

   `ReadYourWritesSubjectBasis<Role>` is `Local{registration_ref,terminal_marker_ref:StrongMarkerRef,exact_visible_logical_floor,sorted_written_branch_heads[StrongMarkerRef],retention_floor_ref,authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>,public_floor_set_digest}|Meta{registration_ref,terminal_global_marker_ref:StrongMarkerRef,exact_visible_global_floor,sorted_written_branch_heads[StrongMarkerRef],retention_floor_ref,authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Meta>,public_floor_set_digest}`. `ReadYourWritesIssuanceBundle<Role>` owns that basis, one `PublicRywFloorSet`, the prebuilt capability replay record/canonical bytes, and their byte-match proof. A RYW capability therefore has an exact internal wait/retention subject even when every public position is opaque.

## Invariants & interactions
Enforces FG-INV-15, FG-INV-19, FG-INV-20. Consumes replay manifests/registry, authority bindings, result-owner registry, crypto/time verifier floors and disclosure policy. Wire projections, result machines, FGP, status, compaction, backup/restore and W12 public formats consume it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Exact rows/codecs cover ReplayPublicHandleRecord, ReplayExecutionIndex/Record, every projection/handle/token/commitment alias, disclosure receipt, graph/floor set, three public bundles, RYW subject/issuance, construction order and retention floor.
- Unit/golden tests freeze opaque and disclosed bytes, receipt-free digests, signatures/MACs, non-self-referential response commitments, detailed/compacted equality and handle/key rotation behavior.
- Property/security tests prove no internal selector, no cross-principal/epoch/kind correlation, current same-or-narrower authorization, frozen bytes preserved, terminal bundle live authority until protected bytes compact, and replay output through ordinary retention.
- Mutation/fuzz rejects ObjectId/counter/ref leakage, wrong projection domain/kind/receipt/bitmap, self-including digest, policy recomputation, stale handle, role substitution and DP seed/protected evidence exposure.
- E2E creates opaque/disclosed terminal, never-registered, merge and replay/RYW artifacts; reconnects, compacts, rotates keys/policy, restores and replays while bytes remain identical or lookup is uniformly NotVisibleOrUnknown.
- JSONL emits {event_version,projection_domain_digest,projection_kind,subject_handle_commitment,disclosure_mode,receipt_digest?,bundle_kind?,bundle_digest?,response_commitment?,replay_handle_state?,replay_execution_state?,result_delivery_id?,authorization_relation,recovery_action,replay_command}; no raw handles, internal refs/counters or hidden bodies.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: ObjectId selectors, hash-of-hidden-fact handles, generic public digest types, recomputing redacted bytes, TerminalAuthorityCommitment while protected bundle bytes remain, and artifact-output delivery for replay execution results.

## Provenance
Plan section 13.2 lines 1031-1045 and Appendix D.

title: Build the shared protected-output delivery kernel and ordinary result integration
description:
## What & scope
Implement the three durable protected-output owners and their Protocol state machines: query/statement results (including `AutocommitWriteTerminal`), durable artifact outputs (`Export|ReplayManifestProjection|ProofBundle`), and protected errors — plus ACK/release/resume transitions, release evidence, replay handles, and the Drop-cannot-release law.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6/B5: an agent's result must survive its process. Independent retention with explicit ACK/release makes delivery an owned, evidence-carrying obligation instead of a socket side effect; protected errors as bounded durable outputs close the classic side channel where error paths bypass release discipline.

## Design — normative detail
Result lifecycle: `Accepted -> Bound -> Registered -> Executing -> Buffered -> PublicationSubmitted -> PendingVisibility|Deliverable -> SenderAttached|SenderPaused -> IndependentlyRetained -> Acknowledged|ReleasedUnacked`; sender state is not durable disposition. For `Autocommit{ReadWrite,WriteReturning}` the buffered manifest owner is the distinct posture-valid `AutocommitWriteTerminal`; prepared ownership retains it through prepare/commit/audit; no streamable result lease exists until the semantic commit is TerminalReady, the exact terminal audit outcome is released through the gap-free Protocol visibility advance, the Local/Global delta and durability postconditions are satisfied, and an exact independently retained delivery lease is installed by inline or independent activation. Commit completion never waits for client ACK; ACK/release only discharges the independent result promise. `RESULT_BEGIN` carries `{result_delivery_handle,delivery_state_token,owner:PublicResultOwnerProjection,result_resume_capability,read_release_authorization:ReadReleaseAuthorizationEvidence,audit_release:AuditReleaseEvidence,schema,result_answer_contract,canonical_encoding_version,result_digest,total_chunks,total_len,replay_manifest_projection?}`; chunks/END carry the canonical-chunk encoding; ACK is legal only after the matching END transcript (`RESULT_ACK{...,complete_result_end_transcript_digest,client_ack_nonce}`); `RESULT_ACKED` returns `capability_disposition:Rotated{resume_capability}|Consumed{consumption_proof}`. Rotation is ordered via `ResultCapabilityLineage {current_replay_ref,current_commitment,generation,immediate_predecessor:None|LiveUntilSuccessorAcknowledgedOrSubjectTerminal{replay_ref,consuming_request_digest}|Compacted{commitment,request_digest,tombstone_ref}}`; RotateForResume/ACK/Release/expiry CAS the same type-specific active state token; exact immediate-predecessor retry reproduces the successor; the acyclic order is manifest -> released owner/policy -> fresh time basis/evidence -> capability replay object -> protocol activation/transition -> applied lease/retention -> protocol index/root.

Artifact outputs: `DurableArtifactOutputKind=Export|ReplayManifestProjection|ProofBundle`; `DurableArtifactOutputRequestKey {database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch,posture,tenant,principal,non_widenable_authority_digest,kind,scoped_idempotency_key,canonical_request_digest}` — reusing the scoped key with any body/domain/authority drift fails before source observation or charge. `DurableArtifactOutputManifest {format_version,kind,public_format_contract_oid,public_scope_projection,disclosure_contract_digest,canonical_encoding_version,byte_count,ordered_chunks[CanonicalResultChunkDescriptor],canonical_output_digest,source_retention_refs[],resource_charge_ref,body_digest}`. Semantic `ArtifactOutputRequestRecord<Role>` is `Reserved{authority_bound_header,source_pins,resource_reservations}|MaterializedDetached{authority_bound_header,manifest_ref,output_delivery_id,delivery_policy_ref,audit_gate_commitment,detachment_commitment}|FailedDetached{terminal_authority_commitment,protected_error_key,public_error_commitment,audit_gate_commitment}` and never stores a delivery lease, capability, ACK, release, or protocol-record ref. Protocol `ArtifactOutputDeliveryRecord<Role>` is exactly `PendingVisibility{common,manifest_ref,policy_ref,escrow_ref,audit_gate_commitment}|ReleasedAwaitingActivation{common,manifest_ref,policy_ref,escrow_ref,audit_release_evidence,release_maintenance_ref}|ActiveDeliverable{common,manifest_ref,lease_time_basis_ref,lease_generation,capability_lineage_ref,escrow_ref,sender_generation}|Acknowledged{common:Terminal,ack_commitment,capability_tombstone_ref,escrow_disposition_commitment}|ReleasedUnacked{common:Terminal,release_or_expiry_commitment,capability_tombstone_ref,escrow_disposition_commitment}`; audit visibility changes PendingVisibility only to ReleasedAwaitingActivation; independent activation supplies a fresh `ArtifactOutputLeaseTimeBasis<Role>`, exact time evidence, and a prebuilt generation-zero `ResumeCapabilityReplayRecord`; pending/released states have no time window/capability and emit neither READY nor bytes; terminal arms retain no strong authority, manifest, lease, payload, capability replay, escrow, or predecessor edge; Local/Meta payloads root only the semantic registry, `RootManifest`'s protocol state roots only the delivery index.

Protected errors: `ProtectedErrorManifest {error_format_version,public_reason:PublicReasonProjection,padded_public_fields,canonical_error_bytes,error_digest,disclosure_contract_digest,maximum_replay_window,body_digest}`; `protected_error_classes.toml` maps hidden constraint/existence/authorization causes to `PublicReasonProjection::Opaque{OperationDidNotComplete,...}` unless the bundle carries the exact portable receipt for one registered disclosed code. `ProtectedErrorDeliveryRecord<Role> = PendingVisibility|ReleasedAwaitingActivation|ActiveDeliverable|SentReplayable{common,send_completion_ref:StrongRef<ProtectedErrorSendCompletionRecord>,replay_time_basis_ref,escrow_ref}|Acknowledged|Expired`; SentReplayable owns the exact profiled replay basis, never a raw `replay_until`; `ERROR_ACK` or profiled expiry alone disposes escrow — socket loss, cancellation, drain, and Rust Drop do not. Errors have no fifth durable capability: replay requires the original scoped request key under a fresh same-principal Ready binding, exact current disclosure authority, and fresh `TimeValidationEvidence::Usable`; exact retry returns the same padded public error, conflicting digests fail uniformly; a failure in this path closes or returns a fixed protocol-mechanics failure — never recursively another protected error.

Release evidence: `ClientResultReleaseAuthority = Fgp{presented_resume_capability_commitment,session_binding,auth_context_generation,request_frame_digest}|Embedded{stream_release_token_commitment,host_session_generation,explicit_release_call_digest}|Bolt{bolt_session_binding,qid,request_kind:DISCARD|RESET,request_message_digest}`; `ResultReleaseEvidence` is exactly `ClientRelease{receipt_ref:StrongRef<AuthenticatedClientResultReleaseReceipt<Role>>}|LeaseExpired{expiry_evidence_ref}` — Rust Drop, transport loss, QUERY_CANCEL, drain, and process/session death cannot construct it. `QUERY_CANCEL` controls computation and the current sender only; after independent retention it can only durably pause that session's sender after joining transport obligations. ACK/release are themselves ordered role commands, not in-memory cursor updates: Local dispatch orders `LocalResultDeliveryTransitionSpec` — the Local Maintenance `Acknowledge|ReleaseUnacked` union with exact owner/manifest/lease/ActiveDeliverable/digest/prior-state/escrow/audit fields, where Acknowledge requires `AuthenticatedClientResultAckReceipt<Local>` and release requires role-valid release/expiry evidence; apply creates one ACK/release record, the terminal retention successor, and the protocol escrow disposition, never changes a semantic payload or delivery frontier (the semantic command already detached that frontier), and before terminal publication fences the sender generation, cancels Queued frames, and joins Writing frames. Sharded dispatch orders the same transitions through `GlobalResultDeliveryTransitionSpec` with Meta outcome/directory types (Appendix D 3110's Local/Sharded dispatch parity). Replay handles: `ReplayPublicHandleRecord<Role>` is `Active{authority_bound_header,replay_handle:OpaquePublicNonce,manifest_ref,disclosure_contract_digest,handle_generation,created_at_role_command_seq}|Revoked{...}|Expired{...}`; replay execution uses `ReplayExecutionIndex<Role>` plus the ordinary result owner arm `ReplayExecution{registration_ref,publication_applied_ref}` — never an ad hoc stream.

Delivery frames and the coded transfer path: `EXPORT_ACCEPTED`/`REPLAY_ACCEPTED` name the canonical request and output-request handle; artifact BEGIN/CHUNK/END frames carry a typed public delivery handle/state token, a Resume capability only in ActiveDeliverable, and the public projection digest — never internal refs. `REPLAY_GET{request_key,replay_handle,requested_projection}` retrieves `PublicReplayManifestProjection`; `REPLAY_EXECUTE{request_key,replay_handle,requested_projection,fetch,resource_request}` returns `REPLAY_EXECUTE_ACCEPTED` then uses ordinary result frames. FGP's optional forward-error-corrected delivery is a distinct wire schema, never the at-rest storage types: `FEC_BEGIN` carries `PublicFecTransferDescriptor`; `FEC_SYMBOL` carries `WireFecSymbolRecord`, MACed with the channel-exporter-derived `K_wire_symbol` and verified against the transfer descriptor before admission; `FEC_END` carries `{transfer_id,descriptor_digest,emitted_symbol_count,transfer_digest}`. Reconnect creates a new transfer descriptor/key over the same public output digest — a transfer never resumes under an old channel key. `WireFecSymbolRecord` is a channel-bound transfer record; the at-rest `SymbolRecord`, `CiphertextId`, `EncodingId`, `PlacementDescriptor`, object DEKs, and placement metadata remain forbidden wire types (enforced by w10-wire-projections' taint checker). Compression/FEC is negotiated only after authenticated public metadata and resource reservation (`FrameLimits` bounds FEC symbols and reserves before decoding — w10-fgp-core); FEC symbols charge zero logical rows in the generated flow-cost matrix (w10-flow-send-obligations).

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-15 (verbatim core): every result-producing feature uses one generated, noninterchangeable owner arm and the state-shaped independent-retention machine: PendingVisibility and ReleasedAwaitingActivation retain manifest/policy/resource escrow, ActiveDeliverable additionally owns lease/replay/send authority, and ACK or explicit authenticated release/expiry atomically installs compact terminal evidence with no strong bulk predecessor; QUERY_CANCEL, Drop, disconnect, drain, and process death cannot release it; resume/ACK/release/expiry CAS one delivery version with deterministic immediate-predecessor retry. FG-INV-14: active owners are GC roots until exact terminal transfer/release. FG-INV-16: escrow disposed exactly once. FG-INV-20: pre-visibility observation forbidden. Padded error byte/timing classes carry differential-noninterference FG-EVID artifacts; expiry profiles are configuration rows.

## Interactions
Consumes `w9-audit-release` (visibility advance evidence), `w9-activation-batching` (ProtectedOutput activation/disposition batches), `w2-fused-autocommit` (fused arm interplay), `w5-determinism` (canonical result encoding/chunking), `w10-capabilities` (Resume lineage), `w10-flow-send-obligations` (send bridge). Consumed by `w10-embedded`, `w10-python`, `w10-bolt`, `w10-adapters`, `w10-formats` (Export kind), `w10-cdc`, `w10-server`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Generated owner/state reachability checker: every arm reachable, no undeclared transition. DPOR: result release/resume/ACK/expiry and sender-death interleavings; assert Drop/disconnect/drain never constructs `ResultReleaseEvidence`. Local/Sharded dispatch-parity fixtures: the same ACK/release request produces equivalent terminal evidence through `LocalResultDeliveryTransitionSpec` and `GlobalResultDeliveryTransitionSpec`. Crash matrix at each arm boundary (publication, visibility, activation, send-completion bridge, ACK) with recovery to the exact same state. Idempotency: duplicate ACK/RELEASE/ERROR_ACK returns recorded disposition; conflicting artifact request key fails before observation/charge. Differential noninterference: hidden causes produce byte-identical padded errors and timing within declared envelope. e2e: kill-and-resume script across all three owners logging every state transition, escrow disposition, and capability rotation. FEC transfer tests: symbol MAC key separation — a symbol MACed under another channel's exporter key or another transfer's descriptor rejects before admission; cross-type negative fixture — at-rest `SymbolRecord` bytes fail to decode as `WireFecSymbolRecord`; reconnect mid-transfer mints a fresh descriptor/`K_wire_symbol` and the resumed delivery re-derives from the canonical output boundary with a byte-identical reassembled `canonical_output_digest`; `FEC_END` counts/digests must match the descriptor commitments or the transfer fails closed with no partial-result claim. DETAILED LOGGING: the implementation logs every state transition of all three owners `{owner_kind, delivery_id, from_arm, to_arm, state_version, escrow_disposition?, capability_generation?}`, every release-evidence construction `{source_arm: ClientRelease|LeaseExpired, receipt_or_expiry_ref}`, every FEC transfer `{transfer_id, descriptor_digest, emitted_symbol_count, reconnect_generation}`, and per-frame send-guard consumption; the kill-and-resume e2e and the FEC e2e (export a multi-chunk artifact over FEC, kill the connection mid-transfer, reconnect, complete, ACK) assert the presence and field-completeness of these log events and assert the logged reassembly digest equals `canonical_output_digest`.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: escrow leakage under crash storms — covered by FG-INV-14/16 oracles. Rejected: socket-owned exports (lost on disconnect); error-as-exception (leaks and unbounded retention); a durable error capability (fifth kind rejected — scoped-key replay suffices); commit-waits-for-ACK (couples durability to client liveness).

## Provenance
§13.3 (992, 1017-1023, 1031), Appendix D 2770, 2792, 2796-2798, 2833 (export/replay acceptance and FEC frames), 2886-2912, 3063-3069, 3090-3093 (FEC frame schemas), 3094-3102, 3110 (delivery-transition dispatch), 3116 (wire/at-rest FEC separation); App A 1496 (`LocalResultDeliveryTransitionSpec`); §13.3 line 1047.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

The exact ReadyChannel/Embedded result completion, ACK, resume, and release-authority schemas below are runtime obligations of this Bead and supersede the older Fgp|Embedded|Bolt source union.

`AuthenticatedClientResultReleaseReceipt<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is the immutable pre-release proof `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,session_authorization_ref:StrongRef<SessionAuthorizationRecord<Role>>,auth_context_generation,session_binding,public_authority_commitment,posture_and_role:Local|Meta,result_owner_identity,result_delivery_id,expected_active_delivery_state_version,expected_active_retention_digest,request_id,stream_id,strictly_monotone_release_nonce,source:ClientResultReleaseAuthority,canonical_release_request_digest,server_process_incarnation,accepted_child_state_version,server_signing_key_epoch,signature}`. The public commitment is a redundant integrity projection of the full header/session record, never a substitute. It is created only after an explicit ReadyChannel `RESULT_RELEASE` equivalent, embedded `release()`, or Bolt V1/V2 DISCARD/RESET request passes current-epoch authentication, nonreplay, exact owner/delivery/state, and same-or-narrower authority checks. Duplicate request bytes reproduce the same receipt; nonce, source, body, authority, or state drift fails.
`ResultEndSendCompletionRecord` is the immutable durable bridge from ephemeral channel transport to result ACK: `{surface:NativeFgp|Http2|Grpc|WebSocket,authority_binding_public_commitment,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch,session_binding,server_process_incarnation,sender_generation,result_owner_identity,result_delivery_id,delivery_state_version,resume_capability_commitment,surface_terminal_frame_and_canonical_fgp_result_end_digest,complete_canonical_byte_length,canonical_result_digest,flow_reservation_identity,flow_bytes_and_rows_committed,write_start_authority_and_frame_time_requirement_set_commitment,transport_sent_obligation_commitment,sent_completion_nonce,server_signing_key_epoch,signature}`. It is constructed only after the complete authenticated surface terminal frame reaches `TransportSendObligation::Sent`, its adapter transcript byte-matches canonical `RESULT_END`, the exact flow reservation is reconciled, and the write-start authority/time requirement-set commitment byte-matches the send obligation; it owns no result bulk bytes and is retained through ACK/reconnect/expiry resolution. `EmbeddedResultFullyConsumedRecord<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is the distinct embedded-only proof `{session_authorization_ref:StrongRef<SessionAuthorizationRecord<Role>>,host_session_generation,result_owner_identity,result_delivery_id,delivery_state_version,stream_owner_token_commitment,complete_canonical_byte_length,canonical_result_digest,completion_source:ExplicitFinish|IteratorExhaustion,canonical_finish_call_digest,server_process_incarnation,signing_key_epoch,signature}`. It is constructible only after the embedded cursor has yielded every canonical byte and `finish()` (including iterator exhaustion's exact `finish()` path) joins all borrows/tasks; partial read, Drop, local EOF inference, or release cannot construct it.
`ResultAckAuthority<Role>` is the closed union `ReadyChannelResumeCapability{validation_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence>,presented_resume_capability_commitment,result_end_send_completion_ref:StrongRef<ResultEndSendCompletionRecord>}|EmbeddedFullyConsumed{record_ref:StrongRef<EmbeddedResultFullyConsumedRecord<Role>>}`. `AuthenticatedClientResultAckReceipt<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is the distinct immutable proof `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,session_authorization_ref:StrongRef<SessionAuthorizationRecord<Role>>,ack_authority:ResultAckAuthority<Role>,auth_context_generation,session_binding,public_authority_commitment,posture_and_role:Local|Meta,result_owner_identity,result_delivery_id,expected_active_delivery_state_version,expected_active_retention_digest,request_id,stream_id,strictly_monotone_ack_nonce,canonical_ack_request_digest,server_process_incarnation,accepted_child_state_version,server_signing_key_epoch,signature}`.
