Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement consensus GC: typed-root collection, safe points, quarantine, retention cuts
description:
## What & scope
Implement the replicated, fenced GC semantic plane of §14.5 + App A: the pipeline `CollectTypedRoots(stable_membership_epoch,config_payload_floor) -> ResolveMarkedPhysicalRealizations -> ProposeSafePoint -> ValidateAllTypedRootsAndCuts(prepared,commands,leases,pins,merge,privacy,replay,keys,backups,audit,transparency) -> CommitGcEpochThroughRaft -> Reclaim`, with `GcProposal`/`GcDecisionRecord`, quarantine installation, the no-new-reference rule, and the provisional/activated retention-cut distinction. Physical execution/dispatch is split into `w11-gc-physical`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
In a replicated system, reclamation is the most dangerous operation: reclaiming bytes another member, an in-flight prepared owner, a backup pin, or a privacy obligation still needs is unrecoverable. The design makes GC a consensus decision over recomputed proofs — every follower re-derives the candidate set — and inserts an audit-visible quarantine between authorization and physical action. B5: reclaim authority is proof-carrying and crash-replayable; B1: one GC epoch history inside the Raft order.

## Design — normative detail
**What stops reclamation** (§14.5): uncertain membership, incomplete new-configuration payload closure, partition, missing root/prepared-owner acknowledgement, external privacy-continuity mismatch, or unavailable key wrap. Backup/restore follows §16, never a decode-proof shortcut.

`GcProposal` is the Local pre-order bounded-set authorization `{gc_id,basis_state:WeakStateIdentity,basis_logical_command_seq,basis_commit_seq,basis_raft_index,configuration_ref,checkpoint_ref,config_payload_floor_ref,activated_retention_cut_ref,retention_map_digest,complete_typed_root_inventory_ref:StrongRef<GcRootInventory>,candidate_derivation_profile_oid,sorted_reclaim_objects_and_realizations,exact_reclaim_set_digest,required_storage_profile_and_member_set,completed_remote_release_refs[GcRemoteReleaseCompletionRef],excluded_live_prepared_certificate_remote_key_backup_legal_hold_replay_audit_capability_restore_result_workspace_and_delivery_obligation_commitment,terminal_audit_gate}` — weak basis identities, strong current floors/inventories. Every follower **recomputes the candidate** and either rejects the command or applies `GcDecisionRecord {proposal_ref,applied_control_ref,stable_configuration_ref,config_payload_floor_ref,retention_map_digest,typed_root_validation_digest,decision:Rejected{stable_reason}|Accepted{gc_id,authorized_reclaim_set_digest,required_storage_member_set_digest,quarantine_generation}}`; the input never names this result.

An accepted decision does **not** authorize physical work. GC has two non-overlapping state machines. Semantic `GcSemanticState<Role>` is `ProposedOrRejected|Quarantined{gc_id,authorization_commitment,quarantine_generation,reclaim_set_digest,operation_family_commitment,no_new_reference_rule_id,physical_state:AwaitingPhysicalDisposition}|PhysicalCompletedPendingCut{terminal_evidence_commitment}|CancelledBeforePhysicalStart{terminal_evidence_commitment}|Retired`. `LocalGcApplyQuarantineSpec` requires `reclaim_set SUBSET-OF authorized_set`, disjointness from every current RootSlot, candidate result, Protocol/Prepared/Consensus owner, and independently retained obligation, plus a current reachability recomputation and newly-reachable disjointness proof, and exact generation-zero member operation plans (`{generation=0,operation_id,idempotency_token_digest,storage_member_id,storage_profile_oid,target_inventory_digest,canonical_request_transcript_digest}`) conforming to the bounded `GcOperationFamily`. Semantic apply installs `LocalGcReclaimAuthorizationRecord` and `Quarantined` only — it does not create or mutate a Protocol operation record. **Every encoder, dedupe lookup, prepared receipt, command validator, compactor, and root publisher enforces the registered no-new-reference rule** against the audit-visible quarantine (resurrection-by-dedupe is structurally blocked). The quarantine and every checkpoint/configuration/backup/restore floor retain the complete family, all generation-zero plans, and the deterministic successor recipe through terminal disposition.

Retention cuts: an operational checkpoint install creates a `ProvisionalRetentionCutSet` that may authenticate bytes already absent under inherited activated coverage but **cannot satisfy any new-reclamation, key-destruction, backup-pin-release, remote-release, topology-retirement, or ownership-discharge predicate**; only an `ActivatedRetentionCutSet` authorizes new physical release. A replacement provisional must dominate every absorbed activated absence until its own activation. After physical completion is imported (see `w11-gc-physical`), a later activated cut moves `GcSemanticState` to `Retired` and permits Protocol evidence compaction.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-14 (full relevant text): GC follows every generated strong and currently uncut conditional edge; only registered weak/locator/observation fields are nonretaining. Independent obligations — including state-shaped active result/output owners, allocation/escrow holds, transaction ownership/capability lineage, audit pipeline entries, DP seeds/charges, prepared/certificate state, backup/restore/format/bulk/derived state, remote grants, and keys — remain roots until their exact terminal transfer/release. Provisional cuts authorize no new reclaim. Physical GC uses Requested -> Started -> Completed or all-members CancelledBeforeStart with signed exact receipts; any Started member makes cancellation impossible. Heavy detail retires only after visibility and an activated cut. Also FG-INV-16 (obligations) and FG-INV-07 (input never names result). GC pause/debt metrics are slo class.

## Interactions
Extends `w2-gc-core` (single-node typed-roots GC) with membership fencing from `w11-membership-config` (`stable_membership_epoch`, `ConfigPayloadFloor`, gc_ack_policy); consumes `w2-retention-checkpoints` (cut sets), `w9-key-lifecycle` (key-wrap availability stops reclaim; key destruction shares the quarantine pattern), `w11-raft-multi` (ordered proposal/decision, publication evidence). `w11-gc-physical` owns dispatch; `w11-backup`/`w11-restore` states are retained roots here; W12 (`w12-recovery-gc`) generalizes with Meta authorization.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Follower-recompute differential: a proposal derived at the leader is independently recomputed on each follower; mutated candidate sets (one extra object, one missing exclusion) are rejected deterministically. Reachability: generated mark-then-resolve model over all typed roots; dedupe-resurrection storm (concurrent writer re-inserting quarantined content) blocked by no-new-reference rule at every enforcement point (encoder, dedupe, receipt, validator, compactor, publisher — one test each). Stop-condition matrix: each of the six stop conditions (uncertain membership, incomplete payload closure, partition, missing ack, privacy-continuity mismatch, unavailable key wrap) independently halts before `CommitGcEpochThroughRaft`. Provisional-cut negative: provisional cut presented for each release predicate class must fail. Crash rows at quarantine install, decision apply, and every boundary listed in App A (proof, begin, dispatch, receipts, fences, terminal import, cut activation, evidence retirement). E2e with logs: run GC epochs under mixed load with an active backup pin and a live prepared owner; logs must show both excluded with typed reasons.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: leader-computed GC applied blindly by followers (single corrupted view reclaims shared bytes); timeout-based cancellation (any Started member forbids cancel — see `w11-gc-physical`); decode-proof shortcut for backup-covered bytes (backup pins are roots, full stop). Risk: quarantine retention inflates space under stalled physical execution — bounded by dispatch liveness SLOs and explicit successor generations.

## Provenance
§14.5 (line 1078, GC), App A lines 2037-2041 + 2049; App F FG-INV-07/14/16.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement durable-format capability, activation, escape latch, and decoder retirement
description:
## What & scope
Implement §16.7 rolling durable-format activation: `FormatCapabilityManifest` advertisement, `FormatCompatibilityState<Role>`, the five-arm `FormatTransitionSpec` union, the first-target-escape latch/arm/guard/receipt protocol, additive-minor skip laws, breaking-major transforms, `RewriteEquivalent`, and `RetireOldDecoder`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Rolling upgrades across a replicated cluster are where databases silently corrupt themselves: a new binary writes bytes an old voter cannot decode, or a downgrade reinterprets them. The design makes decoder compatibility a proved, advertised, consensus-ordered property — **never inferred from a binary version** — and makes the first authoritative escape of target-format bytes a fenced, receipted, permanently non-downgradeable event. B5: activation is evidence-first; B1: one format history inside the Raft order.

## Design — normative detail
Every process presents a signed immutable `FormatCapabilityManifest {binary_build_id,toolchain_profile,logical_schema_major_ranges,per_schema_read_minor_ranges,per_schema_write_epoch_ranges,bootstrap_and_root_slot_versions,required_flag_and_extension_support,canonical_default_law_ids,transform_artifact_ids,protocol_version_ranges,manifest_epoch,signer_id,signature}`; an advertisement is accepted only after its bytes and the implementation-generated decoder/encoder conformance suite agree. `FormatCompatibilityState<Role>` (rooted in Local/Meta canonical state, certified into Shard projection) records `{generation,active_read_epoch_set,active_write_epoch,target_epoch?,phase,exact_voter_storage_reader_support_matrix_ref,first_target_write_position?,rewrite_generation?,old_decoder_retention_floor,body_digest}`. Protocol negotiation uses its own connection state and never selects a durable write epoch.

`FormatTransitionSpec<Role>` is the closed Semantic ordered union: `AdvertiseTarget{target_epoch,sorted_member_capability_refs,exact_current_and_prospective_configuration_refs,support_matrix_ref,required_transform_refs,rollback_profile}`; `ActivateWriteEpoch{advertisement_ref,expected_old_write_epoch,target_write_epoch,bootstrap_transition_plan_ref,all_current_and_joint_quorum_decode_proof_ref}` (contains no guessed future position; its applied record supplies `activation_applied_position`); `RecordFirstTargetWrite{activation_ref,escape_receipt_ref,expected_latch_state:Escaped}`; `RewriteEquivalent{activation_ref,source_epoch,target_epoch,bounded_object_set,semantic_equivalence_proof_refs,physical_publication_plan}`; `RetireOldDecoder{activation_ref,old_epoch,target_epoch,checkpoint_and_config_floor_refs,complete_reachable_object_scan_ref,backup_restore_replay_capability_promise_floor_refs,all_member_target_only_support_ref}`. Local uses `LocalFormatTransitionSpec`; W12 Meta uses `GlobalFormatTransitionSpec`, shards accept only certified install/rewrite/retirement apply specs. **Unsupported commands cannot be proposed, voted, acknowledged for payload availability, applied, snapshotted, or served; under joint consensus both old and new voter/storage quorums satisfy the active read/write matrix.**

The irreversible cutoff precedes the first **authoritative escape** of target bytes. Pre-arm encoding is allowed only in an isolated, whole-inode-fenced, unowned staging area absent from prepared ownership, receipts, consensus, authenticated indexes, reachability roots, and service-visible paths. Consensus state owns the predecessor-format-readable `FormatFirstTargetEscapeLatch<Role> = NotArmed{activation_identity,activation_applied_position,old_write_epoch,target_write_epoch}|Armed{...,arm_operation_id,assigned_maintenance_index,first_escape_plan:{subject_class,object_or_root_kind,exact_target_identity_and_digest,exact_target_closure_inventory_digest,intended_publication_class,bootstrap_or_rootslot_transition_digest?},support_matrix_commitment,configuration_commitment,nonretaining_prior_latch_digest}|Escaped{armed_fields,arm_visibility_evidence_ref,first_escape_receipt_ref}`. `FormatFirstTargetEscapeArmSpec<Role>` is a Raft maintenance command encoded entirely under the predecessor-compatible epoch; it publishes Armed in Consensus/Raft state and RootManifest **before** any staged target byte may become prepared-owned, receipted, ordered, acknowledged, authenticated-indexed, rooted, or slot-visible. **Armed is itself the permanent no-downgrade boundary — even if the planned escape later fails — with no ordinary unarm transition**; it names one exact first-escape plan so recovery can finish only that operation or require a fenced new-incarnation migration.

After the Armed-containing RootSlot is durable, `FormatArmVisibilityEvidence<Role>` (latch commitment, containing raft-state-root/manifest identities, winning slot+generation, other-slot observation, `RootPublicationEvidence`, configuration/writer-fence commitment) is constructed — reconstructible after crash, never embedded back into Armed. A linear runtime-only `FirstTargetEscapeGuard<Role>` rereads the current manifest/slot, verifies the exact still-current Armed latch and evidence, and is consumed immediately before the first irreversible target action. Completion mints `FormatFirstTargetEscapeReceipt<Role> {header:FenceBoundIrreversibleReceiptHeader,armed_latch_commitment,arm_visibility_evidence_ref,target_epoch,target_identity_and_kind,first_escape_class:PreparedReceipt|RaftAcceptance|ReplicaAcknowledgement|RootPublication|RootSlotPublication,exact_durability_or_consensus_receipt,resulting_manifest_or_log_position,signer_and_configuration_evidence,body_digest,signature}` and maintenance CASes Armed -> Escaped. Only then may `RecordFirstTargetWrite` reconcile the Semantic state — the semantic command is no longer the safety boundary. Crash anywhere after Armed remains non-downgradeable and recovers the one named escape idempotently.

Laws: activation authorizes a future target writer only through the Armed latch at the exact ordered prefix; no encoder selects target bytes from `FormatCompatibilityState` alone. Additive-minor readers may skip a length-delimited unknown field only when its registered `canonical_default_law_id` proves absence and skipping are semantically identical; an unknown required flag, union tag, reference edge, retention rule, security rule, or non-defaultable field fails closed. A breaking logical major requires an explicit total transform with old/new semantic equivalence evidence and a new registered construction DAG; with no reverse transform, durable Armed makes downgrade permanently fail-closed. RootSlot/bootstrap major changes additionally require a pre-activation dual-reader bootstrap plan whose old path can still locate/authenticate the active root — otherwise offline migration or new-incarnation restore, never rolling activation. `RewriteEquivalent` creates new physical/canonical objects before swapping typed roots and preserves old versions until the floor closes. `RetireOldDecoder` is legal only when no reachable root, prepared/log suffix, checkpoint, backup/base, restore lease, replay manifest, durable capability, remote grant, or promised historical interval can require old bytes.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-10 (excerpt, binding text): durable-format writes occur only under an activated `FormatCompatibilityState`: all current/joint voters and storage readers decode the active closure, first-target-write is irreversible, downgrade is refused after it, and old decoders retire only after exhaustive reachable/backup/restore/replay floors; closure or capability failure repairs or fails closed, never rolls back or partially interprets. FG-INV-07 (Armed fields known before encoding the containing root; no future identities). Rolling-upgrade duration is slo class.

## Interactions
Consumes `w11-raft-multi` (maintenance commands, latch in `RaftStateRoot`), `w11-membership-config` (joint-quorum decode proofs, support matrix vs configurations), `w2-root-bootstrap` (RootSlot/RootManifest publication, dual-reader bootstrap plans), `g0-identity-registries` (schema/epoch registries, `canonical_default_law_id`s, construction DAGs), `w11-backup` (backup/restore floors gate `RetireOldDecoder`). W12 arms feed `w12-conversion`; `verif-torture` owns the release-gate campaigns.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Conformance: manifest acceptance requires generated decoder/encoder suite agreement; mismatched advertisement rejected. Matrix: proposing/voting/acking/applying/snapshotting/serving an unsupported command each independently rejected; joint-quorum matrix violations rejected. Latch: crash between Arm publication and escape — recovery completes only the named plan; crash after Escaped — `RecordFirstTargetWrite` idempotent; unarm attempts unencodable. Staging: staged target bytes reachable from any owned/receipted/indexed/rooted path before Armed is a generated negative. Minor-skip: unknown defaultable field skipped only with a registered law; each fail-closed category (required flag, union tag, reference edge, retention rule, security rule, non-defaultable field) has a fixture. Permanent release gates (§16.7 list): rolling old/new/joint membership, unknown-tag, old-backup restore, replay, every arm/escape/receipt/reconcile boundary, old-binary open, bootstrap tear, transform mismatch, GC/key-retention. E2e with logs: 3-member rolling upgrade old->joint->new with activation, one forced crash post-Arm; logs record latch transitions, escape class, receipt identity, and per-member support matrices.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: version-number-inferred compatibility; semantic-command-as-safety-boundary (the latch/receipt protocol is the boundary; `RecordFirstTargetWrite` merely reconciles); silent unknown-field skipping (registered default laws only); rolling bootstrap-major activation without a dual-reader plan. Risk: Armed-but-never-escaped clusters are permanently non-downgradeable by design — operators are warned at Arm time, and the fenced new-incarnation migration is the documented exit.

## Provenance
§16.7 (lines 1212-1220); App F FG-INV-07/10.

title: Implement GC physical execution: dispatch guards, member receipts, cancellation
description:
## What & scope
Implement the Protocol-plane physical execution machinery for consensus GC: `GcPhysicalExecutionRecord`, irreversible dispatch attempts and guards, the per-member idempotent operation state machine with signed receipts, standalone cancellation authorization, and the Semantic disposition import that closes the loop.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Physical deletion is irreversible and distributed; the failure mode to kill is "we think it never started, so we cancelled — but a member had started." The design gives each member a linear idempotent operation state with monotonic counters and makes any authenticated Started/Completed observation permanently rule out cancellation. B5: every destructive byte action is preceded by durable, fenced evidence and followed by a signed receipt.

## Design — normative detail
After the quarantine's role-valid `CanonicalPublicationEvidence<Role>` exists, Protocol maintenance initializes `GcPhysicalExecutionRecord<Role>` with `{gc_id,authorization_commitment,quarantine_generation,operation_family:GcOperationFamily,all_generation_plan_and_disposition_lineage,current_generation,dispatch_mode:Open|CancellationFenceInstalled{fence_generation}|CancellationReconciling{fence_generation}|NoStartFenced{fence_generation,evidence_record_ref}|CompletionRequired{authority_commitment},physical_state:Requested|Started|Progress|CompletingAfterCancellationRace|Completed{complete_receipt_bijection,terminal_evidence}|CancelledBeforeStart{complete_never_started_bijection,terminal_evidence},body_digest}` in `GcPhysicalExecutionIndex<Role>`. `NoStartFenced` blocks every reclaim send; `CompletionRequired` permanently forbids the cancelled terminal. A successor generation may cover only targets proved locally AbandonedBeforeSend or provider-CancelledBeforeStart in the prior generation; exhaustion fails closed; started/completed targets keep their original operation IDs and are never repeated.

Dispatch: `GcPhysicalExecutionInitializeSpec` byte-matches the publication evidence and family/base-plan commitment and creates exactly one `IrreversibleDispatchAttempt<GcMemberReclaim>::Armed` per active plan. `GcPhysicalDispatchMarkSentUnknownSpec` advances exactly one Armed attempt to SentUnknown before transport eligibility. The generated `GcIrreversibleDispatchGuard` revalidates the current all-plane root inventory, exact quarantine generation and reclaim-set disjointness, dispatch mode, configuration, writer/member fences, continuity, authority, service epoch, and time immediately before sending the byte-identical member request. Receipt/status/cancel imports (`GcPhysicalStartReceiptImportSpec`, Progress/Completion/Cancellation imports, `GcParticipantCancellationFenceInstallSpec`/StatusImport/EvidenceFinalize, `GcParticipantRollForwardSpec`, `GcPhysicalSuccessorGenerationSpec`, `GcPhysicalEvidenceRetireSpec`) mutate only the Protocol index and registered dispatch slots; maintenance may read Semantic commitments but cannot write `GcSemanticState`, `GcReclaimQuarantineRoot`, a logical locator, or a semantic sequence. Cross-plane matching uses signed commitments and the same RootManifest publication — never a strong ObjectId edge between planes.

Member service: one linear idempotent state per `(operation_id,idempotency_token_digest)`: `NotRegistered -> Requested{canonical_request_digest,request_registration_counter} -> Started{member_monotonic_counter,pre_operation_physical_root_digest} -> Completed{member_monotonic_counter,post_operation_physical_root_digest,receipt_digest}`; cancellation allows `Requested -> CancelledBeforeStart{...}` or the explicit idempotent tombstone `NotRegistered -> CancelledBeforeStart{...}` which permanently rejects later registration/start (roll-forward must use the family-derived successor ID). The machine cannot move Started/Completed -> Cancelled, regress a counter, or bind an existing operation ID to different bytes; **timeout changes no state**. A member durably persists and fences Started before its first irreversible byte/key action. Receipts (`GcPhysicalStartReceipt`/`GcPhysicalCancellationReceipt`/`GcPhysicalMemberReceipt`) begin with `FenceBoundIrreversibleReceiptHeader` and bind gc_id, authorization commitment, quarantine generation, operation/idempotency identities, member/profile, target inventory digest, canonical request transcript digest, pre-op physical root digest, and monotonic counters; completion adds the exact deleted-or-crypto-erased inventory, post-op root and probe digests, durability evidence, completion counter/time profile, and signature. Lost responses recover by status lookup under the same operation ID; signed NotRegistered alone permits only the same request or the registered cancel-before-start under a fresh guard — never inferred success or local abandonment.

Cancellation: standalone Local `LocalGcCancellationAuthorizeSpec {quarantine_record_ref,protocol_no_start_fenced_evidence_ref,complete_member_target_family_and_no-start_bijection,current_unchanged_physical_root_proof,terminal_audit_gate}` cannot be constructed from a timeout or partial member set. `GcPhysicalDispositionImportSpec<Role> = Completed{quarantine_publication_evidence,protocol_terminal_evidence,current_reachability_recomputation_ref,no_resurrection_proof_ref}|Cancelled{...,complete_never_started_bijection_proof,cancellation_authority:GcCancellationAuthorityFor<Role>}` imports portable signed terminal evidence and alone moves Semantic state to `PhysicalCompletedPendingCut` or `CancelledBeforePhysicalStart`. The Cancelled arm requires an exact bijection over AbandonedBeforeSend/DispatchNeverSentProof or provider-CancelledBeforeStart receipts and `dispatch_mode=NoStartFenced`; SentUnknown, Requested, Started, CompletionRequired, or missing evidence blocks it. Missing, duplicate, wrong-family/generation/member/inventory, stale-root/fence, partial, wrong-role, mixed-aggregate, or cross-plane-substituted evidence rejects import.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-14 (excerpt): physical GC uses Requested -> Started -> Completed or all-members CancelledBeforeStart with signed exact receipts; any Started member makes cancellation impossible; missing participants remain blocking. FG-INV-16 (excerpt): no GC quarantine obligation is lost, duplicated, or released while obligated. Dispatch latency and stalled-attempt aging are slo class.

## Interactions
Blocked by `w11-fenced-gc` (quarantine/publication evidence) and `w2-gc-core` (physical retirement primitives); consumes `w9-time-authority` (guard time evidence). The same universal dispatch pattern (Armed/SentUnknown/guard/status-first recovery) is shared with backup external operations (`w11-backup-publication`) and key destruction (`w9-key-lifecycle`) — implement once, specialize per contract.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
DPOR/model tests over the member state machine: no transition regresses counters, no Started->Cancelled, tombstone permanence. Race: cancellation fence vs. in-flight start (CompletingAfterCancellationRace path); authenticated Started observation forces CompletionRequired forever. Lost-response: kill transport after send; recovery must status-query the same operation ID; NotRegistered-then-retry and Started-then-import both verified. Crash/lab rows (App A list): quarantine, initialize, dispatch, provider cancel tombstone, start/destructive action, receipt import, fence/status/evidence, successor generation, terminal state, Semantic import/publication/ack, cut activation, evidence retirement. Bijection negatives: missing member, duplicated receipt, substituted inventory digest each reject disposition import. E2e with logs: 3-member reclaim with one member crashed pre-start and one post-start; logs show successor generation for the never-started target only, and final Completed bijection.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: timeout-implies-cancelled (the central hazard); retrying with fresh operation IDs after ambiguity (breaks idempotency lineage; only byte-identical retry is legal); cross-plane strong refs (would let Protocol GC state retain Semantic bytes or vice versa). Risk: permanently stalled SentUnknown attempts pin quarantine — surfaced via slo aging alerts and resolved by status-first recovery, never by guessing.

## Provenance
App A lines 2043-2049; §14.5; App F FG-INV-14/16.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement ConfigurationState, joint quorums, ConfigPayloadFloor, reconfiguration ladder
description:
## What & scope
Implement membership: SWIM+Lifeguard as evidence-only failure detection, the exact `ConfigurationState` schema, joint-quorum validation, the pre-order `ConfigurationTransitionSpec`, the applied `ConfigPayloadFloor` with its weak-checkpoint-observation law, `MandatoryInventory`, and the nine-step reconfiguration ladder ending in `RetireOld`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
§14.2: **membership and payload authority are consensus decisions, never gossip**. SWIM+Lifeguard supplies suspicion/routing/donor evidence only; it cannot change membership. This protects B1 (one authoritative configuration history inside the Raft order) and B5 (retirement authorized only by proof-carrying floors). The floor design solves a real retention trap: a naive floor that strongly retains its basis checkpoint would chain `F_n -> Q_n -> F_(n-1)` forever, making configuration history unreclaimable.

## Design — normative detail
`ConfigurationState` is `{database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,group_role:Local|Meta|Shard{shard_id},group_id,configuration_epoch,form:Stable{voters[],storage_members[]}|Joint{old_voters[],new_voters[],old_storage_members[],new_storage_members[]},sorted_member_descriptors[{member_id,replica_namespace,consensus_signing_key_epoch,payload_receipt_key_epoch,roles,failure_domains[]}],raft_quorum_rule,payload_recoverability_predicate,failure_domain_map,gc_ack_policy,predecessor:WeakConfigurationIdentity?,transition_nonce}`. It has **no self ID** — the ObjectId of its bytes is its identity. Joint requires independent old/new consensus quorums AND the payload predicate over both sets. One-member is the ordinary stable specialization. Every same-group receipt/certificate carries `configuration_state_ref` plus `payload_predicate_digest` and must match the enclosing log/hard-state/snapshot/prepared-root/manifest/command domain. Another group imports it only through `RemoteConfigurationRef` with signed adoption evidence and retention floor; **numeric epoch or equal member list is never authority**.

A pre-order `ConfigurationTransitionSpec` (`{phase:ProposeJoint|CommitJoint|CommitNew|CommitRetirementFloor,basis...}`) carries a nonretaining basis identity, current/prospective configuration refs, the candidate closure proof, and expected prefix. Its applied `ConfigPayloadFloor` **does not retain the spec, basis root, checkpoint, or checkpoint vector**. Exact schema: `{schema_version,payload_schema_oid,protocol_registry_epoch,basis_state:WeakStateIdentity,basis_logical_command_seq,basis_commit_seq,basis_raft_index,closed_through_raft_index,closed_through_logical_command_seq,current_configuration_ref,prospective_joint_configuration_ref?,prospective_final_configuration_ref,failure_domain_policy_ref,current_checkpoint:WeakCheckpointIdentity,checkpoint_state_vector_digest:WeakDigest,retained_command_suffix_endpoints,retained_marker_suffix_endpoints,mandatory_inventory_root:StrongRef<MandatoryInventory>,prepared_owner_floor_ref,receipt_certificate_signer_floor_ref,audit_ticket_fence_floor_ref,retention_cut_floor_ref,branch_key_allocator_merge_floor_ref,outcome_conflict_floor_ref,delivery_replay_derived_floor_ref,continuity_service_floor_ref,remote_trust_release_floor_ref,gc_key_destruction_floor_ref,backup_restore_floor_ref,migration_transition_floor_ref,coverage_bitmap,nonretaining_predecessor_floor_digest:WeakDigest}`; its ObjectId is the floor identity; it has no strong edge to basis root, checkpoint/vector, predecessor floor, transition spec, or applied command.

**Weak-checkpoint-observation law**: `MandatoryInventoryEntry.value` is `RetainedStrong{typed_ref:RegisteredStrongRef}` for independently mandatory objects or `CurrentCheckpointObservation{checkpoint:WeakCheckpointIdentity,checkpoint_state_vector_digest:WeakDigest,logical_inventory_digest,availability_receipt_refs[StrongRef]}`; neither the observation nor its receipts become a logical reachability edge to checkpoint/vector/prior-floor bytes. The separately strong `LogicalStatePayload.recovery_checkpoint_ref` owns the current checkpoint/vector; floor validation requires the weak observation to equal and cover exactly that current checkpoint. Every operational checkpoint install atomically supplies the paired refreshed floor through §5.4, whose projection excludes the prior floor — so replacing `F_n` cannot create a direct or indirect `F_n -> Q_n -> F_(n-1)` retention chain. If the authoritative prefix or current checkpoint advances during transfer, the candidate floor is extended/recomputed before installation; a stale floor cannot authorize retirement. `MandatoryInventory` is `{schema_version,payload_schema_oid,protocol_registry_epoch,role,ordered_entries[MandatoryInventoryEntry],coverage_bitmap,body_digest}`; `MandatoryInventoryClassRegistry` maps each stable class tag to one exact target kind, reference encoding, slot, live predicate, cut/release predicate, and owning floor field; the bitmap equals every activated class exactly once; unknown/duplicate/missing/wrong-role/dormant entries fail G0.

**Reconfiguration ladder**: `ProposeJoint -> CatchUpLog -> TransferMandatoryClosure -> VerifyFloorAtBasis -> CommitJoint -> CommitNew -> RefreshFloorThroughCommitNew -> CommitRetirementFloor -> RetireOld`. `CommitJoint`, `CommitNew`, and `CommitRetirementFloor` are the typed Raft `ConfigurationTransitionSpec` entries themselves, so each semantic configuration transition increments `LogicalCommandSeq`; heartbeats/no-ops do not. The final retirement floor proves the prospective durability set can recover through the committed `CommitNew` transition and every mandatory retained suffix/object and protected retry/accounting/idempotency closure under the new failure-domain policy. **Old members cannot leave, discard payload, or advance GC until that final floor command is committed and acknowledged.** Statistical suspicion may tune alerts but never authorizes membership, payload retirement, or GC.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-14 (excerpt): GC follows every generated strong and currently uncut conditional edge; only registered weak/locator/observation fields are nonretaining; provisional cuts authorize no new reclaim. FG-INV-07 (excerpt): every pre-order input excludes its future command/result/root — the transition spec never names its applied floor. FG-INV-16 binds floor obligations. `CurrentCheckpointObservation` is the sole weak checkpoint exception per role and must byte-match the separately strong current payload checkpoint (App A). SWIM tuning parameters are `FG-CFG`/slo class, never safety inputs.

## Interactions
Builds on `w11-raft-multi` (typed Raft entries, certificates) and `w11-payload-availability` (per-domain receipts inside floors; joint predicate over both sets); consumes `w2-retention-checkpoints` (checkpoint install pairing, `ProvisionalRetentionCutSet`/`ActivatedRetentionCutSet`) and `w2-commit-protocol`. Gates `w11-fenced-gc` (GC needs `stable_membership_epoch` + floor), `w11-backup` (floors retain nonterminal backup state), `w11-format-activation` (joint quorums must satisfy the read/write matrix), and W12 reconfiguration.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Property tests: joint-quorum validator (independent old/new majorities; adversarial overlapping sets); epoch/member-list-equality never grants authority (negative fixtures). Retention: model-check that floor replacement never creates a path to predecessor-floor bytes (graph reachability assertion over generated reference tables); deleting each mandatory-inventory class in turn is a generated negative fixture. Ladder: sim campaign running the full nine steps under crash/partition at every step; assert old members refuse leave/discard/GC-advance until retirement floor committed+acknowledged; stale-floor-authorizes-nothing negative (advance prefix mid-transfer, assert recomputation demanded). Checkpoint race: advance checkpoint during `TransferMandatoryClosure`, assert `VerifyFloorAtBasis` fails and the floor is extended. Log assertions in e2e: each ladder step logs phase, basis positions, floor identity, and coverage bitmap.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: gossip-driven membership (split-brain under partition); floors that strongly retain checkpoints (unbounded retention chain — the explicit anti-law); implicit configuration change via heartbeat metadata (semantic transitions must increment `LogicalCommandSeq`). Risk: ladder liveness under repeated checkpoint advance; bounded by recompute-then-install being idempotent and the floor basis being monotone.

## Provenance
§14.2 (lines 1071-1075), App A lines 1552, 1914, 2031-2033, 2037; App F FG-INV-07/14/16.

title: Implement donor payload receipts and PayloadAvailabilityCertificate recoverability
description:
## What & scope
Implement the payload-availability plane for multi-member commit: donor-side prepared-payload storage and root publication, signed/MACed `PayloadReceipt`s, and the canonical `PayloadAvailabilityCertificate` that proves the configured recoverability predicate before a `CommitCommand` may be proposed.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
§14.1: before proposal, each donor has root-published its `PreparedCommitRecord`, and the leader collects receipts proving the payload closure is durably recoverable in named failure domains. This is what makes ordered commitment safe under crash-fault replication without byte-identical replicas (the Aegis doctrine allows repair ESIs, ciphertext encodings, and placement to differ). B5: availability is proved by typed evidence, not assumed from acks; the certificate is a strong command edge, so the proof travels with the history.

## Design — normative detail
`RemotePreparedIdentity` is `{storage_member,prepared_ownership_id,base_closure_inventory_digest,latest_record_observation:NonRetainingRemoteObservation{record_digest:WeakDigest,observed_prepared_payload_root_generation}?}` — it names the stable signed ownership promise; the optional diagnostic is neither a local ObjectId nor a reachability edge.

A `PayloadReceipt` binds `{database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,configuration_state_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,payload_predicate_digest,storage_member,failure_domain,local_writer_fence_epoch,prepared_owner:RemotePreparedIdentity,encoding_and_placement_requirements[],symbol/source-block coverage,fsync_generation,proposal_freshness_basis_ref:StrongRef<PayloadReceiptProposalFreshnessBasis>,proposal_freshness_evidence_ref:StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>,nonce}` plus a domain-separated member signature/MAC. Construction is acyclic: the freshness basis is built from the complete stable receipt body excluding itself, its evidence ref, nonce, and signature; the evidence is then built; the final receipt signs both typed identities. The signer must still hold the matching `WriterLeaseGuard`/`FenceToken`; a receiver verifies the epoch against the member's current fenced identity/configuration and requires `TimeValidationEvidence::Usable` for `FormNewProposal` immediately before using the receipt. Successor records preserve ownership/base closure and may only strengthen current closure. **Proposal freshness is never a storage lease, retention horizon, or deletion permission**: an expired receipt may remain valid evidence of durable ownership but cannot form a new proposal.

Receipts bind the stable `PreparedOwnershipId`, base-closure digest, and exact `EncodingId`/`PlacementId` coverage in named failure domains. The canonical `PayloadAvailabilityCertificate` repeats namespace/incarnation, the exact configuration ref/predicate digest, canonically lists receipt refs, the exact base logical-object plus encoding/placement requirements, the FEC recoverability calculation, verifier version, and threshold signature (built via the universal `CertificateAttemptPlan`/lock/share protocol from `w11-raft-multi`). It proves the configured recoverability predicate — including quorum one, where the local durable copy satisfies it — and is a **strong command edge**: the `CommitCommand` cannot be proposed without it, and it is retained with the history.

Under joint configurations the payload predicate must hold over **both** old and new sets (§14.2), so the certificate names the configuration whose predicate it proves and reconfiguration transfer (`w11-membership-config`) recomputes floors when the predicate set changes.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-07 (excerpt): before receipt/order, D1 owns one exact closure under stable prepared ownership; timeout releases no prepared owner. FG-INV-16 (excerpt): no prepared closure is lost, duplicated, refunded, released, or exposed while obligated; under declared quorum/storage/network/time/continuity/resource fairness, every obligation reaches one legal terminal or recoverable state. FG-INV-09 (excerpt): symbol MACs cover their complete noncircular transcripts; incompatible encodings never combine. The recoverability computation feeds the `FG-CFG-01` modeled-durability report (CTMC/MTTDL with fitted rates, failure domains, sensitivity bounds) — configuration-model claim class, not an invariant.

## Interactions
Consumes `w2-commit-protocol` (D1 payload durability barrier, D2 authorize/command/order/publish; availability + order-attempt certificates), `w2-object-identity` (§5.1 SymbolRecord/MAC transcripts), `w2-fec-scrub` (RaptorQ profiles and the recoverability calculation), `w9-time-authority` (`TimeValidationEvidence`), `w11-raft-multi` (certificate protocol, fenced replies). Produces receipts/certificates consumed by `w11-membership-config` (floor receipts per domain), `w11-anti-entropy` (donor authority), `w11-writer-anywhere`, and W12 (`w12-prepare` generalizes to shard prepares).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Unit/property: receipt transcript round-trip; freshness-basis acyclicity (mutation tests that no receipt field includes its own digest chain); wrong-epoch/wrong-fence/wrong-configuration receipt rejection; expired-receipt-cannot-propose but still-counts-as-ownership tests. Sim campaigns: donor crash after root-publish/before receipt; leader crash after collecting k-of-n receipts; verify recovery reconciles prepared ownership and never double-releases (FG-INV-16 leak oracle). Certificate: recoverability predicate evaluated against adversarial placement inventories (missing failure domain, duplicate member, coverage gap) must reject; quorum-one specialization passes with the local copy. Differential: FEC recoverability calculation checked against an independent decoder simulation (deterministic decode campaign). Crash-matrix rows at each of: prepared-root publication, receipt sign, receipt import, certificate plan/lock/share/publish, proposal. Logged e2e script: 3-member cluster, kill one donor mid-commit, assert commit completes with predicate proved by remaining domains and logs show the exact receipt set in the certificate.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: treating donor acks as availability (no typed evidence); letting receipts double as retention leases (conflates freshness with storage authority — the explicit non-law above); byte-identical replica requirement (blocks encoding/placement divergence and repair). Risk: time-authority unavailability stalls `FormNewProposal`; mitigation: freshness is only needed at proposal formation, and the per-use window is bounded by `w9-time-authority` guard budgets.

## Provenance
§14.1 (line 1068), App A line 2029, §5.2 D1/D2, App F FG-INV-07/09/16, FG-CFG-01.

title: Extend fgdb-order to multi-member Raft with role-tagged durable state and certificates
description:
## What & scope
Extend W2's quorum-one `fgdb-order` Raft into full multi-member consensus: leader election, log replication, snapshot install, and the universal quorum-signing protocol, all over the exact Appendix A role-tagged durable formats. One-member remains the ordinary stable specialization — the same code path, not a fork.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
§14.1: **one commit state machine with durable Raft state**. §5.2 remains authoritative in one-member and multi-member configurations, preserving B1 — replication must not create a second commit discipline. B5 requires that every consensus artifact be typed, digest-bound, and reconstructible: the generated log-to-state verifier proves the exact role-specific root/config/prefix at a cut, so recovery is proof-carrying rather than heuristic.

## Design — normative detail
Transactions advance `Draft -> Validated -> FinalPrepared -> PreparedRootDurable -> PayloadAvailable -> Proposed(term,index) -> CommandCommitted -> Applied(logical_command_ref,marker_ref) -> Acknowledged`. Consensus commits the normative strongly referenced `CommitCommand`; the standalone `CommitMarker`, `LogicalStatePayload`, `LogicalCommandRecord`, and outer state root are deterministically created in that acyclic order after `LogicalCommandSeq`/`CommitSeq`/HLC assignment.

Durable formats (no-extra-mutable-file doctrine): `RaftLogSegment` carries exact domain/index/term/entry fields and a generated closed command union over Local semantic txn/control, Meta semantic txn/control, Shard prepare/decision/control, and `Maintenance{command:RaftMaintenanceCommand}` (role-tagged outer union `Local{command_ref}|Meta{command_ref}|Shard{shard_id,command_ref}`; role/group validation rejects substitution). `RaftHardState` is `{database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,group_role,group_id,current_term,voted_for?,log_first,log_last,commit_index,applied_index,visible_index,configuration_state_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,snapshot_ref?,maintenance_applied_index,certificate_attempt_ledger_root_ref,prepared_order_attempt_root_ref,audit_signer_journal_root_ref,protocol_state_identity:WeakStateIdentity}`. Maintenance commands (`LocalMaintenanceCommand` etc.) advance Raft/maintenance indexes and declared nonsemantic planes only — never semantic sequences/HLC/heads; a self-staleness fixture fails any maintenance handler that changes semantic order.

Snapshots are exact **applied-cut** objects. `RaftConsensusCutProjection<Role>` is prebuilt and snapshot-self-excluding (`{...,last_included_index:K,term_at_K,vote_and_commit_state_at_K,configuration_at_cut_ref,prospective_configuration_refs,log_prefix_digest,retained_suffix_begin_index:K+1,certificate_prepared_remote_obligation_and_configuration_floors,format_first_target_escape_latch,takeover_adoption_head_projection,snapshot_slot:SelfExcluded{InstallThisSnapshot},body_digest}`); the construction-DAG generator rejects any path from projection back to the snapshot under construction. `RaftSnapshot` common fields include `last_included_index:K`, `term_at_K`, `configuration_at_cut_ref`, `semantic_applied_position_at_K`, `maintenance_applied_index_at_K`, `prepared_ownership_state_ref`, `consensus_cut_projection_ref`, `retained_suffix_begin_index:K+1`, floors, `log_prefix_digest`, `log_to_all_planes_proof_ref`, `body_digest`; the invariant is `last_included_index = K = successor RaftHardState.applied_index_at_cut`; construction order is cut projection -> snapshot -> successor `RaftHardState{snapshot_ref}` -> successor `RaftStateRoot`, never a cycle. Local/Meta payloads carry the applied semantic root at K, the complete role-valid `AuditVisibilityProtocolState` through K (with possibly earlier visible root/position and unresolved candidate queue), prepared root, and selectors — never described as a visible-only cut. `RaftStateRoot<Role>` gathers hard state, retained log segments, configurations, matching applied-cut snapshot, prepared/certificate ledgers, remote-obligation floors, transition locks, `FormatFirstTargetEscapeLatch<Role>`, `TakeoverAdoptionHead<Role>`, protocol state, unresolved candidates, and `BodyDigest`.

A node syncs the new closure before vote/append/receipt/durability replies; every reply follows a durable RootManifest publication. Every append reply or reply batch mints a fresh `RaftHardState`/`RaftStateRoot`/`RootManifest` closure plus one serialized `RootSlot` publication — a gated §17 cost derived from Appendix G. **Multi-member must not fuse** append-reply and post-apply D2 publications (fusion is legal only at one member, where recovery cannot observe the intermediate state and the receipted-but-unordered crash window falls under §5.2 abandonment arms). Leader loss yields capability-scoped `Unknown`. The `RaftHardFrame` bootstrap-frame spike is a G0/G1 decision (owned by `g0-format-arms`); its honest scope: per-append scalars alone don't stop closure re-minting because `certificate_attempt_ledger_root_ref`, `prepared_order_attempt_root_ref`, and `audit_signer_journal_root_ref` churn per commit.

Universal signing protocol for quorum artifacts: `CertificateUnsignedBodyDigest<T>` is a registered domain-separated transcript over every semantic field including the full authority/configuration/predicate header and pre-minted `certificate_attempt_id`, excluding exactly `certificate_attempt_plan_ref`, lock/share arrays, and aggregate/signature fields. Flow: a nonsemantic maintenance entry quorum-roots `CertificateAttemptPlan {certificate_attempt_id,certificate_kind,subject_identity,authority_domain,configuration_ref,payload_predicate_digest,certificate_schema_id/version,canonical_unsigned_body_digest,canonical_signer_subset,threshold,signature_algorithm_and_encoding}` in `CertificateAttemptLedger` -> each signer durably installs `CertificateSignerLock{...,state:Locked}` in its fenced journal -> emits `CertificateSignatureShare` -> completed certificate carries plan ref, sorted lock/share bijection, signer bitmap, canonical aggregate -> `CertificatePublish` maintenance entry records `Published`. Ledger states: `Absent -> Planned -> Collecting -> Published` or `Planned|Collecting -> AbandonPending -> Abandoned` (via `CertificateAttemptAbandonSpec` requiring a quorum-impossibility proof and non-publication proof; successor attempts use a new attempt ID, same unsigned-body digest unless the semantic owner legally changed). At most one Published certificate identity per `(kind,subject,unsigned-body digest)`; conflicting published digests are fatal evidence. Signer order/encoding/subset fixed by plan so crash/retry/leader change reproduces one certificate byte string and ObjectId.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-07: the concrete durable strong/uncut-conditional graph is acyclic; every pre-order input excludes its future command/result/root; before receipt/order D1 owns one exact closure under stable prepared ownership; timeout releases no prepared, certificate, audit, result, allocation, escrow, or retention owner. FG-INV-08: logical-command order and marker subsequence contiguous; every role-tagged Raft snapshot matches its precise cut, root, configuration, maintenance state, applied/visible positions. FG-INV-10: recovery selects the highest structurally credible authenticated role closure; every irreversible seal/receipt/Raft action/certificate/slot write rechecks both authorities. Per-commit sync-op counts are exact structural Appendix G registry rows (registry class, generation-bijection enforced), never invariants and never benchmark values: §17's ordered-sync gate must byte-match the registry barrier chain including its fusion-legality column (a legal fusion counts as one ordered sync operation, never zero), while the measured latency/throughput numbers over those counts are `slo.toml`/benchmark rows.

## Interactions
Extends `w2-order-raft`; consumes `w2-commit-protocol` (D1/D2, capsules), `w2-root-bootstrap` (RootSlot/RootManifest publication sequencer), `w2-group-commit` (batching/fusion law), `w2-recovery`. Produces the consensus substrate for `w11-membership-config`, `w11-payload-availability`, `w11-read-contracts`, `w11-fenced-gc`, `w11-format-activation`, and all W12 Meta/Shard roles. Certificate signing protocol is consumed by every W11 certificate (backup closure, GC, reconfiguration).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Deterministic-sim (fgdb-sim) multi-member election/replication/snapshot campaigns; generated log-to-state verifier proves root/config/prefix at every cut, and a later-root/earlier-cut pairing is rejected. Crash matrix rows at every append/vote/receipt/apply/publication boundary; fsync-lie and torn-write rows per FG-INV-10. Certificate fixtures (G0-generated): include/exclude, signer substitution, duplicate/missing share, threshold, aggregate mutation, abandonment, successor subset, maintenance self-staleness — for every registered certificate schema; crash stops before/after each plan/lock/share/publication/abandon stage and across leader/configuration change, asserting byte-identical certificate reproduction. Truncation tests: log truncation refused until the generated-complete floor (prepared transfers, cursors, replay, continuities, remote trust/retention, backup, keys, configs) closes. Bench: ordered sync operations per commit and per append batch by posture and audit class, published side-by-side with Appendix G derivations. E2e with logs: a 3-member fgdb-sim cluster under mixed semantic/maintenance load runs one leader crash, one follower crash, and one snapshot install while transactions drive `Draft -> Validated -> FinalPrepared -> PreparedRootDurable -> PayloadAvailable -> Proposed -> CommandCommitted -> Applied -> Acknowledged` end-to-end; the run must converge with identical role closures on all members. DETAILED LOGGING: every append/vote/receipt/apply/publication boundary logs `{term,index,commit_index,applied_index,visible_index,maintenance_applied_index}`; every reply logs its RootSlot generation and RootManifest identity; certificate lifecycle events log attempt ID, kind, signer subset, and ledger state (Planned/Locked/share-emitted/Published/AbandonPending/Abandoned); snapshot events log the cut coordinates (`K`, `term_at_K`, `retained_suffix_begin_index`). The generated log-to-state verifier replays these logs against every recovered cut, and byte-identical certificate reproduction across crash/leader change is asserted from the logged attempt lineage.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: ambient abbreviated Raft schemas (all state is registry-typed); fusing publications at multi-member (followers reply before commit — unsound); skipping per-batch root publication without the `RaftHardFrame` redesign (would put recovery-relevant bytes outside the published root closure, needing new FG-INV-08/FG-INV-10 clauses, a changed verifier, and takeover coverage). Risk: publication cadence cost; mitigation is the priced Appendix G model plus the recorded G0 spike outcome.

## Provenance
§14.1 (lines 1068-1070), App A lines 1554-1568, App F FG-INV-07/08/10.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement LeaderRead/ReadIndex/FollowerLease/RYW read contracts and AuthorizationLease
description:
## What & scope
Implement the replicated read plane of §14.3: linearizable `LeaderRead` and `ReadIndexRead`, the signed `AuthorizationLease` (the sole schema), separately signed `FollowerLeaseRead`, bounded-staleness projection, read-your-writes (RYW), and revocation/audit-visibility coupling — including the rule that data staleness never grants security staleness.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Read scale is the main payoff of replication (Aegis doctrine), but a follower read must never become a security downgrade: a follower whose policy/revocation/key state lags could otherwise serve data a fresh authority would refuse. The design pushes complete, signed authorization bindings into leases so a follower either proves it can answer under current authority or fails closed to the leader. B6: agents get typed positions (`PublicLogicalPositionProjection`) instead of raw counters, so RYW works across sessions without leaking internal Raft/audit state. B1: all reads name one committed history.

## Design — normative detail
`LeaderRead` and `ReadIndexRead` provide linearizable data paths. The sole `AuthorizationLease` schema is the signed `{consensus_domain:ConsensusDomain,issuer_id,authority_leader_member_id,authority_raft_term,security_leader_epoch,lease_generation,source_token_or_capability_commitment,token_id,authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,permitted_operation_class:ReadOnly,permitted_snapshot_interval,exact_role_bearing_read_bindings,allowed_query_operator_disclosure_scope,result_answer_contract_ceiling,time_authority_profile_oid,not_before,expires_at,signer_id,signing_key_id,signer_epoch,signature}`. The signed transcript includes the complete binding and window; root/service/leader/token/ceiling drift invalidates it.

`FollowerLeaseRead` is separately signed and contains `{consensus_domain,authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,follower_member/configuration/term/lease identity,closed semantic positions,visible protocol position,retention lease identity,profiled window,authorization_lease_ref,signer fields,signature}`. It is legal only when: the requested visible state/protocol evidence is closed at the signed cut, all bytes/keys are retained, and both leases validate under fresh time guards. Otherwise the follower contacts the authority leader or fails closed. **Data staleness never grants security staleness, and hidden candidates never leak** — the visible protocol position (audit-visibility pipeline endpoint, from FG-INV-04) bounds what any read path may observe.

Bounded-staleness reads expose only the authorized public position projection. RYW uses the sole exact replay body and a `PublicLogicalPositionProjection` — never raw Raft/logical/commit/audit counters; presentation permits only routing/wait for an already committed public position under current same-or-narrower authority. Restore/cutover service-epoch change invalidates old capability/lease bytes **before observation**: every request binds `{cluster_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch}` and stale values fail before any data touch.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-04 (excerpt): Local/Meta applied state may advance ahead of public state only through the rooted gap-free audit visibility pipeline, and every read/result/side channel begins at its visible endpoint; every request, cursor, capability, and forwarded shard operation matches the current incarnation/service epoch. FG-INV-20 (excerpt): authorization precedes every observation or effect; capability lookup/status/release is same-principal, same-or-narrower, current-epoch, and uniformly nonrevealing on failure; equal epoch scalars with different roots/service epochs never substitute. Follower-read hit rates and staleness distributions are `slo.toml` claim class.

## Interactions
Consumes `w11-raft-multi` (terms, commit/visible indexes, ReadIndex), `w2-snapshots-leases` (`ReadSnapshot`, generation lease inodes/retention), `w9-threat-tokens` (macaroons/discharges the lease commits to), `w9-enforcement` (visible-endpoint and mandatory access types), `w9-time-authority` (fresh time guards for both leases). Produces the read surface used by `w10-fgp-core`/`w10-adapters`, and generalized by `w12-registration-snapshot` and W12's `LeaderRead/ReadIndex/FollowerLease/RYW/AuthorizationLease` row.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Unit: lease transcript round-trip; each drift axis (root, service epoch, leader term, token, answer-contract ceiling) independently invalidates. Property: follower serves only when closed-at-cut + retained + both leases + fresh time; each conjunct's negation forces leader-contact-or-fail-closed (all four negatives). Linearizability: Elle-style histories over LeaderRead/ReadIndexRead under partition and leader change. Security: revoke a capability at the leader, verify a lagging follower cannot serve under the old lease (data-staleness-vs-security-staleness test); hidden-candidate leak oracle (applied-ahead-of-visible state never observable via follower reads, error surfaces, or timing-position leaks). RYW: cross-session replay body + `PublicLogicalPositionProjection` waits/routes correctly; raw-counter exposure is a generated negative. Restore-cutover: flip service epoch mid-session; every in-flight request fails before observation with typed stale-epoch errors, verified by e2e logs recording epoch pairs per request. E2e script with logs: a 3-member cluster serves concurrent LeaderRead/ReadIndexRead/FollowerLeaseRead/bounded-staleness/RYW traffic under injected partition, leader change, and a mid-run capability revocation; every read logs `{read_class,consensus_domain,lease_generation,authority_raft_term,security_leader_epoch,signed_cut_positions,visible_protocol_position,decision:serve|forward_to_leader|fail_closed,typed_error?}` and every RYW presentation logs the `PublicLogicalPositionProjection` it waited on or routed to. Post-run log verification proves: no follower served under a lease after revocation became visible at the leader; no raw Raft/logical/commit/audit counter appears in any client-visible logged field; measured staleness distributions and follower-hit rates populate the `slo.toml` rows.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: follower reads gated only on data positions (security lag hole); exposing Raft indexes to clients for RYW (couples clients to consensus internals and leaks audit positions); best-effort lease validation with async revocation (violates authorization-before-observation). Risk: leader-contact fallback under partition degrades read availability — accepted; availability is an slo line, correctness is not negotiable.

## Provenance
§14.3 (line 1076), App F FG-INV-04/20.
design:
## Authoritative post-decomposition contract delta (d96bf0f)

The ReadYourWrites validation, wait authorization, admission-retention, and Shard import contract below is mandatory and supersedes the description's generic RYW wording.

   `ReadYourWritesCapabilityReplayRecord` is `{fields:{header:DurableCapabilityHeader{capability_kind=ReadYourWrites},body:{posture,txn_outcome_capability_commitment,registration_handle:PublicRegistrationHandle,floors:PublicRywFloorSet,capability_lineage_token:PublicStateToken<ReadYourWritesLineage>}},canonical_capability_bytes,capability_commitment,subject_basis_ref:StrongRef<ReadYourWritesSubjectBasis<Role>>,authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,issuer/key/verifier/time-window/floor fields,body_digest}`. The public body contains no redundant authority ceiling; the header/binding owns it. The subject basis supplies the exact marker/branch/visibility/retention map and byte-matches `floors`. It contains no WeakMarkerIdentity, raw Raft/logical/commit/audit counter, or local ref on wire. It is issued only with TerminalReady and permits waiting/reading at an authorized subset of the opaque committed floor set under current same-or-narrower authority. `ReadYourWritesWaitAuthorizationRecord<Role>` is `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,validation_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence>,requested_floor_subset_digest,capability_floor_set_commitment,expected_lineage_leaf_digest,canonical_wait_request_digest,request_nonce,body_digest}`; it selects only `ReadYourWritesWait`, byte-matches current or the exact action-recorded predecessor retry, and is strongly retained by `ReadYourWritesWaitSpec<Role>` and its pending/terminal public send guard until the wait response or installed-successor retry resolves. A scalar floor, registration handle, or prior admission cannot substitute. All capability kinds have exact restart/rotation/lost-response/expiry/substitution byte tests.
No per-read Meta control projection or new certificate kind is created. `ImportedReadYourWritesValidationProjection` is the Shard-local registered value `{source_read_access_admission_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ReadAccessAdmissionRecord<Meta>>,certified_source_authority_projection_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<MetaAuthorityBindingProjection>,source_validation_identity:RemoteObjectIdentity,source_validation_body_digest:BodyDigest<DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence>,source_global_prefix,source_meta_configuration_identity,requested_floor_subset_digest,internal_floor_set_commitment,public_floor_projection,current_shard_security_projection:ShardSecurityStateProjection,current_active_meta_projection_root_ref:StrongRef<ActiveMetaProjectionRoot>,combined_authority_projection:ShardAuthorityBindingProjection,body_digest:BodyDigest<ImportedReadYourWritesValidationProjection>}`. The exported Meta read admission's `ReadAccessCommon<Meta>.read_your_writes_basis` must be `ValidatedLocalOrMeta` and name exactly `source_validation_identity/body_digest`, requested subset, and floor commitment; the projection identity and typed body digest equal the exact retained DCVE selected by that basis, and its export closure and two-sided grant retain that validation generation and floor basis. The separately typed authority-projection CRSR must match the admission's `MetaAuthorityBindingProjection`, source prefix/configuration/grant, and principal/scope. The Shard validator requires that prefix/configuration still be selected by its current ActiveMetaProjectionRoot and constructs `combined_authority_projection.certified_source_authority_projection_ref` from the exact CRSR together with the embedded current Shard-local security projection. The resulting complete Shard authority, requested subset, and both floor commitments must byte-match. This is a request-scoped certified import, not a long-lived `MetaProjectionSlot`, and it contains no capability bytes, verifier material, session authority, raw cross-group strong ref, or future Shard-state edge. `ReadAccessCommon<Role>.registered_snapshot_and_workspace_scope` contains the closed `read_your_writes_basis` value `None|ValidatedLocalOrMeta{validation_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence>,requested_floor_subset_digest,capability_floor_set_commitment}|ImportedShardProjection{projection:ImportedReadYourWritesValidationProjection}`. BEGIN, EXECUTE, and EXECUTE_TEXT select `ValidatedLocalOrMeta` before any snapshot or graph observation exactly when their optional ReadYourWrites capability is present; the validation ref must select the corresponding action row, role, request, and current floor subset. The corresponding exact Local or Meta BEGIN reservation/registration fields below carry the same basis, so registration, later read admission, and every authorized snapshot retain one byte-identical validation generation. A Shard can receive only the exact imported projection and cannot reference or revalidate the client capability. `None` carries no placeholder digest. This basis is retained by the admission and every derived authorized snapshot until the read closes; a different floor subset, validation action, capability generation, role, or security binding requires a distinct admission.

title: Implement rooted restore abandonment, no-observation proof, and terminal pins
description:
## What & scope
Implement rooted restore abandonment across prebootstrap, Local, Meta, and Shard: tombstone skeleton, pending terminal-pin owner, no-target-observation proof, catalog predecessor fencing, abandonment operation/manifest, participant apply certificates, transient cleanup, and terminal pin installation.

## Why
Abandonment is a terminal protocol, not cleanup by deletion. It must prove whether any target identity or service observation escaped, fence the catalog/continuity predecessor, retain enough evidence to prevent reuse, dispose every reservation/key/object/lease, and keep the abandoned target forever nonservable.

## Design — exact normative contract
`RestoreNoTargetObservationProof<Role>` is generated from the exact role schema and binds `{restore_id,restore_epoch,target_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch,role_and_group,current_hidden_state_root_identity,current_root_slot_generations,zero_ordinary_writer_lease_proof,zero_READY_handshake_session_query_transaction_result_delivery_and_capability_issuance_proof,no_service_promotion_receipt_proof,profile_specific_catalog_or_zero_catalog_observation,complete_endpoint_set,service_admission_log_commitment,audit_commitment,checker_version,signatures}`. Sharded abandonment requires a Meta proof and one certified proof from every configured shard.

`CatalogAbandonPredecessor` is the exact portable closed union `AuthenticatedAbsent{target_row_key,authenticated_empty_map_proof,expected_catalog_map_root_digest,row_nonreuse_floor}|ReservedHidden{target_row_head_bytes_digest_and_version,reservation_id_and_digest,admission_hidden_proof}|ActivatedHidden{target_row_head_bytes_digest_and_version,reservation_id_and_activation_digest,composite_receipt_required_proof}`. The catalog tombstone action may install or idempotently join a `CatalogAuthorityHead::TombstonedNoEndpoint` successor from any exact arm and permanently advances the row nonreuse floor; it may not infer absence from a lookup miss. Thus abandonment remains legal before `CatalogReserveHidden`, after reservation, or after hidden activation.

The cleanup-only action kind `CatalogTombstoneRestoreTarget` has two distinct pre-order bodies. `PreBootstrapCatalogTombstoneRestoreTargetActionBody` is `{abandonment_authority_seed:RestoreAbandonmentAuthoritySeed,catalog_profile:ExternalCasCataloged|DirectoryBoundCataloged,predecessor:CatalogAbandonPredecessor,prebootstrap_abandonment_spec_and_zero_publication_commitment,operation_id,idempotency_key_digest}`. `CanonicalCatalogTombstoneRestoreTargetActionBody<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` has the same seed/profile/predecessor/operation fields but requires the role's authority-binding public commitment and originating abandonment-operation public commitment. Neither body contains cleanup recipe digests, an abandonment-manifest digest, future skeleton/tombstone body, result head, receipt, or publication evidence.

The universal registry emits `PreBootstrapCatalogTombstoneRestoreTargetContract<Profile>` with `origin_plane=RestorePreBootstrap` and source gate `PreBootstrapAbandonmentCleanupGate`, plus `CanonicalCatalogTombstoneRestoreTargetContract<Role,Profile>` with `origin_plane=CanonicalProtocol` and the audit-visible `RestoreAbandonOperationRecord<Role>` candidate source gate. Their operation namespaces, request bindings, attempts, evidence, and imports are disjoint. `CatalogAuthorityHead` is the reference-free CAS-linear `{target_row_key,predecessor:Absent{authenticated_catalog_map_root_digest_and_version,row_nonreuse_floor}|Prior{head_digest,cas_version},cas_version,row_nonreuse_floor,state:ReservedHidden|ActivatedHidden|TombstonedNoEndpoint{restore_id,target_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch,catalog_profile,origin_plane,abandonment_authority_seed_digest,operation_id,idempotency_key_digest,admission_visible:false,endpoint_set_empty:true,no_reactivation_or_same_incarnation_reservation:true},authority_counter,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`; no state arm contains its own head digest or result CAS version, and absent creation never fabricates predecessor-head bytes. The authority performs one linearizable direct transition and returns exact `CatalogTombstoneRestoreTargetReceipt<Contract> {external_request_binding:ExternalActionRequestBinding{dispatch_contract_id=Contract},predecessor:CatalogAbandonPredecessor,result_head_complete_bytes,result_head_digest_and_cas_version,action_body_digest,authority_counter,signer_set_epoch,signatures}`. Already-applied is equivalent only when every field, plane, seed, contract, complete returned head byte, and result version match; refusal/conflict proves zero effect and cannot authorize the next abandonment stage.

`PreBootstrapCatalogRestoreTargetTerminalDisposition` is `Cataloged{contract_id:PreBootstrapCatalogTombstoneRestoreTargetContract<Profile>,action_body_digest,terminal_import_artifact_ref:PreBootstrapArtifactRef<PreBootstrapExternalTerminalImportArtifact<PreBootstrapCatalogTombstoneRestoreTargetContract<Profile>>>,portable_terminal_evidence_artifact_ref:PreBootstrapArtifactRef<PortableExternalActionTerminalEvidence<PreBootstrapCatalogTombstoneRestoreTargetContract<Profile>>>,receipt_artifact_ref:PreBootstrapArtifactRef<CatalogTombstoneRestoreTargetReceipt<PreBootstrapCatalogTombstoneRestoreTargetContract<Profile>>>,result_catalog_authority_head_artifact_ref:PreBootstrapArtifactRef<CatalogAuthorityHead>,status_and_nonreuse_accumulator_commitment}|EmbeddedNoCatalog{zero_catalog_applicability_proof}`. `CanonicalCatalogRestoreTargetTerminalDisposition<Role,Profile>` is `Cataloged{contract_id:CanonicalCatalogTombstoneRestoreTargetContract<Role,Profile>,action_body_digest,terminal_import_ref:StrongRef<ExternalTerminalImportRecord<CanonicalCatalogTombstoneRestoreTargetContract<Role,Profile>,Role>>,portable_terminal_evidence_ref:StrongRef<PortableExternalActionTerminalEvidence<CanonicalCatalogTombstoneRestoreTargetContract<Role,Profile>>>,receipt_ref:StrongRef<CatalogTombstoneRestoreTargetReceipt<CanonicalCatalogTombstoneRestoreTargetContract<Role,Profile>>>,result_catalog_authority_head_ref:StrongRef<CatalogAuthorityHead>,status_and_nonreuse_commitment}|EmbeddedNoCatalog{zero_catalog_applicability_proof}`. The referenced head must decode the exact `TombstonedNoEndpoint` arm and byte-match the receipt. No-root continuity/DirectoryBound closure, journal-key destruction authorization, and the no-root terminal certificate require the prebootstrap type; rooted finalize requires the canonical type. EmbeddedNoCatalog cannot encode a placeholder catalog result. Catalog evidence and its result head remain rooted through their declared status/nonreuse floor, and no plane can consume the other's disposition.

`CanonicalCatalogedTargetCleanupRecipe<Role:AuthorityOwningRole,Profile>` is the pre-order `{catalog_predecessor:CatalogAbandonPredecessor,contract_id:CanonicalCatalogTombstoneRestoreTargetContract<Role,Profile>,operation_id,idempotency_key_digest,canonical_action_body:CanonicalCatalogTombstoneRestoreTargetActionBody<Role>,required_terminal_head_arm:TombstonedNoEndpoint,required_receipt_evidence_and_import_schema_ids,recipe_digest}` and contains no future result. `RestoreAbandonAuthorityProfile<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is the generated exact union `ExternalCasCataloged{catalog_cleanup_recipe:CanonicalCatalogedTargetCleanupRecipe<Role,ExternalCasCataloged>,expected_continuity_head_commitment,continuity_cleanup_recipe:CanonicalAbandonByCas{predecessor:RestoreAbandonableContinuityPredecessor,contract_id:CanonicalRestoreContinuityAbandonContract<Role>,operation_id,idempotency_key_digest,canonical_action_body_recipe}}|DirectoryBoundCataloged{creation_evidence_ref:StrongRef<DirectoryBoundCreationEvidence<Local>>,fixed_local_continuity_digest,catalog_cleanup_recipe:CanonicalCatalogedTargetCleanupRecipe<Local,DirectoryBoundCataloged>,expected_local_state_root_and_slot,local_abandon_publication_recipe}|DirectoryBoundEmbeddedNoCatalog{creation_evidence_ref:StrongRef<DirectoryBoundCreationEvidence<Local>>,fixed_local_continuity_digest,zero_catalog_applicability_proof,expected_local_state_root_and_slot,local_abandon_publication_recipe}`. The generated family exposes the two DirectoryBound arms only for `Role=Local`; `Role=Meta` is statically ExternalCasCataloged. Because a canonical restore root already proves a reserved/refined continuity state, no canonical profile has a no-mutation/absent-continuity arm.

`RestoreAbandonSpec` is the closed `Local{restore_id,expected_hidden_state,no_target_observation_proof_ref:StrongRef<RestoreNoTargetObservationProof<Local>>,authority_profile:RestoreAbandonAuthorityProfile<Local>,abandonment_pin_pending_owner_ref:StrongRef<RestoreAbandonmentPinPendingOwner<Local>>,abandonment_manifest_body_recipe,source_lease_disposition:ReleaseRequired,terminal_audit_gate}|ShardedMeta{restore_id,expected_hidden_meta_state,meta_no_target_observation_proof_ref:StrongRef<RestoreNoTargetObservationProof<Meta>>,exact_sorted_shard_no_observation_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<RestoreNoTargetObservationProof<Shard>>],complete_group_commitment,authority_profile:RestoreAbandonAuthorityProfile<Meta>,meta_abandonment_pin_pending_owner_ref:StrongRef<RestoreAbandonmentPinPendingOwner<Meta>>,sorted_shard_abandonment_pin_pending_owner_recipes[RestoreAbandonmentPinPendingOwnerRecipe<Shard>],complete_shard_recipe_group_and_no_observation_bijection,abandonment_manifest_body_recipe,source_lease_disposition:ReleaseRequired,terminal_audit_gate}`. Apply remains hidden and enters AbandonAuthorizedHidden.
