`RestoreCanonicalAcquisitionWorkingSet<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is the pre-freeze target-keyed closure `{authority_bound_header,plan_copy_ref,bootstrap_refinement_copy_ref:CanonicalBootstrapOpenersRef<Role>,verified_object_refinement_copy_ref:CanonicalVerifiedObjectInventoryRef<Role>,source_gate_copy_ref,archive_receipt_ref,sorted_key_provider_receipt_refs,identity_key_disposition_evidence,source_k_oid_wrap_and_key_commitment,target_k_oid_wrap_and_key_commitment,sorted_object_dek_opener_recipes,decoder_and_format_profile_inventory,complete_plan_refinement_manifest_projection_object_key_provider_receipt_and_opener_bijection,live_prebootstrap_dispatch_root_identity_and_generation,body_digest}`. It is usable only with a live `RestoreProjectionBuildGuard` that revalidates the current dispatch root and source-lease owner; by itself it authorizes no source read or provider action.

`RestoreSourceAcquisitionBundle<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is created only after bridge freeze and is `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,plan_import_record_ref:StrongRef<RestoreSourceAcquisitionPlanImportRecord<Role>>,working_set_ref:StrongRef<RestoreCanonicalAcquisitionWorkingSet<Role>>,source_gate_ref:StrongRef<RestoreSourceAcquisitionSourceGate>,archive_receipt_ref:StrongRef<PortableRestoreArchiveAcquisitionReceipt>,canonical_lease_record_ref:StrongRef<RestoreSourceLeaseRecord<Role>>,frozen_latest_lease_generation_and_portable_state_digest,sorted_key_provider_receipt_refs[RestoreKeyProviderReceiptRef],identity_key_disposition_evidence:RestoreIdentityKeyDispositionEvidence,source_k_oid_wrap_and_key_commitment,target_k_oid_wrap_and_key_commitment,sorted_object_dek_opener_recipes[{source_object_identity,source_ciphertext_and_encoding_identity,portable_receipt_member_commitment,opener_policy_oid,target_recipient_commitment,proof_of_inventory_membership}],decoder_and_format_profile_inventory,complete_prebootstrap_artifact_plan_gate_manifest_projection_object_key_provider_receipt_opener_and_cleanup_bijection,bridge_freeze_commitment,body_digest}`. It contains only wrapped material/recipient commitments and canonical copies of typed portable receipts; no prebootstrap artifact locator remains load-bearing after import. Missing source `K_oid`, missing target `K_oid` creation/rewrap, a missing DEK opener, uncovered subject, unclassified format, or created artifact without cleanup disposition fails before the first authoritative target-format escape.

The acquisition uses the registered pre-bootstrap dispatch machine because the target has no canonical RootManifest yet. Before the plan, recovery creates the stable journal/capsule authority above. `RestoreAcquisitionDispatchRoot` is a two-slot, tear-checked and MAC-authenticated, whole-inode-fenced **local mirror/cache** in the exclusive `journal_staging_inode`—outside the target database directory and registered as the sole pre-bootstrap local mutable-root exception. Each slot MAC covers `{restore_id,journal_id,current_journal_authority_head_digest_and_cas_version,portable_plan_digest_or_recipe_digest,plan_availability_certificate_identity,current_staging_incarnation,journal_staging_inode_identity,slot_index,generation,predecessor_slot_digest,complete action map and typed artifact locators,current prebootstrap time basis,current lease owner,resource dispositions,state}` under `K_restore_journal`; recovery rejects equal-generation disagreement, invalid MAC, wrap/claim/head mismatch, rollback, or artifact-locator substitution. No local generation is dispatch-capable until the matching encrypted generation-capsule recipe is available in the required failure domains, the journal authority head has advanced to it, and the local mirror byte-matches that result.

Its payload state is `Building|AcquiredProjectionAllowed|BridgeFrozenForCanonicalCreation{bridge_freeze_spec_artifact_ref,working_set_projection_and_bridge_recipe_commitment,frozen_latest_source_lease_generation_and_portable_state_digest,recovery_incarnation_refresh_family_state?,complete_terminal_attempt_and_resource_owner_bijection}|FirstRootPublicationFrozen{first_root_freeze_spec_artifact_ref,closed_recovery_incarnation_refresh_family_final_ordinal?,final_recovery_incarnation_lease_generation_and_window?,final_sealed_import_bundle_and_creation_guard_commitment,complete_terminal_attempt_family_member_and_resource_owner_bijection}|AbandonmentDrainPending{sealed_abandon_intent_artifact_ref,frozen_new_action_projection_and_creation_guards,outstanding_preexisting_attempt_bitmap,zero_canonical_publication_proof}|AbandonmentAuthorized{sealed_abandonment_spec_artifact_ref,complete_terminal_preexisting_attempt_inventory,complete_action_and_resource_disposition_plan,zero_canonical_publication_proof}|CleanupInProgress{sealed_abandonment_spec_artifact_ref,sorted_action_dispositions,sorted_resource_dispositions,outstanding_cleanup_bitmap}|TerminallyAbandoned`. `AcquiredProjectionAllowed` permits source opens, transform/projection construction, status resolution, and exact source-lease renewal through the live journal. `RestoreBridgeFreezeSpec` is a sealed prebootstrap artifact whose fields commit the completed working set, transform/projection identities and digests, exact first-bridge recipes, latest source-lease owner generation/state, current ExternalCas RecoveryOnly incarnation-lease generation if applicable, zero unresolved source/provider attempt proof, the closed source-renew family ordinal, and the complete action/resource owner/disposition bijection. Its one journal-authority-backed root transition consumes every projection/source-use guard, forbids new source/provider operations and source-lease renewal, and enters `BridgeFrozenForCanonicalCreation` while leaving only the bounded recovery-incarnation refresh family open.

The sole operation after bridge freeze but before the second freeze is exact `RecoveryIncarnationLeaseAcquireOrRefresh` for an ExternalCas target. Its action body preserves database/security identity, target incarnation, writer identity, `RecoveryOnly` scope, current continuity head/CAS, and first-root action digest; only the current predecessor lease generation/status, requested validity window, and pre-minted member identity advance. It grants no archive/key/source access. A successful refresh advances the journal head/dispatch state, invalidates every unrooted sealed-import/bundle/creation-guard candidate derived from the prior lease, and deterministically rebuilds candidates against the new lease. DirectoryBound has no such action.

`RestoreFirstRootPublicationFreezeSpec` is the second sealed prebootstrap artifact. It consumes the current bridge-frozen state, exact latest terminal recovery-lease member/head, final sealed-import/bundle/creation-guard recipes, and a proof that no refresh member is Armed, SentUnknown, unresolved, or authorizable beyond the selected final ordinal. Its journal-authority-backed transition closes the recovery-incarnation refresh family and enters `FirstRootPublicationFrozen`; only then are the final `SealedPreBootstrapDispatchJournalImport<Role>`, `RestoreSourceAcquisitionPlanImportRecord<Role>`, `RestoreSourceAcquisitionBundle<Role>`, and role-valid first-root creation guard constructible. After this second freeze the only legal outcomes are byte-exact first-root publication under that guard or transition to abandonment drain. If the closed lease/window becomes unusable before publication, the restore fails closed to abandonment and a new restore attempt; the family can never reopen.

Abandonment begins with `PreBootstrapRestoreAbandonIntent`, not a cleanup gate. Its journal-authority-backed transition enters `AbandonmentDrainPending`, revokes every **new** action/projection/creation authorization, and freezes the exact set of already Authorized/Armed/SentUnknown attempts. `PreBootstrapAbandonmentDrainCarryForwardGuard<Action>` is inhabitable only for one frozen preexisting attempt: it preserves the attempt's original request and original source-gate commitment, permits status-first recovery, permits byte-identical retry only when the original row/status/eligibility allows it, and permits an Armed-unsent attempt to use its original never-sent proof. It cannot create a new operation, change bytes, open source data, build projection, or publish service. Registered ArchiveAcquire and every other provider-started attempt therefore roll forward under their original identity until Applied/AlreadyApplied/refused/conflict or a definitive never-sent terminal; an unchanged Registered head is never zero-effect.

Only after the outstanding bitmap is empty may `PreBootstrapRestoreAbandonAuthorizeSpec` construct the exact total cleanup plan and enter `AbandonmentAuthorized`. That state permanently revokes all old carry-forward guards; only new action-specific release/burn/revoke/destroy cleanup operations, their status recovery, and disposition publication are legal. CleanupInProgress monotonically records one typed action/resource disposition at a time under `PreBootstrapAbandonmentCleanupGate`. Every attempt uses the universal generated state machine and owns action-typed `PreBootstrapArtifactRef` values for status results, receipts/refusals/conflicts, portable terminal evidence, and import records; a digest alone is not recoverable authority. `PreBootstrapDispatchPublicationEvidence<Action>` and `PreBootstrapNeverSentProof<Action>` are specific to the journal authority plus local mirror and cannot be decoded as ordinary RootManifest evidence.

While `BridgeFrozenForCanonicalCreation`, recovery may construct and independently verify only unrooted candidate copies for the sealed import, canonical lease, plan import, bundle, and creation guard; every refresh invalidates them. Only `FirstRootPublicationFrozen` may construct the final canonical artifacts, whose immutable history covers every pre-first-root renewal/refresh/status transition and whose creation guard consumes that exact final journal head/mirror generation. Journal-key destruction/zeroization waits until the detailed-import floor is replaced by the explicitly preterminal `PreBootstrapDispatchTerminalAccumulator<Role>`. Abandonment instead seals the complete disposition transcript and retains its loss-tolerant recovery capsule through the same external nonreuse/status floor.

Prebootstrap time validation is explicit. `PreBootstrapTimeAuthorityBasis` is the portable certified `{restore_id,claimed_continuity_or_identity_reservation_authority,plan_digest,plan_availability_certificate_digest,permitted_time_profile_identities_and_digests,authority_domains_and_epochs,challenge_service_contracts,maximum_round_trip_and_uncertainty,valid_through,signer_set_epoch,signatures}` committed by every target claim/head. `PreBootstrapTimeAuthorityObservationImport` pairs that basis with a challenged portable observation and same-process `LocalChallengeRoundTripWitness`; it creates a linear nonserializable guard for only the named prebootstrap action. The first Local/Meta bridge proves exact profile/epoch/service handoff or a dual-signed transition into the canonical `TimeAuthorityRegistry`; no prebootstrap observation survives restart or authorizes post-bootstrap work.

`PendingRestoreAcquisitionGuard` is the linear/nonexportable `{restore_id,portable_plan_artifact_ref:PreBootstrapArtifactRef<PortableRestoreSourceAcquisitionPlan>,plan_availability_certificate_artifact_ref,exclusive_journal_staging_inode_identity_and_whole_inode_lease,current_dispatch_root_generation,current_prebootstrap_time_basis,exact_current_target_claim_continuity_reservation_and_grant_observation_imports,resource_bounds,remaining_action_bitmap,allowed_effects:DispatchOrAbandon,unconsumed}`. It may publish only registered prebootstrap attempts, immutable unreachable prebootstrap artifacts, lease-owner generations, or the abandonment transition. It becomes `RestoreProjectionBuildGuard<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` only after target `K_oid` exists and the complete required-success/equivalent action bijection/current lease owner are terminally imported. That linear guard is `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,canonical_working_set_ref:StrongRef<RestoreCanonicalAcquisitionWorkingSet<Role>>,live_dispatch_root_identity_and_generation,current_prebootstrap_lease_owner_and_time_guard,authorized_archive_ref_set,decoder_opener_key_and_resource_inventory,allowed_effects:OpenTransformProjectRenewFreezeOrAbandon,unconsumed}`. Every archive/key open re-reads `PreBootstrapRestoreSourceLeaseCurrent`, the live grant/time evidence, and the unchanged action/resource inventory; the working set or a transform-plan digest alone never authorizes a read. The guard may build the exact transform plan/projection, renew through the same journal, or convert to abandonment. After projection and bridge recipes are complete it may consume itself only into `RestoreBridgeFreezeSpec`; the bridge-frozen guard can create/rebuild unrooted canonical candidates, refresh only the recovery-incarnation lease, enter the second freeze, or abandon, but can perform no source open or renewal. The second frozen guard can only publish the one first root or abandon.

Pre-bootstrap abandonment has separate total action and resource disposition protocols because no RestoreRegistry exists yet. `PreBootstrapActionDisposition` is the closed one-per-action union `NotAuthorized{action_key,zero_authorization_membership_proof}|AuthorizedNeverArmed{action_key,authorization_artifact_ref,zero_armed_membership_proof}|AbandonedBeforeSend{action_key,armed_publication_evidence_artifact_ref,typed_prebootstrap_never_sent_proof_artifact_ref}|Succeeded{action_key,typed_receipt_artifact_ref,portable_terminal_evidence_artifact_ref,terminal_import_artifact_ref,final_external_head_commitment}|NoEffect{action_key,disposition:PermanentlyRefused|ConflictNoEffect|ExpiredNotRegisteredNoEffect,typed_provider_tombstone_artifact_ref,portable_terminal_evidence_artifact_ref,terminal_import_artifact_ref,unchanged_external_head_commitment}`.

`UnpublishedTargetObjectSetQuarantine` is the exact prebootstrap artifact `{restore_id,journal_id,projection_result_identity_and_digest,zero_root_slot_and_zero_canonical_reference_proof,sorted_logical_ciphertext_encoding_placement_and_segment_inventory,sorted_local_staging_members[{filesystem_profile,mount_device,target_manifest_staging_inode_or_segment_identity,name_generation,whole_inode_or_segment_fence,expected_extent_inventory}],sorted_remote_members[{provider,target_identity,operation_family_and_pre_minted_cleanup_ids}],target_k_oid_disposition_basis,complete_projected_object_to_physical_owner_bijection,cleanup_floor,body_digest}`. `UnpublishedTargetObjectSetDisposition` is `CryptoErasedAwaitingPhysicalGc{quarantine_ref,target_k_oid_destroy_receipt_and_terminal_evidence,proof_every_ciphertext_depends_on_destroyed_fresh_target_identity,registered_physical_gc_family_and_retention_floor}|PhysicallyDeleted{quarantine_ref,sorted_local_member_deletion_receipts[FenceBoundIrreversibleReceiptHeader+exact_inode_name_generation_extent_proof],sorted_remote_deletion_terminal_imports[ExternalTerminalImportRecord<RestoreUnpublishedTargetPhysicalDelete,PreBootstrap>],complete_target_to_receipt_bijection,zero_remaining_owned_placement_proof}`. Crypto erasure is legal only for a clone-created fresh target identity; same-identity recovery must physically delete or retain quarantine until ordinary GC can prove deletion. Remote/object-store deletion uses registered dispatch; local deletion uses a member-issued fenced physical receipt. Neither a directory scan nor dropping a filename is terminal evidence.

`PreBootstrapResourceDisposition` is the closed one-per-resource union `ReleasedArchiveLease{resource_key,lease_identity,released_through_generation,disposition_action_key,typed_receipt_and_full_no_successor_proof_ref}|RegisteredArchiveAcquisitionRolledForwardThenReleased{resource_key,original_archive_acquire_action_key,registered_head_and_status_lineage_commitment,active_receipt_and_lease_identity,release_action_key,release_receipt_and_full_no_successor_proof_ref}|BurnedReservation{resource_key,reservation_kind,reservation_id,claim_id?,disposition_action_key,typed_burn_receipt_and_nonreuse_commitment}|CatalogTargetCleanup{resource_key,target_catalog_row_key,profile:ExternalCasCataloged|DirectoryBoundCataloged,terminal_disposition:PreBootstrapCatalogRestoreTargetTerminalDisposition::Cataloged}|ContinuityCleanup{resource_key,restore_id,target_incarnation,terminal_disposition:PreBootstrapRestoreContinuityCleanupDisposition}|DirectoryBoundZeroPublicationClosed{resource_key,target_manifest_staging_inode_and_fence_identity,zero_root_slot_proof,claim_burn_set_commitment,catalog_disposition:Cataloged{catalog_resource_key_and_terminal_commitment}|EmbeddedNoCatalog{zero_catalog_applicability_proof}}|RevokedTransientRecoveryWrap{resource_key,wrap_or_grant_identity,disposition_action_key,typed_terminal_evidence_commitment}|DestroyedFreshUnpublishedTargetObjectIdKey{resource_key,key_origin_proof,zero_canonical_publication_proof,disposition_action_key,typed_terminal_evidence_commitment}|UnpublishedTargetObjects{resource_key,quarantine_ref:PreBootstrapArtifactRef<UnpublishedTargetObjectSetQuarantine>,terminal_disposition:UnpublishedTargetObjectSetDisposition}|RetainedTombstonedNoUse{resource_key,permanent_nonuse_commitment}`. Source-key destruction has no arm. ExternalCas cleanup has exactly one ContinuityCleanup row and, unless its authenticated profile proves no target catalog applies, one prior CatalogTargetCleanup row; a no-mutation continuity disposition is just as explicit as a CAS abandonment. DirectoryBound uses DirectoryBoundZeroPublicationClosed, requires its catalog sub-arm to match the profile, and cannot encode a continuity action. `TerminallyAbandoned` proves every projected logical object, ciphertext, encoding, placement, segment/extent, transient wrap, fresh key, claim, lease, and continuity/catalog resource appears exactly once in this disposition inventory.

`PreBootstrapRestoreAbandonIntent` is first sealed with the exact zero-canonical-publication proof, frozen current action/resource inventory, and cleanup-policy recipe, then its authenticated journal transition enters `AbandonmentDrainPending` as above. After every preexisting attempt terminalizes, `PreBootstrapRestoreAbandonAuthorizeSpec` seals the now-exact total action/resource disposition plan and enters `AbandonmentAuthorized`. Only that durable state can construct `PreBootstrapAbandonmentCleanupGate` and enter CleanupInProgress. It schedules exactly the lease release, reservation burns, profile-valid continuity abandonment or DirectoryBound zero-publication closure, transient-wrap revocations, clone-target-key destruction/tombstoning, and unpublished target-object disposition required by the resource inventory. If ArchiveAcquire was already RegisteredPending, drain recovery preserves its original request/source gate until it reaches Active, then the later cleanup plan immediately releases the returned lease and records `RegisteredArchiveAcquisitionRolledForwardThenReleased`. Release/status remains legal after lease expiry under its exact cleanup contract; claim/ordinary acquisition does not. No cleanup send is legal while the root remains Building, AcquiredProjectionAllowed, BridgeFrozenForCanonicalCreation, or AbandonmentDrainPending.

Terminal journal state is `TerminallyAbandoned{sorted_action_dispositions[PreBootstrapActionDisposition],complete_planned_action_and_family_member_bijection,sorted_resource_dispositions[PreBootstrapResourceDisposition],complete_claimed_acquired_created_resource_bijection,action_to_resource_disposition_relation,full_operation_idempotency_request_source_gate_status_and_typed_terminal_lineage_commitment,final_external_head_set_commitment,zero_canonical_publication_proof,terminal_body_digest}`. No two-receipt shortcut or duplicate release/burn row exists. Crash before Armed may use the typed never-sent proof; crash after SentUnknown must status-resolve the same bytes; crash after acquisition can only resume the same projection/creation until AbandonmentAuthorized is durable, after which it can only complete the exact disposition set. The plan availability capsule, claimed authorities, external heads, typed portable artifacts, and sealed journal—not an unrooted local file—are durable recovery authority.

Before `K_restore_journal` can be destroyed on the no-RootManifest path, recovery constructs unsigned reference-free `PortablePreBootstrapAbandonmentTerminalCertificateBody {restore_id,journal_id,predecessor_active_journal_head_bytes_digest_and_cas_version,predecessor_head_and_dispatch_state_generations,final_active_capsule_digest,plan_recipe_and_final_plan_digests,plan_and_refinement_availability_certificate_digests,terminal_journal_body_digest,complete_action_and_family_member_terminal_accumulator_root,complete_resource_disposition_accumulator_root,final_external_head_and_provider_operation_tombstone_set,permanent_operation_id_and_reservation_nonreuse_floors,zero_canonical_RootManifest_RootSlot_and_target_authority_publication_proof,profile_terminal_disposition:ExternalCasCataloged{catalog_tombstone_terminal_commitment,continuity_cleanup_disposition:PreBootstrapRestoreContinuityCleanupDisposition}|DirectoryBoundCataloged{catalog_tombstone_terminal_commitment,zero_publication_closure_commitment}|DirectoryBoundEmbeddedNoCatalog{zero_catalog_applicability_proof,zero_publication_closure_commitment},unpublished_target_object_terminal_disposition_commitment,journal_key_commitment,journal_key_destruction_authorization_digest,retention_floor,body_digest}`. It names only the already-existing Active predecessor, never the future terminal head. The profile arm, action accumulator, and resource accumulator must agree exactly on whether catalog and continuity actions existed; no generic “abandoned” bit can hide a missing cleanup stage.

## Invariants & interactions
Enforces FG-INV-01, FG-INV-08 through FG-INV-11, FG-INV-14, FG-INV-16, and FG-INV-20. Consumes the G0 irreversible-dispatch and prebootstrap artifact registries, authority bindings, time prebootstrap evidence, archive backup publication/grants, continuity profiles, and filesystem whole-inode fencing. It precedes canonical restore lease/history, transform/reconciliation, abandonment, bridge, and promotion.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every named artifact, union arm, journal transition, action family, guard, receipt, freeze, accumulator, import and disposition has an exact stable registry row, bounds, MAC/AAD/body transcript, construction DAG, retention/cleanup floor, and canonical import target/disposition.
- Unit/golden tests freeze journal headers/generations, action keys, plan refinements, relocation chains, dispatch bindings, artifacts, and bridge-import bytes.
- Property/model tests prove one active journal authority, monotone generations, complete action/terminal bijection, no third publication substrate, no target-key identity before K_oid, no ordinary read/serve authority, and exactly-once canonicalization.
- Fuzz/mutation rejects cross-restore/journal/plane/contract artifacts, stale relocation, wrong staging inode, wrong MAC/key epoch, future canonical refs, missing terminal accumulator entries, conflicting refinements, and unknown required tags.
- Crash/DPOR tests every write/sync/rename/fence/refinement/dispatch/status/relocation/import/first-root boundary plus writer takeover and ENOSPC/torn-write/bit-flip.
- E2E starts from a published backup in an isolated harness-owned fixture, acquires/refines sources, crashes and relocates the journal, resumes all external attempts status-first, publishes the first hidden root, and proves byte-identical canonical import. Simulated loss is used; no repository/user file is deleted.
- JSONL emits {event_version,restore_id,journal_id,journal_generation,authority_head_digest,relocation_generation?,phase,action_family,action_key,dispatch_contract_id?,operation_id?,attempt_generation?,artifact_kind?,refinement_digest?,freeze_state?,terminal_disposition?,canonical_import_digest?,first_root_generation?,recovery_action,replay_command}. Logs exclude journal keys, plaintext keys, secrets, protected source bytes, and raw capabilities.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: ordinary ObjectIds before target K_oid, a second staging journal, mutable unframed logs, canonical/prebootstrap terminal substitution, local timeout as absence, and first-root publication without complete import/freeze evidence. The protocol is large because ambiguity here can fork identity.

## Provenance
Plan Appendix A lines 2241-2339; section 16.6 restore.

title: Implement receipt-first restore promotion, independent reopen, completion, and release
description:
## What & scope
Implement the exact post-readiness restore closure: hidden activation/visibility and service preparation, receipt-first continuity and catalog promotion, Global/Shard/Local promotion certificates, independent archive and target reopen proofs, Operational transition, audit-visible completion, source cleanup/release, and terminal registry compaction.

## Why
A valid hidden database is not yet a service. Continuity must advance before catalog exposure, catalog must require the composite receipt, each endpoint must independently reopen from durable bytes, and completion must retain source authority until every target/postcondition is proved. Otherwise stale endpoints or old capabilities can observe a half-promoted identity.

## Design — exact normative contract
`RestorePromotionAuthorityProfile` is the portable closed union `ExternalCasCataloged{expected_reserved_continuity_head_digest_and_cas_version,expected_catalog_predecessor_digest_and_version,continuity_transition_body_digest,catalog_endpoint_set_commitment}|DirectoryBoundCataloged{directory_bound_creation_evidence_public_commitment,fixed_local_continuity_digest,expected_catalog_predecessor_digest_and_version,catalog_endpoint_set_commitment}|DirectoryBoundEmbeddedNoCatalog{directory_bound_creation_evidence_public_commitment,fixed_local_continuity_digest,zero_external_catalog_applicability_proof,embedded_endpoint_or_inprocess_admission_commitment}`. The two DirectoryBound arms are Local-only; Sharded/Meta is always ExternalCasCataloged. The signed `RestoreServicePromotionManifest` is the portable closed posture union with common `{restore_id,database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,target_posture:Local|Sharded,service_visibility_epoch,authority_profile:RestorePromotionAuthorityProfile,signer_set_epoch,threshold_signatures}` and exactly one body: `Local{local_prepare_evidence:PortableCertificateProjection<LocalRestoreServicePrepareCertificate>,local_configuration_and_endpoint_commitment}` or `Sharded{meta_prepare_evidence:PortableCertificateProjection<GlobalRestoreServicePrepareCertificate>,sorted_shard_ready_evidence[PortableCertificateProjection<RestoreShardServiceReadyAck>],complete_group_topology_configuration_and_endpoint_commitment}`. `PortableCertificateProjection<T>` embeds the target `RemoteObjectIdentity`, complete export projection bytes, canonical configuration/trust evidence bytes, and signatures; it contains no `StrongRef`, `CertifiedRemoteStrongRef`, or consumer-local locator. Nullable cross-posture/profile fields are forbidden.

`RestorePromotionRootSeal<Role>` closes the proof-of-reopen race. After the role's promotion/finalize/open candidate is durably public under the role-valid proof—`PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Local|Meta>` for Local/Meta, `ShardStatePublicationCertificate` for Shard—and RootSlot-visible, recovery first builds `RestorePromotionRootSealRecipe<Role>` and completes the exact pin-ledger activation family. Only after `RestoreTerminalPinDurabilityReceipt<Role,Operational>` exists does it construct the seal `{authority_binding:AuthorityBindingFor<Role>,recipe:RestorePromotionRootSealRecipe<Role>,sealed_role_state_root_ref:StrongRef<RoleStateRoot>,sealed_root_manifest_ref:StrongRef<RootManifest>,typed_physical_inventory_ref:StrongRef<RestoreTerminalPhysicalInventory<Role,Operational>>,pin_durability_receipt_ref:StrongRef<RestoreTerminalPinDurabilityReceipt<Role,Operational>>,seal_digest}`. The receipt byte-matches the recipe digest and inventory but never contains the seal identity; the recipe excludes the receipt, so the construction graph is publication -> recipe/inventory -> pin activation receipt -> seal. The publication evidence, applied identity, state root, manifest, and winning slot must describe one publication; a Shard seal never claims an audit-visibility advance it does not have. The role-specific ordered seal-install spec installs the seal into still-hidden `OperationalPendingIndependentReopen::Sealed`. Before seal installation the only legal work is exact promotion recovery, source-lease renewal where owned, Local/Meta audit visibility or Shard publication recovery, pin activation/status recovery, evidence canonicalization/key cut, shutdown, or seal installation. Afterward only those operations plus reopen confirmation are legal. Every allowed successor preserves the same Active pin ledger/basis; ordinary admission, unrelated maintenance, checkpoint, GC, reconfiguration, key/policy/schema/data mutation, and a second promotion are rejected.

`RestoreIndependentReopenProof<Role>` opens the seal from an independent fresh process/context, not merely the current mutable head. It binds the seal, reopens every typed pinned object/encoding/key, reconstructs the sealed canonical/prepared/Raft closure, revalidates the exact profile-specific promotion authority receipt and service epoch, and supplies an authenticated proof that every successor from the sealed root to the current pending root is one of the allowed nonsemantic/recovery classes. An ExternalCas proof revalidates catalog and continuity heads; DirectoryBoundCataloged revalidates the catalog row plus inode-bound local promotion receipts; DirectoryBoundEmbeddedNoCatalog revalidates the inode/fence/slot lineage and zero-catalog-applicability proof. Slot churn or a lease renewal therefore cannot erase the proof basis or legitimize an intervening mutation. The role-specific reopen-confirm command consumes that exact proof and is the only transition to `Operational`; its published successor installs `RestoreTerminalPinBasis<Role>::Operational`. An abandonment finalize/apply instead installs `RestoreRetentionAnchor<Role>::AbandonmentPinPending` from the prebuilt pending owner; only the later role-specific pin-install command, after the abandonment root is durably published and its physical inventory is pinned, replaces that anchor with `RestoreTerminalPinBasis<Role>::Abandoned`. Local/Meta retain the matching terminal pin basis until `RestoreSourceLeaseReleaseFinalizeSpec`; that finalize atomically removes the Local pin owner or starts the Meta participant-release protocol and emits no promotion-shaped authority for an abandoned restore. Each shard retains its matching basis through its operational or abandonment acknowledgement and removes it only through `ShardRestoreTerminalPinReleaseSpec` consuming the matching certified terminal authorization. Release/tombstone floors retain every basis, seal or abandonment evidence, inventory, proof where applicable, and pin receipt until all configured shard release acknowledgements and the source-release terminal are complete. Crash tests cut every seal-build or abandonment-basis build, pin, slot publish, proof open, confirm, source-access cleanup, source-release, and shard-pin-release step, including arbitrary slot convergence and allowed lease renewals.

Promotion is profile-discriminated and service remains hidden throughout. For cataloged profiles the catalog exposes a CAS-linear per-database row head, so unrelated rows never force request rewriting. `ServiceCatalogPromotionReservationReceipt` is the portable result of `CatalogReserveHidden` and binds `{external_request_binding,restore_or_transition_id,target_database_and_security_identity,target_posture,target_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch,manifest_digest,expected_target_row_predecessor_digest_and_version,reservation_id,reservation_digest,reserved_target_row_digest_and_version,endpoint_set_commitment,state:ReservedHiddenNonexpiring,authority_signatures}`. The row CAS accepts only the exact predecessor, `AlreadyReservedEquivalent` for the same operation/request, or a semantically equivalent target-row descendant whose target remains absent/hidden with identical reservation semantics. It never accepts an arbitrary rebased row. The reservation is nonexpiring after the profile's pending boundary and blocks every competing endpoint install.

`ServicePromotionExternalOperationKind` is `CatalogReserveHidden|ContinuityEnterPromotionPending|CatalogActivateReserved|ContinuityFinalizeOperational`, specialized by `operation_subject:Restore{restore_id}|RoleTransition{migration_nonce}`. The continuity arms are inhabitable only for ExternalCas. Each external action has a distinct `ServicePromotionExternalOperationRecord<Role>` created by an ordered hidden Semantic authorize spec with exact action-body recipe, operation/idempotency identity, expected predecessor, original promotion authorization/header, resource hold, and no future publication evidence. Only its role-valid publication initializes the universal Armed/SentUnknown/status/receipt-import machine.

The exact profile sequences are:

- `ExternalCasCataloged`: (1) external `CatalogReserveHidden`; (2) external continuity CAS `RestoreReserved|CloneReserved|RoleTransitionReserved -> PromotionCatalogPending`; (3) external `CatalogActivateReserved` to `CatalogActivatedHidden{admission=CompositePromotionReceiptRequired}`; (4) external continuity CAS `PromotionCatalogPending -> Operational{PromotionReceiptRequired}`. The four noninterchangeable results are `CatalogPromotionReservationReceipt`, `PromotionContinuityPendingReceipt`, `CatalogPromotionActivationReceipt`, and `PromotionContinuityFinalizeReceipt`, each with its exact request binding/status/import lineage.
- `DirectoryBoundCataloged`: (1) external `CatalogReserveHidden`; (2) ordered Local `DirectoryBoundEnterPromotionPendingSpec` consumes the current `DirectoryBoundCreationEvidence<Local>`, hidden prepare certificate, reservation receipt, live inode lease/sequencer, and exact current slot, then RootSlot-publishes `DirectoryBoundPromotionPending`; only afterward may `DirectoryBoundPromotionPendingReceipt` be issued with `FenceBoundIrreversibleReceiptHeader`, prior/result state-root and slot evidence, fixed local continuity digest, and catalog-reservation binding; (3) external `CatalogActivateReserved` binds that local pending receipt and remains admission-hidden; (4) ordered Local `DirectoryBoundFinalizeOperationalAuthoritySpec` consumes the activation receipt and current pending state, RootSlot-publishes `DirectoryBoundOperationalReceiptRequired`, then emits distinct `DirectoryBoundOperationalAuthorityReceipt` with exact inode/fence/slot/state lineage. No external continuity action, record, CAS version, status, or receipt is created.
- `DirectoryBoundEmbeddedNoCatalog`: ordered Local pending and operational-authority transitions exactly as above but bind the manifest's zero-catalog-applicability proof and in-process admission commitment; no catalog action/row/version/receipt and no external continuity action exist.

The pending transition is the irreversible no-downgrade boundary for both DirectoryBound profiles. Before it, cancellation requires exact no-send/no-publication evidence and, for DirectoryBoundCataloged, a durable catalog reservation cancellation/tombstone. After it, recovery has only profile-specific roll-forward authority. Every local transition revalidates the same creation evidence, live inode lease, publication sequencer, fixed continuity digest, hidden service gate, and exact predecessor RootSlot immediately before publication; a member-issued receipt from unreachable staging or a different inode is invalid.

`RestoreServicePromotionReceipt` is the portable closed union `ExternalCasCataloged{restore_id,manifest_digest,service_visibility_epoch,catalog_reservation_lineage,continuity_pending_lineage,catalog_activation_lineage,continuity_finalize_lineage,prior_pending_and_operational_continuity_heads_and_cas_versions,catalog_predecessor_reserved_and_activated_versions,endpoint_set_commitment,complete_four_stage_bijection_digest,authority_signatures}|DirectoryBoundCataloged{restore_id,manifest_digest,service_visibility_epoch,catalog_reservation_lineage,directory_bound_pending_receipt_bytes_and_digest,catalog_activation_lineage,directory_bound_operational_authority_receipt_bytes_and_digest,creation_evidence_public_commitment,fixed_local_continuity_digest,catalog_predecessor_reserved_and_activated_versions,endpoint_set_commitment,complete_profile_stage_bijection_digest,authority_signatures}|DirectoryBoundEmbeddedNoCatalog{restore_id,manifest_digest,service_visibility_epoch,directory_bound_pending_receipt_bytes_and_digest,directory_bound_operational_authority_receipt_bytes_and_digest,creation_evidence_public_commitment,fixed_local_continuity_digest,zero_catalog_applicability_proof_digest,embedded_admission_commitment,complete_profile_stage_bijection_digest,authority_signatures}`. `ExternalCasRestoreServicePromotionManifestRef` and `ExternalCasRestoreServicePromotionReceiptRef` are generated tag-refined strong references whose validators require respectively the Sharded/ExternalCas manifest arm and the ExternalCasCataloged receipt arm; variant syntax is never used as a reference target. The receipt exists only after every stage of its one profile succeeds, and decoders reject cross-profile optionality or fabricated placeholder versions.

`RestorePromotionConflictAbandonSpec` is profile-specific. ExternalCasCataloged and DirectoryBoundCataloged first install a rooted no-endpoint catalog tombstone/cancel the reservation. ExternalCas then CASes the matching reserved or PromotionCatalogPending continuity head to RestoreAbandoned; DirectoryBound instead orders the inode-fenced local abandonment state and never emits a continuity CAS. Embedded DirectoryBound orders only that local abandonment. No profile can restore the same incarnation to service after its permanent conflict/abandon terminal.

`GlobalRestoreServiceFinalizeSpec {restore_id,prepare_certificate_ref:StrongRef<GlobalRestoreServicePrepareCertificate>,manifest_ref:ExternalCasRestoreServicePromotionManifestRef,promotion_receipt_ref:ExternalCasRestoreServicePromotionReceiptRef,exact_sorted_ready_ack_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<RestoreShardServiceReadyAck>],expected_meta_restore_state:WeakStateIdentity,expected_profile_terminal_authority_state,service_visibility_epoch,terminal_audit_gate}` verifies the complete rooted ExternalCas four-stage lineage and clears Meta restore state only into `OperationalPendingIndependentReopen::Unsealed`; request admission and routing remain disabled. After its audit visibility advance it yields `GlobalRestoreServiceFinalCertificate {SameGroupCertificateHeader,restore_id,finalize_record_ref:StrongRef<GlobalControlRecord>,manifest_profile_and_receipt_digests,ready_ack_commitment,post_apply_global_state_root_ref:StrongRef<GlobalStateRoot>,service_visibility_epoch,visibility_certificate_ref:StrongRef<PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Meta>>,certificate_attempt_ref:StrongRef<CertificateAttemptRecord>,canonical_signature_set}`.

A shard leaves `RecoveryReconciling` only through `ShardRestoreServiceOpenSpec {final_certificate_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<GlobalRestoreServiceFinalCertificate>,own_ready_ack_ref:StrongRef<RestoreShardServiceReadyAck>,locally_verified_promotion_receipt_ref:ExternalCasRestoreServicePromotionReceiptRef,expected_local_restore_state:WeakStateIdentity,service_visibility_epoch}` under its exact outer Meta authority, and that command selects `OperationalPendingIndependentReopen::Unsealed`, not Operational. After the open root has a durable `ShardStatePublicationCertificate`, it builds/installs the role seal above. A fresh process then creates `ShardRestoreIndependentReopenProof`, and `ShardRestoreReopenConfirmSpec {restore_id,final_certificate_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<GlobalRestoreServiceFinalCertificate>,seal_ref:StrongRef<RestorePromotionRootSeal<Shard>>,independent_reopen_proof_ref:StrongRef<ShardRestoreIndependentReopenProof>,expected_pending_state:OperationalPendingIndependentReopen::Sealed,service_visibility_epoch}` selects OperationalAwaitingSourceAccessClosure. Only after `ShardRestoreSourceAccessCloseSpec` installs the exact closure may the applied-and-durable ParticipantComplete root produce `RestoreShardOperationalAck {SameGroupCertificateHeader,restore_id,final_certificate_identity,own_ready_ack_identity,reopen_confirm_applied_identity,source_access_close_applied_identity,post_close_state_root_ref:StrongRef<ShardLogicalStateRoot>,reopen_publication_certificate_ref:StrongRef<ShardStatePublicationCertificate>,seal_ref:StrongRef<RestorePromotionRootSeal<Shard>>,operational_terminal_pin_basis_ref:OperationalRestoreTerminalPinBasisRef<Shard>,independent_reopen_proof_ref:StrongRef<ShardRestoreIndependentReopenProof>,source_access_closure_ref:StrongRef<ShardRestoreSourceAccessClosure>,terminalizing_projection_commitment,applied_shard_raft_index,service_visibility_epoch,root_slot_durability_digest,certificate_attempt_ref:StrongRef<CertificateAttemptRecord>,canonical_signature_set}`. The seal supplies the earlier open-root publication evidence; the reopen certificate byte-matches `reopen_confirm_applied_identity`, and the closure/basis/projection byte-match the post-close root. Meta routing waits for the target shard ack; direct shard endpoints reject every pending-reopen or pending-source-closure phase and require the current ExternalCas receipt, final Meta certificate, Operational participant-complete root, and reopen proof.

Meta follows the same pattern after finalize: it installs `RestorePromotionRootSeal<Meta>`, a fresh context produces `MetaRestoreIndependentReopenProof`, and `GlobalRestoreServiceCompletionSpec {restore_id,final_certificate_ref:StrongRef<GlobalRestoreServiceFinalCertificate>,meta_seal_ref:StrongRef<RestorePromotionRootSeal<Meta>>,meta_independent_reopen_proof_ref:StrongRef<MetaRestoreIndependentReopenProof>,exact_sorted_operational_ack_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<RestoreShardOperationalAck>],promotion_receipt_ref:ExternalCasRestoreServicePromotionReceiptRef,expected_restore_registry_state:PromotedAwaitingReopen,expected_meta_pending_state:OperationalPendingIndependentReopen::Sealed,expected_source_lease_generation,terminal_audit_gate}` verifies one ack from every required shard and alone selects Meta Operational. Its audit visibility advance installs `RestoreRetentionAnchor::TerminalPinBasis` with the operational basis and moves the registry to `AwaitingSourceAccessCleanup::Operational`; only the later complete source-access cleanup finalize may enter AwaitingSourceRelease. It neither hides an unready group nor releases the source lease/pins directly.

The exact Local path is independent of sharded evidence. `LocalRestoreReadyCertificate` is `{SameGroupCertificateHeader,restore_id,restore_epoch,service_visibility_epoch,current_hidden_state_root_ref:StrongRef<LogicalStateRoot>,reconciliation_completion_proof_ref:StrongRef<RestoreReconciliationCompletionProof<Local>>,ready_closure_inventory_ref:StrongRef<RestoreReadyClosureInventory<Local>>,current_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,current_checkpoint_ref:StrongRef<RecoveryCheckpoint>,current_config_floor_ref:StrongRef<ConfigPayloadFloor>,root_slot_durability_digest,one_digest_signer_lock_ref,quorum_signatures}`. `LocalRestoreActivationSpec` is `{restore_id,ready_certificate_ref:StrongRef<LocalRestoreReadyCertificate>,expected_local_restore_state:WeakStateIdentity,expected_configuration_checkpoint_and_floor,promotion_authority_basis:ExternalCasCataloged{expected_reserved_continuity_digest_and_cas_version}|DirectoryBound{creation_evidence_ref:StrongRef<DirectoryBoundCreationEvidence<Local>>,fixed_local_continuity_digest},service_visibility_epoch,terminal_audit_gate}` and moves only Reconciling -> VisibilityCommitted. After its gap-free release, `LocalRestoreActivationCertificate` owns the hidden root, exact ready evidence, profile basis, and `visibility_certificate_ref:StrongRef<PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Local>>`. `LocalRestoreServicePrepareSpec` is `{restore_id,activation_certificate_ref:StrongRef<LocalRestoreActivationCertificate>,expected_local_restore_state:WeakStateIdentity,exact_configuration_and_endpoint_set,promotion_authority_profile_recipe:ExternalCasCataloged{expected_catalog_predecessor_version}|DirectoryBoundCataloged{expected_catalog_predecessor_version}|DirectoryBoundEmbeddedNoCatalog{zero_catalog_applicability_proof},service_visibility_epoch,terminal_audit_gate}` and moves only to ServicePreparedHidden; its gap-free release yields `LocalRestoreServicePrepareCertificate` over the prepare record, hidden root, visibility certificate, endpoint/configuration commitment, exact promotion-authority profile basis, epoch, and signer transcript.

The Local arm of `RestoreServicePromotionManifest` executes exactly its selected profile and produces that profile's composite receipt first. `LocalRestoreServicePromotionSpec {restore_id,prepare_certificate_ref:StrongRef<LocalRestoreServicePrepareCertificate>,manifest_ref:StrongRef<RestoreServicePromotionManifest{target_posture=Local}>,promotion_receipt_ref:StrongRef<RestoreServicePromotionReceipt>,exact_profile_stage_operation_dispatch_or_local_publication_lineage_refs,expected_local_restore_state:WeakStateIdentity,expected_profile_terminal_authority_state,service_visibility_epoch,terminal_audit_gate}` requires manifest/prepare/receipt/profile equality and clears restore state only into `OperationalPendingIndependentReopen::Unsealed` after its exact `PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate<Local>` is durable; its registry becomes PromotedAwaitingReopen and still owns the source lease. It then installs `RestorePromotionRootSeal<Local>`. The exact generated `RestoreIndependentReopenProof<Role>` schema is the seal-bound proof above, including the allowed-successor-chain proof rather than an unpinned observation of whichever slot happens to be current. A fresh process produces `LocalRestoreIndependentReopenProof`; `LocalRestoreServiceCompletionSpec {restore_id,promotion_record_ref:StrongRef<LogicalCommandRecord>,promotion_receipt_ref:StrongRef<RestoreServicePromotionReceipt>,seal_ref:StrongRef<RestorePromotionRootSeal<Local>>,independent_reopen_proof_ref:StrongRef<LocalRestoreIndependentReopenProof>,expected_restore_registry_state:PromotedAwaitingReopen,expected_pending_state:OperationalPendingIndependentReopen::Sealed,expected_source_lease_generation,terminal_audit_gate}` alone selects Operational; its gap-free release installs `RestoreRetentionAnchor::TerminalPinBasis` with the operational basis, moves the registry to `AwaitingSourceAccessCleanup::Operational`, and yields the completion visibility certificate. Complete source-access cleanup then enters AwaitingSourceRelease; source release uses the ordered operation/dispatch/receipt/finalize protocol above. Completion never directly drops the lease or pin.

Every handshake/session/request/forwarded shard request/transaction/query child/delivery cursor/cross-session capability carries `{cluster_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch}`. Mixed or stale epochs fail before authorization or observation. `RestoreSourceLease` remains live through promotion/finalize/open, independent target reopen, operational acknowledgements, and the role-valid post-open completion audit visibility advance. `CloneNewIdentity` uses the same transform/result/guard/reconciliation/promotion machinery but assigns a new database/security namespace, `K_oid`, continuity domain, current groups/authority, and Audit clone boundary; historical evidence remains carried, old capabilities remain invalid, and source authority is never current target authority. `source_posture == expected_posture` is mandatory for both modes; Local-to-W12 is a later separate role transition.

## Invariants & interactions
Consumes bridge/readiness certificates, audit release, catalog/continuity dispatch, source cleanup/pins, role service authority, backup archive reopen, target VFS reopen, result/cursor capability migration and time evidence. Existing restore-promotion implementation and W12 sharded restore consume this exact format/protocol task.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Exact schemas/rows exist for every prepare/activation/visibility/service/promotion/open/reopen/completion/release/summary artifact and Local/Meta/Shard role arm.
- Unit/golden tests freeze the receipt-first DAG, catalog predecessor, continuity head, service epoch, participant set, independent reopen transcripts, completion inventory, source-release operation and terminal summary.
- Property/model tests prove continuity-before-catalog, hidden-before-receipt, no serve before independent reopen, one promotion or abandonment, current service epoch on every capability/frame, complete participant/postcondition closure, and source release last.
- Mutation/fuzz rejects stale continuity/catalog versions, missing receipt leg, wrong role/configuration, incomplete shard/open proof, reused old capability, wrong service epoch, missing audit visibility, premature cleanup/release, and circular future refs.
- Crash/DPOR E2E restarts at every activation/visibility/prepare/CAS/receipt/open/seal/reopen/complete/audit/release boundary for Local and sharded fixtures. Direct hidden endpoints remain unreachable; archive and target reopen are performed by fresh processes.
- JSONL emits {event_version,restore_id,role_and_group,phase,continuity_head_digest?,catalog_head_digest?,composite_receipt_digest?,service_visibility_epoch,participant_count,participant_ack_count,archive_reopen_digest?,target_reopen_digest?,completion_inventory_digest?,audit_visibility_position?,source_release_state?,terminal_summary_digest?,recovery_action,replay_command}. Public output never exposes hidden endpoints or internal refs.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: catalog-first publication, serving a hidden root, same-process-only reopen, source lease release at logical completion, reusing old service capabilities, and a single global done bit without role acknowledgements. Any incomplete proof leaves service hidden and source retention live.

## Provenance
Plan Appendix A lines 2569-2601; G2/G3 restore gates.

title: Integrate restore promotion profiles, endpoint gating, and CloneNewIdentity
description:
## What & scope
Implement the back half of restore: the role-tagged `RestoreState` phase machines, ready certificates, profile-discriminated service promotion via external continuity/catalog CAS yielding `RestoreServicePromotionReceipt`, the `RestorePromotionRootSeal`/`OperationalPendingIndependentReopen` reopen ladder, endpoint gating on `{cluster_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch}`, independent target reopen, completion and lease release, and `CloneNewIdentity`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
A restored database must be provably complete, then visible, then service-prepared, then promoted — with each transition a consumed certificate, so no crash or race can advertise a half-reconciled database (FG-INV-04's hidden-restore clause). Clone gets first-class identity hygiene: new namespace and keys, explicit audit linkage without impersonating the source. B5: promotion is an externally linearized CAS event; B6: agents observe typed phases, never a flapping endpoint.

## Design — normative detail
**Activation and promotion.** Canonical Local phases: `Reconciling -> VisibilityCommitted -> ServicePreparedHidden -> Operational`; Sharded Meta adds `ActivationOrdered` after Reconciling; each shard is `Reconciling -> ActivationAppliedHidden -> VisibilityApplied -> ServicePreparedHidden -> Operational` (`RestoreState` closed role union; each applied phase stores only its input command + assigned order, never future records). "Ready" is not an unsequenced mutation: it is a same-group certificate over a current hidden `Reconciling` root whose exhaustive reconciliation status is `Complete`; certificates are owned by the certificate ledger and consumed by later commands — `RestoreState` never points forward. Visibility is never endpoint publication. After every shard is visibility-applied, Meta orders `GlobalRestoreServicePrepareSpec`, shards order their prepare and export ready acks, and only then can a portable manifest CAS the continuity head and external catalog and yield `RestoreServicePromotionReceipt`. `GlobalRestoreServiceFinalizeSpec` and each `ShardRestoreServiceOpenSpec` must consume that existing receipt before clearing restore state. Promotion is profile-discriminated: `RestorePromotionAuthorityProfile` is the closed union `ExternalCasCataloged|DirectoryBoundCataloged|DirectoryBoundEmbeddedNoCatalog` (the two DirectoryBound arms are Local-only; Sharded/Meta is always ExternalCasCataloged), and `ServicePromotionExternalOperationKind` is `CatalogReserveHidden|ContinuityEnterPromotionPending|CatalogActivateReserved|ContinuityFinalizeOperational` — each stage an ordered hidden authorize spec plus the universal Armed/SentUnknown/status/receipt-import machine, whose four noninterchangeable ExternalCas stage receipts compose the profile-stage bijection inside `RestoreServicePromotionReceipt` (for DirectoryBound profiles the ordered local pending transition is the irreversible no-downgrade boundary and no external continuity action exists). For cataloged profiles the catalog exposes a CAS-linear per-database row head; `ServiceCatalogPromotionReservationReceipt` (state `ReservedHiddenNonexpiring`) blocks every competing endpoint install, and the row CAS accepts only the exact predecessor, `AlreadyReservedEquivalent` for the same operation/request, or a semantically equivalent hidden target-row descendant — never an arbitrary rebased row. Clearing restore state never selects `Operational` directly: promotion/finalize/open installs only `OperationalPendingIndependentReopen::Unsealed` (registry `PromotedAwaitingReopen`, still owning the source lease); recovery builds `RestorePromotionRootSealRecipe<Role>`, completes pin-ledger activation (`RestoreTerminalPinDurabilityReceipt<Role,Operational>`), and installs `RestorePromotionRootSeal<Role>` (state `Sealed`; construction graph publication -> recipe/inventory -> pin activation receipt -> seal, and the receipt never contains the seal identity); a fresh process produces the seal-bound role `RestoreIndependentReopenProof` — including the authenticated proof that every successor from the sealed root to the current pending root is an allowed nonsemantic/recovery class, so slot churn or an allowed lease renewal cannot erase the proof basis — and the role completion/reopen-confirm spec consuming that exact proof is the only transition to `Operational`, installing `RestoreRetentionAnchor::TerminalPinBasis` and moving the registry to `AwaitingSourceAccessCleanup::Operational`; only complete source-access cleanup then enters `AwaitingSourceRelease` (lease release itself is `w11-restore-lease` scope). Between promotion and reopen confirmation only exact promotion recovery, source-lease renewal where owned, audit-visibility/publication recovery, pin activation/status recovery, evidence canonicalization/key cut, shutdown, and seal installation/reopen confirmation are legal — ordinary admission, unrelated maintenance, checkpoint, GC, reconfiguration, key/policy/schema/data mutation, and a second promotion are rejected. Fabric/direct endpoints require the current receipt plus role-valid local open state, and Meta routing additionally requires the destination shard operational ack (`RestoreShardOperationalAck`, produced only after the shard's reopen-confirm and `ShardRestoreSourceAccessCloseSpec` closure); every handshake, request, session, forwarded shard request, query/transaction child, delivery cursor, and cross-session capability binds `{cluster_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch}` — missing/stale fails before observation. The `RestoreSourceLease` remains live through independent target reopen (`RestoreIndependentReopenProof` from a fresh process) and the post-open completion record, then releases.

**Clone.** `CloneNewIdentity` uses the same lease/transform/guard/reconciliation/service gate but assigns a new database/security namespace, `K_oid`, continuity domain, group IDs, and current authority; posture is preserved (Local stays Local; Local->W12 is a separate audited activation). Historical signed evidence sits behind an explicit clone boundary; a new `AuditDomainId` plus signed `AuditCloneBoundary` links source evidence without claiming old tickets were target-issued; the privacy domain remains shared unless an externally authorized disjoint-population record permits a new one. Old capabilities are invalid.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-04 (excerpt): restore/role-transition state remains unobservable while reconciliation, activation, pipeline release, service preparation, or independent reopen is pending; every request, cursor, capability, and forwarded shard operation matches the current incarnation/service epoch. FG-INV-16 (excerpt): the restore-source lease is released only at its exact terminal (post-reopen completion record). FG-INV-07 (each applied phase stores only its input command + assigned order; `RestoreState` never points forward). Promotion latency is slo class; clone drills are deployment-gate evidence.

## Interactions
Blocked by `w11-restore` (reconciled hidden root, transform, guards); consumes `w2-continuity-profiles` (continuity-head CAS, external catalog), `w9-audit-release` (the durable role-valid `PortableSemanticVisibilityCertificate` gating the promotion spec and every `ServicePromotionExternalOperationRecord` dispatch initialize), and `w9-audit-continuity` (`AuditDomainId`, `AuditCloneBoundary` for clone linkage). `w11-restore-lease` release runs after the completion record. Fabric endpoint gating is consumed by `w10-server`/`w10-fgp-core`; the Meta/Shard ladders feed `w12-backup-restore`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Phase machine: per-role transition exhaustiveness (Local three-phase, Meta four-phase, Shard four-phase); ready certificate signable only over `Reconciling + Complete` (mutation negatives: Pending slot, wrong root, forward pointer). Hidden state: connection/session/capability attempts in every pre-promotion phase fail **before observation** with typed errors; visibility-without-promotion serves nothing. Promotion: finalize/open specs without an existing `RestoreServicePromotionReceipt` rejected; two promotion contenders — external CAS admits one; stale `{cluster_incarnation,service_visibility_epoch}` on every surface (handshake, request, forwarded shard op, cursor, cross-session capability) fails closed. Reopen/completion: `RestoreIndependentReopenProof` from a fresh process precedes the completion record; lease release before completion rejected. Seal/reopen ladder: promotion clearing state directly to `Operational` is unencodable (only `OperationalPendingIndependentReopen::Unsealed`); completion/reopen-confirm without the seal-bound proof rejected; a reopen proof built from the same process or from the current mutable head instead of the installed seal rejected; slot churn or an allowed lease renewal between seal and reopen preserves the proof basis while a disallowed intervening mutation fails it; disallowed work in the Unsealed/Sealed windows (ordinary admission, checkpoint, GC, reconfiguration, key/policy/schema/data mutation, second promotion) each rejected; Meta routing before the destination shard operational ack rejected. Profile matrix: each of the three promotion profiles executes exactly its stage sequence (four-stage ExternalCas bijection; DirectoryBound pending transition as irreversible boundary), and cross-profile receipt fields or fabricated placeholder versions are rejected; catalog CAS admits `AlreadyReservedEquivalent` retries idempotently and rejects a competing reservation with a different operation/request. Clone: new namespace/`K_oid`/continuity domain/group IDs asserted; old capabilities invalid; source-posture preservation (Local stays Local); `AuditCloneBoundary` links without claiming source tickets; shared privacy domain unless the disjoint-population record exists. Crash rows at every activation/visibility/prepare/promotion/seal-build/seal-install/reopen/confirm/finalize/open/completion boundary. E2e drill with logs: `RecoverSameIdentity` to Operational then `CloneNewIdentity` drill; logs record phase transitions, promotion receipt identity, pending-reopen states, seal and reopen-proof identities, service epochs, and clone boundary artifacts.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: serving from `ServicePreparedHidden` (visibility is never endpoint publication); "ready" as an unsequenced state mutation (it is a certificate over a hidden root); Local->W12 posture change during clone (separate audited activation); minting a fresh privacy domain by default (requires externally authorized disjoint-population record). Risk: promotion-CAS authority unavailability delays cutover — the restore state is stable and resumable indefinitely; no timeout path exists by design.

## Provenance
§16.6 (lines 1208-1210), App A lines 2547, 2569-2601; App F FG-INV-04/07/16.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

This bead owns end-to-end orchestration across those primitives, profile-discriminated endpoint admission/gating, adapter/status integration, CloneNewIdentity semantics, conformance matrices, and whole-flow E2E only.
