Every state transition that can affect a held predicate is generated with a mandatory reservation-conflict check — a conflicting commit/head change, key retirement, policy/revocation reclamation, topology retirement, resource release, or GC must wait, transfer the reservation exactly, or reject. `GlobalFinalCertificationCancelSpec` names the exact Active reservation, complete hold-release recipe, and `NoTerminalPlanLockShareOrOrderProof` (built from one linearizable barrier; invalid if any terminal semantic plan, signing attempt, terminal command, Ordered supplement, candidate, or external audit CAS exists); apply moves to `CancelledBeforeSignature` and releases exactly its holds; the admission fence remains Armed so recovery can take a higher certification generation or a certified abort. Once a signing plan or any lock exists, cancellation is permanently illegal and the selected terminal must finish.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-02: the (batch-scoped) reservation is the single legal live owner of the shared final-certification basis; exclusivity is per generation, not per candidate. FG-INV-17: once an Active reservation freezes the basis, rebase is forbidden; conflicting drift must use the proved pre-signature cancel/restart path, while any terminal audit plan/lock/share requires completion of that selected basis. Invariant-class; checkpoint/configuration/backup/restore/GC inventories must include the root, every Active record, both hold roots, and all audit/order maintenance evidence.

## Interactions
Consumes admission fences from `w12-prepare` and audit-plan sequencing from `w9-audit-release`; the certifier (`w12-certification`) selects into it; `GlobalTxnCommand` apply (`w12-decision-visibility`) consumes it; hold checks constrain `w12-escrow-dp-alloc`, `w12-topology`, `w12-recovery-gc`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Deleting any generated reservation-conflict check is a G0 negative fixture. Tests: CAS forbids two successors; cancel-after-lock permanently illegal; reservation survives crash/reconfiguration with holds transferred exactly; batch arm: per-candidate sub-hold consumed only by its member's terminal; abort reservation with `MetaAbort` selection byte-matches the admitted abort command. Reserve/sign/cancel ordering model per FG-INV-17. E2E: scripted Meta group under concurrent terminals — reserve -> sign -> consume for both MetaCommit and MetaAbort selections, plus reserve -> cancel-before-signature -> higher-certification-generation re-reserve, while injected conflicting maintenance (branch-head change, key retirement, policy/revocation reclamation, topology retirement, resource release, GC) runs against held predicates and must wait, transfer exactly, or reject; include one batch-arm run proving per-candidate sub-holds are consumed only by their members' terminal commands and the one-member batch byte-matches the single-candidate schema. DETAILED LOGGING (required): every reservation state transition logs `{registration identity, admission_generation, certification_generation, selection kind, state Active|CancelledBeforeSignature|Consumed, coordinate/obligation hold-root ids, conflicting-transition verdict wait|transfer|reject}`; every cancel logs its `NoTerminalPlanLockShareOrOrderProof` quiescence barrier id; tests assert the log stream reconstructs the exact CAS history of `TerminalCertificationReservationRoot<Meta>`.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: long-held reservations block conflicting maintenance (by design). Rejected: terminal-command revalidation of mutable bases; timeout-released holds.

## Provenance
App A 1736-1750, 1896-1900; §14.6 (1087); App F FG-INV-02/17 (3131/3146).

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Prove and torture W12 formal, crash, recovery, and format contracts
description:
## What & scope
Deliver W12's separate bounded formal models, durable-format/protocol fuzzing, and exhaustive fault/recovery torture over Meta, every shard, and Local-to-Sharded activation. This task owns the post-1.0 formal/torture evidence that the 1.0 formal and Local crash beads must not claim.

## Why
Sharding adds new authorities and multi-phase ownership transfers whose safety is not a corollary of Local proofs: pre-response begin reservation, global certification, distributed visibility, remote trust/release, distributed key destruction and GC, Sharded backup/restore, topology transitions, and irreversible Local retirement. The plan names ten separate W12 TLA+/TLC models and requires crash proofs at every phase. They need explicit bounds, refinement bridges, live format readers, real-process campaigns, and negative evidence.

## Formal lanes (scoped and honest)
Create separate TLA+/TLC models for: (a) begin reservation, attempt generation, ticket claim, statement/workspace publication, terminal/autocommit delivery, status, cancellation, read close; (b) admission, shard prepare, signer-locked terminal candidate, external CAS/mirror, decision publication, shard audit projection/post-visibility acknowledgement/global-delta publication; (c) provisional-cut replacement with inherited absent bytes and later activation; (d) closed-attempt build/attest/publish plus detailed/compacted status equivalence; (e) six-stage remote release; (f) staged distributed key activation and physical destruction; (g) GC quarantine/no-resurrection and physical completion; (h) exact backup publication/release; (i) restore reservation, leaves-first transformation, hidden activation/visibility/service preparation, receipt-first finalize/open/reopen/completion; (j) Local-to-W12 activation, authority transfer, RetiredLocal finalization, reclamation. Include partitions, Meta/shard joint reconfiguration, conflict-index lifetime, constraint reservations, topology moves, and declared fairness.

Each proof-lane manifest names exact abstraction, role/posture/feature activation predicate, state/participant bounds, crash/failure assumptions, fairness, checked properties, checker command and digest, implementation trace schema, refinement/conformance status, and everything not proved. Trace export demonstrates captured executions are allowed by the model; it is not called a full implementation-refinement proof. Runtime monitors do not inherit model-check completeness.

## Fault, recovery, and fuzz campaigns
- Crash/partition at every Sharded Genesis and Local freeze/seal/certificate/projection/first-entry/authority-transfer/RetiredLocal/finalize/reclamation point.
- Crash at every begin reservation, ticket/statement/workspace/delivery, prepare/certification/availability, Meta audit candidate/external batch CAS/mirror/visibility, decision, shard projection/ack, global-delta, TerminalPending/compaction, remote-release, key, GC, backup, restore, and topology boundary.
- Per Meta/shard matrices for payload/certificate loss, checkpoint+suffix recovery, donor loss/poisoning, leader loss, current/joint configuration floors, rolling upgrade/downgrade refusal, exact status, backup, restore, service-open, and no-resurrection.
- Fuzz every new W12 durable reader/decoder, role-tagged command/frame, cut/proof, remote-ref trust envelope, manifest, certificate, and transition registry row. Cross-role substitution, mixed encoding, truncated/duplicate/reordered arrays, stale epochs, invalid sorted bijections, and strong-reference cycles fail closed.
- LDFI uses the full dependency lineage; residual random chaos guards blind spots. Every scenario declares filesystem, failure, placement, quorum, external-authority, time, continuity, resource, and fairness models.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Unit tests for model translators, invariant predicates, trace exporters/importers, durable reader validation, fault-hook placement, campaign generation, and manifest/schema lint; mutation tests prove each property/checker catches a seeded violation.
- Property/metamorphic tests verify encode/decode stability, cross-role rejection, batch/order invariance only where registered, idempotent retry, no premature release/reclaim, no timeout fracture, and recovery convergence to a global-oracle-legal state.
- Model checks complete at every registered bound with counterexample replay tests; at least one intentionally weakened model per lane produces the expected counterexample, preventing vacuous properties.
- Simulation torture executes every generated active crash row with the W12 global/protocol oracles attached; matrix completeness fails for any activated transition with no row.
- Real-process E2E boots Meta and at least three shards, then performs Local conversion, multi-statement cross-shard commit, membership and topology transition, remote release, key rotation/destruction, GC, exact backup, and receipt-first restore while killing/partitioning processes at selected phases; it independently reopens the archive/target and proves no stale endpoint/capability/role or old ObjectId is accepted.
- A final evidence audit proves every live W12 invariant clause maps to a unit/property/model/simulation/E2E result and structured diagnostic ancestry. Otherwise `sharding=true` remains absent.

## Detailed structured diagnostics
Every model run and campaign row emits JSONL `{run_id,phase:"W12",lane_id,model_digest,bounds,fairness_profile,scenario_id,seed,role,group_id,configuration_topology_service_epochs,command_transition,crash_point_id,fault_hypothesis_id,logical_txn_meta_shard_positions,attempt_statement_workspace_decision_remote_key_gc_backup_restore_ids,expected_property,actual,oracle_verdicts,recovery_verdict,verdict}`. Model counterexamples include complete state traces and the exact checker command. Runtime failures include the complete secret-redacted §15.1 artifact, minimized workload/schedule/input, first divergence, all evidence identities, and executable replay command; sampled commands run in CI. Passing rows use the same schema, and the W12 gate report is rebuilt from logs alone.

## Dependencies and phase boundary
Consumes the completed W12 implementation, the W12 simulation/global-oracle task, and the reusable 1.0 formal/torture engines. Feeds only the W12 verification epic and W12 gate. It must never become a dependency of G4 or retroactively expand a G1-G4 claim.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: one monolithic unbounded model; calling trace conformance refinement proof; sampling durability boundaries; clean-shutdown-only distributed tests; reusing Local model results; weakening semantics to avoid Meta sequencing. State explosion is managed with separate bounded models and refinement manifests, never hidden scope.

## Provenance
Plan §15.3, §15.5 and §19 Gate W12; Appendix F W12 clauses; Appendix A W12 role/public formats.

title: Implement the one scalar semantic clock: Meta sequences, HLC, and the record chain
description:
## What & scope
Build the Meta consensus group's semantic clock and command-record chain: Meta-issued `GlobalLogicalCommandSeq`, transaction-only `GlobalCommitSeq`, global logical HLC, the `GlobalTxnRecord`/`GlobalControlRecord`/`GlobalStateRoot`/`GlobalStatePayload` chain, the order-attempt supplement machinery, and the W12 history-reference wrappers. Shard Raft order is deliberately nonsemantic.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1: in sharded posture the three counters are Meta-issued global *aliases*, not vector clocks; Chronicle, branches, Ripple, and replay keep one scalar time. B5: order/HLC freshness is deliberately outside stable semantic prepared ownership and signed audit bytes, so evidence never has to be re-signed when an order race is lost. Rejected at §3.4/§14.6: vector time, federated shard histories, shard-local semantic bypass.

## Design — normative detail
**Clock rules.** Every canonical mutation passes through Meta; shard Raft indices order durability/apply only and never move time or heads. Meta computes HLC from the previous persisted value and normalized proposal observations. I/O batching of already-certified entries is allowed; same-basis certification only under the virtual-serial law (`w12-certification`).

**Order supplements.** `MetaOrderSubject = Terminal{final_certification_reservation_ref:StrongRef<GlobalFinalCertificationReservation>,required_state:Active,selected_terminal_digest} | Control{typed_payload_ref:StrongRef<GlobalSequenceNeutralSpec>,spec_body_digest,expected_state_conditions_digest,terminal_audit_freeze_commitment}`. The proposer builds `MetaOrderAttemptInput {order_attempt_id,subject,semantic_prepared_ownership_id,hlc_proposal_evidence_ref:StrongRef<MetaHlcProposalEvidence>,expected_next_global_logical_command_seq,expected_next_global_commit_seq:NotApplicable|Commit{value},configuration_ref,body_digest}` plus a `MetaOrderAttemptAvailabilityCertificate`. Commit applicability derives from the immutable selected terminal/control kind — abort/read/control cannot smuggle a commit-sequence assignment. Voters derive next sequence/HLC only from that input and current persisted HLC; if the observation ages out or the expected sequence loses a race, the supplement is retired with a linearizable nonorder proof (`OrderAttemptRetirementEvidence`) and a fresh attempt is certified without changing semantic ownership, reservations, or audit bytes. `PreparedOrderAttemptRoot<Meta>` entries are `Available{input_ref,availability_certificate_ref,maintenance_install_index}|Ordered{role_order,commit_order:None|Some,semantic_command_identity,semantic_raft_index}|RetiredStale{retirement_evidence_ref,successor_attempt_id}`. A terminal reservation CAS, or a control spec's exact idempotency/expected-state CAS, admits at most one ordered semantic command across all supplements.

**Record chain.** `GlobalTxnRecord {predecessor:ConditionalGlobalCommandRef,command_ref:StrongRef<GlobalTxnCommand>,decision:Committed|Aborted,assigned_global_logical_command_seq,assigned_global_commit_seq?,global_logical_hlc,marker_ref:StrongMarkerRef?,final_effect_digest,resulting_global_state_payload_digest:WeakDigest}`. `GlobalControlOrigin = Prior{predecessor}|LocalActivationBridge{transition_ref,frozen_local_head,Lf,Cf,Hf,local_chain_mmr_checkpoint_projection_digests}|RecoveryBridge{bridge_spec_ref,source_manifest_identity,transform_and_projection_digest}` — only the first activation record may use `LocalActivationBridge`, only the first guarded restore record `RecoveryBridge`. `GlobalStateRoot {payload_ref:StrongRef<GlobalStatePayload>,global_command_head:StrongGlobalCommandRef?}`. Every registration, statement publication, admission/cancel/read-close, policy/key/topology/GC/remote-retention transition, directory publication, decision/delta publication, activation, and restore bridge enters this one contiguous Meta chain. `GlobalStatePayload` is the generated Meta Semantic-plane schema (branch head/manifest/key-epoch roots, topology, conflict index, begin/attempt/statement/outcome indexes, constraint/reservation roots, resource/privacy/DP, policy/revocation, audit/transparency, retention/derived/replay/backup/restore, decision-certificate and delta-batch registries, compaction floors); audit continuity and delivery owners live only in `AuditVisibilityProtocolState<Meta>` under the RootManifest Protocol slot — a payload alias field is illegal.

**History wrappers (within-group only):** `StrongGlobalCommandRef/ConditionalGlobalCommandRef(axis=GlobalLogical)/WeakGlobalCommandIdentity` target `GlobalTxnRecord|GlobalControlRecord`; `ConditionalGlobalTxnInputRef` targets an already-built `GlobalTxnCommand`, valid only when the record at that sequence names the same input; `StrongShardCommandRef/ConditionalShardCommandRef(axis=ShardRaft)/WeakShardCommandIdentity` target `ShardCommandRecord`. Cross-group carriage always requires `CertifiedRemoteStrongRef`. Shard state: `ShardCommandRecord {origin:Prior|RecoveryBridge,shard_raft_index,command,result_refs,resulting_shard_payload_digest}`; shard order cannot move branch heads or semantic time.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-08: logical-command predecessor order and the transaction-marker subsequence are contiguous at their sequences; every role-tagged Raft snapshot matches its precise visible cut/root/configuration/positions; fresh Sharded Genesis/Local activation never mix role histories. FG-INV-07: the durable strong/uncut-conditional graph is acyclic; every pre-order input excludes its future command/result/root; `command_contracts.toml` is bijective with every role command arm. FG-INV-01: matching retries return the recorded lineage. Sequencer throughput/latency numbers are benchmark-class (Appendix G/§17), disclosed as serial + batched ceilings.

## Interactions
Consumes quorum machinery from `w2-order-raft`/`w11-raft-multi` and the D1/D2 commit discipline from `w2-commit-protocol`. Produces the ordering substrate for `w12-registration-snapshot`, `w12-certification`, `w12-decision-visibility`; `GlobalStatePayload` roots consumed by `w12-constraints-authority`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Unit/property: checked counter mismatch, duplicate subject, self-staleness, retirement-after-order, command/supplement substitution all fail closed. Crash tests: stale HLC evidence before/during signing, intervening commands, leader/configuration change, multiple fresh supplements — exactly one semantic application ever. Generated log-to-state verifier proves exact role-specific root/config/prefix at every cut; cross-role command injection rejected (gate requirement). E2E script: 10k mixed txn/control commands across leader failovers; assert contiguous `GlobalLogicalCommandSeq`, commit-seq increments only on committed transactions, HLC monotone; log every retired supplement with its nonorder proof id.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: per-command Meta apply chain is the residual ceiling (stated honestly at the gate). Rejected: vector clocks; shard-local sequence assignment; signing order/HLC into audit bodies (would force re-signing on order races).

## Provenance
§14.6 bullet 1 (1081); App A 1402-1404, 1644-1656, 1752-1754; §19:1350.

title: Implement exact Meta/Shard roots, keys, checkpoints, prepared, and certificate formats
description:
## What & scope
Implement exact Meta/Shard canonical payload, root, command, key-distribution/destruction, checkpoint/floor, prepared-root, certificate-ledger, and projection formats. This task is the durable schema prerequisite for W12 meta clock, preparation, certification, constraints, decision, recovery and key lifecycle.

## Why
W12 cannot be a role-erased extension of Local Chronicle. Meta owns global semantic order; Shards own nonsemantic partition state. Their roots, logs, checkpoints, prepared ownership, keys and certificates require disjoint tags and complete generated inventories so cross-role bytes and omitted state are rejected.

## Design — exact normative contract
Shard canonical state is parallel but deliberately nonsemantic. The following brace list is a compact navigation projection of generated `ShardLogicalStatePayload`, not its field registry: `{database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,bootstrap_phase:Genesis|CheckpointInstalled|Operational|OperationalPendingIndependentReopen|RecoveryReconciling|RecoveryAbandoned|RoleTransitionPreparedHidden,role_transition_activation_state_ref:StrongRef<RoleTransitionActivationState>?,shard_id,topology_epoch,partition_state_roots,shard_constraint_state_root,constraint_reservation_index_root,prepared_attempt_root,applied_decision_index_root,terminal_abort_tombstone_root,fragment_delta_batch_index_root:StrongRef<ShardFragmentDeltaBatchIndex>,shard_derived_component_registry_root,shard_key_material_registry_root,active_meta_projection_root:StrongRef<ActiveMetaProjectionRoot>,global_applied_logical_command_seq,global_applied_commit_seq,meta_policy_epoch,meta_revocation_index,meta_key_epoch_commitment,audit_visible_global_prefix,retention_map_root:StrongRef<RetentionMap>,backup_registry_root,restore_state_ref:StrongRef<RestoreState>?,restore_retention_anchor:RestoreRetentionAnchor<Shard>,remote_retention_authority_root:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionObligationRoot>,remote_retention_consumer_root:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionConsumerRoot>,remote_configuration_trust_root:StrongRef<RemoteConfigurationTrustRoot>,shard_recovery_checkpoint_ref:StrongRef<ShardRecoveryCheckpoint>?,shard_config_payload_floor_ref:StrongRef<ShardConfigPayloadFloor>?}`; it has fresh three-state bootstrap, hidden role-transition preparation, and restore reconciliation/abandonment. During restore it remains `RecoveryReconciling` through activation, visibility apply, and `ShardRestoreServicePrepareSpec`; those produce hidden `ActivationAppliedHidden`, `VisibilityApplied`, and `ServicePreparedHidden`. `ShardRestoreAbandonApplySpec` alone selects RecoveryAbandoned with no restore-state ref, payload `RestoreRetentionAnchor::AbandonmentPinPending`, and registry `AbandonedAwaitingTerminalPin`; that phase admits only certified Meta abandonment recovery, exact abandonment-pin installation, source-lease projection refresh, and terminal controls and can never serve. After that root is durable, `ShardRestoreAbandonmentPinInstallSpec` alone replaces the pending anchor with `RestoreRetentionAnchor::TerminalPinBasis` and enters `AbandonedParticipantComplete`; only then may the Shard issue its abandon acknowledgement. The exact `ShardRestoreServiceOpenSpec` for the same restore, final Meta certificate, and already-issued promotion receipt clears restore state only into `OperationalPendingIndependentReopen::Unsealed`; seal installation and `ShardRestoreReopenConfirmSpec` with a fresh independent proof alone reach Operational, and request admission rejects every pending phase. `ActiveMetaProjectionRoot` is keyed by the generated exhaustive `MetaProjectionSlot` registry, not a five-slot hand list. Every slot value has exactly one source: `Genesis{certificate_ref:StrongRef<ShardedGenesisCertificate>,payload_ref:StrongRef<GenesisMetaProjectionPayload>,projection_digest}|Activation{transition_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedRoleTransitionRef>,projection_ref:StrongRef<CertifiedTransitionArtifactRef<LocalToShardProjection>>,payload_ref:StrongRef<ActivationMetaProjectionPayload>,projection_digest}|Control{source_global_control_identity,source_global_prefix,payload:TypedCertifiedMetaProjectionPayload,projection_digest}`. The registry includes every shard-relevant topology, catalog/schema, constraint/owner, branch/head/key/grant, ID-allocation, policy/revocation/audit, retention/trust, derived-generation, backup/restore, GC/reconfiguration, and delivery/frontier effect; each Global control kind has exactly one generated `NoShardEffect{proof rule}` or typed targeted slot-update row. Genesis/activation payloads are typed consumer-local closures constructed after their certificate and contain no raw remote edge. Aggregate scalars byte-match rooted values and are cross-checks only. `ShardConstraintStateRoot` contains aggregate contributions and prepare-keyed reservation refs; prepare installs and decision consumes/releases them. `ShardCommandOrigin` is the closed union `Prior{predecessor:ConditionalShardCommandRef}|RecoveryBridge{bridge_spec_ref:StrongRef<RecoveryBridgeSpec<Shard>>,source_manifest_identity:WeakDigest,transform_and_projection_digest}`. `ShardCommandRecord` is `{origin:ShardCommandOrigin,shard_raft_index,command:StrongRef<ShardPrepareCommand|ShardDecisionApplyCommand|ShardControlCommand>,result_refs[StrongRef],resulting_shard_payload_digest:WeakDigest}`; only the first guarded restore record uses `RecoveryBridge`, while fresh Genesis has no head and all later records use `Prior`. `ShardLogicalStateRoot` is `{payload_ref:StrongRef<ShardLogicalStatePayload>,shard_command_head:StrongShardCommandRef?}`. Shard order cannot move branch heads or semantic time. Generated checkpoint/floor/backup/GC coverage includes every root above.

For Shard, generated activated slots additionally include `shard_security_state_projection_ref`, `shard_allocation_lease_and_reservation_root`, `shard_escrow_grant_and_reservation_root`, `shard_valid_time_projection_ref`, `shard_result_transport_projection_root`, `shard_format_compatibility_projection_ref`, `shard_bulk_staging_root`, `shard_derived_build_registry_root`, `shard_gc_operation_root`, `shard_backup_protocol_root`, `shard_restore_registry_root`, and `shard_capability_migration_root`. Each is either shard-owned protocol state or a certified Meta projection selected through `ActiveMetaProjectionRoot`; none is a second semantic authority. The scalar `meta_policy_epoch` and `meta_revocation_index` are cross-checks of `shard_security_state_projection_ref`, not authorization inputs by themselves.

Key authority is Meta-owned but ciphertext/envelope material follows its data shard, using an acyclic four-phase protocol. First, `GlobalBranchKeyDistributionPlan {plan_id,operation:Fork|Grant|Rotate,topology_state_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,expected_prior_branch_head_and_key_registry_digests,new_branch_and_epoch_record_refs[StrongRef],sorted_per_shard_recipes[{shard_domain:ConsensusDomain,assigned_partition_ranges,expected_envelope_write_key_epochs,material_commitment,recipient_and_wrap_policy,required_remote_grant_ref:StrongRef<RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence>}],complete_shard_range_and_material_commitment,activation_cas,policy_epoch}` is prebuilt without any shard certificate. `GlobalBranchKeyDistributionPlanSpec` orders it and changes only the plan registry to `Distributing`; the new epoch is nonqueryable.

Second, each shard imports a certified-remote plan/typed recipe and orders `ShardKeyMaterialStageSpec {plan_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<GlobalBranchKeyDistributionPlan>,own_recipe_index,expected_topology_epoch,expected_shard_configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,expected_prior_key_registry_entry,local_envelope_wrap_opener_root_refs[StrongRef],complete_local_material_inventory_ref:StrongRef<KeyMaterialInventory>,payload_availability_certificate_ref:StrongRef<PayloadAvailabilityCertificate>}`. Apply installs `ShardKeyMaterialProjection {plan_identity,graph,branch,envelope_epoch,write_key_epoch,assigned_partition_ranges,local_envelope_wrap_opener_root_refs,availability_floor,status:Staged}`. Staged material cannot satisfy a read, effect basis, prepare, backup-as-active, or current key lookup. The shard then creates purpose-specific `ShardKeyMaterialAvailabilityCertificate {SameGroupCertificateHeader,purpose:StagedAvailability,plan_identity,shard_id,topology_epoch,configuration_identity,staged_projection_ref:StrongRef<ShardKeyMaterialProjection>,exact_partition_and_material_commitment,inventory_root_ref:StrongRef<KeyMaterialInventory>,payload_availability_certificate_ref:StrongRef<PayloadAvailabilityCertificate>,one_digest_signer_lock_ref,quorum_signatures}`.

Third, Meta builds `GlobalKeyEnvelopeManifest {plan_ref:StrongRef<GlobalBranchKeyDistributionPlan>,topology_state_ref:StrongRef<TopologyState>,branch_epoch_registry_candidate_ref:StrongRef,sorted_shard_availability_refs[CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<ShardKeyMaterialAvailabilityCertificate>],complete_shard_range_and_material_commitment,meta_grant_root_ref:StrongRef,body_digest:BodyDigest<GlobalKeyEnvelopeManifest>}` and orders `GlobalBranchKeyManifestActivationSpec {plan_ref,manifest_ref:StrongRef<GlobalKeyEnvelopeManifest>,expected_plan_state:Distributing,expected_prior_branch_head_and_key_registry_digests,activation_cas,terminal_audit_gate}`. The registered body transcript excludes only `body_digest`. Apply verifies one matching certificate for every and only planned shard/range, atomically activates the branch/key epoch, and moves the replaced epoch to `Retiring`; it never creates material. Fourth, each shard consumes the generated typed Meta projection through `ShardKeyMaterialActivateSpec`, byte-matches plan/manifest/material commitment, and changes only its matching `Staged -> Active` entry. Reads/effects/prepares require both the Active local entry and an active-Meta-projection prefix at or beyond activation. Old material remains Active/Retiring and retained until every dependent operation and replacement acknowledgement closes.

## Invariants & interactions
Enforces FG-INV-01, FG-INV-08 through FG-INV-16, and FG-INV-20 for W12. Consumes G0 identity/command/state-slot/authority contracts, W11 Raft/configuration/payload/format/key contracts, role-transition formats and certified remote trust. All W12 semantic/protocol tasks depend on it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every field/root/command/ref/checkpoint/floor/prepared/key/certificate/projection type has stable role-specific registry rows, reference strengths, construction DAG, exact-cut and inventory coverage.
- Unit/golden tests freeze fresh Genesis and operational vectors, role tags, command origins, RootSlot closure, key stages, certificate ledgers, prepared transfers, checkpoint vectors and every floor field.
- Property/model tests prove Meta-only semantic time, Shard nonsemantic order, exact payload/root/log agreement, pre-order ownership before consensus, staged keys unusable until projection activation, destruction only after zero/completion, and complete floors.
- Mutation/fuzz rejects Local/Meta/Shard substitution, omitted/duplicate slot, wrong group/config/prefix, future applied/certificate ref, missing prepared closure, incomplete key stage, stale projection, raw remote edge, and checkpoint/suffix mismatch.
- Crash/DPOR E2E boots Meta plus multiple Shards, prepares/transfers/applies, rotates keys/configuration, checkpoints and recovers with loss at every log/root/slot/certificate/receipt boundary.
- JSONL emits {event_version,role_and_group,command_kind,role_prefix,root_kind,root_digest,slot_generation,checkpoint_digest?,floor_digest?,prepared_owner_id?,certificate_kind?,certificate_digest?,key_generation?,key_state?,projection_slot?,configuration_digest,recovery_action,replay_command}; secrets and raw key material excluded.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: generic role parameter accepted on wire, digest-only floors, Shard semantic clocks, keys active by local convention, certificate logs outside rooted closure, and hand-maintained projection slot lists. Missing coverage disables W12.

title: Implement GlobalPrepareAdmission, effect bases/fragments, and fence-free shard prepares
description:
## What & scope
The write path from finalized workspaces to durable shard prepares: `ShardEffectBasis`, deterministic participant routing, the single union authorization decision, `GlobalTxnOutcomePreparationRecord`, `GlobalPrepareAdmissionSpec` + `MetaTerminalAdmissionFence`, `ShardEffectFragment`, and `ShardPrepareCommand/Record/Certificate`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1: one admission, one immutable participant/reservation set, one final-effect digest — Meta alone decides. B5: every shard input is a certified-remote wrapper; nothing is ambient. Rejected: per-shard authorization approvals substituting for the union decision; coordinator-fenced prepares (prepares are deliberately fence-free — replica fence epochs never enter canonical semantic objects).

## Design — normative detail
**Effect bases.** Post-rebase, each shard builds `ShardEffectBasis {global_txn_id,registration_generation,shard_id,registered_snapshot,topology_epoch,active_meta_projection_root_ref,authority_projection,operation_audit_admission_commitment,sorted_coordinate_bindings,write_key_material_projection_refs,final_effect_refs[ConditionalCoordinateRef],logical_delta_fragment_template_ref,read_witness_refs,final_write_summary,constraint_requests_and_deltas,resource_charge_basis,intent_semantics_oid,basis_effect_digest}`. `basis_effect_digest` hashes the effect-only projection through `intent_semantics_oid`; it excludes authorization/audit/outcome/resource/fragment/prepare/certificate objects but includes the authority-projection commitment. Every basis must deterministically finalize the certified workspace overlay — never re-execute or omit a prior statement.

**Routing fixed point.** `ParticipantRoutingDerivationProof` records ordered fixed-point rounds (cross-partition effects, cascades, constraint owners). Meta builds `ParticipantRoutingCertificate` with sorted bases/participants/constraint owners and `global_final_effect_digest = H("fgdb:global-effect:v1", sorted(shard_id,basis_effect_digest))`. Missing/extra bases, mixed authority projections, non-fixed-point cascades fail closed. Then exactly one `GlobalAuthorizationDecisionRecord` — the global validator replays the permit across the union including hidden cascades and disclosure contracts; per-shard approvals cannot substitute. Meta then creates resource transitions plus `GlobalTxnOutcomePreparationRecord` (terminal compare contract, `terminal_domain:CommitIfCertifiedElseAbort{global_final_effect_digest,allowed_stable_abort_reason_classes}`, optional Sharded `TerminalWriteResultPreparation`) — but no outcome event/resolution/terminal gate yet.

**Admission.** `GlobalPrepareAdmissionSpec` names expected published-statement frontier, delivery-terminal frontier, statement-index digest, workspace generation, cumulative read-witness and logical-effect roots, routing certificate, sorted participants/constraint owners/bases, meta constraint reservation requests, the authorization decision, resource transitions, outcome preparation, audit admission (`Claimed|NotRequired`, ticket stays unresolved), `global_final_effect_digest`, expected branch heads/key epochs/topology/policy/revocation/conflict basis. Apply requires ReadWrite, exact fixed-point equality, a contiguous frontier with every statement terminally `Published|Failed|Abandoned`, every Buffered output delivery-terminal or independently retained, no Open statement, no prior admission — then atomically installs `PrepareAdmitted`, creates Meta reservations, and constructs `MetaTerminalAdmissionFence::Armed` freezing branch heads, key epochs, write coordinates, constraint-reservation/resource sets, statement/delivery/workspace/witness/effect commitment, topology/policy/revocation/conflict basis. The fence deliberately contains no assigned future sequence or HLC. Any drift afterwards requires admitted abort/release plus a NEW registration generation; digest substitution never recertifies stale work.

**Fragments & prepares.** Only after admission is visible may shards build `ShardEffectFragment` (every Meta object an exact CRSR bound to Meta domain/configuration, this consumer domain, availability, and two-sided grant; only `basis_ref` is shard-local; envelope digest excluded from the global effect digest) and order fence-free `ShardPrepareCommand` keyed `prepare_key:{global_txn_id,registration_generation,admission_generation}`: the shard first applies every Meta command through the admission (typed projection or exhaustive irrelevance proof), then byte-verifies authority projection, active Meta projection, topology/policy/revocation/key/audit, configuration, admission, basis, fragment, and the D1 `ShardPreCommandBaseAvailabilityCertificate`. Apply builds `ShardPrepareRecord` (states `Prepared|GloballyCommitted|GloballyAborted|Applied|GcEligible`), installs canonical constraint reservations atomically, then the quorum signs `ShardPrepareCertificate` (followers recompute all fields). Late prepare after an abort tombstone, a second admission generation under one registration, or any stale projection rejects.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-07 (W12 write order): registration/workspace -> effect bases/routing -> authorization/resource/outcome/admission -> shard fragments/prepares -> constraints/serialization -> final-certification holds -> Meta command; every pre-order input excludes its future command/result/root; timeout releases no prepared owner. FG-INV-02: at most one legal live generation owns each reservation/hold. FG-INV-06: routing/coarsening and workspace overlays preserve witness contracts — missing routing or prior-touched-shard overlay causes conservative failure, never a dropped edge. Invariant-class; prepare fan-out latency benchmark-class.

## Interactions
Consumes workspaces/witnesses from `w12-statement-machine`, coordinator choreography shape from `w4-coordinator`, availability certificates from `w11-payload-availability`. Produces prepares/reservations for `w12-certification` and `w12-decision-visibility`; constraint requests for `w12-constraints-authority`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Gate: "Fence-free prepares... pass exact DAG/crash proofs"; "every participant prepare has durable availability and one terminal decision; no timeout fractures atomicity under crash/partition/leader loss/reconfiguration." Tests: substitution matrices (wrong role/group/incarnation/configuration/grant, locally-encoded Meta StrongRef unrepresentable); admission with an Open statement or undetached result rejected; drift-after-admission forces new generation; crash at every prepare state (Preparing/Receipted/Ordered/committed-unapplied/applied-visibility-pending) across reconfiguration transfer phases. E2E: 3-shard write with induced shard lag; assert prepare waits for admission-prefix apply, logging per-shard applied prefix at prepare time.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: exhaustive irrelevance proofs on quiet shards add work (mitigated by `MetaRelevanceRangeProof` contiguity). Rejected: fenced prepares; re-execution at prepare time; catch-all basis commitments replacing typed refs.

## Provenance
§14.6 bullet 2 (1083); App A 1734, 1818-1822, 1848; §19:1350/1354.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement W12 recovery: prepared pinning, compaction, six-stage release, distributed GC
description:
## What & scope
Everything that keeps W12 safe over time: prepared-closure pinning and the nonblocking-impossibility stance, `NeverRegisteredFloor` and three-phase `ClosedAttemptCompaction`, the `CertifiedRemoteStrongRef` trust/retention system with the six-stage release handshake, reconfiguration ownership transfer, and the distributed GC protocol with fenced cancellation.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1/B5: partitions may block but can never reverse decisions or reclaim uncertain state; every release is an explicit typed handshake, never inferred from time or a missing client. Rejected: presumed-abort timeouts; inferring release from absence; cross-group raw strong references.

## Design — normative detail
**Prepared pinning.** Prepared closures remain pinned through terminal decision, post-visibility participant acks, overlap/retention floors, and staged GC. No prepared participant times out or guesses; it recovers Meta's decision. `MetaConfigPayloadFloor`/`ShardConfigPayloadFloor` are exact closed schemas whose typed subfloors cover begin status, attempt families, statements/results, conflict overlap, attempt compaction, audit claim/signer, prepared owners, certificate ledger, decision and delta publication, retention cuts, remote trust/release, key lifecycle, derived generations, GC, backup, restore, activation/retirement, continuity/service, reconfiguration/topology; missing/duplicate/wrong-role/raw-cross-group coverage fails G0.

**Attempt compaction.** `NeverRegisteredFloorSpec` removes only proved staging: `NeverRegisteredEvidence` + `NoReservationBindingProof` (reservation never consumed by registration nor exported), rewrites Detailed -> Compacted preserving the same replay ref and byte-identical public bytes. `ClosedAttemptCompactionSpec` has three separately ordered phases and neither decides Prepared work: **build** verifies every selected attempt is TerminalReady and audit-visible with complete decision/certificate publication, every admitted shard post-visibility ack, committed Global-delta publication/frontier (or no-delta proof), all statements terminal, all results Acknowledged/ReleasedUnacked/independently retained, workspace/remote-grant release evidence, overlap closed — creating an unsigned compact `ClosedAttemptCompactionFloorRecord` in `PendingAttemptCompactionRoot` (build does NOT advance the authoritative floor); **attest** — only after the record and its audit visibility advance are durable does the quorum create `AttemptCompactionAttestation` (no strong edge to the build command/prior floor/heavy evidence); **publish** — `GlobalClosedAttemptFloorPublishSpec` rewrites selected entries to `CompactedTerminal`, installs `GlobalAttemptCompactionFloor` (no strong/CRSR path to the previous floor), and only then, after visibility and an activated checkpoint cut, is heavy evidence reclaimable. Detailed/compacted NeverRegistered and terminal outcomes are byte-identical (gate). `GlobalOutcomeExpirySpec` alone drops replay/bundle edges via permanent `ExpiredTombstone`s.

**Remote trust & six-stage release.** W12's one cross-consensus edge is `CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<T>` over `ExportLeaf<T>`, `RemoteAuthorityConfigurationEvidence` (trust transition `Genesis{root artifact}|Successor|ValidatedCheckpointSuccessor`; current-member signatures alone never a trust root), `RemotePayloadAvailabilityEvidence`, and `RemoteRetentionGrantEvidence` (`grant_id = H("fgdb:remote-grant:v1",...)`). Release is the explicit six-transition handshake: (1) consumer orders `RemoteRetentionReleaseRequestSpec` -> `ReleaseRequested` (type state cannot acquire new refs under the old grant); (2) consumer quorum certificate + portable leaf -> `ReleaseCertified`; (3) authority imports and orders `RemoteRetentionReleaseApplySpec` -> `RemoteRetentionReleaseTombstone` (no strong edge to the released target); (4) authority ack certificate + portable leaf; (5) authority publish -> `RemoteReleaseSummaryEntry` under the permanent release-proof floor; (6) consumer `ConsumeReleaseAck` with current no-old-grant-ref proof. Meta/Shard reconfiguration uses explicit `PreparedOwnershipTransferRecord<Role>` (Owned -> Transferring -> Transferred only after new owner holds base+superset closure and the transition floor plus Raft/snapshot acknowledgement) and remote-config trust adoption (`ShardReconfigurationAuthorizationSpec`, `ShardConfigurationAdoptionEvidence/Spec`, `RemoteGrantRetirementPlan`) before old retirement.

**Distributed GC.** Certified preflight (`ShardGcPreflightSpec/Record/Evidence`, `MetaGcPreflightRecord`) -> `GlobalGcAuthorizationSpec/Record` (bounded candidate sets; an Active/ReleaseRequested grant target is never a candidate; a planned remote release is not completion — `GcRemoteReleaseCompletionRef` accepts only stage-5/6 or imported permanent evidence) -> per-role Semantic quarantine (`ShardGcApplySpec`/`MetaGcApplyQuarantineSpec`: followers recompute from CURRENT state; require `reclaim ⊆ authorized ∩ preflight`, disjointness from the reachable set, exact family/plan bijection; every encoder/dedupe/validator rejects new edges to quarantined identities) -> Protocol physical machine -> `PortableGcPhysicalTerminalEvidence` -> Semantic disposition import -> four noninterchangeable acks (`MetaGcCompletedAck|ShardGcCompletedAck|MetaGcCancelledAck|ShardGcCancelledAck`) -> `GlobalGcCompletionSpec`. Cancellation is fenced and monotone: `Executing -> CancellationPreparing -> CancellationAuthorized|CompletionRequired -> CancelledBeforeAnyParticipantStart|Completed`; any Started observation permanently forces roll-forward.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-14: W12 requires bounded preflight, Meta authorization, current-root disjoint quarantine, no resurrection, exact member completion, progress, and aggregate completion; missing participants remain blocking; heavy detail retires only after visibility and an activated cut. FG-INV-07: timeout releases no prepared, certificate, audit, result, allocation, escrow, or retention owner. FG-INV-01: detailed and compacted proofs return byte-identical public outcomes. FG-INV-16: no obligation is lost/duplicated/refunded while obligated; under declared fairness every obligation reaches one legal terminal. Invariant-class; MTTDL modeling stays FG-CFG-01.

## Interactions
Consumes acks/floors from `w12-decision-visibility`, GC core from `w2-gc-core`/`w11-fenced-gc`, checkpoints from `w2-retention-checkpoints`. Produces compaction floors consumed by status surfaces (`w10-capabilities`) and the retirement predicates for `w12-topology`/`w12-backup-restore`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Gate: "Meta/Shard GC must pass Requested/Started/Completed-or-all-cancelled state machines before aggregate completion"; "attempt compaction's build/attest/publish protocol proves every result/workspace/remote-grant/public-status obligation before release"; "remote configuration trust and the six-stage grant release... pass models and physical evidence gates"; "every cross-group edge passes two-sided CertifiedRemoteStrongRef trust/retention/GC tests." Tests: status race matrix (build/visibility/attestation/publish/expiry/post-cut reclamation) requiring identical validated-capability response bytes; six-stage crash at every transition leaving target root/permanent proof/replayable pending state; GC tests covering every start position, all-no-start, ambiguous status, prepare/fence/start races, successor exhaustion, mixed ack substitution, configuration/topology change; dedupe-resurrection storms. E2E: scripted 1-Meta/3-shard cluster — prepared transactions pinned through an induced partition and leader loss with zero timeout decisions (recovery fetches Meta's decision), a full six-stage remote-grant release drill, NeverRegistered plus build/attest/publish closed-attempt compaction under concurrent status lookups (byte-identical public responses before, during, and after), and two distributed GC runs: one cancelled mid-flight with all-participants-no-start (CancelledBeforeAnyParticipantStart) and one forced to CompletionRequired by a first Started observation. DETAILED LOGGING (required): every six-stage release transition logs `{grant_id, release_nonce, stage 1-6, role, applied ref}`; every GC participant logs `{operation family/generation, fence generation, participant state Pending|FenceInstalled|NoStartFenced|StartedObserved|RollForwardPending|Completed|Cancelled, evidence/ack ids}`; compaction logs `{compaction_id, phase build|attest|publish, selected attempt keys, prior/new floor digests}`; prepared-ownership transfers log `{ownership ids, command_status, transition_phase}`; tests replay the logs against the registered state machines and fail on any missing or out-of-order transition.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: blocking GC under partition accumulates debt (accepted — safety over reclamation). Rejected: timeout-terminated prepares; stage-4 certificate as release completion; floors that decide Prepared work.

## Provenance
§14.6 bullet "Recovery and nonblocking impossibility" (1093); App A 1396-1400, 1676-1690, 1788-1816; §19:1352-1354.

title: Implement W12 BEGIN/ticket/registration and the ReadIndex-fenced global snapshot
description:
## What & scope
Build the W12 transaction front door: durable BEGIN reservation, operation-ticket admission, Meta attempt registration with workspace generation zero, the registered ReadIndex-fenced global snapshot, and the shard-read witness basis discipline. Statements/publication live in `w12-statement-machine`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1/B6: an agent's BEGIN gets a durable, idempotent, capability-visible lineage *before* any attempt exists, and every read observes one exact global prefix — no shard ever serves data ahead of ticket visibility or registration. B5: authorization and audit admission precede observation, evidence-first. Rejected: optimistic shard-first reads reconciled later ("local SSI plus hope", §14.6), and overloading a claimed operation ticket for lifecycle scaffolding.

## Design — normative detail
**Ticket-first.** When the audit profile requires it, Meta first mirrors one pending operation ticket; only then may it order the `ReadOnly|ReadWrite` registration with matching read/mutation permit and `OperationAuditAdmission` (`NotRequired{evidence}|PendingUnclaimed{ticket_ref,ticket_admission_record_ref,operation_request_basis_commitment}|Claimed{ticket_ref,claim_record_ref,owner:{global_txn_id,registration_generation},operation_request_basis_commitment}`). The registration's own control gate is a validated lifecycle-scaffolding `NotRequired` proof and cannot consume the operation ticket. The claim remains unresolved until the one terminal read-close/commit/abort event.

**BEGIN lineage.** `TxnOutcomeCapabilityFields` (header/body/MAC bytes exist before ordering; `capability_commitment` is their domain-separated digest). `GlobalBeginIdempotencyIndex` maps `(namespace,incarnation,tenant,principal,scoped_begin_idempotency_key)` to exactly `Reserved|BoundDetailed|BoundCompacted|NeverRegisteredDetailed|NeverRegisteredCompacted|ExpiredTombstone`. `GlobalBeginReservationSpec` (sequence-neutral: header, key, request digest, operation class/isolation/`TransactionErrorPolicy`, capability replay ref, audit admission, absence proof, staging resource reservation) applies to `GlobalBeginReservationRecord` + atomic `Reserved` + `GlobalOutcomeDirectoryValue::BeginStaging`; only then may Fabric emit `BEGIN_ACCEPTED`. Byte-identical retry returns identical canonical capability bytes even after key rotation; any drift fails. `BeginTerminalEvidence = Denied|AuthenticatedAbandon|RegionClosed{BeginRegionClosedReceipt}|Superseded`; time passage, socket suspicion, process death inhabit no arm; `GlobalBeginTerminalSpec` resolves the exact pending ticket and creates the compactable NeverRegistered record — never an attempt/family/burn.

**Registration.** `GlobalAttemptRegistrationSpec` binds header, `global_txn_id`, begin binding (`BindReserved|IdempotentBound`), token, `TxnOperationCeiling`, autocommit classification (required exactly for AutocommitExecute, forbidden for ExplicitBegin), requested snapshot + minimum acceptable, permit, error policy (`AbortTransactionOnStatementError|ContinueOnDeclaredRecoverable{recoverable_error_class_table_oid}`; savepoints rejected at BEGIN), initial workspace recipe, audit admission, topology basis, `registration_generation`, and family expectation `First{authenticated_absence_proof}|Successor{prior_generation,prior_terminal_outcome_proof_ref,prior_release_and_overlap_floor_ref}|IdempotentRetry`. Applied only via `GlobalControlCommand(kind=RegisterAttempt)`: binding claims the operation ticket, checks the conflict safe-snapshot frontier, inserts Active family/attempt/conflict entries, flips the outcome directory to `W12`, constructs `GlobalAttemptRegistration` and workspace generation zero (exact same header, ProvenReadOnly cumulative potential) plus the `Registered` outcome. `AttemptFamilyState` enforces one active registered generation; parallel generations, gaps, token rebinding, ceiling drift fail closed.

**Global snapshot & shard reads.** The registered ReadIndex-fenced global snapshot follows registration; no shard read precedes ticket visibility or registration. A shard read proves its active Meta topology/policy/revocation/key/audit projection covers the registration prefix and binds the operation-audit commitment; before any shard read, operation and applicable statement tickets are imported/claimed through the two certified registrations; the shard rechecks revocation. `ShardReadWitnessBasis` binds execution scope (`ReadExecutionScope::ShardTerminal|ShardStatement`), the complete `ShardAuthorityBindingProjection` (not a digest), registered snapshot, workspace overlay root, `ActiveMetaProjectionRoot`, read state root + checkpoint certificate + `ShardHistoryInventory`, `ReadAccessAdmissionRecord` (exists before the first cursor/storage/statistics observation), witness refs, answer contract, result fragment digest, and the after-the-fact `ReadResultReleaseDecisionRecord`. Reads evaluate registered snapshot plus the exact ordered local workspace overlay certified by the imported global generation; a missing prior-touched-shard delta or false empty-overlay proof fails. Meta aggregates via `ReadParticipantRoutingCertificate` (fixed point over every routed read/expansion/constraint-disclosure and previously touched workspace shard). Queries choose one global prefix and wait/fail until every routed shard has applied/proved it and retained that history.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-20: authorization precedes every observation or effect; W12 registration claims operation/statement tickets before observation; shard work carries only exact certified projections; equal epoch scalars with different roots never substitute. FG-INV-01: W12 reserves the begin key and outcome-capability bytes before response; `AttemptFamilyState` admits only generation-zero First, exact prior+1 Successor after a registered Terminal with proved release/overlap floor, or byte-identical IdempotentRetry; NeverRegistered creates no family/generation/burn. FG-INV-04: every read begins at the visible endpoint of the audit pipeline. All are invariant-class clauses in `invariants.toml`; begin-path latency is benchmark-class.

## Interactions
Consumes `w12-meta-clock` (control ordering), `w9-audit-pipeline` (tickets), `w11-read-contracts` (ReadIndex fencing), `w4-ssi-witnesses` (witness types). Produces registrations/workspaces for `w12-statement-machine` and `w12-prepare`; begin/outcome directories consumed by `w12-recovery-gc` compaction.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Gate lines: "BEGIN durably reserves its key/outcome capability before response; registration atomically claims the operation ticket and roots workspace zero before every serializable read." Tests: lost-response BEGIN retry returns byte-identical capability; concurrent First/Successor/IdempotentRetry races; NeverRegistered-no-family negatives; shard read attempted before registration visibility must fail (oracle-checked); stale Meta projection at shard read rejected; crash at every point between reservation, registration, and first shard read with recovery to a single lineage. E2E: scripted 3-shard cluster, 1k concurrent BEGINs with induced duplicate delivery, log reservation/registration/first-read prefixes and assert monotone coverage.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: ticket-first adds an external round trip on Required audit profiles (amortized via batching, priced in §16/§17). Rejected: reading before registration; consuming the operation ticket for scaffolding; fabricating attempt identities for denied BEGINs.

Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. ## Authoritative post-decomposition contract delta (d96bf0f)

The exact Meta BEGIN/registration ReadYourWrites validation basis and Shard import contract below are part of this implementation unit.

BEGIN has its own durable, idempotent lineage before an attempt exists. `TxnOutcomeCapabilityFields` is the shared exact inline value `{header:DurableCapabilityHeader{capability_kind=TxnOutcome},body:{request_kind:ExplicitBegin|AutocommitExecute,scoped_request_idempotency_key_digest,txn_token,outcome_capability_key},mac}`; the body
