title: Build the Chronicle compactor: verify-equivalence pipeline and root-slot convergence
description:
## What & scope
Implement §5.5's compaction actor for Chronicle segments: the `BUILD -> VERIFY_EQUIVALENCE -> D1_NEW_OBJECTS -> ROOT_PUBLISH -> SLOT_CONVERGE -> WAIT_SAFE_POINT -> RETIRE` pipeline, the complete mark-root inventory, the serialized `CompactionRootPublish` permit, the `RootSlotConvergenceGuard`/`SlotConvergence` permit protocol with `RootSlotConvergenceEvidence`, marker-batch and `PackedObjectGroup` rewrite ownership, and staging-namespace durability. Retention-cut semantics live in w2-retention-checkpoints; GC decision/quarantine in w2-gc-core.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1's immutable content-addressed store only works economically if dead bytes are rewritten out without ever mutating published objects in place. frankensqlite's ECS native mode (§2.3) supplies the mark-and-compact-with-leases starting point, but Chronicle re-specifies root protocol, digest identity, and equivalence proof — graph durability does not inherit correctness by analogy. B5: compaction emits reconstructible evidence (equivalence digests, convergence evidence), not trust-me rewrites.

## Design — normative detail
The pipeline marks from BOTH valid root slots and explicitly traverses: logical-command/generated-complete installed-checkpoint cuts, stable prepared-payload and consensus-log ownership, every branch/base, branch key-epoch/envelope/grant roots and the branch-merge ledger, transaction/DP outcomes, all external continuity links, resume-cursor/delivery/replay registries and archives, delivered-output payloads, audit ticket/event/resolution/CAS-receipt/gap/audit roots, snapshot and delivery leases, backup/legal holds, key/key-wrap, and current/prospective configuration/floors. It resolves marked logical/subobject identities through nonretaining physical locators, builds new immutable encodings, **proves old/new canonical logical digests equal**, and publishes the new `RootManifest` through a serialized `CompactionRootPublish` permit.

Slot convergence: after rereading and fully validating the highest slot/closure, a linear `RootSlotConvergenceGuard` requests a `SlotConvergence` permit whose acquisition rechecks that the CURRENT winner is still the exact target manifest, writer/continuity/service tuple, and bootstrap. Only while holding the permit may it publish the other slot at checked `winner_generation+1` with byte-identical target fields. Any intervening ordinary, audit, checkpoint, restore, role-transition, retirement, or other convergence publication changes the winner and makes acquisition or the immediate pre-write recheck fail stale; convergence restarts from the new winner and can never overwrite it with an older manifest at a higher generation. Success syncs and rereads both slots and produces reconstructible `RootSlotConvergenceEvidence {manifest_identity, first_slot_generation, second_slot_generation, identical_bootstrap_digest, two_slot_reread_digest, durability_profile, first_and_second_root_publication_evidence}`. Convergence is physical-only: it advances no logical/Raft/commit/HLC sequence and cannot select a different manifest. Recovery at every crash chooses the highest credible slot; retry converges the remaining slot.

Old encodings retire only after (a) both valid slots converge away from the old closure, (b) convergence evidence is reproducible, and (c) no independent lease can expose them. Active marker batches are never rewritten in place. Compaction owns the rewrite of partially dead `PackedObjectGroup`s: reclamation coarsens to the pack (a pack is reclaimable only when every member is), member ObjectIds are stable across rewrite, and the object-location index locators are republished — the same trade marker batches already accept. Staging namespace creation, sealing, rename, convergence, and retirement include the required directory durability operations; staging files are unreachable state cleaned only by a recovery procedure that proves it.

Safe point: computed under a consensus-fenced membership epoch (§14); loss of quorum, uncertain membership, an unacknowledged root, or a missing key wrap stops reclamation. Replica positions and CRDT gossip are observations, never GC authority. The actor is supervised and rate-limited against foreground latency; space amplification, checkpoint cadence, and controller settings are empirical/configuration gates with named workloads and model assumptions, not safety invariants.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12 (invariant): every claimed answer-equivalent seal, compaction, codec/format rewrite preserves logical values, multiplicity, order, visibility, security projection, and AnswerContract. FG-INV-10 (invariant): the two-slot `manifest.root` protocol always selects the highest structurally credible authenticated role closure; every irreversible slot write rechecks both authorities. FG-INV-14 (invariant excerpt): GC/compaction follows every generated strong and currently uncut conditional edge; only registered weak/locator/observation fields are nonretaining. FG-CFG-02 (configuration-model class): controller stability with predicted margin and soak results. §6.6 write-amplification component breakdown and §17 byte-economy metrics (benchmark class) price the pack-rewrite trade.

## Interactions
Traverses cuts and floors from w2-retention-checkpoints; publishes via w2-root-bootstrap's publication sequencer; rewrites packs per w2-object-packing's homogeneity/locator laws; respects snapshot generation leases from w2-snapshots-leases (a held shared lease pins the old closure); never touches prepared/consensus ownership from w2-commit-protocol. w2-gc-core consumes the safe-point discipline; w2-branch-retire relies on compaction for merge-ledger summary rewrite. Format rows from g0-format-arms.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Crash/DPOR tests cut before/after each convergence write, sync, reread, cancellation, and generation allocation while racing ordinary, prepared/Raft-only, audit-candidate-visibility, checkpoint, restore, role-transition, retirement, and another convergence publication; equal-generation ambiguity and checked generation exhaustion are covered. Equivalence oracle: old/new canonical logical digest equality proof is mandatory before publish; a mutated rewrite must be rejected. Property: convergence never regresses the winner; recovery always picks the highest credible slot. Pack tests: partially dead pack rewritten with stable member OIDs and republished locators; mixed-domain pack build fails closed. E2e: sustained-load compaction with logs of permit acquisitions, winner generations, evidence digests, and reclaimed-byte accounting; foreground p99 regression gate per §17.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: in-place rewrite of published objects (immutability is the foundation of content addressing); convergence without a permit/recheck (older-manifest-at-higher-generation hazard); gossip-derived safe points (unfenced membership loses data). Risk: convergence livelock under high publication churn — bounded by restart-from-winner semantics; risk: compaction debt under churn — FG-EVID-03 endurance gate with compaction-debt ceiling stated in §6.6 terms.

## Provenance
§5.5 (441-448), §5.3 (417), §5.1 PackedObjectGroup row (342), §2.3.

title: Implement incarnation+allocation continuity: DirectoryBound/ExternalCas/TPM-NV arms
description:
## What & scope
Implement the paired continuity profiles: `IncarnationContinuityProfile` (`DirectoryBound | ExternalCas`, carried in every `RootSlot` as `incarnation_continuity_profile_id` + `cluster_incarnation_continuity_digest` + `continuity_cas_version`) and the 1:1-bound `AllocationContinuityProfile` (closed union `ExternalCas | DirectoryBound`, plus the registered TPM-NV-class variant of the `DirectoryBound` arm), including `IdentityContinuityRecord`, the fenced local allocation-continuity journal, the exact threat-model scoping, and the FG-INV-11 residual-risk registry row.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1 makes history authoritative, so the deadliest attack is rollback: restoring an old copy and re-issuing identities or epochs already spent. The embedded posture (B6 agents on laptops) cannot require a network authority for every epoch advance, while W12/Meta/Sharded postures must have externally anchored anti-rollback. The profile pair makes this trade explicit, registered, and priced (§16 per-posture external-authority footprint table) — and the residual risk of the local arm is a first-class registry row, not fine print (B5 honesty discipline).

## Design — normative detail
**IncarnationContinuityProfile**: `DirectoryBound` — ordinary embedded/local writes rely on the exact whole-inode lease; same-identity restore to another directory is forbidden (clone only); payload headers use no external record ref and a fixed local continuity digest. `ExternalCas` — the Appendix A `ClusterIncarnationContinuityRecord` and a live member-bound `ClusterIncarnationLease` are mandatory; takeover fetches the exact current continuity head, byte-matches namespace/incarnation/CAS/visibility, and acquires `OrdinaryWrite` or `RecoveryOnly` scope; a stale/later/unavailable head makes the database read-only. W12 requires ExternalCas. RootManifest and RootSlot repeat and cross-check the same continuity/profile/digest/version/visibility tuple; the generated payload common header carries `{incarnation_continuity_profile_id, cluster_incarnation_continuity_record_ref?, cluster_incarnation_continuity_digest, continuity_cas_version, service_visibility_epoch}` — `DirectoryBound` = None-ref + fixed digest; `ExternalCas` = Some + exact byte equality with the live authority.

**AllocationContinuityProfile** is a closed union `ExternalCas | DirectoryBound` bound 1:1 to the slot's IncarnationContinuityProfile. Under `ExternalCas`, before an epoch may issue an ID, a threshold-signed/witnessed `IdentityContinuityRecord { database_security_namespace_id, allocation_epoch, predecessor_digest, external_registry_id, cas_version, status, issued_at, signer_set_epoch, threshold_signatures }` is durably CAS-published outside the rollbackable database closure (operator HSM/KMS registry or configured witnesses) and copied into Chronicle; the external copy is the anti-rollback authority, the Chronicle copy is checked against it. Under `DirectoryBound` there is no external record: the epoch fence is a local allocation-continuity journal record ordered under the same whole-inode fence and fixed-local-continuity-digest pattern the cluster-incarnation record registers for that profile; every epoch advance is an ordered, fenced local publication — an embedded DirectoryBound database mints its first and every subsequent epoch with no external service. W12, Meta, and Sharded postures require ExternalCas.

**Threat-model scoping (exact and registered)**: the DirectoryBound arm fences *copy-based restore* — a copied directory fails inode-identity takeover — and is never an anti-rollback authority; block-level or volume-snapshot rollback preserves device and inode identity and is **outside** DirectoryBound's declared threat model for the entire database closure, allocation included. The carve-out is cheap by construction: the external fence detects only cross-epoch rollback and enforces restore floors — the record binds epoch and predecessor digest, never high-water marks — so DirectoryBound forfeits protection only on a same-identity-restore path that posture already forbids outright. **TPM-NV variant**: a registered DirectoryBound variant may bind epoch advances to a local hardware monotonic counter (TPM-NV-class) as the allocation-epoch fence, restoring cross-epoch rollback detection for embedded deployments without a network authority. **Restore law**: a same-identity restore must acquire an epoch strictly above the external continuity floor before writes; if that authority/floor cannot be proved, the database opens read-only or requires `CloneNewIdentity`. `AllocationEpochReservation` under DirectoryBound (mode `CloneNewIdentity` only) takes `external_retired_floor`/`external_allocator_floor_digest` from the source's fenced local allocation-continuity journal, authenticated from the source manifest closure, with the same strictly-beyond checked arithmetic; under ExternalCas they remain the external authority's floors.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-11 (verbatim): allocation epochs, leases, and canonical spent commitments are monotonic under the registered `AllocationContinuityProfile` bound 1:1 to the incarnation-continuity posture — externally monotonic under `ExternalCas` (mandatory for W12/Meta), locally monotonic under `DirectoryBound`'s allocation-continuity journal beneath the same whole-inode fence — and prevent VId/EId/generated-key alias, overlap, or reuse across crash, label change, branch, merge, clone, restore, topology movement, and role activation; the registered residual-risk row applies to the whole closure: under `DirectoryBound`, block-level volume rollback is outside the declared threat model, allocation included. The residual-risk row lives in Appendix F with the same conditional-clause structure FG-INV-10 uses for filesystem profiles. Footprint-table entries are cost/SLO-class artifacts.

## Interactions
Consumes `g0-format-arms` (frozen AllocationContinuityProfile decision incl. TPM variant), `g0-threat-model` (copy-restore vs block-rollback scoping), `g0-claim-registries` (residual-risk clause registration), `w2-root-bootstrap` (slot fields). Produces continuity validation for `w2-writer-takeover` (step 4), the epoch fence for `w2-id-allocator`, restore floors for `w11-restore` and the restore bridges, and the ExternalCas discipline reused by `w9-audit-continuity`/`w9-time-authority`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
ExternalCas model: CAS races, stale head, skipped version, fork detection, threshold-signature validation, Chronicle-copy/external-head byte-equality. DirectoryBound: copied-directory takeover fails inode-identity validation; journal ordering under the whole-inode fence; epoch advance with zero external calls (no network dependency). TPM-NV: simulated NV-counter regression detected. Restore drills: same-identity restore without a provable floor opens read-only or demands CloneNewIdentity; floor-arithmetic overflow fail-closes; DirectoryBound clone takes floors from source journal digests. Negative: slot/allocator profile mismatch (1:1 violation) unencodable; W12/Meta/Sharded posture with DirectoryBound rejected at registry level. Crash: cut before/after external CAS publish, Chronicle copy, and journal fsync. E2E: simulated block-level snapshot rollback under DirectoryBound demonstrates the documented residual outcome; the same scenario under ExternalCas and TPM-NV detects and fail-closes. DETAILED LOGGING: every continuity operation must emit structured events — external CAS fetch/publish `{external_registry_id, cas_version, head_digest, outcome}`, Chronicle-copy vs external-head byte-equality checks with both digests, DirectoryBound journal append/fsync under the whole-inode fence `{allocation_epoch, journal_digest}`, TPM-NV counter reads `{counter_value, expected_floor, verdict}`, every epoch mint/advance `{profile_arm, old_epoch, new_epoch}`, and every fail-closed/read-only/CloneNewIdentity decision with its typed reason — and the e2e rollback drills assert presence and field-completeness of these events, verifying the documented residual outcome and the fail-closed detections from the logged event sequence alone.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: mandatory external authority for all postures (kills the embedded/B6 posture); high-water marks in the external record (every allocation would become an external write — it deliberately binds only epoch+predecessor); pretending DirectoryBound stops volume rollback (hence the registered residual-risk row); one unified profile with runtime flags (unauditable). Risk: operators misreading DirectoryBound as full anti-rollback — doctor names the residual-risk row and the §16 footprint table.

## Provenance
§4.5 (221, 225), §5.1 (344, 364, 378), App A (1886, 2479), FG-INV-11 (App F), §16.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement LogicalDeltaTemplate, LogicalDeltaBatch, delta index and frontier stream
description:
## What & scope
Implement the canonical committed-delta stream: `LogicalDeltaTemplate` construction/validation at finalization, `LogicalDeltaBatch<LocalCommitted>` materialization at apply, `LocalDeltaBatchIndex` + `local_delta_frontier` maintenance, and the delta-retention-cut machinery (`DeltaRetentionObligationRef`, `DeltaRetentionCutEvidence`, `ProvisionalDeltaRetentionCut`, `LocalDeltaBatchRetentionCutSpec` -> `ActivatedDeltaRetentionCut<Local>`). The `ShardFragment`/Global role schemas are generated here as types but produced by W12.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B4's whole premise (§9.1 unification claim): recursive evaluation, materialized views, subscriptions, and incremental analytics — features vendors build separately — share computation over Z-sets advanced by a total committed time. §3.3 adopts DBSP's linear-time core over canonical post-commit deltas. The source is deliberately NOT the unresolved intent log: intents lack final order, authorization, and effect resolution. B1: the delta stream is the temporal database in delta form; B6: agent-native CDC gets exact, provable provenance. The 2026 market synthesis flags derived-state freshness as a buyer pain point; this stream is the substrate for Ripple's answer.

## Design — normative detail
Finalization persists the sequence-neutral `LogicalDeltaTemplate {format, intent_semantics_ref:StrongRef<IntentSemantics>, final_effect_digest, source_intent_root_digest, coordinate_entries[]}`; entries are canonically sorted `{graph, branch, relation_id, validated_schema_binding, schema_transition:None|Some{transition_ref:StrongRef<SchemaTransition>}, delta_payload_ref:ConditionalCoordinateRef, delta_payload_digest}` and are exactly equal to the canonical before/after change. The payload is a canonical exact Z-set over `CanonicalRow`; duplicate coordinates/relations, zero weights, noncanonical order, a transition inconsistent with its binding, or a payload not equal to the capsule's before/after effects are invalid. The capsule strongly owns the template and commits its digest; per §5.2 step 4, the template digest must match the referenced bytes and the template must match the final effect set — neither field may appear without the other. Prepared-root traversal follows every conditional payload edge as strong (no committed marker/cut context); after commit the marker supplies the retention coordinate, preserving per-coordinate before/after schema identity for atomic multi-graph commits without naming the future marker or defeating per-graph retention cuts. No-op intents emit no row delta; schema changes use separate versioned system relations.

`LogicalDeltaBatch<Role>` has a generated common body `{format, role, coordinate_entries[{source_binding, resulting_binding, relation_id, delta_payload_ref:RegisteredStrongRef<DeltaPayload>}], batch_digest}` and exactly two role schemas: `<LocalCommitted>` adds `{source_template_digest:WeakDigest, commit_marker_identity:WeakMarkerIdentity, commit_seq, frontier:Local{commit_seq}}`; `<ShardFragment>` adds shard/decision fields. `batch_digest` covers every preceding canonical field and is the batch idempotency key; the ObjectId is `LogicalDeltaBatchId<Role>`, a deterministic function of registered canonical fields and directly owned payload identities — retry and rematerialization reproduce identical bytes or fail closed. A batch is derived, never a second source of truth: it may be rematerialized while its authoritative suffix remains, or retained independently by derived/subscription/replay/backup leases without retaining that suffix. Template/marker fields are nonretaining provenance; included payloads are owned directly. Only `LocalCommitted` may inhabit `CommittedDeltaSourceRef::Local`; shard fragments are never a public CDC source.

Apply law (§5.2 step 6): Local transaction apply materializes the exact batch BEFORE constructing the candidate payload, verifies it against the committed capsule/template/marker, inserts `(next_commit_seq -> batch_ref)` into `LocalDeltaBatchIndex`, and advances `local_delta_frontier` to that commit sequence in the SAME state transition — the batch is reachable from the candidate root at the first crash point at which the commit exists; there is no separate Local delta-publish command and no unrooted interval. Under required audit, the candidate index/frontier remain applied-but-not-visible in their exact pipeline entry until a gap-free audit-visibility advance releases them. `LocalTerminalCompletionSpec` accepts its delta postcondition only when the visible payload's index contains that exact marker/batch and its frontier is at least the commit sequence; a missing, duplicate, gapped, wrong-marker, or wrong-frontier insertion fails apply.

`LocalDeltaBatchIndex {format, retained_after_commit_seq, frontier, entries[every commit_seq in (retained_after_commit_seq, frontier] -> StrongRef<LogicalDeltaBatch<LocalCommitted>>], retired_prefix_commitment, active_cut_ref:StrongRef<ActivatedDeltaRetentionCut<Local>>?}` is a bounded authenticated window requiring a gap-free exact map in its retained interval, not an append-only strong map. `DeltaRetentionObligationRef<Role>` is the generated closed union of role-valid cursor/delivery, derived-generation, replay, backup/export, CDC, shard-ack/global-publication, and explicit administrative history promises. `DeltaRetentionCutEvidence<Role> {role_and_group, basis_index_digest, cut_through_position, exact_sorted_obligation_refs[], transferred_batch_owner_refs[], released_or_gap_transition_refs[], authoritative_rematerialization_availability_or_retirement_proof, complete_obligation_bijection, checker_version}` proves every promise at or below the cut has moved to an independent strong owner, completed/released, or taken an explicit `GAP`/new-baseline transition. `ProvisionalDeltaRetentionCut<Role>` authenticates inherited absence only. The ordered `LocalDeltaBatchRetentionCutSpec` installs `ActivatedDeltaRetentionCut<Local>` and advances `retained_after_commit_seq` only after the paired checkpoint/floor and ordinary activated retention cut cover the same position; apply replaces old strong entries with the prefix commitment in the same transition. A missing retained entry is corruption; a query below a proved cut returns `HistoryUnavailable` or the already-recorded gap contract. Baseline/delta resume promises root their exact `DeliveredBaselinePayload`/`DeliveredDeltaPayload`/`DeltaDeliveryEnvelope` through the outstanding cursor lease; atomic delta provenance additionally owns its source batch, while coalesced provenance needs source history only when its advertised proof scope requires it — otherwise a missing promised range produces a visible `GAP` and a new baseline.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-15 (invariant, restated): for every registered exact derivative, integrating ordered deltas equals batch evaluation, and retained Local/Global batches own each payload exactly once; cursor baseline/delta rules forbid delta before baseline ACK and expose every gap; public digests cover exact authorized canonical bytes/provenance, never keyed object IDs. FG-INV-04 clause (invariant): applied state may advance ahead of public state only through the rooted gap-free audit-visibility pipeline. FG-EVID-04 (slo class, never an invariant): derived-state freshness bounds in watermark/commit-seq units ride on this stream.

## Interactions
Produced inside w2-commit-protocol's apply and validated by w2-txn-lifecycle's terminal completion; delta cuts pair with w2-retention-checkpoints' ordinary activated cuts. Consumed by w6-zset-circuits, w6-delta-consumption, w6-subscriptions, w6-views, and w10-cdc; w2-branch-retire drives the no-successor `GAP` transition for retired-branch cursors; W12 (w12-decision-visibility) generates the sibling role schemas. Types from w1-foundation-types; schema rows from g0-identity-registries.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Unit: canonical-sort, zero-weight, duplicate-coordinate, and binding-inconsistent-transition rejection. Property: rematerialization byte-identity (batch ID and bytes reproduce or fail closed). Crash matrix around index insert / frontier advance / audit release proving no unrooted interval and no partial delta visibility. Differential oracle: integrating ordered deltas equals batch evaluation over randomized workloads (FG-INV-15 harness). Retention: crash, lease-transfer, concurrent-cursor, cut-replacement, and rematerialization tests at every boundary; no checkpoint cut silently invalidates a promised resume range. E2e: subscription resume across an activated delta cut, logging the obligation bijection, transferred owners, and any GAP transitions.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: consuming the unresolved intent log (order/authorization/effects not final); untagged batches (apply never constructs one); a separate delta-publish command (creates an unrooted interval). Risk: index-window growth under slow consumers — bounded by obligation-typed cuts plus explicit GAP contracts rather than unbounded retention.

## Provenance
§9.1 (738-742), §5.2 step 4/6 (390-391, 397), §5.4 (437), App A rows (~1918-1928).

### Fidelity addendum — all role index and cut schemas freeze here
G0/W2 must freeze, code-generate, and golden-test the later role schemas even though W2 implements only Local production. In addition to `LocalDeltaBatchIndex`, the exact future types are:

- `GlobalDeltaBatchIndex {format,retained_after_global_commit_seq,frontier,entries[every global_commit_seq in (retained_after_global_commit_seq,frontier] -> StrongRef<GlobalLogicalDeltaBatch>],retired_prefix_commitment,active_cut_ref:StrongRef<ActivatedDeltaRetentionCut<Meta>>?}`: a gap-free exact retained window.
- `ShardFragmentDeltaBatchIndex {format,shard_id,retained_after_global_commit_seq,observed_through_global_prefix,entries[participating committed global_txn_id/global_commit_seq -> StrongRef<LogicalDeltaBatch<ShardFragment>>],nonparticipant_or_noncommit_coverage_commitment,retired_prefix_commitment,active_cut_ref:StrongRef<ActivatedDeltaRetentionCut<Shard>>?}`: an exact bijection with every locally applied committed participant decision, never synthetic fragments for unrelated commits.
- The role-specific ordered cut inputs are exactly `LocalDeltaBatchRetentionCutSpec`, `GlobalDeltaBatchRetentionCutSpec`, and `ShardFragmentDeltaRetentionCutSpec`, each producing `ActivatedDeltaRetentionCut<Role>` only after its paired checkpoint/floor and ordinary activated retention cut cover the same position.

Implementation ownership remains phase-correct: W2 implements Local; W12 decision/apply implements Shard/Meta production and publication. Registry/golden/property tests are shared now. Exhaustive tests inject a missing, extra, duplicate, nonparticipant, gapped, wrong-role, wrong-frontier, stale-cut, or untransferred-obligation entry and require fail-closed apply. Logs emit role/group, retained-after position, frontier/observed prefix, entry count/root, coverage commitment, active-cut identity, and per-obligation transfer/release/GAP disposition.

and is explicit it must exist BEFORE the first optimized line. It was already a `planned`
row in workspace_topology.toml (layer verification, position 2, role "executable semantics
oracle", owner_bead fgdb-verif-reference-3kkp) — activating it is the registered path, not
a new claim.

THE LOAD-BEARING DESIGN DECISION: before-images are CHECKED, not trusted. Every DeltaRow
that mutates existing state carries an explicit before image; applying one against a state
whose actual before differs is a refusal, never an overwrite. That is what makes the delta
stream self-verifying — an apply-order bug, a dropped row, a duplicated row, or a template
built from the wrong basis each surface as a typed disagreement NAMING THE ROW instead of
as state that is quietly wrong. An oracle that repaired its input would make every stream
look applicable, which is the same as checking nothing.

LAWS THAT TURNED OUT TO MATTER MORE THAN EXPECTED:
- THE CASCADE LAW is an EQUALITY, not a containment. A vertex deletion's declared
  incident-edge image must be exactly the incident set: too few leaves a dangling edge,
  too many claims a retirement that never happened. Mutating equality -> containment turns
  exactly this law red, so both directions are witnessed.
- OPERATION-KEY IDEMPOTENCE MUST NOT BECOME AMNESIA. The oracle stores the applied ROW per
  operation key, not just the key. Storing only the key would make a DIFFERENT row bearing
  a reused key a silent no-op — strictly worse than double-counting, because the effect
  vanishes and nothing reports it.
- TEMPLATE APPLY IS ALL-OR-NOTHING (validated against a clone, swapped in only on full
  success). A partially applied commit would describe a state no commit stream produced.

WHY IT BELONGS HERE: ValidTime rows were already being APPLIED by the oracle with no way to
ask what they meant, and §15 lists temporal selectors among the semantics fgdb-reference
must implement. This closes the read side of a family whose write side already worked.

TWO SEMANTIC DECISIONS ARE NOW PINNED, and both had a plausible wrong alternative:

1. PERIODS ARE HALF-OPEN [start, end). With a closed upper bound, adjacent periods [0,10)
   and [10,20) would both be live at 10, so a value replaced at an instant would have two
   simultaneous versions and "the state at T" would be a set rather than a function. The
   boundary is SWEPT (start-1, start, end-1, end) because the middle is where every
   convention agrees and therefore where a wrong one hides. An unbounded end is live forever
   after its start; an ABSENT period is live at every instant — valid time is an optional
   assertion about when a fact holds, and a fact with no such assertion is not thereby
   time-limited to nothing.

2. TEMPORAL REFERENTIAL INTEGRITY. An edge is visible only when its own period is live AND
   BOTH ENDPOINTS ARE LIVE. Filtering edges by their own period alone is the obvious
   implementation and it returns a historical view containing an edge to a vertex that does
   not exist at that instant — the same dangling edge apply refuses. A time-travel query
   that can return a graph the database would never have accepted is not answering the
   question it claims to. THIS IS THE ONE TO PRESERVE if the selector is ever reimplemented
   over Strata.

MUTATION NUMBERS: closing the upper bound reddens 7 of 9; dropping endpoint liveness
reddens 2; dropping ONLY the dst check reddens exactly 1 (the test written for that
near-miss). Two of the nine laws exist solely to catch near-misses that would otherwise pass

semantics that happens to agree.

today only because nothing couples them). Bitemporal (valid time vs decision/commit time)
is untouched — the selector reads valid time only, and the commit_seq axis is the marker
chain's. Those are w4-valid-time's and the branch work's.

title: Implement first-escape allocation reservations, binding roots, and spent tombstones
description:
## What & scope
Implement the first-escape allocation law: `AllocationValueKind`, `TxnAllocationSlotKey`, `EscapingAllocationCause`, `EscapingAllocationBinding`, `LocalEscapingAllocationReservationSpec` + `EscapingAllocationReservationRecord`, `TxnAllocationBindingRoot`, `AbandonedAllocationTombstone`, `AllocationBindingCompactionSpec`, and the confined-values counterpart `FinalizationAllocationPlan<Role>`. Split from `w2-id-allocator`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
An identity becomes externally stable at its **first escape**, not at transaction commit: once a value reaches result bytes, a procedure response, an audit record, or a later statement's workspace, no rebase may ever remap it (B5 determinism; B6 agents cache returned IDs across turns). Reserving at escape rather than at proposal keeps confined values cheap (assigned in finalization from commit-order allocation) while making every exposed value durably owned before exposure.

## Design — normative detail
`AllocationValueKind` is the closed union `VertexId{graph,partition} | EdgeId{graph,partition} | GeneratedKey{graph,generator_id,key_type}`. `TxnAllocationSlotKey = { posture:Local|Sharded, attempt_identity, statement_seq_or_terminal, tmp_ref_ordinal, value_kind }` and is never a client value. `EscapingAllocationCause = PublishedStatementResult | LaterStatementWorkspace | ProcedureOrUdfBoundary | DurableProvenanceOrAudit | TerminalResultPreparation`; the `TerminalResultPreparation` arm is optional because a terminal-only value may instead be assigned in finalization before publication. `EscapingAllocationBinding = { slot_key, permanent_value, lease_ref:Local{StrongRef<IdRangeLease>}|Shard{StrongRef<ShardIdRangeLease>}, lease_offset, escape_cause, first_escaping_statement_seq, canonical_binding_digest }`; the permanent value must equal the role/kind/epoch/partition/offset encoded by its lease; generated-key encoders additionally obey the registered generator profile. A binding is immutable, namespace-scoped, and cannot be repurposed for a different temporary reference, attempt, kind, or create.

A proposal may use a temporary reference only while it is confined to one statement evaluator. Before an element identity or generated key can occur in buffered/public result bytes, a procedure response, an audit/provenance record, or a later statement's workspace, the owning ordered stream durably reserves it **before** the first escaping manifest/workspace/procedure object is constructed. In Local posture that means ordering `LocalEscapingAllocationReservationSpec { registration_ref:StrongRef<LocalAttemptRegistration>, expected_workspace_generation_ref, expected_allocator_root:WeakStateIdentity, sorted_binding_recipes[], sorted_lease_refs[StrongRef<IdRangeLease>], fresh_lease_use_evidence_refs[StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>], expected_unconsumed_offsets_and_spent_commitment, resulting_allocation_binding_root_ref:StrongRef<TxnAllocationBindingRoot>, resulting_workspace_generation_recipe, terminal_audit_gate }`. In Sharded posture the owning shard first orders `ShardEscapingAllocationReserveSpec` and Meta then orders `GlobalEscapingAllocationReservationSpec` over certified `ShardEscapingAllocationEvidence` — those shard/Meta analogues are implemented in `w12-escrow-dp-alloc`; shard holds remain independently rooted until Meta publication, and a Meta failure cannot make a certified slot reusable. Apply checks a canonical bijection between recipes and fresh offsets, marks every offset consumed in `IdAllocatorState`, installs `EscapingAllocationReservationRecord { source_spec_ref, applied_control_ref, registration_ref, sorted_bindings, resulting_binding_root_ref, permanent_spent_commitment }`, and advances the workspace generation atomically. The statement publication or later terminal preparation names that record and can encode only its permanent values; a lost response retries the same record and result bytes. Only identities proved not to have escaped may be assigned during finalization from commit-order allocation.

Confined temporary references also require durable allocation **before** their permanent values enter a capsule or shard effect basis — "assign in commit order" is not an ambient counter operation. `FinalizationAllocationPlan<Role>` is the sequence-neutral pre-order object `{ role, registration_identity, admission_generation, finalization_generation, expected_allocation_binding_root_ref:StrongRef<TxnAllocationBindingRoot>, allocator_basis:WeakStateIdentity, topology_and_owner_basis, sorted_mappings[{slot_key, value_kind, permanent_value, lease_ref, lease_offset, source_intent_ordinal}], sorted_lease_use_evidence_refs[StrongRef<TimeValidationEvidence>], exact_before_lease_cursor_and_high_water_values, exact_after_lease_cursor_and_high_water_values, permanent_spent_extension_commitment, complete_confined_tmp_ref_bijection, exhaustion_and_checked_overflow_proof, body_digest }`. It excludes every previously escaped slot, has no future command/result/root, and must map every and only remaining create/generated-key references in the normalized effect set; `w4-coordinator` builds it during finalization and `w2-commit-protocol` step 3 consumes it.

`TxnAllocationBindingRoot` maps every escaped `TxnAllocationSlotKey` to exactly one binding and carries `{ generation, attempt_identity, through_statement_seq, sorted_spent_commitments, root_digest }`. Rebase and finalization must preserve all existing leaves and may append only new escapes; if the logical create disappears, conflicts with a constraint, or changes kind/partition, the attempt aborts or records `AbandonedAllocationTombstone { binding_digest, attempt_terminal_identity, reason_class, permanent_spent_commitment }`. Abort, no-op, statement failure after reservation, lease expiry, compaction, branch fork/merge, topology movement, backup/restore, and same-identity recovery retain the spend through the allocator's cumulative spent commitment even after detailed binding evidence is cut. `AllocationBindingCompactionSpec` may replace closed-attempt detail only with a checked cumulative spent-range extension and exact tombstone commitment; it never returns capacity.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-11 (verbatim escape clauses): any value is durably reserved no later than its first escape to a result, later workspace, procedure/UDF, provenance/audit, or terminal preparation; confined values are reserved by the finalization plan before capsule/effect construction; rebase preserves prior bindings and may append only; disappearance/conflict/abort creates permanent spent tombstones. FG-INV-02: at most one live owner per allocation offset. FG-INV-17 interaction: finalization preserves every escaped binding byte-for-byte, even after rebase, or rejects the attempt.

## Interactions
Consumes `w2-id-allocator` (leases, allocator state), `g0-command-contracts` (the spec is a `RegisteredCommandInput` row), `w1-generated-parsers`. Produces the binding preservation contract consumed by `w2-commit-protocol` step 3 (verify and preserve every previously ordered escaping allocation), `w4-coordinator`/`w4-merge-ladder` (rebase append-only law; finalization-plan construction), `w5-executor` (RETURNING/procedure boundaries trigger reservation), `w12-escrow-dp-alloc` (Shard/Meta global reservation analogues).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
The App A test list (verbatim rows), phased by build order: the Local rows — force crash/lost response before and after every Local publication; abort after exposure; retry under a new process; expire a lease; prove the visible value is stable and no offset is ever issued twice — run NOW against synthetic attempt-registration/workspace fixtures (the real statement machine is w2-txn-lifecycle, a dependent). The shard and Meta publication rows execute at w12-escrow-dp-alloc; the expose-an-ID-to-a-later-statement and forced-rebase rows execute at w4-coordinator/w4-merge-ladder; the restore-an-old-backup and move-a-partition rows execute at w11-restore and the W12 topology beads — each registered here as named matrix rows so the later beads inherit them rather than reinvent them. Property: binding-root append-only under randomized rebase sequences; spent commitments monotone; compaction never returns capacity; binding/lease role-kind-epoch-partition-offset equality checked at decode. Negative: escape without a prior reservation is a construction-DAG failure; repurposing a binding for a different slot key rejected; a reservation against stale workspace generation fails apply; a `FinalizationAllocationPlan` containing a previously escaped slot, an incomplete confined-tmp-ref bijection, a mapping outside the normalized effect set, or a missing exhaustion/checked-overflow proof fails apply. E2E script logs every reservation spec, offset consumption, tombstone, finalization-plan mapping, and cumulative spent commitment across a crash/retry/restore sequence.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: commit-time-only assignment (identities escape earlier via RETURNING/procedures); reserving every proposal value eagerly (wastes ID space and ordering bandwidth on confined values); allowing rebase to remap exposed values with client notification (breaks B6 agents and audit provenance irreparably). Risk: reservation-ordering overhead on chatty statement workloads — only escaping values pay it.

## Provenance
§4.5 (225), App A (1888-1896), FG-INV-02/11/17 (App F).

title: Implement tiered RaptorQ repair: reconstructibility law and checkpoint-fold recode
description:
## What & scope
Implement §5.7's repair core: the scrubber's verification/repair/escalation ladder, the dynamic FEC reconstructibility tiering law, the checkpoint-fold recode rule with its fail-closed cut gate, and the `RebuildFromSuffix` recovery transition. Coverage mechanics (sweeps, sampling, e-processes) and the FG-CFG-01 MTTDL report are the sibling subtask `w2-scrub-coverage`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1 stores everything as coded immutable objects, so silent corruption is the long-tail killer. The tiering law exists because paying the full RaptorQ repair budget on *rebuildable* bytes is waste: an object re-derivable from the authoritative checkpoint plus the retained command suffix does not need the same redundancy as a sole-source object. But rebuildability is a property of *retention state*, which changes at checkpoint install — so the tier must be dynamic and the fold moment handled exactly, or a "cheap" object silently becomes the only copy. §2.1: asupersync's RFC 6330 RaptorQ (GF(256) SIMD, decode proofs, per-symbol auth, deterministic decode planner) is used, never reimplemented; frankensqlite's "RaptorQ everywhere" doctrine is executed with tiered scope, and B1's RaptorQ-protected commit mechanism stays literally true because every commit-mechanism object keeps the full budget.

## Design — normative detail
**Scrubber**: verifies record framing, authenticated headers, ciphertext digests, full logical digests after decode, and decode proofs; repairs missing symbols only within one `EncodingId`; escalates insufficient local symbols to replica or backup recovery. Twenty-percent local repair overhead is an erasure budget inside the declared source-block/failure-domain placement model, not a promise against whole-device or correlated loss.

**Dynamic reconstructibility law**: reconstructibility is a dynamic property of retention state, never a static object-kind column. An object is **Chronicle-reconstructible** exactly while it is re-derivable from the authoritative checkpoint plus the retained contiguous logical-command suffix (§5.4's recovery equation) AND is not reachable from the authoritative checkpoint closure; rooted Tier D blocks and rebuildable derived objects are the intended members. Only a Chronicle-reconstructible object may carry a registered reduced-repair (low- or zero-repair-symbol) `fec_profile`; every sole-source authoritative object owes the full budget. **Checkpoint-fold recode**: the eligibility window closes at checkpoint install — a `CopiedStrong` recipe references live objects rather than materializing bytes, so the install that folds a reduced-repair object into the authoritative closure plus the retention cut that removes the prior suffix together make that object sole-source. Checkpoint install therefore must either (a) recode every folded reduced-repair object under the full-budget profile — legal without re-encryption, since recoding changes only `EncodingId`, never `ObjectId` or `CiphertextId` (§5.1) — or (b) materialize independent full-FEC checkpoint payloads; and the cut activation that permits physical reclamation of the prior suffix **fails closed** until the chosen path is durable. Scrub failure on a reduced-repair object escalates through a registered `RebuildFromSuffix` recovery transition — re-derive from the authoritative basis, re-verify the keyed `ObjectId`, re-encode — joining the replica/backup escalation ladder instead of local symbol repair; replicated postures may additionally lean on replica repair through the same ladder.

**Non-negotiables**: object-level AEAD, keyed `ObjectId` verification, and per-symbol MACs remain mandatory for every profile — a plain-CRC or otherwise unauthenticated profile is rejected, and tiering never weakens FG-INV-09's identity recomputation or §5.1's symbol-authentication transcript. `ScratchStore` (§6.7) was already outside the coded domain: the tier boundary names an existing scope, it creates no new exemption.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-09 (verbatim, binding): `ObjectId` recomputes from the exact keyed, namespaced canonical logical transcript; symbol MACs cover their complete noncircular transcripts; incompatible encodings never combine — tiering must not weaken any clause. The fold gate is an FG-INV-14-adjacent fail-closed law (cut activation blocked until recode/full-FEC payload durable). Repair-budget adequacy per tier is FG-CFG-01 configuration-model territory (see `w2-scrub-coverage`), never an invariant.

## Interactions
Consumes `w2-object-identity` (identity verification; recode-changes-only-EncodingId law), `w2-root-bootstrap` (reachable-encoding enumeration from roots), `g0-format-arms` (frozen FEC reconstructibility class + checkpoint-fold recode rule), `w1-crypto`. Produces: repair/escalation services for `w11-anti-entropy`/`w11-payload-availability`; the recode path exercised by `w2-compaction`; the checkpoint-fold recode rule and fail-closed cut gate consumed by `w2-retention-checkpoints` — that task depends on this one and jointly owns the gate at its checkpoint-install/cut-activation hooks; tier state consumed by `w2-scrub-coverage` for per-tier reporting.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Unit: symbol repair strictly within one `EncodingId` (cross-encoding attempts rejected); decode-proof verification; unauthenticated/plain-CRC profile registration rejected at build. Property: recode preserves `ObjectId`/`CiphertextId` and changes `EncodingId`; state-machine invariant check across install/cut transitions — an object reachable from the checkpoint closure never holds a reduced-repair profile. Fold-rule crash matrix: crash between checkpoint install and recode completion, between recode and cut activation, and during `RebuildFromSuffix` — cut activation provably blocked until the chosen path is durable; after recovery no sole-source object carries a reduced-repair profile. Corruption campaigns: bit rot, truncated tails, MAC-invalid symbols, whole-segment loss across both tiers — verify repair vs `RebuildFromSuffix` vs escalation selection and fail-closed behavior beyond the erasure model. E2E: scrub cycle over a database with both tiers, logging every verification, repair, rebuild, and escalation decision with tier attribution.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: static per-object-kind FEC tiers (rebuildability is retention-state-dependent; a static column lies at fold time); skipping AEAD/MAC on reduced-repair objects (integrity/authenticity are orthogonal to redundancy — mandatory everywhere); treating RaptorQ as protection against correlated/whole-device loss (that is replication/backup's job). Risk: recode storms at checkpoint install on large fold sets — mitigated by the independent-full-FEC-payload alternative and compaction scheduling; risk: tier misclassification bugs — mitigated by the closure-reachability invariant check and the fail-closed cut gate.

## Provenance
§5.7 (473-478), §2.1 RaptorQ row (64), §5.4 recovery equation, FG-INV-09 (App F), §19 G0 batch (1313).

## Fresh-eyes foundation provenance addition
The scrubber explicitly evaluates and reuses the artifact conventions and decode-proof precedent from the allowed franken_networkx foundation crate `fnx-durability`; any code reuse remains inside the closed fnx-* universe and must preserve Chronicle's distinct content-addressed, encrypt-then-code, tiered repair contract. Differential unit/property tests compare shared integrity/decode-proof fixtures where semantics align and document every intentional divergence. The E2E corruption campaign logs the selected convention/profile, reconstructibility calculation, proof-artifact digest, repaired symbol inventory, divergence class, and replay seed without protected bytes.

title: Specify and implement FilesystemDurabilityProfile FGFS-LINUX-LOCAL-V1 + doctor probes
description:
## What & scope
Implement the versioned `FilesystemDurabilityProfile` registry (`filesystem_profiles.toml`), the initial `FGFS-LINUX-LOCAL-V1` profile, the `fgdb doctor --write-profile` conformance probe suite, the open-time recheck, the per-operation-class sync-obligation column, the read-only profile variant for `ArchiveReadOnlyOpen`, and the registered APFS/Windows roadmap rows.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Durable write mode requires a versioned profile, not a filesystem-name guess: every RootSlot write, rename publication, and lease primitive in Chronicle (B1) is only as strong as the kernel/filesystem/mount contract under it. Making the assumption an explicit, probed, checked-in artifact is the B5 evidence discipline applied to storage: the profile is an explicit storage assumption — doctor cannot transmute lying hardware into a proof. The per-operation-class sync column exists so Appendix G's barrier-chain costs are derivable rather than folklore.

## Design — normative detail
`FilesystemDurabilityProfile` is a signed/checked-in artifact `{ profile_id, profile_version, os/kernel_range, allowed_filesystems_and_mount_predicates, forbidden_layers/options, required_lock_primitive, owner_death_rule, stable_inode_rule, slot_write_rule, file_sync_rule, directory_sync_rule, rename_no_replace_rule, cache_flush_assumption, probe_suite_oid }`. `FGFS-LINUX-LOCAL-V1` admits only regular files on checked-in, kernel/mount-option-pinned local ext4 (`data=ordered|journal`, barriers enabled) or XFS (barriers and log-force flushes enabled), with staging and final paths on the same mounted filesystem. DAX, network/cluster filesystems, FUSE/overlay layers, disabled barriers, an unidentifiable mount/device, and every unregistered combination are read-only. Any future platform profile must prove the same contract before enabling writes: a nonblocking process-death-released exclusive whole-inode lease linearizable among FrankenGraphDB writers; one cancel-correct in-process publication sequencer; `pwrite` confined to the permit-selected inactive slot even if that slot tears arbitrarily; no collateral damage to the other slot; durable file-data/metadata after its declared sync; durable create/no-replace same-directory rename after parent-directory sync; and no acknowledged volatile-cache state after a successful flush.

**Per-operation-class sync obligations** are a registered column keyed `frame-pwrite|create|rename|unlink`, probed by `fgdb doctor --write-profile`; obligations are per operation class, never a blanket rule. Under `FGFS-LINUX-LOCAL-V1` a bootstrap-frame slot `pwrite` owes only the frame file's declared sync, because parent-directory syncs are owed exactly by operations that create, rename, or unlink an inode; the exemption is bound to the bootstrap-frame contract (fixed-size, pre-created, namespace-stable frame whose dirent was made durable once at `CreateNew`), and the per-generation lease-inode create plus parent-directory sync is paid at physical-generation cadence, never per commit. The column's counts feed the per-operation-class barrier chains tabulated in Appendix G. `FilesystemInstanceRecord { profile_id, probe_suite_oid, mount_id, filesystem_type, canonical_mount_options, device_chain_digest, directory_device_inode, manifest_device_inode, checked_at, result_digest }` is diagnostic evidence, never a transferable proof or semantic root. `fgdb doctor --write-profile` performs a scratch-directory conformance probe; open repeats the mount, stable-inode, and option checks.

**Roadmap rows (registered, not silent omissions)**: `FGFS-APFS-LOCAL-V1` — F_FULLFSYNC file-sync rule, flock-class whole-inode lease as `required_lock_primitive`, `renamex_np(RENAME_EXCL)` publication, directory-fsync rule — is first-class post-1.0 work explicitly gated on asupersync shipping a non-io_uring reactor backend (a named foundation dependency). Windows follows APFS (rename/lock semantics strictly harder); its absence from 1.0 is a recorded decision. A read-only profile variant supports `ArchiveReadOnlyOpen` (§13) without write-contract proof.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-10's conditional structure binds here: "under the accepted filesystem/crash profile, the two-slot `manifest.root` protocol always selects the highest structurally credible authenticated role closure..." — the profile is the named condition of that invariant, with a registered activation predicate per profile row in `invariants.toml` (`g0-claim-registries` clause-activation contract). Probe results and instance records are FG-EVID-class diagnostics; barrier-chain counts are Appendix G cost-registry rows — exact structural counts in the registry class, generation-bijection enforced, never benchmark claims; the measured µs budgets over those chains are `slo.toml`/benchmark rows keyed {operation_class,posture,audit_class}.

## Interactions
Consumed by `w2-root-bootstrap`/`w2-root-publication` (per-class durability actions), `w2-writer-takeover` (lease primitive, owner-death rule), `w2-snapshots-leases` (shared OFD lock as the registered shared lease primitive), `w2-recovery`, `w10-archive-open` (read-only variant), `obs-doctor` (probe integration), `perf-cost-ci` (barrier-chain derivability law). Consumes `g0-format-arms` (sync-obligation column + read-only variant decisions), `g0-cost-registry`, `g0-claim-registries`, `w1-foundation-types`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Probe suite: scratch-directory tests for lock linearizability (two processes, nonblocking exclusive acquisition, owner-death release), rename-no-replace atomicity, file/directory sync durability (dm-flakey/dm-log-writes-style crash simulation in the lab VFS), slot-confined pwrite, and flush honesty; a deliberately lying-sync profile must be rejected (a named crash-matrix row). Open-time recheck tests: mount-option drift, overlay insertion, device change — all flip to read-only with typed diagnostics. CI: the sync-obligation column must derive the exact Appendix G barrier-chain counts (generation law); a profile row without probe entrypoints fails registry checks. E2E: the write-profile probe runner (this bead's library entrypoint, later surfaced as `fgdb doctor --write-profile` by `obs-doctor`, which depends on this bead) on ext4 and XFS fixtures logs every probe, its syscall trace, and the resulting instance-record digest; unregistered filesystems (btrfs default, NFS, overlayfs) produce read-only verdicts; the doctor CLI surfacing of these same probes is validated when obs-doctor lands (gate-g4).

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: filesystem-name sniffing (`statfs` magic alone) — mount options and layers change semantics; blanket fsync-everything (unaffordable and hides which operation owes what); treating doctor pass as proof (evidence about a moment; hardware can lie). Risk: kernel behavior drift across the pinned range — mitigated by probe-suite versioning and open-time rechecks; risk: profile proliferation — each new profile pays the full proof contract.

## Provenance
§5.1 (348, 362), App A (1441), §19 roadmap (1330), FG-INV-10 (App F), App G.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement the fused autocommit-write arm LocalAutocommitWriteSpec
description:
## What & scope
Implement the registered fused fast-write arm: `LocalAutocommitWriteSpec`, one sequenced semantic command fusing attempt registration, prepare admission, the ordered final-certification reservation, and commit semantics for eligible single-statement autocommit writes, plus its own `command_contracts.toml` row, construction-DAG recipe, and regenerated crash matrix. This is normative current-revision content, not an optional extra.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6/B5 and market: agent workloads are dominated by small single-statement writes; the unfused path costs 4+ sequenced commands. The fused arm sets the honest floor at exactly **two** sequenced semantic commands per audit-NotRequired autocommit write (**three** under a Required profile, because ordered ticket admission must be audit-visible before any protected processing) — a registered Appendix G row (§17's fast write class), competitive with WAL engines while keeping full capsule/evidence semantics. The floor is two, not one, because `LocalTerminalCompletionSpec` consumes durability/visibility evidence of the commit's own publication and FG-INV-07 forbids any pre-order input naming its future applied record — no single-command arm can exist.

## Design — normative detail
Eligibility: single-statement autocommit writes whose bind-time `CanonicalStatementClassification` proves fused-arm eligibility; ineligible, multi-statement, or explicit-transaction work uses the unfused arms unchanged. The one command carries registration + prepare admission + the ordered final-certification reservation + commit semantics with identical canonical effects, one terminal audit gate, one D1 payload closure, one order-attempt supplement; `LocalTerminalCompletionSpec` remains the second sequenced command. Amended observation rule, scoped to exactly this arm and no other: coordinator-local permit verification and admission precede every statement/storage observation (FG-INV-20 preserved) while durable registration lands atomically with the commit; a pre-order crash leaves no durable record and an exact retry re-executes from scratch — safe because no identity or result escaped, and the autocommit idempotency-key CAS at apply guarantees at-most-once durable effect. That one apply constructs the `TxnOutcomeRecord` lineage as the compressed `Registered -> PrepareAdmitted -> CommittedPendingPostconditions` history, so `status()` semantics are unchanged. Both registration arms decode and byte-match the capability replay record; the Autocommit binding stores the scoped client key and classification before work; exact lost-EXECUTE retry returns the same registration/classification/outcome capability, drift fails.

Appendix G row (`Autocommit write, fused arm`): 2 sequenced commands NotRequired / 3 Required; ~4–8 total Raft entries; ordered barrier chain = D1 payload barrier (SemanticPayload/PreparedOwnership: capsule + mandatory strong closure + `PreparedCommitRecord` + `RootSlot`; per-txn, group-fusable), append-reply hard-state publication (Consensus; per-batch), D2 apply publication (Protocol: entry + slot; per-batch; MAY fuse with append-reply in quorum-one), completion publication (per-batch); external authority: none NotRequired, synchronous ticket CAS Required; ~15–20 durable objects minted (capsule, effect set, delta template, delta batch, authorization decision, resource transitions, outcome preparation, prepared record + successor, two availability certificates, order-attempt input, HLC evidence, command, marker, command record, state root, pipeline entry, manifest generation). With this arm and `SnapshotQuery` registered, `SnapshotQuery` is the only surface consuming zero sequenced semantic commands and zero Protocol-plane maintenance transitions (§5.2/§13); every durable operation class carries a declared budget of sequenced semantic commands, total Raft log entries, and ordered durability barriers as a registered cost-registry row; an implementation exceeding its row fails the registry check rather than silently spending more.

RETURNING: the fused arm may carry `TerminalWriteResultPreparation::Local`; completion consumes it via `AtomicProtocolDetach`, creating owner/escrow/Protocol retention leaf and only `{delivery_id,detachment_commitment}` in the semantic frontier (PendingVisibility / ReleasedAwaitingActivation / legal inline ActiveDeliverable per the standard rule).

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-20 restated for this arm: authorization precedes every observation or effect — coordinator-local admission verifies the complete capability and policy binding before any statement or storage observation; the amendment moves only the durable registration point, never the authorization point. FG-INV-07: no pre-order input names its future command/result/root — the two-command floor is its direct corollary. FG-INV-01: at-most-once durable effect via the autocommit idempotency-key CAS at apply; matching retries return the recorded lineage. Claim types: the 2/3-command and ~4–8-entry figures are exact structural counts in `latency_anatomy.toml` (generation-bijection enforced); fused-write latency is an `slo.toml` row; same-change law applies to any future weight.

## Interactions
Builds on w2-commit-protocol (capsule/D1/D2 machinery reused verbatim), w2-txn-lifecycle (registration/statement schemas), w2-prepare-terminal (fence/reservation semantics compressed into one apply), w2-outcome-tokens (compressed lineage), g0-command-contracts (registry row + bijection CI), g0-cost-registry (the priced row); w5-binder supplies real `CanonicalStatementClassification` later (fixtures until then); w10-fgp-core exposes the arm to autocommit EXECUTE.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Regenerated crash matrix specific to this arm: pre-order crash leaves zero durable record (scan asserts no orphan objects); post-order pre-completion crash recovers to CommittedPendingPostconditions and completes. Idempotency: concurrent duplicate EXECUTE with same key -> one durable effect, both callers converge on same token/outcome; drifted body fails. Registry CI: command-count/barrier-chain counters instrumented in the log and byte-compared against the Appendix G row (build fails on exceedance). Differential: fused vs unfused execution of identical eligible statements produces identical canonical effects, marker content, and status() history. Oracle: FG-INV-20 admission-before-observation matrix including this arm. Bench: fused-write p50/p99 gate per §17 with derivability check (latency >= barrier count x pinned fsync p50). E2E: scripted client run issuing eligible single-statement autocommit writes end-to-end (embedded API and FGP autocommit EXECUTE), asserting in structured logs exactly 2 sequenced semantic commands (3 under a Required profile), the compressed Registered -> PrepareAdmitted -> CommittedPendingPostconditions lineage, TerminalReady exposure, and an ineligible statement downgrading to the unfused arm; then kill -9 pre-order (exact retry re-executes from scratch, scan shows no orphan durable record) and post-order (recovery completes to CommittedPendingPostconditions), resolving via status(). DETAILED LOGGING: implementation logs {autocommit idempotency-key digest, classification OID, eligibility verdict with downgrade reason, fused command OID, order-attempt id, per-barrier events (plane, amortization class), apply CAS outcome, outcome lineage transitions}; tests assert these fields.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: eligibility misclassification silently downgrades to unfused (correct but slower) — acceptable; upgrading ineligible work is forbidden and tested. Risk: retry storms re-executing from scratch — bounded by idempotency-key CAS. Rejected: a one-command arm (violates FG-INV-07); rejected: relaxing durable-registration-before-observation for any other class (amendment is scoped to exactly this arm); rejected: treating fused writes as a separate semantics (identical canonical effects required, differentially tested).

## Provenance
Plan §5.2 l.403, App A l.1480, App G l.3179/3193, App F FG-INV-01/07/20.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Milestone W2/G1: Chronicle engine core through deterministic recovery
description:
## What & scope
Aggregate the exact W2 Chronicle/durability subset required to pass Gate G1 “The Engine Lives,” without pulling in W2's later One-Version-Universe extensions. This milestone covers identity/encoding/placement, self-sufficient three-phase bootstrap, filesystem profile and writer fencing, quorum-one Raft and publication, HLC/order attempts, stable prepared ownership, commit/control/transaction lifecycle and outcomes, final-capsule publication, recovery, exact checkpoint/cut installation and activation safety, snapshots/leases, Local continuity/allocation, compaction/Local GC, Local audit visibility, fused autocommit, and FEC object recovery. It explicitly excludes branch fork/grant/merge/retire, Ripple batch publication, protected-output owner activation, full transparency products, group-commit optimization, and exhaustive scrub campaigns, which remain in the full W2 epic consumed by G2 or later gates.

## Why
The workstream is broader than the first convergence gate. Depending on its full epic made G1 wait for G2 functionality and Warden/Aegis transitive dependencies, obscuring the critical path and undermining the gate's purpose as an early complete engine proof. A phase milestone preserves one final architecture: later tasks extend registered arms and capabilities; they do not replace G1 code or introduce substitute storage/transaction models.

## Design and phase contract
Every included task implements its final exact schema/state machine. Where a later capability is inactive, G1 validates the generated feature-disable row and rejects its commands/tags. G1's bootstrap is Genesis -> CheckpointInstalled -> Operational only; restore schemas are frozen but full receipt-first service promotion is G2/G3. Quorum-one uses the same Raft/config/snapshot interfaces later extended by W11. Checkpoint/cut logic includes inherited absent bytes and proves Provisional replacement authorizes no new reclaim before separate activation. Local audit visibility covers the complete required candidate/pipeline/release semantics needed by G1 without Fabric transport.

The milestone publishes a generated `G1ChronicleCapabilityManifest` listing exact active command/state/schema/checker rows and exact disabled later rows. Its closure is derived from child registry/evidence IDs; it cannot be hand-maintained or treat a frozen W12/G2 row as implemented. The full W2 epic depends on/contains all these same child tasks plus later extensions.

## Success Criteria
- All included W2 child tasks close with their unit/property/model/fuzz/simulation/E2E and structured diagnostic-event rows green.
- Fresh creation, checkpoint installation, operational publication, two-slot recovery, writer death/takeover, stale-writer rejection, prepared-root ownership, command/marker suffix replay, and exact-cut snapshot recovery pass every registered crash point.
- Genesis and operational checkpoint-vector generation covers every payload field exactly once and proves inherited absence cannot authorize new reclamation before activation.
- Commit/control/transaction/outcome, Local allocation/continuity, resource/constraint/escrow hooks, Local audit visibility, compaction, Local GC, and FEC repair preserve canonical logical state under restart/cancellation.
- A G1 embedded E2E traverses authorized bind/execute/final-capsule/D1/D2/recovery/replay using these Chronicle interfaces and emits a content-addressed failure bundle on any fault.
- Unit tests validate capability-manifest derivation and reject any branch/Ripple/protected-output/transparency/group-commit/exhaustive-scrub row incorrectly marked active through this milestone.
- Detailed JSONL gate rollup names child bead/checker IDs, command/state/schema rows, fault point, root/marker/checkpoint/cut commitments, obligation states, verdict, evidence refs, and replay command; logs contain no protected payload or keys.
- Completion does not claim the excluded W2 extensions; the full W2 epic and G2 remain blocked until those exact tasks close.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: keeping G1 dependent on all W2 work, cloning a simplified Chronicle, or stubbing later registered states. Risk: milestone drift as registry rows change; generated activation closure and same-change CI force explicit reassignment.

## Provenance
Plan §19 W2 workstream and Gate G1/G2 separation; G1 exit criteria; Appendix F clause activation contract.

title: Implement single-node typed-roots GC: proposal, quarantine, physical execution, retirement
description:
## What & scope
Implement Local-role garbage collection: `GcProposal`/`GcDecisionRecord`, the Semantic quarantine machine (`GcSemanticState`, `LocalGcApplyQuarantineSpec`), the Protocol physical-execution machine (`GcPhysicalExecutionRecord`, dispatch guards, member receipts), standalone Local cancellation, terminal disposition import, and §5.3's exclusive-lease physical retirement discipline. W12's fenced distributed GC (w11-fenced-gc / w12-recovery-gc) builds on these machines.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1's immutable one-version universe only survives contact with disks if reclamation is provably safe: GC deletes ciphertext and keys, the two irreversible operations in the system. The design splits authorization (Semantic, ordered, follower-recomputed) from execution (Protocol, receipted, idempotent) so no timeout, crash, or lost response can ever be read as permission to destroy — B5's evidence discipline applied to the destructor. §2.3's mark-and-compact-with-leases donor pattern is re-specified with typed roots because a generic mark phase over untyped references cannot express independent obligations (leases, holds, escrow, audit) as roots.

## Design — normative detail
`GcProposal` is the Local pre-order bounded-set authorization `{gc_id, basis_state:WeakStateIdentity, basis_logical_command_seq, basis_commit_seq, basis_raft_index, configuration_ref, checkpoint_ref, config_payload_floor_ref, activated_retention_cut_ref:StrongRef<ActivatedRetentionCutSet>, retention_map_digest, complete_typed_root_inventory_ref:StrongRef<GcRootInventory>, candidate_derivation_profile_oid, sorted_reclaim_objects_and_realizations, exact_reclaim_set_digest, required_storage_profile_and_member_set, completed_remote_release_refs[], excluded_live_prepared_certificate_remote_key_backup_legal_hold_replay_audit_capability_restore_result_workspace_and_delivery_obligation_commitment, terminal_audit_gate}` — weak basis identities plus strong current floors/inventories only. Every follower recomputes the candidate and either rejects or applies `GcDecisionRecord {proposal_ref, applied_control_ref, stable_configuration_ref, config_payload_floor_ref, retention_map_digest, typed_root_validation_digest, decision:Rejected{stable_reason}|Accepted{gc_id, authorized_reclaim_set_digest, required_storage_member_set_digest, quarantine_generation}}`; the input never names this result. An accepted decision authorizes NO physical work.

Two non-overlapping state machines. Semantic: `GcSemanticState<Role> = ProposedOrRejected | Quarantined{gc_id, authorization_commitment, quarantine_generation, reclaim_set_digest, operation_family_commitment, no_new_reference_rule_id, physical_state:AwaitingPhysicalDisposition} | PhysicalCompletedPendingCut{terminal_evidence_commitment} | CancelledBeforePhysicalStart{terminal_evidence_commitment} | Retired`. `LocalGcApplyQuarantineSpec` requires `reclaim_set` a subset of the authorized set, disjointness from every current RootSlot, candidate result, Protocol/Prepared/Consensus owner, and independently retained obligation, plus exact conformance of every generation-zero member plan `{generation=0, operation_id, idempotency_token_digest, storage_member_id, storage_profile_oid, target_inventory_digest, canonical_request_transcript_digest}` to the bounded operation family; semantic apply installs `LocalGcReclaimAuthorizationRecord` + `Quarantined` only. Every encoder, dedupe lookup, prepared receipt, command validator, compactor, and root publisher enforces the registered no-new-reference rule against the audit-visible quarantine — resurrection by deduplication is structurally blocked.

Protocol: after role-valid `CanonicalPublicationEvidence` exists, maintenance initializes `GcPhysicalExecutionRecord` with `dispatch_mode:Open|CancellationFenceInstalled{fence_generation}|CancellationReconciling{fence_generation}|NoStartFenced{fence_generation, evidence_record_ref}|CompletionRequired{authority_commitment}` and `physical_state:Requested|Started|Progress|CompletingAfterCancellationRace|Completed{complete_receipt_bijection, terminal_evidence}|CancelledBeforeStart{complete_never_started_bijection, terminal_evidence}`. Init creates exactly one `IrreversibleDispatchAttempt<GcMemberReclaim>::Armed` per active plan; a mark-sent spec advances exactly one Armed attempt to SentUnknown before transport eligibility; the generated `GcIrreversibleDispatchGuard` revalidates the current all-plane root inventory, exact quarantine generation and reclaim-set disjointness, dispatch mode, configuration, writer/member fences, continuity, authority, service epoch, and time immediately before sending the byte-identical member request. A successor generation may cover only targets proved locally AbandonedBeforeSend or provider-CancelledBeforeStart; started/completed targets keep original operation IDs and are never repeated; exhaustion fails closed. Member machine, keyed `(operation_id, idempotency_token_digest)`: `NotRegistered -> Requested -> Started{member_monotonic_counter, pre_operation_physical_root_digest} -> Completed{counter, post_operation_physical_root_digest, receipt_digest}`; cancellation allows `Requested -> CancelledBeforeStart` or the explicit idempotent tombstone `NotRegistered -> CancelledBeforeStart` that permanently rejects later registration; the machine can never move Started/Completed to Cancelled, regress a counter, or rebind an operation ID; timeout changes no state. Receipts begin with `FenceBoundIrreversibleReceiptHeader` and bind gc_id, authorization commitment, quarantine generation, operation/token, member, profile, target inventory, request transcript, pre-operation root digest, and counter; completion adds the exact deleted-or-crypto-erased inventory, post-operation root and probe digests, durability evidence, and signature. A member durably persists and fences Started before its first irreversible byte/key action; a lost response is recovered by status lookup under the same operation ID; signed NotRegistered permits only the same reclaim request or the registered cancel-before-start under a fresh guard — never inferred success or local abandonment.

Cancellation and terminal: `LocalGcCancellationAuthorizeSpec {quarantine_record_ref, protocol_no_start_fenced_evidence_ref, complete_member_target_family_and_no_start_bijection, current_unchanged_physical_root_proof, terminal_audit_gate}` -> `LocalGcCancellationAuthorizationRecord`; never constructible from a timeout or partial member set. `GcPhysicalDispositionImportSpec = Completed{quarantine_publication_evidence, protocol_terminal_evidence:PortableGcPhysicalTerminalEvidence, current_reachability_recomputation_ref, no_resurrection_proof_ref} | Cancelled{..., complete_never_started_bijection_proof, cancellation_authority}` alone moves Semantic to `PhysicalCompletedPendingCut`/`CancelledBeforePhysicalStart`; any authenticated Started/Completed observation permanently rules out cancellation and forces CompletionRequired. A later activated retention cut moves Semantic to Retired and permits Protocol evidence compaction. Cross-plane matching uses signed commitments/certificates and the same RootManifest publication — never a strong ObjectId edge between planes.
