Physical retirement of manifest generations (§5.3): first remove the generation from every canonical/independent root, activate the matching retention cut, converge both RootSlots away from it; then open/verify the exact descriptor-selected lease-inode identity and nonce and acquire its EXCLUSIVE profile-registered whole-inode lock (exclusive OFD under `FGFS-LINUX-LOCAL-V1`) before deleting or crypto-erasing any covered realization; the lock is held through the destructive operation and durable directory updates; locking a replacement at the same pathname is a hard failure. Orphan lease-inode cleanup requires a generated proof that no authenticated slot, RootManifest, prepared/consensus closure, backup, restore plan, snapshot, or retirement attempt can still name its descriptor — age or directory scanning never suffices. Process death releases locks but never changes canonical reachability.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-14 (invariant, restated): GC follows every generated strong and currently uncut conditional edge; only registered weak/locator/observation fields are nonretaining; independent obligations remain roots until their exact terminal transfer/release; provisional cuts authorize no new reclaim; physical GC uses Requested -> Started -> Completed or all-members CancelledBeforeStart with signed exact receipts, and any Started member makes cancellation impossible; heavy detail retires only after visibility and an activated cut. FG-INV-16 (invariant): no GC quarantine is lost, duplicated, or released while obligated. FG-INV-10 (invariant): every irreversible action rechecks both root authorities. Reclaim throughput/latency impact is benchmark-class.

## Interactions
Requires `ActivatedRetentionCutSet` + `RetentionMap` from w2-retention-checkpoints; shares the safe-point/convergence discipline and walker infrastructure with w2-compaction; exclusive-lock retirement uses w2-snapshots-leases' generation-lease inodes and w2-filesystem-profiles' lock primitives; ordering/followers via w2-commit-protocol; command rows from g0-command-contracts. w2-branch-retire's drain and key-destruction gating reuse these walkers; w9-key-lifecycle's destruction pipeline mirrors the quarantine/receipt idiom; w11-fenced-gc and w12-recovery-gc extend to distributed roles.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Crash/lab tests cut every quarantine, initialize, dispatch, provider cancel-tombstone, start/destructive action, receipt import, fence/status/evidence, successor-generation, terminal-state, Semantic import/publication, cut-activation, and evidence-retirement boundary. FG-INV-14 enforcement suites: mark-then-resolve, dedupe-resurrection, start-vs-cancel, and partial-member crash storms. Multiprocess retirement tests: death before/after exclusive acquisition, inode substitution/unlink-recreate, orphan cleanup with proof requirement. No-new-reference enforcement tests across encoder/dedupe/prepared/compactor/root-publisher paths. Property: follower recomputation derives the identical bounded set or rejects; import rejects missing/duplicate/wrong-family/stale-root/partial/cross-plane-substituted evidence. E2e: full propose -> decide -> quarantine -> dispatch -> receipts -> disposition -> cut -> retire run with complete lineage logging (operation IDs, counters, receipt digests, root digests).

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: timeout-as-success (lost responses resolve only via signed status); single-plane GC (a mutable physical status inside Semantic state would create cross-plane strong edges); reference counting (cannot express typed independent obligations); gossip-derived safe points. Risk: quarantine pile-up under blocked members — observable, blocking-by-design; `PartialBlocking` is surfaced, never silently skipped.

## Provenance
§5.5 (447), §5.3 (413-417), App A GC rows (~2039-2049), §2.3, FG-INV-14/16.

title: Implement group commit: barrier chains, batching choreography, quorum-one fusion law
description:
## What & scope
Implement group-commit batching for the §5.2 write path: the WriteCoordinator batching choreography (§7.6), the per-operation-class ordered durability-barrier chains (Appendix G), and the quorum-one append+apply fusion law. Deliver the instrumentation that proves the implementation matches its registered cost rows.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5 + Appendix G constitution: §1's constraint 12 demands that no mechanism accrete protocol weight without a priced row; group commit is where the priced rows meet the syscall layer. Market: single-writer embedded engines win on fsync amortization; FrankenGraphDB must match WAL-engine commit throughput while paying for capsule evidence — group commit is the mechanism that makes the ~15–20-object write census affordable at concurrency > 1.

## Design — normative detail
The protocol has two **durability barriers**, not literally two syscalls: each barrier includes every file and parent-directory sync its operation class owes under the registered filesystem profile's per-class sync obligations (`frame-pwrite|create|rename|unlink`, §5.1); Appendix G tabulates the per-operation-class barrier chains, each barrier stating plane (`SemanticPayload|Protocol|PreparedOwnership|Consensus|Bootstrap` from `DurableStateSlotRef`), what syncs, the amortization law (`per-txn|per-group|per-batch|deferrable`), and the fusion-legality column. Group commit amortizes both barriers. What amortizes: the Raft hard-state append (Consensus, per-batch), the D2 apply publication (Protocol: maintenance entry + protocol-root slot, per-batch), completion publication (per-batch), and statement publications (per-group). What is per-txn but group-fusable: the D1 payload barrier (capsule + mandatory strong closure + `PreparedCommitRecord` + `RootSlot`). What group commit does NOT amortize: sequenced semantic command counts (protocol counts are exact structural registry values — batching never removes a command); external synchronous authority interactions (audit ticket-issuance CAS is strictly serial per `AuditDomainId`); durable objects minted per transaction. Every append reply or reply batch mints a fresh `RaftHardState`/`RaftStateRoot`/`RootManifest` closure plus one serialized `RootSlot` publication; group commit shares that closure across the batch.

Fusion law (normative column, not an implementation option discovered under load): in a one-member (quorum-one) configuration, the append-reply hard-state publication and the post-apply D2 protocol publication MAY fuse into one ordered slot update — no follower exists to observe the intermediate, recovery cannot observe it (both sides land in the same `RootManifest`/`RootSlot` closure), and the receipted-but-unordered crash window fusion touches is exactly the window governed by §5.2's two abandonment arms, which fusion changes nothing about. In any multi-member configuration the two publications MUST NOT fuse: followers reply to append before commit, so the hard-state publication is an independently observable protocol obligation with its own durability meaning. A build that fuses against a MUST NOT row fails closed at the G0 conformance gates; a legal fusion still counts as one ordered sync operation, never zero, in §17's ordered-sync-count gate.

Choreography (§7.6): WriteCoordinator is a supervised asupersync actor. Commit requests arrive on a two-phase MPSC whose reserve/commit protocol prevents a cancelled producer from publishing a partial queue entry. Its response is a oneshot obligation whose unresolved terminal state is detected by the obligation/leak oracle (detection is not confused with impossibility). Group-commit batching uses bounded queues and the three-lane scheduler with an explicitly tested fairness/deadline policy — never a claim that an EDF hint alone proves starvation freedom. These are typed runtime contracts plus lab-tested state-machine obligations, not guarantees inherited without integration evidence. Group semantics from §5.2 step 2: each accepted transaction is evaluated against the committed basis plus earlier accepted effects in that group; barrier chains for the group are emitted in deterministic order.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-16: no oneshot obligation or queue entry is lost/duplicated; under declared fairness every obligation reaches one legal terminal or recoverable state (asupersync leak/quiescence oracle). FG-INV-10 (fusion side): recovery must not be able to observe a half-fused publication; both sides land in one closure. Claim types per the constitution: barrier chains and command counts are exact structural rows in `latency_anatomy.toml` generated from `command_contracts.toml` (hand-declared only for external-RTT class and group-commit amortization, each naming the contract rows it summarizes); throughput/latency budgets are `slo.toml` rows keyed {operation_class,posture,audit_class}; maintenance-stream capacity is FG-CFG-04. Three CI laws bind the registry: derivability (a latency gate >= ordered-barrier count x pinned measured fsync p50; a throughput gate <= the apply ceiling implied by sequenced-command count x measured serial apply cost — a failing gate is a registry error and fails the build, not the benchmark), coverage (every stated scale objective has a `stream_capacity.toml` scenario), and same-change update (any change adding commands/barriers/external interactions/identity structure updates both tomls in the same change; CI regenerates and diffs).

## Interactions
Wraps w2-commit-protocol (barriers D1/D2) over w2-order-raft (append/reply closure minting); fusion legality consumed by w2-recovery (crash-window reasoning) and w11-raft-multi (MUST NOT arm); counters feed perf-cost-ci (registry generation/derivability CI) and perf-bench-core (§17 gates); g0-cost-registry owns the tomls this bead must match; w2-filesystem-profiles supplies per-class sync obligations.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Conformance fixtures: quorum-one build with fusion on/off both pass recovery; multi-member build attempting fusion fails closed at the G0 gate. Instrumentation: every barrier logs {plane, files+dirs synced, amortization class, batch size, fused?}; a CI check byte-compares the observed chain per operation class against the Appendix G row. Crash tests at batch boundaries: kill between D1 of member k and batch append; between append and fused/unfused D2; assert per-txn outcomes independent (no false-shared fate beyond the batch contract). Fairness lab: three-lane scheduler under adversarial load meets the tested deadline policy; starvation counterexample search. Leak oracle: cancelled producers never publish partial entries; unresolved oneshots detected. Bench gates: commits/s at concurrency {1,16,256} and ordered sync ops per commit/append batch by posture and audit class, checked by the derivability law against pinned fsync p50. E2E: scripted mixed commit workload at concurrency {1,16} on a quorum-one build, asserting in logs batch formation {batch id, member txn tokens, lane}, exactly one shared RaftHardState/RaftStateRoot/RootManifest closure and one serialized RootSlot publication per reply batch, fused vs unfused D2 publication events, and independent per-txn outcomes; repeated against a multi-member fixture asserting the MUST NOT arm refuses fusion. DETAILED LOGGING: every barrier logs {plane, files+dirs synced, amortization class, batch size, fused?} (the CI byte-compare source); the three-lane scheduler logs lane occupancy and deadline decisions consumed by the fairness lab; tests assert these fields.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: batch-size latency tension — governed by the tested deadline policy, gated p99. Risk: fusion masking a real multi-member obligation — prevented by the normative MUST NOT column and conformance gate. Rejected: discovering fusion opportunities empirically at runtime (unverifiable durability meaning); rejected: counting a fused publication as zero sync ops (dishonest §17 accounting); rejected: unbounded queues (loses backpressure honesty); rejected: claiming EDF-hint starvation freedom without lab evidence.

## Provenance
Plan §5.2 l.407, §7.6 l.647–649, §14.W1 l.1070, App G l.3171–3193; App F FG-INV-10/16, FG-CFG-04.

title: Build HLC proposal evidence and the repeatable order-attempt supplement machinery
description:
## What & scope
Implement the repeatable order/HLC supplement layer that §5.2 deliberately keeps outside stable semantic prepared ownership and signed audit bytes: `HlcProposalEvidence`, `LocalOrderSubject`, `LocalOrderAttemptInput`, `LocalOrderAttemptAvailabilityCertificate`, `PreparedOrderAttemptRoot`, and `OrderAttemptRetirementEvidence` (Local arms; Meta forms are W12 but the schemas are registered now).

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5: separating the stable semantic base (signed once) from the repeatable order/HLC supplement (rebuilt per proposal) is what makes retries evidence-clean — neither HLC nor assigned order ever appears in signed audit bodies, so time-authority hiccups cannot invalidate audit evidence or force re-signing. B1: `commit_hlc` derived deterministically from ordered evidence gives trustworthy `AS OF TIMESTAMP` semantics.

## Design — normative detail
`LocalOrderSubject` is `Terminal{final_certification_reservation_ref:StrongRef<LocalFinalCertificationReservation>,required_state:Active,selected_terminal_digest}|Control{typed_payload_ref:StrongRef<SequenceNeutralSpec>,spec_body_digest,expected_state_conditions_digest,terminal_audit_freeze_commitment}`. `LocalOrderAttemptInput` is `{order_attempt_id,subject:LocalOrderSubject,semantic_prepared_ownership_id,hlc_proposal_evidence_ref:StrongRef<LocalHlcProposalEvidence>,expected_next_logical_command_seq,expected_next_commit_seq:NotApplicable|Commit{value},configuration_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,writer_fence_epoch,body_digest}`. Commit applicability derives from the immutable selected terminal/control kind; abort/read/control cannot smuggle a commit-sequence assignment. `LocalOrderAttemptAvailabilityCertificate` uses the universal signer protocol, names the exact input/semantic owner/base-closure digest, covers the already-built supplement closure while excluding itself/the future command; its plan/lock/share/publication maintenance entries never change expected semantic counters. `PreparedOrderAttemptRoot<Role>` is `{generation,entries[order_attempt_id -> Available{input_ref,availability_certificate_ref,maintenance_install_index}|Ordered{role_order,commit_order:None|Some,semantic_command_identity,semantic_raft_index}|RetiredStale{retirement_evidence_ref,successor_attempt_id}],subject_to_latest_attempt_map,body_digest}`. `OrderAttemptRetirementEvidence` proves at a linearizable read barrier that the attempt was never a semantic log entry/candidate, identifies the counter drift that made it stale, and retains its plan/certificate closure. Only nonsemantic maintenance installs/retires entries; semantic apply atomically selects Ordered. Checked counter mismatch, duplicate subject, self-staleness, retirement-after-order, and command/supplement substitution fail closed. The ordered command strongly names exactly one role-matching order-attempt input and availability certificate; voters derive the next sequence/HLC only from that input plus the current persisted HLC and require its subject, semantic owner, spec/reservation, and any audit-freeze commitment to match. An aged-out observation or lost sequence race retires the supplement with a linearizable nonorder proof and certifies a fresh attempt without changing semantic ownership or any reservation/audit plan/lock/share/terminal bytes; every failed supplement remains rooted until the prepared/order-attempt floor proves nonorder. A terminal reservation CAS, or a control spec's exact idempotency/expected-state CAS, admits at most one ordered semantic command across all supplements.

HLC: durable kinds are `LocalHlcProposalEvidence {database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,role:Local,configured_source_id,source_profile_oid,signed_observation,observation_uncertainty,normalization_policy_oid,observation_body_digest}` and the Meta multi-observation form; the registered policy fixes source eligibility, quorum, interval-to-candidate rule, maximum accepted age, and `maximum_forward_jump` relative to the previous logical HLC; missing/duplicated/untrusted/stale/future-skewed/arithmetically invalid observations reject the proposal. Deterministic apply computes `checked_increment(previous_logical_hlc)`, derives the one normalized candidate from the evidence, rejects candidates beyond the checked forward-jump bound, and advances `logical_hlc_state = max(checked_increment, normalized_candidate)`; any sequence/HLC overflow rejects before mutation and permanently fail-closes further semantic mutation against the persisted maximum; arithmetic never wraps or saturates. Shards never propose semantic HLC; no command carries a parallel scalar or observation list.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-07 (every pre-order input excludes its future command; supplement certificates exclude themselves); FG-INV-08 (contiguity of orders/indexes); FG-INV-16 clause coverage for order-attempt entries as obligations that reach one legal terminal (Ordered or RetiredStale with retained closure). HLC forward-jump/age bounds are registered policy configuration, not invariants.

## Interactions
Consumed by w2-commit-protocol (step 6), w2-prepare-terminal (`AdmittedTxnAbortCommand` order subject), w2-txn-lifecycle (every lifecycle control orders through a supplement), w2-recovery (reconciles Available vs Ordered vs RetiredStale), w9-time-authority (source profiles/observations). Roots live in `RaftHardState.prepared_order_attempt_root_ref` (w2-order-raft).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Property tests: max-law monotonicity, checked_increment overflow fail-close (permanent), forward-jump rejection. Fuzz: evidence decode, duplicate/unsorted Meta observations. DPOR/crash: install -> order -> retire races; retirement-after-order rejection; stale supplement replaced while semantic owner unchanged; recovery finds Available entries and classifies them; App A crash rows: stale evidence before/during signing, intervening commands, leader/configuration change, multiple fresh supplements racing, and exactly one semantic application across all supplements. Oracle: no signed audit body contains HLC or assigned order (scanner over all audit transcripts); apply-derived `commit_hlc` reproducibility across replicas/replay. Logged evidence: every rejection carries typed reason (stale/untrusted/jump/age) with source id and policy OID. E2E (harness-level at this bead — the commit stack and the `(commit_hlc, commit_seq)` index are dependents): scripted ordering sequence driving synthetic Terminal and Control order subjects through fgdb-order under a simulated clock-source outage and recovery — ordering stalls with typed stale/age rejections and resumes after fresh observations; a replay of the same ordered evidence derives byte-identical HLC state in a second process. The full commit-sequence variant runs at w2-commit-protocol and the `AS OF TIMESTAMP` resolution through apply-derived `commit_hlc` runs at w2-snapshots-leases (both dependents), against the machinery this bead delivers. DETAILED LOGGING: every supplement transition logs {order_attempt_id, subject kind (Terminal|Control), semantic_prepared_ownership_id, state (Available|Ordered|RetiredStale), expected vs observed counters}; HLC apply logs {previous logical HLC, checked_increment, normalized candidate, chosen max, normalization policy OID}; tests assert these fields.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: clock-source outages stalling commits — bounded by policy max-age with typed rejections; availability degrades honestly rather than corrupting order. Rejected: HLC inside the stable prepared closure (every retry would re-sign audit bytes); rejected: wall-clock scalars in commands (unverifiable, replay-divergent); rejected: saturating HLC arithmetic (silently reorders history).

## Provenance
Plan §5.2 l.393–399, App A l.1752–1754, l.952, App F FG-INV-07/08/16.

title: Implement IdAllocatorState, IdRangeLease, and the never-recycled 128-bit identity shape
description:
## What & scope
Implement the canonical ID allocator: the 128-bit never-recycled VId/EId identity shape and its recorded width decision, `IdAllocatorState` in `LogicalStatePayload`, `IdRangeGrantSpec`/`IdRangeLease` (and the distinct `ShardIdRangeLease` schema), epoch advance under the continuity fence, and the branch/merge/W12 allocator laws. The first-escape reservation machinery is the sibling subtask `w2-escape-bindings`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1's history, branches, backups, and client references are only unambiguous if element identity is stable and never reused: external identity is `(DatabaseSecurityNamespaceId, GraphId, VId)`. B6 agents hold identities across sessions and branches; a recycled slot would silently alias unrelated data. The 128-bit width is a **final recorded decision**: the `u64 allocation_epoch` survives unbounded same-identity restores (every write-enabled restore takes a fresh epoch strictly above the external continuity floor) and partition exhaustion advances epochs under the never-recycle law; the 20-bit `partition_id` aligns identity with W12 ownership mobility so identities never change when partition ownership moves. The rejected 64-bit alternative is recorded with its reason: `partition_id` (20) plus `monotone_slot` (44) already fill 64 bits, so any 64-bit split must shrink epoch, partition, or slot, and every such split either makes externally fenced epoch advances routine on the ingest path (a hot partition at the §17 bulk-load gate exhausts a shrunken slot space in seconds — exactly the external-authority coupling the embedded posture must avoid) or leaves terminal-exhaustion headroom incompatible with restore drills under the epoch-per-restore rule, while dropping the partition field would redesign `IdRangeLease` and the allocator/escape object model. On-disk cost is governed by the §6.2/§6.3 identity-column encoding law, not the logical width — physical formats do not pay raw 128-bit identities where the registered shared-prefix codecs apply.

## Design — normative detail
`VId` is 128-bit `{ allocation_epoch: u64, local_id: { partition_id: 20 bits, monotone_slot: 44 bits } }`; deleted or abandoned leased slots remain spent forever; local exhaustion advances to a newly reserved epoch or returns a structured limit — it never wraps, reuses, or silently aliases a GraphId. `EId` has the same epoch+partition+slot shape in an edge-kind domain and is never a run position; `(src, edge_type, dst, user_key?)` is an indexed logical tuple while run positions/property locators are replaceable physical addresses; parallel edges remain distinct across compaction, merge, and time travel, and `InsertionOrder` never depends on layout. A sequence-neutral first-creation effect stores `BirthOrdinal { intent_ordinal, merge_ordinal, element_id }`; its creating `MarkerRef` supplies `commit_seq`, yielding durable `OriginBirthOrder { commit_seq, intent_ordinal, merge_ordinal, element_id }` in applied versions/checkpoints/runs without rebuilding the pre-order capsule; importing an existing identity into another branch preserves that origin and separately records branch admission (§5.6).

**Allocation is canonical state plus a profile-bound continuity fence, not a process counter**: `IdAllocatorState` binds `{ graph_id, element_kind, allocation_epoch, identity_continuity_record_ref, topology_epoch, per_partition_high_water, spent_range_commitments, exhausted_partitions }` in `LogicalStatePayload` (`id_allocator_root`). Epoch advance is fenced per `w2-continuity-profiles` (ExternalCas `IdentityContinuityRecord`, DirectoryBound fenced journal, or TPM-NV variant) before first use. Pre-order `IdRangeGrantSpec<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` binds the requested range, allocator basis, `authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>`, and issuance profile/window. `IdRangeLease<Role> = { authority_bound_header, lease_id, graph, element_kind, allocation_epoch, partition, half_open_range, applied_control_ref:AppliedControlRef, time_authority_profile_oid, issuance_not_before, issuance_not_after, permanent_spent_commitment, body_digest }`; its authenticated transcript covers the complete authority binding and profiled window. Use consumes fresh `TimeValidationEvidence::Usable`; expiry ends issuance authority only through matching `Expired` evidence, and every epoch/range pair remains permanently spent, never overlapping or recycled. Lease ranges are disjoint, authority-scoped, crash-recoverable, and never recycled even when partly unused; expiry never removes a range from the permanent spent set. `ShardIdRangeLease` is the distinct shard-owned schema `{ authority_projection:ShardAuthorityBindingProjection, meta_grant_ref:CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<MetaIdRangeGrantCertificate>, shard_id, lease_id, graph, element_kind, allocation_epoch, partition, half_open_range, shard_install_applied_ref, time_authority_profile_oid, issuance_not_before, issuance_not_after, permanent_spent_commitment, body_digest }`; the applied tag must match the owning Local/Meta/Shard state machine and assigned position — role substitution or a digest-only authority projection is unencodable. `IdRangeLease` and `ShardIdRangeLease` are registered `TimeBoundSubject` arms.

**Branch/merge/W12 laws**: branches share the graph allocator rather than forking its namespace; merge/import verifies the source identity namespace and remaps only through an explicit recorded graph-clone transform; W12 range grants and every cross-shard escape reservation are Meta-Raft fenced before use. A same-identity restore must acquire an epoch strictly above the external continuity floor before writes.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-11 (verbatim core): allocation epochs, leases, and canonical spent commitments are monotonic under the registered profile and prevent VId/EId/generated-key alias, overlap, or reuse across crash, label change, branch, merge, clone, restore, topology movement, and role activation. FG-INV-02 clause: each allocation offset has at most one legal live owner; duplicate consume fails. Exhaustion behavior is a structured-limit contract, not a statistical claim.

## Interactions
Consumes `w2-continuity-profiles` (epoch fence, restore floors), `g0-command-contracts` (grant-spec rows), `g0-identity-registries`, `w1-foundation-types` (u128/bitfield types), `w1-generated-parsers`. Time-evidence contract: lease use consumes fresh `TimeValidationEvidence::Usable` and expiry requires matching `Expired` evidence under w9-time-authority's rollback-protected contract — an interaction, not a build blocker: the evidence type contract and the `IdRangeLease`/`ShardIdRangeLease` `TimeBoundSubject` rows are registered at G0 (the same convention w4-escrow-transitions records). Produces identity issuance for `w2-escape-bindings` (reservations against leases), `w2-commit-protocol` step 3 (resolving still-confined temporaries), `w4-coordinator` (finalization allocation), `w3-identity-encoding` (physical codecs for the 128-bit shape), `w12-escrow-dp-alloc` (global analogues).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Property: lease disjointness and permanent-spend monotonicity under randomized grant/expiry/crash sequences; epoch advance strictly monotone per profile; no offset issued twice across crash/retry (model-checked allocator state machine). Exhaustion: fill a partition's 44-bit slot space (simulated) — epoch advance under the profile fence or a structured limit, never wrap; checked epoch arithmetic fail-closes on overflow. Negative: overlapping lease ranges unencodable; `ShardIdRangeLease` decoding as Local rejected; lease use without fresh `TimeValidationEvidence::Usable` rejected; digest-only authority projection unencodable. Restore drill: old-backup restore mints an epoch strictly above the floor; past spent ranges remain spent. E2E: allocator lifecycle script logging every grant, lease window, high-water mark, and spent-range commitment across crash/restart/restore.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: 64-bit identity (recorded rejection above); process-counter allocation (not crash-recoverable, not fenceable); per-branch allocator namespaces (merge would need global remapping); recycling partly used expired leases (aliasing under lost-response retries). Risk: spent-range commitment growth — bounded by cumulative-commitment compaction (`w2-escape-bindings`).

## Provenance
§4.5 (219-228), App A (1886), FG-INV-02/11 (App F).

title: Implement the W2 Local audit visibility core and G1 recovery/oracle surface
description:
## What & scope
Implement the W2-owned Local audit visibility core required by G1: externally monotonic ticket admission, PendingUnclaimed to Claimed(owner) lifecycle, exact terminal freeze/attempt basis, ordered candidate pipeline with Required/NotRequired entries, authenticated external resolution-batch import, gap-free visible-prefix advance, protected-output release to ReleasedAwaitingActivation, permanent-gap handling, recovery and bounded backpressure. W9 later adds full Warden policy/declassification/operational hardening over this exact core.

## Why
The plan assigns Local audit continuity, admission, terminal and visibility interfaces to W2 and G1 explicitly tests them. Leaving the only implementation in a later W9 bead makes G1 either wait on an entire later workstream or close before its claimed Local visibility protocol exists. This task restores the intended phase boundary without weakening the audit model.

## Design — normative detail
- Local audit tickets are externally monotonic and enter PendingUnclaimed before protected observation/effect. Registration/control atomically claims the exact owner; denied/never-registered paths resolve through the Unclaimed origin.
- Terminal work first consumes the exact G0 AuditTerminalFreeze/attempt contract. A candidate contains immutable event/resolution/terminal basis and pipeline order but remains hidden.
- LocalAuditVisibilityPipeline is a rooted gap-free ordered sequence. Required entries wait for exact portable external batch CAS receipt; NotRequired/system entries carry registered structural proof. Out-of-order external completion never permits leapfrogging.
- AuditVisibilityAdvanceInputRef and Local maintenance input bind expected protocol root/generation, complete contiguous prefix, exact external continuity head succession, released ticket/outcome bijection and every pending protected-output release recipe.
- Apply atomically advances the visible semantic endpoint and Protocol audit/output indexes in one RootManifest/RootSlot publication. Pending outputs become ReleasedAwaitingActivation without clock/lease/capability; fresh activation remains separate.
- PermanentGap is a durable externally authenticated completeness transition with bounded/nonrevealing admission behavior, never a local skip.
- Recovery reconstructs candidate queue, attempt ledger, external heads/receipts and Protocol indexes, then idempotently finishes committed maintenance before service.

## Invariants & claims
FG-INV-03, FG-INV-04, FG-INV-16 and FG-INV-20 are binding. Candidate construction is not visibility; visibility is exact contiguous release. No semantic back-edge to Protocol state, no optional freeze, no output before release, and no time-service dependency in visibility advance.

## Interactions
Consumes W2 commit/order/root/recovery, G0 audit/authority/dispatch contracts, audit continuity, result/output owner registry and independent oracles. W9 protected-signing/pipeline/release tasks depend on and extend this core. W6/W10/W11/W12 consume its stable release/certificate interface but not Local internal refs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Unit/golden tests cover ticket/claim/freeze/candidate/pipeline/protocol-state/advance/permanent-gap schemas and every role-invalid/cross-plane negative.
- Property/model tests generate multiple unresolved candidates and prove exact prefix, no omission/reorder/duplicate, ticket-output bijection, atomic visible endpoint/output release, and backpressure bounds.
- Independent oracle recomputes SCC/visibility and external-head succession without reusing implementation transition code.
- Crash/DPOR matrix injects around ticket CAS, claim, freeze, signer attempt, candidate publication, external batch CAS, response import, advance ordering/apply, D2 slot publication and recovery.
- G1 E2E creates mixed Required/NotRequired Local transactions with multiple unresolved candidates, completes external batches out of order, restarts, advances only the valid prefix, exercises permanent gap/backpressure, and proves protected results remain unavailable until separate activation.
- Detailed JSONL emits {event_version,audit_domain_id,ticket_digest,owner_kind,claim_state,freeze_id?,attempt_id?,pipeline_order,candidate_digest,requirement_class,external_head_digest,cas_version,batch_digest?,resolution_state,visible_prefix_before,visible_prefix_after,protected_output_count,release_recipe_count,protocol_generation,slot_generation,recovery_action,replay_command}. Logs redact hidden event/reason/output bodies; assertions fail on missing/duplicate/out-of-order events.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: making the whole W9 plane a G1 prerequisite, optional audit fences, mutable queues, latest-head visibility, time-dependent release, and post-filtering protected outputs. This Local core is final architecture, not a stub; W9 extends authority/policy breadth rather than replacing it.

## Provenance
Plan W2 row lines 1318, G1 lines 1334-1336, audit section 12.8 and Appendix A audit formats.

title: Implement transport-independent Local result, DP-result, and replay owner machines for G2
description:
## What & scope
Implement the transport-independent W2 Local protected-output owner/state machines required by G2: ordinary query/statement/autocommit results plus DpResult and ReplayExecution arms, AtomicProtocolDetach, PendingVisibility, ReleasedAwaitingActivation, ActiveDeliverable, Acknowledged and ReleasedUnacked, explicit authenticated release/profiled expiry, complete ACK, resume lineage, rooted Protocol indexes, resource escrow, compaction and recovery. FGP framing/sockets remain W10/G3.

## Why
G2 explicitly claims these owner machines, but the current graph places implementation only in W10, which is a G3 workstream. This task makes durable ownership and recovery available independently of any network transport while preserving the one frozen result_owner_arms contract.

## Design — normative detail
- Consume the exact G0 result-owner registry and role-exact Local schemas. No new owner union is hand written.
- Local statement/read/autocommit, DP commit-result and replay-execution publication use one registered AtomicProtocolDetach: semantic frontier records only delivery ID/detachment commitment; Protocol index receives the independent retention record and resource escrow in the same RootManifest generation.
- Required audit yields PendingVisibility. Gap-free visibility yields ReleasedAwaitingActivation without time/capability. Fresh inline/independent activation alone creates ActiveDeliverable with lease and resume lineage.
- Acknowledge requires the durable RESULT_END-equivalent sink-completion transcript supplied by the test host or later transport adapter. Release requires authenticated embedded release receipt or profiled expiry. Cancel, Drop, task/session/process death and generic EOF never construct either.
- Resume/ACK/release/expiry CAS the same state version; immediate-predecessor retry reproduces the same successor; terminal records remove strong bulk/live-authority/lease/replay/escrow edges and retain compact nonreuse evidence.
- A transport-neutral host-sink trait is final abstraction: it exposes queued/writing/sent obligations and canonical END completion, not sockets or fake in-memory release semantics.

## Invariants & claims
FG-INV-14, FG-INV-15, FG-INV-16, FG-INV-19, FG-INV-20. Commit/attempt completion does not wait for client ACK, but no promised byte is reclaimed until independent ownership reaches a legal terminal disposition.

## Interactions
Depends on W2 transaction/audit/root/resource contracts, W5 replay and W9 DP schemas so every arm is inhabited in tests. W10 result/artifact/error/FGP tasks adapt the same state machine; backup/restore/GC/format/key and service-transition walkers traverse it through durable state slots. Gate G2 depends directly on this task.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Generated owner/state reachability and conservation checkers cover all five owner arms and every state.
- Unit/golden tests cover schemas, host-sink completion, embedded release receipt, expiry, resume, ACK, compaction and role/arm substitution.
- Property/DPOR tests race audit release/activation, resume/ACK/release/expiry, sender death, attempt compaction, service/key/time rotation and resource transfer; exactly one successor and no leaked/reclaimed bytes.
- Crash matrix covers semantic detach, Protocol publication, audit advance, activation, every sink obligation state, terminal evidence, snapshot/cut, backup/restore and GC.
- G2 E2E runs Local statement/autocommit, DP and replay execution through an embedded host; kills/restarts between chunks and after END/release/ACK; resumes byte-identical output or observes one compact terminal disposition. Disconnect/Drop/cancel nonrelease is asserted.
- Detailed JSONL emits {event_version,owner_arm,semantic_owner_commitment,delivery_id,from_state,to_state,state_version,manifest_digest,lease_generation?,capability_generation?,host_sink_generation?,sink_obligation_state?,completion_digest?,release_evidence_kind?,resource_escrow_state,bulk_retained,recovery_action,replay_command}. Tests reconstruct ownership/conservation and fail on missing/duplicate/out-of-order events.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: waiting for W10 to make G2 true, fake memory-only retention, client ACK as commit condition, cancel/Drop release, semantic back-edges, and a separate DP/replay stream. The host-sink boundary is transport-neutral but not a prototype substitute.

## Provenance
Plan W2 row line 1318, G2 line 1340, Appendix A result formats and FG-INV-15.

### Detailed diagnostic-event contract
The Local owner machines emit versioned redacted JSONL for every semantic/protocol boundary: `event_version,event_id,run_id,owner_kind:Result|DpResult|Replay,owner_identity_public_commitment,txn_or_request_public_commitment,semantic_state_before,semantic_state_after,protocol_state_before,protocol_state_after,manifest_digest,answer_or_disclosure_contract_commitment,authority_binding_public_commitment,audit_gate_public_state,resource_escrow_public_commitment,lease_or_capability_lineage_commitment?,send_guard_arm?,durable_disposition,checker_id,verdict,failure_class,artifact_refs,replay_command`. Unit/cardinality tests require candidate, atomic commit/detachment, pending visibility, release/activation, delivery/replay, expiry/release, and terminal tombstone events in the registered order; crash/retry E2E reconstructs both planes without a debugger. Logs never contain rows, DP seeds, query text, capability bytes, local object locators, tenant/principal identity, or hidden result existence; authorized/unauthorized runs are compared for event-presence and timing-class noninterference.

### Phase boundary correction — exact DP owner before Warden activation
G2 owns the exact transport-independent `DpResult` state/retention/release arm, but does not activate or claim the W9 DP mechanism, external irreversible debit authority, continuity import, seed wrap, or noise execution. Its unit/property/simulation/E2E fixtures construct registered structurally valid synthetic `DpOutputCandidate<Local>` values through a test-only constructor whose type/field/authority/result contracts are identical to production and which is unavailable outside verification builds; fixtures prove ownership conservation only and are labeled `mechanism_evidence=NotActivated`. W9/G3 depends on this owner machine and supplies real charge authorization/receipt, seed/noise, audit, time, and continuity evidence before the DP capability bit can appear. This is a final abstraction with an inactive producer, not a stub owner or substitute mechanism.

title: Implement the keyed identity pipeline: ObjectId, CiphertextId, EncodingId, SymbolRecord
description:
## What & scope
Implement §5.1's complete noncircular identity pipeline for every durable logical object: keyed `ObjectId`, deterministic compression, one object-level AEAD under a per-ciphertext DEK, `CiphertextId`, `EncodingDescriptorWithoutId`/`EncodingId`, `PlacementDescriptorWithoutId`/`PlacementId`, RaptorQ symbolization, and per-symbol MACs over the exact `SymbolRecord` transcript — plus collision-bucket verification, dedup/namespace laws, and the non-self-referential construction rules.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1's promise — logical identity that survives recompression, re-encryption, and RaptorQ re-encoding within one keyed security namespace — requires identity layers separating *what an object is* (ObjectId), *how it is protected* (CiphertextId), *how it is coded* (EncodingId), and *where it lives* (PlacementId). That is what lets branches, dedup, replication, backup, recoding, and KMS rewrap each change exactly one layer. Keying the ObjectId prevents honest-but-curious storage from running an offline plaintext dictionary against the public slot (`g0-threat-model`); frankensqlite's Argon2id/encrypt-then-code design is the starting point (§2.3), but nonce, AAD, per-encoding DEK, symbol-MAC, rewrap, and KMS/HSM details are respecified here — no correctness inherited.

## Design — normative detail
`ObjectId = BLAKE3_keyed(K_oid, "fgdb:logical:v1" ‖ DatabaseSecurityNamespaceId ‖ canonical_plaintext_header ‖ canonical_plaintext_payload)`, full 256-bit. `DatabaseSecurityNamespaceId` is an immutable random 256-bit database-creation identity distinct from the human/catalog `DatabaseId`; `K_oid` is an immutable random database identity key shared only with authorized replicas/restore principals and wrapped through the root/bootstrap/key-escrow chain; both exist before any ObjectId is verified. A 128-bit prefix is only a lookup accelerator; collision buckets always verify full digest, object kind, length, and canonical plaintext before deduplication or substitution. Same-identity restore preserves namespace and key; clone restore creates both anew and must re-address and re-encrypt the complete logical closure. Dedup never crosses security namespaces unless a deployment policy explicitly accepts equality leakage via a separately specified shared namespace/key domain.

Pipeline: canonical plaintext is deterministically compressed under `CodecProfile`; a random per-ciphertext DEK performs **one** object-level AEAD with AAD `("fgdb:object-aead:v1", ObjectId, CipherDescriptorWithoutDigest)`. `CipherDescriptorWithoutDigest = { logical_oid, object_kind, canonical_plaintext_len, codec_profile, compressed_len, data_crypto_profile, dek_id, object_nonce_or_siv, object_tag_len }` — it excludes FEC and placement. `CiphertextId` hashes descriptor + ciphertext + profile-sized object tag; `CiphertextRecord = { descriptor, ciphertext_id, ciphertext_digest, object_tag_digest, protected_length }`. `EncodingDescriptorWithoutId = { ciphertext_id, fec_profile, transfer_length, oti_common, oti_scheme, symbol_size, source_block_count, symbol_auth_profile }` holds every parameter changing RaptorQ decoding or symbol authentication; `EncodingId = BLAKE3("fgdb:encoding:v1" ‖ canonical(EncodingDescriptorWithoutId))`. The same authenticated ciphertext may be recoded under another complete encoding descriptor without re-encryption. `PlacementDescriptorWithoutId = { encoding_id, placement_epoch, failure_domain_policy, location_form }` where `location_form = ContiguousSpan{failure_domain_id,segment_id,offset,encoded_len,symbol_inventory_digest} | Explicit{sorted_symbol_inventory_and_locators,failure_domains}`; `PlacementId = BLAKE3("fgdb:placement:v1" ‖ canonical(...))` — neither the ID nor a digest of the record is an input to itself. Adding/moving symbols creates a new placement record, never a new encoding identity.

RaptorQ encodes the complete ciphertext-plus-object-tag. `K_symbol = KDF(DEK, "fgdb:symbol-auth:v1" ‖ EncodingId)` MACs the exact canonical `SymbolRecord` transcript: domain/version plus every serialized header field except the MAC bytes, then the payload — framing lengths, identities, object kind, source block, ESI, transfer length, OTI, flags, auth profile, payload length; no shorter competing transcript. Wire format: `SymbolRecord { magic="FGEC", format_version:u16, header_len:u16, record_len:u32, logical_oid:[u8;32], ciphertext_id:[u8;32], encoding_id:[u8;32], object_kind:u16, source_block:u32, esi:u32, symbol_len:u32, transfer_length:u64, oti_common:u64, oti_scheme:u32, flags:u32, symbol_mac_profile:u16, symbol_mac_len:u16, payload, symbol_mac }`. Symbols never reuse an object AEAD nonce as per-symbol nonces; symbols from different `EncodingId`s never mix; a decoder obtains the complete descriptor/OTI/auth profile from an authenticated `EncodingDescriptorWithoutId` (or FGP's authenticated encoding prelude) before accepting any symbol — a bare SymbolRecord is never self-authorizing. DEK/ciphertext identity is separate from `wrap_key_epoch`: KEK/KMS rewrap changes only immutable `KeyWrap` records, never `CiphertextId`/`EncodingId`. RaptorQ protects erasures only within the declared source-block/placement model; replication/backup protects failure-domain loss. Truncated/noncanonical tails are ignored only in proved-unreferenced staging; a reachable sealed tail triggers authenticated repair or fail-closed recovery. Every stored digest declares one class — `TargetDigest`, `TranscriptDigest` (registered recipe), `WeakIdentityDigest`, or `BodyDigest<T>` with `{domain_separator, schema_major, included/excluded field tags}`.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-09 (verbatim): `ObjectId` recomputes from the exact keyed, namespaced canonical logical transcript; `CiphertextId`, complete `EncodingId`, and non-self-referential `PlacementId` recompute from their registered descriptors and bytes/inventory; root bootstrap reconstructs all identities without indexes; child-key AAD and symbol MACs cover their complete noncircular transcripts; collision buckets verify full identity and incompatible encodings never combine; every stored digest is explicitly Target, Transcript, WeakIdentity, or BodyDigest with one generated include/exclude recipe. Golden vectors and profile bounds are FG-EVID-class artifacts.

## Interactions
Consumes `g0-identity-registries` (five registries, BodyDigest transcripts, acyclic construction checks), `w1-crypto` (BLAKE3-keyed, AEAD profiles, KDF), `w1-codecs` (compression), `w1-generated-parsers` (registry-generated encoders/golden vectors). Produces the identity substrate for `w2-object-packing`, `w2-root-bootstrap` (RootBootstrap reproduces these descriptors byte-for-byte), `w2-fec-scrub` (recode law), `w2-commit-protocol` (capsule closures), all `w3-*` objects, and `w9-key-lifecycle` (KeyWrap/rewrap separation).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Full keyed-identity/descriptor/AAD recompute oracle: encode → decode → recompute all four identities from bytes alone. Property tests: recode under a new `EncodingDescriptorWithoutId` preserves `ObjectId`/`CiphertextId` and changes `EncodingId`; move/add symbols changes only `PlacementId`; KEK rewrap changes only `KeyWrap`. Negative fixtures: wrong `K_oid`, wrong namespace, mixed-`EncodingId` symbol sets, truncated MAC, competing shorter transcript, self-referential placement — all fail closed. Mutation, golden, and cross-version corpora per registry row; FEC-wire fuzz over `SymbolRecord` framing; collision-bucket test with engineered 128-bit prefix collisions verifying full-digest/kind/length/plaintext checks. CI: the generated digest/field checker rejects unknown exclusions, two body-digest fields, implicit zero placeholders, digest-over-self. E2E: a pipeline-lifecycle script builds a randomized multi-kind object corpus and drives encode → store → recode under a new `EncodingDescriptorWithoutId` → KEK/KMS rewrap → symbol move/add → decode, then recomputes all four identities from the stored bytes alone and byte-compares them against the originals across a process restart. DETAILED LOGGING: the implementation and tests must emit structured events for every identity computation/verification `{object_kind, namespace_id, profile_ids, computed_identity, expected_identity, verdict}`, every AEAD seal/open with its AAD transcript digest, every symbol-MAC accept/reject with `{encoding_id, source_block, esi, symbol_mac_profile}`, every collision-bucket candidate with its full-digest/kind/length/plaintext check results, and every dedup/substitution decision; the e2e verifier replays the log stream and fails on any missing event or identity/verdict mismatch, so post-implementation verification is possible from logs alone.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: unkeyed content addressing (offline dictionary attack); placement inside encoding identity (every move would re-identify); self/future-referential descriptor digests (bootstrap cycles); per-symbol reuse of the object AEAD nonce; cross-namespace dedup by default (equality leakage). Risk: profile drift between Appendix A and code — mitigated by registry-generated encoders and golden vectors as the single source.

## Provenance
§5.1 (278-280), App A (1445-1458), §2.3 encryption row, FG-INV-09 (App F).
notes:
INCREMENT 5 LANDED 2bbc615: scrub/doctor evidence. ScrubReport carries a three-state
verdict — Intact / Degraded{corrupt_symbols, surviving_overhead} / Lost{typed reason} —
because a boolean cannot express the state that matters most: corruption present AND
located, object still recoverable, re-encode now while it is cheap. Corruption is located
per symbol by its own MAC (tested 1..6 simultaneous rots, one-for-one). Lost reasons are
typed so escalation is chosen not guessed (InsufficientSymbols -> replica/backup repair or
rebuild-from-suffix; IdentityMismatch -> these are the wrong bytes). Every report carries
the SHA-256 content hash of asupersync's DecodeProof, on BOTH decode arms — a failed decode
is evidence too. Deterministic per symbol set; different survival patterns attest
differently, so the hash commits to HOW the decode went. 7 laws green.

CHRONICLE NOW 47 tests / 5 law files: identity_pipeline, symbol_record, erasure_recovery,
packed_group, scrub_evidence. Commit series f630102, ff873b9, 4d5eaa1, 688ba3d, 2bbc615
over fgdb-crypto 580074d + 5fabf5d.

STILL OPEN ON THIS BEAD:
6. Reduced-repair profile tiering (plan L477). Correctly ordered AFTER the
   checkpoint/retention increment: eligibility is a DYNAMIC property of retention state
   ("Chronicle-reconstructible exactly while re-derivable from the authoritative
   checkpoint plus the retained contiguous logical-command suffix, and not reachable from
   the authoritative checkpoint closure"), so it cannot be built before that state exists.
   The scrub layer is the natural home for the escalation ladder it needs
   (RebuildFromSuffix), and ScrubVerdict::Lost{reason} is already shaped for it.

CAPSULE CONTAINER LANDED 2026-07-29 (JadeSnow) — 03e7d7e, crates/fgdb-chronicle/src/capsule.rs
+ tests/capsule_container.rs, 12 laws, mutation-proven. 118 chronicle tests total.

WHY IT WAS NEEDED: capsules were being written to disk as RAW PLAINTEXT. Doctrine 5 says
every durable object but manifest.root is content-addressed and erasure-coded, and that
this is what removes the need for a double-write journal. Raw bytes are a different
mechanism wearing the same shape — a substitute, not a subset (doctrine 7) — and they
quietly withdrew the justification for having no journal.

THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MOST, because it was a real gap between doctrine and code:
decode_object REFUSES a symbol whose MAC fails rather than skipping it, so a SINGLE
flipped bit destroyed a capsule that could survive eight lost symbols. The corruption law
failed on first run and that is how I found it. The fix is NOT in decode_object — that
contract is deliberate and pinned by erasure_recovery.rs ("a corrupted symbol is rejected
before it can perturb a decode"), and it is right for a decoder whose caller believes in
its symbols. The authentication filter belongs in the CAPSULE layer, which is the thing
that does not believe its input: it read whatever was on disk and some of it may have
rotted. Filtering there is what turns corruption into plain erasure. Consequence: symbols
are verified twice, once for membership and once by the decoder as its own precondition —
deliberate, since recovery is not a hot path and the alternative is a decoder that trusts
its caller.

ANY OTHER READER OF SYMBOLS FROM DISK NEEDS THE SAME FILTER, and I CHECKED: scrub.rs
already does it, and did so first. Its "Pass 1: authenticate every symbol independently. A
rejected symbol is a located corruption; it simply does not enter the decode" is the same
two-pass shape capsule::recover now uses, so this is an established convention in the
crate rather than something I invented — which is the stronger reason to keep it. No
defect there; the question is closed.

DESIGN POINTS WORTH KEEPING:
- The header is CHECKED, not trusted. The expected ObjectId comes from the commit marker,
  never from the file, so a rewritten header can only fail — it cannot redirect recovery.
- The nonce is DERIVED from the object identity, so sealing is deterministic. A random
  nonce would give one object two encodings and deduplication could never fire.
- A container truncated in its SYMBOL region keeps what survived and drops the partial
  symbol; refusing to parse would turn a recoverable object into an unrecoverable one.
- No compression: codec_profile = 0 because declaring a profile we do not apply would make
  the descriptor lie. fgdb-codec chooses that later.

NOT DONE: CommitCoordinator still writes raw plaintext. Wiring needs the coordinator to
hold crypto material (k_oid, namespace, DEK, CapsuleProfile), which changes its
constructor and fgdb-sim's call sites. Deriving the oid inside commit() would additionally
retire the CapsuleRefMismatch error class, since a caller could no longer name one object
and store another.

WIRED 2026-07-29 — e940592. The commit path now seals through the capsule codec; capsules
are erasure-coded on disk, and read_capsule recovers through it. 128 chronicle+sim tests.

THE API CHANGE IS THE RESULT, not a side effect. commit() took (capsule_oid,
capsule_bytes); it now takes the plaintext and DERIVES the identity, handing it to
marker_for as a second argument. A caller can no longer name one object and store another —
the error class is gone at the source instead of being checked for. CapsuleRefMismatch
stays meaningful (marker_for gets the derived id and could still name a different one) but
no longer has to defend against the store disagreeing with its own caller.

A CONSEQUENCE WORTH KNOWING BEFORE TOUCHING THE TAMPER TESTS: with content-addressed
capsules, ON-DISK TAMPERING CAN NO LONGER REACH THE TEMPLATE-DIGEST CHECK. The ObjectId is
the keyed hash of the plaintext, so substituted content is rejected by content-addressing
first. The digest check is still live but its reachable case is now a MARKER that declares
a digest its capsule does not have — a caller-side error, not a tamper vector. Both cases
are witnessed separately in durability_semantics_e2e.rs; do not collapse them.

ALSO: crash_point_matrix's capsule_oid(seq) used to be an invented 32-byte pattern and is
now keys().identify(&capsule_bytes(seq)). Those tests can no longer assert against an
identity the store would never produce.

REMAINING ON THIS BEAD: the capsule profile is a constant (CapsuleProfile::balanced,
symbol_size 256 / 8 repair symbols) chosen by the caller. The plan makes the repair budget
a policy decision per RECONSTRUCTIBILITY TIER, so a real tiering table belongs to the
retention/checkpoint work. Also unset: codec_profile is 0 because nothing compresses yet —
declaring a profile we do not apply would make the descriptor lie, so fgdb-codec chooses
that later.

comments.text: FRESH-EYES REVIEW 2026-07-29 at committed f630102 plus current symbol WIP. Three fail-closed gaps: (1) IdentifiedObject::protect subtracts arbitrary descriptor.object_tag_len from sealed.len; an oversized value panics and any non-16 value creates a descriptor/CiphertextId tag split inconsistent with the XChaCha opener. It also does not bind/check descriptor object_kind, canonical_plaintext_len, compressed_len, or data_crypto_profile against the stage/body. Make descriptor construction/transition fallible and profile-validated. (2) current SymbolRecord::for_encoding accepts caller object_kind, EncodedObject drops the kind, and verify never compares it; a MAC-valid wrong-kind record passes. Propagate/derive/check kind. (3) parse_framing accepts bytes.len() > record_len and ignores the tail; exact-record verification must require equality or return explicit consumption, because reachable noncanonical tails fail closed. Secondary: fixtures use transfer_length=4096 for roughly 528 protected bytes, demonstrating missing descriptor/body coherence; the header mutation test's generic is_err proves rejection but not MAC coverage when structural/foreign checks fire first. comments.text: FRESH-EYES CAPSULE REVIEW 2026-07-29 at landed 03e7d7e. The new capsule container does not discharge the prior object-kind and endianness findings in comments 884/885. Direct cross-kind control: capsule::seal passes object_kind to IdentifiedObject::new but passes an empty canonical_header; IdentifiedObject::new stores object_kind without hashing it, and capsule::recover recomputes the ObjectId with the same empty header. Add a mutation-sensitive cross-kind regression and bind the kind in the canonical identity header before wiring this to CommitCoordinator. SymbolRecord::for_encoding still accepts an arbitrary object_kind and verify still does not compare it with encoding.cipher_descriptor().object_kind. Also repair_symbols is outside CiphertextId, EncodingId, and every symbol MAC, while recover ignores it: changing only CapsuleDescriptor.repair_symbols preserves successful recovery but changes erasure_budget(). The new claim that the complete header is checked is therefore false; this field is untrusted policy/telemetry unless bound by an authenticated placement/inventory contract. All capsule fixed integers remain big-endian despite the Appendix-A little-endian rule already recorded in comment 885. Agent Mail 21173 sent urgent to JadeSnow, CC GreenKnoll/LilacLion. I edited no Chronicle path.

title: Implement PackedObjectGroup with the pack-homogeneity law and D1-boundary packing
description:
## What & scope
Implement `PackedObjectGroup`, the registered `physical_record_kinds.toml` class that packs the length-delimited canonical plaintext bytes of many small logical objects into one physical record paying **one** compress/AEAD/FEC/placement pipeline, plus its mandatory homogeneity law, subobject locator indexing, reclamation coarsening, and byte-economy reporting. `MarkerBatch` is respecified as exactly such a pack.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1 makes every commit produce several small control-plane objects (capsule, effect set, delta template, authorization decision, resource transitions, outcome-preparation record). Paying a full pipeline (compression header + AEAD tag + FEC symbolization + placement record) per tiny object multiplies metadata bytes per user commit — a direct threat to the §17 byte-economy targets and §6.6 write-amplification model (B2's economics). Packing generalizes the `MarkerBatch` trade the plan already accepts: one pipeline per group, members keep logical identity. The saving is priced, never assumed (B5 discipline).

## Design — normative detail
The pack, not the member, owns the `CiphertextId`/`EncodingId`/`PlacementId` chain. Every member keeps its keyed `ObjectId`, computed and verified over its own canonical plaintext exactly per `w2-object-identity`. The object-location index maps each member OID to an authenticated `(pack_encoding, offset, length)` subobject locator in the same registered metadata-tree locator class marker batches already use; entries remain nonretaining locators. `PreparedCommitRecord.exact_realizations` already carries `object_or_subobject_id`, so prepared ownership names packed members without new schema surface. `StrongRef` semantics, generated reachability/GC walkers, and content addressing are unchanged because references target logical ObjectIds, never placements; a pack never acquires an `ObjectKind`; a packed member deduplicates against any other realization only through the full-digest/kind/length/plaintext verification every collision candidate already pays.

**Mandatory homogeneity law**: a pack is homogeneous in (a) key domain — every member belongs to exactly one write-key domain: the branch envelope/write-key epoch for branch-scoped payloads, or the database-scoped commit-stream key domain for commit-mechanism objects (markers, capsules, command records); (b) tenant/authority domain — one `DatabaseSecurityNamespaceId` and one tenant; (c) retention/floor class. Thus the pack DEK's wrap binds a single source epoch and creation boundary under §12.5's envelope rules, and crypto-erasure granularity never coarsens across epochs, tenants, or floors. A mixed pack fails closed at build time. Reclamation coarsens to the pack — a pack is reclaimable only when every member is — and compaction owns the rewrite of partially dead packs (the same trade marker batches accept).

**Packing boundary = existing D1 boundaries, no new ordering step**: the coordinator packs one ordered group's control-plane commit objects at the seal §5.2 step 5 already performs; each per-proposal order-attempt supplement and its availability certificate pack analogously at their own step-6 D1 boundary; later command/command-record/marker objects ride their existing publication boundaries under the same rule. Packing adds no new ordered durability barrier. Packs report through §17 byte-economy metrics — metadata bytes per small durable object and Chronicle stream bytes per user commit, by operation class — and §6.6's write/space-amplification component breakdown.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-09 applies unchanged to members: every member `ObjectId` recomputes from its own canonical plaintext; the pack's physical identities recompute from the pack descriptor/bytes. FG-INV-14 clause: subobject locator entries are registered nonretaining fields; GC reclaims the pack only when every member is unreachable and no independent obligation roots any member. The byte-economy saving is a benchmark/SLO-class claim (Appendix G / §17 rows), never an invariant; the homogeneity law is a G0 build-time format law with negative fixtures.

## Interactions
Consumes `w2-object-identity` (member identity + pack pipeline), `g0-format-arms` (frozen `PackedObjectGroup` decision + homogeneity law), `g0-identity-registries` (physical-record row, locator class), `g0-cost-registry` (byte-economy rows). Produces packing used by `w2-commit-protocol` (step-5/step-6 D1 seals), `w2-group-commit` (group boundary = pack boundary), `w2-compaction` (partially-dead-pack rewrite), `w3-write-amp` (component breakdown), `perf-bench-core` (metadata-bytes gates).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Unit: build/decode round-trip for packs of 1..N members; member OID verification from subobject locators; pack digest recompute. Negative: mixed key-domain pack, mixed tenant, mixed retention class — build fails closed with typed errors; a `StrongRef` targeting a pack (rather than a member OID) is unencodable. Property: dedup of a packed member against an unpacked realization requires full plaintext verification; GC never reclaims a pack with one live member; compaction rewrite of a partially dead pack preserves all live member ObjectIds and logical digests. Crash matrix, phased: at this bead, harness-level pack-seal atomicity — cut a simulated durability boundary before/after pack seal and assert a torn or partial pack is detected and treated as absent (no partial-member ambiguity); the step-5 and step-6 D1 integration rows (recovery sees either no pack or a complete sealed pack inside a real commit) are registered now as named matrix rows and executed at w2-commit-protocol's crash matrix and verif-torture. Bench: metadata bytes per small durable object with packing on/off, logged per operation class and checked against the Appendix G row; e2e script logs pack sizes, member counts, and reclamation coarsening events.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: per-member pipelines (metadata blowup — the reason this exists); packs as logical objects with ObjectKind (would corrupt the reference model); heterogeneous packs (would coarsen crypto-erasure across epochs/tenants/floors, violating §12.5 granularity); a new pack-publication barrier (packing must ride existing D1 boundaries). Risk: pathological packs with one hot + many dead members inflating space-amp — mitigated by compaction rewrite policy and the §6.6 breakdown making it visible.

## Provenance
§5.1 (line 342), §19 G0 decision batch (1313), §12.5 envelope rules, §17/§6.6 metrics.

title: Implement fgdb-order: quorum-one Raft core, hard state, snapshots, log verifier
description:
## What & scope
Build the `fgdb-order` crate: the durable Raft log/state core and quorum-one driver that every durable FrankenGraphDB posture orders through. Scope: `RaftLogSegment`, `RaftHardState`, `RaftSnapshot` (applied-cut), `RaftConsensusCutProjection`, `RaftStateRoot`, `ConfigurationState` consumption, the role-tagged maintenance-command routing, the generated log-to-state verifier, and gap classification during log examination. Multi-member protocol (`fgdb-raft`) layers on top later (w11); this bead delivers the one-member/quorum-one specialization that single-node embedded and server postures run in production. Only `:memory:` runs the same state machine without a durability claim.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5 (determinism/evidence): one commit state machine for single-node and replicated means single-node correctness evidence transfers to clusters instead of maintaining two recovery authorities. B1: the ordered log is the spine of the One Version Universe — `CommitSeq`/`LogicalCommandSeq` derive from it. Market: SQLite-class embedded durability with a story that scales to consensus without a rewrite; competitors (Neo4j, Kùzu) keep separate WAL vs replication machinery. The frankensqlite donor (§2.3) supplies the no-extra-mutable-file, root-publication architecture; Raft here is not middleware but the ordering substrate under it.

## Design — normative detail
`RaftLogSegment` carries the exact domain/index/term/entry fields and a generated closed command union over Local semantic txn/control, Meta semantic txn/control, Shard prepare/decision/control, and `Maintenance{command:RaftMaintenanceCommand}`. `RaftMaintenanceCommand` is the role-tagged outer union `Local{command_ref:StrongRef<LocalMaintenanceCommand>}|Meta{command_ref:StrongRef<MetaMaintenanceCommand>}|Shard{shard_id,command_ref:StrongRef<ShardMaintenanceCommand>}`; role/group validation rejects substitution. Maintenance commands advance Raft/maintenance indexes and their declared nonsemantic planes only; they never advance semantic sequences/HLC/heads or mutate a semantic payload. A self-staleness fixture must fail any maintenance handler that changes semantic order.

`RaftHardState` is `{database_id,database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,group_role,group_id,current_term,voted_for?,log_first,log_last,commit_index,applied_index,visible_index,configuration_state_ref:StrongRef<ConfigurationState>,snapshot_ref?,maintenance_applied_index,certificate_attempt_ledger_root_ref:StrongRef<CertificateAttemptLedger>,prepared_order_attempt_root_ref:StrongRef<PreparedOrderAttemptRoot>,audit_signer_journal_root_ref:StrongRef<AuditSignerJournalRoot>,protocol_state_identity:WeakStateIdentity}`. `ConfigurationState` (`{database_id,...,configuration_epoch,form:Stable{voters[],storage_members[]}|Joint{old/new voters and storage members},sorted_member_descriptors[...],raft_quorum_rule,payload_recoverability_predicate,failure_domain_map,gc_ack_policy,predecessor:WeakConfigurationIdentity?,transition_nonce}`) has its ObjectId as identity, never stored inside itself; one-member is the ordinary Stable specialization; cross-group import only via `RemoteConfigurationRef` — equal member lists or bare config OIDs never authorize replay.

`RaftConsensusCutProjection<Role>` is the prebuilt snapshot-self-excluding projection (last_included_index K, term at K, vote/commit state at K, configuration-at-cut ref, prospective configs, log-prefix digest, retained_suffix_begin_index K+1, floors, format escape latch, takeover head projection, `snapshot_slot:SelfExcluded{InstallThisSnapshot}`); the construction-DAG generator rejects any path from it back to the snapshot under construction. `RaftSnapshot` is a role-tagged exact **applied-cut** union with the invariant `last_included_index = K = successor RaftHardState.applied_index_at_cut`; retained suffix begins exactly K+1; construction order is cut projection -> snapshot -> successor `RaftHardState{snapshot_ref}` -> successor `RaftStateRoot`, never a cycle; every semantic/protocol/prepared/consensus object through K is owned by the snapshot closure and none is double-owned as a suffix entry; an unresolved Local/Meta audit candidate may cross the visible sub-prefix because the snapshotted protocol state owns its complete queue. It is never a visible-only cut. `RaftStateRoot<Role>` is `{hard_state_ref,retained_log_segment_refs,configuration_state_refs,matching_applied_cut_snapshot_ref?,prepared_and_certificate_ledger_refs,remote_obligation_floor_refs,transition_lock_refs,format_first_target_escape_latch,takeover_adoption_head,role_protocol_state_ref,unresolved_candidate_closure_refs,body_digest}`; hard-state and snapshot refs must agree.

No-extra-mutable-file doctrine: a node syncs the new closure before vote/append/receipt/durability replies; every append reply or reply batch mints a fresh `RaftHardState`/`RaftStateRoot`/`RootManifest` closure plus one serialized `RootSlot` publication. Every reply follows a durable RootManifest publication of the appropriate semantic/protocol/consensus state. Local Raft publication may advance RootSlot without semantic change. Leader loss yields capability-scoped `Unknown`, never a guess.

The generated log-to-state verifier proves the exact role-specific root/config/prefix at a cut; no later root may pair with an earlier cut (`LogToAllPlanesProof` is a strong RaftSnapshot field). Gap classification: entries at or below snapshot cut K are benignly absent (owned by the applied-cut closure); a missing/damaged entry inside the retained suffix (K, durable tail] is corruption and fails closed (repairable only through the FEC/replica ladder, never partially interpreted); an unacknowledged torn tail above the durable commit point may be truncated, but truncation stops at visible audit-safe state and waits for the generated-complete floor covering prepared transfers, cursors, replay, external continuities, remote trust/retention, backup, keys, and current/prospective configurations.

The `RaftHardFrame` bootstrap-frame spike (a G0 decision, owned by g0-format-arms) is consumed here: per-append scalars alone cannot stop closure re-minting because `certificate_attempt_ledger_root_ref`, `prepared_order_attempt_root_ref`, and `audit_signer_journal_root_ref` churn per commit; skipping per-batch root publication makes the retained log tail a bootstrap input requiring new subordinate clauses under FG-INV-08/FG-INV-10, a changed log-to-state verifier, and takeover coverage, with the frame embedding the same database/security-namespace/incarnation/writer-fence tuple as `RootSlot`. Implement to the recorded spike outcome either way.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-07: the concrete durable strong/uncut-conditional graph is acyclic; every pre-order input excludes its future command/result/root; `command_contracts.toml` is bijective with every role command arm/handler. FG-INV-08: logical-command predecessor order and the transaction-marker subsequence are contiguous at their sequences; every role-tagged Raft snapshot matches its precise visible cut, root, configuration, maintenance state, and applied/visible positions; Raft indexes are contiguous. FG-INV-10: the two-slot `manifest.root` protocol always selects the highest structurally credible authenticated role closure; every irreversible seal, receipt, Raft action, certificate, and slot write rechecks both authorities; closure failure repairs or fails closed, never rolls back. Claim types: ordered sync operations per commit and per append batch (by posture and audit class) are §17 gated benchmark numbers derived from Appendix G `latency_anatomy.toml`; they are registry/slo rows, never invariants.

## Interactions
Consumed by w2-commit-protocol (orders `CommitCommand`), w2-hlc-order-attempt (order-attempt roots live in hard state), w2-group-commit (append/reply batching and fusion), w2-recovery (log reconciliation), w2-snapshots-leases (visible index), w9-audit-pipeline (maintenance command family), w11-raft-multi (`fgdb-raft` builds multi-member on `fgdb-order`). Consumes w2-object-identity (ObjectId/StrongRef machinery), w2-root-bootstrap (RootSlot/RootManifest publication), g0-command-contracts (generated command unions), g0-cost-registry (priced closure re-mint), w1-foundation-types, w1-crypto.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Unit: role/group/incarnation substitution rejection for every command family; ConfigurationState one-member quorum math. Property: snapshot cut invariant (K equality, suffix begins K+1, no double ownership) under randomized snapshot/install schedules. Generated: log-to-state verifier runs in CI against every constructed cut; construction-DAG checker rejects projection-to-snapshot cycles. Crash matrix: torn-root/marker-tail/stale-writer/bootstrap/recovery rows; every-write/fsync-lie/path-replacement/rollback profiles (FG-INV-10 fixture set). Gap classification suite: benign below-cut absence, retained-suffix hole (must fail closed with typed corruption error and full logging of segment identity/index/digest), torn-tail truncation halting at the generated-complete floor. Self-staleness fixture over all maintenance handlers. Fuzz `RaftLogSegment` decode. Bench: one-member append-to-apply sync count measured and checked against the Appendix G derivability law. E2E (harness-level at this bead — the §5.2 commit stack is a dependent, not a dependency): scripted single-node durable session — open, drive a mixed stream of registered command-union entries (Maintenance commands plus generated fixture semantic entries from the G0 command unions) through the quorum-one append/apply/publication path, kill -9 at randomized points, restart, and assert the generated log-to-state verifier accepts the recovered cut and recovered state matches a reference replay of the same entry stream; the identical script re-runs with real committed writes through the full §5.2 stack once w2-commit-protocol lands, and again at gate-genesis. DETAILED LOGGING: every append/apply/snapshot-install event logs {role, group, term, index, cut K where applicable}; every RootSlot publication logs {slot generation, closure digest, trigger: append-reply|apply|maintenance}; gap-classification outcomes log {segment identity, index, digest, classification}; tests assert these fields.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: per-append closure re-minting cost in the embedded hot path — mitigated by the priced `RaftHardFrame` spike and group commit; the cost is gated, not hidden. Rejected: a separate mutable WAL file (second recovery authority, violates the no-extra-mutable-file doctrine); rejected: treating single-node as a WAL special case with Raft bolted on later (two commit state machines, non-transferable evidence); rejected: ambient abbreviated Raft schemas without database/namespace/incarnation/role/group domains (enables cross-group replay).

## Provenance
Plan §5.2 (l.393, l.407), §14.W1 item 1 (l.1068–1070), App A l.1552–1562, App F FG-INV-07/08/10, App G, §18.1 (fgdb-order row).

title: Build TxnOutcomeRecord, TxnOutcomeIndex, token capabilities, compaction and expiry
description:
## What & scope
Implement the Local token/outcome authority: `TxnOutcomeRecord`, `TxnOutcomeIndex`, `LocalBeginIdempotencyIndex`, `txn_token`/`TxnOutcomeCapability` semantics, `LocalTxnOutcomeSummaryRoot`, `LocalOutcomeCompactionSpec`, and `LocalOutcomeExpirySpec`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6: agents need a durable, MAC-scoped answer to "what happened to my transaction?" that survives crashes, retries, compaction, and years of retention — this index is that answer, with byte-identical responses across detailed and compacted forms. B1: outcomes are part of the version universe, retained under explicit floors rather than evaporating with server memory.

## Design — normative detail
`txn_token` is the opaque durable idempotency identity inside §13's MACed `TxnOutcomeCapability`, scoped to database security namespace/incarnation/service-visibility epoch, tenant/principal, authority ceiling, and an issuance/expiry interval. `TxnOutcomeIndex` is the sole Local token/capability lookup and attempt-lifecycle authority, mapping each scoped token to `Detailed{outcome_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeRecord>}|Compacted{summary_root_ref:StrongRef<LocalTxnOutcomeSummaryRoot>,leaf_key_digest}|ExpiredTombstone{token_digest}`. `TxnOutcomeRecord` is predecessor-linked `{header,txn_token,predecessor_ref?,state:BeginStaging|NeverRegistered|Registered|PrepareAdmitted|CommittedPendingPostconditions|Committed|Aborted|ReadClosed,audit_state:NotRequired{evidence}|ClaimedPending{ticket_digest,claim_identity}|TerminalGateCommitted{ticket_digest,event_digest,resolution_digest,gate_commitment,candidate_pipeline_order},completion_state,time_authority_profile_oid,issued_at,expires_at,minimum_lookup_retention_floor}`; it moves only through `BeginStaging -> Registered/StatementOpen -> PrepareAdmitted -> CommittedPendingPostconditions -> Committed` or the typed `Aborted`/`ReadClosed`/`NeverRegistered` terminals. Every successor header equals or is a registered nonwidening successor of the registration binding; scalars are never independently forgeable. Public terminal/audit state is the join of the immutable terminal-gate commitment with the current protocol `VisibleAuditOutcomeIndex`; a missing/mismatched release remains FinalizingOpaque. No Sharded arm is encodable.
