Every rooted receipted or ordered obligation appears exactly once in the selected inventory/checkpoint. `TakeoverAdoptionCheckpoint<Role> = { covered_adoption_record_digest:WeakDigest, covered_fence_epoch_range, latest_continuity_commitment, sorted_still_live_owner_refs[], sorted_terminal_or_transferred_dispositions, complete_covered_obligation_bijection_proof, predecessor_checkpoint_digest:WeakDigest?, body_digest }`; it may replace Detailed only after every covered receipt/owner is terminal or represented by an exact current owner/ref, and an activated cut may then release the prior manifest/inventory/record closure. Invalid, missing, duplicated, or unrooted evidence makes takeover recovery-only/read-only — never silently abandoned. Takeover step 7 constructs inventory → adoption record → successor Consensus/Raft root with Detailed head → RootManifest/RootSlot before the new writer token can exist.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-10: every irreversible receipt rechecks both authorities and binds its fenced source context. FG-INV-16 clause: no receipted/ordered obligation is lost, duplicated, refunded, released, or exposed while obligated across takeover — enforced here by the complete bijection proof. BodyDigest recipes are registered per `durable_fields.toml` (FG-INV-09 digest-class law).

## Interactions
Consumes `w2-writer-takeover` (protocol steps, guards), `w2-root-publication` (`RootPublicationEvidence` binding), `g0-identity-registries` (schema/BodyDigest rows), `w1-crypto` (signatures). Produces the receipt header used by `w2-commit-protocol` (PayloadReceipt), `w2-order-raft` (acceptance/ack receipts), `w11-payload-availability` (donor receipts), `w2-gc-core` (physical-operation receipts); adoption heads consumed by `w2-recovery` and `w11-membership-config`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Unit: header encode/decode goldens; BodyDigest recompute per registered recipe. Property: inventory bijection — randomized obligation sets round-trip with exactly-once representation; checkpoint replacement legal only when every covered item is terminal or re-owned. Negative fixtures: receipt with omitted header field unencodable; receipt from unreachable staging rejected despite valid signature; missing/duplicated/unrooted validation forces recovery-only mode; adoption record naming a future RaftStateRoot is a construction-DAG failure; an old receipt without an unbroken adoption chain rejected. Crash: takeover interrupted between inventory build and adoption publication — restart reconstructs an equivalent inventory (deterministic given the same recovered closure). E2E: multi-epoch succession (5+ takeovers) with obligations spanning epochs, logging each validation, chain proof, and eventual checkpoint compaction.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: trusting signature validity alone for old receipts (unreachable-staging forgeries); retaining the full manifest chain per adoption (unbounded retention — checkpoint compaction instead); embedding the future resulting root in the adoption record (cycle). Risk: adoption-chain verification cost after many successions — bounded by checkpoint compaction.

## Provenance
§5.1 (366, 370-374), FG-INV-10/16 (App F).

title: Build the transparency layer: MMR, TransparencyCheckpoint, WitnessPolicy, proof scopes
description:
## What & scope
Implement the externally verifiable layer: the global marker MMR, `TransparencyCheckpoint`, `WitnessPolicy`, `TransparencyCrossLogReceipt`, `TransparencyCheckpointValidationRecord`, the three transparency claim grades, feed proof scopes, proof-carrying transfer hooks, authenticated point reads, the `externally_verifiable` format markings with their compatibility law, and the verifier-SDK conformance surface.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6+B5: content addressing, the marker chain hash, and decode proofs make the database auditable by its operator; this layer cashes the same architecture into proofs a party who does NOT trust the server can check — the missing half of the trust story for agent memory, cross-organization branches, and regulated pipelines (§2.4 lists the accumulator as build-it-ourselves). Honest scoping is the differentiator: three distinct claim grades instead of blanket "verifiable" marketing.

## Design — normative detail
**MMR scope.** The MMR commits the globally ordered marker entries with explicit leaf indices and tree size (`MarkerRef` is the transaction-history identity used by MMR leaves, §5.1). Inclusion proves one marker belongs to that committed history; consistency proves append-only extension relative to a previously trusted root. Neither proof establishes semantic correctness of the capsule nor completeness of a filtered query result.

**Three claims, no branch-name leakage.** `LocalRollbackDetection`: one client caches a signed checkpoint and rejects rollback relative to its own last root; says nothing cross-client. `WitnessedEquivocationDetection`: requires authenticated gossip or cross-log receipts; promises detection/evidence after inconsistent heads meet, not prevention. Only `WitnessedNonEquivocation {witness_policy_ref}` may claim split-view prevention. `WitnessPolicy` is content-addressed `{format_version, log_id, security_domain_id, policy_epoch, claim_class:EquivocationDetection|NonEquivocation, ordered_witnesses[{witness_id, key_id, verification_key, endpoint_identity, optional_cross_log_authority}], n, threshold_t, byzantine_bound_f, signature_profile, consistency_proof_profile, durable_head_state_profile, anti_rollback_profile, authenticated_gossip_profile:None|Required{transport_auth_profile, peer_identity_registry, checkpoint_message_schema, replay_window, evidence_retention_floor, maximum_convergence_delay}, activation_log_size, maximum_checkpoint_age, cross_log_policy:None|Required{ordered_authorities, threshold}, rotation:Genesis|JointSuccessor{predecessor_policy_ref}}`. Canonical validation requires exactly `n` unique ordered witnesses, `0 <= f < t <= n`, supported profiles, and — before NonEquivocation is usable — **`2t > n + f`**, so any two signing quorums intersect in more than `f` witnesses. Each honest witness durably stores `{log_id, security_domain_id, policy_oid, last_size, last_root, anti_rollback_counter}` before acknowledging a signature; it signs only a verified append-only consistency extension, never two roots at one size or non-extending histories; rollback or loss of this state disables the witness until an authenticated recovery/rotation procedure — it cannot silently start fresh. A policy rotation checkpoint needs BOTH old and new valid quorums before the new policy activates. If intersection, durable witness state, consistency proofs, or freshness fails, the API downgrades to detection/local scope or fails closed — it never labels later gossip as preventive non-equivocation. Branch identities/heads remain visible only through capability-authorized proofs or explicit metadata declassification; witnesses sign opaque domain commitments without learning branch names. The branch commitment is domain-separated and reveals no plain branch identity/head; mutually hidden branch sets use distinct security-domain logs.

`TransparencyCheckpoint {format_version, mode:LocalRollbackDetection|WitnessedEquivocationDetection{witness_policy_ref}|WitnessedNonEquivocation{witness_policy_ref}, log_size, global_mmr_root, branch_head_commitment_root, security_domain_commitment, previous_checkpoint_digest:WeakDigest, consistency_proof_from_previous, issuance_time_authority_profile_oid, issuance_window:{not_before, expires_at}, operator_key_id, operator_signature, sorted_witness_signatures[{witness_id, key_id, signature}], cross_log_receipt_refs[StrongRef<TransparencyCrossLogReceipt>], rotation_proof:None|JointActivation{old_policy_ref, new_policy_ref, old_sorted_signatures[], new_sorted_signatures[]}}`; every signature covers the domain-separated canonical body excluding all signature arrays; a witnessed mode requires its policy identity, a threshold of distinct configured keys, and any required cross-log receipts; freshness is never inferred from an unprofiled `issued_at` scalar. `TransparencyCrossLogReceipt` is reference-free and signed; its target inclusion leaf is exactly the domain-separated source checkpoint digest plus source log/domain/policy/size/root — causality without comparing clocks from different authorities. Local `TransparencyCheckpointValidationRecord<Role>` binds checkpoint, `TransparencyCheckpointFreshnessBasis {log_id, security_domain_id, witness_policy_oid, checkpoint_body_digest, log_size, claim_class}`, `TimeValidationEvidence`, and sorted cross-log validations (each with `CrossLogTransparencyFreshness` + time evidence); wall time, logical HLC, or raw age calculations are never substitutes. Canonical cross-log validation requires `1 <= cross_log_policy.threshold <= count(unique ordered authorities)`, with at least that many receipts from distinct configured authority/key pairs; every accepted receipt's source policy/log/security-domain/checkpoint-digest/size/root must equal the current checkpoint exactly, its target inclusion proof and target-checkpoint consistency proof must verify under the named target policy/log/size, and both the source checkpoint and each receipt/target checkpoint need independently usable profiled freshness evidence in their own time domains — no validator orders or subtracts instants across domains/epochs; duplicates, foreign source roots, stale evidence, missing target-checkpoint verification, or self-asserted target sizes fail. `JointActivation` additionally requires: the old policy equals the currently active policy; `new.rotation == JointSuccessor{predecessor=old}`; old/new log and security-domain identities are equal; `new.policy_epoch > old.policy_epoch`; the checkpoint mode names the new policy; `log_size >= new.activation_log_size`; and valid distinct-key thresholds under BOTH policies — only after that exact activation checkpoint may successors use the new policy alone.

**Feed proof scopes.** Raw CDC over the global log proves continuity with contiguous leaf/range proofs. A `SUBSCRIBE MATCH` frame can prove membership of its source commits, not complete predicate evaluation. Filtered completeness is claimed only if each commit carries an authenticated, capability-domain-specific delta commitment — including an EMPTY commitment — and the client receives a complete range of those commitments; otherwise the API labels the proof `membership_only`. **Proof-carrying transfer**: backup/replica archives carry object inventories, full digests, `EncodingId`s, key wraps, and decode proofs — proving byte closure and successful decode; restore additionally verifies the canonical logical checkpoint digest before promotion. **Authenticated point reads**: a sealed authorized namespace may expose Merkleized index roots, but a proof covers only the specified key/value and root; absence, range completeness, capability projection, and freshness each require their corresponding proof and watermark.

**Externally verifiable formats.** `TransparencyCheckpoint`, `WitnessPolicy`, the inclusion/consistency-proof encodings, the filtered-changefeed delta-commitment format, and the MMR leaf/checkpoint transcript recipes carry an `externally_verifiable` marking in their G0 format-registry rows, with one registered compatibility law: a third-party verifier pinned to a witness-policy epoch must verify every checkpoint issued within that epoch, and any format transition on a marked surface rides the existing dual-quorum policy rotation — an operator can never force-upgrade external verifiers inside an epoch. The dependency-free verifier SDK — BLAKE3, threshold-signature verification, MMR inclusion/consistency proofs, canonical decoders for exactly the marked formats; a several-KLOC budget — is a registered post-1.0 workstream row with golden-proof conformance vectors in the `CanonicalResultChunkDescriptor` style (§8.8); it reproduces this section's proof-scope labels verbatim (`membership_only`, detection versus prevention), never claims non-equivocation in local-only mode, and doubles as a differential oracle for the proof-producing code under §15.4's independence discipline.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-08 (invariant, restated): authenticated global-history continuity is required; transparency claim grades remain distinct, and non-equivocation requires the declared intersection, durable-witness, rotation, and freshness premises — it is conditional on the declared witnessed-transparency policy and never claimed in local-only mode. Freshness bases are FG-INV-16 window-class artifacts. Witness liveness/convergence delay is a configuration/benchmark claim.

## Interactions
MMR leaves come from w2-commit-protocol's marker chain; signatures/hashes from w1-crypto; format rows + `externally_verifiable` markings from g0-format-arms; claim-grade constitution from g0-claim-registries; freshness windows/time evidence from w9-time-authority. Consumed by w10-cdc (feed proofs), w11-backup/w11-restore (proof-carrying transfer), and — as ecosystem consumers rather than 1.0 build-order dependents — the registered post-1.0 verifier SDK (the independently implemented differential oracle for the proof-producing code under §15.4's independence discipline; its golden-proof conformance vectors are checked-in bytes via w1-format-test-corpora) and cross-org branch-grant recipients (w2-branch-grants, cross-org trust).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Property grid over `(n, t, f)`: `2t > n + f` accepted, boundary and violating configurations rejected at policy validation. Split-view model (FG-INV-08 enforcement): two forked heads against a witness set with `f` Byzantine members — prevention holds iff the policy is valid and witnesses maintain durable state; witness-state rollback disables signing. Rotation: activation without both quorums rejected; each `JointActivation` condition (wrong predecessor, unequal log/security-domain identities, non-increasing policy_epoch, mode naming the old policy, `log_size < activation_log_size`, threshold failure under either policy) independently violated and rejected. Cross-log validation tests: threshold/distinct-authority counting, foreign-source-root and self-asserted-target-size rejection, and a negative asserting no code path orders or subtracts instants across time domains/epochs. Downgrade: stale freshness or missing gossip profile yields detection/local labels, never silent upgrade. Feed labeling: filtered feed without a complete commitment range must be labeled `membership_only` (including the empty-commitment case). Golden proof vectors for inclusion/consistency/cross-log receipts with byte-stable encodings; verifier-SDK conformance harness runs them and differentially checks the producer. Leakage test: witness-visible bytes contain only opaque domain commitments. E2e: client caches a checkpoint, server rolls back, client rejects with logged evidence chain. DETAILED LOGGING (required of implementation and tests): checkpoint issuance logs mode, log_size, global_mmr_root, policy oid/epoch, and each witness signature outcome (witness_id, key_id, accept/reject with reason); validation logs the freshness basis, time-evidence identities, threshold/intersection arithmetic inputs, and every downgrade or fail-closed decision with the exact failed premise; feed-proof labeling logs the claimed scope (`membership_only` versus complete-commitment-range) and the completeness-check result; the split-view, rotation, and leakage suites assert their verdicts from these logs.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: blanket "verifiable" claims without grade separation; freshness from unprofiled scalars; gossip-as-prevention; witness sets without durable anti-rollback state (would sign forks after restart). Risk: witness-operations burden — mitigated by explicit policy schema, rotation with joint quorums, and fail-closed downgrade rather than optimistic labels.

## Provenance
§5.8 (487-498), App A WitnessPolicy/TransparencyCheckpoint rows (~2643-2653), freshness windows (~2163-2165), §2.4, §15.4.

title: Implement the Local txn lifecycle: BEGIN, registration, statements, completion
description:
## What & scope
Implement the durable Local transaction lifecycle command family: `LocalBeginReservationSpec`/`LocalBeginTerminalSpec`, `LocalAttemptRegistrationSpec`, `LocalTxnWorkspaceGeneration`, the statement machine (`LocalStatementIndex`, `LocalStatementRegistrationSpec`, `LocalStatementPublicationSpec`, `LocalStatementAbortSpec`), `LocalReadCloseSpec`, `LocalTerminalCompletionSpec`, and the fixed construction DAG. Prepare/terminal fencing is w2-prepare-terminal; token/outcome indexes are w2-outcome-tokens; the fused arm is w2-fused-autocommit.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6 (agent-native): agents crash, retry, and race themselves; every lifecycle step is a durable idempotent CAS so an exact retry joins the original state and drift fails closed — no "did my BEGIN happen?" ambiguity. B5: lifecycle state is evidence (typed records, frontiers, proofs), not coordinator RAM. Honest cost: a durable autocommit read is exactly three sequenced semantic commands — `LocalAttemptRegistrationSpec::Autocommit`, `LocalReadCloseSpec`, `LocalTerminalCompletionSpec` (~6–10 Raft entries) — because read-close semantic success waits for terminal completion and no terminal result returns before `TerminalReady`; this is a registered Appendix G row, and `SnapshotQuery` (w10) exists precisely to give reads a 0-command class.

## Design — normative detail
**BEGIN.** A BEGIN first orders `LocalBeginReservationSpec {authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>,canonical_begin_request_digest,operation_class:ReadOnly|ReadWrite,isolation_profile,transaction_error_policy,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>,scoped_begin_idempotency_key,expected_index_absence:WeakAbsenceProof,staging_resource_reservation_ref,operation_audit_admission:PendingUnclaimed|NotRequired,terminal_audit_gate:LifecycleScaffoldingNotRequired}`. The header is the sole namespace/incarnation/service/tenant/principal/ceiling/policy/revocation source and byte-matches the replay object, resource reservation, and audit admission. Apply constructs `LocalBeginReservationRecord {header,source_spec_ref,applied_control_ref,canonical_begin_request_digest,txn_token,capability_replay_ref,capability_commitment,reserved_at_logical_command_seq,staging_generation}`, installs Reserved, constructs `TxnOutcomeRecord::BeginStaging`; `BEGIN_ACCEPTED` is exposed only after Reserved plus BeginStaging are visible. Byte-identical retry returns the same identities. `LocalBeginTerminalSpec {reservation_ref,internal_reason_class,no_registration_or_effect_proof_ref,public_projection_bundle_ref,terminal_audit_gate}` alone consumes Reserved and creates `LocalNeverRegisteredRecord` plus the NeverRegisteredDetailed index arm; deterministic apply invents no reason mapping/receipt/handle/response bytes; timeout, disconnect, or memory loss alone is never terminal evidence; a terminal begin key can never later bind. The spec derives txn_token/capability commitment from the decoded replay object (request_kind ExplicitBegin, exact request/domain/authority/profile/window equality); no duplicate inline capability encoding is trusted.

**Registration.** `LocalAttemptRegistrationSpec` has the closed binding `ExplicitBegin{reservation_ref,expected_index_value:Reserved,capability_replay_ref}|Autocommit{autocommit_idempotency_key,canonical_request_digest,classification_ref:StrongRef<CanonicalStatementClassification>,expected_absence_proof,capability_replay_ref}` plus common `{authority_bound_header,authority_permit_ref,requested_snapshot_bounds,txn_operation_ceiling,transaction_error_policy,initial_workspace_recipe,operation_audit_admission,terminal_audit_gate}`. Apply verifies header/permit/replay/reservation/audit admission/snapshot/ceiling name one complete Local binding, checks any autocommit classification against the ceiling, atomically claims the operation ticket when required, moves Reserved -> BoundDetailed (or creates the autocommit BoundDetailed lineage), constructs `LocalAttemptRegistration {…,request_kind:ExplicitBegin|AutocommitExecute,txn_token,registered_snapshot,operation_audit_admission:Claimed|NotRequired,registered_at_logical_command_seq}`, then workspace generation zero, then `TxnOutcomeRecord::Registered`. A Local token has exactly one attempt (no attempt-family generation); autocommit uses `LocalAttemptRegistrationSpec::Autocommit` and the same lifecycle without emitting BEGIN frames. No statement/storage observation may precede visible registration — the sole registered amendment is the fused autocommit-write arm (w2-fused-autocommit). Exact lost-EXECUTE retry returns the same registration/classification/outcome capability; body or authority drift fails.

**Workspace & statements.** `LocalTxnWorkspaceGeneration {header,registration_ref,authority_relation_to_registration:Exact|Narrowed{nonwidening_proof_ref},workspace_generation,predecessor_ref?,through_statement_seq,statement_registration_ref?,published_intent_batch_ref?,overlay_root_ref,cumulative_effect_root_ref,cumulative_read_witness_root_ref,cumulative_mutation_potential,branch_key_epoch_commitment}`; generation zero holds the registration's exact header, canonical empty overlay, ProvenReadOnly potential; every successor carries the same or a proved-narrower binding — a policy/revocation/service/principal/purpose/ceiling change without the registered nonwidening proof aborts before observation. `LocalStatementIndex` maps `(registration_identity,statement_seq)` and scoped idempotency key to exactly one of `Open{registration_ref}|Published{publication_applied_ref,workspace_generation_ref,output}|Failed{abort_applied_ref,stable_failure_class}|Abandoned{abort_applied_ref,typed_reason}`. `LocalStatementRegistrationSpec` binds exact_next_statement_seq, statement idempotency key, classification ref+digest, canonical statement/parameter digests, requested result answer contract, expected prior statement frontier, expected workspace generation, optional nonwidening proof, error policy, statement audit admission; apply requires no Open statement, claims the statement ticket when required, constructs `LocalStatementRegistration`, inserts Open; exact retry joins, any drift fails. `LocalStatementPublicationSpec` (statement+attempt refs, expected Open, claimed audit admission, read access admission + read result release decision refs, `LocalSerializationCertificate` ref, expected prior/successor workspace generations, successor witness/effect roots, `published_output`, expected frontiers, terminal audit gate) atomically changes Open -> Published, advances statement/workspace/delivery frontiers, and constructs the succeeding `TxnOutcomeRecord::Registered`. `LocalStatementPublishedOutput` is `NoResult{no_result_proof_ref,terminal_delivery_frontier_digest}|Buffered{manifest_ref,canonical_result_digest,delivery_policy_ref,inline_activation_recipe?}` — the recipe is legal only when this apply is provably the next gap-free visible candidate and the gate is NotRequired. Buffered apply creates the applied publication reference, resource transfer, independent-retention record (`PendingVisibility` unless a legal inline activation creates `ActiveDeliverable`). `LocalStatementAbortSpec` alone changes Open -> Failed|Abandoned, resolves the statement ticket, proves no result/workspace effect, releases named resources, advances its no-result terminal frontier, and applies the registration-pinned `ContinueAttempt|AbortAttempt` policy. Every statement is durably Open before execution and terminally Published/Failed/Abandoned; successful statements advance one predecessor-linked workspace generation; result bytes remain spill-backed under a nonexpiring `PendingVisibility` hold. The gap-free audit-visibility transition changes that owner only to `ReleasedAwaitingActivation`; a distinct fresh `ProtectedOutputActivationSpec` later creates the first delivery time basis, lease, and capability.

**Read close & completion.** `LocalReadCloseSpec {registration_ref,operation_audit_admission,mode:AutocommitResult{read_access_admission_ref,read_result_release_decision_ref,buffered_result_manifest_ref,canonical_result_digest,result_answer_contract,delivery_policy_ref,inline_activation_recipe?}|ExplicitClose{expected_statement_frontier,expected_delivery_detachment_frontier,result_disposition_proof_refs[],complete_publication_chain_digest,workspace_generation_ref,cumulative_read_witness_root_ref,zero_cumulative_write_effect_proof_ref,no_open_statement_proof_ref},local_serialization_certificate_ref,expected_conflict_index_basis,terminal_audit_gate}` advances LogicalCommandSeq/HLC but not CommitSeq, creates ReadClosed, atomically detaches autocommit results under the pending/released/inline-active rule, and never waits for activation or client ACK. `LocalTerminalCompletionSpec {pending_outcome_ref,semantic_outcome,terminal_public_projection_bundle_ref,prebuilt_read_your_writes_issuance_ref:None|Some,expected_required_postcondition_bitmap,observed_satisfied_postcondition_bitmap,configured_durability_evidence_ref,local_delta_frontier_evidence_ref,result_disposition:NoTerminalResult|ReadTerminalResult{delivery_disposition_proof_ref}|AutocommitWriteReturning{preparation_ref,required_posture:Local,inline_activation_recipe?},resource_release_refs[],audit_visibility_evidence_ref,expected_conflict_overlap_floor,terminal_audit_gate}` monotonically adds verified bits, validates (never manufactures) frozen public/capability artifacts, creates `TerminalReady` only when the required bitmap is exactly satisfied, cannot alter the semantic outcome, and accepts its delta postcondition only when the visible payload's index contains the exact marker/batch and its frontier is at least the commit sequence. Fixed construction DAG: registration -> workspace zero -> outcome; statement successor workspace and manifest -> publication spec/command -> applied publication/detachment/outcome -> payload/record/root; prepare-admission -> … -> completion (w2-prepare-terminal); no input names its future applied record, payload, command record, root, lease, marker, or summary leaf.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-01 (at most one immutable terminal outcome per scoped key/token; matching retries return the recorded lineage; NeverRegistered creates no family/generation/burn; TerminalReady only after exact postcondition bitmap/audit visibility/result detachment). FG-INV-07 (registered order: begin reservation -> claimed registration/workspace zero -> claimed statement -> …; pre-order inputs exclude future records). FG-INV-20 (authorization precedes every observation; registration claims tickets before observation). The 3-command read / command-count facts are Appendix G structural counts; latency budgets are `slo.toml` rows.

## Interactions
Orders through w2-order-raft via w2-hlc-order-attempt supplements; commits via w2-commit-protocol; prepare/terminal fencing in w2-prepare-terminal; tokens/outcomes in w2-outcome-tokens; classifications from w5-binder (schema registered at G0 so W2 can proceed with fixtures); result delivery machinery consumed by w10-result-machines; audit gating by w9-audit-pipeline/w9-activation-batching; witnesses by w4-ssi-witnesses.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
CAS model tests for begin/registration/statement/outcome (lost response, concurrent identical/conflicting retries, terminal-begin-key-never-binds). Property: workspace generation monotonicity + nonwidening enforcement; statement frontier contiguity; exactly-one-Open. Crash matrix at every command boundary (BEGIN accepted vs invisible; Open statement orphaned then aborted; publication applied but completion pending). Negative fixtures: authority drift, ceiling violation, wrong predecessor, duplicate statement seq. E2E script: explicit multi-statement txn (5+N commands per App G row) with structured logs asserting each durable state transition and frontier advance; autocommit read asserting exactly 3 sequenced semantic commands in the log. Oracle: FG-INV-20 pre-observation type matrix; status-equivalence between detailed and replayed responses.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risk: lifecycle chattiness for tiny reads — answered by `SnapshotQuery` (0 commands) and the fused write arm, not by weakening durability of the durable classes. Rejected: coordinator-RAM transaction state with best-effort recovery (loses idempotency evidence); rejected: BEGIN as a no-op until first write (agents cannot distinguish lost BEGIN from rejection); rejected: out-of-band cancellation flags (must be `TxnAbortSpec`, w2-prepare-terminal).

## Provenance
Plan §5.2 l.403, App A l.1478–1484, l.1496, l.1526–1528, l.1534; App G l.3178/3180/3193; App F FG-INV-01/07/20.
design:
## Authoritative post-decomposition contract delta (d96bf0f)

The exact Local BEGIN/autocommit ReadYourWrites validation basis below is part of this implementation unit and must be retained from reservation through registration/read close.

`LocalBeginIdempotencyIndex` maps `(database_security_namespace_id,cluster_incarnation,tenant,principal,scoped_begin_idempotency_key)` to exactly `Reserved{reservation_ref:StrongRef<LocalBeginReservationRecord>,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>}|BoundDetailed{registration_ref:StrongRef<LocalAttemptRegistration>,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>}|BoundCompacted{summary_root_ref:StrongRef<LocalTxnOutcomeSummaryRoot>,leaf_key_digest,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>}|NeverRegisteredDetailed{terminal_ref:StrongRef<LocalNeverRegisteredRecord>,public_projection_bundle_ref:StrongRef<NeverRegisteredPublicProjectionBundle<Local>>,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>}|NeverRegisteredCompacted{summary_root_ref:StrongRef<LocalTxnOutcomeSummaryRoot>,leaf_key_digest,public_projection_bundle_ref:StrongRef<NeverRegisteredPublicProjectionBundle<Local>>,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>}|ExpiredTombstone{scoped_key_digest,txn_token_digest,capability_commitment,expiry_evidence_digest}`. `LocalBeginReservationSpec` is `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>,canonical_begin_request_digest,operation_class:ReadOnly|ReadWrite,isolation_profile,transaction_error_policy,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>,read_your_writes_basis:None|Validated{validation_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence>,requested_floor_subset_digest,capability_floor_set_commitment},scoped_begin_idempotency_key,expected_index_absence:WeakAbsenceProof,staging_resource_reservation_ref:StrongRef<ResourceLedgerTransition>,operation_audit_admission:LocalOperationAuditAdmission::PendingUnclaimed|NotRequired,terminal_audit_gate:LifecycleScaffoldingNotRequired}`. The validated arm is required exactly when BEGIN presents a ReadYourWrites capability and must select the `ReadYourWritesBeginAdmission` Local row before any observation. The header is the sole namespace/incarnation/service/tenant/principal/ceiling/policy/revocation source and byte-matches the replay object, RYW basis, resource reservation, and audit admission. Apply constructs `LocalBeginReservationRecord {authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>,source_spec_ref:StrongRef<LocalBeginReservationSpec>,applied_control_ref:AppliedControlRef,canonical_begin_request_digest,txn_token,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>,capability_commitment,read_your_writes_basis,reserved_at_logical_command_seq,staging_generation}`, installs Reserved with the replay ref, and constructs `TxnOutcomeRecord::BeginStaging`; only that visible state permits BEGIN_ACCEPTED. Byte-identical retry returns the same identities. `LocalBeginTerminalSpec {reservation_ref,internal_reason_class,no_registration_or_effect_proof_ref,public_projection_bundle_ref:StrongRef<NeverRegisteredPublicProjectionBundle<Local>>,terminal_audit_gate}` alone consumes Reserved and creates `LocalNeverRegisteredRecord {reservation_ref,internal_reason_class,no_registration_or_effect_proof_ref,public_projection_bundle_ref,terminal_audit_gate,applied_control_ref}` plus NeverRegisteredDetailed. The bundle's internal subject/reason/request/domain byte-match the spec; deterministic apply invents no reason mapping, receipt, handle, or response bytes. A required ticket resolves directly from PendingUnclaimed with `AuditResolutionOrigin::Unclaimed`. Timeout, disconnect, or memory loss alone is not terminal evidence, and a terminal begin key can never later bind. The spec/record decode the replay object, require request_kind ExplicitBegin and exact request/domain/authority/profile/window equality, and derive txn_token/capability commitment from it; no duplicate inline capability encoding is trusted.
`LocalAttemptRegistrationSpec` has the closed binding `ExplicitBegin{reservation_ref:StrongRef<LocalBeginReservationRecord>,expected_index_value:Reserved,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>,read_your_writes_basis_from_reservation}|Autocommit{autocommit_idempotency_key,canonical_request_digest,classification_ref:StrongRef<CanonicalStatementClassification>,expected_absence_proof:WeakAbsenceProof,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>,read_your_writes_basis:None|Validated{validation_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence>,requested_floor_subset_digest,capability_floor_set_commitment}}` plus `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>,authority_permit_ref:AuthorityPermitRef<Local>,requested_snapshot_bounds,txn_operation_ceiling:TxnOperationCeiling,transaction_error_policy,initial_workspace_recipe,operation_audit_admission:LocalOperationAuditAdmission::PendingUnclaimed|NotRequired,terminal_audit_gate:LifecycleScaffoldingNotRequired}`. The ExplicitBegin basis must byte-equal the reservation field; an Autocommit validated basis selects `ReadYourWritesExecuteAdmission` before observation. Apply verifies the header, permit, replay object, begin reservation, RYW basis, audit admission, snapshot, and ceiling all name one complete Local binding; verifies any autocommit classification is within the ceiling; atomically claims the operation ticket when required; changes explicit Reserved -> BoundDetailed or creates the autocommit BoundDetailed lineage under the scoped client key; and constructs `LocalAttemptRegistration {authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Local>,source_spec_ref,applied_control_ref,reservation_ref?,capability_replay_ref:StrongRef<TxnOutcomeCapabilityReplayRecord>,read_your_writes_basis,request_kind:ExplicitBegin|AutocommitExecute,txn_token,txn_operation_ceiling,autocommit_classification_ref?,registered_snapshot,authority_permit_ref,transaction_error_policy,operation_audit_admission:LocalOperationAuditAdmission::Claimed|NotRequired,registered_at_logical_command_seq}` followed by workspace generation zero and the succeeding `TxnOutcomeRecord::Registered`. A Local token has exactly one attempt; there is no Local attempt-family generation. No statement/storage observation may precede visible registration, with exactly one registered amendment: the fused single-statement autocommit write arm `LocalAutocommitWriteSpec` (§5.2), whose coordinator-local permit verification and admission precede every observation (FG-INV-20 preserved) while durable registration lands atomically with the commit in one sequenced semantic command carrying registration, prepare admission, the ordered final-certification reservation, and commit semantics. The amendment is scoped to exactly that arm and no other: a pre-order crash leaves no durable record, an exact retry re-executes from scratch, and the autocommit idempotency-key CAS at apply guarantees at-most-once durable effect. Both arms decode and byte-match the replay record; ExplicitBegin must match the reservation's same ref, while Autocommit requires request_kind AutocommitExecute and stores the scoped client key and classification before work. Exact lost EXECUTE retry returns the same registration/classification/outcome capability; body or authority drift fails.

title: Implement WriterTakeoverProtocol: lease→recover→fence-root→enable, and CreateNew
description:
## What & scope
Implement the normative `WriterTakeoverProtocol`, the separate `CreateNew` fresh-creation transition, the linear guards `PendingFenceGuard`/`PendingCreationGuard`, the nonconstructible `FenceToken`, and fence checks on every irreversible step. Receipt headers and history adoption live in sibling subtask `w2-takeover-adoption`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1 requires exactly one writer whose authority is provable at every irreversible step: a stale process that lost its lease must be unable to seal, receipt, acknowledge Raft, or publish — even microseconds after losing it. Fence-root-before-enable makes takeover itself a published, ordered event, so recovery and receipts are always attributable to an epoch. There is deliberately no timeout or administrative force path around either lease or sequencer (B5: no unproven liveness shortcuts).

## Design — normative detail
Takeover steps (normative): (1) open the database directory and `manifest.root` without symlink traversal, record mount/device/inode identity, acquire the nonblocking exclusive lease on that exact open inode; (2) create the sole `RootPublicationSequencer` for that leased inode, re-resolve the path, reject replacement or identity drift; (3) under the lease, authenticate the highest structurally credible slot and mandatory closure, recover Raft/audit-visibility-pipeline/restore state, reconcile every prepared owner; (4) validate the slot's `IncarnationContinuityProfile`: `DirectoryBound` requires the original directory/inode continuity and forbids a restore bridge; `ExternalCas` fetches the exact current continuity head, byte-matches namespace/incarnation/CAS/visibility state, and acquires a member-bound lease with `OrdinaryWrite` or narrowly `RecoveryOnly` scope; (5) compute `new_epoch = 1 + max(epoch values in the selected slot and its authenticated reachable RootManifest/seals/prepared records)` with checked overflow — unrooted staging cannot raise the fence; (6) mint a linear, nonexportable `PendingFenceGuard { lease, publication_sequencer, stable_identity, old_epoch, new_epoch, exact_recovered_root, continuity_head_and_incarnation_guard }` whose sole effects are building/sealing this fence-only successor and requesting the exact `FenceTakeover` publication permit; (7) persist a successor `RootManifest` preserving the same canonical logical root and every receipted/ordered obligation, publish/sync the inactive slot at `new_epoch`, reread/authenticate that exact slot, revalidate continuity; only then (8) consume the guard into the ordinary nonconstructible combined writer/incarnation token in `CommitCx` (or recovery-only token) and enable only the effects that scope allows. The pending guard cannot create user data, issue a receipt, acknowledge/propose ordinary Raft, alter canonical state, or publish any other root. A crashed old owner may leave immutable staging bytes; its already receipted/ordered ownership remains live and is adopted by recovery, but it may not issue a new receipt or publish after either epoch changes. A stale/later/unavailable external continuity head makes the database read-only.

The takeover checker accepts only `NoGuard -> LeaseHeld(identity) -> ClosureRecovered(old_epoch) -> PendingFenceGuard(old_epoch+1) -> FenceRootDurableAndReread(old_epoch+1) -> WriterEnabled(FenceToken)`. Creation is `NoGuard -> StagingInodeLease -> PendingCreationGuard(epoch=1) -> CompleteStagingRootVerified -> RenameNoReplaceAndDirectorySync -> CanonicalRootReread -> WriterEnabled`. **CreateNew**: open directory without symlinks, create a uniquely named staging root inode with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL`, acquire its whole-inode lease, receive a `PendingCreationGuard` limited to constructing the complete Genesis closure and valid epoch-1 slot; fully write+sync staging, verify in place, atomically promote via same-directory `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)` (or registered equivalent), sync the parent directory, re-resolve and verify `manifest.root` is the same leased inode, reread/authenticate, then consume the guard. A racing loser never truncates or adopts the winner's file; its staging inode remains unreachable, eligible only for generation/name-scoped recovery cleanup. Crash before promotion leaves no canonical `manifest.root`; after directory sync, a complete valid one. There is no empty/partial canonical tomb and no "empty file means ours" state.

`FenceToken` is nonserializable and nonconstructible outside the VFS/commit boundary; it binds the live lease handle, stable directory/root identity, profile, slot generation, and epoch. Every ordinary segment/object/root seal, immutable-root build, prepared-root publication, `PayloadReceipt`, Raft proposal or follower acknowledgement, checkpoint/certificate publication, and RootSlot write compares the local FenceToken against the live inode lease and published epoch immediately before its irreversible step; under `ExternalCas` it also revalidates the exact external continuity head/CAS and a live member-bound `ClusterIncarnationLease` with required scope; under `DirectoryBound` the guard proves the unchanged creation directory/inode and cannot authorize cross-directory same-identity recovery. Losing a lease, a higher epoch/incarnation/CAS, expired external authority, or path/inode/profile/visibility drift poisons the guard and fails closed. Local fence epoch is excluded from canonical capsule/marker/state-root bytes (cluster incarnation and service visibility are canonical), so replicas agree. Every immutable segment trailer records `{ database_security_namespace_id, cluster_incarnation, local_writer_fence_epoch, segment_id, sealed_len, inventory_digest, trailer_checksum }`; after promotion the local VFS refuses a seal, prepared-root update, receipt signature, Raft acknowledgement/proposal, or root publication without the matching live token. Read-only multi-process opens remain supported.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-10 (verbatim clause): before the ordinary token, only the typed takeover, fresh-creation, or guarded restore publication may occur; every irreversible seal, receipt, Raft action, certificate, and slot write rechecks both authorities. Pending-guard type restrictions are compile-time capability boundaries (B5), not review conventions.

## Interactions
Consumes `w2-root-bootstrap`/`w2-root-publication` (slot authentication, `FenceTakeover` permit), `w2-filesystem-profiles` (lease primitive, owner-death, rename rules), `w2-continuity-profiles` (step-4 validation), `g0-command-contracts` (publication-class rows). Produces the `FenceToken`/`CommitCx` guard for `w2-commit-protocol`, `w2-order-raft`, `w2-group-commit`, `w2-gc-core`, and w3/w4; adoption completed by `w2-takeover-adoption`, consumed by `w2-recovery`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Type-level: pending guards implement no user-segment/prepared-owner/receipt/Raft/canonical-transition/general-root traits (compile-fail tests); FenceToken nonconstructible outside the boundary. Crash matrix (App A rows, verbatim): cut after every lease/identity/recovery/object-sync/slot-write/slot-sync/staging-rename/directory-sync/reread step; owner death; path replacement; mount drift; stale descriptors; epoch overflow; competing creators; orphan staging; lying-sync profile rejected. Property: `new_epoch` ignores unrooted staging; the fence-only root preserves the canonical logical root, Raft/audit candidate, prepared root, and durable/applied/visible positions byte-for-byte. Multiprocess: a second process attempting publication after lease loss is refused at every irreversible operation; old-epoch receipted obligations remain adoptable while new old-epoch receipts are refused. E2E: 100+ kill -9/takeover cycles logging the epoch chain and every refused stale operation.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: timeout-based takeover (split-brain under pause/partition); administrative force flag (unfenceable); lockfile-content fencing instead of a published root epoch (invisible to recovery/receipts); receipt-issuing pending guards. Risk: step-5 epoch-scan cost — bounded by closure size, measured in recovery benches.

## Provenance
§5.1 (364, 376-378), App A (1443), FG-INV-10 (App F).

title: Build the extent-based buffer manager, ScratchStore, and query memory discipline
description:
## What & scope
Build §6.7: the extent-based buffer manager over variable-size segments with pointer swizzling, optimistic epoch-protected reads, the shared admission/eviction policy trait (ARC and an S3-FIFO-style design) with ghost shadow evaluation, io_uring/O_DIRECT I/O with executor-planned readahead, region-heap query memory, the non-authoritative `ScratchStore` spill domain, admission bounds with structured `ResourceExhausted`, and NUMA affinity.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Umbra's lesson: variable-size segments beat fixed pages for graph-shaped objects (runs and chunks are inherently variable). LeanStore's OLC discipline: no reader latches on scan-heavy workloads. frankensqlite's ARC/MVCC-aware pool, padded sharded tables, aligned direct-I/O buffers, and prefetch-on-descent form the mechanical-sympathy checklist (§2.3). B2's scan economics need declared-intent prefetch of segment chains; B3's morsel executor needs region-scoped memory so a query *is* an asupersync region and cancellation drains morsels and frees its heap deterministically; B5 needs `ScratchStore` provably outside the durability/FEC domain so spill can never masquerade as authoritative bytes — §5.7's tiered-FEC law leans on exactly this pre-scoped boundary.

## Design — normative detail
**Buffer**: an extent-based buffer manager over variable-size segments; segment handles are swizzlable — hot segments pin to direct pointers, cold segments fault through the manager. Reads use optimistic epoch-protected access (asupersync EBR): version-stamped, retry-on-conflict, no reader latches (LeanStore OLC discipline). **Admission/eviction**: ARC and an S3-FIFO-style design share one policy trait and may be ghost-evaluated in shadow. A snapshot protects object generations from GC; only an active `BufferHandle` pins a frame in RAM — frames needed later by the same snapshot may be evicted and faulted back. Ghost metadata is cleaned when object generations become unreachable, and scans use admission bypass/resistance. **I/O**: io_uring via asupersync fs; O_DIRECT with page-aligned buffers; readahead is planned by the executor — runs declare their scan intent and the buffer manager prefetches segment chains (B-tree-descent prefetch generalized). **Query memory and scratch**: every query's resident scratch uses its region heap. Spill uses a separate `ScratchStore`: region-scoped, non-authoritative, non-fsynced, NOT RaptorQ-coded, outside the database manifest, and keyed by a startup-cleanable generation; region close unlinks only its own proven scratch objects. Admission bounds all database-accounted allocations and preserves an emergency reserve; allocation failure, or an operator whose minimum resident set cannot fit, returns structured `ResourceExhausted` with no partial success unless the query explicitly requested truncation. The plan claims no immunity from host overcommit, allocator failure, or unaccounted foundation defects. **NUMA**: partition-to-socket affinity for pinned segments; the morsel scheduler prefers local partitions.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-16 (excerpt): no structured task, pin, scratch object, or lease is lost, duplicated, refunded, released, or exposed while obligated; under declared fairness, every obligation reaches one legal terminal or recoverable state — `BufferHandle` pins and scratch-unlink obligations are direct instances, checked by the asupersync leak/quiescence oracle. FG-INV-14 (excerpt): GC follows every generated strong edge; a snapshot protecting object generations is a root until release — the buffer manager must never be the thing keeping bytes alive. Claim classes: hit-rate/fault-latency numbers are benchmark class; eviction-policy promotion evidence via the shared trait's shadow evaluation is `FG-CAL-01`; controller/settings stability is `FG-CFG-02`.

## Interactions
Consumes filesystem profiles, sync semantics, and doctor probes from `w2-filesystem-profiles`; snapshot/generation pinning from `w2-snapshots-leases`; core types and region/EBR plumbing from `w1-foundation-types`. Produces: fault/pin services for `w3-tier-d`, `w3-tier-r`, `w3-properties` reads and `w3-seal-compact` merges; the scan-intent prefetch API consumed by `w5-executor`; `ScratchStore` consumed by `w5-executor` spill and `w8-materialization`; the `ResourceExhausted` surface consumed by `w10-qos` admission.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
OLC correctness: concurrent mutate/read property tests under `fgdb-sim` DPOR — no torn reads, bounded retry counts. Evict/refault: a snapshot-held generation is evicted and faulted back byte-identical; ghost metadata is cleaned exactly when generations become unreachable (leak oracle). Policy trait: ARC and S3-FIFO pass one shared conformance suite; ghost shadow evaluation emits FG-CAL-01-complete comparison logs. Scan-pollution test: a full-partition scan under admission bypass keeps hot-set hit rate within budget. Crash: `ScratchStore` generations from a dead process are startup-cleaned; a structural CI check proves nothing inside the database manifest references scratch paths. `ResourceExhausted`: memory-capped runs return the structured error with zero partial results unless truncation was requested; the emergency reserve is never breached (log assertion). NUMA: locality counters reported on the reference machine. Bench: fault-path latency distributions and readahead effectiveness, with flamegraph artifacts on regression. E2e script: start a database, run a mixed scan+point workload sized above RAM so faults, evictions, and readahead all engage; spill one query through ScratchStore; kill the process mid-query; restart and verify startup scratch cleaning plus byte-identical refaults of snapshot-held generations. Detailed logging (mandatory, asserted by the tests): segment fault/evict events log {segment_id, object_generation, policy, latency_us}; pin lifecycle logs {buffer_handle_id, acquire|release, owner}; policy shadow evaluation logs paired {policy, hit, ghost_hit} records per access class; ScratchStore lifecycle logs {scratch_generation, create|unlink, owning_region}; every ResourceExhausted logs {query_id, requested_bytes, accounted_bytes, emergency_reserve_intact}; readahead logs {declared_intent, segments_prefetched, prefetch_hits} so effectiveness is reconstructible from the event stream.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: fixed-size page pool (graph segments are variable-size); reader latches (scan-hostile); fsynced or FEC-coded spill (would drag scratch into the durability domain and the repair budget); relying on the OS page cache (O_DIRECT plus planned readahead instead). Risks: swizzle/eviction races (epoch protocol + DPOR coverage); io_uring behavior variance across kernels (delegated to `w2-filesystem-profiles` probes).

## Provenance
§6.7; §2.1 (asupersync fs/EBR/regions); §2.3 (frankensqlite buffer lessons); §5.7 (ScratchStore outside the coded domain); §3 (Umbra/LeanStore lessons).

title: Build Tier-D/sealed-run bulk staging for the §7.5 load paths
description:
## What & scope
Build Strata's bulk-load staging: direct sealed-run construction from canonical bulk batches, optional staged-run accelerators for online load, the effect-equivalence acceptance rule, offline fenced direct construction, and Tier-D staging integration. This is the storage half of §7.5's bulk paths — the transaction/manifest/registry machinery is `w4-bulk-ddl`, which depends on this bead (not vice versa).

## Why (bets, market, goals)
The §17 cold-bulk-load gate — >=40M edges/s sustained, I/O-bound at >=60% of the NVMe sequential-write ceiling — is unreachable through the transactional Tier-D path; it requires building sorted sealed runs directly from parsed input. But B1/B5 forbid a second semantics: §7.5's rule is that **physical runs are optional accelerators and can never define an effect** — only the `CanonicalBulkLoadManifest`'s logical commitments are truth. This bead supplies the run construction and equivalence machinery that makes bulk fast without a bulk side-door. `fnx-readwrite`'s fuzz-hardened parsers (edgelist, adjlist, GraphML, GML, JSON node-link, Pajek, GEXF) feed the sealed-run builder directly (§2.2), serving agent-native ingestion (B6).

## Design — normative detail
**Builder**: consumes `CanonicalBulkLogicalBatch` content (referenced by `BulkSourceChunkManifest.canonical_logical_batch_ref: StrongRef<CanonicalBulkLogicalBatch>`) and produces sorted `AdjRunSegment`s, property chunks, and directory/ordinal segments per `(partition, edge_type, direction)`, with identity columns under the registered codec and `canonical_stable_id_digest` computed over decoded stable IDs. Staged runs appear only as `optional_staged_run_refs[]` on chunk manifests — bounded, content-addressed, non-authoritative. **Acceptance rule (normative)**: at finalization, staged runs are selected only when their **effect-equivalence proof and apply basis match** the committed net effect; otherwise ordinary Strata construction regenerates them — a stale or drifted staged run is discarded, never patched. **Online load**: pins one registered snapshot, ingests bounded chunks, builds optional sealed runs, and continuously catches up the exact self-contained delta stream from the pin through a declared watermark (catch-up applies deltas through ordinary Tier-D machinery). **Offline fenced load**: legal only with `OfflineBulkEpochFence { coordinate, expected_empty_graph_and_branch_root, expected_schema_root, exclusive_graph_epoch, zero_active_snapshot_txn_subscription_or_derived_consumer_proof, writer_fence_and_configuration, resource_and_audit_owner }` durably installed before parsing; the fence merely permits direct construction of initial sealed runs — finalization still flows through an ordinary transaction/marker and all constraints, and any nonempty/current-head drift rejects publication. **Recovery** resumes the exact request or drives explicit abort — it never infers success from run bytes; abort carries a staging disposition and staged bytes are unreachable-and-disposable under proved recovery rules. **Commitments**: each chunk's gap-free ordinal, source byte range, source digest, per-row original source-row digests (§7.5: each row has its original source-row digest), `row_count`, and `logical_effect_digest`, plus the manifest's deterministic Merkle root, are the truth the builder must reproduce exactly.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-18 (excerpt, binding): bulk ingestion commits only canonical logical batches through ordinary transactions, and optional staged runs can be discarded without changing exact answers or authorization; index/build controls remain invisible until a transactional SchemaOp activates a validated generation. FG-INV-12 (excerpt): staged-run selection is a claimed answer-equivalence and must be proof/digest-backed. FG-INV-11 (excerpt): identities in bulk-built runs obey the allocator/lease law — no bulk path mints identity outside `IdRangeLease` ranges, and no epoch/range pair is reused. The 40M edges/s figure is a benchmark-class §17 gate under a pinned manifest, never a format truth.

## Interactions
Consumes run/segment builders and formats from `w3-tier-r`; the Tier-D staging/publication barrier from `w3-tier-d`; identity codecs from `w3-identity-encoding`; canonical delta/effect digest definitions from `w2-delta-batches`; content addressing from `w2-object-identity`; spill via `w3-buffer`'s `ScratchStore` for giant-partition sorts. Produces: the staging surface that `w4-bulk-ddl`'s `BulkLoadRegistry` state machine (`Reserved -> Ingesting -> Sealed -> CommitPrepared -> Committed | Aborted`) drives; the parser feed target for `w10-formats` readers; the workload for `perf-bench-core`'s cold-load gate.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Equivalence differential: for randomized corpora, the staged-run path and ordinary-construction path produce identical logical digests and identical decoded adjacency/property scan results (no query surface exists in this bead's dependency closure; the query-answer form of the same equivalence re-runs at `w4-bulk-ddl` and epic-w3 closure once Loom lands). Drift negative: mutating one row after staging causes an apply-basis/effect-proof mismatch — the staged run is rejected and regenerated, with a typed rejection logged. Determinism: the same chunk set yields byte-identical Merkle roots and digest sets across runs and processes. Crash rows (the Strata slice of §7.5's matrix): cut at every chunk boundary, at seal, during tail catch-up, and at physical-run rejection; recovery never treats orphan run bytes as state; ENOSPC during run build yields a typed failure with disposable staging. Fenced-load negatives: a nonempty graph or schema-root drift rejects publication; ordered abort provably releases the fence. Bench: cold CSV/Parquet-lite to sealed runs at >=40M edges/s on the pinned reference manifest, with I/O-utilization and per-stage byte breakdowns logged and flamegraph artifacts on regression. E2e script: parse a named fnx-readwrite corpus into chunk manifests; build optional staged runs; mutate one staged run's source row to force the drift-rejection/regeneration path; finalize through the ordinary transaction; then run the offline fenced variant on an empty graph and verify both loads produce identical logical digests and identical decoded adjacency/property scan results versus a pure-Tier-D-path load of the same corpus (the query-answer form of this comparison re-runs at `w4-bulk-ddl` once Loom lands). Detailed logging (mandatory, asserted by the tests): every chunk logs {load_id, chunk_ordinal, source_byte_range, source_digest, row_count, logical_effect_digest}; staged-run acceptance logs {run_ref, effect_equivalence_proof_digest, apply_basis, accepted|rejected(typed_reason)}; fence lifecycle logs {coordinate, install|consume|release, drift_check_result}; catch-up logs {pinned_snapshot, watermark, deltas_applied}; recovery logs {resumed|aborted, staging_disposition, orphan_bytes_discarded} so the no-side-door property is verifiable from logs alone.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: bulk side-door semantics (run bytes defining effects); in-place ingest into published tiers; patching drifted staged runs (regeneration is the rule); trusting recovery to run bytes. Risks: catch-up starvation under hot concurrent ingest (bounded by the declared watermark); sort memory on giant partitions (ScratchStore spill); duplicate/conflicting chunk retries (the manifest's ordinal/digest law makes drift fail).

## Provenance
§7.5 (bulk paths, fence, acceptance rule); §6.3 (run construction); §2.2 (fnx-readwrite); §17 (cold-load gate); App F FG-INV-18.

title: Implement canonical stable-key shared-prefix identity-column codecs (4KiB/256 law)
description:
## What & scope
Specify and implement the canonical stable-key encoding for identity columns everywhere Strata stores stable identities: `dst_VId` and `EId` entries in Tier D blocks, the `stable_eids` and `origin_birth_orders` columns in sealed runs, reverse-family variants, and the registration of these layouts as codecs in the run/block codec tables with logical-digest-validator coverage.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
The 128-bit identity `VId = { allocation_epoch: u64, local_id: { partition_id: 20 bits, monotone_slot: 44 bits } }` (§4.5; EIds share the epoch+partition+slot shape) is a final, recorded decision — the u64 epoch survives unbounded same-identity restores and the 20-bit partition aligns identity with W12 ownership mobility. But raw 128-bit identities would destroy block economics. The encoding law makes the logical width nearly free on disk (B2 space), lets encodings evolve without a format-identity change (B1/B5: digest-covered codec evolution), and preserves search performance (SIMD lower-bound on a fixed-width suffix). §4.5 states it directly: the on-disk cost of the width is governed by this law, not by the logical width.

## Design — normative detail
The law (§6.2, normative): canonical stable-key encoding is defined for identity columns as a **registered order-preserving shared-prefix layout** in which a block-header (or run-header) dictionary carries the `allocation_epoch`+`partition_id` components and the `monotone_slot` suffix is fixed-width or delta/FOR-coded. The layouts are registered as codecs in the run/block codec tables and, like every codec choice, are covered by the logical-digest validator over stable IDs, so encodings evolve without a format-identity change. Search law: binary search and SIMD lower-bound operate on the fixed-width suffix under the header-extracted prefix, which preserves canonical big-endian epoch||partition||slot order exactly. Reverse-family blocks — destination-grouped, carrying source-partition EIds — may require multi-entry dictionaries and degrade gracefully toward raw width under adversarial prefix diversity. Sizing arithmetic (normative context): a Tier D block is about 4 KiB and holds at most 256 `(dst_VId, EId, user_key_ref?, prop_row_ref, flags)` entries; that sizing presumes this encoding at <=16 B per entry — raw 128-bit identities would cap a 4 KiB block near 95 entries. In sealed runs, `stable_eids` and `OriginBirthOrder` columns are identity columns under the same law — delta/FOR-encoded against the run-header prefix dictionary, named in `codec_table`, covered by `canonical_stable_id_digest` over the *decoded* stable IDs — and a sorted sealed run compresses the EId column to a few bytes per entry. `OriginBirthOrder { commit_seq, intent_ordinal, merge_ordinal, element_id }` (§4.5) is encoded under the same discipline. The identity-column codec definitions are part of the frozen G0 decision batch (`g0-format-arms`); implementation may trail but must match the frozen rows.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-11 (excerpt): canonical forward incidence, stable IDs, origin/birth/branch orders, properties, ordinal maps, holes, and any reverse materialization agree — a codec may never change a decoded identity, and no epoch/range pair is ever aliased by encoding. FG-INV-12 (excerpt): codec rewrites are claimed answer-equivalences and must preserve logical values, multiplicity, order, visibility. FG-INV-09 (excerpt): every stored digest is explicitly Target, Transcript, WeakIdentity, or BodyDigest with one generated include/exclude recipe — the identity-column digest recipe is registry-generated, never hand-rolled. The §17 byte-economy row "identity-column bytes per live edge, by tier (Tier D block entries and sorted sealed runs), reverse-family blocks reported separately" is a benchmark-class gate fed by this bead.

## Interactions
`g0-format-arms` freezes the codec rows; `g0-identity-registries` owns `durable_fields`/BodyDigest transcript recipes; `w1-codecs` supplies varint/FOR/bitpack/SIMD primitives; `w2-object-identity` supplies digest plumbing. Consumers: `w3-tier-d` (block entries, binary search/SIMD lower-bound), `w3-tier-r` (run columns), `w3-vertex-directory` (directory keys), `w3-write-amp` (the named metric), `w3-seal-compact` (digest validator on every rewrite), `w3-bulk-staging` (bulk-built runs).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Property tests: for random identity sets, encoded order equals canonical big-endian epoch||partition||slot order (order preservation); exact roundtrip; lower-bound/binary-search equivalence vs decoded arrays, including SIMD paths. Arithmetic CI check: entry width <=16 B on representative distributions; an adversarial prefix-diversity corpus shows monotone graceful degradation with logged bytes/entry. Golden vectors registered per codec arm. Digest tests: two legal encodings of the same identities produce equal logical digests and distinct physical checksums. Fuzz: corrupted dictionaries/suffix streams produce typed decode failures, never wrong identities. Bench: identity-column bytes per live edge reported by tier on pinned corpora, wired into the §17 byte-economy gate and the §6.6 component breakdown; reverse-family reported separately. E2e script: ingest a corpus whose identities span multiple allocation epochs and partitions; drive blocks through seal into sealed-run columns; re-encode one run under a second legal codec arm; verify equal `canonical_stable_id_digest`, exact order preservation, and SIMD-vs-scalar lower-bound equivalence end-to-end. Detailed logging (mandatory, asserted by the tests): every encode logs {container(block|run|reverse_family), codec_arm, dictionary_entry_count, entry_count, bytes_per_entry, suffix_width}; every decode failure logs a typed error {container_id, failure_kind} (never a silently wrong identity); digest validation logs {logical_digest, physical_checksum} pairs per re-encoding; the adversarial prefix-diversity test logs the full bytes/entry degradation curve so graceful degradation is verifiable post-implementation.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: 64-bit identities — the §4.5 recorded decision: `partition_id` (20) plus `monotone_slot` (44) already fill 64 bits, so any 64-bit split either makes externally fenced epoch advances routine on the ingest path (a hot partition at the §17 bulk-load gate exhausts a shrunken slot space in seconds) or leaves terminal-exhaustion headroom incompatible with restore drills, while dropping the partition field would redesign `IdRangeLease` and the allocator/escape model. Rejected: paying raw width (95-entry blocks); order-destroying dictionary compression (breaks binary search and k-way merge). Risk: reverse-family dictionary blowup under adversarial destination diversity — bounded by the graceful-degradation clause and priced in the byte-economy metric.

## Provenance
§6.2 (encoding law); §6.3 (run columns); §4.5 (identity shape and width decision); §17 (byte economy); App A `AdjRunSegment`.

title: Implement property storage: Tier-D row patches and columnar sealed chunks
description:
## What & scope
Implement §6.4 property storage: immutable Tier-D row patches beside adjacency deltas, columnar sealed vertex and edge property chunks, membership-bitmap-gated label scans, stable-EId sidecars, replaceable-locator discipline, and the generation-pinned embedding-matrix contract.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Properties must obey exactly the same immutability and visibility laws as incidence or B1 collapses into two consistency stories. Grouping by stable partition and storage family — never mutable label — generalizes the Teseo/§4.5 lesson (labels are membership, not placement) so label churn never rewrites data. Columnar sealed chunks feed Loom's vectorized executor (B3), and generation-pinned embedding matrices are the honest substrate for vector indexes and agent-native hybrid retrieval (B6): "zero-copy" is a checkable predicate here, not a marketing claim (§2.2's `GraphView` honesty doctrine).

## Design — normative detail
Vertex property chunks are grouped by `(stable partition, property/storage family)`, not mutable label. Label scans apply versioned membership bitmaps BEFORE reading rows. Edge property chunks are grouped by `(edge_type, property, run generation)` and are sequential by replaceable run row, with a stable EId sidecar — run positions and property locators are replaceable physical addresses (§4.5), the EId sidecar is the identity, so compaction may re-address rows without touching identity. Published Tier-D property patches are immutable objects and obey the same MVCC/branch visibility rules as adjacency blocks: predecessor chains, the walk-until-all-predicates-satisfied visibility rule, sibling-branch-version skipping; mutable row-patch buffers are staging only, dropped on abort and discarded by crash recovery. Patches hang off `DeltaBlockVersion.property_patch_refs[]` and the `prop_row_ref`/property-locator slots in block entries and the vertex directory. Embedding matrices are generation-pinned inputs to vector indexes; "zero-copy" is used only when requested dtype, alignment, authorization, and snapshot generation actually match — any mismatch takes an honest copy. The reserved `_expires_at` property slot (§4.8 TTL) lives in this storage and must be representable in both patch and columnar forms.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-03: property patch chains are finite, acyclic, strictly newer-first, within one owning generation. FG-INV-04 (excerpt): visibility obeys snapshot/branch/valid-time/create-retire/own-write rules plus the erasure-tombstone conjunct (§12.6) and the expiry predicate (§4.8) — both evaluate over property state stored here. FG-INV-11 (excerpt): properties agree with canonical forward incidence, stable IDs, and ordinal maps. FG-INV-12: sealing patches into columnar chunks is a claimed answer-equivalent transition and must be digest-proved. Scan/compression numbers are benchmark class.

## Interactions
Consumes block/patch publication machinery from `w3-tier-d`; run generations and `property_locators` from `w3-tier-r`; canonical committed effects from `w2-delta-batches`; content addressing from `w2-object-identity`. Produces: columnar chunk inputs for `w5-executor`; generation-pinned matrices for `w7-vector`; locator resolution for `w3-vertex-directory`; seal input for `w3-seal-compact`; byte components for `w3-write-amp`. `w9-redaction-erasure` and `w4-ttl-expiry` visibility conjuncts read this state; `w4-valid-time` slices bind row visibility intervals.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Property/fuzz: patch-chain visibility differential across branches and own-write overlays against a bead-local executable model of the §6.2/§6.4 visibility rules (predecessor chains, walk-until-all-predicates-satisfied, sibling-branch-version skipping); the same seeded corpus re-runs as a differential vs the reference engine (`verif-reference`) once it lands — an epic-w3 closure prerequisite, since verif-reference sits downstream of the Loom intent vocabulary and is not a build dependency of this bead. Label-flap metamorphic: sustained AddLabel/RemoveLabel churn changes bitmaps and derived projections only — chunk ObjectIds stay stable (asserted from logs). EId-sidecar stability: across compaction cycles, locators change while identities and decoded values never do. Crash rows: crash between patch publication and root publication leaves the patch unreachable; recovery is digest-clean. Zero-copy negatives: dtype, alignment, authorization, or generation mismatch forces a copy (instrumented assertion). Seal equivalence: columnar chunks decoded row-by-row equal patch-merged rows at every sampled snapshot. Bench: columnar property-scan throughput on the pinned corpus, reported with component byte breakdown (gates live in `perf-bench-core`). E2e script: write vertices and edges with properties across two branches; patch one hot property repeatedly to grow a chain; seal to columnar chunks; run label-gated scans and two embedding-matrix requests (one satisfying and one violating the zero-copy predicate); crash between patch publication and root publication; recover and verify the full visibility differential end-to-end. Detailed logging (mandatory, asserted by the tests): patch publication logs {patch_object_id, owning_block_version, chain_depth, generation}; seal logs {chunk_object_id, family, run_generation, row_count, digest_pair}; label scans log {label, bitmap_generation, rows_gated_out}; every zero-copy decision logs {requested_dtype, alignment, authorization, snapshot_generation, zero_copy|honest_copy(reason)}; recovery logs unreachable-patch discard counts so digest-clean recovery is provable from logs.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: label-grouped physical placement (label mutation would rewrite storage); durable mutable row buffers (a second source of truth); unconditional zero-copy claims. Risks: wide-property amplification (family grouping plus §6.6 component reporting makes it visible); hot-property patch-chain depth (seal cadence, churn telemetry).

## Provenance
§6.4; §6.2.5; §4.5 (labels/locators); §4.8 (`_expires_at`); §2.2.
