Remaining scope here: edge property patches (the block header's reserved property_patch_refs count + per-entry locators, ruling fgdb-2t7q 3B), label membership bitmaps, columnar sealed chunks, EId sidecars, embedding matrices, and the patch-chain MVCC beyond create-once.

title: Implement seal/compact with logical-digest equivalence and governed merge policies
description:
## What & scope
Implement seal (Tier D -> R0) and generational compaction (R0…Rk k-way merge) as digest-proved, answer-equivalent physical transitions; the governed merge-policy family with shadow evaluation, pinned deterministic tables, and the static size-tiering fallback; SPRT/dwell anti-thrash guards; and the equivalence validators run on every representation transition, including Tier I<->D promotion/demotion.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1 makes every published object immutable, so storage evolution is object replacement — and the only safe replacement is one proved to mean the same thing, which is why the logical-digest validator over stable IDs covers every codec and ordinal-map choice. B2's economics are made or lost in compaction; §17 law 3 (never hide compaction — foreground latency during compaction/checkpoint/GC/index-build is part of the result) and the endurance compaction-debt ceiling make its cost first-class. The governed policy family is B5 applied to LSM folklore: leveled-vs-tiered becomes a bounded, evidence-audited, deterministically-fallbacked table rather than a tuning superstition.

## Design — normative detail
**Physical-equivalence law**: seal and compact build new immutable encodings and must prove old/new canonical logical digests equal over stable IDs before publication; the validator covers codec and map choice, so any legal re-encoding is admissible and any semantic drift is unpublishable (this is what lets encodings evolve without a format-identity change). **Generational law** (§6.3): seal produces an R0 run from Tier D; merges produce R0…Rk per partition. A snapshot pins run generations via epochs; compaction publishes a new segment set atomically in the manifest and retires the old under lease — readers never block, never see mixed generations. Strata compaction rides Chronicle's serialized machinery (`w2-compaction`): `BUILD -> VERIFY_EQUIVALENCE -> D1_NEW_OBJECTS -> ROOT_PUBLISH -> SLOT_CONVERGE -> WAIT_SAFE_POINT -> RETIRE`, with the safe point computed under a consensus-fenced membership epoch; loss of quorum, uncertain membership, an unacknowledged root, or a missing key wrap stops reclamation; the actor is supervised and rate-limited against foreground latency. **Merge policy is a governed family, not a constant** (§6.3, normative): per `(partition, edge_type, direction)`, a bounded leveled<->tiered family is evaluated in shadow and deployed as a pinned deterministic table; static size-tiering is the permanent fallback. Birth–death and stability analyses are named configuration models with sensitivity bounds, while dwell/hysteresis and measured churn are runtime guards — they do not prove universal absence of oscillation. Every migration/policy change emits a §6.6 decision card `{state, candidates, cost interval, minimum dwell, uncertainty, pinned deterministic fallback}`; SPRT promote/demote evidence is conditional on its declared observation model and loss matrix while minimum dwell and benefit>conversion-cost+uncertainty remain deterministic anti-thrash rules; policy-vs-fallback comparison is an e-process (`FG-CAL-01`) reverting through a stream-sequenced `DecisionPolicyEpoch`; all calibration windows key off the single §15.0 regime clock.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12 (excerpt, binding): every claimed answer-equivalent seal, compaction, codec/format rewrite preserves logical values, multiplicity, order, visibility, security projection, and AnswerContract; no build progress changes schema visibility before its transactional activation. FG-INV-14 (excerpt): GC follows every generated strong/uncut-conditional edge; heavy detail retires only after visibility and an activated cut — old generations retire only under lease plus safe point. FG-INV-11 (excerpt): forward/reverse-family agreement must survive every merge (reference-graph and forward/reverse compaction metamorphics are its named enforcement). Claim classes: churn/reversal metrics and the compaction-debt ceiling are benchmark/`FG-EVID-03`; policy stability `FG-CFG-02`; promotion evidence `FG-CAL-01`.

## Interactions
Consumes Tier D roots/blocks from `w3-tier-d`; run formats/builders from `w3-tier-r`; property patch-merge semantics and columnar chunk formats from `w3-properties` (seal covers property patches into §6.4 columnar chunks, and the equivalence oracle covers properties); identity codecs and digest recipes from `w3-identity-encoding`; the Chronicle compaction/root-publication protocol from `w2-compaction`; snapshot pins from `w2-snapshots-leases`; SPRT/e-process machinery from `w1-sketch-calibrate`. Produces: new run generations for all `w3-tier-r` consumers; retirement inputs for `w2-gc-core`; churn/debt telemetry for `w3-write-amp` and `perf-bench-scale`; the shared equivalence validator reused by `w3-bulk-staging` (staged-run acceptance) and derived rebuilds.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Equivalence oracle: for randomized workloads, decoded post-seal/post-compact adjacency and properties equal the pre-image at every pinned snapshot and branch — self-checked at this bead by decoding both sides through Strata's own read path; the independent differential vs `verif-reference` re-runs the same corpora once verif-reference lands (an epic-w3 closure prerequisite: verif-reference sits downstream of the Loom intent vocabulary and is not a build dependency of this bead); mutation testing — corrupting one entry during BUILD makes VERIFY_EQUIVALENCE fail and nothing publishes. Crash matrix: cut at every stage boundary (BUILD, VERIFY_EQUIVALENCE, D1_NEW_OBJECTS, ROOT_PUBLISH, SLOT_CONVERGE, WAIT_SAFE_POINT, RETIRE); recovery never exposes mixed generations and never loses the old set before the new is durable. Pin test: a long-lived snapshot holds WAIT_SAFE_POINT without blocking readers or subsequent compactions. Policy: shadow evaluation on pinned workloads yields deterministic tables; SPRT churn soak shows zero minimum-dwell violations; an injected model violation triggers fallback reversion through a logged `DecisionPolicyEpoch`. Foreground-latency gate: p99 during compaction reported per §17 law 3; the endurance compaction-debt ceiling (debt bytes + generation count at the stated ingest fraction) fails the run when exceeded even if point latencies pass. Logging: every seal/compact emits build ID, input/output generation IDs, the digest pair, policy epoch, and regime epoch. E2e script: a sustained-ingest soak that continuously seals and compacts under concurrent pinned readers, with one crash injection at each of the seven pipeline stages; afterwards the harness replays the logs to reconstruct every generation transition and fails if any seal/compact event is missing a required field. Detailed logging (mandatory, beyond the per-event fields above): stage transitions log {build_id, stage, wall_time}; safe-point computation logs {membership_epoch, blocking_pins[]}; retirement logs {retired_generation_ids, lease_proof}; every policy decision logs the complete decision card {state, candidates, cost_interval, minimum_dwell, uncertainty, pinned_fallback} plus current SPRT/e-process state and `DecisionPolicyEpoch`.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: in-place merge (violates B1); a universal leveled or universal tiered policy (workload-dependent — the family is bounded instead); claiming oscillation-freedom (only guards and measured churn are claimed). Risks: compaction starvation under sustained ingest (rate limiting + debt ceiling); digest-validation CPU cost (amortized at build, measured); lease leaks delaying retirement (FG-INV-16 leak oracle coverage).

## Provenance
§6.3 (generational law, merge-policy family); §6.2.3 (publication barrier); §6.6 (cards/SPRT/e-process/regime clock); §5.5 (compaction protocol); §17 (laws 3/5, endurance rows); App F.

title: Implement Tier D delta blocks: immutable DeltaBlockVersion, partition roots, MVCC chains
description:
## What & scope
Implement Tier D, Strata's delta tier (§6.2): the immutable `DeltaBlockVersion` durable unit, `DeltaPartitionRoot` and immutable skip-list nodes, per-block MVCC predecessor chains, the volatile staging machinery (block locks, transaction-private nodes, bump arenas, EBR), the bounded hot-burst overflow log with its drain actor, and hub striping. Everything published is immutable and content-addressed; everything mutable is discardable staging.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
This is the write side of B2: the hot minority of descriptors absorbs transactional churn in sorted, cache-friendly blocks (Sortledton lesson) with delta-chain-per-block concurrency (GTX lesson) and latch-free append staging (RadixGraph lesson), while B1 demands that nothing mutable ever becomes authoritative — frankensqlite's page-granularity MVCC (version chains in a bump arena, `Snapshot { high: CommitSeq }`, O(1) current-line fast path, EBR) is adapted to block granularity, but its durable arena indexes are demoted to decoded caches because branch ancestry is semantic visibility, not an integer rule. Deterministic recovery from the Chronicle suffix (B5) only works if staging is worthless by construction.

## Design — normative detail
**Sorted edge blocks.** The durable unit is immutable `DeltaBlockVersion {format, partition_id, descriptor_key, stripe_range, sorted_entries[], visibility_intervals[], property_patch_refs[], predecessor: ConditionalCoordinateRef<DeltaBlockVersion>?, canonical_logical_digest}`. A block is about 4 KiB and holds at most 256 `(dst_VId, EId, user_key_ref?, prop_row_ref, flags)` entries sorted by stable identity, encoded under the registered identity-column codec (`w3-identity-encoding`; <=16 B/entry — raw 128-bit identities would cap near 95 entries). `DeltaPartitionRoot {partition_id, generation, descriptor_map_ref, sorted_block_head_refs[], overflow_state: Empty|Drained{through_commit_seq}, canonical_partition_digest}` plus immutable skip-list nodes represent a vertex's zero, one, or hub-sized two-level block family. Every reference is typed and every published root is content-addressed.
**Per-block MVCC.** A published block head reaches an immutable predecessor chain; no durable bump-arena index or process pointer appears in canonical bytes. Readers continue down the chain until the FIRST version satisfying **all** sequence, branch-ancestry, schema, retirement, and own-write visibility predicates; a newer sibling-branch version is skipped rather than terminating the search. The current-line fast path may collapse this to one compare only under a verified lineage token. Process-local `VersionArena`/`prev_idx` layouts are discardable decoded caches for those immutable objects, never the authoritative chain.
**Concurrency, staging, visibility.** Eager block locks, latch-free transaction-private nodes, bump arenas, and EBR are strictly volatile staging machinery. Before any logical state/root/RootSlot can name the result, the writer must canonicalize and seal complete `DeltaBlockVersion` and `DeltaPartitionRoot` objects, verify their logical digest against the committed effects/marker, and root the immutable partition generation atomically with the candidate state. Publication never stamps or mutates an old object or authoritative pointer. Abort drops only volatile staging; crash recovery discards every unrooted arena/overflow node and deterministically reconstructs from the Chronicle command/effect suffix. Readers merge committed immutable roots plus their own private overlay; another transaction's staging is unobservable. Giant hubs stripe the neighbor-ID space into independently locked/versioned candidate ranges, and witness granularity follows the durable stripe identity.
**Hot-burst overflow.** A bounded per-partition append log may absorb spikes only as volatile, transaction-tagged staging. The drain actor preserves commit order and verifies the canonical logical digest while producing immutable blocks; the same root-publication barrier applies. The log is neither a durable source of truth nor recoverable state, and admission backpressures before memory is exhausted. A future durable overflow representation would require a separately registered immutable object and state transition; none exists in v1.
**Property deltas** ride beside adjacency deltas as row patches (`w3-properties` owns their sealed layout).

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-02 (excerpt): for every exclusive block, at most one legal live generation owns or may consume it; stale, cancelled, expired, or prior-configuration owners can neither mutate nor release it. FG-INV-03 (full text): every physical version chain is finite, acyclic, strictly newer-first by commit order, and every link remains within one owning object generation — enforced via the Lean chain model plus arena-decode, generation-substitution, debug, property, and fuzz oracles. FG-INV-04 (excerpt): visibility obeys snapshot high sequence, branch ancestry, create/retire rules, and own-write overlays; distinct branch heads never alias. The ~4 KiB/256-entry constants are format constants conditioned on the registered identity codec; ingest-rate numbers are benchmark class (§17 transactional-ingest gate).

## Interactions
Consumes identity codecs and search law from `w3-identity-encoding`; content addressing/keyed ObjectIds from `w2-object-identity`; committed effect digests and the `LogicalDeltaTemplate` apply basis from `w2-delta-batches`; snapshot pinning from `w2-snapshots-leases`; core types from `w1-foundation-types`; registry rows from `g0-identity-registries`. Produces: block/stripe identities consumed by `w4-mvcc-locks` (canonical lock order) and `w4-ssi-witnesses` (witness granularity follows stripes); seal input for `w3-seal-compact`; merge input for `w3-vertex-directory`-anchored reads and `w5-executor`; byte counters for `w3-write-amp`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Unit/property: sorted-entry law and 256-entry cap; digest recompute (mutating any entry breaks `canonical_logical_digest`); predecessor-chain acyclicity/newer-first fuzz. MVCC oracle: randomized interleavings under `fgdb-sim` where readers walk chains across branches — a newer sibling-branch version never terminates a search, asserted by an in-bead visibility model; the differential vs `fgdb-reference`'s visibility engine executes once `verif-reference` lands (verif-reference depends on this bead, so a dep here would cycle) and is validated at gate-genesis. Crash-matrix rows: cut before/after canonicalize, digest-verify, and root publication; recovery must discard every unrooted arena/overflow node and rebuild identical partition digests from the Chronicle suffix, logging recovered-vs-expected digest pairs. Overflow: spike test proves bounded memory and backpressure; drain preserves commit order; drained blocks byte-match direct-publication blocks. Hub stripes: concurrent writers on disjoint stripes commit independently; witness-granularity assertion. E2e script: ingest, publish, crash, recover, scan — logging root generations, chain depths, digest verifications, and staging-discard counts.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: durable bump-arena indexes or process pointers in canonical bytes (donor arena kept as cache only); a durable overflow log (second source of truth); in-place version stamping (breaks B1); monotone-TxnId visibility (replaced by durable transaction idempotency + branch-ancestry semantics). Risks: chain-depth blowup on hot blocks (seal cadence, churn telemetry via `w3-write-amp`); staging memory spikes (admission backpressure).

## Provenance
§6.2; §6.1; §3.1 (Sortledton/GTX/RadixGraph/LiveGraph); §2.3; App F FG-INV-02/03/04.
design:
## External-review boundary (2026-07-22)

FG-ADR-SOTA-STORAGE-DELTA-CHAIN-FIELD remains review_due. The pinned RadixGraph v1 paper supports atomic Size/fetch-add slot reservation and latch-free reads, not the registry summary’s literal “latch-free MPSC append.” DGS supports only workload-scoped measured comparisons, and no primary Spruce artifact was independently pinned. Implement Strata from the actually evidenced mechanisms and keep benchmark portability and MPSC semantics unclaimed until separately proved.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FIRST SLICE LANDED 2026-07-31 as def35d6 (JadeSnow): fgdb-strata is activated and tier one has its durable artifact.

WHAT LANDED: the canonical delta-block format. A sorted, versioned adjacency run with an exact byte
layout, a fail-closed decoder, and snapshot-visible scans read from the encoded bytes. 18 laws.

THE DECISION WORTH PRESERVING: a format, not a map. The obvious first slice is a BTreeMap keyed by
(src, relation, dst) with the tier visibility semantics on top; it is smaller, it would pass a
differential against the reference oracle, and it is exactly what doctrine 7 prohibits -- "no HashMap
presented as storage", "a subset of a final abstraction, never a substitute". An in-memory map has no
durable form, so nothing about it can be wrong the way storage is wrong. A byte layout can be
non-canonical, truncated, trailing, or decode to something other than what was encoded, and each of
those is now a law. The round-trip law caught a real one on its first run: the decoder read created_at
at offset 32 instead of 40, treating dst as eight bytes rather than sixteen.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT, and this bead still owns all of it: immutable DeltaBlockVersion identity,
partition roots, MVCC chains across blocks, sealing, and any index over a SET of blocks. What landed
manages one block: written once, read back. The module doc lists the absences so the gap is legible
rather than implied.

NEXT SLICE, in the order that keeps each one honest: (1) DeltaBlockVersion identity -- content-address
a block so a partition root can name it; (2) partition roots over a set of blocks; (3) MVCC chains,
which is where a read must merge across blocks and where the reference oracle differential finally has
a subject. Do not skip to (3) with an in-memory index over (1) and (2) -- that is the same substitute
the format was chosen to avoid.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SLICE 3 OF 4 LANDED 2026-07-31 (JadeSnow): partition roots, ead28a6. Blocks def35d6, identity 3f96a86.

WHAT EXISTS NOW: a block format (canonical, fail-closed, scans from the encoded bytes), a derived
content identity per block, and a root that names an ordered set of blocks by identity with the
sequence range each covers. resolve_blocks proves both halves -- that the bytes ARE the named block,
and that the block spans what the root claimed. Either check alone leaves a lie the other catches.

THE DESIGN QUESTION SLICE 4 MUST ANSWER, recorded on BlockRef rather than left to be discovered.
AdjacencyEntry carries created_at and retired_at in ONE entry. That is complete within a block and
cannot express "an entry created in an earlier block was retired later", because an immutable block
cannot be edited. Merging across blocks therefore requires choosing between:

  (a) TOMBSTONE ENTRIES -- a later block carries an entry for the same key whose retirement shadows
      the earlier creation. Cheap to write; makes a read a merge over every block that could mention
      the key, so the root's range summary stops being sufficient to skip a block.
  (b) VERSION CHAINS PER KEY -- a block carries every version of the keys it touches. Reads get
      simpler, writes get amplification, and sealing has to rewrite chains.

Neither is stored today, which is deliberate: this slice cannot make the choice by accident. Whoever
takes slice 4 should decide explicitly and write down which and why, because every later tier (sealed
runs, archived anchors, compaction) inherits it.

THE LAW THAT WILL MATTER MOST IN SLICE 4: a merged read across blocks must agree with the reference
oracle's ReferenceGraph over the same delta stream. That is the first point where Strata has a
differential subject at all -- everything so far is format law with no semantic counterpart. Do not
build the merge without wiring that differential in the same increment; a merge tested only against
its own expectations is exactly the substitute doctrine 7 warns about.

must assert it found the expected value there before writing: the root's decoder-order test had the
same slip and patched the wrong block's field until it did.

title: Permit truthful overlapping Strata spans under tombstone supersede
description:
## Finding

At HEAD 0309dc809cbda806640e705b8de4ff4b748e873f, the Tier-D root format contradicts the tombstone-supersede model landed in 6e0c6f0. `PartitionRoot::validate` requires adjacent block spans to be disjoint, while `BlockWriter` represents a later retirement by restating the original version with its old `created_at` and new `retired_at`. A create sealed at sequence 1 followed by retirement at sequence 6 therefore produces truthful spans 1..1 and 1..6, and `encode_root` rejects the writer-produced root. The plan at section 6.1 instead defines newest-to-oldest LSM merge with tombstones; later-block precedence is already implemented by `merge_neighbours` and `compact`.

## Root cause

The non-overlap rule and its tests predate the explicit cross-block tombstone model. Block ranges summarize entry visibility intervals for safe skipping, not exclusive ownership of commit sequences. Overlap is therefore required. Publication order remains semantic because a later block supersedes an earlier statement of the same version.

## Acceptance

- Root validation permits truthful overlapping visibility spans while retaining a deterministic publication-order law.
- Writer regression: seal a creation, retire it later, publish, encode/decode/resolve the root, and prove the edge is visible before but absent at/after retirement.
- Boundary regression: retirement and re-creation at the same commit remain representable and answer correctly.
- Compacted output can be encoded as lawful blocks and referenced by a lawful root without changing answers at or above the retention floor.
- Existing root framing, range-integrity, writer differential, compaction, and reopen tests remain green.
- Exact-file UBS, fmt, strict clippy, cargo test, and repository gate results are recorded; any foreign gate failure is reported without misattribution.

title: Make BlockWriter publication fail closed on an invalid root
description:
## Finding

At HEAD e5d1470, `BlockWriter::publish` documents that `published_at` must be at or above every block sequence and returns `Result`, but it constructs and returns `PartitionRoot` without invoking the root validator. A writer that has folded a row at sequence 5 therefore returns `Ok` when asked to publish at sequence 4; only a later, separate call to `encode_root` discovers `RootError::BlockAfterPublication`. This violates the publication boundary and allows an invalid root to escape the producer that promised to refuse it.

## Root cause

Root validation is private to encode/decode. The writer and format were built as separate slices, and the integration test validates only after `publish` has already succeeded. The `Result` surface has no root-validation error arm.

## Acceptance

- Root structural validation is reusable without allocating/throwing away a canonical encoding.
- `BlockWriter::publish` validates the finished root before returning it and exposes a typed root error.
- A regression proves publication below a sealed block returns the exact `BlockAfterPublication` error from `publish`, while equality at the frontier succeeds.
- Existing writer/root/compaction, oracle, and durable-stream tests remain green.
- Exact-file UBS, fmt, strict clippy, cargo test, and repository gate results are recorded; the known unowned workspace gate failure is not misattributed.

title: Make BlockWriter row refusals state-atomic
description: Finding at HEAD 951cb71: BlockWriter::apply advances last_seq before a row succeeds, and DeleteVertex retires cascade edges one by one. Therefore UnknownEdge can consume the offered sequence, and a cascade whose later EId is unknown can partially remove earlier live edges despite returning Err. The same remove-before-push ordering also makes a retirement vulnerable to a later push failure. Root cause: the fold mutates frontier and live state before all fallible preconditions are discharged. title: Implement Tier R sealed runs: AdjRunSegment layout, EF offsets, neighbor codecs
description:
## What & scope
Implement Tier R (§6.3): the immutable `AdjRunSegment` object, Elias–Fano offset directories, the per-list `NeighborCodec` closed union, identity-column storage for `stable_eids`/`origin_birth_orders`, marker-aware hole/retire metadata, ordinal-map tagging, the honest intersection contract, and generational run management (R0…Rk) with epoch pinning.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
This is the scan/space side of B2: CSR is adopted as sealed per-`(stable partition, edge_type, direction)` runs — unbeatable scans without pretending CSR can absorb updates — and Aspen's immutable structural sharing is adopted at run granularity, so snapshots and branches share cold runs for free (B1). The cold majority must sit *below* CSR via per-list compression to cure the field's 4–9x space disease. Loom's WCOJ/intersection performance (B3) depends on codecs whose rank/select claims are honest, and Kùzu-style dense-ID speed is captured safely as snapshot-local `OrdinalMapId` projections that never leak into identity (§4.5).

## Design — normative detail
The App A row is normative: `AdjRunSegment { graph, branch_projection, source_partition, direction, edge_type, source_ordinal_map_id, destination_map_table[{partition, ordinal_map_id}], source_ordinal_range, edge_count, seq_range, codec_table, offsets_ef, encoded_neighbor_lists, stable_eids, origin_birth_orders, branch_admission_orders?, marker_aware_retire_or_hole_data, property_locators, canonical_stable_id_digest, checksum }`. Layout per run segment: header (fenceposts, stats, checksum, seq-range, `source_ordinal_map_id`, `destination_map_table[]`) · Elias–Fano offsets for O(1) list location · per-list `NeighborCodec` chosen from `EliasFano`, `StreamVByte { skip_table }`, or `DenseIntervals` · stable EIds/`OriginBirthOrder`s and replaceable property locators · versioned marker-aware hole/retire metadata. Ordinal discipline: a source ordinal is meaningful only under the source map; each encoded destination is either a stable VId or `(destination_map_slot, dst_ordinal)` where the slot names an explicit `{ destination_partition, OrdinalMapId }`; no ordinal crosses a map boundary untagged. Codec/map choice is covered by the logical-digest validator over stable IDs (`canonical_stable_id_digest` over decoded IDs). Identity columns: `stable_eids` and `origin_birth_orders` obey the §6.2/§6.3 canonical stable-key encoding law — order-preserving run-header prefix dictionary plus delta/FOR-coded slot suffix, named in `codec_table` — and a sorted sealed run compresses the EId column to a few bytes per entry. Honest intersection contract: Elias–Fano neighbor lists support rank/select directly; StreamVByte lists use skip/fence metadata and bounded blockwise decode; dense intervals use interval arithmetic; Loom intersects without **full-list** decompression where the codec permits it — there is no claim that Elias–Fano offsets provide rank/select over a separate varint stream. Generational law: seal produces R0 from Tier D; merges produce R0…Rk per partition; a snapshot pins run generations via epochs; compaction publishes a new segment set atomically in the manifest and retires the old under lease — readers never block, never see mixed generations. Hole/tombstone law (§6.1): holes carry creation/retirement marker references or a lineage-pinned effective-interval sidecar; a branch-agnostic scalar retire sequence or current hole bitmap may never hide an edge from a sibling branch or older snapshot. Direction law (§6.1): canonical forward runs always exist; reverse runs are declared synchronously maintained materializations, enabled by default and disableable per edge type only with the registered reverse-scan fallback, and every present/required reverse family must equal the transpose of authorized forward incidence at each snapshot — disabling changes performance, never semantics. Mutable labels never identify a primary run.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12 (excerpt): every claimed answer-equivalent seal, compaction, or codec/format rewrite preserves logical values, multiplicity, order, visibility, security projection, and AnswerContract. FG-INV-11 (excerpt): canonical forward incidence, stable IDs, origin/birth/branch orders, properties, ordinal maps, holes, and any reverse materialization agree. FG-INV-04 (excerpt): create/retire visibility rules bind hole/retire metadata — it must be marker-aware, never scalar-global. Claim classes: neighbor-scan rates (>=500M edges/s per core decoded-cache; EF+varint decode >=4 B/edge effective) are §17 benchmark gates; compression ratios are corpus-tied benchmark results, never universal facts.

## Interactions
Consumes seal candidates from `w3-tier-d` (via `w3-seal-compact`'s pipeline); identity-column codecs from `w3-identity-encoding`; EF/varint/bitpack/SIMD kernels from `w1-codecs`; content addressing from `w2-object-identity`; frozen record-kind rows from `g0-identity-registries`. Produces: run segments consumed by `w5-executor` (scans, intersections, FreeJoin), `w7-index-core` builds, `w8-projection`, `w6-maintainers`; destination-map/ordinal tagging consumed by `w3-vertex-directory` and `w5-branch-stats`; `property_locators` consumed by `w3-properties`; byte/zone telemetry for `w3-write-amp`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Golden vectors per codec arm (registry-generated, `w1-generated-parsers` conventions); property tests: encode/decode roundtrip over adversarial gap distributions; per-codec rank/select/skip correctness vs naive decode. Fuzz: corrupted headers, offsets, and codec tags must fail checksum/digest — never mis-decode. Digest-validator test: re-encoding a run under a different legal codec/map choice yields an identical `canonical_stable_id_digest` and a different checksum. Ordinal-boundary negatives: an untagged cross-map ordinal is unencodable/rejected at build. Snapshot-pin test: a reader pinned to an old epoch scans the old generation while compaction publishes a new set — no blocking, no mixed generations (assert generation IDs in scan logs). Branch/hole metamorphics: retiring an edge on branch A leaves it visible to sibling branch B and to older snapshots. Bench gates: neighbor scan >=500M edges/s per core and >=10B edges/s node aggregate on the pinned decoded-cache manifest (memory-bandwidth-bound: EF+varint decode >=4 B/edge effective) — gate rows and manifest registered here, executed on §15.6's deterministic apparatus via `verif-perf-apparatus`/`perf-bench-core` with manifests-green at gate-g4; per-codec intersection microbenches with flamegraph artifacts on regression run in-bead under plain cargo bench. Transpose oracle: at every sampled snapshot/branch, each present reverse family equals the transpose of authorized forward incidence, and disabling a reverse family per edge type changes plans, never answers (differential vs the registered reverse-scan fallback). E2e script: seal a corpus into R0, compact through two generations while a pinned reader stays open, scan and intersect through every codec arm in both directions, then corrupt one segment and verify typed failure end-to-end. Detailed logging (mandatory, asserted by the tests): segment publication logs {segment_object_id, partition, edge_type, direction, generation, edge_count, codec_table, canonical_stable_id_digest, checksum}; scans log {segment_object_id, generation, codec_arm, decode_mode(rank_select|skip_block|interval)}; epoch pin/retire events log {epoch, pinned_generations[]}; corruption tests log the typed checksum/digest failure kind.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: one global codec (per-list choice is load-bearing); rank/select claims over varint streams (dishonest); ordinals as identity (adopted only as `OrdinalMapId`-scoped projections; compaction may renumber without changing VId); label-identified runs. Risks: adversarial prefix diversity in reverse-family runs (graceful degradation to raw width, priced in `w3-write-amp`); zone-map staleness (versioned, marker-aware metadata only).

## Provenance
§6.3; §6.1; §3.1 (CSR/Aspen/Kùzu); §4.5; App A `AdjRunSegment`.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FROM THE 2026-07-31 REALITY CHECK (docs/REALITY_CHECK_AND_BRIDGE_PLAN.md, Phase 4 Round 3). Two
inputs this bead should have before the layout is frozen, plus a new blocker.

NEW BLOCKER, deliberately added: fgdb-lc1t (persistent structures). Tier R is NOT YET WRITTEN, which
means it can be born with structural sharing at no extra cost, and retrofitting persistence into a
sealed-run layout later is a rewrite rather than an optimization. plan:451 requires O(1) branch
creation over "structurally shared objects"; if tier R lands non-persistent, B1 git-style branching
and B6 branch-per-agent isolation are both economically dead. Decide there first.

ELIAS-FANO IS THE RIGHT CODING AND THE BEAD ALREADY HALF-SAYS IT ("EF offsets"). Vigna 2013,
quasi-succinct indices: a monotone sequence of n values from a universe of u stores in about
2 + log2(u/n) bits per element -- within about half a bit of the information-theoretic bound -- with
O(1) random access via the broadword select structure, and fast forward-skipping via the upper-bits
bitmap. For adjacency offsets that is the difference between larger-than-memory scans being real and
being aspirational. Note the partial-sums/select machinery is the same primitive the vertex directory
needs (fgdb-w3-vertex-directory-nde), so build it once.

AND THE POINT OF DOING IT AT ALL: §2 says Loom runs "over Strata runs that are already tries". That is
only true if the run layout is the trie a worst-case-optimal join wants to walk -- see the note added
to the Loom beads about Generic Join and the AGM bound. If tier R is built as a flat CSR without the
trie structure and the WCO join is added later, the headline B3 bet quietly degrades into a normal
hash join with a fancy name. The storage layout decision here IS the join decision.

CONSIDER ALSO: ribbon filters (Dillinger & Walzer 2021) per sealed run for key-level skipping. The
partition root already carries sequence ranges, which lets a reader skip by SEQUENCE; a ribbon filter
lets it skip by KEY, which is what a point read needs. Ribbon strictly dominates Bloom at equal
false-positive rate -- roughly 30 percent less space with better cache locality.

title: Build the vertex directory, Tier-I inline adjacency, ordinal maps, and label bitmaps
description:
## What & scope
Build the vertex directory (§6.5), Tier I inline micro-adjacency (§6.1), snapshot-local ordinal maps, and label-membership bitmaps: the per-partition, per-generation packed mapping between dense ordinals and stable identity plus locator/descriptor state.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Teseo's adopted lesson: the vertex table must not be a straitjacket — ours is an index, not the store. Kùzu's dense-ID performance is captured as snapshot-local `OrdinalMapId` projections without ever letting ordinals become identity (§4.5), so compaction can renumber freely. Tier I gives the small-degree majority a zero-indirection point-read path (B2 economics behind the §17 point-read gate: >=8M lookups/s across cores, p99 < 15us warm), and authorized-degree-after-masking is the B6/Warden-critical property that prevents unauthorized edge types from leaking through counts.

## Design — normative detail
Per stable partition and generation, a packed array maps snapshot-local dense ordinal to `{ stable VId, label-set ref, property locator, small active-descriptor vector, sparse descriptor-table ref }`; a reverse map resolves VId to that generation's ordinal. IDs are never recycled (§4.5). Degree is O(1) per **authorized** descriptor only after Warden masking; unauthorized edge types do not contribute. Directory and label-membership segments are versioned immutable objects. Tier I (§6.1, normative): a small bounded vector in the vertex row stores the first few active `(direction, edge_type, descriptor)` entries; the descriptor may inline up to eight `(dst_VId, EId, prop_locator)` incidences; mutable tiers never store a bare snapshot ordinal; additional edge types live in a sparse immutable descriptor table, so schema cardinality cannot bloat every row; overflow promotes to Tier D, and demotion is a verified representation transition. Ordinal-map law (§4.5): dense ordinals are snapshot-local projections, not identity — each sealed generation may map stable VIds to compact u32/u64 ordinals for CSR, bitmaps, and SIMD; a projection is named by `OrdinalMapId` and cannot escape its segment/index generation; compaction may renumber projections without changing VId. Label law (§4.5): labels are versioned membership, never placement identity — membership indexes map `(label, partition) -> VId/ordinal bitmap` for a specific snapshot generation; `AddLabel`/`RemoveLabel` update membership and affected derived projections without changing VId or rewriting incidence; `(src_label, type, dst_label)` access paths are derived indexes that may duplicate locators but never own the edge. The directory also carries the canonical constraint-map reference for external keys (resolution semantics live in `w4-constraints`' `ConstraintStateRoot`).

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-11 (excerpt): allocation epochs/leases prevent VId/EId alias, overlap, or reuse across crash, label change, branch, merge, clone, restore, topology movement, and role activation; canonical forward incidence, stable IDs, ordinal maps, and holes agree. FG-INV-20 (excerpt): authorization precedes every observation or effect — degree and descriptor enumeration are post-masking, and unauthorized edge types contribute nothing observable, including via counts or errors. FG-INV-04: versioned directory/membership segments obey snapshot/branch visibility. Point-read throughput/latency numbers are §17 benchmark gates, never invariants.

## Interactions
Consumes the identity shape/codecs from `w3-identity-encoding`; the never-recycle allocator law from `w2-id-allocator`; bitmap/rank-select kernels from `w1-codecs`; content addressing from `w2-object-identity`; registry rows from `g0-identity-registries`. Produces: descriptor lookup driving the merge law in `w3-tier-d`/`w3-tier-r` reads and `w5-executor`; ordinal maps consumed by `w3-tier-r` destination tagging, `w5-branch-stats`, and `w8-projection`; label bitmaps consumed by `w3-properties` label scans, `w5-planner`, and `w7-index-core`; masking hooks exercised by `w9-enforcement`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Property: ordinal<->VId bijection per generation; compaction renumbering never changes VId (metamorphic across compaction cycles); structural CI check that no registered mutable-tier schema stores a bare snapshot ordinal. Tier I: the 9th active incidence triggers promotion to Tier D with a digest-verified representation transition; demotion is equally verified; the inline path answers point-existence without touching Tier D/R (asserted via I/O counters in test logs). Label-flap: 10k AddLabel/RemoveLabel cycles leave incidence bytes untouched (stable ObjectIds). Authorization oracle: for every policy fixture, reported degree equals the sum over authorized descriptors; negatives prove unauthorized types are invisible in counts, enumeration, and error shapes. Bench: §17 point-read rows on the pinned manifest (vertex-by-key, 1-hop existence) with warm/cold breakdown logged. E2e script: create a partition; insert vertices and grow one descriptor past the Tier-I inline bound (verifying the digest-verified promotion); flap labels; run point reads and authorized-degree queries under two policy fixtures; force a compaction renumbering; then re-verify the ordinal<->VId bijection and re-run the same reads end-to-end. Detailed logging (mandatory, asserted by the tests): every Tier I<->D promotion/demotion logs {vid, descriptor_key, from_tier, to_tier, entry_count, digest_pair}; directory and membership segment publication logs {partition_id, generation, object_id}; label mutations log {vid, label, bitmap_generation}; ordinal-map creation logs {ordinal_map_id, generation, cardinality}; the authorization oracle logs {policy_fixture, expected_degree, observed_degree} per fixture so post-implementation verification can replay masking correctness from the logs.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: vertex-table-as-store (Teseo straitjacket); global dense vertex IDs (compaction would rewrite identity — hence `OrdinalMapId` scoping); label-keyed directories (placement identity). Risks: descriptor-table misuse for hot types (the bounded vector/sparse table split is normative); per-generation directory bloat (structural sharing; measured in the §6.6 space breakdown).

## Provenance
§6.5; §6.1 (Tier I); §4.5; §3.1 (Teseo/Kùzu); §17.

title: Implement write/space-amplification accounting and migration decision-card machinery
description:
## What & scope
Implement §6.6: the write-amplification and space-amplification accounting model with mandatory component breakdowns, the identity-column bytes-per-live-edge metric, representation-migration decision cards, and the Sextant statistical machinery around migrations — SPRT promote/demote evidence, e-process policy trials, counterfactual-audit disclosure, shadow-only learning, and the single regime clock.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
This is B5 applied to storage: adaptive behavior must be evidence-carrying, deterministically fallbacked, and priced. Storage engines mislead most easily through averaged amplification numbers and hidden compaction cost; the §17 standing laws bind every published number — (2) distributions not averages, (3) never hide compaction, (4) memory is a first-class metric, (5) adaptive numbers disclose their policy epoch, (6) no unpriced protocol weight. B2's tiering only stays honest if promotion/demotion churn, conversion cost, and identity-column overhead are continuously measured and gated.

## Design — normative detail
Definitions (normative): **write amplification** = `all physical bytes written / canonical logical input bytes`, including canonical forward plus any configured reverse-incidence materializations, properties, constraint and optimizer indexes, checkpoints, FEC, staging waste, and every merge level; reports publish the component breakdown. **Space amplification** names the logical baseline and includes key wraps, repair symbols, and retained history. **Identity-column bytes per live edge**, reported by tier — Tier D block entries, sealed-run `stable_eids`/`OriginBirthOrder` columns, and any configured reverse-family materialization — are a named component of both breakdowns under the registered identity-column encoding and feed §17 law 4's bytes-per-live-edge metric. Numerical targets in §17 are benchmark gates, not format truths. **Every representation migration emits a decision card** with state, candidates, cost interval, minimum dwell, uncertainty, and pinned deterministic fallback. Sextant rules (§6.6, all normative): (a) *Migration evidence is sequential, dwell is a hard guard* — an SPRT may evaluate promote/demote evidence under an explicit observation model and loss matrix; its reported error rates are conditional on those assumptions; minimum dwell and benefit-greater-than-conversion-cost-plus-uncertainty remain deterministic anti-thrash rules even when the model is invalid. (b) *Policies remain on trial* — an e-process compares a policy with its pinned fallback on a declared outcome stream; promotion evidence is `FG-CAL-01`; failure of assumptions or evidence reverts to the fallback through a stream-sequenced `DecisionPolicyEpoch`; it is not a production safety-invariant checker. (c) *Counterfactual audit has a support condition* — logged selection probability permits importance-weighted or doubly robust evaluation only for candidate actions with positive logging-policy support and adequate effective sample size; a deterministic action table with zero support cannot evaluate arbitrary alternatives; every report names overlap, clipping, estimator, sample size, and confidence assumptions (`FG-EVID-01`). (d) *Learning never directly touches the serving path* — continuous policies learn in shadow and deploy only as versioned deterministic tables; the deployed table inherits no universal guarantee by distillation. (e) *One regime clock* — all calibration windows and retune decisions key off a single changepoint detector (Bayesian online changepoint + Shiryaev–Roberts, §15.0) emitting logged regime-epoch IDs, so "policy changed because regime 47 began" is a replayable causal statement.

## Invariants & claim types
Deliberately no new invariants — the claim-type constitution is the content. Classes: the §17 byte-economy rows (metadata bytes per small durable object; Chronicle stream bytes per user commit; identity-column bytes per live edge by tier) and the tier-migration churn row (promote/demote reversals per descriptor, minimum-dwell violations **must be zero**, conversion-cost regret, soak limit cycles — SPRT type-I/II bounds apply only to declared decision hypotheses, never as reversal-rate bounds) are benchmark class. `FG-CAL-01`: adaptive policy vs pinned fallback requires null/outcome filtration, alpha, support/overlap, effective sample size, loss, and fallback, with stream-sequenced promotion only. `FG-EVID-01`: decision-card/OPE completeness. `FG-EVID-03`: endurance evidence — compaction-debt ceiling stated in §6.6 model terms, long-run memory-stability bound, occupancy-model prediction vs observation. `FG-CFG-02`: controller stability with predicted margin and soak results.

## Interactions
Consumes byte counters instrumented in `w3-tier-d`, `w3-tier-r`, `w3-properties`, `w3-seal-compact`; the identity-column metric from `w3-identity-encoding`; Appendix G operation classes and the same-change CI law from `g0-cost-registry` (§17 law 6: any change adding per-object identity structure updates the registry in the same change); SPRT/e-process/changepoint machinery from `w1-sketch-calibrate`. Produces: decision cards consumed by `w3-seal-compact` and tier migration; breakdown reports consumed by `perf-bench-core`, `perf-bench-scale`, `obs-slo`, and `verif-sextant` (FG-CAL row wiring).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Unit: amplification arithmetic on synthetic workloads with known byte flows; the component breakdown must sum to the total (CI assertion). Decision-card completeness checker: every migration in a soak run has a card with all six fields; a missing field fails CI. Dwell-guard test: an adversarial oscillating workload produces zero minimum-dwell violations even while SPRT evidence flip-flops (guard dominates model). E-process reversion drill: injected assumption violation reverts to fallback through a logged `DecisionPolicyEpoch`. Regime-clock test: two controllers observing the same injected changepoint log the identical regime-epoch ID. Endurance wiring: the 2h merge-to-main and 24h nightly runs report debt bytes and generation count against the ceiling; exceeding it fails the run even when point latencies pass. Disclosure check: every adaptive report names its policy epoch and publishes the fallback's number beside it (§17 law 5). E2e script: run the shared endurance fixture end-to-end (ingest, seal/compact churn, forced migrations), then regenerate the write/space-amplification report solely from the emitted event logs and assert it matches the live report exactly — accounting must be reconstructible from the log stream alone. Detailed logging (mandatory, asserted by the tests): every accounted physical write logs {component(forward|reverse|properties|constraint_index|optimizer_index|checkpoint|FEC|staging_waste|merge_level_k), bytes, tier}; every migration logs the six decision-card fields plus {descriptor_key, sprt_state, dwell_remaining, DecisionPolicyEpoch, regime_epoch_id}; identity-column metrics log {tier, bytes_per_live_edge, reverse_family_flag}; e-process reversions log {policy, evidence_state, fallback_epoch}.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: universal write-amp constants (workload-dependent by nature); online learning on the serving path; counterfactual claims without positive support; SPRT bounds marketed as reversal-rate bounds. Risks: counter overhead on hot paths (sharded/relaxed counters, cost measured); model-fetishism (the deterministic guards are unconditional by design).

## Provenance
§6.6; §15.0; §17 (laws 2–6, byte-economy/endurance/churn rows); App F statistical-gate table; App G.

title: UPSTREAM asupersync: crashpack replay command is a placebo — nothing reads the emitted env vars, and libtest has no --seed flag
description: SimHarness I1, verified by construction against the pinned checkout (e464a48). src/trace/crashpack.rs:898-933 (ReplayCommand::from_config) emits ASUPERSYNC_WORKERS=N ASUPERSYNC_MAX_STEPS=M cargo test --lib -- --seed S [--crashpack P]; the rerun hints (src/lab/runtime.rs:3121-3144, asupersync-macros/src/lab_test.rs:526-529,656-658) say ASUPERSYNC_LAB_TEST_SEED=S cargo test <name>. PROOF: grep over the whole pinned tree — NOTHING reads ASUPERSYNC_LAB_TEST_SEED / ASUPERSYNC_WORKERS / ASUPERSYNC_MAX_STEPS / ASUPERSYNC_SEED (only writers and docs reference them; docs/replay-debugging.md:176 documents the phantom override). Seeds are compile-time macro attributes (lab_test.rs:230 for __asupersync_seed in #start..#end). Worse: libtest has no --seed flag, so the emitted command exits 'Unrecognized option' before running anything; --lib misses the integration-test targets fgdb actually uses; and the pack records neither test name nor code commit (runtime.rs:1457-1464 sets commit_hash: None; CrashPackConfig has no test-name field).
