title: Specify AnswerRequirement/AnswerContract typing with freshness and transfer totality
description:
## What & scope
Define and implement the three deliberately different approximation phase types — execution-time `AnswerRequirement`, definition-time `ApproximationProfile`, and realized `AnswerContract` — plus the orthogonal freshness constraint and the transfer-totality law every GLA operator must satisfy. This is the semantic typing that makes every realized logical stream carry an honest exactness/approximation/freshness claim.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5/B6: agents must be able to demand exactness, permit qualified approximation, or bound derived-source staleness — and get a typed, replayable answer either way. The market failure this fixes: ANN/vector and stale-view systems that silently return approximate or lagging data as if exact. Freshness is expressed in watermark units precisely so no time-authority observation joins the hot read path (Appendix G cost discipline).

## Design — normative detail
`AnswerRequirement = Exact | AllowApproximate { permitted_kinds[], population_constraint?, minimum_quality?, evidence_floor, on_unmet: ExactFallback|Fail }` is an execution-time demand and contains no chosen generation. Default is `Exact`; any query-language approximation clause narrows the requirement and an empty intersection is rejected at binding. An `AnswerRequirement` may additionally carry an optional orthogonal `freshness_constraint: FreshnessConstraint { maximum_source_lag: WatermarkLagBound, on_unmet: ExactFallback|Fail }`, bounding how far any consumed advancing derived source generation (view, index, or maintainer output) may lag the executing snapshot's pinned read frontier; the bound is expressed in source-generation/watermark (commit-sequence) units, never as a wall-clock quantity. An unmet freshness bound behaves exactly like an unmet approximation demand — `ExactFallback` evaluates through the pinned exact path against the read frontier and `Fail` rejects with a typed error — and the realized `AnswerContract` already pins `source_generation_identities[]`, from which the realized lag is derived and reported in the result certificate without any new contract field. The reserved freshness fields (here and `SubscriptionDeliveryPolicy`) are a frozen G0 decision.

`ApproximationProfile { approximation_kind, population_contract, algorithm_profile_oid, semantic_build_and_search_parameter_schema, quality_evidence_schema, deterministic_exact_fallback_oid? }` is definition-time policy and likewise contains no generation identity. Only after access paths and parameters are bound does execution realize `AnswerContract = Exact | Approximate { approximation_kind, population_contract, error_or_recall_contract, source_generation_identities[], source_generation_digests[], algorithm_profile_oid, candidate_and_search_profile, evidence_identity, deterministic_fallback_oid? }`. A contract never strongly references the generation that carries it; the surrounding bound plan, generation registry, result/certificate envelope, and replay closure own concrete roots explicitly, avoiding definition/generation identity cycles.

Every realized logical stream is typed with an `AnswerContract` — a semantic type, not a certificate footnote. Transfer totality: each operator registers a total transfer rule that produces a contract satisfying the `AnswerRequirement`, proves exact completion, invokes the pinned exact fallback, or rejects the composition. Absence-sensitive, non-monotone, recursive, aggregate, distinct, and top-k operations cannot turn missing candidates into an exact result; they accept approximate inputs only under a registered sound calculus and otherwise fall back or fail. `Mutate` and every `Exact` requirement consume exact inputs only. All approximation-affecting generation topology, candidate/search depth, fusion, stopping, sampling, and evidence identities are pinned in the bound query/plan/certificate/replay closure and are never classified as result-neutral physical tuning. An approximate result remains byte-replayable under its pinned closure but is not thereby promoted to exact semantics. The `AnswerContract` surface additionally carries per-class delivery-behavior rows: §13's `SnapshotQuery` read class registers its `AnswerContract` behavior row recording non-resumable, no-replay, no-durable-outcome semantics — what that class gives up (durable outcome lookup, idempotent retry joining, result resume, replay evidence, exactly-once delivery) is part of the declared class contract, not an implementation weakness — and `w10-snapshotquery` consumes exactly this row (frozen in the G0 decision batch by `g0-format-arms`).

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12: every answer-equivalent rewrite preserves the `AnswerContract`; approximate candidate/topology changes create a new pinned semantic generation. FG-EVID-04 (slo-class, never an invariant): derived-state freshness bounds in watermark/commit-sequence units with realized lag distribution and typed `FreshnessBreach` rate. FG-CAL-03: ANN recall/drift evidence (population, keyed sample, exact baseline, candidate policy, confidence interval, rebuild action). Per the claim-type constitution, freshness/recall numbers are slo/benchmark/evidence class; the typing and transfer laws themselves are invariant-class.

## Interactions
`w5-binder` intersects caller requirement with language clauses; `w5-gla-algebra` registers the per-operator transfer rules (Appendix C answer-contract column); `w5-planner` may not trade contracts for cost; `w5-replay` pins realized contracts in manifests; `w6-freshness` implements `WITH FRESHNESS` and `FreshnessBreach` on this foundation; `w7-vector`/`w7-hybrid` realize `Approximate` contracts with recall evidence; `w10-result-machines` serializes contracts into certificates; `w10-snapshotquery` consumes the registered `SnapshotQuery` behavior row.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Type-level tests: requirement/profile contain no generation identity (compile-time or registry check); contract carries no strong ref to its carrying generation. Empty requirement-intersection rejection test. Unmet-freshness behavior differential: `ExactFallback` result byte-equals the pinned exact path against the read frontier; `Fail` returns the typed error — executable once the downstream realizers land (`w5-executor` for the exact path, `w6-freshness` for the freshness surface; both are epic-w5/gate-g1 prerequisites that depend on this bead), while at this bead the `on_unmet` arms are enforced as type-level/registry contracts. Transfer-totality checker over the operator registry: every registered operator has a total rule (CI fails on gaps). Certificate reports realized source lag derived from `source_generation_identities[]` with no new field. Fuzz: adversarial requirement/profile combinations never produce an unqualified `Exact` from approximate inputs. E2E script (runs once `w5-executor`/`w6-freshness` land — an epic-w5 closure prerequisite, since the realizing beads depend on this one): same query under `Exact`, `AllowApproximate`, and freshness-bounded requirements, logging realized contract, fallback decisions, and lag.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: approximation as a certificate footnote; wall-clock freshness bounds (would force time-authority observations onto the hot read path); contracts strongly referencing their generation (identity cycles); "best effort" transfer rules (partial rules make operators silently unavailable-as-exact). Risk: registered sound calculi for approximate-input operators are research-adjacent — the fallback/reject arms keep the system honest when no calculus exists.

## Provenance
Plan §8.3 (690–692), G0 decision batch (line 1313), Appendix F FG-EVID-04/FG-CAL-03.

title: Build fgdb-bind: PreparedQueryTemplate, BoundQuery, and CanonicalStatementClassification
description:
## What & scope
Build `fgdb-bind`: name/scope and correlated-reference resolution, deterministic role assignment, group variables, parameter inference/coercion, null and duplicate semantics, graph/table shape checking, path legality/termination, capability-domain injection, and incrementalizability classification; the `PreparedQueryTemplate`/`BoundQuery` pipeline; PREPARE as an authorized idempotent child operation; and the immutable `CanonicalStatementClassification` including bind-time `SnapshotQuery` and fused-autocommit class selection.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B3/B6: preparation must never freeze an execution option it never received, `@now` must never be mistaken for a permanent head, and clients (agents) declare ceilings and expectations — never the semantic class. Server-derived classification is what makes admission, authorization, witnesses, and retry semantics trustworthy: a write-capable semantic no-op stays write-classified because those semantics cannot be inferred from the final zero effect. Bind-time class selection is also what makes the `SnapshotQuery` fast read class (§17: ≥8M lookups/s, p99 < 15µs warm) honest rather than a client-claimed bypass.

## Design — normative detail
`fgdb-bind` first constructs `PreparedQueryTemplate { language_contract_oid, catalog_contract, graph_reference_specs[{binding_role_id, graph_id, branch_selector, system_selector_spec, valid_selector_spec, required_schema_contract}], parameter_types, non_widenable_authority_ceiling, typed_logical_template, output_schema_contract }`. At each execution the caller supplies an `AnswerRequirement` (default `Exact`); any query-language approximation clause narrows it and an empty intersection is rejected. After parameters and both temporal selectors are known, snapshot acquisition resolves every spec into a concrete `GraphReferenceBinding`; binding then produces `BoundQuery<Role> {prepared_template_ref:StrongRef<PreparedQueryTemplate>, logical_state_root_identity:WeakStateIdentity, graph_reference_bindings[], normalized_valid_time_bindings[], topology_epoch, authority_binding:AuthorityBindingFor<Role>, authority_binding_body_digest, purpose_class, answer_requirement, instantiated_logical_plan, output_schema}`. Prepared handles pin the template and may be reused only while its catalog/schema compatibility predicates hold under same-or-narrower authority. Physical/logical plan-cache entries, certificates, and replay pin the concrete `BoundQuery`; their key includes the binding body digest, purpose, role, and service epoch — and per §4.2 the per-coordinate schema binding is part of snapshot identity and of every plan-cache key, so prepared plans invalidate precisely rather than consulting one ambient epoch. A cross-authority, cross-graph, historical, or valid-time self-join plan cannot substitute one reference's authority/head/schema/period for another. Optimizers consume only this bound typed IR.

Preparation is itself an authorized, idempotent child operation because even parameter/output schemas can reveal protected catalog facts; the complete PREPARE protocol — `SessionAuthorityBinding`, `PrepareRequestRecord`, `PreparedStatementRecord`, the scoped idempotency index, the `PublicFrameSendGuard::PreparedMetadata` revalidation, EXECUTE handle/state-token resolution, and session-drain fencing — is specified and implemented in the split-out subtask `w5-prepare-protocol`; this bead supplies the template and classification objects that protocol freezes.

Classification: `TxnOperationCeiling = ReadOnlyOnly | ReadWriteAllowed` (client-declared). `CanonicalMutationPotential = ProvenReadOnly | MayMutateGraph | MayMutateSchema | MayInvokeReplicatedProcedure`; `CanonicalOutputClass = NoRows | Rows`; derived `CanonicalStatementClass` is `ReadOnly{output}` only for ProvenReadOnly, `WriteReturning` for any mutation potential + Rows, `WriteNoResult` for any mutation potential + NoRows. `CanonicalStatementClassification` is the immutable binder object `{classification_version, prepared_template_ref, bound_query_ref, prepared_template_digest, canonical_bound_query_digest, parameter_digest, language_contract_oid, binder_and_normalizer_semantics_oid, exact_graph_reference_bindings, exact_write_coordinate_set, sorted_procedure_udf_module_effect_contract_refs[StrongRef<ExecutableEffectContract>], mutation_potential, output_class, derived_statement_class, required_txn_operation_ceiling, required_warden_operation_classes, determinism_and_external_effect_profile, classification_digest:BodyDigest<CanonicalStatementClassification>}`, constructed after parameters, graph roles, schemas, modules/procedures, and temporal selectors resolve and before statement registration. Every executable artifact has one immutable bounded effect contract; parameters cannot choose an undeclared class. The generated statement-kind matrix maps every bound-IR tag and effect-contract arm to exactly one mutation/output row; unknown tags, wildcard fallback, or an unclassified procedure fail binding. Attempt registration stores only the client ceiling; statement registrations, intent batches, audit bases, authorization decisions, owner/result selection, workspace generations, and idempotent request digests all name the same classification. Workspace generation zero starts `cumulative_mutation_potential=ProvenReadOnly`; publication takes the monotone join — a mutation-capable statement can never be reclassified away. A class exceeding the attempt ceiling rejects before storage observation. Read-close is legal only from cumulative ProvenReadOnly. Rebase regenerates effects/results but cannot reinterpret the stored classification; exact retry returns the stored classification across ambient schema/policy/module drift, while a newly bound different class conflicts under the old idempotency key.

`SnapshotQuery` eligibility is bind-time and policy-driven, never a client verb: a statement is eligible exactly when its classification proves ProvenReadOnly single-statement autocommit within the class's declared output/row/time bounds, the effective `AuditCompletenessProfile` does not name the operation class Required, the classification carries no DP or Warden-classified operation class (`required_warden_operation_classes` empty, ordinary `output_class`), and the namespace's registered class policy permits the class — a governed namespace may force every read onto the durable path. Under a Required-read profile eligibility fails closed with a typed, data-independent rejection steering to the durable class; silent upgrade is forbidden. Symmetrically, single-statement autocommit writes whose classification proves fused-arm eligibility select `LocalAutocommitWriteSpec` (owned by `w2-fused-autocommit`).

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-20: authorization precedes every observation — PREPARE is itself authorized; `SnapshotQuery` admission performs coordinator-local verification of the complete capability and policy binding before any statement or storage observation, with the same oracle coverage as durable read classes. FG-INV-01: scoped idempotency — matching retries return recorded lineage, conflicting transitions fail. FG-INV-04: plan/snapshot identity includes per-coordinate schema binding. Classification correctness artifacts are invariant-class; eligibility-policy tables are configuration-class.

## Interactions
Consumes `w5-parsers` ASTs and `g0-language-contracts` OIDs; `g0-command-contracts` supplies registry rows for prepare/execute commands; `w2-snapshots-leases` supplies snapshot acquisition; `w4-secure-view` supplies authority bindings; `w5-prepare-protocol` implements the PREPARE lifecycle over this bead's objects. Produces the classification consumed by `w2-txn-lifecycle`, `w2-fused-autocommit`, `w10-snapshotquery` (the `LocalSnapshotQuery` admission arm binds `classification_ref`), `w5-intent-log`, `w5-planner`, and `w9-enforcement`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Generated malicious-underclassification tests covering every GQL/openCypher tag, subquery, DDL, mutating CALL/UDF/module, output/no-output form, dynamic graph role, adapter, and PREPARE-versus-EXECUTE_TEXT path. Ceiling-exceed rejects before storage observation (verified by observation-order instrumentation). SnapshotQuery eligibility negatives: DP class, nonempty `required_warden_operation_classes`, Required audit profile, forbidding namespace policy — each returns the typed data-independent rejection. Plan-cache key tests: schema-epoch change on one bound coordinate invalidates exactly the affected entries. E2E: prepare/execute/retry script logging classification digest, ceiling, and selected class per statement.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: client-declared statement class (unauditable); inferring class from realized effects (retry/admission semantics need the a-priori class); a session-level authority ref instead of the explicit `SessionAuthorityBinding` union. Risk: the statement-kind matrix must stay total as the grammar grows — enforced by fail-on-unknown-tag and generated coverage.

## Provenance
Plan §8.1 (664–672), §13 item 3 (SnapshotQuery eligibility, line 1025), §5.2 fused-arm eligibility (line 403), §4.2 (205), Appendix A `ReadAccessAdmissionRecord` (line 2619).

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement branch-aware base+delta StatsSegments with security-inheriting fallback
description:
## What & scope
Implement the optimizer's statistics plane with per-branch coverage: versioned `StatsSegment`s, the base+delta branch model pinned at fork boundaries, lazily instantiated per-branch delta maintainers riding Ripple, the explicit ordered staleness/fallback lattice, and fail-closed security composition.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1: 10k live branches must be cheap — a fork that copied statistics (or eagerly spawned maintainers) would make branch creation O(statistics) and idle branches expensive; instead a fork costs nothing until the planner first asks. B4: the delta layer is Ripple's own machinery — §9.6's degree/label statistics maintainers are exactly how StatsSegments stay fresh. B5: every rung of the lattice is recorded evidence; statistics degrade plan quality, never correctness.

## Design — normative detail
Statistics are versioned `StatsSegment`s with a branch/schema/policy watermark: label/type counts, authorized degree histograms, property sketches, zone maps, and sampled path correlations. Plans may use only statistics whose security domain cannot reveal hidden population information; otherwise they use capability-specific projections or conservative public bounds. Shrinkage, unseen-mass floors, robust estimators, influence caps, and targeted synopsis refresh are candidate estimators evaluated on named workloads; their risk properties are conditional on their model/population and never promoted into semantic invariants.

Per-branch coverage is base+delta: a fork does not copy statistics but pins a shared ancestor-base segment at the branch manifest's `fork_boundary_logical_command_seq`, and branch-delta segments are derived from exactly the branch's post-fork divergence. The delta layer rides Ripple's existing Z-set consumption (§9.6), and per-branch delta maintainers are instantiated lazily on first planner demand, never eagerly at fork. The staleness/fallback lattice is explicit and ordered: (1) exact per-branch segment, (2) base+delta composition, (3) the ancestor watermark with a typed staleness annotation, (4) the conservative public bounds — and a plan records which rung it consumed. Security composition fails closed: a branch-delta segment inherits the most restrictive security domain of any contributing segment or degrades to the public bounds, because a branch-delta correction must never reveal a hidden population that the base segment lawfully concealed. Statistics remain non-semantic on every rung — ancestor fallback degrades plan quality, never correctness — and per-branch segment/maintainer cost is a declared parameter of §5.6's 10k-branch gate.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-20 (restated): authorization precedes observation across statistics — a hidden population lawfully concealed by the base segment stays concealed through every delta composition. Estimator risk properties are FG-CAL-02-adjacent evidence (population/window/strata/coverage disclosures), never invariants. Maintainer staleness is a §9.6 staleness contract surfaced in certificates (slo-class per FG-EVID-04 discipline); the 10k-branch churn cost is a benchmark-class gate parameter and feeds the FG-CFG-04 maintenance-stream capacity model.

## Interactions
`w5-planner` consumes segments and records the rung; `w2-branch-fork` supplies the branch manifest and `fork_boundary_logical_command_seq`; `w6-delta-consumption` supplies the Z-set delta stream the maintainers consume; `w6-maintainers` hosts the degree/label maintainer family; `w1-sketch-calibrate` supplies sketch/estimator machinery; `perf-bench-scale` runs the 10k-branch churn gate; `w9-enforcement` defines the security domains statistics inherit.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Fork-cost test: creating a branch performs zero statistics copying and spawns zero maintainers (instrumented allocation/task counters); first planner demand instantiates the delta maintainer exactly once (idempotent under concurrent demand). Lattice tests: with the delta maintainer lagging, plans consume rung 3 with the typed staleness annotation; with it absent, rung 4; rung consumed is present in the plan record/decision card. Security negatives: construct a base segment concealing a population from capability C; verify that no branch-delta composition observable under C reveals counts/histograms distinguishable from the public-bounds answer (statistical-distance check in the test harness, logged). Correctness differential: identical query results across all four rungs (only plans differ). Bench: 10k-branch churn gate with per-branch maintainer memory/CPU cost reported as the declared gate parameter; maintainer freshness (watermark lag) distribution logged. E2E script: fork a branch, run the same planner-costed query on parent and child before divergence, apply post-fork commits, then re-plan with the delta maintainer (a) absent, (b) lagging, (c) caught up, asserting identical query results throughout; the script logs per plan the branch, rung consumed, staleness annotation, security domain of every consumed segment, and maintainer instantiation/watermark events — the implementation must emit these as structured events so rung selection is auditable after the fact.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: copy-on-fork statistics (O(branches) space, stale immediately); eager per-fork maintainers (10k idle branches saturate the maintenance stream — exactly what FG-CFG-04 prices); allowing a "more accurate" delta correction to bypass the base segment's security domain (fails closed instead). Risk: lattice rung flapping under churn — mitigated by recording the rung per plan so quality regressions are attributable.

## Provenance
Plan §8.5 statistics bullet (702), §9.6 (806–810), §5.6 10k-branch gate, FG-CFG-04.

title: Engine WriteBatch lands CompareAndSet (NoOp | AbortWrite)
description:
Land CompareAndSet on the engine WriteBatch: the two policies a single atomic write can honestly mean.

## Background
`fgdb-reference` reduces `CompareAndSet` under Appendix B's mismatch trichotomy (`NoOp | StatementError | TxnAbort`). The trichotomy is invisible at the effect level — the cases differ in what SURVIVES. The engine `WriteBatch` is one atomic write, not a multi-statement transaction. It cannot distinguish `StatementError` (discard this statement, keep earlier ones) from `TxnAbort` (discard everything). Offering `StatementError` on WriteBatch would be a substitute.

This bead is the live subset: `compare_and_set_vertex_property` / `compare_and_set_edge_property` with `WriteMismatchPolicy::NoOp | AbortWrite`. `AbortWrite` refuses before D2 and names expected vs actual. `NoOp` emits no row and the rest of the batch continues. Same-value success is a no-op. Read-your-own-writes use the existing batch-prefix overlay.

It does **not** land `StatementError`, txn statement boundaries, or the intent log. Do **not** parent-child this to open `94z`, `819`, or `mhae`. Related to `819` and `94z`. Closing this does not close them.

## Technical Approach
- Public `WriteMismatchPolicy { NoOp, AbortWrite }` on `fgdb`. Do not import `fgdb-reference`. Do not name an arm `StatementError`.
- `WriteError::CompareAndSetMismatch { elem, name, expected, actual }` — only `AbortWrite` produces it, and only before anything durable.
- Unknown element is `UnknownVertex` / `UnknownEdge`, same as `set_*_property`.
- Prefix overlay: a CAS after a `set_*_property` in the same batch sees the prefix value.
- A mismatch under `NoOp` is `continue` (no row), matching ensure-noop.

## Success Criteria
- Matching expected writes the new value.
- Same-value match emits no property change (graph unchanged).
- `AbortWrite` on mismatch is `CompareAndSetMismatch` naming both values; nothing durable; graph unchanged.
- `NoOp` on mismatch leaves the property and lets a sibling create in the same batch commit.
- Same-batch set-then-CAS against the new value succeeds (read-your-own-writes).
- Independent differential vs reference `CompareAndSet` (`NoOp` / `TxnAbort`) agrees on the graph.
- `cargo test -p fgdb --test spine` exit 0; `cargo test -p fgdb-sim --test spine_differential` exit 0; clippy `-D warnings` on `fgdb` and `fgdb-sim` exit 0.
- `94z` and `819` stay open.

## Test Plan
- Spine: match, same-value, AbortWrite mismatch, NoOp mismatch + sibling write, same-batch RYW, unknown vid. Assertions name elem, key, expected, actual, policy.
- Differential: independent engine vs reference histories for match, AbortWrite/TxnAbort miss, and NoOp miss.

## Considerations
- `StatementError` waits on `fgdb-w2-txn-lifecycle-mhae`. Do not map it to AbortWrite under the reference name.
- CAS sets a value; it does not unset. Removal stays `set_*_property(..., None)`.
acceptance_criteria: match writes; AbortWrite names both values and does not commit; NoOp continues the batch; same-batch RYW; spine + spine_differential exit 0; 94z and 819 stay open
close_reason: WriteBatch compare_and_set_vertex/edge_property with WriteMismatchPolicy::NoOp|AbortWrite. AbortWrite is CompareAndSetMismatch before D2. No StatementError arm. cargo test -p fgdb --test spine exit 0 (37 passed). cargo test -p fgdb-sim --test spine_differential exit 0 (13 passed, including compare_and_set_agrees_independently_with_the_reference). clippy -D warnings on fgdb and fgdb-sim exit 0. 94z and 819 stay open.

title: Engine WriteBatch lands delete-if-present without changing delete_*
description:
Land idempotent delete-if-present on the engine WriteBatch. Do not change `delete_*`.

## Background
`fgdb-reference` reduces `DeleteVertex` / `DeleteEdge` of a missing identity to nothing: a delete is a statement about the end state, and that state is already what was asked for. The engine `delete_vertex` / `delete_edge` refuse `UnknownVertex` / `UnknownEdge` before D2. That refusal is load-bearing — spine pins it — and must stay.

This bead is the live subset: `delete_vertex_if_present` / `delete_edge_if_present`. Live identity deletes as today (including cascade). Absent or already-deleted emits no row. Named `if_present` so it cannot be mistaken for a silent change to `delete_*`.

It does **not** land the intent log, statement boundaries, or a change to the Unknown* contract. Do **not** parent-child this to open `94z` or `819`. Related to both. Closing this does not close them.

## Technical Approach
- Add `if_present: bool` on the existing DeleteVertex / DeleteEdge pending rows. `delete_*` stays `false`.
- At preflight, `if_present && !live_now` is `continue` (no row). `if_present == false` still `Unknown*`.
- Cascade and before-images for a live if-present delete are the same path as `delete_*`.
- A batch of only missing if-present deletes folds to an empty net and still commits (same as create+delete cancel / ensure-noop-only).

## Success Criteria
- `delete_vertex` of a missing vid is still `UnknownVertex` and consumes no sequence.
- `delete_vertex_if_present` of a live vid retires it (and incident edges).
- `delete_vertex_if_present` of a missing or already-deleted vid is not `UnknownVertex`.
- Same pair for edges.
- Independent differential vs reference `DeleteVertex`/`DeleteEdge` of missing identities agrees on the graph.
- `cargo test -p fgdb --test spine` exit 0; `cargo test -p fgdb-sim --test spine_differential` exit 0; clippy `-D warnings` on `fgdb` and `fgdb-sim` exit 0.
- `94z` and `819` stay open.

## Test Plan
- Spine: existing Unknown* law still holds; if-present live delete works; if-present missing is not Unknown*; if-present after delete is not Unknown*; sibling write in the same batch as a missing if-present still commits. Assertions name vid/eid and the error arm.
- Differential: engine if-present-missing + sibling create vs independent reference Delete of missing + create.

## Considerations
- Do not weaken `delete_*`. A grep of UnknownVertex in spine must stay red on a second `delete_vertex`.
- Spent vs never-existed are the same for if-present: not live, no-op. Ensure still refuses spent on create; delete-if-present has nothing to resurrect.
acceptance_criteria: delete_* still Unknown*; if_present live deletes; if_present missing is not Unknown*; spine + spine_differential exit 0; 94z and 819 stay open
close_reason: WriteBatch::delete_vertex_if_present and delete_edge_if_present are live. delete_* still Unknown* and consume no sequence. cargo test -p fgdb --test spine exit 0 (38 passed). cargo test -p fgdb-sim --test spine_differential exit 0 (14 passed, including delete_if_present_agrees_independently_with_the_reference). clippy -D warnings on fgdb and fgdb-sim exit 0. 94z and 819 stay open.

title: Enforce CGSE determinism: semantic/scalar profiles, tie-breaks, canonical result encoding
description:
## What & scope
Implement the query-level determinism contracts (CGSE): versioned `SemanticProfile`s, `CanonicalScalarProfile` with `STRICT_PORTABLE`, numeric execution profiles, tie-break policies, and the §8.8 canonical result encoding (`CanonicalResultChunk`/`CanonicalResultChunkDescriptor`). The strict contract: within the pinned evidence closure, the same query produces a byte-identical canonical result encoding — across parallelism, spill, factorization, safe replanning, and supported hardware.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5: determinism is the substrate for replay (FG-INV-19), differential testing, caching, and agent trust — an agent comparing two runs must see identical bytes or a named contract difference, never scheduler noise. B6: canonical result digests are what certificates, subscriptions, and idempotent retries compare. Where GQL leaves latitude (result ordering, path enumeration order, duplicate semantics under morphism modes), FrankenGraphDB pins behavior and documents each pin.

## Design — normative detail
Each pin set is a versioned `SemanticProfile` referenced from `LanguageContract` — never an ambiguous bare name like `gql-2024-strict` — fixing null/UNKNOWN handling, duplicate semantics per morphism mode, ordering defaults, coercion rules, and tie-break bindings. Two results are comparable only under the same language+semantic+scalar contracts; corrigendum/dialect drift becomes a new content-addressed artifact. Temporal clauses get algebraic semantics: snapshot-relativized pattern matching; `BETWEEN` yields per-binding validity intervals with interval-algebra predicates.

`CanonicalScalarProfile` defines equality, hashing, total ordering, collation, coercion, and durable/result encoding for every value, with property tests enforcing equal implies same_hash, comparator totality/transitivity, and encode/decode/order coherence. `STRICT_PORTABLE` canonicalizes NaNs and signed zero; fixes decimal scale/rounding/overflow; stores timestamp instant, zone/offset semantics, and a content-addressed tzdb version; pins Unicode data/normalization/segmentation and each non-binary collation by ObjectId; fixes map-key order over canonical bytes; and rejects unavailable profile artifacts rather than consulting host locale/tzdb. Floating execution uses fixed logical reduction trees independent of SIMD width, fixes denormal/rounding behavior, forbids target-dependent contraction, and uses pinned math kernels. A scalar/SIMD fast path ships in strict mode only after bit-identity testing on every supported target; otherwise it is RELAXED and the certificate names target/build behavior.

Tie-breaks: every query declares a tie-break policy; the strict default is storage-independent `LexMin` over canonical scalar/element encodings. `ORDER BY` wins. `InsertionOrder` is defined as immutable element-origin order and is available only when elements carry durable `OriginBirthOrder {commit_seq, intent_ordinal, merge_ordinal, element_id}`; `BranchAdmissionOrder` is a separately named policy. Compaction/run order never defines either. `fnx-parity` is an explicit projection profile with its own adjacency-order metadata. Parallelism, spilling, factorization, and safe replanning must preserve the canonical logical row sequence or require RELAXED posture.

Result delivery (§8.8): streaming begins only at an operator's declared safe emission point. Two-phase channel obligations provide bounded backpressure; output-row/byte, egress, idle-time, and snapshot-age reservations prevent a slow client from holding unbounded resources. The canonical result digest covers schema, canonical values, multiplicity, and logical order before framing. Factorized frames encode a canonical logical factorization DAG — not Strata run references — and clients may request flat frames without changing result identity. `CanonicalResultChunk` is the exact logical plaintext target `{format_version=1, canonical_encoding_version, chunk_ordinal, canonical_offset, canonical_len, frame_boundary_policy_oid, canonical_bytes:BoundedBytes<1_MiB>, body_digest}`: `canonical_len` equals the byte length, chunks are contiguous from offset zero, and every boundary lies between complete canonical value/row/factorization frames; an individual value above the v1 value bound is rejected before materialization rather than split ambiguously. `CanonicalResultChunkDescriptor` is the only outer owner of ciphertext identity and public chunk digest; its ordinal/offset/length/encoding fields must byte-match the decrypted target. The target has one `logical_object_kinds.toml` row, a registered BodyDigest transcript, exact 1 MiB plaintext and decoder-allocation bounds, golden vectors for flat/factorized/null/graph/scalar/extreme-value cases, mutation and truncation corpora, and a generated fuzz target. Decrypted protected-result buffers use the ordinary authority/send guard and are wiped on cancel, error, or final frame ownership transfer; no plaintext chunk, keyed ObjectId, or placement detail enters logs or crashpacks.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12 (restated): canonical scalar equality, hashing, and encoding are coherent; every answer-equivalent variant preserves values, multiplicity, order, visibility, security projection, `AnswerContract`. FG-INV-19 boundary: strict floating results use the portable profile; RELAXED results are reproducible only within their recorded target/build scope, and the certificate names it. Golden vectors and the scalar-law suite are oracle-class artifacts; the chunk kind row and BodyDigest transcript are registry (invariant-class) artifacts.

## Interactions
`w5-parsers`/`g0-language-contracts` reference SemanticProfile/scalar profile OIDs; `w5-executor` kernels obey the numeric profile and emission points; `w5-factorization` supplies the canonical logical factorization DAG whose transport encoding this bead canonicalizes; `w5-replay` compares canonical encodings before transport framing; `w2-txn-lifecycle` and `w5-intent-log` reuse `OriginBirthOrder` for `InsertionOrder`; `w10-result-machines`/`w10-snapshotquery` frame descriptors on the wire; `w1-crypto` supplies the encryption whose descriptor must byte-match; `obs-observatory` enforces the redaction rule.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Scalar-law property/fuzz suite (equal implies same_hash; totality/transitivity; encode/decode/order coherence). Cross-target strict bit-identity CI: every supported dispatch path and target produces identical canonical bytes for the numeric corpus; a fast path failing bit-identity is demoted to RELAXED, and the certificate-naming test verifies target/build disclosure. Tie-break differential: identical canonical row sequence across parallelism degrees, spill decisions, factorization choices, and legal replans; `InsertionOrder` unavailable-without-`OriginBirthOrder` negative. tzdb/locale hermeticity: host locale/tzdb mutation cannot change any result (sandbox test); unavailable profile artifact rejects. Chunk conformance: golden vectors (flat/factorized/null/graph/scalar/extreme-value); mutation and truncation corpora; generated fuzz target; oversized-value rejected before materialization; descriptor/target byte-match verification; buffer-wipe test on cancel/error/transfer; log/crashpack scan proving no plaintext chunk, keyed ObjectId, or placement detail escapes. E2E script: one seeded query executed across parallelism degrees 1/8/32 with forced spill and one legal replan, then in strict mode on two supported targets, asserting byte-identical `CanonicalResultChunk` sequences end-to-end; the run logs SemanticProfile and scalar-profile OIDs, tie-break policy, declared emission points, chunk ordinal/offset/length/digest per chunk, and any RELAXED-posture target/build disclosure. Detailed logging: determinism CI must emit structured per-run records (profile OIDs, target/build, per-chunk digests) sufficient to attribute any divergence to a named contract difference rather than scheduler noise.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: consulting host locale/tzdb (unpinnable); SIMD-width-dependent reductions (breaks bit-identity); defining InsertionOrder from run/compaction order (layout-dependent lies); putting result identity after framing (would make fetch size and wire factorization semantic). Risk: the strict fast-path test matrix is expensive — bounded by the supported-target list being explicit and small.

## Provenance
Plan §8.2 (676–681), §8.6 (711), §8.8 (727–731).

title: Implement the Diff operator family: DIFF syntax to coverage-qualified delta streams
description:
## What & scope
Implement the reserved `Diff{endpoint_a, endpoint_b, coverage_contract}` operator family owning §8.1's `DIFF` syntax: evaluation over same-branch and cross-branch endpoint pairs, coverage accounting against retention, authorization through both endpoint visibilities, and the canonical insertion/retraction delta-table output composable with views and subscriptions.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1/B6: "what changed between `main@yesterday` and `experiment@now`" is the core agent workflow primitive of the One Version Universe — branches and time are only useful if their difference is a first-class, typed, authorized query. B4: the DIFF-defined stream is a Z-set view, so subscriptions to a diff ride Ripple's ordinary incremental machinery. The G0 decision batch freezes the `DIFF` operator family row and its reserved syntax (`g0-format-arms`), so this is normative 1.0 surface, not an extra.

## Design — normative detail
Syntax (from `w5-parsers`, reserved under the FQL dialect discipline): `DIFF <graph_ref_a> … <graph_ref_b>` where each endpoint is an ordinary graph reference carrying the full `graph@branch AS OF <time|seq>` selector surface. Output: canonical delta tables — insertions/retractions with element identity, slice, and period columns — composable with views and §9.5 subscriptions like any other typed stream. The syntax reservation makes the operator available only after this row's conformance tests exist; evaluation, coverage, authorization, and answer-contract semantics are owned entirely by this Appendix C row.

Appendix C row (normative): memory/spill — streaming over ordered delta batches with registered spill for reordered or aggregated ranges. Incremental contract — same-branch endpoints integrate the retained `LogicalDeltaBatch` range, or scan the Tier 1 columnar logical-effect history (§5.4) for older intervals; cross-branch endpoints reuse the squash-merge evaluator's canonical logical difference against recorded merge bases (§5.6); the DIFF-defined stream is a Z-set view composing with §9.5 subscriptions. Replan/witness contract — batch/materialization boundary; the witness domain is both endpoints' visibility domains plus the covered commit range; evaluated only through `fgdb-secure-view` against both endpoint visibilities under authorization-precedes-observation (FG-INV-20) — a diff can reveal existence or retirement at one endpoint, so hidden elements follow the capability-redacted conflict-graph discipline. Answer-contract rule — emits canonical insertion/retraction delta tables with element identity, slice, and period columns; `Exact` only under complete retained coverage of the requested interval; otherwise a typed coverage-qualified `Approximate` contract whose population contract names the covered subrange; a proved retention cut inside the interval yields typed `HistoryUnavailable`, never silent partiality.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-20 (restated for this operator): authorization precedes every observation — coordinator verifies the complete capability/policy binding for *both* endpoint visibilities before any storage observation; hidden constraints follow one explicit disclosure contract. FG-INV-04: distinct branch heads or valid-time selectors never alias — the two endpoints resolve as independent graph-reference roles that cannot substitute authority/head/schema/period for each other. Coverage claims are answer-contract semantics (invariant-class typing); diff throughput is benchmark-class.

## Interactions
`w5-parsers` reserves syntax; `w5-gla-algebra` hosts the row; `w2-delta-batches` supplies the retained ordered `LogicalDeltaBatch` stream and the Tier 1 columnar history is a `w2-retention-checkpoints` retention product; `w2-branch-merge` supplies the squash-merge evaluator and recorded merge bases; `w4-secure-view` mediates both visibilities; `w6-zset-circuits`/`w6-subscriptions` consume the DIFF stream as a Z-set view; `w5-answer-contracts` types the coverage-qualified outputs.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Conformance tests exist before syntax activates (the parser's reserved-error flips only on this suite passing — verified in CI ordering). Differentials: (1) same-branch DIFF over a retained range byte-equals integration of the `LogicalDeltaBatch` range; (2) the same interval answered from Tier 1 columnar history byte-equals the batch-integration answer; (3) cross-branch DIFF byte-equals the squash-merge evaluator's canonical logical difference against the recorded merge base. Retention-cut test: KEEP-policy cut inside the requested interval yields typed `HistoryUnavailable`; a cut outside yields `Exact`; partial coverage yields `Approximate` naming the exact covered subrange. Authorization negatives: an element hidden at one endpoint is neither emitted nor inferable from output shape/count (uniform redaction discipline), tested against the obligation-leak oracle. Subscription e2e: subscribe to a DIFF view, drive commits on both branches, log per-delivery coverage contract, answer contract, and watermark; verify retraction weights on rollback-like history.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: diff as a client-side two-snapshot scan (O(graph), unauthorized inference risk, no coverage semantics); silent partial results when retention has cut history (the typed `HistoryUnavailable` arm exists precisely to forbid this); a separate diff-specific change format (reuses canonical logical deltas). Risk: cross-branch semantics depend on the squash-merge evaluator's difference definition — kept consistent by reusing that evaluator rather than re-implementing.

## Provenance
Plan §8.1 (659), Appendix C Diff row (2759), §5.4/§5.6 references, G0 batch (line 1313).

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement canonical effects, provenance envelopes, and NetEffectNormalForm
description:
## What & scope
Split from `w5-intent-log`: finalization's canonical effect vocabulary, `EffectProvenance`, the coordinate/global effect envelopes, `NetEffectNormalForm`, `CommittedEffectSet`, and the derivation of the sequence-neutral `LogicalDeltaTemplate`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B5/B4: effects are the single truth that storage application, Ripple deltas, merge re-evaluation, and audit all derive from — with explicit before/after images, so retraction (Z-set), time travel, and cascade auditing need no reconstruction. A closed effect vocabulary is what lets FG-INV-18 state "committed effects equal logical before/after state" as a checkable equation.

## Design — normative detail
Finalization evaluates all commands and emits only canonical effects: `CreateVertexEffect {permanent_vid, allocation_binding_or_finalization_proof, birth_ordinal, labels, canonical_props, valid_time_assignment}`; `DeleteVertexEffect {vid, complete_before_version, retirement_basis, sorted_retired_incident_edge_before_images[], sorted_constraint/temporal/escrow_contribution_retractions[]}`; `LabelMembershipEffect {vid, label, before, after}`; `CreateEdgeEffect {permanent_eid, allocation_binding_or_finalization_proof, birth_ordinal, src, type, dst, canonical_key?, props, valid_time_assignment}`; `DeleteEdgeEffect {eid, complete_before_version, retirement_basis, sorted_constraint/temporal/escrow_contribution_retractions[]}`; `PropertyEffect {elem, property, before, after}`; `ValidTimeEffect {elem, contract_id, before, after, before_version_identity, temporal_constraint_transition_refs[], witness_basis}`; `CounterEffect {operation_key, elem, property, algebra_profile, delta, before, after, overflow:Reject}`; `EscrowAdjustmentEffect {domain_id, epoch, operation_key, contribution_key?, elem_property_or_cardinality_subject, delta, before_value, after_value, consumed_reservation_refs[], produced_right_kind_and_amount, target_owner, conservation_basis_digest}`; `SketchEffect {operation_key, sketch_profile_oid, before_state_digest, after_state_ref, realized_answer_contract}`; `SchemaEffect {transition:CoordinateSchemaTransition, canonical_catalog_schema_constraint_index_operations[]}`; `ConstraintStateEffect {apply_basis, before_schema_root, before_schema_epoch, after_schema_root, after_schema_epoch, before_constraint_root, after_constraint_root, exact_removed_and_added_contributions[]}`; `ResourceChargeEffect {reservation_id, scope, before_charge, after_charge, reason}`.

Every effect carries `EffectProvenance {source_batch_ref:StrongRef<GraphIntentBatch>, source_intent_ordinal, source_statement_seq, source_coordinate_role, source_observation_commitment, merge_or_import_origin?, authorization_decision_digest, canonicalization_profile_oid}`. `CoordinateEffectEnvelope {coordinate:WriteCoordinateBinding, effect_ordinal, effect, provenance}` is the sole coordinate source, so nested effects cannot disagree. `GlobalEffectEnvelope` is the closed union `Resource{transition_ref, effect} | Audit{ticket_and_event_commitment} | AuthorityGlobalEscrow{domain_id, operation_summary_ref, effect}`; a coordinate effect cannot smuggle a global charge and a global effect cannot mutate graph state; resource and audit ownership are typed strong refs, never bare IDs or an English "handled elsewhere" promise. `NetEffectNormalForm` groups by coordinate and logical identity/key, cancels only inverse effects proved unobserved and algebraically cancellable, preserves create/delete before-images and all unique operation keys, sorts cascades/contributions canonically, and rejects two incompatible terminal values; it includes a proof mapping every source intent to its surviving effects or an explicit `NoOp{captured_basis, policy}` — no intent disappears implicitly. `CommittedEffectSet<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is `{authority_bound_header, intent_semantics_ref, ordered_source_batch_refs[], statement_observation_commitments[], net_effect_normal_form_ref, coordinate_effect_envelopes[], global_effect_envelopes[], complete_allocation_binding_commitment, constraint_temporal_escrow_evidence, authorization_decision_ref:StrongRef<AuthorizationDecisionRecord<Role>>, resource_transition_refs[], audit_ownership_commitment, body_digest}` — explicit before/after semantics, permanent IDs/BirthOrdinals, branch-aware retirement bases, full cascade before-images, no conditional operation; every child effect/provenance/resource reference must agree with the same complete authority binding (equal policy/revocation scalars under a different principal, purpose, ceiling, or service epoch are noninterchangeable). The sequence-neutral graph/branch/relation/schema/intent-semantics-keyed `LogicalDeltaTemplate` is derived from the normal form and differential-tested against applying the gap-free ordered batches once under the pinned `IntentSemanticsOid` to the recorded basis; create/delete/property/valid-time/counter/escrow/sketch/schema/constraint deltas are exact typed rows, and only the committed `MarkerRef` turns the template into an ordered `LogicalDeltaBatch`.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-18: canonical committed effects equal logical before/after state over normalized valid-time slices; workspace finalization equals ordered published statements. FG-INV-17: every semantic drift regenerates effects before final-certification reservation. FG-INV-02: escrow finite-side conservation equations hold at every transition (`conservation_basis_digest`). All invariant-class; the template-vs-batch differential is an oracle artifact.

## Interactions
Consumes `w5-intent-log` batches/observations; `w2-delta-batches` owns the Template/Batch canonical stream this bead feeds; effects applied by `w4-coordinator` and merged by `w4-merge-ladder`; `w6-delta-consumption` integrates the deltas; `w9-audit-pipeline` consumes provenance; `verif-reference` recomputes the before/after equation.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Differential: `LogicalDeltaTemplate` integration equals one-shot batch application under the pinned `IntentSemanticsOid` (byte-for-byte). The Appendix B fuzz campaign's effect half: delete/duplicate effects/provenance, reorder cascades, then compare normal form, committed effects, and integrated deltas byte-for-byte. Totality property: every source intent maps to surviving effects or explicit `NoOp` (mapping proof checked). Envelope negatives: a global charge inside a coordinate effect, a graph mutation inside a global effect, and a nested-effect coordinate disagreement each reject. Authority-agreement negatives: equal scalars with different principal/purpose/ceiling/service-epoch reject. E2E script: a multi-statement transaction with creates, cascading deletes, counter/escrow/sketch updates, and a `SchemaOp` runs end-to-end; the script logs per statement the emitted effect ordinals by arm, the normal-form mapping proof summary (each intent → surviving effects or `NoOp`), the `CommittedEffectSet` body digest, and the derived `LogicalDeltaTemplate` digest, then verifies template integration equals one-shot batch application. Detailed logging: finalization must log every cancellation decision (inverse pair plus its proved-unobserved basis) and every envelope rejection with its typed reason, so fuzz-campaign failures are attributable from logs alone.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: after-image-only effects (breaks retraction and audit); free-form cancellation in the normal form (only proved-unobserved, algebraically cancellable inverses cancel); bare-ID resource/audit ownership. Risk: cascade before-image volume on hub deletes — bounded by sorted canonical encoding and priced by §6.6, never by dropping images.

## Provenance
Plan Appendix B (2694–2733).

title: Live NetEffectNormalForm at reference commit (p6tm owner slice)
description:
Implement the live subset of NetEffectNormalForm at reference finalization so multi-write transactions can commit.

## Background
`fgdb-p6tm` is the absence of `fgdb-w5-effects-normal-form-819` showing up as a real commit failure. Evaluation emits effects in statement order (so `SET p=3; SET p=7` on a vertex whose property is 5 becomes `{before:5,after:3}` then `{before:3,after:7}`). `LogicalDeltaTemplate::build` then byte-sorts those rows. Byte order is a total order over encoded identity, not a topological order over before-images. When they disagree, `apply_template` refuses `PropertyBeforeMismatch`. Increasing chains sort safely by accident; decreasing-then-increasing chains never commit.

The 819 umbrella also asks for `CommittedEffectSet`, authority envelopes, and G0 identity registries. Those are blocked. Doctrine 7 allows a *subset* of the final abstraction, not a substitute. This bead is that subset: the fold 819 specifies for families that already exist as `ReferenceGraph` state. It is not a Property-only reorder, and it does not pretend the G0-blocked artifact has landed.

This bead is a child of `fgdb-w5-effects-normal-form-819`. It does **not** depend on `fgdb-g0-identity-registries-hrx`. Closing this bead does **not** close 819.

## Technical Approach
Do not rewrite evaluation-order rows in place. Diff the snapshot graph (durable before-image `apply_template` will see) against the workspace (after-image after every intent applied). Emit target-disjoint rows:

- Vertices/edges in workspace but not basis → one Create with the workspace payload (labels, props, valid-time already folded in).
- Vertices/edges in basis but not workspace → one Delete against the **basis** version and the **basis** cascade image. Intra-txn property writes must not appear beside that delete (sorter would apply delete first, and the workspace version is not the durable version).
- Create-then-delete of a fresh identity → emit nothing (inverse cancellation).
- Live elements whose props/labels/valid-time differ → one row per changed key, `{first before, last after}`. Identity chains (`before == after`) emit nothing.
- DeleteVertex cascade absorbs incident DeleteEdge rows; do not emit both.
- Counter/escrow/sketch/schema/constraint: emit only when the corresponding maps differ, using the first source row's operation key / contract identity. Do not invent keys.

Wire the fold in `Transaction::commit` **before** `LogicalDeltaTemplate::build`. Keep SSI write-set collection on the raw evaluation-order `self.effects` list; only the template payload is normalized. Report `WriteCommitted.effects` as the **net** row count (already anticipated by the mutation-capable no-op write-terminal tests).

Implementation lives in `crates/fgdb-reference/src/normal.rs` (`normalize(basis, workspace, source) -> NetEffectNormalForm` with a totality `mapping` from every source row to `Survives` or `NoOp{Identity|InverseCancellation|Absorbed}`).

## Success Criteria
- `SET p=3; SET p=7` after a basis value of 5 commits and the durable graph holds 7. One net Property row `{before:5, after:7}`.
- Create + SetProp in one txn commits as one Create whose payload is the workspace after-image.
- Create + SetProp + Delete of a fresh identity commits as a net no-op (0 rows; vertex absent).
- SetProp + Delete of an **existing** vertex commits as one Delete whose `before_version` is the basis version, not the workspace version.
- Existing SI / genesis / no-op write-terminal tests stay green. `a_statement_error_still_commits_the_rest` still reports 2 net effects for two different vertices.
- `cargo test -p fgdb-reference` exits 0. `cargo clippy -p fgdb-reference --all-targets -- -D warnings` exits 0.

## Test Plan
- Unit (`normal.rs`): chained property collapse; identity chain emits nothing; create+delete cancels; property-then-delete rewrites to basis version; create+property folds into create. Mapping totality asserted on each.
- E2E (`transaction_anomalies.rs`, through `Transaction::commit` / `apply_template`): `decreasing_then_increasing_property_chain_commits` (the p6tm probe); `create_set_delete_in_one_transaction_cancels`; `property_then_delete_of_existing_vertex_commits`; `create_then_set_commits_as_one_create`.
- Regression: full `fgdb-reference` suite (230 tests at implementation time).

## Considerations
- `apply_template` uses `apply_row_open` then one `finalize_statement_versions` per commit. Versions do **not** advance between template rows. A Delete that captured a workspace version after a same-txn Property will mismatch the durable basis even if applied in evaluation order. State-diff is what makes the before-image honest.
- Empty net (everything cancelled) still publishes a coordinate entry with zero rows and consumes the commit sequence. That is already the mutation-capable no-op write-terminal law.
- Engine `WriteBatch` in `crates/fgdb` still refuses `OrderSensitiveBatch` for a second write to the same `(elem, key)`. That is **out of scope** — file a sibling bead. Closing this bead does not claim the engine folds.
- 819 remaining (CommittedEffectSet, CoordinateEffectEnvelope, GlobalEffectEnvelope, authority-agreement negatives) stays on 819 and stays blocked on G0.
acceptance_criteria: SET p=3; SET p=7 after basis 5 commits as one Property{before:5,after:7}; create+set folds; create+set+delete cancels; property+delete uses basis version; cargo test -p fgdb-reference exits 0; 819 remains open
close_reason: Landed in crates/fgdb-reference/src/normal.rs; Transaction::commit diffs snapshot vs workspace before LogicalDeltaTemplate::build. cargo test -p fgdb-reference exit 0 including decreasing_then_increasing_property_chain_commits. clippy -D warnings 0. 819 stays open.

title: Fold NetEffectNormalForm into engine WriteBatch (replace OrderSensitiveBatch)
description:
Fold NetEffectNormalForm into the engine WriteBatch path so multi-write batches commit instead of refusing OrderSensitiveBatch.

## Background
The reference oracle now folds same-target writes at `Transaction::commit` (`fgdb-nenf-live-reference-*`). The production engine does not. `crates/fgdb/src/lib.rs` tracks `(elem, key)` touches in a batch and returns `WriteError::OrderSensitiveBatch` on a second write. That is a substitute convention beside 819: it makes the p6tm shape unrepresentable at the engine API rather than emitting canonical net effects.

An embedded `SET p=3; SET p=7` in one `WriteBatch` must commit with the same net as the reference path: one Property `{first before, last after}` applied against the durable snapshot. Refusing the second write is not the 819 design and is not what a GQL multi-statement transaction will produce once Loom lands.

This bead is a child of `fgdb-w5-effects-normal-form-819` and depends on the live reference fold so the engine can share the same before/after laws (or re-implement the same state-diff against the engine snapshot/writer). It does **not** require G0 identity registries.

## Technical Approach
Replace the `OrderSensitiveBatch` refusal with a fold at batch finalization, **before** `LogicalDeltaTemplate::build`.

Two acceptable implementations, in order of preference:

1. Lift `NetEffectNormalForm` types + the fold contract into `fgdb-delta-types` (or a tiny shared module the engine may call) and feed it the engine's prefix snapshot + in-batch after-image. Do not copy the algorithm by hand into `fgdb` if that creates two definitions of "net".
2. If sharing would pull `fgdb-reference` into the engine (forbidden: reference is test-only), put the fold in `fgdb-delta-types` as a pure function over two row lists / two content maps, and have both crates call it.

Preserve v3 statement-versioning (`fgdb-ge6a`): updates in one batch do not advance the version overlay; delete-after-update must CAS the **durable** before-version, not an intra-batch head. The reference fold already does this by reading the basis version. The engine must do the same.

Create-then-delete in one batch must cancel. Create-then-set must fold into the create payload. Two sets on different keys remain two rows.

Do **not** weaken `apply_template` before-image checks to make unsorted rows apply. The fold is the fix.

## Success Criteria
- A WriteBatch that does `set(v, p, 3)` then `set(v, p, 7)` on a live vertex with `p=5` commits. Reopen / snapshot read returns 7.
- The same batch produces one Property row in the committed template, not two, and not `OrderSensitiveBatch`.
- Create+set+delete of a fresh vertex in one batch is a net no-op.
- Set+delete of an existing vertex commits as one delete against the durable version.
- Existing engine e2e (`open_write_read_drop_reopen`, crash-at-any-instant, incremental snapshot) stay green.
- `cargo test -p fgdb` exits 0. clippy `-D warnings` on the crate exits 0.

## Test Plan
- Unit: batch builder fold table (two sets decreasing; two sets identity; create+set; create+set+delete; set+delete of live vertex). Log per case: input pending rows, net rows by arm, template digest.
- E2E: persist, drop, reopen, read the property. A crash between D1 and D2 still leaves all-or-nothing.
- Differential: the same intent sequence through `fgdb-reference::Transaction` and through `fgdb::WriteBatch` produce equal net row families (ignore version ObjectIds if the engine's transcript domain differs; compare before/after payloads).
- Negative: two creates of the same vid still refuse (`VertexAlreadyExists` / identity spent), not fold.

## Considerations
- `OrderSensitiveBatch` exists because an earlier engine path applied rows in sorted order without a fold. Removing the refusal without the fold re-opens p6tm in production.
- Do not report the engine as folding if the only change is renaming the error.
- Sharing code with the reference crate is not allowed. Sharing *types* in `fgdb-delta-types` is the intended layer.
- This does not land CommittedEffectSet or envelopes. Those remain on 819.
acceptance_criteria: WriteBatch set(p=3)+set(p=7) commits; one net Property row; create+set+delete is no-op; differential vs reference payloads; cargo test -p fgdb exits 0
close_reason: Finished the missing differential. Independent engine WriteBatch vs reference Transaction graph agreement in fgdb-sim::net_effect_fold_agrees_independently_with_reference_transactions. Also fixed cascade fold: same-batch created edges are stripped from DeleteVertex cascade; basis cascade edges stay. cargo test -p fgdb-sim --test spine_differential exit 0 (10/10); cargo test -p fgdb --test spine 32/32; clippy -D warnings 0.
