title: Build incremental analytics maintainers with staleness contracts and recompute fallback
description:
## What & scope
Host per-algorithm incremental maintainers in Ripple: delta-PageRank (residual propagation), incremental connected components (union-find plus bounded rebuild on deletes), incremental triangle/k-core counts, and degree/label statistics (how §8.5's `StatsSegment`s stay fresh). Each maintainer declares a staleness contract and a recompute fallback; the bounded-error class gets a calibrated recompute advisor.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
This directly answers the market's "derived state goes stale" complaint (§3.3 adapt verdict) — including for the vector/FTS indexes, whose ingestion pipelines (§10) are Ripple consumers too. B4 makes warm analytics a registered consumer of the same delta stream; B5 requires the contract be typed: exactness claims are structural, error bounds are deterministic or explicitly model-qualified, and statistical controllers only *advise*.

## Design — normative detail
For algorithm families with known delta algorithms, Ripple hosts maintainers that keep results warm under updates. Each maintainer declares a **staleness contract** — `exact | bounded-error(ε) | eventually-refreshed` — surfaced in query certificates; recompute via Prism is the universal fallback. For `bounded-error(ε)` maintainers, a conformal/risk controller (over `fgdb-calibrate`'s e-process core) may advise recompute under its named calibration population and exchangeability/nonexchangeability assumptions; the semantic contract is enforced by deterministic error bounds or exact validation where available; otherwise the result is explicitly approximate and carries the model-qualified error evidence. Assumption alarms trigger deterministic recompute/fallback but do not retroactively guarantee prior estimates. Branch statistics (§8.5): per-branch coverage is base+delta — a fork pins a shared ancestor-base `StatsSegment` at the branch manifest's `fork_boundary_logical_command_seq`, branch-delta segments derive from exactly the branch's post-fork divergence, the delta layer rides Ripple's Z-set consumption, and per-branch delta maintainers are instantiated **lazily on first planner demand, never eagerly at fork**. Branch retirement (§5.6) drops per-branch `StatsSegment`s and Ripple maintainer instances as derived state, and per-branch segment/maintainer cost is a declared parameter of the 10k-branch churn gate. Every maintainer output surface has an `erasure_obligations.toml` row (§12.6). Beacon consumers follow the same pattern: dense projections are derived, Ripple-maintained, snapshot-cursored adjacency views; 2-hop/landmark path indexes are maintained by Ripple or rebuilt/dropped under their declared update regime. Expiry-bearing inputs obey `w6-delta-consumption`'s closed declaration law (`ExpiryInsensitive | AS OF | ConsumesExpiryEpochTick`).

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-18: rebuildable indexes/views/caches — maintainer state included — can be discarded without changing exact answers or authorization. FG-INV-15 applies to any maintainer registered `exact`: integrating ordered deltas equals batch evaluation. Statistical machinery is claim-typed, never invariant: controller evidence follows FG-CAL-02's disclosure shape (population, selection/window, exchangeability or nonexchangeability method, strata, marginal target, realized coverage, drift); staleness surfaced in certificates joins the realized `AnswerContract` (approximate results carry error evidence per §8.3). The 10k-branch churn cost is a benchmark/slo row.

## Interactions
Runs on `w6-zset-circuits`; consumes `w6-delta-consumption`. `w1-sketch-calibrate` provides the conformal/e-process controller substrate; `w5-branch-stats` consumes the stats maintainers; `w5-answer-contracts` carries staleness into certificates; `w8-projection`/`w8-kernels` provide the Prism recompute fallback; `w7-vector`/`w7-fts`/`w7-path-temporal` ingestion feeds are downstream consumers; `w2-branch-retire` drops instances; `perf-bench-scale` owns the 10k-branch gate.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Per-maintainer differential: maintained result vs from-scratch recompute after randomized insert/delete/mixed churn — exact class must match exactly; bounded-error class must satisfy ε deterministically where a deterministic bound is declared, else outputs are labeled approximate with evidence attached (checked by certificate inspection). Deletion-heavy stress for union-find bounded rebuild and k-core decrements. Controller tests: assumption alarm triggers deterministic recompute; advice never alters the semantic contract; logged calibration population/assumptions in every advisory decision card. Lazy instantiation: no maintainer exists at fork; first planner demand instantiates and is logged; branch retire drops instances and the erasure walker covers them. E2E script: fork a branch → run mixed insert/delete churn → first planner demand lazily instantiates the stats maintainer → query certificates surface each maintainer's staleness contract → force an assumption alarm driving deterministic recompute → retire the branch and verify maintainer instances and per-branch `StatsSegment`s drop as derived state and the erasure walker covers their surfaces, with crash/restart injection between churn, instantiation, and retirement. DETAILED LOGGING (implementation and tests): every maintainer instantiation logs algorithm family, branch, declared staleness contract, and the triggering planner demand; every incremental update logs the consumed batch ID and the declared expiry arm; every recompute-advice decision logs its calibration population, assumptions, and advisory outcome; every deterministic recompute/fallback logs its trigger; tests assert certificates and logs agree on the staleness contract actually served. Bench: maintained-vs-recompute latency ratio on pinned fixtures; per-branch maintainer memory/cost reported into the 10k-branch churn gate.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: promoting conformal advice to enforcement; eager per-fork maintainer instantiation (defeats 10k-branch churn); universal "incremental is cheaper" claims (recompute fallback is always retained). Risk: delete-heavy workloads eroding incremental advantage — the staleness contract plus fallback keeps semantics honest while §17 measures the economics.

## Provenance
§9.6 (806–810); §8.5 (702); §3.3; §5.6 (469–471); §12.6 (914); §10 (823, 828); Appendix F FG-INV-15/18, FG-CAL-02.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Implement incremental fixpoint recursion for the validated subset (FixpointSpec)
description:
## What & scope
Implement recursion as incremental fixpoint: `FixpointSpec`, nested time, differentiated/semi-naïve evaluation for the validated subset, stratification enforcement, and termination/budget contracts. Batch-side `Fixpoint` execution lives in Loom; this bead owns its incremental maintenance and the shared legality matrix.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B4's claim explicitly covers the *registered* recursive-query subset: reachability/transitive-closure-class views stay warm under deltas instead of recomputing. B5 demands honesty about what is proved: only convergent recursion ships; everything else fails with a typed error rather than emitting a partial fixpoint. §3.3's DBSP verdict is scoped for exactly this reason — "only the validated operator/recursion subset is incremental."

## Design — normative detail
`FixpointSpec` records recursive SCCs, monotonicity class, finite active-domain bound, duplicate rule, and termination contract; nested time is `(commit_seq, iteration)`. Monotone finite-domain SCCs use differentiated/semi-naïve evaluation. Negation and non-monotone aggregates must be stratified outside a recursive SCC unless a separately proved complete-lattice semantics exists. Every accepted recursion has a finite domain, convergence proof, or explicit visible budget; non-convergence returns a structured error rather than a partial fixpoint unless truncation was explicitly requested. Only registered derivatives are incrementally maintained — "for free" is not a substitute for an operator law. The GLA `Fixpoint` operator (§8.3) and the path/recursion executor operators (§8.7) implement the same legality/algorithm matrix, and mode-aware history, captures, temporal intervals, and cost state are spillable; incremental maintenance under deletions may require retained support state (§3.3) and is not promised equal physical cost to insertion.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-15 derivative=batch applies per registered recursive derivative: integrating ordered deltas through the fixpoint equals batch re-evaluation at the same frontier. Termination contracts are structural typed errors, not slo rows. §15.5 anchor scope: Ripple's formal proofs cover only the explicitly registered operator/annotation subset — the recursion legality matrix is part of that registered subset, and anything outside it is simply not incremental.

## Interactions
Runs on `w6-zset-circuits`. Operator definitions and Appendix C `Fixpoint` contracts come from `w5-gla-algebra`; batch execution and the shared-typed-algebra/distinct-physical-contracts split from `w5-executor`. `w6-views` hosts recursive views; `w10-udf-vm` Datalog rules compile into this subset; `verif-oracles` runs SCC/recursion differentials against the reference engine.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Differential: semi-naïve vs naïve vs batch on generated monotone programs (reachability, ancestors, same-generation) under insert-only, delete-heavy, and mixed churn — deletions must exercise retained support state and still equal batch. Negatives: unstratified negation or a non-monotone aggregate inside an SCC is rejected at registration; an unregistered operator inside a recursive SCC is rejected; a claimed complete-lattice semantics without its separate proof is rejected. Budget exhaustion returns the structured error carrying iteration count and frontier (logged), and truncation is honored only when requested. Property: nested-time ordering is lexicographic (`commit_seq` major, `iteration` minor) and iterations never interleave across commits. Deterministic seed replay under the lab runtime. E2E script: register a reachability view over the validated subset → apply insert-only, delete-heavy, and mixed committed churn → verify the maintained fixpoint equals batch re-evaluation at each frontier → exhaust a declared budget and verify the structured error surfaces end-to-end, with crash/restart injection between delta application and fixpoint iterations. DETAILED LOGGING (implementation and tests): every fixpoint activation logs `FixpointSpec` identity, recursive SCC set, monotonicity class, and termination contract; every iteration logs its nested time (`commit_seq`, `iteration`), delta sizes, and retained-support growth; every registration rejection logs the exact legality-matrix rule violated; budget exhaustion logs iteration count and frontier; tests assert the logs reconstruct the iteration trace byte-deterministically under seed replay.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: unbounded recursion with best-effort timeout semantics; heuristic re-execution as a stand-in for non-monotone incrementalization; blanket "recursion is incremental" claims. Risk: support-state growth on delete-heavy recursive views — resource-accounted with recompute fallback through the view's declared fallback policy.

## Provenance
§9.3; §8.3/§8.7; §3.3; Appendix C.

title: Implement delta delivery: envelopes, digests, leases, resume capabilities, and ACKs
description:
## What & scope
Implement the delivery half of §9.5: `DeliveredDeltaPayload`, `DeltaDeliveryEnvelope`, internal/public digest separation, `SubscriptionDeliveryLeaseRecord`, the Resume capability and `PublicCursorStateCommitment`, the pending-output record, the publish→release→activate→ACK transition set, and the authenticated disposition receipts.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
A standing-query delta must own its **delivered output** — the exact authorized query-result Z-set — not merely its base-graph input batch, or authorization and replay both break (B5/B6). The internal/public digest split is the governance story: clients get verifiable bytes without learning internal frontiers, batch identities, or cadence unless declassified.

## Design — normative detail
`DeliveredDeltaPayload {format, output_schema, result_answer_contract, canonical_encoding_version, canonical_zset_segment_refs:StrongRef[], canonical_payload_len, output_payload_digest}` holds the exact authorized result Z-set stream; `output_payload_digest = BLAKE3("fgdb:delivered-zset:v1" || canonical(format, output_schema, result_answer_contract, canonical_encoding_version, canonical_payload_len, exact logical Z-set bytes))`; segment refs are storage ownership only and the public digest is recomputed from reassembled canonical bytes. The durable internal `DeltaDeliveryEnvelope<Role:AuthorityOwningRole> {authority_bound_header, format, derived_identity_digest, baseline_id, start_frontier, resulting_frontier, delivery_id:OpaquePublicNonce, delivery_sequence, authorized_cursor_position, output_payload_ref, output_payload_digest, provenance, internal_delivery_digest}` separates output from provenance. `provenance = Atomic{source:CommittedDeltaSourceRef, source_batch_digest} | Coalesced{source_role:Local|Global, first_batch_id, last_batch_id, ordered_source_commitment, source_count}`; frontiers/IDs are role-tagged; the coalesced commitment includes every same-role source ID/digest including zero-net intermediates; cross-role ranges are invalid and require a baseline boundary. Preactivation leases retain their Local source variant after activation; a preserved outstanding Local lease is never deliverable after the service-epoch change — no old-epoch token resumes it and no delivery range crosses roles — and it must be terminally disposed (ACK, authenticated release, profiled expiry, or reset supersession) before `PostActivationCursorTransition` (legal only with no outstanding or pending Local output; `w6-sub-resets`) creates the new Sharded `PendingInitialVisibility` baseline, never a cross-role delta. The full header must byte-match the cursor, derived identity, payload result contract, policy, and release decision — a tenant/principal/authority digest is insufficient. `InternalDeliveryDigest = BLAKE3("fgdb:internal-delivery:v1" || canonical(envelope excluding internal_delivery_digest))` commits the full source range and is server-side/audit-authorized only. `AuthorizedDeltaPublicProvenance` is Appendix D's closed `Opaque|Declassified` union; `PublicDeliveryDigest = BLAKE3("fgdb:public-delivery:v1" || canonical(delivery_id, delivery_sequence, authorized_cursor_position, format, output_schema, result_answer_contract, canonical_encoding_version, canonical_payload_len, output_payload_digest, authorized_public_provenance))` — the Opaque arm contains no source/frontier/cadence fact; Declassified includes only its explicitly authorized, audit-released projection. `DeliveryId` is a pre-minted opaque public nonce, not the envelope ObjectId. Clients validate only `output_payload_digest`, `PublicDeliveryDigest`, authorized public provenance, and exact bytes; internal provenance and `InternalDeliveryDigest` never cross the default wire boundary.

Resumption: durable resumption uses Appendix D's generated wire-safe `ResumeCapabilityBody::SubscriptionCursor{cursor_handle:PublicCursorHandle, issuance_cursor_state_token:PublicStateToken<Cursor>, capability_lineage_token:PublicStateToken<ResumeLineage>, public_derived_identity_commitment, baseline_handle:PublicBaselineHandle, public_state_commitment}` (App D 2788) — intentionally not bound to one connection. `resume_capability_arms.toml` is the single source for both the body and `ResumeCapabilitySubjectBasis`; the internal subject arm is `SubscriptionCursor{cursor_creation_request_digest, resume_cursor_id, cursor_state_version, public_derived_identity_commitment, baseline_id, public_state_commitment}`, carried with `capability_generation` and `lineage` inside the server-side `ResumeCapabilityReplayRecord` (§13.3 line 1010) — internal cursor IDs, state versions, and generations live only there and never in the public capability body (no mutable state hint or numeric internal generation is encoded; §9.5 line 770's inline field list conflates body and subject basis, and the generated Appendix D union is authoritative). `PublicCursorStateCommitment` is the domain-separated digest of cursor version, public state tag, baseline ID and `PublicBaselineDigest`, `PublicLogicalPositionProjection`, and, when outstanding, the opaque delivery ID and `PublicDeliveryDigest`; it never includes a raw Local/Global frontier, batch/source identity, internal `DeliveryDigest`, lease ObjectId, `DerivedIdentity`/digest, or derived-state provenance. The server cursor record — not token contents — is authoritative and byte-matches the commitment against its public projection. A capability replays only through the exact current-or-immediate-predecessor rule, is never widened by `AUTH_REFRESH`, and becomes unusable after expiry, revocation/reset, incarnation or service-visibility change, successor consumption beyond the replay window, or baseline retirement; it is lookup authority, **not** a GC root — its replay object is retained by the active Protocol owner.

`SubscriptionDeliveryLeaseRecord<Role> {authority_bound_header, role_and_group, resume_cursor_id, cursor_state_version, delivery_lease_id, lease_generation, sender_generation, time_basis_ref:StrongRef<SubscriptionDeliveryLeaseTimeBasis<Role>>, not_before, expires_at, delivery: Baseline{payload_ref, baseline_id, internal_baseline_digest, public_baseline_digest, internal_frontier, public_cursor_position} | Delta{envelope_ref, delivery_id, internal_delivery_digest, public_delivery_digest, resulting_internal_frontier, public_cursor_position} | ResetNotice{payload_ref, public_reset_commitment, prior_public_cursor_position}, body_digest}`. `PendingCursorOutputRecord<Role>` = `PendingVisibility{authority_bound_header, resume_cursor_id, expected_active_idle_state_version, kind: Delta{envelope_ref, policy_ref} | Reset{reset_record_ref, notice_payload_ref, policy_ref}, audit_gate_commitment, resource_reservation_ref} | ReleasedAwaitingActivation{same_owned_output_fields, audit_release_evidence, release_maintenance_ref}`; its header byte-matches the active cursor, envelope/reset policy, and release subject; it never owns a lease/capability or changes the public cursor projection.

Transitions: `PublishDeltaPending` leaves the cursor byte-identically `ActiveIdle` and inserts one pending output (batched across the cursors of one Ripple flush tick); audit release changes only that pending leaf to `ReleasedAwaitingActivation`; `SubscriptionDelta` activation consumes it and atomically selects `ActiveOutstandingDelta` with a fresh lease/successor capability. `AckBaselineComplete` requires both an authenticated baseline ACK receipt and `CursorOutputEndSendCompletionRecord`, joins/fences sender obligations, moves BaselineDeliverable→ActiveIdle, advances the acknowledged frontier, retires the lease, and installs the prebuilt successor replay record atomically; `AckDeltaComplete` likewise. `RotateCapability` preserves state while replacing the exact replay lineage. All per-cursor activation and ACK/rotation bookkeeping rides §12.8's `ProtectedOutputActivationBatchSpec`/`ProtectedOutputDispositionBatchSpec` as per-subject sub-records, all-or-nothing; the activation batch consumes exactly one `TimeValidationEvidence` whose subject is the `ActivationBatch` transcript, while disposition sub-records carry their own authenticated receipts, `CursorOutputEndSendCompletionRecord` bridges, or profiled expiry evidence — an `ActivationBatch`-subject time evidence is never a disposition input. `CursorOutputEndSendCompletionRecord` binds the authority public commitment; role/domain/service/session/process/cursor/output kind; ID/state/sender generation; exact END frame transcript; payload/public digest; flow reservation/cost; write-start frame-time requirement-set commitment; and the matching `TransportSendObligation::Sent` — the only bridge into a baseline/delta/reset ACK. `AuthenticatedClientSubscriptionDispositionReceipt<Role> {authority_bound_header, session_authorization_ref, auth_context_generation, session_binding, public_authority_commitment, cursor_identity, cursor_state_version, lease_identity?, public_digest, request_nonce, source:Fgp|Embedded, action:AckBaseline|AckDelta|AckReset|ReleaseOutstanding|CloseWithoutOutstanding, canonical_request_digest, server_process_incarnation, signing_key_epoch, signature}` must equal or be proved narrower than the active cursor/lease binding. Current/immediate-predecessor replay makes lost READY/SNAPSHOT_ACKED/ACKED/RESUMED/RESET/DISCONNECT/CLOSE replies byte-identical; anything older fails.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-15: "Resume/ACK/release/expiry CAS one delivery version with deterministic immediate-predecessor retry. Cursor baseline/delta rules forbid delta before baseline ACK and expose every gap. Public digests cover exact authorized canonical bytes/provenance, never keyed object IDs." FG-INV-16: leases/receipts never lost, duplicated, refunded, released, or exposed while obligated. FG-INV-15's owner-machine clause states verbatim that QUERY_CANCEL, Drop, disconnect, drain, and process death cannot release the active owner. FG-CFG-04: steady-state delivery costs one observation plus one maintenance entry per activation tick per role/group — a capacity-model row, never an invariant. §17 benchmark: subscription end-to-end p99 < 10 ms.

## Interactions
Consumes `w6-subscriptions` state machine and `w6-delta-consumption` source refs; `w9-audit-release` releases pending leaves; `w9-activation-batching` activates and disposes in batches; `w1-crypto` supplies BLAKE3 domains/signing; `w10-fgp-core`/`w10-capabilities` carry frames and Resume capability bytes; `w10-cdc` shares the Global-batch-only rule.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Sender-death and lost-response DPOR: replay of current/immediate-predecessor replies byte-identical; older replay fails. Digest tests: recomputation from reassembled bytes; tamper negatives per field; Opaque-arm leak test proving no source/frontier/cadence fact is derivable from framed bytes. Coalesced-provenance completeness including zero-net intermediates; cross-role range rejected. Posture: a preactivation lease retains its Local variant after activation; a preserved outstanding Local lease is rejected for delivery after a service-epoch change (negative test), `PostActivationCursorTransition` is rejected while that output remains outstanding/pending, and only after its terminal disposition does the transition create the new Sharded `PendingInitialVisibility` baseline — with each rejection and the lease posture logged. Batch activation all-or-nothing with stale/duplicated/omitted sub-records applying nothing and matching retry returning the identical maintenance result. Lease expiry, capability rotation/widening negatives, `AUTH_REFRESH` non-widening. E2E latency bench (p99 < 10 ms) with per-stage timestamps logged (publish, release, activation, send, ACK). E2E script: subscribe → baseline delivery/ACK → committed churn producing atomic and coalesced deltas (including zero-net intermediates) → client-side validation of `output_payload_digest`, `PublicDeliveryDigest`, and authorized public provenance recomputed from exact reassembled bytes → sender death and capability resume mid-stream → authenticated disposition receipts exercising every `action` arm, with crash/restart injection at each pipeline stage. DETAILED LOGGING (implementation and tests): every publish/release/activation/send/ACK event logs cursor ID, cursor state version, `delivery_id`, `delivery_sequence`, lease ID, lease generation, sender generation, activation batch identity, and the public digest framed; envelope construction logs the provenance arm taken (Atomic vs Coalesced with source count); tests assert the Opaque-arm log projection reveals no source/frontier/cadence fact and that the logged pipeline reconstructs every delivery's publish→ACK lineage.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: delivering base-graph input batches as "the delta" (unauthorized, unreplayable); binding capabilities to connections; per-delivery time observations (rejected as window-predictability and cost failure — batch-shaped evidence instead); envelope ObjectId as public delivery ID. Risk: digest-domain sprawl — all domains are registry rows with golden vectors.

## Provenance
§9.5 (770–774, 790–792, 798); §12.8 (972–976); Appendix B (1928); Appendix D; Appendix F FG-INV-15/16, FG-CFG-04.

### Fidelity addendum — exact cursor owner machine and internal frontier type
`DeliveryFrontier` is the closed internal-only union `Local{commit_seq,batch_frontier}|Global{global_commit_seq,batch_frontier}`. It is never a public token/frame field. `SubscriptionCursorDeliveryIndex<Role>` owns `cursors[resume_cursor_id -> StrongRef<SubscriptionCursorDeliveryRecord<Role>>]` and `active_leases[delivery_lease_id -> StrongRef<SubscriptionDeliveryLeaseRecord<Role>>]` plus generation, state counts, terminal-disposition floor, and root digest; `PendingCursorOutputIndex<Role>` separately owns at most one pending data output per cursor and, when enabled, at most one standing `FreshnessBreach` notice beside it.

The common bodies are exact: `SubscriptionCursorActiveCommon<Role>={role_and_group,authority_bound_header,cursor_creation_request_digest,resume_cursor_id,cursor_state_version,semantic_detachment_identity,escrow_ref,internal_baseline_digest,public_baseline_digest,public_derived_identity_commitment,public_state_commitment,nonretaining_predecessor_digest}` and terminal common replaces live authority/escrow with `TerminalAuthorityCommitment<Role>` and terminal state/public commitments. The closed owner tags are exactly `PendingInitialVisibility|ReleasedInitialAwaitingActivation|BaselineDeliverable|ActiveIdle|ActiveOutstandingDelta|ResetNoticeDeliverable|ResetAwaitingBaselineActivation|ResetBaselineDeliverable|ExplicitlyPaused|Closed|Expired` with the fields and ownership laws in section 9.5: only Deliverable/Paused tags root leases; pending/released/reset-awaiting-baseline tags own bytes/policy/escrow but no absolute window; terminal tags own no escrow, lease, payload, capability replay, or live authority.

The generated Protocol transition inventory is exactly `ReleaseInitialVisibility|ActivateInitialBaseline|AckBaselineComplete|PublishDeltaPending|ReleaseDeltaVisibility|ActivateDelta|AckDeltaComplete|PublishResetPending|ReleaseResetVisibility|ActivateResetNotice|AcknowledgeReset|ActivateResetBaseline|RotateCapability|PauseForDisconnect|ResumeAfterDisconnect|PostActivationCursorTransition|CloseCursor|ExpireCursor`. Only `CreateSubscriptionCursorSpec<Role>` is semantic and uses `AtomicProtocolDetach`. Alias tags such as `CreateLease`, `AckComplete`, `BeginReset`, or `ResetOrExpire` are invalid. Model/DPOR tests exhaust every legal edge and every illegal cross-edge; conservation checks prove exactly one current record, at most one lease, bounded pending output, and exact escrow/byte/capability ownership. Logs add from/to owner tag, internal frontier commitment (never raw value on public logs), index generation/root, pending-output cardinalities, and conservation verdict.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.
design:
## Authoritative post-decomposition contract delta (d96bf0f)

The channel-versus-embedded subscription completion and capability-validation contract below supersedes the older source:Fgp|Embedded receipt rendering.

`CursorOutputEndSendCompletionRecord` binds the surface (`NativeFgp|Http2|Grpc|WebSocket`), authority public commitment, role/domain/service/session/process/cursor/output kind and ID/state/sender generation, exact surface END and canonical FGP END transcript, payload/public digest, flow reservation/cost, write-start frame-time requirement-set commitment, and the matching `TransportSendObligation::Sent`; it is the channel-transport bridge into a baseline/delta/reset ACK. `EmbeddedCursorOutputFullyConsumedRecord<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is the distinct embedded-only `{session_authorization_ref:StrongRef<SessionAuthorizationRecord<Role>>,host_session_generation,cursor_identity,cursor_state_version,output_kind_and_id,lease_identity,stream_owner_token_commitment,public_digest,completion_source:ExplicitFinish|IteratorExhaustion,canonical_finish_call_digest,server_process_incarnation,signing_key_epoch,signature}` and is constructible only after complete consumption plus joined borrows/tasks. `SubscriptionDispositionAuthority<Role>` is `ReadyChannelResumeCapability{validation_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence>,presented_resume_capability_commitment}|EmbeddedCursorOwner{stream_owner_token_commitment,host_session_generation}`; `SubscriptionDispositionCompletion<Role>` is `ChannelSent{record_ref:StrongRef<CursorOutputEndSendCompletionRecord>}|EmbeddedFullyConsumed{record_ref:StrongRef<EmbeddedCursorOutputFullyConsumedRecord<Role>>}|NotApplicable`. `AuthenticatedClientSubscriptionDispositionReceipt<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,session_authorization_ref:StrongRef<SessionAuthorizationRecord<Role>>,disposition_authority:SubscriptionDispositionAuthority<Role>,completion:SubscriptionDispositionCompletion<Role>,auth_context_generation,session_binding,public_authority_commitment,cursor_identity,cursor_state_version,lease_identity?,public_digest,request_nonce,action:AckBaseline|AckDelta|AckReset|ReleaseOutstanding|CloseWithoutOutstanding,canonical_request_digest,server_process_incarnation,signing_key_epoch,signature}`. Only the ReadyChannel arm selects a ResumeSubscriptionCursor validation row; it byte-matches the exact request, capability commitment, session, current cursor lineage, authority header, and action. ACK actions require the matching ChannelSent or EmbeddedFullyConsumed completion selected by their authority source; ReleaseOutstanding and CloseWithoutOutstanding require NotApplicable. The Embedded authority is a non-capability cursor-owner proof and cannot carry a validation ref. Receipt/action bijection is exact: AckBaseline -> `SubscriptionAckBaseline`, AckDelta -> `SubscriptionAckDelta`, AckReset -> `SubscriptionAckResetOrGap`, and ReleaseOutstanding or CloseWithoutOutstanding -> `SubscriptionClose`. Its full header/session binding must equal or be proved narrower than the active cursor/lease binding; public commitments are integrity projections only. `CloseCursor` requires `outstanding_disposition=None{receipt:CloseWithoutOutstanding}|Acknowledged{receipt:AckBaseline|AckDelta|AckReset,completion}|Released{receipt:ReleaseOutstanding,sender_fence_and_join_proof}|ResetSuperseded{typed_gap_supersession_evidence}` and also proves the pending-output index empty or terminally disposes each remaining leaf (the one pending data output plus, when present, the standing `FreshnessBreach` notice). It atomically creates `Closed`, derives the terminal authority commitment from the last active header, disposes escrow, and tombstones capability lineage; a generic CLOSE frame, socket loss, drain, or Rust Drop cannot construct that evidence. `ExpireCursor` requires profiled expiry evidence for the exact current lease/capability/action, sender fence/join, pending-output disposition, and escrow disposition. `PostActivationCursorTransition` is the certified Local-to-Sharded transition and is legal only with no outstanding or pending Local output; it creates a new Sharded PendingInitialVisibility baseline, never a cross-role delta. No catch-all `ResetOrExpire` exists. Current/immediate-predecessor replay makes lost READY/SNAPSHOT_ACKED/ACKED/RESUMED/RESET/DISCONNECT/CLOSE replies byte-identical; anything older fails. Checkpoints, protocol snapshots, backup/configuration floors, restore, and GC preserve all cursor/pending-output/lease/replay records. Disconnect never releases.
`DeliveryFrontier = Local{commit_seq,batch_frontier}|Global{global_commit_seq,batch_frontier}` is internal-only. The exact `SubscriptionCursorDeliveryRecord`, `PendingCursorOutputRecord`, and `SubscriptionDeliveryLeaseRecord` schemas are those in §9.5; no Appendix rendering may add a raw applied Local/Global command sequence to a public projection. `SubscriptionDeliveryTransitionSpec<Role>` is generated across the Protocol maintenance tags `ReleaseInitialVisibility|ActivateInitialBaseline|AckBaselineComplete|PublishDeltaPending|ReleaseDeltaVisibility|ActivateDelta|AckDeltaComplete|PublishResetPending|ReleaseResetVisibility|ActivateResetNotice|AcknowledgeReset|ActivateResetBaseline|RotateCapability|PauseForDisconnect|ResumeAfterDisconnect|PostActivationCursorTransition|CloseCursor|ExpireCursor`; only `CreateSubscriptionCursorSpec<Role>` is semantic and uses `AtomicProtocolDetach`. Its generated `client_action_authority` field is closed: `PauseForDisconnect` and `ResumeAfterDisconnect` carry `DirectResumeCapability{validation_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence>}` selecting respectively `SubscriptionPause` or `SubscriptionResumeAfterPauseOrDisconnect`; `AckBaselineComplete`, `AckDeltaComplete`, `AcknowledgeReset`, and `CloseCursor` carry `DispositionReceipt{receipt_ref:StrongRef<AuthenticatedClientSubscriptionDispositionReceipt<Role>>}` with the exact receipt/action mapping; all system release/activation/publish/reset/posture-transition/expiry tags carry their distinct structural authority and cannot encode either client arm. ACK transitions require the receipt's exact channel or embedded completion proof, remove exact leases, and retain the receipt and any nested validation ref through successor acknowledgement or subject terminality. Reset owns a successor baseline payload/policy before selection but creates its delivery lease only after reset ACK. The posture transition creates a Sharded PendingInitialVisibility baseline under the promoted epoch; no Global delta exists before its ACK, no old-epoch token resumes it, and no range crosses roles. Capability bytes authorize lookup only through rooted cursor lineage.

title: Implement cursor resets, pause/resume, close/expire, and authority evolution
description:
## What & scope
Implement the lifecycle half of §9.5: the reset ladder (`PublishResetPending` → notice → ack → successor baseline), terminal no-successor resets, explicit pause/resume, `CloseCursor`/`ExpireCursor` with total disposition evidence, `PostActivationCursorTransition`, and the `STICKY_AUTHORITY`/`LIVE_AUTHORITY` authorization-evolution contract.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Agent branches end, schemas migrate, authority changes, buffers overflow — a governance-grade changefeed (B6) must express every discontinuity as an explicit, acknowledged, capability-rotating transition, never a silent gap (B5). Close/expire evidence discipline exists because Rust `Drop`, socket loss, or operator impatience must never be able to destroy an obligated delivery state (FG-INV-16).

## Design — normative detail
Resets: `PublishResetPending` constructs the complete `CursorResetRecord`, reset-notice payload, successor baseline payload/policy, and audit candidate but **not** a lease/capability, and leaves the current public cursor projection unchanged. Audit release changes only that pending leaf to `ReleasedAwaitingActivation`; `SubscriptionResetNotice` activation builds a fresh notice lease, consumes the pending leaf, and selects `ResetNoticeDeliverable`. `AcknowledgeReset` requires `CursorOutputEndSendCompletionRecord` plus `AuthenticatedCursorResetAckReceipt<Role>`, retires the notice lease, and selects `ResetAwaitingBaselineActivation` — still with no successor-baseline lease. Only the later `SubscriptionResetBaseline` activation uses fresh time evidence to build that baseline lease/capability and selects `ResetBaselineDeliverable`; its ordinary baseline ACK returns `ActiveIdle`. Thus neither audit delay nor time spent waiting for the client to acknowledge a reset consumes the successor delivery window. A terminal reset — branch retirement (§5.6) or another declared no-successor cause — carries a `CursorResetRecord` with no successor baseline: the acknowledged `GAP` notice completes the cursor into `Closed` (framed as `SUBSCRIPTION_ENDED`) with the ordinary close dispositions. BUFFER overflow drives `PublishResetPending{Gap}`; COALESCE keeps the hidden source commitment internal unless declassified.

Pause/resume: ordinary socket loss is runtime sender detachment and requires no durable state mutation. Explicit `PauseForDisconnect` fences and joins the current sender, preserves the exact active state and outstanding lease in `PausedCursorState` — a generated, nonrecursive inline copy of exactly the role-valid `BaselineDeliverable|ActiveIdle|ActiveOutstandingDelta|ResetNoticeDeliverable|ResetAwaitingBaselineActivation|ResetBaselineDeliverable` fields, owning every still-outstanding payload/lease and no prior cursor record — installs `CursorDisconnectRecord`, rotates the capability, and advances no frontier. `ResumeAfterDisconnect` is the sole explicit-paused reattachment transition: under a fresh Ready/current-authority binding it either reuses a still-usable exact lease or atomically replaces it with a freshly validated lease for identical bytes, increments sender generation, rotates capability, and restores the preserved active tag. Runtime-detached owners may attach a new sender through the same validation/fencing path without fabricating ExplicitlyPaused. Neither path is ACK, release, gap, or reset.

Terminals: `CloseCursor` requires `outstanding_disposition = None{receipt:CloseWithoutOutstanding} | Acknowledged{receipt:AckBaseline|AckDelta|AckReset, end_send_completion_ref} | Released{receipt:ReleaseOutstanding, sender_fence_and_join_proof} | ResetSuperseded{typed_gap_supersession_evidence}` and also proves the pending-output index empty or terminally disposes each remaining leaf (the one pending data output plus, when present, the standing `FreshnessBreach` notice). It atomically creates `Closed`, derives the terminal authority commitment from the last active header, disposes escrow, and tombstones capability lineage; a generic CLOSE frame, socket loss, drain, or Rust `Drop` cannot construct that evidence. `ExpireCursor` requires profiled expiry evidence for the exact current lease/capability/action, sender fence/join, pending-output disposition, and escrow disposition. `PostActivationCursorTransition` is the certified Local→Sharded transition, legal only with no outstanding or pending Local output; it creates a new Sharded `PendingInitialVisibility` baseline, never a cross-role delta. No catch-all `ResetOrExpire` exists. Disconnect never releases. Checkpoints, protocol snapshots, backup/configuration floors, restore, and GC preserve all cursor/pending-output/lease/replay records.

Authority evolution: `STICKY_AUTHORITY` fixes a non-widenable creation authority and terminates on revocation/expiry. `LIVE_AUTHORITY` ends the old segment at a policy boundary with `AUTHORITY_RESET { old_digest, new_digest, effective_seq }`, then emits a newly authorized snapshot plus `START_AFTER`; an optional retraction/insertion diff is used only when its disclosure is policy-approved. Ordinary data deltas never silently mix authority domains, and a cursor cannot resume across a reset without acknowledging the new baseline. Schema or branch changes likewise use a declared migration/reset contract.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-15: cursor rules expose every gap; reset supersession is typed. FG-INV-16: no obligated owner is lost, duplicated, refunded, released, or exposed while obligated; expiry can only order the registered rollback/status-safe path; under declared fairness every obligation reaches one legal terminal or recoverable state. FG-INV-15's owner-machine clause is what names QUERY_CANCEL, Drop, disconnect, drain, and process death as unable to release the active owner. FG-INV-14: terminal transitions are the exact release points for GC roots (escrow disposition, capability tombstone). FG-INV-20: capability lookup/status/release is same-principal, same-or-narrower, current-epoch, uniformly nonrevealing on failure.

## Interactions
Extends `w6-subscriptions`/`w6-sub-delivery`; `w2-branch-retire` triggers the terminal no-successor reset when a subscribed branch retires; `w9-activation-batching` hosts reset-notice/reset-baseline activation and close/expiry dispositions as batch sub-records; `w9-time-authority` profiles expiry evidence; `w10-fgp-core` frames `SUBSCRIPTION_ENDED`/`AUTHORITY_RESET`; `w12-conversion` consumes `PostActivationCursorTransition`.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Reset-ladder DPOR including terminal GAP into `Closed`; window-preservation test (slow reset ACK does not consume the successor window). Pause/resume crash matrix: crash between fence and record install, between lease replace and tag restore; identical-bytes lease replacement verified by digest. Close-forgery negatives: CLOSE frame alone, socket loss, drain, and `Drop` each fail to construct disposition evidence; every `outstanding_disposition` arm exercised. Expiry with profiled evidence only; missing evidence delays, never force-closes. Authority: LIVE boundary emits `AUTHORITY_RESET` then snapshot; resume-across-reset without baseline ACK fails; STICKY terminates on revocation. `PostActivationCursorTransition` rejected while any Local output is outstanding/pending. All transitions logged with cursor ID, state version, lease generation, and disposition kind; reset transitions additionally log `CursorResetRecord` identity, successor-baseline presence/absence, and supersession-evidence kind; pause/resume log fence/join proof identity and sender generations; close/expire log each disposed pending-output leaf and the escrow disposition. E2E script: subscribe → baseline ACK → deltas → explicit `PauseForDisconnect` → `ResumeAfterDisconnect` → LIVE_AUTHORITY policy boundary (`AUTHORITY_RESET` → newly authorized snapshot → `START_AFTER`) → BUFFER-overflow `Gap` reset through the full ladder to successor-baseline ACK → branch retirement driving the terminal no-successor GAP into `Closed`/`SUBSCRIPTION_ENDED` → `CloseCursor` and `ExpireCursor` on separate cursors with total disposition evidence, with crash/restart injection at every transition and replay assertions that lost replies are byte-identical under the current/immediate-predecessor rule.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: a catch-all `ResetOrExpire`; auto-close on disconnect; silent authority mixing in data deltas; unacknowledged resets. Risk: operator pressure to force-close stuck cursors — the answer is the evidence path (release receipt or profiled expiry), never a bypass.

## Provenance
§9.5 (794–800); §5.6 (469–471); §12.8 (974); Appendix F FG-INV-14/15/16/20.

### Fidelity addendum — reset records, notice payload, and wire projection
The plan names `CursorResetRecord` and `CursorResetNoticePayload` as durable objects; their registry rows must be exact rather than placeholder refs. `CursorResetRecord` freezes `{authority_bound_header,resume_cursor_id,expected_active_idle_state_version,reset_reason:Gap|AuthorityBoundary|SchemaBoundary|BranchRetired|DeclaredMigration,prior_internal_frontier,prior_public_cursor_position,successor:ResumableBaseline{baseline_payload_ref,successor_policy_ref,successor_public_cursor_position}|Terminal{registered_no_successor_reason},hidden_source_supersession_commitment,audit_gate_commitment,public_reset_commitment,body_digest}`. `CursorResetNoticePayload` is the bounded public projection `{format,reset_notice_id:OpaquePublicNonce,public_reset_commitment,expected_authorized_cursor_position,available_from_authorized_position,successor:ResumableBaseline{successor_baseline_handle,successor_public_baseline_digest}|Terminal,authorized_public_reason_class,canonical_payload_len,body_digest}`. It contains no raw Local/Global frontier, source batch, derived identity, hidden authority root, or keyed ObjectId. The record owns the successor baseline/policy before selection; the notice payload owns only the authorized projection.

Appendix D's exact GAP projection is `GAP{cursor_handle,cursor_state_token,reset_notice_handle,public_reset_commitment,expected_authorized_cursor_position,available_from_authorized_position,successor:ResumableBaseline{successor_baseline_handle,successor_public_baseline_digest}|Terminal,resume_capability,read_release_authorization,audit_release}`. `Terminal` is legal exactly for the no-successor reset and GAP_ACK then closes into `SUBSCRIPTION_ENDED`. `CursorResetNoticePayload`, `SubscriptionDeliveryLeaseRecord::ResetNotice`, pending-output Reset, reset ACK receipt, and the GAP frame must byte-match the same public commitment and successor arm.

Golden/mutation tests alter every included/forbidden field; schema tests reject nullable successors, a Terminal arm with a baseline, a Resumable arm without both baseline fields, raw frontier leakage, reason widening, or cross-role successor. E2E covers every reset reason, Required-audit delay, crash at publish/release/activate/END/ACK/baseline activation, and the terminal branch-retirement path. Logs record reset record/notice identities, reason class, successor arm, state version, public commitment, audit/activation/ACK evidence identities, and terminal disposition, while suppressing hidden source/frontier data.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

## Authoritative post-d96bf0f contract reconciliation

Cursor ACK/release/close transitions distinguish channel END-send completion from embedded full consumption and require the exact SubscriptionDispositionAuthority/action-to-validation mapping.

The following current plan text is authoritative and supersedes any older rendering in this Bead:

`CursorOutputEndSendCompletionRecord` binds the surface (`NativeFgp|Http2|Grpc|WebSocket`), authority public commitment, role/domain/service/session/process/cursor/output kind and ID/state/sender generation, exact surface END and canonical FGP END transcript, payload/public digest, flow reservation/cost, write-start frame-time requirement-set commitment, and the matching `TransportSendObligation::Sent`; it is the channel-transport bridge into a baseline/delta/reset ACK. `EmbeddedCursorOutputFullyConsumedRecord<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is the distinct embedded-only `{session_authorization_ref:StrongRef<SessionAuthorizationRecord<Role>>,host_session_generation,cursor_identity,cursor_state_version,output_kind_and_id,lease_identity,stream_owner_token_commitment,public_digest,completion_source:ExplicitFinish|IteratorExhaustion,canonical_finish_call_digest,server_process_incarnation,signing_key_epoch,signature}` and is constructible only after complete consumption plus joined borrows/tasks. `SubscriptionDispositionAuthority<Role>` is `ReadyChannelResumeCapability{validation_ref:StrongRef<DurableCapabilityValidationEvidence>,presented_resume_capability_commitment}|EmbeddedCursorOwner{stream_owner_token_commitment,host_session_generation}`; `SubscriptionDispositionCompletion<Role>` is `ChannelSent{record_ref:StrongRef<CursorOutputEndSendCompletionRecord>}|EmbeddedFullyConsumed{record_ref:StrongRef<EmbeddedCursorOutputFullyConsumedRecord<Role>>}|NotApplicable`. `AuthenticatedClientSubscriptionDispositionReceipt<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is `{authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>,session_authorization_ref:StrongRef<SessionAuthorizationRecord<Role>>,disposition_authority:SubscriptionDispositionAuthority<Role>,completion:SubscriptionDispositionCompletion<Role>,auth_context_generation,session_binding,public_authority_commitment,cursor_identity,cursor_state_version,lease_identity?,public_digest,request_nonce,action:AckBaseline|AckDelta|AckReset|ReleaseOutstanding|CloseWithoutOutstanding,canonical_request_digest,server_process_incarnation,signing_key_epoch,signature}`. Only the ReadyChannel arm selects a ResumeSubscriptionCursor validation row; it byte-matches the exact request, capability commitment, session, current cursor lineage, authority header, and action. ACK actions require the matching ChannelSent or EmbeddedFullyConsumed completion selected by their authority source; ReleaseOutstanding and CloseWithoutOutstanding require NotApplicable. The Embedded authority is a non-capability cursor-owner proof and cannot carry a validation ref. Receipt/action bijection is exact: AckBaseline -> `SubscriptionAckBaseline`, AckDelta -> `SubscriptionAckDelta`, AckReset -> `SubscriptionAckResetOrGap`, and ReleaseOutstanding or CloseWithoutOutstanding -> `SubscriptionClose`. Its full header/session binding must equal or be proved narrower than the active cursor/lease binding; public commitments are integrity projections only. `CloseCursor` requires `outstanding_disposition=None{receipt:CloseWithoutOutstanding}|Acknowledged{receipt:AckBaseline|AckDelta|AckReset,completion}|Released{receipt:ReleaseOutstanding,sender_fence_and_join_proof}|ResetSuperseded{typed_gap_supersession_evidence}` and also proves the pending-output index empty or terminally disposes each remaining leaf (the one pending data output plus, when present, the standing `FreshnessBreach` notice). It atomically creates `Closed`, derives the terminal authority commitment from the last active header, disposes escrow, and tombstones capability lineage; a generic CLOSE frame, socket loss, drain, or Rust Drop cannot construct that evidence. `ExpireCursor` requires profiled expiry evidence for the exact current lease/capability/action, sender fence/join, pending-output disposition, and escrow disposition. `PostActivationCursorTransition` is the certified Local-to-Sharded transition and is legal only with no outstanding or pending Local output; it creates a new Sharded PendingInitialVisibility baseline, never a cross-role delta. No catch-all `ResetOrExpire` exists. Current/immediate-predecessor replay makes lost READY/SNAPSHOT_ACKED/ACKED/RESUMED/RESET/DISCONNECT/CLOSE replies byte-identical; anything older fails. Checkpoints, protocol snapshots, backup/configuration floors, restore, and GC preserve all cursor/pending-output/lease/replay records. Disconnect never releases.

Implementation, tests, retained evidence, and public-surface behavior must use this exact corrected contract. No Markdown plan edit is required or authorized by this reconciliation.

title: Implement the subscription cursor machine: creation, baselines, and the 11-arm state union
description:
## What & scope
Implement §9.5's durable standing-query/changefeed cursor core: subscription creation (`CreateSubscriptionCursorSpec<Role>`), the dual-commitment `DeliveredBaselinePayload`, the semantic record and resource escrow, the Protocol-plane indexes, and the closed 11-arm `SubscriptionCursorDeliveryRecord<Role>` state union with its one-record/one-lease/one-pending-output laws. Delivery envelopes/leases/ACKs are `w6-sub-delivery`; resets/pause/close/expire are `w6-sub-resets`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Changefeeds are the agent-native (B6) surface for reactive memory and the B4 payoff users can see. The design's central move: a subscription is durable, capability-resumable server state whose visibility is gated by the audit pipeline (release) and time-evidence activation (leases) — so a subscription is governance-grade like every other protected output, unlike every competitor's connection-bound changefeed. The three-stage pending→released→deliverable split exists so neither audit delay nor a time-authority outage consumes a client-visible delivery window or blocks semantic visibility.

## Design — normative detail
Creation first materializes a canonical `DeliveredBaselinePayload` for one internal `DerivedIdentity`, its sorted source coverage, one posture-tagged internal batch frontier `w`, and the `PublicLogicalPositionProjection` authorized as this cursor's `START_AFTER` position. Two deliberately different commitments: `InternalBaselineDigest` covers the complete derived identity, source coverage, raw frontier, public contract, and exact bytes — retained only server-side. `PublicBaselineDigest = BLAKE3("fgdb:public-baseline:v1" || canonical(format, baseline_id, public_cursor_position, output_schema, result_answer_contract, canonical_encoding_version, canonical_payload_len, exact_concatenated_canonical_result_bytes))` — it excludes `DerivedIdentity`, raw coverage/frontier, storage refs, and itself. `baseline_id` is a pre-minted opaque public nonce, not the keyed ObjectId of the payload.

`CreateSubscriptionCursorSpec<Role>` is the sole initial semantic transition. It installs `SubscriptionCursorSemanticRecord<Role> {cursor_creation_request_digest, resume_cursor_id, internal_derived_identity_ref:StrongRef<DerivedIdentity>, baseline_payload_ref:StrongRef<DeliveredBaselinePayload>, internal_baseline_digest, public_baseline_digest, public_cursor_position, delivery_policy_ref:StrongRef<SubscriptionDeliveryPolicy<Role>>, semantic_resource_transition_ref:StrongRef<ResourceLedgerTransition>, audit_gate_commitment, detachment_commitment}` and, in the same RootManifest publication, transfers the charge into `SubscriptionResourceEscrow<Role>` and creates exactly one Protocol owner. Initial state selection: a same-apply-visible NotRequired candidate with a valid inline recipe may create `BaselineDeliverable`; a visible candidate without fresh time evidence creates `ReleasedInitialAwaitingActivation`; every Required candidate and every candidate behind an earlier pipeline gap creates `PendingInitialVisibility`. Pending/released states strongly own baseline/policy/escrow but contain **no** `not_before`, `expires_at`, delivery lease, capability bytes, capability nonce, or sender authority, and cannot emit `SUBSCRIBE_READY` or baseline bytes. Audit-visibility maintenance only moves Pending→Released; the independent activation maintenance supplies a fresh `SubscriptionDeliveryLeaseTimeBasis<Role>`, time evidence, and the prebuilt generation-zero Resume capability, and selects `BaselineDeliverable`.

Indexes: `SubscriptionCreationIndex` durably maps the scoped subscription key (`SUBSCRIBE_BEGIN`'s `subscription_idempotency_key` under the complete authority domain) and canonical request digest to exactly one semantic cursor creation plus its Protocol pending owner: exact retry reproduces `SUBSCRIBE_ACCEPTED` while the owner is PendingVisibility/ReleasedAwaitingActivation and reproduces the frozen `SUBSCRIBE_READY` only after BaselineDeliverable; any drift fails; no creation entry owns an absolute lease or Resume capability before activation, and this entry plus `w6-sub-resets`' capability-safe close tombstone make lost creation- and close-response replay deterministic. `SubscriptionCursorDeliveryIndex<Role:AuthorityOwningRole>` is the Protocol-plane canonical pair of maps `cursors[resume_cursor_id -> StrongRef<SubscriptionCursorDeliveryRecord<Role>>]` and `active_leases[delivery_lease_id -> StrongRef<SubscriptionDeliveryLeaseRecord<Role>>]` plus generation, state counts, terminal-disposition floor, and root digest. The separate bounded `PendingCursorOutputIndex<Role>` maps a cursor to at most one data-output `PendingCursorOutputRecord<Role>` (plus, when the reserved freshness policy field is inhabited, at most one standing `FreshnessBreach` notice record beside it — never in the data-output slot); keeping an applied-hidden delta/reset out of the current cursor value prevents an existing capability from detecting it. `SubscriptionCursorActiveCommon<Role>` = `{role_and_group, authority_bound_header:AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>, cursor_creation_request_digest, resume_cursor_id, cursor_state_version, semantic_detachment_identity, escrow_ref:StrongRef<SubscriptionResourceEscrow<Role>>, internal_baseline_digest, public_baseline_digest, public_derived_identity_commitment, public_state_commitment, nonretaining_predecessor_digest}`. `SubscriptionCursorTerminalCommon<Role>` = `{role_and_group, terminal_authority_commitment:TerminalAuthorityCommitment<Role>, cursor_creation_request_digest, resume_cursor_id, terminal_cursor_state_version, semantic_detachment_identity, public_baseline_digest, public_derived_identity_commitment, terminal_public_state_commitment, nonretaining_predecessor_digest}` — no escrow, lease, payload, capability replay, or live authority edge.

The closed state union: `PendingInitialVisibility{common, baseline_payload_ref, baseline_policy_ref, public_cursor_position, audit_gate_commitment}` | `ReleasedInitialAwaitingActivation{common, baseline_payload_ref, baseline_policy_ref, public_cursor_position, audit_release_evidence}` | `BaselineDeliverable{common, lease_ref, capability_lineage_ref:StrongRef<ResultCapabilityLineage>, public_cursor_position}` | `ActiveIdle{common, acknowledged_internal_frontier, last_acked_public_delivery_commitment?, current_capability_lineage_ref, public_cursor_position}` | `ActiveOutstandingDelta{common, lease_ref, prior_acknowledged_internal_frontier, resulting_internal_frontier, current_capability_lineage_ref, public_cursor_position}` | `ResetNoticeDeliverable{common, reset_record_ref, notice_lease_ref, current_capability_lineage_ref, prior_public_cursor_position}` | `ResetAwaitingBaselineActivation{common, reset_record_ref, reset_ack_ref, successor_baseline_payload_ref, successor_policy_ref, successor_public_cursor_position, current_capability_lineage_ref}` | `ResetBaselineDeliverable{common, reset_record_ref, successor_baseline_lease_ref, successor_capability_lineage_ref, successor_public_cursor_position}` | `ExplicitlyPaused{common, pause_record_ref, preserved_delivery_state:PausedCursorState, detached_sender_generation, current_capability_lineage_ref}` | `Closed{common:Terminal, terminal_digest, close_request_digest, outstanding_disposition_commitment, capability_tombstone_ref, escrow_disposition_commitment}` | `Expired{common:Terminal, terminal_digest, expiry_evidence_commitment, capability_tombstone_ref, escrow_disposition_commitment}`. Laws: exactly one current cursor record; at most one outstanding lease; at most one pending future data output. Only Deliverable/Paused states root a lease. Internal fields serve recovery, retention, coalescing proof, and authorized audit; only registered public projections are tokenized or framed.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-15: state-shaped independent-retention machine — Pending/Released retain manifest/policy/escrow; Active arms additionally own lease/replay/send authority; baseline/delta rules forbid delta before baseline ACK and expose every gap. FG-INV-16: no cursor lease/escrow/output lost, duplicated, refunded, or exposed while obligated; audit candidates hidden until the exact batch and gap-free visibility advance. FG-INV-14: cursor records, pending outputs, and leases are GC roots until exact terminal transfer. FG-INV-20: a protected candidate becomes observable only after its signer-locked terminal event, external resolution batch, and gap-free visibility advance.

## Interactions
Baselines come from a `w6-views` `DerivedIdentity`; frontiers/batches from `w6-delta-consumption`; `w5-answer-contracts` types the baseline's `result_answer_contract`. `w9-audit-release` performs Pending→Released via `AuditVisibilityAdvanceSpec` release recipes; `w9-activation-batching` performs Released→Deliverable via `ProtectedOutputActivationSpec::SubscriptionInitialBaseline` inside activation batches with `TimeBoundSubject::ActivationBatch` evidence. `w6-sub-delivery` and `w6-sub-resets` add the remaining transitions; `w10-fgp-core`/`w10-capabilities` frame `SUBSCRIBE_READY` and the Resume capability; `w12-registration-snapshot` later adds the Sharded posture.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
State-union exhaustiveness and generated-schema round-trip tests for every arm. DPOR over create/release/activate interleavings proving: audit delay and time-authority outage never consume a delivery window nor block semantic visibility; Pending/Released can never emit `SUBSCRIBE_READY` or baseline bytes (negative frame tests). Index-law property tests (one current record, one outstanding lease, one pending data output) under concurrent maintenance batches. Crash matrix at every transition; recovery proves checkpoints/protocol snapshots/backup/configuration floors/restore/GC preserve all cursor/pending-output/lease/replay records. Escrow conservation across create→terminal paths. E2E script with logged pipeline order, release evidence identity, activation batch ID, lease ID, and both baseline digests. Creation idempotency: a duplicate `SUBSCRIBE_BEGIN` with the exact scoped key and canonical request digest reproduces `SUBSCRIBE_ACCEPTED` (pending/released) or the byte-identical frozen `SUBSCRIBE_READY` (deliverable); a conflicting request digest under the same key fails uniformly with no second creation.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: connection-bound subscriptions (socket loss is not durable state); baseline bytes flowing before activation; a single digest serving both internal and public roles (leaks derived identity/frontier); cursor state living in semantic payloads (would make release-time facts retroactive parts of candidate roots). Risk: state-machine breadth — mitigated by generated closed unions and exhaustive arm tests.

## Provenance
§9.5 (766–770, 776–792); §12.8 (962–976); Appendix D 3106 (`SubscriptionCreationIndex`); Appendix F FG-INV-14/15/16/20.

title: Implement post-commit triggers: exactly-once durable scheduling records, honest external-effect typing
description:
## What & scope
Implement §9.5's post-commit trigger contract: registered post-commit triggers produce **exactly-once durable scheduling records**, and external effect semantics are typed honestly — an external effect is exactly-once only with a transactional sink; otherwise the invocation carries a stable idempotency key and is at-least-once. The plan never derives external exactly-once effects from an internal obligation alone. This bead also owns §9.5's adjacent claims boundary: MMR proofs authenticate commit membership and raw-log continuity as scoped in §5.8 and do not prove arbitrary MATCH-circuit completeness — trigger/changefeed surfaces and their documentation must repeat that scope, never widen it.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B4 makes committed effects the single source for every reactive feature, and triggers are the smallest such consumer. B5 (§1.11 “claims have types”) forbids the folkloric “exactly-once webhook”: the internal durable scheduling record is the exactly-once object, and the external leg is typed at-least-once unless a transactional sink participates — keeping the trigger surface honest where shipping systems overpromise. Agent workloads (B6) that chain actions off database changes need exactly this split: a durable, replay-safe scheduling record inside the database, and an idempotency key they can deduplicate on outside it.

## Design — normative detail
Per §9.5: “Post-commit triggers provide exactly-once durable scheduling records. External effects are exactly once only with a transactional sink; otherwise the invocation carries a stable idempotency key and is at-least-once. The plan never derives external exactly-once effects from an internal obligation alone.” Implementation consequences of already-normative laws: triggers consume the canonical committed delta stream (`w6-delta-consumption`), never the unresolved intent log, and observe only the audit pipeline's visible endpoint (FG-INV-04); each scheduling record is created durably and deterministically from its trigger registration and the role-tagged committed source (the same retry-reproduces-identical-bytes-or-fails-closed discipline §9.1 fixes for batch IDs), so crash/retry can never mint a duplicate or skip a qualifying commit silently; the stable idempotency key rides every external invocation attempt for the non-transactional-sink case. Any protected or externally visible trigger output follows the same audit-release/activation discipline as other protected outputs (§12.8) rather than bypassing it. MMR/transparency wording on this surface cites only commit membership and raw-log continuity per §5.8's scope.

## Invariants & claim types
The durable scheduling record inherits FG-INV-16's obligation discipline: not lost, duplicated, refunded, released, or exposed while obligated, reaching one legal terminal or recoverable state under declared fairness. FG-INV-04: triggers consume only the pipeline's visible endpoint, never applied-hidden state. FG-INV-15's deterministic batch-identity clause supplies the dedupe basis. The external at-least-once statement is a typed claim boundary, never upgraded: no invariant or doc row may promise external exactly-once without a transactional sink.

## Interactions
Consumes `w6-delta-consumption` (canonical committed delta stream and role-tagged batch identity). `w6-subscriptions`/`w6-sub-delivery` define the neighboring changefeed surface whose delivery/ACK machinery a transactional-sink integration rides; `w10-cdc` shares the honest external-delivery typing for the public CDC surface; `w9-audit-release` gates any protected trigger output; the W2 MMR/transparency work (§5.8) owns the proof scope this bead's surfaces cite.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Property: exactly-once scheduling — for randomized committed workloads with crash/restart injection between commit, scheduling-record creation, and invocation dispatch, each (trigger registration, qualifying commit) pair yields exactly one durable scheduling record, and retry reproduces identical bytes or fails closed (named scenarios: `trigger_crash_before_record`, `trigger_crash_after_record_before_dispatch`, `trigger_duplicate_dispatch_retry`). At-least-once leg: a fault-injected non-transactional sink observes one or more invocations, every attempt carries the same stable idempotency key, and a deduplicating test sink converges to exactly one effect; negative: the status/doc surface never reports a non-transactional sink as exactly-once. Transactional-sink e2e: commit → delta batch → scheduling record → sink consumes record and applies its effect in one transaction → exactly one external effect under repeated crash/retry. Visibility negative: a trigger can never fire from applied-hidden state (pre-visibility candidate produces no scheduling record). E2E script: register a trigger, run a mixed commit workload with crash injection at every arrow (commit → batch apply → scheduling record → dispatch → sink ACK), then verify the scheduling-record ledger is a bijection with qualifying commits. DETAILED LOGGING (implementation and tests): every scheduling-record creation logs trigger registration identity, role-tagged source batch ID, deterministic record key, and idempotency key; every dispatch attempt logs attempt ordinal, idempotency key, sink class (transactional or not), and outcome; tests assert the log stream reconstructs the exactly-once ledger and exposes any duplicate or missing record.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected (plan-explicit): deriving external exactly-once effects from an internal obligation alone; firing triggers off the unresolved intent log; widening MMR proofs into MATCH-circuit completeness claims. Rejected: per-attempt fresh idempotency keys (defeats external dedupe). Risk: users read “exactly-once durable scheduling record” as “exactly-once webhook” — mitigated by the typed at-least-once surface, the sink-class field in every dispatch log, and documentation that repeats the claim boundary.

## Provenance
§9.5 (804); §9.1 (742); §5.8; §12.8; §1.11; Appendix F FG-INV-04/15/16.

title: Implement materialized table/graph views: DerivedGeneration, ViewReadPolicy, watermarks
description:
## What & scope
Implement `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` end to end: the `DerivedGeneration` identity, constructed-graph element identity (`ViewElementKey`/`ViewElementRef`), the four-arm `ViewReadPolicy`, source-coverage/tailing rules, fork/merge/authority/schema rebuild-tail-reset rules, declared deletion/multiplicity/inversion semantics, and model-qualified staleness envelopes.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Fresh materialized views are the market's named pain ("derived state goes stale") and the B6 agent workload's backbone (fresh subgraph views per agent branch). B4 supplies maintenance; B1 supplies branch semantics views must respect; B5 requires that view identity be rebuild-pure so full recompute and incremental maintenance are indistinguishable — the property the derivative-vs-batch oracle checks.

## Design — normative detail
`CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` produces either `BindingTable(schema)` or an explicitly declared `ConstructedGraph(graph_schema)`; arbitrary scalar/path/aggregate results are never mislabeled as virtual labels or edge types. A view generation is `DerivedGeneration { identity: DerivedIdentity, root_oid, global_batch_frontier, answer_contract: AnswerContract }` using §12.4's common identity, so its coordinate-coverage set, schema roots/epochs, definition, circuit build profile, security/semantic epochs, authorization contract, and exact/approximate semantics cannot drift independently. A definer view pins the definer-authority digest plus a separately authorized result-exposure policy; an invoker view is maintained/read in an authority-partitioned domain or recomputed through that invoker's secure view.

Constructed graphs use a rebuild-pure view-local identity namespace: canonical `ViewElementKey` bytes commit definition OID, construction-clause ordinal, output kind, canonical source-binding identity, and deterministic multiplicity/occurrence ordinal. The durable/API identity is `ViewElementRef { key_digest:[u8;32], canonical_key_bytes }`; the digest is only an accelerator — equality/order always verify the complete bytes, so there is no collision-allocation choice or authoritative map to lose. Base and constructed identities form the tagged `ElementIdentity::Base(VId|EId) | Constructed(ViewElementRef)`. A generation may assign dense local ordinals, but they are discardable projections that never escape it. Full recompute and incremental maintenance therefore derive identical identities from definition and inputs alone. The definition fixes duplicate/parallel-edge keys, endpoint mapping, property-conflict aggregation, provenance, and deletion/multiplicity laws.

Reads: a query supplies target `GraphReferenceBinding[]` and selects `ViewReadPolicy = WaitForSnapshot | TailCompensate | AtWatermark | AllowStale`. Each generation carries sorted `DerivedSourceCoverage[]` inside `DerivedIdentity`, associating every input role/relation with a base binding and `Fixed|Advancing` tracking mode. A generation is *direct* only when every advancing source base equals its role's target coordinate, every fixed source still names its exact retained historical binding, and the global frontier agrees. Forward tailing is legal only when branch-lineage proofs show every advancing base is the exact ancestor of its target and contiguous crash-atomic batches cover every required source and the shared global frontier; fixed inputs never move. Roles may be coalesced only by a registered circuit equivalence law. A fork requires its registered fork overlay/base rule; a squash merge appears as an ordinary target-branch delta. For a generation newer than any historical target, the reader uses a retained compatible generation, a proved exact inverse path with full support/history, or recomputes/fails; it never reads future state, and waiting cannot fix a historical query. `AtWatermark`/`AllowStale` return effective bindings/frontier. Every view declares deletion/multiplicity/inversion semantics, retained support, memory/spill bounds, and fallback. Staleness envelopes may be computed from a max-plus maintenance model under named arrival/service assumptions and used as a configuration gate: CREATE rejects an SLO the current model predicts cannot be met, but the returned artifact is a model-qualified estimate; runtime monitors expose actual watermark lag and assumption violations; correctness relies on the explicit read policy, never the prediction. Branch retire (§5.6) drops view/maintainer instances as derived state; every view-generation surface has an `erasure_obligations.toml` row (§12.6). Expiry law (§4.8, closed): a view whose inputs are expiry-bearing must declare, with its registered definition, exactly one of `ExpiryInsensitive`, an explicit `AS OF` evaluation basis, or `ConsumesExpiryEpochTick` — an undeclared definition over an expiry-enabled input fails closed at CREATE/registration; a `ConsumesExpiryEpochTick` view integrates the epoch tick's canonical retraction deltas so the maintained result equals batch evaluation at the epoch boundary, and an `ExpiryInsensitive` view never drifts across ticks.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-15: derivative-vs-batch equality, checked on complete canonical keys and graph contents for constructed graphs. FG-INV-12: exact derived rebuilds preserve logical values, multiplicity, order, visibility, security projection, and AnswerContract. FG-INV-18: rebuildable views can be discarded without changing exact answers or authorization. FG-CFG-03 (configuration-model class, not invariant): staleness SLO feasibility discloses arrival/service assumptions, resource reservation, predicted envelope, actual watermark, fallback policy.

## Interactions
Consumes `w6-zset-circuits` and `w6-delta-consumption` (including its §4.8 expiry and §4.6 valid-time delta laws; `w4-ttl-expiry` supplies the expiry predicate and the `ConsumesExpiryEpochTick` retraction stream the declaration law binds); `w5-answer-contracts` types every generation's `answer_contract`; `w2-branch-fork` supplies branch-lineage proofs and the fork overlay/base rule; `w4-index-lifecycle` provides the shadow→validate→activate pattern for view (re)builds; `w5-planner` consumes views as rewrite targets; `w6-subscriptions` builds baselines from one internal `DerivedIdentity`; `w9-redaction-erasure` walks view generations via the obligation registry; `obs-observatory` surfaces watermark lag.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Derivative-vs-batch oracle comparing complete `ViewElementKey` canonical bytes and graph contents after randomized delta programs, including duplicate/parallel-edge and property-conflict cases. Read-policy conformance suite: all four policies against direct, tailable, and incompatible generations; historical query against a newer generation must use retained generation/inverse path or fail — never wait, never read future state. Fork/squash-merge/authority-change/schema-change matrix exercising each declared rebuild/tail/reset rule. CREATE-time staleness-gate test: a model-infeasible SLO is rejected; the accepted artifact is labeled model-qualified. Crash-atomicity of tail batches; watermark-lag monitor e2e with logged assumption violations; erasure-obligation walker covers a view generation. Expiry-law suite: CREATE over an expiry-enabled input without a declared arm fails closed at registration with a typed, logged error; a `ConsumesExpiryEpochTick` view equals batch evaluation at an epoch-tick boundary (differential); an `ExpiryInsensitive` view is byte-stable across ticks. E2E script: CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW (one `BindingTable`, one declared `ConstructedGraph`) → committed delta churn including duplicate/parallel edges and property-conflict aggregation → read under each of the four `ViewReadPolicy` arms → branch fork and squash merge exercising the registered fork overlay/base and target-delta rules → authority change and schema change exercising their declared rebuild/tail/reset rules → full recompute and identity comparison against the maintained generation, with crash/restart injection at tail-batch and generation-publication boundaries.
