DETAILED LOGGING (implementation and tests): every generation publication logs `DerivedIdentity`, `root_oid`, `global_batch_frontier`, and `answer_contract`; every read logs the policy arm, the direct/tailed/retained-generation/inverse-path/recompute-or-fail decision, the effective bindings/frontier returned, and any lineage-proof failure; the staleness monitor logs actual watermark lag and each named assumption violation; tests assert derivative-vs-batch runs log identical `ViewElementKey` digests and that every read-policy decision is reconstructible from the logs.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: authoritative ordinal maps for constructed elements (a map to lose); virtual-label mislabeling of scalar results; silent cross-authority maintenance for invoker views; treating the max-plus envelope as a guarantee. Risk: inverse-path reads are subtle — shipped only with full support/history proofs, else recompute/fail.

## Provenance
§9.4 (754–762); §12.4/§12.6 (914); §4.8 (266); §5.6 (469–471); §8.5 (707); Appendix F FG-INV-12/15/18, FG-CFG-03.

title: Implement exact integer Z-set circuits, annotation families, and the Ripple runtime
description:
## What & scope
Implement `fgdb-ripple`'s core circuit engine: exact integer Z-set arithmetic (`ZWeight`), the annotation-family discipline, operator-derivative registration for GLA, factorized delta forms, and the spillable LSM-backed arrangement store. This bead owns the semantic domain and circuit runtime; it does not own delta-stream consumption (`w6-delta-consumption`) or any user-facing feature (views/subscriptions/maintainers).

## Why (bets, market, goals)
DBSP's linear-time core is adopted (§3.3) because integer-weighted deltas with registered derivatives power views, subscriptions, recursion, and maintainers from one algebra (B4) — the composition no shipping system has. Exactness is non-negotiable under B5: a bounded weight type makes retraction arithmetic silently wrong at overflow, falsifying derivative=batch (FG-INV-15); hence checked-promote bigint. Factorized delta forms tie B3's executor representation to B4 without flattening cost cliffs. §2.4 records that the Z-set incremental engine is new construction — no foundation crate provides it.

## Design — normative detail
`ZWeight` uses checked `i128` as a fast representation and promotes before overflow to an in-house canonical signed-limb integer (built on `fgdb-bigint` from W1). Limb allocation/spill is resource-accounted; exhaustion aborts or lags the derived computation **without publishing partial state**. The semantic domain is the integer additive group, never a bounded partial imitation. The engine provides lift/differentiate/integrate/delay; registered derivatives for GLA operators, each honoring its Appendix C incrementalization contract; factorized delta forms with proved flattening equivalence; and spillable LSM-backed arrangements per §8.7's larger-than-memory contract (Appendix C declares per-operator minimum resident set, stable merge order, I/O complexity, cleanup, and `ResourceExhausted` behavior). Batch and incremental plans share the typed algebra but have distinct physical optimization/resource contracts.

Annotation families (§9.2): logical change weights always form the integer additive group required for retractions. Optional annotations are separate products: Boolean annotations express existence; provenance-polynomial/DAG annotations express why-provenance; tropical values express costs. Each family registers operator, deletion, differentiation, boundedness, and serialization laws; an unregistered family cannot exist. Replacing Z weights with Boolean or tropical values is forbidden because it erases the additive inverses needed for general deletion. A `Confidence` annotation family over the `[0,1]` semiring is registered by name as a post-1.0 candidate under exactly this discipline — it exists only once its five laws are registered (provenance-polynomial growth is precisely why the boundedness law is mandatory) — and confidence is orthogonal to §8.3's `AnswerRequirement`/`AnswerContract` approximation typing: a confidence-annotated result is not thereby approximate, and an approximate result acquires no confidence semantics. Only registered derivatives are incrementally maintained — "for free" is not a substitute for an operator law.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-15 clause (invariant): "For every registered exact derivative, integrating ordered deltas equals batch evaluation." FG-INV-16 clause: no structured task or scratch object is lost, duplicated, or leaked — arrangement spill runs under asupersync's leak/quiescence oracle. §15.5: Lean/TLA+ anchors cover only the explicitly registered operator/annotation subset — a scoped proof obligation, never a blanket claim. Benchmark class (never invariant): §17 row "Ripple view maintenance: delta application ≥ 1M input-changes/s per circuit worker" on a pinned fixture manifest.

## Interactions
`w1-foundation-types` supplies bigint/delta/claim types; `w5-gla-algebra` and `w5-factorization` define the operators and factorization laws whose derivatives register here; `w6-delta-consumption` feeds committed batches; `w6-recursion`, `w6-views`, `w6-subscriptions`, and `w6-maintainers` instantiate circuits on this runtime; Beacon feeders (`w7-index-core`) and `w5-branch-stats` delta maintainers are downstream consumers; `verif-oracles` hosts the derivative-vs-batch differential.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Unit/property: additive-group laws (associativity, commutativity, inverse, zero) across the i128/bigint promotion boundary; randomized overflow-promotion equivalence against a reference bigint implementation; annotation-family law tests per registered family plus a negative test that an unregistered family fails instantiation. Differential: derivative-vs-batch for every registered GLA derivative on generated workloads including deletions and zero-net churn. Factorized-delta flattening equivalence (identical rows, multiplicity, logical order). Spill: forced-low-memory runs produce identical integrated state; exhaustion yields abort/lag with no partial publication, with the resource-account trace logged. Deterministic seed replay under the lab runtime. E2E script: build a circuit over registered GLA derivatives → feed committed batches through lift/differentiate/integrate/delay under forced i128→bigint promotion and forced arrangement spill → compare integrated state against batch evaluation → inject limb-allocation exhaustion and verify abort/lag with no partial publication, with deterministic seed replay reproducing the identical trace. DETAILED LOGGING (implementation and tests): the runtime logs every i128→limb promotion event with counters, every arrangement spill/merge event with its resource-account delta, every per-batch integration outcome, and every exhaustion abort/lag decision; annotation-family registration logs the five laws checked; tests assert the resource-account trace balances and that no partial state was published across injected exhaustion. Bench harness measuring input-changes/s per circuit worker with pinned fixture and manifest, wired to the §17 gate.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Bigint promotion cost on hot paths (mitigation: i128 fast path plus logged promotion counters); provenance-polynomial state growth (mandatory boundedness law plus resource accounting). Rejected: saturating/wrapping weights; floating-point weights; a Boolean-only "presence" engine; incrementalizing unregistered operators; promoting the `Confidence` family before its laws exist.

## Provenance
§9.1–9.2; §8.7 (725); §3.3; §2.4; Appendix C; Appendix F FG-INV-15/16.

title: Build A+-style adjacency views and dense projections as extra Strata run families
description:
## What & scope
Implement §10.2's adjacency views: user-declared alternative sort orders/partitionings of an edge type's runs — e.g. `INDEX ON :RATED ORDER BY (dst, rating DESC)` — giving Graphflow-style tunable secondary adjacency for query shapes the primary run order cannot serve; plus dense projections: bitmap or dense-tile adjacency views over selected `(label, type, label)` subgraphs.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B2: these are just extra run families — the whole Strata machinery (seal/compact, Elias–Fano offsets, `NeighborCodec` family, generational merge, atomic manifest publication) is reused, so adjacency views inherit the crash/GC/retention story for free instead of forking a parallel store. B3: dense projections feed §8.7's masked-semiring kernels (SpMV/SpMSpV) and set-intersection fast paths. B4: dense projections are derived, Ripple-maintained, and snapshot-cursored.

## Design — normative detail
Secondary adjacency: additional run families keyed by the declared order/partitioning; the kind profile in `IndexDefinition` binds adjacency order/projection. Layout, codecs (`NeighborCodec ∈ { EliasFano, StreamVByte{skip_table}, DenseIntervals }`), generational merge, and atomic manifest publication are Tier-R machinery (§6.3); snapshots pin run generations via epochs; readers never see mixed generations. Codec/map choices remain covered by the logical-digest validator over stable IDs.

Dense projections: bitmap or dense-tile adjacency views over selected `(label, type, label)` subgraphs — derived, Ripple-maintained, snapshot-cursored — feeding the semiring kernels and set-intersection fast paths **without ever becoming a storage-tier citizen** (explicitly never a Strata tier; tier policy must not leak into semantics).

Both kinds are `DerivedRebuildable` (discardable); selection/tailing follows w7-index-core's direct/tail/reject law; deletion semantics follow the definition's update/deletion regime.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12: every claimed answer-equivalent seal, compaction, and codec rewrite preserves logical values, multiplicity, order, visibility, security projection, and AnswerContract. FG-INV-15: for every registered exact derivative, integrating ordered deltas equals batch evaluation (derivative-vs-batch oracle applies to dense-projection maintenance). FG-INV-18: rebuildable views can be discarded without changing exact answers or authorization. Benefit/throughput numbers are `benchmark` class.

## Interactions
Consumes w3-tier-r (run/segment machinery, neighbor codecs, honest intersection contract), w3-seal-compact (lifecycle + digest validators), w6-delta-consumption (maintenance stream), w7-index-core (definition/selection/watermarks). Produces access paths for w5-planner (secondary-order plans), the executor's `TrieCursor` family, and w8-kernels (masked-semiring inputs).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) Metamorphic: secondary-order run contents equal primary adjacency under reorder (logical-digest equivalence over stable IDs). (2) Derivative-vs-batch differential for dense projections under insert/delete workloads including label changes. (3) Crash-matrix rows for view seal/compact; snapshot-cursor tests proving kernel readers pin generations across concurrent compaction. (4) Bench: intersection fast-path and secondary-order benefit vs primary-order plans on a pinned fixture, with committed baseline, variance budget, and flamegraph artifact on regression. Logging: view maintenance emits watermark positions and per-generation coverage. (5) E2E script: declare a secondary-order index (`INDEX ON :RATED ORDER BY (dst, rating DESC)`) and a dense projection over a pinned `(label, type, label)` fixture; run a mixed insert/delete/label-change workload through the Ripple tail; execute the same query via the primary order, the secondary order, and the kernel fast path and assert logical-digest-equal results; force a compaction mid-scan and assert pinned-generation reads; then discard both views and assert exact answers and authorization are unchanged (FG-INV-18). Detailed logging (mandatory implementation events, parsed by the tests): each maintenance delivery logs delta-batch id and watermark position; each seal/compact/manifest publication logs the generation ids swapped; each reader logs its pinned generation set — tests assert these records exist and reconcile with results.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: making dense projections a storage-tier citizen (leaks tier policy into semantics); a bespoke adjacency-index format (Strata reuse is the point of B2). Risk: maintenance cost under churn — the Ripple staleness contract plus discard/rebuild is the fallback; these views are never load-bearing for correctness.

## Provenance
§10.2 (823), §6.3, §8.7, §9.6.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable. The E2E row proves public composition and cannot substitute for a missing unit/property row. Each row names its diagnostic-event schema, fixture profile, deterministic seed or vector, retained evidence artifacts, and one replay command; the owning gate fails if any owned row is absent, waived without an allowed expiring waiver, or reported only through an undifferentiated green bar.

title: Build property B-tree and hash indexes with SSI range-gap witnesses and constraint access
description:
## What & scope
Implement `fgdb-btree`: property B-tree and hash indexes over stable constraint domains and label-membership projections, with composite keys, canonical scalar key encoding, SSI range-gap witnesses, watermarks, and authority domains as parts of the access contract. Covers both `ConstraintCriticalSynchronous` maps (unique/key/cardinality — access implementation only; ownership stays with `fgdb-constraints`) and `DerivedRebuildable` optimizer indexes and filters.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1: property lookups must be branch/snapshot/valid-time exact — the index is an access path into the One Version Universe, not a cache of one head. B5: the access contract (gaps, watermarks, authority domains) is typed so SERIALIZABLE certification can rely on index scans without phantom holes; governance (the §3.3 market gap) means authority domains are part of the contract, never a post-filter.

## Design — normative detail
Unique/key/cardinality maps are `ConstraintCriticalSynchronous`: branch/head/schema-scoped canonical state owned by Chronicle/Txn's `fgdb-constraints`; Beacon provides the access implementation but never asynchronous ownership or a second truth. If constraint state is missing/corrupt, affected writes block until a verified base-state rebuild; recovery never accepts a constraint-affecting write while enforcement is unavailable. Optimizer indexes and filters are `DerivedRebuildable`: discardable without changing exact answers or authorization.

Keys: composite keys use the registered canonical scalar encoding under the definition's scalar/collation profiles, with explicit null/duplicate/missing-value laws from the `IndexDefinition`. Canonical scalar equality, hashing, ordering, and encoding must be coherent (FG-INV-12), so B-tree order, hash bucketing, and digest equality can never disagree.

SSI integration (§7.3): every scan/probe declares its abstract logical-read domain via the `IndexRange { index_generation, low_key, high_key, gaps, early_stop_boundary }` witness, with the three executable contracts `concretization(w)` (the set of logical positive and negative observations represented), `may_affect(final_write, w)`, and `refine(coarse, trace)`. `ORDER BY`/`LIMIT`, uniqueness probes, and early-terminated scans register the gaps or remaining domains whose absence affected the result. Refining a predicate to only the elements returned or encountered is forbidden unless the binder proved a point predicate. A bare physical block address is never a witness.

Watermarks/authority: each generation advertises advancing coverage in commit-sequence units; lookups follow w7-index-core's direct/tail/reject law; authorization applies during statistics, candidates, and traversal.

`Point(2D/3D)` sits outside every registered comparator and index-kind profile in 1.0: a declared index over a `Point` property fails closed as a typed error, and the canonical `Point` byte encoding serves digests and equality only, never a spatial order — the registered §3.4 non-goal (decision owned by g0-format-arms), with the Z/Hilbert-curve-over-B-tree route recorded as the post-1.0 path. This bead mentions and tests the fail-closed behavior; it does not own the decision.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12: canonical scalar equality, hashing, ordering, and encoding are coherent; every claimed answer-equivalent rebuild/compaction/codec rewrite preserves logical values, multiplicity, order, visibility, security projection, and AnswerContract. FG-INV-06: every witness conservatively represents all logically relevant positive, negative, gap, valid-time slice, early-stop, and path-cut observations, and refinement preserves their concretization and `may_affect` behavior (`concretization(refined) ⊆ concretization(coarse)` plus preservation of every gap/absence/early-stop boundary). FG-INV-18: synchronous constraints must hold before commit; rebuildable indexes are discardable. FG-INV-02: for every constraint-owner reservation, at most one legal live generation owns or may consume it. Latency/throughput numbers are `benchmark` class only.

## Interactions
Consumes w7-index-core (definition/selection kernel, watermarks), w4-ssi-witnesses (witness algebra, refine-vs-abort budget), w4-constraints (uniqueness/cardinality semantics, `ConstraintStateRoot`), w1-collections (ART/succinct in-memory structures), w5-planner (`IndexProbe` operator, decision cards); g0-format-arms registered the `Point` non-goal. Builds/activation flow through w7-index-core from w4-index-lifecycle.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) Scalar-law property/fuzz suite: order/hash/encode coherence across all registered scalar types including null/duplicate/missing-value laws. (2) Phantom model tests: insert precisely the missing keys that could invalidate negative results (uniqueness probes, gap scans, early-stopped LIMIT scans) — each must surface an SSI conflict via the registered `IndexRange` gaps. (3) Constraint drill: corrupt a unique map; affected writes block; verified rebuild unblocks; no constraint-affecting write accepted while enforcement is unavailable. (4) `Point` negative: `CREATE INDEX` on a `Point` property returns the typed fail-closed error. (5) §7.5 battery rows: crash during segment seal/compact, rebuild-switch, definition-drift, branch-fork/merge, delete. (6) Differential: lookups/range scans vs `fgdb-reference` across branch forks and valid-time slices. Logging: every probe emits generation, key range, gap count, and early-stop boundary. (7) E2E script: create unique-constraint and optimizer B-tree/hash indexes on a branched fixture; run concurrent writers issuing uniqueness probes, gap scans, and early-stopped LIMIT scans under SERIALIZABLE while injecting precisely the phantom keys from (2); assert SSI aborts surface with the registered `IndexRange` gaps; fork a branch, run the same probes at both heads, and verify branch/snapshot/valid-time-exact answers vs `fgdb-reference`; finish with the (3) constraint-corruption drill exercised end-to-end. Detailed logging (mandatory implementation events, parsed by the tests): every probe logs `{index_generation, key range, gap_count, early_stop_boundary}`; constraint-enforcement block/unblock transitions and verified-rebuild completion log typed events — tests verify witness registration and blocking behavior from these logs.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: spatial ordering in 1.0 (registered non-goal); physical block addresses as witnesses; asynchronous unique enforcement. Risk: witness refinement becoming a second query — refine-vs-abort is a budgeted decision card with conservative-abort fallback (§7.3, §20); the knob defaults conservative.

## Provenance
§10.1 (822), §7.3 (594-614), §12.4, §6.2, Appendix F.

title: Build segment-based full-text index: tokenizers, BM25, Levenshtein fuzzy over term ART
description:
## What & scope
Implement `fgdb-fts`: a segment-based inverted index with in-house tokenization (Unicode word-boundary plus language-pluggable stemmers), BM25 scoring with positions/phrase support, and fuzzy matching (edit distance ≤ 2) via Levenshtein automata over the term ART. frankensqlite's FTS5 module is the in-family behavioral reference.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B2: FTS segments follow the same seal/compact lifecycle as Strata runs (§3.3 verdict: "Adopt, segment-based with the same seal/compact lifecycle"), inheriting crash/GC/retention behavior instead of forking a bespoke store. B4: ingestion is a Ripple consumer (§9.6 names the vector/FTS ingestion pipelines explicitly), so commit→searchable is a measured watermark — directly answering the derived-state-freshness market gap. B6: hybrid retrieval (w7-hybrid) needs honest BM25 statistics under authority — governance is the other flagged market gap. Tokenization is in-house per the plan's dependency constraints.

## Design — normative detail
Segments: postings segments are sealed immutable objects; seal (mutable tail → segment) then generational merge, atomic manifest publication, snapshot-pinned generations, readers never see mixed generations — the Tier-R pattern applied to postings.

Tokenization: in-house Unicode word-boundary tokenization with language-pluggable stemmers. The FTS kind profile in `IndexDefinition` binds Unicode/tokenizer/normalizer/stemmer/stopword/scorer **artifact OIDs**, so tokenizer or scorer drift is identity drift (a new definition/generation), never a silent behavior change; g0-language-contracts pins the Unicode bundle.

Scoring: BM25 with positions and phrase queries; fuzzy matching at edit distance ≤ 2 via Levenshtein automata over the term ART (w1-collections). All membership/score/order-affecting parameters (scorer artifact, stopword set, normalizer) are semantic per w7-index-core's semantic-parameter law.

Authority: per §12.4, BM25 statistics require exact-domain state or a proved sufficient decomposition; hidden elements cannot influence scores; authorization applies during statistics, candidates, and scoring (§10's law), never as a final filter.

Freshness: newly committed documents ride the canonical delta stream into the mutable tail; commit→delta-tail-searchable and commit→merged-generation latencies are the reported/gated freshness metrics (§17), bounded at query time by the optional `FreshnessConstraint` in watermark units.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12: exact rebuild equivalence preserves logical values, multiplicity, order, visibility, security projection, and AnswerContract; text-profile coherence. FG-INV-20: authorization precedes every observation including statistics and scoring — corpus statistics are computed over the authorized exact domain, never global-then-filtered. FG-INV-15: integrating ordered deltas equals batch evaluation for postings maintenance. FG-INV-04: erased subjects (erasure-tombstone conjunct, §12.6) and expired elements (expiry predicate, §4.8) are unobservable through postings, statistics, and fuzzy candidates. Claim classes: freshness is FG-EVID-04 (slo-class: bound in watermark/commit-sequence units, realized lag distribution, typed `FreshnessBreach` rate, fallback policy); staleness SLO feasibility is FG-CFG-03 (`slo.toml`).

## Interactions
Consumes w7-index-core (definition/selection/watermarks), w1-collections (term ART, Levenshtein automata substrate), w1-codecs (postings compression: varint/bitpack/roaring-class), w3-seal-compact (lifecycle pattern + digest validators), w6-delta-consumption (ingestion stream), g0-language-contracts (pinned Unicode bundle/collations). Consumers: w7-hybrid (candidates + BM25 statistics), w5-planner (text access paths).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) Differential vs frankensqlite FTS5 behavioral corpus for tokenization, BM25 ranking, phrase, and fuzzy queries. (2) Property/fuzz: tokenizer determinism across platforms under the pinned Unicode bundle; postings encode/decode roundtrip fuzz. (3) Levenshtein automaton: exhaustive edit ≤ 2 equivalence vs brute-force on sampled dictionaries. (4) Erasure test: after an `ErasureCutSpec` erasure cut, the subject's terms are unobservable in postings, statistics, and fuzzy candidate enumeration. (5) §7.5 battery rows: crash, stale-tail, rebuild-switch, definition-drift (changed stemmer artifact = new generation). (6) Freshness bench: commit→delta-tail-searchable p50/p99 under sustained ingest, logging watermark lag per delivery; gate wired per §17's derived-state freshness row. (7) E2E script: build an FTS index over a pinned document corpus; ingest committed documents while querying phrase/fuzzy/BM25 rankings under a `FreshnessConstraint`, asserting typed fallback/failure behavior when the watermark bound is unmet; swap the stemmer artifact OID and assert a new generation (definition drift), never silent behavior change; execute an erasure cut and re-run the observability checks end-to-end. Detailed logging (mandatory implementation events, parsed by the tests): ingestion logs per-delivery watermark lag; every query logs generation identity, tokenizer/scorer artifact OIDs, and realized freshness; erasure processing logs tombstone-conjunct application — tests verify the freshness and erasure claims from these logs.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: external tokenizer/search library dependencies (in-house per plan); score-time output filtering as the authority mechanism (statistics must be exact-domain or a proved decomposition). Risks: stemmer/language coverage — pluggable stemmer artifact OIDs make adding a language an identity change, not a code fork; global-statistics staleness under heavy tails — declared staleness contract with merged-generation statistics and disclosed lag.

## Provenance
§10.3 (824), §3.3 (148), §12.4, §6.3 pattern, §9.6, §17, Appendix F.

title: Implement the hybrid retrieval operator: HybridSearchSpec, exact RRF fusion, contracts
description:
## What & scope
Implement the hybrid retrieval operator (§10.6): one GLA operator fusing full-text, vector, and graph-expansion sources under a single pinned `HybridSearchSpec`, with exact deterministic fusion arithmetic and honest answer-contract composition.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B6: GraphRAG/agent-memory is the 2026 adoption wave and hybrid convergence is explicit in the market synthesis (§3.3) — buyers want text+vector+graph in one governed query. B3: this is a Loom GLA operator, not a bolt-on service, so planning, witnesses, contracts, and replay compose through the ordinary machinery. B5: fusion is exact, deterministic arithmetic; approximation appears only as typed contracts, never as silent float drift.

## Design — normative detail
`HybridSearchSpec` pins: target `GraphReferenceBinding[]`; an explicit input-role→`IndexSnapshot { identity: DerivedIdentity, root_oid, answer_contract }` mapping; every snapshot's coordinate coverage/global frontier; text/vector candidate depths; expansion budget/path semantics; fusion build/profile ObjectIds; duplicate aggregation; tie policy; authority domain; output `AnswerRequirement`; and exact fallback. Candidate depths change the recall population, so they are semantic parameters pinned in the spec/contract — never physical tuning.

Fusion laws: RRF fixes positive integer `k0`, one-based rank, missing-modality zero, and canonical per-source ties; STRICT comparison uses exact rational cross-products with overflow promotion to canonical big integers (w1-foundation-types signed-limb exact integers), while exposed Decimal128 scores use the profile's fixed scale/rounding. Weighted fusion names exact Decimal128 weights and versioned normalizers.

Graph expansion defines duplicate/path-score aggregation and prunes only with admissible upper bounds. Authority: BM25 statistics, ANN traversal, seed resolution, and expansion use the authorized bindings; hidden elements cannot influence scores or routing.

Contract composition: the GLA operator composes every input contract, tail state, fusion stage, and expansion stage; it emits `Exact` only after complete exact sources/fallback and otherwise emits a fully populated `Approximate` contract satisfying the requirement. Per §8.3's transfer-rule law, absence-sensitive downstream operators cannot turn missing candidates into an exact result; unmet requirements trigger the pinned exact fallback or a typed failure.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-20: authorization precedes every observation — restated here for seed resolution, statistics, routing/scoring, and expansion; hidden elements cannot influence any observable. FG-INV-12: same pinned spec plus generations produce identical canonical results; changed candidate depths or fusion profile is a different identity, never a tuning knob. FG-INV-19: replay pins the spec, source generation identities/digests, and evidence identity; the approximate result stays byte-replayable without being promoted to exact. FG-INV-06: expansion registers path cuts/gaps so SERIALIZABLE reads over hybrid results remain sound. Claim types: hybrid quality/recall evidence follows FG-CAL-03 discipline per source population (`evidence.toml`); latency numbers are `benchmark` class.

## Interactions
Consumes w7-fts (text candidates + authorized BM25 statistics), w7-vector (ANN candidates + Approximate contracts), w5-gla-algebra (operator registration; Appendix C rows define memory, factorization, cancellation, witness, incrementalization, path-preservation, authorization, answer-contract transfer, and replanning contracts), w5-answer-contracts (requirement/contract realization), w5-planner (`HybridSearch` logical operator, decision cards), w1-foundation-types (bigint rationals, Decimal128 profile). Surfaced to agents through w10 protocol surfaces.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) Determinism: byte-identical canonical results across runs and platforms for a pinned spec; the STRICT rational path exercised with overflow-promoting fixtures. (2) RRF unit/property tests: `k0` positivity, one-based ranks, missing-modality zero, canonical tie behavior — cross-checked against a naive exact-rational reference implementation. (3) Contract composition: any approximate source or uncompensated tail forces a fully populated `Approximate`; `Exact` emitted only after complete exact sources/fallback; unmet requirement triggers exact fallback or typed failure. (4) Authority differential: runs with and without capability-hidden seeds/documents/vectors produce identical scores, routing, candidate sets, and expansions. (5) Pruning admissibility: property test that the bound function dominates true scores on randomized graphs; pruned-vs-unpruned top-k equality. (6) E2E script: text+vector+expansion query over a pinned corpus logging spec digest, per-source generation identities, fusion trace, and realized contract; replay must be byte-identical.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: float-order-dependent fusion (nondeterministic cross-platform ranking); post-hoc filtering of unauthorized results (violates authorization-before-observation); inadmissible pruning inside an `Exact` claim. Risk: exact-rational comparison cost — exposed scores ride the fixed-scale Decimal128 path; the STRICT rational path is budgeted and benchmarked.

## Provenance
§10.6 (829), §8.3, §3.3 (149), Appendix C, Appendix F.

title: Implement fgdb-index-core: IndexSnapshot coverage law, watermarks, authority split
description:
## What & scope
Build `fgdb-index-core`: the shared kernel every Beacon index kind implements against. It owns: the `IndexSnapshot` type and the total generation-selection (direct/tail/reject) decision procedure; the canonical versioned `IndexDefinition` schema; the `IndexAuthority` union; watermark/advancing-coverage bookkeeping in commit-sequence units; rebuildability/discard semantics; and the wiring of every kind into delta-tail maintenance and the shadow-build lifecycle. Scope excludes kind-specific data structures (children own those) and the build state machine (w4-index-lifecycle owns `DerivedBuildRegistry`).

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B1: which states a generation answers for must be a checkable proof obligation. B4: tails ride the canonical post-commit delta stream — incremental reindexing (a named 2026 market gap, §3.3) becomes structural. B5: selection is total with typed rejection. B6: agents consume `AnswerContract`s and watermark-unit freshness bounds instead of guessing lag.

## Design — normative detail
Every index generation exposes `IndexSnapshot { identity: DerivedIdentity, root_oid, answer_contract: AnswerContract }`; an index definition normally has one canonical advancing source role. A query separately supplies target `CoordinateSchemaBinding[]`. Selection law: a root is **direct** only at exact binding/frontier equality; it **may tail** only when each advancing `DerivedSourceCoverage.base_binding.selected_head` is a proved ancestor on that exact branch and a contiguous delta path reaches every target under the shared frontier. Fork overlays and squash-merge deltas follow their explicit branch rules. A newer/nonancestor root is unusable except through a retained matching historical generation or a separately proved inverse/recompute path. Definition/topology/authority/profile mismatch is not "close enough". No path silently omits a tail. Authorization applies during statistics, candidates, traversal, scoring, and result construction — never as a final filter.

`DerivedIdentity` (shared with views, §12.4): `{ authority_bound_header: AuthorityBoundHeader<Role>, kind, definition_oid, source_coverage: sorted Vec<DerivedSourceCoverage{ input_role_id, source_relation_id, base_binding: CoordinateSchemaBinding, tracking_mode: Fixed|Advancing, lineage_digest }>, global_batch_frontier?, topology_epoch, language_contract_oid?, semantic_profile_oid, scalar_profile_oid, collation_profile_oid?, redaction_profile_oid, build_profile_oid }`. Equal epoch/digest scalars under another policy/revocation root cannot share an identity or cache/build generation. A lookup must match all fields before applying an explicitly registered tail/rebuild rule; no singular graph/head/schema key may stand in for a coordinate set.

`IndexDefinition` is canonical and versioned, not opaque DDL text. Common fields bind source graph predicate/bound expressions, branch policy, authority mode, semantic/scalar/collation profiles, null/duplicate/missing-value laws, a definition-time `ApproximationProfile?`, and update/deletion regime. Kind profiles bind: B-tree/hash key encoding/comparator; FTS Unicode/tokenizer/normalizer/stemmer/stopword/scorer artifact OIDs; vector dtype/dimension/metric/normalization plus HNSW/IVF/PQ and recall-population contract; adjacency order/projection; path edge/label/cost projection and deletion semantics. Semantic-parameter law: every parameter that can change membership, score, order, recall population, or stopping — including approximate topology seed/generation, candidate/search depth, quantizer, rerank count, early-stop rule — is semantic and appears in `definition_oid`, `DerivedIdentity`, the `ApproximationProfile`, or the consuming realized `AnswerContract`; only proved answer-preserving layout/scheduling knobs may live in a physical build profile. Independent rebuilds may claim equivalence only when they reproduce the same exact contents or the same pinned approximate generation/answer contract; a rebuilt ANN topology is a new semantic generation even from the same DDL.

`IndexAuthority = ConstraintCriticalSynchronous | DerivedRebuildable`. `ConstraintCriticalSynchronous` is the branch/head/schema-scoped canonical state owned by Chronicle/Txn's `fgdb-constraints`; Beacon may provide its access implementation but never asynchronous ownership or a second truth. Derived indexes may be discarded. Missing/corrupt constraint state blocks affected writes until a verified base-state rebuild; recovery never accepts a constraint-affecting write while enforcement is unavailable.

Freshness hooks: an `AnswerRequirement` may carry `freshness_constraint: FreshnessConstraint { maximum_source_lag: WatermarkLagBound, on_unmet: ExactFallback|Fail }`, bounding advancing-generation lag behind the executing snapshot's pinned read frontier in watermark (commit-sequence) units, never wall-clock — no time-authority observation joins the hot read path; realized lag derives from the contract's `source_generation_identities[]`.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12: approximate candidate/topology changes create a new pinned semantic generation; no build progress or physical index artifact changes schema visibility before its ordinary transactional SchemaOp activation; every claimed answer-equivalent exact derived rebuild preserves logical values, multiplicity, order, visibility, security projection, and AnswerContract. FG-INV-18: index/build controls remain invisible until a transactional SchemaOp activates a validated generation; rebuildable indexes can be discarded without changing exact answers or authorization. FG-INV-20: authorization precedes every observation or effect across storage, statistics, routing/scoring, temporal selection, and derived state; equal epoch scalars with different roots/service epochs never substitute. FG-INV-15: for every registered exact derivative, integrating ordered deltas equals batch evaluation. FG-INV-04: index reads obey the erasure-tombstone conjunct (§12.6) and the expiry predicate (§4.8). Claim classes: staleness SLO feasibility is FG-CFG-03 (`slo.toml`); realized freshness is FG-EVID-04 (slo-class, never an invariant); recall is FG-CAL-03 (`evidence.toml`).

## Interactions
Consumes: w4-index-lifecycle (`DerivedBuildRegistry`, `DerivedGenerationValidationCertificate`, transactional `SchemaOp::ActivateDerivedGeneration`), w6-delta-consumption (delta-batch/frontier stream for tails), w3-seal-compact (segment-set publication, digest validators), w9-enforcement (§12.4 authority reuse law), w4-constraints (`ConstraintStateRoot` ownership), w5-answer-contracts (`AnswerRequirement`/`AnswerContract`/freshness). Produces the trait/kernel surface for w7-btree, w7-adjacency-views, w7-fts, w7-vector, w7-path-temporal, w7-hybrid; w5-planner consumes selection decisions.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) Property tests: selection over randomized branch DAGs — direct only at exact equality; tail accepted iff ancestry plus contiguity hold (cross-checked against `fgdb-reference` lineage prover); newer/nonancestor roots rejected with typed reasons. (2) Mutation tests: delete one delta batch from a tail — selection must reject or fully compensate, never serve a silent gap; profile/authority/definition mismatch is never selected. (3) Expose §7.5 gate-battery hooks to every kind: differential, metamorphic, crash, stale-tail, definition-drift, policy/revocation, branch-fork/merge, delete, approximation-generation, rebuild-switch. (4) Logging: every selection emits a structured decision record (identity fields compared, tail interval, proof kind, rejection reason). (5) Constraint-unavailability drill: corrupt a constraint component; affected writes block while non-constraint reads continue; verified base-state rebuild restores writes. (6) E2E script: register two index definitions across two branches; drive commits through the delta tail; issue lookups at direct, tail-provable, and newer/nonancestor coordinates and assert direct/tail/reject decisions with typed reasons; then activate a rebuilt generation through the ordinary `SchemaOp::ActivateDerivedGeneration` transaction and assert the switch is atomic while replay pinned to the retained old root is unaffected. Detailed logging (mandatory implementation events, parsed by the tests): in addition to (4)'s selection decision records, log watermark advancement, tail-integration batches (batch id, frontier), authority-check outcomes, and activation/discard lifecycle events keyed by identity digest — tests reconstruct the complete selection and maintenance history from logs.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: best-effort selection repaired by output filtering (violates FG-INV-20 and the no-silent-tail law); a singular graph/head key as coverage identity (aliases branches and valid-time selectors); asynchronous constraint enforcement (a second truth). Risk: ancestry/tail proof cost on hot paths — mitigate with lineage-proof caches keyed by identity digest, authority-partitioned per §12.4.

## Provenance
§10 (816-820), §12.4 (896-898), §8.3 (690), §7.5 (643-645), Appendix F.

title: Build adaptive 2-hop/landmark path indexes and the persistent-union-find temporal index
description:
## What & scope
Implement `fgdb-pathidx`: (a) adaptive path/reachability indexes — 2-hop/pruned-landmark labeling built on demand for explicit graph/authority projections (§10.5); (b) the temporal connectivity index — rollback/persistent union-find plus offline segment-tree-over-time generations answering `CONNECTED … AS OF` probes over sealed history (§10.7).

## Why (bets, market, goals)
B3: repeated reachability/shortest-path load is common in agent/GraphRAG workloads; on-demand labeling turns per-query BFS into sub-100µs probes. B1: exact historical connectivity at any covered sequence is a One Version Universe capability no mainstream competitor offers. B5: the `(1−1/e)` badge law and the sealed-exact contract embody calibrated adaptivity — optimization claims carry their theorem's actual preconditions or are labeled `HEURISTIC`. SOTA (§3.5): rollback/persistent union-find (Conchon & Filliâtre lineage) and offline dynamic connectivity are adopted **as one Beacon generation type**, with explicit projection, interval, deletion, branch-overlay, and fallback contracts rather than a universal polylog claim.

## Design — normative detail
Path/reachability (§10.5): 2-hop/pruned-landmark labeling is built *on demand* for an explicit graph/authority projection when repeated reachability or shortest-path load justifies it, then maintained by Ripple or rebuilt/dropped under its declared update regime. Landmark and portfolio selection may use lazy greedy. A `(1−1/e)` badge is legal only when the registered measured-benefit objective is proved nonnegative, monotone, and submodular under the actual cardinality budget; other byte, dependency, or matroid constraints use the theorem matching that constraint or label the choice `HEURISTIC`. Every decision still publishes objective samples, marginal-gain trace, feasibility checks, uncertainty, deterministic fallback, and any valid upper bound — never a generic "optimality certificate". The kind profile binds path edge/label/cost projection and deletion semantics.

Temporal connectivity (§10.7): rollback/persistent union-find and offline segment-tree-over-time generations accelerate declared graph projections. Each generation pins branch, edge-type/label projection, authority domain, sequence range, and deletion semantics. **Sealed-exact projection semantics**: `sealed-exact` roots may answer only covered snapshots — a probe at sequence `s` is served exactly iff `s` lies inside the generation's covered sequence range for the matching projection/branch/authority-domain tuple; exactness is a property of the (projection, root) pair, so probes for other label/type projections, other branches, other authority domains, or uncovered sequences must not reuse the root. An uncovered tail or branch overlay is compensated **completely** or the probe falls back to BFS at the requested snapshot. Online approximate roots are never selected for an exact `CONNECTED` contract. Construction (§3.5): exact historical connectivity for a sealed operation interval via a segment tree over time (edge presence intervals mapped onto segment-tree nodes) plus rollback DSU in DFS order, with preprocessing/space and query costs stated for that construction — never claimed universally; insert-only current windows admit a cheaper plain DSU.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12: a new topology/coverage is a new generation; exact rebuilds preserve logical values, multiplicity, order, visibility, security projection, and AnswerContract. FG-INV-18: on-demand indexes are discardable without changing exact answers or authorization; recompute (BFS/Prism) is the universal fallback so the index is never load-bearing for correctness. FG-INV-20: authorization precedes traversal/routing — the projection's authority domain is part of generation identity. FG-INV-15: when Ripple-maintained, integrating ordered deltas equals batch evaluation. Claim types: probe latency is `benchmark` class — §17 row: provisional <100µs per probe over every sequence sampled by the pinned sealed-history fixture, exact only for a matching `sealed-exact` projection/root, with branch overlays or uncovered tails compensated or falling back. The submodularity badge is proof-class only within its named model; measured benefit is `benchmark`; the maintainer staleness contract (`exact | bounded-error(ε) | eventually-refreshed`, §9.6) surfaces in query certificates.

## Interactions
Consumes w7-index-core (generation identity/selection incl. sequence-range coverage), w4-index-lifecycle (build/validate/transactional-activate for offline generations), w6-maintainers (Ripple incremental connected-components maintainer, staleness contracts, Prism recompute fallback), w6-delta-consumption (tail stream), w5-planner (probe-vs-index-vs-BFS choice with decision cards; `PathFind`/`VarLengthExpand` integration). Path reads compose with w4-ssi-witnesses `PathCut` witnesses under SERIALIZABLE.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) Differential: probes vs BFS ground truth at every sampled sequence over randomized temporal graphs, including deletes (offline segment-tree construction) and insert-only windows (plain DSU); branch-overlay cases compensated or refused, never approximated silently. (2) Coverage property tests: probes outside the sequence range, or with wrong projection/branch/authority, are never served by a sealed-exact root — typed rejection plus a logged fallback record. (3) Exact-contract negative: an online approximate root is never selected when the contract demands exact `CONNECTED`. (4) Submodularity gate: the `(1−1/e)` badge is emitted only when the registered objective's nonnegativity/monotonicity/submodularity checks pass under the actual cardinality budget; matroid/byte-budget variants emit matching-theorem or `HEURISTIC` labels; decision artifacts contain objective samples, marginal-gain trace, feasibility checks, uncertainty, fallback, and upper bound. (5) Bench: the <100µs probe gate on the pinned sealed-history fixture with full distribution reporting. (6) Lifecycle: on-demand build trigger, Ripple maintenance, rebuild/drop under the declared update regime; crash rows during generation build. (7) E2E script: seal a temporal history fixture; build a `sealed-exact` generation for one projection/branch/authority tuple; probe `CONNECTED … AS OF` across covered sequences, an uncovered tail, a forked branch overlay, and a wrong-projection probe — asserting exact answers, complete compensation or BFS fallback, and typed rejection respectively; then trigger on-demand 2-hop labeling under repeated reachability load and verify probe/fallback parity with BFS at every stage. Detailed logging (mandatory implementation events, parsed by the tests): every probe logs generation identity, requested sequence, coverage verdict (covered | compensated | fallback | rejected), and fallback cost; landmark-selection decisions log the complete (4) artifact set; build/maintenance logs carry watermark positions — tests assert these records reconcile with returned results.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Rejected: universal polylog dynamic-connectivity claims (the adopted construction states costs for its sealed interval only); generic optimality certificates for landmark selection; serving branch overlays approximately (must compensate completely or fall back). Risk: maintenance cost under delete-heavy churn — the declared update regime permits rebuild/drop, and correctness never depends on the index.

## Provenance
§10.5 (828), §10.7 (830), §3.5 (179), §9.6, §17 (1254), §18.1 (1290), Appendix F.

title: Build vector ANN with historical topology: HNSW generations, quantizers, recall evidence
description:
## What & scope
Implement `fgdb-vector`: vector ANN with historical topology — HNSW over mutable delta plus immutable generation roots, SQ8/PQ/IVF-PQ physical codecs with versioned reconstruction-error evidence, the authorized-snapshot recall apparatus, exact fallback, and the commit→searchable freshness pipeline.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
The 2026 market synthesis (§3.3) flags fresh transactional ANN under real governance as an unmet buyer need (GraphRAG/agent-memory adoption; gaps: governance, derived-state freshness, incremental reindexing); §10.4 is the deliberate leapfrog. SOTA verdict (§3.3): adopt HNSW/IVF-PQ **only** with pinned historical authorized roots, complete delta-tail compensation, exact fallback, and population-qualified recall evidence. B5: recall is typed statistical evidence, never proof. B1: replay pinned to a retained old root is immutable. B6: agents get honest Approximate contracts.

## Design — normative detail
Generations: HNSW uses mutable delta plus immutable generation roots, but each query pins one `IndexSnapshot { identity: DerivedIdentity, root_oid, answer_contract }`. Nodes newer than the requested snapshot cannot participate as routing bridges. Rebuild creates a new root and never changes replay pinned to a retained old root; a rebuilt ANN topology is a new semantic generation even when configured from the same DDL (`topology_epoch` in `DerivedIdentity`). A coverage base older than a target is usable only with the exact per-coordinate ancestry and contiguous-tail proof (w7-index-core law); otherwise the query waits or selects an exact scan — never output-filters an incompatible topology into a false claim of snapshot completeness. Exact reranking is exact only within the candidate set: it cannot repair missed candidates.

Confidentiality law: a capability-hidden node may never affect candidate membership, routing hops, scores, stopping, timing class, resource/error metadata, or any other observable in **any** answer mode unless a formally verified authority-partitioned/filter-aware topology proves the declared noninterference law; `Approximate` may weaken recall, never confidentiality. Per §12.4, HNSW/graph-routing topology requires exact authorized topology or a separately proved filter-aware construction. Deleted-but-authorized nodes are a separate temporal question: they participate only when the pinned snapshot/answer contract explicitly includes their historical visibility.

Codecs: SQ8/PQ/IVF-PQ are physical codecs with versioned reconstruction-error evidence. A JL projection may carry a probabilistic multiplicative bound with dataset size, dimension, and failure probability; PQ generally carries residual/additive or empirical distance-error bounds, not a universal `(1±ε)` guarantee. The kind profile binds vector dtype/dimension/metric/normalization plus HNSW/IVF/PQ parameters and the recall-population contract. Every membership/score/order/recall-population/stopping-affecting parameter — topology seed/generation, candidate/search depth, quantizer, rerank count, early-stop rule — is semantic and pinned in `definition_oid`/`DerivedIdentity`/`ApproximationProfile`/realized `AnswerContract`; only proved answer-preserving layout/scheduling knobs live in the physical build profile.

Approximation machinery (§8.3): definition-time `ApproximationProfile { approximation_kind, population_contract, algorithm_profile_oid, semantic_build_and_search_parameter_schema, quality_evidence_schema, deterministic_exact_fallback_oid? }`; execution-time `AnswerRequirement = Exact | AllowApproximate { permitted_kinds[], population_constraint?, minimum_quality?, evidence_floor, on_unmet: ExactFallback|Fail }`; realized `AnswerContract = Exact | Approximate { approximation_kind, population_contract, error_or_recall_contract, source_generation_identities[], source_generation_digests[], algorithm_profile_oid, candidate_and_search_profile, evidence_identity, deterministic_fallback_oid? }`. STRICT queries may request an exact fallback.

Recall evidence: sampling is keyed and names the query population, exact baseline, snapshot/authority domain, sample design, and alpha; e-processes are health evidence and rebuild triggers, not proof of per-query recall — no sample can "certify" each insert.

Freshness (commit→searchable hooks): ingestion is a Ripple consumer; report and gate logical commit→delta-tail-searchable and commit→merged-generation p50/p99 (values provisional) plus watermark lag under sustained ingest (§17); `AnswerRequirement.freshness_constraint` bounds source lag in watermark units with `ExactFallback|Fail`. Embedding matrices are generation-pinned inputs (§6.4); "zero-copy" only when requested dtype, alignment, authorization, and snapshot generation actually match.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12: approximate candidate/topology changes create a new pinned semantic generation; no build progress changes schema visibility before its transactional SchemaOp activation. FG-INV-19: exact approximate generations are replay evidence slots — an approximate result remains byte-replayable under its pinned closure but is never promoted to exact semantics. FG-INV-20: authorization precedes routing/scoring/candidate observation. FG-INV-18: rebuildable generations discardable. Claim classes: recall/drift is FG-CAL-03 (`evidence.toml`: authorized snapshot population, keyed sample, exact baseline, candidate policy, confidence interval, rebuild action); freshness is FG-EVID-04 (slo-class); §17 benchmark gate: 10M × 768-d f32 HNSW, provisional ≥20k QPS at measured recall ≥0.95 on a pinned authorized-snapshot corpus, publishing exact-baseline sampling and confidence interval, with commit→delta-tail-searchable and commit→merged-generation latencies reported separately.

## Interactions
Consumes w7-index-core (identity/selection/semantic-parameter law), w4-index-lifecycle (shadow build → validate → transactional activation; `DerivedGenerationValidationCertificate` binds the approximation profile), w6-delta-consumption (ingestion tail), w5-answer-contracts (contract realization), w1-sketch-calibrate (e-process recall monitors), w9-enforcement (authority-partitioned topology law), w3-properties (generation-pinned embeddings). Consumers: w7-hybrid, w5-planner; perf-freshness-vector gates the numbers.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
(1) Historical topology: a query pinned to an old root is unaffected by rebuild (byte-replay under the FG-INV-19 closure); injected newer nodes produce no observable change in candidates, hops, scores, stopping, or timing class. (2) Noninterference differential: runs with and without capability-hidden nodes are observably identical across all answer modes, timing class included. (3) §7.5 approximation-generation battery: changed seed/search-depth/quantizer/rerank/early-stop must yield a new generation identity; masquerade attempts fail CI. (4) Recall apparatus: keyed sampling vs exact baseline on the pinned corpus; FG-CAL-03 disclosure-completeness check; e-process rebuild-trigger drill. (5) Fallback conformance: STRICT and unmet `AllowApproximate` demands route to exact scan and return `Exact` contracts. (6) Deleted/erased vectors: deleted-but-authorized participate only under explicit historical visibility; erased subjects are unobservable, including as routing bridges. (7) Bench wiring: QPS/recall gate plus freshness p50/p99 with watermark-unit logging, committed baselines, flamegraph on regression. (8) E2E script: build an HNSW generation over the pinned authorized-snapshot corpus; sustain vector ingest through the delta tail while querying under both `AllowApproximate` and STRICT; trigger a rebuild mid-run and assert old-root replay byte-stability plus a new generation identity; revoke a capability mid-run and assert noninterference across all observables; finish by producing the keyed recall sample and freshness report. Detailed logging (mandatory implementation events, parsed by the tests): every query logs its pinned `IndexSnapshot` identity, candidate/search profile, realized `AnswerContract`, and timing class; ingestion logs per-delivery watermark lag; rebuild/activation logs generation transitions; recall runs log sample keys and exact-baseline references — tests verify contracts and evidence from these logs.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
§20 risk row: HNSW under MVCC/capabilities/compaction is known-hard industry-wide; mitigation is exactly this design — pinned historical authorized topology roots, complete delta-tail compensation, retained exact fallback, population-labeled recall evidence; output filtering and exact rerank cannot repair missed candidates. Rejected: one mutable in-place HNSW graph (breaks replay and snapshot pinning); filter-during-search over unauthorized topology without a verified noninterference proof; universal `(1±ε)` PQ claims.

## Provenance
§10.4 (825-827), §3.3 (147, 149), §8.3, §12.4, §6.4, §17 (1250, 1271), §20 (1365), Appendix F.
design:
## External-review boundary (2026-07-22)

FG-ADR-SOTA-INCREMENTAL-MARKET-GAPS remains review_due. The four pinned papers support technical risks around governance, derived-state freshness/reindexing, agent-memory security, and fresh ANN only. They do not prove buyer demand, market size, or universal absence from shipping products. Implementation may target the technical gaps; product/market claims require separate evidence.

title: Upstream a borrowed neighbor-cursor/GAT interface into franken_networkx
description:
## What & scope
Upstream work inside franken_networkx itself: design and land a borrowed neighbor-cursor/GAT interface with an associated node-index type in `fnx-algorithms`, then migrate algorithm families to be generic over it, so Prism can traverse Strata's decoded/merged authorized cursors without whole-graph materialization. Maintains the interim `DECODED_CACHE` compatibility labeling until each family migrates.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
The current `GraphView` trait in `fnx-algorithms` offers string access plus integer-index rows: `neighbors_indices(&self, idx) -> Option<&[usize]>` and `in_neighbors_indices`. That contract borrows flat `usize` simple-graph rows. Strata stores compressed `u32/u64` ordinals in a typed directed multigraph with per-list codecs, so the borrow cannot be satisfied zero-copy. Section 2.2 is explicit: `GraphView` is "a compatibility target, not a zero-copy match today", and "no zero-copy claim survives unless the upstream interface and physical representation actually permit it". The closed dependency universe (Section 1) makes upstreaming the sanctioned path — fnx is one of the three foundation projects we may modify, and nothing external may be imported instead. Serves B2 (analytics read tiered storage in place, no widened private copy) and B3 (no second graph representation as the price of analytics). Section 20 carries the matching risk row: fnx algorithms not yet trait-generic or external-memory where required; W8 upstream/cursor work is the named mitigation.

## Design — normative detail
Interface: a borrowed neighbor-cursor/GAT interface with an associated node-index type, so `u32`/`u64` ordinal spaces need no widening copy and the borrow is per-cursor-step rather than per-row slice — which is what makes compressed and multi-source-merged adjacency implementable at all. Algorithms generic over that interface traverse decoded/merged authorized cursors — merged across Tier-D delta blocks and Tier-R sealed runs — without whole-graph materialization.

The cursor adapters must honor Tier-R realities (Section 6.3): per-list `NeighborCodec` is one of `EliasFano`, `StreamVByte { skip_table }`, or `DenseIntervals`; a source ordinal is meaningful only under its source map; each encoded destination is either a stable VId or `(destination_map_slot, dst_ordinal)` where the slot names an explicit `{ destination_partition, OrdinalMapId }`; no ordinal crosses a map boundary untagged. Migration proceeds by family per Section 11.4's coverage strategy. Every migrated algorithm keeps NetworkX-parity semantics locked — fnx is the parity-locked semantics oracle, and `fnx-classes` (IndexMap adjacency, insertion-order semantics) remains the compatibility reference. Until a family migrates, compatibility uses explicit epoch-shared `Vec<usize>` caches labeled `DECODED_CACHE` (owned by w8-projection); the label persists in certificates so no consumer mistakes it for zero-copy.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12: cursor-path execution must be answer-equivalent to slice-path/cached-path execution — logical values, multiplicity, and order preserved. FG-INV-20: cursors reach algorithms only as authorized cursors constructed behind `fgdb-secure-view`; the upstream trait must not grow an escape hatch yielding unauthorized adjacency. Claim class: zero-copy is a verified capability claim made only where interface and physical representation actually permit it; traversal-overhead numbers on this bead are evidence-class measurements with committed baselines, not gates.

## Interactions
Consumes w3-tier-r (codec and merge semantics the cursor adapters honor), w3-vertex-directory (ordinal maps behind the associated node-index type), w1-foundation-types. Produces the trait and migrated families consumed by w8-projection (cursor path replacing `DECODED_CACHE` per family), w8-materialization (streaming source), and verif-differential (cursor-generic algorithms checked against the `fnx-classes` reference and NetworkX parity fixtures — the two-hop oracle chain).

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Trait published in fnx with a GAT node-index type. Initial migration set covers at least shortest paths (BFS/Dijkstra), PageRank, connected components, and k-core. Property tests: on `fnx-generators` graphs (SBM, Barabasi-Albert, Watts-Strogatz, LFR, lattices), cursor-path results equal existing slice-path results under identical `TieBreakPolicy`. Differential: migrated algorithms still pass fnx's NetworkX-parity fixtures unchanged. No-materialization proof: tests assert bounded peak allocation (no hidden O(V+E) cache) via allocation accounting on large generated graphs. Fuzz: cursor adapters over adversarial codec mixes — EliasFano/StreamVByte/DenseIntervals interleavings, hub overflow rows, empty lists, map-slot boundary crossings. Bench evidence: cursor traversal overhead vs `DECODED_CACHE` recorded with baseline artifacts and complexity-witness `observed_count` regression tracking. Logging: test builds log adapter path, codec mix, and map-slot crossings per traversal. E2E script: run one migrated algorithm (e.g. BFS) end-to-end over a Strata-backed graph through the cursor path and over the same graph through the `DECODED_CACHE` path; assert identical results and witness semantics under the same `TieBreakPolicy`; assert the standalone-fnx NetworkX-parity suite still passes on the upstreamed trait; and assert peak-allocation accounting stays bounded on the cursor path. The logging requirements above (adapter path, codec mix, map-slot crossings, plus per-traversal allocation accounting) are mandatory events the e2e script parses, so the no-materialization claim is verifiable from logs.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risks: GAT/lifetime friction with merged multi-source cursors; interface churn destabilizing standalone fnx users (mitigation: additive trait, parity suite stays in fnx CI). Rejected: permanently widening Strata rows to `usize` (memory blowup, defeats B2); forking fnx rather than upstreaming (violates the single-source foundation doctrine); changing fnx semantics to fit storage (the parity lock forbids it); claiming zero-copy for the cache path.

## Provenance
Plan Section 11.2; Section 2.2 GraphView row; Section 6.3; Section 1; Section 20.

title: Implement masked-semiring SpMV/SpMSpV native kernels behind differential gates
description:
## What & scope
Implement Prism's native compute kernels: masked-semiring SpMV and SpMSpV (sparse matrix-vector and sparse-matrix sparse-vector products over registered semirings with masks), built in-house per the closed dependency universe, as the fast execution backend for frontier-style algorithms — BFS, PageRank, WCC/label propagation, SSSP, and staged successors — over authorized projections and materialized representations.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
Section 18.2 lists "masked-semiring SpMV/SpMSpV kernels" among the components the closed universe requires us to build ourselves; the GraphBLAS idea is adopted as a technique, but no external library may be imported. Section 11.4 fixes the order of work: native kernels are added only after differential semantics tests — the fnx implementation is the semantics oracle and a kernel is a provably-equivalent accelerator, never a second semantics. Kernels are what make the Section 17 benchmark row achievable: LDBC Graphalytics (BFS/PR/WCC/CDLP/LCC/SSSP) within 1.5x of dedicated static analytics engines on transactional storage — the Sortledton bar. Serves B2 (kernels consume Strata's compressed forms directly where the codec honestly permits) and B5 (kernel identity rides in witnesses and replay closures).

## Design — normative detail
Kernel model: y = A applied to x over a declared semiring (additive/multiplicative monoids with identities and annihilator), with input/output masks restricting the computed entry set; SpMSpV exploits sparse frontiers. Semiring/mask configurations are registered per algorithm family, never ad hoc. Masks encode visibility/filter structure already established by the `AuthorizedProjection` — masks are never an authorization mechanism; authorization happened at projection construction (FG-INV-20), and kernels only ever see authorized data.

Storage contract (Section 6.3, the honest intersection contract): Elias-Fano neighbor lists support rank/select directly; `StreamVByte { skip_table }` lists use skip/fence metadata and bounded blockwise decode; `DenseIntervals` use interval arithmetic; there is no claim that Elias-Fano offsets provide rank/select over a separate varint stream. Kernels operate in projection ordinal spaces: a source ordinal is meaningful only under its source map; destination `(destination_map_slot, dst_ordinal)` tags must be honored at partition boundaries; hub stripes/overflow rows (Section 6.2) get dedicated row handling.

Determinism: each kernel declares its numeric/determinism profile per Sections 8.2/8.6 — strict floating results use the portable profile; anything target-dependent requires `RELAXED` posture and is reproducible only within its recorded target/build scope. The kernel implementation hash, CPU-feature contract, and kernel/profile registry entries ride in the `ComplexityWitness` binding and in the `ReplayManifest`'s `ExecutableArtifactSet` — FG-INV-19/Section 8.6 require `Replayable` to identify the CPU-feature contract and kernel/profile registry. Iterative uses record the Section 11.4 residual artifacts: norm, numeric profile, iteration trace, stopping rule, and the mathematical assumptions behind any convergence bound.

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12: kernel-backed execution is a claimed answer-equivalent path — logical values, multiplicity, order, visibility, security projection, and AnswerContract preserved vs the fnx oracle under the same projection and `TieBreakPolicy`; proved physical equivalence cannot change strict output. FG-INV-20: no kernel observation precedes authorization; masks must not reintroduce unauthorized reads or leak hidden-element existence through timing/statistics facts. FG-INV-19: replay of kernel-executed queries requires the exact kernel/profile registry and CPU-feature contract in the manifest; a missing artifact weakens the effective grade attributably, never silently. Claim classes: the Graphalytics 1.5x target is benchmark-class with committed baselines and variance-aware gating; any adaptive kernel-selection policy is FG-CAL-01 territory — pinned deterministic fallback, stream-sequenced promotion, disclosed filtration/alpha/support.

## Interactions
Consumes w8-projection (ordinal spaces; visibility-derived masks), w8-materialization (spilled/streamed inputs for out-of-core operation), w3-tier-r (codec access paths under the intersection contract), w1-codecs (SIMD primitives), w5-determinism (numeric profiles, canonical result encoding). Produces witness-bound implementation paths consumed by w8-witnesses; benchmark rows consumed by perf-bench-core; differential rows consumed by verif-differential.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Differential gate as exposure precondition: kernel results byte-equal the canonical results of the scalar fnx implementation across the `fnx-generators` corpus (SBM, Barabasi-Albert, Watts-Strogatz, LFR, lattices, social datasets) under each registered directedness/multigraph/self-loop law and `TieBreakPolicy`, strict profile. Property tests: registered semirings satisfy associativity/identity/annihilator laws under the masked operations; mask correctness — no entry outside the mask is computed or observable, including via instrumented timing-fact counters. Fuzz: empty/full masks, empty frontiers, hub overflow rows, map-slot boundary crossings, codec mixes. Bench gates: Graphalytics BFS/PR/WCC/CDLP/LCC/SSSP within the 1.5x bar on transactional storage, with committed baselines, variance-aware gating, and complexity-witness `observed_count` regression tracking — bench rows, fixtures, and baselines registered here; the gated runs execute on §15.6's deterministic apparatus via `verif-perf-apparatus`/`perf-bench-core`, manifests-green at gate-g4. Cross-SIMD-width determinism: scalar vs vectorized paths byte-equal under the strict profile, or the profile is explicitly declared `RELAXED`. Logging: kernel hash, numeric profile, CPU features, mask density, per-iteration frontier sizes, iterations to convergence. E2E script: execute `CALL fnx.pagerank` over an authorized projection with the kernel backend enabled and then disabled; assert byte-equal canonical results under the strict profile; verify the witness carries the kernel implementation hash and CPU-feature contract; and replay the kernel-executed run from its `ReplayManifest` to the same canonical result digest. The listed logging fields (kernel hash, numeric profile, CPU features, mask density, per-iteration frontier sizes, iterations to convergence) are mandatory implementation log events, not test-only instrumentation; tests assert their presence and their consistency with the witness bindings.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risks: floating-point reassociation across SIMD widths breaking strict determinism (pin the reduction order or declare `RELAXED`); kernel/oracle drift as fnx evolves (the differential suite runs continuously in CI, not once at exposure). Rejected: importing SuiteSparse:GraphBLAS or any external kernel library (closed universe); kernels as an unauthorized fast path bypassing projections; masks as the authorization mechanism; shipping kernels before differential semantics tests (Section 11.4 forbids it).

## Provenance
Plan Section 11.4; Section 18.2; Sections 6.2-6.3; Sections 8.2/8.6; Section 17.

title: Build the MATERIALIZED spill path and external-memory operator exposure gate
description:
## What & scope
Build Prism's `MATERIALIZED` execution path: streaming/spilling an authorized projection into a generation-scoped representation for algorithms that are not cursor-generic; the operator exposure gate deciding whether an fnx algorithm may become a database operator at all; and the per-operator external-memory/spill contracts (cleanup + I/O bounds) every exposed operator must declare. Includes the small-graph mutable-working-copy path via `fnx-classes`/`fnx-views`.

## Why (bets, market, goals)
FrankenGraphDB sells a larger-than-memory product contract; an analytics surface that silently assumes RAM-resident graphs would break it. Section 11.4's discipline keeps coverage honest: an algorithm without a bounded-memory story stays in the source catalog rather than shipping as a trap. Serves B3 (analytics under the same resource governance as queries), B5 (evidence-class residual artifacts for convergence claims), and B6 (typed `ResourceExhausted` carrying registered minimums, so agents can reason about failures instead of guessing).

## Design — normative detail
Algorithms not cursor-generic take a `MATERIALIZED` path that streams/spills an authorized projection into a generation-scoped representation. Exposure gate (normative): an algorithm is exposed as a database operator only after it has either (a) a bounded cursor path or (b) a declared external-memory/spill implementation with cleanup and I/O bounds; otherwise it remains in the source catalog rather than violating the larger-than-memory product contract. `ResourceExhausted` remains legal when even the registered minimum resident set or scratch quota is unavailable — not as a substitute for designing the operator. W8 extends coverage by family and adds native kernels only after differential semantics tests.

Residual artifacts (normative): each run records norm, numeric profile, iteration trace, stopping rule, and the mathematical assumptions behind any convergence bound; deterministic iteration count alone does not create cross-machine floating identity.

Representation: spill blocks are generation-scoped — pinned to the projection's snapshot/epoch — written through the Section 6.7 buffer/scratch discipline, and registered as obligations so cancellation and crash cleanup are deterministic. Small graphs may take the `fnx-classes`/`fnx-views` mutable-working-copy path (IndexMap adjacency, insertion-order semantics — the NetworkX-parity compatibility reference; borrowed/cached snapshot views) when an algorithm needs a mutable working copy; that path is bounded by the registered minimum resident set. Per-operator larger-than-memory contracts follow the Section 8.7 house style — external merge sort, radix/grace partitioning, partitioned builds — each operator declaring its own partitioning/spill scheme rather than inheriting a global one. The registered minimum resident set and scratch quota come from the algorithm's `FnxSignatureRegistry` larger-than-memory implementation class (w8-projection).

## Invariants & claim types
FG-INV-12 (restated): every claimed answer-equivalent seal, compaction, codec/format rewrite, spill, factorize/flatten, or workspace materialization preserves logical values, multiplicity, order, visibility, security projection, and AnswerContract — the `MATERIALIZED` path is exactly such a claimed-equivalent transformation and must prove it. FG-INV-16 (restated): no structured task, scratch object, or result/workspace lease is lost, duplicated, refunded, released, or exposed while obligated; under declared fairness every obligation reaches one legal terminal or recoverable state — spill scratch and checkpoints are such obligations. FG-INV-14: scratch remains a GC root until its exact terminal release. Claim classes: convergence bounds and iteration traces are evidence-class residual artifacts; long-run memory stability is FG-EVID-03 endurance-gate territory; declared-vs-measured I/O bound divergence is itself a finding.

## Interactions
Consumes w8-projection (authorized projection streams; registry implementation classes and quotas), w5-executor (morsel/spill machinery and external-algorithm precedents), w3-buffer (buffer/scratch/EBR discipline), w1-foundation-types. Produces materialized representations consumed by w8-kernels; scratch obligations governed by w8-scheduling; crash rows consumed by verif-torture; equivalence checks consumed by verif-differential.

## Acceptance criteria & tests
Exposure-gate CI: the operator registry refuses to activate an algorithm lacking both a bounded cursor path and a declared external-memory implementation with cleanup and I/O bounds, with negative fixtures per missing element. Spill correctness: on `fnx-generators` graphs sized beyond the scratch quota, `MATERIALIZED` results equal in-memory reference results; peak resident set stays within registered minimum plus quota (asserted and logged). `ResourceExhausted` tests: raised only when the registered minimum is genuinely unavailable; the error carries the registered numbers. Crash matrix: kill during spill write, mid-iteration, and after completion-before-release — recovery leaves zero orphaned scratch, with obligation accounting reaching terminal state under the asupersync leak/quiescence oracle. Residual-artifact tests: iteration trace, stopping rule, norm, and stated assumptions present and schema-valid for every iterative algorithm. Logging: path=`MATERIALIZED`, generation id, spill bytes, partition counts, I/O-bound conformance, iteration-trace reference, cleanup completion. E2E script: run a non-cursor-generic algorithm via `CALL fnx.<algorithm>` over a projection sized beyond the scratch quota so it spills; cancel a concurrent identical run mid-spill; assert correct results on the surviving run, deterministic scratch cleanup and obligation quiescence on the cancelled run, and `path=MATERIALIZED` certificates with schema-valid residual artifacts on both. The listed logging fields (path, generation id, spill bytes, partition counts, I/O-bound conformance, iteration-trace reference, cleanup completion) are mandatory implementation log events; tests parse them to verify I/O-bound conformance and cleanup completion.

## Risks & rejected alternatives
Risks: wrongly declared I/O bounds (divergence is treated as a release finding); representation drift between spilled blocks and projection epochs. Rejected: exposing in-memory-only algorithms as operators (violates the product contract); using `ResourceExhausted` as a coverage strategy; one global spill format instead of per-operator declared contracts; treating deterministic iteration counts as cross-machine floating-point identity.

## Provenance
Plan Section 11.4; Section 2.2 (fnx-classes/fnx-views rows); Section 8.7; Section 6.7.

### Verification-layer classification
The task-specific checks above must be registered in the universal verification contract as distinct unit, property/model/mutation or fuzz, simulation/concurrency/fault, and E2E rows rather than one aggregate test. The unit layer exhaustively covers every locally owned canonical type, validator, state-transition arm, arithmetic/boundary rule, error mapping, and gate/manifest evaluator, including invalid and unavailable-feature cases. Property/model tests vary every normative field and legal transition boundary and compare against an independent oracle where one exists. Simulation covers cancellation, crash/restart, virtual time, authority/configuration change, and obligation ownership wherever applicable.
