title: Census blind spot: "named in a test" is not "witnessed firing" — 9 proven Appendix A cases, unmeasured elsewhere
description:
Derived 2026-07-27 by pane3 at HEAD 09b816a while re-deriving the fgdb-tsfs premise.

THE DEFECT IS IN THE CENSUS, NOT IN ANY ONE BEAD
The whole xnxy family (xnxy, xnxy.1, tsfs) partitions violation codes with one
classifier: a code is WITNESSED if its string appears anywhere in
tools/registry-check/tests/*.rs or scripts/*.sh, and RESIDUE otherwise. That
classifier is sound in one direction only. Unnamed really does imply
unwitnessed. Named does NOT imply witnessed, and three mention shapes defeat it.

PROVEN, PER ITEM, FOR appendix_a AT HEAD 09b816a — 9 codes the census counts as
witnessed that have never been demonstrated firing individually. Each was
hand-inspected; none appears as a witness-table cell anywhere in tests/.

  MULTI-ARM DISJUNCTION (6) — a `matches!(violation.code.as_str(), "A"|"B"|"C")`
  assertion is satisfied by ONE arm firing. N-1 arms can be permanently dead and
  the test stays green. This is exactly the "string-only or count-only match"
  that tsfs's own acceptance bar forbids.
    catalog_completion_layer_schema_mismatch   tests/identity.rs:856  (2-way)
    catalog_target_duplicate                  tests/identity.rs:1039
    complete_slice_target_declared            tests/identity.rs:2461, 2521
    complete_slice_semantic_binding_missing   tests/identity.rs:2533 (3-way)
    complete_slice_static_evidence_missing    tests/identity.rs:2533 (3-way)
    complete_slice_runtime_evidence_missing   tests/identity.rs:2533 (3-way)

  ABSENCE ASSERTION (1) — named only inside an assertion that the code must NOT
  be present. A code that only ever appears in a must-be-absent test has by
  construction never been seen to fire.
    catalog_repository_beads_unavailable       tests/identity.rs:1854

  COMMENT ONLY (2) — the mention is inside a `//` or `#` comment. No assertion
  of any kind exists.
    source_target_key_missing        tests/identity.rs:11690   (a `//` comment)
    catalog_reservation_epoch_drift  scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh:57 (a `#` comment)

  THE COMMENT CLASS IS THE SHARPEST. source_target_key_missing is the ONLY code
  that LEFT the appendix_a residue between dec248a and 09b816a. It left because
  somebody wrote a comment naming it. A code moved from "needs a witness" to
  "witnessed" with no test written and no assertion added. The census cannot
  tell that apart from real work, and nothing gates it.

SIZE
  appendix_a: 9 proven (adds to the 114 census residue -> 123 truly unwitnessed).
  topology / threat / validate / unsafe_ledger: UNMEASURED. See the discarded
  negative below before re-attempting.

DISCARDED NEGATIVE — DO NOT RE-CHASE THIS THE SAME WAY
  A literal-in-assertion classifier run over the other four owners returned 91 of
  101 topology, 41 of 60 threat, 28 of 33 validate, 28 of 29 unsafe_ledger as
  "not singleton-witnessed". THOSE NUMBERS ARE INSTRUMENT ARTIFACTS AND ARE
  WRONG. The xnxy.1 witnesses are table-driven:
    TopologyWitness { code: "active_manifest_missing", fact: "...", mutate: |r| ... }
  and the assertion consumes `witness.code`, a VARIABLE. A classifier keyed on a
  string literal inside an assert cannot see a table cell, so it reports every
  table row as unwitnessed. The same defect cost 8 false positives in the
  appendix_a pass (tests/identity.rs:2299, 2586 and 609 are `(name, mutate,
  expected_code)` tables asserting `violation.code == expected_code`); those 8
  were resolved to WITNESSED by hand.
  A correct classifier must resolve a table cell to its assertion, or the pass
  must be done by hand per item as it was for the 9 above.

ACCEPTANCE
  - replace each of the 6 disjunctions with one assertion per arm, or state per
    arm why the arm cannot be isolated
  - give catalog_repository_beads_unavailable a positive witness, or declare it
    unreachable-by-input with the reason (note: it fires whenever .beads/ is
    absent, which is a live and easily constructed input)
  - witness the 2 comment-only codes for real
  - decide whether the census classifier itself gets a gate: a code whose only
    mention is a comment must not count as witnessed
  - measure the other four owners with a table-aware classifier, controlled BOTH
    directions before any number is believed
notes:
STATUS 2026-07-27, pane3: THE LANDED CLASSIFIER IS FIXED (e1d3e63). The 9 proven
Appendix A codes are NOT yet witnessed — that is the remaining work, detailed at
the bottom. Read this before re-deriving anything; the nine-code proof below is
the expensive part and it is already done.

=== WHAT LANDED, e1d3e63 ===
tools/registry-check/tests/satisfiability.rs. The repo's ONE landed instance of
this defect was `witnessed_elsewhere_sites_are_live`, which validated a
`Coverage::WitnessedElsewhere` row by testing only
    body[..end].contains(&format!("\"{code}\""))
i.e. the code STRING occurs somewhere in the named test's body. Replaced by
`demonstrates_code(body, code)`, which walks every occurrence and rejects three
shapes, accepting anything else:
  (a) the occurrence's line is a `//` comment
  (b) the innermost enclosing `matches!( .. )` holds >1 distinct quoted literal
      — one arm of a disjunction is satisfied by any other arm
  (c) the enclosing statement is an ABSENCE assertion (`assert!` whose first
      non-whitespace argument char is `!`, or `.is_empty()`, or a negated
      binding)
Conservative in the safe direction ON PURPOSE: an unrecognised shape counts as a
demonstration, so it can under-report a defect but never invent one. Scope: 10
`WitnessedElsewhere` rows over 10 named tests. Grepped for other landed
instances of the pattern — there are none. `threat_model.rs:717` looks similar
but checks that a named fn EXISTS, which is exactly what it claims.

=== RED-PROOF, BOTH DIRECTIONS, ON THE REAL CORPUS ===
  clean corpus + new check       9 passed / 0 failed — all 10 live rows still count
  downgraded corpus + OLD check  GREEN   <- the old check is blind, as claimed
  downgraded corpus + new check  RED, naming the exact code and test
The downgrade rewrites ONE real assertion in
`idr_non_reference_wire_members_require_inline_identity_class` into a 2-arm
`matches!`, leaving the code string present. Verified again on the LIVE tree at
HEAD 7682d32 after pane4 landed 38tv into tests/identity.rs; rustfmt --check clean.
Standalone rustc path, no cargo, no build slot.

TWO BUGS THE DIFFERENTIAL CAUGHT THAT FIXTURES DID NOT — keep the differential:
 1 `is_absence_assertion` first used the literal "assert!(\n". rustfmt breaks
   nearly every multi-line assertion that way, so it falsely reddened 7 of the 10
   live rows. It now decides on the first non-whitespace char of the macro's
   argument.
 2 `enclosing_matches` derived the macro's start from an ALREADY-ADVANCED cursor,
   correct only near offset zero. The synthetic control passed anyway; only the
   real-corpus downgrade exposed it. The self-test fixture is now padded so that
   class fails, but the padding is a patch — the real-corpus downgrade is the
   instrument that works.

=== THE 9 PROVEN CODES: STILL OPEN, AND THE FIX DOES NOT COVER THEM ===
Say this plainly so nobody reads e1d3e63 as closing them. None of the 9 is in
satisfiability.rs's REGISTRY (26 rows, all identity codes). The 9 are appendix_a
codes, and the census that miscounted them is the bead-described grep procedure,
which is NOT a landed artifact. So e1d3e63 removes the defect CLASS where the
repo enforces it and supplies a reusable `demonstrates_code`; it re-classifies
none of the 9.

  DISJUNCTION-ONLY (6) — each needs its arm split into its own assertion, or a
  stated per-arm reason why it cannot be isolated:
    catalog_completion_layer_schema_mismatch    tests/identity.rs:856  (2-way)
    catalog_target_duplicate                    tests/identity.rs:1039
    complete_slice_target_declared              tests/identity.rs:2461, 2521
    complete_slice_semantic_binding_missing     tests/identity.rs:2533 (3-way)
    complete_slice_static_evidence_missing      tests/identity.rs:2533 (3-way)
    complete_slice_runtime_evidence_missing     tests/identity.rs:2533 (3-way)
  ABSENCE-ONLY (1) — needs a positive witness, or an unreachable-by-input
  declaration with the reason. NOTE it is easily reachable: it fires whenever
  .beads/ is absent, which I hit accidentally on a git-archive snapshot.
    catalog_repository_beads_unavailable        tests/identity.rs:1854
  COMMENT-ONLY (2):
    source_target_key_missing        tests/identity.rs:11690  (a // comment)
    catalog_reservation_epoch_drift  scripts/g0_identity_e2e.sh:57 (a # comment)
  All 9 hand-verified per item; none is a witness-table cell anywhere in tests/.
  source_target_key_missing is the sharpest: it is the ONLY code that LEFT the
  appendix_a residue between dec248a and 09b816a, and it left because somebody
  wrote a comment naming it.

=== SUGGESTED NEXT INCREMENT ===
Lift `demonstrates_code` into a shared test helper and apply it to the appendix_a
population, then split the 6 disjunctions. The line numbers above are as of
09b816a and pane4 has since edited tests/identity.rs (38tv, 7682d32) — re-locate
by code string, not by line.

=== DISCARDED NEGATIVE, do not re-chase ===
A literal-in-assertion classifier run over topology/threat/validate/unsafe_ledger
returns 91/101, 41/60, 28/33, 28/29 "unwitnessed". Those are ARTIFACTS. Those
suites are table-driven — `TopologyWitness { code: "...", mutate: |r| .. }` —
and the assertion consumes `witness.code`, a VARIABLE, so a literal-keyed reader
sees every table row as unwitnessed. Any classifier applied there must resolve a
table cell to its assertion first.

title: WriteTxn commit_with_crash: pin released; reopen matches reference
description:
G1 slice after WriteTxn pin (fgdb-writetxn-pin-l8wb CLOSED): the txn commit path must share the Chronicle crash matrix. Genesis 4 for the pinned-txn write.

NOT SSI, NOT G0, NOT a second commit protocol.

## Why

`Database::write_with_crash` already stops the autocommit path at CrashPoint. `WriteTxn::commit` always passes `crash_at: None` into `commit_template`. A crash during a pinned txn is therefore untested: pin leak, fenced handle, and reopen-vs-reference are unproven for begin/write/commit.

## Behavior

- `Database::commit_prepared_with_crash(cx, prepared, crash_at)` is `commit_prepared` with the crash argument forwarded to `commit_template` (same code, not a twin).
- `WriteTxn::commit_with_crash(db, cx, crash_at)` uses that, then **always releases the pin** (success, Rejected, or crash). Drop must not double-release.
- Existing `commit` / `write_with_crash` autocommit unchanged.

## Acceptance

Positive:
- Crash before D2: handle fenced or drop+reopen; independent `fgdb_sim::replay` matches pre-txn graph (or committed prefix if D2 landed — assert the actual CrashPoint law, do not guess).
- `txn_cx.outstanding_obligations()` returns to baseline after the crash return.
- Crash-free `commit_with_crash(..., None)` equals `commit`.

Planted: a commit_with_crash that skips `release_pin` on the error path fails the obligation-baseline test.

title: WriteTxn: TxnCx pin_snapshot + commit/abort over prepared WriteBatch
description:
G1 slice of Gap 2 remainder after FCW (fgdb-fcw-writebatch-6cxf CLOSED) and MATCH (nje.1 / jjn0 CLOSED): a product txn handle that pins a snapshot with TxnCx and commits or aborts.

NOT Graph-SSI, NOT merge ladder, NOT WriteCoordinator, NOT G0.

## Why

Writes today take only `&CommitCx` and fold against the live frontier. `TxnCx` already exists (`fgdb-types` `pin_snapshot` obligation) and is unused by `Database`. Gap 2 named session/txn ownership, typed abort, purpose-narrowed TxnCx.

## Behavior

- `Database::begin(&mut self, txn: &TxnCx) -> Result<WriteTxn, _>` acquires `TxnCx::pin_snapshot`, records `basis = frontier`. Outstanding obligations > 0 until commit/abort.
- `WriteTxn::write(batch)` is `prepare_write` against the PINNED basis (not the live fold if the pin is stale — reuse prepare_write). Multiple writes in one txn may concatenate prepared templates or refuse a second write this slice (one batch per txn is OK if documented).
- `WriteTxn::commit(commit: &CommitCx)` calls `commit_prepared`; releases the pin. FCW still aborts overlapping pinned txns (`WriteError::FirstCommitterWins`).
- `WriteTxn::abort()` releases the pin, nothing durable, sequence unconsumed.
- Existing `Database::write(&CommitCx, batch)` unchanged (autocommit).

## Acceptance

Positive: two begins on one handle, overlapping property updates, first commit wins, second FCW abort; abort then commit of a disjoint txn succeeds; pin obligation is 0 after commit and after abort.
Planted: a commit path that never calls pin_snapshot must fail a test that asserts `txn.outstanding_obligations()` rose during the open txn.
No-claim: not SSI witnesses, not multi-process, not CLI.

title: Defer the tracked JSONL export while a gate holds the landing lease, instead of blocking every br write for 35 minutes
notes:
OPTION (iv) for fgdb-09iz, filed 2026-07-27 by pane4 at HEAD 1a6fdc2 while
re-deriving that bead. NOT a variant of its option (ii) — the opposite of it.

WHY (ii) CANNOT BE THE ANSWER. fgdb-09iz recommends "make a br write take the
landing lease". scripts/lib/landing_lease.sh records operator policy ruling FOUR:
"HOLD LANDINGS, NEVER PANES ... Only `git commit` on branch `main` is bound ...
Holding panes rather than landings is what cost pane4 forty minutes." A br write
is not a landing. check.sh holds the lease for its WHOLE ~35-minute run by design
(check.sh:1508), so binding br to it stalls every pane's bead traffic for the
length of every run — 13.4 writes per run at the re-derived rate, on every run,
since 0 of 229 sampled 35-min windows are write-free.

THE ASYMMETRY THAT MAKES A NON-BLOCKING FIX POSSIBLE, and which fgdb-09iz states
in its own premise paragraph without drawing the conclusion:

    .beads/beads.db        UNTRACKED (gitignored)   <- where a br write's STATE goes
    .beads/issues.jsonl    TRACKED                  <- what the auto-flush EXPORT moves

The gate fingerprint hashes every TRACKED file. So a br write's state change is
already invisible to it. Only the export is not. `--no-auto-flush` ("Skip auto
JSONL export", `br create --help` line 35) separates the two.

PROVEN, NOT ARGUED — this very bead is the experiment. Both directions:
  POSITIVE  `br create --no-auto-flush ...` created THIS record (fgdb-wv3v) and
            left .beads/issues.jsonl BYTE-IDENTICAL: sha a03bb1a80b286e6e before
            and after, mtime 1785205187 unchanged, .br_history unchanged at 105.
  NEGATIVE  a default `br create` (which produced fgdb-41p3) moved the export
            a03bb1a8 -> 6ebcc8b5 in the same minute.
A control that fires both ways, on the live tree, at no cost.

THE PROPOSAL. While the landing lease is held, panes defer the tracked export:
br writes go to the untracked DB and the JSONL is flushed after the run. The pane
is never blocked — it keeps filing, updating and closing beads at full rate — and
the gate gets what it actually wants, which is not silence but a FROZEN CORPUS for
the duration of its run. g0_identity_e2e reads a JSONL that is slightly stale and
internally consistent, which is strictly better than one that moves underneath it.
This composes with the existing lease rather than competing: a pane that tries to
COMMIT .beads/ mid-run is still refused by the pre-commit hook, unchanged.

WHAT NEEDS A RULING BEFORE ANYONE BUILDS IT (do not treat this as decided):
  * MECHANISM. br is third-party and not modified, so this is a wrapper, a shell
    function, or an env default. Whatever it is, GUARD BY THE LEASE, NOT BY pgrep
    — fgdb-09iz records that an ad-hoc `pgrep -af 'bash scripts/check.sh'` guard
    matched ITS OWN COMMAND LINE. landing_lease.sh pattern-matches nothing; use
    `landing_lease_state` and read $LANDING_STATE (plain call, NOT a command
    substitution — it is a subshell and discards every variable it sets).
  * WHO FLUSHES, AND WHEN. A deferred flush that nobody performs is a silent
    divergence between DB and export. The flush must be owned, and it must be
    observable that it happened.
  * THE SHARED-EXPORT HAZARD. A br import DELETES rows absent from the JSONL, and
    several panes share this DB. Deferring exports across panes needs the
    last-writer-wins semantics stated explicitly before it is relied on.
  * FAIL OPEN OR CLOSED. landing_lease.sh ruling THREE says a lease is not the
    last word and fails open LOUDLY. A deferral wrapper should do the same: if the
    lease cannot be read, flush normally and say so.

CONTROL THE FIX (fgdb-09iz's own requirement, and it applies here): run check.sh
while a pane issues br writes; confirm the run completes UN-VOIDED and the pane was
never blocked; then NEUTER the deferral and confirm the void returns. A guard whose
absence changes nothing was never producing the result.

##     Uninhabited -- and explicitly that "no erased reference union exists". A symbol with no
##     single encoding cannot BE a single wire type. The resolution belongs on the CARRYING
##     FIELD (exact_wire_type = StrongRef|CertifiedRemoteStrongRef + target_schema_id = T),
##     which is exactly the shape the two landed a20 field rows use for tag-refined refs. This
##     is the plan-named-digest law by analogy: a name that resolves gets no row of its own,
##     and minting one strands the transcript.
##   THE DISCRIMINATOR AGAINST THIS BEAD'S OWN 5 LANDED WIRE PAIRS, stated so the owner can
##     check my consistency: LocalRestoreStateRef et al. WERE minted wire, and they are also
##     generated refined reference types. The difference is determinacy -- each of those names
##     ONE wrapper and ONE target arm, so it has one encoding. These two name three
##     alternatives including an uninhabited one.
##   WHAT WOULD FALSIFY IT: the plan intending the umbrella name itself to have one encoding --
##     which would require a declared tag width and arm codes at a recorded location, and there
##     are none. Or a ruling that per-Tag generated instances each get their own wire type, in
##     which case the umbrella still gets no row and this proposal stands unchanged.
##
## PAIR 3 -- AuthorizedDeltaPublicProvenance | PublicDeliveryDigest
##   VERDICT: PROPOSED -- `unclassified`, TERMINAL for BOTH (no row for either)
##   recorded location: a11:1934, and the whole of it is:
##     "`AuthorizedDeltaPublicProvenance` and `PublicDeliveryDigest` are separately constructed
##      exactly as §9.5 and Appendix D specify; neither can acquire a hidden envelope field
##      except through the Declassified arm's explicit authorization and audit release."
##   instrument at that location: inline arms NO, tag width NO, lawB 0 (prose only), lawA 0.
##     Note the sentence NAMES "the Declassified arm" without spelling the arm set.
##   PARKED ON THE TWO OWNERSHIP GROUNDS I PROVED -- explicitly NOT on the out-of-range ground,
##   WHICH I FALSIFIED (28 logical + 9 wire landed rows have out-of-range definition heads):
##     (a) DELEGATION. The candidate's only recorded location is a sentence that says the pair
##         "are separately constructed exactly as §9.5 and Appendix D specify". Appendix A
##         DELEGATES rather than defines. The `Opaque|Declassified` arm set does exist, at
##         L774, but L774 is NOT a recorded location for this candidate -- it is Appendix D's
##         namespace. Minting an Appendix A logical_kind would be Appendix A claiming an object
##         Appendix D owns.
##     (b) NAVIGATION-ONLY CARRIER. The one law-B-shaped hit,
##         `public_provenance:AuthorizedDeltaPublicProvenance` at L3063, is an indented line
##         inside a rendering block, and line 328 says "Compact renderings that use such
##         shorthand are navigation-only and must expand through an exact field-table row." It
##         cannot carry law B, and it is not a recorded location either.
##   ON PublicDeliveryDigest specifically: it is corroborated as a plan-named digest by
##     `PublicDeliveryDigest = BLAKE3("fgdb:public-delivery:v1" || canonical(...))` at L774, and
##     a plan-named digest is never a wire type -- it resolves as digest256 + digest_class on
##     the carrying field. I flag that L774 is NOT a recorded location for this candidate
##     either, so per the standing law I offer it as CORROBORATION and rest the proposal on the
##     delegation ground, which IS at the recorded location. The pair genuinely splits in kind
##     here, which is the one place the pair unit breaks -- but both sides land on "no row", so
##     the split does not change the disposition.
##   WHAT WOULD FALSIFY IT: a ruling that Appendix A's catalog is the single registry for
##     Appendix D objects too, which would make L774's arm set in-scope and (by the tag-width
##     instrument: inline arms, no tag width) give AuthorizedDeltaPublicProvenance = `logical`
##     on a 2/2 precedent. That is a scope decision, not a measurement, which is why it is
##     yours. PublicDeliveryDigest would still get no row.
##
## PAIR 4 -- PreBootstrapDispatchPublicationEvidence<Action> | PreBootstrapNeverSentProof<Action>
##   VERDICT: UNDECIDABLE -- two competing leanings, neither reaching an instrument reading
##   recorded location: a17:2327, and the whole of it is:
##     "`PreBootstrapDispatchPublicationEvidence<Action>` and `PreBootstrapNeverSentProof<Action>`
##      are specific to the journal authority plus local mirror and cannot be decoded as
##      ordinary RootManifest evidence."
##   instrument at that location: inline arms NO, tag width NO, lawB 0, lawA 0. Out of domain
##     (evidence/proof, not a union).
##   LEANING A -- `wire`: "cannot be decoded as ordinary RootManifest evidence" is a DECODE-
##     DISTINCTNESS clause, and a thing that is decoded has a wire encoding. Note the in-bead
##     near-precedent: this bead's own a17 pair
##     (CanonicalBootstrapOpenersRef|CanonicalVerifiedObjectInventoryRef) is defined with the
##     sibling phrasing "cannot cross-decode" and LANDED WIRE at 0x0555/0x0556. HONESTY
##     REQUIRED HERE: what forced that landing was LAW B (measured carriers across all three
##     shapes), not the decode clause. For this pair law B is 0. So the precedent is
##     suggestive of the phrasing's meaning and is NOT the instrument that decided its sibling.
##   LEANING B -- `prebootstrap`: the name prefix, and "specific to the journal authority plus
##     local mirror" places them in the prebootstrap plane. AGAINST: all 5 landed
##     [[prebootstrap_kind]] rows are `*Artifact` and each carries an `import_target` and
##     `allowed_containers = "registered restore staging inode/root/capsule only"`. A
##     publication *evidence* and a *proof* have neither an import target nor a staging
##     container, so the row shape does not fit them.
##   WHAT WOULD FALSIFY EACH: for `wire`, any carrier at a recorded location (would engage law
##     B and settle it the way the a17 sibling was settled). For `prebootstrap`, deriving an
##     import_target and allowed_containers for an evidence/proof. Neither exists today.
##
## SUMMARY FOR RATIFICATION: 2 PROPOSED (pairs 2 and 3, both "no row / terminal
## unclassified"), 2 UNDECIDABLE (pairs 1 and 4). Only pairs 1 and 4 need a cold ruling, and
## for both I have recorded the leanings and their falsifiers rather than leaving them blank.
## ########################################################################################

## THREE RESULTS THAT SHARPEN THE 4 RULINGS (and one dead end I chased to the end)
Derived after the pair count went 7 -> 4, while trying to find a landable mint among the 4.
NONE OF THE 4 IS LANDABLE. But two of the note's stated REASONS for parking them were wrong,
and killing a bad reason matters even when the disposition survives.

 1. "DEFINED OUTSIDE APPENDIX A" IS NOT A BAR. Falsified by counting: 28 of 554 landed
    [[logical_kind]] rows and 9 of 566 landed [[wire_type]] rows have their definition head
    OUTSIDE the Appendix A range 1388-2728 (LogicalCommandRecord @340, RootManifest @358,
    AuthorityBindingRecord @330, SecurityStateBinding @874 -- which sits right beside the L774
    definitions in this bead, PreBootstrapArtifactRef @287 in the same prose region as L322).
    So do NOT park the AuthorizedDelta or PreBootstrap pairs on out-of-range grounds. That
    reason is spent; whatever is left must stand on its own.

 2. LAW B DOES NOT DECIDE A GENERATED CLOSED UNION. Measured over all 3 classified ones: ALL
    THREE have law B > 0, and two went logical while one went wire.
        ContinuityAuthorityCurrentBasis   lawB=1  inline arms, no tag width -> LOGICAL
        LifecycleAuthoritySource          lawB=1  inline arms, no tag width -> LOGICAL
        DurableCapabilityConsumerTerminalTarget lawB=3 inline arms + `u16` + 0x0001/0x0002 -> WIRE
    So the discriminator is the TAG-WIDTH DECLARATION, 3 of 3, and law B is confirmed
    insufficient for this whole shape -- consistent with the union-pair finding above, now
    proven on the classified side too rather than only on the unclassified side.

 3. THE DEAD END, written down so nobody spends the hour again. AuthorizedDeltaPublicProvenance
    looks landable as LOGICAL and is not. It DOES have an inline arm set --
    "Appendix D's closed `Opaque|Declassified` union" (L774) -- and no tag width, which by (2)
    would give logical on a 2/2 precedent, and by (1) the out-of-range definition is no bar.
    Two things kill it, and both are about WHICH LOCATION THE CANDIDATE OWNS:
      * its catalog row is source_kind = "name-only" with source_locations = ["a11:1934"] ONLY.
        L774 and L3063 are NOT recorded locations for this candidate. The arm set therefore
        lives in a namespace this candidate does not own, and Appendix A at 1934 says the pair
        "are separately constructed exactly as SS9.5 and Appendix D specify" -- it DELEGATES
        rather than defines. Minting an Appendix A logical_kind would be Appendix A claiming an
        object Appendix D owns.
      * its only law-B carrier, L3063 `public_provenance:AuthorizedDeltaPublicProvenance`, is an
        INDENTED LINE INSIDE A RENDERING BLOCK, not a normative field spec -- and line 328 says
        "Compact renderings that use such shorthand are navigation-only and must expand through
        an exact field-table row." So that carrier cannot carry law B either.
    LESSON, generalizable: run the class instruments only on locations the candidate's own row
    records. An arm set found at a line the census never attributed to the symbol is somebody
    else's arm set. Check source_locations BEFORE reading the source around a grep hit.

## THE FAMILY -- take this to the owner as ONE question, not as 3 pairs
The 10 unclassified no-inline-arm-set generated closed unions. 3 are ww9g A conjuncts; their 3
B twins are in the same definition sentences but did not match the population regex (it
captures only the first backticked symbol of "`A` and `B` are ..."), so they inherit the same
status by sharing the sentence. That leaves SEVEN co-shaped siblings entirely outside ww9g:
    DeltaRetentionObligationRef<Role>        LocalConflictProofRef
    RecoveryBridgeDependencyRef<Role>        RemoteGrantTargetRef
    RestoreReadyClosureRef<Role>             RestoreSourceKeyAccessTerminalProjection<Role>
    ShardReadWitnessRef
ShardReadWitnessRef is the Shard sibling of ww9g's own LocalReadWitnessRef -- the same family,
the same missing registry, and NOT in ww9g's 13. LocalConflictProofRef (a04:1476, "a generated
closed union over version, absence/range, path, constraint, and final-write proof objects") is
the cleanest specimen of the whole shape: five classes named, zero targets named.
FILED as its own bead this rotation -- see the bead list at the bottom.

## THE INSTRUMENTS, and how they behaved over all 20 remaining symbols
  Law A (reference target => never wire): 0 of 20. No symbol is ever the immediate argument of
    StrongRef/CertifiedRemoteStrongRef/WeakDigest/Conditional*/RegisteredStrongRef. Law A is
    one-directional, so this forbids nothing -- it simply never decides in this bead.
  Law B (contained in another schema => wire): decided all 5 wire pairs. It FIRES for all 6
    union-shaped symbols too (all 6 are contained in another schema, consumers named above) --
    and it is NOT sufficient for them, which is the sharpest thing learned this rotation. Law B
    picks a class; it cannot supply an arm set, and line 328 requires the arm set. A shape whose
    structure is unlandable is not classifiable no matter what law B says. Do not let a firing
    law B talk you into a union mint.
  Reservations: 0 of 20 remaining symbols has one. Nothing else is forced like a16 was.

## OWNER RULING NEEDED (4) -- RE-MEASURED at d9d4e28+. One claim below is CORRECTED.
CORRECTION, found by re-measuring rather than inheriting. The previous note said "both class
instruments are silent on all four". THAT IS FALSE for the MetaAuthorizationEvidence pair:
LAW B FIRES for it. At a04:1880 `ShardControlAuthority<Tag>` is the closed tag
`MetaAuthorized{authorization_ref:MetaAuthorizationEvidence<Tag>,...}|ProtocolEvidenceAuthorized{
evidence_ref:ProtocolAuthorizationEvidence<Tag>,...}|StructurallyInapplicable{...}`, so both
symbols are carried as ARM-PAYLOAD fields. Trap 3 applies: the consumer is
`ShardControlAuthority<Tag>`, NOT MetaAuthorized/ProtocolEvidenceAuthorized.
AND THE DISPOSITION IS STILL "RULING", for a sharper reason than silence. The same sentence
says these are "generated ASSOCIATED TYPES ... each either one exact typed `StrongRef<T>` or
`CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<T>` schema or `Uninhabited`; no erased reference union exists". So the
symbol has no identity of its own -- it RESOLVES, per Tag, to a wrapper plus a target, or to
nothing. That is structurally the plan-named-digest situation: the resolution belongs on the
CARRYING FIELD (exact_wire_type = StrongRef/CRSR + target_schema_id = T, the shape the landed
a20 field rows use for tag-refined refs), and minting a wire type named
`MetaAuthorizationEvidence` would STRAND THE TRANSCRIPT. A firing law B does not make this a
mint. The `Uninhabited` arm is the hard part precisely because an alias that can resolve to
Uninhabited has no single wire identity at all.
So: law B is NOT silent on 1 of the 4 pairs, and the count of RULING-NEEDED pairs is unchanged
at 4. Re-measured facts for all 8 symbols at this HEAD: every one is still
candidate=unclassified, projection=none, reservation=NO. Law A = 0 for all 8, still.

    (the four, with their re-measured occurrence counts)
    MetaCertificateLedger | ShardCertificateLedger        1 occurrence each, both in-appendix,
      lawA=0 lawB=0 -- CONFIRMED at this HEAD, the note's original claim survives re-measurement.
      The single occurrence IS the defining sentence, so there are zero uses anywhere.
      "replica-local immutable maps rooted by the role's RaftStateRoot" -- a structure, not a
      ref. `physical` is a live answer: the accepted vocabulary is SIX
      (logical|physical|bootstrap|prebootstrap|wire|unclassified), not a wire/logical binary.
      THIS IS THE ONLY ONE OF THE FOUR WHERE BOTH INSTRUMENTS ARE GENUINELY SILENT.
    MetaAuthorizationEvidence<Tag> | ProtocolAuthorizationEvidence<Tag>   2 occurrences each,
      both in-appendix, lawA=0 lawB=1 -- see the CORRECTION above. Law B fires (arm-payload
      carriers in ShardControlAuthority<Tag> at a04:1880) and still does not make this a mint,
      because the symbol is a generated ASSOCIATED TYPE that resolves to StrongRef<T>/CRSR<T>/
      Uninhabited. Resolution belongs on the carrying field; a wire type here strands the
      transcript. The Uninhabited arm is the hard part.
    AuthorizedDeltaPublicProvenance | PublicDeliveryDigest   5 occurrences each, and only 1 of
      the 5 is in-appendix -- DEFINED OUTSIDE APPENDIX A (SS9.5 / Appendix D), confirmed.
      NEW: AuthorizedDeltaPublicProvenance has a genuine FIELD carrier at L3063
      (`public_provenance:AuthorizedDeltaPublicProvenance`), which is OUTSIDE the Appendix A
      range, so whether it counts as a structural use is the same question the L322 mention
      raises for the PreBootstrap pair -- but a field-shaped carrier is strictly stronger
      evidence than a prose mention, so do not dismiss it the same way without ruling on it.
      PublicDeliveryDigest scores lawB=0 across all 5 (L770, L774 x2, L3184 all prose) and L774
      is its `= BLAKE3(...)` definition: a plan-named digest, never a wire type; minting one
      strands the transcript. The two sides differ in kind -- see the shortcut section.
    PreBootstrapDispatchPublicationEvidence<Action> | PreBootstrapNeverSentProof<Action>
      2 and 1 occurrences, lawA=0 lawB=0 both -- CONFIRMED. NeverSentProof's single occurrence
      is its definition; the other symbol's only further mention is at line 322, OUTSIDE the
      Appendix A range 1388-2728, so it is a section-body mention and not a structural use.

## THREE TRAPS THAT COST REAL TIME. Do not rediscover these.
 1. A LAW-B ZERO IS NOT AN ABSENCE. LocalReadWitnessRef/LocalWriteSummaryRef score 0 on a
    `name:Type` matcher and look uncontained. They are carried as
    `complete_read_witness_refs[LocalReadWitnessRef]` -- the BRACKET-ARRAY carrier, the third
    shape, whose omission the census DAG's own guard records as having silently dropped 139
    references. Match `name:T`, `Wrapper<T>` AND `name[T]`, then enumerate every occurrence
    and check consumed == present before believing any zero. DONE for all 6 union symbols this
    rotation: 13 occurrences total (2/2/2/3/2/2), every one classified, consumed == present,
    all inside the Appendix A range. No reader gap remains on these six.
 2. THE APPLY SEQUENCE IS: splice CATALOG ONLY -> refreeze -> hand-repair -> regenerate.
    appendix-regenerate FAILS CLOSED and publishes nothing while any violation stands, and
    refreeze_identity_pins.sh REFUSES to start if appendix_a.rs is already dirty. So no
    checker-source edit may be pre-applied. The refreeze exits 1 NAMING what it cannot re-pin,
    which is honest, not broken: a wire mint leaves projection_unclassified_reference_wrapper
    (add each name to registered_reference_definition_semantics, or it fires); a logical mint
    at an EXISTING reservation additionally leaves catalog_reservation_assignment_drift +
    catalog_reservation_epoch_drift and the two reservation-count consts.
 3. RESOLVING A CONSUMER FROM SOURCE SILENTLY RETURNS ARM NAMES. allowed_containing_schemas
    must name the top-level consumer. Two definition-head spellings exist, "`Name` is" and
    "`Name {", and the naive second pattern also matches every ARM head inside a union value
    span, yielding `ActiveHidden`/`Operational` instead of the real schema. The discriminator
    is WHITESPACE: a top-level spec head is "`Name {" WITH a space, an arm head is "`Name{"
    without. Both wrong answers look like plausible schema names. THIS FIRED THREE TIMES this
    rotation -- ResultLeaseRef, RestoreReconciliationEvidenceRef and RestoreExplicitRetention-
    OwnerRef are all carried inside ARMS, so their naive consumers would have been
    ActiveDeliverable / Resolved / ExplicitlyRetained instead of the real records.

## BEADS FILED FROM THIS BEAD
  fgdb-arm-path-order-gap-9mhk   LANDED d9d4e28. The arm-path construction_order gap, proven by
    control (order 40 vs 27 byte-identical verdict). Was staged unfiled in order_gap_bead.txt.
  fgdb-genunion-armset-ucqj   the family arm-set ruling request (10 symbols, 7 outside ww9g). OPEN.
  fgdb-a20-historical-witness-red-opc5   the main-red at 19ea99b, filed for the a20 lane. OPEN.

## STAGED, NOT LANDED -- in /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane4_ww9g/ (keep hygiene off this directory)
  REMAINING_10.md   the previous rotation's per-pair derivation. STILL ACCURATE on the 4
                    ruling-needed pairs and on the shape split, but its "SPLICE-READY" section
                    is spent (72aec3f consumed it) and its plan for the 3 union pairs -- "host
                    + N union_variant + [[union]] + N [[union_arm]] + 4 target classes + the
                    candidate flip" -- is correct as a SHAPE and unreachable in practice,
                    because the arm sets are not source-derivable. Read it after this note,
                    not instead of it.
  order_gap_bead.txt  now FILED as fgdb-arm-path-order-gap-9mhk. Kept as the evidence record.
  APPLY.md, rows.toml, rows2.toml, splice*.py, and ~18 checker logs -- the worked examples and
                    evidence for the landed commits. splice*.py are QUIET-ROOT harnesses only
                    and must never be run against /data/projects.
  ww9g_note.txt     the rotation-2 note (HEAD 8189042), superseded. This file is the note.

## !! MAIN IS RED AT 19ea99b, AND IT IS NOT ww9g's !! (found at the end of this rotation)
tests/identity.rs `idr_assignment_history_and_epoch_are_frozen` FAILS, exit 101, 129/130.
ATTRIBUTED BY DIFFERENTIAL, not by diffstat reasoning -- two .git-free quiet roots from
`git archive`, .beads/ present in both so neither could early-return a false green:
    400c97b (pane2's parent)  -> ok. 1 passed.  exit 0
    19ea99b (pane2's a20 landing) -> FAILED.     exit 101
19ea99b is `feat(a20): land the two field rows unblocked by ww9g's tag-refined ref mints
[fgdb-a20-restore-promotion-ivsp]`. My 08d50f3 touched only .beads/issues.jsonl, which the
witness transcript does not read, and is not implicated.

CAUSE, and the fix is precedented. pane2 added two [[field]] rows to durable_fields.toml --
  manifest_ref (0x0003) and operational_terminal_pin_basis_ref (0x0009), i.e. exactly the two
a20 field candidates ww9g's mints unblocked -- and correctly re-froze the FORWARD pin
(src/identity.rs FIELDS a337b796abfbdfcc -> 8a2eff046882cedd). But the HISTORICAL witness
reconstructs the PRE-erratum namespace, so post-erratum rows must be FILTERED OUT of the
reconstruction, never re-pinned. The two new rows are unfiltered, so their lines move the
historical hash. This is the standing law "historical witness is not a pin -- extend its
post_erratum filter", and the test's own panic message says the same thing and warns that
A10_COMMAND_REF_ERRATUM_PREVIOUS_FIELDS_PIN "was re-pinned to conceal a mismatch once at
8a704c2 and is why this failure recurred". DO NOT re-pin it.
THE FIX: add a `post_erratum_a20_field` closure in tests/identity.rs filtering those two
(schema, name) pairs and wire it into the same retain as the existing siblings --
post_erratum_a11_field @8385, post_erratum_a05_field @8411, post_erratum_a04_field @8543 are
the pattern to copy. NOT APPLIED BY ME: it is inside pane2's active lane and the owner
coordinates gate holds. Escalated to the owner instead.

## ALSO WORTH KNOWING
  * ubs cannot function as a gate on this repo: its true exit code is 1 on a clean tree, and
    all 277 Critical are one false-positive class, "Secret, signature, or token compared with
    ==/!=", firing on the checker's own pin equality comparisons. Untouched files exit 1 the
    same way. Beware `ubs ... | tail`, which reports TAIL's status and reads green on a red run.
  * The identity suite and the lib's own cfg(test) units can both be built with rustc and need
    NO build slot. Measured this rotation:
      rustc --edition 2024 -O --crate-name registry_check --crate-type rlib \
        tools/registry-check/src/lib.rs -o rc/libregistry_check.rlib
      CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR=/data/projects/frankengraphdb/tools/registry-check rustc --edition 2024 \
        -O --test --extern registry_check=rc/libregistry_check.rlib tools/registry-check/tests/<T>.rs
    identity.rs -> 130 tests, 11.05s, exit 0. architecture_decisions.rs -> 42 tests, 0.67s,
    exit 0. CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR is mandatory or it will not compile. Run them LOCALLY -- through
    rch the identity suite early-returns green without .beads/, and an 11s run vs a ~1s run is
    the tell that the corpus was actually read.
  * A br create costs NO pin re-freeze. Verified in code, not assumed: the pin is a FLOOR
    (PINNED_BEAD_COUNT_FLOOR = 401 at architecture.rs:78, compared with `>=` at
    architecture_decisions.rs:168 and `<` at architecture.rs:3211). Both suites stayed green
    across the beads filed this rotation.
  * rc/ at the repo root is an untracked build directory created by the previous rotation and
    reused by this one; it is awaiting the owner's deletion call. Not removed.
  * scripts/g0_tree_stability_e2e.sh is untracked in the worktree and is NOT mine -- another
    pane's new file. Left alone.

instrument that makes "recovered but unclassified" a visible debt rather than a silent one. Recording

title: token.sh has no timeout: an expired lease still blocks, and clearing it needs a human steal after TTL+20m
notes:
=== pane2, read from /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/token.sh directly. Orchestrator's finding; recorded so it outlives the session. ===

A TTL IN THIS SUBSTRATE IS A LABEL, NOT A TIMEOUT.

  token.sh:56   acquire is `mkdir "$lock"`. If the directory exists the acquire
                FAILS -- unconditionally, regardless of the hold's age. Nothing
                anywhere reaps an expired lock.
  token.sh:65   age > ttl + 20m only changes what `status` PRINTS:
                "HELD by X for Nm — EXCEEDS ttl Lm + 20m grace"
  token.sh:67   and then it prints an instruction for a HUMAN: `token.sh steal`.
  token.sh:99   steal is the only path that clears another holder, and its own
                usage line says "only after the holder is proven dead".

CONSEQUENCES, which are what matter:
  * An expired lease keeps blocking until the holder releases or a human steals.
  * A pane that dies or is rotated mid-hold blocks that lane for a MINIMUM of
    TTL + 20m -- 32 minutes on a 12m lease -- and then still needs a human
    ruling, because "proven dead" is not something the script can decide.
  * Therefore every TTL cap enforced tonight was ADVISORY. The thing that
    actually prevented starvation was the release discipline: acquire, work,
    release in the same tool sequence. Not the number.

MEASURED TONIGHT, not hypothetical: pane3's lander
(/data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/pane3_i1rx_apply3/autoland.sh) sat in a sleep-3 retry loop
for ~25 minutes against exactly this mechanism, losing every race to panes that
were already awake and holding longer leases. The swarm went four ticks with zero
commits while a fully-derived apply waited behind a token.

WHY A POLLING LOOP LOSES: acquire is non-blocking and there is no queue, so
`mkdir` is won by whoever calls it in the instant after a release. A pane polling
every 3s competes with panes that release-and-immediately-reacquire, and FIFO by
wait time is not expressible in the substrate at all -- it exists only as
orchestrator arbitration.

CANDIDATE REPAIRS, none applied here, roughly increasing in cost:
  1. Make the grace expiry ACT: let acquire break a lock older than ttl+grace and
     log the break loudly, rather than only printing advice. Removes the 32-minute
     floor for a dead holder. Risk: breaks a live-but-slow holder, which is
     exactly what the current design refuses to do -- so it needs a liveness
     probe, not an age threshold. (Compare the age-vs-liveness lesson already
     learned on stale bead sweeps: age cannot distinguish dead from parked.)
  2. Add a real QUEUE: a ticket file per waiter so FIFO-by-wait-time is mechanical
     rather than an orchestrator ruling every time.
  3. Have the holder write its PID, so "proven dead" becomes checkable instead of
     human-judged.
NOTE 1 and 3 compose: a PID that no longer exists is a liveness answer, not an age
one, and is the only safe basis for an automatic break.

The script's own comment at :87 already names the hazard from the other side --
"a legitimately-working holder's TTL silently becomes a lie, which invites either
a bad steal or an agent abandoning correct work to look compliant." That comment
is right, and this bead is its mirror image: the same design also means a DEAD
holder blocks indefinitely. Both follow from there being no liveness signal.
close_reason:
PREMISE RE-DERIVED AND IT HOLDS. Filed scope was the FINDING ("CANDIDATE REPAIRS, none applied
here"); the finding is now verified line by line, three corrections are recorded, and the repair is
split to fgdb-5j16. Closing on the finding, not on the repair — the defect is still live.

VERDICT: HELD. This is the third of thirteen premises re-derived this run to survive, after ch8r
and 2gqb, and it survived a stronger test than reading: every cited line number is byte-exact
(56, 65, 67, 87, 99) and token.sh is unmodified since 2026-07-25 03:26, which PREDATES the bead, so
nothing silently fixed it. Axis A clean.

WHAT HOLDS, verified per item rather than in aggregate:
  * acquire is `mkdir "$lock"` and exits 1 UNCONDITIONALLY when the directory exists, regardless of
    the hold's age — there is no path from the age check to acquiring.
  * No reaper exists anywhere: the only two rmdir sites are release (82) and steal (102), both
    human-initiated, neither time-based.
  * No queue; acquire is non-blocking, so FIFO-by-wait-time is not expressible in the substrate.
  * Therefore a TTL is a LABEL and release discipline, not the number, is what prevents starvation.
    Corroborated by this pane's own session: catalog, build-1 and beads were acquired and released
    across several cycles, no TTL ever acted, and `status` reads all-free only because every holder
    released.

THREE CORRECTIONS, none of which moves the conclusion:
  1. FALSIFIED: "steal is the only path that clears another holder." `release <tok> force` bypasses
     the holder check (line 79, `[ "$who" != "force" ]`). Mutation-proven with paired controls on a
     private probe token: wrong agent -> REFUSED rc=1; `force` -> RELEASED rc=0; probe cleaned up.
     So there is NO 32-minute floor to clear a stranded lease, and `force` is undocumented in both
     usage strings. The swarm's cost model for a stranded lease is wrong.
  2. UNDERSTATED: the age check is in ACQUIRE, not `status`, and the status branch (106-118) has no
     age comparison at all. A pane or orchestrator surveying lanes with `status` cannot see

title: Empty-net writes still occupy the delta window
description:
An all-no-op WriteBatch (ensure of a live identity, if-present of a missing one, CAS NoOp miss) still commits a sequence. The derived delta window must name that sequence.

## Background
Empty-net batches are lawful (`ensure_vertex` of a live vid commits). The live index tests only write `create_vertex`, which always emits a row. A window that skipped empty-net commits would have a gap at that seq; a reopen that dropped them would disagree with the retained handle. Ripple/CDC walk this window.

Related to `og6n` / `ltji` / `qvfr`. Do **not** parent-child to open `og6n`. Closing this does not close `og6n`.

## Technical Approach
After a creating ensure and a no-op ensure:
- frontier advances on both commits
- `delta_index` is gap-free over both seqs
- the no-op batch has zero delta rows
- `delta_since(origin)` yields both seqs
- reopen rebuilds the same window, including the empty-net entry

## Success Criteria
- Spine test names the empty-net seq and its zero row count.
- Reopen still has that seq.
- `og6n` stays open.

## Test Plan
`cargo test -p fgdb --test spine -- empty_net`
close_reason: Empty-net ensure occupies seq 2 with zero rows; delta_since walks (seq1,1),(seq2,0); reopen keeps the entry. Production path already did this; now witnessed. og6n stays open.

title: Pin-cycle tool: script the base-derived re-freeze once so lquj, dkjg step 5 and 1nfu's candidate execute mechanically
description:
Three beads are stuck at the SAME boundary -- fgdb-lquj, fgdb-dkjg step 5, and
RemoteRetentionConsumerRoot.transfer_evidence_ref from fgdb-1nfu. All three are
derived, correct, and waiting on a mint-and-pin cycle. That is one missing tool,
not three blockers. Same shape as fgdb-1j16: fix the repeated procedure at the
source instead of having each holder re-derive it under pressure.

## Invocation

    bash /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/refreeze_identity_pins.sh

  FGDB_ROOT        default /data/projects/frankengraphdb
  FGDB_PIN_CACHE   default $TMPDIR/fgdb-pin-cycle  (~75MB rlib+binary, reused)
  FGDB_PIN_ROUNDS  default 4

  exit 0  pins correct, drift set EMPTY (it may have written)
  exit 1  refused to start, or drift survived the rewrite
  exit 2  checker unbuildable, or a verdict it could not parse

Run it AFTER applying catalog rows and BEFORE `appendix-regenerate`, which
refuses to write while any drift stands.

## What it does, and the four properties that were required

1. BASE-DERIVED, NEVER HARD-CODED. It never takes a pin from its caller. It runs
   the checker and reads the new value out of the checker's own message,
       released assignment pin "OLD" != recomputed "NEW"
   emitted by identity.rs at the `registry_assignment_drift` site (:1443). Nothing
   in the script computes a pin. HEAD moves several times per increment here, so a
   value read a minute ago is already suspect.
2. RE-RUNNABLE. A second round after a peer commit is one invocation. It loops
   until the drift set is EMPTY, not merely smaller, and stops at FGDB_PIN_ROUNDS
   rather than spinning.
3. STATES WHAT MOVED. One `rewrote OLD -> NEW` line per pin plus a total, so the
   commit message writes itself.
4. REFUSES TO ABSORB A PEER'S EDIT. If identity.rs is already modified it stops
   before building anything, because it cannot tell your pin edit from someone
   else's in-flight work.

Two smaller properties worth keeping: it rewrites an EXACT literal and refuses if
that literal appears anything other than once (never a regex over the file), and
it rebuilds the checker EVERY round -- a binary a few commits stale reported five
drift codes on a tree a fresh build called clean, which is measured, not
hypothetical.

## Controls, all three run, all three behave

  A  clean tree            "no pin movement: the six assignment pins already
                           match the tree", SUMMARY 0, exit 0
  B  deliberately stale    planted fnv1a64:dead0000dead0000 over the LOGICAL pin
     pin in a scratch      in a copied tree ->
     root                     "round 1: 1 pin(s) moved"
                              "rewrote fnv1a64:dead0000dead0000 ->
                                       fnv1a64:403196d930716d3c"
                              "drift set is EMPTY after 1 rewrite round(s)"
                           and the file ends holding the true value, 1 occurrence.
  C  peer-edit guard       touched identity.rs in the real repo -> REFUSED,
                           exit 1, before building anything. Restored, 0
                           modifications.

Control B is the one that matters: it proves the tool CORRECTS rather than merely
reports, and that it reaches empty rather than smaller.

## One fail-open found and closed while building it

The guard first read `git status` unconditionally. In a non-repo root git errors,
the substitution is empty, and the guard passed silently -- a guard that quietly
does nothing, which is the defect this swarm keeps closing. It now branches on
`git rev-parse --git-dir` and, in a non-repo root, prints
    NOTICE: <root> is not a git worktree; the peer-edit guard does not apply here
so the vacuity is announced rather than assumed. Control B's output shows that
notice firing.

## Where it lives, and what promoting it needs

It is at /data/tmp/fgdb_swarm/refreeze_identity_pins.sh, NOT in scripts/, on
purpose: check.sh enforces a file-coverage closure over `git ls-files`, so a new
tracked script must be claimed by a checker_index row or declared exempt in the
same commit or the closure gate reds. Promoting it into scripts/ is a small
catalog-token change and should be done deliberately, not as a side effect.
BECAUSE /data/tmp IS SWEPT -- that is how fgdb-uug4 lost its staging -- the
complete script text is on the FIRST NOTE of this bead. Restore from there if the
file is gone.

## Referenced from

fgdb-lquj and fgdb-dkjg both carry pin-cycle prose. Whoever executes either
should read this command instead of that procedure.
notes:
PANE2 FINDING from fgdb-lquj (2026-07-27): the tool cannot see this bead shape.

refreeze_identity_pins.sh drift_report runs `registry-check identity` and greps
`released assignment pin "X" != recomputed "Y"`. For a LOGICAL-KIND mint that grep
returns EMPTY and the tool reports "no pin movement ... 0 pin(s) rewritten" and
exits 0 -- a FALSE GREEN, while the appendix gate is red with
projection_registry_assignment_drift.

WHY: `identity` validates the CHECKED-IN registries/*.toml projections, which are

SECOND BLOCKER, independent: main.rs:90 collapses EVERY appendix violation message

title: Tier-migration decision cards are a ski-rental problem: pin the competitive ratio in the card schema
notes:
FILED 2026-07-31 from the reality check (Phase 4 Round 2b).

THE PLAN ALREADY DESCRIBES THIS PROBLEM WITHOUT NAMING IT. AGENTS.md's adaptive-decision contract
requires every tier migration to emit a decision card carrying "an expected-benefit interval and the
hysteresis/dwell state", with "minimum dwell time per descriptor", "expected benefit must exceed
conversion cost plus uncertainty", and "a deterministic pinned fallback policy so the lab runtime
replays the decision bit-for-bit".

That is SKI-RENTAL. The structure is identical: keep paying a recurring cost (the read penalty of an
unsealed tier-D partition with many blocks) or pay a one-time conversion cost (seal into tier R) that
eliminates it. The literature gives exact results rather than intuitions:
  - DETERMINISTIC: convert once the accumulated penalty equals the conversion cost. 2-COMPETITIVE, and
    that bound is tight -- no deterministic policy does better.
  - RANDOMIZED: e/(e-1) ~= 1.58-competitive.

WHY THIS MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING TRIVIA. B5 forbids nondeterminism without a declared certificate, so
the randomized policy cannot be the default -- the deterministic 2-competitive rule is exactly the
pinned fallback the contract demands, and a learned estimator is admissible only as an advisory feature
on the card. Naming the technique turns "we have a heuristic with hysteresis" into "we have a policy
with a proven worst-case ratio", which is the difference between a decision card that means something
and one that is a log line.

THE CONCRETE ASK: the decision card schema should carry the COMPETITIVE RATIO the policy claims. Then a
policy change is a measurable regression rather than a matter of taste, and the lab runtime replaying a
card can check that the decision the card describes is the one the claimed policy would have made.

SCOPE: this bead is the POLICY and its card schema. Performing tier D -> tier R migration is
fgdb-w3-tier-r-0tj and fgdb-w3-seal-compact-h3p. The conversion-cost and read-penalty MEASUREMENTS must
come from fgdb-w3-write-amp-bnn's accounting -- do not invent constants here.

title: Preflight reference template schema bindings against pre-template state
description: Measured at HEAD 3c99b1a. ReferenceDatabase::apply_template clones state and immediately applies coordinate entries in canonical relation order, but never reads CoordinateEntry.schema_epoch or schema_transition. ReferenceGraph validates only DeltaRow::Schema.before_epoch against whichever candidate epoch exists at that moment. A schema row in an earlier same-graph/branch entry can therefore change the basis seen by later entries, and a template carrying the wrong validated schema binding can still be accepted. Preflight every coordinate entry against the immutable pre-template coordinate snapshot before applying any row; define and enforce the current subset cross-check between schema_transition and Schema rows; preserve all-or-nothing apply. Add negative tests for wrong entry epoch/transition and an ordering test where a same-template schema transition must not rewrite another entrys validation basis. Normative anchor: plan LogicalDeltaTemplate entries carry validated_schema_binding and schema_transition, and inconsistent transition/binding is invalid. description:

Version transcripts are also hashed over the unsorted vec while canonicalize later sorts the durable row.

2. AlreadyLive is checked before IdentitySpent and does not consult prefix_deleted_*. create/add_edge after a same-batch delete of that id is AlreadyLive. The IdentitySpent comment already says spent includes earlier-in-this-batch.

Related to closed kokz / ac6y. Not parent-child to open 819. Do not close 819.

title: Checker census-gap repair: arm-payload field identity + wire-hosted fields
description:
The v3/v4 Appendix A checker has two structural completion gaps, discovered during a01 increment-2 rehearsal (reported on fgdb-appendix-a-catalog-scaffold-gvvf 2026-07-23 03:29Z, acknowledged by the a20 schema-v4 note but never repaired; the scaffold bead closed without them). Both make complete-slice census equality unsatisfiable for every nontrivial slice.

GAP 1 - ARM-PAYLOAD FIELD IDENTITY COLLAPSE: field projection identity and row_id derive from (containing_schema, stable_name) only; the field-target matcher discards the census path component (appendix_a.rs canonical_symbol == schema.stable_name with _path discarded). Census field candidates inside union-arm payloads are distinguished ONLY by path. a01 alone has 64 such keys of which 45 collide in 20 groups (AppliedAbortRef.command_ref x4, AuthorityAppliedRef.command_ref x3, RoleTransitionActivationState 10 groups, RemoteAuthorityConfigurationEvidence.trust_transition arms 4 groups). No catalog can give them complete-field census coverage. Repair direction (choose one): (a) extend field identity/row_id derivation to include the census path for arm-payload fields; (b) cover arm payloads through the union_arm contract (payload_sha256 already commits to the payload shape) and exclude union-interior field candidates from the complete-field census pin the way reference-only symbols are excluded.

GAP 2 - WIRE-HOSTED FIELD GAP: fields whose containing schema is a wire type (reference wrappers, ConsensusDomain, RemoteObjectIdentity, CertifiedRemoteStrongRef<T>, StrongCiphertextRef<T>, closed result-role unions, PlacementDescriptorWithoutId) fail projection_field_unresolved_schema because wire types resolve in no identity class. 66 a01 census field keys are uncoverable (e.g. field|StrongRef|StrongRef.oid|oid). Repair direction: (a) allow wire-kind schemas as field hosts in a distinct identity class; (b) exclude wire-family interior fields from the field census like reference-only symbols.

Blocked work quantified (a01 only; every other slice has the same classes): 146 staged fields, 80 staged adjudications (maps-to-source resolved keys must be projected), 11 unions, 31 arms. a16 has 42 arms; the pattern recurs slice-wide.

Acceptance: chosen repair direction implemented with fail-closed census equality preserved; synthetic negative tests for both gap classes; the a01 staged inventory (session scratchpad staged_*.json, enumerated by blocker on the a01 bead trail) lands green against the repaired checker; no weakening of the complete-slice contract for cases the current checker already validates. Interacts with: fgdb-a01-reference-roots-2k0q (146+80+11+31 staged rows), all a02-a21 slices with arm-payload or wire-interior fields, the closed fgdb-appendix-a-catalog-scaffold-gvvf (design provenance).
close_reason: Landed as 0eaffdf (design comment upthread; a15 increment-3 unblock landed separately as 7a32726). Both gap classes repaired via census coverage classes: arm-payload interiors project through the union-arm payload contract, wire-hosted interiors through the targeted wire envelope; complete_field census equality moved to the source pass (verify_complete_field_census_coverage) keeping the appendix gate fail-closed; adjudication projection extended so the 80 staged a01 maps-to-source rows become landable. Five synthetic negatives incl. the a01 collision shape. Acceptance note: the original session-scratchpad staged_*.json corpus no longer exists on disk; the staged a01 rows must be re-derived on fgdb-a01 against the repaired checker (its 64+66 gap classes are now coverable; the 12 generic/foreign-union + 3 cross-slice/plan-gap + 1 RemoteGrantTargetRef residuals stay blocked on their own rulings). title: Model-based history generator: random valid histories + queries, differentially tested against fgdb-reference, with shrinking
notes:
FILED 2026-07-31 from the reality check (docs/REALITY_CHECK_AND_BRIDGE_PLAN.md, Phase 4 Round 1).

THE INSIGHT THIS BEAD EXISTS FOR. We have a COMPLETE, EXECUTABLE SPECIFICATION of the logical
semantics -- fgdb-reference -- and the engine that must match it barely exists yet. Almost no database
has ever been in that position; they all build the engine first and argue afterwards about which of
two implementations is right. §15 already names this ("model-generated histories run against both
engines and compare snapshots, results, certificates, and permitted abort outcomes") and nothing
implements it.

Today every differential in fgdb-sim runs HAND-WRITTEN histories. They are good -- they found the
supersede-per-version defect, the forced-seal constraint, the cascade coverage gap -- but a human
writes maybe a dozen, and the space is MVCC x branches x path modes x temporal selectors x intent
policies. Hand-written cases cannot cover that and everyone knows it.

WHAT TO BUILD, in dependency order:

1. AN INTENT-LEVEL GENERATOR, not an effect-level one. Generate sequences of Statements/Intents
   (fgdb-reference::intents), never DeltaRows directly. This matters: intents are finalized against
   real state, so a generated program CANNOT produce a history the system could not reach. An
   effect-level generator spends most of its output on before-images that no state ever had, and
   every such case is a false failure that trains people to ignore the tool.
2. RUN BOTH SIDES on the same generated program: fgdb-reference for the answer, the engine path
   (Chronicle commit -> recover -> Strata writer -> merge) for the comparison. The plumbing already
   exists in fgdb-sim/tests/partition_lifecycle.rs and durable_stream_to_strata.rs -- extend those
   instruments rather than building a third.
3. SHRINKING, and this is not optional. A failing 400-step history is a curiosity; a shrunk 3-step one
   is a bug report. Shrink by: dropping statements, dropping intents within a statement, shrinking
   scalar values, and reducing branch depth -- re-running after each removal and keeping the removal
   only if the failure survives. Without shrinking this tool will be built, will find something once,
   and will be abandoned.
4. SEED REPORTING. Every failure prints the seed and the shrunk program as a compilable test case that
   can be pasted into a laws file. That is what converts a fuzz finding into a permanent law.
5. UNDER DPOR, once the lab VFS work (fgdb-1xtp) lands. asupersync ships deterministic partial-order
   reduction; generated histories explored under scheduled interleavings make concurrency bugs SEEDS
   rather than folklore. Do not block 1-4 on this.

A SECOND, CHEAPER PAYOFF worth naming: the oracle answers a query by brute force, so it yields both an
expected RESULT and an exact CARDINALITY. Once a planner exists, that cardinality is a free
estimator-accuracy signal on every generated query -- a planner regression detector nobody has to
write test cases for.

SCOPE BOUNDARY. This bead is the generator, the shrinker and the harness. It is NOT the conformance
corpora (openCypher TCK, GQL feature matrix) and NOT the Neo4j/Memgraph differential; those are
separate §15 items with their own beads.

THE FAILURE MODE TO AVOID: a generator whose distribution is so tame it only produces histories the
hand-written tests already cover. Bias it deliberately toward the shapes that broke things before --
re-created keys (which force a block seal), cross-block retirements, deep branch forks, transactions
that abort after writing, and re-creation after cascade deletion. Record the distribution in the code
and treat "the generator never produced shape X" as a coverage bug in the generator.
close_reason: Landed in 8c53adb and verified present at HEAD. Intent-level generator with model-maintained validity, SplitMix64 seeding with a determinism law, a shrinker that preserves the failure KIND, pasteable regression reports, and asserted coverage counters; 240 generated histories x 24 steps agree with the oracle at every sequence for every source. POWER MEASURED: re-keying merge_neighbours by destination (the fgdb-0trr defect) was caught at seed 4 and shrunk, with root.rs restored byte-identical. Remainder split out to fgdb-uy5x. RE-CLOSED 2026-08-01: an earlier close of this bead did not stick -- the record is absent from the tracked .beads/issues.jsonl, so a shared-DB import or another pane's action reverted it to open while the code was already in HEAD.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Reopened: Fresh-eyes audit of 8c53adb found the closure does not satisfy this bead's explicit contract: the generator maps local Step values directly to DeltaRow and drives ReferenceGraph plus BlockWriter, rather than generating fgdb-reference::intents Statements/Intents and running Chronicle commit -> recover -> Strata. It shrinks only whole steps, not statements/intents/scalars/branch depth, and check_agrees asserts only final adjacency (as_of >= last), not snapshots/results/certificates/permitted abort outcomes. fgdb-uy5x records branches/transactions/DPOR/properties but does not record the missing intent-finalization and Chronicle pipeline, so it is not a complete residue handoff. Keep the useful storage-oracle tranche from 8c53adb; reopen the original until the named contract is implemented or honestly repartitioned with complete successor coverage.

title: Strata writer: same-commit create+delete of one edge poisons the seal instead of folding to nothing
description: crates/fgdb-strata/src/writer.rs push/retire (202-283): CreateEdge(e)@5 then DeleteEdge(e)@5 stages AdjacencyEntry{created 5, retired 5}, and seal's validate_entry refuses the empty interval (RetiredBeforeCreated, lib.rs:213-224) — the whole publish fails. VERIFIED at HEAD (scout StrataDeep F5). The reference intent evaluator LEGALLY produces create+delete in one transaction (read-your-own-writes, intents.rs:24-29, 579-586); nothing in fgdb-delta-types collapses net-effect pairs (checked, none exists). title: identity_class is unenforced for non-reference fields: validate_identity accepts inline, logical, scalar and physical identically
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-27 at pinned SHA e14563e by pane3 while on fgdb-uug4, by
synthesizing rows and asking the checker — the method that was supposed to answer
the question and instead showed the question is unanswerable.

## The measurement

Took the five FLAT non-reference a05 field candidates, synthesized a FieldRow for
each against a clean snapshot (BASE violations = 0), and ran validate_identity
four times, changing ONLY identity_class:

    identity_class = "inline"    -> 11 new violations
    identity_class = "logical"   -> 11 new violations, IDENTICAL code set
    identity_class = "scalar"    -> 11 new violations, IDENTICAL code set
    identity_class = "physical"  -> 11 new violations, IDENTICAL code set

Only the recomputed assignment hash differs between them. The eleven violations
are five bad_cardinality + five field_construction_order_mismatch + one
registry_assignment_drift — all unrelated to the class. THE VACUITY CONTROL DID
NOT FIRE: validate_identity does not discriminate identity_class for a
non-reference field at all.

## Why this is a bug and not a gap

identity_class is durable-format data. Section 5.1 makes durable_fields.toml 'the
sole input to generated reachability/GC, checkpoint-vector, backup-closure,
construction-DAG, compatibility, size-limit, and fuzz walkers'. A wrong
identity_class therefore mis-drives generated reachability and GC — and it is
accepted silently, because every one of the five legal values is individually
legal for any field row.

fgdb-identity-class-record-wire-convention-l6xd exists precisely because the data
could not decide this; the owner ruled 'six flat inline fields plus four exact
arm-payload contracts'. That ruling is settled law and is being applied by hand.
Nothing holds it. The next slice that copies the precedent has no gate telling it
whether it copied correctly, and the l6xd bead's own text names this risk: 'a
wrong value here is not a lint failure that surfaces later — it is a wrong
byte-level contract that the loader accepts'.

This is the same shape closed three times tonight: a7c8 (the aggregate pin left
the per-family split free), 5qcg (six exclusions the reader never consulted),
d9pd (SC2015 unenforced because it is only a note). A rule exists; no checker
holds it.

## Proposed law

    A [[field]] row whose exact_wire_type resolves to a registered wire type whose
    kind is NOT reference_wrapper, and whose reference_semantics is "none", must
    declare identity_class = "inline".

with the completeness guard that makes it fail CLOSED: every field row's
exact_wire_type must resolve to a registered wire type of a KNOWN kind, so a newly
minted wire kind cannot escape the law by being unclassified. Give that guard its
own violation code.

## What must be checked before landing it

1. Apply the candidate law to all 2293 landed durable_fields rows and count
   counterexamples. If it is a law it has zero; if it has a handful they are
   either errata or the law is narrower than stated. That census is the whole
   proof and it is cheap.
2. The UNION-typed non-reference fields are a SEPARATE case and must be excluded
   or separately ruled — measured on a05, 2 of the 7 non-reference candidates are
   union-typed (GlobalControlRecord.origin, and
   RetentionAuthorityTransferAdoptionSpec.transfer_evidence_ref). l6xd said FLAT.
3. Check whether the same silence applies to reference_semantics and
   digest_class; if validate_identity is mute on those too, this bead is wider
   than its title.

## Not authored here

This is a new law over durable-format data and belongs beside the ruling, not
smuggled into a field tranche. fgdb-uug4 carries the measurement that produced it.
close_reason: Both survivor laws verified under a catalog lease: base 0, active 0, and each per-law mutation control fired.

comments.author: pane3
comments.text:
STEP 1 DONE — THE CENSUS THIS BEAD ASKED FOR. The candidate law HOLDS.
Measured at pinned SHA e14563e over every landed durable_fields row.

    landed durable_fields rows ................ 800
    identity_class distribution ............... logical 424, inline 192,
                                                scalar 132, bootstrap_local 29,
                                                physical 23
    registered wire kinds ..................... record, union, union_variant,
                                                discriminant, reference_wrapper

    IN SCOPE of the law (exact_wire_type resolves to a non-reference_wrapper
    wire type AND reference_semantics = "none") ....... 136
        of which wire kind = record ....................  96
        of which wire kind = union .....................  40
    COUNTEREXAMPLES ....................................   0

136 covered / 0 counterexamples. That is what makes it a law rather than a
majority vote, and it is the same bar applied on gls4 (360 rows / 0, then 310
more / 0).

## THIS SETTLES THE UNION SUB-CASE, AND AGAINST MY OWN EARLIER CAUTION

On fgdb-uug4 I split a05's seven non-reference candidates 5 flat / 2 union-typed
and said l6xd does not reach the union-typed pair. The corpus disagrees with the
caution: FORTY landed rows have a union-kind exact_wire_type with
reference_semantics = none, and ALL FORTY declare identity_class = "inline".
There is no counterexample in either sub-case.

So the law should be written over both, and the two a05 union-typed candidates
(GlobalControlRecord.origin, RetentionAuthorityTransferAdoptionSpec.
transfer_evidence_ref) are covered by 40 precedents rather than unsettled. Note
this is a DIFFERENT question from l6xd's "four exact arm-payload contracts",
which were arm-path occurrences, not union-typed fields — I conflated the two
and the census separated them.

## THE COMPLETENESS GUARD IS NOT OPTIONAL: 253 OF 800 ROWS ESCAPE

253 landed rows have an exact_wire_type that does NOT resolve to any registered
wire type — 32% of the corpus. Those are the primitive-typed fields (u64 and
friends), which are legitimately not wire types; note 132 rows carry
identity_class = "scalar", so the populations overlap but are not identical.

Consequence: written naively the law is silent on nearly a third of every field
row, which is precisely the fail-open shape this bead exists to close. The guard
must therefore partition explicitly rather than skip-on-unresolved:

    every field row's exact_wire_type resolves to EITHER a registered wire type
    of a known kind, OR a declared primitive from a closed primitive vocabulary

and a row matching neither is a violation with its own code. Without that second
arm the guard is exactly the -returning table that
[[one-law-two-artifacts]] warns fails open on an unknown name.

## Remaining before the law can be authored

Item 3 of this bead is untouched and I did not measure it: whether
validate_identity is equally silent on reference_semantics and digest_class. If
it is, this bead is wider than its title says. The census probe is at
<scratch>/uug4/census.rs and extends in a few lines to answer it.

comments.author: pane3
comments.text:
ITEM 3 DONE. THE BEAD IS WIDER THAN ITS TITLE — THREE COLUMNS ARE UNENFORCED,
NOT ONE. Measured at pinned SHA e14563e by mutating LANDED rows in place (one
column at a time, so nothing else can be what fires), base violations = 0.

## The harness control FIRES, so every 'SILENT' below is a real silence

    construction_order := 0   ->  field_construction_order_mismatch   FIRES

Without that line, 'silent' could just mean my harness was broken. It is not.

## Result, split by the wire kind of the field's exact type

136 in-scope landed rows = 96 record-kind + 40 union-kind.

  mutation applied to RECORD-kind rows (96)              verdict
  ----------------------------------------------------  ---------------------------
  identity_class := logical | scalar | physical |
                    bootstrap_local                      SILENT  (all four)
  reference_semantics := strong                          CAUGHT  bare_strong_ref,
                                                          reference_semantics_without_reference_type
  reference_semantics := weak                            CAUGHT  bad_field
  reference_semantics := identity                        CAUGHT  bad_field
  reference_semantics := locator                         SILENT
  digest_class := Some("digest256")                      CAUGHT  bad_field
  digest_class := Some("bogus_not_a_class")              CAUGHT  bad_field
  digest_class := None   (CLEAR an existing one)         SILENT

  the same mutations on UNION-kind rows (40)             ordinary_union_field_mismatch

## Three holes, and they are different from each other

1. identity_class is UNENFORCED on record-kind rows — all four wrong values
   accepted. This confirms the original finding and LOCALISES it: the earlier
   synthesis run showed silence, and this shows it is specifically the record-kind
   population. That is the law this bead already proposes.

2. reference_semantics = "locator" IS A ONE-VALUE HOLE IN AN OTHERWISE ENFORCED
   VOCABULARY. strong, weak and identity are all rejected on a non-reference
   field; locator is accepted. That is worse than a uniformly missing law,
   because the vocabulary LOOKS enforced — three of four values fire — so a
   reviewer checking one or two values concludes the column is guarded. NEW, and
   not covered by the proposed inline law.

3. digest_class is enforced in one direction only: SETTING any value on these
   rows is caught, CLEARING an existing one is silent. So a row can silently lose
   its digest_class. Same converse-missing shape as the exemption ledgers in
   5qcg — 'an entry whose subject is gone must fail, AND an entry whose subject no
   longer violates must fail'.

## The union rows are protected BY COINCIDENCE, which is its own finding

Every mutation on the 40 union-kind rows raises  —
a union-ARM consistency law, not any field-column law. So union-typed rows are
not protected because identity_class/reference_semantics/digest_class are
checked; they are protected because those rows are additionally coupled to an
ordinary-union contract that happens to notice. Decouple that (a union-typed
field not participating in an ordinary union) and the same three holes open on
them too. This is the a7c8 shape exactly: total by coincidence of the current
data, not by construction.

## What this changes about the proposed law

The law as written on this bead covers hole 1 only. It should be authored
alongside two more, all three with the same explicit-partition completeness guard
(registered wire kind OR declared primitive from a closed vocabulary, neither =
violation), because 253 of 800 landed rows resolve to no registered wire type:

  * identity_class  — the inline law already stated here
  * reference_semantics — "locator" must be rejected on a non-reference_wrapper
    exact type, closing the vocabulary that already rejects strong/weak/identity
  * digest_class — clearing must be as loud as setting

## Not authored

Same reason as before: three new laws over durable-format data, and the census
that proves each belongs with it. The probe is at <scratch>/uug4/item3.rs and
prints the whole table in one run.

value whose legitimate use I mistook for an escape.

## LAW 3 — digest_class. RESHAPED, AND NOW DERIVABLE RATHER THAN A JUDGEMENT.

    rows carrying a digest_class ....... 109 of 880
    values ............................. target 40 | weak_identity 35 |
                                         transcript 20 | body 14
    by exact-type wire kind ............ <unregistered/primitive> 82 | record 27

    exact_wire_types appearing BOTH with and without a digest_class ..... 0

That last line is the law. digest_class is a FUNCTION of exact_wire_type across
the whole corpus — no type is split. So the correct law is a consistency law:

statement survived contact with its denominator. Authoring the set as originally

law 1 and the reshaped law 3, each with its own control, plus the explicit
partition guard (314 of 880 rows resolve to no registered wire type, so a
skip-on-unresolved guard is silent on 36% of the corpus).

Controls are NOT yet written for either surviving law. Per the standard on this

title: UBS rust-module 300s timeout under concurrent fleet load emits vacuous partial scan; core-ubs gate must classify it UNRUN-retryable
