comments.text:
RE-MEASUREMENT at 7e9d7e1, 2026-07-26 (pane4, mock/placeholder sweep lane).
Both gates named in this bead are still red; the numbers have moved.

## architecture-check: 11 violations (exit 1), was 4 orphans, now 5

  bead_source_count            .beads/issues.jsonl has 353 distinct records,
                               declared 338, independently pinned 338
  bead_binding_hash_mismatch   declared fnv1a64:6ef322219e81d5c1,
                               recomputed fnv1a64:e2ce5e93a40c410a
  independent_bead_binding_hash_mismatch   same recomputed value vs the code pin
  bead_resolution_class_count  class "bet_label" has 201 rows, declared 188, pinned 188
  bead_class_count_total       declared class counts sum to 335, bead_count is 338
  bead_provenance_not_total    resolved 348 of 353 records
  bead_provenance_orphan x5    fgdb-5cgb, fgdb-active-kind-arm-bijection-break-cuvx,
                               fgdb-bead-table-transcript-gap-a7c8, fgdb-gb9g, fgdb-zwhh

The fifth orphan is new since this bead was filed. All five are present in HEAD.
Note this bead (fgdb-zwhh) is itself one of the orphans.

## cargo fmt --check: still red, 42 `Diff in` hunks

## Split of the remaining work, measured

Of the 11, SEVEN are mechanically fixable by a pure re-freeze — recompute and
write `bead_count`, `bet_label_count`, the four class counts, and `binding_hash`
in `registries/architecture_decisions.toml`, plus `PINNED_BEAD_COUNT`,
`PINNED_BET_LABEL_COUNT`, `PINNED_BEAD_BINDING_HASH` and then
`PINNED_SEMANTIC_CONTRACT_HASH` in `tools/registry-check/src/architecture.rs`.
No judgement required; the checker prints every recomputed value.

FOUR are not mechanical: the five orphans (and the two totals that are derived
from them) need each orphan bead to acquire a bet label, an exact override, or a
family rule. That is a CLAIM about which ADR owns each bead, so it should be made
by whoever filed it, not by a passing re-freeze. Assigning a bet label to another
pane's bead to clear a count is exactly the shortcut that makes a provenance
registry stop meaning anything.

## Why this keeps recurring, which may be the real bead here

The pins move on every bead CREATION, and the doctrine (correctly) requires the
re-freeze to ride in the same commit as the created record. Under a six-agent
swarm that is a treadmill: `.beads/issues.jsonl` is one shared whole-file export,
so any pane's routine flush sweeps every other pane's new records, and the
re-freeze obligation lands on whoever commits — who is generally not the author
and cannot supply the missing bet labels.

Observed directly today: six bead records created by pane4 were swept into
pane3's commit 7e9d7e1 ("chore(beads): file the unsafe-islands remainder and the
two red gates") without a re-freeze. No fault of pane3's — the export is
whole-file and the sweep is invisible in a line-level diff stat. But the result
is that main's provenance pins are stale again within minutes of any repair, so
"re-freeze the pins" is not a fix, it is a chore with a half-life.

Worth considering as the actual remedy: make the pin a function of the file
rather than a copy of it (i.e. verify a computed digest against a committed
transcript that the flush regenerates), or scope the count pins to exclude
records whose provenance is unresolved so that orphans fail loudly on their own
row instead of also breaking three unrelated aggregate pins.

independently. So a correct token holder still exports records it did not

pins so unresolved-provenance records fail on their own row instead of also
breaking three aggregate pins that any pane can trip by existing.

comments.text:
CLOSING MEASUREMENT (pane4, 2026-07-26). Both gates named in this bead are GREEN
at HEAD 6950174, measured against a pristine `git archive HEAD` copy, lock-free,
no cargo.

## Gate 1 — bead-provenance pins: GREEN, 27/27

    rustc --edition=2024 --crate-type=lib --crate-name registry_check \
      tools/registry-check/src/lib.rs -o lib2.rlib
    CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR=<archive>/tools/registry-check rustc --edition=2024 --test \
      tools/registry-check/tests/architecture_decisions.rs --extern registry_check=lib2.rlib
    -> test result: ok. 27 passed; 0 failed.

All four rows named in this bead now pass: architecture_registry_parses_and_validates,
architecture_bead_provenance_is_total_pinned_and_bidirectional,
architecture_neg_semantic_change_with_stable_id,
architecture_neg_rule_tables_and_resolution_pins.
Zero `bead_provenance_orphan`. Zero `bead_provenance_not_total`.

## Gate 2 — cargo fmt --check: GREEN, 0 hunks

    find crates tools -name '*.rs' | xargs rustfmt --edition 2024 --check
    -> rc=0, 0 `Diff in` hunks over 115 files.

Was 56, then 42. The remaining 42 were cleared by their owners during the session.

## How the five orphans were actually discharged — NOT by bet labels

The ORPHAN OWNERSHIP MAP (comment above) routed five orphans. They were adopted in
`2cba0a8` ("split a16 law-gated residue"), by `[[bead_override]]` rows rather than
by bet labels — five new rows, `bead_override` 13 -> 18, `exact_override_count`
13 -> 18:

    appendix-a13-source-authority-residue        fgdb-gb9g   -> FG-ADR-CON-06
    appendix-a20-promotion-candidate-boundary    fgdb-5cgb   -> FG-ADR-CON-06
    appendix-a-active-kind-arm-bijection         ...-cuvx    -> FG-ADR-CON-06
    architecture-bead-rule-transcript-coverage   ...-a7c8    -> FG-ADR-CON-11
    unsafe-islands-red-gates                     fgdb-zwhh   -> FG-ADR-CON-11

That mechanism is *stricter* than a bet label, not weaker: a bet label resolves to
the generic `FG-ADR-BET-B{n}`, whereas an override names a specific frozen ADR. And
it edits `registries/**` (catalog-token-guarded) instead of the shared bead records
(the sweep treadmill described above). It was the right call.

## AUDIT OF THE FIVE BETS, derived from the plan's B1-B6 rather than from the row

The ruling required each bet to be derived from the plan's own definitions, because
a wrong one is a silent mis-classification no checker catches. The two ADRs used
declare their own bets, so each override implies a bet:

    FG-ADR-CON-06  "published-recovery-root-source-of-truth"   affected_bets = ["B1"]
    FG-ADR-CON-11  "typed-claims"                              affected_bets = ["B5"]

Independent derivation, per record:

- **fgdb-gb9g -> B1. Correct.** a13 is "Branch manifest, key grants, retirement, and
  merge formats". B1 is explicit that "git-style database branches" are the same
  append-only content-addressed commit stream as MVCC/time-travel/replication.
  Branch manifest + merge format is Chronicle durable format. (Caveat recorded, not
  a dispute: the key-grant/KeyEnvelope portion has an Aegis/B6 flavour; the record's
  live content is field-identity rows and reference-semantics laws, which are B1.)

- **fgdb-5cgb -> B1. Correct, and the best fit of the five.** a20 is restore
  promotion / reopen / completion / release. CON-06 is literally "reconstruct
  canonical state from the published checkpoint and contiguous logical-command
  suffix". Restore promotion *is* the recovery-root story.

- **fgdb-bead-table-transcript-gap-a7c8 -> B5. Correct.** A bare row count standing
  in for table integrity is a weaker claim class justifying a stronger one, which is
  CON-11 verbatim.

- **fgdb-zwhh (this bead) -> B5. Correct.** "While these are red, 'I ran the gates'
  cannot distinguish a change that broke something from one that did not" is a
  claim-typing failure, not a durable-format one.

- **fgdb-active-kind-arm-bijection-break-cuvx -> B1. Defensible, but narrow —
  recorded as a finding, not repaired.** The record has two halves. Its stated
  "decision needed" (seven durable logical object kinds `active` vs `reserved`,
  0x028f/0x0550-0x0555) is a durable code-space choice: B1, CON-06, correct. But its
  other half — "enforcement lived ONLY in two `const _: () = assert!` inside
  fgdb-types; registry-check, the identity suite, architecture-check and the G0
  identity e2e were ALL GREEN on the exact tree that would not build" — is CON-11/B5,
  and it is what shipped `validate_active_logical_kind_arms` in 47807be.

  I considered adding FG-ADR-CON-11 to that override row and decided against it. The
  B5 half is not unowned: `fgdb-bead-table-transcript-gap-a7c8` is the sweep cuvx
  triggered, and it is already bound to CON-11. Adding a second ADR whose content is
  bound elsewhere would be churn on a green gate, under a contended catalog token,
  for no gate benefit. CON-06 alone is not *wrong* for cuvx; it is *primary*.
  Flagging rather than editing, so the next owner can disagree with the reasoning
  in front of them.

Net: 4 of 5 clean, 1 defensible-but-narrow with its complement separately owned.
No mis-classification found.

## THE CLASS FIX — and the ruling's proposed fix is the wrong one

Ruled: "a validation that a bet label must be b1..b6 is the permanent fix." Measured,
that validation ALREADY EXISTS and already works. Probe of four synthetic records
through `architecture::validate_architecture`:

    ["b9"]      -> bead_bet_label_unknown naming "b9"  AND  bead_provenance_orphan
    ["w1"]      -> bead_provenance_orphan ONLY; the message never mentions w1
    ["w1","b1"] -> nothing; resolves bet_label, the w1 silently discarded
    ["b3"]      -> nothing; resolves bet_label

`looks_like_bet_label` (architecture.rs:2147) is `b` + all-digits. A workstream tag
fails that predicate, so it is filtered out of `allowed_labels` (:2226-2233) and
**never reaches the vocabulary check at :2235**. The b1..b6 rule is not missing; it
is unreachable for this input.

Nor can workstream tags be rejected: 236 label-instances (w1..w12, g0..g4) exist
across the 375 records, and only 9 records carry one with no bet label — 8 of which
already resolve by another mechanism. A prohibition would red 236 legitimate rows.

The permanent fix is therefore a scoped *diagnostic*, not a new prohibition, filed as
its own bead per the ruling: `bead_workstream_label_in_bet_position`, emitted only on
the would-otherwise-orphan path, naming the bead and the offending label.

## Closing this bead

Both gates it names are green and independently reproduced above. The treadmill it
diagnosed is real and unfixed, but it is scoped on the successor bead plus the
existing `scripts/bead_provenance_preflight.sh`, which already reports the exact
required re-freeze before a `.beads/` commit. This record has served its purpose.

title: Strata block creation fsyncs the inode but not either containing directory
description: Measured at HEAD ca69ab9cd3d5a2eb312944f3cdfbc4fb1fe647b0. crates/fgdb-strata/src/store.rs BlockStore::open creates strata-blocks with create_dir_all, and BlockStore::put creates each content-addressed block with create_new, writes it, and calls file.sync_all through CommitCx, but never syncs strata-blocks or the database parent directory. A crash can therefore lose the block dirent or the strata-blocks dirent after put returned Ok, contradicting the module claim that the block is durable and making a published partition root point at absent bytes. Closure should use the same ordered creation barrier proven by fgdb-83qs: inode sync, containing-directory sync, and database-parent sync when the block directory is new or uncertain after reopen; add loss/survival crash-image controls and keep existing dedup/collision behavior.
notes:
Implemented and landed as 2fceaf7. BlockStore::open now accepts &CommitCx, creates strata-blocks without recursive root creation, rejects a non-directory or symlink at that path, and establishes the ordered child-directory to database-parent durability barrier on every open so an uncertain prior creation is repaired. BlockStore::put now establishes file-inode to strata-blocks-directory durability before success; equal existing bytes are not rewritten but re-enter the barrier after reopen. Added production-path crash hooks plus loss and survival controls and barrier-order unit tests.

Focused evidence on the exact landed content: cargo fmt --all -- --check exit 0; cargo test -p fgdb-strata --lib --test block_store exit 0 with 2 library and 14 integration tests; cargo test -p fgdb-strata --all-targets --no-fail-fast exit 0 with 83 tests; cargo clippy -p fgdb-strata --all-targets -- -D warnings exit 0; ubs on the two owned paths exit 0 with zero critical findings; git diff --check exit 0.
